refined_question: Let n >= 1, let z=(z_1,...,z_n), let C[z]=C[z_1,...,z_n], and write D_i = partial/partial z_i for 1 <= i <= n. Let Delta := sum_{i=1}^n D_i^2 be the Laplace operator on C[z]. If P(z) in C[z] is a homogeneous polynomial of degree 4 whose Hessian matrix Hes P = (D_i D_j P)_{1<=i,j<=n} is nilpotent (that is, P is Hessian nilpotent), is it true that there exists N >= 1 such that Delta^m(P(z)^(m+1)) = 0 for every integer m >= N?

Let n≥1 and z=(z1,...,zn). Suppose P(z) is either a polynomial in C[z] or a formal power series in C[[z]] such that o(P)≥2 and (Hes P)(0) is nilpotent, so that for the associated symmetric formal map F(z)=z-∇P(z) the formal inverse has the form G(z)=z+∇Q(z), where Q(z) is the inversion pair of P(z). If P is self-inverting, i.e. Q(z)=P(z), must P be Hessian nilpotent; equivalently, must the full Hessian matrix Hes P(z) be nilpotent?

Let z=(z_1,\dots,z_n), and let P(z) be either a polynomial in C[z] or a formal power series in C[[z]] with o(P)\ge 2 and (Hes\,P)(0) nilpotent. Let Q(z) denote the inversion pair of P, defined by requiring that the symmetric formal map F(z)=z-\nabla P(z) have formal inverse G(z)=z+\nabla Q(z). If P is self-inverting, i.e. Q(z)=P(z), is P necessarily Hessian nilpotent? More generally, classify all self-inverting polynomials and formal power series, and in particular classify all Hessian nilpotent self-inverting polynomials and formal power series.

Does there exist an integer n>=1 and a Hessian nilpotent formal power series P(z) in C[[z_1,...,z_n]] but not in C[z_1,...,z_n]], where Hes P=(∂^2P/∂z_i∂z_j) is nilpotent and Delta=sum_{i=1}^n ∂^2/∂z_i^2, such that for every N>=1 there exists m>=N with Delta^m(P(z)^{m+1}) != 0? ([impan.pl](https://www.impan.pl/shop/en/publication/transaction/download/product/85371))

Let z = (z1, ..., zn) be commuting variables, let P(z) ∈ C[[z]] be a formal power series of order at least 2 (equivalently, whose lowest total degree is at least 2), and let Δ = Σ_{i=1}^n ∂^2/∂zi^2 be the Laplace operator. If Δ^m(P(z)^m) = 0 in C[[z]] for all sufficiently large integers m, must the Hessian matrix Hes P = (∂^2P/∂zi∂zj) be nilpotent; equivalently, must P(z) be Hessian nilpotent?

Let P(z) in C[z1, ..., zn] be a homogeneous harmonic polynomial of degree d >= 2. Fix a decomposition, as in Theorem 8.1, of the form P(z) = sum_{i=1}^k h_{alpha_i}(z)^d, where h_{alpha_i}(z) := <alpha_i, z>, each alpha_i lies in X(C^n) = {alpha in C^n | <alpha, alpha> = 0}, and the polynomials h_{alpha_i}(z)^d are linearly independent. Define the labeled graph G(P) on vertex set [k] = {1, ..., k} by joining i and j exactly when <alpha_i, alpha_j> != 0, with edge labels given by these pairings (or, when d is even, equivalently by the symmetric weights h_{alpha_i}(z)^{(d-2)/2}<alpha_i, alpha_j>h_{alpha_j}(z)^{(d-2)/2}). What necessary or sufficient conditions on this labeled graph G(P) guarantee that P is Hessian nilpotent, i.e. that the Hessian matrix Hes P = (partial^2 P / partial z_i partial z_j) is nilpotent? In view of Corollary 8.5, it is enough to answer this for connected G(P).

Let P(z) in C[z] be a homogeneous harmonic polynomial of degree d>=2, written in the form P(z)=sum_{i=1}^k h_{alpha_i}(z)^d with alpha_i in X(C^n):={alpha in C^n | <alpha,alpha>=0}, where h_beta(z):=<beta,z> for the standard C-bilinear form and the polynomials h_{alpha_i}(z)^d are linearly independent. Define the graph G(P) by taking vertex set [k]={1,...,k} and joining i and j by an edge iff <alpha_i,alpha_j> != 0; in the labeled version, label each edge either by <alpha_i,alpha_j> or, when d is even, by h_{alpha_i}(z)^((d-2)/2)<alpha_i,alpha_j>h_{alpha_j}(z)^((d-2)/2). Assuming P is Hessian nilpotent, i.e. Hes P is nilpotent, find necessary or sufficient conditions on the (labeled) graph G(P) that imply Delta^m(P(z)^{m+1})=0 for all sufficiently large m.

Does there exist a real number ε>0 such that infinitely many positive integers n are barriers for the arithmetic function f_ε(m)=ε v(m), where v(m) denotes the number of distinct prime divisors of the positive integer m and v(1)=0; that is, does there exist ε>0 for which infinitely many n satisfy m+ε v(m)≤n for every positive integer m<n?

Let d(m) denote the number of positive divisors of the positive integer m, and define
c(n):=max_{1\le m<n}(m+d(m))-n\qquad(n\ge 2).
Is it true that c(n)\to\infty as n\to\infty? Equivalently: does the quantity max_{1\le m<n}(m+d(m))-n become arbitrarily large for sufficiently large n?

Let I ⊂ Q[pAAA, pAAC, ..., pTTT] be the homogeneous prime ideal of the Zariski closure in C4 ⊗ C4 ⊗ C4 of the 4×4×4 tables (pijk), indexed by i,j,k ∈ {A,C,G,T}, that admit a decomposition pijk = ρAiσAjθAk + ρCiσCjθCk + ρGiσGjθGk + ρTiσTjθTk. Disregarding the normalization linear form p... - 1, is I generated by the known homogeneous invariants of degrees 5 and 9—namely the GL(C4)^3-translates of the quintics obtained from A adj(B) C - C adj(B) A = 0 on 3×4×4 subtables, together with the degree-9 Strassen invariants obtained as the numerators of det(A B^{-1} C - C B^{-1} A) on 3×3×3 subtables? ([citeseerx.ist.psu.edu](https://citeseerx.ist.psu.edu/document?doi=38db4554eb60454d45f6cd8b7d75a190bed051f4&repid=rep1&type=pdf&utm_source=openai))

Let X be the variety of 4×4×4 tables (p_{ijk}) with i,j,k ∈ {A,C,G,T}, given parametrically by p_{ijk} = ρ_Aiσ_Ajθ_Ak + ρ_Ciσ_Cjθ_Ck + ρ_Giσ_Gjθ_Gk + ρ_Tiσ_Tjθ_Tk, and let I = I(X) be its homogeneous prime ideal in Q[pAAA, pAAC, pAAT, ..., pTTG, pTTT]. Equivalently, X is the naive Bayes model / CI model [X1 ⟂ X2 ⟂ X3 | Y], i.e. the third secant variety of P^3 × P^3 × P^3. Determine I; in particular, do the known homogeneous polynomial invariants of degrees 5 and 9—namely the quintics of Proposition 1 and the degree-9 module generated by the Strassen invariant in Proposition 2—suffice to cut out X? ([math.berkeley.edu](https://math.berkeley.edu/~bernd/imaprob.pdf))

Characterize all complex projective subvarieties M ⊂ P^n (for arbitrary n), with projective coordinates (p0:...:pn), whose maximum likelihood degree is 1; that is, determine exactly which algebraic statistical models M have the property that for Zariski-generic data u=(u0,...,un) ∈ N^(n+1), the rational function L_u(p)=p0^u0 p1^u1 ··· pn^un /(p0+...+pn)^(u0+...+un), which is homogeneous of degree 0 and hence well defined on P^n, has exactly one complex critical point when restricted to the smooth locus of M away from the zero/pole divisor of L_u.

Let M be a subvariety of the complex projective space P^n with homogeneous coordinates (p0 : p1 : ... : pn), representing an algebraic statistical model via M intersected with the probability simplex P^n_{>=0}. For generic data u = (u0, ..., un) in N^{n+1}, consider the likelihood function L_u(p) = p0^{u0} p1^{u1} ... pn^{un} / (p0 + p1 + ... + pn)^{u0 + ... + un}, and define the maximum likelihood degree MLdeg(M) to be the number of complex critical points of L_u restricted to M, counting only critical points on the nonsingular locus of M that are neither poles nor zeros of L_u. Find a geometric characterization of those projective varieties M for which MLdeg(M) = 1.

Let M be a subvariety of the complex projective space P^n with homogeneous coordinates (p0 : p1 : ... : pn), viewed as an algebraic statistical model via M ∩ P^n_{>=0}. For generic data u = (u0, ..., un) in N^(n+1), consider the likelihood function L(p) = p0^u0 p1^u1 ... pn^un / (p0 + p1 + ... + pn)^(u0+...+un). Determine a geometric characterization of those projective varieties M for which the restriction of L to M has exactly one complex critical point, counting only nonsingular critical points and excluding zeros and poles of L; equivalently, characterize those algebraic statistical models whose maximum likelihood estimator is a rational function of the data. ([citeseerx.ist.psu.edu](https://citeseerx.ist.psu.edu/document?doi=38db4554eb60454d45f6cd8b7d75a190bed051f4&repid=rep1&type=pdf&utm_source=openai))

For the determinantal variety M_{m,n}^{<= r} subset P^(mn-1) of m x n matrices (p_ij) of rank at most r, determine its maximum likelihood degree as a function of m, n, and r; that is, for a generic data table u = (u_ij), determine the number of critical points of the likelihood function L_u(p) = (product over i,j of p_ij^{u_ij}) / (sum over i,j of p_ij)^(sum over i,j of u_ij) on M_{m,n}^{<= r}, counting only critical points that are neither zeros nor poles.

In the concrete DNA-alignment example of Section 3 of Sturmfels' paper, let M be the set of all positive real 4x4 matrices P = (p_{ij}) of rank at most 2. For the observed alignment in which each match occurs four times and each mismatch occurs two times, consider the likelihood function
L(P) = (product_{i=1}^4 p_{ii})^4 (product_{i != j} p_{ij})^2 (sum_{i=1}^4 sum_{j=1}^4 p_{ij})^{-40}.
Is it true or false that the matrix
(1/40) * [[3,3,2,2],[3,3,2,2],[2,2,3,3],[2,2,3,3]]
is a global maximizer of L over M?

Classify all subsets S of the family of almost-principal minors [i ⊥⊥ j | K], where Σ=(σab) ranges over real symmetric positive definite 5×5 matrices, i and j are distinct elements of [5], K ⊆ [5]\{i,j}, and [i ⊥⊥ j | K] denotes the determinant of the submatrix of Σ with row indices {i}∪K and column indices {j}∪K. Equivalently, determine exactly which zero patterns S occur as S={ [i ⊥⊥ j | K] : [i ⊥⊥ j | K](Σ)=0 } for some Σ ∈ PD5. ([citeseerx.ist.psu.edu](https://citeseerx.ist.psu.edu/document?doi=38db4554eb60454d45f6cd8b7d75a190bed051f4&repid=rep1&type=pdf&utm_source=openai))

For a mean-zero Gaussian random vector X on R^n with covariance matrix Σ ∈ PD_n, let [i ⟂⟂ j | K] denote the almost-principal minor of Σ with row indices {i} ∪ K and column indices {j} ∪ K, where K ⊂ {1,…,n} and i,j ∈ {1,…,n} \ K; by Lemma 4.1, [i ⟂⟂ j | K] = 0 if and only if Xi is conditionally independent of Xj given XK. Which collections of such conditional independence statements—equivalently, which semigraphoids—are realizable by some positive definite covariance matrix Σ, and hence arise as Gaussian conditional independence models M = {Σ ∈ PD_n : [i ⟂⟂ j | K] = 0 for the prescribed statements}, viewed algebro-geometrically through the real locus of the complex variety defined by these equations?

Let Σ be a real symmetric positive-definite 5×5 matrix. For each pair of distinct indices i, j ∈ [5] and each subset K ⊆ [5] \ {i, j}, let a_{ij|K} := det(Σ_{iK, jK}) be the corresponding almost-principal minor, where the row index set is {i} ∪ K and the column index set is {j} ∪ K. Which subsets S of the set {a_{ij|K} : i ≠ j, K ⊆ [5] \ {i, j}} occur as the vanishing set {a_{ij|K} : a_{ij|K} = 0} of some real symmetric positive-definite 5×5 matrix Σ?

For a fixed n, let PD_n be the cone of real positive definite symmetric n×n matrices, and let SubMod_n ⊂ R^{2^n} be the cone with coordinates H_S indexed by all subsets S ⊆ {1,2,…,n}, defined by the inequalities H_{ {i}∪K } + H_{ {j}∪K } ≤ H_{ {i,j}∪K } + H_K for every K ⊆ {1,…,n} and i,j ∉ K. For Σ ∈ PD_n, define H(Σ) by H(Σ)_I = -log det(Σ_I), where Σ_I is the principal minor indexed by I. Since Gaussian conditional independence models are exactly the inverse images under H of faces of SubMod_n, characterize the image H(PD_n), determine how H(PD_n) intersects the faces of SubMod_n, and describe the fibers of H. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/0707.4558))

Let X1, ..., Xn be discrete random variables with finite state counts d1, ..., dn, and let V ⊂ C^{d1} ⊗ C^{d2} ⊗ ··· ⊗ C^{dn} be the conditional independence variety determined by a chosen collection of statements of the form Xi ⊥⊥ Xj | X_K, i.e. the determinantal variety cut out by the corresponding 2×2 minor equations. Let V^str be the associated strict CI variety, consisting of those tables in V for which exactly the chosen CI statements hold and no other CI statement Xi ⊥⊥ Xj | X_K holds, and let M = V^str ∩ R_{>0}^{d1d2···dn} be the corresponding strict CI model. Must every such strict CI model M contain a point whose coordinates are all rational numbers?

Let R be a real closed field, let P subset R[X1,...,Xk] be a finite family of polynomials with s = #(P) and d = max_{P in P} deg(P), and let S subset R^k be the P-semi-algebraic set defined by an arbitrary Boolean formula with atoms P = 0, P > 0, or P < 0. Is there an algorithm, measured in the arithmetic-complexity model of Definition 2.2, whose complexity is single exponential in k (that is, bounded by (sd)^{k^{O(1)}}), which computes the full Betti sequence b_0(S),...,b_k(S), where b_i(S) = dim_Q H^i(S,Q)? Equivalently, can the fixed-ell result of Theorem 6.10, which computes b_0(S),...,b_ell(S) in time (sd)^{k^{O(ell)}}, be strengthened to a single-exponential algorithm for all Betti numbers of an arbitrary semi-algebraic set?

Let R be a real closed field and let S ⊂ R^k be a semi-algebraic set. Writing b_i(S) for the i-th Betti number of S with Q-coefficients in the sense of the survey (for closed and bounded S, b_i(S) = dim_Q H^i(S)), is there a complexity-theoretic explanation for the apparent algorithmic asymmetry that the low Betti numbers, the top Betti numbers, and the Euler-Poincare characteristic of semi-algebraic sets seem easier to compute than the intermediate ("middle") Betti numbers? More specifically, can one prove a hardness result, or formulate a complexity-theoretic analogue of the smooth projective complex variety phenomenon, showing that the middle Betti numbers essentially carry the difficult topological information? ([math.purdue.edu](https://www.math.purdue.edu/~sbasu/ams_final_submission.pdf))

Let P_1, ..., P_ell in R[X_1, ..., X_k] be polynomials with deg(P_i) <= 2, and let S = {x in R^k : P_1(x) >= 0, ..., P_ell(x) >= 0} be the resulting basic closed semi-algebraic set. In the survey’s arithmetic-complexity model, is there an algorithm for computing b_0(S), the number of connected components of S, with complexity k^O(ell), or at least k^O(ell^2), rather than only via the currently available all-Betti-number approach yielding k^(2^O(ell))? Equivalently in the paper’s intended sense, can connected-component counting in the quadratic case be done substantially more efficiently than by invoking the known algorithm for all Betti numbers, given that general roadmap methods would still be exponential in k here?

Let R be a real closed field, let Q in R[X_1,...,X_k] be of degree at most d with Z(Q,R^k) := {x in R^k : Q(x)=0} of real dimension k_0, let P be a finite subset of R[X_1,...,X_k] with #P = s and deg(P) <= d for all P in P, and let S be a P-semi-algebraic subset of Z(Q,R^k) (that is, S is defined by a Boolean formula with atoms P=0, P>0, or P<0 for polynomials P in P). Since the best known roadmap algorithm computes a roadmap of S in complexity s^(k_0+1) d^(O(k^2)) (Theorem 4.15), can one improve this to complexity s^(k_0+1) d^(O(k)), so that deciding or counting the semi-algebraically connected components of S has asymptotically the same complexity as testing emptiness in the sense of Theorem 4.12? In the special case that S is contained in the unit ball, can such an improvement also provide the corresponding effective O(k)-exponent bound on the length of semi-algebraic connecting paths, thereby yielding an effective version of the D'Acunto-Kurdyka d^(O(k)) length bound for real algebraic sets? ([math.purdue.edu](https://www.math.purdue.edu/~sbasu/ams_final_submission.pdf))

Let Ω ⊂ C^n be an open connected set, let ψ : Ω → C be holomorphic, and set Γ = ∇ψ. Assume that k := max_{ξ∈Ω} rank DΓ(ξ) satisfies 1 ≤ k ≤ n−1, and that for every ξ ∈ Ω^(k) := {ξ ∈ Ω : rank DΓ(ξ) = k}, the level set Γ^{-1}(Γ(ξ)) is the affine (n−k)-plane ξ + κ(ξ), where κ(ξ) := ker DΓ(ξ) = ker D^2ψ(ξ). Viewing κ as a holomorphic map Ω^(k) → G_{n-k}(C^n), define the essential singular set Ω_sing := {ξ ∈ Ω : κ is not continuously extendible over ξ)}. Must Ω_sing be a union of affine spaces?

Let K ∈ {R,C}, and let (A, A) be a maximal Banach ideal of bounded linear operators between Banach spaces over K. Say that (A, A) satisfies the principle of A-local reflexivity (A-LRP) if for every finite-dimensional Banach space E, every Banach space Y, every finite-dimensional subspace F ⊂ Y′, every operator T ∈ L(E,Y″), and every ε > 0, there exists S ∈ L(E,Y) such that A(S) ≤ (1 + ε)A(T), ⟨Sx,y′⟩ = ⟨y′,Tx⟩ for all (x,y′) ∈ E × F, and j_Y Sx = Tx for all x ∈ T^{-1}(j_Y(Y)), where j_Y : Y → Y″ is the canonical embedding. Must every maximal Banach ideal (A, A) satisfy the A-LRP?

Let (\mathfrak A,\mathbf A) be a maximal Banach ideal over \mathbb K\in\{\mathbb R,\mathbb C\}. Is the following equivalence always true? (i) (\mathfrak A,\mathbf A) is right-accessible, meaning that for every finite-dimensional Banach space M, every Banach space F, every T\in \mathfrak L(M,F), and every \varepsilon>0, there exist N\in FIN(F) and S\in \mathfrak L(M,N) such that T=J_N^F S and \mathbf A(S)\le (1+\varepsilon)\mathbf A(T). (ii) (\mathfrak A,\mathbf A) satisfies the \mathfrak A-local reflexivity principle, meaning that for every finite-dimensional Banach space M, every Banach space F, every N\in FIN(F'), every T\in \mathfrak A(M,F''), and every \varepsilon>0, there exists S\in \mathfrak L(M,F) such that \mathbf A(S)\le (1+\varepsilon)\mathbf A(T), \langle Sx,b\rangle=\langle b,Tx\rangle for all x\in M and b\in N, and j_F Sx=Tx for every x\in M with Tx\in j_F(F)?

Let (\mathfrak{A}_P,\mathbf{A}_P) be Pisier’s explicitly constructed maximal Banach ideal, which the paper recalls is not right-accessible. Does (\mathfrak{A}_P,\mathbf{A}_P) satisfy the \mathfrak{A}_P-local reflexivity principle in the sense of Definition 1.1; that is, for every pair of real or complex Banach spaces E and Y with E finite-dimensional, every finite-dimensional subspace F\subset Y', every operator T\in \mathfrak{A}_P(E,Y''), and every \varepsilon>0, does there exist a bounded linear operator S:E\to Y such that \mathbf{A}_P(S)\le (1+\varepsilon)\mathbf{A}_P(T), \langle Sx,y'\rangle=\langle y',Tx\rangle for all x\in E and y'\in F, and j_Y Sx=Tx for every x\in T^{-1}(j_Y(Y)), where j_Y:Y\to Y'' is the canonical embedding?

In Pietsch’s standard notation for operator ideals, where \(\circ\) denotes composition of ideals, is the specific composition product \(((\mathfrak{L}_1\circ\mathfrak{L}_\infty)^{**})\circ\mathfrak{L}_2\) a normed operator ideal? Equivalently: does this product admit an ideal norm on its components between arbitrary Banach spaces?

Let (\mathfrak{C}_2,\mathbf{C}_2) denote the maximal injective Banach ideal of all cotype-2 operators, and let (\mathfrak{L}_\infty,\mathbf{L}_\infty) denote the ideal of \mathfrak{L}_\infty-factorizable operators, over the scalar field considered in the paper. Does the canonical product ideal (\mathfrak{C}_2^*\circ\mathfrak{L}_\infty,\mathbf{C}_2^*\circ\mathbf{L}_\infty) have property (I); that is, for every pair of Banach spaces X,Y, every finite-rank operator T\in(\mathfrak{C}_2^*\circ\mathfrak{L}_\infty)(X,Y), and every \varepsilon>0, do there exist a Banach space Z and operators A\in\mathfrak{C}_2^*(Z,Y), B\in\mathfrak{L}_\infty(X,Z) such that T=AB, the range A(Z) is finite-dimensional, and \mathbf{C}_2^*(A)\,\mathbf{L}_\infty(B)\le(1+\varepsilon)\,(\mathbf{C}_2^*\circ\mathbf{L}_\infty)(T)?

Let B be a maximal Banach operator ideal (over the paper's fixed scalar field), and suppose there exist Banach spaces X_0 and Y_0 such that X_0' and Y_0 are of cotype 2 and B^*(X_0,Y_0) \not\subseteq L_2(X_0,Y_0). Assume moreover that the product ideal B\circ L_\infty has property (I). Is the additional hypothesis that B\circ L_\infty be right-accessible actually necessary for the conclusion of Corollary 2.6? Equivalently, under these same assumptions but without assuming right-accessibility of B\circ L_\infty, must the B-local reflexivity principle fail?

Let G be an infinite-dimensional Lie group modeled on a locally convex real vector space, and let H ≤ G be an arbitrary subgroup. Must there exist a Lie group structure on H, modeled on a locally convex space, such that the inclusion homomorphism λ:H→G is smooth, the induced Lie algebra map L(λ):L(H)→L(G) is injective, and, for every k in N∪{infinity} and every C^k-manifold X, a map f:X→H is C^k if and only if λ∘f:X→G is C^k; i.e. does every subgroup of an infinite-dimensional Lie group admit the structure of an initial Lie subgroup of the ambient group?

Let G = direct limit G_n = union_{n in N} G_n be the direct-limit Lie group of an ascending sequence G_1 subseteq G_2 subseteq ... of finite-dimensional real Lie groups with smooth inclusion homomorphisms, and let H subseteq G be any subgroup. Writing H_n := G_n intersection H, does H admit the direct-limit Lie group structure H = direct limit H_n for which the inclusion lambda: H -> G is initial in the sense that, for every k in N union {infinity} and every C^k-manifold M, a map f: M -> H is C^k if and only if lambda o f: M -> G is C^k?

Let G = varinjlim G_n be the direct-limit Lie group of an ascending sequence G_1 ⊆ G_2 ⊆ ··· of finite-dimensional real Lie groups with smooth inclusion homomorphisms. If Hom_c(R,G) denotes the space of continuous one-parameter subgroups of G, endowed with the compact-open topology and the Hofmann–Morris operations (gamma+eta)(t) := lim_{n->∞}(gamma(t/n)eta(t/n))^n, (r·gamma)(t) := gamma(rt), and [gamma,eta](t^2) := lim_{n->∞}(gamma(t/n)eta(t/n)gamma(-t/n)eta(-t/n))^{n^2}, does Hom_c(R,G) become a topological Lie algebra, and is the canonical map x |-> (t |-> exp_G(tx)) an isomorphism of topological Lie algebras L(G) ≅ Hom_c(R,G)?

Let M be a σ-compact smooth manifold over R of dimension n > 0, let p be a point of M, and choose a smooth chart κ: U → V ⊂ R^n with κ(p)=0. If F=(F_1,…,F_n) is a formal diffeomorphism at 0, i.e. an invertible n-tuple of formal power series in R[[x_1,…,x_n]] with F(0)=0 and det(D_0F)>0, does there exist a compactly supported C∞-diffeomorphism φ of M such that φ(p)=p, det(T_pφ)>0, and the formal Taylor series of κ∘φ∘κ^{-1} at 0 is exactly F?

In the tunneling Hamiltonian framework applied to one-dimensional charge-density-wave transport modeled by a driven sine-Gordon scalar field—with initial and final states represented as Gaussian wavefunctionals and the Hamiltonian including a periodic pinning potential and an external driving term—should the Gaussian wavefunctional coefficients and the physical parameters of the sine-Gordon potential be fixed by imposing topological-charge quantization Q = [φ(+∞) − φ(−∞)]/(2π) and by using Coleman's false-vacuum bounce solution to determine the soliton domain-wall tension, and will this topologically determined choice reproduce the experimentally observed Zener-like current–electric field dependence I(F) ∝ exp(−α/F) as evidence of a first-order false-vacuum phase transition and associated quantum-switching behavior relevant for quantum-coherent phase evolution in quantum computing?

In the sine-Gordon–based charge-density-wave transport model of Beckwith (2008), the tunneling Hamiltonian employs Gaussian wavefunctionals Ψ_initial[φ] = c_1 exp[−α ∫ dx (φ − φ_F)^2] and Ψ_final[φ] = c_2 exp[−α ∫ dx (φ − φ_T)^2], with parameter α identified as the inverse soliton-pair separation L⁻¹ and equal to the Euclidean energy-gap difference ΔE_gap = V_E(φ_F) − V_E(φ_T) between the false vacuum φ_F ≡ φ^1 and true vacuum φ_T ≡ φ^2π. Beckwith derives an analytical current–electric-field relation matching Zener-like experimental behavior and notes its similarity to the 1+1-dimensional Schwinger electron–positron pair-production rate. Can the values of α and the associated tunneling coefficients be determined instead by a topological phase-transition framework—namely a first-order false-to-true vacuum transition mediated by an integer topological charge—such that this topological model reproduces the same I–E functional form and energy-gap scaling as the analytical derivation?

In the one-dimensional driven sine–Gordon model of charge-density-wave transport, can topological charge arguments—specifically through the Bogomolnyi inequality—uniquely determine both (1) the Gaussian wavefunctional width α (with α≈L⁻¹, L being the soliton–antisoliton separation) and (2) the magnitude of the sine–Gordon driving coefficient so that α≡ΔE_gap≡V_E(φ_F)−V_E(φ_T)? Does this selection provide a false-vacuum-based initial-condition criterion for a first-order phase transition manifested in the abrupt Zener-type I–E curve and thereby enable quantum-coherent switching suitable for quantum-computing devices?

In the quasi-one-dimensional charge-density-wave transport model treated with a driven sine-Gordon (massive-Schwinger-type) potential and Gaussian initial and final wavefunctionals for a nucleated soliton-antisoliton pair across a pinning gap, should the coefficients in those wavefunctionals and the relative sizes of the potential terms be fixed by vanishing-topological-charge/Bogomol’nyi arguments tied to the false-vacuum picture, or are they adequately determined by the experimental setup alone when fitting the current-electric-field behavior?

In Beckwith’s tunneling-Hamiltonian model of ultra-fast charge-density-wave transport, should the coefficients in the Gaussian initial/final wavefunctionals and in the driven sine-Gordon potential that describes soliton–antisoliton tunneling be fixed by topological-charge arguments—via the Bogomol'nyi inequality and Coleman-style false-vacuum reasoning—or are those coefficients adequately determined by experimental inputs alone when fitting the observed I-E curves for NbSe3?

How does the self-consistent functional renormalization group (FRG) approach, developed for disordered elastic manifolds, systematically capture the physics of multiple metastable minima and quasi-degenerate states in the non-perturbative regime, specifically considering that this regime is characterized by a non-analytic disorder correlator and requires the incorporation of full replica symmetry breaking?

Can the shock and droplet relations derived from the one- and two-loop ε=4−d expansion of the functional renormalization group for a d-dimensional elastic manifold at finite temperature be quantitatively tested by numerical measurement of the fixed-point disorder correlator R(u) (the second cumulant) and higher cumulants?

Consider a d-dimensional elastic manifold in a quenched random potential at bare temperature T>0, whose renormalized disorder correlator R(u) under functional RG flows toward a zero-temperature fixed point as the effective temperature T_L=T L^{-θ}→0 (with θ the thermal scaling exponent). At T=0, R(u) acquires a cusp at u=0, making its derivatives ambiguous. How does the finite-temperature FRG flow regularize these singularities—analogous to viscosity ν∼T in the decaying Burgers equation mapping—and thereby define a unique zero-temperature critical theory, and by what systematic matching of the outer solution R(u) for u=O(1) to the inner thermal boundary layer solution at u∼T_L can one compute the cusp-related derivatives of R(u) at u=0 with all ambiguities removed?

In the context of the functional renormalization group applied to pinned elastic manifolds of internal dimension d at finite temperature T>0, the direct perturbative loop expansion for the renormalized disorder correlator R(u) breaks down in the thermal boundary layer regime (u∼O(T)), as demonstrated by its failure already in the d=0 Sinai model and the ensuing requirement for a nonperturbative ERG functional hierarchy. Is there a systematic reorganization or resummation of this finite-temperature loop expansion that reproduces the exact ERG results for R(u) and remains quantitatively valid beyond one- and two-loop orders for arbitrary d and T?

For the intrinsic family of iterated osp(1|2) tensor operators S_κ(c0,d0), with c0,d0 ∈ R defined by [S_{1/2}×S_{1/2}]^0 = c0·1^0, [S_{1/2}×S_{1/2}]^{1/2} = d0·√2·S_{1/2}, and [S_{1/2}×S_κ]^{κ+1/2} = S_{κ+1/2}, can one complete the unresolved “ultimate identification process” left after the quasi-final relation (12.5), namely identify, for all admissible integral or half-integral spins a,b,c,d,e and summation index f, the homogeneous polynomials arising from products of the closure polynomials P^π in the binomial basis {(c0 + d0^2)^{Ω-m}(d0^2)^m}_{m=0}^Ω — where P^π(λ,κ) = (d0)^{τ_π} Σ_{m=0}^{[π]} x_m^π(λ,κ)(c0 + d0^2)^{[π]-m}(d0^2)^m and the x_m^π are conjecturally integral — so as to derive a genuine unified osp(1|2) triangle sum rule written in terms of the supertriangle Δ^S and parity-independent 6-j^S symbols, rather than the earlier ordinary-triangle-type relation analyzed in Appendix C? ([academia.edu](https://www.academia.edu/77591116/Concept_of_a_veritable_osp_1_2_super_triangle_sum_rule_with_6_j_S_symbols_from_intrinsic_operator_techniques_an_open_problem))

For the iterated osp(1|2) tensor operators S^kappa(c0,d0), with c0,d0 in R, defined by [S^(1/2) x S^(1/2)]^0 = c0 1^0, [S^(1/2) x S^(1/2)]^(1/2) = d0 sqrt(2) S^(1/2), and [S^(1/2) x S^kappa]^(kappa+1/2) = S^(kappa+1/2), let omega in (1/2) Z_{>=0}, lambda,kappa in (1/2) Z_{>=0} with 0 <= omega <= inf(lambda,kappa), and let tau_omega = [omega+1/2]-[omega]. If P^omega(lambda,kappa) is the symmetric polynomial defined by the set-A closure relation [S^lambda x S^kappa]^(lambda+kappa-omega) = (-1)^(4 omega (lambda+kappa)) P^omega(lambda,kappa)/(E(lambda,kappa;lambda+kappa-omega) nabla^S(lambda kappa lambda+kappa-omega)) S^(lambda+kappa-omega), and if one expands it as P^omega(lambda,kappa) = (d0)^(tau_omega) sum_{m=0}^{[omega]} x_m^omega(lambda,kappa) (c0+d0^2)^([omega]-m) (d0^2)^m with x_m^omega(lambda,kappa)=x_m^omega(kappa,lambda), can one determine explicit formulas, valid for all omega and all m, for the coefficients x_m^omega(lambda,kappa), in a way consistent with the Appendix B recursion relations, and in particular prove Conjecture 1 that these coefficients are integers?

Let τ_ρ := [ρ + 1/2] - [ρ], so τ_ρ = 0 for integral ρ and τ_ρ = 1 for half-integral ρ. For the osp(1|2) closure-relation polynomials P^π(λ,κ) introduced in Section 8 (with admissible spin labels λ, κ, π in 1/2 N_0), write
P^π(λ,κ) = (d0)^τ_π sum_{m=0}^{[π]} x_m^π(λ,κ) (c0 + d0^2)^[π]-m (d0^2)^m,
so that P^π(λ,κ)/(d0)^τ_π is homogeneous of degree [π] in c0 + d0^2 and d0^2 (and, for π > 1, x_[π]^π(λ,κ)=0). Is Conjecture 1 true: for every admissible λ, κ, π and every m = 0,1,...,[π], is x_m^π(λ,κ) always an integer?

In the osp(1|2) intrinsic tensor-operator framework of Sections 8–10, let Pπ(λ,κ) denote the high-rank closure polynomial in the implicit variables d0 and c0+d0² defined by Eq. (8.1), namely by the factor multiplying S_{λ+κ−π} in the closure relation [S_λ × S_κ]_{λ+κ−π}, and let, for κ≥λ≥1/2, Qπ(λ;κ) denote the low-rank closure polynomial defined by Eq. (10.1), namely by the factor multiplying S_{κ−λ+π} in [S_λ × S_κ]_{κ−λ+π}; here λ, κ, π are integral or half-integral ranks and π is restricted so that κ−λ+π lies in the allowed low-rank range [|κ−λ|, κ−1/2] (equivalently 0≤π≤λ−1/2 when κ≥λ). Is it true, as Conjecture 2 asserts, that for every such admissible λ, κ, and π one has Qπ(λ;κ)=Pπ(λ,κ−λ+π)?

For the iterated osp(1|2) tensor operators S^κ(c0,d0) with c0,d0 ∈ ℝ used in the paper, and at the specific stage where the two recoupled expressions for [[S^a × S^b]^c × S^d]^e lead to the quasi-final identity (12.5), is it mathematically legitimate to identify the coefficients of the common tensor operator S^e term-by-term in order to obtain a genuine △S-sum rule for 6-j^S symbols, despite the fact that the same paper proves the existence of nontrivial zero tensor operators by construction—namely the families given in Theorem 1 for integral k,k′ and in Theorem 2 for integral k and half-integral κ?

For admissible parity-independent osp(1|2) 6-j^S symbols, can one determine the unknown polynomials P^ω(λ,κ) (with ω=p in the integral case and ω=π in the half-integral case) and their binomial expansion coefficients x_m^ω(λ,κ) in the basis (c0+d0^2)^(Ω-m)(d0^2)^m, so as to complete the intrinsic-operator identification of the two triple-tensor-product expressions and thereby prove a genuine osp(1|2) super-triangle sum rule—written with supertriangles Δ^S rather than the su(2)/su_q(2) triangles ∇—for the parity-independent 6-j^S coefficients?

Within Bréhamet’s intrinsic-operator construction of iterated osp(1|2) tensor operators S^κ(c0,d0) from a basic rank-1/2 operator, with c0,d0 in R and closure relations expressed using the supertriangle Δ^S, can one determine, for every admissible integral or half-integral rank configuration (λ,κ,π), a general closed formula for the polynomials P^π(λ,κ)—equivalently for their binomial expansion coefficients x (conjecturally integers) in the basis (c0+d0^2)^(Ω-m)(d0^2)^m, and hence also for Q^π(λ,κ) if Conjecture 2 holds—so that the final identification step in the triple-tensor-product calculation closes and yields a genuine osp(1|2) super-triangle sum rule in terms of 6-j^S symbols and Δ^S?

Let ν(G) denote the least cardinal κ such that G admits a κ-coloring with no infinite monochromatic subset A ⊆ G satisfying A = xA^{-1}x for some x ∈ G. Investigate the invariant ν(G) for non-commutative groups; in particular, is ν(F_2) finite for the free group F_2 on two generators? ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/0901.3356))

Let G be an infinite group. Is it true that for every natural number r, every coloring chi: G -> {1, ..., r}, and every natural number n, there exist a color i, a finite subset A subseteq chi^{-1}(i), and an element g in G such that |A| >= n and A = gA^{-1}g, where A^{-1} := {a^{-1} : a in A}?

Let ν(G) be the least number of colors needed to color a group G so that G contains no infinite monochromatic subset symmetric with respect to any point, and call a subset E⊆G central if for every finite r-coloring of G with r<ν(G) there exists an infinite monochromatic subset A⊆G symmetric with respect to some x∈E (for G=ℤ^n, in additive notation, A=2x−A). For each n>3, determine c(ℤ^n), the minimum cardinality of a central subset of ℤ^n, and investigate the structure of central sets in ℤ^n.

Let G be a finite group of odd order, and let r>1 be an integer. Define MS(G,r) to be the least upper bound of all cardinal numbers t such that every coloring χ:G→{1,…,r} contains a monochromatic subset A⊂G with A=gA^{-1}g for some g∈G and |A|≥t, and set ms(G,r):=MS(G,r)/|G|. Is it true that ms(G,r)>1/r^2 for every finite group G of odd order and every integer r>1? ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/0901.3356))

Fix ε > 0 and an integer r ≥ 2. For a finite group G, let MS(G,r) be the least upper bound of all t such that every r-coloring χ:G→{1,…,r} contains a monochromatic subset A ⊆ G with |A| ≥ t and A = gA^{-1}g for some g ∈ G; equivalently, A is symmetric with respect to the group symmetry x ↦ gx^{-1}g. Define ms(G,r) = MS(G,r)/|G|. Does there exist a finite (not necessarily Abelian) group G such that ms(G,r) < ε?

Let G be a connected compact topological group with normalized Haar probability measure μ. For r∈N, let ms(G,r) be the supremum of all ε such that every measurable r-coloring G=C1∪⋯∪Cr contains a measurable monochromatic subset A⊂Ci that is symmetric in the group sense, i.e. A=gA^{-1}g for some g∈G, and satisfies μ(A)≥ε. Does there exist a connected compact group G and an integer r such that ms(G,r)<1/r^2? In particular, what is the exact value of ms(SO(3),2)? ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/0901.3356))

For integers n>1 and r>1, let S^n be the n-dimensional sphere equipped with its normalized isometry-invariant Borel probability measure, and let I_2^+(S^n) be the family of nontrivial involutive axial symmetries of S^n, i.e. the isometries given by 180-degree rotations about lines through the center of the sphere. Is ms(S^n,I_2^+(S^n),r)=1/r^2?

Let X be a compact subset of R^n, n>2, of positive Lebesgue measure, equipped with the normalized Lebesgue measure mu, and let S_X be the family of all nonidentity isometries s of R^n such that s(X)=X. For a finite number r, define ms(X,r) to be the least upper bound of all eps such that every measurable r-coloring of X contains a measurable monochromatic subset A subset X with mu(A) >= eps and s(A)=A for some s in S_X. Classify ms(X,r) for all such X. In particular, determine ms(X,r) for all regular polyhedra in R^n, n>2, and compute ms(T,2) for the solid regular tetrahedron T in R^3. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/0901.3356))

Determine the blurred maximal symmetry numbers bms([n], r) for the discrete interval [n] = {1,2,...,n}, where [n] is viewed inside Z with normalized counting measure mu(A) = |A|/n and admissible symmetries s_g(x) = g - x for g in Z. That is, for a blurred r-coloring beta = (beta_1,...,beta_r) consisting of functions beta_i : Z -> [0,1] with sum_{i=1}^r beta_i = chi_[n], define bms([n], r; beta) = max_{1 <= i <= r} sup_{g in Z} (1/n) sum_{x in Z} beta_i(x)beta_i(g - x), and let bms([n], r) = inf_beta bms([n], r; beta). Compute these values, at least for small n and r; in particular, determine bms([n], 2) for small n.

Calculate the invariant ms([0,1], r), at least for r = 2, where [0,1] is endowed with Lebesgue measure and admissible symmetries are the central reflections x ↦ c − x of the real line; equivalently, determine
ms([0,1], r) = inf_{χ:[0,1]→{1,…,r} measurable} max_{1≤i≤r} sup{λ(B) : B ⊆ χ^{-1}(i), B is measurable, and B = c − B for some c ∈ R}.
In particular, determine ms([0,1], 2).

Determine the exact value of the constant c for the unit interval [0,1] with Lebesgue measure and central symmetries, where
ms([0,1], r) := inf_{[0,1]=A1∪⋯∪Ar} max_{1≤i≤r} sup{ λ(B) : B ⊆ Ai is measurable and B = x - B for some x ∈ R },
the infimum being taken over all measurable r-colorings (partitions) of [0,1]. Equivalently, compute the asymptotic constant
c = lim_{r→∞} ms([0,1], r) r^2 = inf_{r≥2} ms([0,1], r) r^2,
known from the paper’s cited source to satisfy 1/2 ≤ c ≤ 5/6.

For a fixed integer r>=1, let [n]={1,...,n} be equipped with normalized counting measure and central symmetries x -> g-x (g in Z), and let [0,1] be equipped with Lebesgue measure and central symmetries x -> c-x (c in R). Let ms([n],r) denote the normalized maximal size of a monochromatic centrally symmetric subset guaranteed in every r-coloring of [n], and let bms([n],r) denote the corresponding blurred invariant. Since ms([n],r) -> ms([0,1],r) and bms([n],r) -> ms([0,1],r) as n -> infinity, determine the rate of convergence of these sequences to ms([0,1],r); in particular, does there exist alpha>0 such that |ms([n],r)-ms([0,1],r)| = O(1/n^alpha), and does bms([n],r) converge asymptotically faster than ms([n],r)? ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/0901.3356))

For fixed integers k>=1 and q>=k+1, does there exist a constant C=C(k,q) such that for every integer p>=q and every finite k-uniform hypergraph H with the property that among every p edges of H some q have a common vertex, the transversal number tau(H) satisfies tau(H) <= C p^k?

Let V:S^{m-1}->S^{m-1}, where S^{m-1}={x in R^m : x_i >= 0 and sum_{i=1}^m x_i = 1}, be a quadratic stochastic operator given by (Vx)_k = sum_{i,j=1}^m P_{ij,k} x_i x_j, with P_{ij,k} >= 0, P_{ij,k} = P_{ji,k}, and sum_{k=1}^m P_{ij,k} = 1. A Volterra QSO is one with P_{ij,k} = 0 whenever k is not in {i,j}; in that case the associated skew-symmetric matrix is called transversal when all its even-order leading principal minors are nonzero. Can one define an analogue of transversality for an arbitrary quadratic stochastic operator, and give necessary and sufficient conditions on the heredity coefficients P under which the operator is transversal?

For a general quadratic stochastic operator V:S^{m-1}->S^{m-1} with heredity coefficients (p_{ij,k}), define a notion of transversality that extends the Volterra case—where a Volterra QSO is called transversal when its associated skew-symmetric matrix has all even-order principal minors nonzero—and determine necessary and sufficient conditions on the coefficient matrix of V under which V is transversal.

Fix a prime p. Given a p-compact group X, does there exist a sequence of finite groups and homomorphisms G_0 \xrightarrow{f_1} G_1 \xrightarrow{f_2} G_2 \xrightarrow{f_3} \cdots such that, for the induced maps Bf_i: BG_i \to BG_{i+1}, the mapping telescope (equivalently, homotopy colimit) satisfies (hocolim_i BG_i)^\wedge_p \simeq BX?

Fix a prime p. Let {BX_m}_{m∈N} be a direct system of classifying spaces of p-local finite groups with continuous maps f_m: BX_m → BX_{m+1}, and suppose that hocolim_m BX_m ≃ BX, where BX is the classifying space of a p-compact group X. Given a map g: BG_p^∧ → BX, where BG_p^∧ denotes the p-completed classifying space of a finite group G (or, as allowed parenthetically in the paper, of a p-local finite group), must there exist an index m and a map ĝ: BG_p^∧ → BX_m such that g is homotopic to the composite BG_p^∧ → BX_m → BX induced by the direct system; equivalently, can g be made to factor through some finite stage BX_m in a homotopy-commutative triangle? ([msp.org](https://msp.org/gtm/2007/11/gtm-2007-11-020s.pdf))

Let A be the mod 2 Steenrod algebra, let A_* denote its dual, and let Sq^0: Ext_A^{s,t}(F_2, F_2) -> Ext_A^{s,2t}(F_2, F_2) be the squaring operation induced on the cohomology of the Steenrod algebra by the Frobenius map A_* -> A_*, x -> x^2. For a fixed homological degree s, write Ext_A^s(F_2, F_2) for the full Ext group in degree s over all internal degrees t, and let Im((Sq^0)^i) be the image of the i-fold iterate on Ext_A^s(F_2, F_2). Is it true that there exists a number r = r(s), depending only on s, such that for every i >= r the map (Sq^0)^{i-r}: Im((Sq^0)^r) -> Im((Sq^0)^i) is an isomorphism? ([msp.org](https://msp.org/gtm/2007/11/gtm-2007-11-020s.pdf))

Let A be the mod-2 Steenrod algebra. For every bidegree (s,t), where alpha(t) = k if t = 2^{i_1} + ... + 2^{i_k} with i_1 < ... < i_k (equivalently, alpha(t) is the number of 1s in the binary expansion of t), prove or disprove Kuhn’s conjecture that Ext_A^{s,t}(F_2, F_2) = 0 whenever alpha(t) > s. This is posed in Section 3 in the context of the mod-2 Singer transfer tau_{s,t}, whose domain is noted to vanish in those bidegrees by Wood’s verification of the Peterson conjecture. ([msp.org](https://msp.org/gtm/2007/11/gtm-2007-11-020s.pdf))

Let p be a prime, let A be the mod-p Steenrod algebra, and let τ_{s,t}: Hom_A^{t-s}(H^*((Z/p)^s; F_p), F_p)^{GL_s(Z/p)} -> Ext_A^{s,t}(F_p, F_p) denote the Singer transfer. Can the resulting bigraded transfer τ^{*,*} be realized as the edge homomorphism of some spectral sequence, in a way that provides a sensible measure of the extent to which τ^{*,*} fails to be an isomorphism of bigraded algebras?

Fix a positive integer s, and let A denote the mod-p Steenrod algebra. Is there a uniform calculation of the s-th Adams-filtration line Ext_A^{s,*}(F_p, F_p) valid for every sufficiently large prime p (with the threshold allowed to depend on s)? Equivalently in the paper's heuristic language, for fixed s does Ext_A^{s,*}(F_p, F_p) become eventually "independent of p" as p grows, in the sense suggested by the Singer-transfer comparison between Ext_A^{s,*+s}(F_p, F_p) and Hom_A^*(H^*((Z/p)^s; F_p), F_p)_{GL_s(Z/p)}?

For every integer s >= 1, let V_s be an s-dimensional vector space over F_2, let A be the mod-2 Steenrod algebra, and let PH_d(BV_s) subset H_d(BV_s) denote the primitive subspace consisting of homology classes annihilated by all positive-degree Steenrod operations. Is Singer's algebraic transfer a monomorphism in rank s; that is, is the graded map Tr_s = direct sum over d >= 0 of Tr_s^d, where Tr_s^d: F_2 tensor_{GL_s} PH_d(BV_s) -> Ext_A^{s,s+d}(F_2,F_2), injective for every s? ([msp.org](https://msp.org/gtm/2007/11/gtm-2007-11-020s.pdf))

Let p be a prime, let P_* be the polynomial part of the dual Steenrod algebra, so that P_* is isomorphic to F_p[xi_1, xi_2, xi_3, ...], and let P denote its graded dual Hopf algebra. The Frobenius pth-power map on P_* induces an algebra endomorphism P^0: Ext_P^{s,t}(F_p, F_p) -> Ext_P^{s,pt}(F_p, F_p). Fix a homological degree s > 0. Is it true that for every internal degree t and every homogeneous class z in Ext_P^{s,t}(F_p, F_p), there exists an integer n >= 0 such that (P^0)^n(z) is nilpotent in the bigraded algebra Ext_P^{*,*}(F_p, F_p)?

Let p be a prime, let P_* be the polynomial part of the dual Steenrod algebra with P_* ≅ F_p[ξ_1, ξ_2, ξ_3, ...], and let P be its dual Hopf algebra. Fix s>0. Is it true that for every internal degree t and every homogeneous class z in Ext_P^{s,t}(F_p,F_p), the class P^0 z in Ext_P^{s,pt}(F_p,F_p) is nilpotent in the bigraded algebra Ext_P^{*,*}(F_p,F_p), where P^0 is the algebra endomorphism induced by the p-th power map on P_*? ([msp.org](https://msp.org/gtm/2007/11/gtm-2007-11-020s.pdf))

For each integer n >= 1, let G_n = GL_n(F_2) and let G_{2n} = GL_{2n}(F_2). Define the maximal elementary abelian 2-subgroup A_{n,n} = { [[I_n, U], [0, I_n]] : U in M_n(F_2) } <= G_{2n}, so that H^*(A_{n,n}; F_2) = F_2[x_{i,j} | 1 <= i,j <= n] with each x_{i,j} in cohomological degree 1. Since N_{G_{2n}}(A_{n,n}) = G_n x G_n, restriction along A_{n,n} -> G_{2n} lands in the invariant ring H^*(A_{n,n}; F_2)^{G_n x G_n}. If det_n := det(x_{i,j}) in F_2[x_{i,j}] is the resulting homogeneous invariant of degree n, is det_n in the image of the degree-n restriction map H^n(G_{2n}; F_2) -> H^n(A_{n,n}; F_2)^{G_n x G_n}?

For each integer n >= 1, let G_{2n} = GL_{2n}(F_2), let A_{n,n} = { [[I_n, X], [0, I_n]] : X in M_n(F_2) } \cong (Z/2)^{n^2}, and let res : H_*(G_{2n}; F_2) -> H_*(A_{n,n}; F_2)^{G_n x G_n} be the restriction map, where N_{G_{2n}}(A_{n,n}) = G_n x G_n and H_*(A_{n,n}; F_2) = F_2[x_{i,j} | 1 <= i,j <= n] with each x_{i,j} in degree 1. If det_n = det(x_{i,j}) in H_n(A_{n,n}; F_2)^{G_n x G_n}, is H_n(G_{2n}; F_2) isomorphic to F_2 and generated by a class whose restriction is det_n? ([msp.org](https://msp.org/gtm/2007/11/gtm-2007-11-020s.pdf))

Let E = 7_+^{1+2} be the extraspecial group of order 7^3 and exponent 7, and let BG denote the p-completed classifying space of a finite group with Sylow 7-subgroup E, or more generally the classifying space of a 7-local finite group over E. Determine the complete p = 7 analogue of Theorem 6.2 in Yagita’s companion paper: for every 7-local finite group over E occurring in the Ruiz–Viruel classification, write the full stable wedge decomposition of BG into the standard indecomposable summands X_{q,k}, L(2,k), and L(1,k) (with M(2) = L(2,0) ∨ L(1,0)), and arrange these decompositions in a graph in the same sense as Theorem 6.2, namely so that a label X1 ... Xs G records a stable equivalence BG ≃ X1 ∨ ··· ∨ Xs. In particular, extend the partial p = 7 graph given in Theorem 9.4 to a complete graph. ([msp.org](https://msp.org/gtm/2007/11/gtm-2007-11-019s.pdf))

Within the framework of semi-analytic galaxy formation models developed to reproduce the observed bright end of the galaxy luminosity function, under what conditions and with what duty cycle can intermittent “radio-mode” AGN feedback—modeled as episodic mechanical energy injection by jets or bubbles at the centres of cluster-scale (M≳10¹⁴ M_⊙) dark matter haloes—inject sufficient power to offset radiative cooling (Λ(T)∝ρ²) and suppress cooling flows at all radii out to the virial radius, given that not every cluster exhibits central radio sources and that the steep density dependence of cooling makes stabilization challenging?

To what quantitative extent do semi-analytic ΛCDM galaxy formation models that implement a radio-mode AGN feedback prescription (e.g. as in Croton et al. 2006 or Bower et al. 2006) reproduce the observed star-formation histories of local (z≈0) massive elliptical galaxies (defined as those with stellar mass M_*≳10^11 M_⊙), when model-predicted mass-weighted ages and star-formation time-scales are directly compared to those derived from spectral fitting analyses of observed galaxy spectra?

In the context of modern semi-analytic galaxy formation models—where satellite galaxies undergo instantaneous, complete removal of their hot gas reservoir (“strangulation”) upon accretion, leading to an excess of faint red satellites and a sparsely populated green valley—what specific prescription for hot gas stripping timescales and efficiencies (e.g., those derived from high-resolution hydrodynamical simulations by McCarthy et al. 2008 and implemented by Font et al. 2008 in the Durham model) is required to slow star-formation quenching and reproduce the observed satellite colour distribution?

Within ΛCDM-based semi-analytic models of galaxy formation that compute disk scale radii via realistic angular momentum–conservation prescriptions, why has no model been able to reproduce both (1) the observed local (z≈0) galaxy luminosity function and (2) the zero-point of the Tully–Fisher relation—defined by the correlation between disk luminosity and circular velocity measured at the half-mass radius—and is this discrepancy attributable primarily to approximations in analytic disk size modelling or to more fundamental limitations of the cold dark matter paradigm?
Let G be a lattice-ordered group (an ℓ-group). If G is ℓ-simple, must every convex normal subgroup of G be trivial? ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/0906.2621.pdf))

Let G be a free lattice-ordered group (free ℓ-group), equipped with its given lattice order. Does there exist a total order on the underlying group of G that extends this lattice order and makes G a weakly abelian totally ordered group?

Let G be an ℓ-group. Assume that G is Engel, meaning that for every x,y in G there exists a positive integer n=n(x,y) such that [x,_n y]=1, with no uniform bound on n assumed. Must G be residually ordered (equivalently, o-approximable or representable), that is, must G be a subdirect product of totally ordered groups?

Is the conjugacy problem soluble for nilpotent finitely presented ℓ-groups; that is, given a finite presentation of a nilpotent lattice-ordered group in the ℓ-group language (group and lattice operations) and two terms representing elements of the group, is there an algorithm to decide whether those elements are conjugate in the underlying group?
For each positive integer n ≠ 1, let F_n denote the free lattice-ordered group (free ℓ-group) on n generators. Is F_n Hopfian; that is, is F_n not ℓ-isomorphic to a proper quotient of itself?

Let G and H be finitely presented abelian ℓ-groups (that is, lattice-ordered abelian groups), finitely presented in the ℓ-group language {+, −, 0, ∨, ∧}. If G and H are elementarily equivalent in that first-order language, must G and H be ℓ-isomorphic?

Let G be a group such that for every nonidentity element g in G, every integer n >= 1, and every x1, ..., xn in G, the product (x1^{-1} g x1)(x2^{-1} g x2)...(xn^{-1} g xn) is not equal to 1. Must G admit a total order <= such that a <= b implies ac <= bc for all a, b, c in G?

For each positive integer n, if a group G admits a total order invariant under right multiplication and satisfies the n-Engel identity [x,{}_n y]=1 for all x,y in G, where [x,{}_1 y]=x^{-1}y^{-1}xy and [x,{}_{k+1} y]=[[x,{}_k y],y], must G admit a right-invariant total order < with the Conrad property that whenever 1<f<g, there exists m=m(f,g) in Z_{>0} such that f g^m f^{-1}>g? ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/0906.2621.pdf))
For every right-orderable group G, is the group ring of G embeddable, as a ring, in some skew field?

Does there exist a nontrivial finitely generated group G with no proper nontrivial normal subgroups that admits a total order < preserved by right multiplication; that is, x<y implies xg<yg for all x,y,g in G?

Does there exist a countable right-orderable group U such that every countable right-orderable group G embeds into U as a group, where "right-orderable" means that G admits a total order invariant under right multiplication?

Does there exist a countable group U that admits a two-sided invariant total order and is universal for countable groups with this property, in the sense that every countable orderable group G embeds into U as a group?

For each fixed positive integer n, if G is a group admitting a total order <= such that a<=b implies ac<=bc for all c in G, and if G satisfies [x,_n y]=1 for all x,y in G (where [x,_1 y]=[x,y] and [x,_{k+1} y]=[[x,_k y],y]), must G be nilpotent?

For each positive integer n, does every torsion-free group G satisfying [x,_n y]=1 for all x,y in G (where [x,_1 y]=[x,y] and [x,_{k+1} y]=[[x,_k y],y]) admit a total order that is invariant under both left and right multiplication; equivalently, is every torsion-free n-Engel group orderable?

Does every orderable group G—that is, every group admitting a two-sided total order—admit an injective group homomorphism G -> H into some O∗-group H, where an O∗-group is a group such that every partial order on H compatible with the group structure extends to a total order making H a totally ordered group (an o-group)? ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/0906.2621.pdf))
Does there exist a simple group G such that every partial order on G can be extended to a total order on G making G a totally ordered group; equivalently, does there exist a simple O∗-group?

Let G be a group admitting a total order that makes G a totally ordered group, and suppose that G has a normal abelian subgroup A such that G/A is nilpotent. Must every partial order on G extend to a total order on G making G a totally ordered group; equivalently in the paper’s notation, must every orderable abelian-by-nilpotent group be an O*-group?

For each positive integer k, construct a group G_k that admits exactly 2k distinct two-sided invariant total orders; equivalently, G_k should have exactly 2k total orders making it a totally ordered group. In particular, this includes the unresolved sample cases k = 5 and k = 9, i.e. groups with exactly 10 and exactly 18 total orders.

Does there exist a finitely presented group G that is orderable, in the sense that G admits a total order invariant under both left and right multiplication, and whose group-theoretic word problem is insoluble?

Does there exist a group G together with a total order <= that is invariant under both left and right multiplication such that, for every g, h in G with 1 < g and 1 < h, there exists x in G satisfying x^-1 g x = h?

Let G be a group equipped with a bi-invariant total order <. Assume that G is abelian-by-nilpotent, meaning that G has a normal abelian subgroup A with nilpotent quotient G/A. Must there exist a divisible group D equipped with a bi-invariant total order <_D and an injective group homomorphism f:G -> D such that, for all x,y in G, x<y if and only if f(x)<_D f(y)? If, in addition, G is nilpotent-by-abelian, meaning that G has a normal nilpotent subgroup N with abelian quotient G/N, does the same conclusion follow? ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/0906.2621.pdf))

Let V be a variety of residually ordered ℓ-groups, meaning lattice-ordered groups that are subdirect products of ordered groups. Assume that the underlying groups of members of V satisfy no nontrivial group law. Must V contain a free linearly ordered (totally ordered) group, and must V in fact be exactly R = RO, the variety of all residually ordered ℓ-groups? ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/0906.2621.pdf))
Does there exist a group G such that the set of all distinct right orders on G—that is, total orders on G preserved by multiplication on the right—has cardinality exactly ℵ0?

Does there exist a soluble group G that is orderable in the two-sided sense (that is, G admits a total order invariant under both left and right multiplication) such that its abelianization G/[G,G], where [G,G] is the commutator subgroup, is periodic, i.e. every element of G/[G,G] has finite order?

Does there exist a projective, nonsingular, geometrically irreducible F_{27^2}-maximal curve X such that, for its Frobenius linear series D = |(27+1)P_0| with P_0 in X(F_{27^2}), one has dim(D) = 3 and generic D-order sequence (epsilon_0, epsilon_1, epsilon_2, epsilon_3) = (0,1,3,27)?

Does there exist, for some prime power q, an F_{q^2}-maximal curve X of Frobenius dimension 3—that is, with Frobenius linear series D := |(q+1)P_0| for an F_{q^2}-rational point P_0 and dim(D)=3—such that the generic D-order sequence is (0,1,ε_2,q) with ε_2 = 2, and such that there exists a point P ∈ X(F_{q^2}) whose (D,P)-order sequence has second entry j_2(P)=3?

Does there exist a prime power q and a smooth, projective, geometrically irreducible F_{q^2}-maximal curve X such that, for an F_{q^2}-rational point P_0 on X and the associated Frobenius linear series D := |(q + 1)P_0|, one has dim(D) = 3, the generic D-order sequence 0 = epsilon_0 < epsilon_1 = 1 < epsilon_2 < epsilon_3 = q satisfies epsilon_2 = 2, and there exists a point P in X(F_{q^2}) whose (D,P)-orders 0 = j_0(P) < j_1(P) = 1 < j_2(P) < j_3(P) = q + 1 satisfy j_2(P) = q + 1 - floor((2/3)(q + 1))?

Let q be an odd prime power with q ≡ 2 (mod 3), let K=F_{q^2}, let F=K(x,y) be the function field defined by y^((q+1)/3)+x^((q+1)/3)+1=0, choose w in K with w^((q+1)/3)=3, and let Fbar=F(z) where z^3=wxy. Since Section 5 proves that Fbar is an F_{q^2}-maximal function field of genus (q^2-q+4)/6 and Frobenius dimension 3, are the F_{q^2}-maximal function fields with Frobenius dimension 3 and genus (q^2-q+4)/6 constructed in [14] F_{q^2}-isomorphic to Fbar?

Let (h,t)∈ℕ₀² denote the current counts of heads and tails in a sequential fair-coin tossing game. For each finite horizon N, define f_N(h,t) by the boundary condition f_N(h,N−h)=max{h/N,1/2} for 0≤h≤N and by backward induction f_N(h,t)=max{h/(h+t), (f_N(h+1,t)+f_N(h,t+1))/2} for h+t<N. Let F(h,t)=lim_{N→∞} f_N(h,t), which exists. The optimal stopping rule is: stop if F(h,t)=h/(h+t) and continue otherwise. The open problem is to determine exactly for which (h,t)∈ℕ₀² one has F(h,t)=h/(h+t)—equivalently, to rigorously characterize the stopping region S={ (h,t): F(h,t)=h/(h+t) } by proving, for each (h,t) in S, that h/(h+t)≥(f_N(h+1,t)+f_N(h,t+1))/2 holds for all N.

Let β_n be the stopping boundary in the infinite-horizon Chow–Robbins coin-tossing game (Chow and Robbins, 1965): one observes fair, independent coin tosses, let H and T be counts of heads and tails, and stops the first time H–T ≥ β_n to maximize the expected proportion of heads at stopping. The still-open problem for n=8 is to determine whether β_8=2. Equivalently, letting F(h,t) denote the optimal expected payoff starting from state (h,t), decide whether F(5,3)<5/8, i.e. whether it is optimal at (5,3) to stop and secure the payoff 5/8 rather than to continue.

Given the observed global thermodynamic arrow of time—characterized by a universal increase in coarse-grained entropy—what cosmological mechanism best accounts for its origin: (i) a special low-entropy cosmic initial condition at the big bang (a global high-density state), (ii) a Boltzmann-style giant chance fluctuation in an eternal universe, or (iii) another process? Moreover, if the thermodynamic arrow arises from the big-bang initial condition, what are the implications for recollapsing (oscillating) cosmological models, in which the classical thermodynamic arrow would classically reverse upon recollapse?

In the framework of a universally valid Schrödinger evolution for the global wave function of the universe (as, for example, in the Wheeler–DeWitt approach for Friedmann cosmologies), should the observed cosmological arrow of time be implemented by (a) a fundamentally time-asymmetric non-unitary collapse law—despite the lack of experimental confirmation for any modification of the Schrödinger equation—or by (b) Everettian branching defined by irreversible decoherence (retarded entanglement) under unitary evolution? Specifically, what precise initial condition on the global wave function (e.g., a non-entangled “simple” symmetric state) is required to suppress recoherence to a negligible probability and thereby guarantee the emergence of autonomous quasi-classical branches with a well-defined temporal orientation?

In loop quantum cosmology, the quantum Hamiltonian constraint becomes a difference equation in the cosmic scale factor a that admits solutions continued through a=0 to negative values of a, corresponding to an ‘inside‐out’ reversal of spatial orientation. Given that (i) the Hamiltonian is invariant under a→−a, (ii) the emergent WKB time parameter (from a Born–Oppenheimer expansion in α=ln a) breaks down at a=0 and cannot be analytically continued across the bounce, and (iii) a low‐entropy boundary condition at a=0 is required to define the thermodynamic arrow for all other degrees of freedom, what is the consistent physical interpretation of the negative‐a branch, and how can one impose a low‐entropy condition at a=0 without assuming an even lower‐entropy state at a<0 so as to avoid an inversion of the thermodynamic arrow?

Let K_n denote the class of fundamental groups of complements of locally flat PL embeddings S^n into S^{n+2}. Theorem 1.1 proves that if A and B are chosen from {K_0, K_1, K_2, K_3, S, M, G} with B properly contained in A and A containing K_3, then there is no algorithm which, given a finite presentation of a group known a priori to lie in A, decides whether that group lies in B. Does this same undecidability statement remain true when A = K_2; equivalently, for each B in {K_0, K_1}, is there no algorithm that, given a finite presentation of a group known to be a 2-knot group, decides whether the presented group lies in B? The paper notes that this would follow if some 2-knot group has unsolvable word problem.

Is the isomorphism problem algorithmically unsolvable for K_2, the class of fundamental groups of complements of locally flat PL 2-knots S^2 into S^4? In other words, is there no algorithm that, given finite presentations of two groups known a priori to lie in K_2, always decides whether those two groups are isomorphic? ([ems.press](https://ems.press/content/serial-article-files/44199))
Does there exist a locally flat PL 2-knot K subset S^4 such that its complement group G = pi_1(S^4 - K), equivalently a group G in K_2, has unsolvable word problem?

Let K_2 denote the class of groups pi_1(S^4 \ Sigma^2), where Sigma^2 subset S^4 is a locally flat PL-embedded 2-sphere (a 2-knot). Is it true that for every finitely presented group G there exists a group K in K_2 such that G embeds in K as a subgroup?

Let C be a class of infinite sequences (A_1, A_2, A_3, ...) of abelian groups, closed under componentwise isomorphism, and for a finitely presented group G let H_*(G) := (H_1(G), H_2(G), H_3(G), ...) denote its integral homology sequence. Assume there exist finitely presented groups G_1 and G_2 such that H_1(G_1) isomorphic to H_1(G_2), H_*(G_1) belongs to C, and H_*(G_2) does not belong to C. Theorem 5.1 shows that the set of finite presentations P for which H_*(P) belongs to C is not recursive. For which such classes C can this conclusion be strengthened to say that the set of finite presentations P with H_*(P) in C is not recursively enumerable?

For each fixed non-negative integer g, does there exist an algorithm that, given a finite PL description of a locally flat embedding Σ_g ↪ S^4 of a closed connected orientable surface Σ_g of genus g, decides whether the embedding is unknotted, i.e. PL-equivalent in S^4 to the standard genus-g embedding?

Let m > 1, and let {(t_n, sigma_n)}_{n>=1} be a stationary ergodic sequence with E sigma_1 < m E t_1. For the G/G/m queue with FCFS discipline, define the Kiefer-Wolfowitz vector of virtual waiting times by W_1 = 0 and W_{n+1} = R(W_n + e_1 sigma_n - 1 t_n)^+, where e_1 = (1,0,...,0), 1 = (1,...,1), R orders coordinates in weakly increasing order, and positive part is taken coordinatewise. It is already known that, from zero initial state, W_n converges almost surely coordinatewise to a limit with minimal stationary distribution pi_min, and hence converges weakly to pi_min. Is it true that, under these assumptions alone and without any further restriction on the driving sequence, one in fact has total-variation convergence to pi_min, namely sup_{A in B(R_+^m)} |P(W_n in A) - pi_min(A)| -> 0 as n -> infinity?

Fix γ > 0. Consider a stable first-come-first-served G/G/m queue with a finite number m of identical servers, where {σ_n}_{n≥1} and {t_n}_{n≥1} are mutually independent i.i.d. sequences of nonnegative service times and interarrival times, respectively, satisfying ρ := E[σ_1]/E[t_1] < m, and let D denote the stationary waiting time of the queue (whose stationary distribution is unique in this i.i.d. setting). What are the necessary and sufficient conditions for the finiteness of E[D^γ] in the boundary case where ρ is an integer?

Let D be the stationary waiting time in a stable GI/GI/2 first-come first-served queue with i.i.d. interarrival times of mean a and i.i.d. service times with distribution B and mean b, and let rho = b/a. In the critical-load case rho = 1 (so b = a), assuming that the service-time distribution B is subexponential, determine the exact asymptotic behavior of P(D > x) as x -> infinity; in particular, what is the corresponding exact tail asymptotic in the regularly varying case singled out in the paper?

Consider the stable GI/GI/2 first-come, first-served queue with i.i.d. interarrival times τ_n of mean a, i.i.d. service times σ_n of mean b, load ρ=b/a in (1,2), and stationary waiting time D. Let B̄(x)=P{σ>x} and B̄_r(x)=b^{-1}∫_x^∞ B̄(y)dy. Determine the exact asymptotic behavior of P(D>x) as x→∞ when the service-time distribution is heavy-tailed with all power moments finite but is not in the intermediate-regularly-varying class, for example when B̄(x)=exp(-x^β) with 0<β<1.

In the stable GI/GI/2 first-come-first-served queue with independent i.i.d. interarrival times {t_n} and service times {sigma_n}, load rho := E[sigma_1]/E[t_1] < 2, and stationary waiting time D, what are the asymptotically typical rare-event sample paths leading to {D > x} as x -> infinity in the two open cases singled out by Foss: (a) rho = 1, at least for some particular subexponential service-time distribution (for example, regularly varying), and (b) 1 < rho < 2 when the service-time distribution is heavy-tailed in the sense that E[e^{c sigma_1}] = infinity for every c > 0 but E[sigma_1^p] < infinity for every p > 0 (for example, P(sigma_1 > x) = e^{-x^beta} with beta in (0,1))? ([paperzz.com](https://paperzz.com/doc/7045455/some-open-problems-related-to-stability-1-multi))

Consider a queueing system with a finite number m of identical servers, already in the case m = 2, with a separate queue in front of each server. Let {(t_n, sigma_n)} be a stationary ergodic input sequence, where t_n is the interarrival time between customers n and n+1 and sigma_n is the service time of customer n. Each arriving customer is routed immediately by the join-the-shortest-queue rule, i.e. to a queue of minimal current length, with ties broken at random among the shortest queues. Assuming only the natural stability condition E[sigma_1] < m E[t_1] and no further hypotheses, how many stationary regimes can the resulting JSQ system-state process have?

In the multi-server join-the-shortest-queue system, already in the two-server case, with stationary ergodic input sequence {(t_n, sigma_n)} where t_n is the interarrival time between customers n and n+1 and sigma_n is the service time of customer n, each server has its own queue, and each arrival joins a shortest queue (breaking ties at random among the shortest queues), assume the obvious load/stability condition E[sigma_1] < m E[t_1] (in particular E[sigma_1] < 2 E[t_1] when m = 2). What are the weakest additional assumptions, if any, beyond stationary ergodicity and this stability condition, that guarantee that the associated join-the-shortest-queue system has a unique stationary regime?

For a finite system of identical servers—explicitly, in the paper, say two servers—with stationary ergodic input {t_n, sigma_n} (t_n the interarrival time between customers n and n+1, sigma_n the service time of customer n), separate queues at the servers, and join-the-shortest-queue routing with random tie-breaking among shortest queues, and assuming only the natural stability condition inherited from the paper (E[sigma_1] < m E[t_1], hence E[sigma_1] < 2 E[t_1] in the two-server case), are any assumptions beyond stability required for the distribution of the JSQ system state to converge to a stationary regime, and if so, under what conditions can one prove weak convergence or even convergence in total variation?

Consider the continuous greedy-server model on a fixed circle S with its usual arc-length distance. Particles arrive according to a Poisson process of rate λ, with independent uniform arrival locations on S. Each service time is deterministically equal to 1. After each service completion, the server chooses a currently waiting particle that minimizes the distance from its present location, travels to it at a fixed speed v ∈ (0,∞) without rerouting in response to arrivals during the trip, serves it, removes it, and repeats. Is this system stable, in the usual queueing sense of positive recurrence, for every arrival rate λ < 1 and every fixed speed v ∈ (0,∞)?

Fix a circle of arbitrary length L > 0 and a parameter epsilon > 0. Black particles arrive on the circle as a Poisson rain of rate lambda, with arrival locations uniform on the circle, and each black particle stays until deleted. Independently, white particles arrive as a Poisson rain of rate 1, with uniform arrival locations; each white particle immediately disappears, but at its arrival epoch it inspects the epsilon-neighbourhood of its arrival point (for the circle metric) and, if that neighbourhood contains any black particles, deletes the black particle nearest to it. Is the resulting continuous-state-space greedy system stable, for every lambda < 1, independently of the circle length L and of epsilon?

Consider the three-server queueing system from Section 4 of Foss (2009): arrivals form a Poisson process of rate λ; each arrival independently becomes class i with probability 1/3 for i=1,2,3; class 1 can be served by servers 1 (left) and 2 (right), class 2 by servers 2 (left) and 3 (right), and class 3 by servers 3 (left) and 1 (right); each arrival is routed to the accessible server with the smaller current workload; and the service-time distribution is F_l when the customer is served by its left server and F_r when it is served by its right server. Is it possible that the stability conditions of this system depend on both the initial workload state and the full distributions F_l and F_r, rather than being determined solely by coarse summary characteristics of those driving distributions? ([ar5iv.labs.arxiv.org](https://ar5iv.labs.arxiv.org/pdf/0909.0462))

Consider the open polling system with two stations and two heterogeneous servers described as follows. For each station i in {1,2}, arrivals form a Poisson input of rate lambda_i = 1. For i,j in {1,2}, service times of server j at station i are i.i.d. exponential with rate mu_i^(j). Both servers use the exhaustive service policy: after a service completion, a server immediately begins another service at its current station if a customer is available there; otherwise it moves instantaneously to the other station; and if there is no free customer at either station, the server becomes passive. Restrict the parameter vector (mu_1^(1), mu_1^(2), mu_2^(1), mu_2^(2)) to the open cube (0,1)^4. Is it true that the subset of parameter values for which the polling system's state process is null recurrent has positive 4-dimensional Lebesgue measure?

Consider the single-channel slotted multi-access system in which all packets have the same unit transmission time, the number of packet arrivals during each slot is Poisson with parameter λ>0, and W_n denotes the number of packets in the system at the beginning of slot n. In slot n, every packet currently present attempts transmission independently, all with the same probability p_n. A slot is called successful if exactly one packet transmits, a collision if two or more packets transmit, and empty if none transmit; after a collision, the transmitting packets remain in the system and retry later, while after a successful transmission the transmitted packet departs. Suppose the access probabilities are defined inductively so that p_{n+1} may depend only on p_n and on the one-bit indicator of whether slot n contained a successful transmission. Then (W_n,p_n) is a time-homogeneous Markov chain. Does there exist any protocol of this restricted success/no-success-feedback form for which the Markov chain (W_n,p_n) is positive recurrent (ergodic, in the paper's wording) for some λ>0?

Let F,G: C^2 -> C^2 be polynomial endomorphisms such that det(Jac(F))=det(Jac(G))=1. Assume that F and G agree on the algebraic set V(xy)={(x,y) in C^2 : xy=0}, equivalently on the union of the two coordinate axes. Must it follow that F=G on all of C^2?

Fix a positive integer n and let k be a field of characteristic 0. Let GA_n(k) = Aut_k(k[x_1,\dots,x_n]) be the group of polynomial automorphisms of affine n-space A_k^n, and let TA_n(k) \subseteq GA_n(k) be the tame subgroup generated by affine and triangular automorphisms. Do there exist finitely many one-parameter subgroups H_1,\dots,H_r \subseteq GA_n(k) such that GA_n(k) = \langle TA_n(k), H_1,\dots,H_r \rangle?

Let k be a field, let x, y, z be indeterminates, and for each integer n >= 1 and polynomial f(x) in k[x], set A_{n,f} := k[x,y,z]/(x^n z - y^2 - f(x)y). Find an intrinsic algebraic invariant I(A), defined for normal finitely generated k-algebras A, which captures the algebraic rigidity of the "tubular neighborhood of infinity" and may be viewed as adding a "continuous" dimension to the homotopy type at infinity, such that I distinguishes, in a straightforward way (even if the calculations are complicated), all isomorphism classes among the algebras A_{n,f}.

Fix a ground field k. Classify, up to G-equivariant isomorphism, all pairs (G, X) where G is a connected solvable linear algebraic k-group and X is a normal affine G-variety containing G as an open orbit (that is, a normal affine equivariant embedding of G), such that every point stabilizer G_x for x in X is semisimple; in particular, determine this classification in the special case where the maximal tori of G have dimension 1.

Let R = C[a,b] and B = R[X,Y,Z]. If D is a locally nilpotent R-derivation of B that admits a slice, i.e. there exists s in B with D(s)=1, must Ker(D) be isomorphic, as an R-algebra, to the polynomial ring R[U,V] = R[2]?

Let G = Aut(A^2_C) be the group of polynomial automorphisms of the complex affine plane, and for a finite sequence of integers (d1,...,dℓ) with each di >= 2 let G_(d1,...,dℓ) denote the subset of automorphisms of polydegree (d1,...,dℓ). For integers d >= 2 and e >= 1, is the one-step polydegree stratum G_(d+e) contained in the Zariski closure of the two-step stratum G_(d,e+1) inside G; equivalently, does G_(d+e) ⊆ overline{G_(d,e+1)} hold in Aut(A^2_C)?

Let k be a field, let GA_n(k) = Aut_k k[x_1, ..., x_n], and for each 1 ≤ i ≤ n let V_i := k ⊕ kx_1 ⊕ ··· ⊕ kx_i and G_i := {φ ∈ GA_n(k) : φ(V_i) = V_i}. Is GA_n(k) generated by the subgroups G_1, ..., G_n? Moreover, is the subgroup ⟨G_1, ..., G_n⟩ the generalized amalgamated product of the G_i along their pairwise intersections G_i ∩ G_j?

Let k be a field and n ≥ 2. For 1 ≤ i ≤ n, let V_i = k ⊕ kx_1 ⊕ ··· ⊕ kx_i ⊂ k[x_1, ..., x_n], let G_i = {φ ∈ GA_n(k) : φ(V_i) = V_i}, and let H_i = G_i ∩ TA_n(k), where TA_n(k) is the tame automorphism subgroup of GA_n(k). Is TA_n(k) the generalized amalgamated product of the subgroups H_1, ..., H_n along their pairwise intersections?

Let Ω be an open subset of R^n, and let μ be a positive measure on Ω such that ∫Ω h(x) dμ is finite for every polynomial h ∈ C[x1,...,xn]. Suppose f ∈ C[x1,...,xn] satisfies ∫Ω f(x)^m dμ = 0 for every integer m ≥ 1. Must it then follow that for every polynomial g ∈ C[x1,...,xn], one has ∫Ω f(x)^m g(x) dμ = 0 for all sufficiently large m?

Let n ≥ 1, let B be an open subset of R^n, and let σ be a positive measure on B such that ∫_B h(z) dσ(z) is finite for every polynomial h ∈ C[z_1,…,z_n]. Define M_B(σ) := {f ∈ C[z_1,…,z_n] | ∫_B f(z) dσ(z) = 0}. Is M_B(σ) a Mathieu subspace of the C-algebra C[z_1,…,z_n]? Equivalently, whenever f ∈ C[z_1,…,z_n] satisfies ∫_B f(z)^m dσ(z) = 0 for all m ≥ 1, must it follow that for every g ∈ C[z_1,…,z_n] there exists N such that ∫_B f(z)^m g(z) dσ(z) = 0 for all m ≥ N?

Let k be any field, let A be a finitely generated commutative k-algebra, and let M1, M2 be k-linear subspaces of A. Assume that each Mi is a Mathieu subspace of A in the sense that for every a,b in A, if a^m belongs to Mi for all sufficiently large m, then a^m b belongs to Mi for all sufficiently large m. Must the linear sum M1 + M2 also be a Mathieu subspace of A?

Let K be a field, let R be a K-algebra, and let K[z] denote the polynomial K-algebra in one variable. If the free product of K-algebras R * K[z] is isomorphic to the free associative K-algebra K⟨x_1,...,x_n⟩ of rank n, does it follow that R is isomorphic to the free associative K-algebra K⟨x_1,...,x_{n-1}⟩ of rank n-1?

Let K be either R or C, and let n ≥ 1. For which integers n does the full matrix algebra M_n(K) admit a grading by an abelian group Γ, say M_n(K) = ⊕_{γ∈Γ} A_γ, together with a bilinear map ⟨ , ⟩ : Γ × Γ → Z_2, such that A_γ A_δ ⊂ A_{γ+δ} for all γ, δ ∈ Γ and every homogeneous x ∈ A_γ, y ∈ A_δ satisfies xy = (-1)^{⟨γ,δ⟩} yx? ([sophie-moriergenoud.perso.math.cnrs.fr](https://sophie-moriergenoud.perso.math.cnrs.fr/Publi/GradCommProceedings.pdf))

Over the paper’s ambient ground field K = ℝ or ℂ, can one develop an algebraic-geometric notion of the spectrum of a Γ-commutative algebra A = ⊕γ∈Γ Aγ, where Γ is an abelian group and there is a bilinear map ⟨·,·⟩: Γ × Γ → ℤ2 such that homogeneous elements satisfy ab = (−1)^{⟨ā,b̄⟩} ba, so as to attach geometric objects to Γ-commutative algebras, with the well-developed ℤ2-commutative/supergeometric case as the basic reference point, and in particular to obtain a new viewpoint on Clifford algebras and Clifford analysis?

Let Ω ⊂ R^n, with n = 2 or 3, be a sufficiently smooth bounded domain. Consider the incompressible homogeneous Jeffreys/Oldroyd initial-boundary value problem with no-slip boundary condition,

u_t + (u·∇)u - Div sigma + ∇p = f_0, div u = 0, u|_{∂Ω} = 0,

sigma + lambda_1 D_a sigma/Dt = 2 eta (E(u) + lambda_2 D_a E(u)/Dt),

where 0 < lambda_2 < lambda_1, eta > 0, E(u) = (∇u + (∇u)^T)/2, and D_a/Dt is Oldroyd’s objective derivative with parameter a ∈ [-1,1]. For data in the strong-solution class used in the paper (in particular, f_0 ∈ L^2(0,T;H^1(Ω)^n) ∩ W^1_2(0,T;H^{-1}(Ω)^n), u_0 ∈ H^2(Ω)^n ∩ V, and the corresponding initial stress datum in the H^2-type symmetric-tensor class), local-in-time strong solvability is known, and global-in-time strong solvability is known only under smallness assumptions on the data and parameters. Is it true that this bounded-domain problem admits a global-in-time strong solution without any such smallness assumption, already in the case n = 2?

Let Ω be a sufficiently regular bounded domain in R^n with n = 2 or 3, let T > 0, and consider the incompressible Jeffreys model with Oldroyd derivative D_a/Dt, -1 <= a <= 1, η > 0, and 0 < λ2 < λ1: ∂_t u + (u·∇)u - Div σ + ∇p = f in (0,T)×Ω, σ + λ1 D_aσ/Dt = 2η(E(u) + λ2 D_aE(u)/Dt), div u = 0 in (0,T)×Ω, and u = 0 on (0,T)×∂Ω.
