For arbitrary initial data and body force in the regularity class for which the local strong solution exists, does that local strong solution necessarily extend to a global strong solution on the whole interval [0,T] without any smallness assumptions on the data? In particular, can one prove such global strong solvability even in two space dimensions?

Let Ω⊂R^n be an arbitrary domain, with n∈{2,3}, let T>0, η>0, and 0<λ2<λ1, and assume f∈L^2(0,T;V*), a∈H, and σ0∈W^{-1}_2(Ω;S^{n×n}) satisfy σ0-2η(λ2/λ1)E(a)∈L^2(Ω;S^{n×n}), where E(v)=1/2(∇v+∇v^T). For the incompressible Jeffreys initial-boundary value problem vt+(v·∇)v-Divσ+∇p=f, σ+λ1(σt+(v·∇)σ)=2η(E(v)+λ2(E(v)t+(v·∇)E(v))), divv=0, v|∂Ω=0, v(0)=a, σ(0)=σ0, does the weak solution given by the existence theorem, in the natural class v∈L^2(0,T;V)∩Cw([0,T];H), vt∈L^1(0,T;V*), σ∈L^2(0,T;L^2(Ω;S^{n×n}))∩Cw([0,T];H^{-1}(Ω;S^{n×n})), have to be unique, i.e. can one remove the additional 3D Serrin-type assumptions used in the conditional uniqueness theorem? ([nzdr.ru](https://www.nzdr.ru/data/media/biblio/kolxoz/P/PC/PCfm/Zvyagin%20V.G.%2C%20Vorotnikov%20D.A.%20Topological%20Approximation%20Methods%20for%20Evolutionary%20Problems%20of%20Nonlinear%20Hydrodynamics%20%28de%20Gruyter%2C%202008%29%28ISBN%203110202220%29%28245s%29_PCfm_.pdf))

For the autonomous initial-boundary value problem for the incompressible Jeffreys-type viscoelastic medium considered in the paper—posed in a bounded sufficiently smooth domain Omega subset of R^n, n >= 2, with homogeneous Dirichlet boundary condition and time-independent body force—can one prove that the minimal trajectory attractor of weak solutions and the corresponding global attractor have finite Hausdorff dimension, and can this be done without the special restrictions on the Jeffreys coefficients, the external force, and the initial data that are imposed in the reviewed attractor-existence theorem?

Let Ω ⊂ R^n (n = 2 or 3) be a bounded domain with the boundary regularity assumed in the paper, and let f belong to the force space used in the paper’s weak formulation. For the stationary incompressible Jeffreys-type viscoelastic fluid model in Ω with no-slip boundary condition v|∂Ω = 0, momentum equation (v·∇)v − Div σ + ∇p = f, div v = 0, and the paper’s constitutive law σ + λ1 Dσ/Dt = 2η(E(v) + λ2 DE(v)/Dt), where E(v) = (∇v + (∇v)^T)/2 and D/Dt is the objective derivative fixed in the paper, does there exist at least one generalized (weak) stationary solution for every admissible choice of the coefficients and every admissible external force f, without imposing any additional smallness-type restrictions on those data?

Let Ω ⊂ R^n, n ∈ {2,3}, be a sufficiently regular bounded domain, let T > 0, let E(u) = (∇u + (∇u)^T)/2, and consider the incompressible Jeffreys system on (0,T) × Ω: ∂t u + (u·∇)u − div σ + ∇p = f, σ + λ1(∂t σ + (u·∇)σ) = 2μ(E(u) + λ2(∂t E(u) + (u·∇)E(u))), div u = 0, with no-slip boundary condition u = 0 on ∂Ω and initial data u(0)=a, σ(0)=σ0. For coefficients μ > 0 and 0 < λ2 < λ1, and for data f ∈ L^2(0,T; V*), a ∈ H, and σ0 ∈ H^{-1}(Ω; R_sym^{n×n}) satisfying σ0 − (2μλ2/λ1)E(a) ∈ L^2(Ω; R_sym^{n×n}), does there exist a weak solution (u,σ) with u ∈ L^2(0,T; V) ∩ Cw([0,T]; H), ∂t u ∈ L^1(0,T; V*), and σ ∈ L^2(0,T; L^2(Ω; R_sym^{n×n})) ∩ Cw([0,T]; H^{-1}(Ω; R_sym^{n×n})) for every T > 0?

For the incompressible constant-density Jeffreys/Oldroyd model in a bounded domain Ω ⊂ R^n (with n ≥ 2), given by div v = 0, ∂_t v + (v·∇)v - Div σ + ∇p = f, the no-slip boundary condition v|∂Ω = 0, and the objective constitutive law σ + λ1 Dσ/Dt = 2η(E(v) + λ2 DE(v)/Dt), where E(v) = (∇v + (∇v)^T)/2 and D/Dt is an objective derivative in the sense of (2.17), does the associated evolutionary initial-boundary value problem admit global-in-time solutions that are periodic in time, without imposing any additional restrictive assumptions on the coefficients (beyond the standard Jeffreys regime λ1 > λ2), on the external force, or on the initial data?

Let Ω ⊂ R^n (n = 2 or 3) be a bounded smooth domain and T > 0. Consider the incompressible Jeffreys/Oldroyd-type initial-boundary value problem on (0,T) × Ω with unknowns v, p, σ, divergence constraint div v = 0, homogeneous Dirichlet boundary condition for v, and constitutive law σ + λ1(∂tσ + (v·∇)σ + σW(v) − W(v)σ) = 2η(E(v) + λ2(∂tE(v) + (v·∇)E(v) + E(v)W(v) − W(v)E(v))), where E(v) = (∇v + ∇v^T)/2 and W(v) = (∇v − ∇v^T)/2. Is the review’s cited weak-solvability theorem for this genuine corotational/Jaumann objective-derivative model (reference [53]) actually correct, i.e. does the problem admit global weak solutions for admissible data, or does the apparent gap in the published limit passage for the nonlinear stress terms — seemingly requiring an unjustified identity such as η|_{t=0} = 0 — mean that the weak-solvability question for the unsmoothed Jaumann model remains open?

For the autonomous initial-boundary value problem for an incompressible Jeffreys-type viscoelastic medium in a bounded domain, given by the incompressibility condition (0.2), momentum equation (0.4), no-slip boundary condition (0.5), and constitutive relation with the full material derivative (2.15), with prescribed initial velocity and initial stress, can one construct a global attractor for the class of global weak solutions despite the lack of uniqueness and the failure of the classical invariant-dissipative semigroup approach, by using the framework of minimal trajectory attractors; and, in the nonautonomous case, can one analogously construct a uniform attractor?

In the generator coordinate method applied to one-dimensional quadrupole collective motion in even–even nuclei, the Gaussian overlap approximation is used to derive a collective Hamiltonian H(q,p) with an inertial function M(q) evaluated using real generator coordinates q. (i) How accurate and reliable are the resulting inertial functions M(q) when time-odd mean-field effects and collective momenta p are neglected? (ii) Given that reproducing the correct collective mass for center-of-mass motion requires introducing complex generator coordinates to treat p explicitly [7], what microscopic prescription or variational principle can be used to select or determine the real generator coordinates q in the quadrupole GCM so that both the coordinate dependence q and its conjugate momentum p are consistently accounted for, ensuring a faithful description of large-amplitude dynamics?

How significant are the contributions of time-odd mean-field components (those breaking time-reversal symmetry) induced by the time evolution of the self-consistent mean field to the inertial function B(q) in microscopic calculations of large-amplitude collective motion, and how can these contributions be microscopically evaluated using modern nuclear energy density functionals (such as Skyrme, Gogny, or covariant EDFs) within frameworks like the ASCC method or GCM-GOA, in contrast to their omission in the conventional cranking (ATDHFB) mass?

In the adiabatic self-consistent collective coordinate (ASCC) framework for large-amplitude collective motion in superfluid nuclei, one extracts a collective path parameterized by a coordinate q with conjugate momentum p, and derives a collective Hamiltonian H(q,p,n)=V(q)+½ B(q)p²+λ(q)n, where B(q) is the inverse inertial function (collective mass M(q)=1/B(q)). What are the microscopic mechanisms that determine M(q) at each point along the collective path? In particular, how do (i) the strength of pairing correlations, (ii) successive single-particle level crossings at the Fermi surface, (iii) the Barranco et al. nucleon-pair hopping mechanism (the “hopping mass”), and (iv) smooth adiabatic rearrangements of single-particle wavefunctions each contribute to, and combine in, setting the inertia against an infinitesimal change δq in the collective coordinate?

How can one, within the moving-frame HFB plus local QRPA framework described in Sec. 5.1, derive the full five-dimensional Bohr–Mottelson quadrupole collective Hamiltonian by: (i) solving the moving-frame HFB equation (Eq. 40) at each point (q₁,q₂) of the two-dimensional collective submanifold to obtain |ϕ(q)〉; (ii) defining the β and γ deformation variables via Eqs. (42)–(43) and mapping (q₁,q₂) one-to-one onto the (β,γ) plane as a collective hypersurface (Fig. 3); (iii) computing the vibrational inertial masses B_i(β,γ) through the LQRPA equations (Eqs. 44–45); (iv) determining the three rotational moments of inertia J_k(β,γ) by solving the Thouless–Valatin equations (Eq. 52) at every off-equilibrium (β,γ) point; and (v) quantizing the resulting curvilinear kinetic energy terms by the Pauli prescription to obtain the quantized 5D collective Schrödinger equation?

In the framework of zero‐temperature nuclear large‐amplitude collective motion, what fully microscopic, non‐perturbative extension of the adiabatic self‐consistent collective coordinate (ASCC) method—or an alternative approach based on time‐dependent Hartree–Fock–Bogoliubov (TDHFB) theory—can be developed to treat odd‐A nuclei (i.e.
systems with one or more quasiparticles on an HFB vacuum) so as to self‐consistently construct the collective submanifold and derive a collective Hamiltonian that describes tunneling between distinct HFB local minima, while simultaneously accounting for the coupling and interplay between quasiparticle degrees of freedom and collective coordinates beyond the perturbative RPA/QRPA‐based particle–vibration‐coupling approximations?

How can one formulate a fully self-consistent microscopic theory of large-amplitude collective motion (LACM) in nuclei at finite temperature, and what are the underlying microscopic mechanisms of damping and dissipation that govern the evolution of these collective motions as one proceeds from low-lying yrast excitations to the compound-nucleus regime?

In triaxially deformed cold nuclei near the yrast line at high angular momentum, the wobbling mode—describable as a boson-like small-amplitude vibration of the rotating mean field—exhibits significant anharmonicity in observed double-excitation bands. What is the dynamical behavior of this wobbling mode as its amplitude grows beyond the random-phase approximation regime, ultimately leading to an instability of the uniformly rotating HFB solution with respect to this collective rotational degree of freedom? Furthermore, how can the microscopic large-amplitude collective-motion theory (e.g., the adiabatic self-consistent collective coordinate method) be formulated and applied to describe both (a) the nonlinear evolution from small- to large-amplitude wobbling and the onset of rotational instability, and (b) the large-amplitude chiral vibrations connecting the right- and left-handed triaxial HFB configurations?

Within the context of Section 2.1 of Matsuo and Nakatsukasa (2010), can the strong-coupling (BEC-like) ¹S₀ neutron pairing correlations predicted for low-density pure neutron matter, as well as the quarteting correlations (including α-particle condensation) predicted for low-density symmetric nuclear matter, be identified in finite nuclei—specifically, through spatial di-neutron correlations in two-neutron-halo nuclei (e.g., ¹¹Li, ⁶He), surface di-neutron correlations in medium- and heavy-mass neutron-rich isotopes, and α-cluster occupancy in the 0⁺₂ Hoyle state of ¹²C? If so, are these finite-nucleus signatures quantitatively connected to the same underlying microscopic mechanisms (such as pair coherence lengths comparable to inter-particle spacings and cluster S-orbit occupation) that characterize dilute-matter correlations, and which observables or computational approaches would most directly establish this link?

In the many-body theoretical framework for nuclei at the neutron and proton drip lines that includes short-range nucleon–nucleon interactions, long-range many-body correlations with pairing, and explicit coupling to the particle continuum with proper boundary conditions, what formalism provides a consistent microscopic description of weakly bound drip-line systems? Within this formalism, how does pairing induce an anti-halo effect that suppresses the spatial extension of weakly bound neutron orbitals, and to what extent do Fujita–Miyazawa-type three-body forces determine the location of the drip lines, for example in oxygen isotopes?

Within the framework of nuclear density functional theory that incorporates continuum single-particle states and pairing correlations, how do the properties of low-energy electric dipole (E1) excitations—commonly referred to as pygmy dipole resonances—in medium-to-heavy neutron-rich isotopic chains evolve as the one-neutron separation energy decreases toward the neutron drip line? Specifically, to what extent are these E1 modes collective versus single-particle in character, what microscopic mechanism underlies their emergence (e.g., coherent neutron-skin oscillation versus transitions of weakly bound neutrons), and how are they influenced by strong pairing and di-neutron correlations in the low-density neutron skin?

How can the universal nuclear energy density functional E[ρ] and its associated pairing functional E_pair[\tildeρ] be systematically extended so as to (i) reproduce the extra binding (Wigner energy) observed in N=Z nuclei near the proton drip line—potentially through an isoscalar (T=0) pairing term—and (ii) span regimes of low-density clustering and high-density three-body interactions, for which no exact analytic limits are known, thereby enabling empirical data on drip-line nuclei (at densities ρ<<ρ₀ and ρ>>ρ₀) to constrain the functional form?

How can one formulate and implement a fully self-consistent quasiparticle random phase approximation—i.e. the linear response (small-amplitude) limit of the time-dependent Hartree-Fock-Bogoliubov equations—that simultaneously (i) treats pairing correlations on the same footing as mean fields, (ii) incorporates explicit continuum single-particle orbitals with proper outgoing-wave boundary conditions, (iii) allows for arbitrary nuclear shape deformations (e.g. axial symmetry), and (iv) includes all residual interactions derived from the underlying nuclear energy density functional? Furthermore, what numerical algorithms and computational strategies are required to handle the effectively infinite quasiparticle phase space arising from explicit continuum treatment and to enable large-scale parallel computation for applications to both finite drip-line nuclei and inhomogeneous nuclear matter?

In the context of gamma-ray-burst afterglows, at a specified post-burst time, (1) how many distinct relativistic outflow components (for example, the forward shock propagating into the ambient medium, the reverse shock driven into the ejecta, or other localized emission regions) contribute to the observed multiwavelength emission, and (2) what are the quantitative contributions of the synchrotron and inverse-Compton processes to the flux in different energy bands (for instance, below and above 10^2 MeV) during both the early (t≲1 day) and late (t≳1 day) phases of the afterglow evolution?

In the framework of the model by Komissarov et al. (2010), consider a long/soft GRB jet that is Poynting-flux dominated (magnetization σ_j≫1), emerges from its progenitor star with Lorentz factor Γ_j∼100 and half-opening angle θ_j∼a few degrees, and then undergoes rarefaction-driven acceleration upon losing external pressure support. How does this rarefaction acceleration modify the product Γ_jθ_j so as to produce panchromatic jet breaks on very early observer-frame time-scales (t_break≲1 h), and what is the current observational evidence from Swift afterglows for the existence of such very early jet breaks in real long/soft GRBs?

In the context of chiral ∆I=1 bands in triaxial nuclei with one high-j proton and one high-j neutron, how can one construct a fully microscopic theoretical framework that (1) treats the nonlinear quantum tunneling between the two aplanar mean-field solutions corresponding to left- and right-handed configurations, thereby reproducing the observed energy splitting of the partner bands, and (2) restores the broken rotational symmetry by yielding laboratory-frame eigenstates with good total angular momentum, without relying on semiclassical tilted-axis cranking or phenomenological particle-rotor approximations?

In odd–odd triaxially deformed nuclei that exhibit near-degenerate ΔI = 1 chiral doublet bands with the same parity, can one construct a two-dimensional collective Hamiltonian on the polar (θ) and azimuthal (ϕ) orientations of the rotational axis—replacing the rigid triaxial core in the particle-rotor model (which couples two high-j quasiparticles, e.g. πh₁₁/₂⊗νh₁₁/₂, to a fixed-deformation rotor)—where the collective potential and mass parameters are extracted microscopically from constrained tilted-axis cranking mean-field (relativistic density functional) calculations? Would such a formulation incorporate vibration–rotation coupling and enable a fully microscopic description of quantum tunneling between left- and right-handed chiral configurations?

In the normal linear regression prediction problem with unknown variance, where y | (beta, sigma^2) ~ N_n(X beta, sigma^2 I_n) and y~ | (beta, sigma^2) ~ N_m(X~ beta, sigma^2 I_m) are conditionally independent, beta in R^k, sigma^2 > 0, rank(X~) = k, and the special design assumption (AS1) holds: m >= k >= 3, n = mN for some positive integer N, and X = 1_N \otimes X~ = (X~', ..., X~')', is it true that, for alpha-divergence risk with -1 <= alpha < 1, the generalized Bayes predictive density p_hat_S,1 induced by the shrinkage prior pi_S,1(beta, sigma^2) proportional to (beta' X~' X~ beta)^(1-k/2) (sigma^2)^(-2) dominates the best invariant predictive density p_hat_I,1 induced by the right invariant prior pi_I,1(beta, sigma^2) proportional to (sigma^2)^(-1), in the sense that R_alpha((beta, sigma^2), p_hat_S,1) <= R_alpha((beta, sigma^2), p_hat_I,1) for all (beta, sigma^2), with strict inequality for some (beta, sigma^2)?

In the canonical predictive-density problem equivalent to the normal linear regression model with unknown variance, and under the paper's α-divergence predictive risk R_α with -1 <= α < 1, does the best invariant predictive density remain inadmissible in the low-dimensional cases k = 1 or k = 2; and, if so, can one identify Bayesian predictive densities that dominate it uniformly over the parameter space?

In the normal linear regression predictive-density problem with unknown error variance, after the paper’s canonical reduction so that the predictive dimension is d = k, let the benchmark be the best invariant predictive density, i.e. the generalized Bayes predictive density under the right invariant prior. Since Theorem 1.3 establishes domination of this benchmark under the R_1 risk (the alpha = 1 case) even when d = 1 or d = 2, is it still inadmissible under the R_alpha risk for -1 <= alpha < 1 when d = k is 1 or 2, and, if so, which Bayesian predictive density or class of Bayesian predictive densities dominates it?

Construct a genuinely new compact simply connected Kähler manifold X over the complex numbers with H^0(X, Ω_X^*) = C[σ] for an everywhere nondegenerate holomorphic 2-form σ — equivalently, a compact hyperkähler (irreducible holomorphic symplectic) manifold in Beauville’s sense — such that X is not deformation equivalent to any of the known examples reviewed in §1.2: the Hilbert schemes S^[r] of points on K3 surfaces, the generalized Kummer manifolds K_r(T) associated with 2-dimensional complex tori, or O’Grady’s exceptional examples in dimensions 6 and 10. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1002.4321.pdf))

Let X and X' be compact hyperkähler (irreducible holomorphic symplectic) manifolds of the same complex dimension. Suppose there exists a Hodge isometry lambda:(H^2(X,Z),q_X) -> (H^2(X',Z),q_X'), i.e. an integral isometry for the Beauville-Bogomolov forms that respects the Hodge decompositions on H^2(-,C). What can one conclude about the geometric relation between X and X'? In particular, can one force X and X' to be isomorphic by requiring that lambda preserve some additional structure?

Let X be a compact hyperkähler manifold of complex dimension 2r, and let q: H^2(X,Z) -> Z be its canonical primitive Beauville-Bogomolov quadratic form, characterized by the Fujiki relation integral_X alpha^(2r) = f_X q(alpha)^r for every alpha in H^2(X,Z), where f_X is the Fujiki constant/index. Must q always be even? More generally, which primitive integral quadratic forms q (necessarily of signature (3, b_2(X) - 3)) can occur on H^2(X,Z), and which values can occur for f_X?

For each integer r >= 1, are there only finitely many deformation types of compact hyperkähler manifolds X of complex dimension 2r, where hyperkähler is understood in Beauville's sense: X is a compact simply-connected Kähler manifold with an everywhere nondegenerate holomorphic 2-form σ and H^0(X, Ω_X^*) = C[σ]?

Let X be a compact hyperkähler fourfold over C (equivalently, an irreducible holomorphic symplectic manifold of complex dimension 4). Since Proposition 2 states that either b2(X)=23 or 3<=b2(X)<=8, can one exclude some further cases, in particular can b2(X)=3 occur? Moreover, if b2(X)=23, must X be deformation equivalent to the Hilbert square S^[2] of a K3 surface S?

Let X be a compact hyperkahler manifold over C (equivalently, an irreducible holomorphic symplectic manifold) of complex dimension 2r, and let q: H^2(X,Z) -> Z be its Beauville-Bogomolov quadratic form. Is the following higher-dimensional analogue of the K3 elliptic-fibration criterion true? (a) If L != O_X is a nef line bundle on X with q(c1(L)) = 0, must there exist a Lagrangian fibration f: X -> P^r such that L is isomorphic to f^*O_{P^r}(k) for some integer k >= 1? (b) More generally, is it true that there exists a hyperkahler manifold X' bimeromorphic to X together with a Lagrangian fibration X' -> P^r if and only if X admits a line bundle L != O_X with q(c1(L)) = 0? Here a Lagrangian fibration means a proper holomorphic map whose general fiber is a connected r-dimensional Lagrangian submanifold for the holomorphic symplectic form.

Let X be a compact hyperkähler manifold over C (equivalently, an irreducible holomorphic symplectic manifold). Does there exist a complex deformation X' of X and a proper surjective holomorphic map h:X'→B to a complex manifold B such that, if dim X'=2r, the general fibre F of h is connected, has dimension r, and the holomorphic symplectic form on X' restricts to 0 on F? Equivalently: does every hyperkähler deformation class contain a member admitting a holomorphic Lagrangian fibration?

Let X be a compact hyperkähler manifold over C of complex dimension 2r, and let T subset X be a Lagrangian submanifold for the holomorphic symplectic form on X, assumed to be a complex torus. Must T be a fibre of a Lagrangian fibration X -> P^r? In Beauville’s weaker version of the problem, is T at least a fibre of a bimeromorphic Lagrangian fibration?

Let (S,L) be a K3 surface over C with a polarization of genus g, where g = 1,2,3,\dots, and let S[r] = Hilb^r(S) be the Hilbert scheme of length-r subschemes of S. For r = 2, choose a polarization H on S[2] (in Beauville's notation, for general S and g ≥ 3 a natural choice is H = h - e). Describe the general polarized projective deformation of the hyperkähler fourfold (S[2],H); failing a full description, construct further locally complete families of polarized projective hyperkähler manifolds that specialize to S[2] in codimension 1. Ask the same question for S[r] with r ≥ 3.

Let X be a projective hyperkähler manifold over C, in Beauville’s sense (equivalently, an irreducible holomorphic symplectic manifold). For any finite collection of line-bundle classes D1,...,Dk in Pic(X), viewed as divisor classes in CH^1(X), and any class z in the integral Chow ring CH(X) that can be written as a polynomial with integer coefficients in D1,...,Dk and in the Chern classes c_i(T_X), does the vanishing of its cycle class cl(z) in integral singular cohomology H^*(X, Z) imply that z = 0 in CH(X)?

Let X be a complex Fano manifold and let tau be a holomorphic Poisson bivector on X. For each even integer s, define X_s := {x in X | rk(tau_x^#) = s}, where tau^#: Omega_X^1 -> T_X is the skew-symmetric morphism determined by tau, and set X_{<=s} := union over even k <= s of X_k. Is it true that X_{<=s} contains an irreducible component of dimension > s?

Let (X, tau) be a compact complex manifold endowed with a holomorphic Poisson structure tau in H^0(X, Lambda^2 T_X). For an even integer s, let X_s := {x in X | rk(tau^#(x)) = s}, where tau^#: Omega_X^1 -> T_X is the skew-symmetric bundle map induced by tau. If X_s is non-empty, must X_s contain a component of dimension strictly greater than s?

Let X be a projective complex manifold of odd dimension 2r+1 endowed with a holomorphic contact structure, i.e. a twisted 1-form theta in H^0(X, Omega^1_X ⊗ L) for some line bundle L such that theta ∧ (d theta)^r is nowhere vanishing. Must X be either the projective cotangent bundle PT^*M of a compact complex manifold M, or the unique closed adjoint-group orbit X_g contained in P(g) for some simple complex Lie algebra g? ([nzdr.ru](https://nzdr.ru/data/media/biblio/kolxoz/M/MD/MDdg/Ebeling%20W.%2C%20Hulek%20K.%2C%20Smoczyk%20K.%20%28eds.%29%20Complex%20and%20differential%20geometry%20%28Springer%2C%202011%29%28ISBN%203642202993%29%28O%29%28431s%29_MDdg_.pdf))

Let X be a complex projective manifold of odd dimension 2r+1 endowed with a holomorphic contact structure, i.e. a twisted 1-form θ∈H^0(X,Ω_X^1⊗L) for some line bundle L such that θ∧(dθ)^r is nowhere zero, and assume that X is Fano. Must X be homogeneous? ([nzdr.ru](https://nzdr.ru/data/media/biblio/kolxoz/M/MD/MDdg/Ebeling%20W.%2C%20Hulek%20K.%2C%20Smoczyk%20K.%20%28eds.%29%20Complex%20and%20differential%20geometry%20%28Springer%2C%202011%29%28ISBN%203642202993%29%28O%29%28431s%29_MDdg_.pdf))

Let M be a compact quaternion-Kähler Riemannian manifold, meaning that its holonomy group is Sp(1)Sp(r) for some r (so dim_R M = 4r). If M has positive scalar curvature, must M be a homogeneous Riemannian manifold, i.e. must its isometry group act transitively on M?

In the Euclidean plane, let P be a polygon with at least four sides circumscribed about a circle, and let D be the set consisting of all diagonals of P together with all lines determined by the tangency points of any two non-adjacent sides of P. Problem 2 shows that D always contains at least three concurrent lines. Find the geometric conditions on P under which there exists a point through which pass more than three distinct lines of D.

In the Euclidean plane, let A1A2...An be a polygon with n>=4 sides circumscribed to a circle, meaning that each side is tangent to the same circle. Let D be the set consisting of all diagonals of the polygon together with every line joining the tangency points of two non-adjacent sides. What is the maximum possible number of lines in D that can be concurrent at a single point, and for which polygons or under which geometric conditions is this maximum attained?

In the Euclidean plane, let P be an n-gon with n≥4 whose sides are all tangent to a fixed ellipse E contained in P. Consider the family of lines consisting of every diagonal of P and, for each pair of non-adjacent sides of P, the line joining their tangency points with E. How many lines in this family can be concurrent at a single point? ([fs.unm.edu](https://fs.unm.edu/MultispaceMultistructure.pdf))

Work in the Euclidean plane. Let A, B, C be a triangle, let A1 in BC, B1 in CA, C1 in AB, and suppose the cevians AA1, BB1, CC1 are concurrent at P. Problem 6 proves that (PA/PA1)(PB/PB1)(PC/PC1) = (AB·BC·CA)/(A1B·B1C·C1A). Unsolved Problem 6 asks for a polygonal extension of this result. Formulate a precise and natural analogue for a Euclidean n-gon A_1A_2...A_n by specifying a notion of concurrent polygonal cevians A_iA_i' meeting at a common point P, together with the exact incidence conditions on the points A_i', and then determine and prove the corresponding product identity so that the case n = 3 recovers the triangle formula above.

In the Euclidean plane, let A_1A_2...A_m be an m-gon (with indices taken modulo m), and let P be an interior point, called a pedal point. For each i, let A_i' be the foot of the perpendicular from P to the side A_iA_{i+1}; the polygon A_1'A_2'...A_m' is the pedal polygon of P. As the polygonal generalization of the orthic-triangle setting of Problem 7, determine what geometric properties this pedal polygon has. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1003.2153.pdf))

In Euclidean 3-space, as a polyhedral analogue of Problem 7's orthic/pedal construction, let Q = A1A2...An be a polyhedron and let P be a point in its interior. For each edge A_iA_j of Q, let A'_{ij} be the orthogonal projection of P onto that edge. Regard the collection of all such feet as defining the edge pedal polyhedron of P with respect to Q. What geometric properties of this edge pedal polyhedron can be established as the 3-dimensional extension of the planar orthic/pedal configuration studied in Problem 7?

Let A1A2...An be a polyhedron with faces F1,...,Fp, and let P be a point in its interior. For each face Fi, let Ai' be the orthogonal projection of P onto Fi. The polyhedron formed by the points A1',A2',...,Ap' is called the face pedal polyhedron of P (with p equal to the number of faces of the original polyhedron). What geometric properties does this face pedal polyhedron have?

In Euclidean 3-space, let S1 and S2 be two spheres with centers O1 and O2 whose surfaces intersect in a circle C. Fix a ratio k, and let O be the point on the line O1O2 such that O1O = k·OO2. For any point A on C, draw a line through A that meets S1 and S2 again at M1 and M2, respectively, and let M be the point on the segment M1M2 satisfying M1M = k·MM2. Investigate the geometric locus of M; in particular, determine whether the locus contains the sphere centered at O with radius OA, excluding the intersection circle C, and resolve the open case in which the line M1M2 and the line O1O2 lie in different planes.

Is there a microscopic, quantitative theory of temperature- and magnetic-field-dependent transport in strongly interacting two-dimensional electron and hole systems (Wigner–Seitz radius r_s ≫ 1) that applies seamlessly in both the ballistic regime (k_B T ≫ ħ/τ) and the diffusive regime (k_B T ≪ ħ/τ) and reproduces the nearly identical resistivity and giant positive parallel-field magnetoresistance observed in high-mobility Si MOSFETs, GaAs/AlGaAs, and SiGe heterostructures?

Let X = R^n with its Euclidean inner product, let f : X -> ]-infinity,+infinity] be a proper lower semicontinuous convex function of Legendre type, let U := int dom f, and let C be a nonempty subset of U that is closed in X. Define the left Bregman distance by D_f(x,y) = f(x) - f(y) - <∇f(y), x-y> for y in U (and D_f(x,y) = +infinity for y not in U), and define the left Bregman projection by P_left,C(y) := argmin_{x in C} D_f(x,y) for y in U. Assume that C is left D_f-Chebyshev, meaning that P_left,C(y) is a singleton for every y in U. Fact 3.1 states that if f is supercoercive, i.e. lim_{||x||->infinity} f(x)/||x|| = +infinity, then C must be convex. Is that supercoercivity assumption actually necessary, or does every nonempty closed left D_f-Chebyshev set C ⊂ U have to be convex for an arbitrary Legendre function f?

Let X = R^n, let f : X → ]−∞,+∞] be a Legendre function, set U = int dom f, and let C ⊆ U be nonempty and closed. Write x* = ∇f(x), C* = ∇f(C), and U* = int dom f*. For the Bregman distance D_f(x,y) = f(x) − f(y) − <∇f(y), x − y> when y ∈ U (and D_f(x,y) = +∞ otherwise), call C right D_f-Chebyshev if for every x ∈ U the right nearest-point set P→_{f,C}(x) = { y ∈ C | D_f(x,y) = inf_{z∈C} D_f(x,z) < +∞ } is a singleton. Fact 3.2 asserts that if dom f = X and C* ⊆ U*, then C* is convex. Are the hypotheses dom f = X and C* ⊆ U* genuinely essential for this implication? ([publish-01.obsidian.md](https://publish-01.obsidian.md/access/2ecc43874ee55b4bcda191e62beb467b/Files/c13.pdf))

Let X=R^J be a finite-dimensional Euclidean space, let f∈Γ_0(X) be a Legendre function with full domain dom f=X, set U:=int(dom f)=X, and define the Bregman distance by D_f(x,y)=f(x)-f(y)-<∇f(y),x-y> for x∈X and y∈U. For a nonempty closed convex set C⊂U, let the right Bregman nearest-point map be P^right_{f,C}(y):=argmin_{x∈C} D_f(x,y). Does there exist such a Legendre function f that is not quadratic and nevertheless has the property that, for every nonempty closed convex subset C of U and every y∈U, P^right_{f,C}(y) is a singleton; equivalently in the paper's terminology, every nonempty closed convex subset of U is right D-Chebyshev? ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1003.3127))

Let n be a positive integer, let U = R^n_{++}, and let f:U->R be the negative entropy f(x)=sum_{i=1}^n (x_i log x_i - x_i). For a nonempty subset C of U with cl(C) subset U, define the right Bregman nearest-point map by P^->_{C}(y) := argmin_{x in C} D_f(x,y), where D_f(x,y)=f(x)-f(y)-<grad f(y),x-y>=sum_{i=1}^n [x_i log(x_i/y_i)-x_i+y_i]. Characterize exactly those subsets C of the strictly positive orthant for which P^->_{C}(y) is a singleton for every y in U; equivalently, characterize the right D_f-Chebyshev subsets of R^n_{++} for the negative-entropy (Kullback-Leibler) Bregman distance.

Let X = R^n with its Euclidean structure, let f : X -> ]-infinity,+infinity] be a Legendre function, set U = int dom f, and let C be a nonempty closed subset of U. Define the left Bregman nearest-point map by P_left,f,C(y) = argmin_{x in C} D_f(x,y), where D_f(x,y) = f(x) - f(y) - <grad f(y), x-y> for y in U. Assume that f is twice continuously differentiable on U and that grad^2 f(y) is positive definite for every y in U. Without assuming that f is supercoercive, must P_left,f,C be single-valued outside a Lebesgue-null subset of U and on a residual subset of U? Equivalently, is the supercoercivity hypothesis in Fact 1.3.5 genuinely necessary for the almost-everywhere and generic single-valuedness of the left Bregman nearest-point map?

Let X = R^n, let f : X -> (-infinity,+infinity] be a Legendre function, let U = int dom f, and let C be a nonempty closed bounded subset of U. Define the Bregman distance by D_f(x,y) = f(x) - f(y) - <grad f(y), x-y> for y in U, and define the left Bregman farthest-point map by Q_left,C(y) = {x in C : D_f(x,y) = sup_{c in C} D_f(c,y) < +infinity}. Assume that f is twice continuously differentiable on U and that grad^2 f(y) is positive definite for every y in U. Is the supercoercivity assumption on f in Fact 4.4 actually necessary for the conclusion that Q_left,C is single-valued on U outside a meager Lebesgue-null subset of U? ([citeseerx.ist.psu.edu](https://citeseerx.ist.psu.edu/document?doi=bc7bfc1f3fe86b66e48fce0a9522c5dd560c873b&repid=rep1&type=pdf&utm_source=openai))

Let X = ℝ^n, let g: X → [-∞,+∞] be proper and lower semicontinuous, and let q(x) = (1/2)‖x‖^2. For 0 < λ < λ_g and μ > μ_g, Section 7 defines the Euclidean Moreau/Klee envelopes and maps by e_λg(x) = inf_w [g(w) + λ^{-1}q(x-w)], P_λg(x) = argmin_w [g(w) + λ^{-1}q(x-w)], φ_μg(y) = sup_x [μ^{-1}q(y-x) - g(x)], and Q_μg(y) = argmax_x [μ^{-1}q(y-x) - g(x)], and proves that single-valuedness of P_λg and Q_μg is equivalent to differentiability of e_λg and φ_μg and to essential strict convexity of g + λ^{-1}q and g - μ^{-1}q; it also proves that the μ-Chebyshev point p_μ, defined as the unique minimizer of φ_μg, is characterized by p_μ ∈ conv Q_μg(p_μ). What are the exact analogues of these results when the halved Euclidean distance q is replaced by a Bregman distance D_f generated by a Legendre function f on ℝ^n; that is, how should one formulate and characterize the Bregman versions of the λ-Chebyshev function, the μ-Klee function, the associated envelope/proximal/farthest constructions, and the Chebyshev point of g? ([citeseerx.ist.psu.edu](https://citeseerx.ist.psu.edu/document?doi=bc7bfc1f3fe86b66e48fce0a9522c5dd560c873b&repid=rep1&type=pdf&utm_source=openai))

In the Section 7 framework over the Euclidean space X = R^n, with q(x) = (1/2)\|x\|^2 and the associated Moreau/proximal operators e_μ f, P_μ f and farthest-envelope/farthest-point operators φ_μ g, Q_μ g, do the finite-dimensional Euclidean results on μ-Chebyshev and μ-Klee functions—especially the single-valuedness and characterization results of Facts 7.5 and 7.7, together with their corollaries—extend to infinite-dimensional Hilbert spaces, or even to general Banach spaces?

For every nonsingular projective variety X over \mathbb{C}, every genus g, and every curve class \beta, let \overline{M}_g(X,\beta) be the moduli space of genus-g stable maps to X of class \beta, let \overline{M}_g be the moduli space of stable genus-g curves, and let π: \overline{M}_g(X,\beta) \to \overline{M}_g be the morphism that forgets the map and stabilizes the domain. The space \overline{M}_g(X,\beta) carries its deformation-theoretic virtual fundamental class [\overline{M}_g(X,\beta)]^{vir}. Is the cohomology class π_*[\overline{M}_g(X,\beta)]^{vir} always contained in the tautological ring of \overline{M}_g? ([people.math.ethz.ch](https://people.math.ethz.ch/~rahul/agnes.pdf))

Fix a genus g, a nonsingular projective variety X over \mathbf{C}, and a curve class \beta on X. Let \pi:\overline{M}_g(X,\beta)\to\overline{M}_g be the forgetful morphism from the moduli space of stable maps to the moduli space of stable curves, and let [\overline{M}_g(X,\beta)]^{\mathrm{vir}} be its virtual fundamental class. When does the Chow pushforward \pi_*([\overline{M}_g(X,\beta)]^{\mathrm{vir}}) belong to the tautological ring R^*(\overline{M}_g)\subset A^*(\overline{M}_g)? In particular, is this always the case when X is defined over \overline{\mathbf{Q}}, as suggested in the paper?

Let X be an Enriques surface over C. Prove that the Gromov-Witten theory of X, determined by the stable-map moduli spaces M_g(X, beta) for all genera g and curve classes beta, satisfies the Virasoro constraints.

For every nonsingular projective 3-fold X over C, prove that the full Gromov–Witten theory of X—defined via the moduli spaces M_g(X, β) of stable maps, for all genera g and curve classes β—is equivalent to the Donaldson–Thomas theory of X defined via moduli of ideal sheaves of curves in X, thereby establishing the GW/DT correspondence for arbitrary 3-folds beyond the already known toric cases.

For a nonsingular projective variety X of dimension d>3, can one define Donaldson–Thomas invariants attached to moduli spaces of sheaves on X by constructing a mathematically sound replacement for the 3-fold virtual fundamental class formalism—where, for a sheaf E, infinitesimal deformations are governed by Ext^1(E,E), obstructions by Ext^2(E,E), and the usual 2-term obstruction theory fails because higher Ext^i(E,E) for i>2 need not vanish—thereby extending the dimension-3 theory defined via moduli of ideal sheaves of curves, or more recently via stable pairs? ([people.math.ethz.ch](https://people.math.ethz.ch/~rahul/agnes.pdf))

For the moduli space M_{2n}^{K3} of polarized K3 surfaces (S, L) with L^2 = 2n, what is the correct analogue of the tautological ring in its cycle theory? More specifically, is the natural candidate the subring of the Chow ring generated by the classes of the Noether-Lefschetz loci, i.e. the loci parameterizing polarized K3 surfaces with higher-rank Picard lattices?

For a fixed degree 2n, let M^{K3}_{2n} denote the moduli space of polarized K3 surfaces (S, L) with L^2 = 2n. The Noether-Lefschetz loci in M^{K3}_{2n} parametrize polarized K3 surfaces whose Picard lattices have higher rank. Do the classes of the Noether-Lefschetz divisors span the rational Picard group Pic(M^{K3}_{2n}) ⊗_Z Q?

Let S be a nonsingular projective K3 surface over C, and let β ∈ Pic(S) be a nonzero effective curve class. For the reduced Gromov-Witten Hodge integrals R_{g,β}(S) = ∫_[M̄_g(S,β)]^red (-1)^g λ_g, define for each primitive effective class α ∈ Pic(S) the Gromov-Witten potential F_α(λ,v) = Σ_{g≥0} Σ_{m>0} R_{g,mα}(S) λ^{2g-2} v^{mα}, and define BPS counts r_{g,mα} by the identity F_α(λ,v) = Σ_{g≥0} Σ_{m>0} r_{g,mα} λ^{2g-2} Σ_{d>0} (1/d)(sin(dλ/2)/(λ/2))^{2g-2} v^{dmα}. Prove the full Katz-Klemm-Vafa conjecture: the numbers r_{g,β} depend only on h = 1 + <β,β>/2 (equivalently, not on the divisibility of β), and the resulting invariants r_{g,h} satisfy the formal power series identity Σ_{g≥0} Σ_{h≥0} (-1)^g r_{g,h}(y^{1/2} - y^{-1/2})^{2g} q^h = Π_{n≥1} 1/((1-q^n)^20(1-yq^n)^2(1-y^{-1}q^n)^2).
Find effective mathematical methods for calculating the higher-genus Gromov-Witten invariants of compact Calabi-Yau 3-folds.

In two-dimensional simulations of large-scale polycrystalline solidification using single-phase orientation-field models I and II (with free energies given by Eqs. (20) and (21) and dynamics ∂ₜθ = -M_θ δF/δθ for the local crystallographic angle θ [Eq. (23)]), what is the magnitude of the discrepancy between the predicted evolution of grain orientations and grain boundaries and the physically correct, dislocation-mediated orientation changes required by coherent crystalline matter, and for which ranges of grain size, misorientation, and orientation-mobility parameters do these errors become significant in practical large-scale simulations?

For each n\in\mathbb{N}, let R_\infty^n:=\max\{d(X,\ell_\infty^n): X \text{ is an } n\text{-dimensional Banach space over the same scalar field as } \ell_\infty^n\}, where \ell_\infty^n is the classical n-dimensional space with the sup norm and d(X,Y):=\inf\{\|T\|\,\|T^{-1}\|: T\!:X\to Y \text{ is a linear isomorphism}\} is the Banach\u2013Mazur distance. Determine the asymptotic behavior of R_\infty^n as n\to\infty.

For 0 < δ ≤ 1, let K(δ) be the infimum of all K > 1 such that every normalized weakly null sequence (en) in a Banach space E has a subsequence (xn) satisfying: (xn) is a normalized basic sequence with basis constant at most K, and for every k ∈ N, every real scalars a0, ..., ak, and every subset G ⊆ {i ∈ {0, ..., k} : δ ≤ |ai| ≤ 1}, one has ‖Σ_{i∈G} ai xi‖ ≤ K ‖Σ_{i=0}^k ai xi‖. Does there exist a universal constant M > 1 such that K(δ) ≤ M for every 0 < δ ≤ 1?

Let X be a real or complex Banach space, and let (x_n) be a normalized basic sequence in X. Say that (x_n) is a Rosenthal basis if every normalized block sequence (v_n) of (x_n) (that is, each v_n is a norm-one finite linear combination of successive x_i's, with successive pairwise disjoint supports) has a subsequence equivalent, as a basic sequence, to (x_n). Is it true that every Rosenthal basis is equivalent to the standard unit vector basis of c_0 or of ℓ_p for some 1 ≤ p < ∞?

Let X be a reflexive Banach space over R or C. For X, let SP_w(X) denote the class of all basic sequences (e_n) that arise as spreading models of normalized weakly null sequences in X in the Brunel-Sucheston sense; namely, there exists a normalized basic sequence (x_n) in X and a sequence ε_n > 0 with ε_n ↓ 0 such that for every n in N, every scalars a_0,...,a_n in [-1,1], and every n <= k_0 < ... < k_n in N, (1+ε_n)^(-1)||Σ_{i=0}^n a_i e_i|| <= ||Σ_{i=0}^n a_i x_{k_i}|| <= (1+ε_n)||Σ_{i=0}^n a_i e_i||. Suppose that SP_w(X) consists of a single equivalence class of basic sequences, i.e. |SP_w(X)/~| = 1, where ~ denotes equivalence of basic sequences. Must that unique spreading model be equivalent to the standard unit vector basis of c_0 or of ℓ_p for some 1 <= p < infinity?

Let X be a reflexive Banach space. For a normalized weakly null sequence (x_n) in X and a normalized basic sequence (e_n), say that (x_n) generates (e_n) as a spreading model if there exist positive numbers delta_m -> 0 such that for every m in N, every scalars a_1,...,a_m in [-1,1], and every m <= k_1 < ... < k_m, one has | ||sum_{i=1}^m a_i x_{k_i}|| - ||sum_{i=1}^m a_i e_i|| | < delta_m. Let SP_w(X) be the class of all spreading models generated by normalized weakly null sequences in X, modulo equivalence ~ of basic sequences. If SP_w(X)/~ is countable, must there exist a normalized weakly null sequence in X whose spreading model is equivalent to the standard unit vector basis of c_0 or of ℓ_p for some 1 <= p < infinity?

Let X be a real or complex Banach space with a normalized Schauder basis (x_n). Assume that for every normalized block sequence (y_n) of (x_n) — that is, each y_n is a norm-1 finitely supported linear combination of successive basis vectors x_i, with strictly increasing supports — the closed linear span [y_n] is isomorphic to X. Must X be isomorphic to c_0 or to ℓ_p for some 1 ≤ p < ∞?

Does every separable Banach space X that is not isomorphic to a Hilbert space contain a sequence (X_n) indexed by the natural numbers of closed infinite-dimensional subspaces of X such that, whenever m ≠ n, the Banach spaces X_m and X_n are not isomorphic?

Let X be a separable Banach space which, for some ε>0, fails to have type 2−ε or fails to have co-type 2+ε, in the usual Banach-space sense. Must X contain a family of 2^ℵ0 closed linear subspaces that are pairwise non-isomorphic as Banach spaces? ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1006.2668))

Let X be a complemented subspace of the classical Banach space C([0,1]) of scalar-valued continuous functions on [0,1] with the supremum norm. Must X be isomorphic, as a Banach space, to C(K) for some closed subset K of [0,1]? ([citeseerx.ist.psu.edu](https://citeseerx.ist.psu.edu/document?doi=646d208f31321fe467b685afc0b97665b5f04a31&repid=rep1&type=pdf&utm_source=openai))

Let C[0,1] denote the Banach space of scalar-valued continuous functions on [0,1] with the supremum norm, and let T:C[0,1]→C[0,1] be a bounded linear operator. Let X be a separable Banach space containing no subspace isomorphic to c0. Suppose there exists a subspace Y⊂C[0,1] such that Y is isomorphic to X and T|Y:Y→C[0,1] is an isomorphic embedding; equivalently, T fixes a copy of X. Must there then exist a subspace Z⊂C[0,1] isomorphic to C[0,1] such that T|Z is an isomorphic embedding?

Let X be an infinite-dimensional Banach space. For lambda > 1, say that X is lambda-distortable if there exists an equivalent norm |.| on X such that for every infinite-dimensional subspace Y of X,
sup{ |y|/|z| : y,z in Y and ||y|| = ||z|| = 1 } >= lambda.
Say that X is boundedly distortable if it is lambda-distortable for some lambda > 1 but not for every lambda > 1. Does there exist a boundedly distortable Banach space?

Let X be either Tsirelson's space T or its dual T*. Is X boundedly distortable; that is, does there exist some lambda > 1 and an equivalent norm |.| on X such that for every infinite-dimensional subspace Y of X one has sup{|y|/|z| : y, z in Y and ||y|| = ||z|| = 1} >= lambda, while there exists some mu > 1 for which X is not mu-distortable?

Find a purely combinatorial proof, avoiding ultrafilters and the existing topological-dynamical arguments on βN, of Gowers’s theorem that for every uniformly continuous function f:S_{c_0}→R, where S_{c_0}={x∈c_0:||x||_∞=1}, and for every ε>0, there exists an infinite-dimensional linear subspace Y⊆c_0 such that sup{|f(y)-f(z)|:y,z∈S_Y}≤ε, where S_Y={y∈Y:||y||_∞=1}. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1006.2668))

Converse Aharoni problem. Let X be a separable Banach space such that for every separable Banach space Y there exists a subset A ⊆ X and a bi-Lipschitz bijection from Y onto A. Must X contain a closed linear subspace linearly isomorphic to c0?
For every infinite-dimensional Banach space X, does there exist a closed proper subspace Y of X such that the quotient Banach space X/Y is infinite-dimensional and has a Schauder basis?
For every infinite-dimensional Banach space X, does there exist a closed linear subspace Y of X such that the quotient Banach space X/Y is separable and infinite-dimensional?

Let X be an infinite-dimensional Banach space, and let Y range over the closed subspaces of X. What is the longest ordinal length of a transfinite Schauder basis that can occur in a Banach-space quotient X/Y? In particular, must every non-separable Banach space X admit an uncountable biorthogonal system, that is, an uncountable family {(x_i,f_i)}_{i∈I}⊂X×X* such that f_i(x_j)=δ_{ij} for all i,j∈I?

Assume the P-ideal dichotomy (PID): for every P-ideal I of countable subsets of a set S (i.e. for every sequence (A_n) in I there is A in I such that A_n \ A is finite for all n), either there is an uncountable T ⊆ S such that every countable subset of T belongs to I, or S can be partitioned into countably many pieces having no infinite subset in I. Under PID, are the following equivalent? (1) Every non-separable Banach space X has an uncountable biorthogonal system, i.e. there exist an uncountable set Γ and a family {(xγ, xγ*)}_{γ∈Γ} ⊆ X × X* such that xγ*(xδ) = δγδ for all γ, δ ∈ Γ. (2) The bounding number 𝔟 equals ℵ2, where 𝔟 is the least cardinality of an unbounded family in (ω^ω, ≤*), with f ≤* g meaning f(n) ≤ g(n) for all sufficiently large n.

Let X be a Banach space. Call a nonempty convex set C subset X a support set if for every x in C there exists x^* in X^* such that x^*(x) = inf_{y in C} x^*(y) < sup_{y in C} x^*(y). Which Banach spaces X admit a support set? In particular, must every non-separable Banach space admit a support set?

Let X be a Banach space with density character dens(X) > ℵ_1. Must there exist a nonempty convex set C ⊆ X such that every point x ∈ C is a support point of C; that is, for each x ∈ C there exists x* ∈ X* with x*(x) = sup{ x*(y) : y ∈ C }?

Let X be a Banach space of density character strictly greater than the cardinality of the continuum 𝔠. Must X contain a countably infinite unconditional basic sequence? More generally, can the answer change under additional structural hypotheses on X, for example if X is assumed to be reflexive?

For a prime p>3, can one construct a field F and a central division F-algebra A of degree p such that A is not cyclic, i.e. A contains no maximal subfield K/F that is a cyclic Galois extension of F? ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1006.3304.pdf))

Let F be a field, and let D be a finite-dimensional central division algebra over F. If the period per(D), i.e. the order of its Brauer class [D] in Br(F), is a prime number p, must D be a crossed product? Equivalently, must D contain a maximal subfield K such that K/F is Galois?

Let p be a prime, let F be a field of characteristic p, and let A be a central simple F-algebra of degree p^2 whose period (i.e. the order of [A] in Br(F)) is a power of p. Must A be a crossed product? Equivalently, must A contain a maximal commutative étale F-subalgebra of degree p^2 that is Galois over F?

Let F be a field with cohomological dimension at most 2. Is every finite-dimensional central simple F-algebra A over F a crossed product; that is, does A contain a maximal commutative étale F-subalgebra L/F of degree deg(A) that is Galois over F?

Let A be a central F-division algebra of degree n (so dim_F A = n^2). Among all finite groups G for which there exists a separable maximal subfield K \subset A with [K:F] = n such that the Galois closure L of K/F inside a separable closure F_sep of F satisfies Gal(L/F) \cong G, determine the group(s) of minimal order. In particular, must every central F-division algebra A of degree n contain a separable maximal subfield K whose Galois closure over F has Galois group A_n?

Let F be a field and D a central division F-algebra. Must there exist a finite abelian Galois extension L/F such that D ⊗_F L is split? Equivalently, is every F-division algebra split by an abelian group? For specified fields F, can one give upper bounds on the degree [L:F] (equivalently, on the order of an abelian splitting group) of such an abelian Galois splitting field?

Let F be a field, and write G ⇒_F G' to mean that every G-crossed product whose center contains F is also a G'-crossed product. For a prime p and an integer m prime to p, with C_p normal in the semidirect product C_p ⋊ C_m, determine whether C_p ⋊ C_m ⇒_F C_p × C_m. In the particularly interesting case of a quasi-symbol—namely, an F-division algebra A of degree p split by a Galois extension K/F with Gal(K/F) ≅ C_p ⋊ C_m and K^{C_p} = F(ζ_p) for a primitive p-th root of unity ζ_p (so char(F) ≠ p)—must A be cyclic?

For every field F and every positive integer n, is the n-torsion subgroup {}_nBr(F) := {[A] in Br(F) : n[A] = 0} generated, as a subgroup of Br(F), by Brauer classes of cyclic central simple F-algebras of degree (dividing) n? ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1006.3304v2.pdf))

Let F be a field with char(F) != 7 and such that F does not contain a primitive 7th root of unity. Is the 7-torsion subgroup {}_7Br(F) = { [A] in Br(F) : 7[A] = 0 } generated, as a subgroup of Br(F), by the Brauer classes of cyclic central simple F-algebras of degree 7?

For a field F and a positive integer n, is the n-torsion subgroup {}_n Br(F) := { alpha in Br(F) : n alpha = 0 } generated, as a subgroup of Br(F), by Brauer classes [A] of central simple F-algebras A of degree n?

Let F be a field, let p be a prime, and let integers r <= s be given. Assume that the p^r-torsion subgroup _{p^r}Br(F) of the Brauer group is generated by classes of cyclic algebras. Define l_F(p^r,p^s) to be the least integer l such that every central simple F-algebra of degree p^s and period dividing p^r is similar (equivalently, Brauer-equivalent) to a tensor product of l cyclic F-algebras of degree p^r; if no such uniform bound exists, set l_F(p^r,p^s)=infinity. Compute l_F(p^r,p^s).

Let F be a field and let p≥3 be a prime. Assume that pBr(F) and p^2Br(F) are generated by cyclic algebras, and define ℓ_F(m,n) (for m|n with the same prime factors) to be the least integer t such that every central simple F-algebra of degree n and period dividing m is similar to a tensor product of t cyclic F-algebras of degree m, with ℓ_F(m,n)=∞ if no such t exists. Find an upper bound, without imposing any additional roots-of-unity hypothesis, for ℓ_F(p,p^2) and for ℓ_F(p^2,p^2).

Let K be a field. For a central simple K-algebra A, write ind(A) for the degree of the division algebra Brauer-equivalent to A and per(A) for the order of its Brauer class [A] in Br(K). Define the Brauer dimension Brd(K) to be the least integer d >= 0 such that ind(A) divides per(A)^d for every central simple K-algebra A over K, and set Brd(K)=∞ if no such d exists. If F/F_0 is a finitely generated field extension and Brd(F_0)<∞, must Brd(F)<∞?

Can one define an integer-valued notion dim on some class of fields, closed under adjoining one transcendental indeterminate t, such that for every field F in that class one has Br.dim(F) ≤ dim(F)-1 and dim(F(t)) = dim(F)+1, where Br.dim(F) denotes the smallest integer d for which ind(A) divides per(A)^d for every central simple F-algebra A, and Br.dim(F)=∞ if no such d exists? ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1006.3304))

Let F be a field and n>=2. Let UD(F,n) be Amitsur’s generic division algebra of degree n over F, obtained from the F-algebra generated by two generic n-by-n matrices, and let Z(F,n)=Z(UD(F,n)) be its center (equivalently, the field of fractions of the center of the ring of two generic n-by-n matrices). If m divides n, let Z_m(F,n) denote the center of the generic division algebra of degree n and period m constructed from UD(F,n) as in Section 5; and for a subgroup H<=S_n, let Z_H(F,n) denote the center of the corresponding generic central simple algebra (in particular, of the generic H-crossed product when |H|=n and H is transitive). For each of the extensions Z(F,n)/F, Z_m(F,n)/F, and Z_H(F,n)/F, is the field extension rational, stably rational, or retract rational?

Let F be a field, let H be the regular transitive subgroup of S_9 isomorphic to C_3 x C_3, and let Z_H(F,9) denote the center of the generic H-crossed product F-algebra of degree 9 defined in Section 5. Determine whether the extension Z_H(F,9)/F is rational (purely transcendental), stably rational (becomes purely transcendental after adjoining finitely many algebraically independent variables), or at least retract rational over F.

Let F be a field, let n be a positive integer, and let p be a prime. For the functor K/F ↦ H^1(K,PGL_{n,F})—equivalently, the functor assigning to each field extension K/F the set of isomorphism classes of central simple K-algebras of degree n—determine the essential dimension ed_F(PGL_n) and the essential p-dimension ed_{F,p}(PGL_n). In particular, determine ed_F(PGL_4) for fields F of characteristic 2, and determine ed_F(PGL_5). ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1006.3304))

Fix a base field F, an integer n >= 2, and a finite group G of order n. Let Fields_F be the category of field extensions K/F with F-embeddings, let CPAlg_n(K) be the set of isomorphism classes of crossed product central simple K-algebras of degree n, and let Alg_G(K) be the set of isomorphism classes of G-crossed product central simple K-algebras of degree n. With ed taken over F, and with ed(G) denoting the essential dimension of the finite algebraic group G, determine what structural conclusions about degree-n central simple algebras can be extracted from essential-dimension bounds by: (i) finding bounds for ed(CPAlg_n) and ed(Alg_G), (ii) computing ed(Alg_G) - ed(G), and (iii) deciding whether the equality ed(CPAlg_n) = ed(PGL_n) implies that every central simple K-algebra of degree n, for every field extension K/F, is a crossed product. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1006.3304.pdf))

Let F be a field, and let ed_F(G) denote the essential dimension over F of the algebraic group G, i.e. of the functor H^1(-,G). Compute ed_F(GL_8/μ_2) when char(F)=2, compute ed_F(GL_16/μ_2) when char(F)≠2, and, for every odd prime p, compute ed_F(GL_{p^2}/μ_p) over arbitrary fields F.

Let F be a field, let A be a central simple F-algebra, and let σ be an orthogonal or symplectic involution on A that is anisotropic in the sense that σ(x)x=0 implies x=0 for every x∈A. For every finite field extension K/F of odd degree, must the scalar-extended involution σ_K:=σ⊗id_K on A_K:=A⊗_F K remain anisotropic? (As noted in the paper, in the orthogonal case when char(F)=2, the analogous formulation should use a quadratic pair.)

Let F be a field, let A be a central simple F-algebra, and let σ be an anisotropic orthogonal involution on A. If F_A:=F(SB(A)) is the function field of the Severi–Brauer variety of A, is the scalar-extended involution σ_{F_A} on A_{F_A}=A\otimes_F F_A necessarily anisotropic; equivalently, does σ_{F_A}(x)x=0 imply x=0 for every x\in A_{F_A}?

Let F be a field, and let G/F be an absolutely almost simple linear algebraic group that is anisotropic over F. Let S(G) denote the set of homological torsion primes of G in the sense of Serre, equivalently the set listed by Dynkin type in Table 7 of the paper: S(A_n) is the set of prime divisors of n+1; S(B_n) = S(C_n) = S(D_n) = S(G_2) = {2}; S(F_4) = S(E_6) = S(E_7) = {2,3}; and S(E_8) = {2,3,5}. Is it true that for every finite field extension K/F with [K:F] prime to every prime in S(G), the base change G_K remains anisotropic over K?

For every smooth, projective, geometrically connected surface X over a finite field F_q with char(F_q) = p ≠ 2, if Br(X)_nd := Br(X)/Div Br(X), is the canonical Artin-Tate pairing ⟨·,·⟩_AT : Br(X)_nd[2^∞] × Br(X)_nd[2^∞] → Q/Z alternating?

Let F be a field, and let A and B be finite-dimensional central simple F-algebras that are division algebras. Find a structural criterion that characterizes exactly when the tensor product A ⊗_F B contains a nonzero zero divisor.

Let F be a field containing a fixed primitive n-th root of unity rho_n, and for a,b in F^x let (a,b)_{n,F} denote the degree-n symbol F-algebra generated by x and y subject to x^n=a, y^n=b, and yx=rho_n xy. If A=(a,b)_{n,F} and B=(c,d)_{n,F} are degree-n symbol algebras with ind(A tensor_F B)=n, must there exist degree-n symbol algebras A' and B' such that A' is Brauer-equivalent to A, B' is Brauer-equivalent to B, A' and B' share a common maximal subfield over F, and A' tensor_F B' is isomorphic to A tensor_F B?

Let F be a field, and let A and B be central F-division algebras. If the index of their tensor product satisfies ind(A\otimes_F B)<(ind A)(ind B), characterize the field extensions K/F that are common splitting fields of A and B; that is, for which both A\otimes_F K and B\otimes_F K are split.

Let F be a field, and let A and B be central simple F-algebras of the same degree. Assume that their Brauer classes [A] and [B] generate the same cyclic subgroup of Br(F). If F(A) and F(B) denote the generic splitting fields of A and B (equivalently, the function fields of the Severi-Brauer varieties SB(A) and SB(B)), must F(A) and F(B) be F-isomorphic?

Let F be a field, let D and D' be F-division algebras, and let C be a specified class of field extensions E/F (for example, all finite extensions, or all extensions of transcendence degree at most 1 over F). Suppose that for every E/F in C, E splits D if and only if E splits D'. Must the Brauer classes [D] and [D'] generate the same cyclic subgroup of Br(F)? ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1006.3304))

Let F be a field, and let D1 and D2 be central F-division algebras of degree 3. Assume that for every field extension E/F with transcendence degree trdeg_F(E)=1, one has D1 ⊗_F E ≅ M_3(E) if and only if D2 ⊗_F E ≅ M_3(E); equivalently, D1 and D2 have the same splitting fields of transcendence degree 1 over F. Must the Brauer classes [D1] and [D2] generate the same cyclic subgroup of Br(F)?

Let F be a field finitely generated over either a prime field or an algebraically closed field, and let D and D' be quaternion division F-algebras. Suppose that D and D' have the same finite splitting fields, in the sense that for every finite field extension E/F, the algebra D⊗F E is split if and only if D'⊗F E is split. Must D and D' be isomorphic as F-algebras? Even more strongly, does the same conclusion already follow under the stronger hypothesis that D and D' have the same maximal subfields (i.e. every maximal subfield of one embeds over F into the other, and vice versa)?

Let F be a field finitely generated over its prime subfield or over an algebraically closed field. If D is a finite-dimensional central division F-algebra, is the set of Brauer classes [D'] in Br(F), where D' ranges over finite-dimensional central division F-algebras such that for every finite field extension L/F one has D ⊗F L split if and only if D' ⊗F L split, finite? ([math.ualberta.ca](https://www.math.ualberta.ca/~chernous/ChernousovPublications/survey080114.pdf))

Fix a field F. Determine all finite groups G for which there exists a finite-dimensional central division F-algebra A that is a G-crossed product over F; concretely, in the division-algebra setting, this asks for A to contain a maximal subfield L such that L/F is Galois with Gal(L/F) ≅ G. In other words, classify the F-admissible finite groups. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1006.3304.pdf))

Let G be a finite group such that every Sylow subgroup of G is metacyclic (equivalently, for each prime p dividing |G|, a Sylow p-subgroup P of G has a cyclic normal subgroup N with cyclic quotient P/N). Must G be Q-admissible; that is, does there exist a central division algebra D over Q having a maximal subfield L such that L/Q is Galois and Gal(L/Q) ≅ G?

Let F be a field and let A be a central simple F-algebra. For each field extension L/F, write SK1(A tensor_F L) := SL1(A tensor_F L)/[(A tensor_F L)^x,(A tensor_F L)^x], where SL1 denotes the reduced-norm-1 subgroup. If SK1(A tensor_F L)=0 for every field extension L/F, must ind(A), the degree of the division algebra Brauer-equivalent to A, be square-free?
For which positive integers n does there exist a field F such that the classical Brauer group Br(F) has exactly n elements, i.e. |Br(F)| = n?

Let F be a field, let Br(F) denote its classical Brauer group, and for a prime p let (Br(F))_p be the p-primary component of Br(F), i.e. the subgroup consisting of Brauer classes of p-power order. Is the Brumer-Rosen Conjecture true: for every field F and every prime p, must one of the following hold: (a) (Br(F))_p = 0; (b) (Br(F))_p contains a nonzero divisible subgroup; or (c) p = 2 and (Br(F))_2 is an elementary abelian 2-group? ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1006.3304.pdf))
Does there exist a field F such that its Brauer group Br(F), i.e. the Brauer group of Brauer classes of central simple F-algebras over F, is isomorphic as an abelian group to Z/3Z?

Let Φ^t:Ω→Ω be an open dynamical system, with t∈ℤ for maps or t∈ℝ for flows, and let H⊂Ω be a piecewise smooth hole (of the same dimension as Ω for maps and codimension 1 for flows). Define the survivor set Ω_t={x∈Ω: Φ^s(x)∉H for all s∈(0,t]} and, for an initial probability measure μ_0, the survival probability P(t)=μ_0(Ω_t). Assume the escape rate γ=−lim_{t→∞}(1/t)ln P(t) exists, the renormalized survivor measures μ_t(A)=μ_0(Φ^{-t}(A)∩Ω_t)/μ_0(Ω_t) converge to a conditionally invariant measure μ_∞, and the natural invariant measure on the repeller is ν(A)=lim_{t→∞}e^{γt}μ_∞(A∩Ω_t). Under what dynamical hypotheses—especially beyond the strongly or uniformly hyperbolic cases already understood, and in particular for maps without uniform hyperbolicity and for flows—does the escape-rate formula γ=∑_{i:λ_i>0}λ_i−h_KS(ν) hold, where the Lyapunov exponents λ_i and the Kolmogorov-Sinai entropy h_KS are computed with respect to ν? ([people.maths.bris.ac.uk](https://people.maths.bris.ac.uk/~macpd/open/open.pdf))

Let H be a hole in an open billiard, let h=|H|/|M| denote its relative size, let Omega_t={x in Omega : Phi^s(x) notin H for all s in (0,t]}, and let P(t)=mu_0(Omega_t) be the survival probability for the natural equilibrium initial measure mu_0. For a family of open billiards with variable hole size h, for which billiards, and in which asymptotic regimes of simultaneously small hole and long time, does P(t) asymptotically reduce to a one-parameter scaling form F(ht), i.e. depend only on the product ht?

In the usual closed planar billiard system of a point particle moving in a compact polygonal domain D ⊂ R^2 with mirror-like reflections at the sides, does every triangular billiard—and, more generally, every polygonal billiard—admit at least one periodic trajectory, meaning a trajectory that after finitely many reflections returns to its initial position and direction, with no direction prescribed in advance?

In an open polygonal billiard with hole H, let Omega_t = {x in Omega : Phi^s(x) notin H for every s in (0,t]} and let P(t) = mu_0(Omega_t) denote the survival probability for the usual initial measure mu_0 (typically the equilibrium measure on the flow or collision space). Is the asymptotic behaviour of P(t) as t -> infinity entirely determined by neighbourhoods of periodic trajectories that never escape through H?

For stadium-like billiards whose intermittency is generated by bouncing-ball or, more generally, marginally unstable periodic orbits, can one give a comprehensive characterization of the resulting dynamical properties—including escape/survival behavior—in terms of the reinjection dynamics of trajectories that leave the bouncing-ball (or analogous marginally unstable) region and are reinjected into it? ([people.maths.bris.ac.uk](https://people.maths.bris.ac.uk/~macpd/open/open.pdf))

Let H be a hole in the phase space Omega of an open billiard, let Omega_t = {x in Omega : Phi^s(x) not in H for all s in (0,t]}, and let P(t) = mu_0(Omega_t) be the survival probability for the usual equilibrium initial measure mu_0 of the billiard flow (or of the boundary collision map). For a generic billiard whose closed dynamics is expected to have mixed phase space in the Kolmogorov-Arnold-Moser sense, is there a universal long-time decay rate for P(t) in the corresponding open billiard? More specifically, does the stickiness caused by elliptic islands lead, in generic cases, to a universal algebraic asymptotic P(t) ~ C t^{-alpha}, analogous to the conjectured area-preserving-map exponent alpha approximately 2.57?

In the usual continuous-time open-billiard setting for the billiard flow, with Ωt={x∈Ω: Φs(x)∉H for all s∈(0,t]} and survival probability P(t)=μ0(Ωt), consider a mushroom billiard, or a similar billiard whose phase space is mixed but whose regular and chaotic components are separated by a smooth boundary, and assume the hole H lies in the chaotic region. Characterize the escape properties associated with that regular-chaotic boundary; in particular, determine how the long-time survival/escape behaviour is affected, and possibly slowed, both by stickiness from embedded marginally unstable periodic orbits in the chaotic component and by the boundary/interface itself.

In the statistical-mechanics setting of low-dimensional billiards that model hard-ball transport—especially Lorentz gases (infinite collections of convex scatterers) and Ehrenfest gases (infinite collections of polygonal scatterers), including the more physically realistic case of randomly placed non-overlapping obstacles—what is the weakest microscopic dynamical behavior of the billiard flow, or of its collision map, that is required to produce a "chaotic" macroscopic limit, where the microscopic candidates include measure-theoretic properties such as recurrence and ergodicity and the macroscopic benchmarks include a "normal" diffusion coefficient or a limiting Wiener process? ([people.maths.bris.ac.uk](https://people.maths.bris.ac.uk/~macpd/open/open.pdf))

For an open quantum billiard, modeled by the Dirichlet Helmholtz problem (∇^2 + k^2)ψ = 0 on a billiard domain D ⊂ R^d that allows escape to infinity, let {k_n} be the scattering resonances (so Im(k_n) < 0 in the open case). Is the following fractal Weyl conjecture true: for some fixed positive constant C, the resonance counting function N_C(k) = #{n : Re(k_n) < k, Im(k_n) > -C} is of order k^(d_H+1) as k → ∞, where d_H is the partial Hausdorff dimension of the classical non-escaping set (the trapped set/repeller)?

Fix an open billiard flow Phi^t on phase space Omega with a piecewise smooth hole H subset Omega (or, in the immediately preceding generalised setting, one of the billiard models with soft walls, external fields, dissipative/stochastic scattering, or time-dependent boundaries), and let Omega_t = {x in Omega : Phi^s(x) is not in H for all s in (0,t]} and P(t) = mu_0(Omega_t) for a prescribed initial probability measure mu_0 at time t = 0. For that fixed billiard problem, can the survival probability P(t) be computed exactly, or at least asymptotically expanded as t tends to infinity beyond its leading term, particularly in the integrable and dispersing cases singled out by the paper? ([people.maths.bris.ac.uk](https://people.maths.bris.ac.uk/~macpd/open/open.pdf))

In the open-system setting of the paper, with phase space Ω, hole H⊂Ω, dynamics Φ^t, surviving set Ω_t={x∈Ω: Φ^s(x)∉H for all s∈(0,t]}, and survival probability P(t)=μ0(Ω_t) for an initial measure μ0, give a general description of how recurrences of the underlying dynamics—periodic orbits and more general recurrent behaviour—affect the escape problem, both when those recurrences occur near the hole H and when they occur elsewhere in phase space, in systems with little or no hyperbolicity.

For an open billiard with hole(s) H and escape data given by the survival probabilities P(t)=mu_0(Omega_t) of trajectories that avoid H up to time t, where Omega_t={x in Omega : Phi^s(x) not in H for all s in (0,t]}, and, when it exists, the corresponding long-time escape rate gamma, what aspects of the underlying billiard dynamics can be reconstructed from those escape measurements alone? In particular, can such escape data recover, even partially, the geometry of the billiard domain D itself—that is, can one 'peep' the shape of a drum?

Fix α ∈ (0,1). Consider the discrete α-copolymer model defined from a persistent renewal process τ with IID gaps satisfying K(n)=P(τ_1=n) ~ C_K / n^(1+α), an IID Bernoulli(1/2) sign sequence ξ independent of τ, and an IID disorder sequence ω with M(t)=E[e^{tω_1}]<∞ for all t, E[ω_1]=0, and E[ω_1^2]=1. Let F(λ,h)=lim_{N→∞}(1/N)E[log Z_{N,ω,λ,h}] be the quenched free energy and h_c(λ)=sup{h : F(λ,h)>0} the critical curve. Determine the universal constant m_α characterized by lim_{λ↓0} h_c(λ)/λ = m_α, equivalently the exact weak-coupling slope of the critical curve for this class of models, beyond the currently known bounds max{1/2, g(α)/sqrt(1+α), 1/(1+α)} ≤ m_α < 1. ([fcaraven.github.io](https://fcaraven.github.io/download/papers/cgt.pdf))

Consider the discrete α-copolymer model of Sections 1.2–1.4: τ is a persistent renewal on N∪{0} with K(n)=P(τ_1=n) ~ C_K / n^(1+α), ξ_j are i.i.d. Bernoulli(1/2) signs independent of τ, Δ_n = Σ_{j≥1} ξ_j 1_{(τ_{j-1},τ_j]}(n), and ω = {ω_n} is an i.i.d. disorder sequence independent of (τ,ξ) with E[ω_1]=0, Var(ω_1)=1, and M(t)=E[e^{tω_1}]<∞ for every t∈R. For λ≥0 and h≥0, let Z_{N,ω,λ,h}=E[exp(-2λ Σ_{n=1}^N (ω_n+h)Δ_n)], let F(λ,h)=lim_{N→∞} N^{-1} E[log Z_{N,ω,λ,h}], and define the critical curve by h_c(λ)=sup{h : F(λ,h)>0}. In the weak-coupling regime, Theorem 2 gives the universal limit m_α:=lim_{λ↓0} h_c(λ)/λ for every α∈(0,1). Show that for α=1/2 one has the strict inequality m_{1/2}>2/3.

For the discrete α-copolymer model of Section 1.2—namely, a copolymer built from a persistent renewal law K(n) ~ C_K n^{-(1+α)} with α>0 and IID disorder ω satisfying E[ω_1]=0, E[ω_1^2]=1, and E[e^{tω_1}]<∞ for all t—let h_c(λ) denote the quenched critical curve. In the weak-coupling regime α∈(0,1), Theorem 2 shows that the universal slope m_α := lim_{λ↓0} h_c(λ)/λ exists, while Theorem 1 gives the lower bound m_α ≥ 1/(1+α). Does there exist any α∈(0,1) for which this lower bound is actually sharp, i.e. m_α = 1/(1+α), for the original discrete copolymer model? ([fcaraven.github.io](https://fcaraven.github.io/download/papers/cgt.pdf))

For the general α-copolymer model of Section 1.2—based on a persistent renewal law K(n) ~ C_K n^{-(1+α)} with α > 0, IID disorder ω with E[ω1] = 0, E[ω1^2] = 1 and finite exponential moments, and under the same additional disorder-law hypotheses under which the smoothing estimate (20) is proved (for instance Gaussian or bounded charges)—let F(λ,h) = lim_{N→∞} (1/N) E[log Z_{N,ω,λ,h}] be the quenched free energy and h_c(λ) = sup{h : F(λ,h) > 0} the critical curve. Is the known smoothing bound F(λ, h_c(λ) + δ) ≤ (1+α)c(λ)δ^2 for every λ > 0 and δ > 0 improvable, in the precise sense that the exponent 2 can be replaced by some strictly larger exponent?

For the standard disordered copolymer near a selective interface considered in arXiv:1010.5587, fix λ>0, let F(λ,h)=lim_{N→∞}(1/N)log Z_{N,ω}^{λ,h} be the quenched free energy, and let h_c(λ)=sup{h:F(λ,h)>0} be the critical curve. In the localized phase h<h_c(λ), define
μ(λ,h):=-lim_{N→∞}(1/N)log E[(1+exp(-2λ∑_{n=1}^N(ω_n+h)))/Z_{N,ω}^{λ,h}],
so that Theorem 1.3 identifies 1/μ(λ,h) as the scale governing longest-excursion asymptotics and gives 0≤μ(λ,h)≤F(λ,h) (with a quadratic lower bound). Is it true that, for every fixed λ>0,
lim_{h↑h_c(λ)} (log μ(λ,h))/(log F(λ,h)) = 1?
In other words, does the length scale controlled by μ(λ,h) diverge, up to logarithmic equivalence, at the same rate as 1/F(λ,h) when the critical curve is approached from the localized side?

In the general copolymer model of Section 1.2, let τ be a persistent renewal process with K(n) = P(τ_1 = n) ~ C_K n^{-(1+α)} for some α > 0, let ξ = (ξ_j) be IID Bernoulli(1/2) signs independent of τ, let ω = (ω_n) be IID disorder with E[ω_1] = 0, E[ω_1^2] = 1, and E[e^{tω_1}] < ∞ for all t ∈ R, and let P_{N,ω,λ,h} be the quenched polymer measure defined in equation (4) on the variables Δ_n := Σ_{j≥1} ξ_j 1_{(τ_{j-1},τ_j]}(n) ∈ {0,1}. Fix λ > 0 and h ≥ 0 such that (λ,h) lies in the interior of the delocalized region D := {(λ,h) : F(λ,h) = 0}, where F is the quenched free energy defined in equation (6). Is it true that, for every ε > 0, one has P_{N,ω,λ,h}(Δ_n = 0 for every n ∈ [εN, N] ∩ N) → 0 as N → ∞ for P-almost every disorder realization ω?

Given a finite graph G in adjacency-matrix form, decide whether there exists a finite set P ⊂ R^2 and a bijection φ:V(G)→P such that for every two distinct vertices u,v ∈ V(G), uv ∈ E(G) if and only if the line segment joining φ(u) and φ(v) does not contain or pass through any other point of P. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1012.5187))

Characterize the undirected graphs G that are point visibility graphs of finite point sets in the Euclidean plane; that is, determine necessary and sufficient conditions for the existence of a finite set P⊂R^2 and a bijection between V(G) and P such that two vertices of G are adjacent exactly when the line segment joining the corresponding points of P contains or passes through no other point of P.

Given a finite simple undirected graph G=(V,E) that is promised to be the visibility graph of some finite point set in the Euclidean plane, construct coordinates for a point set Q={q_v : v in V} subset of R^2 such that for every distinct u,v in V, uv is an edge of G if and only if the straight-line segment q_u q_v contains no other point of Q; equivalently, output a planar point-set realization of G as a point visibility graph. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1012.5187))

Let P be a set of points in the plane, and let G be its point visibility graph, with vertex set P and with an edge pq whenever the line segment joining p and q contains no other point of P. Must every such visibility graph G with clique number ω(G) ≤ 4 satisfy χ(G) ≤ 5?

Does there exist an absolute constant c such that for every finite point set P⊂R^2, if G is the point visibility graph of P (that is, V(G)=P and two vertices p,q∈P are adjacent exactly when the line segment pq contains no other point of P) and ω(G)=5, then χ(G)≤c?

Prove the Big-Line-Big-Clique conjecture in either of the two parameter families isolated in the paper: show that either (a) for every integer ℓ >= 2 there exists an integer n(6,ℓ) such that every finite set P ⊂ R^2 of at least n(6,ℓ) distinct points contains either ℓ collinear points or a 6-point subset S ⊂ P whose points are pairwise mutually visible in P (that is, for every distinct p,q ∈ S, the open segment pq contains no point of P), or (b) for every integer k >= 2 there exists an integer n(k,4) such that every finite set P ⊂ R^2 of at least n(k,4) distinct points contains either 4 collinear points or a k-point subset S ⊂ P whose points are pairwise mutually visible in P.

Let P be a finite set of points in the Euclidean plane in general position (that is, no three points of P are collinear). Define b(P) to be the minimum cardinality of a set Q ⊂ R^2 \ P such that every open segment with endpoints in P contains at least one point of Q. For each n, define b(n) := min{ b(P) : P ⊂ R^2, |P| = n, and no three points of P are collinear }. Prove that lim_{n→∞} b(n)/n = ∞.

Let obs(G) denote the obstacle number of a graph G, i.e., the minimum number of simple polygonal obstacles in an obstacle representation of G in which the vertices of G are represented by points in the plane, all represented points and obstacle vertices are in general position, and two vertices u,v are adjacent if and only if the straight-line segment joining their corresponding points avoids every obstacle. Is there an absolute constant c such that every n-vertex graph G satisfies obs(G) <= c n?
