Can one prove, in this obstacle setting, the analogue of Theorem 10: namely that the Wigner distributions of u_j are semiclassically negligible away from K^+, and that every semiclassical measure mu obtained from a subsequence is a decay-eigenmeasure for the billiard flow, in the sense that (phi^t)_* mu = e^{-t Lambda} mu on T^*B(0,R_0) for all t >= 0, with Lambda determined by the asymptotic resonance widths (equivalently, after the standard scaling z(h) = h^2 k_j^2 / 2, by lim Im z(h)/h = -Lambda/2)?

Let P(hbar)=-(hbar^2/2)Delta+V(x) be the semiclassical scattering Hamiltonian of equation (21), with V in C_c^infty(R^d) and supp V contained in the interaction region B(0,R0), and let p(x,xi)=|xi|^2/2+V(x). Assume that for some fixed energy E>0 the trapped set K_E subset p^{-1}(E) is a hyperbolic repeller. Fix C>0 and Lambda>=0, and assume there exists a semiclassical sequence of long-living resonances z(hbar) in D(E, C hbar) with associated metastable states u(hbar), normalized by ||u(hbar)||_{L^2(B(0,R0))}=1, such that along some subsequence S one has Im z(hbar)/hbar -> -Lambda/2 and the Wigner distributions W_hbar u(hbar) converge weak-* on T^*B(0,R0) to a measure mu. Since Theorem 10 implies that any such limit must satisfy (phi_t)_* mu = e^{-t Lambda} mu in T^*B(0,R0) for every t>=0, which Lambda-eigenmeasures for the Hamiltonian flow (necessarily supported on the outgoing tail K_E^+) can actually occur as semiclassical measures of metastable states? Is there a distinguished, or even unique, limiting measure?

Fix a semiclassical scattering Hamiltonian P(hbar) on a manifold X, and assume that outside a compact interaction region B(0,R_0) the manifold is Euclidean so that any scattering state u_E=u_E(hbar) at energy E>0 satisfies (P(hbar)-E)u_E=0 and decomposes near infinity into incoming and outgoing waves. Prescribing the incoming part u_{E,in} then uniquely determines the full state u_E. Suppose moreover that the classical Hamiltonian flow Phi^t on the energy shell p^{-1}(E) has a hyperbolic trapped set K_E, with incoming tail K_E^-={rho in p^{-1}(E): Phi^t(rho) remains bounded as t -> +infinity}. In the semiclassical limit hbar -> 0, what is the spatial (equivalently, microlocal phase-space) structure of u_E inside the interaction region B(0,R_0), and how is that structure shaped by the exceptional trajectories issued from the incoming Lagrangian manifold of u_{E,in} that, instead of escaping after a short transient, spend long times near K_E or belong exactly to K_E^-?

Let Q^{ab} \subseteq \overline{Q} be the maximal abelian extension of the rational numbers Q. Is Q^{ab} an ample (equivalently, large) field; that is, does every smooth curve C over Q^{ab} with C(Q^{ab}) \neq \varnothing have infinitely many Q^{ab}-rational points?

Let Q_solv be the compositum, inside a fixed algebraic closure of Q, of all finite solvable Galois extensions of Q; equivalently, let Q_solv be the maximal Galois extension of Q whose Galois group over Q is prosolvable. Is Q_solv an ample field, i.e. does every smooth geometrically integral curve C over Q_solv with C(Q_solv) nonempty have infinitely many Q_solv-rational points?

Let Q_solv be the maximal solvable extension of Q inside a fixed algebraic closure of Q. Is Q_solv an ample field; that is, does every smooth curve over Q_solv that has a Q_solv-rational point necessarily have infinitely many Q_solv-rational points? ([tau.ac.il](https://www.tau.ac.il/~haran/Papers/theta-hilbertian.pdf))

Let S be a finite set of places of Q, possibly including \infty, and write Q_{tot,S} for the maximal algebraic extension of Q in which every place in S totally splits, and Q_{solv} for the compositum of all finite solvable extensions of Q. Is the field K:=Q_{tot,S}\cap Q_{solv} pseudo-S-closed in the sense of Conjecture 1.1; that is, does K satisfy the corresponding S-adic local-global principle (equivalently, in the paper’s introductory formulation, does every smooth absolutely irreducible curve over K that has points over all classical closures of K above the places in S already have a K-rational point)?
Let ℚ^ab denote the maximal abelian extension of ℚ. Does every non-zero abelian variety A/ℚ acquire infinite Mordell–Weil rank over ℚ^ab; equivalently, is dim_ℚ(A(ℚ^ab) ⊗_ℤ ℚ) = ∞ for every such A?

Let K be an infinite field, and let G_K = Gal(K^sep/K) be its absolute Galois group. If G_K is prosolvable (i.e. a profinite inverse limit of finite solvable groups), must K be ample, in the sense that every smooth K-curve with a K-rational point has infinitely many K-rational points?

Let K be an infinite field, and let G_K=Gal(K^sep/K) be its absolute Galois group endowed with the Krull topology. If G_K is finitely generated as a profinite (equivalently, topological) group, must K be ample; that is, must every smooth geometrically integral curve C over K with C(K) nonempty have infinitely many K-rational points?

Let K be an infinite field, and let G_K := Gal(K^sep/K) be its absolute Galois group endowed with the profinite topology. If G_K is topologically finitely generated, must K be ample; that is, must every smooth K-curve with a K-rational point have infinitely many K-rational points?

Let K be a field. Recall that K is called ample if every smooth geometrically integral K-curve over K that has a K-rational point in fact has infinitely many K-rational points. Define K to be virtually ample if some finite extension of K is ample, and weakly ample if for every smooth geometrically integral K-curve C/K there exists a finite extension L/K, depending on C, such that C(L) is infinite. Is every weakly ample field virtually ample? Is every virtually ample field ample?

Let K be an infinite field such that its multiplicative group K^times is divisible (equivalently: for every integer n >= 1 and every a in K^times, the equation x^n = a has a solution in K). Must K be ample; that is, must every smooth curve C over K with C(K) nonempty satisfy |C(K)| = infinity?

Let K be an infinite field. Assume that K is radically closed, meaning that for every integer n >= 1 the multiplicative group K^\times is n-divisible (equivalently, every a in K^\times has an n-th root in K, or K^\times = (K^\times)^n for all n >= 1). Must K be ample, i.e. a large field in the sense that every smooth K-curve with a K-rational point has infinitely many K-rational points?
Must every infinite field K, regarded as a pure field, be algebraically closed whenever every subset of K definable with parameters in the language of rings is either finite or cofinite?

Does there exist a field K that is not ample such that for every finite Galois extension L/K and every split epimorphism α:H→Gal(L/K) of finite groups, the induced finite split embedding problem (L(t)/K(t),α) admits a proper solution F/K(t) whose solution field F is regular over L, where t is transcendental over K?

Let M be a parameter space, and seek families of holomorphic germs {f_{λ,a}}_{a∈M}⊂End(C,0) of the form f_{λ,a}(z)=λz+z^2g_a(z), where z∈C, f'_{λ,a}(0)=λ, and λ∈S^1 is not a root of unity. Call such a germ elliptic, and say that it is holomorphically linearizable at 0 if it is locally holomorphically conjugate to z↦λz. For λ∈S^1\{roots of unity}, impose the Brjuno condition sum_{k=0}^∞ 2^{-k} log(1 / min_{1≤h≤2^{k+1}} |λ^h-λ|) < ∞. Find families for which, for every parameter a∈M, the germ f_{λ,a} is holomorphically linearizable at 0 if and only if λ satisfies this Brjuno condition. In particular, is every elliptic polynomial germ—and at least every elliptic cubic polynomial germ—holomorphically linearizable exactly when its multiplier is a Brjuno number?

Let B(\theta) be the Brjuno function, defined for irrational \theta\in\mathbb{R}/\mathbb{Z}, and let r(\theta) be Yoccoz's radius function: the infimum, over all holomorphic germs f(z)=e^{2\pi i\theta}z+O(z^2) that are injective on the unit disk, of the radius of convergence of the unique formal linearization of f tangent to the identity. If we set \u03a5(\theta)=\log r(\theta)+B(\theta) for irrational \theta, does \u03a5 extend to a 1/2-H\u00f6lder continuous function on all of \mathbb{R}/\mathbb{Z} (equivalently, on [0,1) with endpoints identified)?

Let f,g be germs of holomorphic local dynamical systems in one complex variable at 0, each having a nonlinearizable irrationally indifferent fixed point at the origin (equivalently, a Cremer point), with multipliers f'(0),g'(0) in S^1\setminus\{roots of unity\}. Let K_f and K_g denote the germs at 0 of their Pérez-Marco stable sets (hedgehogs). Is it true that f and g are topologically locally conjugate if and only if they have the same multiplier and the germs (K_f,0) and (K_g,0) are homeomorphic?

Let φ and η be germs of one-parameter unfoldings of tangent-to-the-identity one-variable holomorphic diffeomorphisms, in the precise fibered class considered in Section 1. Assume that, for a sequence of parameter values x_n → 0, the one-variable fiber germs φ|_{x=x_n} and η|_{x=x_n} are holomorphically conjugate under the exact auxiliary hypotheses imposed in Proposition 1.2 on those fiberwise conjugacies. Must φ and η then be analytically conjugate as germs of unfoldings?

Let f,g ∈ End(C,0) be non-identity parabolic germs, i.e. germs of holomorphic self-maps of one complex variable fixing 0 whose multipliers f'(0) and g'(0) are roots of unity. Is there an effective procedure to decide whether f and g are holomorphically locally conjugated near 0 by a local biholomorphism?

Fix n>=1, and let f in End(C^n,O) be a non-invertible dominant holomorphic germ fixing the origin O, with homogeneous expansion f(z)=sum_{j>=c(f)} P_j(z), where each P_j is an n-tuple of homogeneous polynomials of degree j and P_{c(f)} is not identically O; thus c(f) is the order of f. For the iterates f^k, define c_infinity(f):=lim_{k->+infinity} c(f^k)^{1/k}. Must c_infinity(f) always be an algebraic integer of order at most n, i.e. do there always exist integers a_0,...,a_{n-1} such that c_infinity(f)^n+a_{n-1}c_infinity(f)^{n-1}+...+a_0=0? Moreover, does there always exist a constant delta in (0,1] such that delta c_infinity(f)^k <= c(f^k) <= c_infinity(f)^k for every k>=1?

Let n>=1 and let f in End(C^n,O) be a non-invertible dominant holomorphic germ fixing the origin O, where 'dominant' means det Jac(f) is not identically zero, and let c(f) be the order of f defined by its homogeneous expansion f(z)=sum_{j>=c(f)} P_j(z) with P_j an n-tuple of homogeneous polynomials of degree j and P_{c(f)} not identically zero. Is it true that the integer sequence (c(f^k))_{k>=1}, where f^k denotes the k-th iterate, eventually satisfies a linear recurrence with constant integer coefficients; equivalently, do there exist integers r>=1, N>=1, and a_0,...,a_{r-1} such that c(f^{k+r}) + a_{r-1} c(f^{k+r-1}) + ... + a_0 c(f^k) = 0 for every k>=N?

Let E be a finite-dimensional complex vector space with a direct-sum decomposition E = E1 ⊕ ··· ⊕ Ep, and let F : (E,0) → (E,0) be an analytic germ having an adapted superattracting fixed point in the sense that, for each j ∈ {1, ..., p}, there exists a nondegenerate homogeneous map Hj : Ej → Ej of degree kj ≥ 2 such that, writing Fj := πj ◦ F and vj := πj(v), one has Fj(v) = Hj(vj) + O(||v|| · ||vj||^{kj}) as v → 0. If H := H1 ⊕ ··· ⊕ Hp is the quasihomogeneous part of F, is the existence of a local Böttcher coordinate—namely an analytic isomorphism germ Φ : (E,0) → (E,0) with Φ(0) = 0, D0Φ = id, and Φ ◦ F = H ◦ Φ—equivalent to the existence of an admissible p-tuple of analytic vector-field germs (ζ1, ..., ζp), where each ζj is tangent to Ej, vanishes on {vj = 0}, satisfies ζj(v) = ϑj(v) + o(||v||) with ϑj(v) = (v; vj), the ζj commute pairwise, and each ζj is tangent, on some neighborhood U with F : U → F(U) proper, to the critical value set of F^n for every n ≥ 1?

Let O be the origin in C^n, let f in End(C^n,O) be a superattracting germ, and write its homogeneous expansion as f(z) = sum_{j >= c(f)} P_j(z), where c(f) >= 2 and H := P_{c(f)} is the first nonzero homogeneous term. Let Crit(f) = {det(df) = 0} and PCrit(f) = union_{k >= 0} f^k(Crit(f)). Assume that, as a germ at O, PCrit(f) is a topological cone near O (that is, the image of a standard cone under a local homeomorphism). Under what additional hypotheses, if any, does there exist a local homeomorphism Phi fixing O such that Phi o f = H o Phi near O? In particular, must such a topological local conjugacy always exist when H is non-degenerate, i.e. H^{-1}(O) = {O}?

Let E be a complex vector space decomposed as E = E1 ⊕ ··· ⊕ Ep, and let F:(E,0)→(E,0) be an analytic germ with an adapted superattracting fixed point, meaning that for each j there is a nondegenerate homogeneous map Hj:Ej→Ej of degree kj ≥ 2 such that Fj(v)=Hj(vj)+O(∥v∥∥vj∥^{kj}) as v→0; write H = H1 ⊕ ··· ⊕ Hp for the quasihomogeneous part of F. Is F locally biholomorphically conjugate to H by a germ Φ with Φ(0)=0 and D0Φ=id if and only if there exists an admissible p-tuple of analytic vector field germs (ζ1,…,ζp), where each ζj is tangent to Ej, vanishes on E′j={vj=0}, satisfies ζj(v)=ϑj(v)+o(∥v∥) with ϑj(v)=(v;vj), the fields commute pairwise, and each ζj is tangent, on some sufficiently small neighborhood U on which F:U→F(U)⊆U is proper, to the critical value set of F^n:U→F^n(U) for every n ≥ 1?

Let A_n = C[z_1, ..., z_n] and let Δ_n = sum_{i=1}^n ∂^2/∂z_i^2. If P ∈ A_n is a homogeneous polynomial of degree 4 whose Hessian matrix Hes(P) = (∂^2P/∂z_i∂z_j) is nilpotent, must one have Δ_n^m(P^{m+1}) = 0 for all sufficiently large integers m; equivalently, does there exist M such that for every m ≥ M, Δ_n^m(P^{m+1}) = 0?

Classify, up to local holomorphic conjugacy, the 3-dimensional non-invertible dominant rigid holomorphic fixed-point germs f:(M,p)->(M,p) over C (equivalently, after choosing local coordinates, germs f in End(C^3,O)) such that df_p is not invertible, det Jac(f) is not identically zero, and the generalized critical set Crit∞(f):=union_{k>=0} f^{-k}(Crit(f))=union_{k>=0} Crit(f^k), where Crit(f)={det(df)=0}, is, as a germ at p, the union of q smooth irreducible components W_1,...,W_q with 0<=q<=3 having simple normal crossings at p and satisfying f(W_j)=intersection_{i in I_j} W_i for some I_j subset {1,...,q} for each j. ([pagine.dm.unipi.it](https://pagine.dm.unipi.it/abate/articoli/artric/files/10.1007_s13324-011-0017-y.pdf))

For which non-invertible dominant holomorphic germs f in End(C^3, O) — where End(C^3, O) denotes germs of holomorphic self-maps of C^3 fixing O, and dominant means det Jac(f) is not identically zero — does there exist a modification pi: M~ -> C^3 based at O (i.e. a finite composition of blow-ups of submanifolds or points whose first center contains O and whose later centers meet the inverse image of O), a point p in E := pi^{-1}(O), and a holomorphic germ f~ in End(M~, p) such that pi o f~ = f o pi and f~ is rigid, or at least weakly rigid, in the sense that Crit^infty(f~) = union_{k>=0} Crit(f~^k) = union_{k>=0} f~^{-k}(Crit(f~)) is, as a germ at p, a union of smooth irreducible components with simple normal crossings, and in the rigid case each irreducible component W_j of Crit^infty(f~) satisfies f~(W_j) = intersection_{i in I_j} W_i for some I_j subset of {1, ..., q}?

For every n≥2, let f∈End(C^n, O) be a holomorphic germ tangent to the identity of multiplicity ν≥2, meaning that in local coordinates f(z)=z+P_ν(z)+P_{ν+1}(z)+⋯ with P_ν≠0 homogeneous of degree ν, and assume that O is an isolated fixed point of f. Must there exist a projective direction [v]∈P^{n−1}(C) and a Fatou flower tangent to [v], that is, ν−1 parabolic curves tangent to [v] whose domains are the connected components of D_{δ,ν}={ζ∈C: |ζ^{ν−1}−δ|<δ} for some sufficiently small δ>0?

Let f ∈ End(C^n,0) be a holomorphic germ tangent to the identity, so that f(z)=z+P_ν(z)+P_{ν+1}(z)+⋯ with ν≥2 and P_ν a nonzero homogeneous polynomial map of degree ν. For a representative f:U→C^n, let K_f=⋂_{k≥0} f^{-k}(U) be its stable set, and for each characteristic direction [v]∈P^{n-1}(C) of f (i.e. P_ν(v)=λv for some λ∈C), consider the associated directors/indices. Describe the germ at 0 of K_f, not just the subset of points whose orbits converge to 0 tangentially to a characteristic direction, in terms of the characteristic directions and their directors/indices, and determine what further invariants, if any, are needed to account for the whole stable set.

Let f ∈ End(C^n,O) be a holomorphic germ tangent to the identity of multiplicity ν ≥ 2, with convergent homogeneous expansion f(z)=z+P_ν(z)+O(||z||^{ν+1}), where P_ν=(P_{ν,1},…,P_{ν,n}) is the first nonzero term and each P_{ν,j} is a homogeneous polynomial of degree ν. Assume that every characteristic direction of f, meaning every nonzero v ∈ C^n with P_ν(v)=λv for some λ ∈ C, is non-degenerate in the sense that λ ≠ 0. If g denotes the local time-1 map of the homogeneous holomorphic vector field dot z=P_ν(z), must f be topologically locally conjugated to g near O?

How can one complete the formal classification, up to formal conjugacy, of holomorphic germs f in End(C^n,O) tangent to the identity and of multiplicity ν >= 2, written as f(z) = z + P_ν(z) + P_{ν+1}(z) + ..., by finding formal normal forms and formal invariants for those germs having degenerate characteristic directions (possibly as their only characteristic directions), where a characteristic direction is a nonzero v in C^n with P_ν(v) = λv and is degenerate when P_ν(v) = 0?

Let Q=(Q1,Q2) be a homogeneous vector field of degree ν≥2 on C^2, and let G be the associated geodesic field on the total space of a suitable line bundle over P^1(C). In the local coordinates (z,v) induced by the usual non-homogeneous coordinate centered at [1:0]∈P^1(C), suppose G has the form G=g1(z)v∂/∂z+(ν−1)g2(z)v^2∂/∂v, where g1(z)=Q2(1,z)-zQ1(1,z) and g2(z)=Q1(1,z). For ζ0∈C, let μj(ζ0) be the order of vanishing of gj at ζ0, and assume that the point (ζ0,0), corresponding to [1:ζ0]∈P^1(C), is an irregular singularity, i.e. μ1(ζ0)>μ2(ζ0)+1. Describe the local dynamics of G about the irregular singularity (ζ0,0).

Let \(n\ge 2\) and let \(\lambda=(\lambda_1,\dots,\lambda_n)\in(\mathbb C^*)^n\). For \(m\ge 2\), define
\[\widetilde\omega_\lambda(m):=\min_{1\le j\le n}\;\min_{\substack{2\le |Q|\le m\ Q
otin \operatorname{Res}_j(\lambda)}} |\lambda^Q-\lambda_j|,\]
where \(\operatorname{Res}_j(\lambda)=\{Q\in\mathbb N^n:|Q|\ge 2,\ \lambda^Q=\lambda_j\}\). Suppose that \(\lambda\) does not satisfy the reduced Brjuno condition, i.e. there is no strictly increasing sequence \(\{p_
u\}_{
u\ge 0}\) with \(p_0=1\) such that
\[\sum_{
u\ge 0} p_
u^{-1}\log \widetilde\omega_\lambda(p_{
u+1})^{-1}<\infty.\]
Must there exist a germ \(f\in\operatorname{Diff}(\mathbb C^n,0)\) with \(df_0=\operatorname{Diag}(\lambda_1,\dots,\lambda_n)\) that is formally linearizable (by a formal change of coordinates tangent to the identity) but not holomorphically linearizable?

Fix n>=1 and lambda=(lambda_1,...,lambda_n) in C^n, and for m>=2 define Omega_lambda(m)=min{|lambda_1^{k_1}...lambda_n^{k_n}-lambda_j| : k_1,...,k_n in N, 2<=k_1+...+k_n<=m, 1<=j<=n, lambda_1^{k_1}...lambda_n^{k_n}!=lambda_j}. Can one find a parameter space M and a family {f_{lambda,a}}_{a in M} subset End(C^n,O) of holomorphic germs fixing O, each formally conjugate to the linear map z |-> diag(lambda_1,...,lambda_n) z and satisfying df_{lambda,a}(O)=diag(lambda_1,...,lambda_n), such that for every a in M the germ f_{lambda,a} is holomorphically linearizable if and only if sum_{k>=0} 2^{-k} log(1/Omega_lambda(2^{k+1}))<infinity? In particular, when n=2 and (lambda_1,lambda_2) is non-resonant, is every germ of the form f(z)=(lambda_1 z_1,lambda_2 z_2)+Q(z), with Q=(Q_1,Q_2) a pair of quadratic homogeneous polynomials, holomorphically linearizable if and only if (lambda_1,lambda_2) satisfies that Brjuno condition? ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1107.4876))

Let f(n) denote the maximum number of edges in a graph on n vertices in which every two cycles have different lengths. Determine whether
lim_{n->infty} (f(n)-n)/sqrt(n) = sqrt(2.4).
Let f(n) denote the maximum number of edges in a graph on n vertices such that no two cycles in the graph have the same length. Is it true that lim inf_{n→∞} (f(n) − n)/√n ≤ √3?

Let f(n) denote the maximum number of edges in a graph on n vertices in which all cycles have pairwise distinct lengths. Is it true that, as n → ∞ through the positive integers, lim inf ((f(n) - n)/√n) ≤ √2.4? ([archive.ymsc.tsinghua.edu.cn](https://archive.ymsc.tsinghua.edu.cn/pacm_download/168/4692-cycle.pdf))

For each integer n≥3, let f2(n) be the maximum number of edges of a 2-connected graph G with |V(G)|=n such that any two distinct cycles of G have different lengths. Is it true that the limit exists and satisfies lim_{n→∞}(f2(n)-n)/√n = 1? ([archive.ymsc.tsinghua.edu.cn](https://archive.ymsc.tsinghua.edu.cn/pacm_download/168/4692-cycle.pdf))
For each integer n >= 3, determine the maximum possible value of |E(G)| over all Hamiltonian graphs G on n vertices such that any two distinct cycles of G have different lengths.
Is Jia’s conjecture true that, if g(n) is the minimum, over all graphs, of the number of edges in a graph containing a cycle of every length k=1,2,\dots,n, then g(n)=n+\log_2 n+O(1) as n\to\infty?

Fix a positive integer n and nonnegative integers a1, a2, ..., an. For a graph G on n vertices, let (c1, c2, ..., cn) be its cycle length distribution, where ci denotes the number of cycles of length i in G. Determine f(a1, a2, ..., an), the maximum possible number of edges in a graph G satisfying ci ≤ ai for every 1 ≤ i ≤ n.

For each fixed integer k >= 2, let ex(n, C_{2k}) be the Turán number of the cycle C_{2k}, that is, the maximum number of edges in a finite simple n-vertex graph containing no subgraph isomorphic to C_{2k}. Is it true that there exists a constant c = c(k) > 0 such that ex(n, C_{2k}) >= c n^(1+1/k) for all sufficiently large n?

Is Hajós conjecture true: for every finite simple Eulerian graph G, where 'Eulerian' means that G is not necessarily connected and every vertex has even degree, if cd(G) denotes the minimum integer t such that E(G) can be partitioned into t edge-disjoint circuits, then must cd(G) ≤ |V(G)|/2?

Extend the plane classification of Theorem 5.3 to higher dimensions: for each integer r ≥ 2, let X ⊂ R^n be a compact set of positive Lebesgue measure, regarded as a symmetry measure space with admissible symmetries S = Iso(X) \ {id}, and define ms_r(X) to be the maximal symmetry number of X, i.e. the infimum, over all measurable r-colorings χ : X → {1, ..., r}, of the supremum of μ(B) over all measurable monochromatic subsets B ⊂ X for which B = s(B) for some s ∈ S. Classify ms_r(X) for all n > 2. In particular, determine ms_r(X) for every regular convex polyhedron X in R^n with n > 2, and determine ms_2(T) for the regular tetrahedron T ⊂ R^3.

Let S^n ⊂ R^(n+1) be the unit n-sphere, equipped with its O(n+1)-invariant probability Borel measure, and let S_2^+ be the family of all non-identity involutive orientation-preserving isometries of S^n, equivalently the rotations by π about lines through the origin. For integers n,r > 1, is ms_r(S^n, S_2^+) ≥ 1/r^2?

For integers n,r>=1, let n={0,1,...,n-1} be viewed as a subset of Z with counting measure and with admissible central symmetries s_c(x)=c-x for c in Z. A blurred r-coloring of n is a family chi=(chi_1,...,chi_r) of functions chi_i:n->[0,1] such that sum_{i=1}^r chi_i(x)=1 for every x in n. Extending each chi_i by 0 outside n, define the blurred maximal symmetry number by bms_r(n)=inf_chi sup_{1<=i<=r} sup_{c in Z} sum_{x in Z} chi_i(x)chi_i(c-x). Calculate the exact values of bms_r(n), at least in the cases of small n and, in particular, for the two-color case r=2.

For each integer r >= 1, determine the exact value of ms_r(I), where I = [0,1] is viewed as a measurable subset of the symmetry measure space (R, lambda, S) with lambda the Lebesgue measure and S = {s_c : c in R}, s_c(x) = 2c - x; equivalently, determine the largest epsilon such that every measurable r-coloring I = C_1 union ... union C_r contains a measurable monochromatic subset A subseteq C_i with lambda(A) >= epsilon and A = s_c(A) for some c in R. In particular, determine ms_2(I).

Let I=[0,1] be endowed with Lebesgue measure, and let ms_r(I) denote the maximal symmetry number for measurable r-colorings of I with respect to central symmetries of the real line; that is, ms_r(I) is the largest α such that every measurable coloring I=C_1∪⋯∪C_r contains a monochromatic measurable set A⊆C_i of measure at least α with A=2c−A for some c∈R. Theorem 6.2(6) states that there exists a constant S′, with 1/2≤S′<5/6, such that S′=inf_{r∈N} r^2 ms_r(I)=lim_{r→∞} r^2 ms_r(I). Determine or estimate S′, and decide whether it is equal to the constant S from Theorem 6.1, i.e. the autoconvolution-based constant for which ms_r(I)≥S/r^2 for all r∈N.

For a fixed integer r>1, let I=[0,1] be endowed with Lebesgue measure and the family of central symmetries s_c(x)=2c-x for c in R, and let n={0,1,...,n-1} subset Z be endowed with the counting measure and the symmetries \tilde{s}_c(x)=c-x for c in Z. Let ms_r(X) denote the maximal symmetry number of X, i.e. the infimum over all measurable r-colorings of X of the largest measure/cardinality of a monochromatic subset A subset X with A=s(A) for some admissible symmetry s, and let bms_r(X) denote the corresponding blurred maximal symmetry number obtained by taking the infimum over measurable blurred r-colorings {\chi_i}_{i=1}^r with \chi_i:X->[0,1] and sum_i \chi_i equiv 1. Since Theorem 6.2 shows that ms_r(I)=lim_{n->∞} ms_r(n)/n, bms_r(I)=lim_{n->∞} bms_r(n)/n, and ms_r(I)=bms_r(I), determine how quickly the normalized sequences ms_r(n)/n and bms_r(n)/n converge, as n->∞, to their common limit ms_r(I)=bms_r(I).

Fix an integer r >= 2. Let G be a compact Abelian topological group with normalized Haar measure μ, and let S = {s_g : G -> G, s_g(x) = 2g - x} be the family of central symmetries of G (equivalently, in multiplicative notation, s_c(x) = c x^{-1} c). Define ms_r(G) := ms(G,S;r) to be the infimum, over all measurable r-colorings G = A_1 ∪ ... ∪ A_r, of max_{1 <= i <= r} sup_{g in G} μ(A_i ∩ s_g(A_i)). Characterize exactly those compact Abelian groups G for which ms_r(G) = 1/r^2. ([mathnet.ru](https://www.mathnet.ru/php/getFT.phtml?jrnid=im&option_lang=eng&paperid=310&what=fullteng))

Let G be a finite group of odd order. For an integer r >= 2, let ms_r(G) denote the maximal symmetry number of G with respect to the family of central symmetries s_c(x) = c x^{-1} c; equivalently, ms_r(G) is the largest real number alpha such that every r-coloring of G contains a monochromatic subset A with A = c A^{-1} c for some c in G and |A| >= alpha|G|. Is it true that ms_r(G) > 1/r^2 for every finite group G of odd order and every integer r >= 2?

For every ε > 0 and integer r > 1, does there exist a finite group G such that, with central symmetries s_c(x)=cx^{-1}c for c∈G and normalized counting measure on G, the maximal symmetry number
ms_r(G)=inf_{χ:G→{1,…,r}} max_{1≤i≤r} max_{c∈G} |χ^{-1}(i)∩s_c(χ^{-1}(i))|/|G|
 satisfies ms_r(G)<ε? ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1111.1015))

Let G be a connected compact topological group, endowed with its normalized Haar probability measure μ and the family of central symmetries s_c(x)=cx^{-1}c (c∈G). For a positive integer r, let ms_r(G) denote the maximal symmetry number of G, i.e. the largest ε∈[0,1] such that every measurable r-coloring of G contains a monochromatic measurable subset A with μ(A)≥ε and s_c(A)=A for some c∈G. Does there exist a connected compact topological group G and some r∈N such that ms_r(G)<1/r^2? In particular, what are the exact values of ms_2(SO(3)) and ms_2(S^3), where S^3 is the multiplicative group of unit quaternions?

Let G be an infinite group, and endow G with its family of central symmetries x -> g x^{-1} g (g in G). Let ms_r(G) and ms_r^+(G) be the corresponding cardinal symmetry numbers defined on the algebra of all subsets of G using the measures card(A)=|A| and card^+(A)=|A|^+, respectively. Is it true that for every finite cardinal r both ms_r(G) and ms_r^+(G) are infinite?

Let K be an infinite field and let G = SL(K). View G as the symmetry measure space (G, card^+, S), where the underlying σ-algebra is P(G), card^+(A) = |A|^+ for A ⊂ G, and S = {s_c : c ∈ G} is the family of central symmetries s_c(x) = c x^{-1} c. Is it true that for every finite cardinal r, the cardinal symmetry number MS_r^+(G) = ms_r(G, card^+, S) is equal to |G|^+?

Let F_2 be the free group on two generators, equipped with its family of central symmetries, and let ms_r^+(F_2) denote the corresponding successor-cardinal symmetry number from Section 8. Is ms_r^+(F_2) uncountable for every finite cardinal r?

For the hyperbolic plane H^2 endowed with the family S = {s_c : c in H^2} of central symmetries, where s_c(x) is the unique point such that c is the midpoint of the hyperbolic geodesic segment [x, s_c(x)], is the dimension symmetry number mds_r(H^2) nonnegative for every integer r >= 2?

Given a symmetry measure space X = (X, μ, S), where μ is a monotone measure on a σ-algebra of subsets of X with values in a complete linearly ordered set and S is a family of bijective μ-preserving admissible symmetries of X, determine for each cardinal r and each λ in the value set of μ the (r, λ)-centerpole number c_r^λ(X): the least cardinality of a subfamily S' ⊂ S such that every measurable r-coloring χ : X → r (that is, each color class χ^{-1}(i) is μ-measurable) contains a monochromatic measurable set A ⊂ X with μ(A) ≥ λ and A = s(A) for some s ∈ S'; if no such subfamily exists, set c_r^λ(X) = ∞.

For natural numbers n and r with r <= n, let X be either R^n or Z^n, where Z^n carries the Euclidean metric induced from R^n, and let central symmetry about c in X mean the map s_c(x)=2c-x. Define c_r^0(X) to be the least cardinality of a set C subseteq X such that every r-coloring chi:X->{0,1,...,r-1} contains an unbounded monochromatic subset S subseteq X with S = s_c(S) for some c in C (equivalently, asdim(S) >= 0). Is c_r^0(R^n) = c_r^0(Z^n) for all n,r with r <= n?

Since c^0_4(R^4)=12, let C⊂R^4 be a 12-point set, and for each c∈R^4 write s_c(x)=2c-x for the central symmetry about c. Call C 4-centerpole if every 4-coloring χ:R^4→{0,1,2,3} admits an unbounded monochromatic set S⊂R^4 and a point c∈C such that S=2c-S. Let 2={0,1}, let 2^3_{<t}={x∈2^3:x_1+x_2+x_3<t} and 2^3_{>t}={x∈2^3:x_1+x_2+x_3>t}, and define the (3,1)-sandwich by Ξ^3_1=({-1}×2^3_{<1})∪({0}×2^3_{<3})∪({1}×2^3_{>1})⊂Z×Z^3=Z^4⊂R^4. Must every 12-element 4-centerpole set C⊂R^4 be affinely equivalent to Ξ^3_1?

Calculate c_5^0(R^5), the (5,0)-centerpole number of Euclidean 5-space R^5 (viewed as the additive group with central symmetries x ↦ 2c - x): determine the least cardinality of a set C ⊂ R^5 such that for every 5-coloring χ : R^5 → {0,1,2,3,4} there exist a point c ∈ C and an unbounded monochromatic subset S ⊂ R^5 satisfying S = 2c - S. Equivalently, determine the smallest number of centers that forces an unbounded monochromatic subset symmetric with respect to one of those centers in every 5-coloring of R^5. The currently known bounds are 18 ≤ c_5^0(R^5) ≤ c_5^0(Z^5) ≤ 25.

For each integer r >= 1, let c_r^0(R^r) be the smallest cardinality of a set C subseteq R^r such that every r-coloring chi: R^r -> {0,1,...,r-1} contains an unbounded monochromatic subset S subseteq R^r that is centrally symmetric with respect to some point c in C, i.e. S = 2c - S. What is the asymptotic growth of the sequence (c_r^0(R^r))_{r>=1} as r -> infinity? In particular, is this growth polynomial in r or exponential in r?

For integers n >= 1 and r >= 1 and a finite nonnegative integer λ < n, view R^n as a symmetry measure space whose admissible symmetries are the central symmetries s_c(x) = 2c - x (c in R^n) and whose measure is asymptotic dimension, normalized so that bounded sets have asymptotic dimension -1. Let c_r^λ(R^n) be the smallest cardinality of a set C subset R^n such that every r-coloring χ: R^n -> {0, ..., r-1} contains a monochromatic subset A subset R^n with A = 2c - A for some c in C and asdim(A) >= λ. Calculate or estimate c_r^λ(R^n) for various values of r and λ.

Let G be a group (in particular, one may focus on the Abelian case) and let S = {s_c : c ∈ G} be the family of central symmetries, where s_c(x) = c x^{-1} c (equivalently, s_c(x) = 2c − x in additive Abelian notation). Regard G as the symmetry measure space (G, asdim, S), where asdim:P(G)→[-1,∞] is the asymptotic-dimension measure defined by: asdim(A) ≤ n if and only if for every finite subset F ⊂ G there exists a cover 𝒰 of A with finite mesh(𝒰) = ⋃_{U∈𝒰} U^{-1}U such that, for some finite subset B ⊂ G, each x ∈ G \ B has xF meeting at most n+1 members of 𝒰; equivalently, finite subsets are exactly those with asdim = -1. For each cardinal r ≥ 1, calculate or estimate the dimension symmetry number mds_r(G) := ms_r(G, asdim, S), i.e. determine or bound the quantity mds_r(G) = inf_{χ:G→r} sup_{i∈r, c∈G} asdim(χ^{-1}(i) ∩ s_c(χ^{-1}(i))).

Given an arbitrary group G, regarded as the symmetry measure space (G, asdim, S) where S={s_c:c∈G} and s_c(x)=cx^{-1}c, calculate or evaluate, for each cardinal r and each asymptotic-dimension threshold λ, the centerpole number c_r^λ(G): the least cardinality of a set C⊂G such that every r-coloring χ:G→r contains a monochromatic subset A⊂G with asdim(A)≥λ and A=cA^{-1}c for some c∈C, with c_r^λ(G)=∞ if no such C exists. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1111.1015))

Let F_2 be the free group on two generators, viewed as the symmetry measure space (F_2, asdim, S) with S the family of central symmetries. For each r in N, is the 0-centerpole number c_r^0(F_2) finite; equivalently, does there exist a finite set C subseteq F_2 such that every r-coloring chi:F_2->r contains an infinite monochromatic subset A subseteq F_2 with A = c A^{-1} c for some c in C?

Let F_2 be the free group on two generators. Define c_2^0(F_2) to be the least cardinality of a subset C ⊂ F_2 such that for every 2-coloring χ:F_2→{0,1} there exist an element c∈C and an infinite monochromatic subset A⊂F_2 with A = cA^{-1}c (equivalently, A is invariant under the central symmetry x↦cx^{-1}c). Is c_2^0(F_2) equal to 4, 3, or 2?

Upper Matching Conjecture (UMC). Let 𝒢(2n,r) denote the set of simple r-regular graphs on 2n vertices, let φ(k,G) be the number of k-matchings of G, and define Θ(k,n,r):=max{φ(k,G): G∈𝒢(2n,r)}. If qG denotes the disjoint union of q copies of G, then for every pair of positive integers q and r, and every k=1,...,qr, is it true that Θ(k,qr,r)=φ(k,qK_{r,r})?

Lower Matching Conjecture (finite form). For positive integers n and r, and for each integer k with 1 <= k <= n, let G range over all undirected loopless r-regular bipartite multigraphs on 2n vertices, let phi(k,G) denote the number of k-matchings of G (that is, sets of k pairwise disjoint edges), and define lambda(k,n,r) := min_G phi(k,G). Is it true that for every such n, r, and k, one has lambda(k,n,r) >= (n choose k)^2 * ((nr - k)/(nr))^(rn - k) * (kr/n)^k?

Let phi(k,G) denote the number of k-matchings in a loopless undirected multigraph G, and define omega(k,n,r) := min{phi(k,G) : G in G_co,mult(2n,r)}, where G_co,mult(2n,r) is the class of r-edge-colorable r-regular multigraphs on 2n vertices. For each fixed integer r >= 3, is it true that the perfect-matching minimum omega(n,n,r) grows exponentially with n; that is, do there exist constants C_r > 0 and c_r > 1 such that omega(n,n,r) >= C_r c_r^n for all sufficiently large n?

Let G = (V,E) be an infinite r-regular graph with countably many vertices. For p in [0,1], define the p-matching entropy h_G(p) by h_G(p) = limsup_{k->infty} log(phi(m_k,G_k)) / |V_k|, where phi(m,G) denotes the number of m-matchings of G, G_k = (V_k,E_k) is a sequence of finite graphs converging to G in the sense used in the paper, and 2m_k/|V_k| -> p. Let ∞K_{r,r} denote the countable disjoint union of copies of the complete bipartite graph K_{r,r}. Is it true that h_G(p) <= h_{∞K_{r,r}}(p) for every p in [0,1]?

Let G_{co,mult}(2n,r) denote the set of loopless r-regular r-edge-colorable multigraphs on 2n vertices, and for G in G_{co,mult}(2n,r) let φ(k,G) be the number of k-matchings of G. Define
ω(k,n,r) := min{φ(k,G) : G in G_{co,mult}(2n,r)}.
Fix an integer r ≥ 2 and a real number p in (0,2/3). Is it true that there exists a constant c=c(r,p)>1 such that, for all sufficiently large n and every integer k with ceil(pn) ≤ k ≤ floor(2n/3), one has ω(k,n,r) ≥ c^n? If so, can one obtain a quantitatively good explicit lower bound for this exponential rate of growth?

For integers n≥2 and 2≤k≤n, let Ψ_{2n} be the Edmonds matching polytope of K_{2n}, i.e. the set of all real 2n×2n symmetric doubly stochastic matrices B=[b_{ij}] with b_{ii}=0 such that, for every odd subset S⊂{1,…,2n} with 3≤|S|≤2n−3, one has ∑_{i,j∈S} b_{ij}≤|S|−1. Define μ_{k,n}:=min_{B∈Ψ_{2n}} haf_k(B), where haf_k(B) is the sum of the haffnians of all principal 2k×2k submatrices of B (equivalently, the total weight of k-matchings of K_{2n} with edge-weights b_{ij}). Determine μ_{k,n}, or obtain sharp general lower bounds for it; in particular, determine for which pairs (k,n) one has the van der Waerden/Tverberg-type identity μ_{k,n}=haf_k((2n−1)^{-1}A(K_{2n})) and whether equality can occur only at B=(2n−1)^{-1}A(K_{2n}).

For each integer n >= 2, let Psi_{2n} be the set of all real 2n x 2n symmetric doubly stochastic matrices B=[b_ij] with zero diagonal such that sum_{i,j in S} b_ij <= |S|-1 for every odd subset S of {1,...,2n} with 3 <= |S| <= 2n-3. For B in Psi_{2n}, let haf_n(B) := sum_M product_{(i,j) in M} b_ij, where the sum runs over all perfect matchings M of K_{2n}, and define mu_{n,n} := min_{B in Psi_{2n}} haf_n(B). Since mu_{n+m,n+m} <= mu_{n,n} mu_{m,m}, the limit mu := lim_{n->infty} (1/n) log mu_{n,n} exists. Is mu > -infinity?

For each fixed integer r >= 2, let G=(V,E) be a countable infinite r-regular graph, and define its p-matching entropy by h_G(p) = limsup_{k -> infinity} (1/|V_k|) log phi(m_k,G_k), where G_k=(V_k,E_k) is a sequence of finite graphs converging to G, phi(m_k,G_k) is the number of m_k-matchings of G_k, and 2m_k/|V_k| -> p. In the bipartite case, the asymptotic lower matching conjecture asserts that h_G(p) >= f(p,r) for all p in [0,1], where f(p,r) = (1/2)(p log r - p log p - 2(1-p) log(1-p) + (r-p) log(1-p/r)). What is the correct analogue of this ALMC lower-bound inequality for arbitrary, not necessarily bipartite, infinite r-regular graphs, at least for p in [0, 2/3]?

Let G be a countably infinite connected bridgeless 3-regular graph, under the paper's standing convention that graphs are undirected, loopless, and may have multiple edges. For p-monomer entropy defined by h_G(p)=limsup_{k->infinity} |V_k|^{-1} log phi(m_k,G_k) over finite graphs G_k converging to G with 2m_k/|V_k| -> p, the bipartite asymptotic lower matching conjecture asserts h_G(p) >= f(p,3), where f(p,3)=1/2*(p log 3 - p log p - 2(1-p) log(1-p) + (3-p) log(1-p/3)). What is the correct analogue of this lower-bound inequality for such non-bipartite bridgeless cubic graphs; equivalently, what explicit lower-entropy statement should replace the bipartite ALMC in the infinite connected bridgeless 3-regular setting?

Given an arbitrary series sum_{n=1}^infty a_n of positive real numbers, with no monotonicity or other regularity assumptions on the term sequence (a_n), what decides whether the series converges or diverges? In particular, does there exist any universal convergence test, or even an algorithm, that determines convergence versus divergence for all such positive series?

Problem 3. Let A⊂N, and let φ:N→(0,∞) be an increasing function with lim_{n→∞} φ(n)=∞. Define the upper density of weight φ by d̄_φ(A):=limsup_{n→∞} |A∩{1,2,…,n}|/φ(n). If d̄_{n/ln n}(A)>0, must the subseries ∑_{n∈A} 1/n of the harmonic series diverge? More generally, for each fixed k∈N, does the same conclusion hold when the weight is φ_k(n)=n/[(ln n)(ln ln n)⋯(ln∘⋯∘ln)(n)], where the last factor is the k-fold iterated natural logarithm and n is taken sufficiently large so that all iterated logarithms are defined and positive?

Let A be a subset of N = {1,2,3,...}. If the positive subseries sum_{n in A} 1/n diverges, must it follow that for every integer k >= 3 there exist integers a >= 1 and r >= 1 such that a, a+r, ..., a+(k-1)r all belong to A?

Given a topological group G, does there exist a zero-dimensional topological group H (that is, dim H = 0) with w(H) = w(G) and a continuous surjective homomorphism H -> G? In particular, for which almost metrizable topological groups G—meaning G contains a compact subset of countable character—does such a zero-dimensional quotient representation of the same weight exist?

Let X be a metrizable space. Under what conditions is the free universal algebra of an uncountable signature over X paracompact? In particular, is the free topological linear space L(X) of X over the discrete field of real numbers paracompact?

Let X be a zero-dimensional compact homogeneous space, where homogeneous means that for every x1, x2 in X there exists a homeomorphism h:X→X with h(x1)=x2. Let S(X) ⊂ X^X be the semigroup of all continuous self-mappings of X, endowed with the topology of pointwise convergence inherited from the Tychonov product X^X. A topological semigroup S with identity e is called left bounded if for every neighborhood U of e there exists a finite set F ⊂ S such that S = FU. Is the semigroup S(X) left bounded for every zero-dimensional compact homogeneous space X?

Let X be a zero-dimensional homogeneous topological space, where homogeneous means that for any points x1,x2∈X there exists a homeomorphism h:X→X with h(x1)=x2. Let S(X)⊂X^X be the semigroup of all continuous self-maps of X, endowed with the topology of pointwise convergence inherited from the Tychonoff product X^X, and let id_X denote its identity element. Say that a semigroup with identity e is right bounded if for every neighborhood U of e there exists a finite set F such that S=UF. Must the topological semigroup S(X) be right bounded for every zero-dimensional homogeneous space X?

Let X be a compact space, and let S(X)⊂X^X be the semigroup of all continuous self-maps of X, endowed with the topology of pointwise convergence inherited from the Tychonoff product X^X. Suppose H is a subgroup of S(X) that acts transitively on X and is distal, in the sense that for any distinct points x1,x2∈X and any point x∈X there exists a neighborhood U of x such that {h(x1),h(x2)}⊄U for every h∈H. Must H be left bounded; equivalently, for every neighborhood V of the identity e in H, is there a finite set F⊂H such that H = FV?

Let G be a group endowed with a topology tau such that every left and right shift x -> gx and x -> xg is a homeomorphism; assume that for every neighborhood U of the identity e there exists a finite set F subseteq G with G = FU = UF. Must G have countable cellularity, i.e. must every family of pairwise disjoint nonempty open subsets of G be countable? The same question is asked under the additional assumption that inversion x -> x^(-1) is continuous, equivalently when G is quasitopological.

Let X be a zero-dimensional compact homogeneous topological space, where zero-dimensional means dim X = 0. Must there exist a group operation on the underlying set X such that, with its given compact topology τ, the pair (X,τ) is a left-topological group, i.e. τ is invariant under every left shift l_g:x -> gx? In particular, if K is a first-countable zero-dimensional compact space, does the product space K^ω admit such a left-topological group structure?
Does every compact left topological group G carry a Borel probability measure μ, not assumed invariant, such that μ(U) > 0 for every nonempty open set U ⊂ G?

Let G be a paratopological group, that is, a group equipped with a topology such that the multiplication map G × G → G is jointly continuous, with no assumption that inversion is continuous. Suppose that G is right ω-bounded in the sense that for every neighborhood U of the identity element e there exists a countable subset F ⊂ G such that G = U F. Must G then be left ω-bounded, meaning that for every neighborhood U of e there exists a countable subset F ⊂ G such that G = F U?

Does there exist an o-bounded topological group G—and even a metrizable one—such that Player I has a winning strategy in the Open-Finite game OF(G)? Here, G is called o-bounded if for every sequence (U_n)_{n∈ω} of neighborhoods of the identity (equivalently, of the origin) there exist finite sets F_n ⊂ G such that G ⊂ ⋃_{n∈ω} F_n U_n; in OF(G), at inning n, Player I chooses such a neighborhood U_n and Player II chooses a finite set F_n ⊂ G, and Player II wins exactly when G ⊂ ⋃_{n∈ω} F_n U_n.

Let A ⊂ R be a compact set, and assume that its difference set A - A := {a - a′ : a, a′ ∈ A} is a neighborhood of 0 in R (equivalently, contains an open interval about 0). Must the fourfold sumset 4A := A + A + A + A = {a1 + a2 + a3 + a4 : a1, a2, a3, a4 ∈ A} have non-empty interior in R?

Fix an integer n > 2. Is it true that for every n-tuple of real numbers theta_1, ..., theta_n one has lim inf as q -> +infty, with q ranging over positive integers, of q·||q theta_1||·...·||q theta_n|| equal to 0, where ||x|| denotes the distance from x to the nearest integer? ([studocu.com](https://www.studocu.com/hk/document/hong-kong-university-of-science-and-technology/general-physics-with-calculus/on-open-problems-in-diophantine-approximation-1202/146248134))

For every integer n >= 2, let Lambda be a full lattice in R^(n+1), and define its multiplicative minimum by N(Lambda) = inf{|x_1 x_2 ... x_(n+1)| : x = (x_1, ..., x_(n+1)) in Lambda \ {0}}. If N(Lambda) > 0, must Lambda be an algebraic lattice in the paper’s sense—namely, a lattice arising from a full Z-module in a totally real algebraic number field K of degree n+1 under the embedding of K into R^(n+1) given by its n+1 real embeddings?

Let n\in\mathbb{N}, let \mathcal{R}_n := \{\mathbf r=(r_1,\dots,r_n)\in[0,\infty)^n : r_1+\cdots+r_n=1\}, and for \mathbf r\in\mathcal{R}_n define
Bad(\mathbf r) := \left\{\mathbf y=(y_1,\dots,y_n)\in\mathbb{R}^n : \exists c(\mathbf y)>0\ \text{such that}\ \max_{1\le i\le n} \|qy_i\|^{1/r_i} \ge c(\mathbf y) q^{-1}\ \text{for all}\ q\in\mathbb{N}\right\},
with the convention \|qy_i\|^{1/0}=0. Is it true that for every finite or countable subset W\subset\mathcal{R}_n one has
\dim_H\!\left(\bigcap_{\mathbf r\in W} Bad(\mathbf r)\right)=n?

Fix a prime number p. Let ||x|| denote the distance from x to the nearest integer, and for a positive integer q write q = p^{ν_p(q)}q_1 with gcd(q_1,p)=1, so that |q|_p = p^{-ν_p(q)}. Is it true that for every real number θ one has lim inf_{q -> +infty, q in Z_+} q |q|_p ||qθ|| = 0? This is the de Mathan-Teulié p-adic (mixed) Littlewood conjecture.

For M > 2, determine the correct order, as M -> infinity, of the best universal lower bound c(M) with the following property: for every sequence of real numbers {t_j}_{j>=1} satisfying t_{j+1}/t_j >= 1 + 1/M for all j >= 1, there exists a real number alpha such that ||alpha t_j|| > c(M) for all j >= 1, where ||x|| denotes distance to the nearest integer. Peres-Schlag’s Theorem 9 gives c(M) >= gamma/(M log M) for some absolute constant gamma > 0, while the example in (13) shows that for every large integer M there are such sequences for which every alpha has ||alpha t_j|| <= C/M for infinitely many j, so the optimal homogeneous order cannot exceed constant/M. Can Theorem 9 be improved, and what is the optimal dependence on M in this homogeneous case (equivalently, is the true order constant/M up to absolute factors, or does an additional logarithmic loss remain unavoidable)?

Let ||·|| denote distance to the nearest integer. Theorem 8 states that if psi:[1,∞)->(0,∞) is increasing, satisfies psi(t)->+infinity as t->+infinity, and for every w >= 1 obeys sup_{x >= 1} psi(wx)/psi(x) < +infinity, then there exist real numbers theta_1, theta_2 that are linearly independent over Z together with 1, and real numbers eta_1, eta_2, such that inf_{x in Z_+} x psi(x) ||x theta_1 - eta_1|| ||x theta_2 - eta_2|| > 0. Does this conclusion remain true when psi is replaced by a positive constant function psi(t) = psi_0 > 0 for all t?

Let α,β ∈ (0,1) with α+β=1, and write ||x|| for the distance from x to the nearest integer. Define
BAD(α,β) = {(θ1,θ2) ∈ R^2 : inf_{q∈Z_{>0}} max(q^α||qθ1||, q^β||qθ2||) > 0}.
For a fixed vector Θ=(θ1,θ2) ∈ R^2, define its twisted inhomogeneous weighted badly approximable set by
BAD^Θ(α,β) = {(η1,η2) ∈ R^2 : inf_{q∈Z_{>0}} max(q^α||qθ1-η1||, q^β||qθ2-η2||) > 0}.
Harrap proved that if Θ ∈ BAD(α,β), then BAD^Θ(α,β) has full Hausdorff dimension. Is it true that for every Θ ∈ R^2, without assuming Θ ∈ BAD(α,β), one still has dim_H BAD^Θ(α,β)=2?

Fix integers m,n>=1 and fix norms |.|_m on R^m and |.|_n on R^n. For a real matrix Theta in Mat_{n,m}(R) satisfying the paper's nondegeneracy assumption, let z_nu=(x_nu,y_nu) in Z^m x Z^n be the sequence of best-approximation vectors to Theta with respect to these norms, ordered so that M_nu:=|x_nu|_m is strictly increasing. Define G(Theta):=lim inf_{nu->infinity} M_nu^(1/nu). What is the sharp universal lower bound, depending only on m, n, |.|_m, and |.|_n, for G(Theta); equivalently, what is the exact value of inf{G(Theta): Theta in Mat_{n,m}(R) satisfies the paper's nondegeneracy condition}?

Let \Theta=(\theta_1,\theta_2)\in\mathbb R^2 be such that 1,\theta_1,\theta_2 are linearly independent over \mathbb Q, and for t\ge 1 define
\psi_+(t)=\min\{\,\|\theta_1 x_1+\theta_2 x_2\|: x_1,x_2\in\mathbb Z_{>0},\ \max(x_1,x_2)\le t\,\},
where ||\cdot|| denotes distance to the nearest integer. Define
\omega_+(\Theta)=\sup\{\gamma>0: \liminf_{t\to\infty} t^\gamma\psi_+(t)<\infty\}.
What is the exact value of
\inf_{\Theta}\omega_+(\Theta),
where the infimum is over all such \Theta? Equivalently, given Schmidt's lower bound \omega_+(\Theta)\ge \varphi=(1+\sqrt5)/2 for every \Theta and Moshchevitin's upper bound \inf_{\Theta}\omega_+(\Theta)\le \sigma, where \sigma is the largest real root of x^4-2x^2-4x+1\approx 1.94696, determine the true optimal exponent in this positive-integer two-variable problem.

For the first open higher-dimensional case m = 3—and analogously for each fixed m ≥ 3—does there exist a vector Θ = (θ_1, ..., θ_m) ∈ R^m such that 1, θ_1, ..., θ_m are linearly independent over Z and such that, with
ω_+(Θ) := sup { γ ∈ R : ||θ_1 x_1 + ... + θ_m x_m|| < (max_{1 ≤ i ≤ m} x_i)^(-γ) for infinitely many (x_1, ..., x_m) ∈ Z_{>0}^m },
one has ω_+(Θ) < 2?

Does there exist an absolute constant M such that for every positive integer q there is an integer a with 1 <= a < q and gcd(a,q)=1 for which the regular finite continued fraction of the reduced rational a/q, written a/q = [0; b_1, ..., b_s], has all partial quotients bounded by M (that is, b_j <= M for every j)? Equivalently, can one choose a universal bound on partial quotients that works for some reduced fraction with every denominator q? Zaremba's original form of the conjecture asks whether one may take M = 5.

Fix an integer s>=2 and a digit set D={d_0,...,d_k} subset {0,1,...,s-1} with 0=d_0<d_1<...<d_k<s, 1<=k<=s-2, and gcd(d_1,...,d_k)=1. For N in N define K_s^D(N) = {x in N_0 : x<N and x = sum_{j=0}^h delta_j s^j for some h>=0 with each delta_j in D}. Is it true that there exists a constant sigma = sigma(s) > 0 such that, for every integer m>=1 with gcd(m,s)=1 and every N > m^sigma, the set K_s^D(N) contains an element from every residue class modulo m; equivalently, for every lambda in Z/mZ there exists x in K_s^D(N) with x congruent to lambda mod m?

Let p be a prime, let U\subset (\mathbb Z/p\mathbb Z)^\times be a multiplicative subgroup, let v\in (\mathbb Z/p\mathbb Z)^\times, and put R=vU. Theorem 29 in arXiv:1202.4539 asserts that if |R|\ge 10^8 p^{7/8}(\log p)^{5/2}, then there exists a\in R such that, writing a/p=[b_1,\dots,b_\ell] for the finite continued-fraction expansion of a/p, one has \sum_{j=1}^\ell b_j\ll \log p\,\log\log p (and hence, by the preceding discrepancy estimate used in the paper, D(a,p)\ll \log p\,\log\log p). Can the exponent 7/8 in this size hypothesis be replaced by some smaller absolute exponent \beta<7/8, uniformly in p, U, and v, while keeping the same conclusion?

For fixed s >= 2 and q >= 2, and for a = (a_1,...,a_s) in Z^s with gcd(a_1,...,a_s,q) = 1, let K_q(a) = {({a_1 k/q},...,{a_s k/q}) : k = 1,...,q} subset [0,1)^s be the s-dimensional Korobov-Hlawka point set. Let disc(K_q(a)) denote its discrepancy from the uniform distribution with respect to axis-parallel half-open boxes, and set Delta_q(a) := q * disc(K_q(a)). Is it true that for every fixed dimension s one has min_a Delta_q(a) <<_s (log q)^(s-1) as q -> infinity? In other words, can one remove the extra factor log log q from the best known general upper bound min_a Delta_q(a) <<_s (log q)^(s-1) log log q?

Let ?(x):[0,1]->[0,1] denote the Minkowski question mark function, and for each n in N define d_n := ∫_0^1 cos(2π n x) d?(x), where d?(x) is the Stieltjes measure associated with ?. Prove or disprove that d_n -> 0 as n -> infinity.

Please verify the paper ID: arXiv:1202.4539 contains no question about fixed points of the Minkowski question-mark function, so this draft cannot be refined into a paper-faithful stand-alone research question for that paper.

Let xi_{j,n} (j = 1, ..., 2^n) denote the Stern-Brocot points at level n, in the indexing used in formula (67), and let ?(x) be Minkowski’s question-mark function. Define R_n by
R_n := sum_{j=1}^{2^n} (xi_{j,n} - j/2^n)^2 - 2^n integral_0^1 (?(x)-x)^2 dx.
Is it true that R_n tends to 0 as n tends to infinity? ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/abs/2504.07456?utm_source=openai))

Let x=[0;a_1,a_2,\dots]\in(0,1) be irrational, and let ?(x)=g_{1/2}(x) denote Minkowski's question-mark function. Determine the best possible constants kappa_1 and kappa_2 such that limsup_{t\to\infty}(a_1+\cdots+a_t)/t<kappa_1 implies ?'(x)=+infinity, while liminf_{t\to\infty}(a_1+\cdots+a_t)/t>kappa_2 implies ?'(x)=0.

Let T(n) be the set of partitions lambda of the positive integer n for which the positive multiplicities of the part sizes are pairwise distinct, and let f(n)=|T(n)|. Theorem 3.1 proves that ln f(n) ~ (6^(1/3)/3) n^(1/3) ln n as n -> infinity. Determine the lower-order asymptotic terms of ln f(n) beyond this leading term.

Let T(n) be the set of ordinary partitions of the positive integer n in which the positive multiplicities of the part sizes are pairwise distinct (the paper’s 'Wilf partitions'), and let f(n)=|T(n)|. Theorem 3.1 shows only that ln f(n)∼(6n)^{1/3}ln((6n)^{1/3}) as n→∞. Determine a first-order asymptotic formula for f(n) itself; that is, find an explicit main term A(n) such that f(n)∼A(n) as n→∞.

Let T(n) be the set of ordinary integer partitions of the positive integer n in which the multiplicities of the distinct part sizes that occur are pairwise distinct (these are the Wilf partitions), and let f(n)=|T(n)|. Is it true that f(n+1) ≥ f(n) for every integer n ≥ 1?

For each positive integer n, let T(n) be the set of Wilf partitions of n, written canonically as pairs (m, p) = ((m_1, ..., m_r), (p_1, ..., p_r)) with r >= 1, m_1, ..., m_r distinct positive integers, 1 <= p_1 < ... < p_r distinct part sizes, and sum_{i=1}^r m_i p_i = n. Define the involution σ_n : T(n) -> T(n) by σ_n((m, p)) = (p_π, m_π), where π is the permutation of {1, ..., r} such that m_{π(1)} < ... < m_{π(r)}. As n -> infinity, find asymptotics for the number of fixed points of σ_n, that is, for |{(m, p) in T(n) : σ_n((m, p)) = (m, p)}|.|

Let X = (Xn)n≥0 be the one-dimensional nearest-neighbor excited random walk on Z, started at 0 and defined under the averaged law P0 associated with a cookie-environment law P on Ω = M{-1,+1}^{Z×N} via the transition rule (1.1). Find hypotheses on the environment law P that force a directional zero-one law, namely that P0[supn≥0 Xn = +∞], P0[infn≥0 Xn = -∞] ∈ {0,1}; and, equivalently whenever P satisfies (SE) and (EL), that P0[Xn → +∞], P0[Xn → -∞] ∈ {0,1}. ([sites.math.duke.edu](https://sites.math.duke.edu/~rtd/readS18/KosZer.pdf))

Let X=(X_n)_{n≥0} be the nearest-neighbor excited random walk on Z started at 0, with quenched transition rule P_{0,ω}[X_{n+1}=X_n+e | X_0,...,X_n] = ω(X_n,e,#\{0≤k≤n : X_k=X_n\}) for e in {-1,+1}, and let P be the law of the cookie environment. Assume that the stack process (ω(z,·,·))_{z in Z} is stationary and ergodic under spatial shifts ((SE)); that there exists a deterministic M in N such that P-a.s. M(z)≤M for every z in Z, where M(z):=inf{j in N_0 : ω(z,e,i)=1/2 for all e in {-1,+1} and all i>j} ((BD)); and that for each z in Z and e in {-1,+1}, P[forall i in N : ω(z,e,i)>0]>0 ((WEL)). Writing δ:=E[sum_{i≥1}(2ω(0,1,i)-1)] (equivalently δ=E[sum_{e in {-1,+1}, i≥1}ω(0,e,i)e]), is the analogue of Theorem 3.10(3.10) still true with (SE) in place of (IID): namely, must X be recurrent (every site visited infinitely often P0-a.s.) when δ is in [-1,1], transient to the right (X_n→+∞ P0-a.s.) when δ>1, and transient to the left (X_n→-∞ P0-a.s.) when δ<-1?

Let X = (X_n)_{n >= 0} be the one-dimensional nearest-neighbor excited random walk on Z started at X_0 = 0, under the annealed law P_0, in a random cookie environment omega as defined in equation (1.1). Assume the hypotheses of Theorem 3.10, namely either (i) (SE) and (POS1) with P[omega(0,1,.) = (1,1/2,1/2,...)] < 1, or (ii) (IID), (BD), and (WEL), and assume that the walk is transient in the sense of Theorem 3.10 (equivalently, in d = 1, delta > 1 or delta < -1, where delta = E[sum_{i >= 1}(2 omega(0,1,i) - 1)] is the expected total drift in a cookie stack). Determine the annealed probability P_0[forall n >= 1 : X_n != 0], i.e. the probability that the excited random walk never returns to its starting point.

Let X=(X_n)_{n≥0} be a nearest-neighbor excited random walk on Z^d, d≥2, started at 0 under the averaged law P_0 associated with a cookie-environment law P on Ω, and for each nonzero direction ℓ∈R^d define A_ℓ := {lim_{n→∞} X_n·ℓ = ∞}. Find assumptions on P that imply the directional-transience zero-one law P_0[A_ℓ] ∈ {0,1} for every ℓ∈R^d with ℓ≠0. In particular, is this zero-one law already implied by (IID), meaning that the cookie stacks (ω(z,·,·))_{z∈Z^d} are i.i.d. under P; (BD), meaning that there exists a deterministic M<∞ such that P-a.s. M(z)≤M for all z, where M(z)=inf{j∈N_0: ω(z,e,i)=1/(2d) for all e∈E and all i>j}; and (UEL), meaning that there exists κ>0 such that P-a.s. ω(z,e,i)≥κ for all z∈Z^d, e∈E, and i∈N?

Let X=(X_n)_{n≥0} be the excited random walk on Z^d, d ≥ 2, started at 0, in a nearest-neighbor cookie environment ω=(ω(z,e,i))_{z∈Z^d,e∈E,i∈N}, where E={±e_1,...,±e_d}. Assume that under the environment law P the cookie stacks (ω(z,·,·))_{z∈Z^d} are i.i.d. and uniformly elliptic, i.e. there exists κ>0 such that P-a.s. ω(z,e,i)≥κ for every z∈Z^d, e∈E, and i∈N. Under the averaged law P_0, is X necessarily either recurrent, meaning that every site z∈Z^d is visited infinitely often P_0-a.s., or transient, meaning that no site is visited infinitely often P_0-a.s.?

Let P be a probability law on cookie environments Ω = M_E^{Z^d×N}, where E = {±e_j : 1 ≤ j ≤ d}, and let X = (X_n)_{n≥0} be the corresponding nearest-neighbor excited random walk on Z^d started at 0 under the averaged law P0. Assume d ≥ 2, that P satisfies either (IID) or (SE), and that P is uniformly elliptic in the sense that there exists κ > 0 such that P-a.s. ω(z,e,i) ≥ κ for all z in Z^d, e in E, and i in N. Suppose moreover that P is balanced, i.e. P-a.s. ω(z,e,i) = ω(z,-e,i) for every z in Z^d, e in E, and i in N. Must X be recurrent when d = 2, in the sense that every site of Z^d is visited infinitely often P0-a.s., and transient when d ≥ 3, in the sense that no site is visited infinitely often (equivalently, |X_n| → ∞) P0-a.s.? ([sites.math.duke.edu](https://sites.math.duke.edu/~rtd/readS18/KosZer.pdf))

Let X=(X_n)_{n≥0} be the nearest-neighbor excited random walk on Z^d, where d≥1, started at 0 and defined by (1.1), in a random cookie environment ω such that the family of cookie stacks (ω(z,·,·))_{z∈Z^d} is i.i.d. under P and satisfies ellipticity (EL): for every z∈Z^d, e∈E={±e_j:1≤j≤d}, and i∈N, one has P-a.s. ω(z,e,i)>0. Fix a nonzero vector ℓ∈R^d. Is it true that X_n·ℓ/n converges to 0 P_0-a.s. on the event {|X_n|→∞}^c as n→∞? ([math.sinica.edu.tw](https://www.math.sinica.edu.tw/bulletins/20131/2013106.pdf?utm_source=openai))

For the nearest-neighbor one-dimensional excited random walk X=(X_n)_{n>=0} on Z started at 0 in a cookie environment omega, assume the cookie stacks (omega(z,.,.))_{z in Z} are i.i.d. and weakly elliptic, meaning P[forall i>=1: omega(0,1,i)>0] > 0 and P[forall i>=1: omega(0,-1,i)>0] > 0. Let delta := E[sum_{e in {+1,-1}, i>=1} omega(0,e,i)e] in [0,infinity] denote the expected total drift per stack, and let v := lim_{n->infinity} X_n/n be the almost sure speed (whose existence is known under (SE)+(POS1)). Theorem 5.2 proves under (BD), i.e. under a deterministic uniform bound on the number of non-placebo cookies per site, that v=0 for delta in [0,2] and v>0 for delta>2. Does this same ballisticity criterion remain valid if (BD) is replaced by (POS1), i.e. if every cookie has nonnegative drift to the +1 direction, equivalently omega(0,1,i) >= 1/2 almost surely for every i>=1?

For the one-dimensional nearest-neighbor excited random walk X = (X_n)_{n≥0} on Z started at 0 under the averaged law P0, let δ := E[∑_{i≥1} ∑_{e∈{-1,+1}} ω(0,e,i)e] be the expected total drift per site. In the critical case δ = 1, Theorem 6.3 shows that under (IID), (BD), and (WEL) there exists b > 0 such that X_[n·]/(b√(n log n)) converges in distribution in D[0,∞) with the J1 topology to S(·), where B is standard Brownian motion and S(t) := max_{s≤t} B(s). Does this same J1 functional limit theorem remain valid if one replaces (IID), (BD), and (WEL) by the hypothesis package (6.2), namely: stationary ergodic cookie stacks (SE), nonnegative drift of every cookie toward +1 (POS1), uniform ellipticity (UEL), and the integrability condition E[sup{i∈N : |ω(0,1,i) - 1/2| ≥ ε}] < ∞ for each ε > 0? If so, can the nonnegative-drift assumption (POS1) also be removed?

For the nearest-neighbor excited random walk X = (X_n)_{n≥0} on Z^d started at 0 and defined from a random cookie environment ω ∈ Ω := M_E^{Z^d×N} by equation (1.1), find probability measures P on (Ω, F), excluding the RWRE case in which ω(z, e, i) is P-a.s. independent of i, such that for P-almost every environment ω the quenched law P_{0,ω} of either X_n (for d ≥ 1) or, in the one-dimensional setting, the hitting time T_n := inf{m ≥ 0 : X_m = n}, after suitable centering and normalization as needed (possibly depending on ω), converges weakly as n → ∞ to a nondegenerate limit distribution.

Let X be a finite pure monomial order ideal in variables y_1,...,y_r, and write its h-vector as h(X)=(1,h_1,...,h_e), where e is the common degree of the maximal monomials of X (the socle degree) and the type t is the number of maximal monomials. A sequence is unimodal if it is nondecreasing up to some index and nonincreasing thereafter. What is the largest integer t such that every pure O-sequence of type t is unimodal, independently of the codimension r and the socle degree e? In particular, is every pure O-sequence of type 2 unimodal in arbitrary codimension? ([www3.nd.edu](https://www3.nd.edu/~jmiglior/MNZ5POSexp.pdf))

Fix a codimension r. Let h = (1, h1, ..., he) be a pure O-sequence in r variables, i.e. the h-vector of a pure monomial order ideal in K[y1, ..., yr], where e is arbitrary and the type is the number of maximal monomials. Determine the largest threshold t = t(r) such that every pure O-sequence of codimension r and type at most t is unimodal, where unimodal means weakly increasing up to some index and weakly decreasing thereafter. ([www3.nd.edu](https://www3.nd.edu/~jmiglior/MNZ5POSexp.pdf))

Fix a positive integer r. Let h = (1, h_1, ..., h_e) be a pure O-sequence, i.e. the h-vector of a finite pure monomial order ideal, with codimension h_1 = r and socle degree e (the common degree of its maximal monomials). What is the largest integer e for which every pure O-sequence of codimension r and socle degree e is unimodal, meaning weakly increasing up to some degree and weakly decreasing thereafter?

Determine the least integer r for which there exists, over any field K, a finite pure monomial order ideal X ⊂ K[y1,...,yr] whose maximal monomials all have degree 4 and whose h-vector (i.e. the sequence counting monomials of X in each degree) is h(X)=(1,r,h2,h3,h4) and is nonunimodal.

For each fixed positive integer e, let P(*,e,t) denote the finite set of h-vectors h=(1,h1,...,he) that occur as Hilbert functions of standard graded artinian monomial level algebras A=K[x1,...,xr]/I, where r is allowed to vary, I is a monomial ideal, and the socle soc(A)=0:_A(x1,...,xr) is concentrated in degree e and has K-dimension t; equivalently, P(*,e,t) is the set of pure O-sequences of socle degree e and type t over all codimensions. Determine, as t tends to infinity, the asymptotic behavior of #P(*,e,t), and in particular the correct order of magnitude of #P(*,e,t). ([www3.nd.edu](https://www3.nd.edu/~jmiglior/MNZ5POSexp.pdf))

What is the smallest integer n such that there exists a pure simplicial complex on n vertices whose rank vector (that is, its pure f-vector, counting faces in each rank and beginning with 1 for the empty face) is nonunimodal?

Let Δ be a finite matroid complex on V = {1, ..., r}, i.e. a pure simplicial complex such that every restriction Δ|W to a subset W ⊆ V is also pure. Let f(Δ) denote its face vector, and let h(Δ) denote the h-vector of its Stanley-Reisner ring K[Δ] = K[x1, ..., xr]/IΔ, where IΔ = (xF = ∏_{i∈F} xi : F ∉ Δ). Must f(Δ) always be unimodal, or even log-concave? Likewise, must h(Δ) always be unimodal, or even log-concave?

For every finite matroid complex Δ on V = {1, ..., r}, let S = K[x_1, ..., x_r] be the standard graded polynomial ring over a field K, and let I_Δ = (x_F : F not in Δ) be its Stanley-Reisner ideal. Since K[Δ] = S/I_Δ is Cohen-Macaulay and level, its h-vector h(K[Δ]) is the Hilbert function of any artinian reduction. Is h(K[Δ]) always a pure O-sequence, i.e. the Hilbert function of some artinian monomial level algebra?

Let K be a field of characteristic zero, let R = K[x_1, ..., x_r], and let I = (f_1, ..., f_r) be an Artinian homogeneous complete intersection in R (equivalently, f_1, ..., f_r is a homogeneous regular sequence, so A = R/I is finite-dimensional). For r >= 4, must A have the Weak Lefschetz Property; that is, for a general linear form L in R_1, is the multiplication map times L: A_i -> A_{i+1} of maximal rank for every integer i?

Does the Interval Conjecture for Pure O-sequences hold in codimension 3? Precisely: let h=(1,3,h_2,...,h_e) be the h-vector of a finite pure monomial order ideal in K[y_1,y_2,y_3] (equivalently, a pure O-sequence of codimension 3, with socle degree e). If, for some index i with 2<=i<=e and some integer alpha>0, both (1,3,h_2,...,h_i,...,h_e) and (1,3,h_2,...,h_i+alpha,...,h_e) are pure O-sequences, must every intermediate sequence (1,3,h_2,...,h_i+beta,...,h_e) with beta=0,1,...,alpha also be a pure O-sequence? The paper proves this interval property for socle degree e<=3 in arbitrary codimension; is it true without any bound on e when the codimension is 3?

For each integer q>=2, let v=q^2+q+1 and define h(q)=(1, v, vC(q+1,2), vC(q+1,3), ..., vC(q+1,q+1)). Determine exactly for which q the sequence h(q) is a pure O-sequence; equivalently, determine exactly for which q there exists a pure simplicial complex on v vertices with pure f-vector h(q), i.e. a Steiner system S(2,q+1,v), equivalently a finite projective plane of order q. ([www3.nd.edu](https://www3.nd.edu/~jmiglior/MNZ5POSexp.pdf))

Does there exist, over some (equivalently any) field K, a pure monomial order ideal X in K[y1,...,y21] whose maximal monomials all have degree 5 and whose degree counts are h(X)=(1,21,210,1330,5985,1197)? In other words, is (1,21,210,1330,5985,1197) a pure O-sequence?

Does there exist an explicit family (f_n)_{n>=1}, where each f_n : F_2^n -> F_2 and the language L = { x in {0,1}^* : f_|x|(x) = 1 } lies in NP, such that for every n and every polynomial p : F_2^n -> F_2 whose unique multilinear representative in F_2[x_1,...,x_n] has total degree at most floor(log_2 n), one has |E_{x uniform in F_2^n}[(-1)^(f_n(x)+p(x))]| <= 1/n? ([cs.cmu.edu](https://www.cs.cmu.edu/~odonnell/papers/aobf-open-problems.pdf))

Tomaszewski’s Conjecture: For every positive integer n and every vector a = (a_1,…,a_n) ∈ R^n with Σ_{i=1}^n a_i^2 = 1, if x = (x_1,…,x_n) is chosen uniformly from {-1,1}^n (equivalently, x_1,…,x_n are independent uniform signs), must one have Pr[|⟨a,x⟩| ≤ 1] = Pr[|Σ_{i=1}^n a_i x_i| ≤ 1] ≥ 1/2? ([cs.cmu.edu](https://www.cs.cmu.edu/~odonnell/papers/aobf-open-problems.pdf))

For each fixed rho in (0,1), let T_rho denote the standard noise operator on the discrete cube, defined by (T_rho f)(x) = E[f(y)] where x is uniform on {-1,1}^n and y is a rho-correlated copy of x. Is it true that there exists a function a_rho(t) = o(1/t) as t -> infinity such that, for every n >= 1 and every function f : {-1,1}^n -> [0,infinity) with E[f] = 1, one has Pr_x[(T_rho f)(x) >= t] <= a_rho(t) for all sufficiently large t?

Does there exist a universal polynomial p such that, for every integer n >= 1 and every Boolean function f : {-1,1}^n -> {-1,1}, the degree deg(f) of the unique multilinear real polynomial agreeing with f on {-1,1}^n satisfies deg(f) <= p(s(f)), where s(f) = max_{x in {-1,1}^n} |{i in [n] : f(x) != f(x^{\oplus i})}| and x^{\oplus i} denotes x with its i-th coordinate flipped?

For every n >= 1 and k >= 1, let f : {-1,1}^n -> {-1,1} range over all degree-k polynomial threshold functions, in the standard sense that f(x) = sgn(Q(x)) for some real multilinear polynomial Q of degree at most k with Q(x) != 0 for all x in {-1,1}^n. Must the maximum possible total influence
I[f] = sum_{i=1}^n Pr_x[f(x) != f(x_1,...,-x_i,...,x_n)]
be attained by a symmetric function depending only on S_n = x_1 + ... + x_n, namely by a function of the form f(x) = sgn(p(S_n)) where p is a real univariate polynomial of degree k whose sign alternates on the k+1 attainable values of S_n closest to 0?

For every integer n ≥ 1, every real C ≥ 1, and every nonempty set A ⊆ F_2^n with sumset A + A := {a + a' : a, a' ∈ A} satisfying |A + A| ≤ C|A|, is it true that A is contained in the union of at most C^{O(1)} affine subspaces of F_2^n, each having cardinality at most |A|?

For every n >= 1, every Boolean function f : {-1,1}^n -> {-1,1} computable by a DNF with s > 1 terms, and every ε in (0,1/2], if f has Fourier-Walsh expansion f(x)=Σ_{S⊆[n]} hat f(S) χ_S(x) under the uniform measure on {-1,1}^n, where χ_S(x)=∏_{i∈S} x_i, must there exist a set F⊆2^[n] and an absolute constant C such that Σ_{S∉F} hat f(S)^2 <= ε and |F| <= s^{C log(1/ε)}?

Bernoulli Conjecture. Does there exist an absolute constant C > 0 such that for every integer n >= 1 and every finite set T subset of R^n, if one defines b(T) = E[max_{t in T} <t, epsilon>] for epsilon with independent uniform coordinates in {-1,1}, and g(T) = E[max_{t in T} <t, G>] for G with independent N(0,1) coordinates, then there exists a finite set T' subset of R^n such that g(T') <= C b(T) and, for every t in T, there exists t' in T' with ||t - t'||_1 <= C b(T)?

Is there a universal constant C > 0 such that for every integer n ≥ 1 and every Boolean function f : {-1,1}^n → {-1,1}, if f has Fourier–Walsh expansion f(x) = ∑_{S⊆[n]} widehat{f}(S) χ_S(x), then its spectral entropy H[widehat{f}^2] := ∑_{S⊆[n]} widehat{f}(S)^2 log_2(1 / widehat{f}(S)^2) satisfies H[widehat{f}^2] ≤ C · I[f], where I[f] := ∑_{S⊆[n]} |S| widehat{f}(S)^2 is the total influence of f?

Let n be an odd positive integer, and let f:{-1,1}^n -> {-1,1} be a linear threshold function, i.e. f(x)=sgn(a_0 + sum_{i=1}^n a_i x_i) for some real coefficients a_0,...,a_n. For rho in [0,1], define Stab_rho[f]=E[f(x)f(y)], where x and y are uniform rho-correlated points of {-1,1}^n. Let Maj_n(x)=sgn(x_1+...+x_n). Is it true that for every rho in [0,1], one has Stab_rho[f] >= Stab_rho[Maj_n]?

Fix integers r >= 1 and odd n >= 1, and fix epsilon in (0,1/2). For each Boolean function f : {-1,1}^n -> {-1,1}, let X be uniform on {-1,1}^n, and conditional on X let Y^(1),...,Y^(r) be independent epsilon-noisy copies of X, meaning that for every i in {1,...,r} and j in {1,...,n}, Y_j^(i) = X_j with probability 1 - epsilon and Y_j^(i) = -X_j with probability epsilon, independently over all i and j. Define P(f) = Pr[f(Y^(1)) = f(Y^(2)) = ... = f(Y^(r))]. Among all odd functions f (that is, f(-x) = -f(x) for every x), is P(f) always maximized by a majority function Maj_k on some odd number k <= n of input coordinates, viewed as an n-variable function by ignoring the remaining n - k coordinates?

Is it true that there exists an absolute constant C such that for every n,k >= 1, every Boolean function f : {-1,1}^n -> {-1,1} that is the Boolean AND of k linear threshold functions h_j(x)=sgn(a_{j,0}+sum_{i=1}^n a_{j,i} x_i) (so f(x)=1 iff h_1(x)=...=h_k(x)=1), and every noise rate delta in [0,1], one has NS_delta[f] <= C sqrt(log k) sqrt(delta), where NS_delta[f] := Pr[f(x) != f(y)] for x uniform on {-1,1}^n and y obtained from x by independently flipping each coordinate with probability delta?

For every odd integer n and every p with 0<=p<1/2, let f:{-1,1}^n->{-1,1} be unbiased, i.e. E_{x uniform on {-1,1}^n}[f(x)]=0. Let z=(z_1,...,z_n) in {-1,0,1}^n have independent coordinates with P(z_i=1)=P(z_i=-1)=p/2 and P(z_i=0)=1-p. Writing f^{ml} for the unique real multilinear polynomial that agrees with f on {-1,1}^n, is it always true that E_z[|f^{ml}(z)|] <= E_z[|Maj_n^{ml}(z)|], where Maj_n(x)=sgn(x_1+...+x_n) is the n-bit majority function?

Does there exist an absolute polynomial p(ε) = c·ε^C with c,C > 0 such that for every n, every ε > 0, and every subset A ⊆ F_2^n for which one must delete at least ε·2^n elements to obtain a triangle-free set (that is, a set containing no x,y ∈ F_2^n with x, y, and x+y all in the set), the ordered triangle density satisfies Pr[x ∈ A, y ∈ A, x+y ∈ A] ≥ p(ε), where x and y are chosen independently and uniformly from F_2^n?

For every fixed α ∈ (0,1], does there exist a constant C = C(α) such that, for every n and every set A ⊆ F_2^n with |A| ≥ α·2^n, the sumset A + A := {a + a' : a, a' ∈ A} contains a linear subspace V ≤ F_2^n whose codimension satisfies codim(V) = n - dim(V) ≤ C√n?

For every n,k∈N and every function f:{−1,1}^n→[−1,1] with Fourier expansion f(x)=sum_{S⊆[n]} fhat(S) χ_S(x) satisfying fhat(S)=0 whenever |S|>k, where Var[f]=sum_{S≠∅} fhat(S)^2 and Inf_i[f]=sum_{S∋i} fhat(S)^2 (equivalently, variance and influences are taken with respect to the uniform measure on {−1,1}^n), must there exist a coordinate i∈[n] and a universal constant C>0 such that Inf_i[f] ≥ (Var[f]/k)^C?

Fix a possibly infinite collection A = { (A_i, sigma_i) }_{i >= 1} of induced affine constraints over F_2, where for each i the constraint A_i = (a_{i,1}, ..., a_{i,m_i}) is an affine constraint on ell_i variables in the sense that a_{i,1}(X_1, ..., X_{ell_i}) = X_1 and, for j >= 2, a_{i,j}(X_1, ..., X_{ell_i}) = X_1 + sum_{t=2}^{ell_i} c_{i,j,t} X_t with c_{i,j,t} in F_2, and where sigma_i is in {0,1}^{m_i}. For each n, let P_n consist of all functions f : F_2^n -> {0,1} such that for every i there do not exist x_1, ..., x_{ell_i} in F_2^n with ( f(a_{i,1}(x_1, ..., x_{ell_i})), ..., f(a_{i,m_i}(x_1, ..., x_{ell_i})) ) = sigma_i. Must the property family P = {P_n}_{n >= 1} always admit a one-sided-error constant-query tester; that is, for every epsilon > 0, is there a query bound q_A(epsilon), independent of n, and a randomized oracle algorithm that makes at most q_A(epsilon) queries, always accepts every f in P_n, and rejects with probability at least 2/3 every f : F_2^n -> {0,1} that is epsilon-far from P_n?

For fixed n >= 1 and 0 <= rho, mu, nu <= 1, let gamma_n denote the standard Gaussian measure on R^n. Among all measurable sets A,B subseteq R^n with gamma_n(A)=mu, gamma_n(B)=nu, and A=-A, determine the minimum possible value of P[X in A, Y in B], where X,Z are independent N(0,I_n) random vectors and Y = rho X + sqrt(1-rho^2) Z (equivalently, (X,Y) are standard rho-correlated n-dimensional Gaussian vectors).

Let n ≥ 2 and 3 ≤ q ≤ n+1. Let γ_n denote the standard Gaussian measure on R^n, and for ρ ∈ [-1,1] define the Ornstein–Uhlenbeck operator by T_ρ f(x) = ∫_{R^n} f(ρx + √(1-ρ^2)y) dγ_n(y). If A_1,...,A_q ⊂ R^n is a measurable partition of R^n, meaning ⋃_{i=1}^q A_i = R^n and γ_n(A_i ∩ A_j) = 0 for i ≠ j, and if S_1,...,S_q is the regular simplicial conical partition determined by the vertices z_1,...,z_q of a regular simplex centered at the origin in R^n, with S_i given by the Voronoi cell where ⟨x,z_i⟩ is maximal (up to Gaussian-null tie sets), is it true that: (i) for every ρ ∈ (0,1], among all such partitions satisfying γ_n(A_i) = 1/q for all i, the quantity J(A_1,...,A_q) = Σ_{i=1}^q ∫_{R^n} 1_{A_i}(x) T_ρ(1_{A_i})(x) dγ_n(x) is maximized by the regular simplicial conical partition; and (ii) for every ρ ∈ [-1,0), among all measurable partitions of R^n, the same quantity J is minimized by the regular simplicial conical partition?

Is it true that for every Boolean function f:{-1,1}^n->{-1,1}, if f(x)=sum_{S subseteq [n]} hat f(S) prod_{j in S} x_j is its standard Fourier-Walsh (equivalently, unique multilinear real) expansion under the uniform measure, and deg(f)=max{|S|: hat f(S) != 0}, then one has sum_{i=1}^n hat f({i}) <= sqrt(deg(f))?

Fix d∈N and ε∈(0,1). Determine the least integer k=k(d,ε) such that the following holds: for every n∈N, every degree-d multivariate polynomial p:ℝ^n→ℝ, and every ℝ^n-valued random vector X=(X1,…,Xn) with the properties that each Xi has the standard Gaussian distribution and every k-tuple Xi1,…,Xik is independent, one has |Pr[p(X)≥0]−Pr[p(Z)≥0]|≤ε, where Z∼N(0,In) is the standard n-dimensional Gaussian. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1204.6447))

For every fixed constant δ > 0, does there exist a constant c = c(δ) > 0 such that, for all n and s ≥ 1, every probability distribution φ on {0,1}^n satisfying |E_{y∼φ}[χ_S(y)]| ≤ s^{-c} for every nonempty S ⊆ [n] δ-fools every DNF formula on n variables with at most s terms? Equivalently, if f : {0,1}^n → {-1,1} is computable by a DNF of size at most s and φ is s^{-c}-biased in the above sense, must |E_{x∼U_n}[f(x)] - E_{y∼φ}[f(y)]| ≤ δ?

For every positive integer n, let IP_{2n}: F_2^{2n} -> {-1,1} be the inner-product-mod-2 function defined by IP_{2n}(x,y) = (-1)^{sum_{i=1}^n x_i y_i}, where x,y in F_2^n and the sum is taken modulo 2. Is it true that every real polynomial p(x_1,...,x_n,y_1,...,y_n), with no restriction on degree, such that p(x,y) > 0 exactly when IP_{2n}(x,y)=1 and p(x,y) < 0 exactly when IP_{2n}(x,y)=-1 for all (x,y) in {0,1}^{2n}, must contain at least 3^n nonzero monomials?
