For every fixed ε > 0, does there exist a polynomial p_ε such that every monotone Boolean function f : {-1,1}^n -> {-1,1} is ε-close, with respect to the uniform measure on {-1,1}^n, to a Boolean function g : {-1,1}^n -> {-1,1} that depends on at most p_ε(deg(f)) coordinates, where deg(f) denotes the degree of the standard multilinear polynomial representing f?

Let (f_n)_{n \ge 1} be a sequence of monotone Boolean functions f_n : {-1,1}^n -> {-1,1}, where monotone means that x_i \le y_i for all i implies f_n(x) \le f_n(y). For each n, define the total influence I[f_n] = \sum_{i=1}^n Pr_{x \in {-1,1}^n}[f_n(x) \ne f_n(x^{\oplus i})], where x^{\oplus i} is obtained from x by flipping its i-th coordinate, and define the maximum sensitivity sens[f_n] = \max_{x \in {-1,1}^n} |{ i \in [n] : f_n(x) \ne f_n(x^{\oplus i}) }|. Is it true that every such monotone family satisfies I[f_n] = o(sens[f_n]) as n -> infinity?

For each positive integer n, determine the minimum possible degree deg(f) of a real-valued function f:{-1,1}^n -> [-1,-2/3]∪[2/3,1], where deg(f) denotes the total degree of the unique multilinear polynomial over R agreeing with f on {-1,1}^n, subject to the conditions that f(x) ∈ [2/3,1] whenever sum_{i=1}^n x_i >= n/2 and f(x) ∈ [-1,-2/3] whenever sum_{i=1}^n x_i <= -n/2.

For each positive integer \(n\), let \(\mathrm{AND}:\mathbb{F}_2^n\to\{-1,1\}\) be the \{-1,1\}-valued indicator of the point \((1,\dots,1)\), i.e. \(\mathrm{AND}(1,\dots,1)=1\) and \(\mathrm{AND}(x)=-1\) for all \(x\neq(1,\dots,1)\). Suppose there exist polynomials \(q_1,\dots,q_m:\mathbb{F}_2^n\to\mathbb{F}_2\) of degree at most 2 and real coefficients \(c_1,\dots,c_m\) such that, for every \(x\in\mathbb{F}_2^n\), \(\mathrm{AND}(x)=\sum_{i=1}^m c_i(-1)^{q_i(x)}\). What lower bound, as a function of \(n\), must hold on the minimum possible number \(m\) of quadratic phase terms in such an exact representation?

Let A be a self-adjoint operator on a separable Hilbert space H, and let φ be a cyclic vector for A (more generally, in the paper’s rank-one perturbation setup, φ is allowed in H_{-1}(A) so that the perturbations are well defined). For each real alpha, define the rank-one perturbation A_alpha = A + alpha(·, φ)φ, and let mu and mu_alpha denote the scalar spectral measures of A and A_alpha with respect to φ. Characterize, in terms of the unperturbed spectral measure mu, the singular continuous part (mu_alpha)_{sc} of mu_alpha.

Let I be an interval in R and let B be a measurable subset of R. Does there exist a family {mu_beta}_{beta in R} of spectral measures arising from a family of rank-one perturbations such that, for every beta in B, the corresponding perturbation has singular spectrum dense in I and embedded there in absolutely continuous spectrum, while for every beta in R\B the corresponding operator has purely absolutely continuous spectrum on I?

Let H_ω be the discrete random Schrödinger operator on l^2(Z^2) given by H_ω = -Δ + Σ_{n∈Z^2} ω_n⟨·,δ_n⟩δ_n, where -Δ is the standard nearest-neighbor discrete Laplacian on Z^2 and {ω_n}_{n∈Z^2} are independent identically distributed real random variables with common law uniform on [-c,c]. Is it true that for every c>0, the operator H_ω has almost surely purely singular spectrum, i.e. no absolutely continuous spectral component?

Let H_omega be the standard discrete random Schrödinger operator on l^2(Z^d), with d >= 2, given by H_omega = -Delta + V_omega, where V_omega(n) = omega_n and the random variables {omega_n}_{n in Z^d} are i.i.d. Bernoulli with P(omega_n = 1) = P(omega_n = -1) = 1/2. Is it true that, for each fixed d >= 2, H_omega has almost surely purely singular spectrum; equivalently, does H_omega almost surely have no absolutely continuous spectral component?

Let T be a completely nonunitary contraction on a separable complex Hilbert space with equal finite defect indices (n,n), where n>1, and let Θ_T be its operator-valued Sz.-Nagy-Foias characteristic function. Can one develop a finite-rank Aleksandrov-Clark theory for the family of rank-n unitary perturbations of T that extends the classical rank-one Clark-operator proof to the non-inner operator-valued setting—namely, obtain a higher-rank analogue of the rank-one formulas in Proposition 1.2 and Theorem 1.3 for the adjoint Clark operator/normalized Cauchy transform, and from it recover by a Clark-theoretic argument that Θ_T is inner if and only if the corresponding unitary perturbations have purely singular spectral measures, together with explicit matrix-valued Radon-Nikodym formulas for the absolutely continuous parts of those measures?

Let U_A denote the rank-d unitary perturbations of a fixed unitary operator U on a complex separable Hilbert space, obtained by varying a d x d unitary parameter A on a fixed finite-dimensional cyclic perturbation subspace, so that the associated Clark/spectral data are matrix-valued measures M_A rather than scalar measures. For two distinct parameters A and B, what is the correct higher-rank analogue of the rank-one Aronszajn-Donoghue theorem: which statements about the singular parts survive, which fail if one only looks at the scalar traces tr M_A and tr M_B, and what modified matrix-valued notion of mutual singularity or orthogonality should replace scalar mutual singularity for the singular parts M_{A,s} and M_{B,s}?

In the rank-one Aleksandrov-Clark setting of Section 6 of arXiv:1205.4376, let theta be the non-inner scalar characteristic function, let Delta = (1-|theta|^2)^{1/2}, let K_theta be the Sz.-Nagy-Foias model space, and let Phi_1^*: L^2(mu) -> K_theta denote the adjoint Clark operator for the alpha = 1 Clark measure mu. Starting from formula (6.3), which expresses Phi_1^* f through the projection P_theta onto K_theta, derive the equivalent explicit Sz.-Nagy-Foias representation of Phi_1^* f in terms of boundary values of the regularized Cauchy transform (for example T_+ f and T_+ 1), so that no occurrence of P_theta remains. State the formula for both components of Phi_1^* f for f in C^1(T), and indicate the L^2(mu)-extension by continuity; also verify that in the inner case this reduces to the normalized Cauchy transform.

Let theta be the contractive characteristic function in the rank-one Clark setting, let gamma be a fixed point of the unit circle T, and let mu_gamma be the corresponding Aleksandrov-Clark measure. For f in L^2(mu_gamma), consider the normalized Cauchy transform V_gamma f(z) := C_{f mu_gamma}(z) / C_{mu_gamma}(z) for z in the unit disk D. In the non-inner case, can one obtain an explicit formula controlling the boundary jump of V_gamma f across T, in terms of the interior and exterior boundary values and the structure of mu_gamma, analogous to the classical inner Clark theory; and can that jump formula then be used to formulate the paper's intended non-inner analogue of pseudocontinuation for the associated de Branges-Rovnyak/Clark-model functions?

Let θ be the characteristic function of the rank-one perturbation problem in the Aleksandrov-Clark setting, viewed as a contractive analytic function on the unit disk, and let {U_γ}_{γ∈T} be the associated family of rank-one unitary perturbations in the cyclic case. For each γ∈T, determine precisely how the non-tangential boundary values of θ on the unit circle govern the spectral measure of U_γ; equivalently, characterize from the boundary data of θ which parts of the Aleksandrov-Clark measure of U_γ are absolutely continuous, which belong to the singular spectrum, and when point masses occur.

In the paper’s rank-one unitary perturbation / Clark-theory setting, let theta be the scalar characteristic function of the associated completely nonunitary contraction, with theta a Schur-class function on the unit disk. Kapustin imposes the additional assumption that theta be non-extreme, equivalently that its defect function Delta=(1-|theta|^2)^(1/2) satisfy the Szego condition integral over T of log Delta dm > -infinity (equivalently integral over T of log(1-|theta(ξ)|^2) dm(ξ) > -infinity). Does this additional hypothesis admit a characterization purely in spectral terms, i.e. directly from the spectral data of the associated rank-one unitary perturbations / Aleksandrov-Clark measures?

Consider a general feedback-controlled physical system that, at each discrete control step, acquires mutual information I between its macrostate X and the controller’s action C. Denote by R_open the maximum performance under any open-loop protocol and by R_closed the maximum performance under any feedback protocol using information I. What is the tightest possible upper bound on the performance improvement ΔR=R_closed−R_open as a function of I, for performance measures R including work extracted, thermodynamic efficiency, power output, or particle flux? How does this bound extend to scenarios of repeated correlated feedback operations and to the continuous-time limit?

Given a feedback controller operating at temperature T with Boltzmann constant k_B that performs M correlated repeated actuations on a system (i.e. without relaxation to equilibrium between steps), let X_k denote the system’s macrostate and C_k the control action at the k-th step. From the system’s viewpoint, the total entropy reduction is ΔS_system=−k_B∑_{k=1}^M I(X_k;C_k|C^{k−1}) (in nats) [Eq. (13)–(15) of [13], Section 2.4]. From the combined system-plus-controller viewpoint, Zurek’s algorithmic complexity analysis [6,7] establishes that the minimum work required to erase the full measurement record σ is W_erase≥k_B T ln2·K_U(σ) [Subsection 2.1]. What is the precise mathematical relationship between K_U(σ) and the sequence of conditional mutual informations {I(X_k;C_k|C^{k−1})} such that the Landauer‐bound work of memory erasure provides the exact upper limit on ΔS_system?

Consider a physical system whose state X(t) evolves continuously under dynamics with characteristic time scales τ_c, and a feedback controller that measures the system and applies control actions C_k at discrete times t_k=kτ. Cao and Feito (2009) showed that for correlated repeated discrete actuations the total average entropy reduction of the system is ΔS_discrete=–∑_{k=1}^N I(X_k;C_k|C^{k–1}) (Section II.4, Eq. (15)). In the limit of continuous actuation τ→0 (τ≪τ_c), how can one rigorously derive the corresponding continuous-time entropy reduction rate in terms of differential entropy and mutual information rates, accounting for the nontrivial relationship between discrete Shannon entropies H(·) and continuous differential entropies h(·)?

In a feedback-controlled flashing ratchet where at each discrete time step τ a controller measures the sign of the net force on N Brownian particles and switches a spatially periodic potential on or off, can the general entropy reduction formalism of Cao & Feito (2009) — which proves that the total average entropy reduction due to M control steps is ΔS_info=∑_{k=1}^M I(C_k;X_k|C_{1:k-1}) (Section II.4) — be applied to derive an explicit upper bound on the average entropy reduction rate ΔS_info/T for this ratchet? Furthermore, can this bound, together with a restatement of the previously obtained performance relations J_closed–J_open≤C √I and P_closed–P_open≤D I (Section II.3) in terms of the non-redundant information rate İ=lim_{T→∞}1/T I(C_{1:N};X_{1:N}), be used to establish a complete thermodynamic description of the feedback-controlled flashing ratchet under isothermal conditions, including limits on extractable work, heat flow, and efficiency?

For a nanotechnology device or biological system comprising two interacting subsystems—one serving as the feedback controller (C_k) and the other as the controlled system (X_k)—determine how the general information-theoretic limit on closed-loop control (ΔH_closed ≤ ΔH_open + I(X;C) from Section II.B, Eq. (4)) and the thermodynamic entropy-reduction result for repeated correlated feedback actuation (ΔS_info = −k_B∑_{k=1}^M I(X_k;C_k|C_{k−1},…,C_1) from Section II.D, Eq. (14)) impose quantitative constraints on the maximum achievable performance measures—such as transport flux, power output, and work extraction—in such systems, both per control step and per unit time.

Does there exist a complex Banach algebra A such that A is approximately amenable—meaning that for every Banach A-bimodule X and every continuous derivation D:A -> X*, there exists a net (x_i) in X* with D(a)=lim_i(a·x_i-x_i·a) for every a in A—but A is not boundedly approximately amenable, in the sense that for some Banach A-bimodule X and some continuous derivation D:A -> X*, no approximating net of inner derivations can be chosen uniformly bounded in operator norm as maps A -> X*?

Must every boundedly approximately amenable complex Banach algebra A have a two-sided bounded approximate identity; equivalently, is bounded approximate amenability strictly stronger than bounded approximate contractibility only when the bounded approximate identity fails?

Let A be a Banach algebra. Suppose A is approximately amenable, in the sense that for every Banach A-bimodule X, every continuous derivation D:A→X* is approximately inner in norm. Must A itself be pseudo-amenable; equivalently, must there exist a (not necessarily bounded) net (u_i) in the projective tensor product A \widehat{\otimes} A such that a·u_i-u_i·a→0 and π_A(u_i)a→a for every a∈A? ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1207.4511))

Let A be a complex Banach algebra. Assume that A is approximately amenable, in the sense that for every Banach A-bimodule X and every continuous derivation D:A→X*, there exists a net (x_i) in X* such that D(a)=lim_i(a·x_i−x_i·a) in the norm of X* for each a in A. Must A then admit a two-sided approximate identity, i.e. a net (e_α) in A with e_α a→a and a e_α→a for every a in A? Moreover, can such a net always be chosen bounded in norm, so that sup_α ||e_α|| < ∞?

Let A and B be complex Banach algebras, and equip the direct sum A ⊕ B with the usual coordinatewise multiplication and ℓ1-sum norm. Suppose that A and B are approximately amenable, in the sense that for every Banach bimodule X over the algebra in question, every continuous derivation into X* is approximately inner. Must A ⊕ B be approximately amenable, even without assuming that either A or B has a bounded approximate identity?

Let A and B be Banach algebras, and let A \hat{\otimes} B denote their Banach-space projective tensor product endowed with the canonical algebra multiplication. Is A \hat{\otimes} B approximately amenable (respectively, pseudo-amenable) whenever both A and B are approximately amenable (respectively, pseudo-amenable)? ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1207.4511))

Let A and B be Banach algebras, and let T:A→B be a Banach algebra homomorphism such that T(A) is dense in B. Fix one generalized amenability property P from the nearby list considered in the paper—namely approximate amenability, bounded approximate amenability, sequential approximate amenability, bounded approximate contractibility, sequential approximate contractibility, pseudo-amenability, pseudo-contractibility, bounded pseudo-amenability, bounded pseudo-contractibility, sequential pseudo-amenability, or sequential pseudo-contractibility. If A has property P, must B also have property P?

Does Theorem 3.9 extend from codimension 1 to arbitrary finite codimension? Precisely: if A is a boundedly approximately contractible Banach algebra and J is a finite-codimensional two-sided ideal of A, must J admit a bounded approximate identity, that is, a norm-bounded net (e_alpha) in J such that e_alpha j -> j and j e_alpha -> j for every j in J?

Let A be a Banach algebra and J a closed two-sided ideal of A. Assume either: (i) A is pseudo-amenable, meaning that there exists a net (u_alpha) in A \hat{\otimes} A such that a u_alpha - u_alpha a -> 0 and \pi(u_alpha)a -> a for every a in A; or (ii) A is approximately amenable, meaning that for every Banach A-bimodule X and every continuous derivation D: A -> X* there exists a net (m_i) in X* with D(a) = lim_i (a·m_i - m_i·a) for all a in A, and moreover A has an approximate identity. Under what conditions must J have a two-sided approximate identity, i.e. a net (e_beta) in J such that e_beta x -> x and x e_beta -> x for every x in J?

For every locally compact group G, with A(G) its complex Fourier algebra, is A(G) approximately amenable if and only if it is pseudo-amenable; equivalently, is A(G) approximately amenable exactly when A(G) has an approximate identity (not necessarily bounded)?

For every locally compact group G and every proper Segal algebra S^1(G) on G (equivalently, every nontrivial Segal subalgebra of L^1(G), with its usual convolution Banach-algebra structure), must S^1(G) fail to be approximately amenable?

Let G be a locally compact group and let ω: G → (0, ∞) be a continuous weight, and write L^1(G, ω) for the corresponding complex Beurling algebra under convolution. If Ω(x) := ω(x)ω(x^{-1}), then amenability of L^1(G, ω) is known to be equivalent to amenability of G together with boundedness of Ω on G. Since L^1(G, ω) has a bounded approximate identity, approximate amenability and pseudo-amenability coincide here. Is it true that L^1(G, ω) is approximately amenable if and only if it is amenable; equivalently, if and only if G is amenable and Ω is bounded on G?

Let S be a semigroup, and let ℓ^1(S) denote its complex semigroup Banach algebra with convolution given on point masses by δ_s * δ_t = δ_{st}. Determine necessary and sufficient conditions on S for ℓ^1(S) to be approximately amenable, in the sense that for every Banach ℓ^1(S)-bimodule X every continuous derivation D: ℓ^1(S) → X* is approximately inner, and determine necessary and sufficient conditions on S for ℓ^1(S) to be pseudo-amenable, in the sense that there exists an approximate diagonal (u_i) in the projective tensor product of ℓ^1(S) with itself such that a·u_i - u_i·a → 0 and π(u_i)a → a for all a ∈ ℓ^1(S).

Does there exist a complex uniform algebra A, in the standard sense of a uniformly closed unital subalgebra of C(K) for some compact Hausdorff space K (with the supremum norm), such that A is not amenable but is approximately amenable or pseudo-amenable as a Banach algebra?

Open problem. Let X be a Banach space, and let K(X) denote the Banach algebra of compact operators on X, equipped with composition as multiplication and the operator norm topology. Characterize those Banach spaces X for which K(X) is approximately amenable, in the sense that for every Banach K(X)-bimodule Y and every continuous derivation D: K(X) -> Y* there exists a net (y_i) in Y* with D(a) = lim_i (a·y_i - y_i·a) for each a in K(X), and characterize those Banach spaces X for which K(X) is pseudo-amenable, in the sense that there exists a net (m_i) in the projective tensor product K(X) ⊗̂ K(X) such that a·m_i - m_i·a -> 0 and π(m_i)a -> a for all a in K(X), where π: K(X) ⊗̂ K(X) -> K(X) is the multiplication map. In particular, does there exist a Banach space X such that K(X) is not amenable but is approximately amenable or pseudo-amenable?

Let A be a C*-algebra, regarded as a Banach algebra. Does there exist such an A that is approximately amenable in the sense that for every Banach A-bimodule X and every continuous derivation D:A→X*, there is a net (x_i)⊂X* with D(a)=lim_i(a·x_i−x_i·a) in norm for every a∈A, but A is not amenable as a Banach algebra (equivalently, not nuclear)? If such C*-algebras exist, characterize exactly which C*-algebras are approximately amenable.

Let G be a locally compact amenable group, and let S^1(G) be a Segal algebra on G (equivalently, a Segal subalgebra of L^1(G) with the convolution product). Must S^1(G) be pseudo-amenable, in the sense of Definition 1.3, i.e. must it admit an approximate diagonal?

Let x be a nicely defined cardinal invariant of the continuum. Assume that whenever x = \aleph_1, the negative strong polarized relation \binom{x}{\omega} \nrightarrow \binom{x}{\omega}^{1,1}_2 holds; equivalently, whenever x = \aleph_1 there is a coloring c : x \times \omega \to 2 such that no sets A \subseteq x and B \subseteq \omega with |A| = x and |B| = \omega make c constant on A \times B. Must it follow that x = \mathfrak{c}?

Is it consistent with ZFC that the splitting number 𝔰 equals ℵ1 and nevertheless the strong polarized partition relation \binom{𝔰}{\omega} \rightarrow \binom{𝔰}{\omega}^{1,1}_2 holds; that is, for every coloring c: 𝔰 × ω → 2 there exist A ⊆ 𝔰 and B ⊆ ω with |A| = 𝔰 and |B| = ω such that c restricted to A × B is constant?

Is it consistent with ZFC that the classical splitting number \mathfrak{s} on \omega satisfies \mathfrak{s}>\aleph_2 and nevertheless every coloring c:\mathfrak{s}\times\omega\to 2 admits a monochromatic rectangle A\times B with A\subseteq\mathfrak{s}, B\subseteq\omega, |A|=\mathfrak{s}, and |B|=\omega; that is, \binom{\mathfrak{s}}{\omega}\to\binom{\mathfrak{s}}{\omega}^{1,1}_2?

Is it consistent with ZFC that the splitting number \(\mathfrak{s}\) equals the ultrafilter number \(\mathfrak{u}\) and nevertheless the strong polarized partition relation \(\binom{\mathfrak{s}}{\omega}\to\binom{\mathfrak{s}}{\omega}^{1,1}_2\) holds; that is, for every coloring \(c:\mathfrak{s}\times\omega\to 2\) there are sets \(A\subseteq\mathfrak{s}\) and \(B\subseteq\omega\) with \(|A|=\mathfrak{s}\) and \(|B|=\omega\) such that \(c\restriction(A\times B)\) is constant?

Is it relatively consistent with ZFC that the splitting number \(\mathfrak{s}\) - the least size of a family \(\mathcal{S}\) of infinite subsets of \(\omega\) such that every infinite \(X\subseteq\omega\) is split by some \(S\in\mathcal{S}\), i.e. both \(|X\cap S|=\omega\) and \(|X\setminus S|=\omega\) - satisfies \(\mathfrak{s}<\mathfrak{c}=2^{\aleph_0}\), and nevertheless the strong polarized relation \(\binom{\mathfrak{s}}{\omega}\to\binom{\mathfrak{s}}{\omega}^{1,1}_2\) holds, meaning that every coloring \(c:\mathfrak{s}\times\omega\to 2\) admits \(A\subseteq\mathfrak{s}\) and \(B\subseteq\omega\) with \(|A|=\mathfrak{s}\), \(|B|=\omega\), and \(c\restriction(A\times B)\) constant?

Is it consistent with ZFC that 𝔡 = ℵ1, where 𝔡 is the dominating number (the least size of a family D ⊆ ω^ω that dominates ω^ω under eventual domination ≤*), and that for every coloring c : 𝔡 × ω → 2 there exist A ⊆ 𝔡 and B ⊆ ω with |A| = 𝔡 and |B| = ω such that c is constant on A × B?

Is it consistent with ZFC that the dominating number \mathfrak{d}=\min\{ |F| : F\subseteq\omega^\omega\ \text{and}\ (\forall g\in\omega^\omega)(\exists f\in F)\, g\leq^* f\} is singular (that is, \operatorname{cf}(\mathfrak{d})<\mathfrak{d}) and nevertheless the strong polarized relation \binom{\mathfrak{d}}{\omega}\to\binom{\mathfrak{d}}{\omega}^{1,1}_2 holds, meaning that for every coloring c:\mathfrak{d}\times\omega\to 2 there exist A\subseteq\mathfrak{d} and B\subseteq\omega with |A|=\mathfrak{d} and |B|=\omega such that c\upharpoonright(A\times B) is constant?

Is it consistent with ZFC that the dominating number \mathfrak{d} is at most the ultrafilter number \mathfrak{u}, and nevertheless the strong polarized partition relation \binom{\mathfrak{d}}{\omega} \rightarrow \binom{\mathfrak{d}}{\omega}^{1,1}_2 holds; that is, for every coloring c : \mathfrak{d} \times \omega \to 2 there exist A \subseteq \mathfrak{d} and B \subseteq \omega with |A| = \mathfrak{d} and |B| = \omega such that c is constant on A \times B, where \mathfrak{d} is the least size of a family in \omega^\omega dominating under eventual domination and \mathfrak{u} is the least size of a base for a nonprincipal ultrafilter on \omega?

Let \mathfrak d denote the dominating number. Assume in a ground model V that the strong polarized relation \binom{\mathfrak d}{\omega}\rightarrow\binom{\mathfrak d}{\omega}^{1,1}_2 holds; equivalently, every coloring c:\mathfrak d\times\omega\to 2 has a monochromatic rectangle A\times B with |A|=\mathfrak d and |B|=\omega. If one forces over V by adding \lambda many random reals for some cardinal \lambda>\mathfrak d^V, must the resulting extension still satisfy \binom{\mathfrak d}{\omega}\rightarrow\binom{\mathfrak d}{\omega}^{1,1}_2? ([shelah.logic.at](https://shelah.logic.at/files/95093/1012.pdf))

Is it consistent with ZFC that the independence number \mathfrak{i} on \omega is \aleph_1 and that the strong polarized partition relation \binom{\mathfrak{i}}{\omega} \to \binom{\mathfrak{i}}{\omega}^{1,1}_2 holds; that is, for every coloring c: \mathfrak{i} \times \omega \to 2 there exist A \subseteq \mathfrak{i} and B \subseteq \omega with |A| = \mathfrak{i} = \aleph_1 and |B| = \omega such that c\upharpoonright(A \times B) is constant? ([shelah.logic.at](https://shelah.logic.at/files/95093/1012.pdf))

Is there a model of ZFC in which the independence number \(\mathfrak{i}\) is at most the ultrafilter number \(\mathfrak{u}\), and the strong polarized partition relation \(\binom{\mathfrak{i}}{\omega} \to \binom{\mathfrak{i}}{\omega}^{1,1}_2\) holds; that is, for every coloring \(c:\mathfrak{i}\times\omega\to 2\), there exist \(A\subseteq\mathfrak{i}\) and \(B\subseteq\omega\) with \(|A|=\mathfrak{i}\) and \(|B|=\omega\) such that \(c\) is constant on \(A\times B\)?

Is it consistent that there exists a real-valued measurable cardinal \kappa such that \binom{\kappa}{\omega}\to\binom{\kappa}{\omega}^{1,1}_2; that is, for every coloring c:\kappa\times\omega\to 2 there are sets A\subseteq\kappa and B\subseteq\omega with |A|=\kappa and |B|=\omega such that c is constant on A\times B?

Is it consistent with ZFC that 𝔠 = 2^{ℵ₀} is strictly larger than ℵ₂ and that, for every cardinal κ with ℵ₁ ≤ κ ≤ 𝔠, every coloring c: κ × ω → 2 admits sets A ⊆ κ and B ⊆ ω such that |A| = κ, |B| = ω, and c restricted to A × B is constant; equivalently, that (κ over ω) → (κ over ω)^{1,1}_2 for every κ ∈ [ℵ₁, 𝔠]?

Is it consistent with ZFC that the splitting number \(\mathfrak{s}\) equals the continuum \(\mathfrak{c}=2^{\aleph_0}\), that \(\mathfrak{s}=\mathfrak{c}>\aleph_2\), and that for every cardinal \(\kappa\) with \(\aleph_1\le \kappa\le \mathfrak{c}\), every coloring \(c:\kappa\times\omega\to 2\) admits sets \(A\subseteq\kappa\) and \(B\subseteq\omega\) such that \(|A|=\kappa\), \(|B|=\omega\), and \(c\restriction(A\times B)\) is constant; equivalently, \(\binom{\kappa}{\omega}\to\binom{\kappa}{\omega}^{1,1}_2\) for every such \(\kappa\), including \(\kappa=\mathfrak{s}\) itself? ([shelah.logic.at](https://shelah.logic.at/files/95093/1012.pdf))

Is it consistent with ZFC that, for the countable strong polarized spectrum S = { κ : ℵ1 ≤ κ ≤ 𝔠 and binom{κ}{ω} → binom{κ}{ω}^{1,1}_2 }, one has S = { κ : ℵ1 ≤ κ ≤ 𝔠 and κ ≠ ℵω }; more generally, can 𝔠 be arbitrarily large with S = { κ : ℵ1 ≤ κ ≤ 𝔠 and cf(κ) > ω }? Here binom{κ}{ω} → binom{κ}{ω}^{1,1}_2 means that every coloring d: κ×ω → 2 admits A ⊆ κ and B ⊆ ω with |A| = κ and |B| = ω such that d is constant on A×B.

Is it consistent with ZFC that the spectrum S = {κ ≥ ℵ1 : for every coloring c: κ×ω → 2 there exist A ⊆ κ and B ⊆ ω with |A| = κ and |B| = ω such that c is constant on A×B} has two distinct breaking points below ℵω, i.e. that the truth value of this strong polarized relation changes at two distinct cardinals θ0 < θ1 < ℵω?

Is there a model of ZFC in which \mathfrak a=\mathfrak s, where \mathfrak a is the least size of a maximal almost disjoint family of infinite subsets of \omega and \mathfrak s is the splitting number, and such that for every coloring c:\mathfrak a\times\omega\to 2 there exist A\subseteq\mathfrak a and B\subseteq\omega with |A|=\mathfrak a and |B|=\omega for which c\upharpoonright(A\times B) is constant? ([shelah.logic.at](https://shelah.logic.at/files/95093/1012.pdf))

In ZFC, let \mathfrak{p} and \mathfrak{s} denote the pseudointersection number and the splitting number on \omega. Is the two-color strong polarized relation \binom{\mathfrak{p}}{\omega}\to\binom{\mathfrak{p}}{\omega}^{1,1}_2 equivalent to \mathfrak{p}<\mathfrak{s}; that is, is it true that every coloring c:\mathfrak{p}\times\omega\to 2 admits A\subseteq\mathfrak{p} and B\subseteq\omega with |A|=\mathfrak{p}, |B|=\omega, and c restricted to A\times B constant if and only if \mathfrak{p}<\mathfrak{s}?

Assume \aleph_1 < \kappa < \lambda = \mathfrak{c} = 2^{\aleph_0} in the ground model, and assume the strong polarized relation \binom{\kappa}{\omega} \to \binom{\kappa}{\omega}^{1,1}_2 holds; that is, every coloring c: \kappa \times \omega \to 2 admits sets A \subseteq \kappa and B \subseteq \omega with |A|=\kappa and |B|=\omega such that c\!\upharpoonright(A\times B) is constant. Let \mathbb{P}=\mathrm{Levy}(\kappa,\lambda) be the Lévy collapse. Is it possible that in the forcing extension V^{\mathbb{P}} the strong polarized relation fails, i.e. \binom{\kappa}{\omega} \nrightarrow \binom{\kappa}{\omega}^{1,1}_2?

Is it consistent with ZFC that the club principle ♣_{ℵ1} holds and, simultaneously, every coloring c: \omega_1 \times \omega \to 2 admits sets A \subseteq \omega_1 and B \subseteq \omega with |A|=\omega_1 and |B|=\omega such that c is constant on A \times B; equivalently, that \binom{\omega_1}{\omega} \to \binom{\omega_1}{\omega}^{1,1}_2 holds?

Does ZFC prove that for every uncountable successor cardinal κ, \binom{2^\kappa}{\kappa} \nrightarrow \binom{2^\kappa}{\kappa}^{1,1}_2; equivalently, is there a coloring c: 2^\kappa \times \kappa \to 2 such that for no A \subseteq 2^\kappa and B \subseteq \kappa with |A| = 2^\kappa and |B| = \kappa is c constant on A \times B?

For every inaccessible but not weakly compact cardinal \kappa, does the negative strong polarized partition relation \binom{2^\kappa}{\kappa} \nrightarrow \binom{2^\kappa}{\kappa}^{1,1}_2 hold; that is, is there a coloring c: 2^\kappa × \kappa → 2 such that for no sets A ⊆ 2^\kappa and B ⊆ \kappa with |A| = 2^\kappa and |B| = \kappa is c constant on A × B? ([shelah.logic.at](https://shelah.logic.at/files/95093/1012.pdf))

Let κ be a measurable cardinal. Is there a forcing extension V^P in which κ remains measurable and the strong polarized relation \binom{2^\kappa}{\kappa} \to \binom{2^\kappa}{\kappa}^{1,1}_2 holds; that is, for every coloring c:2^\kappa \times \kappa \to 2 there exist A \subseteq 2^\kappa and B \subseteq \kappa with |A|=2^\kappa and |B|=\kappa such that c\upharpoonright(A \times B) is constant? Likewise, if κ is strongly compact, is there an analogous forcing extension in which κ remains strongly compact and the same relation holds?

Is it consistent that there exists a cardinal \kappa such that \kappa is weakly compact but not measurable and the strong polarized relation \binom{\kappa^+}{\kappa} \to \binom{\kappa^+}{\kappa}^{1,1}_2 holds; that is, for every coloring c: \kappa^+ \times \kappa \to 2 there are sets A \subseteq \kappa^+ and B \subseteq \kappa with |A| = \kappa^+ and |B| = \kappa such that c is constant on A \times B?

In ZFC, if \(\kappa\) is a regular cardinal \((\operatorname{cf}(\kappa)=\kappa)\) that is not weakly compact, must there exist a coloring \(c:\kappa^+\times\kappa\to 2\) such that for no sets \(A\subseteq\kappa^+\) and \(B\subseteq\kappa\) with \(|A|=\kappa^+\) and \(|B|=\kappa\) is \(c\restriction(A\times B)\) constant; that is, must the negative strong polarized relation \(\binom{\kappa^+}{\kappa}\nrightarrow\binom{\kappa^+}{\kappa}^{1,1}_2\) hold?

Let λ be any strong limit singular cardinal. Is it consistent with ZFC—necessarily in a model where 2^λ > λ^+—that the positive strong polarized relation (λ^+, λ) → (λ^+, λ)^{1,1}_2 holds? Likewise, is it consistent that (2^λ, λ) → (2^λ, λ)^{1,1}_2 holds?

Is it consistent with ZFC that there exists a singular cardinal λ with cf(λ)=ω and 2^θ=θ^+ for every θ<λ such that at least one of the following strong polarized partition relations holds: (λ^+, λ) → (λ^+, λ)^{1,1}_2, meaning that every coloring c:λ^+×λ→2 has a monochromatic rectangle A×B with |A|=λ^+ and |B|=λ; or (2^λ, λ) → (2^λ, λ)^{1,1}_2, meaning that every coloring c:2^λ×λ→2 has a monochromatic rectangle A×B with |A|=2^λ and |B|=λ?

Assume that λ is a singular cardinal with λ > cf(λ) and 2^λ > λ^+. Is it a theorem of ZFC that for every ordinal α < λ^+ and every coloring c: λ^+ × λ → 2, there exist sets A ⊆ λ^+ and B ⊆ λ of order types α and λ, respectively, such that c is constant on A × B; equivalently in the paper’s notation, does \binom{\lambda^+}{\lambda} \to \binom{\alpha}{\lambda}^{1,1}_2 hold for every α < λ^+?

In ZFC, must every cardinal λ with cf(λ) < λ that is not a strong limit cardinal satisfy the negative balanced strong polarized partition relation (λ^+ over λ) ↛ (λ^+ over λ)^(1,1)_2; that is, for every such λ, is there a coloring c: λ^+ × λ → 2 such that no sets A ⊆ λ^+ and B ⊆ λ with |A| = λ^+ and |B| = λ make c constant on A × B?

Let λ be a strong limit singular cardinal that is not a limit of measurable cardinals. Is it consistent that for every cardinal μ with λ < μ ≤ 2^λ and every coloring c: μ×λ→2, there exist sets A⊆μ and B⊆λ such that |A|=μ, |B|=λ, and c is constant on A×B?

Over the field ℂ, for each small-order finite abelian group G (in particular G = Z2, Z3, Z4, or Z2 × Z2), classify all G-gradings on the mixed paraparticle (co)algebras PBF and PFB—that is, on the Relative Parabose Set and Relative Parafermi Set algebras of Section 2—that are compatible with their algebra structure and, dually, with their coalgebra structure. Equivalently, determine up to isomorphism all ℂG-module/comodule algebra structures and ℂG-module/comodule coalgebra structures on PBF and PFB, including alternative inequivalent gradings (notably inequivalent Z2 × Z2-gradings for PBF), but without passing to the separate problem of classifying compatible braidings or R-matrices.

Over the field C, let G be one of the small finite abelian groups considered in the first research objective (for example Z2, Z3, Z4, or Z2 x Z2), and let A be one of the paraparticle (co)algebras under study, especially PBF or PFB, equipped with a G-grading, equivalently a CG-(co)action preserving its algebra and coalgebra structures. For each such grading, classify all skew-symmetric bicharacters theta: G x G -> C* for which A admits compatible graded algebra and graded coalgebra structures making it into a G-graded, theta-braided Hopf algebra (braided group), i.e. a Hopf algebra in the braided monoidal category of CG-modules; equivalently, determine all corresponding triangular universal R-matrices of CG, or all corresponding braidings on the categories of CG-modules/comodules, and decide which of these actually yield braided group structures for A, especially for PBF and PFB, independently of any prescribed color-graded Lie realization.

Over ℂ, for each G-grading on the mixed paraparticle (co)algebras P_BF and P_FB—especially gradings by small-order finite Abelian groups G such as Z_2, Z_3, Z_4, and Z_2×Z_2 that preserve the corresponding (co)algebra structure—and for each corresponding compatible braided group structure (equivalently, each G-graded, ϑ-braided Hopf structure determined by a bicharacter, universal R-matrix, or braiding of the associated G-module/comodule category), can one apply or develop suitable bosonization or bosonization-like techniques to obtain associated ordinary Hopf structures, with no grading and with trivial braiding, while retaining equivalent representation theory? ([inspirehep.net](https://inspirehep.net/files/f14d346255a1967f0ad17ce6926fc341))

For the parabosonic algebra PB over the complex numbers, with generators B_i^± indexed by i = 1, 2, ... and with order p any fixed positive integer, can the braided construction outlined in Sections 4.1–4.2 be completed by explicitly evaluating the PB-action obtained from the braided comultiplication on the Z2-graded tensor product of p copies of the first (p = 1) Fock-like representation—specifically, by deriving a workable multinomial expansion for finitely supported monomials in the odd CCR creation operators b_i^{(r)+} = I tensor ... tensor b_i^+ tensor ... tensor I acting on the p-fold bosonic vacuum—so as to write explicit formulas for the action of the generators B_i^± and the corresponding matrix elements on the order-p parabosonic Fock-like module realized inside that graded tensor-product representation?

Over ℂ, fix a positive integer p. In the Section 4 braided construction for the infinite-degree free parabosonic algebra P_B—and analogously for the free parafermionic algebra P_F—one forms p-fold Z_2-graded tensor-product representations from suitably graded CCR/CAR modules (for P_B, via the homogeneous maps induced by the braided comultiplication), and it is already known that the standard order-p Fock-like module occurs as an irreducible factor. When these graded tensor-product representations are decomposed into irreducible components, is the standard p-Fock-like module the only constituent up to equivalence, or can there also appear additional direct summands, or at least submodules, carrying representations inequivalent to the standard p-Fock-like module?

Over C, with "super" meaning Z2-graded and with suitable gradings and braidings of Ws and Was chosen in the sense envisaged by Section 3, can one generalize the braided tensor-product method of Section 4.1 from the free parabosonic and parafermionic algebras PB and PF to the mixed paraparticle algebras PBF and PFB by realizing the symmetric Clifford-Weyl algebra Ws as a suitable graded quotient algebra of PBF and the antisymmetric Clifford-Weyl algebra Was as a suitable graded quotient algebra of PFB, and then explicitly constructing the Fock-like representations of PBF and PFB as irreducible submodules occurring in the decomposition of the corresponding graded tensor product representations; and, in order to carry out those explicit computations, can one establish the required multinomial theorem for expressions mixing commuting and anticommuting variables?

For a fixed positive integer p, over C, in the Fock-like representation ⊕_{n=0}^p ⊕_{m=0}^∞ V_{m,n} of the mixed paraparticle algebra P_BF(1,1) (and, where applicable, analogously for P_FB(1,1)), with dim V_{m,n} = 2 except dim V_{0,n} = dim V_{m,0} = dim V_{m,p} = 1, with parabosonic/parafermionic creation-annihilation operators b^+, b^-, f^+, f^- satisfying (f^+)^(p+1) = 0, and with [x,y] = xy - yx and {x,y} = xy + yx, do the candidate Hamiltonians H_dyn = (ω_b/2){b^+,b^-} + (ω_f/2)[f^+,f^-] + ((ω_f - ω_b)p)/2 + (λ/2)({b^-,f^+} + {b^+,f^-}) and H_dyn^* = (ω_b/2){b^+,b^-} + (ω_f/2)[f^+,f^-] + ((ω_f - ω_b)p)/2 + λ_1 b^-f^+ + λ_2 f^+b^- + λ_2^* b^+f^- + λ_1^* f^-b^+ (with ω_b and ω_f possibly depending on m, n, or both) yield exactly solvable paraparticle generalizations of the Jaynes–Cummings model for a monochromatic parabosonic field coupled to a (p + 1)-level system, in the sense that one can explicitly determine the energy spectrum, eigenfunctions, and transition rates for the transitions V_{m,n} → V_{m-1,n+1} ⊕ V_{m+1,n-1}, and then compare those predictions directly with theoretical and experimental results? ([inspirehep.net](https://inspirehep.net/files/f14d346255a1967f0ad17ce6926fc341))

For each n≥1, let Av_n(1324)={π∈S_n: π avoids the classical pattern 1324} and let s_n(1324)=|Av_n(1324)|. Determine s_n(1324) exactly; failing that, determine an exact asymptotic formula for s_n(1324) as n→∞. In particular, determine the value of the Stanley-Wilf limit L(1324)=lim_{n→∞} s_n(1324)^{1/n}, i.e. the exponential growth rate of the unique unresolved Wilf class of classical permutation patterns of length 4 represented by 1324. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1210.7320))

Prove or disprove the following 'increasing columns' conjecture for the classical pattern 1324: for every n,k ∈ Z_{≥0}, if S_n^k(1324) denotes the number of permutations π ∈ S_n that avoid 1324 and satisfy inv(π)=k, then S_n^k(1324) ≤ S_{n+1}^k(1324). Here L(1324)=lim_{m→∞}|S_m(1324)|^{1/m} is the Stanley-Wilf limit. By the paper's Theorem 17, a proof of this conjecture would yield the upper bound L(1324) ≤ e^{π√(2/3)} ≈ 13.001954.

Let S_n^k(1324) := |{π ∈ S_n : π avoids the classical pattern 1324 and inv(π)=k}|, where inv(π) is the number of pairs (i,j) with 1 ≤ i < j ≤ n and π_i > π_j. Prove or disprove that for all nonnegative integers n and k, S_n^k(1324) ≤ S_{n+1}^k(1324).

For each integer k ≥ 1, let Av_p(n) denote the number of permutations of length n that avoid the classical pattern p, and let SW(p) := lim_{n→∞} Av_p(n)^{1/n} be the Stanley-Wilf limit. Is it true that for every k there exists a layered pattern p of length k—equivalently, a direct sum of decreasing permutations—such that SW(p) = max{SW(q) : q is a classical pattern of length k}?

Fix k ≥ 1. Let L_k be the set of layered classical permutation patterns of length k, where a layered pattern is a direct sum of decreasing permutations. For λ ∈ L_k, let Av_λ(n) = |{π ∈ S_n : π avoids λ}|. Determine, up to reverse/complement Wilf-equivalent symmetries if desired, which pattern(s) λ ∈ L_k have the property that there exists N such that for every n > N and every μ ∈ L_k, Av_λ(n) ≥ Av_μ(n). In other words, determine the eventual most easily avoided layered pattern(s) of each length k. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1210.7320))

For each even integer k=2m>=2, let lambda_k be the classical layered permutation of length k with layer sizes (1,2,2,...,2,2,1), equivalently lambda_k = 1 ⊕ 21 ⊕ ... ⊕ 21 ⊕ 1 with m-1 copies of 21. Is it true that lambda_k is, up to the trivial Wilf-equivalent symmetries of reverse and complement, a most avoided classical pattern of length k; that is, does there exist N=N(k) such that for every classical pattern sigma in S_k and every n>=N, one has Av_sigma(n) <= Av_lambda_k(n), where Av_tau(n) denotes the number of permutations of length n avoiding tau?

Prove or refute the following conjecture. For each integer k ≡ 1 (mod 4), let λ_k be the classical layered permutation of length k obtained as the direct sum of decreasing blocks with sizes (1,2,...,2,3,2,...,2,1), so that there are (k-5)/4 blocks of size 2 on each side of the central block of size 3. If Av_τ(n) denotes the number of permutations of length n that avoid the classical pattern τ, is it true that for every classical pattern σ of length k there exists an integer N = N(σ,k) such that Av_σ(n) ≤ Av_λk(n) for all n ≥ N? Equivalently: for k ≡ 1 (mod 4), is λ_k eventually the most avoided classical pattern of length k? ([vdoc.pub](https://vdoc.pub/documents/surveys-in-combinatorics-2013-7rqqau6gfgb0))

Fix k and let sigma, tau be two non-Wilf-equivalent classical permutation patterns in S_k. If Av_sigma(n) denotes the number of permutations in S_n that avoid sigma, can the inequality between Av_sigma(n) and Av_tau(n) reverse more than once as n increases? More weakly, must there exist an integer N such that either Av_sigma(n) < Av_tau(n) for all n > N or Av_sigma(n) > Av_tau(n) for all n > N; equivalently, can two such patterns switch places infinitely often?

For every positive integer k, assume that among all classical permutation patterns of length k, the maximum Stanley-Wilf limit is attained by a layered pattern. If L(τ) = lim_{n→∞} Av_τ(n)^{1/n} denotes the Stanley-Wilf limit of a classical pattern τ ∈ S_k, is the resulting universal bound L(τ) ≤ 2.25 k^2 optimal, or can the coefficient 2.25 be reduced in a bound that holds for all classical patterns of length k?

In the poset P of all finite permutations ordered by classical pattern containment (so σ ≤ τ iff σ occurs as a classical pattern in τ), give a complete characterization of all pairs of permutations σ, τ with σ ≤ τ for which the interval [σ, τ] = {π ∈ P : σ ≤ π ≤ τ} has Möbius function value μ(σ, τ) = 0, where μ is defined recursively by μ(x, x) = 1 and μ(x, y) = -∑_{x≤z<y} μ(x, z) for x < y. ([citeseerx.ist.psu.edu](https://citeseerx.ist.psu.edu/document?doi=907d621189adfb11324bde3f096bb79a478d180e&repid=rep1&type=pdf&utm_source=openai))

In the poset P of all finite permutations ordered by classical pattern containment, characterize all pairs of permutations σ ≤ π (equivalently, all intervals [σ, π]) for which the interval Möbius function satisfies |μ_P(σ, π)| = N_σ(π), where N_σ(π) denotes the number of classical occurrences of σ in π, i.e. the number of subsequences of π whose relative order is σ.

Let P be the poset of all finite permutations ordered by classical pattern containment. For permutations σ and τ with σ ≤ τ, let μ(σ,τ) denote the Möbius function of the interval [σ,τ], and let σ(τ) denote the number of occurrences of σ as a pattern in τ. Does there exist a universal function F: N -> N such that |μ(σ,τ)| <= F(σ(τ)) for every interval [σ,τ] in P, without imposing additional hypotheses on σ or τ such as separability or pattern-avoidance restrictions?

In the permutation pattern poset P of all finite permutations ordered by classical pattern containment, for which pairs of permutations σ ≤ π does the order complex Δ(σ, π) of the open interval (σ, π) = [σ, π] \ {σ, π} have the homotopy type of a wedge of spheres?

In the permutation pattern poset P ordered by classical pattern containment, for permutations σ < π let Δ(σ, π) denote the order complex of the open interval (σ, π), and let Γ be the induced subcomplex on those vertices τ ∈ (σ, π) for which the Möbius value μ(σ, τ) is nonzero. Must Γ always be a pure simplicial complex, i.e. must all of its inclusion-maximal simplices have the same dimension? ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1210.7320))

In the permutation pattern poset P of all finite permutations ordered by classical pattern containment, let [σ, π] be an interval and let Δ(σ, π) denote the order complex of the open interval (σ, π), that is, of [σ, π] with σ and π removed. If σ occurs exactly once as a classical pattern in π and μ(σ, π)=±1, is Δ(σ, π) necessarily homotopy equivalent to a sphere?

In the classical permutation pattern poset P of all finite permutations ordered by pattern containment, characterize the pairs of permutations σ ≤ π for which the order complex Δ(σ, π) := Δ((σ, π)) of the open interval (σ, π), obtained from the interval [σ, π] by deleting its endpoints, is shellable.

Fix k >= 1. View each vincular pattern p of length k as the integer-valued statistic on permutations that counts occurrences of p. Does there exist a constant N(k), depending only on k, such that for any two Z-linear combinations F and G of length-k vincular-pattern statistics, if for every n < N(k) the statistics F and G have the same distribution on S_n (that is, for every t in Z, |{pi in S_n : F(pi) = t}| = |{pi in S_n : G(pi) = t}|), then F and G are equidistributed on S_n for every n?

Let S be the set of all finite permutations, and for each vincular pattern p let f_p: S -> Z be its occurrence-counting function. Let R be the ring of integer-valued functions on S generated by these f_p under pointwise addition and multiplication (equivalently, the ring formed by vincular patterns viewed as functions, since products of such functions again expand as sums of vincular pattern functions). Besides the Babson-Steingrimsson upgrading identity cited in Equation (2) of their paper, for example [ba c] = [ba dc] + [ba cd] + [ca bd] + [cb ad] + [bac] in their notation, do there exist any other nontrivial identities in R among vincular pattern functions that hold for every finite permutation? If so, describe such additional relations.

Let C be a permutation class, meaning a set of permutations closed under taking classical patterns, and let C_n denote the set of permutations in C of length n. Is it true that the sequence |C_n|^(1/n) always converges as n→∞; equivalently, can the definition gr(C):=lim sup_{n→∞}|C_n|^(1/n) always be strengthened to gr(C)=lim_{n→∞}|C_n|^(1/n)?

Let G_fb = {gr(C) : C = Av(B) is a proper permutation class with finite basis B}, where C_n denotes the set of permutations of length n in C and gr(C) = limsup_{n→∞} |C_n|^{1/n}. Is every element of G_fb an algebraic integer, and does G_fb have no accumulation points from above; equivalently, is there no real number alpha and no strictly decreasing sequence gamma_1 > gamma_2 > ... in G_fb with gamma_n -> alpha?

Let C be a permutation class, let C_n denote the set of permutations of length n in C, and define its growth rate by gr(C)=limsup_{n→∞}|C_n|^{1/n}. Determine exactly which real numbers r with κ≤r<λ occur as gr(C) for some permutation class C, where κ≈2.20557 is the least accumulation point of accumulation points of permutation-class growth rates and λ≈2.48187 is the constant such that every real number at least λ is known to be the growth rate of a permutation class.

Let k be an algebraically closed field of characteristic zero, let X = Spec A be an affine scheme over k, let a be a finite-dimensional k-algebra, and let Γ be an algebraic group acting by automorphisms on X (equivalently on A) and on a, with the induced Γ-actions on the k-vector spaces A and a completely reducible. For the resulting equivariant map algebra M(X, a)^Γ = (a ⊗ A)^Γ = {α : X to a regular | α(γ·x) = γ·α(x) for all γ in Γ and x in X}, classify its irreducible finite-dimensional representations.

Let k be an algebraically closed field, let X = Spec A be an affine k-scheme, let Γ be a finite group acting by automorphisms on A and on a target algebra a, and define the equivariant map algebra by M(X, a)^Γ := (a ⊗ A)^Γ. Extend the representation-theoretic study of equivariant map algebras to the case of more general targets a—specifically when a is a Kac-Moody algebra or the Heisenberg algebra, and more generally when a is any algebra equipped with a standard notion of representation—and, in particular, determine the finite-dimensional representations when a is an alternative algebra or a Jordan algebra. ([mysite.science.uottawa.ca](https://mysite.science.uottawa.ca/neher/Papers/2013EMA-survey.pdf))

Over an algebraically closed field k of characteristic 0, generalize the equivariant map superalgebra setting of [Sav] by allowing the target g to be any finite-dimensional simple Lie superalgebra, the coordinate algebra A to be supercommutative (so X = Spec A is a superscheme), and Gamma to be a Z2-graded group acting compatibly on X and g. For the resulting generalized equivariant map superalgebra M(X,g)^Gamma, classify the irreducible finite-dimensional modules, and determine the correct analogue of the evaluation/generalized-evaluation (Kac-module) description of Theorem 3.12.

Can one formulate an analytic analogue of the equivariant map algebra M(X, a)^Γ by replacing the algebraic data of Definitions 1.1 and 1.3 with analytic data—namely, taking X to be a Banach manifold, a to be a Banach algebra, and Γ to be a finite group acting on X and on a by automorphisms—and then studying the algebra of Γ-equivariant differentiable maps α : X -> a satisfying α(γ·x) = γ·α(x)?

Let k be an algebraically closed field of characteristic 0, let X=Spec A be an affine k-scheme, let a be a finite-dimensional k-algebra, and let Gamma be a finite group acting on X and on a by automorphisms; write M(X,a)^Gamma for the algebra of Gamma-equivariant regular maps X->a. Kac's theorem treats the loop case M(k^x,g)^Gamma with g simple Lie and Gamma cyclic, and there is a two-variable extension for M((k^x)^2,g)^Gamma with Gamma=<sigma1,sigma2> abelian, while for arbitrary algebra a there is a cohomological invariant for M((k^x)^2,a)^Gamma. Can one extend these results first to the multiloop algebras of Example 1.5—namely M(a,sigma1,...,sigman,m1,...,mn)=M((k^x)^n,a)^Gamma, where Gamma is isomorphic to (Z/m1Z)x...x(Z/mnZ) and acts on a via commuting automorphisms sigma_i of orders m_i—and then, beyond the multiloop setting, characterize arbitrary equivariant map algebras M(X,a)^Gamma up to isomorphism?

Let k be an algebraically closed field of characteristic 0, let X = Spec A be an affine k-scheme, let a be a finite-dimensional k-algebra, and let Γ be a finite group acting by automorphisms on X and on a. For the equivariant map algebra M(X,a)^Γ = {α : X → a regular | α(γ·x) = γ·α(x) for all x ∈ X and γ ∈ Γ}, determine the k-algebra automorphism group Aut_k(M(X,a)^Γ).

Let k be an algebraically closed field, let X = Spec A be an affine scheme over k, let a be a finite-dimensional unital associative k-algebra, and let Γ be a finite group acting on X and on a by algebra automorphisms, with |Γ| not divisible by char(k). Set M = M(X,a)^Γ, the associative equivariant map algebra of Γ-equivariant regular maps X → a. The irreducible finite-dimensional M-modules are already classified in Section 2. Can one classify all indecomposable finite-dimensional M-modules and determine the block decomposition of the category of finite-dimensional M-modules? ([alistairsavage.ca](https://alistairsavage.ca/pubs/neher-savage-2013-conm602-EMA_survey.pdf))

Assume the standing hypotheses of §§1 and 4.2: X = Spec A is an affine scheme over an algebraically closed field k, Γ is a finite group acting on X and on a finite-dimensional associative algebra a, and M = M(X, a)^Γ. Suppose moreover that a is an associative bialgebra. Using the comultiplication on a, define the associative analogue of the Lie-theoretic multi-orbit evaluation representation for M supported on a finite set of k-rational points with pairwise disjoint Γ-orbits, extending the single-point/single-orbit evaluation modules classified in Theorem 2.1 and Corollary 2.2, and determine the basic structure and isomorphism classes of these multi-orbit evaluation representations.

Let M = M(X, g)^Γ = (g ⊗ A)^Γ be an equivariant map Lie algebra, where X = Spec A is an affine scheme over an algebraically closed field k of characteristic 0 and Γ is a finite group. For irreducible finite-dimensional M-modules V and V' (equivalently, by Theorem 3.2, one-dimensional twists of evaluation modules), determine the higher extension groups ExtM^n(V, V') for all n ≥ 2, extending the Ext^1 theory summarized in §3.2 and, in particular, the geometric behavior exemplified by Proposition 3.5 through the tangent space (mx/mx^2)^*; furthermore, determine how these higher Ext-groups and the global dimension of the category of finite-dimensional M-modules are related to the geometry of X. ([alistairsavage.ca](https://alistairsavage.ca/pubs/neher-savage-2013-conm602-EMA_survey.pdf))

Let M = M(X, g)^Γ = (g ⊗ A)^Γ be an equivariant map Lie algebra, where X = Spec A is affine, Γ is finite, and the base field is algebraically closed of characteristic 0. In any generality where analogues of the untwisted global Weyl modules W_A(λ) (for λ in P+) and local Weyl modules W(ψ) (for finitely supported ψ : X_rat → P+) are defined, extend to this broader EMA setting the known current/loop-algebra results on the composition lengths, dimensions, and characters of the local Weyl modules, and determine whether an analogue of the current-algebra BGG reciprocity also holds for these equivariant map Lie algebras.

Let k be an algebraically closed field of characteristic 0, let X = Spec A be an affine k-scheme, let Γ be a finite group acting on X and on a finite-dimensional Lie algebra g by automorphisms, and let M = M(X,g)^Γ be the corresponding equivariant map Lie algebra of Γ-equivariant regular maps X -> g. For such more arbitrary equivariant map Lie algebras, formulate and study categories of possibly infinite-dimensional M-modules analogous to those already studied for loop and current algebras—specifically, analogues of the type of category O considered for central extensions of loop algebras, of integrable highest weight representations, and of quasifinite representations (that is, representations with finite-dimensional weight spaces), as well as appropriate generalizations of category O.

Let k be an algebraically closed field of characteristic 0, X an affine scheme with coordinate ring A=O_X(X), Γ a finite group acting on X and on a finite-dimensional semisimple Lie algebra g by automorphisms, and M=M(X,g)^Γ=(g⊗A)^Γ. Describe the Lie-algebra first cohomology H^1(M,V) for an arbitrary M-module V; in particular, determine the adjoint-case quotient H^1(M,M_ad)=Der_k(M)/IDer(M). Also determine the Lie-algebra homology groups H_*(M,V), especially H_0(M,M_ad)=M/[M,M], so as to understand when M is perfect ([M,M]=M), a condition singled out in the paper because Theorem 3.2 yields a simpler classification of irreducible finite-dimensional M-modules in that case.

Let k be an algebraically closed field of characteristic 0, let g be a finite-dimensional Lie algebra over k, let A be a commutative associative unital k-algebra, and let Γ be a finite group acting by automorphisms on g and A; set M=(g⊗A)^Γ, and assume that M is perfect. Writing uce(L) for the universal central extension of a perfect Lie algebra L, understand the central extensions of M, preferably uce(M), by relating them to the known untwisted extension uce(g⊗A): after the unique lift of the Γ-action from g⊗A to uce(g⊗A), in what generality does the formula uce((g⊗A)^Γ) ≅ (uce(g⊗A))^Γ hold?

Can one develop a rigorous mathematical theory, naturally framed in terms of multiple interacting Markov chains or Markov chain Monte Carlo, for population-based metaheuristic optimization algorithms in which several search agents evolve along piecewise interacting paths, so as to prove convergence for such algorithms beyond the limited few already analyzed mathematically and to derive rigorous information about their rate of convergence?

For almost all metaheuristic optimization algorithms, including future algorithms, where global diversification (exploration) means generating diverse candidate solutions to search the space on a global scale and local intensification (exploitation) means concentrating the search in a promising region by using information from a currently good solution, is there an optimal way—through algorithmic mechanisms and/or parameter settings—to balance these two components? If such an optimal balance exists, how can it be achieved; if not, what is the best attainable trade-off between them?

For metaheuristic algorithms, where randomization is used to promote global diversification/exploration and deterministic updating promotes local intensification/exploitation, under what conditions can one mathematically explain why a balanced combination of these two components yields a substantially more efficient algorithm than either a purely deterministic algorithm or a purely random algorithm? ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1212.0220))

For a metaheuristic optimization algorithm, can one define a mathematically justified measure or test that determines whether its search dynamics achieve the balanced trade-off between local intensification (exploitation) and global diversification (exploration)—in particular, a coherent balance between randomization and deterministic components—that is associated in the paper with efficient performance and convergence under the given conditions?

Within the theory of heuristic/metaheuristic optimization algorithms, can one give a rigorous mathematical proof—under explicitly stated assumptions and with respect to a specified measure of search efficiency—that incorporating memory or search-history information significantly improves search efficiency relative to a comparable memoryless algorithm, and can one characterize precisely the conditions under which such an improvement holds?

In the metaheuristic-optimization setting considered in the paper, do No-Free-Lunch theorems hold for multiobjective optimization—given that they are proved for single-objective optimization on finite search domains and do not hold for continuous infinite domains—and, if they do or do not hold in the multiobjective case, what implications would that have for algorithm development?

In the setting of metaheuristic optimization considered in this paper, can one develop a formal theoretical analysis and an agreed performance measure for comparing different metaheuristic algorithms, beyond the two widely used criteria of absolute objective value and number of function evaluations?

For the infinite-dimensional Hamiltonian H = sum_{j∈Z^d} ω_j I_j + ε sum_{<i,j>} f_{<i,j>}(I_i, I_j; φ_i, φ_j), equipped with the symplectic structure sum_j dI_j ∧ dφ_j, where the perturbation f_{<i,j>} is analytic and O(I^2), is either short range in the sense |f_{<i,j>}| ≤ C e^{-m|i-j|} for some m > 0 or finite range in the sense f_{<i,j>} = 0 for |i-j| > ρ̃, and where the frequencies ω_j are weakly correlated (for example i.i.d. with a smooth distribution), does there exist any infinite-dimensional invariant KAM torus for initial actions I^0 = (I_j^0)_{j∈Z^d} ∈ R_+^{Z^d} having only polynomial decay, namely I_j^0 = ε_j ≈ |j|^{-M} for some large M > 0? ([cdn.sciengine.com](https://cdn.sciengine.com/doi/pdf/df39fa9b911c46db9c3ce2d6abaff89b))

In the Section 2 setting of finite-dimensional KAM tori (quasi-periodic breathers) for infinite-dimensional Hamiltonian lattice systems, suppose the linearized operator of the system—for example the lattice operator Ω^2 = -Δ_f + v—has pure point spectrum, with part of that spectrum dense in some finite interval. If one removes the short-range hypothesis on the nonlinear interaction (namely, the short-range assumptions used in Theorems 2.5 and 2.6, such as exponential spatial decay of the interaction or short-range U, V in the concrete lattice models), does the system still admit any KAM tori?

In the Section 2 setting of short-range infinite-dimensional Hamiltonian systems, suppose the linearized operator of the system—e.g. Omega^2 = -Delta_f + v in the discrete nonlinear wave/discrete nonlinear Schrodinger examples—has continuous spectrum consisting of an interval (for instance, the interval [beta, beta + 1] arising from the linearization of the coupled lattice equation (2.6) when W(x) = (1/2)x^2 + ...). Can such a system nevertheless admit any KAM tori?

Let Y be a bounded connected planar billiard table with smooth strictly convex boundary, and let φ:Φ(Y)→Φ(Y) be its billiard map on the annular phase space Φ(Y). Call Y integrable if the set of φ-invariant noncontractible topological circles in Φ(Y) has nonempty interior in Φ(Y). Must Y be an ellipse (allowing the disc as a degenerate ellipse)? ([users.math.uoc.gr](https://users.math.uoc.gr/~frantzikinakis/ErgodicUnder2024/ApplicationsBilliardsII.pdf?utm_source=openai))

Let Y ⊂ ℝ^2 be a smooth convex billiard table, i.e. a compact connected convex planar domain with smooth boundary, and consider its billiard flow given by unit-speed motion in Y with specular reflection at ∂Y. Since this billiard flow is a Hamiltonian system with two degrees of freedom, if it is integrable as a Hamiltonian system, is Y necessarily an ellipse?

Let γ⊂R^2 be a closed convex curve, let |γ| denote its perimeter, and for each ℓ>|γ| let G(γ,ℓ) be the closed convex curve containing γ in its interior obtained by the string (gardener) construction. Say that γ satisfies the transitivity property if for every ℓ1>|γ| and every ℓ2>|G(γ,ℓ1)| there exists a unique ℓ3>|γ| such that G(G(γ,ℓ1),ℓ2)=G(γ,ℓ3). Are ellipses the only closed convex curves satisfying this transitivity property? ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1301.2547))

In the setting of the standard planar billiard in a compact, connected domain Y ⊂ R^2 with specular reflection, construct examples with positive metric entropy (in the paper’s convention, positive entropy of the Liouville measure): (a) a billiard table Y that is strictly convex and has boundary ∂Y of class C^1; and (b) a billiard table Y that is convex and has boundary ∂Y of class C^2. ([users.math.uoc.gr](https://users.math.uoc.gr/~frantzikinakis/ErgodicUnder2024/ApplicationsBilliardsII.pdf?utm_source=openai))

Let Y ⊂ R^2 be a compact connected billiard table with piecewise smooth boundary, let Φ be the phase space of its billiard map, and let μ be the induced Liouville measure on Φ. If P ⊂ Φ denotes the set of periodic points of the billiard map and, for each integer n>=2, P_n ⊂ Φ denotes the set of points of exact period n, must one have μ(P)=0?

Let Omega be a compact connected planar billiard table in R^2 with piecewise smooth boundary, in the class considered in Section 3: namely, Omega is semi-dispersive if it is obtained from a not-necessarily-convex polygon by replacing some but not all sides by smooth inward-convex arcs, so that the curved boundary pieces are dispersive components and the remaining boundary pieces are neutral components; more generally, the dispersive components may be any smooth curves convex inward. Must the associated billiard map of every such semi-dispersive billiard table be hyperbolic?

Let Y be a planar dispersive billiard table, and let f_Y(n) denote the number of periodic points of the billiard map of Y whose period is at most n. Does the limit h = lim_{n -> infinity} (log f_Y(n))/n exist?

Let Y be a dispersive billiard table, and let f_Y(n) denote the number of periodic points of its billiard map whose period is at most n. Assume that the limit h = lim_{n->infinity} (1/n) log f_Y(n) exists. Must this number h (which is then automatically finite and positive by equation (2)) equal the topological entropy of the billiard map of Y?

For a fixed integer n >= 3, let T(n) be the moduli space of simple Euclidean n-gons, where polygons are identified up to scaling. This space is a finite union of combinatorial type components. Let lambda be the natural probability measure on T(n) obtained from Lebesgue measure on each combinatorial type component, and let E(n) subset T(n) be the set of n-gons whose billiard dynamics is ergodic. Is lambda(E(n)) > 0?

Exhibit a planar polygonal billiard table P that is irrational in the sense that not all angles between its sides are rational multiples of π, and such that the full billiard flow of P, with the usual specular reflection law away from corners, is not ergodic with respect to its invariant Liouville measure.

Let P be an arbitrary irrational Euclidean n-gon, let φ be its billiard map on the phase space Φ, and let μ be the invariant Liouville measure on Φ. Label the sides of P by a_1, ..., a_n, and for each i let Φ_i ⊂ Φ be the set of phase points whose base point lies on the side a_i, so that Φ = ⊔_{i=1}^n Φ_i and μ(Φ_i) = 2 Length(a_i). If M ⊂ Φ is a measurable φ-invariant set with μ(M) > 0 and Φ_i ⊂ M for some i ∈ {1, ..., n}, must it follow that M = Φ?

For every planar Euclidean polygonal billiard table P, in the broad sense of Section 4 (P need not be convex or simply connected and may include barriers), does the standard billiard in P always admit a nonsingular periodic orbit—that is, a trajectory obeying specular reflection at the sides, never hitting a corner, and returning after finitely many reflections to its initial position and direction? ([users.math.uoc.gr](https://users.math.uoc.gr/~frantzikinakis/ErgodicUnder2024/ApplicationsBilliardsII.pdf?utm_source=openai))

Let P be an irrational Euclidean polygonal billiard table, where 'irrational' means that P is not rational in the sense that not all angles between its sides are rational multiples of π. For ℓ > 0, let f_P(ℓ) denote the number of periodic bands of billiard trajectories in P whose common geometric length is at most ℓ; recall that any periodic orbit with an even number of segments lies in a parallel band of periodic orbits of the same length, whereas odd-periodic orbits are isolated. Determine explicit, efficient upper and lower bounds for the asymptotic growth of f_P(ℓ) as ℓ → ∞.

Let P be a rational polygonal billiard table, meaning that every angle between sides of P is a rational multiple of π, and let f_P(ℓ) denote the number of periodic bands of billiard trajectories in P of Euclidean length at most ℓ. By results of Masur and Boshernitzan, there exist constants 0 < c_*(P) ≤ c^*(P) < ∞ and a threshold ℓ_0(P) such that c_*(P)ℓ^2 ≤ f_P(ℓ) ≤ c^*(P)ℓ^2 for all ℓ ≥ ℓ_0(P). Obtain efficient estimates for the quadratic constants c_*(P) and c^*(P).

Let P be a rational polygonal billiard table in the sense of §4 (not assumed convex or simply connected), meaning that the angles between its sides are rational multiples of π. Let f_P(ℓ) denote the number of periodic bands of billiard trajectories in P of geometric length at most ℓ. Masur and Boshernitzan imply that there exist constants 0 < c_*(P) ≤ c^*(P) < ∞ such that c_*(P)ℓ^2 ≤ f_P(ℓ) ≤ c^*(P)ℓ^2 for all sufficiently large ℓ. Must the ratio f_P(ℓ)/ℓ^2 converge as ℓ → ∞? In other words, does every rational polygon have quadratic asymptotics?

Let P be a polygon with side alphabet A = {a, b, c, ...}. For a finite billiard orbit gamma in P, let w(gamma) be the word recording the successive sides of P hit by gamma, let the combinatorial length of gamma be the number of letters in w(gamma), and let W_n(P) be the set of codes of all billiard orbits of combinatorial length n. Define the full billiard complexity by F(n) = sum_{k <= n} |W_k(P)|, and let F_*(n) denote any conditional (partial) complexity obtained by imposing a specified additional restriction on the family of coded billiard orbits (for example, the periodic case referred to via Problem 11). Find nontrivial explicit upper and lower bounds for F_*(n) for a general polygon P (as noted in the paper, one may replace "general polygon" by "irrational polygon").

For a planar polygonal billiard table P contained in R^2, call a pair x,y in P (possibly with x = y) secure if there exists a finite blocking set B contained in P minus {x,y} such that every billiard orbit in P joining x to y meets B, and call P secure if every pair of points is secure. Characterize the secure polygons. In particular, for rational polygons (those whose side-to-side angles are rational multiples of pi), determine whether security is exactly equivalent to almost integrability, i.e. whether P is secure if and only if P can be tiled under reflections by one of the integrable polygons: a rectangle, an equilateral triangle, a 45-45-90 triangle, or a 30-60-90 triangle.

Let P be a planar Euclidean polygonal billiard table in the sense of the paper, let A(P) be its set of sides, let W_n(P) be the set of side-coding words of all finite billiard orbits in P of combinatorial length exactly n, and let F_P(n) = |W_n(P)| be the full billiard complexity. Does there exist a universal integer d ≥ 3 such that for every polygon P there are constants c_P, C_P > 0 and N_P with c_P n^3 ≤ F_P(n) ≤ C_P n^d for all n ≥ N_P?

Let P be a planar polygonal billiard table, and for x, y ∈ P let C_P(x,y) denote the set of billiard trajectories in P connecting x to y. Say that the pair (x,y) is secure if there exists a finite set B ⊂ P \ {x,y} such that every trajectory in C_P(x,y) meets B, and call P secure if every pair x, y ∈ P (including x = y) is secure. Following the paper, call the rectangles, the equilateral triangle, and the right triangles with angles 45°,45°,90° and 30°,60°,90° the integrable polygons, and call P almost integrable if it is tiled under reflections by one of these integrable polygons. Is a polygonal billiard table P secure if and only if it is almost integrable?

Let (M,g) be a compact smooth Riemannian manifold. Call (M,g) secure if for every pair of points x,y in M there exists a finite set B ⊂ M \ {x,y} such that every geodesic segment in M joining x to y passes through at least one point of B. Is (M,g) secure if and only if g is flat, equivalently, if and only if M has zero sectional curvature everywhere?

Let T be a metric tree, let H be the selfadjoint graph Hamiltonian determined by prescribed vertex conditions, and consider the power-type NLS with initial datum Psi(0) = Psi_0 in the energy domain E (the quadratic-form domain of H),
i ∂_t Psi(t) = H Psi(t) - |Psi(t)|^{2 mu} Psi(t).
Can one prove on trees an analogue of the star-graph well-posedness theorem stated in Section 1.1—namely local existence and uniqueness in E, a maximal-lifespan solution satisfying the blow-up alternative, conservation of mass and energy, and, at least for 0 < mu < 2, global well-posedness—thereby extending the then-available results beyond the dispersive estimates cited in [26,27]?

Let a metric graph be viewed as the one-dimensional limit, in a suitable sense, of a network of thin tubes or guides joined at junctions. For a nonlinear Schrödinger equation posed on the shrinking tube network, does the dynamics converge, as the transverse tube size tends to zero, to the nonlinear Schrödinger equation on the limiting metric graph, understood as a one-dimensional edgewise NLS coupled by vertex matching conditions; and, if so, which vertex boundary conditions are selected at the junctions? More specifically, how do those limiting vertex conditions depend on the way the tubes, guides, and junction region are shrunk, and on whether the boundary condition on the boundary of the thin tubes is Neumann or Dirichlet? ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1304.1182))

Can one rigorously derive, for a graph-like quasi-one-dimensional structure such as a Y-junction, an effective one-dimensional nonlinear Schrödinger/Gross-Pitaevskii equation on the limiting metric graph from a more realistic Bose-Einstein-condensate model—either by passing to the limit from NLS posed on shrinking thin tubes/guides meeting at a junction, or, as a simplification suggested in the paper, by starting directly from a suitably scaled N-body Bose theory on the graph itself—and determine exactly which vertex boundary (matching) condition is selected in the limit, including its possible dependence on the shrinking procedure for the tubes/guides/junction and on the boundary conditions on the tube walls (for example Neumann versus Dirichlet)? In particular, can this boundary-condition problem be solved already for the benchmark two-edge case, i.e. a line with a defect?

Let G be the N-edge star graph, let H = H_α be the Laplacian with attractive δ-coupling α < 0 at the vertex, and consider the focusing NLS i∂_tΨ = HΨ − |Ψ|^{2μ}Ψ on the energy space E. For the reduced action S_ω = E + (ω/2)M and its Nehari manifold N_ω = {Ψ ∈ E \ {0} : I_ω[Ψ] = 0}, it is known that if μ > 0 and −N√ω < α < α*(N,μ,ω) < 0, then S_ω restricted to N_ω has an absolute minimum (the N-tail ground state). The paper’s open question is whether, when this α-threshold fails and the absolute constrained minimum is lost because of runaway/Kirchhoff-type escape, S_ω restricted to N_ω still has a local constrained minimum whose value is strictly larger than inf_{N_ω} S_ω; and, analogously, whether the constrained energy E on the fixed-mass manifold {M[Ψ] = m} has such a local constrained minimum when m lies outside the ground-state existence regime of Theorem 2 (in particular, for 0 < μ < 2 when m > m*(N,μ,α), and with the corresponding critical-case restriction when μ = 2).

For the focusing nonlinear Schrödinger equation on a metric/quantum graph more complicated than a star graph—for instance a tree or a graph with loops—and for a regular branch of standing waves e^{i\omega t}\Phi_\omega, especially one arising by bifurcation from an eigenvalue of the underlying quantum-graph Hamiltonian, can one extend the Weinstein/Grillakis-Shatah-Strauss orbital stability/instability analysis used on star graphs to the non-explicit setting, by determining the Morse index (the number of negative eigenvalues of the relevant selfadjoint operator in the linearization/second variation of the action) and by verifying the Vakhitov-Kolokolov slope condition along the branch? citeturn20view0turn14view2

For the focusing power-type nonlinear Schrödinger equation on a metric/quantum graph, consider finite-energy standing waves Psi_t = e^{i omega t} Phi, where Phi solves the stationary equation associated with the graph Hamiltonian H and the nonlinearity |Phi|^{2mu} Phi. When the underlying linear quantum graph H has an eigenvalue (for example the linear ground state), classical bifurcation theory yields a nonlinear standing-wave branch bifurcating from the zero solution in the direction of that eigenstate. How can one obtain additional branches of nonlinear stationary states that have no such linear counterpart, as happens for the nonlinear excited states already known on star graphs; more specifically, is the correct mechanism that these excited, or more generally bound, states bifurcate from non-small solitary waves when an external potential is turned on?

For the focusing power nonlinear Schrödinger equation on an N-edge star graph 𝒢 with vertex Hamiltonian H_α (δ coupling, with the standing-wave discussion carried out for the attractive case α < 0), is a standing wave e^{iω t} Φ_ω asymptotically stable in the precise sense of eq. (2.18): namely, does every solution u(t) whose initial datum is sufficiently close to Φ_ω in the energy space 𝔈 (the quadratic-form domain of H_α) admit, as t → +∞, a decomposition u(t) = e^{iω_∞ t} Φ_{ω_∞} + U_t * Ψ_∞ + R_∞(t), where U_t is the unitary group generated by H_α, Ψ_∞ and R_∞(t) belong to L2(𝒢), ω_∞ > α^2 / N^2, and the L2(𝒢)-norm of R_∞(t) satisfies ||R_∞(t)|| = O(t^{-β}) for some β > 0?

For the focusing cubic nonlinear Schrödinger equation on a three-edge star graph (Y-junction) with Kirchhoff boundary condition at the unique vertex, in the same high-velocity scattering regime where a single incoming soliton on one edge is known to split approximately into reflected and transmitted solitary waves, does the dynamics admit multisoliton-type asymptotically traveling solutions, and what happens when several fast solitons are arranged to reach the vertex simultaneously? ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1304.1182))

For the focusing cubic nonlinear Schrödinger equation i∂tΨ = HΨ - |Ψ|^2Ψ on a metric graph whose topology is more complicated than a star graph—most notably on a tree, with H the selfadjoint graph Schrödinger/Laplacian operator determined by the vertex conditions—can one prove a fast-soliton scattering theorem analogous to the three-edge Y-junction result of §2.4? More precisely, starting from an incoming high-velocity solitary wave placed on one external edge, can one show that after interaction with the branching vertices the solution is, on the corresponding post-collision timescale, approximated in the same L^2/mass-transfer sense by reflected/transmitted outgoing waves whose weights are governed by the linear scattering data of H, under hypotheses that ensure the linear dispersive/Strichartz estimates required by the star-graph analysis?

In the fast-soliton scattering setting of Section 2.4 of the paper—namely, the focusing cubic nonlinear Schrödinger equation on a three-edge star graph (Y-junction) with Kirchhoff vertex condition, started from a large-velocity incoming truncated soliton on one edge, for which the post-collision solution is proved in L^2 to be approximated on an O(log v) time interval by one reflected and two transmitted solitary waves with amplitudes given by the linear scattering matrix—can this post-collision validity interval be extended to longer times as v goes to infinity, and, if so, is there in the graph setting any genuine analogue of the line-problem mechanism cited in the paper in which such longer-time validity depends on the initial data and on an external potential?

In the fast-soliton scattering setting of Section 2.4 for the focusing NLS on a three-edge star graph (Y-junction) with Kirchhoff coupling—starting from a single large-velocity soliton initially localized on one edge and impinging on the vertex—does an analogous post-collision description remain valid for nonlinearities that are sufficiently close to, but not exactly, the integrable cubic nonlinearity?
