More precisely, can one prove that, for all sufficiently large incoming velocities, the exact solution after the interaction is approximated in the same L^2 sense as in the cubic result by one reflected and two transmitted outgoing solitary waves, throughout a post-interaction timescale comparable to that proved in the cubic integrable case?

For the complex-valued focusing nonlinear Schrodinger equation on the simple star-graph models treated in the paper, can one rigorously describe the intermediate dynamical region in energy space lying between (i) the regime of standing waves and their neighborhood and (ii) the cubic fast-soliton scattering regime on a Kirchhoff Y-junction, and in particular explain mathematically the capture of incoming solitons by the vertex/junction and the generation of outgoing solitons?

Let M be a 3-dimensional smooth manifold, and let (f,g) be a C-infinity-generic pair of smooth vector fields on M. For the time-optimal control problem qdot = f(q) + u g(q), with measurable controls satisfying |u| <= 1 and Lipschitz admissible trajectories, is every time-optimal trajectory piecewise smooth; equivalently in the paper's terminology, does every individual time-optimal trajectory have only finitely many switching points, where a switching point is a point at which the trajectory is not smooth?

Let M be a 3-dimensional smooth manifold, and let f, g be a generic pair of smooth vector fields on M. Consider the fixed-endpoint time-optimal control problem q̇ = f(q) + u g(q), with |u| ≤ 1, where admissible controls are measurable and admissible trajectories are Lipschitz. A switching point of an admissible trajectory is a point where the trajectory is not smooth. For q ∈ M, define sw(q) to be the smallest integer k such that every time-optimal trajectory whose image is contained in some sufficiently small neighborhood of q has at most k switching points, and set sw(q) = ∞ if every neighborhood of q contains a time-optimal trajectory with infinitely many switching points. Is sw(q) < ∞ for every q ∈ M? ([paperzz.com](https://paperzz.com/doc/7063141/some-open-problems---sissa-people-personal-home-pages))

Let M be a 3-dimensional manifold, and let f,g be a generic pair of smooth (C∞) vector fields on M. Consider the fixed-endpoint time-optimal control system q̇=f(q)+u g(q), |u|≤1, where admissible controls u are measurable and admissible trajectories are Lipschitz. Is it true that every individual time-optimal trajectory has only finitely many switching points, where a switching point is a point at which the trajectory is not smooth? ([paperzz.com](https://paperzz.com/doc/7063141/some-open-problems---sissa-people-personal-home-pages))

For the fixed-endpoint time-optimal problem for a smooth single-input control-affine system on an n-dimensional manifold M, qdot = f(q) + u g(q) with |u| <= 1, where f and g are C∞ vector fields, are the known higher-dimensional extremals with accumulating switching points whose chattering structure survives C∞-small perturbations of the pair (f,g) actually time-optimal trajectories?

Let M be a real analytic n-dimensional manifold, and let f, g be real analytic vector fields on M, with no genericity assumption. Consider the fixed-endpoint minimum-time problem for the single-input control system qdot(t) = f(q(t)) + u(t) g(q(t)), with measurable controls u : [0,T] -> [-1,1] and Lipschitz admissible trajectories q : [0,T] -> M. If two points q0, q1 in M are joined by at least one time-optimal trajectory, must there exist a (possibly different) time-optimal trajectory from q0 to q1 whose set of switching points—i.e. points of the trajectory where q fails to be smooth—is at most countable?

Let M be a real analytic n-dimensional manifold, and let f and g be real analytic vector fields on M, not assumed generic. Consider the fixed-endpoint time-optimal problem for the single-input control-affine system q̇ = f(q) + u g(q), |u| ≤ 1, with measurable controls u and Lipschitz admissible trajectories. Assume that two points q0, q1 ∈ M are connected by at least one time-optimal trajectory. In the nontrivial case n ≥ 3, must there exist a time-optimal trajectory from q0 to q1 whose set of switching points—i.e. points where the trajectory is not smooth—does not have positive measure?

Let (M, Delta, g) be a smooth bracket-generating sub-Riemannian manifold, and let gamma_0, gamma_1 : [0,1] -> M be smooth admissible (horizontal) curves such that gamma_0(0) = gamma_1(0) = q_0 and dot{gamma}_0(0) wedge dot{gamma}_1(0) != 0. Must there exist an admissible curve eta joining gamma_0(1) to gamma_1(1) whose sub-Riemannian length satisfies L(eta) < L(gamma_0) + L(gamma_1), i.e. is strictly shorter than the broken path from gamma_0(1) to gamma_1(1) obtained by traversing gamma_0 backward to q_0 and then gamma_1 forward?

Let (M,Δ,g) be a smooth sub-Riemannian structure, with Δ⊂TM a smooth bracket-generating distribution, and fix q0∈M. Let Ωq0 be the smooth Hilbert manifold of H^1 admissible curves γ:[0,1]→M such that γ(0)=q0 and γ˙(t)∈Δγ(t) for almost every t, endowed with the H^1-topology. Consider the endpoint map F:Ωq0→M, F(γ)=γ(1). Must F always admit at least one regular value; that is, does there always exist q∈M such that for every γ∈F−1(q), the differential dFγ is surjective onto TqM?

Let M be a smooth sub-Riemannian manifold and fix q0 in M. Consider the endpoint map from the H^1-Hilbert manifold of admissible paths gamma:[0,1]->M with gamma(0)=q0 to M, gamma->gamma(1), and call its critical points singular curves. It is known that the subset of M reached from q0 by optimal (i.e. length-minimizing) singular curves is nowhere dense. Can this subset nevertheless have positive measure in M? ([paperzz.com](https://paperzz.com/doc/7063141/some-open-problems---sissa-people-personal-home-pages))

Let Δ⊂Tℝ^3 be a rank-2 Martinet distribution near a point q0, meaning that Δ^2:=Δ+[Δ,Δ] has rank 2 at q0 and Δ^3:=Δ^2+[Δ,Δ^2] has rank 3 at q0; let Σ={q near q0 : rank Δ^2_q=2} be the Martinet surface, so that Δ is transverse to Σ and the singular curves are exactly the integral curves of the line field Δ∩TΣ, whose sufficiently short segments are optimal. For a generic sub-Riemannian metric g on Δ, fix ε>0 sufficiently small and let S_{q0}(ε) be the corresponding sub-Riemannian sphere centered at q0. If q∈S_{q0}(ε) lies on an optimal singular curve issuing from q0, determine the C^1-equivalence class of the germ of S_{q0}(ε) at q, where two germs are identified when they are related by a germ of a C^1-diffeomorphism of ℝ^3. ([paperzz.com](https://paperzz.com/doc/7063141/some-open-problems---sissa-people-personal-home-pages))

Let Δ=span{f0,f1} be a smooth rank-2 Engel distribution in a neighborhood of q0∈R^4, meaning that n3(q)=3 and n4(q)=4, where n_k(q) is the span at q of all iterated Lie brackets of f0,f1 of length at most k. In this Engel case, each point lies on a unique singular curve and sufficiently small singular segments are optimal. Equip Δ with a generic sub-Riemannian metric, let S_{q0}(q) denote the sub-Riemannian distance from q0, and fix ε>0 small. If q∈S_{q0}^{-1}(ε) is a point where the optimal singular curve issuing from q0 meets the sphere, what is the C^1-classification, up to germs of C^1-diffeomorphisms of R^4, of the germ at q of the 3-dimensional hypersurface S_{q0}^{-1}(ε)? ([paperzz.com](https://paperzz.com/doc/7063141/some-open-problems---sissa-people-personal-home-pages))

Let q0 ∈ R^2, and let f0, f1 be smooth (C^∞) germs of vector fields at q0. For each k ≥ 1, let n_k(q) denote the span at q of all iterated Lie brackets of f0 and f1 of length at most k. Assume that f0(q0) ∧ f1(q0) = 0, n2(q0) = 1, and n3(q0) = 2. Define S_{q0}(q) to be the almost-Riemannian distance from q0 to q, i.e. the minimal time needed to steer q0 to q by a Lipschitz trajectory of dot q = u0 f0(q) + u1 f1(q) with measurable controls satisfying u0^2 + u1^2 = 1. Determine the generic C^1-equivalence classes of the function germ S_{q0} at q0 arising from such pairs (f0, f1). ([paperzz.com](https://paperzz.com/doc/7063141/some-open-problems---sissa-people-personal-home-pages))

Let Δ⊂TM be a smooth vector distribution on a smooth manifold M. Call an admissible curve singular if it is a critical point of the endpoint map for Δ, and call Δ singular transitive if any two points of M can be connected by a concatenation of singular curves. Must the full symmetry group Sym(Δ):={Φ∈Diff(M) : Φ_*Δ=Δ} be a finite-dimensional Lie group? ([paperzz.com](https://paperzz.com/doc/7063141/some-open-problems---sissa-people-personal-home-pages))

For each integer n ≥ 4, let μ(n) be the least positive integer m with the following property: for every smooth closed convex plane curve γ:S^1→R^2, the m-fold traversal t↦γ(mt), viewed as a curve in R^n via R^2⊂R^n, admits a sufficiently small smooth perturbation γ̃:S^1→R^n such that γ̃ is nondegenerate at every t, i.e. γ̃̇(t) ∧ γ̃''(t) ∧ ··· ∧ γ̃^(n)(t) ≠ 0 for all t∈S^1. Given that μ(2)=1 and μ(3)=2, determine μ(n) for n>3.

For each n > 3, determine μ(n), the smallest positive integer m such that an m-fold traversal of a smooth closed convex plane curve admits a small nondegenerate perturbation as a closed curve in R^n, where nondegenerate means that γ̇(t) ∧ ··· ∧ γ^(n)(t) ≠ 0 for all t ∈ S^1; and decide whether every smooth closed nondegenerate curve γ:S^1→R^n, with orthonormal Frenet frame E:S^1→O(n), satisfies Len(E) > μ(n)·Len(SO(2)), where SO(2) ⊂ O(n) is the standard shortest closed geodesic (with O(n) equipped with its standard bi-invariant metric).

Fix d ∈ {2,3} and an arbitrary open set D ⊂ T^d = R^d/(2πZ^d). Let V = {u ∈ H^1(T^d,R^d) : div u = 0}, and consider the periodic incompressible Navier–Stokes system ∂_t u + (u,∇)u − νΔu + ∇p = η(t,x), div u = 0, with ν > 0. Does there exist, and can one effectively construct, a finite-dimensional subspace E ⊂ {v ∈ V : supp v ⊂ D̄} that is independent of ν, such that for every ν > 0 the corresponding control system admits one or both of the following properties in any time: (i) approximate controllability, meaning that for every u0,u1 ∈ V, every t1 > 0, and every ε > 0, there exists a bounded control η with η(t,·) ∈ E for 0 ≤ t ≤ t1 and a solution u with u(0,·) = u0 and ||u(t1,·) − u1||_{L^2} < ε; and/or (ii) controllability in finite-dimensional projections, meaning that for every u0,u1 ∈ V, every t1 > 0, and every finite-dimensional subspace F ⊂ V, there exists such a bounded control and solution with u(0,·) = u0 and P_F(u(t1,·) − u1) = 0, where P_F is the L^2-orthogonal projector onto F?

For the incompressible Navier–Stokes system on the torus T^d = R^d / 2πZ^d, with d ∈ {2,3}, periodic boundary conditions, and state space V = {u ∈ H^1(T^d, R^d) : div u = 0}, fix an open set D ⊂ T^d. Does there exist, and can one effectively construct, a finite-dimensional subspace E ⊂ {v ∈ V : supp v ⊂ D̄}, independent of the viscosity ν > 0, such that for every u0, u1 ∈ V, every time t1 > 0, and every finite-dimensional subspace F ⊂ V, one can choose a bounded control η : [0,t1] → E for which the corresponding solution of ∂_t u + (u,∇)u − νΔu + ∇p = η, div u = 0, with u(0) = u0, satisfies P_F(u(t1) − u1) = 0, where P_F is the L^2-orthogonal projection onto F?

Let S be a numerical semigroup minimally generated by positive integers n1,...,ne, with gcd(n1,...,ne)=1 and embedding dimension e=e(S)>=3. Determine the Frobenius number F(S), that is, the largest integer not belonging to S, in terms of the generators n1,...,ne.

Given a numerical semigroup S=<n1,...,ne> subseteq N minimally generated by positive integers 0<n1<...<ne with gcd(n1,...,ne)=1 and e>=3, find a formula, in terms of the generators n1,...,ne, for the genus g(S)=|N\S|.

For a numerical semigroup S ⊆ ℕ, let PF(S) = {x ∈ ℕ ∖ S : x + s ∈ S for every nonzero s ∈ S} be its set of pseudo-Frobenius numbers, and let t(S) = |PF(S)| be its type. If one fixes admissible values of one or more standard invariants of S—its multiplicity m(S) = min(S ∖ {0}), embedding dimension e(S) equal to the number of elements in the unique minimal system of generators of S, genus g(S) = |ℕ ∖ S|, and Frobenius number F(S) = max(ℕ ∖ S)—determine or characterize the possible values of t(S). ([cim.pt](https://www.cim.pt/magazines/bulletin/7/article/65/pdf))

Does every numerical semigroup S ⊆ N = {0,1,2,...}, meaning every additive submonoid containing 0 with finite complement in N, satisfy Wilf's inequality e(S)g(S) ≤ (e(S) - 1)(F(S) + 1), where F(S) = max(N\S), g(S) = |N\S|, and e(S) is the cardinality of the unique minimal system of generators of S?

Let N = {0,1,2,...}, and let a numerical semigroup be a submonoid S ⊆ N whose complement N∖S is finite. For each integer g ≥ 0, let n_g denote the number of numerical semigroups S with genus g(S) = |N∖S| = g. Is it true that n_{g+1} > n_g for every g ≥ 0?

Let N = {0,1,2,...}, and for positive integers a and b define the modular numerical semigroup S(a,b,1) := {x in N : ax mod b <= x}, where ax mod b denotes the least nonnegative residue of ax modulo b. Using the standard reduction noted for proportionally modular semigroups, one may assume 1 < a < b. Determine explicit formulas, in terms of a and b, for the Frobenius number F(S(a,b,1)), the multiplicity m(S(a,b,1)), the type t(S(a,b,1)) = |PF(S(a,b,1))|, and the embedding dimension e(S(a,b,1)) of S(a,b,1), where PF(S) = {f in Z \ S : f + s in S for all s in S \ {0}} and e(S) is the size of the unique minimal system of generators of S. (The genus g(S(a,b,1)) is excluded, since the paper notes that a formula for it is already known.)

Let S ⊊ ℕ be a modular numerical semigroup, meaning that there exist positive integers a and b such that S = {x ∈ ℕ : (ax mod b) ≤ x}, where ax mod b denotes the least nonnegative residue of ax modulo b. If e(S) is the embedding dimension of S, g(S) = |ℕ \ S| its genus, and F(S) = max(ℕ \ S) its Frobenius number, does every such modular numerical semigroup satisfy Wilf's inequality e(S)g(S) ≤ (e(S) - 1)(F(S) + 1)?

Let S=⟨n1,…,ne⟩⊂ℕ be a numerical semigroup with unique minimal generating system 0<n1<⋯<ne, and assume that S is proportionally modular, i.e. S={x∈ℕ : ax mod b ≤ cx} for some positive integers a,b,c (equivalently, one may take c<a<b). Write F(S)=max(ℕ\S), g(S)=|ℕ\S|, and t(S)=|PF(S)|, where PF(S)={x∈ℤ\S : x+s∈S for every s∈S\{0}}. Find explicit formulas for F(S), g(S), and t(S) that depend only on the minimal generating system n1,…,ne. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1304.6552))

Does there exist an algorithm that, given the minimal generating set of a numerical semigroup S ⊆ N = {0,1,2,...}, decides whether there exist a,b,c,d ∈ N with b > 0 and c > 0 such that S = {x ∈ N : (ax mod b) ≤ cx − d} ∪ {0}, where ax mod b denotes the least nonnegative residue of ax modulo b?

Given a numerical semigroup T ⊆ N = {0,1,2,...}, determine whether there exist a numerical semigroup S and a positive integer p such that e(S) = 3, where e(S) denotes the cardinality of the minimal system of generators of S, and T = S/p := {x in N : px in S}; more specifically, find a criterion or procedure that distinguishes numerical semigroups of this form from those that are not, and decide whether any numerical semigroup fails to arise in this way. ([cim.pt](https://www.cim.pt/magazines/bulletin/7/article/65/pdf))

Let S ⊆ N be a numerical semigroup, where N denotes the nonnegative integers, and define its half by S/2 = {x ∈ N : 2x ∈ S}. If S satisfies Wilf’s conjecture in the form e(S)g(S) ≤ (e(S)-1)(F(S)+1), where e(T) is the embedding dimension of a numerical semigroup T, g(T)=|N\T| is its genus, and F(T)=max(N\T) is its Frobenius number, must S/2 also satisfy Wilf’s conjecture, i.e. e(S/2)g(S/2) ≤ (e(S/2)-1)(F(S/2)+1)?

Let S ⊆ N be a numerical semigroup, that is, an additive submonoid containing 0 whose complement in N is finite. Call a numerical semigroup irreducible if it cannot be written as the intersection of two numerical semigroups that properly contain it. Since every numerical semigroup can be expressed as a finite intersection of irreducible numerical semigroups, determine, for a given numerical semigroup S, the least integer k such that S = S1 ∩ ··· ∩ Sk for some irreducible numerical semigroups S1,...,Sk, and decide whether there exists a universal positive integer N such that every numerical semigroup S admits such a decomposition with k ≤ N.

Let N={0,1,2,...}. If S⊆N is a numerical semigroup of the form S={0}∪{x∈N : (ax mod b) <= x-c} for some a,b,c∈N with b>0, where ax mod b denotes the least nonnegative remainder of ax modulo b, must S admit a Toms decomposition; equivalently in the sense used in the paper, must S be expressible as a finite intersection of proportionally modular numerical semigroups?

Let S ⊆ ℕ = {0,1,2,...} be a numerical semigroup, and suppose S is the solution set of a finite system of one-variable proportionally modular Diophantine inequalities a_i x mod b_i ≤ c_i x for i = 1, ..., r, where a_i, b_i, c_i are positive integers and a_i x mod b_i denotes the least nonnegative residue of a_i x modulo b_i. Must there exist a finite system of modular Diophantine inequalities a'_j x mod b'_j ≤ x for j = 1, ..., s, with a'_j, b'_j positive integers, whose solution set in ℕ is exactly S? Equivalently, is every numerical semigroup that admits a Toms decomposition a finite intersection of modular numerical semigroups?

Let N = {0,1,2,...}. A numerical semigroup is a subset S of N that contains 0, is closed under addition, and has finite complement in N. For such an S, let FG(S) denote the set of its fundamental gaps, namely those x in N not in S such that {2x,3x} is contained in S (equivalently, kx belongs to S for every integer k >= 2). Find simple checkable conditions on a finite subset X of N minus {0} that allow one to decide whether there exists a numerical semigroup S with FG(S) = X.

Let S ⊆ ℕ be a numerical semigroup, and for a positive integer p define the quotient of a numerical semigroup U by p to be U/p := {x ∈ ℕ : px ∈ U}. A numerical semigroup T is called a double of S if S = T/2. Writing F(T) for the Frobenius number of T, determine a formula depending only on S for the quantity min{F(T) : T is a numerical semigroup and T/2 = S}.

Let ℳ = {S ⊆ ℕ : S is a numerical semigroup and e(S) = m(S)}, where a numerical semigroup is a cofinite submonoid of ℕ containing 0, m(S) is the multiplicity of S (its least positive element), and e(S) is the embedding dimension of S (the number of elements in its unique minimal system of generators). A Frobenius variety is a nonempty family 𝒱 of numerical semigroups such that (i) S,T ∈ 𝒱 implies S ∩ T ∈ 𝒱, and (ii) if S ∈ 𝒱 and S ≠ ℕ, then S ∪ {F(S)} ∈ 𝒱, where F(S) is the Frobenius number of S. Determine the Frobenius variety generated by ℳ, that is, the intersection of all Frobenius varieties containing every maximal-embedding-dimension numerical semigroup.

Let VT be the family of numerical semigroups S subseteq N (that is, cofinite additive submonoids of N containing 0) that admit a Toms decomposition: there exist n >= 1 and positive integers q1,...,qn,m1,...,mn,L such that gcd(qi,mi)=gcd(L,qi)=gcd(L,mi)=1 for every i and S = intersection_{i=1}^n (<qi,mi>/L), where <qi,mi>/L := {x in N : Lx is in the numerical semigroup generated by qi and mi}. A Frobenius variety is a nonempty family V of numerical semigroups such that (i) S,T in V implies S intersect T in V, and (ii) if S in V and S is not equal to N, then S union {F(S)} is in V, where F(S) is the Frobenius number of S. Since VT is a Frobenius variety and every numerical semigroup of embedding dimension 2 belongs to VT, is VT exactly the Frobenius variety generated by all embedding-dimension-two numerical semigroups; equivalently, is VT the least Frobenius variety containing every numerical semigroup whose minimal system of generators has cardinality 2?

Let V be an infinite Frobenius variety of numerical semigroups, where a numerical semigroup is a submonoid S of N = {0,1,2,...} with finite complement, and where V is a nonempty family of numerical semigroups such that (i) S,T in V implies S ∩ T in V, and (ii) if S in V and S ≠ N, then S ∪ {F(S)} is in V, with F(S) the Frobenius number of S. Let G(V) be the rooted tree with vertex set V, root N, and parent relation given by: T is a child of S exactly when S = T ∪ {F(T)}. Is it true that for every n ≥ 0, the number of vertices of G(V) at level n+1 is strictly larger than the number of vertices at level n?

Let N = {0,1,2,...}. A numerical semigroup is a cofinite submonoid S of N, and F(S) denotes its Frobenius number. A Frobenius variety is a nonempty family R of numerical semigroups such that: (i) if S,T are in R, then S intersect T is in R; and (ii) if S is in R and S is not equal to N, then S union {F(S)} is in R. Let G(R) be the rooted tree whose vertices are the elements of R and whose edges are the pairs (S,T) with T = S union {F(S)}, and for n >= 0 let L_n be the set of vertices at distance n from the root N. Characterize those Frobenius varieties R for which |L_{n+1}| > |L_n| for every n >= 0; equivalently, characterize the Frobenius varieties that verify the Bras-Amorós conjecture in the sense of Section 4.

Let V be a Frobenius variety of numerical semigroups, that is, a nonempty family V of cofinite submonoids of ℕ such that (i) S,T∈V implies S∩T∈V, and (ii) if S∈V and S≠ℕ, then S∪{F(S)}∈V, where F(S)=max(ℕ∖S). For S∈V, let g(S)=|ℕ∖S|, and let e_V(S) denote the cardinality of the unique minimal V-system of generators of S as a V-monoid (equivalently, of the unique minimal subset A⊆S such that S is the intersection of all V-monoids containing A). Characterize those Frobenius varieties V for which every S∈V satisfies the inequality e_V(S)g(S) ≤ (e_V(S)−1)(F(S)+1). ([cim.pt](https://www.cim.pt/magazines/bulletin/7/article/65/pdf))

Let Sym be the family of all symmetric numerical semigroups S ⊆ ℕ, where ℕ = {0,1,2,…}, F(S) denotes the Frobenius number of S, and S is called symmetric if for every integer x, x ∉ S implies F(S) − x ∈ S. Determine the least Frobenius variety containing Sym; equivalently, determine the family ⋂{𝒱 : 𝒱 is a Frobenius variety and Sym ⊆ 𝒱}, where a Frobenius variety is a nonempty family 𝒱 of numerical semigroups such that (i) if S,T ∈ 𝒱, then S ∩ T ∈ 𝒱, and (ii) if S ∈ 𝒱 and S ≠ ℕ, then S ∪ {F(S)} ∈ 𝒱. ([cim.pt](https://www.cim.pt/magazines/bulletin/7/article/65/pdf))

Let PS be the class of all pseudo-symmetric numerical semigroups S⊆N, where a numerical semigroup is a cofinite additive submonoid of N, F(S) denotes the Frobenius number of S, and pseudo-symmetric means that F(S) is even and, for every x∉S, either F(S)-x∈S or x=F(S)/2. Determine the Frobenius variety generated by PS; equivalently, determine the least nonempty family V of numerical semigroups containing every S in PS such that (i) if S,T∈V, then S∩T∈V, and (ii) if S∈V and S≠N, then S∪{F(S)}∈V.

Which numerical semigroups T⊆N arise as quotients of complete intersection numerical semigroups by positive integers? Equivalently stated in fully explicit form: characterize all numerical semigroups T for which there exist a complete intersection numerical semigroup S⊆N and an integer p≥1 such that T=S/p:={x∈N: px∈S}.

Let CI be the family of all complete intersection numerical semigroups, i.e. numerical semigroups S ⊆ ℕ whose minimal presentations have cardinality e(S) - 1, where e(S) denotes the embedding dimension of S. Determine the Frobenius variety generated by CI, that is, the smallest family 𝒱 of numerical semigroups containing CI such that: (i) if S,T ∈ 𝒱, then S ∩ T ∈ 𝒱; and (ii) if S ∈ 𝒱 and S ≠ ℕ, then S ∪ {F(S)} ∈ 𝒱, where F(S) is the Frobenius number of S.

Let a numerical semigroup mean a cofinite submonoid S⊆ℕ containing 0. For such an S, let m(S) be its multiplicity (the least positive element of S) and e(S) its embedding dimension (the cardinality of its unique minimal system of generators); say that S has maximal embedding dimension if e(S)=m(S). If S1=⟨n1,…,nr⟩ and S2=⟨m1,…,ms⟩ are numerical semigroups given by their minimal systems of generators, and if α∈S1∖{n1,…,nr} and β∈S2∖{m1,…,ms} satisfy gcd(α,β)=1, their gluing is the numerical semigroup ⟨βn1,…,βnr,αm1,…,αms⟩. Determine, with respect to inclusion, the least family F of numerical semigroups such that (i) every numerical semigroup of maximal embedding dimension belongs to F, and (ii) F is closed under gluing.

Let S be a numerical semigroup, i.e. S is a subset of N containing 0, closed under addition, and with finite complement in N. Let F(S) be its Frobenius number, and assume that S is symmetric, meaning that for every integer x, if x is not in S then F(S) - x is in S. Let e(S) denote the embedding dimension of S, namely the cardinality of its unique minimal system of generators. If sigma is a minimal presentation of S, in the sense that sigma is a finite subset of N^{e(S)} x N^{e(S)} with S isomorphic to N^{e(S)}/<sigma> and |sigma| minimal among all such presentations, does there exist a function f: N -> N such that |sigma| <= f(e(S)) for every symmetric numerical semigroup S?

Let n ≥ 2 and let σ be the n-element subset of ℕ^n × ℕ^n given by σ = {((c1,0,…,0),(0,a12,…,a1n)), ((0,c2,0,…,0),(a21,0,a23,…,a2n)), …, ((0,…,0,cn),(an1,…,a(n,n-1),0))}, where c1,…,cn and the aij are nonnegative integers. What necessary and sufficient conditions on these integers ensure that the quotient monoid ℕ^n/⟨σ⟩, with ⟨σ⟩ the congruence generated by σ, is isomorphic as a commutative monoid to a numerical semigroup? ([cim.pt](https://www.cim.pt/magazines/bulletin/7/article/65/pdf))

In the embedding-dimension-three numerical semigroup setting considered in Section 6, given six positive integers r12, r13, r21, r23, r31, r32, determine necessary and sufficient conditions under which the three integers m1 = r12*r13 + r12*r23 + r13*r32, m2 = r13*r21 + r21*r23 + r23*r31, and m3 = r12*r31 + r21*r32 + r31*r32 are pairwise relatively prime; equivalently, gcd(m1,m2)=gcd(m1,m3)=gcd(m2,m3)=1.

Let H = ⟨n1,n2,n3⟩ be a numerical semigroup minimally generated by three pairwise relatively prime positive integers. For each i in {1,2,3}, define ci = min{k in N_{>0} : k ni belongs to ⟨{n1,n2,n3} \ {ni}⟩}; in particular, c3 = min{k in N_{>0} : k n3 belongs to ⟨n1,n2⟩}. Let u be a positive integer such that u n2 ≡ 1 mod n1, and for positive integers a,b,c define S(a,b,c) = {x in N : a x mod b ≤ c x}. Find a formula, in terms of n1, n2, n3 alone, for the multiplicity m(S(u n2 n3, n1 n2, n3)). Equivalently, find a formula for c3, since c3 = m(⟨n1,n2⟩/n3) = m(S(u n2 n3, n1 n2, n3)); as explained in the paper, such a formula would provide the missing ingredient needed to solve the Frobenius problems for embedding-dimension-three numerical semigroups in this pairwise coprime setting.

Let N = {0,1,2,...}. For a nonempty subset A of N, write <A> for the submonoid of N generated by A. If S is a numerical semigroup and d is a positive integer, define its quotient by d to be S/d = {x in N : dx in S}. For pairwise relatively prime integers a,b,c >= 2 and an integer n >= 3, consider the quotient numerical semigroup S = <a^n,b^n>/c, which is proportionally modular. Prove directly, without invoking Fermat's Last Theorem (or the Wiles-Taylor proof), that S is not minimally generated by the set {a^n, c^(n-1), b^n}; here 'minimally generated by' means that S = <a^n, c^(n-1), b^n> and no proper subset of {a^n, c^(n-1), b^n} generates S.

Let S = <n1 < ... < ne> be a numerical semigroup. For s in S, let omega(S,s) be the least positive integer N such that whenever s divides s1 + ... + sk for some s1, ..., sk in S, there exists a subset {i1, ..., ir} of {1, ..., k} with r <= N such that s divides s_{i1} + ... + s_{ir}; define omega(S) = max{omega(S,n1), ..., omega(S,ne)}. For s in S, let Z(s) = {(x1,...,xe) in N^e : x1 n1 + ... + xe ne = s}, define d(x,y) = max{|x - gcd(x,y)|, |y - gcd(x,y)|} with gcd taken coordinatewise and |x| = x1 + ... + xe, and let t(s) be the least N such that for every i with s - ni in S and every x in Z(s), there exists y = (y1,...,ye) in Z(s) with yi != 0 and d(x,y) <= N; set t(S) = sup_{s in S} t(s). Characterize the numerical semigroups S for which omega(S) != t(S).

Characterize the finite nonempty subsets F of the positive integers for which there exist a numerical semigroup S⊆N_0, with minimal generating set S=⟨n_1,...,n_p⟩, and an element s∈S such that, if Z_S(s)={a=(a_1,...,a_p)∈N_0^p : a_1n_1+...+a_pn_p=s} is the set of factorizations of s and L_S(s)={a_1+...+a_p : a∈Z_S(s)} is its set of lengths, then L_S(s)=F. ([cim.pt](https://www.cim.pt/magazines/bulletin/7/article/65/pdf))

Let S = <n1,...,np> be a numerical semigroup, minimally generated by n1,...,np. For s in S, let Z(s) = {(a1,...,ap) in N_0^p : a1 n1 + ... + ap np = s}. For z = (a1,...,ap) and z' = (b1,...,bp) in Z(s), define gcd(z,z') = (min(a1,b1),...,min(ap,bp)), let |(u1,...,up)| = u1 + ... + up, and set d(z,z') = max(|z - gcd(z,z')|, |z' - gcd(z,z')|). If an N-chain from z to z' means a sequence z = z0, z1, ..., zt = z' in Z(s) with d(zi,zi+1) <= N for every i, define c(s) to be the least N such that every two factorizations of s are joined by an N-chain. Is it true that for every numerical semigroup S there exist n in S and s0 in S such that c(s+n) = c(s) for all s in S with s >= s0?

Let S = <n1,...,n_e> be a numerical semigroup with minimal generators n1,...,n_e, let phi: N^e -> S be given by phi(a1,...,a_e) = a1 n1 + ... + a_e n_e, and let Z(s) = phi^{-1}(s). For x,y in N^e, write gcd(x,y) = (min(x1,y1),...,min(x_e,y_e)) and d(x,y) = max(|x - gcd(x,y)|, |y - gcd(x,y)|), where |(a1,...,a_e)| = a1 + ... + a_e. For s in S, define t(s) to be the least integer N such that for every i in {1,...,e} with s - n_i in S and every x in Z(s), there exists y = (y1,...,y_e) in Z(s) with y_i not equal to 0 and d(x,y) <= N. Is the sequence {t(s)}_{s in S} eventually periodic, in the sense that there exist n in S, n > 0, and M in N such that t(s+n) = t(s) for all s in S with s >= M? ([cim.pt](https://www.cim.pt/magazines/bulletin/7/article/65/pdf))

Can one develop an effective engineering description of deterministic chaos—and, by extension, of Navier–Stokes turbulence—possibly in terms of a new kind of averaging, that can do the job Reynolds averaging was meant to do but cannot do for chaos/turbulence because its mean-plus-small-stochastic-perturbation ansatz leads to an unsolvable closure problem; more specifically, can one find a description with genuine engineering value that improves on fractal dimension and SRB measures as descriptions of strange attractors, and can the paper’s most promising candidate, shadowing (in the horseshoe/Bernoulli-shift framework), be made computationally feasible for shadowing the entire turbulent attractor at moderate Reynolds number, while recognizing that for large Reynolds number fully developed turbulence may be even harder to describe because it is more than chaos in Navier–Stokes equations?

In the incompressible 2D/3D Euler-Navier-Stokes setting considered in the paper, is the correct turbulence-physics mechanism for sufficiently large Reynolds number (equivalently, sufficiently small viscosity) rough dependence on initial data - i.e. short term unpredictability - rather than the sensitive dependence on initial data of chaos? More precisely, given that for the Euler equations the time-t solution map from initial data to the solution at time t is, for every t != 0 within the local-existence interval, continuous but nowhere locally uniformly continuous and nowhere differentiable, and given the paper's claim that for Navier-Stokes at large Reynolds number the derivative of the solution map should be extremely large everywhere because the Navier-Stokes map approaches the Euler map as Re -> infinity (heuristically of size about exp(C sqrt(t Re))), does this explain why high-Reynolds-number violent turbulence can develop substantial effects from arbitrarily small initial perturbations in very short time, whereas turbulence at not-large-enough Reynolds number may instead be due to ordinary chaotic sensitive dependence?

In the specific setting highlighted in Section 4, can the thermodynamic arrow of time be explained by the following chaos-based mechanism: N bouncing balls, or in the large-N case gas molecules, are initially released from one half of a box into the whole box, evolve for sufficiently long time under microscopically time-reversible Newtonian dynamics, and then have all velocities simultaneously reversed, yet unavoidable perturbations amplified by the chaotic flow make the probability that all particles return to the original half box only about 2^{-N}, so that observable macroscopic irreversibility and one-way entropy change emerge despite microscopic reversibility; and, in the analogous cosmological case, would the universe still be expanding if the velocity of every object or molecule were simultaneously reversed? ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1305.2864.pdf))

For the predator-prey model dU/dT = alpha*U*(1 - U/b) - gamma*(U/(U+h))*V and dV/dT = (kappa*gamma*(U/(U+h)) - mu)*V, where U and V are prey and predator densities and alpha, b, h, gamma, kappa, mu are the ecological parameters defined in Section 5, should the paradox of enrichment be understood, in the sense of this paper, as a genuine prediction that increasing the prey carrying capacity b (with the other parameters fixed) makes extinction more likely by destabilizing the steady state and producing a limit cycle approaching the V-axis, or as an artifact of this specific model once one passes to the dimensionless variables u = U/b, v = V*gamma/(alpha*b), t = alpha*T, for which the system depends on H = h/b, r = mu/(kappa*gamma), and k = kappa*gamma/alpha, so that increasing b and decreasing h both simply decrease the same governing capacity-predation number H?

In Section 6 of arXiv:1305.2864, the paradox of pesticides is modeled by the single-pulse forced Lotka-Volterra system dH/dt = H(a - bP) - αΔ(t - T), dP/dt = P(bcH - d) - βΔ(t - T), where H(t) is the pest population, P(t) is the predator population, a, b, c, d, α, β are positive constants, T is the pesticide-application time, and Δ(t - T) = 1/ε for t in [T, T + ε] and 0 otherwise. Starting from a pre-pesticide trajectory of the unforced system, determine how the phase-plane position at the application time T and the pesticide amounts α and β decide whether the post-application orbit leads to suppression of the pest or instead to pest resurgence, meaning that a later maximum of H rises well beyond the crop’s economic threshold. In particular, formulate the question so that it captures the paper’s two claims: spraying when both H and P are relatively large can reduce both populations, whereas spraying when either H or P is relatively small, or spraying too large an amount, can move the system onto a larger cycle and produce a later pest outbreak; and explain why resurgence may still occur even when only the pest is directly reduced by the pesticide.

In the setting of the plankton paradox from Section 7, can Hutchinson’s non-equilibrium explanation—that the ecological equilibrium is not actually reached—be realized within the specific PDE model proposed in the paper: for x ∈ R^3 and species n = 1,…,N, with turbulent water velocity v(t,x), limiting-resource density f(t,x), plankton densities ρ_n(t,x), and species drifts w_n = κ_n∇f + random noise or random walk, does the system ∂_t f + (v·∇)f = -G(ρ_1,…,ρ_N)f + F(t,x), ∂_t ρ_n + [(v+w_n)·∇]ρ_n = H_n(f)ρ_n, where G(0,…,0)=0 and is strictly increasing in each ρ_n, H_n(f_n)=0 and is strictly increasing in f, and F(t,x)>0 is periodic in t with relatively long period, explain how many phytoplankton species can persist while competing for a single limiting nutrient even though competitive exclusion predicts that only one or a few species should survive at equilibrium?

Does there exist an elementary proof—understood in the sense of avoiding Hirzebruch’s original appeal to Thom’s computation of the oriented bordism ring over Q and also avoiding the Atiyah-Singer index theorem—of the Hirzebruch signature theorem asserting that for every closed smooth oriented manifold M one has τ(M) = ⟨L(p1, ..., pk), [M]⟩, where L(p1, ..., pk) is the Hirzebruch L-polynomial in the Pontryagin classes of M; and can one give a geometric explanation of the virtual-signature identity τ(x + y) = τ(x) + τ(y) - τ(x, y, x + y) for x, y in H_{n-2}(M; Z), where τ(x) is the signature of a smooth closed oriented codimension-2 submanifold representing x and τ(x1, ..., xr) is defined by taking the signature of the transverse intersection of representatives?

Let M^n be a smooth real n-manifold and let H ⊂ GL(n,R) be a fixed closed subgroup. Is there a general criterion that determines whether M^n admits an integrable H-structure, i.e. a reduction of the frame bundle of M to H that is locally equivalent to the standard flat H-structure on R^n?

For a smooth real manifold M^{2k+1} and a fixed integer r with 0 <= r <= k, determine necessary and sufficient conditions for M to admit a Pfaffian equation in the large that is locally equivalent to dx_{2k+1} + x_1 dx_{k+1} + ... + x_r dx_{k+r} = 0, equivalently a Pfaffian equation whose class is everywhere 2r+1; in global form, after choosing a defining 1-form alpha (which is inessential up to passing to a two-fold cover if needed), determine when there exists a smooth real 1-form alpha on M such that alpha wedge (d alpha)^r is nowhere zero on M and alpha wedge (d alpha)^(r+1) vanishes identically on M.

Let d(n) be defined by n + d(n) = min{ m in N : RP^n admits a differentiable embedding into R^m }. Determine d(n) for every n; equivalently, determine the optimal Euclidean embedding dimension of RP^n for each n. In particular, for n = 6, determine whether d(6) = 3, 4, or 5, i.e. whether the minimal embedding dimension of RP^6 is 9, 10, or 11.

Does there exist a smooth closed embedded surface Sigma subset E^4 of genus 2 such that the Gaussian curvature K of the metric induced from the standard Euclidean metric on E^4 satisfies K(p) < 0 for every p in Sigma? More strongly, can one choose such a surface with constant negative Gaussian curvature, i.e. K identically equal to c for some constant c < 0?

Let (M^{2n}, J) be a closed almost-complex manifold. For each bidegree (p,q) with 0 ≤ p,q ≤ n and for each Hermitian structure compatible with J, let A^{p,q}(M) be the space of complex-valued (p,q)-forms, let \bar\partial be the component of d that raises q by one, let \bar\partial^* be its L^2-adjoint, and define the d-bar Laplacian by \Box_{\bar\partial} = \bar\partial^*\bar\partial + \bar\partial\bar\partial^*. If H^{p,q} := ker(\Box_{\bar\partial}|_{A^{p,q}(M)}) and h^{p,q} := dim_C H^{p,q}, are the numbers h^{p,q} independent of the chosen Hermitian structure? If not, can one give another definition of numbers h^{p,q}(J), depending only on the almost-complex structure J, that in the integrable case coincide with the usual h^{p,q} of a compact complex manifold?

Does the smooth manifold underlying complex projective 3-space CP^3 admit an integrable complex structure J such that the second Chern class of its holomorphic tangent bundle vanishes, i.e. c_2(T^{1,0}_J CP^3)=0 in H^4(CP^3; Z)?

Let M be the smooth manifold underlying complex projective space CP^n, equipped with its usual differentiable structure. Determine all integrable complex structures on M. In particular, determine all such complex structures that admit a Kähler metric. Since the Kähler case yields only the standard complex structure, the remaining open part is whether M admits any non-Kähler complex structures when n > 2, and, if so, to determine them.

Determine all complex structures on the smooth 4-manifold S^2 × S^2: equivalently, since the only compact complex surfaces diffeomorphic to the standard smooth S^2 × S^2 are the even Hirzebruch surfaces, must every compact complex surface homeomorphic to S^2 × S^2 be biholomorphic to an even Hirzebruch surface, or can there exist a non-Hirzebruch complex surface on a manifold homeomorphic but not diffeomorphic to S^2 × S^2? ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1305.4623))

For each complex dimension n, classify all Q-linear combinations of the Hodge numbers h^{p,q}(X) and Chern characteristic numbers of smooth complex projective n-folds X that depend only on the underlying manifold, distinguishing the four notions of invariance: oriented homeomorphism, oriented diffeomorphism, unoriented homeomorphism, and unoriented diffeomorphism.

Let x:M^n→E^{n+1} be an isometric immersion of a connected n-dimensional Riemannian manifold into Euclidean (n+1)-space, and let Δ denote the Laplacian of the induced metric on M. Suppose the position vector field admits a finite spectral decomposition x=c+x_1+⋯+x_k, where c∈E^{n+1} is constant and each x_i:M→E^{n+1} is nonconstant with Δx_i=λ_i x_i for some real λ_i. Such a hypersurface is said to be of finite type. Classify all finite type hypersurfaces in E^{n+1}; in particular, classify all finite type surfaces in E^3.

Let x: M^2 -> E^3 be an immersion of a connected compact surface M, endowed with the metric induced from E^3 and Laplace-Beltrami operator Delta. Suppose x is of finite type in the sense that its position vector field has a finite spectral decomposition x = c + x_1 + ... + x_k for some constant vector c in E^3 and nonconstant maps x_i: M -> E^3 satisfying Delta x_i = lambda_i x_i. Must x(M) be a round 2-sphere in E^3?

Let x: M^n -> E^{n+1} be an isometric immersion of a connected compact hypersurface. Suppose x is of finite type, meaning that its position vector admits a spectral decomposition x = c + x1 + ... + xk with c in E^{n+1}, each xi non-constant, and Delta xi = lambda_i xi for the Laplace operator Delta of the induced metric on M. Must M be an ordinary hypersphere (equivalently, a round sphere S^n(r) in E^{n+1})?

Let x:M^n→S^{n+1}⊂E^{n+2} be a connected immersed hypersurface of a Euclidean hypersphere. Classify all such hypersurfaces for which, when x is viewed as an immersion into E^{n+2}, the position vector field is of finite type in Chen’s sense; equivalently, x admits a finite spectral decomposition x=c+x_1+⋯+x_k with Δx_i=λ_i x_i for the Laplacian Δ of the induced metric on M.

Let x:M^2→S^3⊂E^4 be a connected immersed surface in the standard 3-sphere, viewed as an E^4-valued immersion, and let Δ be the Laplace-Beltrami operator of the induced metric on M. Does there exist any such surface that is of finite k-type for some integer k>2; equivalently in the paper’s terminology, can one have a decomposition x=c+x1+⋯+xk with c∈E^4 constant, each xi nonconstant, and Δxi=λi xi for k distinct real eigenvalues λ1,…,λk?

Let x:M^2->S^3 subset E^4 be a connected smooth immersed surface in the unit 3-sphere, and interpret 'finite type' in Chen's sense for the Euclidean position vector x, i.e. x = c + x_1 + ... + x_k with Delta x_i = lambda_i x_i for finitely many real eigenvalues lambda_i. Is every such finite type surface necessarily either (i) a minimal surface of S^3, or (ii) a standard 2-sphere in S^3, or (iii) a product of two plane circles S^1(r) x S^1(s) subset S^3 in orthogonal 2-planes of E^4, with r^2 + s^2 = 1?

Let M^n be a connected immersed hypersurface of a hypersphere S^{n+1}(r) ⊂ E^{n+2}, and let x:M → E^{n+2} denote its Euclidean position vector. Classify all such M for which x is of Chen 2-type, i.e. x = c + x1 + x2 with x1, x2 nonconstant and Δx_i = λ_i x_i for two distinct real eigenvalues λ1 ≠ λ2 of the Laplacian Δ of the induced metric on M. In particular, classify all 3-dimensional Chen 2-type hypersurfaces of a hypersphere S^4(r) ⊂ E^5. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1307.6582))

Let x:M^n→S^{n+1}(r)⊂E^{n+2} be a connected Dupin hypersurface of a hypersphere, regarded via its standard immersion into real Euclidean space. Determine precisely when M is of finite Chen type, i.e. when its position vector admits a finite spectral decomposition x=c+x1+⋯+xk with Δxi=λi xi for the Laplacian Δ of the induced metric on M; and determine when a finite-type Dupin hypersurface of a hypersphere must be isoparametric in S^{n+1}(r), that is, have constant principal curvatures.

Does there exist a connected 2-dimensional Riemannian manifold M and an isometric immersion x: M → S^4 ⊂ E^5 whose Euclidean position vector is of 2-type, i.e. admits a spectral decomposition x = c + x1 + x2 with x1 and x2 non-constant E^5-valued maps satisfying Δxi = λi xi for i = 1,2 and λ1 ≠ λ2, such that x is not mass-symmetric in S^4, meaning that the constant vector c is not the center of the ambient 4-sphere?

Let x:M^n→E^{n+2} be an isometric immersion of a connected n-dimensional Riemannian manifold into Euclidean (n+2)-space. Assume that x is of 2-type in the sense that its position vector admits a spectral decomposition x=c+x_1+x_2 with Δx_i=λ_i x_i for two distinct eigenvalues λ_1≠λ_2, and assume it is non-null, i.e. λ_1,λ_2≠0. If the mean curvature vector H has constant length (constant mean curvature), must M be spherical, that is, contained in some hypersphere of E^{n+2}?

Does there exist a connected surface M^2 and a full isometric immersion x: M^2 → S^{2m} ⊂ E^{2m+1} for some m ≥ 2, where "full" means x(M) is not contained in a proper subsphere of S^{2m}, such that x is of Chen 2-type with respect to the Laplacian Δ of the induced metric, i.e. x = c + x_1 + x_2 and Δx_i = λ_i x_i with λ_1 ≠ λ_2? More specifically, can such a surface be mass-symmetric, meaning that the constant vector c equals the center of S^{2m}? ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1307.6582))

Study and classify all linearly independent 2-type isometric immersions x: M -> E^m of connected Riemannian manifolds into real Euclidean m-space; equivalently, classify all immersions whose position vector admits a spectral decomposition x = c + x_1 + x_2 with respect to the Laplacian Δ of M induced by x, where Δx_i = λ_i x_i for i = 1,2 with λ_1 != λ_2, and for which the subspaces E_i := Span{x_i(p) : p in M} subset E^m are linearly independent.

Let x:M^n→E^{n+2} be a finite k-type isometric immersion of a connected Riemannian manifold into real Euclidean space, with spectral decomposition x = c + x_1 + ... + x_k, where c is a constant vector, each x_i is nonconstant, Δx_i = λ_i x_i for the Laplacian Δ of M, and the eigenvalues λ_1,...,λ_k are mutually distinct. For each i, let E_i be the real linear span of {x_i(p): p∈M} in E^{n+2}. Assuming that E_1,...,E_k are linearly independent (equivalently, E_1⊕...⊕E_k is a direct sum), study and classify all such linearly independent codimension-2 submanifolds of Euclidean space.

Let x:M^n→E^m be an isometric immersion of a connected Riemannian n-manifold into Euclidean m-space, let Δ denote the Laplace operator on M, and let H be the mean curvature vector field of x. Assume that x is biharmonic, i.e. Δ^2x=0 identically, equivalently ΔH=0 identically. Other than the minimal case H≡0, classify the biharmonic submanifolds of Euclidean spaces E^m (for arbitrary n and m).

Let x: M^n → E^m be an isometric immersion of a connected Riemannian manifold into Euclidean m-space. If x is biharmonic, meaning Δ^2x = 0 (equivalently, the mean curvature vector field H satisfies ΔH = 0), must M be minimal; that is, must H vanish identically on M?

For every n >= 1, let x:M^n -> E^{n+1} be an isometric immersion of a connected Riemannian n-manifold as a hypersurface. If x is biharmonic, meaning that its inclusion map is biharmonic (equivalently, Delta^2 x = 0, or equivalently, the mean curvature vector field H_vec satisfies Delta H_vec = 0 in the Euclidean ambient space), must x be minimal, i.e. must H_vec vanish identically?

Let x: M^n -> E^m be an isometric immersion of a complete n-dimensional Riemannian manifold M into Euclidean m-space E^m. If x is biharmonic, in the sense that Delta^2 x = 0 (equivalently, Delta H = 0, where H is the mean curvature vector field of M in E^m), must x be minimal; that is, must H vanish identically on M?

Let x:M^2→E^4 be a connected immersed null 2-type surface, meaning that x is a 2-type immersion with spectral decomposition x = c + x1 + x2, where Δx1 = 0 and Δx2 = λx2 for some nonzero constant λ, with Δ the Laplacian of the induced metric on M; consequently, its mean curvature vector H satisfies ΔH = λH. Must M have constant mean curvature, i.e. must |H| be constant on M?

Let x: M → E^m be an isometric immersion of a connected Riemannian manifold into Euclidean m-space, and call M null 2-type if its position vector field admits a spectral decomposition x = c + x1 + x2 with c constant, x1 and x2 nonconstant, Δx1 = 0, and Δx2 = λx2 for some nonzero real constant λ, where Δ is the Laplace-Beltrami operator of the induced metric. Study and classify all such null 2-type submanifolds of Euclidean spaces. In particular, determine all null 2-type surfaces in E^4 and, in the analogous pseudo-Euclidean setting, all null 2-type surfaces in 4-dimensional pseudo-Euclidean spaces.

Let N be a compact connected Riemannian homogeneous manifold with irreducible isotropy action, and let φ : N → E^m be its first standard immersion, namely the isometric 1-type immersion determined by the first positive Laplace eigenvalue of N. For a submanifold M ⊂ N, consider the restricted Euclidean immersion φ|_M : M → E^m. Under what conditions is M of finite type in E^m via φ|_M, in the sense that the position vector of φ|_M has a finite spectral decomposition into eigenmaps of the Laplacian on M? In particular, characterize when φ|_M is of 1-type and when it is of 2-type.

For every Riemannian metric on S^n with n >= 3, and in particular for every Riemannian metric on S^3, is there a higher-dimensional extension of the Lyusternik–Schnirelmann theorem for S^2—that is, of the theorem that every Riemannian metric on S^2 has at least three simple closed geodesics? ([aimath.org](https://aimath.org/pastworkshops/geodesicsproblems.pdf))

Let M be a closed connected manifold with dim M ≥ 2. Does there exist on M a Riemannian metric or a Finsler metric such that the associated geodesic flow g_t on the corresponding unit tangent bundle SM is ergodic with respect to the natural Liouville measure? ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1308.5417))

Let F be an irreversible Finsler metric on the 2-sphere S^2. Is the total number of distinct prime closed geodesics of F—where "prime" means not an iterate of a shorter closed geodesic—necessarily either exactly 2 or infinite? ([aimath.org](https://aimath.org/pastworkshops/geodesicsproblems.pdf))

Conjecture 2.2.2 (Long). Let F be a Finsler metric on S^2. If (S^2, F) admits a hyperbolic prime closed geodesic, must it admit infinitely many distinct prime closed geodesics? ([aimath.org](https://aimath.org/pastworkshops/geodesicsproblems.pdf))
Does every Finsler metric F on the 2-sphere S^2 admit a prime closed geodesic c whose linearized Poincare return map is elliptic?
Let (M,g) be a connected C^∞ Riemannian manifold with complete metric g and finite total Riemannian volume Vol_g(M) < ∞. Must (M,g) admit at least one nontrivial closed geodesic?

Does the cylinder M = R × S^1 admit an irreversible Finsler metric F (i.e. a nonreversible Finsler metric) of finite total volume such that F has no nonconstant closed geodesic? ([aimath.org](https://aimath.org/pastworkshops/geodesicsproblems.pdf))

Let M be a closed connected surface, let omega be a closed 2-form on M, let pi:T^*M->M be the canonical projection, and consider the magnetic flow on T^*M determined by the metric kinetic Hamiltonian H and the twisted symplectic form omega_can + pi^*omega. For every k>0, does the positive energy hypersurface H^{-1}(k) contain a periodic orbit, equivalently, at least one closed magnetic geodesic?

Let M be a closed connected manifold, let g be a Riemannian metric on M, and let ω be a nowhere-vanishing 1-form whose kernel distribution ker ω is nonintegrable. For the associated Kropina metric F = g/ω, defined away from ker ω and viewed there as a one-homogeneous strictly convex function, must there exist a closed geodesic on M? ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1308.5417))

Let (M,g) be a Riemannian manifold, let p,q ∈ M, let ΛM be the free loop space of piecewise smooth maps S^1 → M, and let Λ^T M ⊂ ΛM be the subspace of loops of length at most T. Likewise, let Ω(p,q) be the space of piecewise smooth paths from p to q, and let Ω^T(p,q) ⊂ Ω(p,q) be the subspace of paths of length at most T. As T → ∞, how do the total Betti numbers ∑_i b_i(Λ^T M) and ∑_i b_i(Ω^T(p,q)) grow? In particular, does this growth depend on the Riemannian metric g? ([aimath.org](https://aimath.org/pastworkshops/geodesicsproblems.pdf))

Let M be a Riemannian manifold, and let ΛM denote its free loop space of piecewise smooth loops. If the Betti numbers of ΛM have exponential growth with homological degree (for a fixed choice of coefficients), does the number of closed geodesics on M of length at most T grow exponentially as T → ∞?

Does there exist some n ≥ 2, a Riemannian or Finsler metric g on S^n, and a nonzero class X ∈ H_*(ΛS^n; Z) such that, if Λ^aS^n denotes the subspace of free loops of g-length at most a and cr_g(Y) := inf{a : Y ∈ Im(H_*(Λ^aS^n; Z) -> H_*(ΛS^n; Z))}, one has 0 < cr_g(mX) < cr_g(X) for some m ∈ N?

Klingenberg's conjecture asks: if M is a closed manifold (compact and without boundary) carrying a Riemannian metric g whose geodesic flow phi_g^t on the unit tangent bundle SM is Anosov — i.e. T(SM) admits a Dphi_g^t-invariant splitting E^s ⊕ E^0 ⊕ E^u, where E^0 is the flow direction, and there exist constants C >= 1 and lambda > 0 such that ||Dphi_g^t xi|| <= C e^{-lambda t} ||xi|| for all t >= 0 and xi in E^s, and ||Dphi_g^{-t} eta|| <= C e^{-lambda t} ||eta|| for all t >= 0 and eta in E^u — must M also admit some (possibly different) Riemannian metric h whose sectional curvature is strictly negative on every 2-plane?

Let M be a connected smooth manifold. Suppose M admits a Riemannian metric g with no conjugate points, in the sense that along every g-geodesic every nontrivial Jacobi field vanishes at most once. Must there exist a (possibly different) Riemannian metric h on the same manifold M whose sectional curvatures are everywhere nonpositive?
Let (M,g) be a closed connected C-infinity Riemannian manifold without conjugate points. Must its fundamental group pi_1(M) be semihyperbolic in the sense of Alonso-Bridson?

Let M be a compact manifold without boundary, and let g1 and g2 be Riemannian metrics on M with strictly negative sectional curvature. For each free homotopy class [gamma] of loops in M, let L_{g_i}([gamma]) be the infimum of the g_i-lengths of loops in [gamma] (equivalently, the length of the shortest closed geodesic in that class). If L_{g1}([gamma]) = L_{g2}([gamma]) for every free homotopy class [gamma], must there exist a diffeomorphism phi : M -> M such that phi^* g2 = g1?

Let X be a 2-dimensional metrical simplicial complex such that every simplex of X is hyperbolic with geodesic edges, the CAT(-1) condition holds at every vertex, and every edge is contained in at least two simplices. If the marked length spectrum of X is the function assigning to each free homotopy class of loops in X the infimum of the lengths of loops in that class, does this marked length spectrum determine the metric uniquely up to isometry, either among all locally CAT(-1) metrics on the fixed space X, or among all 2-dimensional metrical simplicial complexes with the same three properties that are homeomorphic to X? ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1308.5417))

Let M be a compact manifold with smooth boundary N = ∂M, and let g be a Riemannian metric on M. The metric g induces a boundary distance function d_g : N × N → R_{≥0}, defined by d_g(p,q) = dist_g(p,q). Under what hypotheses on M, on its boundary N, and on g is (M,g) boundary rigid; that is, whenever g' is another Riemannian metric on M with d_{g'}(p,q) = d_g(p,q) for all p,q ∈ N, must g' be isometric to g?

Let (M1,g1) and (M2,g2) be compact Riemannian manifolds of negative sectional curvature, let phi_i^t denote the geodesic flow of g_i on the unit tangent bundle SM_i, and suppose there exists a homeomorphism h: SM1 -> SM2 such that h o phi_1^t = phi_2^t o h for every t in R. Must (M1,g1) and (M2,g2) be isometric? ([users.fmi.uni-jena.de](https://users.fmi.uni-jena.de/~matveev/Datei/problem_list_submitted.pdf))

Let (M,g) be a compact Riemannian manifold with negative sectional curvature, and let g^t: SM -> SM be its geodesic flow on the unit tangent bundle. Denote by h_top(g) the topological entropy of g^t and by h_Liou(g) the metric entropy of g^t with respect to the Liouville measure on SM. Is it true that h_top(g) = h_Liou(g) if and only if (M,g) is locally symmetric?

Let (M,g) be a closed Riemannian manifold with negative sectional curvature, and let φ_t: SM -> SM be its geodesic flow on the unit tangent bundle. Since φ_t is Anosov, it has a Dφ_t-invariant splitting T(SM) = E^s ⊕ E^0 ⊕ E^u, where E^0 is tangent to the flow. Does there exist such an (M,g) with dim M > 2 for which the stable and unstable bundles E^s and E^u are C^1, but the metric g is not 1/4-pinched?

Does there exist a closed Riemannian manifold (M,g) with strictly negative sectional curvature such that, for the geodesic flow φ_t on the unit tangent bundle SM, a typical unit-speed geodesic has positive Lyapunov exponents whose largest-to-smallest ratio is greater than 2; equivalently, for typical v in SM, if 0 < λ_min^+(v) <= λ_max^+(v) are the smallest and largest positive Lyapunov exponents of Dφ_t along the orbit of v, does one have λ_max^+(v)/λ_min^+(v) > 2, rather than this happening only for exceptional closed geodesics?
Does every finite-volume hyperbolic 3-manifold contain infinitely many simple closed geodesics, i.e. infinitely many embedded closed geodesics?

Let (M,g) be a closed C∞ Riemannian surface of genus at least 2 whose Gaussian curvature satisfies K_g ≤ 0 everywhere. Is the geodesic flow φ^t on the unit tangent bundle SM ergodic with respect to the Liouville measure induced by g? ([users.fmi.uni-jena.de](https://users.fmi.uni-jena.de/~matveev/Datei/problem_list_submitted.pdf))

Let M be a closed surface of genus at least 2. Does there exist a C^∞ Riemannian metric g on M (or at least a C^k metric with k >= 3) for which there is a non-closed geodesic gamma: R -> M such that the Gaussian curvature K_g(gamma(t)) = 0 for every t in R?

Let (M,g) be a closed Riemannian surface of genus at least 2 with Gaussian curvature K_g \le 0 everywhere. For T > 0, let N(T) be the number of free homotopy classes of loops in M that contain a closed g-geodesic of length at most T along which K_g vanishes identically. Must there exist a constant C > 0 such that N(T) \le C T^2 for all T > 0?

Let F be a reversible, quadratically convex Finsler metric on the two-torus T^2, and assume that F has no conjugate points. Must there exist a flat Finsler metric F⋄ on T^2 and a smooth diffeomorphism h: U(T^2,F⋄) -> U(T^2,F) such that h ◦ φ_t^{F⋄} = φ_t^F ◦ h for every t in R, where φ_t^F and φ_t^{F⋄} denote the geodesic flows on the corresponding unit tangent bundles?

Let \(z=(z_1,\dots,z_n)\) be commuting complex variables, let \(\Delta=\sum_{i=1}^n \partial^2/\partial z_i^2\), and let \(P(z)\in \mathbb{C}[z_1,\dots,z_n]\) be a homogeneous polynomial of degree \(4\) whose Hessian matrix \(\operatorname{Hes}P(z)=(\partial^2P/\partial z_i\partial z_j)\) is nilpotent. Must it follow that \(\Delta^m P(z)^{m+1}=0\) for all sufficiently large integers \(m\); equivalently, does there exist \(N\) such that \(\Delta^m P(z)^{m+1}=0\) for every \(m\ge N\)?

Let M be a complete simply connected Riemannian manifold without conjugate points, and let α, β: ℝ → M be arclength-parametrized geodesics. If dist(α(t), β(t)) → 0 as t → −∞, must dist(α(t), β(t)) → ∞ as t → ∞?

Let (M,g) be a connected Riemannian manifold of dimension at least 3 with no conjugate points. If γ0 and γ1 are closed g-geodesics that are freely homotopic as closed curves in M, must there exist a continuous map H:S^1×[0,1]→M such that H(·,0)=γ0, H(·,1)=γ1, and for every s∈[0,1] the loop H(·,s) is a closed g-geodesic?

Let g be a complete Riemannian metric on R^2. Assume that for every geodesic γ in (R^2,g) and every point p in R^2 that does not lie on the image of γ, there exists exactly one nonconstant geodesic through p whose image does not intersect the image of γ. Must g be flat?

Let (M, g0) be a closed symmetric space of noncompact type and of higher rank. If h is a Riemannian metric on M with no conjugate points, must there exist a diffeomorphism phi: M -> M and a constant c > 0 such that h = c phi^* g0?

Let M^2 be a closed surface of genus at least 2, let g be a Riemannian metric on M^2 × S^1 with no conjugate points, and let g̃ be the lift of g to the infinite cyclic cover M^2 × R corresponding to the S^1-factor. Must the Riemannian manifold (M^2 × R, g̃) split isometrically as a direct product (M^2, g1) × (R, dt^2) for some Riemannian metric g1 on M^2?

Let M be a closed connected smooth surface of genus >= 2, endowed with a Riemannian metric g and a magnetic form omega (a closed 2-form), and consider the associated magnetic flow on T^*M defined by the kinetic Hamiltonian with twisted symplectic form dp∧dx + pi^*omega. Fix an energy level of this flow such that the topological entropy of the flow restricted to that level is zero. If the magnetic geodesics on that energy level have no conjugate points (in the magnetic sense), must the system be locally symmetric, i.e. must g have constant curvature and omega be a constant multiple of the g-volume form?

Does there exist a closed smooth manifold M of dimension at least 2 and a Riemannian metric g on M such that K_g(\sigma) > 0 for every 2-plane \sigma \subset T_xM at every x \in M, and such that the geodesic flow on the unit tangent bundle SM is ergodic (with respect to the Liouville measure)?

Fix a connected smooth closed manifold M and a regularity k (with k a nonnegative integer or k = infinity). Let G be the space of all smooth Riemannian metrics on M, equipped with the C^k-topology. Do the metrics g in G whose geodesic flow on the unit tangent bundle S_gM has positive topological entropy form a dense subset of G?

Let M be a closed smooth manifold, fix k in {0,1,2,...,∞}, and let R^k(M) denote the space of all smooth Riemannian metrics on M endowed with the weak C^k-topology (equivalently, in local coordinates, convergence of the metric coefficients and all partial derivatives up to order k). Is the subset of R^k(M) consisting of metrics whose geodesic flow has positive topological entropy dense in R^k(M) with respect to this C^k-topology?

Let M be a smooth connected closed manifold, fix a regularity level k, and let G be the space of all smooth Riemannian metrics on M endowed with the weak C^k topology (equivalently, local C^k convergence of the metric coefficients in a finite atlas). Do the metrics g in G whose geodesic flow on the unit tangent bundle SM has positive topological entropy form a dense subset of G?

Given a smooth closed manifold M with a smooth Riemannian metric g, is the subset of M consisting of all points that lie on at least one closed g-geodesic dense in M? ([aimath.org](https://aimath.org/pastworkshops/geodesicsproblems.pdf))

For every compact connected smooth surface S with genus(S) >= 1 and every smooth Riemannian metric g on S, must there exist a geodesic gamma: R -> S whose image is dense in S, i.e. such that the closure of gamma(R) is all of S?

Give a complete global description of all Finsler metrics F on the 2-sphere S^2, without assuming reversibility, whose flag curvature is constant and identically equal to 1. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1308.5417))

Can one construct explicit Finsler metrics F on S^2 of constant positive flag curvature (equivalently, after normalization, flag curvature 1) that are not Zoll—in the sense that not all geodesics are closed with the same common length—and that admit no nontrivial Killing vector field?
Let (M, F) be a closed Finsler manifold of positive flag curvature. If N1, N2 ⊂ M are closed totally geodesic submanifolds with dim(N1) + dim(N2) >= dim(M), must N1 and N2 intersect?

Let (M,F) be a closed 3-dimensional reversible Finsler manifold, meaning F(x,v)=F(x,-v) for all (x,v) in TM, and assume that M has positive flag curvature everywhere. Let N be a closed totally geodesic 2-dimensional submanifold of M. Is it true that every closed geodesic in M either intersects N or has image entirely contained in N?

Let (M,g) be an oriented closed Riemannian surface of genus >= 1, let Γ be a nontrivial free homotopy class of loops in M, and let p∈M. Gaidukov's theorem asserts that there exist a closed geodesic γ:R->M in the class Γ and a geodesic ray β:[0,∞)->M with β(0)=p such that dist_g(β(t),γ(t)) -> 0 as t -> ∞. Formulate and prove a higher-dimensional analogue of this statement for closed Riemannian manifolds of dimension n >= 3; in particular, determine whether the correct replacement for the single closed geodesic should be a minimizing invariant set for the geodesic flow, such as the support of a Mather minimal measure, and whether every point p lies on a geodesic ray asymptotic to that minimizing set.

Let σ(g)=area(S^2,g)/sys(S^2,g)^2, where sys(S^2,g) denotes the least length of a nontrivial closed geodesic of the metric g on S^2. Let g0 be the standard round metric on S^2, and let g1 be the singular metric on S^2 obtained by gluing two congruent equilateral triangles along their boundaries. Does there exist, in the space of metrics on S^2 with conical singularities, a continuous or smooth one-parameter family {gt}t∈[0,1] with g0=g0 and g1=g1 such that t↦σ(gt) is decreasing?

Let g_round be the standard round metric on S^2, normalized so that Area(S^2,g_round)=4π. Does every smooth Riemannian metric g on S^2 with Area(S^2,g)=4π that is sufficiently close to g_round (in the chosen topology on the space of metrics) admit a nontrivial closed geodesic of length at most 2π?

Is it true that for every integer n >= 2, if g is a Riemannian metric on RP^n whose total Riemannian volume equals that of the canonical metric g_can on RP^n (the standard metric induced from the round unit sphere), then (RP^n, g) admits a closed geodesic of g-length at most π?
If M is either S^3 or S^2 × S^1, and g is a Riemannian metric on M with Vol(M,g) = 1, must (M,g) admit a closed geodesic of length at most 1024?

Let M be a connected closed (compact without boundary) C^∞ manifold that is not covered by a sphere, and let g be a Riemannian metric on M such that every arclength-parametrized g-geodesic is closed. Must (M, g) be a compact rank one symmetric manifold equipped with its standard metric?

Let (M, g) be a closed Riemannian manifold not covered by a sphere, and assume that every geodesic of g is closed. Must (M, g) be a compact rank one symmetric manifold (CROSS) with the standard metric?

Let (M,g) be a smooth connected compact manifold without boundary endowed with a Lorentzian metric. Using the convention of Section 9.1 that a closed geodesic means a smooth embedding γ:S^1→M satisfying the geodesic equation ∇_{γ̇}γ̇ = 0, must every such Lorentzian manifold admit at least one closed geodesic?

Let M be a connected closed smooth manifold, and let g be a geodesically complete semi-Riemannian metric of indefinite signature on M. Does there exist a nonzero smooth real 1-form η on M such that for every affinely parameterized light-like geodesic γ: ℝ → M, there are constants C1(γ) ∈ ℝ \ {0} and C2(γ) ∈ ℝ with η(γ̇(t)) = C1(γ) t + C2(γ) for all t ∈ ℝ?

Let M be a closed smooth manifold (compact without boundary), and let g be a smooth semi-Riemannian metric on M, possibly restricted to a prescribed signature. Which geometric hypotheses on g, ideally easy to verify or satisfied by broad natural classes of examples, guarantee geodesic completeness in the sense that every geodesic gamma:(a,b)->M extends to a geodesic defined on all of R?

Let (M,g) be a compact Lorentzian manifold. Assume that there exist a smooth function u:M->R and a Lorentzian metric g0 on M of constant sectional curvature such that g = e^{2u}g0 on all of M. Must (M,g) be geodesically complete; equivalently, does every g-geodesic gamma:(a,b)->M extend to a geodesic defined on all of R?

Does there exist a connected closed surface M of genus g(M) ≥ 2 and a Riemannian metric g on M such that the geodesic flow of g is completely integrable, in the sense that the kinetic-energy Hamiltonian admits an additional first integral functionally independent of it on an open everywhere dense subset of phase space (or, in the stronger interpretation explicitly noted in the paper, on a full-measure subset)? ([aimath.org](https://aimath.org/pastworkshops/geodesicsproblems.pdf))

Does there exist a smooth Riemannian metric g on a closed connected surface M of genus at least 2 such that the geodesic flow φ_t on the unit tangent bundle SM has zero metric entropy with respect to the Liouville measure?

Let M be a closed surface of genus at least 2, and let F1,F2: TM -> [0,∞) be Finsler metrics on M. Suppose that every F1-geodesic, considered as an unparameterized curve in M, is also an F2-geodesic. Must there exist a constant c > 0 and a closed 1-form beta on M such that F1(x,v) = c F2(x,v) + beta_x(v) for every (x,v) in TM?
Does there exist a connected closed C∞ surface M of genus g ≥ 2 carrying a non-Riemannian C∞ Finsler metric F that satisfies the Landsberg condition?

Let g be a smooth Riemannian metric on the 2-torus T^2. Suppose the geodesic flow of g on the tangent bundle T(T^2) admits a nonconstant first integral F:T(T^2)→R such that, in local coordinates (x^1,x^2;v^1,v^2), F is a polynomial of total degree 3 in the velocity variables v^1,v^2 (so some cubic term is not identically zero). Must g admit a nonzero Killing vector field?

Let Ω ⊂ ℝ² be a strictly convex domain bounded by a smooth curve, and consider the internal billiard in Ω, where a point moves with unit speed along straight-line segments and reflects elastically at ∂Ω according to the law that the angle of reflection equals the angle of incidence. If there exists a non-constant smooth function on the tangent bundle that is constant along every billiard trajectory, must the boundary ∂Ω be an ellipse?

For every Riemannian metric g on S^2, does there exist a graph G in the Riemannian surface (S^2,g) whose underlying topological graph is the Θ-graph (two vertices joined by three edges), such that each edge of G is a geodesic and, at each vertex, the sum of the outgoing unit tangent vectors along the incident edges is zero?

Let (S,g) be a closed Riemannian surface. A stationary net is a graph G⊂S such that every edge of G is a geodesic and, at each vertex, the sum of the outgoing unit tangent vectors along the incident edges is zero; all vertices have valence at least 3. Call G non-trivial if it has at least one vertex of valence at least 3, equivalently if it is not a disjoint union of simple closed geodesics. Must non-trivial stationary nets be dense on S, in the sense that for every non-empty open set U⊂S there exists a non-trivial stationary net G with G∩U≠∅?

Let (M,g) be a closed pseudo-Riemannian manifold with Levi-Civita connection nabla. Assume there exists a nonzero endomorphism field A in Gamma(End(TM)) such that g(A X, Y) = g(X, A Y) for all vector fields X,Y, nabla A = 0, and A is nilpotent (equivalently, A^N = 0 for some integer N >= 2). Must M, or at least a double cover of M, admit a nonzero light-like parallel vector field V (that is, nabla V = 0 and g(V,V) = 0)? ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1308.5417))

Let M be a smooth manifold. Describe all pairs of Finsler metrics F and G on M that are affinely equivalent in the sense of Section 12, namely: every geodesic of F, when parameterized so that F(gamma dot) is constant, is also a geodesic of G as a parameterized curve.

Let M be a smooth manifold and [∇] a smooth projective structure on M, meaning an equivalence class of torsion-free affine connections with the same unparameterized geodesics (equivalently, Γ̄^i_{jk}=Γ^i_{jk}+δ^i_k φ_j+δ^i_j φ_k). Construct scalar projective differential invariants of [∇] whose simultaneous vanishing is equivalent to local metrizability in the following sense: for almost every point p∈M, there exists a neighborhood U of p and a nondegenerate Riemannian or semi-Riemannian metric g on U whose Levi-Civita connection belongs to [∇]|_U. The two-dimensional case is already known, so the unresolved content is in higher dimensions. ([users.fmi.uni-jena.de](https://users.fmi.uni-jena.de/~matveev/Datei/problem_list_submitted.pdf))

Locally on a smooth 2-manifold, does every smooth irreversible path structure—meaning a smooth family of oriented curves such that through each point x and each nonzero tangent vector v in T_xM there passes a unique curve tangent at x to a positive multiple of v—arise as the family of oriented unparameterized geodesics of some (possibly irreversible) Finsler metric?

Does the smooth manifold S^3 admit two Lorentzian metrics g and h, of signature (2,1), that are projectively equivalent in the sense that they have the same geodesics as unparameterized curves, but are not proportional by any nonzero constant factor?

Let E_n={x_k=1, x_i+x_j=x_k, x_i·x_j=x_k : i,j,k∈{1,...,n}}. For each positive integer n, let f(n) be the least non-negative integer b such that every subsystem S⊆E_n having a unique solution in non-negative integers x_1,...,x_n has that solution in [0,b]^n. Is the function f computable? Equivalently, is there an algorithm which, given n, outputs this least universal bound f(n) for unique non-negative solutions of subsystems of E_n?

Given that Fermi-LAT has detected γ-ray emission from five radio-loud narrow-line Seyfert 1 galaxies (where only 1H 0323+342 has published host-galaxy imaging, with ambiguous spiral/merger‐remnant morphology) and the host morphologies of the other four remain unclassified, does high-resolution optical or near-infrared imaging provide evidence that one or more of these γ-ray–emitting radio-loud NLSy1s are actually hosted by early-type (elliptical or S0) galaxies rather than by spiral galaxies?

Let n be a positive integer. For a group K and an automorphism phi in Aut(K) with phi^n = id, define X_{n,phi}(K) = { x in K | x x^phi x^{phi^2} ... x^{phi^{n-1}} = 1 }. Define
c_n = sup { |X_{n,phi}(H)| / |H| : H is a finite group, phi in Aut(H), phi^n = id, and X_{n,phi}(H) != H }.
For a finite group G, let H_n(G) = < x in G | x^n != 1 >.
Question: (a) If n > 1 and c_d < 1 for every prime-power divisor d of n, must c_n < 1? (b) If there exists an integer k_n depending only on n such that |G : H_n(G)| <= k_n for every finite group G with H_n(G) != 1, must c_n < 1? (For part (b), this is open even when n > 5 is prime.)
Let S be a finite simple group, and let G be a finite group. Suppose there exists a set-theoretic bijection f:G→S such that, for every x∈G, the order of x divides the order of f(x). Must G be simple?

Let G be either the symmetric group S_n or the alternating group A_n on n letters, and let H, K <= G be solvable subgroups. Does there exist an absolute integer N such that for every n >= N and every such pair H, K, one can find an element x in G with H ∩ K^x = 1, where K^x = x^{-1}Kx? More specifically, is this true for every n >= 21? (The paper notes that the statement fails at n = 20: if G = S_20 and H = K = (S4 ≀ S4) × S4, then no such x exists.)

Let S be a solvable subgroup of a finite group G such that G has no nontrivial solvable normal subgroups. Must there exist elements g1,g2,g3,g4,g5 in G such that S^{g1} \cap S^{g2} \cap S^{g3} \cap S^{g4} \cap S^{g5} = 1, where S^g = g^{-1}Sg?

Let p be a prime, let Ω be a set, and let G be a transitive subgroup of the finitary symmetric group FSym(Ω). Let N be a normal subgroup of G, and let S be a transitive Sylow p-subgroup of G (with 'Sylow p-subgroup' understood in the locally finite sense). Must the following hold: (i) S ∩ N is a Sylow p-subgroup of N; (ii) SN/N is a Sylow p-subgroup of G/N; and (iii) any two transitive Sylow p-subgroups of G are locally conjugate in G, meaning that for any such subgroups X and Y there exists a locally inner automorphism φ of G carrying X to Y, where φ is locally inner if for every finite subset A of G there exists g(A) in G such that φ(a) = g(A)^(-1) a g(A) for all a in A?

Fix a prime p. Let Ω be a set, let G ≤ FSym(Ω) be a transitive subgroup, and let S be a transitive Sylow p-subgroup of G. Must S contain a transitive subgroup H such that H is a totally imprimitive p-group and, for every h ∈ H, every cycle in the cycle decomposition of h has support a block for H?

Let G be a finite soluble group. Suppose that for every prime p dividing |G|, a Sylow p-subgroup of G is an involutive Yang-Baxter group; that is, each such Sylow subgroup is isomorphic to the permutation group of a finite involutive non-degenerate set-theoretic solution of the Yang-Baxter equation, equivalently, to the multiplicative group of a finite left brace. Must G itself be an involutive Yang-Baxter group?

Let r(m) := {r + tm : t in Z} for integers m >= 1 and 0 <= r < m. If r1(m1) and r2(m2) are disjoint residue classes, let tau_{r1(m1),r2(m2)} be the involution of Z that swaps r1 + tm1 with r2 + tm2 for every t in Z and fixes all other integers, and let CT(Z) be the subgroup of Sym(Z) generated by all such class transpositions. For each integer k >= 2, let CT_k := <tau_{r1(k),r2(k)} : 0 <= r1 != r2 < k>; then CT_k is isomorphic to S_k because these generators permute the k residue classes modulo k. Define CT(k) := <CT_2, CT_3, ..., CT_k>. Is it true that for every integer k > 3, the group CT(k) is abstractly isomorphic to the symmetric group S_N, where N = lcm(2,3,...,k)?

Fix a prime p, and let F be a free pro-p group of finite rank d>=2. Does there exist a finite family of open subgroups U1,...,Un of F, with F among them, such that the only closed subgroup H<=F satisfying H<=Ui and H characteristic in Ui (with respect to continuous automorphisms) for every i=1,...,n is the trivial subgroup H=1?

Does every finite group G admit a just finite presentation; that is, does there exist a presentation G ≅ ⟨X | R⟩ such that G is finite and, for every relator r ∈ R, the group presented by ⟨X | R∖{r}⟩ is infinite?

For each of the following two types of groups, determine whether some, all, or no members of that type can occur as homomorphic images of a nonprincipal countable ultraproduct of groups, that is, of an ultraproduct (prod_{n∈ω} G_n)/U with U a nonprincipal ultrafilter on ω: (i) infinite finitely generated Burnside groups (the original wording of Bergman's Question 18; in Kourovka 21.11 this appears as infinite finitely generated groups of finite exponent); and (ii) the finitary symmetric group FSym(X) on an infinite set X, consisting of the permutations of X with finite support. In the second case, the question is to be read in light of Corollary 14, which already excludes permutation groups containing an element with exactly one infinite orbit. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1401.0300.pdf))

Let U be a fixed nonprincipal ultrafilter on ω, and write ℤ^ω/U for the corresponding ultrapower of the additive group ℤ. Suppose B is a group such that for every b∈B there exists a homomorphism φ_b: ℤ^ω/U → B whose image contains b (equivalently, b lies in a subgroup H_b≤B that is a homomorphic image of ℤ^ω/U). Must there exist groups G_i, indexed by i∈ω, such that B is a homomorphic image of the U-ultraproduct (∏_{i∈ω} G_i)/U?
