Since a subgroup of Z^ω is known to have algebraic dual of free abelian rank 2^{aleph_0}, does there exist a subgroup G <= Z^ω, where Z^ω is the countable direct product of copies of Z, such that Hom(G, Z) is a free abelian group of rank strictly larger than 2^{aleph_0}; more specifically, can one achieve rank 2^{2^{aleph_0}}?

Let G be an arbitrary group and let α ∈ End(G). Assume that for every group H and every homomorphism f: G → H, there exists an endomorphism βf ∈ End(H) such that βf ∘ f = f ∘ α. Must it follow that either α is conjugation by some element s ∈ G (equivalently, α(g) = sgs^{-1} for all g ∈ G), or α is the trivial endomorphism g ↦ 1_G of G?

For every infinite set Ω, let S_Ω = Sym(Ω) be the full symmetric group on Ω, and let B be an arbitrary subgroup of S_Ω. Form the amalgamated free product S_Ω *_B S_Ω in the category of groups, where the two factors are amalgamated along the common subgroup B via the given inclusions B ↪ S_Ω. Must there exist an injective group homomorphism S_Ω *_B S_Ω → S_Ω? Here the embedding is asked for only as an abstract group embedding into S_Ω, not necessarily one that is over B.

Does there exist a group G such that, for every subset X ⊆ G that generates G as a group, there is a finite integer n_X with the property that every g ∈ G can be expressed as a word of length at most n_X in the alphabet X ∪ X^{-1}, but for some subset Y ⊆ G that generates G as a monoid, the positive-word lengths with respect to Y are unbounded; equivalently, for every m ∈ N there exists g ∈ G that cannot be written as a product of at most m elements of Y?

Let M be a class of metabelian groups. For any class X of groups, write H(X) for the class of homomorphic images of groups in X, S(X) for the class of groups isomorphic to subgroups of groups in X, P(X) for the class of groups isomorphic to unrestricted direct products of families of groups in X, and Pf(X) for the class of groups isomorphic to direct products of finite families of groups in X. Since, by Birkhoff’s theorem, H(S(P(X))) is the variety of groups generated by X, must one always have H(S(Pf(M))) ⊆ S(H(P(S(M))))? ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1401.0300.pdf))

Let G be a finite group, and let A1, A2, A3 be subsets of G such that the map A1 × A2 × A3 → G given by (a1,a2,a3) ↦ a1a2a3 is bijective. Must the subgroup ⟨A2⟩ generated by A2 have order divisible by |A2|?

Let S and M be groups of finite Morley rank. Assume that S is infinite, that M is non-trivial and connected, and that M acts definably and faithfully on S by automorphisms. Call the action irreducible if S has no definable, non-trivial, proper M-invariant subgroup. Suppose moreover that S is a simple group and that every proper definable subgroup of S is nilpotent. Must the given action be equivalent to the conjugation action of S on itself; that is, do there exist definable group isomorphisms alpha: M -> S and beta: S -> S such that beta(m·s) = alpha(m) beta(s) alpha(m)^(-1) for all m in M and s in S?

Let G and V be groups of finite Morley rank. Assume that G is a simple group with no involutions, that V is connected, and that G acts definably and faithfully on V by automorphisms. Assume further that the action is irreducible, in the sense that V has no definable non-trivial proper G-invariant subgroup. Prove that the only possible such action is the standard conjugation action of G on itself: namely, V is definably isomorphic to G, and under some definable isomorphism V ≅ G the given action of G on V corresponds to the action of G on itself by conjugation.

Let M be a simple algebraic group over an algebraically closed field, where "simple" means that M has no proper non-trivial connected normal subgroups, and let Z(M) denote the center of M. Suppose that M acts on a simple group S of finite Morley rank by a definable action M x S -> S with trivial kernel, and assume that the action is irreducible in the sense that M preserves no definable non-trivial proper subgroup of S. Must it follow that S is isomorphic to M/Z(M)?

For finitely generated Hopfian groups G and H, does the standard restricted wreath product G ≀ H := (⊕_{h∈H} G) ⋊ H, where H acts on the index set H by left translation, necessarily have the Hopf property; equivalently, is every surjective endomorphism of G ≀ H an automorphism?

For each fixed integer n >= 4, classify up to isomorphism the finite nonabelian simple groups G whose enhanced power graph E(G) — the graph with vertex set G in which distinct elements x and y are adjacent exactly when the subgroup <x,y> is cyclic — contains no induced cycle C_n; and, in particular, classify up to isomorphism the finite nonabelian simple groups G for which E(G) is chordal, equivalently, contains no induced cycle C_m for any m >= 4.

Let G be a finite group, and let P(G) be the power graph with vertex set G, where distinct vertices x,y in G are adjacent if and only if x belongs to <y> or y belongs to <x>. A cograph is a graph with no induced subgraph isomorphic to a path on 4 vertices, and a chordal graph is a graph with no induced cycle C_n for any n >= 4. Must it be true that, for every finite group G, if P(G) is a cograph, then P(G) is chordal? ([alglog.org](https://alglog.org/21tkt.pdf?utm_source=openai))
For every finite simple group G and every pair of prime divisors p_1, p_2 of |G|, allowing p_1 = p_2, do there exist Sylow p_i-subgroups H_i ≤ G for i = 1, 2 such that G = ⟨H_1, H_2⟩?

Let G be a non-trivial finite group, let p_1,\dots,p_k be the distinct prime divisors of |G|, and for each i fix a Sylow p_i-subgroup H_i of G. Is it true that there exists a single element x \in G such that, for every i=1,\dots,k, the subgroup H_i \cap x^{-1}H_i x is minimal with respect to inclusion among the family {H_i \cap g^{-1}H_i g : g \in G}?

Let G ≤ Sym(Ω) be a finite nonabelian simple group acting transitively on a finite set Ω, and let Δ(G) = {g ∈ G : g has no fixed point on Ω} be the set of derangements for this action. Must every element g ∈ G be expressible as g = xy with x, y ∈ Δ(G)?

Let G ≤ Sym(Ω) be a finite simple group acting transitively on a finite set Ω, and let δ(G) denote the proportion of derangements in this action, that is, δ(G) = |{g ∈ G : g fixes no point of Ω}| / |G|. Must one always have δ(G) ≥ 89/325? This bound would be best possible, since δ(G) = 89/325 when G = ^2F_4(2)' acts on the cosets of a maximal parabolic subgroup of shape 2^2.[2^8].S_3.
Let G ≤ Sym(Ω) be a finite primitive permutation group with base size b(G)=2. Is it true that for every α, β ∈ Ω there exists γ ∈ Ω such that G_{α,γ}=1 and G_{β,γ}=1?

Does every discrete group admitting a one-relator presentation have the Haagerup property, meaning that it admits a metrically proper isometric action on some possibly infinite-dimensional Hilbert space?

Let N be a finite soluble group. Viewing N as a set, let Hol(N) denote the normalizer in Sym(N) of the subgroup of left translations of N. Must every subgroup R <= Hol(N) that acts regularly on N be a soluble group?

After fixing a standard encoding of finite groups as input, determine whether the following decision problem is decidable and, if it is, determine its computational complexity: given a finite group G, does there exist a finite group H whose derived (commutator) subgroup H' = [H,H] is abstractly isomorphic to G?

Let G be a totally disconnected locally compact group with rational discrete cohomological dimension cd_Q(G) <= 1, where cd_Q is computed in the category of discrete Q[G]-modules. Does there exist a connected graph Λ and a graph of profinite groups (𝒢,Λ)—that is, profinite vertex-groups and edge-groups together with injective open continuous edge maps—such that G is topologically isomorphic to the Bass-Serre fundamental group π_1(𝒢,Λ) equipped with its canonical t.d.l.c. topology?

Does there exist a group G such that, for every pair of nonempty finite subsets A and B of G, there is an element x in G with a unique factorization x = ab where a is in A and b is in B, but G admits no partial order < satisfying the condition that for every g in G and every nonidentity h in G, at least one of gh > g or gh^{-1} > g holds? ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1401.0300.pdf))

Let G be a finite group, let p be a prime, and let w be a multilinear commutator word, i.e. a commutator of weight n in n distinct variables. Denote by G_w = {w(g1, ..., gn) : g1, ..., gn in G} the set of w-values, and by w(G) = <G_w> the corresponding verbal subgroup. Assume that for every x, y in G_w such that x has p'-order and y has order divisible by p, the product xy has order divisible by p. Must the verbal subgroup w(G) be p-nilpotent?

Let K be the class of profinite groups, and define a transfinite hierarchy {H_αK} of totally disconnected, locally compact groups analogously to Kropholler's hierarchy from Problem 15.45: H_1K consists of those tdlc groups that admit an admissible action on a finite-dimensional contractible complex whose cell stabilisers are open and belong to K; for successor ordinals, H_{α+1}K := H_1(H_αK); and for limit ordinals λ, H_λK := ⋃_{β<λ} H_βK. Is it true that every stage H_αK is closed under profinite extensions, i.e. for every ordinal α does (H_αK)K ⊆ H_αK hold, where (H_αK)K denotes the class of tdlc groups G with a closed normal subgroup N ∈ H_αK such that G/N is profinite?

Is every soluble totally disconnected, locally compact group G of type FP∞ constructible, in the sense that G can be obtained from the trivial group by a sequence of profinite extensions and ascending HNN-extensions? ([alglog.org](https://alglog.org/21tkt.pdf?utm_source=openai))

Does there exist an infinite group G with spread s(G)=1, where s(G) is the greatest nonnegative integer k such that for every choice of nontrivial elements x_1, ..., x_k in G there exists an element y in G with the subgroup generated by x_i and y equal to G for every i=1, ..., k, and s(G)=∞ if no such maximum exists?

Does there exist a group G such that every finitely generated subgroup of G is finite, G has no nontrivial proper characteristic subgroups, the natural action of Aut(G) on G has only finitely many orbits, and G is not residually finite (equivalently, some nontrivial element of G maps to the identity in every homomorphism from G to a finite group)?

Let n >= 1 and let G be a subgroup of GL_n(Q). Suppose that the natural action of Aut(G) on G has only finitely many orbits. Must G be virtually soluble; that is, must G contain a soluble subgroup of finite index?

Can a torsion-free, finitely presented, metabelian group that is self-similar—in the sense that it admits a faithful state-closed representation by automorphisms of a regular one-rooted m-tree for some positive integer m—contain a subgroup isomorphic to the restricted wreath product H = ℤ ≀ ℤ?

Let T_{d,c} denote the class of d-generated torsion-free nilpotent groups of nilpotency class c. A group is called self-similar if it admits a faithful state-closed representation by automorphisms of a regular one-rooted m-tree for some positive integer m. It is known that every group in T_{d,2} is self-similar, every group in T_{2,3} is self-similar, and that T_{4,3} contains groups that are not self-similar. Does T_{3,3} contain a group that is not self-similar?
Let G be a finite group. Suppose there exists a positive integer k such that |{g in G : ord(g) = k}| >= |G|/2. Must G be solvable?

Let A_5 act naturally on a 5-element set, and for each n >= 1 let W_n be the n-fold iterated permutational wreath product A_5 ≀ A_5 ≀ ··· ≀ A_5 (with n factors), so that W_n acts on 5^n points. Let W = varprojlim_n W_n with respect to the natural projection maps W_{n+1} -> W_n, viewed as a profinite group. Does W contain an abstract subgroup Gamma <= W that is finitely generated, dense in W for the profinite topology, and of subexponential word growth?
Does there exist an infinite simple group G such that G admits a finite presentation and d(G) > 2, where d(G) denotes the minimal number of generators of G?
Does there exist an infinite simple group G that is finitely presented and has finite cohomological dimension greater than 2?
Does there exist a finitely presented group G such that, for some non-trivial group H (with no further assumptions on H), the group G is isomorphic to the direct product G × H?

Let G be a group. A function f: G -> R is called a quasimorphism if sup_{g,h in G} |f(g)+f(h)-f(gh)| < infinity. It is called homogeneous if its restriction to every cyclic subgroup of G is a homomorphism. Suppose that G admits an unbounded homogeneous quasimorphism f: G -> R that is not a group homomorphism. Must G contain a non-abelian free subgroup?

Let G be a finitely generated group. An isometric action of G on a metric space S is called acylindrical if for every ε > 0 there exist R, N > 0 such that for every x, y ∈ S with d(x, y) ≥ R, there are at most N elements g ∈ G satisfying d(x, gx) ≤ ε and d(y, gy) ≤ ε. A group is called acylindrically hyperbolic if it is not virtually cyclic and admits an acylindrical action on a Gromov-hyperbolic metric space with unbounded orbits. If G is acylindrically hyperbolic, must its full automorphism group Aut(G) also be acylindrically hyperbolic? ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1401.0300.pdf))
For every finite 3-group T, does there exist a nontrivial characteristic subgroup C <= T such that, for every finite group G having T as a Sylow 3-subgroup, if H = N_G(C), then T ∩ [G,G] = T ∩ [H,H]?

Fix a prime p. Determine all integers n >= 1 such that, for every finite p-group P, the following implication holds: if P contains an abelian subgroup of order p^n, then P contains a normal abelian subgroup of order p^n; and if P contains an elementary abelian subgroup of order p^n (that is, a subgroup isomorphic to (C_p)^n), then P contains a normal elementary abelian subgroup of order p^n. In the status recorded in Problem 21.51, this amounts to settling the remaining unresolved cases: p = 5 with n = 6, and p > 5 with n = (p+3)/2, (p+5)/2, or (p+7)/2; moreover, for p = 2 in the elementary-abelian case, the implication holds only for n = 1.

For every finite non-abelian simple group L and every conjugacy class D of involutions of L, let Gamma be the complete graph whose vertex set is D, and color each edge {a,b} (with a,b in D and a != b) by the group-theoretic order ord(ab) of the product ab in L. Equivalently, two edges {a,b} and {c,d} have the same color exactly when ord(ab) = ord(cd). Let Aut(Gamma) be the group of all permutations tau in Sym(D) such that ord(ab) = ord(a^tau b^tau) for all distinct a,b in D. Must every element of Aut(Gamma) be induced by an automorphism of L; equivalently, is Aut(Gamma) contained in the permutation group on D induced by the setwise stabilizer of D in Aut(L)?

Let L be a finite non-abelian simple group, let D be a conjugacy class of involutions in L, and let Γ be the complete graph with vertex set D. Define an equivalence relation on the edge set of Γ by declaring (a, b) ~ (c, d) if and only if |ab| = |cd|. Let Aut(Γ) be the group of all permutations τ in Sym(D) such that (a, b) ~ (aτ, bτ) for every edge (a, b). For each integer t that occurs as |ab| for some a, b in D, define Aut_t(Γ) to be the set of all permutations τ in Sym(D) such that (a, b) ~ (aτ, bτ) whenever |ab| = t. Then Aut(Γ) is the intersection over all such t of Aut_t(Γ). If p is the second-smallest prime divisor of |L|, is it always true that Aut(Γ) = Aut_2(Γ) ∩ Aut_p(Γ)?

Let G be a finite soluble group, and let S = <sigma, rho | sigma^2 = rho^3 = 1, sigma rho sigma = rho^2> <= Aut(G), so that S is isomorphic to S_3. Assume that G is a group with triality, meaning that for M(G) := {[g, sigma] = g^{-1} g^sigma | g in G} one has m · m^rho · m^(rho^2) = 1 for every m in M(G). Suppose moreover that G = [G, S], and that there exist elements m_1, ..., m_d in M(G) such that G = <m_i^s : 1 <= i <= d, s in S>, and that x^n = 1 for all x in M(G). Must there exist a function f(d, n) such that the Fitting height h(G) satisfies h(G) <= f(d, n)?

For a fixed prime power q = p^f, let GL_n(F_q) be the general linear group over the field F_q, and define m_n(q) := max{ l_p(H) : H <= GL_n(F_q) and H is p-solvable }, where l_p(H) denotes the p-length of the finite p-solvable group H. Is it true that lim_{n->infty} m_n(q)/log_2(n) = 1?

Does there exist a pair of absolute constants C1 and C2 such that, for every finite nilpotent group A acting by automorphisms on every finite soluble group G, the Fitting height h(G) satisfies h(G) ≤ C1ℓ(A) + C2c(G,A), where ℓ(X) denotes the composition length of a finite group X and c(G,A) is the number of trivial A-modules occurring among the factors of a chosen A-invariant composition series of G? In the coprime case (|A|,|G|)=1, this parameter is equal to ℓ(C_G(A)). ([alglog.org](https://alglog.org/21tkt.pdf?utm_source=openai))

Let X be a nonempty class of finite groups such that every group in X has odd order and X is closed under taking subgroups, homomorphic images, and extensions. Suppose G is a finite group, N is a normal subgroup of G, and H <= G is X-maximal, meaning that H belongs to X and no subgroup K with H < K <= G belongs to X. Must H ∩ N be an X-maximal subgroup of N?

Does there exist an infinite group G such that, for every subset A ⊆ G, all subsets B ⊆ G that are maximal by inclusion subject to the condition that the product AB = {ab : a ∈ A, b ∈ B} is direct—that is, every element of AB has a unique representation ab with a ∈ A and b ∈ B—have the same cardinality? ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1401.0300.pdf))

Let G and H be finite groups, and for any finite group X define χ1(X) to be the multiset {χ(1) : χ ∈ Irr(X)} of degrees of the irreducible complex characters of X, counted with multiplicity. Assume that χ1(H) = χ1(G). Must H be isomorphic to G in each of the following cases: (i) G is almost simple, that is, S ≤ G ≤ Aut(S) for some nonabelian finite simple group S; (ii) G is quasisimple, that is, G is perfect and G/Z(G) is a nonabelian finite simple group? The corresponding statement is known when G itself is simple.

Let p be a prime and G a finite group. Write Z_(p) for the localization of Z at p, and let K_0(F_pG) be the Grothendieck group of finitely generated left F_pG-modules. Let X be the set of Grothendieck classes in K_0(F_pG) arising from reductions modulo p of simple QG-modules. Is it true that the group ring Z_(p)G is semiperfect if and only if, for every projective indecomposable left F_pG-module P, its class [P] lies in the subsemigroup N·X of K_0(F_pG); equivalently, [P] = sum_i n_i[M_i] for some n_i in N and some M_i in X?

Fix a group G = F_n ⋊ Z, where F_n is a free group of finite rank n. Is there an algorithm which, given a finite list S = {s_1, ..., s_k} of elements of G (encoded with respect to a fixed finite generating set of G), outputs a finite presentation for the subgroup H = <S> <= G?

For a fixed group G = F_n ⋊ Z, where F_n is a free group of finite rank n and Z is the infinite cyclic group, does there exist an algorithm that, given an element w ∈ G and finitely many elements h_1, ..., h_k ∈ G, decides whether w belongs to the subgroup H = ⟨h_1, ..., h_k⟩?

Let n >= 1 and let F be a field of characteristic p > 0. Define Γ = {σ in Aut_F(F[x1, ..., xn]) : σ(x_i) ≡ x_i mod (x1, ..., xn)^2 for every i}, the subgroup of polynomial automorphisms congruent to the identity modulo all terms of total degree at least 2. The paper notes that Γ is residually p. Is it true that Γ satisfies a nontrivial pro-p identity, that is, does there exist a nontrivial word in a finitely generated free pro-p group that evaluates to 1 under every substitution of elements of Γ?

For every prime p and integer e >= 0, let G be a finite p-soluble group, let P be a Sylow p-subgroup of G, and let A be a normal subgroup of P of exponent p^e. If A^G = <A^g | g in G> denotes the normal closure of A in G, is the p-length l_p(A^G) bounded above by a function of p and e alone? More strongly, can one choose such a bound to depend only on e and not on p? Here l_p(X) denotes the minimal number of p-group factors in a normal series of the finite p-soluble group X whose other factors are p'-groups.

For every finite soluble group G and every automorphism φ of G, where C_G(φ) = {g in G : φ(g) = g}, must there exist a subgroup H ≤ G such that [G : H] is bounded by a function of |φ| and |C_G(φ)|, and such that the Fitting height h(H) is bounded either (a) by a function of |φ| alone, or even (b) by a function of the composition length of the cyclic group ⟨φ⟩ alone?

Does there exist a function f such that, for every finite soluble group G and every finite nilpotent subgroup A ≤ Aut(G), the Fitting height h(G) of G (that is, the least length of a normal series of G with nilpotent factors) satisfies h(G) ≤ f(|A|, |C_G(A)|), where C_G(A) = {g in G : g^a = g for all a in A}?

Let G be a finite soluble group and let φ be an automorphism of G. Let C_G(φ) = {g ∈ G : g^φ = g} be the fixed-point subgroup, and let r be its (Prüfer) rank. Does there exist a function f : N × N → N such that the Fitting height h(G) satisfies h(G) ≤ f(|φ|, r)?

Let G be a finite group. Call G semi-abelian if there exists a chain of subgroups 1 = G0 ≤ G1 ≤ ··· ≤ Gn = G such that for each i = 0, 1, ..., n − 1, the subgroup Gi+1 is isomorphic to a quotient of a semidirect product Ai ⋊ Gi for some abelian group Ai. Must every such G be monomial; that is, must every irreducible character of G be induced from a linear character of some subgroup of G? ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1401.0300.pdf))
Does there exist an algorithm that, given a finite one-relator presentation G = ⟨x1, ..., xn | r = 1⟩, decides whether the presented group G is Gromov-hyperbolic (word-hyperbolic)?

Let G be an RFRS orientable Poincaré-duality group of dimension n (with coefficients in Z unless another commutative coefficient ring is specified). Is the following equivalent to vanishing of all field-valued L^2-Betti numbers over prime fields: there exist a finite-index subgroup G0 ≤ G and an epimorphism φ:G0→Z such that ker φ is an orientable Poincaré-duality group of dimension n−1 over all fields? Equivalently, are the following two conditions equivalent: (i) there exist G0 and φ as above with ker φ orientable PD_{n−1} over every field; and (ii) β_i^(2)(G;K)=0 for every i and every prime field K?

Do there exist a group G and two fields F1 and F2 such that G is of type FL(F1) and of type FL(F2), but χ_{F1}(G) ≠ χ_{F2}(G), where for a ring R, saying that G is of type FL(R) means that the trivial RG-module R admits a finite resolution by finitely generated free RG-modules, and for a field F one defines χ_F(G)=Σ_{i≥0}(-1)^i dim_F H_i(G;F)?

Let G be a group. Call G a Tarski monster if G is finitely generated, non-cyclic, and every proper non-trivial subgroup of G is isomorphic to every other proper non-trivial subgroup of G. Do there exist amenable Tarski monsters in either of the following two cases: (a) G is torsion-free; (b) G has exponent p for some prime p?

Let r(m) = {r + km | k ∈ Z} for integers m >= 1 and 0 <= r < m. If r1(m1) ∩ r2(m2) = ∅, let τ_{r1(m1),r2(m2)} be the involution of Z that swaps r1 + km1 with r2 + km2 for every k ∈ Z and fixes every other integer. Let CT(Z) be the subgroup of Sym(Z) generated by all such class transpositions. Is the conjugacy problem in CT(Z) algorithmically decidable; that is, given two elements g,h ∈ CT(Z), each specified as a finite word in class transpositions, is there an algorithm to decide whether there exists x ∈ CT(Z) such that xgx^{-1} = h?

Let r(m) = {r + km | k in Z} for integers 0 <= r < m, and for disjoint residue classes r1(m1), r2(m2) let τ_{r1(m1),r2(m2)} be the involution of Z that interchanges r1 + km1 and r2 + km2 for each k in Z and fixes all other integers. Let CT(Z) be the subgroup of Sym(Z) generated by all such class transpositions. Given an element g in CT(Z), effectively presented for example by a finite word in class transpositions, is there an algorithm deciding, separately, whether (a) g permutes some nontrivial partition of Z into residue classes, i.e. a partition Z = A1 ⊔ ... ⊔ Ak with k >= 2 in which each Ai is a residue class and g{A1,...,Ak} = {A1,...,Ak}; (b) every cycle of g on Z is finite; and (c) every cycle of g on Z is infinite?

For integers 0 <= r < m, write r(m)=r+mZ. If r_1(m_1) and r_2(m_2) are disjoint residue classes of Z, let τ_{r_1(m_1),r_2(m_2)} be the involution of Z that interchanges r_1+km_1 and r_2+km_2 for every k in Z and fixes all other integers. Let CT(Z) be the subgroup of Sym(Z) generated by all such class transpositions. For a set P of odd primes, let CT_P(Z) <= CT(Z) be the subgroup generated by those class transpositions τ_{r_1(m_1),r_2(m_2)} whose moduli m_1 and m_2 have only prime factors in P∪{2}. If P_1 and P_2 are distinct sets of odd primes with P_1 not contained in P_2 and P_2 not contained in P_1, is the subgroup generated by CT_{P_1}(Z) and CT_{P_2}(Z) necessarily a proper subgroup of CT_{P_1\cup P_2}(Z)?

Does there exist a field K of odd characteristic (equivalently, char K = p > 2), an integer n >= 3, and an irreducible elementary net (carpet) σ = (σij)1<=i!=j<=n over K such that each σij is a nonzero additive subgroup of K, the off-diagonal net relations σirσrj ⊆ σij hold whenever i, r, j are pairwise distinct, the elementary net subgroup E(σ) = < tij(α) = I + αeij : α in σij, i != j > contains no new elementary transvections tij(β) with β not in σij (so σ is closed), but there do not exist additive subgroups σii ⊆ K for 1 <= i <= n such that the full family (σij)1<=i,j<=n satisfies σirσrj ⊆ σij for all i, r, j (so σ is not completable)?

Fix an integer n ≥ 2, let d be an integer not divisible by n-th powers of primes, assume x^n − d is irreducible over Q, set θ = √[n]{d}, and let K = Q(θ). Embed K* into Aut_Q(K) by multiplication maps x ↦ ax, where Aut_Q(K) denotes the group of all invertible Q-linear maps of the Q-vector space K, and let T be the image. Via the basis 1, θ, θ^2, ..., θ^(n−1), identify Aut_Q(K) with G = GL(n, Q), and let T(d) be the corresponding unsplit maximal torus. If H ≤ G contains T(d) and a one-dimensional transformation, let σ = σ(H) be the associated net, let G(σ) be the corresponding net group, and let E(σ) be the subgroup of G(σ) generated by all transvections. Must H lie in the normalizer N_G(E(σ)) of E(σ) in G? ([alglog.org](https://alglog.org/21tkt.pdf?utm_source=openai))

Let p be a prime and let G be a pro-p group. Assume that, for every n >= 0, the continuous cohomology group H^n(G, F_p) with coefficients in the discrete trivial G-module F_p is finite. Must the mod-p cohomology ring H^*(G, F_p) = ⊕_{n>=0} H^n(G, F_p), under cup product, be finitely generated as an F_p-algebra?

Does there exist a finitely generated left-orderable group H such that, for every nonidentity element g in H, there exists a finitely generated subgroup G <= H with g in G for which g is distorted; that is, for some (equivalently, any) finite generating set S of G, if L_S denotes the corresponding word length, then L_S(g^n)/n -> 0 as n -> infinity? Here 'left-orderable' means that H admits a total order invariant under left multiplication.

Does there exist a finitely generated group G that admits a left-invariant total order and has exactly two conjugacy classes, namely {1} and G \ {1} (equivalently, every two nonidentity elements of G are conjugate)?

For every finite simple group Γ and every integer n ≥ 3, let F_n be the free group of rank n and let N_n(Γ) = {N ◁ F_n : F_n/N ≅ Γ}. Is the natural action of Aut(F_n) on N_n(Γ), given by α · N = α(N), transitive? (The paper notes that the analogous statement is false for n = 2.)

Conjecture (Lubotzky, Problem 21.82). For every integer n >= 3, let F_n be the free group of rank n. Is it true that there is no characteristic subgroup K of F_n for which the quotient F_n/K is a finite simple group? ([alglog.org](https://alglog.org/21tkt.pdf?utm_source=openai))

Let G be a finitely generated metabelian group. For each n >= 1, let S_n be the symmetric group on {1, ..., n}, equipped with the normalized Hamming distance d_n(σ, τ) = (1/n)|{x in {1, ..., n} : σ(x) != τ(x)}|. Suppose {f_n} is a sequence of set-theoretic maps f_n: G -> S_n such that d_n(f_n(g)f_n(h), f_n(gh)) -> 0 as n -> infinity for every g, h in G. Must there exist a sequence of group homomorphisms rho_n: G -> S_n such that d_n(rho_n(g), f_n(g)) -> 0 as n -> infinity for every g in G? Equivalently: is every finitely generated metabelian group permutation-stable?

Fix an integer r ≥ 3. Is the group SL_r(Z) flexibly P-stable in permutations? Equivalently, if d_H denotes the normalized Hamming metric on permutations of a finite set, does every asymptotic homomorphism σ_k: SL_r(Z) → Sym(X_k) on finite sets X_k—meaning that d_H(σ_k(gh), σ_k(g)σ_k(h)) → 0 for every g,h ∈ SL_r(Z)—admit finite supersets X_k ⊂ Y_k with |Y_k|/|X_k| → 1 and genuine homomorphisms τ_k: SL_r(Z) → Sym(Y_k) such that d_H(σ_k(g), τ_k(g)|_{X_k}) → 0 for every g ∈ SL_r(Z)?

Let G be a finitely generated group. For σ,τ in S_n, define d_n(σ,τ)=(1/n)|{x in {1,...,n} : σ(x) != τ(x)}|. A sequence of set-theoretic maps f_n:G->S_n is called an almost-homomorphism if d_n(f_n(g)f_n(h),f_n(gh))->0 as n->infinity for every g,h in G. The group G is called permutation-stable if for every almost-homomorphism {f_n} there exists a sequence of group homomorphisms ρ_n:G->S_n such that d_n(ρ_n(g),f_n(g))->0 as n->infinity for every g in G. For α in S_n and β in S_m with n<=m, define d_n^flex(α,β)=(1/n)(|{x in {1,...,n} : α(x) != β(x)}|+(m-n)). The group G is called flexibly permutation-stable if for every almost-homomorphism {f_n} there exist integers m_n>=n and group homomorphisms ρ_n:G->S_{m_n} such that d_n^flex(f_n(g),ρ_n(g))->0 as n->infinity for every g in G. Must every finitely generated flexibly permutation-stable group be permutation-stable?

Is every group G sofic? Equivalently, for every group G, every finite subset F ⊆ G with 1_G ∈ F, and every ε > 0, does there exist an integer n ≥ 1 and a map φ: F → S_n, where S_n is the symmetric group on {1, ..., n}, such that φ(1_G) = id_{S_n}, d_n(φ(gh), φ(g)φ(h)) < ε for all g, h ∈ F with gh ∈ F, and φ(g) is fixed-point-free for every g ∈ F \ {1_G}; here d_n(σ, τ) = (1/n)|{x ∈ {1, ..., n} : σ(x) ≠ τ(x)}|?

Let d be a positive integer and let G be a finite group. Suppose that G has a family of subgroups {H_i} such that each H_i can be generated by at most d elements and gcd({[G:H_i]}) = 1. Must G itself be generated by at most d+1 elements; equivalently, is d(G) <= d+1, where d(G) denotes the minimum size of a generating set of G?

Let k(G) denote the number of conjugacy classes of a finite group G. Burnside proved that if G has odd order, then |G|-k(G) is divisible by 16. Is it true that for every positive integer m there exists a finite non-abelian group G(m) of odd order such that |G(m)|-k(G(m))=16m? ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1401.0300.pdf))
For every integer n > 39, does the number k(S_n) of conjugacy classes of the symmetric group S_n fail to divide the group order |S_n| = n!? ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1401.0300.pdf))

Let Γ be a graph of diameter d, and for each i ∈ {1,2,…,d} let Γ_i be the graph on the same vertex set as Γ in which two vertices u,w are adjacent if and only if d_Γ(u,w)=i. Does there exist a Q-polynomial distance-regular graph Γ of diameter 3 such that both Γ_2 and Γ_3 are strongly regular?

For every prime p and every finite group G, let IBr_p(G) denote the set of irreducible p-Brauer characters of G (in the usual modular representation-theoretic sense over an algebraically closed field of characteristic p), and let |G|_{p′} denote the largest divisor of |G| that is coprime to p. Must one always have sum_{φ in IBr_p(G)} φ(1)^2 >= |G|_{p′}? The paper notes that this is known when p = 2.

Let p be a prime and G a finite group. Is it always true that |IBr_p(G)| <= max{ k(H) : H <= G and p does not divide |H| }, where IBr_p(G) denotes the set of irreducible p-Brauer characters of G and k(H) denotes the number of conjugacy classes of H?

Let G be a group, let k ⩾ 2, let H1,...,Hk be subgroups of G, and let g1,...,gk ∈ G. Assume that the left cosets g1H1,...,gkHk are pairwise disjoint and that their union is G. Must there exist distinct i,j ∈ {1,...,k} such that [G:Hi] = [G:Hj]? citeturn9search0

Let GK(G) be the labelled Gruenberg–Kegel graph of a finite group G: its vertices are the prime divisors of |G|, and two distinct primes p and q are adjacent if and only if G contains an element of order pq. Let the underlying unlabeled abstract graph of GK(G) be obtained by forgetting the prime labels. Say that G is recognizable by the isomorphism type of its Gruenberg–Kegel graph if, whenever H is a finite group whose underlying unlabeled Gruenberg–Kegel graph is isomorphic to that of G, one has H ≅ G. Are there infinitely many pairwise non-isomorphic finite groups G with this property?

Does there exist a finite almost simple but non-simple group G, with nonabelian simple socle S satisfying S < G ≤ Aut(S), such that for every finite group H, if the abstract unlabeled graph obtained from the Gruenberg–Kegel graph of H by forgetting the prime labels is isomorphic to the corresponding abstract graph for G, then H ≅ G?

Let G be a periodic group, i.e. a group in which every element has finite order, and suppose that G contains an involution. If, for every element x in G of even order, the centralizer C_G(x) is locally finite, must G itself be locally finite? ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1401.0300.pdf))
For every positive rational number r in Q_{>0}, does there exist a finite group G such that |Aut(G)|/|G| = r, where Aut(G) denotes the automorphism group of G?

Let w = w(x1,...,xn) be a multilinear commutator word, that is, a commutator of weight n in n distinct variables. For a group G, let G_w = {w(g1,...,gn) : g1,...,gn ∈ G} be the set of w-values, and let w(G) = ⟨G_w⟩ be the corresponding verbal subgroup. Suppose there exist finitely many cyclic subgroups C1,...,Cm ≤ G such that G_w ⊆ C1 ∪ ... ∪ Cm. Must there exist a finite normal subgroup N ◁ w(G) such that w(G)/N is cyclic?

Conjecture: Let G ≤ Sym(Ω) be a transitive permutation group on a finite set Ω. For every pair of distinct points α, β ∈ Ω, does there exist an element g ∈ G such that g(α) = β and the number of fixed points of g on Ω is not equal to 1?

Let A and G be finite groups with (|A|,|G|)=1, let C = C_G(A), let C′ = [C,C], and write Irr_A(G) for the set of A-invariant ordinary irreducible complex characters of G. For χ ∈ Irr_A(G), let χ∗ ∈ Irr(C) denote its Glauberman–Isaacs correspondent. Is it true that
|{χ ∈ Irr_A(G) : χ(c) ≠ 0 for every c ∈ C}| = |C/C′|?
Equivalently as a proposed stronger route to this count, can one prove that χ(c) ≠ 0 for every c ∈ C if and only if χ∗ is linear?

Classify the finite almost simple groups G — that is, finite groups with non-abelian finite simple socle T satisfying T ≤ G ≤ Aut(T) — that occur, up to isomorphism, as the full automorphism groups of regular polytopes of rank 3; equivalently, determine exactly which such groups G admit a generating triple of involutions ρ0, ρ1, ρ2 with two of them commuting.

Let V be a variety of groups generated by a finite group. For each integer n >= 1, let F_V(n) denote the relatively free group of rank n in V, and set f(n) = |F_V(n)|. Is it true that the limit lim_{n->infinity} (log f(n))^(1/n) exists, and that this limit is always an integer?

Let {G_i}_{i∈I} be an arbitrary family of Hausdorff topological groups, each of which is minimal (that is, it admits no strictly coarser Hausdorff group topology) and Raikov complete (that is, complete with respect to its two-sided uniformity). Must the product topological group ∏_{i∈I} G_i, equipped with the product topology, also be minimal? ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1401.0300.pdf))

Let w=w(x1,...,xn) be a nontrivial word in the free group on x1,...,xn. For k≥0 define e0(x1,...,xn)=x1 and e_{k+1}(x1,...,xn)=w(e_k(x1,...,xn),x2,...,xn). Say that a group G satisfies the Engel-type iterated identity w if for every x1,...,xn∈G there exists m=m(x1,...,xn)∈N such that e_m(x1,...,xn)=1. Suppose G is a finitely generated branch group in the sense that G acts faithfully and level-transitively on a rooted tree T, for each vertex v the rigid vertex stabilizer consists of elements acting trivially outside the subtree T_v, the n-th rigid level stabilizer is generated by the rigid vertex stabilizers of vertices at level n, and every rigid level stabilizer has finite index in G. Must G be a torsion group? ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1401.0300.pdf))

Let w be a group word. For a residually finite group G, let G_w denote the set of all values of w in G, and let w(G)=⟨G_w⟩ be the corresponding verbal subgroup. If G_w is finite, must w(G) also be finite? Equivalently, is every group word concise in the class of residually finite groups?

Let φ(x) be a first-order formula in the pure language of groups, with exactly one free variable x. For a group G, write G_φ={g∈G : G ⊨ φ(g)} and φ(G)=⟨G_φ⟩. Say that φ is concise in a class C of groups if, whenever G∈C and G_φ is finite, the subgroup φ(G) is also finite. Is every such one-variable first-order formula concise in the class of residually finite groups (that is, groups in which every nontrivial element has nontrivial image in some finite quotient)?

Let G be a countable topological group, and assume that G can be partitioned into countably many dense subsets. Must there exist a sequence (F_n)_{n∈N} of pairwise disjoint finite subsets of G such that for every nonempty open subset U of G there exists m∈N with F_n ∩ U ≠ ∅ for all n > m?

Let G be a finite group, let Irr(G) be the set of irreducible complex characters of G, and for χ∈Irr(G) define the codegree cod(χ)=|G:ker χ|/χ(1). Set Cod(G)={cod(χ):χ∈Irr(G)}. If π(n) denotes the set of prime divisors of a positive integer n and π(G)=π(|G|), define σ(G)=max{|π(m)|:m∈Cod(G)}. Is it true that |π(G)|≤4σ(G) for every finite group G? ([alglog.org](https://alglog.org/21tkt.pdf?utm_source=openai))

Let G be a finite solvable group. For each irreducible complex character χ of G, define its codegree by cod(χ)=|G:ker χ|/χ(1), and let Cod(G)={cod(χ): χ∈Irr(G)} be the set of irreducible character codegrees of G. Is it always true that the derived length dl(G) satisfies dl(G)≤|Cod(G)|−1? (As background, the paper notes that the Fitting height of G is known to be at most min{|Cod(G)|−1, |Cod(G)|/2+1}.)

Let S be a finite simple exceptional group of Lie type, let x be a nonidentity element of Aut(S), and set G = <x, Inn(S)>. Define α_S(x) to be the least integer m such that G is generated by m conjugates of x in G. Determine, for each such S, the exact quantity M(S) = max{α_S(x) : 1 != x in Aut(S)}; in particular, is it always true that M(S) <= 5?

Classify, up to isomorphism, all finite nonabelian simple groups S other than the Suzuki groups ^2B_2(q) (where q = 2^(2m+1) >= 8) for which there exists a nonidentity automorphism x in Aut(S) such that for every g,h in <x, Inn(S)>, the subgroup <x^g, x^h> has order not divisible by 3; such an automorphism x is called a tau-automorphism, and such a group S is called a tau-group. Also determine whether any tau-automorphism can have odd order.

Let X be a nonempty class of finite groups that is closed under taking subgroups, homomorphic images, and extensions. For such a class X, assuming X is not the class of all finite groups, define its symmetric boundary to be the largest integer n for which the symmetric group S_n belongs to X. For each complete class X, let BS(X) denote the least nonnegative integer m with the following property: for every finite group G and every conjugacy class D of G, if every m elements of D generate a subgroup belonging to X, then the subgroup <D> generated by D also belongs to X. For each positive integer n!=3, define f_+(n)=max BS(X) and f_-(n)=min BS(X), where X ranges over all complete classes of finite groups with symmetric boundary n. Determine f_+(n) for n=4,5,6, given that f_+(1)=2, f_+(2)=3, and f_+(n)=2(n-1) for all n>=7; and decide whether f_-(n)=n for every positive integer n!=3, as is already known for n=1,2,4.

For every finite group G and prime p, define a class function Ψ_{p,G} on G by Ψ_{p,G}(x)=0 when x is p-singular (that is, when p divides |x|), and Ψ_{p,G}(x)=|{u∈C_G(x): u has p-power order}| when x is p-regular. Is Ψ_{p,G} always an ordinary character of G? If it is, does there always exist a finitely generated projective RG-module P, where R is a complete discrete valuation ring of characteristic 0 with fraction field K=Frac(R) a splitting field for G and all subgroups of G and residue field k=R/J(R) a splitting field of characteristic p for G and all subgroups of G, such that the ordinary character of K⊗_R P is Ψ_{p,G}? ([alglog.org](https://alglog.org/21tkt.pdf?utm_source=openai))

Does there exist an absolute integer d such that every finite group G with |H:[H,H]| ≤ |G:[G,G]| for every subgroup H ≤ G (equivalently, every finite weakly ab-maximal group, where [X,X] denotes the commutator subgroup of X) is solvable of derived length at most d?

For every positive integer n, every finite group G, and every family C_1, ..., C_n of subsets of G such that each C_i is either a left coset or a right coset of some subgroup H_i ≤ G, if U := C_1 ∪ ··· ∪ C_n is a proper subset of G, must one always have |G ∖ U| ≥ |G|/2^n?

Let G be a branch group in the standard sense. Must H_b^n(G; R) = 0 for every integer n ≥ 1, where R is viewed as a trivial G-module? Equivalently, is every branch group boundedly acyclic? ([alglog.org](https://alglog.org/21tkt.pdf?utm_source=openai))

Question 21.117. (a) Does there exist a finitely generated simple abstract group G such that G is of exponential growth but not of uniformly exponential growth; that is, if for a finite generating set S one writes B_{G,S}(n) for the radius-n word ball and omega(G,S) = lim_{n->infty} |B_{G,S}(n)|^(1/n), then omega(G,S) > 1 for some finite generating set S, but inf_T omega(G,T) = 1 when T ranges over all finite generating sets of G? (b) Does there exist a finitely generated hereditarily just-infinite abstract group G with the same growth property? Here, "just-infinite" means that G is infinite and every nontrivial normal subgroup of G has finite index, and "hereditarily just-infinite" means that every finite-index subgroup of G is just-infinite.
Does there exist a group G such that G is not isomorphic to R/N for any residually finite group R and any amenable normal subgroup N of R?

Does there exist a group G containing a sequence of finite-index subgroups (G_n)_{n\ge 1} such that, for each positive integer n, there exists a group homomorphism f_n:G_n\to \mathbb{Z} whose kernel is of type F_n but not of type F_{n+1}? Here, a group is of type F_n if it admits a classifying space K(-,1) with finite n-skeleton.

For some prime p, does there exist a pro-p group G that is (relatively) strictly finitely presented—meaning that G is the pro-p completion of a finitely presented discrete group, respectively of a discrete group finitely presented in some finitely based variety of groups—but is not finitely axiomatizable, i.e. is not determined up to isomorphism within the class of all pro-p groups by a single first-order sentence in the language of groups? In particular, for every prime p and every d >= 1, is the free pro-p group F_d on d topological generators finitely axiomatizable within the class of all pro-p groups?

Fix a prime p. Say that a group Γ is p-Jordan if there exist constants J > 0 and e ≥ 0, depending only on Γ, such that for every finite subgroup G ≤ Γ there exists a normal abelian subgroup A ◁ G of order prime to p with [G : A] ≤ J · |P|^e, where P is a Sylow p-subgroup of G (equivalently, |P| = |G(p)|). Define the p-Jordan exponent e(Γ) to be the infimum of all real numbers e for which such a constant J = J(e, Γ) exists. If Γ is p-Jordan, must this infimum always be attained? Equivalently, does there always exist J such that the above inequality holds with exponent e = e(Γ)? And, in all cases, must one have e(Γ) ≤ 3?
For every group word w = w(x1, ..., xn) and every profinite group G, must the set of word values Gw = {w(g1, ..., gn) : g1, ..., gn in G} be either finite or of cardinality at least 2^{aleph_0}?

Let A be a finite pre-Lie ring of cardinality p^n, where p is a prime, and assume that A satisfies the technical hypotheses called Properties 1′ and 1″ in A. Smoktunowicz, 'An extension of the group of flows method for finite pre-Lie rings' (equivalently, Property 3 in the paper’s later notation). If one applies to A the generalized group-of-flows construction defined in Definition 66 of that paper—the extension of the classical Agrachev–Gamkrelidze construction obtained by replacing the classical division-by-p step by the paper’s pullback/division maps—does one always obtain a genuine group law on A? Equivalently at the level intended in Kourovka Problem 21.123: is the pseudobrace produced by this generalized construction always in fact a brace with the same additive group as A?

Let G be a CAT(0) free-by-cyclic group, meaning that G has a normal free subgroup F with cyclic quotient G/F and that G acts properly discontinuously and cocompactly by isometries on a CAT(0) metric space. Must G be virtually special, i.e. must some finite-index subgroup of G be isomorphic to the fundamental group of a Haglund-Wise special cube complex? More weakly, must some finite-index subgroup of G embed into a right-angled Artin group?

Let m ≥ 1, let F_m be the free group of rank m, and let φ ∈ Aut(F_m) be a polynomially growing automorphism of maximal degree m−1, meaning that for some (equivalently, any) free basis {x_1, ..., x_m} of F_m, the sequence max_i |φ^n(x_i)| grows at the rate of n^{m−1}, where |g| denotes the minimal word length of g in the letters x_1^{±1}, ..., x_m^{±1}. If F_m ⋊_φ Z denotes the semidirect product in which a generator of Z acts on F_m by φ, is F_m ⋊_φ Z virtually special, i.e. does it have a finite-index subgroup isomorphic to the fundamental group of a special complex in the sense of Haglund–Wise? In particular, does this hold for the Hydra groups G_m = ⟨a_1, ..., a_m, t | t^{−1}a_1t = a_1, t^{−1}a_it = a_ia_{i−1} for 2 ≤ i ≤ m⟩? ([alglog.org](https://alglog.org/21tkt.pdf?utm_source=openai))

Does there exist a finitely presented subgroup H ≤ A of some right-angled Artin group A whose Dehn function δ_H, considered up to the standard equivalence of Dehn functions, is either super-exponential, or else sub-exponential but not equivalent to any polynomial?

Let G be a right-angled Artin group. For each g ∈ [G,G], let cl(g) denote the least number of commutators in G whose product is g, and define the stable commutator length by scl(g) := lim_{n→∞} cl(g^n)/n. Is scl(g) a rational number for every g ∈ [G,G]? (For free groups this is known by Calegari’s Rationality Theorem.)

Let A[F4] and A[H4] denote the Artin groups associated to the spherical Coxeter types F4 and H4, respectively. Are A[F4] and A[H4] commensurable; that is, do there exist finite-index subgroups H_F <= A[F4] and H_H <= A[H4] such that H_F is isomorphic to H_H?

Let A[Γ] and A[Ω] be Artin groups of spherical type, meaning that their associated Coxeter groups W[Γ] and W[Ω] are finite. If A[Γ] and A[Ω] are quasi-isometric as finitely generated groups (equivalently, with respect to word metrics coming from finite generating sets), must they be commensurable; that is, do there exist finite-index subgroups H ≤ A[Γ] and K ≤ A[Ω], not necessarily of the same index, such that H ≅ K?

Is the following conjecture true? For every integer n>2 and every n-element subset A of a finite additive abelian group G of odd order, there exists an ordering A={a1,...,an} such that the n cyclic adjacent sums a1+a2, a2+a3, ..., a_{n-1}+a_n, a_n+a1 are pairwise distinct. ([maths.nju.edu.cn](https://maths.nju.edu.cn/~zwsun/196a.pdf?utm_source=openai))

Construct explicitly a subgroup H of a Golod group G = <1 + x1 + I, 1 + x2 + I, ..., 1 + xr + I> <= 1 + F/I, where r >= 2, F is the free algebra of polynomials without constant terms in noncommuting variables x1, ..., xr over a field of characteristic p > 0, and I is an ideal such that F/I is a non-nilpotent nil-algebra, together with a surjective homomorphism H ↠ A onto an infinite AT-group A in the sense of A. V. Rozhkov (Math. Notes 40 (1986), no. 5, 827-836).

Using a Golod-type construction in the sense intended by the paper, for each prime number p construct a finitely generated group G such that every element of G has p-power order, for every nonidentity element g ∈ G there exists a homomorphism from G onto a finite p-group whose image of g is nontrivial, and the centre Z(G) is finite and nontrivial; equivalently, 1 < |Z(G)| < ∞.

Let G be an arbitrary group. Suppose that for every countable subgroup H <= G there exists an ordinal tau and an ascending subnormal series 1 = H_0 <= H_1 <= ... <= H_tau = H such that H_alpha is normal in H_{alpha+1} for every alpha < tau, H_lambda = union_{beta < lambda} H_beta for every limit ordinal lambda <= tau, and each factor H_{alpha+1}/H_alpha is abelian. Must G itself admit such a subnormal series?

Let t_G : positive integers → positive integers be the type of a finite group G, defined by t_G(n) = |{x in G : x^n = 1}|. Let R(G) denote the solvable radical of G. Determine whether the following assertions are true: (i) if H is a finite group and there exists a finite group G with R(G) = 1 such that t_H(n) = t_G(n) for every positive integer n, then R(H) = 1; and (ii) if G is a finite almost simple group, meaning that T ≤ G ≤ Aut(T) for some nonabelian finite simple group T, and H is a finite group with t_H(n) = t_G(n) for every positive integer n, then H is isomorphic to G.

Let G and H be finite groups, and for any finite group X let χ1(X) denote the multiset of degrees χ(1) of all ordinary irreducible complex characters χ in Irr(X), counted with multiplicity. If χ1(H) = χ1(G) and the solvable radical R(G) of G is trivial (that is, R(G) = 1), must the solvable radical of H also be trivial?

Let G be a profinite group such that the set {x^G : x in G and x has infinite order} has cardinality strictly less than 2^{ℵ_0}. Must G be a torsion group, that is, must every element of G have finite order?

Let G be a finite p-group, and let H = {g^p : g in G}. Assume that H is itself a subgroup of G. Must H be a powerful p-group; that is, must [H,H] <= H^p when p is odd and [H,H] <= H^4 when p = 2? In particular, when p != 2 and exp(G) = p^2, does this force H to be abelian? And when p = 2 and exp(G) = 8, if the set of squares {g^2 : g in G} is a subgroup, must it be abelian?

Let G be an infinite finitely presented group such that every subgroup of G of infinite index is a free group. Must G be isomorphic to either a free group or to the fundamental group of a closed connected surface?

Let G be a Gromov-hyperbolic group that is virtually compact special, meaning that some finite-index subgroup of G is the fundamental group of a compact special cube complex in the sense of Haglund–Wise. Assume that the set {b_2(H) = dim_Q H_2(H; Q) : H <= G, [G : H] < infinity} is bounded (equivalently, there exists C such that b_2(H) <= C for every finite-index subgroup H of G). Must G have a finite-index subgroup that is either a finitely generated free group or the fundamental group of a closed surface of negative Euler characteristic?

Let G be a torsion-free group of type F∞, meaning that G admits a classifying space K(G,1) whose n-skeleton is finite for every n ≥ 1, and suppose that G has infinite cohomological dimension. Must G contain a subgroup isomorphic to Thompson’s group F?

Let G = G1 *_H G2 be a free pro-p product with amalgamation, where G1 and G2 are coherent pro-p groups and the amalgamated subgroup H is polycyclic. Must G be coherent in the pro-p sense; equivalently, must every finitely generated closed subgroup of G be a finitely presented pro-p group?

Fix distinct primes p and q. Is it true that for every finite group K there exists a finite group H containing a subgroup isomorphic to K and elements a, b in H with |a| = p and |b| = q such that, for every g, h in H, one has H = <a^g, b^h>?

Is R. Thompson's group F, defined by F = <x_0, x_1, ... | x_n^{x_i} = x_{n+1} for i < n and n = 1, 2, ...> = <x_0, ..., x_4 | x_1^{x_0} = x_2, x_2^{x_0} = x_3, x_2^{x_1} = x_3, x_3^{x_1} = x_4, x_3^{x_2} = x_4>, where g^h := h^{-1}gh, an automatic group? ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1401.0300.pdf))
Let F denote Thompson's group F. Is it true that for every subgroup H ≤ F, either H is elementary amenable or there exists a subgroup K ≤ H with K ≅ F?

Let F denote Richard Thompson's group F, and let ℤ denote the infinite cyclic group. In the standard quasi-isometry sense for finitely generated groups (equivalently, for Cayley graphs with word metrics), is F quasi-isometric to F × ℤ? Separately, is F quasi-isometric to F × F?

Fix an integer n ≥ 3. If G is an abstract group of type F_{n-1}, meaning that G admits a classifying space K(G,1) with finite (n-1)-skeleton, must there exist a group H of type F_n and an injective homomorphism G → H? More strongly, can H always be chosen to be of type F_∞? ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1401.0300.pdf))

For every group G that admits a right ordering (that is, a total order invariant under right multiplication), let RRC(G) be the set of subgroups H <= G that are convex with respect to some right ordering of G. Is RRC(G), ordered by inclusion, always a sublattice of the subgroup lattice Sub(G); equivalently in lattice-theoretic terms, whenever H,K are in RRC(G), must both H ∩ K and the subgroup generated by H ∪ K again belong to RRC(G)?

Let G be a right-orderable group. Call a subgroup H ≤ G right-relatively convex if there exists a right-invariant total order ≤ on G such that H is convex with respect to ≤, i.e. whenever h1 ≤ g ≤ h2 with h1,h2 ∈ H, then g ∈ H. Is the inclusion-ordered lattice of right-relatively convex subgroups of G distributive if and only if it is a chain?

Does there exist a Dlab group G together with an order making G an ordered group and an automorphism alpha: G -> G that preserves this order but is not inner; that is, alpha is not of the form alpha(x) = g x g^{-1} for some fixed g in G and all x in G?

Let G = A ⋊ B, where A is a normal elementary abelian subgroup and B is an elementary abelian subgroup with B ≅ G/A. Assume that A contains an element a such that C_B(a) = 1. If H = ⟨a,B⟩, must one have rank(Z(H) ∩ H') ≤ rank(B), where Z(H) denotes the center of H, H' its derived subgroup, and rank means the dimension of an elementary abelian group over its prime field?

Let x:M^n→E^{n+1} be an isometric immersion of a connected n-dimensional Riemannian manifold into Euclidean (n+1)-space, and let Δ denote the Laplace operator on M. Say that x is of finite type if its position vector field admits a finite spectral decomposition x=c+x_1+⋯+x_k, where c∈E^{n+1} is constant and each x_i:M→E^{n+1} is a non-constant map satisfying Δx_i=λ_i x_i for some constants λ_i. Classify all finite type hypersurfaces in E^{n+1}; in particular, classify all finite type surfaces in E^3.

Let x:M→E^3 be an isometric immersion of a compact connected surface into Euclidean 3-space, and let Δ be the Laplace operator of the induced metric on M. Suppose x is of finite type, in the sense that its position vector admits a decomposition x=c+x1+...+xk for some constant vector c∈E^3 and finitely many nonconstant E^3-valued maps xi satisfying Δxi=λi xi. Must the immersed surface x(M) be an ordinary round 2-sphere in E^3? ([journals.math.tku.edu.tw](https://journals.math.tku.edu.tw/index.php/TKJM/article/download/1564/1137/3950))

Let x:M→E^3 be an isometric immersion of a connected Riemannian surface into real Euclidean 3-space, and call M a finite type surface if its position vector field has a finite spectral decomposition x=c+x1+⋯+xk with c constant, each xi nonconstant, and Δxi=λixi for the Laplace operator Δ of the induced metric. Must every such finite type surface be either a minimal surface in E^3, or an open portion of an ordinary round 2-sphere, or an open portion of a circular cylinder? ([journals.math.tku.edu.tw](https://journals.math.tku.edu.tw/index.php/TKJM/article/download/1564/1137/3950))

For every n≥1, if x:M^n→E^{n+1} is a compact connected isometric hypersurface immersion whose position vector field has a finite spectral decomposition x=c+x1+...+xk with Δxi=λi xi for finitely many nonconstant E^{n+1}-valued eigenmaps of the Laplace operator Δ on M, must x(M) be an ordinary hypersphere, i.e. a round sphere S^n(r) in E^{n+1}?

Let x: M^n -> S^{n+1}(r) subset E^{n+2} be a connected smooth hypersurface immersion into a hypersphere of real Euclidean space, regarded also as an immersion into E^{n+2}. Assume x is of 2-type in the sense of finite type, namely that its Euclidean position vector admits a spectral decomposition x = c + x_1 + x_2 with c in E^{n+2} constant and Delta x_i = lambda_i x_i for i = 1, 2, where Delta is the Laplace-Beltrami operator of M and lambda_1 != lambda_2. Classify all such 2-type hypersurfaces in hyperspheres of E^{n+2}; in particular, determine all 2-type hypersurfaces M^3 subset S^4 subset E^5.

Let x: M^n -> S^{n+1} \subset E^{n+2} be an isometric immersion of a connected Riemannian n-manifold as a hypersurface of a hypersphere in Euclidean space. Classify those hypersurfaces for which, viewed as an immersion into E^{n+2}, the position vector field is of finite Chen type; that is, x admits a finite spectral decomposition x = c + x_1 + ... + x_k with c \in E^{n+2} constant, each x_i a nonconstant E^{n+2}-valued map on M, and Δx_i = λ_i x_i for the Laplace operator Δ of M.

Let x:M^2→S^3⊂E^4 be an isometric immersion of a connected surface into the unit 3-sphere, viewed as a submanifold of Euclidean 4-space. Assume that M is of finite type in the sense of Chen, namely that its Euclidean position vector admits a finite spectral decomposition x=c+x1+...+xk with Δxi=λi xi for the Laplace operator Δ on M. Must M be one of the following and only these: (i) a minimal surface in S^3, (ii) a standard round 2-sphere in S^3, or (iii) a product S^1(a)×S^1(b) of two plane circles in S^3, with a^2+b^2=1 (and, in the nonminimal 2-type case, a≠b)? ([journals.math.tku.edu.tw](https://journals.math.tku.edu.tw/index.php/TKJM/article/viewFile/1564/873))

Let x: M -> S^{n+1} ⊂ E^{n+2} be a Dupin hypersurface, meaning that the multiplicities of its principal curvatures are constant and each principal curvature is constant along its corresponding principal directions. Determine precisely when M is of finite type in the sense of Chen, i.e. when the Euclidean position vector of the inclusion admits a finite Laplace-Beltrami spectral decomposition x = c + x_1 + ... + x_k with Δx_i = λ_i x_i, and determine precisely when a finite-type Dupin hypersurface of a hypersphere must be isoparametric, that is, have constant principal curvatures.

Does there exist a connected Riemannian surface M with an isometric immersion x:M→S^4⊂E^5 such that, viewed as an E^5-valued immersion, x is of 2-type in the sense that x=a+x1+x2 with Δx_i=λ_i x_i and λ1≠λ2, but x is not mass-symmetric in S^4, i.e. the center of gravity of M in E^5 does not coincide with the center of the ambient 4-sphere?

Does there exist a connected Riemannian surface M together with an isometric immersion x: M -> S_c^{2p} subset E^{2p+1} into some even-dimensional hypersphere, such that x(M) lies fully in S_c^{2p} and, viewed as an E^{2p+1}-valued immersion, x is of 2-type in the sense that x = a + x1 + x2 with Δxi = λi xi for two distinct eigenvalues λ1 != λ2 of the Laplace operator Δ on M? In particular, does there exist such an example that is mass-symmetric, meaning that the center of gravity of M in E^{2p+1} coincides with the center c of the hypersphere?

Let x:M→E^m be an isometric immersion of a connected Riemannian manifold into real Euclidean m-space. Assume x is of 2-type, meaning that its position vector field admits a spectral decomposition x=c+x_1+x_2, where c∈E^m is constant, x_1 and x_2 are nonconstant E^m-valued maps, and Δx_i=λ_i x_i for distinct real eigenvalues λ_1 and λ_2, with Δ the Laplace operator of M. For i=1,2, let E_i⊂E^m be the subspace spanned by {x_i(p): p∈M}. Determine and classify those 2-type immersions for which E_1 and E_2 are linearly independent subspaces of E^m. ([journals.math.tku.edu.tw](https://journals.math.tku.edu.tw/index.php/TKJM/article/download/1564/873/4133))

Let x:M^n->E^(n+2) be a k-type isometric immersion of a connected Riemannian manifold into Euclidean space, with spectral decomposition x=c+x_1+...+x_k, where each x_i is a nonconstant E^(n+2)-valued map satisfying Delta x_i=lambda_i x_i and the eigenvalues lambda_1,...,lambda_k are mutually distinct. For each i, set E_i:=span{x_i(p): p in M} subset E^(n+2). Study and classify all codimension-2 Euclidean submanifolds for which the subspaces E_1,...,E_k are linearly independent (equivalently, x is linearly independent in Chen's sense).

Let x: M^n → E^{n+2} be an isometric immersion of a connected Riemannian n-manifold, and let Δ denote the Laplace operator of M. Suppose the position vector admits a 2-type spectral decomposition x = a + x1 + x2 with x1, x2 non-constant, Δxi = λi xi, λ1 ≠ λ2, and λ1λ2 ≠ 0 (so x is non-null 2-type). If M has constant mean curvature, i.e. |H| is constant, must x(M) be contained in a hypersphere of E^{n+2}?

Let x : M^n → E^m be a connected isometric immersion of a Riemannian manifold into real Euclidean space, and suppose that x is of null 2-type in the finite-type sense, namely that its spectral decomposition has the form x = c + x1 + x2 with Δx1 = 0 and Δx2 = λx2 for some nonzero real constant λ. Study and classify such null 2-type submanifolds. In particular, classify all null 2-type surfaces in E^4 and all null 2-type surfaces in 4-dimensional pseudo-Euclidean spaces.

Let x: M^n → E^m be an isometric immersion of a connected Riemannian manifold into Euclidean m-space, let Δ denote the Laplace operator on M, and let H be the mean curvature vector field of x. Classify the biharmonic Euclidean submanifolds, namely those for which Δ²x = 0 identically, equivalently ΔH = 0 identically: other than minimal submanifolds, which submanifolds of E^m are biharmonic?

For every isometric immersion x: M^n -> E^m of a Riemannian manifold into Euclidean m-space, if x is biharmonic in the sense that Delta^2 x = 0 (equivalently, Delta H = 0, where H is the mean curvature vector field), must H vanish identically? Equivalently, is every biharmonic submanifold of a Euclidean space minimal? ([journals.math.tku.edu.tw](https://journals.math.tku.edu.tw/index.php/TKJM/article/viewFile/1564/873))

Hypersurface case of Chen’s original biharmonic conjecture: let x:M^n→E^{n+1} be an isometric immersion of a connected Riemannian hypersurface into real Euclidean space. If x is biharmonic, in the sense that Δ^2x=0 (equivalently ΔH=0), where Δ is the Laplace operator on M and H is the mean curvature vector, must H vanish identically? ([journals.math.tku.edu.tw](https://journals.math.tku.edu.tw/index.php/TKJM/article/download/1564/873/4133))

For arbitrary n and m, let x : M^n -> E^m be a complete isometric immersion of a connected Riemannian n-manifold into Euclidean m-space. If x is biharmonic, i.e. Delta^2 x = 0, equivalently Delta H⃗ = 0 identically, where H⃗ is the mean curvature vector field of M and Delta is the Laplace operator on M, must M be minimal, i.e. H⃗ ≡ 0?

In the projection‐operator framework for compound‐nuclear reactions (Section 2), how can one formulate a practical reaction theory for the transitional regime—characterized by average resonance widths Γ comparable to the level spacing D—encountered in reactions on light nuclei and on neutron‐rich nuclei far from the valley of stability, so as to accurately compute cross sections when neither the statistical Hauser–Feshbach limit (Γ≫D) nor the isolated‐resonance R‐matrix limit (Γ≪D) applies, while coherently accounting for both direct and compound mechanisms and avoiding computationally prohibitive Gaussian Orthogonal Ensemble ensemble integrals?

In the surrogate-reaction method, the neutron-induced compound-nucleus cross section σ_{αχ}(E)=∑_{J,Π}σ^{CN}_{α}(E,J,Π)G^{CN}_{χ}(E,J,Π) is obtained by combining calculated formation cross sections σ^{CN}_{α}(E,J,Π) with branching ratios G^{CN}_{χ}(E,J,Π) extracted from measured coincidence probabilities P_δ(E,J,Π) for forming a nucleus with spin–parity (J,Π) in a surrogate transfer or inelastic reaction δ. How can one develop a unified theoretical framework that (1) predicts the spin–parity population P_δ(E,J,Π) of the highly-excited intermediate system produced in δ, and (2) models the damping of this intermediate into an equilibrated compound nucleus, so that the resulting extracted σ_{αχ}(E) agree reliably with direct measurements?

For charged-current quasielastic-like muon neutrino scattering on ^12C with a few-GeV neutrino flux (such as in MiniBooNE at ⟨E_ν⟩≈0.8 GeV and MINERvA up to ∼10 GeV), what is the quantitative contribution of two-particle–two-hole excitations and their interference with meson-exchange two-body currents to the flux-averaged double differential cross section d^2σ/(dE_μ dcosθ_μ), and how can this contribution be unambiguously determined by direct comparison to the measured muon energy–angle distributions rather than inferred from inclusive sum-rule enhancements?

In the generalized orthogonal Procrustes model of Bandeira-Khoo-Singer, let d > 1, n > 2, and m >= d + 1. Let A in R^{d x m} have i.i.d. coordinates uniform on [0,1], let O_1, ..., O_n be any sequence of orthogonal matrices in O_d, and observe A_i = O_i A + sigma eta_i in R^{d x m}, where each eta_i has i.i.d. N(0,1) entries. Assuming ||A||_F is fixed so that the MLE reduces to the quasi-MLE min over O_1,...,O_n in O_d of sum over i<j of ||O_i^T A_i - O_j^T A_j||_F^2, equivalently to the rank-constrained program max Tr(CX) subject to X positive semidefinite, X_{ii} = I_d for all i, and rank(X) <= d, with block matrix C defined by C_{ij}^T = A_j A_i^T, does there exist a constant sigma_* > 0 such that for every sigma < sigma_*, with high probability over A and the noise, the optimizer of the SDP relaxation obtained by dropping rank(X) <= d still has rank exactly d, and therefore coincides with the quasi-MLE without any rounding step?

Let d>1, n>2, and m>=d+1. Let A in R^{d x m} be a random point cloud whose m columns are i.i.d. uniform on [0,1]^d, and let O_1,...,O_n belong to O_d, where O_d={O in R^{d x d}: OO^T=I_d}, be any orthogonal matrices. For observations A_i=O_iA+sigma eta_i in R^{d x m}, where each eta_i has i.i.d. N(0,1) entries, define C in R^{dn x dn} by its d x d blocks C_{ij}=A_iA_j^T. After fixing ||A||_F, the generalized orthogonal Procrustes quasi-MLE is the rank-constrained semidefinite program maximize Tr(CX) subject to X positive semidefinite, X_{ii}=I_d for i=1,...,n, and rank(X)<=d; its SDP relaxation is obtained by dropping the rank constraint. Is it true that there exists sigma*>0 such that, whenever sigma<sigma*, with high probability over the random A and Gaussian noise, the solution of the relaxed SDP has rank d, and hence matches the quasi-MLE, i.e. the solution of the rank-constrained problem?

In a three-dimensional, zero-temperature, polarized atomic Fermi gas at zero background density—described by the zero-range wide-resonance Hamiltonian (Eq. (1)) with s-wave scattering length a>0—let α=m/M be the impurity-to-fermion mass ratio below the Efimov threshold α_c (the smallest α for which three- or four-body Efimov states appear). For which values of α<α_c and a>0 does there exist at least one stable non-Efimovian vacuum bound state comprising one impurity plus N≥5 identical fermions (e.g., pentamer, hexamer), whose energy lies below all dissociation thresholds into any combination of smaller impurity-fermion clusters?

Consider the Hamiltonian H of a single spinless impurity of mass M interacting via s-wave contact interactions of scattering length a with a three-dimensional ideal Fermi gas of identical fermions of mass m at zero temperature (the wide-resonance, zero-range model of Eq. (1)). Let k_F denote the Fermi wave vector when a Fermi sea is present, and define the dimensionless interaction parameter 1/(k_Fa) for the gas case (or equivalently a for the vacuum case). For fixed mass ratio m/M and fixed interaction parameter (a in vacuum or 1/(k_Fa) with a Fermi sea), does there exist a finite maximum integer N_max such that no non-Efimovian bound state of the impurity with N>N_max fermions can be stable (i.e., have energy below all decay thresholds) in either vacuum or immersed in the Fermi gas? Prove or provide a counterexample.

Let ε>0, r>0, and let f:ℝ_+→ℝ be smooth with f(0)=0. Consider the complex-valued equation for v=v(t,x), t>0, x∈ℝ^d, obtained from the general model (3) by taking P2(ε∇)=I, α2=0, and α3=0:

i∂_t v + Δv + (1+f(ε^r|v|^2))|v|^2v = 0,

with d=2 in the no-group-velocity-dispersion case and d=3 in the anomalous-group-velocity-dispersion case (in particular including the cubic-quintic case f(s)=-s and saturated nonlinearities for which (1+f(s))s is bounded). Can one rigorously establish for solutions to this equation the oscillatory filamentation behavior observed in physical experiments and numerical simulations—namely, that the solution focuses, then defocuses, then refocuses, and so on in an almost periodic fashion?

Let d ∈ {2,3}, with d = 2 corresponding to the no-GVD case and d = 3 to the anomalous-GVD case, let r > 0, and let v0 ∈ H^1(ℝ^d). Assume that the solution v of the focusing cubic NLS i∂t v + Δv + |v|^2v = 0 on ℝ^d with v(0) = v0 blows up in finite time T > 0. For the corresponding solution vε of the nonlinear regularization i∂t vε + Δvε + (1 + f(ε^r|vε|^2))|vε|^2vε = 0, vε(0) = v0, where f is one of the standard nonlinear corrections considered in Section 4.1.1 of the paper—either f(s) = -s (cubic-quintic case) or a smooth saturated nonlinearity with f(0) = 0 and s(1 + f(s)) bounded on ℝ+—describe the behavior of vε(t) as ε → 0 for times t > T, i.e. after the blow-up time of the cubic NLS solution.

For the scalar ionization models considered in Section 4.1.2—namely, in the regime of no or anomalous GVD, with α1 = 0 when d = 2 and α1 = 1 when d = 3, and with the remaining parameters fixed to P2 = I, α2 = 0, α3 = 0, and f = 0—let x = (X⊥, z) ∈ R^d, X⊥ ∈ R^(d-1), Δ⊥ denote the transverse Laplacian, c_g = c_g e_z, and assume α4, α5 ≥ 0, c > 0, K > 0. For the fixed-frame system i(∂t + c_g∂z)u + ε(Δ⊥ + α1∂z^2)u + ε(|u|^2 - ρ)u = -iεc(α4|u|^(2K-2)u + α5ρu), ∂tρ = εα4|u|^(2K) + εα5ρ|u|^2, and for its moving-frame approximation i∂τv + (Δ⊥ + α1∂z^2)v + (|v|^2 - ρ̃)v = -ic(α4|v|^(2K-2)v + α5ρ̃v), -c_g∂zρ̃ = εα4|v|^(2K) + εα5ρ̃|v|^2, supplemented with the boundary condition lim_{z→+∞}(∇⊥)^l ρ̃(τ, X⊥, z) = 0 for every l ≥ 0, prove that the corresponding local solutions in the natural classes used in Section 4.1.2 extend globally forward in time in dimensions d = 2 and d = 3; equivalently, show that these ionization terms prevent finite-time breakdown for the two specific models (54) and (55).

For the scalar modified NLS Eq. (60), i P_2(ε∇) ∂_t v + Δ v + |v|^2 v = 0 on R^d in the no/anomalous GVD setting of §4.1 (so d = 2 when α_1 = 0 and d = 3 when α_1 = 1), with α_2 = α_3 = 0, f = 0, ε > 0, v complex-valued, and P_2(ε∇) a second-order-at-most, self-adjoint, positive operator, assume only partial off-axis dependence in the precise sense that there exist linearly independent vectors v_k ∈ R^d, k = 1, ..., j, with j < d (j = 1 if d = 2; j = 1 or 2 if d = 3), such that (P_2(ε∇)v,v) >= ||v||_{L^2}^2 + ε^2 Σ_{k=1}^j ||v_k · ∇v||_{L^2}^2. Can one establish a local and global well-posedness theory for Eq. (60) in this partial off-axis regime and determine, in light of the conserved energy and the modified mass (P_2(ε∇)v(t),v(t)) = (P_2(ε∇)v_0,v_0), whether adding only this partial off-axis dependence prevents finite-time breakdown of solutions? ([david-lannes.perso.math.cnrs.fr](https://david-lannes.perso.math.cnrs.fr/wp-content/uploads/2019/01/dumaslannesszeftel.pdf))

Let ε > 0 and α3 ∈ Rd, and consider the scalar self-steepening equation obtained from the paper’s general model (3) by setting P2 = I, α2 = 0, and f = 0:

i∂t v + (Δ⊥ + α1∂z²)v + (1 + iε α3·∇)(|v|²v) = 0,

for a complex-valued function v = v(t, x) with x = (X⊥, z) ∈ Rd, where α1 = 0 in the no-group-velocity-dispersion case and α1 = 1 in the anomalous-group-velocity-dispersion case; accordingly, d = 2 in the former case and d = 3 in the latter. For solutions of this Eq. (68) that blow up in finite time, what blow-up scenarios can occur? In particular, can one rigorously characterize whether self-steepening can produce blow-up profiles whose pulse profile develops the shock-like asymmetry or optical-shock behavior discussed by the authors?

Let d be 2 or 3, write x=(X_perp,z) in R^(d-1) x R, and let Delta_perp = partial_x^2 when d=2 and Delta_perp = partial_x^2 + partial_y^2 when d=3. For each complex-valued initial datum v_0 in H^1(R^d), consider the maximal H^1 solution v:[0,T_max) x R^d -> C of the normal-GVD (hyperbolic/non-elliptic) cubic NLS:

i partial_t v + (Delta_perp - partial_z^2)v + |v|^2 v = 0,
 v|_{t=0} = v_0.

Is it true that T_max = +infinity for every v_0 in H^1(R^d), i.e. that all H^1 solutions to equation (69) are global in dimensions 2 and 3? ([david-lannes.perso.math.cnrs.fr](https://david-lannes.perso.math.cnrs.fr/wp-content/uploads/2019/01/dumaslannesszeftel.pdf))

For the normal-GVD scalar specialization of (3), namely the hyperbolic cubic NLS
i \partial_t v + (\Delta_\perp - \partial_z^2)v + |v|^2 v = 0
on \mathbb{R}^d with d \in \{2,3\}, where z is the propagation direction, X_\perp are the transverse variables, \Delta_\perp = \partial_x^2 in d=2 and \Delta_\perp = \partial_x^2 + \partial_y^2 in d=3, and v(0)=v_0 \in H^1(\mathbb{R}^d), can one rigorously describe the pulse-splitting dynamics suggested by numerical simulations for equation (69)—namely, that a concentrating pulse reaches a certain threshold and then splits into two lower-amplitude pulses moving apart, possibly through repeated multiple splitting—in the energy-space setting?

For the scalar cubic NLS-type equation

i(1-ε²∂²_z)∂_t v + Δv + (1+iε∂_z)(|v|²v)=0,

with complex-valued unknown v=v(t,x), ε>0, z the propagation direction, Δ the full spatial Laplacian, and where 1-ε²∂²_z models partial off-axis variation of the group velocity while iε∂_z(|v|²v) models longitudinal self-steepening in the same z-direction, do solutions exhibit the self-steepening phenomenon in the paper’s sense (optical-shock-type/asymmetric pulse-profile formation), or does the partial off-axis variation prevent self-steepening from taking place? ([david-lannes.perso.math.cnrs.fr](https://david-lannes.perso.math.cnrs.fr/wp-content/uploads/2019/01/dumaslannesszeftel.pdf))

For the cubic vectorial NLS-type model considered in §4.4, namely

i P2(ε∇)∂t v + (Δ⊥ + α1∂z^2)v + i α2 v + (1/3)(1 + i ε α3·∇)[(v·v) conj(v) + 2|v|^2 v] = 0,

with v : [0,T) × R^d -> C^2, ε > 0, P2(ε∇) a second-order-at-most self-adjoint positive operator, α1 ∈ {0, ±1}, α2 >= 0, α3 ∈ R^d, and with the scalar equation recovered when the initial data lie in a one-dimensional real subspace of C^2 as in Remark 2, can one investigate the vectorial counterparts of the scalar open problems posed earlier in the paper in §§4.1–4.3 and 4.5—namely the corresponding questions about modified-nonlinearity dynamics, global existence versus finite-time breakdown, pulse splitting, self-steepening, mixed partial-off-axis/self-steepening effects, and rigorous justification of the underlying Maxwell equations on time scales [0, T/ε] with T >= T_foc?

Under the same wave-packet and polarization assumptions as in Section 3—namely, for Maxwell initial data U|_{t=0} = u_0(x)e^{ik·x/epsilon} + c.c. with u_0 in B = H^{t_0}(R^d)^n (t_0 > d/2) or in the Wiener algebra W(R^d)^n, satisfying u_0 = pi_1(k)u_0 + epsilon r and the standing hypotheses of the corresponding derivation—can one rigorously justify at least one of the NLS-type approximations derived from Maxwell's equations in Section 3, in the same sense as the paper's O(epsilon) error estimates for U_app(t,x) = u_app(t,x)e^{i(k·x-omega t)/epsilon} + c.c., on a diffractive time interval [0, T/epsilon] with T >= T_foc, where T_foc is the focusing time of the standard cubic focusing NLS (1)?

For a linear system Ax = b with A ∈ ℂ^{n×n}, a fixed fine-grid relaxation scheme M, a coarse-variable choice C ⊂ Ω (or, more generally, coarse averages defined by an averaging matrix X in the HCR setting), and a specified interpolation strategy P for the associated AMG two-grid solver, how should one define a compatible-relaxation process and an associated estimate based on its asymptotic convergence factor ρcr so that this estimate accurately predicts the convergence factor of the resulting two-grid method?

In bootstrap algebraic multigrid for a sparse linear system Ax=b, especially the general HPD setting emphasized in Section 5, after the coarse set C and local interpolatory sets C_i are chosen, what systematic strategy should couple the weighted least-squares definition of interpolation P in (3.1) from a test-vector set V with the Section 4 bootstrap procedure that computes and updates those TVs (via relaxation/MG on A_l x_l=0 and the multilevel generalized eigensolver, combining V^r and V^e), so that the resulting self-learning AMG interpolation attains an optimal balance of setup work and accuracy and is robust in practice? ([global-sci.com](https://global-sci.com/index.php/nmtma/article/download/14078/28063/29293))

For general sparse Hermitian positive definite linear systems Ax=b, how can one develop a bootstrap algebraic multigrid (BAMG) algorithm that (i) selects and efficiently updates the coarse-variable set C using compatible relaxation together with algebraic distance, with updates triggered by local CR slowness; (ii) constructs interpolation P by the local least-squares fit (3.1), i.e. for each i∈F=Ω\C chooses a row p_i over an interpolatory neighborhood C_i to fit a set of test vectors V={v^(1),...,v^(k)}, but with genuinely local weights ω_κ extending the current LSR/global-weight approach; (iii) computes and improves the test vectors by relaxation on the homogeneous problems A_l x_l=0 and by the multilevel generalized eigensolver with an effective balance between setup work and accuracy; and (iv) incorporates all available problem information, especially geometric information, so that in the HPD variational setting R=P^H and A_c=RAP the resulting BAMG hierarchy is easy to tune, robust, and fast enough for practical use on a carefully chosen and diverse set of test problems, including systems of PDEs? ([global-sci.com](https://global-sci.com/nmtma/article/download/14078/28063/29293))
