For a non-Hermitian matrix A ∈ C^{n×n}, in a Galerkin bootstrap algebraic multigrid hierarchy with restriction R: C^n → C^{n_c}, interpolation P: C^{n_c} → C^n, and coarse operator A_c = R A P, what is the correct characterization of the algebraically smooth error subspace that coarse-grid correction must represent—equivalently, the near-kernel components that the BAMG test vectors used to construct R and P should capture—when, for nonnormal A, eigenvectors or singular vectors associated with small singular values do not in general characterize that near kernel? More specifically, can this smooth-error space be identified from relaxation on the homogeneous system A x = 0 (for example, via Kaczmarz) through its relation to the field of values F(A) = {<A x, x>/<x, x> : x ∈ C^n, x ≠ 0}, in a way that also ensures that the Galerkin coarse operator does not acquire a zero eigenvalue and produce coarse-grid over-correction or divergence? ([global-sci.com](https://global-sci.com/index.php/nmtma/article/download/14078/28063/29293))

In the BAMG framework for sparse linear systems A x = b over C^n, where smooth-error test vectors are generated by bootstrapping on the homogeneous system A x = 0 and prolongation rows p_i are defined by the local least-squares interpolation problem (3.1) on interpolation neighborhoods C_i, can one continue to develop BAMG solvers for indefinite/non-elliptic problems such as Helmholtz and Schrödinger operators whose low eigenspaces contain many eigenfunctions that are locally different from one another, so that from sufficiently fine scales onward—when no single small-caliber prolongation operator suffices—one instead constructs several locally orthogonal prolongation operators and the corresponding multiple-Galerkin coarse spaces/operators with optimal computational cost; and, beyond the currently implemented one-dimensional Helmholtz and Schrödinger cases that require two prolongation operators, how far can this strategy be extended to these and other non-elliptic problems, and ultimately to fast solvers for general sparse matrix equations?

Let D(P) denote the number of distinct Euclidean distances determined by pairs of points from a finite set P \subset \mathbb{R}^2, and let D(n)=\min\{D(P): P\subset \mathbb{R}^2,\ |P|=n\}. Determine the exact asymptotic value of D(n) as n\to\infty.

Let P ⊂ R^2 be a finite set of n points, and let D(P) denote the number of distinct Euclidean distances determined by pairs of points of P. Write D(n):=min_{|P|=n} D(P). Since the exact asymptotic behavior of D(n) is unknown, call P near-optimal if D(P)=O(n/sqrt(log n)). Characterize the near-optimal point sets.

Let P ⊂ R^2 be a set of n points, and let D(P) denote the number of distinct Euclidean distances determined by pairs of points of P. Is there an absolute constant ε > 0 such that for every C > 0 there exist c = c(C) > 0 and n0 = n0(C) with the following property: whenever n >= n0 and D(P) <= C n/sqrt(log n), there is a line l ⊂ R^2 for which |P ∩ l| >= c n^ε?

Let P be a set of n points in R^2, and let D(P) denote the number of distinct Euclidean distances determined by pairs of points of P. Assume that P is near-optimal in the sense that D(P)=O(n/sqrt(log n)). Prove or disprove that, for a sufficiently small positive constant epsilon, no algebraic curve C subset R^2 defined by a polynomial in R[x,y] of total degree bounded by an absolute constant contains Omega(n^{1/2+epsilon}) points of P.

Let D(P) denote the number of distinct Euclidean distances determined by unordered pairs of distinct points of a finite set P ⊂ R^2. For n ∈ N, define Dcurve(n) := min D(P), where the minimum is taken over all n-point sets P contained in a real plane algebraic curve γ ⊂ R^2 of degree bounded by an absolute constant, under the restriction that γ contains no line and no circle. Determine the asymptotic growth of Dcurve(n) as n → ∞.

For each positive integer n, let D(P) denote the number of distinct Euclidean distances determined by pairs of distinct points of a finite set P subseteq R^2, and define D_no3(n) = min{D(P) : P subseteq R^2, |P| = n, and no three points of P are collinear}. Determine the exact value of D_no3(n) for every n.

For each integer n ≥ 2, let \widehat{D}_{\mathrm{conv}}(n) denote the largest integer with the following property: every set P ⊂ R^2 of n points in (strict) convex position contains a point p ∈ P such that the Euclidean distances {|pq| : q ∈ P, q ≠ p} take at least \widehat{D}_{\mathrm{conv}}(n) distinct values. Determine the exact value of \widehat{D}_{\mathrm{conv}}(n). ([adamsheffer.wordpress.com](https://adamsheffer.wordpress.com/wp-content/uploads/2013/06/distprobs3.pdf))

Let D(P) denote the number of distinct Euclidean distances determined by unordered pairs of distinct points of a finite set P subset R^2. Define D_gen(n) := min { D(P) : P subset R^2, |P| = n, no three points of P are collinear, and no circle contains four points of P }. Determine the asymptotic growth of D_gen(n) as n -> infinity.

Determine the asymptotic growth of D_para(n) as n tends to infinity, where D_para(n) is the minimum number of distinct Euclidean distances determined by an n-point set P in R^2 such that P is in general position (no three points of P are collinear and no four are cocircular) and no four points of P are vertices of a parallelogram.

For each fixed integer d >= 3, let D_d(n) be the minimum, over all n-point sets P subset of R^d, of the number of distinct Euclidean distances {||p-q|| : p, q in P, p != q}. Determine the asymptotic order of growth of D_d(n) as n -> infinity.

Let D(P) denote the number of distinct Euclidean distances determined by pairs of distinct points of a finite set P⊂R^3. Define D_3^o(n)=min{D(P): |P|=n and P is contained in a common 2-sphere in R^3}. Determine the asymptotic order of growth of D_3^o(n) as n→∞.

For each fixed integer d >= 4, determine the asymptotic order, as n goes to infinity, of D_d^o(n), where D_d^o(n) is the minimum possible number of distinct Euclidean distances in the set {|p-q| : p,q in P, p != q} over all n-point sets P contained in a hypersphere (that is, a (d-1)-sphere) in R^d.

For a fixed ambient dimension d and a fixed bound on algebraic degree, let D_curve^{(d)}(n) be the minimum, over all n-point sets P contained in a constant-degree algebraic curve gamma subset of R^d that contains no algebraic helix, of the number of distinct Euclidean distances determined by pairs of points of P. What is the asymptotic growth of D_curve^{(d)}(n) as n tends to infinity?

For each fixed integer d ≥ 3, let V ⊂ ℝ^d be an algebraic variety and let P ⊂ V be a finite set of n points. Define D(P) := |{|p-q| : p,q ∈ P, p ≠ q}|, the number of distinct Euclidean distances determined by pairs of points of P. Derive asymptotically non-trivial bounds for D(P) as n → ∞ for point sets constrained to such varieties, and determine which geometric restrictions on V (for example, whether exceptional cases analogous to planes or spheres must be excluded in the surface case) are needed to guarantee such bounds. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1406.1949))

For integers 1 <= m <= n, let D(P1,P2) be the number of distinct Euclidean distances ||p-q|| determined by pairs (p,q) in P1 x P2, where P1,P2 are finite subsets of R^2, and define D(m,n) := min{D(P1,P2) : P1,P2 subset R^2, |P1|=m, |P2|=n}. Determine the asymptotic order of growth of D(m,n) as a function of m and n.

For positive integers m and n, let D_lines(m,n) be the minimum possible cardinality of the set {||p-q|| : p in P1, q in P2}, where P1 and P2 are finite subsets of R^2 with |P1|=m and |P2|=n, P1 is contained in a line l1, P2 is contained in a line l2, and l1 and l2 are neither parallel nor orthogonal. Here only Euclidean distances between a point of P1 and a point of P2 are counted. Determine the asymptotic order of growth of D_lines(m,n) as a function of m and n.

For integers 1<=m<=n, let Dcurves(m, n) be the minimum possible cardinality of the bipartite Euclidean distance set {|p-q| : p in P1, q in P2}, taken over all finite sets P1 subset gamma1 and P2 subset gamma2 with |P1|=m and |P2|=n, where gamma1,gamma2 subset R^2 are constant-degree algebraic curves such that there is no line L1 subset gamma1 and line L2 subset gamma2 with L1 parallel to L2 or L1 orthogonal to L2, and no circles C1 subset gamma1 and C2 subset gamma2 that are concentric. Determine the asymptotic growth of Dcurves(m, n) as a function of m and n.

Let D_line(m,n) denote the minimum possible cardinality of {||p-q|| : p in P1, q in P2}, where P1,P2 are finite subsets of R^2 with |P1|=m and |P2|=n, P1 is contained in some line l in R^2, P2 is otherwise arbitrary, and only these cross-distances between P1 and P2 are counted. Assuming without loss of generality that m<=n, what is the asymptotic order of D_line(m,n) as a function of m and n?

Let P1, P2 be finite point sets in the real plane, with |P1| = m and |P2| = n, and let D(P1, P2) denote the number of distinct Euclidean distances between a point of P1 and a point of P2. Define Dline(m,n) to be the minimum of D(P1, P2) over all such pairs for which P1 is contained in a line l and P2 is otherwise unrestricted, with m <= n without loss of generality. Determine the asymptotic order of Dline(m,n), as a function of m and n, under the additional assumption that there exists an absolute constant C such that every line parallel or orthogonal to l contains at most C points of P2.

For Euclidean distance in R^2, let D(3,n)=min |{||p-q|| : p∈P1, q∈P2}|, where the minimum is over all point sets P1,P2⊂R^2 with |P1|=3, |P2|=n, and P1 non-collinear. Only distances between a point of P1 and a point of P2 are counted. Determine the asymptotic growth rate of D(3,n) as n→∞.

Let P,Q be finite subsets of R^d with d >= 3, and let D(P,Q) = |{||p-q|| : p in P, q in Q}|, where only distances between one point of P and one point of Q are counted. Derive non-trivial bounds for higher-dimensional bipartite distinct-distances problems in R^d; equivalently, obtain non-trivial upper and/or lower bounds for D(P,Q) in this bipartite setting. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1406.1949))

For a finite point set P⊂R^2, let subset(P) be the maximum cardinality of a subset P'⊂P such that for any two distinct unordered pairs {a,b},{c,d}⊂P' with a≠b and c≠d, one has |ab|≠|cd|; equivalently, every positive Euclidean distance determined by P' occurs at most once. Define subset(n):=min_{|P|=n} subset(P). Determine the asymptotic growth of subset(n) as n→∞.

For n = m^2, let L = [m] × [m] ⊂ Z^2 ⊂ R^2 be the m × m integer lattice. Define subset(L) to be the maximum cardinality of a subset A ⊂ L such that no two distinct unordered pairs of points of A determine the same positive Euclidean distance; equivalently, there do not exist a, b, c, d ∈ A with ||a - b||2 = ||c - d||2 > 0, even if the two pairs share a point. What is the asymptotic value of subset(L) as n → ∞?

Fix an integer d >= 3, and assume n is a perfect dth power. Let L_d = {1,2,...,n^(1/d)}^d ⊂ Z^d ⊂ R^d. Define subset(L_d) to be the maximum cardinality of a subset S ⊂ L_d such that no two distinct unordered pairs of points of S determine the same positive Euclidean distance; equivalently, every nonzero distance spanned by S occurs at most once. Find the asymptotic value of subset(L_d) as n -> infinity.

For each fixed integer d ≥ 3, let subsetd(n) denote the maximum integer t such that every set P of n distinct points in R^d contains a subset P' ⊂ P with |P'| = t and with no repeated positive Euclidean distances among its pairs of points; that is, whenever x,y,u,v ∈ P' satisfy ||x-y|| = ||u-v|| > 0, the unordered pairs {x,y} and {u,v} are the same. Determine the asymptotic order of subsetd(n) as n → ∞.

Let subset'(n) be the largest integer with the following property: every finite set P ⊂ R^2 with |P| = n contains a subset P' ⊂ P of size at least subset'(n) such that no three points of P' span an isosceles triangle. Determine the asymptotic growth of subset'(n) as n → ∞. ([adamsheffer.wordpress.com](https://adamsheffer.wordpress.com/wp-content/uploads/2013/06/distprobs3.pdf))

As n → ∞, determine the asymptotic growth of ϕ(n,3,2), where for positive integers n,k,l, ϕ(n,k,l) denotes the minimum number of distinct Euclidean distances determined by an n-point set P ⊂ ℝ^2 such that every k-point subset of P determines at least l distinct distances; equivalently here, determine the minimum number of distinct distances determined by an n-point planar set that does not span any equilateral triangles. ([adamsheffer.wordpress.com](https://adamsheffer.wordpress.com/wp-content/uploads/2013/06/distprobs3.pdf))

As n → ∞, determine the asymptotic growth of φ(n,3,3), where for a finite set P ⊂ R^2, D(P) denotes the number of distinct Euclidean distances {|pq| : p,q ∈ P, p ≠ q}, and φ(n,3,3) is the minimum of D(P) over all n-point sets P ⊂ R^2 such that every 3-point subset of P determines at least 3 distinct pairwise distances. ([adamsheffer.wordpress.com](https://adamsheffer.wordpress.com/wp-content/uploads/2013/06/distprobs3.pdf))

Let ϕ(n,k,l) denote the minimum number of distinct Euclidean distances determined by an n-point set P⊂R^2 such that every k-point subset of P determines at least l distinct distances. Determine, as n→∞, the asymptotic growth of ϕ(n,4,3). ([adamsheffer.wordpress.com](https://adamsheffer.wordpress.com/wp-content/uploads/2013/06/distprobs3.pdf))

Let φ(n,4,4) be the minimum possible cardinality of the distance set {|pq| : p,q∈P, p≠q} over all sets P⊂R^2 of n distinct points such that every 4-point subset Q⊂P determines at least 4 distinct pairwise Euclidean distances among its 6 interpoint distances. Determine the asymptotic order of growth of φ(n,4,4) as n→∞.

For each positive integer n, let φ(n,4,5) be the minimum possible value of D(P), where P ⊂ R^2 is an n-point set and D(P) denotes the number of distinct Euclidean distances determined by unordered pairs of points of P, under the condition that every 4-point subset Q ⊂ P determines at least 5 distinct distances among its 6 pairwise distances. Determine the asymptotic growth of φ(n,4,5) as n → ∞. In particular, is Erdős’s suggested quadratic behavior φ(n,4,5) = Θ(n^2) correct?

As n -> infinity, determine the asymptotic growth of phi(n,5,9), where phi(n,5,9) denotes the minimum possible number of distinct Euclidean distances determined by a set P of n distinct points in R^2 such that every 5-point subset Q of P determines at least 9 distinct values among the 10 pairwise distances {|pq| : p,q in Q, p != q}. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1406.1949))

For positive integers n, k, and l, let varphi(n,k,l) be the minimum number of distinct Euclidean distances determined by an n-point set P in R^2 such that every k-point subset of P determines at least l distinct distances among its binom(k,2) pairwise distances. Find stronger general bounds for varphi(n,k,l) as a function of n, k, and l.

Let P be a finite set of n points in R^2, and let D(P) := |{||p-q|| : p,q in P, p != q}| be the number of distinct Euclidean distances spanned by P. Assume that D(P) = O(n/sqrt(log n)) (equivalently, P is near-optimal in the paper's terminology). Prove or disprove that the additive energy E(P) := |{(a,b,c,d) in P^4 : a+b = c+d}|, where addition is vector addition in R^2, must be large.

Let A⊂R be a finite set, and define its difference set by A-A={a-a' : a,a'∈A}. View A×A as a finite subset of R^2, with distances understood in the Euclidean metric. What is the asymptotic growth, as a function of |A|, of the largest possible cardinality |A-A| among sets A for which the Cartesian product A×A spans few distinct distances in the plane?

For each positive integer n, let \hat D(n) denote the minimum value with the following property: every set P of n points in the Euclidean plane R^2 contains a point p in P that determines at least \hat D(n) distinct Euclidean distances to the other points of P. Determine the asymptotic growth of \hat D(n) as n \to \infty.

For a finite set P\subset\mathbb{R}^2 and a point p\in P, let \hat D_p(P):=|\{\,|pq|:q\in P\setminus\{p\}\,\}| be the number of distinct Euclidean distances from p to the other points of P. Define \hat D_\Sigma(P):=\sum_{p\in P}\hat D_p(P), and let \hat D_\Sigma(n):=\min_{|P|=n}\hat D_\Sigma(P), where the minimum is over all n-point sets P\subset\mathbb{R}^2. Determine the asymptotic order of \hat D_\Sigma(n) as n\to\infty; in particular, is the integer-lattice upper bound \hat D_\Sigma(n)=O(n^2/\sqrt{\log n}) tight, i.e. does one have \hat D_\Sigma(n)=\Theta(n^2/\sqrt{\log n})?

Let L(m,n) be the minimum possible value of |{dist(p,ℓ) : p ∈ P, ℓ ∈ ℒ}|, where P ⊂ ℝ^2 is a set of m points, ℒ is a set of n lines in ℝ^2, and dist(p,ℓ) is the usual Euclidean distance from the point p to the line ℓ. Determine the asymptotic order of L(m,n) as a function of the positive integers m and n.

Let P be a finite subset of R^2, and define v(P):=|{p-q : p,q in P, p!=q}|, the number of distinct vectors determined by ordered pairs of distinct points of P. Define v_gen(n):=min{v(P) : P subset R^2, |P|=n, and P has no three collinear points and no four cocircular points}. Determine the asymptotic order of growth of v_gen(n) as n -> infinity.

Let X be a real separated locally convex space, and let C, D ⊂ X be nonempty convex sets. For a convex set E ⊂ X, define its quasi-relative interior by qri E := {x ∈ E : cl(cone(E - x)) is a linear subspace of X}. Since Proposition 1.2 shows that qri C + qri D ⊆ qri(C + D), is the conjectured equality qri(C + D) = qri C + qri D valid for all such C and D, or can one find convex sets C and D for which the inclusion is strict, i.e. qri C + qri D ⊊ qri(C + D)?

Let X be a real separated locally convex space, and let A,B be convex subsets of X. For a convex set E subset X, define its quasi interior by qi(E) := {x in E : cl(cone(E-x)) = X}, where cone(E-x) := {t(y-x) : t >= 0, y in E} and cl denotes closure in the given topology of X. Assume qi(B) is nonempty. Must one always have the Minkowski-sum identity A + qi(B) = qi(A+B), where A+B := {a+b : a in A, b in B}?

Let X be a real separated locally convex space, and let C,D ⊆ X be nonempty convex sets. For any convex set E ⊆ X, define its quasi-relative interior by qri(E) := {x ∈ E : cone(E − x) is a linear subspace of X}. Assume that C ∩ qri(D) ≠ ∅ and D ∩ qri(C) ≠ ∅. Must one have qri(C ∩ D) ⊆ qri(C) ∩ qri(D)?

Let [0,r] = {0,1,...,r} be viewed as a subset of Z. A set A subseteq [0,r] is called more-sums-than-differences (MSTD) if |A+A| > |A-A|, where A+A = {a+a' : a,a' in A} and A-A = {a-a' : a,a' in A}. Can one give an explicit, concrete, nonrandom construction of families F_r subseteq P([0,r]) consisting entirely of MSTD sets whose density |F_r|/2^(r+1) improves on the previously obtained order C/r^4, and in particular does there exist such an explicit family for which there is a constant c > 0 with |F_r| >= c*2^(r+1) for all sufficiently large r?

Let B be a finite subset of Z^2, with B + B = {b + b' : b, b' ∈ B} and B - B = {b - b' : b, b' ∈ B}. Call B an MSTD set if |B + B| > |B - B|. The paper notes that the smallest MSTD set in Z is A = {0, 2, 3, 4, 7, 10, 12, 14}, and that A × {0, 1} (indeed A × T for any 2-point set T ⊂ Z) is then an MSTD set of size 16 in Z^2. Can one construct a finite MSTD set in Z^2 directly, without first going through an MSTD set in Z via this Cartesian-product lift?

For each fixed integer k ≥ 1, do there exist constants C_k,D_k > 0 such that, for all sufficiently large n, whenever A ⊆ Z_n is a basis and its order ρ_n(A) := min{h ≥ 1 : hA = Z_n}, where hA = {a_1 + ··· + a_h : a_i ∈ A}, satisfies ρ_n(A) > n/(k+1) + C_k, there is an integer ℓ with 1 ≤ ℓ ≤ k for which |ρ_n(A) - n/ℓ| < D_k?

Let G = {g_i : i >= 0} be the greedy set of nonnegative integers defined by g_0 = 0 and, for each i >= 1, letting g_i be the least positive integer not already in {g_0, ..., g_{i-1}} such that {g_0, ..., g_i} contains no nontrivial solution to 5w + 2x = 5y + 2z. Let a_0 = 0, and for each i >= 1 define a_i = floor((5 + 7 sum_{j=0}^{i-1} a_j)/2). Let A be the set of all finite sums of distinct terms a_i. Is the conjecture in 2009.1.5 true that G = {5x + y : x in A and 0 <= y <= 4}?

Let A={a_0<a_1<a_2<...}⊆N_0 be a basis of order 2 for N_0, meaning that every m∈N_0 can be written as m=a_i+a_j for some i,j≥0 (allowing i=j). For a fixed N≥1, must there exist a set A'={a_0<a_1<...<a_{N-1}<b_N<b_{N+1}<...}⊆N_0 such that A' is again a basis of order 2 for N_0 and is minimal, in the sense that for every x∈A', the set A'\{x} is not a basis of order 2 for N_0?

In the formal power series ring Z[[x]], does there exist a choice of signs epsilon_{m,k} in {-1,1} for every m >= 1 and k >= 1 such that, after replacing the right-hand side of prod_{m>=1} 1/(1-x^m) = prod_{m>=1}(1 + x^m + x^{2m} + ...) by prod_{m>=1}(1 + epsilon_{m,1} x^m + epsilon_{m,2} x^{2m} + ...), every coefficient of the resulting expanded series belongs to {-1,0,1}? ([theoryofnumbers.com](https://www.theoryofnumbers.com/cant/CANTProblemSessions.pdf))

Can one prove, without any use of the prime number theorem, that ζ(2)=π^2/6 has finite irrationality measure; that is, can one show that there exists a finite real number μ such that the inequality |ζ(2)-p/q|<q^{-μ} has only finitely many solutions in coprime integers p and q with q>=1? ([web.williams.edu](https://web.williams.edu/Mathematics/sjmiller/public_html/math/papers/CANTProblemSessions.pdf))

Give an elementary proof that infinitely many prime numbers are not members of any twin-prime pair; that is, prove that there exist infinitely many primes p such that both p-2 and p+2 fail to be prime. The proof should be elementary in the sense intended in the paper, avoiding non-elementary input such as Dirichlet's theorem on primes in arithmetic progressions.

Let C = {f(n) : n in N}, where f is a polynomial of degree at least 2, and fix an integer h >= 2. For N >= 1, let C(N) = C ∩ [N], with [N] = {0,1,...,N} (equivalently, one may start at 1), and for A subset [N] write hA = {a_1 + ... + a_h : a_1,...,a_h in A}. Call A an h-basis of C(N) if hA ⊃ C(N), and define D_h(C,N) = min{|A| : A subset [N], hA ⊃ C(N)}. If the limit exists, set Gamma_h(C) = lim_{N to infinity} |C(N)| / D_h(C,N)^h. Must Gamma_h(C) = 0 for every polynomial-value sequence C of degree at least 2?

Let G be a finite abelian group of order n, and let S = x_1 ··· x_{n+r} be a sequence over G with r ≥ 1. Define Σ_n(S) = {x_{i_1} + ··· + x_{i_n} : 1 ≤ i_1 < ··· < i_n ≤ n + r}, and let supp(S) be the set of distinct terms occurring in S. Must every such S satisfy the following: either 0 ∈ Σ_n(S), or else |Σ_n(S)| ≥ r + |supp(S)| − 1? ([diambri.org](https://www.diambri.org/N-sum-revised-CPC-1872-f.pdf))

For each positive integer n, let [n]={1,2,...,n}, and let μ(n) be the minimum cardinality of a subset A⊆[n] such that A contains no three distinct elements x,y,z with x+z=2y and A is maximal with respect to inclusion among subsets of [n] with that property. Is it true that μ(4^t)=2^t for every positive integer t, and more generally that μ(n)≥√n for every positive integer n?

Let K \subseteq \mathbb{R}^2 be compact, and assume that K meets every congruence class modulo \mathbb{Z}^2; equivalently, for every x \in \mathbb{R}^2 there exists y \in K with x-y \in \mathbb{Z}^2. Define A := (K-K) \cap \mathbb{Z}^2. Since the nearby theorem states that such an A is a finite subset generating the additive group \mathbb{Z}^2, determine which finite generating sets A \subseteq \mathbb{Z}^2 can arise in this way. More specifically, can one choose K so that A \subseteq \{(x,y) \in \mathbb{Z}^2 : xy=0\}? In particular, can one realize exactly the axis-cross set A = {(0,0),(\pm1,0),(0,\pm1)}?

Determine all infinite sequences of odd integers (d_i)_{i>=0} such that every integer n in Z has a unique finitely supported expansion n = sum_{i>=0} epsilon_i d_i 2^i with epsilon_i in {0,1}; equivalently, determine all odd sequences (d_i)_{i>=0} for which Z = ⊕_{i>=0} {0, d_i 2^i}.

Let A ⊆ N_0 := {0,1,2,...} with 0 ∈ A, and for each integer h ≥ 1 write hA := A + ··· + A (h summands). Assume that, for every h ≥ 1, the asymptotic density d_L(hA) exists and satisfies d_L(hA) = lim_{n→∞} |hA ∩ [1,n]|/n = 0. Since 0 ∈ A, the iterated sumsets form a nested chain A ⊆ 2A ⊆ 3A ⊆ ··· . Must some nontrivial additive structure nevertheless appear in the family {hA}_{h≥1}? Equivalently, is there any structural phenomenon that must occur for this increasing sequence of iterated sumsets despite the fact that every hA has asymptotic density 0? ([theoryofnumbers.com](https://www.theoryofnumbers.com/cant/CANTProblemSessions.pdf))

Fix any archimedean matrix norm ||.|| on M_2(R), and let B_N := {gamma in SL_2(Z) : ||gamma|| <= N}. Define the additive energy of B_N by E(B_N) := # {(gamma_1,gamma_2,gamma_3,gamma_4) in B_N^4 : gamma_1 + gamma_2 = gamma_3 + gamma_4}. Since |B_N| is of order N^2, one has the trivial lower bound E(B_N) >> N^4, while the paper records an easy upper bound E(B_N) << N^5. Obtain a genuinely nontrivial upper bound for E(B_N), ideally proving that for every epsilon > 0, E(B_N) = O_epsilon(N^(4+epsilon)) as N -> infinity.

Does every finite group G admit a generating set A such that, if l_A(g) denotes the word length of g with respect to A and S_A(r) := {g in G : l_A(g) = r}, then the sphere-size sequence (|S_A(1)|, |S_A(2)|, |S_A(3)|, ...) is unimodal; that is, there exists m >= 1 for which |S_A(1)| <= ... <= |S_A(m)| >= |S_A(m+1)| >= ... , with |S_A(r)| = 0 for all sufficiently large r?

Which functions f: N_0 -> N_0 occur eventually as ordered two-sum representation functions of sets of nonnegative integers? Equivalently, determine exactly which sequences f(n) of nonnegative integers have the property that there exists a set A ⊆ N_0 and an integer n0 such that for every n >= n0, f(n) = r_A(n), where r_A(n) := #{(a1,a2) in A x A : a1 + a2 = n}.

Ruzsa conjectured the following. Let N be the natural numbers. For X ⊂ N, define X(x) = #{n ∈ X : 1 ≤ n ≤ x} and σ(X) = inf_{x ≥ 1} X(x)/x. For A,B ⊂ N, let A + B = {a + b : a ∈ A, b ∈ B}. Call B an essential component if σ(A + B) > σ(A) for every A ⊂ N with 0 < σ(A) < 1. Call B an extraordinary component if lim inf_{σ(A)→0} σ(A + B)/σ(A) = ∞, where the liminf is over subsets A ⊂ N with σ(A) > 0 and σ(A) tending to 0. Must every essential component be an extraordinary component?

Besides the classical Calkin-Wilf pair L_0(z)=z/(z+1) and R_0(z)=z+1 (equivalently, a/b maps to a/(a+b) and (a+b)/b), do there exist maps L,R from the set Q_{>0} of positive rational numbers to itself such that the infinite rooted binary tree obtained from the root 1 by giving each vertex z the two children L(z) and R(z) has vertex set exactly Q_{>0}, with each positive rational occurring once and only once? If so, can one determine all such nontrivial pairs L,R, or at least exhibit any example other than the classical Calkin-Wilf pair?

For an integer m >= 1, let d0 := ceil(log_3 m), equivalently the least integer d with 3^d >= m. For each integer n >= d0, let f(n,m) be the maximum number of affine lines {x, x+d, x+2d} with d != 0 that are completely contained in a subset S ⊂ F_3^n with |S| = m. Is it true that f(n,m) = f(d0,m) for every n >= d0?

Fix a recurrence-defined integer sequence (H_n) with recurrence coefficients c_1, ..., c_L and a corresponding notion of legal decomposition into H_i-summands. Extend the Zeckendorf framework to settings in which existence and uniqueness may fail—so that some positive integers have multiple legal decompositions and some have none—by determining what replaces the usual localized Gaussian summand statistics, including the variant that records the multiplicity of each summand rather than only the total number of summands; and, for such recurrence-based decompositions, derive explicit formulas in terms of c_1, ..., c_L for the limiting distribution of gaps between consecutive summand indices and for the appropriately normalized distribution of the largest gap for integers m in [H_n, H_{n+1}) as n -> infinity, treating Alpert's signed Fibonacci decomposition as a required model case and asking whether its signed gap laws extend to other recurrences.

Let G_n = {(x,y) in Z^2 : xy ≡ 1 (mod n), 1 <= x,y <= n-1}, let C_n = conv(G_n) ⊂ R^2, and let v(n) be the number of vertices of C_n. Since Proposition 1.2 gives v(n) >= 2(τ(n-1)-1), define D(n) = v(n) - 2(τ(n-1)-1). Is it true that v(n) -> infinity as n -> infinity, and can the explicit lower bound in Theorem 1.3 for the lower asymptotic density of the equality set {n >= 2 : D(n)=0} = {n >= 2 : v(n)=2(τ(n-1)-1)} be improved?

Let S be a numerical semigroup, i.e. a cofinite subset S ⊆ N containing 0 and closed under addition, of genus g = |N \ S|. Let ewt(S) denote the number of pairs (a,b) such that 0 < a < b, a is a generator of S (equivalently, a positive element of S not expressible as a sum of two positive elements of S), and b is a gap of S. Is it true that every genus-g numerical semigroup satisfies ewt(S) <= floor((g+1)^2/8)?

Does there exist a finite set A of positive integers such that A is simultaneously more-sums-than-differences and more-products-than-ratios, i.e. such that |A+A| > |A-A| and |A·A| > |A/A|, where A+A = {a+a' : a,a' in A}, A-A = {a-a' : a,a' in A}, A·A = {aa' : a,a' in A}, and A/A = {a/a' : a,a' in A}? If such sets exist, can one construct an explicit infinite family of them, and what is their asymptotic density among subsets of {0,1,...,n-1} in the uniform model?

Let 1 < p < ∞, let L_p(Ω) be a complex L_p-space, and let A be an R-sectorial operator on L_p(Ω), where sectorial operators are understood in the paper’s convention as closed, densely defined operators with dense range. Must the sectorial angle and the R-sectorial angle coincide, i.e. is ω(A) = ω_R(A)? More specifically, if -A generates a bounded analytic C_0-semigroup (T(z)) on L_p(Ω), does this angle equality still hold in each of the following three stronger situations: (i) T(t) is positive for every t ≥ 0; (ii) T(t) is contractive on L_p(Ω) for every t ≥ 0; (iii) T(t) is both positive and contractive for every t ≥ 0?

Let X be a complex UMD-Banach lattice, and let -A generate a bounded analytic C_0-semigroup (T(z)) on X such that T(t) is positive and contractive for every t≥0. Must A satisfy ω_H^∞(A)<π/2; equivalently, must A admit a bounded H^∞(Σ_σ)-functional calculus for some σ<π/2?

Let 1<p<∞, let X=L^p(Ω) over the complex scalars, and let A be a closed densely defined operator with dense range on X such that A is sectorial of angle ω(A)<π/2 and -A generates a contractive C_0-semigroup (e^{-tA})_{t≥0} on X, i.e. ||e^{-tA}||≤1 for all t≥0. Must A then admit a bounded H^∞(Σ_σ)-functional calculus for some angle σ<π/2?
Let X be a complex UMD-Banach lattice, and let -A generate a positive contractive analytic C_0-semigroup on X. Must this semigroup be R-analytic?
Let 1<p<infinity, let X=L^p(Omega), and let -A be the generator of a contractive C_0-semigroup on X. Must A admit a bounded H^infty-calculus with critical angle omega_{H^infty}(A) <= pi/2?

Fix p ∈ (1,∞) \ {2}. Let (T(t))_{t≥0} be a bounded C_0-semigroup on a complex L^p-space L^p(Ω). Characterize precisely those semigroups for which there exist another L^p-space L^p(Ω'), bounded linear maps J: L^p(Ω) → L^p(Ω') and Q: L^p(Ω') → L^p(Ω), and a bounded C_0-group (U(t))_{t∈ℝ} on L^p(Ω') such that T(t) = Q U(t) J for every t ≥ 0; equivalently, characterize the bounded C_0-semigroups on L^p(Ω) that admit a loose dilation in the class of all L^p-spaces with the same exponent p.

Let X be a UMD-Banach lattice and let (T(t))_{t≥0} be a positive, contractive C_0-semigroup on X. Must there exist a UMD-Banach lattice Y such that either: (i) there are contractive linear maps J:X→Y and Q:Y→X and a C_0-group (U(t))_{t∈R} of isometries on Y with T(t)=QU(t)J for all t≥0 (strict dilation), or (ii) there are bounded linear maps J:X→Y and Q:Y→X and a bounded C_0-group (U(t))_{t∈R} on Y with T(t)=QU(t)J for all t≥0 (loose dilation)?

Let X be a complex separable Banach space. Assume that X has the maximal regularity property (MRP), i.e. every negative generator of an analytic C0-semigroup on X has maximal regularity. Must X be isomorphic to a Hilbert space?

For each fixed integer d >= 1, let (z_n)_{n>=0} be an arbitrary sequence in [0,1)^d, and for N >= 1 define its discrepancy by D_N := sup_B |A_N(B)/N - lambda(B)|, where the supremum runs over all axis-parallel subintervals B subseteq [0,1)^d, A_N(B) := # {0 <= n < N : z_n in B}, and lambda is d-dimensional Lebesgue measure. Is it true that there exists a constant c_d > 0, depending only on d, such that for every sequence (z_n)_{n>=0} one has D_N >= c_d (log N)^d / N for infinitely many positive integers N?

Does there exist an absolute constant C such that for every positive integer N there exists an integer a with 1 <= a < N and gcd(a,N)=1 for which the reduced rational number a/N has a finite simple continued fraction expansion a/N = [a_1, ..., a_k] whose partial quotients all satisfy a_i < C?

Is Moser's conjecture true: does there exist an absolute constant B > 0 such that for every integer N >= 1 there exists an integer a with 1 <= a < N and gcd(a,N) = 1 for which, writing a/N in finite simple continued-fraction form as a/N = [0; a1, ..., ar], one has sum_{j=1}^r a_j < B log N?

Fix an integer d >= 2 and a real number chi with 0 < chi < 1. Does there exist a constant C_{d,chi} > 0 such that for every positive integer N, at least chi N^d vectors a = (a_1,...,a_d) in {0,1,...,N-1}^d have the property that the N-point lattice set P_N(a) = {({n a_1 / N},...,{n a_d / N}) : n = 0,1,...,N-1} subset [0,1)^d satisfies D(P_N(a)) >= C_{d,chi} (log N)^(d-1) log log N / N, where D(P_N(a)) denotes the usual discrepancy of this finite point set with respect to axis-parallel half-open boxes in [0,1)^d?

For fixed integers d >= 1 and prime q, does there exist a constant B(d,q) > 0 such that for every delta with 0 < delta < 1, for infinitely many integers m >= 1, at least (1-delta)#M_d(m) of the d-tuples C = (C_1,...,C_d) in M_d(m), where M_d(m) is the set of all d-tuples of m x m matrices over Z_q, provide digital nets over Z_q with N = q^m points whose discrepancy satisfies D_N(C) >= delta B(d,q) (log N)^(d-1) log log N / N?

Fix s >= 1 and a prime q. For each m >= 1, let A_m be the set of all tuples (f,g_1,...,g_s) with f,g_i in F_q[x], deg(f)=m, and deg(g_i)<m for 1 <= i <= s, and let P(f,g_1,...,g_s) subset [0,1)^s be the q^m-point set obtained in Section 2 from the rational functions g_i/f, namely from the points (phi_m(n(x)g_1(x)/f(x)),...,phi_m(n(x)g_s(x)/f(x))) as n runs from 0 to q^m-1, where n(x) is the polynomial attached to the q-adic digits of n and phi_m truncates the Laurent expansion to its first m base-q digits. Does there exist a constant c_{q,s}>0 such that, for every sufficiently large m, at least c_{q,s}|A_m| admissible tuples (f,g_1,...,g_s) yield a net P(f,g_1,...,g_s) whose discrepancy satisfies D_{q^m}(P(f,g_1,...,g_s)) >= c_{q,s}(log(q^m))^(s-1) log log(q^m) / q^m? In other words, can one prove for this rational-function class the same kind of average-type lower bound that Open Problem 2 asks for digital nets over F_q?

For a fixed dimension d >= 1 and each positive integer N, can one find, for a suitable real-valued function phi on integer d-tuples, an asymptotic representation with a "small" error term R_chi(h) for N(h; a_1, ..., a_d) := # { (n_1, ..., n_d) in Z^d : -h <= n_i <= h for i = 1, ..., d and {n_1 a_1/N + n_2 a_2/N + ... + n_d a_d/N} < phi(n_1, ..., n_d) }, namely N(h; a_1, ..., a_d) = sum_{-h <= n_1, ..., n_d < h} phi(n_1, ..., n_d) + R_chi(h), in such a way that for every chi < 1 and every positive integer h this formula holds for at least chi N^d choices of (a_1, ..., a_d) with 0 <= a_i < N? Here {x} denotes fractional part. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1407.2380))

Let d_1, ..., d_l be positive integers with d_1 + ... + d_l = d, and let q_1, ..., q_l be pairwise coprime bases. For a d-dimensional Halton-Niederreiter sequence z_n = (x_n^(1), ..., x_n^(l)) in [0,1)^d, where for each i the component x_n^(i) is a d_i-dimensional digital sequence in base q_i in the sense used in the paper, determine the metrical order of the discrepancy D_N(z_0, ..., z_{N-1}) of almost all such sequences: namely, determine as sharply as possible a smallest upper-order function g(N) and a largest lower-order function f(N) such that, for almost every choice of the component digital sequences, one has D_N = O(g(N)) and D_N = Omega(f(N)) (with the upper bound intended uniformly in N and the lower bound in the usual metrical-discrepancy sense along infinitely many N).

Fix positive integers d_1,\ldots,d_l with d_1+\cdots+d_l=d and pairwise coprime bases q_1,\ldots,q_l. Consider the class of d-dimensional Halton-Niederreiter sequences obtained by juxtaposing, for each i=1,\ldots,l, a d_i-dimensional digital sequence in base q_i; restrict to the finite-row subclass, meaning that every row of every generating matrix of every component sequence has only finitely many nonzero entries. After specifying a suitable probability measure on this class, determine as sharply as possible the metrical order of the discrepancy D_N of the first N points of almost all such finite-row Halton-Niederreiter sequences, i.e. determine the smallest possible upper-order function and the largest possible lower-order function for D_N for almost every sequence with respect to that measure.

Let x_n be the van der Corput sequence in base 2, and define z_n = (x_n, {n√2}) ∈ [0,1)^2 for n ≥ 0, where {·} denotes fractional part. Determine the asymptotic order of the ordinary discrepancy D_N of the first N points z_0, ..., z_{N-1} of this concrete Halton-Kronecker sequence as N → ∞; in particular, decide whether it is an almost low-discrepancy sequence, i.e. whether D_N = O((log N)^(2+ε)/N) for every ε > 0.

For the concrete Halton–Kronecker sequence ((x_n,{n√2}))_{n≥0}, where x_n is the van der Corput sequence in base 2, let A_K denote, for each positive integer K, the largest non-initial partial quotient a_j (j ≥ 1) in the regular continued fraction expansion of 2^K√2, and define B_L := max_{1≤K≤L} A_K. What are the sharp upper and lower bounds for the growth of B_L as L → ∞?

For distinct prime bases b_1, ..., b_s and for every prime N different from each b_i, let H_N = { (n/N, x_n) : 0 <= n < N } be the (s+1)-dimensional Hammersley point set in [0,1)^(s+1), where x_0, ..., x_{N-1} are the first N points of the s-dimensional Halton sequence in bases b_1, ..., b_s. Is it possible, for every such N, to choose a generating vector g = (g_1, ..., g_t) in {1, ..., N-1}^t so that the finite hybrid point set P_N = { (n/N, x_n, {n g_1/N}, ..., {n g_t/N}) : 0 <= n < N } in [0,1)^(s+t+1), where {·} denotes fractional part, has discrepancy improved by almost one factor of log N compared with Kritzer's Theorem 3.2 bound O((log N)^(s+t+1)/N)?

Let x_n = sum_{j>=0} a_j(n) 2^{-(j+1)} be the van der Corput sequence in base 2, where n = sum_{j>=0} a_j(n) 2^j with a_j(n) in {0,1}. Define the 2-dimensional Halton-Kronecker sequence z_n = (x_n, {n sqrt(2)}) in [0,1)^2 for n >= 0, where {t} denotes the fractional part of t. If D_N(z) denotes the discrepancy of the first N points z_0,...,z_{N-1}, i.e. D_N(z) = sup_B |(1/N) # {0 <= n < N : z_n in B} - lambda(B)| with the supremum over all axis-parallel boxes B ⊆ [0,1)^2, can one prove that there exists a constant c > 0 such that D_N(z) >= c (log N)^2 / N for infinitely many positive integers N?

Let phi_2(n) denote the base-2 van der Corput sequence, and for alpha in R define z_n = (phi_2(n), {n alpha}) in [0,1)^2 for n >= 0. If D_N(z_n) denotes the ordinary discrepancy of the first N points z_0, ..., z_{N-1}, show that for Lebesgue-almost every alpha there exists a constant C(alpha) > 0 such that D_N(z_n) >= C(alpha) (log N)^2 / N for infinitely many positive integers N.

Let q be a prime, and let x_n = S(C_1, ..., C_s) be a fixed s-dimensional digital sequence over Z_q generated by matrices C_1, ..., C_s in Z_q^{N x N}, each of whose rows has only finitely many nonzero entries. For alpha in R^t, let ({n alpha})_{n>=0} be the t-dimensional Kronecker sequence obtained by taking componentwise fractional parts, and form the Niederreiter-Kronecker hybrid sequence z_n = (x_n, {n alpha}) in [0,1)^{s+t}. Determine an upper metrical bound, of essentially optimal order in N, for the discrepancy D_N of the first N points z_0, ..., z_{N-1} that holds for Lebesgue-almost every alpha.

Let (n_k)_{k≥0} be the increasing sequence of positive integers such that s_2(n_k) ≡ 0 mod 2, where s_2(n) denotes the sum of the base-2 digits of n. For Lebesgue-almost every alpha in [0,1), determine the exact asymptotic order, as N → ∞, of the discrepancy D_N of the one-dimensional sequence x_k = {n_k alpha}, namely D_N((x_k)_{k≥0}) = sup_{0≤a<b≤1} |#{0≤k<N : x_k in [a,b)} - N(b-a)|.

In J.P. Morgan’s original CreditMetrics setting for a bank portfolio of d credits, where one estimates the percentile of the portfolio’s value one year in the future and each credit corresponds to one simulation coordinate, can one, for a fixed sample size N, carry out in detail the following program: first determine an integer s ≤ d for which an s-dimensional low-discrepancy sample of N points is preferable to pseudo-random sampling in s dimensions; next identify the s credits that contribute most to the total portfolio risk (taking into account, as indicated in the paper, face amount, rating class, and correlation properties within the portfolio); and then run the CreditMetrics simulation with a hybrid sampler that uses the s low-discrepancy coordinates for those selected credits and pseudo-random coordinates for the remaining d − s credits, followed by a performance analysis against pure Monte Carlo and pure quasi-Monte Carlo methods? ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1407.2380))

Decide whether the sequence of fractional parts ({(3/2)^n})_{n >= 0}, equivalently (((3/2)^n mod 1))_{n >= 0}, is uniformly distributed in [0,1); that is, whether for every interval [a,b) ⊂ [0,1), one has lim_{N -> infinity} (1/N) * #{0 <= n < N : {(3/2)^n} in [a,b)} = b-a.

Does there exist a pair (alpha, beta) in R^2 and a constant C > 0 such that, for the 2-dimensional Kronecker sequence x_n = ({n alpha}, {n beta}) in [0,1)^2 for n >= 0, where {t} denotes the fractional part of t, the discrepancy of its first N points,
D_N(x_0,...,x_{N-1}) := sup_B | (1/N) # {0 <= n < N : x_n in B} - lambda(B) |,
with the supremum taken over all axis-parallel subintervals B of [0,1)^2, satisfies
D_N(x_0,...,x_{N-1}) <= C (log N)^2 / N
for every N >= 2?

For an arbitrary infinite sequence omega = (x_n)_{n>=1} in [0,1), define the one-dimensional star discrepancy of its first N points by D_N^*(omega) := sup_{0<=t<=1} |(1/N) #{1<=n<=N : x_n < t} - t|. Let c^* := sup{ c > 0 : for every such sequence omega, one has N D_N^*(omega) >= c log N for infinitely many N }, where log denotes the natural logarithm. Can one improve the best known lower and upper bounds for c^*? ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1407.2380))

Let (x_n)_{n>=0} be a 2-dimensional digital sequence in base 2 in the sense of Niederreiter: there exist generating matrices C_1, C_2 over F_2 such that, writing n = n_0 + n_1 2 + ... and y_{n,j} = C_j (n_0, n_1, ...)^T over F_2, one has x_n^(j) = sum_{r>=1} y_{n,j,r} 2^{-r}, so x_n = (x_n^(1), x_n^(2)) belongs to [0,1)^2. If D_N denotes the discrepancy of the first N points x_0, ..., x_{N-1}, namely the supremum over all axis-parallel subintervals J of [0,1)^2 of |A_N(J)/N - lambda(J)|, does there exist a constant c > 0 such that every such sequence satisfies D_N >= c (log N)^2 / N for infinitely many positive integers N? If the full statement is out of reach, can one at least prove the same lower bound for a paper-mentioned low-discrepancy subclass such as finite-row digital sequences?

Fix coprime integers b1, b2 >= 2, and let H2 = (x_n)_{n>=0} be the two-dimensional Halton sequence x_n = (phi_{b1}(n), phi_{b2}(n)), where if n = sum_{j>=0} n_j b^j then phi_b(n) = sum_{j>=0} n_j b^{-j-1}. For the discrepancy D_N(H2) of the first N points x_0, ..., x_{N-1}, defined by D_N(H2) = sup_B |A_N(B)/N - lambda(B)| with A_N(B) = #{0 <= n < N : x_n in B} and B ranging over all axis-parallel subintervals of [0,1)^2, can one prove a lower bound sharper than the currently known general lower bound for arbitrary sequences in [0,1)^2? In particular, does there exist a constant c = c(b1,b2) > 0 such that D_N(H2) >= c (log N)^2 / N for infinitely many N, thereby showing that the discrepancy of the two-dimensional Halton sequence has the expected order (log N)^2 / N; or is its true order smaller?

How do the temperature and density vary across the prominence-corona transition region (PCTR), and what is the spatial thickness and fine-scale morphological structure of this interface between the cool (~10^4 K), dense prominence plasma and the hot (~10^6 K), tenuous solar corona within the framework of existing non-LTE prominence modeling?

Consider the standard two-queue cyclic polling system Q1,Q2,Q1,... of Section 2: customers arrive to Qi according to independent Poisson processes with rates λi; service times at Qi are i.i.d. copies of Bi with Laplace-Stieltjes transform βi(·); the switch-over time from Qi to Qi+1 is Si with Laplace-Stieltjes transform σi(·); all arrival, service, and switch-over processes are mutually independent; and the parameters are such that the stationary joint queue-length distributions at polling epochs exist. Suppose Q1 uses gated service (only customers present at the start of the visit are served) and Q2 uses 1-limited service (at most one customer is served per visit, if any is present). For i = 1,2, let Fi(z1,z2) denote the PGF of the joint steady-state queue-length vector at the start of a visit to Qi. Determine F1(z1,z2) and F2(z1,z2), equivalently the joint queue-length PGF at polling instants, for this two-queue G/1-L polling system. ([link.springer.com](https://link.springer.com/content/pdf/10.1007/s11134-011-9247-9.pdf))

Let Q1, ..., QN be a single-server cyclic polling system visited in the fixed order Q1, Q2, ..., QN, Q1, ... , and assume the service disciplines are of branching type so that the model admits the multi-type branching-process interpretation of Section 2. Suppose the queues have general renewal arrival processes, queue-specific service times Bi, deterministic switch-over times Si from Qi to Qi+1, the usual mutual independence assumptions, and stable steady-state operation. Writing S = sum_i Si, consider the regime S -> infinity with the proportions Si/S held fixed. Prove Conjecture 4.2 (equivalently, solve Open problem 2): under this S-scaling, the polling system converges to a deterministic cyclic system, in the sense suggested by the Poisson-arrival large-switch-over asymptotics, namely that the fluid-scaled queue lengths at polling instants, and hence the associated visit and intervisit times, become deterministic and correspond to a cycle with continuous demand rates and deterministic service rates.

Classify the N-queue single-server polling systems, in terms of their service, visit, and scheduling disciplines, for which deterministic switch-over times Si tending to infinity yield the deterministic large-switch-over-time behaviour discussed in §4: under the standard scaling by the total switch-over time S (and, in the fixed cyclic case, with fixed ratios Si/S), the system approaches a deterministic limiting regime, as manifested by scaled queue lengths at polling instants becoming deterministic and by analogous large-switch-over-time waiting-time limit theorems. In particular, in the Poisson-arrival setting singled out in the paper, determine whether and under what precise conditions this remains true for systems with dynamic visit orders, i.e. with no predetermined queue order (for example, when the server moves next to the longest queue), as conjectured when the switch-overs exert a regulating effect. citeturn8view0turn9view0turn10view2

Let m and n be integers with m≥3 and n≥2. For a nonnegative order-m, dimension-n tensor A, let γ(A) denote its primitive degree, i.e. the least positive integer r such that T_A^r(x)>0 for every nonzero x∈R_+^n. Define E(m,n):={k∈N : there exists a nonnegative primitive tensor A of order m and dimension n with γ(A)=k}. Determine E(m,n); in particular, is it true that E(m,n)={1,2,...,(n-1)^2+1}?

Let m,n≥2, and let 𝔄=(a_{i_1…i_m}) be a nonnegative tensor over ℝ of order m and dimension n. Assume that 𝔄 is primitive, in the sense that there exists r≥1 such that M(𝔄^r)>0, where powers are taken with respect to Shao’s general tensor product and the majorization matrix is defined by M(𝔄)_{ij}=a_{ij…j} for i,j∈[n]:={1,…,n}. For each j∈[n], say that 𝔄 is j-primitive if there exists k≥1 such that (M(𝔄^k))_{uj}>0 for every u∈[n], and let γ_j(𝔄) be the least such k. Must there always exist positive integers a,b with a<b such that {γ_1(𝔄),γ_2(𝔄),…,γ_n(𝔄)}=[a,b]^o:= {t∈ℤ : a≤t≤b}?

For integers m>=3 and n>=2, let A=(a_{i1...im}) be an order-m, dimension-n tensor with nonnegative real entries, and let A^k denote the k-th power of A under Shao’s general tensor product. Write [n]={1,...,n}, and define the majorization matrix by M(A)_{ij}=a_{ij...j}. Say that A is primitive if there exists r>=1 such that M(A^r)>0; say that A is j-primitive if, for some j in [n], there exists k>=1 such that (M(A^k))_{u j}>0 for every u in [n]; and say that A is irreducible if there is no nonempty proper subset I of [n] such that a_{i1...im}=0 whenever i1 is in I and i2,...,im are all outside I. Is it true that A is primitive if and only if A is irreducible and A is j-primitive for some j in [n]? ([sciencedirect.com](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0024379515002244?utm_source=openai))

For integers m >= 3 and n >= 2, let A = (a_{i_1...i_m}) be a nonnegative tensor of order m and dimension n over R, and let powers A^k be formed using the general tensor product from the paper. Its majorization matrix is M(A) = (a_{ij...j})_{i,j in [n]}, where [n] = {1,2,...,n}. For j in [n], say that A is j-primitive if there exists a positive integer k such that (M(A^k))_{u j} > 0 for every u in [n], and let gamma_j(A) be the least such k. Define r(m,n) = max{ gamma_j(A) : A is a nonnegative non-primitive tensor of order m and dimension n, and A is j-primitive for some j in [n] }. Determine r(m,n), and characterize the nonnegative non-primitive tensors A for which gamma_j(A) = r(m,n) for some j in [n].

Fix integers m,n >= 2 and j in [n]:={1,2,...,n}. Let A=(a_{i_1...i_m}) be a nonnegative tensor in R_+^{[m,n]}, and let M(A) be its majorization matrix, defined by M(A)_{ij}=a_{ij...j}. For k >= 1, let A^k denote the k-th power of A with respect to the general tensor product used in the paper. Call A j-primitive if there exists k >= 1 such that (M(A^k))_{uj} > 0 for every u in [n], and let gamma_j(A) be the least such k. Define R_j(m,n):={gamma_j(A) : A is a nonnegative tensor of order m and dimension n that is j-primitive but not primitive}. Must R_j(m,n) be gap-free, or can it contain gaps, i.e. nonempty consecutive intervals of integers none of whose elements belong to R_j(m,n)?

Using Shao’s general tensor product, let A be a nonnegative real tensor of order m and dimension n, with m,n>=2. Call A strongly primitive if A^k is entrywise positive for some positive integer k, and let η(A) be the least such k. In parallel with the paper’s earlier j-primitive framework, can one define and study the strongly primitive degree η(A), the strongly primitive degree set for fixed (m,n) (that is, the set of all values of η(A) attained by strongly primitive order-m, dimension-n tensors), and a corresponding notion of j-strongly primitive tensor, especially in the genuinely tensor case m>=3 where strong primitivity is strictly stronger than primitivity?

Motivated by the Kishino diagram, classify precisely when a non-trivial closed virtual knot can be obtained as a connected sum of two trivial virtual knots. Since connected sum of closed virtual knots is not well defined, analyze this through the ordered, well-defined connected sum on long virtual knots by determining which distinct long virtual knots have closures equivalent to the unknot, and how different choices of long representatives can produce a non-trivial closed virtual knot after closure.

For flat virtual knots (virtual strings), understood as equivalence classes of flat virtual diagrams with virtual crossings and ordinary crossings stripped of over/under information, modulo generalized flat Reidemeister moves, construct new combinatorial invariants that distinguish these flat virtual knots; in particular, can one extract such invariants from the flat biquandle algebra despite the paper's observation that this algebra is isomorphic to the Weyl algebra and has no non-trivial finite-dimensional representations, beyond the small examples that detect some flat linking beyond mod 2 linking numbers?

For each ordinal α, consider flat virtual diagrams in the sense of Section 2.2—i.e. diagrams with virtual crossings and flat crossings, taken up to the generalized flat Reidemeister I and II moves together with the usual virtual detour moves—but now with every flat crossing labeled by an element of α and with the flat Reidemeister III move allowed only when the sliding strand carries two equal labels a and the crossed flat crossing has label b with a > b. Classify the equivalence classes of diagrams in this α-indexed flat hierarchy.

How can one compare flat virtual-knot theory—where one studies flat virtual diagrams with flat and virtual crossings modulo the generalized flat Reidemeister moves and detour moves—with doodle theory, where a doodle is a flat diagram in the plane modulo Reidemeister moves of types I and II but not III; and, after allowing virtual crossings as well as flat crossings so as to obtain doodles on surfaces of higher genus, how do the basic doodle structures mentioned in the paper, namely Khovanov’s associated group, commutator identities, and doodle cobordism by immersed surfaces without triple points whose cobordism classes lie in a free abelian group, extend or correspond in this virtualized setting? ([impan.pl](https://www.impan.pl/shop/en/publication/transaction/download/product/86155))

Let a virtual 3-manifold mean a formal equivalence class of framed virtual link diagrams modulo the generalized Kirby moves of Kauffman and Dye. For ordinary 3-manifolds presented by surgery on framed classical links K and L, does equivalence of K and L in the virtual Kirby calculus imply equivalence in the classical Kirby calculus (hence no new equivalence beyond the usual one for ordinary 3-manifolds)? More generally, can one give a geometric-topological interpretation of these virtual 3-manifold classes, and does the alternative construction obtained by performing surgery on links in thickened surfaces S_g × R modulo stabilization—i.e. isotopy in the thickened surfaces, homeomorphism of the surface, and addition/removal of empty handles—coincide with the Kauffman-Dye theory?

Let a welded knot or link mean an equivalence class of virtual knot or link diagrams modulo the classical and virtual Reidemeister moves together with the upper forbidden move. Construct good invariants of welded knots and, if possible, classify them by deciding whether Satoh's map from equivalence classes of welded knots (respectively, welded links) to ambient-isotopy classes of ribbon torus embeddings in four-dimensional space is faithful; in particular, does a welded knot with trivial combinatorial fundamental group have to be the trivial welded knot?

In the setting of long virtual knots (equivalently, 1-1 tangles) and long flat virtual knots, can one enlarge the long-knot invariant structure of Manturov [167] by combining it with the biquandle construction of Kauffman–Radford [130] to obtain stronger invariants of long virtual knots, and in particular to extract new classical-knot invariants from that framework? More concretely, if F is a long flat virtual knot diagram and D(F) denotes the descending long virtual knot obtained by resolving each flat non-virtual crossing so that one always passes over before under, then since the long virtual knot type of D(F) is an invariant of F, determine which virtual-knot invariants I make I(D(F)) into effective invariants of long flat virtual knots, carry out sample calculations of such induced invariants, and assess whether this descending-diagram method yields a classification of long flat virtual knots in the sense posed in Section 8.1.

Construct explicit presentations of virtual biquandles for virtual knots and links in which the classical-crossing data is given by a linear biquandle in the sense of the paper—namely, labels lie in an R-module over an associative ring with identity, possibly noncommutative, and the classical switch has the form S = [[A,B],[C,D]] satisfying the biquandle axioms—while the virtual crossings carry additional nontrivial algebraic structure, so that one obtains a genuine virtual biquandle rather than an ordinary biquandle determined only by the classical crossings.

Does there exist a birack X in the sense of Section 6.1—i.e. a set with a switch S: X^2 -> X^2 satisfying invertibility, right invertibility, and the set-theoretic Yang–Baxter equation, but not necessarily the biquandle condition—such that the standard switch-induced representations of the virtual braid groups V B_n are faithful; and, specifically, is Manturov’s invariant of virtual braids from [157] (Recognition of virtual braids; see also [6, 115, 169]) faithful as an invariant of virtual braids?

For oriented virtual links L and L', let BQ(L) denote the fundamental biquandle obtained from an oriented virtual-link diagram by taking one generator for each edge and two relations at each crossing. If BQ(L) and BQ(L') are isomorphic as biquandles, must L and L' be equivalent as virtual links under the generalized Reidemeister moves, up to mirror image, bearing in mind that BQ is already known to take the same value on the orientation-reversed mirror image obtained by reflection in a plane perpendicular to the diagram plane?

Exhibit an explicit biquandle B in the sense of Definition 5.1 of §5.1—that is, a set with the four biquandle operations satisfying the axioms of Definition 5.1—such that B is not strong: for some pair a, b in B, the elements x, y, z, t whose existence is required in axiom (3) are not uniquely determined. This is the paper’s side question asking for a good example of a weak biquandle that is not strong. ([impan.pl](https://www.impan.pl/shop/en/publication/transaction/download/product/86155))

In the setting of virtual knot theory used in the paper, where crossing virtualization means replacing a classical crossing by a crossing of opposite orientation flanked by two virtual crossings, determine whether the following open problem holds: if K is a non-trivial classical knot diagram and K~ is obtained from K by virtualizing some subset of its classical crossings, with K~ still non-trivial and with unit Jones polynomial V(K~)=1, must K~ be non-classical (that is, not virtually equivalent to any classical knot diagram)? More generally, if a virtual knot diagram K has V(K)=1, is K equivalent to a classical diagram by a sequence of virtual Reidemeister moves and crossing virtualizations; and if two classical knot diagrams K and K' are related by such a sequence of crossing virtualizations and virtual Reidemeister moves, must K and K' already be equivalent as classical knots? As stated in the paper, affirmative answers to the last two parts would imply that the unknot is the only classical knot with unit Jones polynomial.

Can one formulate and study a theory of virtual quandle homology, directly analogous to classical quandle homology, and investigate the resulting invariants of virtual knots and links that arise from this virtual-quandle homological framework?

Construct, in the sense of Khovanov's original definition, a Khovanov complex over the ring of integers for arbitrary virtual-knot diagrams, extending and clarifying the orientable-atom-based construction of [169, 171] for large classes of virtual links and resolving the integral-coefficient difficulty caused by virtual state curves that can resmooth to a single curve; then, within this framework, classify K-full virtual knots (those admitting a diagram whose leading term, lowest term, or both come from the B-state) and Kho-full virtual knots (defined analogously for the Khovanov invariant), determine whether such optimal diagrams are always minimal in the number of classical crossings, classify the diagram moves that preserve optimality, decide whether a classical knot with a minimal n-crossing classical diagram can admit any virtual diagram with fewer than n classical crossings, and determine whether the B-state Khovanov homology can contain torsion.

For the Brauer algebra B_n obtained by adjoining virtual crossings to the Temperley–Lieb algebra—equivalently, the paper’s “Virtual Temperley–Lieb Algebra,” described as the algebra of all connections from n points to n points—determine the structure of the Jones–Wenzl projectors when placed in B_n, and decide whether this Brauer-algebra setting admits a useful algebraic generalization of the classical Temperley–Lieb recoupling theory. ([impan.pl](https://www.impan.pl/shop/en/publication/transaction/download/product/86155))

In virtual knot theory, where virtual knots are considered up to the generalized Reidemeister moves and equivalently as stable equivalence classes of knot embeddings in thickened compact oriented surfaces, define a notion of alternating virtual knot, classify the alternating virtual knots, classify all alternating weaves on fixed compact oriented surfaces before stabilization (that is, without adding or removing empty handles), and formulate and prove the appropriate analogue of the classical Tait flyping conjecture in this virtual/surface setting.

For a knot diagram K in the virtual/surface framework, let n be its number of classical crossings, let g be its atom genus (Turaev genus), and let span⟨K⟩ denote the difference between the highest and lowest nonzero degrees of its Kauffman bracket, so that span⟨K⟩ <= 4n - 4g. Can one prove, for a concrete diagram, that its atom genus g is minimal and thereby obtain minimality of the diagram when the bracket bound is sharp; and, more generally, can one use the Kauffman bracket, Thistlethwaite’s spanning tree expansion, atoms, and possibly an expansion into basic zero-crossing pieces and/or Khovanov homology, to derive sharp lower bounds for the minimal number of crossings of projections not only to the plane but to some 2-surface of higher genus, including an estimate of atom genus when the atom is taken in a neighborhood of that surface and the Khovanov-homology thickness is at most 2 + g?

For a virtual link L, let C(L), V(L), and T(L) denote, respectively, the minima over all virtual-link diagrams representing L of the numbers of classical crossings, virtual crossings, and total crossings. For a virtual knot K, let u_v(K) denote the minimum number of classical crossings that must be changed to virtual crossings by direct flattening, over all virtual diagrams of K, in order to unknot K. In the thickened-surface interpretation of virtual links up to stable equivalence, what is the relationship between V(L) and the least genus of a surface representative of L? Is the equality printed in Problem 17, T(L) = V(L) + L, actually true as stated (noting the paper's notation clash), and, more generally, do there exist effective algorithms for computing V(L) for natural classes of virtual knots or links and nontrivial upper or lower bounds for T(L), V(L), and the corresponding minimal classical-crossing quantity arising from virtual-knot polynomials?

In the standard virtual-knot setting of Sections 2.1 and 2.3—where virtual links are represented either by virtual link diagrams modulo the generalized Reidemeister moves or, equivalently, by stable equivalence classes of links embedded in thickened oriented surfaces S_g × R under isotopy, homeomorphisms of the surface, and addition/removal of empty handles—construct a category of “wild virtual knots,” formulate its axiomatics, and prove a theorem characterizing when a wild equivalence between tame virtual links implies that the links are already equivalent in the ordinary tame virtual sense.

For oriented virtual knots, with finite type understood in Kauffman's Vassiliev sense and also in the Goussarov-Polyak-Viro (GPV, Polyak-algebra/arrow-diagram) sense, determine necessary and sufficient obstructions for a Vassiliev finite-type invariant—especially one arising from coefficients of a virtual-knot polynomial extension such as the Conway extensions cited in the paper—to be GPV finite-type; in particular, explain how the polynomial-derived examples fit into Vassiliev theory and account for the known obstruction that any integer-valued Vassiliev invariant invariant under the virtualization move is not GPV finite-type.

Does the converse to the implication recorded in §8.2.4 hold? Precisely: let K be a classical oriented knot in R^3 ≅ R^2 × R. Must K be classically slice whenever, viewed as a virtual knot, it is slice in Kauffman’s sense (that is, virtually concordant to the unknot, equivalently to the empty knot, by a genus-zero cobordism generated by virtual isotopies, births, deaths, and oriented saddle moves), or whenever, viewed as a knot in a thickened surface, it is slice in Turaev’s sense? Moreover, if a knot in a thickened surface is slice in Turaev’s sense, must its stable-equivalence class under isotopy, surface homeomorphism, and addition/removal of empty handles contain a virtual knot that is slice in Kauffman’s sense? ([impan.pl](https://www.impan.pl/shop/en/publication/transaction/download/product/86155))

For the virtual braid group VB_n generated by σ_1, …, σ_{n-1} and ρ_1, …, ρ_{n-1}, where the σ_i generate the braid group B_n, the ρ_i generate the symmetric group S_n, and the mixed relations are σ_iρ_{i+1}ρ_i = ρ_{i+1}ρ_iσ_{i+1} for 1 ≤ i ≤ n−2 and σ_iρ_j = ρ_jσ_i for |i−j| > 1, determine whether the following three Bardakov problems have affirmative answers: (i) VB_n is linear for every n > 3, in the sense that VB_n embeds into GL_m(k) for some natural number m and some field k; (ii) the representation ρ : VB_n → Aut(F_{n+1}), where F_{n+1} = <x_1, …, x_n, y> and ρ is given by σ_i(x_i) = x_ix_{i+1}x_i^{-1}, σ_i(x_{i+1}) = x_i, σ_i(x_k) = x_k, σ_i(y) = y, and ρ_i(x_i) = yx_{i+1}y^{-1}, ρ_i(x_{i+1}) = y^{-1}x_i y, ρ_i(x_k) = x_k, ρ_i(y) = y for k ≠ i, i+1, is faithful for every n > 2; and (iii) there exist non-equivalent virtual links L_v and L'_v that are closures of virtual braids β_v ∈ VB_n and β'_v ∈ VB_m such that the welded links represented by ρ_A(β_v) and ρ_A(β'_v) are equivalent as welded links. ([impan.pl](https://www.impan.pl/shop/en/publication/transaction/download/product/86155))

Let # denote concatenation of long virtual knots, and interpret equality up to equivalence of long virtual knots. Prove an existence-and-uniqueness theorem for decompositions of long virtual knots into prime long virtual knots under concatenation; and determine whether, if A and B are non-classical long virtual knots that are prime with respect to some decomposition of long virtual knots other than concatenation, the concatenation A#B can nevertheless be expressed as a decomposition of that other type into A and B.

In the setting of a virtual cover (k in Sigma x (0,1), Pi, K_N) of a smooth knot K in a compact oriented 3-manifold N, where Pi: Sigma x (0,1) -> N is a covering space, Pi(k)=K, the associated virtual knot upsilon is obtained from k viewed in Sigma x [0,1], and the cover is fundamental when Pi is regular and k lies in a fundamental region, determine to what extent the virtual-cover construction for links in S^3 with at least two components can be extended to one-component links (knots) in S^3; whether one can relate Milnor mu-invariants to invariants of the associated virtual knot and thereby apply Milnor's theory to knots; how the associated virtual knot changes under local non-isotopy moves on a classical link, especially crossing changes, self-Delta moves, and Z-moves; whether virtual covers can detect mutation of classical links; and, using the fact that every virtual knot upsilon arises as the associated virtual knot of a fundamental virtual cover of some two-component link K ⊔ J with J fibered and lk(J,K)=0, find a complete set of moves on such links that preserve the virtual isotopy type of upsilon.

Can precision tests of the Equivalence Principle—specifically its Weak, Einstein, and Strong formulations—empirically distinguish between: (1) a purely metric theory of gravity in which one assumes a torsion‐free affine connection ∇ is the Levi–Civita connection uniquely determined by the spacetime metric g, and (2) a Palatini‐type theory in which the metric g and a symmetric, torsion‐free affine connection ∇ are treated as independent variables in the gravitational action, so that ∇ need not a priori coincide with the Levi–Civita connection of g?

In relativistic theories of gravity where the metric g_{μν} and connection Γ^α_{μν} are treated independently (Palatini versus metric formulations), and assuming matter fields are quantized while gravity remains classical, does the Einstein Equivalence Principle—that (i) inertial and gravitational masses are equivalent (Weak EP), (ii) the outcomes of all local non-gravitational experiments in a freely-falling laboratory are independent of the laboratory’s velocity and spacetime location—remain valid at the quantum level, or can quantum effects (such as non-minimal couplings, higher-order curvature invariants, or quantum fluctuations) lead to measurable violations of its postulates?

Let F be a finite field of characteristic p and order q>2, let μ be the canonical additive character of F, and let s be a positive integer with gcd(s,q-1)=1. For a in F, define the Weil sum W_{F,s}(a)=sum_{x in F} μ(x^s-ax). Say that the power permutation x -> x^s (equivalently, the exponent s) is singular over F if there exists a in F^× such that W_{F,s}(a)=0. Must every invertible exponent s satisfying s ≡ 1 mod (p-1) be singular over F? ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/abs/1412.8530))

Let L be a finite field of characteristic p and order q = p^m, where m = [L : F_p] is a power of 2 and p is either 2 or 3. Let mu be the canonical additive character of L, and for an integer s define the Weil sum W_{L,s}(a) = sum_{x in L} mu(x^s - a x). For the invertible exponent s = q - 2, prove by a method that does not use elliptic curves that the exponent q - 2 is singular in the sense of Helleseth's Vanishing Conjecture.

Let L be a finite field of characteristic p, let q = |L|, let mu_L(x) = exp(2 pi i Tr_{L/F_p}(x)/p) be the canonical additive character of L, and let s be an invertible exponent over L, meaning gcd(s, q - 1) = 1, so that x -> x^s is a permutation of L. For each a in L define W_{L,s}(a) = sum_{x in L} mu_L(x^s - a x), and let the reduced Fourier spectrum of x -> x^s be the set {W_{L,s}(a) : a in L^times}. If [L : F_p] is a power of 2, is it true that this reduced spectrum can never have exactly three distinct values? In other words, does Conjecture 1.1 hold for all remaining cases p > 3, given that the paper proves it already for p = 2 and p = 3?

Let L=F_q be a finite field of characteristic p, let μ(x)=exp(2πi Tr_{L/F_p}(x)/p) be its canonical additive character, and for a map f:L→L and b∈L define f_b(x)=b f(x) and Fourier coefficients by ^hat{f_b}(a)=Σ_{x∈L} μ(bf(x)-ax) for a∈L. If spec(f_b) denotes the Fourier spectrum/distribution of f_b, i.e. the multiset { ^hat{f_b}(a) : a∈L }, then every power permutation f(x)=x^s with gcd(s,q-1)=1 satisfies spec(f_b)=spec(f_1) for all b∈L×. Determine all maps f:L→L for which spec(f_b)=spec(f_1) for every b∈L×.

Let L be a finite field of characteristic 2 and order q > 2, let μ be the canonical additive character of L, and let f(x) = x^s be a power permutation of L, so gcd(s, q - 1) = 1. For a in L, write \hat{f}(a) = Σ_{x in L} μ(x^s - a x), and set D(f) = ∏_{a in L^×} \hat{f}(a). Aubry and Langevin proved in Proposition 1.2 that 3 divides D(f). Is there a 5-adic analogue of this result; that is, must one always have 5 divides D(f) for every such power permutation?

Let L be a finite field of characteristic p and order q, let μ be the canonical additive character of L, and let f(x)=x^s be a power permutation of L, so gcd(s,q−1)=1. For a∈L define the Fourier coefficient F_s(a)=Σ_{x∈L} μ(x^s−ax), and write spec(f)={F_s(a): a∈L×}. Assume that |spec(f)|=4. Find the 4-valued analogue of Katz’s 3-valued theorem from the paper: determine what structural restrictions must hold for such a four-valued power permutation, specifically whether and in what precise form the three-valued conclusions survive—namely singularity (0∈spec(f), equivalently Π_{a∈L×}F_s(a)=0), the congruence s ≡ 1 (mod p−1), and integrality of the spectrum.

Let L be a finite field of characteristic p and order q, let mu be the canonical additive character of L, and let f(x) = x^s be a power permutation of L, i.e. gcd(s, q - 1) = 1. For each a in L, define the Fourier coefficient (Weil sum) f-hat(a) = sum_{x in L} mu(x^s - a x), and let A_1, ..., A_n be the distinct nonzero values in the spectrum spec(f) = {f-hat(a) : a in L} (equivalently, in the reduced spectrum on L^x, since f-hat(0) = 0). For which invertible exponents s is the product A_1 ... A_n divisible by q = |L|?

Let L be a finite field of odd characteristic p, let q = |L|, and let s be an invertible exponent over L (so gcd(s, q - 1) = 1). For u, v in L define N(u,v) to be the number of pairs (x,y) in L^2 satisfying x + y = u and x^s + y^s = v. Call s nice if the set {N(1,v) : v in L} has at most three distinct values. Must 2 always occur among these differential multiplicities; equivalently, if s is nice, must there exist v in L with N(1,v) = 2?

Let L be a finite field of odd characteristic p, and let s be an exponent over L that is not equivalent to 1, in the sense that s ≡ p^j mod (|L|-1) for no integer j. For each v in L, define N(1,v)=#{(x,y) in L^2 : x+y=1 and x^s+y^s=v}. Suppose that the set {N(1,v) : v in L} has at most three distinct values, so that s is a nice exponent in the paper's terminology. Must there exist v in L such that N(1,v)=2?

For every finite field L=F_q of odd characteristic p and every integer s with gcd(s,q-1)=1, viewed modulo q-1, assume that s is not equivalent to 1 in the sense of Section 3 (that is, neither s nor s^{-1} is congruent modulo q-1 to a p-power). Must 2 occur among the differential multiplicities of s; equivalently, must there exist b in L such that the equation (x+1)^s - x^s = b has exactly two solutions x in L?

Let \{\gamma_k\}_{k\ge 0} be a sequence of nonnegative real numbers such that the exponential generating function
f(x)=\sum_{k=0}^\infty \gamma_k\,\frac{x^k}{k!}
is an entire function. For each real parameter p\in\mathbb{R}\setminus\{-1,-2,\dots\}, define the generalized Bessel-type entire function
F_p(x)=\sum_{k=0}^\infty \frac{\gamma_k}{k!\,\Gamma(k+p+1)}x^k.
Characterize all such sequences \{\gamma_k\}_{k\ge 0} for which F_p belongs to the Laguerre–Pólya class \mathcal{L}\!-ℙ for every admissible p. ([sciencedirect.com](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0022247X15007854?utm_source=openai))

Let gamma_k := ln(k+2)/k! for k in N_0. Is {gamma_k}_{k>=0} a classical multiplier sequence; equivalently, does the diagonal operator T:R[x]->R[x] defined by T(x^k)=gamma_k x^k satisfy that T(p) has only real zeros whenever p in R[x] has only real zeros?

Let alpha={alpha_k}_{k=0}^infinity and beta={beta_k}_{k=0}^infinity be classical multiplier sequences of nonnegative real numbers, where a real sequence gamma={gamma_k}_{k=0}^infinity is called a multiplier sequence if the diagonal operator T_gamma: R[x] -> R[x], defined by T_gamma[x^k]=gamma_k x^k for k in N_0, sends every real polynomial with only real zeros to another real polynomial with only real zeros. Characterize all functions Psi: R x R -> R with the property that, for every such pair alpha and beta, the pointwise sequence {Psi(alpha_k,beta_k)}_{k=0}^infinity is again a classical multiplier sequence.

Let p(x)=sum_{j=0}^n a_j x^j be a polynomial in R[x] with a_j>=0 for all j, and define gamma_k:=p(k) for k in N_0. Specializing the paper's introductory Problem 1 to polynomially interpolated nonnegative sequences, characterize those polynomials p for which the composed sequence {gamma_k/k!}_{k=0}^infty = {p(k)/k!}_{k=0}^infty is a classical multiplier sequence; equivalently, determine for which p the entire function sum_{k=0}^infty p(k)x^k/(k!)^2 belongs to the Laguerre-Pólya class L-P^+. As a stronger follow-up in the paper's CZDS sense, determine which such p also make {p(k)/k!}_{k=0}^infty a complex zero decreasing sequence, i.e. for which the diagonal operator T_p on R[x], defined by T_p[x^k]=(p(k)/k!)x^k, satisfies Z_C(T_p[f])<=Z_C(f) for every real polynomial f.

Let p(x)=1+x+x^2, and define the diagonal operator T:R[x]->R[x] by T(x^k)=(p(k)/k!)x^k=((k^2+k+1)/k!)x^k for k in N_0. Since Proposition 20 of the paper already shows that {p(k)/k!}_{k=0}^infty is a multiplier sequence for every quadratic p(x)=cx^2+ax+b with a,b,c>=0, is this specific sequence in fact a complex zero decreasing sequence; that is, does T satisfy Z_C(T[f])<=Z_C(f) for every real polynomial f in R[x], where Z_C counts nonreal zeros with multiplicity?

Let γ_k:=√k/k! for k=0,1,2,…. Determine whether the diagonal operator T:ℝ[x]→ℝ[x] defined by T[x^k]=γ_k x^k is (i) a classical multiplier sequence, meaning that T[p] has only real zeros whenever the real polynomial p has only real zeros, and (ii) a complex zero decreasing sequence (CZDS), meaning that Z_C(T[p])≤Z_C(p) for every p∈ℝ[x], where Z_C counts nonreal zeros with multiplicity.

Is the real entire function φ(x)=∑_{k=0}^∞ √k x^k/(k!)^2 in L-P+, the Laguerre–Pólya class of real entire functions with nonnegative Taylor coefficients? ([sciencedirect.com](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0022247X15007854?utm_source=openai))

Let gamma_k := 1/(k+1)^(k+1) for k in N_0, and let T: R[x] -> R[x] be the diagonal linear operator defined by T[x^k] := (gamma_k/k!) x^k = x^k/((k+1)^(k+1) k!). Determine whether the sequence {gamma_k/k!}_{k=0}^infinity is a classical multiplier sequence; that is, whether T[p] has only real zeros whenever p in R[x] has only real zeros. Also determine whether {gamma_k/k!}_{k=0}^infinity is a complex zero decreasing sequence, meaning that Z_C(T[p]) <= Z_C(p) for every p in R[x], where Z_C counts non-real zeros with multiplicity.

Characterize precisely the classical multiplier sequences {gamma_k}_{k>=0} of real numbers for which there exist entire functions phi, Phi in L-P^+ (not necessarily distinct) and real parameters t,s such that, for every k in N_0, gamma_k = C_k^{phi,Phi}(t,s) := sum_{j=0}^k binom(k,j) B_j^phi(t) B_{k-j}^Phi(s), where B_m^phi(u) is defined by e^{(1-u)x} phi(ux) = sum_{m>=0} B_m^phi(u) x^m/m! (equivalently, if phi(x) = sum_{m>=0} a_m x^m/m!, then B_m^phi(u) = sum_{r=0}^m binom(m,r)(1-u)^r a_{m-r} u^{m-r}). Here "classical multiplier sequence" means that the operator T on R[x] given by T[x^k] = gamma_k x^k preserves real-rootedness.
