([sciencedirect.com](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0022247X15007854?utm_source=openai))
Is the real entire function φ(x)=∑_{k=0}^∞ √k x^k/(k!)^2 a member of the Laguerre–Pólya class L-P^+?

In the standard binary 'vanilla' Optimal AdaBoost setting of the paper, let X be the feature space, Y = {-1,+1}, let D = ((x^(1), y^(1)), ..., (x^(m), y^(m))) be an i.i.d. training sample of size m from an underlying probability space, and let H be a weak-hypothesis class of functions h:X->Y that is AdaBoost-natural with respect to D, meaning: (i) the constant classifier +1 belongs to H; (ii) H is closed under negation; and (iii) every h in H misclassifies at least one example of D. For each round t, let w_t be the AdaBoost example-weight distribution on the m training examples, let err(h; w_t, D) = sum_{l=1}^m w_t(l) 1[h(x^(l)) != y^(l)], and let H(w_t, D) = argmin_{h in H} err(h; w_t, D). Assume, as in the paper's preliminaries, a deterministic tie-breaking rule for choosing a representative minimizer from H(w_t, D). Is the following No-Ties Conjecture true: for mu-almost all underlying probability spaces and mu-almost all measurable hypothesis classes H that are AdaBoost-natural with respect to D, there exist m_0, T_0 > 0 such that whenever m > m_0, then with probability 1 over the sampled dataset D, either (a) for every t > T_0 the minimizer set H(w_t, D) is a singleton, or (b) for every t > T_0 every pair h, h' in H(w_t, D) agrees on all training examples x^(1), ..., x^(m), or else (c) the total current weight of the disagreement set of the tied minimizers tends to 0, i.e. sum_{l=1}^m w_t(l) 1[there exist h, h' in H(w_t, D) with h(x^(l)) != h'(x^(l))] -> 0 as t -> infinity?

In the paper's standard 'vanilla' binary Optimal AdaBoost setting, let X be the feature space, let Y = {-1,+1}, let calD = X x Y, and let D = {(x^(l), y^(l))}_{l=1}^m be a finite training set of i.i.d. examples from a probability space (calD, Sigma, P). Let H be a weak-hypothesis class that is AdaBoost-natural with respect to D, and run Optimal AdaBoost for T rounds, meaning that at each round the weak learner selects a minimum weighted-error hypothesis in H according to the paper's deterministic tie-breaking convention. Is the following true: for mu-almost all probability spaces (calD, Sigma, P), for any dataset D, and for mu-almost all H that are AdaBoost-natural with respect to D, there exist thresholds m' and T' such that whenever |D| = m > m' and T > T', the decision boundary of the binary classifier output by Optimal AdaBoost after T rounds on D (equivalently, the zero set of its combined score function) has P-measure zero?

Let D={(x^(1),y^(1)),…,(x^(m),y^(m))} be a finite labeled sample in [0,1]^n×{-1,+1}. Form the dataset-induced family H_hat of axis-aligned decision stumps by the standard midpoint rule, let E_hat⊆H_hat be the effective subclass obtained by deleting every stump that is dominated on D by another stump in H_hat, and let U_hat^T be the set of distinct stumps selected in the first T rounds of Optimal AdaBoost run on D. For D sampled from a distribution P on [0,1]^n×{-1,+1}, determine nontrivial upper and lower bounds for |H_hat|, |E_hat|, and |U_hat^T| as functions of the sample size m, ambient dimension n, and number of rounds T.

Conjecture 4 (Logarithmic Growth on Unique Stumps). In the Section 3 decision-stump setting of Belanich and Ortiz, let X = [0,1]^n, Y = {-1,+1}, D = X × Y, and let D = ((x^(1),y^(1)),...,(x^(m),y^(m))) be a dataset of size m drawn i.i.d. from a probability space (D, Σ, P). Let H_b be the finite set of midpoint-rule decision stumps induced by D, let E_b be the effective stump set obtained from H_b by deleting every dominated stump, and let U_b^T = union_{t=1}^T {h_t}, where h_t is the decision stump selected at round t by vanilla Optimal AdaBoost under the paper’s deterministic tie-breaking convention. Is it true that, for μ-almost all probability spaces (D, Σ, P) and any dataset D, there exist thresholds m' and T' such that whenever m > m' and T > T', one has E[|U_b^T| | D] <= (log T + 1)^c for some c in [1,2), P-almost surely?

Conjecture 1.1. Let (X,d) be a complete metric space, let C(X) denote the family of all nonempty closed subsets of X, and let H be the Hausdorff metric induced by d. Suppose T:X→C(X) satisfies H(Tx,Ty)<φ(d(x,y)) for all distinct x,y∈X, where φ:[0,∞)→[0,∞) is an L-function in the sense of Lim: φ(0)=0, φ(s)>0 for every s>0, and for every s>0 there exist δ>0 and ε>0 such that φ(t)≤s for all t∈[δ,δ+ε]. Does T necessarily have a fixed point; that is, must there exist x∈X such that x∈T(x)?

Let (X,d) be a complete metric space, let CB(X) denote the family of all nonempty closed bounded subsets of X, and let H be the Hausdorff metric induced by d on CB(X). Suppose T:X -> CB(X) satisfies
H(Tx,Ty) <= d(x,y) - theta(d(x,y)) for all x,y in X,
where theta:[0,+infinity) -> [0,+infinity) belongs to the class A, meaning that there exist epsilon_0 > 0 and a function gamma in Gamma such that, for every t >= 0, theta(t) <= epsilon_0 implies theta(t) >= gamma(t), and Gamma is the class of all subadditive, nondecreasing, continuous maps gamma:[0,+infinity) -> [0,+infinity) with gamma^{-1}({0}) = {0}. Must T have a fixed point; that is, does there necessarily exist x in X such that x belongs to T(x)?

Let G be a topological group. Call G prodiscrete if it is a projective limit of discrete topological groups, equivalently a closed subgroup of an arbitrary product of discrete groups. Is there a satisfactory structure theory for non-discrete prodiscrete groups? More particularly, is there a satisfactory structure theory even for Abelian non-discrete prodiscrete groups?

Open problem. For every pro-Lie group G, with G0 denoting the connected component of the identity and G/G0 equipped with the quotient topology, is the component group G/G0 complete as a topological group? Equivalently, is G/G0 always prodiscrete? ([sidneymorris.net](https://sidneymorris.net/Morris156.pdf))

Characterize those Abelian pro-Lie groups G for which the Pontryagin evaluation morphism \eta_G:G\to\widehat{\widehat{G}}, defined by \eta_G(g)(\chi)=\chi(g), is an isomorphism of topological groups, where \widehat{G}=\operatorname{Hom}(G,\mathbb{T}) is equipped with the compact-open topology, \mathbb{T}=\mathbb{R}/\mathbb{Z}, and an Abelian pro-Lie group means a closed subgroup of a product of finite-dimensional real Lie groups.

Which Abelian pro-Lie groups G are strongly reflexive, meaning that for every subgroup H ≤ G endowed with the inherited topology and every Hausdorff quotient group Q of G, the canonical Pontryagin evaluation map η_A: A -> (A^)^ is an isomorphism of topological groups for A = H and A = Q, where A^ = Hom(A,T) carries the compact-open topology and T = R/Z? ([mdpi.com](https://www.mdpi.com/2075-1680/4/3/294))

For every set I, if K is a compact topological group and f : Z^I -> K is a surjective continuous homomorphism, where Z carries the discrete topology and Z^I the product topology, must f be an open map?

Working over R, let V be the category of real vector spaces with the usual tensor product and W the dual category of weakly-complete real topological vector spaces with completed tensor product ⊗e. If A is a weakly-complete Hopf algebra (that is, a group object in W), write G(A) for its grouplike elements and P(A) = {x in A : c(x) = x ⊗e 1 + 1 ⊗e x} for its primitive elements. Since Theorem 19 shows that G(A) is a pro-Lie group, P(A) is its pro-Lie algebra, and exp_A restricted to P(A) is the exponential map, is there a more elaborate duality theory between real Hopf algebras and weakly-complete Hopf algebras in which these pro-Lie group and pro-Lie algebra features play a role; and, in particular, does the existence of weakly-complete enveloping algebras for weakly-complete Lie algebras imply that every real pro-Lie algebra L admits an associative weakly-complete Hopf algebra U(L) such that L is isomorphic, as a topological Lie algebra, to a closed Lie subalgebra of P(U(L))?

Let G be an abelian topological group that is prodiscrete, i.e. a projective limit of discrete groups (equivalently, a closed subgroup of a product of discrete groups). Suppose G is compactly generated, meaning that G is algebraically generated by a compact subset, and suppose G has no nontrivial compact subgroups. Must G be discrete?

Let G be a compactly generated Abelian prodiscrete topological group, where prodiscrete means that G is a projective limit of discrete groups (equivalently, a closed subgroup of a product of discrete groups). Assume that G is compact-free, i.e. G has no nontrivial compact subgroups. Must G be a finitely generated free Abelian group?

Let g be a finite-dimensional real semisimple Lie algebra. Is the commutator map [ , ]: g x g -> g, defined by (x,y) -> [x,y], surjective? Equivalently, does every element z in g admit x,y in g such that z = [x,y]?

Let G be a connected pro-Lie group in the sense of Hofmann and Morris, i.e. a topological group isomorphic to a closed subgroup of a product of finite-dimensional real Lie groups. If G is transfinitely nilpotent in the standard pro-Lie-theoretic sense used by the authors, must G be pronilpotent?

For pro-Lie groups in the sense of Hofmann and Morris—that is, topological groups isomorphic to closed subgroups of arbitrary products of finite-dimensional real Lie groups—is there a satisfactory theory of (i) Polish pro-Lie groups (separable completely metrizable pro-Lie groups), (ii) separable pro-Lie groups, and (iii) compactly generated pro-Lie groups (pro-Lie groups generated by a compact subset), notably in the connected case?
Are there infinitely many nonnegative integers n such that 2^(2^n) + 1 is composite?
Are there infinitely many prime integers of the form 2^{2^n}+1, where n ranges over the nonnegative integers?
Among positive integers x, is x! + 1 a perfect square if and only if x belongs to the set {4, 5, 7}?

Assuming Conjecture 4.1 of the paper—namely, that for C = {x_i x_j = x_k : i, j, k in {1, ..., 6}, i != j} union {x_j! = x_k : j, k in {1, ..., 6}, j != k}, every subsystem S subseteq C with only finitely many positive-integer solutions has all coordinates bounded by 720!—if the Erdos equation x(x + 1) = y! (where y! denotes the factorial of y) has at most finitely many solutions in positive integers x and y, must every such solution be one of (x, y) = (1, 2) or (2, 3)?

Let Omega be a smooth bounded domain in R^4, let lambda_1 < lambda_2 <= ... be the Dirichlet eigenvalues of -Delta on H_0^1(Omega), and let S be the best Sobolev constant for the critical embedding into L^4. For fixed a,b>0 and 0<delta<bS^2, consider the Kirchhoff-type Brezis-Nirenberg problem
-(a + b int_Omega |grad u|^2 dx) Delta u = lambda u + delta |u|^2 u in Omega,  u=0 on dOmega.
The limiting problem as delta -> 0^+ is
-(a + b int_Omega |grad u|^2 dx) Delta u = lambda u in Omega,  u=0 on dOmega.
Assuming lambda > a lambda_2 (equivalently, by Proposition 1.2, that the limiting problem admits a sign-changing solution), does there exist a sign-changing solution u_delta in H_0^1(Omega) of the Kirchhoff problem such that, as delta -> 0^+, u_delta converges strongly in H_0^1(Omega) to a sign-changing solution of the limiting problem (1.4)?

Let Ω ⊂ R^4 be a smooth bounded domain, let a, b, λ, δ > 0, let λ1 be the first Dirichlet eigenvalue of -Δ on H_0^1(Ω), and let S be the best Sobolev constant for the embedding H_0^1(Ω) ↪ L^4(Ω). In the q = 2 case of the Kirchhoff-type Brezis-Nirenberg problem
-(a + b∫_Ω |∇u|^2 dx)Δu = λu + δ|u|^2u in Ω,  u = 0 on ∂Ω,
does there exist a positive ground state solution in H_0^1(Ω) whenever λ >= aλ1 and δ > bS^2?

For the four-dimensional Kirchhoff-type Brezis-Nirenberg problem
-(a+b\int_\Omega |\nabla u|^2\,dx)\,\Delta u=\lambda u+\delta |u|^2u\quad\text{in }\Omega,
\qquad u=0\quad\text{on }\partial\Omega,
where \Omega\subset\mathbb{R}^4 is a smooth bounded domain, a,b,\lambda,\delta>0, \lambda_1 is the first Dirichlet eigenvalue of -\Delta on \Omega, and S is the best Sobolev constant for H_0^1(\Omega)\hookrightarrow L^4(\Omega), does there exist a nontrivial weak solution u\in H_0^1(\Omega) whenever \lambda\ge a\lambda_1 and \delta>bS^2?

Let Ω ⊂ R^4 be a smooth bounded domain, let a,b,λ,μ > 0, and consider the problem -(a + b∫Ω |∇u|^2 dx)Δu = λu^q + μu^3 in Ω, u > 0 in Ω, u = 0 on ∂Ω, with 1 < q < 3 (equivalently, in the reparametrization used in the draft, 2 < p = q+1 < 4 and the right-hand side is λ|u|^(p-2)u + μ|u|^2u). Writing S for the Sobolev constant of H_0^1(Ω) ↪ L^4(Ω), Theorems 1.3 and 1.6 prove existence under bS^2 < μ < 2bS^2, one of the auxiliary hypotheses λ < λ0(a,b,q,μ), or a > a0(b,q,λ,μ), or b0(a,q,λ,μ) < b < μ/S^2, and, to pass from the auxiliary problems (P_ν) to the original problem (P), the additional assumption that Ω is strictly star-shaped. Are these extra hypotheses genuinely necessary for existence, i.e. can one remove them by taking λ0 = ∞, a0 = 0, and b0 = μ/(2S^2), dropping the condition μ < 2bS^2, and obtaining the same existence conclusion for the original problem on a general smooth bounded domain Ω?

Let Omega be an arbitrary open subset of R^d, let lambda_1 >= 0 be the optimal Poincare-Stekloff constant for H_0^1(Omega), and consider the real-valued Dirichlet problem -Delta u = f(x,u,grad u) in Omega with u in H_0^1(Omega). Assume f : Omega x R x R^d -> R is Caratheodory and satisfies all the other hypotheses of Section 2.1 of Stahn's existence theorem, in particular the growth assumptions there, and the coerciveness estimate f(x,s,xi)s <= (lambda_1 - epsilon)s^2 + L |xi| |s| + h(x)|s| for a.e. x in Omega and all s in R, xi in R^d, with epsilon > 0 and h as in Section 2.1. In Theorem 4 the paper assumes the smallness condition L < L_max(epsilon,lambda_1), where L_max(epsilon,lambda_1) = epsilon/sqrt(lambda_1) if epsilon <= 2 lambda_1 and L_max(epsilon,lambda_1) = 2 sqrt(epsilon - lambda_1) if epsilon >= 2 lambda_1. Is this condition on L actually necessary for the real-valued existence theory on arbitrary open sets? More precisely, if L >= L_max(epsilon,lambda_1), must there exist some open set Omega and some real-valued admissible nonlinearity f satisfying all the remaining hypotheses of Section 2.1 for which the above Dirichlet problem has no weak solution?

For the generalized Robin problem (42) on an arbitrary open set Ω ⊂ R^d, with Robin form a_S corresponding to the maximal μ-admissible set S from Theorem 9, and under the additional embedding hypothesis (45) that replaces the Sobolev embedding in the Moser-iteration argument, are the resulting a priori Lebesgue-space bounds for weak solutions—equivalently, the endpoint L^{q**}(Ω)-bound furnished by that iteration—optimal in general, or can the exponent q** be improved beyond the value obtained from (45)?

Let Omega subset C^n be a domain, and let phi be an arbitrary plurisubharmonic function on Omega. For a pointwise decreasing sequence (phi_j) of bounded plurisubharmonic functions on Omega with phi_j decreasing to phi, consider the Bedford-Taylor Monge-Ampere measures (dd^c phi_j)^n. What can be said about the set of their weak cluster points as Radon measures on Omega?

Let Ω ⊂ C^n be a domain, let φ ∈ PSH(Ω) ∩ L^∞(Ω), and let (φ_j) ⊂ PSH(Ω) ∩ L^∞(Ω) be a sequence such that φ_j → φ in L^1_loc(Ω). For each j, let (dd^c φ_j)^n denote the Bedford-Taylor complex Monge-Ampère measure of φ_j. What can be said about the set of weak cluster points, in the space of Radon measures on Ω, of the sequence of measures ((dd^c φ_j)^n)_j?

Let Ω ⊂ C^n be a domain, and let φ ∈ PSH(Ω) be an arbitrary plurisubharmonic function, with no assumption that φ belongs to the Monge-Ampere domain DMA(Ω). Suppose that for every point x ∈ Ω there exists an open neighborhood U_x ⊂ Ω such that φ|_{U_x} is maximal in U_x, in the sense that for every v ∈ PSH(U_x), if v ≤ φ near ∂U_x then v ≤ φ on U_x. Must φ be maximal in Ω? Equivalently: is maximality a local notion for arbitrary plurisubharmonic functions?

Let Omega be a domain in C^2, let 0 <= alpha < 1, and let phi belong to PSH(Omega) intersect C^{2,alpha}(Omega). Assume phi is maximal in Omega, meaning that whenever v belongs to PSH(Omega) and v <= phi near partial Omega, then v <= phi throughout Omega. Must the support of the positive current dd^c phi be foliated—or at least laminated—by holomorphic discs Delta_t subset Omega such that the restriction phi|_{Delta_t} is harmonic on each disc? ([math.univ-toulouse.fr](https://www.math.univ-toulouse.fr/~zeriahi/DGZ-arXiv2015.pdf))

Let (X, ω) be a compact Kähler manifold of complex dimension n, and let PSH(X, ω) denote the set of ω-plurisubharmonic functions. For φ ∈ PSH(X, ω), say that φ belongs to DMA(X, ω) if there exists a Radon measure μ on X such that, for every sequence φ_j ∈ PSH(X, ω) ∩ C∞(X) decreasing to φ on X, the measures (ω + dd^cφ_j)^n converge weakly to μ; in that case one writes (ω + dd^cφ)^n := μ. Characterize the class DMA(X, ω), i.e. give necessary and sufficient conditions for an ω-psh function on a compact Kähler manifold to belong to the global domain of definition of the complex Monge-Ampère operator.

Let (X, ω) be a compact Kähler manifold, let PSH(X, ω) denote the set of ω-plurisubharmonic functions on X, and define DMA(X, ω) to be the set of all φ ∈ PSH(X, ω) such that there exists a Radon measure μ on X with (ω + dd^cφ_j)^n converging weakly to μ for every decreasing sequence φ_j ∈ PSH(X, ω) ∩ C^∞(X) satisfying φ_j ↓ φ on X. Is DMA(X, ω) convex, i.e. does tφ_0 + (1-t)φ_1 belong to DMA(X, ω) for every φ_0, φ_1 ∈ DMA(X, ω) and every t ∈ [0,1]? And if φ ∈ DMA(X, ω) and ψ ∈ PSH(X, ω), must the pointwise maximum max(φ, ψ) also belong to DMA(X, ω)?

Let B = {z in C^n : ||z|| < 1} be the unit ball, and let phi be a plurisubharmonic function on B such that its complex Monge-Ampere measure (dd^c phi)^n is well defined in the local Bedford-Taylor sense; for example, it is enough to assume that phi is locally bounded on B minus {0}. If (dd^c phi)^n has a Dirac mass at the origin, equivalently if (dd^c phi)^n({0}) > 0, is the Lelong number nu(phi,0) necessarily strictly positive?

Let B be the unit ball in ℂ^n, and let φ ∈ PSH(B) be such that its complex Monge–Ampère measure (dd^cφ)^n is well defined (for example, φ may be assumed locally bounded on B \ {0}). For each j ∈ ℕ, define the weighted Bergman space H(jφ) := {f ∈ O(B) : ∫_B |f|^2 e^{-2jφ} dV < +∞}, let (f_{k,j}) be an orthonormal basis of H(jφ), and set φ_j := (1/(2j)) log(∑_{k=0}^{∞} |f_{k,j}|^2). Does one have convergence of the residual Monge–Ampère masses at the origin, namely (dd^cφ_j)^n({0}) → (dd^cφ)^n({0}) as j → ∞?

Let (X, omega) = (CP^n, omega_FS), where omega_FS is the Fubini-Study Kähler form, and let V := integral_X omega_FS^n. Can one find a point a in CP^n and an omega_FS-plurisubharmonic function G_a such that G_a belongs to DMA(X, omega_FS) in the sense of Definition 1.3, its normalized Monge-Ampère measure satisfies MA(G_a) := V^{-1}(omega_FS + dd^c G_a)^n = delta_a, and its Lelong number nu(G_a, a) is irrational?

Let X be a compact Kähler manifold of complex dimension n, and let T and S be cohomologous positive closed (1,1)-currents on X. Choose a smooth closed real (1,1)-form θ in their common cohomology class and write T = θ + dd^c u and S = θ + dd^c v with u and v θ-plurisubharmonic. Assume u <= v + C on X, i.e. T is more singular than S. If ⟨T^n⟩ and ⟨S^n⟩ denote the non-pluripolar Monge–Ampère products defined by bounded truncation, for example ⟨T^n⟩ = lim_{j→∞} 1_{u>-j}(θ + dd^c max(u,-j))^n, must one always have ⟨T^n⟩ <= ⟨S^n⟩ as positive measures, without assuming that T and S have small unbounded locus?

Let (X, ω) be a compact Kähler manifold, and let ϕ ∈ PSH(X, ω) belong to DMA(X, ω) in the sense of Definition 1.3, so that its complex Monge-Ampère measure (ω + dd^cϕ)^n is well defined by decreasing smooth ω-psh approximation. Assume that this Monge-Ampère measure does not charge the polar set {ϕ = -∞}, i.e. (ω + dd^cϕ)^n({ϕ = -∞}) = 0. Must ϕ belong to the finite-energy/full Monge-Ampère mass class E(X, ω) of Definition 2.2?

Let pi: X -> CP^2 be the blow-up of the complex projective plane at one point, let omega in c_1(X) be a Kahler form, let D in |-K_X| be a smooth anticanonical divisor, and set V := integral_X omega^2. Writing mu_D := V^{-1} omega wedge [D] for the resulting probability measure on D (where [D] is the current of integration along D), does there exist an omega-plurisubharmonic function phi_D on X that belongs to the global domain of definition DMA(X, omega) of the complex Monge-Ampere operator in the sense of Definition 1.3, and whose normalized Monge-Ampere measure satisfies MA(phi_D) = mu_D?

Let Ω ⊂ ℂ^n be a domain, and let μ be a positive Radon measure on Ω. Characterize the measures μ that lie in the range of the Bedford–Taylor complex Monge-Ampère operator on locally bounded plurisubharmonic functions; that is, determine whether there exists a necessary and sufficient uniform integrability condition on μ, analogous in complex dimension 1 to SH(Ω) ⊂ L^1_{loc}(μ), such that μ = (dd^cφ)^n for some φ ∈ PSH(Ω) ∩ L^∞_{loc}(Ω) if and only if μ satisfies that condition.

Let Ω ⊂ C^n be a bounded hyperconvex domain (i.e. Ω admits a negative plurisubharmonic exhaustion), and let μ be a probability measure on Ω. Assume there exists u ∈ PSH(Ω) ∩ C(Ω̄) with u|∂Ω = 0 such that μ ≤ (dd^c u)^n as measures on Ω, where (dd^c u)^n is understood in the Bedford–Taylor sense. Must there exist φ ∈ PSH(Ω) ∩ C(Ω̄) with φ|∂Ω = 0 and (dd^c φ)^n = μ on Ω?

Let (X, ω) be a compact Kähler manifold of complex dimension n, and let V := ∫_X ω^n. Suppose μ is a probability measure on X which is locally dominated by Monge–Ampère measures of bounded plurisubharmonic functions; equivalently, assume there exist u ∈ PSH(X, ω) ∩ L^∞(X) and C > 0 such that μ ≤ C·MA(u), where for bounded ω-plurisubharmonic v one sets MA(v) := V^{-1}(ω + dd^c v)^n. Must there exist φ ∈ PSH(X, ω) ∩ L^∞(X) such that μ = MA(φ)?

Let (X, ω) be a compact Kähler manifold of complex dimension n, let μ be a probability measure on X, let PSH(X, ω) denote the ω-plurisubharmonic functions on X, and let Hol(X, ω) := PSH(X, ω) ∩ Holder(X) be the set of Hölder continuous ω-psh functions. Writing MA(φ) := c(ω + dd^cφ)^n with c = (∫_X ω^n)^(-1), is it true that the following two properties are equivalent: (i) there exists ε_μ > 0 such that e^{-ε_μ ψ} ∈ L^1(μ) for every ψ ∈ PSH(X, ω); and (ii) there exists φ ∈ Hol(X, ω) such that μ = MA(φ)? ([math.univ-toulouse.fr](https://www.math.univ-toulouse.fr/~zeriahi/DGZ-arXiv2015.pdf))

Question 17 (local Hölder subsolution problem). Let Ω ⊂ ℂ^n be a bounded pseudoconvex domain, and let μ be a probability measure on Ω. Suppose there exists a Hölder continuous plurisubharmonic function u ∈ PSH(Ω), with zero boundary values u|∂Ω = 0, such that μ ≤ (dd^c u)^n in Ω, where (dd^c·)^n denotes the local complex Monge–Ampère measure. Must there exist a Hölder continuous plurisubharmonic function φ ∈ PSH(Ω), also with φ|∂Ω = 0, such that μ = (dd^c φ)^n in Ω?

Can one find a proof, using PDE techniques, of the following Kołodziej L^∞ a priori estimate? Let B ⊂ C^n be the unit ball and fix p>1. Suppose φ is plurisubharmonic, smooth on B and continuous on \bar{B}, with φ|_{∂B}=0, and satisfies det(φ_{j\bar{k}})=f in B, where φ_{j\bar{k}}=∂²φ/∂z_j∂\bar{z}_k and f∈L^p(B). Is it possible to prove by PDE methods alone that there exists a constant C=C(n,p)>0 such that ||φ||_{L^∞(B)} ≤ C ||f||_{L^p(B)}^{1/n}?

Let X be a compact n-dimensional Kähler manifold over C, let ω be a semi-positive closed (1,1)-form with V_ω := ∫_X ω^n > 0, fix a volume form dV on X, and let 0 ≤ f ∈ L^p(X,dV) for some p > 1. If φ ∈ PSH(X,ω) satisfies, in the pluripotential sense, (ω + dd^cφ)^n = f dV on X, must φ be globally Hölder continuous on X?

Let (X, ω) be a compact Kähler manifold of complex dimension n, and let S ⊂ X be a smooth totally real submanifold of maximal real dimension n, i.e. T_xS contains no complex line for every x ∈ S. Let μ_S be the normalized n-dimensional Hausdorff measure on S, and let φ_S ∈ E(X, ω) be the unique ω-plurisubharmonic finite-energy function normalized by sup_X φ_S = 0 such that (ω + dd^cφ_S)^n = μ_S. What is the optimal global regularity of φ_S on X? In particular, is φ_S always Lipschitz continuous?

Let X be a compact complex manifold in the Fujiki class, and let α ∈ H^{1,1}(X, R) be a big cohomology class, i.e. a class represented by a Kähler current. Let Amp(α) be its ample locus, namely the set of points x ∈ X for which there exists a Kähler current representing α that is smooth near x. Let μ be a smooth volume form, and let T be the unique finite-energy positive closed (1,1)-current representing α such that ⟨T^n⟩ = μ, where ⟨T^n⟩ denotes the non-pluripolar Monge–Ampère product. Is T smooth in Amp(α)?

Let (X,ω) be a compact Kähler manifold of complex dimension n, let D ⊂ X be a divisor, and let φ ∈ E(X,ω) be an ω-plurisubharmonic finite-energy solution of the complex Monge-Ampère equation (ω + dd^cφ)^n = f ω^n on X, where f ∈ L^1(X,ω^n) and f is C^∞ on X\D. Must φ be C^∞ on X\D? ([math.univ-toulouse.fr](https://www.math.univ-toulouse.fr/~zeriahi/DGZ-arXiv2015.pdf))

Let Ω⊂ℂ^n be a bounded hyperconvex domain, meaning that there exists a negative plurisubharmonic exhaustion ρ on Ω such that {ρ<c} is relatively compact in Ω for every c<0. Let dV denote Lebesgue measure on ℂ^n, and use the paper’s standard normalization dd^c=(i/π)∂∂̄. Suppose u is the unique plurisubharmonic function on Ω that extends continuously to ∂Ω, satisfies u=0 on ∂Ω, and solves (dd^c u)^n=f dV in Ω in the Bedford–Taylor sense, where f is smooth and bounded away from zero (equivalently, f≥ε>0 for some ε>0). Must u be C^∞ on Ω? ([math.univ-toulouse.fr](https://www.math.univ-toulouse.fr/~zeriahi/DGZ-arXiv2015.pdf))

Let Ω ⊂ ℂ^n be a smooth strictly pseudoconvex bounded domain, and let u ∈ PSH(Ω) ∩ C^{1,α}(Ω) with α > 1 - 2/n. Assume that u satisfies the complex Monge–Ampère equation (dd^c u)^n = f dV on Ω in the Bedford–Taylor/pluripotential sense, where dV is the Lebesgue volume measure and f ∈ C^∞(Ω) satisfies f ≥ ε > 0 for some ε. Must it follow that u is smooth on Ω, i.e. u ∈ C^∞(Ω)?

Question 25 (Demailly). Let Ω ⊂ C^n be a smooth strictly pseudoconvex bounded domain, let φ ∈ C^{1,1}(∂Ω), and let u be the unique plurisubharmonic function on Ω that extends continuously to Ω̄, satisfies u|∂Ω = φ, and solves the homogeneous complex Monge–Ampère equation (dd^c u)^n = 0 in Ω. Give a proof, using complex-analytic methods, that u has interior C^{1,1} regularity; equivalently, show that u is C^{1,1} in Ω.

Let Ω ⊂ ℂ^n be a C^{3,1}-smooth strictly pseudoconvex bounded domain, let φ ∈ C^{3,1}(∂Ω), and let u ∈ PSH(Ω) ∩ C(Ω̄) be the unique solution of the Dirichlet problem u = φ on ∂Ω and (dd^c u)^n = f in Ω, where f ≥ 0 and f^{1/n} ∈ C^{1,1}(Ω̄). Krylov’s theorem yields u ∈ C^{1,1}(Ω̄), while Bedford–Fornæss show that these hypotheses do not in general force u ∈ C^2(Ω̄). What are the minimal additional assumptions under which one can guarantee that u belongs to C^2(Ω̄)? ([math.univ-toulouse.fr](https://www.math.univ-toulouse.fr/~zeriahi/DGZ-arXiv2015.pdf))

Let Ω ⊂ ℂ^n be a bounded hyperconvex domain, i.e. there exists a negative plurisubharmonic exhaustion function ρ on Ω such that {ρ < c} is relatively compact in Ω for every c < 0. For each pole w ∈ Ω, define the pluricomplex Green function by g_Ω(z,w) := sup{u(z) : u is plurisubharmonic on Ω, u ≤ 0 on Ω, and u(ζ) ≤ log||ζ−w|| + C_u for all ζ ∈ Ω, for some constant C_u depending on u}. Is it true that g_Ω(·,w) converges to 0 locally uniformly on Ω as w approaches the boundary ∂Ω? ([math.univ-toulouse.fr](https://www.math.univ-toulouse.fr/~zeriahi/DGZ-arXiv2015.pdf))

Does there exist a smoothly bounded strictly pseudoconvex domain Ω ⊂ ℂ^n and a point w ∈ Ω such that the one-pole pluricomplex Green function g_Ω(·,w), defined by g_Ω(z,w)=sup{u(z): u ∈ PSH(Ω), u ≤ 0, and u(s) ≤ log||s−w||+C_u on Ω for some constant C_u}, belongs to C^{1,1}(Ω ∖ {w}) but not to C^2(Ω ∖ {w})?

Let X be a compact complex manifold of complex dimension n ≥ 3, and let ω be the positive (1,1)-form of a Hermitian metric on X (not assumed Kähler). Characterize those Hermitian metrics ω for which the total Monge–Ampère volume is invariant under all bounded ω-plurisubharmonic perturbations, i.e. for which one has ∫_X (ω + dd^c φ)^n = ∫_X ω^n for every bounded upper-semicontinuous function φ on X satisfying ω + dd^c φ ≥ 0 in the sense of currents. ([math.univ-toulouse.fr](https://www.math.univ-toulouse.fr/~zeriahi/DGZ-arXiv2015.pdf))

Let (X, ω) be a compact Hermitian manifold, and set n := dim_C X. Define
T(X, ω) := inf { ∫_X (ω + dd^cφ)^n : φ ∈ C^∞(X) and ω + dd^cφ ≥ 0 }.
Equivalently, the infimum is over smooth ω-plurisubharmonic functions φ ∈ C^∞(X) ∩ PSH(X, ω). Is it possible that T(X, ω) = 0 for some compact Hermitian manifold (X, ω)?

Let (X, ω) be a compact Hermitian manifold, where ω is the positive (1,1)-form of a Hermitian metric and n = dim_C X. Write PSH(X, ω) for the ω-plurisubharmonic functions, i.e. the upper-semicontinuous functions φ on X such that ω + dd^cφ ≥ 0 in the sense of currents. Define
cap(X, ω) := inf{∫_X (ω + dd^cφ)^n : φ ∈ PSH(X, ω), 0 ≤ φ ≤ 1 on X}.
How is cap(X, ω) related to the geometry of the Hermitian pair (X, ω)? In particular, is cap(X, ω) computable in terms of geometric data of (X, ω), and how does it vary under deformations of the Hermitian manifold/form?

Let (X, omega) be a compact Hermitian manifold of complex dimension n, let p > 1, and let 0 != f,g >= 0 belong to L^p(X, omega^n). Suppose u,v in PSH(X, omega) cap C(X) are normalized by sup_X u = sup_X v = 0 and satisfy (omega + dd^c u)^n = f omega^n and (omega + dd^c v)^n = g omega^n, where the extra Hermitian normalizing constants have been absorbed into f and g. Theorem 4.3 proves that if, in addition, f >= c_0 > 0, then for every 0 < alpha < 1/(n+1) one has a stability estimate of the form ||u - v||_infty <= C ||f - g||_p^alpha. Can the hypothesis f >= c_0 > 0 be removed, i.e. does the same L^infty-L^p stability estimate remain valid for arbitrary nonnegative nonzero f,g in L^p(X, omega^n)?

Let (X,ω) be a compact complex manifold of complex dimension n, equipped with a Hermitian metric form ω (so X is not assumed Kähler). Given points z_1, ..., z_k ∈ X and positive numbers τ_1, ..., τ_k satisfying Σ_{j=1}^k τ_j^n < ∫_X ω^n, can one construct a function φ ∈ PSH(X,ω) (equivalently, ω + dd^cφ ≥ 0 in the sense of currents) such that, in local holomorphic coordinates centered at each z_j, one has φ(z) ≤ τ_j log ||z - z_j|| + O(1) as z → z_j for every j = 1, ..., k? ([math.univ-toulouse.fr](https://www.math.univ-toulouse.fr/~zeriahi/DGZ-arXiv2015.pdf))

Let (X, omega) be a compact complex Hermitian manifold of complex dimension n >= 3, and let varphi be a quasi-plurisubharmonic function on X such that T := omega + dd^c varphi is a positive closed (1,1)-current. Is it true that for every epsilon > 0 there exists a finite composition of blow-ups pi_epsilon : X_epsilon -> X such that
pi_epsilon^* T = [D_epsilon] + R_epsilon,
where [D_epsilon] is the current of integration along a simple normal crossing divisor D_epsilon with coefficients in R_+, and R_epsilon is a positive (1,1)-current satisfying nu(R_epsilon, x) < epsilon for all x in X_epsilon?

Let Omega subset C^n be a bounded hyperconvex domain, let phi belong to the Cegrell class F(Omega), let delta_Omega denote the Euclidean diameter of Omega, and define lambda by lambda^n := integral_Omega (dd^c phi)^n. Does there exist a possibly different constant c_n, depending only on n, such that for every s > 0 one has Vol({z in Omega : phi(z) < -s}) <= c_n delta_Omega^(2n) exp(-2ns/lambda), where Vol denotes Lebesgue volume on C^n?

Let X be a compact Kähler manifold, or more generally a compact complex manifold in the Fujiki class, of complex dimension n, and let ω be a smooth semi-positive big (1,1)-form, meaning ∫_X ω^n > 0. For φ ∈ PSH(X,ω), write V := ∫_X ω^n and MA(φ) := V^{-1}⟨(ω+dd^cφ)^n⟩, where ⟨(ω+dd^cφ)^n⟩ denotes the non-pluripolar Monge-Ampère product; define the finite-energy class E(X,ω) := {φ ∈ PSH(X,ω) : MA(φ) is a probability measure}. If φ ∈ E(X,ω), is it true that the Lelong number ν(φ,x) vanishes for every x ∈ X? ([math.univ-toulouse.fr](https://www.math.univ-toulouse.fr/~zeriahi/DGZ-arXiv2015.pdf))

Let (X, ω) be a compact Kähler manifold and let Y ⊂ X be a complex submanifold. Is the restriction map res_Y: PSH(X, ω) → PSH(Y, ω|_Y), U ↦ U|_Y, surjective? Equivalently, does every upper-semicontinuous function u: Y → [-∞, +∞), not identically -∞, satisfying ω|_Y + dd^c u ≥ 0 on Y in the sense of currents, admit an extension U ∈ PSH(X, ω) with U|_Y = u?

Let π:X→Δ be a proper holomorphic submersion onto a complex disc Δ, with fibers X_t:=π^−1(t) compact Kähler manifolds, and let L→X be a pseudoeffective holomorphic line bundle. Set L_t:=L|X_t. Assume that on the central fiber X₀ the restricted line bundle L₀ carries a singular Hermitian metric h₀=e^−φ₀ whose curvature current is semipositive, i.e. dd^cφ₀≥0 on X₀ in the weak sense of currents. Must there exist a singular Hermitian metric h=e^−φ on L over X such that dd^cφ≥0 on X in the weak sense of currents and φ|X₀=φ₀? citeturn8view0

Let Ω \subset \mathbb{C}^n be a bounded pseudoconvex domain, and let φ ∈ PSH(Ω). For z ∈ Ω, say that φ admits a differential test from above at z if there exist a neighborhood V of z and a C^2-smooth function q on V such that (φ - q)(z) = sup_V (φ - q). If E_φ := { z ∈ Ω : φ does not admit a differential test from above at z }, what can be said about E_φ? In particular, although E_φ is known to have empty interior, must E_φ have zero Lebesgue measure, or even zero capacity?

Let Ω ⊂ ℂ^n be a bounded pseudoconvex domain, let f ≥ 0 be a continuous density, and let dV denote the Euclidean Lebesgue measure. Suppose v: Ω → ℝ is continuous and is a viscosity supersolution of -(dd^c v)^n + f dV = 0 in the sense that for every x ∈ Ω and every C^2 function q defined near x with (v - q)(x) = inf(v - q) near x, one has -(dd^c q(x))^n/dV + f(x) ≥ 0. If P(v) := (sup{ψ ∈ PSH(Ω) : ψ ≤ v})* is the plurisubharmonic envelope of v, must P(v) be a Bedford–Taylor pluripotential supersolution of the same equation, i.e. must it satisfy (dd^c P(v))^n ≤ f dV on Ω in the pluripotential sense?

Let X be a compact Kähler manifold of complex dimension n, and let ω be a smooth semipositive big (1,1)-form on X, meaning that ∫_X ω^n > 0. For every ω-plurisubharmonic function φ ∈ PSH(X, ω), equivalently satisfying ω + dd^c φ ≥ 0 in the sense of currents, does there exist a sequence (φ_j)_{j≥1} with φ_j ∈ C^∞(X) ∩ PSH(X, ω) for all j such that φ_j decreases pointwise on X to φ?

Let X be a compact Kähler manifold, let α ∈ H^{1,1}(X, R) be a big cohomology class, and fix a smooth closed (1,1)-form θ ∈ α. Define the canonical θ-plurisubharmonic envelope with minimal singularities by V_θ := sup{v ∈ PSH(X, θ) : sup_X v ≤ 0}. Set P(α) := {x ∈ X : V_θ(x) = -∞} and NB(α) := {x ∈ X : V_θ is not locally bounded near x} (equivalently, V_θ ∉ L^∞_loc at x). Is it always true that P(α) = NB(α)?

Let X be a compact Kähler manifold, let alpha_0 in H^{1,1}(X, R) be a Kähler cohomology class, and let S_0 be a positive closed (1,1)-current representing alpha_0. Consider the Kähler–Ricci flow starting at S_0, namely a family (omega_t)_{0 < t < T_max} satisfying d/dt omega_t = -Ric(omega_t), omega_t -> S_0 weakly as t -> 0, and T_max = sup{ t >= 0 | t K_X + alpha_0 is Kähler }. When S_0 has some nonzero Lelong numbers, DiNezza and Lu construct a maximal family of positive currents (omega_t)_{0 < t < T_max} that are honest Kähler forms on time-increasing Zariski open subsets Omega_t where they satisfy the flow equation. Is it true that, for every t in (0, T_max), the current omega_t has analytic singularities in the sense that its local potentials are of the form (c/2) log(sum_j |f_j|^2) + v with c > 0, v smooth, and the f_j holomorphic; equivalently, does the Kähler–Ricci flow itself provide analytic-singularity approximants of S_0 as t -> 0^+? ([math.univ-toulouse.fr](https://www.math.univ-toulouse.fr/~zeriahi/DGZ-arXiv2015.pdf))

Let Ω ⊂ C^n be a bounded smooth strictly pseudoconvex domain, let T > 0, and consider the parabolic Dirichlet problem ∂_t u = log det(u_{α\barβ}) on Ω × (0,T), with boundary condition u = φ on ∂Ω × (0,T), where φ ∈ C^∞(Ω̄ × [0,T)) satisfies φ(z,t) = u0(z) for z ∈ ∂Ω. Do's Theorem 6.5 shows that if u0 is a bounded plurisubharmonic function on a neighborhood of Ω̄, then there exists a unique solution u ∈ C^∞(Ω̄ × (0,T)) such that each time slice u_t is strictly plurisubharmonic in Ω and u_t converges to u0 as t → 0 (indeed pointwise on Ω̄ and in capacity). Does this theorem extend to the case where the initial datum u0 is an arbitrary plurisubharmonic function, i.e. can one run the same local complex Monge-Ampère flow from arbitrary possibly singular/unbounded psh initial data?

Let X be a compact Kähler space, let T∈(0,+∞], and set X_T=[0,T)×X. Consider the degenerate complex Monge–Ampère flow (ω_t+dd^cφ_t)^n=exp(∂_tφ(t,x)+F(t,x,φ(t,x)))μ(t,x) on X_T, where ω_t=ω(t,·) is a continuous family of semi-positive and big (1,1)-forms on X satisfying ω_t≥θ for some fixed semi-positive and big (1,1)-form θ, F:[0,T)×X×R→R is continuous and nondecreasing in its last variable, μ(t,x)≥0 is a bounded continuous volume form, and φ_t:=φ(t,·). Does the following comparison principle hold: if u is a bounded upper semicontinuous viscosity subsolution and v is a bounded lower semicontinuous viscosity supersolution of this flow on X_T, with u≤v on the parabolic boundary {0}×X, must one have u≤v on all of X_T? ([math.univ-toulouse.fr](https://www.math.univ-toulouse.fr/~zeriahi/DGZ-arXiv2015.pdf))

Let G ≅ C_{n1} ⊕ ··· ⊕ C_{nr} be a finite abelian group with |G| ≥ 3 and 1 < n1 | ··· | nr, and let ℒ(G) = ℒ(B(G)) be the system of sets of lengths of the block monoid B(G) of zero-sum sequences over G. For a finite set L = {m1 < ··· < mk} ⊂ N, define Δ(L) = {m_i - m_{i-1} : 2 ≤ i ≤ k}, and set Δ(G) = ⋃_{L ∈ ℒ(G)} Δ(L). Is it true that max Δ(G) = max{nr - 2, -1 + Σ_{i=1}^r ⌊ni/2⌋}?

For every integer M in N, does there exist a finite abelian group G such that, for every finite nonempty set L \subseteq N_{>=2} with max L - min L <= M, one has L in L(G); equivalently, for every such L there exists a zero-sum sequence B in the block monoid B(G) whose set of factorization lengths is exactly L?

Let G be a finite abelian group with |G|≥3, set n=exp(G) and r=r(G), and let k be maximal such that G contains a subgroup isomorphic to C_n^k. Define Δ*(G)={min Δ(G0): G0⊂G and Δ(G0)≠∅}, where Δ(G0) is the set of distances of the monoid B(G0) of zero-sum sequences over G0. Is it true that Δ*(G) is an interval if and only if either r+k≥n−1, or r+k=n−2 and G≅C_{2r+2}^r?

For a finite abelian group G, let B(G) be the block monoid of zero-sum sequences over G and write L(G)=L(B(G)). Define M_G to be the smallest integer M≥0 such that every set L∈L(G) can be written in the almost arithmetic multiprogression form L=y+(L'∪L*∪L'')⊂y+D+dZ for some d∈Δ*(G), some period D with {0,d}⊂D⊂[0,d], some m≥0 with L*=[0,m]∩(D+dZ), and end pieces L'⊂[-M,-1], L''⊂m+[1,M]. What is the rough asymptotic order of M_G as a function of the Davenport constant D(G)? More specifically, between the explicit general upper bound supplied by Theorem 6.22 and the quadratic lower bound exhibited in Example 6.23, what is the true order of magnitude of the STSL bound for L(G) as D(G)→∞? ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1511.08080))

Let q be a scalar that is not a root of unity, write [X,Y]_q = qXY - q^{-1}YX, and fix scalars k_+, k_-, epsilon_+, epsilon_- with rho = (q + q^{-1})^2 k_+ k_-. Let O_q be the q-Onsager algebra generated by W_0 and W_1 subject to [W_0,[W_0,[W_0,W_1]_q]_{q^{-1}}] = rho[W_0,W_1] and [W_1,[W_1,[W_1,W_0]_q]_{q^{-1}}] = rho[W_1,W_0]. Let A_q be the Baseilhac-Koizumi current algebra generated by {W_{-k}, W_{k+1}, G_{k+1}, tilde G_{k+1} | k in Z_+} with its defining relations, so that its first modes W_0 and W_1 satisfy the same q-Dolan-Grady relations. Let B be the coideal subalgebra of U_q(\widehat{sl}_2) obtained, for the coproduct choice used in the paper, as the image of the homomorphism O_q -> U_q(\widehat{sl}_2) given by W_0 -> k_+ e_1 + k_- q^{-1} f_1 q^{h_1} + epsilon_+ q^{h_1} and W_1 -> k_- e_0 + k_+ q^{-1} f_0 q^{h_0} + epsilon_- q^{h_0}. Prove that A_q, O_q, and B are mutually isomorphic as algebras; equivalently at the level of the intended identifications, prove that A_q gives a second presentation of O_q and that the displayed homomorphism is an algebra isomorphism from O_q onto B.

Let \Bbb F be a field containing q, \epsilon_+, \epsilon_- and assume that q is not a root of unity. Write [X,Y]_q = qXY - q^{-1}YX. Let \mathcal O_q^{\mathrm{aug}} be the augmented q-Onsager algebra generated by K_0, K_1, Z_1, \widetilde Z_1 subject to
[K_0,K_1]=0,
K_0Z_1=q^{-2}Z_1K_0,\quad K_0\widetilde Z_1=q^2\widetilde Z_1K_0,\quad K_1Z_1=q^2Z_1K_1,\quad K_1\widetilde Z_1=q^{-2}\widetilde Z_1K_1,
and
[Z_1,[Z_1,[Z_1,\widetilde Z_1]_q]_{q^{-1}}]=\frac{(q^3-q^{-3})(q^2-q^{-2})^3}{q-q^{-1}}\,Z_1(K_1^2-K_0^2)Z_1,
[\widetilde Z_1,[\widetilde Z_1,[\widetilde Z_1,Z_1]_q]_{q^{-1}}]=\frac{(q^3-q^{-3})(q^2-q^{-2})^3}{q-q^{-1}}\,\widetilde Z_1(K_0^2-K_1^2)\widetilde Z_1.
Let A_q^{\mathrm{diag}} denote the current algebra obtained from the quotient of the reflection equation algebra described immediately before Problem 1-b, generated by its current modes K_\bullet, Z_{\bullet}, \widetilde Z_{\bullet} in the paper's notation. Let B_{\epsilon_+,\epsilon_-}^{\mathrm{diag}}\subset U_q(\widehat{\mathfrak{sl}}_2) be the coideal subalgebra generated by the image of the homomorphism
K_0\mapsto \epsilon_+ q^{h_1},\qquad K_1\mapsto \epsilon_- q^{h_0},
Z_1\mapsto (q^2-q^{-2})(\epsilon_+ q^{-1}e_0 q^{h_1}+\epsilon_- f_1 q^{h_1+h_0}),
\widetilde Z_1\mapsto (q^2-q^{-2})(\epsilon_- q^{-1}e_1 q^{h_0}+\epsilon_+ f_0 q^{h_1+h_0}),
with the same coproduct convention as in the paper. Prove that A_q^{\mathrm{diag}}, \mathcal O_q^{\mathrm{aug}}, and B_{\epsilon_+,\epsilon_-}^{\mathrm{diag}} are pairwise isomorphic as associative algebras, and determine explicit polynomial formulas expressing the current generators of A_q^{\mathrm{diag}} in terms of K_0, K_1, Z_1, \widetilde Z_1 (equivalently, the polynomial relations implementing the identification of A_q^{\mathrm{diag}} with \mathcal O_q^{\mathrm{aug}}).

Let q be not a root of unity and write [X,Y]_q = qXY - q^{-1}YX. Let the augmented q-Onsager algebra be generated by K_0, K_1, Z_1, and tilde Z_1 subject to [K_0,K_1]=0, K_0 Z_1=q^{-2} Z_1 K_0, K_0 tilde Z_1=q^{2} tilde Z_1 K_0, K_1 Z_1=q^{2} Z_1 K_1, K_1 tilde Z_1=q^{-2} tilde Z_1 K_1, [Z_1,[Z_1,[Z_1,tilde Z_1]_q]_{q^{-1}}]=((q^3-q^{-3})(q^2-q^{-2})^3/(q-q^{-1})) Z_1 (K_1^2-K_0^2) Z_1, and [tilde Z_1,[tilde Z_1,[tilde Z_1,Z_1]_q]_{q^{-1}}]=((q^3-q^{-3})(q^2-q^{-2})^3/(q-q^{-1})) tilde Z_1 (K_0^2-K_1^2) tilde Z_1. Let A_q^{diag} be the infinite-dimensional current algebra obtained from the quotient of the reflection equation algebra considered in the paper, with the slight restriction on the Sklyanin-operator power-series expansion noted in footnote 2. For U_q(\widehat{sl}_2) with Chevalley generators {e_i,f_i,q^{h_i}}_{i=0,1} and scalars epsilon_+, epsilon_-, consider the homomorphism K_0 -> epsilon_+ q^{h_1}, K_1 -> epsilon_- q^{h_0}, Z_1 -> (q^2-q^{-2})(epsilon_+ q^{-1} e_0 q^{h_1} + epsilon_- f_1 q^{h_1+h_0}), tilde Z_1 -> (q^2-q^{-2})(epsilon_- q^{-1} e_1 q^{h_0} + epsilon_+ f_0 q^{h_1+h_0}). Show that A_q^{diag}, the augmented q-Onsager algebra, and the resulting coideal subalgebra of U_q(\widehat{sl}_2) are isomorphic, and determine explicit polynomial formulae relating the current modes of A_q^{diag} to K_0, K_1, Z_1, and tilde Z_1.

Assume q is not a root of unity. Let A_q^{diag} be the current algebra obtained from a certain quotient of the reflection equation algebra, and let A_q^{[2N+1]} denote the quotient of A_q^{diag} by the q-analogues of Davies' relations arising on finite-dimensional irreducible A_q^{diag}-modules, i.e. by relations asserting that certain polynomials in the q-Onsager generators W_0 and W_1 of total degree 2N + 1 vanish on the module. Since A_q^{[3]} is isomorphic to the Askey-Wilson algebra AW(3) when N = 1, and AW(3) admits a homomorphism to the double affine Hecke algebra of type C_1, C_1^∨, does there exist a homomorphism from A_q^{[2N+1]} to an algebra generalizing the double affine Hecke algebra of type C_1, C_1^∨? ([ems.press](https://ems.press/content/serial-article-files/46556))

Fix a positive integer N and a nonzero scalar q that is not a root of unity. Let A_q^{diag} denote the current algebra associated in the paper with the augmented q-Onsager algebra, and let W_0,W_1 be the standard q-Onsager generators satisfying the q-Dolan/Grady relations. Following the paper, let A_q^{[2N+1]} denote the quotient of A_q^{diag} by the q-analogues of Davies' relations, that is, by the relations asserting that certain polynomials of total degree 2N+1 in W_0 and W_1 vanish on finite-dimensional irreducible modules. Classify, up to isomorphism, the finite-dimensional irreducible A_q^{[2N+1]}-modules.

Assume q is not a root of unity. Let A_q^{diag} be the current algebra obtained from the quotient of the reflection equation algebra considered in the note, and for each relevant N let A_q^{[2N+1]} be the quotient of A_q^{diag} by the q-analogues of Davies' relations, namely by those relations coming from certain polynomials of total degree 2N+1 in W_0 and W_1 that vanish on finite-dimensional irreducible modules (with A_q^{[3]} isomorphic to AW(3) when N = 1). Classify the finite-dimensional irreducible modules of A_q^{[2N+1]}, and, within that classification, study in detail the finite-dimensional modules associated with the Gasper-Rahman multivariable polynomials cited in the paper as providing an infinite-dimensional basis of the q-Onsager algebra.

Let G be a finite abelian group of order n, written additively, let p be the smallest prime divisor of n, and let h,m be positive integers such that m <= p < hm-h+1. For an m-subset A of G, write hA = {a1+...+ah : a1,...,ah in A}. Since Proposition 1.2 gives rho(G,m,h) = min{p, hm-h+1} = p in this range, is it true that an m-subset A satisfies |hA| = p if and only if A is contained in a coset a+H of some subgroup H <= G with |H| = p?

Let G be a finite abelian group of order n, let p be the smallest prime divisor of n, and let m and h be positive integers with h ≥ 2, m ≤ p, and p = hm - h + 1. For an m-subset A ⊆ G, define hA = {a1 + ··· + ah : a1,...,ah ∈ A} and ρ(G,m,h) = min{|hB| : B ⊆ G, |B| = m}. Since Proposition 1.2 gives ρ(G,m,h) = p in this boundary case, classify all m-subsets A ⊆ G for which |hA| = ρ(G,m,h) = p; equivalently, determine all extremal sets in this remaining case, not only the known examples consisting of arithmetic progressions of length m and subsets contained in a coset a + H of a subgroup H ≤ G with |H| = p.

Let G be a finite abelian group of order n, written additively, let p be the smallest prime divisor of n, and for positive integers m and h define rho_hat(G,m,h) := min{|h^∧A| : A ⊆ G, |A| = m}, where h^∧A is the set of all sums of h distinct elements of A. Is it true that for every pair of integers h and m with h < m <= p, one has rho_hat(G,m,h) = min{p, hm - h^2 + 1}?

Let G be a finite abelian group of order n, written additively, let p be the smallest prime divisor of n, and let A \subseteq G be an m-element subset. Define the h-fold restricted sumset by \hat{h}A = {a_1+\cdots+a_h : a_1,\dots,a_h \in A are pairwise distinct}. Assume 2 <= h <= m - 2 and p > hm - h^2 + 1. Is it true that |\hat{h}A| = hm - h^2 + 1 if and only if either (i) h = 2, m = 4, and A = {a, a+g_1, a+g_2, a+g_1+g_2} for some a, g_1, g_2 \in G, or (ii) A is an arithmetic progression in G (that is, A = {a, a+d, ..., a+(m-1)d} with m distinct terms)?

Let G be a finite abelian group of order n, written additively, let p be the smallest prime divisor of n, let h and m be positive integers with m ≤ p < hm - h^2 + 1, and for each m-subset A ⊆ G define the h-fold restricted sumset by \hat{h}A := {a_1+\cdots+a_h : a_1,\ldots,a_h \in A are pairwise distinct}. Is it true that, for every m-subset A of G, one has |\hat{h}A| = p if and only if A is contained in a coset x+H of some subgroup H ≤ G with |H| = p? ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1512.03038))

Let G be a finite abelian group of order n. For each integer m with 1 ≤ m ≤ n, define ρ(G,m,2)=min{|2A|: A⊆G, |A|=m}, where 2A={a+b: a,b∈A}, and define ρ_{±}(G,m,2)=min{|2_{±}A|: A⊆G, |A|=m}, where for A={a_1,...,a_m} one sets 2_{±}A={∑_{i=1}^m λ_i a_i : λ_i∈Z, ∑_{i=1}^m |λ_i|=2}. Is it true that, for every such G, the set {m∈{1,...,n}: ρ_{±}(G,m,2)≠ρ(G,m,2)} has cardinality strictly less than n/4?

Let \mathbb{Z}_n be the cyclic group of order n, written additively. For a subset A\subseteq \mathbb{Z}_n, define the restricted three-fold sumset by 3^\wedge A:=\{a_1+a_2+a_3:\ a_1,a_2,a_3\in A\text{ are pairwise distinct}\}, and let \widehat{\chi}(\mathbb{Z}_n,3) denote the least integer m such that 3^\wedge A=\mathbb{Z}_n for every m-element subset A\subseteq \mathbb{Z}_n. For the remaining unresolved odd composite cases (equivalently, for every n\ge 15 in the paper’s conjectural formulation), are the lower bounds from Section 0.6 always exact? That is: if n has a prime divisor congruent to 2 mod 3 and p is the smallest such prime, must one have \widehat{\chi}(\mathbb{Z}_n,3)=((1+1/p)n/3)+3 when n=p, \widehat{\chi}(\mathbb{Z}_n,3)=((1+1/p)n/3)+2 when n=3p, and \widehat{\chi}(\mathbb{Z}_n,3)=((1+1/p)n/3)+1 otherwise; and if n has no prime divisor congruent to 2 mod 3, must one have \widehat{\chi}(\mathbb{Z}_n,3)=\lfloor n/3\rfloor+4 when 9\mid n and \widehat{\chi}(\mathbb{Z}_n,3)=\lfloor n/3\rfloor+3 otherwise?

Let A be a finite alphabet, and let x be a recurrent sequence (that is, every finite block occurring in x occurs infinitely often), either one-sided x∈A^N or two-sided x∈A^Z. For n≥1 define its maximal pattern complexity by p_x^*(n)=sup_{0=τ(0)<...<τ(n−1)} #{x_{m+τ(0)}x_{m+τ(1)}...x_{m+τ(n−1)} : m∈Z}, with the natural one-sided modification m∈N when x∈A^N. A sequence x is called pattern Sturmian if p_x^*(n)=2n for every n≥1. Determine all one-sided and two-sided sequences x that are pattern Sturmian. ([eprints.whiterose.ac.uk](https://eprints.whiterose.ac.uk/id/eprint/109936/8/art3A1010072Fs40598_016_0046_6.pdf))

Let x=(x_m)_{m∈ℤ}∈{0,1}^ℤ be a two-sided recurrent pattern Sturmian sequence, meaning that its maximal pattern complexity satisfies p*(n):=sup_{0=τ(0)<⋯<τ(n−1)} #{x_{m+τ(0)}⋯x_{m+τ(n−1)}: m∈ℤ}=2n for every n≥1. For λ∈ℂ, define the discrete Schrödinger operator H on ℓ²(ℤ) by [Hψ](m)=ψ(m+1)+ψ(m−1)+λx_mψ(m). Must the spectrum σ(H) be a zero Lebesgue measure Cantor set, and must every spectral measure of H be singular continuous?

Consider the graph (V,E) corresponding to the Penrose tiling, where V is the vertex set and E is the set of edges. Define an operator H on the Hilbert space l^2(V) by
[Hψ](v)=∑_{w:(v,w)∈E}(ψ(w)-ψ(v))
for every ψ∈l^2(V) and every v∈V. Determine the spectrum σ(H) of H.

Let γ=(√5-1)/2, let {x} denote the fractional part of x, and let χ_[1-γ,1) be the indicator of the interval [1-γ,1). For parameters λ_1,λ_2 ∈ ℂ, define s_j^{λ_j}:ℤ→ℂ by s_j^{λ_j}(k)=λ_jχ_[1-γ,1)({kγ}) for j∈{1,2}. Set V:ℤ^2→ℂ by V(m,n)=s_1^{λ_1}(m)+s_2^{λ_2}(n), and define H:ℓ^2(ℤ^2)→ℓ^2(ℤ^2) by [Hψ](m,n)=ψ(m+1,n)+ψ(m-1,n)+ψ(m,n+1)+ψ(m,n-1)+V(m,n)ψ(m,n). Does there exist a choice of λ_1,λ_2 ∈ ℂ such that the spectrum σ(H) is a Cantorval, that is, σ(H) is the closure of its interior and no connected component of σ(H) is isolated?

Is it true that every one-dimensional self-similar inflation tiling with Pisot scaling factor λ—where λ is a real algebraic integer greater than 1 and all of whose conjugates have modulus less than 1—has pure point dynamical spectrum whenever its abelianisation (substitution) matrix M has irreducible characteristic polynomial, equivalently whenever deg_Q(λ) = dim M, i.e. the number of tile types?

Is the Homological Pisot Conjecture true: for every one-dimensional unimodular Pisot inflation tiling T with expansion factor λ, where λ is a Pisot number, if the first rational Čech cohomology group of the corresponding tiling space has rank equal to the algebraic degree of λ, then must the associated tiling dynamical system have pure point dynamical spectrum?

Let T be a one-dimensional Pisot inflation tiling with scaling factor λ, where λ > 1 is a real algebraic integer all of whose Galois conjugates have modulus less than 1. If cr(T) denotes the almost-everywhere multiplicity of the factor map from the tiling dynamical system of T to its maximal equicontinuous factor, must cr(T) divide the algebraic norm N_{Q(λ)/Q}(λ) of λ (equivalently, its absolute value)?

Let P be any Pinwheel Tiling of R^2 by congruent copies of the right triangle with side lengths 1, 2, and sqrt(5), and let Lambda be the associated set of reference points obtained by placing one point at (1/2, 1/2) in tile coordinates based at the right-angled vertex of each tile. Form the uniform Dirac comb omega = sum_{x in Lambda} delta_x, and let gamma-hat be its diffraction measure, i.e. the Fourier transform of the autocorrelation of omega. Since gamma-hat is circularly symmetric and its only planar pure point atom is the trivial one at the origin, determine the nontrivial sharp rings of gamma-hat: identify the radii r > 0 for which gamma-hat has a ring component supported on the circle {k in R^2 : |k| = r}, and determine the corresponding ring intensities.

Let μ be the diffraction measure on R^2 of the uniform Dirac comb obtained from a Pinwheel tiling by placing one unit point mass at a fixed reference point in each triangular tile (for example, at (1/2, 1/2) relative to the right-angled corner). The paper notes that μ is the Fourier transform of the autocorrelation, is circularly symmetric, has only the trivial pure point mass at the origin, and is otherwise continuous. Does μ contain any absolutely continuous component? ([link.springer.com](https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s40598-016-0046-6))

Let T be an aperiodic, repetitive tiling of dimension d≥1, let Ω be its tiling space, and let p(n) denote the number of patches of radius n in T up to translation. Is it true that p(n)=O(n^d) implies rk(H^*(Ω, Q))<∞?

Let D be a Delone set in R^2, meaning a uniformly discrete and relatively dense subset of the plane, and assume that D is bi-Lipschitz equivalent to Z^2, i.e. there exists a bi-Lipschitz bijection f:D->Z^2. Must there exist a bi-Lipschitz map L:R^2->R^2 such that L(D)=Z^2?

For a strengthened geometric property P of tilings or patterns in R^d, modeled on properties such as bounded-displacement equivalence to a lattice, bi-Lipschitz equivalence to a lattice, or linear repetitivity, classify those tilings T for which every tiling T' that is mutually locally derivable from T, or whose tiling space is topologically conjugate to, or homeomorphic with, the tiling space of T, also satisfies P.

Can one develop and study new geometric properties of tilings or patterns—analogous, but not identical, to bounded-displacement (BD), bi-Lipschitz (BL), and related geometric notions—such that these properties are invariant under mutual local derivability (MLD) and under topological conjugacy or homeomorphism of the associated tiling spaces, in the sense that equivalent tilings share the property? ([eprints.whiterose.ac.uk](https://eprints.whiterose.ac.uk/109936/8/art3A1010072Fs40598_016_0046_6.pdf))

Find a local set of matching rules for tilings of R^2 or R^3 such that, for every admissible tiling defined by those rules, every tile type t has a well-defined density d(t) and satisfies the low-fluctuation estimate |N_t(R)-d(t)vol(R)| <= c_t|∂R| for every region R that is a finite union of tiles, where c_t depends only on t; and such that, for every admissible finite patch P satisfying the same rules, the analogous discrepancy bound |N_P(R)-d(P)vol(R)| <= c_P|∂R| holds for every such region R, where N_P(R) counts occurrences of P wholly contained in R, d(P) is the density of P, vol(R) is Euclidean area/volume, and |∂R| is boundary measure. ([eprints.whiterose.ac.uk](https://eprints.whiterose.ac.uk/109936/8/art3A1010072Fs40598_016_0046_6.pdf))

Find a set of local matching rules in dimension 2, defining tilings with well-defined tile densities d(t), such that for every tile type t there exists a constant c_t depending only on t with the property that, for every region R consisting of a finite union of tiles in any tiling admitted by the rules, one has D_t(R):=|N_t(R)-d(t)vol(R)| <= c_t|∂R|, where N_t(R) is the number of tiles of type t in R and |∂R| is the measure of the boundary of R.

Let d >= 1 be a fixed integer, and let Cl(R^d) denote the compact metric space of closed subsets of R^d endowed with the Chabauty-Fell topology. The groups SL_d(R) and ASL_d(R) act on Cl(R^d) by transport of closed sets: for g acting on R^d and F in Cl(R^d), set g.F = {g(x) : x in F}. Classify all Borel probability measures on Cl(R^d) that are invariant under the action of SL_d(R), and separately classify all Borel probability measures on Cl(R^d) that are invariant under the action of ASL_d(R), where SL_d(R) is the group of volume- and orientation-preserving linear transformations of R^d and ASL_d(R) is the group of volume- and orientation-preserving affine maps of R^d.

Let E⊂R^k be a totally irrational d-dimensional subspace (equivalently, its image in R^k/Z^k is dense), let F be a complementary subspace of dimension k-d with R^k=E⊕F, and let π_E:R^k→E and π_F:R^k→F be the associated projections. For a bounded window W⊂F with non-empty interior and with (k-d)-dimensional Lebesgue measure m_{k-d}(∂W)=0, define the cut-and-project set Y={π_E(n): n∈Z^k, π_F(n)∈W}. Is Y necessarily bi-Lipschitz equivalent to some full-rank lattice Λ⊂E, i.e. must there always exist a bi-Lipschitz bijection Y→Λ, without imposing any further Diophantine hypothesis on E?

Let u be a Leray–Hopf weak solution of the three-dimensional incompressible Navier–Stokes equations on R^3×(0,T] (with zero external force and unit viscosity), and let ω=∇×u. Suppose that there exist β∈(0,1/2) and c>0 such that sin(∠(ω(x,t),ω(y,t)))≤c|x−y|^β for all x,y∈R^3 and t∈(0,T). Does this geometric assumption alone force a genuine gain of spacetime integrability beyond the formal weak-solution threshold, in the sense that there exist exponents s and q such that u∈L^s(0,T;L^q(R^3)) and 2/s+3/q<3/2? ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1604.08083))

Let u be a Leray-Hopf weak solution of the three-dimensional incompressible Navier-Stokes equations on R^3 x (0,T], and let omega = curl u. Assume that u satisfies a classical Ladyzhenskaya-Prodi-Serrin regularity condition
u in L^s(0,T;L^q(R^3)), with 2 <= s < infinity, 3 < q <= infinity, and 2/s + 3/q = 1.
Does such a regularity assumption on u force any corresponding regularity of the direction of the vorticity, in the specific sense used in the paper—namely, does it imply for some beta > 0 a pointwise angle estimate of the form sin(angle(omega(x,t),omega(y,t))) <= C|x-y|^beta for almost every x,y in R^3 and t in (0,T) where the directions are defined—or should one instead expect that no clean general converse from a Serrin condition on u to regularity of the direction of omega exists?

Let X be a smooth complex projective variety of dimension n over C, let A be an ample divisor on X, let P be an arbitrary divisor, let B be a fixed divisor (equivalently, line bundle), and for each sufficiently large integer d set L_d = dA + P, assuming L_d is very ample. Let S_d = Sym H^0(X,L_d), let R(X,B;L_d) = direct sum over m>=0 of H^0(X, B + mL_d), and let K_{p,q}(X,B;L_d) denote the Koszul cohomology groups of this graded S_d-module. Fix an integer q with 2 <= q <= n. Does there exist a constant C_3 = C_3(X,A,B,P) such that, for all sufficiently large integers d, one has K_{p,q}(X,B;L_d) = 0 for every integer p <= C_3 d^(q-1)?

Over C, fix integers n >= 1, b >= 0, 0 <= q <= n, and d >= b + q + 1. Let K_{p,q}(n,b;d) := K_{p,q}(P^n, O_{P^n}(b); O_{P^n}(d)), where K_{p,q} denotes the p-th Koszul cohomology group of weight q, equivalently the space of degree-(p+q) minimal generators in the p-th module of the minimal graded free resolution of R(P^n, O_{P^n}(b); O_{P^n}(d)) over S = Sym H^0(P^n, O_{P^n}(d)). Theorem 2.1 proves that K_{p,q}(n,b;d) != 0 whenever binom(d+q,q) - binom(d-b-1,q) - q <= p <= binom(d+n,n) - binom(d+n-q,n-q) + binom(n+b,q+b) - q - 1. Is this range exact, i.e. does one have K_{p,q}(n,b;d) = 0 for every integer p outside this interval?

Over C, fix integers n >= 2 and d >= 1, let S = Sym H^0(P^n, O_{P^n}(d)), and let R = ⊕_{m >= 0} H^0(P^n, O_{P^n}(md)) be the homogeneous coordinate ring of the d-uple Veronese embedding nu_d: P^n -> P(H^0(P^n, O_{P^n}(d))^*). Is it true that for every integer p with 0 <= p < 3d - 2, the minimal graded free resolution of R over S satisfies E_0 ≅ S and E_i ≅ ⊕ S(-i-1) for all 1 <= i <= p; equivalently, does O_{P^n}(d) satisfy Green-Lazarsfeld Property (N_p) for every p < 3d - 2?

Let X be a smooth complex projective variety of dimension n, let A be an ample divisor and P an arbitrary divisor on X, and for d >> 0 set L_d = dA + P, assumed very ample so that the complete linear series |L_d| embeds X in P^{r_d} with r_d = h^0(X,L_d) - 1. For a line bundle B on X, write k_{p,q}(X,B;L_d) = dim K_{p,q}(X,B;L_d), where K_{p,q}(X,B;L_d) is the Koszul cohomology group of weight q, and write k_{p,q}(X;L_d) for the case B = O_X. Fix an integer q in {1,...,n} and a real number a, and let {p_d} be a sequence of integers satisfying p_d = r_d/2 + a sqrt(r_d)/2 + o(sqrt(r_d)) (equivalently, (2p_d - r_d)/sqrt(r_d) -> a). Is it true that there exists a normalizing function F_q(d), depending on X, A, P, and q, such that F_q(d) k_{p_d,q}(X;L_d) -> e^(-a^2/2) as d -> infinity? More generally, as explicitly suggested immediately after Conjecture 3.2, does the analogous Gaussian asymptotic hold, after suitable normalization, for k_{p_d,q}(X,B;L_d) when B is a fixed twisting line bundle on X?

Working over C, let B = O_{P^2}(-1) and L_d = O_{P^2}(d), and for each d let r_d = h^0(P^2, L_d) - 1. In the Boij-Soderberg decomposition of the two-row Betti table of the graded S-module R(P^2, B; L_d) = direct sum over m>=0 of H^0(P^2, B + mL_d), write kp,q(P^2, B; L_d) = sum_{i=0}^{r_d} x_i(P^2, B; L_d) kp,q(Pi_i), where the pure modules Pi_i are characterized by K_{p,1}(Pi_i) != 0 iff 0 <= p < i and K_{p,2}(Pi_i) != 0 iff i <= p <= r_d, and where x_i(P^2, B; L_d) are the resulting nonnegative rational Boij-Soderberg coefficients. Can one normalize these coefficients x_i(P^2, B; L_d) and the relevant index values i so that, as d -> infinity, they are realized as the values of a smooth function on a dense subset of its domain?

Fix an integer p >= 0. Let X be a smooth complex projective variety of dimension n >= 2, let A be an ample line bundle and P an arbitrary line bundle on X, and set L_d = dA + P, with d sufficiently large so that L_d is very ample. For a line bundle B on X, let K_{p,1}(X,B;L_d) denote the weight-one Koszul cohomology group of the graded S-module R(X,B;L_d) = ⊕_m H^0(X, B + mL_d), where S = Sym H^0(X,L_d). Find necessary and sufficient geometric conditions on the pair (X,B), relative to p, such that there exists d_0 with K_{p,1}(X,B;L_d) = 0 for every integer d >= d_0.

For a rational two-dimensional conformal field theory arising from a vertex operator algebra under the standard rationality assumptions used in the paper, can one prove the convergence of the higher-genus series obtained from intertwining operators, so that these series define higher-genus chiral correlation functions on the relevant Teichmuller/moduli spaces and thereby yield the corresponding higher-genus full correlation functions in the Kontsevich-Segal-Moore-Seiberg framework?

Let n≥2, H:R^{n+1}→R be bounded and Lipschitz, and let u:R^n→R^{n+1} satisfy u∈W^{1,n}(R^n,R^{n+1}), b:=H∘u∈W^{1,n}(R^n)∩L^∞(R^n). Denote by I the Riesz potential I f(x)=∫_{R^n}c_n(x−y)/|x−y|^n f(y)dy mapping H^1(R^n)→L^{n/(n−1)}(R^n), and by R_α the α-th Riesz transform on R^n, α=1,…,n. (a) What is the largest subspace V⊂H^1(R^n) such that the commutator [b,I]:V→L^{n/(n−1)}(R^n) extends boundedly? What is the answer if L^{n/(n−1)}(R^n) is replaced by W^{1,1}(R^n)? In either case, does this V necessarily contain all n×n minors of the Jacobian Du? (b) What is the largest V⊂H^1(R^n) such that, for each α=1,…,n, the commutator [b,R_α]:V→L^1(R^n) is bounded? Does V contain all n×n minors of Du? (c) Does the n-form du^1∧…∧du^n admit an atomic decomposition in H^1(R^n) with atoms that are orthogonal to b (so-called b-atoms)? (d) If u furthermore is a weak solution of the H-system div(|∇u|^{n−2}∇u)=H(u)Ju, do the answers to (a)–(c) change?

Let n >= 3, let B^n ⊂ R^n be the unit ball, let N ⊂ R^m be a compact closed Riemannian manifold isometrically embedded in Euclidean space, and let pi be the nearest-point projection from a tubular neighborhood of N onto N. If u ∈ W^{1,n}(B^n, N) is weakly n-harmonic in the sense that d/dt|_{t=0} E_n[pi o (u + t phi)] = 0 for every phi ∈ W^{1,n}_0(B^n, R^m) ∩ L^∞(B^n, R^m), where E_n[v] = (1/n) ∫_{B^n} |∇v|^n dx, must u be continuous on B^n?

Let n > 2, let B^n ⊂ R^n be the unit ball, let H: R^{n+1} → R be bounded and Lipschitz, and let u = (u_1, ..., u_{n+1}) ∈ W^{1,n}(B^n, R^{n+1}) be a weak solution on B^n of the n-dimensional H-system
-div(|∇u|^{n-2}∇u) = H(u) J_u,
where J_u := ∂_1u × ··· × ∂_n u ∈ R^{n+1} (equivalently, the vector of all n×n minors of Du). Must every such weak solution u be continuous on B^n?

In the higher-dimensional setting n > 2, let m be a positive integer, let u ∈ W^{1,n}(B^n, R^m) be a weak solution of -div(|∇u|^{n-2}∇u) = Ω · (|∇u|^{n-2}∇u) in D'(B^n, R^m), where Ω = (Ω^α_{ij})_{1 ≤ α ≤ n, 1 ≤ i,j ≤ m} belongs to L^n(B^n, R^{m x m} ⊗ R^n), satisfies Ω^α_{ij} = -Ω^α_{ji} for every α, i, j, and (Ω · (|∇u|^{n-2}∇u))^i = Σ_{α=1}^n Σ_{j=1}^m Ω^α_{ij}|∇u|^{n-2}∂_αu^j. With no extra smallness or higher-integrability assumptions, must every such u belong to C^0(B^n, R^m)?

For a fixed dimension n\ge 2 and exponent 1<p<\infty, let p'=p/(p-1), and let R=(R_1,\dots,R_n) be the standard vectorial Riesz transform on \mathbb{R}^n, defined on Schwartz functions by \widehat{R_\alpha f}(\xi)=-i\xi_\alpha|\xi|^{-1}\widehat f(\xi). Writing |Rf|=(\sum_{\alpha=1}^n |R_\alpha f|^2)^{1/2}, is it true or false that there exists a constant C=C(n,p)>0 such that every scalar Schwartz function f on \mathbb{R}^n satisfies \|f\|_{L^{p,\infty}(\mathbb{R}^n)}^{p-1}\le C\left\|\sum_{\alpha=1}^n R_\alpha\big(|Rf|^{p-2}R_\alpha f\big)\right\|_{L^{p',\infty}(\mathbb{R}^n)}?

Let n > 2, let Ω ⊂ R^n be open, let H : R^{n+1} → R be bounded and Lipschitz, and let u = (u^1, ..., u^{n+1}) ∈ W^{1,n}(Ω, R^{n+1}) be a distributional solution of the H-system
-div(|∇u|^{n-2}∇u) = H(u) J_u,
where J_u := ∂_{x_1}u × ··· × ∂_{x_n}u ∈ R^{n+1}. Assume that there exists an index set I ⊂ {1, ..., n+1} with |I| = k for some k ∈ {1, ..., n} such that u^i ∈ L^∞(Ω) for every i ∈ I. Does it follow that u is continuous on Ω?

For n>2, let N⊂ℝ^m be a compact closed Riemannian manifold and consider weak n-harmonic maps u∈W^{1,n}(B^n,N) satisfying -div(|∇u|^{n-2}∇u)=|∇u|^{n-2}A_u(∇u,∇u), and let H:ℝ^{n+1}→ℝ be bounded and Lipschitz and consider weak solutions u∈W^{1,n}(B^n,ℝ^{n+1}) of the H-system -div(|∇u|^{n-2}∇u)=H(u)J_u. Since the solution classes for these equations, and likewise for their approximate versions with right-hand-side perturbations Φ_k→0 in (W^{1,n})*, are weakly sequentially closed in W^{1,n}, can one construct a counterexample to the continuity questions of Problems 2.2 or 2.4 by finding a sequence of singular weak solutions u_k to the perturbed equations such that u_k⇀u weakly in W^{1,n} and the limit u is a singular weak solution of the corresponding unperturbed equation?

Let H: R^{n+1} -> R be bounded and Lipschitz, let u belong to W^{1,n}(R^n, R^{n+1}), and set b:=H(u) in W^{1,n}(R^n) ∩ L^∞(R^n). Write H^1(R^n) for the real Hardy space. Define If(x):=∫_{R^n} c_n (x-y)/|x-y|^n f(y) dy, let R_alpha denote the alpha-th Riesz transform for alpha=1,...,n, and define [b,T]f:=bTf-T(bf). Determine the largest subspace V ⊂ H^1(R^n) such that: (a) [b,I] maps V to L^{n/(n-1)}(R^n; R^n), and likewise when the target is replaced by W^{1,1}(R^n; R^n); in either case, does V contain all n×n minors of Du? (b) for every alpha=1,...,n, [b,R_alpha] maps V to L^1(R^n); does V contain all n×n minors of Du? (c) does the n-form du^1 ∧ ... ∧ du^n admit an atomic decomposition into b-atoms, meaning classical H^1-atoms that are additionally orthogonal to b? (d) do the answers to (a)-(c) change if u is further assumed to be a weak solution of the H-system -div(|∇u|^{n-2}∇u)=H(u)Ju, where Ju:=∂_{x_1}u × ... × ∂_{x_n}u has coordinates equal to the n×n minors of Du?

Let B ⊂ R^n be a ball, let N ≥ 1, and let u ∈ W^{1,n}(B, R^N) be a weak solution of the system -div(|∇u|^{n-2}∇u) = Ω · |∇u|^{n-2}∇u in D'(B), where Ω ∈ L^n(B, so(N) ⊗ R^n) is antisymmetric. Does the additional Lorentz-space assumption Ω ∈ L^{(n,2)}(B, so(N) ⊗ R^n) imply that u is continuous on B?

Given effectively a polycyclic group G, an endomorphism phi in End(G), and elements w,t in G with the promise that there exists a in G such that t = a^-1 w phi(a), determine the computational complexity of finding such an element a; equivalently, determine the complexity of the single twisted conjugacy search problem in polycyclic groups.

Let G be a polycyclic group. Consider the power conjugacy search problem: given elements a,b in G with the promise that there exist n in N and g in G such that a^n = b^g (where b^g := g^{-1}bg), what is the computational complexity of finding one such pair (n,g)?

Given a polycyclic group G, naturally specified by a polycyclic presentation, what is the computational complexity of constructing an explicit faithful matrix representation of G (that is, a matrix embedding of G into some GL_m(Z))?

Open problem. For the class of polycyclic groups, determine the computational complexity of the following decision problem: given a polycyclic group G (effectively presented, e.g. by a polycyclic presentation) and two automorphisms α, β ∈ Aut(G), decide whether α and β are conjugate in Aut(G), that is, whether there exists γ ∈ Aut(G) such that γαγ^{-1} = β.

For the cryptosystems surveyed in the paper whose platform groups are polycyclic groups, determine whether they are resistant to quantum algorithms; in particular, decide whether cryptosystems using infinite polycyclic groups are resistant to cryptanalysis on a quantum computer. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1607.05819))

Let S_2(x,y,z) = x^2(x-y)(x-z) + y^2(y-x)(y-z) + z^2(z-x)(z-y) in R[x,y,z]. Since S_2 is a homogeneous quartic in three variables and is nonnegative for all real x, y, z, determine an explicit identity writing S_2 as a sum of squares of real homogeneous quadratic forms.

Let {P_n}_{n≥0} be a real orthogonal polynomial sequence defined by P_{-1}(x)=0, P_0(x)=1, and P_n(x)=(x-c_n)P_{n-1}(x)-λ_n P_{n-2}(x) for n≥1, where c_n∈ℝ, λ_n>0, lim_{n→∞} c_n=∞, and lim_{n→∞} λ_{n+1}/(c_n c_{n+1})=1/4. If x_{n,1}<⋯<x_{n,n} are the zeros of P_n, define ξ_i=lim_{n→∞}x_{n,i}, η_j=lim_{n→∞}x_{n,n-j+1}, σ=lim_{i→∞}ξ_i, and τ=lim_{j→∞}η_j; in this one-quarter class τ=∞. In the unresolved case σ=-∞, determine the correct analogue of Blumenthal’s theorem: what is the closure of the set of all zeros of the polynomials P_n, and in particular are these zeros dense in the whole real line ℝ? ([sigma-journal.com](https://sigma-journal.com/2016/071/sigma16-071.pdf))

Let {P_n}_{n≥0} be an orthogonal polynomial sequence on the real line determined by P_{-1}(x)=0, P_0(x)=1, and, for n≥1, P_n(x)=(x-c_n)P_{n-1}(x)-λ_n P_{n-2}(x), where c_n∈ℝ and λ_n>0. Assume that {P_n} belongs to the one-quarter class, meaning that c_n→∞ and λ_{n+1}/(c_n c_{n+1})→1/4 as n→∞. If x_{n,1}<⋯<x_{n,n} are the zeros of P_n, define ξ_i=lim_{n→∞}x_{n,i}, η_j=lim_{n→∞}x_{n,n-j+1}, σ=lim_{i→∞}ξ_i, and τ=lim_{j→∞}η_j; in this class τ=∞, and the unresolved case singled out in the paper is σ=-∞. Apart from the Meixner polynomials of the second kind (Meixner–Pollaczek polynomials), does there exist any other orthogonal polynomial sequence in this one-quarter class whose orthogonality measure has spectrum extending over the entire real line?

Let {P_n(x; a)} be one of the hypergeometric or basic-hypergeometric orthogonal polynomial families explicitly discussed in Section 3 of the paper—Laguerre, Gegenbauer, continuous q-ultraspherical/Rogers, Jacobi, or continuous q-Jacobi—and let a and b be admissible parameter sets for which both an ordinary linearization formula P_m(x; a) P_n(x; a) = sum_{r=0}^{m+n} α_{r,m,n}(a) P_r(x; a) and a connection relation P_n(x; a) = sum_{k=0}^{n} β_{k,n}(a,b) P_k(x; b) are valid. For m,n in N0 (assume n >= m), determine explicit closed-form generalized linearization coefficients γ_{k,m,n}(a,b) such that P_m(x; a) P_n(x; a) = sum_{k=0}^{m+n} γ_{k,m,n}(a,b) P_k(x; b), where "closed form" is understood in the paper's sense of formulas built from products of (q-)Pochhammer symbols and fixed-argument hypergeometric or basic-hypergeometric series. ([sigma-journal.com](https://sigma-journal.com/2016/071/sigma16-071.pdf))

Can one develop a systematic symbolic-summation method for multiple hypergeometric sums—particularly those arising from connection coefficients of orthogonal-polynomial families or from multiple iterated integrals, and including multisums more general than the classical Lauricella series—that uses the recurrence/differential information produced by holonomic creative-telescoping and related difference-field techniques to identify, whenever possible, an equivalent lower-order representation (preferably a single hypergeometric sum, and in favorable cases a closed form) and to prove the resulting reduction without relying on ad hoc human guessing of the target form?

Does there exist a fast discrete spherical harmonic transform; that is, an algorithm that converts function values sampled on a grid on the sphere to spherical harmonic coefficients, and also performs the inverse conversion, with complexity roughly O(n log n) for a grid of n points? ([sigma-journal.com](https://sigma-journal.com/2016/071/sigma16-071.pdf))

For orthogonal polynomials determined by a general orthogonality weight, can one develop an easy-to-use method—ideally a software package—that takes the weight as input and returns a uniform asymptotic expansion, together with rigorous error bounds, in a form practical for applications such as quadrature and fast transforms?

For each fixed n≥1, let B_n=(b_{ij})_{1≤i,j≤n} be a real symmetric Bernoulli matrix, meaning that b_{ij}=b_{ji} and the entries are random signs ±1 subject to this symmetry constraint. What is the exact finite-n spectral picture of this ensemble—that is, how can one characterize the spectrum (eigenvalue multiset) of a finite-dimensional random symmetric Bernoulli matrix, in a way that captures the genuinely finite-dimensional structure rather than only the asymptotic universality behavior known for Wigner ensembles?

Given a general invariant random-matrix ensemble, does there exist a corresponding Wigner-like random-matrix family whose limiting spectral density agrees with that of the invariant ensemble, analogously to the facts that Wigner ensembles share their limiting spectral density with the Gaussian Unitary Ensemble and Wishart ensembles share their limiting spectral density with the Laguerre Unitary Ensemble?

Let N_0 = {0,1,2,...}. For real parameters lambda > 0 and delta > 0, and for each n in N_0, define
F_n^{lambda,delta}(t) = integral from 0 to t of (t-theta)^delta C_n^lambda(cos theta) (sin theta)^(2 lambda) dtheta,
for 0 < t < pi, and at t = pi by the same integral formula, where C_n^lambda denotes the Gegenbauer polynomial. Is it true that, for every lambda > 0, delta > 0, and n in N_0, one has F_n^{lambda,delta}(t) > 0 for all t in (0,pi] if and only if delta >= lambda + 1?

Let A_n(t) in Q[t^3] be defined by A_0(t)=1, A_1(t)=0 and, for n=0,1,2,..., ((n^3-(-1)^n t^3) A_n(t) + (n+1)^2(2n+1) A_{n+1}(t) + (n+2)^2(n+1) A_{n+2}(t) = 0). Define A_tilde_n(t)=sum_{k=0}^n A_k(t). Equivalently, A_tilde_n(t) satisfies, for n=1,2,3,..., ((n^3-(-1)^n t^3) A_tilde_{n-1}(t) + n(2n+1) A_tilde_n(t) - n(n+1)^2 A_tilde_{n+1}(t) = 0). Can one prove directly from this three-term recurrence, without appealing to the multiple-zeta-value identity from which the polynomials arise, that for each fixed complex t, lim_{n->infinity} A_tilde_n(t) = product_{j=1}^infinity (1 + t^3/(8 j^3))?

In Section 7's modified multiple-zeta-value setting, let A_n(t) in Q[t^3] be the polynomial sequence defined for n >= 0 by A_0(t)=1, A_1(t)=0, and (n^3 - (-1)^n t^3)A_n(t) + (n+1)^2(2n+1)A_{n+1}(t) + (n+2)^2(n+1)A_{n+2}(t) = 0, where A_n(t) has degree floor(n/2) in x=t^3; and let A_tilde_n(t) = sum_{k=0}^n A_k(t) (equivalently, A_tilde_n satisfies (n^3 - (-1)^n t^3)A_tilde_{n-1}(t) + n(2n+1)A_tilde_n(t) - n(n+1)^2 A_tilde_{n+1}(t) = 0 for n >= 1). Can one find explicit hypergeometric formulas for A_n(t) and A_tilde_n(t) for every n >= 0?

Let 1 < p < ∞ with p ≠ 2, and let μ be a finite measure on an arbitrary measurable space such that L^p(μ) is non-separable. Does there exist a real Banach space having an unconditional basis (in the usual generalized sense for possibly non-separable spaces) that contains a closed linear subspace isomorphic to L^p(μ)?

Let 2<p<∞, and let X be a real Banach space that is a closed linear subspace of L_p(ν) for some non-negative measure ν. If X does not contain an isomorphic copy of ℓ_p(ω_1), where ω_1 is the first uncountable ordinal, must there exist a finite measure μ such that X is isomorphic to a subspace of L_p(μ)?

Working over real Banach spaces, let 2 < p < ∞ and let μ be an arbitrary finite measure. Must the Banach space L^p(μ) be Hilbert generated; that is, does there exist a real Hilbert space H and a bounded linear operator T: H → L^p(μ) whose range is norm-dense in L^p(μ)?

Let X be a real Banach lattice. Suppose there exists a weakly compact set L contained in X such that the smallest sublattice of X containing L is norm dense in X. Must there exist a weakly compact set K contained in X whose closed linear span is all of X?

Let K be an infinite compact Hausdorff space. Assume that K is weakly Radon-Nikodým, meaning that K is homeomorphic to a weak*-compact subset of X* for some real Banach space X that contains no subspace isomorphic to ℓ^1. Must K admit a convergent sequence that is non-stationary (that is, not eventually constant)? ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1607.07787))

Is it relatively consistent with ZFC that there exists a real separable Banach space X such that, if B_X denotes the closed unit ball of X and K(B_X) denotes the partially ordered set of all weakly compact subsets of B_X ordered by inclusion, then K(B_X) is not Tukey equivalent to any of the four posets {0}, N^N, K(Q), or [c]^{<ω}, where K(Q) is the family of compact subsets of Q and [c]^{<ω} is the family of all finite subsets of a set of cardinality c, each ordered by inclusion?

Let X be a real Banach space that contains no closed linear subspace isomorphic to c0.
