Must X have the Gelfand-Phillips property; that is, must every limited set C subseteq X be relatively norm compact, where 'limited' means that for every weak*-null sequence (x_n^*) in X^* one has lim_n sup_{x in C} |x_n^*(x)| = 0?

Determine the least cardinal κ such that there exists a family (X_i)_{i∈I} of real Banach spaces, with |I| = κ and each X_i having property (K), for which the ℓ^1-sum (⊕_{i∈I} X_i)_{ℓ^1} fails property (K). Here property (K) means that every weak*-null sequence (x_n^*) in X_i^* admits a convex block subsequence y_k^* = Σ_{n∈I_k} a_n x_n^* (where each I_k ⊂ ℕ is finite, max(I_k) < min(I_{k+1}), a_n ≥ 0, and Σ_{n∈I_k} a_n = 1) such that y_k^* → 0 in the Mackey topology μ(X_i^*, X_i).

Let X be a real separable Banach space that is weakly sequentially complete, meaning that every weakly Cauchy sequence in X converges weakly in X. Must X have property (K); that is, for every weak*-null sequence (x_n^*) in X^*, does there exist a convex block subsequence (y_k^*) of the form y_k^* = sum_{n in I_k} a_n x_n^*, where I_1, I_2, ... are finite subsets of N with max(I_k) < min(I_{k+1}), a_n >= 0, and sum_{n in I_k} a_n = 1 for each k, such that y_k^* -> 0 in the Mackey topology μ(X^*, X)?

Let X be a real Banach space. Write Ba(X, τ) for the Baire σ-algebra of (X, τ), let w be the weak topology on X and w* the weak* topology on X*, and call a set Γ ⊆ X* total if it separates the points of X. Property D means that Ba(X, σ(X, Γ)) = Ba(X, w) for every total set Γ ⊆ X*, and property D' means that every w*-sequentially closed linear subspace of X* is w*-closed. Are properties D' and D equivalent?

Let K be a compact Hausdorff space, let C_p(K) and C_w(K) denote the Banach space C(K) of continuous real-valued functions on K endowed respectively with the pointwise and weak topologies, and identify P(K) with the set of regular Borel probability measures on K inside C(K)^* equipped with the weak* topology. If a measure μ ∈ P(K), viewed as the linear functional f ↦ ∫_K f dμ on C(K), is measurable with respect to Ba(C_p(K)), must μ belong to Seq(co(Δ_K)), where Δ_K = {δ_t : t ∈ K} and Seq(co(Δ_K)) is the smallest weak*-sequentially closed subset of P(K) containing co(Δ_K)?

Let K be a compact Hausdorff space, and let C(K) be the real Banach space of continuous real-valued functions on K with the supremum norm ||·||_∞. Is the map ||·||_∞: C(K) -> R measurable with respect to the weak Baire sigma-algebra Ba(C(K), w)? Equivalently, in this C(K)-supremum-norm setting, is Ba(C(K), w)-measurability of ||·||_∞ equivalent to weak*-separability of the closed unit ball B_{C(K)^*}, or at least to weak*-separability of the whole dual space C(K)^*?

Let K be a compact Hausdorff space, and let C(K) be the real Banach space of continuous real-valued functions on K with the supremum norm. Assume that the Borel σ-algebra of the weak topology on C(K) is strictly smaller than the Borel σ-algebra of the norm topology, i.e. Bo(C(K), w) ≠ Bo(C(K)). Must there exist a subset A ⊆ C(K) that is discrete for the norm topology and satisfies A ∉ Bo(C(K), w)?

Let K be a compact Hausdorff space, and let C(K) be the real Banach space of continuous real-valued functions on K equipped with the supremum norm. Denote by w the weak topology on C(K), by T_p the topology of pointwise convergence on K, by Bo(C(K), w) and Bo(C(K), T_p) the corresponding Borel σ-algebras, and by Bo(C(K)) the Borel σ-algebra of the norm topology. If Bo(C(K), w) = Bo(C(K)), must it follow that Bo(C(K), T_p) = Bo(C(K))?

Let ℓ∞ be the real Banach space of bounded real sequences equipped with the supremum norm, let w denote its weak topology, and let Bo(ℓ∞, w) and Bo(ℓ∞) be the Borel σ-algebras of the weak and norm topologies, respectively. Does there exist a probability measure μ on Bo(ℓ∞, w) for which there is no probability measure ν on Bo(ℓ∞) satisfying ν|Bo(ℓ∞, w) = μ? ([webs.um.es](https://webs.um.es/joserr/miwiki/lib/exe/fetch.php?cache=cache&id=papers&media=openproblems.pdf))

Let (Ω, Σ, μ) be a complete probability space, let X be a real Banach space, and let P0(X) denote the family of all non-empty subsets of X. Suppose F: Ω → P0(X) is a multi-function with convex closed values such that F^{-}(H) := {t ∈ Ω : F(t) ∩ H ≠ ∅} belongs to Σ for every open half-space H ⊆ X. Must there exist a selector f: Ω → X, meaning f(t) ∈ F(t) for every t ∈ Ω, such that x*∘f is Σ-measurable for every x* ∈ X*? ([webs.um.es](https://webs.um.es/joserr/miwiki/lib/exe/fetch.php?cache=cache&id=papers&media=openproblems.pdf))

Fix a complete probability space (Ω, Σ, μ), and let X be a real Banach space with dens(X)=ω1. Write wk(X) for the family of all nonempty weakly compact subsets of X. Does wk(X) have property (SC), i.e. does there exist a set selector ψ:wk(X)→X with ψ(K)∈K for every K∈wk(X) such that, for every scalarly measurable multifunction F:Ω→wk(X) in the sense that F^{-}(H):={t∈Ω: F(t)∩H≠∅}∈Σ for every open half-space H⊆X, the function ψ∘F:Ω→X is scalarly measurable (equivalently, x*∘(ψ∘F) is Σ-measurable for every x*∈X*)?

Let (Omega, Sigma, mu) be a complete probability space and let X be a real Banach space. Write cwk(X) for the family of all non-empty convex weakly compact subsets of X. Does cwk(X) have property (SC), i.e. does there exist a set selector psi:cwk(X)->X with psi(C) in C for every C in cwk(X) such that, for every scalarly measurable multifunction F:Omega->cwk(X) (meaning F^{-}(H) in Sigma for every open half-space H subset X), the X-valued function psi o F:Omega->X is scalarly measurable?
Characterize the real Banach spaces X with the Lebesgue property (LP), i.e. those for which every Riemann integrable function f:[0,1]→X is norm-continuous Lebesgue-almost everywhere on [0,1].

For which cardinals κ does the real Hilbert space ℓ_2(κ) have the weak Lebesgue property; that is, for which κ is it true that every norm-Riemann integrable function f:[0,1]→ℓ_2(κ), where [0,1] is equipped with Lebesgue measure, is continuous almost everywhere with respect to the weak topology of ℓ_2(κ)?

Let c0 be the real Banach space of all real sequences converging to 0, with the sup norm, and let f:[0,1]→c0 be a bounded function, not assumed Riemann integrable. For a tagged finite partition P=(0=t0<...<tm=1; ξi∈[t_{i-1},t_i]) of [0,1], define the Riemann sum S(f,P)=Σ_{i=1}^m f(ξi)(t_i-t_{i-1}) and the mesh ||P||=max_i(t_i-t_{i-1}). Set I(f)={x∈c0: there exists a sequence of tagged partitions Pn of [0,1] with ||Pn||→0 and S(f,Pn)→x in c0}. Must I(f) be a convex subset of c0 for every bounded function f:[0,1]→c0? ([webs.um.es](https://webs.um.es/joserr/miwiki/lib/exe/fetch.php?cache=cache&id=papers&media=openproblems.pdf))

Let (Ω, Σ, μ) be a complete probability space and let X be a real Banach space. Assume that X has the Pettis integrability property, i.e. every scalarly bounded, scalarly measurable map g: Ω → X is Pettis integrable, where 'scalarly measurable' means that x*∘g is Σ-measurable for every x* ∈ X*. If f: Ω → X is Pettis integrable and ν_f: Σ → X is the associated vector measure defined by ν_f(A) = ∫_A f dμ, is the range R(ν_f) = {ν_f(A) : A ∈ Σ} necessarily separable?

Let (Ω, T, Σ, μ) be a quasi-Radon probability space; that is, (Ω, Σ, μ) is a complete probability space, T ⊂ Σ is a topology on Ω, μ is inner regular with respect to closed sets, and for every upwards directed family G of open sets in T one has μ(∪G) = sup{μ(G) : G ∈ G}. Let X be a real Banach space, and let f : Ω → X be Pettis integrable. If ν_f : Σ → X is the associated countably additive vector measure defined by ν_f(A) = ∫_A f dμ, must its range R(ν_f) = {∫_A f dμ : A ∈ Σ} be relatively norm compact in X?

Let (Ω, Σ, μ) be a complete probability space, and let X be a real Banach space containing no subspace isomorphic to c_0. If f: Ω → X is Pettis integrable and ν_f: Σ → X is the vector measure defined by ν_f(A) = ∫_A f dμ, must the range R(ν_f) = {ν_f(A) : A ∈ Σ} = {∫_A f dμ : A ∈ Σ} be relatively compact in the norm topology of X?

Let U be the class of real Banach spaces X such that every Pettis integrable function f:[0,1]→X (with [0,1] equipped with Lebesgue measure) is McShane integrable, and let 𝒦:= {L compact Hausdorff : C(L)∈U}, where C(L) denotes the Banach space of continuous real-valued functions on L with the supremum norm. Does there exist a compact Hausdorff space K such that K is Eberlein (i.e. homeomorphic to a weakly compact subset of some Banach space), K is not uniform Eberlein (i.e. not homeomorphic to a weakly compact subset of any Hilbert space), and C(K) belongs to U? ([webs.um.es](https://webs.um.es/joserr/miwiki/lib/exe/fetch.php?cache=cache&id=papers&media=openproblems.pdf))

Let X be a real Banach space, let (Ω,Σ,μ) be a complete probability space, and let T1 and T2 be Hausdorff topologies on Ω such that, for each i∈{1,2}, T_i⊂Σ and (Ω,T_i,Σ,μ) is a quasi-Radon probability space; that is, μ is inner regular with respect to the T_i-closed sets and μ(⋃𝒢)=sup{μ(G):G∈𝒢} for every upwards directed family 𝒢⊂T_i. If f:Ω→X is McShane integrable with respect to T1 in the generalized quasi-Radon sense, must f also be McShane integrable with respect to T2? ([webs.um.es](https://webs.um.es/joserr/miwiki/lib/exe/fetch.php?cache=cache&id=papers&media=openproblems.pdf))

Characterize the real Banach spaces X for which there exist a measurable space (Omega, Sigma) and a countably additive vector measure nu: Sigma -> X such that the closed unit ball B_X = {x in X : ||x|| <= 1} is contained in the range R(nu) = {nu(E) : E in Sigma}.

Let K be a weakly compact subset of the real Banach space c_0. Does there exist a measurable space (Omega, Sigma) and a countably additive vector measure nu: Sigma -> c_0 such that K is contained in its range R(nu) := {nu(E) : E in Sigma}?

Let X be a real Banach space, and for i=1,2 let ν_i:Σ_i→X be countably additive vector measures of finite variation on measurable spaces (Ω_i,Σ_i). Assume that R(ν_1)=R(ν_2) as subsets of X and that the scalar variation measures |ν_1| and |ν_2| are perfect in the usual measure-theoretic sense. Is the property of being Pettis differentiable with respect to its own variation measure determined by this common range; that is, must there exist a Pettis integrable f_1:Ω_1→X with ν_1(E)=∫_E f_1 d|ν_1| for every E∈Σ_1 if and only if there exists a Pettis integrable f_2:Ω_2→X with ν_2(E)=∫_E f_2 d|ν_2| for every E∈Σ_2?

Let (Ω,Σ) be a measurable space, let X be a real Banach space that does not contain an isomorphic copy of ℓ₁, and let ν:Σ→X be a countably additive vector measure. Let L^1(ν) denote the Banach lattice of ν-integrable scalar functions, and let I_ν:L^1(ν)→X be the integration operator given by I_ν(f)=∫_Ω f dν. If I_ν is completely continuous, must ν have finite variation, i.e. must |ν|(Ω)<∞?

Let (Ω, Σ) be a measurable space, let X be a real Banach space, and let ν: Σ → X be a non-atomic countably additive vector measure. Writing L^1(ν) for the Banach lattice of scalar-valued ν-integrable measurable functions on (Ω, Σ) modulo ||ν||-a.e. equality, does there exist a set Γ and a countably additive vector measure ν̃: Σ → c_0(Γ), where c_0(Γ) denotes the real Banach space of functions on Γ vanishing at infinity, such that L^1(ν) = L^1(ν̃)?

Let (Ω, Σ) be a measurable space, let X be a real Banach space, and let ν : Σ → X be a countably additive vector measure. Let L^1(ν) be the Banach lattice of ν-integrable scalar functions associated with ν, with norm ||f||_{L^1(ν)} = sup{∫_Ω |f| d|x*ν| : x* ∈ B_{X*}}, where x*ν is the scalar measure A ↦ x*(ν(A)). For each g ∈ B_{L^∞(ν)} and x* ∈ B_{X*}, define γ_{g,x*} ∈ B_{L^1(ν)*} by γ_{g,x*}(f) = ∫_Ω f g d(x*ν). Characterize those vector measures ν for which the resulting norming set Γ = {γ_{g,x*} : g ∈ B_{L^∞(ν)}, x* ∈ B_{X*}} is a James boundary of L^1(ν), that is, for every f ∈ L^1(ν) there exist g ∈ B_{L^∞(ν)} and x* ∈ B_{X*} such that ||f||_{L^1(ν)} = γ_{g,x*}(f).

Let (Ω, Σ, μ) be a probability space, let X be a real Banach space, and let 1 ≤ p < ∞. Write L^p(μ, X) for the Lebesgue-Bochner space of equivalence classes of strongly measurable functions f: Ω → X such that (∫_Ω ||f(ω)||^p dμ(ω))^(1/p) < ∞. If the closed dual unit ball B_{X^*}, endowed with the weak* topology σ(X^*, X), is weak*-sequentially compact, must the closed dual unit ball B_{L^p(μ,X)^*}, endowed with σ(L^p(μ,X)^*, L^p(μ,X)), also be weak*-sequentially compact?

For every probability space (Ω, Σ, μ) and every real Banach space X, suppose X is strongly weakly compactly generated, meaning that there exists a weakly compact set K0 ⊂ X such that for every weakly compact set K ⊂ X and every ε > 0 there is n ∈ N with K ⊂ nK0 + ε B_X, where B_X is the closed unit ball of X. Must the Lebesgue-Bochner space L^1(μ, X), consisting of equivalence classes of strongly measurable functions f: Ω → X such that ∫Ω ||f(ω)|| dμ(ω) < ∞, also be strongly weakly compactly generated?

Let (Ω, Σ, μ) be a probability space, let X be a real Banach space, and let 1 ≤ p < ∞. Denote by L^p(μ, X) the Banach space of equivalence classes of strongly measurable functions f: Ω → X such that ∫Ω ||f||^p dμ < ∞. If X is strongly weakly K-analytic (respectively, strongly weakly countably determined), must L^p(μ, X) also be strongly weakly K-analytic (respectively, strongly weakly countably determined)?

For a fixed exponent 1 < p < ∞, characterize all real Banach spaces X, with no separability assumption, such that the Lebesgue-Bochner space L^p([0,1],X)—that is, the space of equivalence classes of strongly measurable functions f:[0,1]→X with ∫_0^1 ||f(t)||^p dt < ∞, where [0,1] carries Lebesgue measure—has an unconditional basis.

Let X be a separable real Banach space. For which such X is the countable Hilbertian direct sum ℓ_2(X) = { (x_n) : x_n ∈ X, Σ_{n=1}^∞ ||x_n||^2 < ∞ } linearly isomorphic, as a Banach space, to the Lebesgue-Bochner space L_2([0,1],X) of equivalence classes of strongly measurable functions f:[0,1]→X with ∫_0^1 ||f(t)||^2 dλ(t) < ∞, where λ is Lebesgue measure on [0,1]?

Over the real scalars, for which separable Banach spaces X does the Lebesgue-Bochner space L_1([0,1],X)—that is, the space of equivalence classes of strongly measurable functions f:[0,1]→X with ∫_0^1 ||f(t)|| dt < ∞, where [0,1] carries Lebesgue measure—contain a copy of ℓ_2(X), the ℓ_2-direct sum of countably many copies of X?

Characterize the real Banach spaces X for which the Banach spaces ℓ∞(X) and L∞([0,1],X)=L∞(λ,X) are isomorphic, where ℓ∞(X) is the space of bounded X-valued sequences with the supremum norm, [0,1] carries Lebesgue measure λ, and L∞(λ,X) consists of λ-a.e. equivalence classes of essentially bounded strongly measurable X-valued functions.

Let λ be Lebesgue measure on [0,1], and let X = L^1([0,1], λ) be regarded as a real Banach space. Does X have property (D∞), that is: whenever (f_n) is a sequence of strongly measurable maps f_n:[0,1]→X with sup_n ||f_n||_{L^∞([0,1],X)} < ∞ and such that, for every x* ∈ X*, the scalar functions x*∘f_n converge to 0 in λ-measure on [0,1], must there exist a subsequence (f_{n_k}) for which, for every x* ∈ X*, the scalar functions x*∘f_{n_k} converge to 0 λ-almost everywhere on [0,1]?

Does there exist an infinite-dimensional reflexive real Banach space X with property (D1), meaning that whenever (f_n) is a sequence of strongly measurable functions f_n:[0,1]→X with sup_n ||f_n||_{L^1([0,1],X)}<∞ and x*(f_n)→0 in measure on [0,1] for every x*∈X*, there is a subsequence (f_{n_k}) such that x*(f_{n_k}(t))→0 for λ-almost every t∈[0,1] and every x*∈X*? ([webs.um.es](https://webs.um.es/joserr/miwiki/lib/exe/fetch.php?cache=cache&id=papers&media=openproblems.pdf))

Fix a class of k-orbit abstract polytopes (equivalently, a fixed symmetry type graph), and let Gamma be the automorphism group equipped with the distinguished generating set determined by a chosen base flag and, when k >= 3, a chosen spanning tree of the symmetry type graph. In the associated coset-geometry construction, what subgroup-intersection condition, analogous to the string C-group intersection property for regular polytopes and to the known conditions for two-orbit polyhedra, is necessary and sufficient to ensure that the resulting incidence structure is a polytope rather than merely a maniplex?

Let z = (z1, …, zn) and let Δ = Σ_{i=1}^n ∂^2/∂zi^2 be the Laplace operator on C[z1, …, zn]. If P(z) is a homogeneous polynomial of degree 4 such that Δ^m(P(z)^m) = 0 for every integer m ≥ 1 (equivalently, by Proposition 1.2, the Hessian matrix Hes P(z) is nilpotent), must there exist an integer N = N(P) such that Δ^m(P(z)^{m+1}) = 0 for every m ≥ N?

Is there a combinatorial analogue of the classical Quotient Criterion for abstract polytopes that applies to k-orbit abstract polytopes, extending the role that the Quotient Criterion plays in the regular and chiral cases?

Let P be a convex polytope whose facets are combinatorially regular polytopes, not necessarily all of the same type, and let Mon(P) be the monodromy group generated by the involutions sending each flag of P to its i-adjacent flag. Must Mon(P) always be a string C-group (equivalently, with respect to these standard generators, must it satisfy the string commuting relations and the intersection property)?

For a chiral polytope P, its smallest regular cover exists uniquely but may fail to be a polytope. Can there exist a chiral polytope P whose smallest regular cover is not itself a polytope, yet which still has a unique minimal regular cover by regular polytopes, up to isomorphism; or must every chiral polytope with non-polytopal smallest regular cover have multiple minimal regular covers?

Let G = <rho_0, ..., rho_{n-1}> be a (not necessarily finite) string group generated by involutions; that is, rho_i^2 = epsilon for all i and (rho_i rho_j)^2 = epsilon whenever |i-j| > 1. Determine all string C-groups Lambda = <sigma_0, ..., sigma_{n-1}> satisfying the intersection property <sigma_i : i in I> ∩ <sigma_i : i in J> = <sigma_i : i in I ∩ J> for every I, J ⊆ {0, ..., n-1}, for which there exists a surjective generator-preserving homomorphism pi : Lambda -> G with pi(sigma_i) = rho_i for all i, and which are minimal among such covers in the sense that if pi factors through another string C-group cover Lambda' of G via surjective generator-preserving homomorphisms, then Lambda' is isomorphic to Lambda.

For an abstract k-orbit polytope P (that is, a polytope whose automorphism group has exactly k flag-orbits), what is the correct canonical group-theoretic invariant that extends the usual chirality group of a chiral polytope, is independent of auxiliary choices such as a base flag or spanning tree in the symmetry type graph description, and measures in the k-orbit setting the obstruction to P being regular?

Let P(z) be a homogeneous polynomial of degree 4 in C[z_1,\dots,z_n], and assume that P is Hessian nilpotent, i.e. its Hessian matrix Hes P = (∂^2P/∂z_i∂z_j) is nilpotent. Must one have Δ^m(P^{m+1}) = 0 for all sufficiently large integers m, where Δ = \sum_{i=1}^n ∂^2/∂z_i^2? Equivalently, does this vanishing already hold for every m > (3/2)(3^{n-2}-1)?

Let z = (z1, ..., zn) and let P(z) ∈ C[z1, ..., zn] be a homogeneous Hessian nilpotent polynomial of degree 4. Define F_t(z) = z - t∇P(z), and let its formal inverse be written as F_t^{-1}(z) = z + t∇Q_t(z), where Q_t(z) is the deformed inversion pair of P. Must Q_t(z) belong to C[t, z1, ..., zn] for every such P?
For every integers k >= 1 and n >= 3, does there exist a non-degenerate abstract n-polytope P whose automorphism group has exactly k orbits on the flags of P?

Fix n >= 3 and a rank-n symmetry type graph T with k vertices, so that k is the number of flag-orbits. Which groups Γ occur as the full automorphism groups of abstract n-polytopes, respectively n-maniplexes, having symmetry type graph T? More precisely, can one characterize such Γ by means of a distinguished generating set adapted to a chosen root flag and spanning tree of T, so that the object can be reconstructed as a coset geometry, and determine the additional intersection conditions that are necessary and sufficient for the reconstruction to be an abstract polytope rather than merely a maniplex?

Let X be a finite connected n-premaniplex with exactly two vertices; that is, X is a connected pregraph with edge/semiedge colours 0,1,...,n-1 such that each vertex is incident with exactly one edge or semi-edge of each colour and, whenever |i-j|>1, every alternating path of length 4 with colours i and j is closed. Must there exist a rank-n maniplex M whose symmetry type graph, with respect to its full automorphism group, is isomorphic to X?

In the setting of abstract 2-orbit polytopes, do there exist constructions that take an abstract n-polytope to an abstract (n+1)-polytope and produce a 2-orbit symmetry type graph (that is, the quotient of the flag graph by automorphism-group flag-orbits) which is not one of the symmetry type families listed in Theorem 4.2 of the paper and is not obtained from one of those families by duality?

Which symmetry type graphs are realizable by convex polytopes? More precisely: classify those edge-coloured quotient graphs that arise as (i) the combinatorial symmetry type graph of a convex polytope, meaning the quotient of its flag graph by its combinatorial automorphism group, and separately (ii) the geometric symmetry type graph of a convex polytope, meaning the quotient of its flag graph by the geometric symmetry group of a convex realization.

Do there exist abstract n-polytopes P and Q, with n ≥ 3, such that the amalgamation class ⟨P,Q⟩ is nonempty—that is, there exists an abstract (n+1)-polytope all of whose facets are isomorphic to P and all of whose vertex-figures are isomorphic to Q—even though P itself has at least two pairwise non-isomorphic vertex-figures?

Let P and Q be abstract polytopes of the same rank, and fix a flag orbit O1 of P and a flag orbit O2 of Q. Consider amalgamations R of P and Q, meaning abstract polytopes R whose facets are all isomorphic to P and whose vertex-figures are all isomorphic to Q, with the additional rooted condition that a flag of R restricting to orbit O1 on its facet restricts to orbit O2 on its vertex-figure, and conversely. If such a rooted amalgamation exists, must there exist a universal rooted amalgamation of P and Q for this rooted choice, that is, one that covers every other rooted amalgamation of the same type?

Let P and Q be compatible abstract n-polytopes, meaning that each vertex-figure of P is isomorphic to each facet of Q, and let <P,Q> denote the class of all abstract (n+1)-polytopes whose facets are isomorphic to P and whose vertex-figures are isomorphic to Q. Assuming <P,Q> is nonempty, for which pairs (P,Q) does there exist a constant k=k(P,Q) such that every polytope R in <P,Q> has at most k flag-orbits under its full automorphism group?

Given a k-orbit abstract d-polytope P, does there exist a k-orbit abstract (d+1)-polytope U whose facets are all isomorphic to P such that, for every other k-orbit abstract (d+1)-polytope Q with facets isomorphic to P, U covers Q; that is, there is a color-preserving epimorphism from the flag graph of U onto the flag graph of Q? ([matmor.unam.mx](https://matmor.unam.mx/SIGMAP/talks/SIGMAP2018Cunningham.pdf))

Let P and Q be abstract n-polytopes of the same rank. Under what necessary and sufficient conditions does there exist an abstract (n+1)-polytope R whose facets occur in exactly two isomorphism types, represented by P and Q (in the semiregular/facet-intransitive sense intended in the paper, so that each ridge of R is incident with one facet of each type), and when can such an R be chosen finite?

Does there exist an infinite rank-4 polytope of full rank in Euclidean 3-space—that is, a 4-polytope realized in R^3—with chiral combinatorial symmetry? If so, explicitly construct the polytope P_{\{\infty,3,4\}} and prove that it is combinatorially chiral.

Classify all discrete geometrically chiral polytopes of full rank in Euclidean space: for each rank n >= 3, determine all finite chiral n-polytopes that admit faithful realizations in E^n and all infinite chiral n-polytopes that admit faithful realizations in E^{n-1}, up to combinatorial isomorphism (and, where appropriate, up to similarity of realizations).

Let n≥1 and let P(z)∈C[z_1,...,z_n] be a homogeneous polynomial of degree 4 whose Hessian matrix Hes P(z)=(∂^2P/∂z_i∂z_j)_{1≤i,j≤n} is nilpotent. If Δ:=Σ_{i=1}^n ∂^2/∂z_i^2 denotes the Laplace operator, must one have Δ^m(P^{m+1})=0 for all sufficiently large integers m (that is, does there exist M such that Δ^m(P^{m+1})=0 for every m≥M)?

Classify, for all Euclidean dimensions d and ranks n, all finite or infinite n-polytopes P admitting faithful symmetric realizations in E^d such that P has exactly two flag-orbits and is of full rank, meaning that if T(P) denotes its symmetry type graph (recording the flag-orbits and their i-adjacencies), then no (n+1)-polytope realized in the same E^d has symmetry type graph T(P). ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1608.07993))

For each integer d >= 2 and each k with 1 <= k <= d, classify all faithful geometric realizations in Euclidean d-space E^d of abstract regular d-polytopes whose Euclidean symmetry group has exactly k orbits on flags.

For each integer k >= 2, let N_k be the least integer such that there exists no convex d-polytope in Euclidean space whose Euclidean symmetry group has exactly k orbits on flags whenever d >= N_k. Determine N_k for each k, or at least sharpen the known bounds on N_k; in addition, determine whether, for a fixed k, the set of dimensions d < N_k in which geometrically k-orbit convex d-polytopes exist can have gaps (that is, whether there are "holes" in the dimension spectrum).

For a fixed integer k ≥ 2, determine the dimensions d for which there exists a convex d-dimensional polytope whose geometric symmetry group has exactly k orbits on flags; equivalently, determine the dimension spectrum of geometrically k-orbit convex polytopes, improve the known upper bounds N_k from Matteo’s theorem, and decide whether this spectrum has holes.

For integers d >= 2 and k >= 1, classify the combinatorially regular polytopes realized in Euclidean space E^d whose full geometric symmetry group has exactly k orbits on the flags, where a flag is a maximal chain of mutually incident faces.

For which integers k and d does the following hold: whenever an abstract d-polytope P has exactly k flag-orbits under its automorphism group and is isomorphic to the face lattice of a convex d-dimensional polytope, there exists a convex d-polytope Q whose Euclidean symmetry group has exactly k flag-orbits and whose face lattice is isomorphic to P?

Let n >= 1 and let P(z1,...,zn) be a homogeneous polynomial of degree 4 in C[z1,...,zn]. Assume that P is Hessian nilpotent, i.e. its Hessian matrix Hes P = (∂^2P/∂zi∂zj)1<=i,j<=n is nilpotent. If Δ = Σ_{i=1}^n ∂^2/∂zi^2 denotes the Laplace operator, must there exist an integer M = M(P) such that Δ^m(P^(m+1)) = 0 for every integer m >= M?

Let n>=1, let z=(z_1,...,z_n), and let Δ=∑_{i=1}^n ∂^2/∂z_i^2 be the Laplace operator on C[z_1,...,z_n]. If P(z)∈C[z_1,...,z_n] is a homogeneous polynomial of degree 4 whose Hessian matrix Hes P=(∂^2P/∂z_i∂z_j) is nilpotent (i.e. P is Hessian nilpotent), must it follow that Δ^m(P(z)^{m+1})=0 for all sufficiently large integers m?

Develop the realization theory for abstract k-orbit polytopes: given an abstract polytope K whose automorphism group has exactly k orbits on flags, formulate and study faithful symmetric geometric realizations of K in a geometric space S for which the resulting geometric polytope has exactly k flag-orbits under its symmetry group.
For given integers d and k, what are the combinatorially regular polytopes realized in Euclidean space E^d whose geometric symmetry group has exactly k orbits on flags?

Develop a realization theory for abstract m-orbit polytopes: given an abstract polytope K whose automorphism group has exactly m flag-orbits, determine and describe the faithful symmetric geometric realizations of K in a geometric space S whose geometric symmetry group has exactly k flag-orbits; equivalently, make precise for which integers k such k-orbit realizations of an abstract m-orbit polytope can occur, and how they should be studied in a systematic realization-theoretic framework.

For fixed integers d >= 2 and k >= 1, determine/classify the faithful realizations in Euclidean space E^d of abstract regular polytopes whose geometric symmetry group (the group of Euclidean isometries preserving the realization) has exactly k orbits on flags; equivalently in the paper's geometric language, what are the combinatorially regular polytopes in E^d with exactly k geometric flag-orbits?

Let n ≥ 1, let z=(z1,...,zn), and let Δ_n = Σ_{i=1}^n ∂^2/∂z_i^2 act on C[z1,...,zn]. If P(z) is a homogeneous polynomial of degree 4 whose Hessian matrix Hes(P) = (∂^2P/∂zi∂zj) is nilpotent, must it follow that Δ_n^m(P(z)^{m+1}) = 0 for all sufficiently large integers m; equivalently, does there exist M such that for every m ≥ M one has Δ_n^m(P^{m+1})=0?

Let (X, d) be a metric space, let 2^X denote the family of all non-empty closed subsets of X, and let T_W(d) be the Wijsman topology on 2^X, i.e. the weakest topology making every map A -> d(x, A) continuous for each x in X. Is the Wijsman hyperspace (2^X, T_W(d)) normal if and only if X is separable?

Let (X,d) be a metric space, let 2^X denote the set of all nonempty closed subsets of X, and let T_W(d) be the Wijsman topology on 2^X induced by d (equivalently, the topology of pointwise convergence of the maps A ↦ d(x,A), x in X). If the Wijsman hyperspace (2^X,T_W(d)) is normal, must X be separable? Equivalently, since (2^X,T_W(d)) is metrizable exactly when (X,d) is separable, is (2^X,T_W(d)) normal if and only if it is metrizable?

Let (X,d) be a non-separable uniformly discrete metric space, meaning that there exists ε>0 such that d(x,y)≥ε whenever x≠y. Let 2^X denote the set of all non-empty closed subsets of X, endowed with the Wijsman topology T_W(d), i.e. the topology of pointwise convergence of the distance maps A ↦ d(x,A)=inf{d(x,a):a∈A} for x∈X. Must the Wijsman hyperspace (2^X,T_W(d)) be a non-normal topological space? ([openrepository.aut.ac.nz](https://openrepository.aut.ac.nz/bitstreams/be63513c-6554-4988-96ce-96c8dd6f7050/download))

Let (X,d) be a non-separable metric space, let 2^X denote the family of all non-empty closed subsets of X, and let T_W(d) be the Wijsman topology on 2^X induced by d (equivalently, the weakest topology making each map A ↦ d(x,A)=inf{d(x,a): a∈A}, x∈X, continuous). Must the Wijsman hyperspace (2^X, T_W(d)) contain a closed subspace homeomorphic to ω1 × (ω1 + 1), where ω1 and ω1 + 1 carry their usual order topologies? ([openrepository.aut.ac.nz](https://openrepository.aut.ac.nz/bitstreams/be63513c-6554-4988-96ce-96c8dd6f7050/download))

Let (X, d) be a metric space, let 2^X be the set of all non-empty closed subsets of X, and endow 2^X with the Wijsman topology T_W(d) induced by d. If the Wijsman hyperspace (2^X, T_W(d)) is non-normal, must it contain a closed subspace homeomorphic to the ordinal product ω_1 × (ω_1 + 1), where ω_1 and ω_1 + 1 carry their order topologies?

Let (X,d) be a metric space, and let 2^X denote the set of all nonempty closed subsets of X, endowed with the Wijsman topology T_{W(d)} induced by the distance functionals A -> d(x,A) for x in X. Without assuming separability, is the complete metrizability of X equivalent to the possession by the Wijsman hyperspace (2^X, T_{W(d)}) of some completeness-type topological property?

Let X be a completely metrizable topological space, let 2^X denote the family of all non-empty closed subsets of X, and for each metric d compatible with the topology of X let T_W(d) be the Wijsman topology on 2^X, i.e. the weakest topology for which every map A ↦ d(x,A)=inf{d(x,a): a∈A} is continuous for every x∈X. Must the Wijsman hyperspace (2^X, T_W(d)) be strongly Choquet for every such compatible metric d on X, or even strongly α-favorable (in the strong Choquet game sense)?

Let X be a metrizable space, and let 2^X denote the set of all non-empty closed subsets of X. For each metric d compatible with the topology of X, let T_W(d) be the Wijsman topology on 2^X, namely the topology of pointwise convergence of the distance maps A ↦ d(x,A) for x ∈ X. If, for every compatible metric d on X, the Wijsman hyperspace (2^X, T_W(d)) is either strongly Choquet or strongly α-favorable in the strong Choquet game, does it follow that X is completely metrizable, i.e. that X admits a compatible complete metric?

Let (X, d) be a metric space, let 2^X denote the set of all nonempty closed subsets of X, and equip 2^X with the Wijsman topology T_W(d). If the metric topology T(d) on X is pseudocomplete, i.e. X is quasi-regular and has a sequence {P_n : n ∈ N} of open π-bases such that every sequence V_n with V_n ∈ P_n and V_{n+1} ⊆ V_n for all n has nonempty intersection, must the Wijsman hyperspace (2^X, T_W(d)) be pseudocomplete? Likewise, if X is subcompact or base-compact in the Amsterdam sense, i.e. regular and having an open base B such that every regular filterbase, respectively every centered family, contained in B has nonempty intersection, must (2^X, T_W(d)) be subcompact or base-compact, respectively?

Let (X,d) be a metric space, let 2^X denote the family of all non-empty closed subsets of X, and endow 2^X with the Wijsman topology T_W(d), i.e. the weakest topology for which each map A -> d(x,A) = inf{d(x,a) : a in A} is continuous for every x in X. Find characterizations, in terms of properties of the metric space (X,d), for when the Wijsman hyperspace (2^X, T_W(d)) is a Baire space.

Let (X,d) be a metric space, let 2^X denote the set of all non-empty closed subsets of X, and let T_W(d) be the Wijsman topology on 2^X, i.e. the weakest topology for which each distance functional A -> d(x,A):=inf{d(x,a): a in A} is continuous for every x in X. If, for every n in N, the finite product X^n is a Baire space (with the product topology), must the Wijsman hyperspace (2^X, T_W(d)) be a Baire space?

Let (X, d) be a metric space, let 2^X denote the family of all non-empty closed subsets of X, and let T_W(d) be the Wijsman topology on 2^X induced by d (equivalently, the weakest topology for which each map A -> d(x, A) is continuous for every x in X). If X is a Baire space in the topology induced by d, must the Wijsman hyperspace (2^X, T_W(d)) also be a Baire space?

Let (X,d) be a metric space, let 2^X denote the family of all non-empty closed subsets of X, and let T_W(d) be the Wijsman topology on 2^X, i.e. the weakest topology for which each map A↦d(x,A)=inf{d(x,a):a∈A} is continuous for every x∈X. If X is hereditarily Baire, meaning that every non-empty closed subspace of X is a Baire space, must the Wijsman hyperspace (2^X,T_W(d)) be a Baire space?

Let X be a metrizable space, let 2^X denote the set of all non-empty closed subsets of X, and for each metric d compatible with the topology of X let T_W(d) be the Wijsman topology on 2^X, i.e. the weakest topology for which every functional A -> d(x,A) = inf{d(x,a) : a in A} is continuous for each x in X. If (2^X, T_W(d)) is a Baire space for every compatible metric d on X, must X be a Baire space?

Let X be a metrizable space, and let 2^X denote the set of all nonempty closed subsets of X. Suppose that for every metric d compatible with the topology of X, the Wijsman hyperspace (2^X, T_W(d)) is a Baire space. Must the Vietoris hyperspace (2^X, τ_V) also be a Baire space?

Let X be a metrizable space, let 2^X denote the set of all non-empty closed subsets of X, let T_V be the Vietoris topology on 2^X, and for each metric d compatible with the topology of X let T_W(d) denote the Wijsman topology on 2^X induced by d. If (2^X, T_V) is a Baire space, must (2^X, T_W(d)) be a Baire space for every compatible metric d on X? ([openrepository.aut.ac.nz](https://openrepository.aut.ac.nz/bitstreams/be63513c-6554-4988-96ce-96c8dd6f7050/download))

Let F(x) be an algebraic function over Q(x), and identify F with its Laurent expansion at x = 0, F(x) = sum_{n >> -infinity} a_n x^n, choosing a branch that is unramified at x = 0. Assume that for all sufficiently large prime numbers p one has a_p ≡ 0 (mod p). Such an F is called an algebraic function with a Fermat property. Characterize all algebraic functions with a Fermat property, both in general and within any prescribed algebraic function field Q(x,U), where U is algebraic over Q(x) and unramified at x = 0. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1609.09842))

Let R(x) = sum_{n>=0} s(n)x^n in Z[[x]] be an algebraic function over Q(x), unramified at x = 0, such that s(p) = 0 mod p for all sufficiently large primes p; call such an R an algebraic function with a Fermat property. Let F be the additive abelian group of all such functions. For any algebraic function U(x), define U^(partial)(x) = xU'(x), and let D be the subgroup of F generated by all such logarithmic derivatives; let Z[x] be the polynomial subgroup. If V(x) is algebraic over Q(x), unramified at 0 and without a pole at 0, and M >= 2 is an integer, let V(x^M) be a basic power-substituted element, and let P be the subgroup generated by finite sums of such elements. For any algebraic U over Q(x) that is unramified at 0, identify functions with their Laurent expansions at 0 and set F_U = F intersect Q(x,U), D_U = D intersect Q(x,U), and P_U = P intersect Q(x,U). Find the structure of the abelian quotient groups F/(D + Z[x] + P), F_U/(D_U + Z[x]), and F_U/(D_U + Z[x] + P_U). In particular, what is the corresponding quotient in the purely rational case Q(x)?

Let p(n) be the classical partition function, characterized by sum_{n>=0} p(n)x^n = product_{m>=1} (1 - x^m)^(-1). In the formal power series ring Z[[x]], let (n_k)_{k>=1} be the unique sequence of integers defined by the power-product expansion sum_{n>=0} p(n)x^n = product_{k>=1} (1 + n_k x^k). The paper notes that n_k = 1 for every odd k. Explore the arithmetic properties of the sequence (n_k); in particular, is it true that, for every integer k >= 1, one has n_{8k} > 0 and n_{8k+2}, n_{8k+4}, n_{8k+6} < 0?

Let D = { z in C : |z - 1| < 3/2 }, let B(D) be the Banach space of functions analytic on D and continuous on its closure with the supremum norm, and for Re(s) > 1/2 let L_s be the Mayer-Ruelle transfer operator for the Gauss continued-fraction map, defined by (L_s f)(z) = sum_{n >= 1} (z+n)^(-2s) f(1/(z+n)), analytically continued in s to all complex values. Write lambda_n(s) for the canonically indexed eigenvalues of L_s, where the canonical index is the one described in the paper (equivalently, the index attached via polynomial degree and hence by ordering according to magnitude). Using Mayer's determinant relation with the Selberg zeta function, and restricting to the relevant +1/even factor, define for each fixed M in N the fiber S_M = { rho : rho is a nontrivial zero of the Riemann zeta function and lambda_M(rho/2) = 1 }. For a fixed M, what can be said about S_M: is it infinite, how should the conjectural distribution of Riemann zeros change when restricted to S_M, and how can one effectively compute concrete fibers such as S_1?

For a fixed integer k in N, let D={z in C: |z-1|<3/2}, let V be the Banach space of functions analytic on D and continuous on its closure with the supremum norm, and for Re(s)>1/2 define the Mayer-Ruelle transfer operator by L_s[f](z)=sum_{m>=1}(z+m)^(-2s) f(1/(z+m)), extended analytically to all s in C. Let lambda_n(s), n>=1, be its canonically indexed eigenvalues, so that det(1-L_s^2)=product_{n>=1}(1-lambda_n(s)^2)=Z(s), where Z(s) is the Selberg zeta function for PSL_2(Z). The paper states that ord_{s=1-k} Z(s)=dim_C(M_{2k}), where M_{2k} is the corresponding space of cusp forms for PSL_2(Z). Determine how this total vanishing multiplicity dim_C(M_{2k}) is distributed among the canonically indexed factors 1-lambda_n(s)^2 at s=1-k; in other words, identify which indices n contribute to the zero at s=1-k and how much each contributing factor accounts for in the total order of vanishing. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1609.09842))

Fix a proper number field K/Q of degree n>1 and an integral basis omega_1,...,omega_n of O_K. Define the associated norm form by T(a_1,...,a_n)=N_{K/Q}(a_1 omega_1+...+a_n omega_n) for (a_1,...,a_n) in Z^n. Characterize all functions f: Z -> C for which there exists a function h: T(Z^n) -> C such that T(f(a_1),f(a_2),...,f(a_n)) = h(T(a_1,a_2,...,a_n)) for every (a_1,...,a_n) in Z^n.

Let p(X) = X^3 - 3X + 1, let alpha be a root of p, and put alpha' = alpha^2 - 2. Then K = Q(alpha) is the cubic field generated by alpha, {1, alpha, alpha'} is an integral basis of O_K, and the associated norm form is T(a,b,c) = N_{K/Q}(a + b alpha + c alpha') = a^3 - b^3 - c^3 - 3ab^2 - 3ac^2 + 3abc + 6b^2c - 3bc^2 for integers a,b,c. Classify all pairs of functions f: Z -> C and H: T(Z^3) -> C such that T(f(a), f(b), f(c)) = H(T(a,b,c)) for every a,b,c in Z.

Let P be a finite subset of Z^2 with |P| odd. An uphill lattice path is the union gamma of a doubly infinite sequence of directed unit line segments in R^2, each joining a lattice point (a,b) to either (a+1,b) or (a,b+1). A downhill lattice path is defined similarly, except that the allowed steps are (a,b)→(a+1,b) and (a,b)→(a,b-1). A monotone lattice path is either uphill or downhill. Call gamma friendly for P if, after discarding the points of P that lie on gamma, the two connected components of R^2 \ gamma contain the same number of points of P. Is it true that every finite set P ⊂ Z^2 of odd cardinality admits a friendly monotone lattice path?

Let n be a positive integer, and let an n x n square in R^2 be subdivided in the usual way into n^2 unit squares. Say that a line intersects a unit square if the line and the square have a common point lying in the interior of that unit square. What is the minimum number of lines in R^2 needed so that every unit square is intersected by at least one of the lines? In particular, is this minimum equal to n - 1 for every n >= 3? ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1609.09842))

Let ? : [0,1] → [0,1] be Minkowski’s question-mark function, defined for x = [0; a_1, a_2, ...] by ?(x) = 2^(1-a_1) - 2^(1-(a_1+a_2)) + 2^(1-(a_1+a_2+a_3)) - ···. For n ≥ 0, define rational functions Q_n(z) ∈ Q(z) by Q_0(z) = -1/(2z) and, for every n ≥ 1, Q_n(z) = (1/2) Σ_{j=0}^{n-1} (1/j!) (d^j/dz^j Q_{n-j-1})(-1) · (z^j - z^(-j-2)); equivalently, Q_n(z) = B_n(z) z^(-n-1) with B_n(z) a polynomial with rational coefficients. Define the exponential generating series Λ(t) = Σ_{n=0}^∞ Q_n'(-1) t^n / n!, where Q_n'(-1) denotes differentiation with respect to z at z = -1. Is Λ(t) an entire function of the complex variable t, and does it satisfy the Laplace-transform identity ∫_0^∞ Λ(t)e^(-t) dt = ∫_0^1 x^2 d?(x)?

For each integer n >= 2, define psi_n to be the infimum of |Gamma|/n! over all finite subgroups Gamma of GL(n,R) for which there exists a Gamma-superflow. Here, a Gamma-superflow means a flow phi on R^n with vector field Q = (Q_1,...,Q_n) whose components are 2-homogeneous rational functions, such that gamma^(-1) o Q o gamma = Q for every gamma in Gamma, and such that every other vector field Q' satisfying the same invariance for all gamma in Gamma is either a scalar multiple of Q or has strictly larger degree of a common denominator than Q. Given that psi_2 = 2, is it true that psi_n = 2 for every n >= 3?

Let a(0)=0, a(1)=1, a(2n)=a(n), and a(2n+1)=a(n)+a(n+1) be Stern’s diatomic sequence, and for L,N in N_0 define Q^(L)(N)=sum_{n=2^N+1}^{2^(N+1)} a(n)^L. For each fixed L>=0, let μ_L be the unique algebraic number given by Proposition 1 such that Q^(L)(N)/2^N is asymptotic to c_L μ_L^N for some constant c_L. Does there exist a function p on [0,(1+sqrt(5))/2]—ideally analytic, or at least continuous of bounded variation, or more generally a distribution—such that its Stieltjes moments satisfy int_0^((1+sqrt(5))/2) x^L dp(x)=μ_L for every L>=0? ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1609.09842))

Let ϑ(n) denote, for each integer n≥1, the number of compositions (ordered partitions) of n into summands 2^q with q≥0. For every integer a∈Z (including positive, zero, and negative a), it is known that the 2-adic limit Θ(a):=lim_{k→∞}ϑ(2^k+a) exists in Z_2, where Z_2 is the ring of 2-adic integers and the limit is taken in the 2-adic topology. Describe the arithmetic properties of the resulting 2-adic numbers Θ(a) as a function of a. In particular, for each a, determine whether Θ(a), viewed inside Q_2, is a rational number, or more generally algebraic over Q.

Within the tree-level (α′ and loop correction–free) gravi-dilaton effective action in the string frame, including NS-NS and Ramond-Ramond fields, and specializing to spatially flat, homogeneous, isotropic FRW cosmologies: (1) what is the detailed asymptotic behavior of solutions approaching strong-field (singular) regimes; (2) are the known exact RR-containing solutions asymptotically stable attractors and unique within their asymptotic class; and (3) do additional solution branches arise only as subleading corrections in the asymptotic expansions, thereby constraining the classification of admissible singular asymptotic states?

Let I⊂R be an interval, and for a,b∈I with a<b define N_f(a,b;α,β)=α(f(a)+f(b))+β f((a+b)/2), where α,β>0 and 2α+β=1. Find the best possible pair (α*,β*) such that (1/(b-a))∫_a^b f(t) dt ≤ N_f(a,b;α*,β*) for every convex function f∈C^∞(I) and every choice of a<b in I.

Within the framework of classical molecular dynamics simulations of crystal nucleation in supercooled liquids and supersaturated solutions, how can researchers (a) develop and validate improved classical interatomic potentials—including machine‐learning based force fields—with sufficient transferability to accurately describe interfaces, defects, and polymorphic behavior, and (b) design efficient, crystal‐nucleation‐specific enhanced sampling algorithms—such as optimized order parameters for metadynamics or scalable path‐sampling methods—that together enable quantitatively accurate predictions of nucleation rates and mechanisms for systems of practical interest (e.g., pharmaceutical crystallization, ice formation on realistic substrates, and natural gas hydrate formation under pipeline conditions), thereby bridging the current gap between simulation and experimental observations?

What strategies can be developed to perform classical atomistic molecular dynamics simulations of heterogeneous crystal nucleation in supercooled liquids that (a) incorporate increasingly realistic substrate–liquid interfaces—including atomistic defects, impurities, and accurate interfacial force field parameters—and (b) extract general, non–material-specific nucleation trends even if this requires sacrificing some force field accuracy?

Given a modulus of continuity ω, find a compact set K⊂C, regular with respect to the Dirichlet problem, such that the Green function g_{C\setminus K} of C\setminus K with pole at infinity is continuous on C and has modulus of continuity similar to ω; that is, with ω(g_{C\setminus K},δ):=sup{|g_{C\setminus K}(z)-g_{C\setminus K}(w)|:|z-w|≤δ}, require that as δ↓0 either ω(g_{C\setminus K},·) and ω coincide on some null sequence, or, in the weak-equivalence sense spelled out in the paper, there exist constants C1,C2>0 such that C1ω(δ)≤ω(g_{C\setminus K},δ)≤C2ω(δ) for all sufficiently small positive δ.

Given a modulus of continuity ω on [0,∞), find a non-polar compact set K ⊂ ℂ, regular with respect to the Dirichlet problem, such that if g_{ℂ\setminus K} denotes the Green function of ℂ \ K with pole at infinity, then there exist constants C1, C2, δ0 > 0 for which, for every z ∈ ℂ \ K with δ := dist(z,K) ≤ δ0, one has C1·ω(δ) ≤ g_{ℂ\setminus K}(z) ≤ C2·ω(δ).

Find a non-polar compact set K ⊂ ℝ, regular with respect to the Dirichlet problem, such that its Green function g_{ℂ\K} with pole at infinity satisfies a two-sided Hölder estimate near K: namely, there exist α > 0 and constants C1, C2, δ0 > 0 such that for every z ∈ ℂ with dist(z,K) ≤ δ0, one has C1·dist(z,K)^α ≤ g_{ℂ\K}(z) ≤ C2·dist(z,K)^α.

Let K be an infinite compact set, let P_n be the space of holomorphic polynomials of degree at most n endowed with the uniform norm on K, and let M_n(K) denote the operator norm of differentiation on P_n. For compact sets K \subset R^d, say that K has the extension property (EP) if there exists a continuous linear extension operator E(K) -> C^\infty(R^d). Given that there exist compact sets K_1 with EP and K_2 without EP such that M_n(K_1) grows essentially faster than M_n(K_2) as n -> infinity, so that the asymptotic growth of M_n(K) alone does not determine EP in a nonempty zone of uncertainty, characterize the asymptotic growth rates of the Markov factors that define the lower and upper boundaries of this zone of uncertainty for EP.

Let (f_n)_{n≥1} be a sequence of polynomials in C[z], where f_n(z)=sum_{j=0}^{d_n} a_{n,j} z^j with d_n≥2 for every n, and write F_n=f_n∘f_{n-1}∘⋯∘f_1. Assume that (f_n) is a regular polynomial sequence, i.e. there exist constants A_1,A_2,A_3>0 such that |a_{n,d_n}|≥A_1, |a_{n,j}|≤A_2|a_{n,d_n}| for 0≤j<d_n, and log|a_{n,d_n}|≤A_3 d_n for all n. Suppose that the Julia set J((f_n)) of the family (F_n) is a Cantor-type subset of R, and let μ_{J((f_n))} be its equilibrium measure. If P_n(x;μ_{J((f_n))}) denotes the monic orthogonal polynomial sequence for μ_{J((f_n))}, determined by P_{-1}≡0, P_0≡1, and xP_n(x)=P_{n+1}(x)+b_{n+1}P_n(x)+a_n^2P_{n-1}(x), is it true that both recurrence-coefficient sequences (a_n)_{n≥1} and (b_n)_{n≥1} are asymptotically almost periodic, in the sense that each differs by o(1) from the restriction to N of a two-sided almost periodic sequence? ([drna.padovauniversitypress.it](https://drna.padovauniversitypress.it/system/files/papers/AlpanGoncharov_DRNA2017.pdf))

Let K⊂R be a non-polar compact set, let μ_K be the equilibrium measure of K, and for each n≥1 let P_n(x;μ_K) be the n-th monic orthogonal polynomial with respect to μ_K. Define Z_n(μ_K):={x∈R:P_n(x;μ_K)=0} and U_n(μ_K):=inf{|x-x'|:x,x'∈Z_n(μ_K), x≠x'}. Let g_{C\K} denote the Green function of C\K with pole at infinity, and let M_n(K) denote the n-th Markov factor, i.e. the operator norm of differentiation on polynomials of degree at most n equipped with the uniform norm on K. Assuming, when discussing smoothness near K, the regularity background used in §2, what general relationship, if any, exists between the zero-spacing sequence {U_n(μ_K)}_{n≥1} and the smoothness of g_{C\K} near K, and what general relationship, if any, exists between {U_n(μ_K)}_{n≥1} and the Markov factors {M_n(K)}_{n≥1}?

Let K ⊂ R be a non-polar compact set that is regular for the Dirichlet problem, let g_{C\K} denote the Green function of C \ K with pole at infinity, let mu_K be the equilibrium measure of K, and let mu be a probability Borel measure with ess supp(mu) = K such that the isolated points {x_n} of supp(mu) satisfy sum_n g_{C\K}(x_n) < infinity. If condition (3) holds, namely
integral_K log(dmu/dmu_K) dmu_K > -infinity,
must at least one of the paper’s two Widom conditions hold for the monic orthogonal polynomials P_n(·;mu), where W_n^2(mu) := ||P_n(·;mu)||_{L^2(mu)} / Cap(supp(mu))^n, namely
limsup_{n→∞} W_n^2(mu) > 0
or
liminf_{n→∞} W_n^2(mu) > 0?
Conversely, does the Widom condition limsup_{n→∞} W_n^2(mu) > 0 imply condition (3)?

Let K⊂R be a regular non-polar compact set (regular with respect to the Dirichlet problem), let T_{n,K} denote the n-th monic Chebyshev polynomial on K, and define the Widom factors by W_n(K)=||T_{n,K}||_{L^\infty(K)}/Cap(K)^n for n≥1. Does there exist such a set K that is not a Parreau-Widom set but nevertheless satisfies sup_{n≥1} W_n(K)<∞? If, in addition, K has Lebesgue measure 0, must the sequence (W_n(K))_{n=1}^∞ be unbounded? The paper asks the analogous two questions for the equilibrium measure μ_K of K, namely for W_n^2(μ_K)=||P_n(\cdot;μ_K)||_{L^2(μ_K)}/Cap(K)^n, where P_n(\cdot;μ_K) is the n-th monic orthogonal polynomial for μ_K.

Let K ⊂ ℝ be a non-polar compact set that is regular with respect to the Dirichlet problem, let α = min K be its leftmost endpoint, and let μ_K denote its equilibrium measure. Assume that μ_K([α,c]) ∈ ℚ for every c ∈ ℝ outside K. What can be said about K? In particular, must K be a polynomial generalized Julia set, i.e. K = J(f_n) for some regular polynomial sequence (f_n), where F_n = f_n ∘ ⋯ ∘ f_1, each f_n(z) = Σ_{j=0}^{d_n} a_{n,j} z^j has degree d_n ≥ 2, and there exist constants A_1, A_2, A_3 > 0 such that |a_{n,d_n}| ≥ A_1, |a_{n,j}| ≤ A_2|a_{n,d_n}| for 0 ≤ j < d_n, and log|a_{n,d_n}| ≤ A_3 d_n for all n? Moreover, does this hypothesis imply that there exists a sequence of admissible real polynomials (f_n) (meaning: if deg f_n = d_n, then f_n has d_n real simple zeros and d_n−1 critical points y with |f_n(y)| ≥ 1) such that the inverse-image sets F_n^{-1}([-1,1]) form a decreasing sequence and K = ⋂_{n=1}^∞ F_n^{-1}([-1,1])?

Let K⊂ℝ be a non-polar compact set (equivalently, Cap(K)>0), and let μ_K denote its logarithmic equilibrium measure. Suppose there exists a dimension function h: ℝ+→ℝ+ that is increasing and continuous with h(0)=0 such that μ_K is exactly the restriction of the h-Hausdorff measure to K; equivalently, μ_K(B)=Λ_h(B∩K) for every Borel set B. Must the Hausdorff dimension of K satisfy HD(K)=0?

Let (f_n)_{n≥1} be a regular polynomial sequence in C in the sense that each f_n(z)=∑_{j=0}^{d_n} a_{n,j} z^j has d_n≥2 and a_{n,d_n}≠0, and there exist constants A_1,A_2,A_3>0 such that for every n, |a_{n,d_n}|≥A_1, |a_{n,j}|≤A_2|a_{n,d_n}| for 0≤j≤d_n−1, and log|a_{n,d_n}|≤A_3 d_n. Write F_n=f_n∘f_{n-1}∘⋯∘f_1, let J(f_n) denote the Julia set of the non-autonomous sequence (f_n), and let μ_{J(f_n)} be the equilibrium measure of the regular compact set J(f_n). Is it possible to find simple formulas for dim(μ_{J(f_n)}), where dim(μ):=inf{HD(E): μ(E)=1}? ([drna.padovauniversitypress.it](https://drna.padovauniversitypress.it/system/files/papers/AlpanGoncharov_DRNA2017.pdf))

Let R be a commutative ring, let A be an arbitrary R-algebra (not assumed commutative), and let δ:A→A be either an R-derivation or an R-E-derivation, i.e. an R-linear map satisfying δ(ab)=δ(a)b+aδ(b)-δ(a)δ(b), equivalently δ=I-φ for some R-algebra endomorphism φ of A. For each left ideal, right ideal, or two-sided ideal I of A, determine the radical r(δ(I)), where for any R-subspace V⊆A one defines r(V):={a∈A | there exists N such that a^m∈V for all m≥N}.

Problem 1.4(B) asks: let R be a commutative ring, let A be an R-algebra (not assumed commutative), and let δ:A→A be either an R-derivation or an R-E-derivation, meaning an R-linear map satisfying δ(ab)=δ(a)b+aδ(b)-δ(a)δ(b) for all a,b∈A (equivalently, δ=I-φ for some R-algebra endomorphism φ of A). For a fixed choice ϑ∈{left,right,two-sided}, determine which such maps δ have the property that Im δ:=δ(A) is a ϑ-Mathieu subspace of A; that is, whenever a^m∈Im δ for every m≥1, one has ba^m∈Im δ in the left case, a^m c∈Im δ in the right case, or ba^m c∈Im δ in the two-sided case, for all sufficiently large m (i.e. for all m≥N for some N depending on a,b,c).

Let K be a field of characteristic zero, let A be a K-algebra, and let delta be a locally nilpotent K-derivation or a locally nilpotent K-E-derivation of A (that is, delta = I - phi for some K-algebra endomorphism phi of A). For each theta in {left, right, two-sided}, is it true that delta maps every theta-ideal I of A to a theta-Mathieu subspace delta(I) of A? Equivalently: whenever a in A satisfies a^m in delta(I) for every m >= 1, must one have b a^m in delta(I) for all m >= N in the left case, a^m c in delta(I) for all m >= N in the right case, and b a^m c in delta(I) for all m >= N in the two-sided case, for every b, c in A and some N depending on the data?

Let K be a field of characteristic zero, let A be an associative K-algebra, and let δ be either a locally finite K-derivation or a locally finite K-E-derivation, where a K-E-derivation means a K-linear map of the form δ = I - φ for some K-algebra endomorphism φ of A, and locally finite means that for every a in A the K-vector space spanned by {δ^i(a) | i >= 0} is finite-dimensional. Must the image Im δ := δ(A) be a two-sided Mathieu subspace of A; equivalently, whenever a in A satisfies a^m in Im δ for every m >= 1, must it follow that for every b, c in A there exists N such that ba^m c in Im δ for all m >= N?

Let K be a field of characteristic zero, let A be a K-algebra, fix theta in {left, right, two-sided}, and let delta be either a locally nilpotent K-derivation of A or a locally nilpotent K-E-derivation of A, where a K-E-derivation means a K-linear map delta:A->A satisfying delta(ab)=delta(a)b+a delta(b)-delta(a) delta(b) for all a,b in A (equivalently, delta=I_A-phi for some K-algebra endomorphism phi of A), and locally nilpotent means that for every a in A there exists m>=1 such that delta^m(a)=0. Must it be true that for every theta-ideal I of A, the image delta(I) is a theta-Mathieu subspace of A; equivalently, whenever V:=delta(I) and a in A satisfy a^m in V for all m>=1, then for all b,c in A one has ba^m in V if theta=left, a^m c in V if theta=right, and ba^m c in V if theta=two-sided, for all sufficiently large integers m?

Let K be a field of characteristic zero, let A be a K-algebra, and let δ be a K-derivation or a K-ℰ-derivation of A, where a K-ℰ-derivation means a K-linear map of the form δ = I_A - φ for some K-algebra endomorphism φ of A. Assume that δ is locally finite, i.e. for every a in A the K-subspace spanned by {δ^i(a) | i >= 0} is finite-dimensional. Must it follow that for every idempotent e in Im δ, the two-sided principal ideal (e) = AeA is contained in Im δ?

Let K be a field of characteristic zero, let A be a K-algebra, and let delta be a locally nilpotent K-derivation or K-E-derivation of A, where a K-E-derivation means a K-linear map of the form delta = I_A - phi for some K-algebra endomorphism phi of A (equivalently, delta(ab) = delta(a)b + a delta(b) - delta(a)delta(b)), and locally nilpotent means that for every a in A there exists m >= 1 such that delta^m(a) = 0. Fix theta in {left, right, two-sided}. If I is a theta-ideal of A and e in delta(I) is an idempotent, must the principal theta-ideal (e)_theta generated by e be contained in delta(I)?

Let K be a field of characteristic zero, not necessarily algebraically closed, and let A be a K-algebra. Suppose A has a multiplicative algebra grading A = ⊕_{λ∈Λ} A_λ indexed by a subset Λ ⊂ K such that A_λ A_μ ⊆ A_{λμ} for all λ, μ ∈ Λ. Must the K-subspace M := ⊕_{λ∈Λ, λ≠1} A_λ be a two-sided Mathieu subspace of A? Equivalently, if a ∈ A satisfies a^m ∈ M for every m ≥ 1, must it follow that for every b, c ∈ A there exists N such that b a^m c ∈ M for all m ≥ N?

Let n >= 1, let z = (z_1, ..., z_n) be commutative free variables, and let M be the C-subspace of the Laurent polynomial algebra C[z_1^{±1}, ..., z_n^{±1}] consisting of all Laurent polynomials whose constant term (i.e. the coefficient of z_1^0 ... z_n^0) is zero. Is M a Mathieu subspace of C[z_1^{±1}, ..., z_n^{±1}]? Equivalently, if f^m belongs to M for every m >= 1, must g f^m also belong to M for all sufficiently large m and every g in C[z_1^{±1}, ..., z_n^{±1}]?

Does the Damanik–Goldstein–Binder–Lukic conclusion for KdV extend to suitable perturbations of the Korteweg–de Vries equation on x in R: namely, if u(x,0)=u_0(x) with u_0 a suitable almost periodic function of x, does the perturbed Cauchy problem admit a unique global-in-time solution u(x,t) that evolves almost periodically in time?

Let H = (H_ij) be an n x n random band matrix with bandwidth w <= n, defined by H_ij = 0 for |i - j| >= w, and with the independent in-band entries iid, subject only to either real-symmetric symmetry H = H^T or complex-Hermitian symmetry H = H*. Can one prove the Fyodorov-Mirlin conjecture that the microscopic bulk eigenvalue statistics undergo a transition at the scale w ~ sqrt(n), namely: if w/sqrt(n) -> infinity then the local eigenvalue statistics are of GUE type, whereas if w/sqrt(n) -> 0 then the local eigenvalue statistics are Poisson?

For the Anderson model on the lattice Z^3, namely the random Schrödinger operator H = -Δ + V with iid site potentials {V(x)} indexed by x in Z^3, can one rigorously establish the conjectured spectral picture that, although eigenfunctions are localized near the edge of the spectrum, in the bulk of the spectrum the eigenfunctions are delocalized and the eigenvalues exhibit random-matrix statistics, and that there exists a mobility edge μ at which the statistics change from Poisson to random-matrix statistics; moreover, can one construct and analyze models that realize such a Poisson → random-matrix transition?

For general Wigner ensembles—namely n×n real symmetric or complex Hermitian random matrices whose entries are independent subject only to the symmetry constraint—can one prove universality of the microscopic local eigenvalue statistics, both in the bulk and at every endpoint of the support of the ensemble’s equilibrium measure, in the case where that support consists of more than one interval, and can one also analyze and control parameter-dependent regimes in which, as the underlying matrix distribution varies, intervals in the support of the equilibrium measure open and close?

In random matrix theory, for n x n matrix distributions depending on external parameter(s) p and having critical values p_c at which the associated equilibrium measure changes its nature—for example, when intervals in its support open, close, or merge—can one rigorously analyze the corresponding double-scaling limits in which p -> p_c as n -> infinity, and more generally the analogous multi-scaling limits? ([m.mathnet.ru](https://m.mathnet.ru/php/getFT.phtml?jrnid=sigma&option_lang=eng&paperid=1216&what=fullt))

If F_β(s) denotes the Tracy–Widom distribution function for β-ensembles at the spectral edge for a fixed β > 0, can one rigorously obtain explicit formulae for F_β beyond the classical invariant cases β = 1, 2, and 4, in particular by putting Rumanov's β = 6 representation in terms of Painlevé II and an auxiliary ODE on a fully rigorous footing and extending that program to every positive even integer β, and can one rigorously prove the detailed asymptotic formulas for F_β proposed by Borot, Eynard, Majumdar, and Nadal for all β > 0? ([sigma-journal.com](https://sigma-journal.com/2017/016/sigma17-016.pdf))

For the 1+1-dimensional Kardar-Parisi-Zhang equation for a height function h(x,t), x in R, t >= 0, can one prove, for solutions of its Cauchy problem with a wide set of initial data, 3:2:1 KPZ universality in the strong sense of Corwin, Quastel, and Remenik—namely, the full long-time scaling limit with spatial correlations on the t^{2/3} scale and fluctuations on the t^{1/3} scale—and can one identify the resulting limiting process?

For the 1+1-dimensional KPZ equation with height function h(x,t), viewed through the Cauchy problem on x in R and t >= 0, can one rigorously determine the joint space-time statistics of the solution at two or more space-time points—that is, analyze the joint distributions or correlation functions of (h(x1,t1), ..., h(xk,tk)) for k >= 2—rather than only one-point fluctuation laws?

Can one rigorously show that last-passage percolation with general weights belongs to the KPZ universality class in the full 3:2:1 sense—namely, that on scale t the spatial-correlation length is of order t^{2/3} and the centered last-passage-time fluctuations are of order t^{1/3}—rather than only establishing the fluctuation exponent?

Let π_N be a random permutation of {1, ..., N}, and let L_N denote the length of its longest increasing subsequence. Beyond the classical case in which π_N is uniformly distributed on S_N, can one prove that for more general probability distributions on S_N the fluctuations of L_N as N → ∞ are in the KPZ universality class in the sense used in the paper, namely that they occur on the N^(1/3) scale rather than the Gaussian N^(1/2) scale?

In the setting of Problem 3 on interacting particle systems and KPZ, can one understand, in a mathematically precise way, how Tracy and Widom’s 2007–2009 algebraic/combinatorial/analytical solution of the asymmetric simple exclusion process (ASEP) with step initial data actually works, and can that same method of solution be extended from step initial data to more general initial data for ASEP?

Within the KPZ/interacting-particle-systems setting, can one develop a perturbation theory, analogous to KAM theory for integrable dynamical systems, that applies to non-solvable models and can be used to investigate the persistence of the paper’s quoted "integrability" and to demonstrate the robustness of asymptotic scaling phenomena, in particular beyond the exactly solvable examples and the restricted initial-data regimes for which rigorous results are presently known? ([sigma-journal.com](https://sigma-journal.com/2017/016/sigma17-016.pdf))

Let H be an n x n random matrix, real symmetric when β=1 and complex Hermitian when β=2, drawn either from (i) a β=1 invariant ensemble with density proportional to exp(-(nβ/2) tr V(H)) dH, where V is C^4, uniformly convex, and has the growth assumptions of Definition 1.2, or from (ii) a β=1 or β=2 generalized Wigner ensemble in the sense of Definition 1.1. Let X(t) solve the Toda flow dX/dt = [X, X_- - X_-^*], X(0)=H, and for fixed 0<τ<1 and log(ε^{-1})/log n >= 5/3 + τ/2 define the 1-deflation time by T^(1)_{ε,n,Toda,E}(H) := inf{ t : sum_{j=2}^n |X_{1j}(t)|^2 = sum_{i=2}^n |X_{i1}(t)|^2 < ε^2 }. Can one prove, for the open cases singled out in Problem 4—namely β=1 invariant ensembles and β=1 or β=2 generalized Wigner ensembles—that the centered and scaled halting-time variable (T^(1)_{ε,n,Toda,E}(H) - ⟨T^(1)_{ε,n,Toda,E}⟩)/σ_{T^(1)_{ε,n,Toda,E}} has an n -> infinity universal limiting distribution depending only on β and not on the specific ensemble, by establishing the required joint edge statistics of the top eigenvalues λ_n, λ_{n-1}, λ_{n-2} and the first eigenvector components β_n, β_{n-1}, β_{n-2}?

Let H be an n x n random matrix drawn from a real (beta = 1) or complex (beta = 2) invariant or Wigner ensemble, and let T^(1)_{epsilon,n,QR,E} denote the first QR halting/1x1-deflation time. If lambda_j is the eigenvalue of H closest to 0, with lambda_j ~ 0 deep in the bulk of the spectrum, can one determine jointly, as n -> infinity, the statistics of the signed bulk ratios lambda_{j+1}/lambda_j and lambda_{j-1}/lambda_j together with the corresponding normalized eigenvector data, strongly enough to prove a QR analogue of Theorem 1, namely universality for the centered and scaled first QR halting-time statistic? ([sigma-journal.com](https://sigma-journal.com/2017/016/sigma17-016.pdf))

Let H be an n x n real symmetric or complex Hermitian random matrix drawn from an ensemble E, and let A be an isospectral eigenvalue algorithm, discrete or continuous, whose evolution X starts at H and converges to diagonal form. Define the deflation time T_{epsilon,n,A,E}(H) to be the smallest iteration/time for which, for some 1 <= j <= n-1, X has a block decomposition X = [[P, B],[B^*, Q]] with P of size j x j, Q of size (n-j) x (n-j), and ||B|| = ||B^*|| <= epsilon, so that the eigenvalues of the deflated matrix diag(P,Q) agree with those of H up to O(epsilon). Can one prove, for some specific eigenvalue algorithm A (for example A = Toda), a rigorous analog of Theorem 1: namely, in an appropriate joint scaling regime of epsilon and n as n -> infinity, establish a universal limiting law for the properly normalized deflation time T_{epsilon,n,A,E}, independent of the choice of ensemble E within the relevant symmetry class, even though the relevant deflation error depends on the eigenvalues and on all components of the eigenvectors of H?

Can one rigorously establish, for the conjugate-gradient algorithm among the “other numerical algorithms” treated empirically in [40], the same two-component universality for halting-time fluctuations that Problem 4 defines for numerical computation with random data—namely: for random positive-definite n × n linear systems Hx = b with H and b random, if k_ε(H,b) is the first CG iteration for which ||Hx_k - b||_2 < ε and τ_{ε,n,CG,E} := (k_ε(H,b) - ⟨k_ε⟩)/σ_{ε,n,CG,E}, does τ_{ε,n,CG,E} converge, for ε small and n large in the relevant scaling regime, to a limiting law that is independent of the underlying input ensemble E? ([www2.math.ethz.ch](https://www2.math.ethz.ch/EMIS/journals/SIGMA/2017/016/sigma17-016.pdf))

Can the Olver-Nadakuditi-Trogdon method for sampling invariant unitary ensembles—namely, the method based on computing the orthogonal polynomials naturally associated with the ensemble, which in the unitary case samples the distribution to essentially machine accuracy—be extended to orthogonal and symplectic invariant ensembles?

For the half-line initial-boundary value problem for the focusing nonlinear Schrödinger equation i u_t = u_xx + 2|u|^2 u on x>=0, t>=0, with prescribed initial data u(x,0)=f(x) for x>=0 and Dirichlet boundary forcing u(0,t)=e^{iwt} for t>=0, where w is any real number and no a priori expression for the Neumann trace u_x(0,t) is assumed, determine the asymptotic behavior of the solution u(x,t) as t -> infinity.

For the half-line initial-boundary value problem for the focusing nonlinear Schrödinger equation i u_t = u_xx + 2|u|^2 u on x≥0, t≥0, with prescribed initial data u(x,0)=f(x) for x≥0 and Dirichlet boundary forcing u(0,t)=e^{iwt} for t≥0, w∈R, determine the long-time asymptotic behavior of u(x,t) as t→∞; in particular, can one justify the expected low-frequency scenario that, as w↓0, finite-gap (k-gap) solutions of periodic NLS emerge from the boundary driver e^{iwt}? ([sigma-journal.com](https://sigma-journal.com/2017/016/sigma17-016.pdf))

Can one use the Bikbaev–Tarasov Bäcklund-transformation method to solve, on the quarter-plane x >= 0, t >= 0, the initial-boundary value problem for the defocusing nonlinear Schrödinger equation i u_t = u_xx - 2|u|^2 u with prescribed initial data u(x,0) = f(x) on x >= 0 and fixed Robin boundary condition u_x(0,t) + q u(0,t) = 0, by extending the solution from x > 0 to x < 0 and controlling the singularities created by that extension?

Consider the nonlinear Schrödinger initial-boundary value problem on the half-line x>0, t>0 with fixed Robin boundary condition u_x(0,t)+q u(0,t)=0 and smooth initial data satisfying the required compatibility conditions at the corner (0,0). For the known integrable cubic focusing case i u_t = u_xx + 2|u|^2 u, classicality of the solution is obtained via the Bikbaev-Tarasov Bäcklund transform. Can one instead prove, by PDE methods and for a general reasonable smooth nonlinearity replacing 2|u|^2 u (for example 2|u|^4 u), that the resulting solution is classical on the quarter-plane, i.e. C^2 in x and C^1 in t for x>0, t>0?

Motivated by the half-line nonlinear Schrödinger initial-boundary value problem discussed in Problem 5, especially the Robin-boundary case, where for sufficiently smooth initial and boundary data satisfying the necessary compatibility conditions at (0,0) one expects a classical solution (C^2 in the spatial variables and C^1 in time), what can actually be proved in arbitrary spatial dimension about the smoothness of solutions to initial-boundary value problems for dispersive equations?

For the focusing nonlinear Schrödinger equation on the line in the semiclassical/small-dispersion regime ε = ħ -> 0, with general smooth initial data u0(x) = u(x,0), can one solve the non-self-adjoint forward scattering problem by determining the full extended scattering data u0 -> (r(z), {λ_j}, {c_j}) for the relevant scattering operator T(ħ), and then apply the Olver/Deconinck-Olver-Trogdon numerical Riemann-Hilbert methodology to compute the corresponding solution u(x,t) of the Cauchy problem in this limit?

For the Airy operator A_s : L^2(s, infinity) -> L^2(s, infinity) with kernel K_Ai(lambda, mu) = (Ai(lambda)Ai'(mu) - Ai'(lambda)Ai(mu)) / (lambda - mu), where Ai is the standard Airy function and det(I - A_s) is the edge-scaling distribution for the largest eigenvalue of GUE, determine the asymptotic behavior as s -> infinity of the eigenfunctions {tilde u_j(.; s)} in the eigenvalue problem A_s tilde u_j(.; s) = tilde lambda_j(s) tilde u_j(.; s), and accurately compute these eigenfunctions for finite s.

For a fixed exponent ell in the regime highlighted by the adjacent discussion (in particular ell>2), consider the Cauchy problem on the real line for the focusing perturbed nonlinear Schrödinger equation i (u_tilde)_t + (u_tilde)_{xx} + 2|u_tilde|^2 u_tilde + epsilon |u_tilde|^ell u_tilde = 0, with initial data u_tilde(x,0)=f_tilde(x) satisfying f_tilde(x)->0 as |x|->infinity. Can one analyze solutions of this Cauchy problem, especially their behavior as t->infinity, in the particularly important case where f_tilde is the initial profile of a 2-soliton solution of the unperturbed focusing NLS (epsilon=0), despite the fact that the sup-norm decay mechanism available in the defocusing problem breaks down because of solitons?

For the semi-infinite Toda shock problem with particles x_k(t), k >= 0, governed for k >= 1 by x_k'' = exp(x_{k-1} - x_k) - exp(x_k - x_{k+1}), with shock initial/boundary data x_k(0) = k and x_k'(0) = 0 for k >= 1 and x_0(t) = 2 a t for a > 0, can one use Riemann–Hilbert/nonlinear steepest-descent methods to give a fully rigorous proof that, for every supercritical drive a > a_crit = 1, the solution in the frame moving with the driving particle x_0(t) has the long-time asymptotics claimed by Venakides–Deift–Oba, namely that as t -> infinity the lattice executes a binary periodic motion?

Consider the driven half-line lattice shock problem with x_k''(t) = F(x_{k-1}(t) - x_k(t)) - F(x_k(t) - x_{k+1}(t)) for k >= 1, together with shock data x_k(0) = k and x_k'(0) = 0 for k >= 1 and boundary drive x_0(t) = 2at, where a > a_crit = 1. If F is a suitably small perturbation of e^x and the perturbed lattice admits a binary periodic state x_k(t+T) = x_k(t), x_{k+2}(t) = x_k(t) for some T > 0 and all k in Z, can one rigorously analyze this general shock problem and prove the numerically observed long-time asymptotics, namely that in the frame moving with the driving particle x_0(t) the solution behaves as in the Toda case and settles into binary periodic motion as t -> infinity?

Can one give a rigorous and explicit solution of the diffraction problem for scalar waves at fixed frequency from two slits in the plane—the mathematical setting of Young's double-slit experiment in optics and its quantum-mechanical analogue—in a form from which the relevant asymptotics of the solution can be extracted?

To what extent can hadronic transport models with string excitation and fragmentation reproduce the experimentally observed baryon stopping—quantified by the rapidity distributions of stopped nucleons dN_B/dy—in Au+Au collisions at √s_NN=5–40 GeV, and thereby provide realistic three‐dimensional initial net‐baryon‐density profiles for subsequent hydrodynamic simulations in the RHIC beam energy scan program?

Can the source terms in the three-fluid hydrodynamics framework of Batyuk et al. (Phys. Rev. C94 (2016) 044917, arXiv:1608.00965)—which model baryon charge and energy–momentum exchange between two baryon-rich projectile/target fluids and a fireball fluid over a finite deposition time—quantitatively reproduce the net-baryon rapidity distributions measured in central heavy-ion collisions at intermediate beam energies (√s_{NN}≈2–20 GeV)?

In full dynamical simulations of relativistic heavy-ion collisions at intermediate beam energies that include a non-equilibrium passage through a QCD critical endpoint or a first-order phase transition with fluctuating hydrodynamics, do the enhancements in higher moments (variance, skewness, kurtosis) of the net-baryon number density survive (i) the Cooper–Frye hypersurface particlization with enforced global conservation of energy, momentum, and baryon number, (ii) the additional Poisson sampling fluctuations on the particlization surface, and (iii) the subsequent hadronic rescattering stage to yield a statistically significant deviation from baseline in final-state cumulant observables?

Does there exist an overcomplete Gabor frame G(g,a,b) = {E_{mb}T_{na}g}_{m,n in Z} for L^2(R), where g is in L^2(R), a,b > 0, T_a f(x) = f(x-a), and E_b f(x) = e^{2 pi i b x} f(x), such that one can choose an ordering {f_k}_{k=0}^infty of all its elements and find a bounded linear operator T: L^2(R) -> L^2(R) with f_k = T^k phi for every k >= 0 (equivalently, {f_k}_{k=0}^infty = {T^k phi}_{k=0}^infty), where phi = f_0?

Fix I in {N_0, Z}. Let g in L^2(R) and a,b > 0 be such that the Gabor system G(g,a,b) = {E_{mb}T_{na}g}_{m,n in Z} is an overcomplete frame for L^2(R). Does there exist an ordering {f_k}_{k in I} of the elements of G(g,a,b), a vector phi in L^2(R), and a bounded linear operator T on L^2(R) (for I = Z, with the negative iterates T^k well defined on the orbit span) such that f_k = T^k phi for every k in I?

Let g in L^2(R) and a,b>0 be such that the lattice Gabor system {E_{mb}T_{na}g}_{m,n in Z}, where E_{mb}f(x)=e^{2 pi i mb x}f(x) and T_{na}f(x)=f(x-na), is an overcomplete frame for L^2(R). Does there exist a bijective ordering {f_k}_{k=0}^infty of the elements of this Gabor frame and a bounded linear operator T:L^2(R)->L^2(R) such that f_k=T^k f_0 for every k in N_0?

Does there exist an overcomplete Gabor frame {E_{mb}T_{na}g}_{m,n in Z} for L^2(R) such that, after a suitable bijective ordering of its elements by Z, the ordered frame can be written in the form {T^k phi}_{k in Z} for some bounded linear operator T:L^2(R)->L^2(R) and some phi in L^2(R)?

Do there exist overcomplete Gabor frames {E_{mb}T_{na}g}_{m,n in Z} for L^2(R), with g in L^2(R) and a,b>0, such that one can choose an ordering {f_k}_{k in Z} of the frame elements for which there exist a bounded linear operator T: L^2(R) -> L^2(R) and a vector phi in L^2(R) satisfying {f_k}_{k in Z} = {T^k phi}_{k in Z}?

Do there exist a function phi in L^2(R) and a number b>0 such that the lattice-translate family {T_{kb}phi}_{k in Z}, where T_a f(x)=f(x-a), is an overcomplete frame sequence for V:=closure(span{T_{kb}phi : k in Z}), and such that one can choose an ordering {f_k}_{k=0}^infty of this same set for which there exist f_0 in V and a bounded linear operator T on V (equivalently, in the paper’s ambient formulation, a bounded operator on L^2(R) restricting to V) satisfying f_k=T^k f_0 for every k>=0?

Let H be a separable complex Hilbert space, let T be a bounded linear operator on H, and let phi in H be such that {T^n phi}_{n=0}^infty is a frame for H. If this frame is norm-bounded below, i.e. inf_{n >= 0} ||T^n phi|| > 0, must {T^n phi}_{n=0}^infty necessarily be a Riesz basis for H?

Let exp(u) = |u|/p(u) for a nonempty finite word u, where p(u) is the least period of u. For k ≥ 2, let RT(k) be the smallest rational number α for which there exists an infinite word over a k-letter alphabet whose finite factors all have exponent at most α, and let FRT(k) be the smallest rational number α for which there exists an infinite word over a k-letter alphabet whose finite factors all have exponent at most α and which contains only finitely many factors of exponent RT(k). Since RT(4) = 7/5, is it true that FRT(4) = RT(4) = 7/5?
