Let w be a finite word of length n over an arbitrary alphabet, and let Sq(w)={u^2 : u is a nonempty word and u^2 occurs as a contiguous factor of w}. Is it true that |Sq(w)| ≤ n for every finite word w with |w|=n?

Let Σ be a finite alphabet, let Σ+ denote the set of nonempty words over Σ, and for each finite word w ∈ Σ* define its square density by ρsq(w) = (1/|w|) · |{x^2 : x ∈ Σ+, and x^2 is a factor of w}|, where the set counts distinct square factors of w. Can one compute a mapping f : Σ* -> Σ* and a constant c > 1 such that, for every w ∈ Σ*, if ρsq(w) >= 1, then ρsq(f(w)) >= c · ρsq(w)?

For every positive integer n, does every finite word of length n over a binary alphabet contain at most n runs, where a run is an occurrence of a repetition of exponent at least 2 that is maximal in the sense that it cannot be extended to the left or to the right to obtain the same type of pattern?

Let u be an infinite word, and for each n ∈ N_0 let R_u(n) denote the least length of a contiguous factor (window) of u that contains every factor of u of length n. Define the recurrence quotient by ρ(u) = lim sup_{n→∞} R_u(n)/n. For each irrational α ∈ [0,1], let ρ(α) denote the recurrence quotient of a Sturmian sequence of slope α, and let S = {ρ(α) : α ∈ [0,1] \ Q}. What is the Hausdorff dimension of S? More generally, for each real a, what is the Hausdorff dimension of S ∩ [a, a + 1]?

Let u be an infinite word over a finite alphabet, let p_u(n) denote the number of distinct factors of u of length n, let R_u(n) be the length of the smallest factor (window) of u containing every factor of u of length n, and define the recurrence quotient by ρ(u) = limsup_{n→∞} R_u(n)/n. Beyond the Sturmian case, develop a study of recurrence quotients for other families of infinite words, in particular for words whose factor complexity satisfies p_u(n) = 2n + 1, and more generally for infinite words in general.

Let w be a uniformly recurrent infinite word over a finite alphabet. For each n >= 0, let P_w(n) be the number of palindromic factors of w of length n, let p_w(n) be the number of all factors of w of length n, and let Gamma_n(w) denote the Rauzy graph of order n of w (vertices: factors of length n; edges: factors of length n + 1). Describe the structure of the Rauzy graphs Gamma_n(w) for those words w that attain the upper bound on palindromic complexity, namely for which P_w(n) + P_w(n + 1) = p_w(n + 1) - p_w(n) + 2 for every n >= 0.

Let A be a finite alphabet, let f: A* -> A* be a morphism, and let a ∈ A be such that a is the first letter of f(a) and the iterates of f on a define a right-infinite fixed point f^ω(a). Recall that an infinite word w ∈ A^N is quasiperiodic if there exists a nonempty finite word q ∈ A+ such that every position of w belongs to some occurrence of q as a factor of w. Is there an algorithm that, given f and a, decides whether the pure morphic word f^ω(a) is quasiperiodic? ([paperzz.com](https://paperzz.com/doc/7042904/ten-conferences-words--open-problems-and))

Let Σ and Δ be finite alphabets, and let h, g: Σ* -> Δ* be morphisms. Recall that the Post Correspondence Problem asks whether there exists a nonempty word x in Σ* such that h(x) = g(x). Call two words y, z in Δ* comparable if one is a prefix of the other. An instance (h, g) is called a unique equality continuation instance if, for every word u in Σ* and every pair of distinct letters a, b in Σ, the comparabilities of h(ua) with g(ua) and of h(ub) with g(ub) together imply h(u) = g(u). Is the Post Correspondence Problem decidable when restricted to unique equality continuation instances?

Let A and B be finite alphabets, and let h,g:A*→B* be morphisms, viewed as an instance I=(h,g) of the Post Correspondence Problem. Call two words x,y∈B* comparable if one is a prefix of the other. Is there an algorithm that, given I, decides whether I is a unique equality continuation instance, meaning that for every u∈A* and every pair of distinct letters a,b∈A, the comparabilities h(ua) and g(ua), and h(ub) and g(ub), force h(u)=g(u)?

Given a finite loopless brick G—that is, a connected nonbipartite matching covered graph of order at least two in which every edge lies in some perfect matching and which has no nontrivial tight cuts—characterize exactly when G is solid, meaning that every separating cut of G is tight (equivalently, that G has no nontrivial separating cuts), and determine the complexity of the decision problem SOLID-BRICK: on input a brick G, decide whether G is solid. In particular, is SOLID-BRICK in NP, and is SOLID-BRICK solvable in polynomial time?

Let G be a loopless cubic graph. Assume that G is a brick, meaning that G is a connected nonbipartite graph in which every edge belongs to some perfect matching and G has no nontrivial tight cuts, where a cut is tight if every perfect matching meets it in exactly one edge. If G is also solid, equivalently if G has no nontrivial separating cuts (a cut is separating if both of its cut-contractions are matching covered), must G be odd-intercyclic; that is, must every two odd cycles of G share a vertex? ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1705.09428))

Among loopless graphs, characterize all bricks G, where a brick is a nonbipartite matching covered graph with no nontrivial tight cuts, such that K4 is not a conformal minor of G; equivalently, determine exactly which bricks are K4-free, meaning that there is no bi-subdivision H of K4 with H a subgraph of G and G - V(H) admitting a perfect matching.

Characterize all bricks G—that is, all connected nonbipartite graphs of order at least two in which every edge belongs to some perfect matching and which have no nontrivial tight cuts, where a cut C is tight if |C \cap M| = 1 for every perfect matching M of G—for which the triangular prism \overline{C_6} is not a conformal minor; equivalently, for which there is no bisubdivision H of \overline{C_6} contained in G such that G - V(H) has a perfect matching.

Determine all connected 7-dimensional homogeneous Riemannian g.o. spaces (M=G/K,g), meaning those for which every geodesic is an orbit γ(t)=exp(tX)·o of a one-parameter subgroup of a connected transitive isometry group G; more generally, obtain a complete classification of homogeneous Riemannian g.o. spaces in every dimension n>7. ([irishmathsoc.org](https://www.irishmathsoc.org/bull79/Arvanitoyeorgos.pdf))

Let (M = G/K, g) be a homogeneous Riemannian manifold, with G a connected transitive group of isometries, base point o = eK, and reductive decomposition g = k ⊕ m. Assume that (M = G/K, g) is not a G-geodesic-orbit space. Can one give an explicit description of all homogeneous geodesics through o—equivalently, of all nonzero X in g for which gamma_X(t) = exp(tX) · o is a geodesic—and hence, by G-homogeneity, of all homogeneous geodesics of M?

For a connected homogeneous Riemannian manifold (M,g), is there an intrinsic, presentation-independent criterion for the geodesic-orbit property—equivalently, can one show that whether every geodesic of (M,g) is an orbit of a one-parameter subgroup is independent of the chosen realization M=G/K by a connected transitive isometry group G and of the chosen Ad(K)-invariant reductive decomposition g=k⊕m? In particular, can such an intrinsic viewpoint explain why the paper often works with G-g.o. spaces rather than asserting the full g.o. property a priori?

For a reductive homogeneous pseudo-Riemannian space (M=G/K,g) with reductive decomposition g=k⊕m, base point o=eK, and invariant nondegenerate symmetric bilinear form on m, can one formulate and prove pseudo-Riemannian analogues of Proposition 2.2 and Proposition 9.3—compatible with the pseudo-Riemannian geodesic lemma of Section 8, so that possible reparametrization in the null case is allowed—that characterize exactly when (i) gamma(t)=exp(t(a+x))·o, with a in k and x in m, is a homogeneous geodesic, and when (ii) gamma(t)=exp(tX)exp(tY)exp(tZ)·o, with X,Y,Z in m, is a geodesic curve?

Let (M=G/K,g) be a homogeneous Riemannian manifold, with G a fixed transitive group of isometries and o=eK. A two-step homogeneous geodesic through o is a geodesic of the form gamma(t)=exp(tX)exp(tY)·o with X,Y in g. Is it true that whenever a geodesic through o can be written, for some k >= 3, as gamma(t)=exp(tX_1)...exp(tX_k)·o with X_1,...,X_k in g, it is already representable as gamma(t)=exp(tX)exp(tY)·o for suitable X,Y in g, so that the search for three-step or higher-step homogeneous geodesics on homogeneous Riemannian spaces reduces to the two-step case?

Given a set J of jobs, where each job j has a processing time p_j, a due date d_j, and a weight w_j, and all jobs must be scheduled nonpreemptively on a single machine, let C_j denote the completion time of job j in the schedule and let T_j := max{C_j - d_j, 0} be its tardiness. Is the problem 1||Σ_{j∈J} w_j T_j of finding a schedule minimizing Σ_{j∈J} w_j T_j fixed-parameter tractable with respect to the parameter p_max := max_{j∈J} p_j; that is, does there exist an algorithm that solves every instance I in time f(p_max)·|I|^{O(1)}? ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1709.01670))

For an instance I of the nonpreemptive single-machine scheduling problem 1|prec|sum_j w_j C_j, consisting of jobs j with processing times p_j, weights w_j, and precedence constraints forming a partial order, let OPT(I) be the minimum value of sum_j w_j C_j and let LP(I) be the lower bound obtained from the natural LP relaxation of the natural ILP formulation considered in Section 3.2. If k := OPT(I) - LP(I), does there exist a polynomial-time kernelization that transforms I into an equivalent instance whose encoding size is bounded by a polynomial in k? ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1709.01670))

For the nonpreemptive single-machine scheduling problems with release dates r_j and due dates d_j, where each job j has processing time p_j, and in the weighted case also weight w_j, let U_j be the indicator that job j is tardy (U_j = 1 if its completion time exceeds d_j, and U_j = 0 otherwise), and let p_max := max_j p_j. Are the problems 1|r_j|∑U_j and 1|r_j|∑w_jU_j W[1]-hard when parameterized by p_max?

Does the nonpreemptive single-machine scheduling problem of minimizing the makespan C_max = max_{j∈J} C_j for a set J of jobs with processing times p_j ∈ N, in the presence of a set F of |F| = τ forbidden time instants such that no job may start or complete at any time in F, admit a fixed-parameter algorithm with running time f(τ)·poly(|I|) when parameterized solely by τ? ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1709.01670.pdf))

Does there exist a computable function f such that the following high-multiplicity identical-parallel-machine makespan problem can be solved in time f(p)·|I|^{O(1)}, parameterized only by p, the number of distinct processing times? Input: a binary-encoded integer m giving the number of identical parallel machines, binary-encoded processing-time values a_1, ..., a_p, and binary-encoded multiplicities n_1, ..., n_p, where n_i jobs have processing time a_i for each i. Task: schedule all jobs nonpreemptively on the m identical machines so as to minimize the makespan C_max.

Is the nonpreemptive three-machine parallel-identical scheduling problem P3|prec, p_j=1|C_max fixed-parameter tractable when parameterized solely by the width w of the partial order induced by the precedence constraints, where p_j=1 for every job j and w is the maximum size of an antichain of jobs; equivalently, is there an algorithm running in time f(w)·n^{O(1)} that computes an optimal minimum-makespan schedule for such instances?

Is each of the following two nonpreemptive scheduling problems fixed-parameter tractable when parameterized by the number m of machines: given m parallel identical machines and jobs j with release dates r_j, due dates d_j, and a common processing time p_j=p (and, in the weighted case, weights w_j), compute an optimal schedule assigning every job to exactly one machine so as to minimize ∑_j w_j U_j, respectively ∑_j U_j, where U_j=0 if job j completes by d_j and U_j=1 otherwise?

Does the machine-restricted just-in-time (equivalently, interval-scheduling) problem P|M_j, d_j-r_j=p_j|Σ_j w_j U_j admit a fixed-parameter algorithm with respect to the number m of parallel identical machines? Concretely: given m identical machines and jobs j with integer weight w_j, processing time p_j, release date r_j, due date d_j satisfying d_j-r_j=p_j, and an eligibility set M_j⊆{1,…,m}, where jobs are processed nonpreemptively on exactly one allowed machine and each machine handles at most one job at a time, can one compute in f(m)·poly(n) time a schedule minimizing Σ_j w_j U_j, where U_j=0 if job j completes by d_j and U_j=1 otherwise?

Let J be a set of jobs to be scheduled on m parallel identical machines, with preemption allowed, and let p := |{p_j : j in J}| be the number of distinct job processing times. Is each of the following optimization problems fixed-parameter tractable with respect to p, that is, solvable in time f(p)·|I|^{O(1)} for some computable function f: (i) P|pmtn,r_j|∑_{j in J} C_j, where each job j has release date r_j and completion time C_j; (ii) P|pmtn|∑_{j in J} U_j, where each job j has due date d_j and U_j = 1 iff C_j > d_j; and (iii) P|pmtn|∑_{j in J} T_j, where T_j = max{C_j - d_j, 0}?

In Graham’s three-field notation, consider the scheduling problem on exactly two identical parallel machines with preemption allowed, where every job j has common processing time p_j=p, weight w_j∈N, due date d_j∈N, and completion time C_j, and the objective is to minimize total weighted tardiness ∑_j w_j T_j with T_j:=max{0, C_j-d_j}. Is the problem P2|pmtn, p_j=p|∑_j w_j T_j W[1]-hard when parameterized by the common processing time p?

Given a nonpreemptive three-machine flow shop instance with job set J, where each job j has exactly three operations that must be processed on machines 1, 2, 3 in this common order with processing times p_{1j}, p_{2j}, p_{3j} in N, and writing p_max := max_{i in {1,2,3}, j in J} p_{ij}, is there an algorithm running in f(p_max) * poly(|I|) time that solves F3||C_max, that is, computes a schedule of minimum makespan C_max?

Given a nonpreemptive job-shop instance on exactly three machines, where each job j consists of n_j totally ordered operations o_{ij}, each operation o_{ij} must be processed on a prescribed machine mu_{ij} in {1,2,3} for an integer processing time p_{ij}, each job can be processed by at most one machine at a time, and each machine can process at most one operation at a time, let p_max := max_{i,j} p_{ij} and n_max := max_j n_j. Is the makespan minimization problem J3||C_max fixed-parameter tractable with respect to the joint parameter (p_max, n_max)?

In the job-shop scheduling problem J||C_max, with m machines and n jobs, where each job j consists of n_j operations that must be processed in a job-specific total order, operation o_{ij} requiring processing time p_{ij} on a prescribed machine μ_{ij}, and with the constraints that each job and each machine can participate in at most one operation at any time, does there exist, for every ε > 0, a computable function f such that one can compute a schedule whose makespan is at most (1+ε) times optimal in time f(m, ε) · poly(n), without any additional dependence on n_max := max_j n_j, the maximum number of operations per job?

Is the open-shop scheduling problem O|p_ij=1, ST_sd,b|C_max fixed-parameter tractable with respect to the parameter g, where the number of machines is part of the input, each job has exactly one unit-time operation on each machine, the operations of each job may be scheduled in arbitrary order, the jobs are partitioned into g batches, and switching on any machine from a job in batch p to a job in batch q incurs a sequence-dependent setup time s_pq ∈ N? ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1709.01670.pdf))

For the non-preemptive m-machine open-shop scheduling problem O|p_ij=1, r_j|∑ w_j U_j, where each job J_j has exactly one unit-time operation on each of the m machines, a release date r_j, a due date d_j, and a weight w_j, and where C_j denotes the completion time of J_j and U_j:=0 if C_j≤d_j and U_j:=1 otherwise, is there an algorithm running in f(m)·|I|^{O(1)} time that computes a schedule minimizing ∑_j w_j U_j (equivalently, maximizing weighted throughput)?

For a fixed physical realization of cosmological inflation, determine the generality of inflation for generic initial data: namely, characterize whether generic cosmological initial data—allowing the inhomogeneities and anisotropies expected in random initial conditions—evolve into an inflationary spacetime, rather than only specially prepared initial states, with the notions of both "generic initial data" and "inflation" made precise within that chosen model.

Within general relativity, determine sufficiently precise theoretical predictions for the emitted gravitational-wave waveforms of binary black hole systems so that they can be used as template waveforms for optimal detection and parameter extraction from gravitational-wave detector data.

For collapse models in general relativity that admit black-hole formation, consider one-parameter families of solutions to the coupled Einstein-matter equations whose prescribed initial data depend continuously on a parameter p measuring the strength of initially imploding matter, so that small p leads to globally regular or dispersive evolution and large p leads to a singular black hole. At the critical value of p corresponding to the threshold of black-hole formation, there is a critical self-similar solution. The research question is: understand and characterize this critical solution and the associated critical phenomena in gravitational collapse in GR, especially in cases with no assumed symmetries.

Resolve the black hole information paradox for a black hole formed by gravitational collapse in general relativity and evaporating completely by Hawking radiation: does semiclassical quantum field theory on a classical curved spacetime really imply that an initial pure quantum state evolves into a mixed thermal final state after the black hole disappears, or is information preserved in the full theory; and, if information is preserved, by what mechanism are both the causality problem (information trapped behind the horizon if superluminal escape is forbidden) and the entanglement problem created by Hawking-pair production overcome?

Can one formulate a mathematically and physically consistent cosmological framework that resolves the cosmological constant problem—namely, why the huge vacuum-energy density predicted by quantum field theory does not gravitate as an enormous cosmological constant, so that the observed effective cosmological constant is naturally tiny rather than requiring cancellation by a bare term to roughly 120 decimal places—and that simultaneously explains the observed acceleration of the Universe over the last few billion years, including the coincidence that the dark-energy density is of the same order as the present matter density, by determining whether dark energy is a true cosmological constant, a dynamical component such as quintessence or phantom energy, or an apparent large-scale effect of modified gravity or backreaction/inhomogeneities?

Can one formulate a fully consistent theory of quantum gravity (QG)—that is, a single unified field theory including general relativity and the standard model of particle physics—valid in the overlap regime where both general relativity and quantum mechanics are essential and current attempts produce divergent gravitational or curvature behavior, and which determines whether spacetime is fundamentally continuous or discrete, whether gravity is graviton-mediated or instead arises from discrete spacetime structure, and whether the theory predicts departures from general relativity at very small scales, very large scales, or in other extreme circumstances?

Formulate precisely, and then prove, Penrose’s weak cosmic censorship conjecture for the Einstein evolution problem in classical general relativity: for generic nonsingular, realistic Cauchy initial data for Einstein’s equations coupled to physical matter, the corresponding maximal Cauchy development should contain no naked singularities; in the asymptotically flat isolated-system setting, this means that light rays from points arbitrarily near a singularity cannot escape to infinity.

In classical general relativity with spacetime dimension D > 4, determine the stability of higher-dimensional black holes under gravitational perturbations, i.e. identify which higher-dimensional black-hole families are stable and which exhibit genuinely higher-dimensional instabilities absent in four-dimensional GR, such as Gregory-Laflamme-type and ultraspinning instabilities. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1710.02105))

Can one rigorously prove, within loop quantum gravity and without first imposing the symmetry reduction used in loop quantum cosmology, that the singularity-resolution results established for spatially homogeneous cosmological spacetimes extend to a more general setting, especially to genuinely inhomogeneous spacetimes?

For the Einstein equations in cosmology, prove a cosmic no-hair theorem in the genuinely inhomogeneous setting: namely, show that for generic inhomogeneous initial data on a regular Cauchy hypersurface, with positive cosmological constant and reasonable matter, if the model is initially expanding then its maximal future development exists globally and asymptotically isotropizes toward de Sitter spacetime at late times.

In the study of asymptotic spatially homogeneous Bianchi type IX cosmological dynamics in general relativity near the past spacelike singularity, prove that the past attractor of the Bianchi type IX dynamical system coincides with the Mixmaster attractor in the paper's sense, namely the Bianchi II variety, rather than merely being a subset thereof. ([scribd.com](https://www.scribd.com/document/710276968/Unsolved-problems-in-mathematical-physics))

Within classical general relativity, prove the locality part of the Belinskii-Khalatnikov-Lifshitz (BKL) conjecture in the general inhomogeneous cosmological setting: for a generic inhomogeneous cosmology approaching a past spacelike singularity, show that the asymptotic evolution becomes local near the singularity, in the sense intended in the paper that particle horizons shrink to zero and communication between distinct timelines is asymptotically suppressed. ([prawobrzeze.info](https://prawobrzeze.info/userfiles/file/zodemiwalib.pdf))

In general relativity, for generic inhomogeneous cosmological solutions of the Einstein field equations approaching a past spacelike singularity in the BKL/mixmaster regime, prove the existence of spike structures—namely spatial points that remain in an old Kasner epoch while neighboring points transition to a new one, so that spatial-derivative terms remain dynamically significant and asymptotic locality can fail there—and determine how the presence of such spikes must enter any eventual proof of the generic spacelike-singularity picture. ([scribd.com](https://www.scribd.com/document/710276968/Unsolved-problems-in-mathematical-physics))

Within general relativity, for a generic inhomogeneous cosmology approaching a past spacelike singularity, determine whether the asymptotic singularity structure is structurally stable when one replaces the previously studied vacuum or simplified matter settings by the general matter fields relevant to the early universe, especially matter of the kinds singled out nearby in the paper such as massless scalar and electromagnetic fields. ([scribd.com](https://www.scribd.com/document/710276968/Unsolved-problems-in-mathematical-physics))

In the cosmological setting of initial singularities, determine whether isotropic singularities—equivalently, conformal singularities for which the conformal structure remains regular at the singularity, in the sense motivated by Penrose's Weyl-curvature hypothesis—are typical in alternative modified theories of gravity, rather than occurring only in special exact models such as the known higher-order curvature, Gauss-Bonnet, or quadratic-Ricci examples.

Let M be a compact smooth 3-manifold, and let (h,K) be a generic smooth vacuum initial data set on M, where h is a Riemannian metric and K is a symmetric 2-tensor satisfying the vacuum Einstein constraint equations. Prove that the maximal vacuum Cauchy development of (h,K) is already the maximal vacuum extension of that data set; in other words, for generic vacuum data on M, the associated maximal globally hyperbolic vacuum spacetime admits no proper vacuum extension beyond its Cauchy horizon.

Under the dominant energy condition, prove or disprove the Penrose inequality in the general Lorentzian setting of classical general relativity: for asymptotically flat initial data with ADM mass whose initial hypersurface contains a marginally (outer) future-trapped surface (apparent horizon), more explicitly a compact spacelike hypersurface S whose boundary consists of a cut C of future null infinity together with a trapped surface, must the ADM mass satisfy the Penrose lower bound determined by the area of the trapped/horizon boundary component, or can one construct a counterexample?

In general relativity, for self-gravitating collisionless matter models, prove global existence of classical spatially inhomogeneous solutions for sufficiently small initial data; and, for the Einstein-Vlasov system, prove an existence-and-uniqueness theorem for general spatially homogeneous solutions—including, as a representative case, Bianchi type IX—and investigate the large-initial-data case.

Within general relativity, prove the full nonlinear stability of the Kerr black hole: if initial data for the Einstein equations are sufficiently close to Kerr initial data, show that the resulting evolution asymptotically tracks a Kerr black hole, with perturbations of the Kerr solution decaying, thereby giving a mathematically rigorous description of Kerr dynamics under nonlinear perturbations. ([scribd.com](https://www.scribd.com/document/710276968/Unsolved-problems-in-mathematical-physics))

In general relativity, can one formulate a mathematically appropriate definition of a dynamical horizon, understood as the evolving boundary of a black hole, in the setting of a spacetime containing a closed oriented spacelike 2-surface (typically S^2) with its two future-directed null normals, where future-trapped surfaces are characterized by area-non-increase along both future null evolutions and apparent horizons by the vanishing of one null mean curvature, and in a way that captures the genuinely nonlinear evolution of horizons rather than only the linearized regime in which the horizon is treated as fixed?

Let (M,g) be a smooth 4-dimensional Lorentzian spacetime satisfying Einstein's field equations. Formulate rigorously what it means for a moving physical body to be a test particle, i.e. to have negligible mass and negligible self-gravitational backreaction on the background spacetime, and prove that in this test-particle (negligible-mass) limit its worldline is a spacetime geodesic of g.

For asymptotically Anti-de Sitter spacetimes, after fixing boundary conditions at infinity, determine whether the conjectured nonlinear instability of AdS—supported in the spherically symmetric Einstein equations coupled to a self-gravitating minimally coupled massless scalar field, where arbitrarily small perturbations can produce a weakly turbulent cascade toward high frequencies and form arbitrarily small black holes—behaves qualitatively differently in models more general than spherically symmetric scalar-field collapse, especially for non-spherical perturbations and in arbitrary spacetime dimension.

In general relativity, for stationary asymptotically flat vacuum black holes in spacetime dimension D > 4, determine whether there is a higher-dimensional analogue of the 4D Schwarzschild/Kerr black-hole uniqueness theorems, after formulating the appropriate higher-dimensional versions of the standard assumptions such as analyticity, non-degeneracy, and connectedness. ([scribd.com](https://www.scribd.com/document/710276968/Unsolved-problems-in-mathematical-physics))

Determine when a smooth 4-dimensional Lorentzian spacetime (M, g) can be explicitly constructed, at least locally, from the scalar polynomial curvature invariants formed from the Riemann tensor and its covariant derivatives, and determine a minimal sufficient set of such invariants for this characterization.

On a smooth 4-dimensional Lorentz manifold (M,g) in general relativity, provide a mathematically rigorous definition of spacetime or space-volume averaging that is well posed and generally covariant, applies to the tensorial geometric and matter fields on the underlying differential manifold, and yields well-defined macroscopic geometry and macroscopic matter fields together with corresponding averaged gravitational field equations, without assuming a priori that the averaged equations retain the exact form of the local Einstein equations and with any correlation terms arising from nonlinearity made explicit.

Within general relativity, can averaging play an important role in cosmology and, in particular, what is the largest scale on which one can coarse-grain inhomogeneous matter and geometry that obey Einstein’s equations on smaller scales so that the resulting averaged macroscopic evolution is still an exact solution of Einstein’s equations?

Let G be a finite simple graph, let μ1 ≥ μ2 ≥ ··· ≥ μn = 0 be the Laplacian eigenvalues of G, and let σ(G) be the largest index σ such that μσ ≥ 2m/n, where m = |E(G)| and n = |V(G)|. Is it true that σ(G) = 1 if and only if G is isomorphic to K1, or to K2 + sK1 for some integer s ≥ 0, or to K1,r + sK1 for integers r ≥ 2 and 0 ≤ s < r - 1, where + denotes disjoint union and K1,r is the star on r + 1 vertices?

In the affine integer plane (R^2, Z^2), let ABC be a nondegenerate integer triangle. For each side, use its integer length as in integer geometry, and for the angle alpha = ∠BAC use the paper's integer-trigonometric invariants: if alpha has LLS-sequence (a0, a1, a2, ...), then ltan(alpha) is the continued fraction determined by that sequence, lsin(alpha) is the integer sine, and lcos(alpha) = lsin(alpha)/ltan(alpha). Formulate an analogue of the Euclidean cosine rule for integer triangles: namely, find a relation playing the role of a^2 = b^2 + c^2 - 2bc cos(alpha), but expressed purely in the integer-geometric invariants of the triangle.

For a fixed integer n >= 3, determine exactly which ordered n-tuples (S_1,...,S_n) of LLS-sequences can occur as the successive angle data of an integer n-gon in the plane R^2 with vertices in Z^2, where each vertex angle is regarded as an integer angle and encoded by its LLS-sequence, the complete invariant of integer angles up to affine lattice-preserving transformations.

Fix n >= 2. Let A be an arrangement of n hyperplanes through the origin in R^n in general position, let C be one of its cones, and let Sail_{S,L}(C) be the sail of Definition 2.2, obtained by deleting from C the union of all subsets U contained in C that are similar to S via stretchings of C and satisfy U ∩ L = empty, and then taking the boundary. In the Klein-polyhedron case, where S is a basis n-simplex of C and L = (C\{0}) ∩ Z^n, classify the combinatorial types of faces that can occur on Sail_{S,L}(C). ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1712.01450))

For a fixed positive integer n, classify up to integer congruence all empty lattice n-simplices Δ ⊂ R^n; that is, all n-dimensional simplices with vertices in Z^n such that Δ ∩ Z^n is exactly the vertex set of Δ, where integer congruence means equivalence under affine automorphisms of R^n preserving Z^n. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1712.01450))

For fixed integers m >= 2 and n >= 3, in the setting of geometric multidimensional continued fractions defined by sails in integer geometry, classify the integer n-gons that are realizable as 2-dimensional faces of an m-dimensional continued fraction, distinguishing the two geometrically different cases according to the integer distance from the supporting plane of the face to the origin (the cone vertex): (i) faces at integer distance 1, i.e. the problem of describing integer convex n-gons that can occur as faces inscribed in full-dimensional simplices of the ambient lattice space; and (ii) faces at integer distance greater than 1, i.e. the corresponding view-obstacle problem in which intervening integer points must be avoided.

For each integer n >= 1, let δ_n be the infimum, over all n-tuples (v_1, ..., v_n) of distinct nonzero integers, of max_{t in R/Z} min_{1 <= i <= n} ||t v_i||_{R/Z}, where ||x||_{R/Z} denotes the distance from x to the nearest integer. Is it true that δ_n = 1/(n+1) for every n >= 1?

Within the rational-cone case of geometric multidimensional continued fractions in real space with lattice Z^n, describe, up to affine integer-lattice congruence, all finite two-dimensional sails—that is, all two-dimensional sails arising from cones whose every 1-edge contains an integer point, so that the sail has finitely many faces—for the standard constructions considered in the paper, in particular Klein sails and Minkowski-Voronoi polyhedra, and determine the corresponding continued fractions.

Fix one of the paper's sail constructions in the sense of Definition 2.2 for cones in R^n with lattice Z^n. For a fixed combinatorial type of lattice polytope (that is, a fixed face-lattice type), determine exactly which collections of sails of the polytope's vertex cones can occur as the polytope ranges over all lattice polytopes of that combinatorial type.

In the algebraic (periodic) setting of geometric multidimensional continued fractions in R^n with lattice Z^n—where an algebraic sail carries a periodic action of its Dirichlet subgroup and the factor-sail is an (n-1)-torus—does there exist, for a fixed sail model such as the Klein or Minkowski-Voronoi sail, an algorithm that decides whether a given type of fundamental domain is realizable by some periodic continued fraction of that model? In the Klein case, the input type should be understood as the associated torus decomposition, namely the integer-congruence types of the polyhedra in a fundamental domain together with their integer distances from the cone vertex.

Let S1 and S2 be periodic Klein sails arising from algebraic cones, so that each sail admits a fundamental domain under the action of its Dirichlet subgroup and the quotient is a torus. Is it true that if S1 and S2 are not integer congruent, meaning that no affine transformation preserving the integer lattice sends one sail to the other, then their torus decompositions are different? Here the torus decomposition of a periodic Klein sail means the collection of integer-congruence types of the polyhedra occurring in a fundamental domain, together with the integer distance of each such polyhedron from the vertex of the cone.

Describe exactly which torus decompositions occur for periodic two-dimensional continued fractions in the sense of Klein: namely, in the algebraic case where an irreducible matrix A in SL(3, Z) has characteristic polynomial irreducible over Q with three real roots, so that the associated two-dimensional Klein sail in R^3/Z^3 is periodic under its Dirichlet subgroup and the factor-sail is a 2-torus, determine all decompositions of that quotient torus (equivalently, of any fundamental domain) by polyhedra, recorded by the integer-congruence class of each polyhedron under affine lattice-preserving transformations and by its integer distance from the cone vertex, that can be realized.

Let C be an algebraic cone in R^n in the sense of Section 3.1[A], namely a cone of the arrangement of invariant hyperplanes of some matrix A in SL_n(Z) whose characteristic polynomial is irreducible over Q and has only real roots, and let S be the corresponding Klein sail (Definition 2.4). Via the action of the Dirichlet subgroup of A, the factor-sail is an (n-1)-torus; its torus decomposition is the collection of integer-congruence classes of the polyhedral faces in a fundamental domain, each endowed with its integer distance from the cone vertex. Is it true that every such torus decomposition contains at least one face that is integer congruent (under an affine lattice automorphism) to a triangle, at least one face at integer distance 1 from the cone vertex, and at least one face at integer distance greater than 1 from the cone vertex?

For a fixed cubic extension K/Q, classify—within the paper’s algebraically periodic geometric-continued-fraction framework (the algebraic sail setting of case [A], implicitly the totally real real-sail situation)—all continued fractions that correspond to K, up to the paper’s ambient integer-lattice equivalence of the associated sails.

In the setting of geometric multidimensional continued fractions in R^n with lattice Z^n, fix one of the standard notions of sail from Definition 2.2. For n >= 3, exhibit at least one explicitly prescribed non-periodic combinatorial structure and prove that there exists a cone C arising from an arrangement of n hyperplanes through the origin in general position, in the non-periodic generic case [G] (that is, C is non-algebraic and its faces contain no integer points), whose sail realizes exactly that prescribed non-periodic combinatorial structure.

For each integer n >= 3, in the setting of geometric n-dimensional continued fractions in R^n with lattice Z^n - that is, sails of arrangements of n hyperplanes through the origin in general position in the sense of Definition 2.2 - determine which integer-congruence classes of faces of these sails attain the maximal geometric relative frequency, where relative frequency is the Möbius-geometric frequency defined in Section 3.4 by integrating the infinitesimal cross-ratio over the space of arrangements.

For faces occurring in sails of n-dimensional geometric continued fractions, with relative frequency understood in the Möbius-geometric sense described in §3.4, is it true that for every positive integer constant C there are only finitely many integer-congruence classes of faces whose relative frequency exceeds C, where integer congruence is taken with respect to affine lattice-preserving transformations of Z^n? ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1712.01450))

For each dimension n >= 3, in the sail-statistics setting of geometric n-dimensional continued fractions (sails with respect to the integer lattice), where relative frequencies are defined via the Möbius-invariant measure on the space of arrangements, is the sum of the relative frequencies over all possible face types that occur in such n-dimensional continued fractions, counted up to integer congruence, finite?

Fix a dimension n ≥ 3. Assume that for n-dimensional geometric continued fractions—namely, sails associated with arrangements of n hyperplanes through the origin in general position in R^n with respect to the lattice Z^n—the total sum of the relative frequencies of all possible face types is finite. What is the correct higher-dimensional analogue of the classical Gauss map for these multidimensional sails, and how do the induced face frequencies compare with the related geometric relative frequencies coming from Möbius geometry, i.e. the frequencies obtained by integrating infinitesimal cross-ratio against the unique projectively invariant Möbius measure on the space of arrangements?

Within the framework of geometric multidimensional continued fractions, find a natural analogue of the classical Farey tessellation for hyperbolic spaces of dimension greater than 2, in a way that also generalizes Farey summation via its geometric realization as a tessellation.

Problem 20 (Jacobi’s last theorem). Let K be a totally real cubic number field, and let y,z∈K satisfy 0<y<1 and 0<z<1, with 1,y,z linearly independent over Q. Does the classical Jacobi-Perron algorithm generate an eventually periodic continued fraction with starting data v=(1,y,z), that is, one whose sequence of Jacobi-Perron partial quotients is periodic after finitely many initial terms?

In the setting of geometric multidimensional continued fractions, study the geometric properties of the Markov spectrum arising from Markov minima of decomposable forms on R^n with respect to the lattice Z^n, using the fact that the minima of such a form are attained at vertices of the sails associated, in the sense of Definition 2.2, to the hyperplane arrangement given by the kernels of its linear factors. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1712.01450))

Is there a generalization of ordinary finite continued fractions that describes 3-bridge knots in the same way that ordinary finite continued fractions describe rational knots (equivalently, two-bridge knots), namely by providing an analogous complete invariant of the knot type?

Conjecture 1.1 asks: for every diversity (X, delta) with |X| = n, does there exist some dimension d and a map phi : X -> R^d into the ℓ1 diversity (R^d, delta_hat), where delta_hat(A) = sum_{i=1}^d max_{a,b in A} |a_i - b_i| for each finite A, such that phi has distortion O(log n); equivalently, are there constants c1, c2 > 0 with c1 c2 = O(log n) for which (1/c1) delta(B) <= delta_hat(phi(B)) <= c2 delta(B) for every finite B ⊆ X?

Let (X,δ) be an n-point diversity with induced metric d(x,y)=δ({x,y}). Define the associated diameter diversity by δ_diam(A)=max_{a,b∈A} d(a,b), and let δ_S(A) be the Steiner diversity of d, so that δ_diam(A)≤δ(A)≤δ_S(A) for every finite A⊆X. Since n-point diameter diversities admit ℓ1 embeddings with O(log^2 n) distortion, n-point Steiner diversities admit ℓ1 embeddings with O(log n) distortion, and Bartal-style random-tree methods do not by themselves successfully embed all diameter diversities, is there a hybrid embedding construction for general n-point diversities that applies a Bartal-type method where possible but switches to a Bourgain-type method on subproblems where tree methods fail, in order to improve the current O(n) general upper bound for embedding diversities into an ℓ1 diversity? ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1712.01960))

Let c_L1(X, δ) denote the minimum distortion of an embedding of a finite diversity (X, δ) into an L1 diversity, where a map φ from (X, δ) to (Y, ρ) has distortion c if there exist c1, c2 > 0 with c = c1 c2 and (1/c1) δ(A) ≤ ρ(φ(A)) ≤ c2 δ(A) for every finite A ⊆ X. If f(n) := sup{|X|=n} c_L1(X, δ), can one use expander hypergraphs, together with the diversity-embedding/hypergraph-cut correspondence cited by Bryant and Tupper, to construct n-point diversities with provably large c_L1(X, δ), and thereby obtain asymptotic lower bounds on the worst-case distortion f(n) for embeddings of diversities into L1?

Let (X,\delta) be a diversity on a finite set X with |X|=n, and let d(x,y)=\delta(\{x,y\}) be its induced metric. Does there exist a universal rule F which, given only the metric space (X,d), outputs an embedding \phi_d\colon X\to \mathbb{R}^{k(d)} into an \ell_1 diversity (\mathbb{R}^{k(d)},\hat\delta), where \hat\delta(B)=\sum_{i=1}^{k(d)}\max_{u,v\in B}|u_i-v_i| for every finite B\subseteq \mathbb{R}^{k(d)}, such that for every diversity \delta on X inducing d there are constants c_1,c_2>0 with c_1c_2=O(\sqrt{n}) and (1/c_1)\delta(A)\le \hat\delta(\phi_d(A))\le c_2\delta(A) for every finite A\subseteq X?

For every integer n >= 1, is the following true? If w is a finite linear word of length n over an arbitrary finite alphabet, then there exists a binary word b of length n such that b has at least as many distinct nonempty abelian-square factors as w. Here a factor means a contiguous subword, and an abelian square is a factor uv with |u|=|v|>0 and u and v having the same Parikh vector; two abelian-square factors are counted as distinct when they are different words.

For each positive integer n, let XNL(n) be the maximum, over all binary linear words w of length n, of the number of equivalence classes of abelian-square factors occurring in w, where a factor means a contiguous subword, an abelian square is a factor uv with equal Parikh vectors, and two abelian-square factors are equivalent iff they have the same Parikh vector. Is there an absolute constant C such that XNL(n) <= C n^(3/2) for all n >= 1?

Does there exist an infinite ternary word w over {0,1,2} such that no contiguous factor of w of the form xy with |x|=|y| and Parikh(x)=Parikh(y) has total length greater than 2? ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1802.04481))

For each integer n >= 1, let MDL(n) be the minimum, over all binary words w in {a,b}^n, of the number of distinct factors x of w such that x = uv with |u| = |v| and u and v have the same Parikh vector. Is it true that MDL(n) = floor(n/4) for every n >= 1? Moreover, for every integer k >= 0, are the only binary words of length 4k + 3 having exactly k distinct abelian-square factors the words a^(2k+1)ba^(2k+1) and b^(2k+1)ab^(2k+1) (equivalently, a^(2k+1)ba^(2k+1) and its complement)?

For each integer n >= 1, let c_n be the minimum, over all circular words w on the binary alphabet {a,b} of length n, of the number of distinct abelian-square factors of w, where an abelian square is a factor xy with |x| = |y| and x and y having the same Parikh vector, factors of a circular word may wrap around the end, only factors of length at most n are counted, and "distinct" means distinct factor words rather than distinct occurrences. Is it true that c_n = (n-1)/2 when n is odd and c_n = (n-2)/2 when n is even, and that the extremal circular words are exactly, up to conjugacy and complement (swapping a and b), the words represented by a^n and a^(n-1)b when n is odd, and by a^k b^(n-k) when n is even with 1 <= k < n odd?

For each positive integer n, among all linear binary words w of length n, what is the minimum possible number of occurrences of abelian squares in w, where an occurrence is a contiguous factor w[i..i+2m-1] with m ≥ 1 that can be written as xy with |x| = |y| = m and x and y having the same Parikh vector, and where different starting positions and/or lengths are counted separately (that is, occurrences are counted with multiplicity, not up to distinctness or equivalence)?

Let Q_n^d be the space of homogeneous degree-d forms on C^n, with n >= 2 and d >= 3, let X_n^d = {f in Q_n^d : Δ(f) != 0} be the locus of nondegenerate forms, and let Φ : X_n^d -> Q_n^{n(d-2)*} be the associated-form morphism attached to the Milnor algebra M(f) = C[z_1,...,z_n]/(f_{z_1},...,f_{z_n}). Is it true that for every regular GL_n-invariant function S on X_n^d there exists a rational GL_n-invariant function R on Q_n^{n(d-2)*}, defined at every point of Φ(X_n^d), such that R o Φ = S? Equivalently in the paper’s motivation, can one canonically extract a complete system of biholomorphic invariants of homogeneous isolated hypersurface singularities from their Milnor algebras (hence, by Saito, from their Tjurina algebras in the homogeneous/quasi-homogeneous case) via associated forms? ([rimath.saitama-u.ac.jp](https://www.rimath.saitama-u.ac.jp/research/pdf/smj31-5.pdf))

For integers n >= 2 and d >= 3, let Q_n^d := Sym^d((C^n)^*) be the vector space of homogeneous degree-d forms on C^n, let X_n^d := {f in Q_n^d : Delta(f) != 0} be the discriminant-nonvanishing locus, and let Phi: X_n^d -> Q_n^{n(d-2)*} be the associated-form morphism, where Q_n^{n(d-2)*} denotes the space of degree n(d-2) forms on the dual space (C^n)^*. Is it true that for every regular GL_n(C)-invariant function S in C[X_n^d]^{GL_n(C)}, there exists a GL_n(C)-invariant rational function R on Q_n^{n(d-2)*}, defined at every point of Phi(X_n^d), such that R(Phi(f)) = S(f) for all f in X_n^d?

Over C, let Q_n^d := C[z_1, ..., z_n]_d, let X_n^d := {f in Q_n^d : Delta(f) != 0}, and let P X_n^d be its projectivization inside P(Q_n^d). For [f] in P X_n^d, define the projectivized gradient morphism by P∇([f]) := <partial f/partial z_1, ..., partial f/partial z_n>, viewed as a point of the Grassmannian of n-dimensional subspaces of Q_n^{d-1}; let Z_n^{d-1} denote the induced SL_n-invariant image/locus of balanced complete intersections of type (d-1, ..., d-1). Let PΨ be the projectivized associated-form morphism sending a balanced complete intersection with nonzero resultant to its Macaulay inverse system (equivalently, associated form) in P(C[e_1, ..., e_n]_{n(d-2)}), and let the codomain quotient be taken on the semistable locus. Is the induced morphism of GIT quotients P∇|_{P X_n^d} : P X_n^d // SL_n -> Z_n^{d-1} // SL_n a closed immersion for every n >= 2 and d >= 3? By Proposition 1.2 together with Theorem 1.3, an affirmative answer would provide the remaining step in the paper’s reduction of Conjecture 1.1.

Let \(\mathcal Q_n^d=\operatorname{Sym}^d((\mathbb C^n)^*)\) be the space of homogeneous degree-\(d\) forms in variables \(z_1,\dots,z_n\), and let \(X_n^d:=\{f\in\mathcal Q_n^d:\Delta(f)
eq 0\}\). Consider the projective gradient morphism \(\mathbb P
abla:\mathbb P X_n^d	o \operatorname{Gr}(n,\mathcal Q_n^{d-1})\), \([f]\mapsto \langle f_{z_1},\dots,f_{z_n}angle\), and the induced morphism on \(\mathrm{SL}_n(\mathbb C)\)-GIT quotients \(\overline{\mathbb P
abla}\). Is the image \(\operatorname{im}(\overline{\mathbb P
abla})\) a normal variety for every \(n\ge 2\) and \(d\ge 3\)?

For every pair of integers n ≥ 2 and d ≥ 3, does there exist a homogeneous SL_n(C)-invariant polynomial J on the vector space C[e_1, ..., e_n]_{n(d-2)} of degree-n(d-2) forms such that the locus
U_n^{n(d-2)} := {F in C[e_1, ..., e_n]_{n(d-2)} : F^perp ∩ C[z_1, ..., z_n]_{d-1} is n-dimensional and admits a basis with nonzero resultant},
where F^perp = {h in C[z_1, ..., z_n] : h(∂/∂e_1, ..., ∂/∂e_n)F = 0},
is a closed subset of the complement of the zero locus of J? ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1803.04005))

Let Q_n^d denote the complex vector space of homogeneous degree-d forms on C^n, let X_n^d={f in Q_n^d: Δ(f)≠0}, and let Φ:X_n^d→Q_n^{n(d-2)*} be the associated-form morphism. In the only cases for which n(d-2)=d, namely (n,d)=(2,4) and (n,d)=(3,3), after identifying (C^n)^{**} with C^n, does Φ descend to a nontrivial rational SL_n-equivariant involution P(Φ):P(Q_n^d)⇢P(Q_n^d), equivalently satisfying P(Φ)^2=id as a rational map?

Fix integers n \ge 2 and d \ge 3, let \mathcal{Q}_n^d be the complex vector space of homogeneous degree-d forms on \mathbb{C}^n, let X_n^d := \{f \in \mathcal{Q}_n^d : \Delta(f) \neq 0\} be the discriminant-complement, and let \Phi : X_n^d \to \mathcal{Q}_n^{n(d-2)*} be the associated-form morphism. Determine the smallest integer p = p(n,d) such that the product \Delta^p\Phi extends to a regular morphism \mathcal{Q}_n^d \to \mathcal{Q}_n^{n(d-2)*}.

For integers n ≥ 2 and d ≥ 3, let X_n^d = {f ∈ C[z_1, ..., z_n]_d : Δ(f) ≠ 0}, let Φ: X_n^d → C[z_1^*, ..., z_n^*]_{n(d−2)} be the associated-form morphism, and let p = p(n,d) be the smallest positive integer such that the product Δ^pΦ extends to a regular morphism C[z_1, ..., z_n]_d → C[z_1^*, ..., z_n^*]_{n(d−2)}. Does there exist any pair (n,d) for which p(n,d) > 1?

Open problem: For a finite simple block graph G, where every block of G is a complete graph, characterize exactly those graphs for which the adjacency matrix A(G) is nonsingular over R; equivalently, determine precisely when det A(G) != 0 (that is, rank A(G) = |V(G)| and nullity ker A(G) = 0) and when A(G) is singular.

Is it true that for every connected simple block graph G with no block isomorphic to K2 — equivalently, every block of G has order at least 3 — the adjacency nullity eta(G)=mult_0(A(G)) of its (0,1)-adjacency matrix A(G) is at most 1?

Let G1 and G2 be finite simple vertex-disjoint connected block graphs, and let v1 ∈ V(G1) and v2 ∈ V(G2). Assume that G1 and G2 are nonsingular, meaning that their (0,1)-adjacency matrices A(G1) and A(G2) are nonsingular over R. If G is obtained from G1 ∪ G2 by adding the single new edge v1v2 (so that G is again a block graph), must G also be nonsingular? ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/abs/1803.03947))

In the almost toric four-dimensional setting considered in Section 2 of the paper, let φ:M^4→B and φ′:M′^4→B′ be Lagrangian fibrations with compact fibres, whose singularities are non-degenerate and of elliptic or focus type only, and let B and B′ be equipped with the singular integer affine structures induced by the action variables. If there exists an affine diffeomorphism ψ:B→B′, must the corresponding Lagrangian fibrations be symplectomorphic?

For a finite-dimensional integrable Hamiltonian system on a symplectic manifold, consider the germ of the associated singular Lagrangian fibration near a degenerate singular point. If two such degenerate singularities are locally diffeomorphic, do there nevertheless exist nontrivial local symplectic invariants that distinguish their germs up to local fibrewise symplectomorphism? If so, determine whether such invariants exist, how many independent invariants there are, and what form they take, already in the case of one degree of freedom.

In the local and semi-global classification of singularities of finite-dimensional integrable systems, determine all topological types of singularities that can occur for algebraically integrable systems with n ≤ 3 degrees of freedom, where algebraic integrability is understood in the paper's most natural sense: the commuting first integrals F1, ..., Fn are polynomials, the phase space together with its symplectic or Poisson structure and time admits a natural complexification, the real system is the real part of a complex integrable system, and the general complex fibers of that complex system are affine parts of Abelian varieties. For each such singularity type, describe its symplectic invariants.

For finite-dimensional integrable systems obtained by toric degenerations, whose momentum-map base is a convex polytope, what are the topology and geometry of the singular fibers and of small neighbourhoods of those fibers? In particular, are the degenerate singular fibers, in most cases, still smooth manifolds or orbifolds, and are they isotropic or even Lagrangian?

In the so-called SYZ model of mirror symmetry, consider a Lagrangian fibration on a Calabi-Yau manifold of complex dimension 3 (real dimension 6). Suppose that its singular locus contains one-dimensional families of singularities of focus-focus type, and that for the given system there are finitely many special singular fibres at the intersections of these families. Give a clear description of these special singular fibres.

Construct a smooth natural Hamiltonian system on T^*S^2 with canonical symplectic structure, namely a Hamiltonian H(x,p)=1/2 g^{ij}(x)p_i p_j+U(x) for some smooth metric g on S^2 and nonconstant smooth potential U:S^2→R, such that there exists a nontrivial first integral F with {H,F}=0 where F is a real polynomial of total degree 5 in the momenta p with smooth x-dependent coefficients, and such that H admits no nontrivial polynomial-in-momenta first integrals of degrees 1, 2, 3, or 4. ([upcommons.upc.edu](https://upcommons.upc.edu/bitstreams/d858abf8-e232-45e3-a199-3adac6cf7893/download))

Let M be a smooth real manifold of dimension n >= 3, equipped with a metric g and a potential U : M -> R, and consider on T^*M with its canonical symplectic structure the natural Hamiltonian H(x,p) = (1/2) g^{ij}(x) p_i p_j + U(x). Construct new examples for which there exist n - 1 additional first integrals F_1, ..., F_{n-1} in C^\infty(M)[p_1, ..., p_n], polynomial in the momenta, such that {H, F_i} = 0, {F_i, F_j} = 0 for all i, j, and dH, dF_1, ..., dF_{n-1} are linearly independent on an open dense subset of T^*M.

Construct explicit four-dimensional Einstein metrics g, with Ric(g) = Lambda g for some constant Lambda, whose geodesic flow admits a polynomial first integral of degree m > 2 in the momenta (equivalently, a Killing tensor of order m > 2), under the assumption that g is stationary axially symmetric, meaning that it admits two commuting vector fields, one time-like and one space-like.

Let (M,g) be a Riemannian symmetric space. Is every symmetric Killing tensor field on M, of arbitrary valence, a finite real linear combination of symmetrized tensor products of Killing vector fields on M?

Does there exist a smooth Riemannian metric g on S^2 and a smooth nonconstant potential U:S^2->R such that the natural Hamiltonian H(x,p)=1/2 g^{ij}(x)p_i p_j+U(x) on T^*S^2, endowed with its canonical symplectic structure, is superintegrable in the class of first integrals polynomial in the momenta—namely, H admits more than dim S^2=2 functionally independent polynomial first integrals on an open dense subset, with the additional superintegrating integrals all of degree at least 3 in the momenta—and yet H admits no nontrivial polynomial first integral of degree 1 or 2 in the momenta, where H and its functions are regarded as trivial integrals?

Does there exist an integer n>2 and a non-conformally flat Riemannian metric g on S^n such that the geodesic Hamiltonian H(x,p)=1/2 g^{ij}(x)p_i p_j on T^*S^n admits 2n-1 functionally independent first integrals, including H, each polynomial in the momenta p with smooth x-dependent coefficients?

Is the following Birkhoff conjecture true for planar Euclidean inner billiards? Let Ω ⊂ R^2 be a strictly convex domain with smooth boundary γ = ∂Ω, and consider the usual elastic billiard inside Ω. Suppose there exists an annular neighborhood U ⊂ Ω of γ that is foliated by billiard caustics, meaning smooth curves C ⊂ U such that any billiard trajectory segment tangent to C remains tangent to C after reflection. Must γ be an ellipse?

Let Gamma ⊂ R^2 be a smooth closed strictly convex curve, and let T be its outer billiard map on the exterior of Gamma. Assume that the entire exterior of Gamma is foliated by curves invariant under T. Must Gamma be an ellipse?

Is the following conjecture true? Let γ ⊂ RP^2 be a smooth closed strictly convex curve, and let F be a smooth foliation by convex closed curves in an exterior neighbourhood of γ, with γ itself as one leaf. For each point p ∈ γ and its tangent line L = T_pγ, define a local involution ι_L of L near p by sending a point x ∈ L near p to the other intersection point of L with the leaf of F passing through x; the point p is fixed by ι_L. Assume that for every tangent line L to γ, the germ ι_L is a projective transformation of the projective line L. Must γ be an ellipse, and must all leaves of F be ellipses belonging to a single pencil of conics? ([upcommons.upc.edu](https://upcommons.upc.edu/bitstreams/d858abf8-e232-45e3-a199-3adac6cf7893/download))

Let γ be a smooth closed strictly convex curve on a complete simply connected non-Euclidean surface of constant curvature, namely on S^2 or H^2, and let T_γ be the corresponding outer billiard map on the exterior of γ. Assume that T_γ is algebraically (polynomially) integrable in the intended sense of this section, namely that the outer billiard dynamics admits a nonconstant polynomial first integral. Prove that γ must be a conic in the corresponding constant-curvature geometry; equivalently, show that conics are the only polynomially integrable outer billiard tables on S^2 and H^2.

Does there exist a smooth strictly convex planar billiard table Ω whose boundary has the symmetry of an ellipse, so that the billiard has the 2-periodic orbit along the y-axis, and an angle α∈R such that the corresponding inner billiard map is locally conjugate, in a neighborhood of that 2-periodic orbit in phase space, to the rigid rotation by angle α?

Let Ω ⊂ R^2 be a strictly convex planar billiard table with smooth boundary γ, and call a p/q-rational caustic an invariant circle of the billiard map consisting of periodic points with rotation number p/q. Does there exist a non-elliptic planar billiard table whose billiard map has p1/q1-rational and p2/q2-rational caustics for two distinct rational rotation numbers p1/q1 ≠ p2/q2? Likewise, does there exist an outer billiard on the exterior of a closed convex plane curve, other than the elliptic case, with rational caustics for two distinct rational rotation numbers?

Fix an integer q0 ≥ 2. Let Ω ⊂ R^2 be a strictly convex planar billiard table with smooth boundary. Assume that for every rational number p/q with 0 < p/q < 1/q0, the billiard map of Ω admits a p/q-rational caustic, meaning an invariant circle consisting of periodic points of rotation number p/q. Must Ω be an ellipse?

Let Ω⊂R^2 be a strictly convex planar billiard table with smooth boundary γ, and let T be the associated billiard map on the phase space of oriented lines intersecting γ. Assume that T admits a family of rotational invariant circles whose set of rotation numbers contains the whole interval (0,1/2), equivalently, for every ω∈(0,1/2) there exists a rotational invariant circle of T with rotation number ω. Must γ be an ellipse?

Let Ω ⊂ R^2 be a smooth strictly convex planar billiard table, with inner billiard map defined by specular reflection at ∂Ω. Suppose that Ω admits a sequence of convex billiard caustics C_n whose corresponding invariant circles have rotation numbers ρ_n converging to some ω ∈ (0,1/2). Must the boundary ∂Ω be an ellipse? ([upcommons.upc.edu](https://upcommons.upc.edu/bitstreams/d858abf8-e232-45e3-a199-3adac6cf7893/download))

Let Omega be a smooth strictly convex billiard table in R^d with d >= 3, and let B be the corresponding billiard map on the symplectic phase space of oriented lines (equivalently, oriented geodesics). Does there exist any non-ellipsoidal Omega for which B preserves an invariant hypersurface in phase space? Likewise, if Sigma is a closed smooth strictly convex hypersurface in a linear symplectic space and T_Sigma is the associated higher-dimensional outer billiard map on the exterior of Sigma, can T_Sigma admit an invariant hypersurface for any non-ellipsoidal Sigma?

Let Σ1, Σ2 ⊂ ℝ^d, with d ≥ 3, be nested closed convex hypersurfaces, with enough regularity for each Σi to define a billiard reflection map Bi on the common phase space ℒ of oriented lines intersecting both Σ1 and Σ2. Assume that B1 and B2 commute on ℒ, i.e. B1∘B2 = B2∘B1. Prove that Σ1 and Σ2 are confocal ellipsoids. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6158379/))

For each d ≥ 2, each n, and each tuple I = (i_1, ..., i_{d-1}) ∈ Z^{d-1}, let P_n denote the space of projective-equivalence classes of generic twisted n-gons (v_k) in CP^d, where v_{k+n} = M∘v_k for some M ∈ SL_{d+1}(C). Define the diagonal hyperplanes P_k^I := (v_k, v_{k+i_1}, ..., v_{k+i_1+...+i_{d-1}}), and define the generalized pentagram map T_{I,I} by T_{I,I}v_k := P_k^I ∩ P_{k+i_1}^I ∩ ... ∩ P_{k+i_1+...+i_{d-1}}^I whenever this intersection is generically defined. Is every such map T_{I,I}: P_n → P_n integrable, in the same sense as the integrable pentagram maps treated in Theorem 1.4? ([math.utoronto.ca](https://www.math.utoronto.ca/khesin/papers/nonintegrability9.pdf))

Let (M, Π) be a smooth Poisson manifold of dimension n and maximal rank 2r, and let F = (f1, ..., fs): M -> R^s be a Liouville integrable system on (M, Π), meaning that the fi pairwise Poisson-commute, are independent on a dense open set, and satisfy r + s = n. Theorem 5.2 gives, near a compact regular integral manifold L_m of X_f1, ..., X_fs through a point m with df1 ∧ ... ∧ dfs(m) != 0 and rank Π(m) = 2r, local action-angle/transverse coordinates (θ1, ..., θr, σ1, ..., σs) with θ_i in R/Z, U ≅ T^r x B^s, Π = sum_{i=1}^r (∂/∂θ_i) ∧ (∂/∂σ_i), and σ_{r+1}, ..., σ_s Casimir/transverse coordinates. Extend this action-angle theorem to a neighbourhood of a Liouville torus when the Poisson structure is singular at the relevant point(s), i.e. when Π is not regular there.

Let (M, Pi, F) be a Liouville integrable system on a smooth real regular Poisson manifold, where dim M = n, rank Pi = 2r is constant, and F = (f_1, ..., f_s): M -> R^s is a tuple of independent Poisson-commuting smooth functions with r + s = n. Assume the regular compact integral manifolds are Liouville tori, so that by the local Poisson action-angle theorem, near each such torus there are coordinates (theta_1, ..., theta_r, sigma_1, ..., sigma_s) with theta_i in R/Z, sigma_j in R, U isomorphic to T^r x B^s, Pi = sum_{i=1}^r (partial/partial theta_i) wedge (partial/partial sigma_i), sigma_{r+1}, ..., sigma_s Casimirs, and the fibers of F given by projection to the B^s factor. Determine the obstructions to globalizing these local action-angle coordinates over the resulting regular torus fibration on a regular Poisson manifold, and in particular how those obstructions are encoded by the foliation of the image of the moment map by affine manifolds.

Let (M,Pi) be a smooth regular Poisson manifold of dimension n and maximal rank 2r, and let F=(f1,...,fs): M -> R^s, with s=n-r, be a Liouville integrable system, meaning that the fi are smooth, pairwise Poisson-commuting, and independent on a dense open set. In this regular Poisson setting, the image F(M) of the moment map is foliated by affine manifolds coming from action variables. Which foliations by affine leaves can occur as such an image F(M)?

Let M be a smooth Poisson manifold of even dimension 2n, and let U⊂M be the dense subset on which the Poisson structure is symplectic. Suppose that M carries a toric action whose restriction to U is Hamiltonian, with moment map μ defined on U. Is there a Delzant-type theorem for the image μ(U) of this moment map?

Find a natural finite-dimensional Liouville-integrable Hamiltonian system from classical mechanics, in the symplectic setting and with compact regular Liouville tori, whose regular torus fibration has nonzero Duistermaat-Chern class, i.e. a genuine Chern obstruction to the existence of global action-angle coordinates. Since this class vanishes for two degrees of freedom, the first interesting cases begin in three degrees of freedom.

Let (M2n, ω) be a symplectic manifold, and let p = (p1, ..., pn) be a classical Liouville integrable system on M, meaning that the pj are smooth real-valued functions with {pi, pj} = 0 for all i, j and with dp1, ..., dpn linearly independent almost everywhere on M. In a semiclassical quantization of M for which a principal symbol map σ is defined, does there exist a quantum integrable system P = (P1, ..., Pn) on the corresponding quantum Hilbert space—namely, n semiclassical self-adjoint operators with exact commutation relations [Pi, Pj] = 0 for all i, j—such that σ(Pj) = pj for every j = 1, ..., n?

Let M^{2n} be a classical symplectic phase space, and let P_1, ..., P_n be semiclassical operators on a quantum Hilbert space associated with M, in a semiclassical calculus where principal symbols p_j = sigma(P_j) are defined. Assume that P_j^* = P_j for each j and [P_i, P_j] = 0 for all i, j. Can one determine, purely from the semiclassical asymptotics as hbar -> 0 of the joint eigenvalues or joint eigenfunctions of the commuting family (P_1, ..., P_n), whether the independence axiom holds; namely, whether the differentials dp_1, ..., dp_n are linearly independent almost everywhere on M?

Let (M, ω, J) be a compact prequantizable Kähler manifold with its Berezin-Toeplitz quantum spaces 𝓗_k and semiclassical parameter k^(-1), and let T_{1,k}, T_{2,k} be commuting self-adjoint Berezin-Toeplitz operators whose joint principal symbol F = (f_1, f_2) : M → R^2 defines a classical integrable system with a nondegenerate focus-focus singularity at a critical point m_0 and critical value c_0 = F(m_0). Formulate and prove an all-orders singular Bohr-Sommerfeld quantization rule that gives necessary and sufficient integrality/cohomological conditions for E_k near c_0 to lie in the joint spectrum of (T_{1,k}, T_{2,k}) modulo O(k^(-∞)), thereby extending the known Toeplitz Bohr-Sommerfeld rules for regular tori and for 1-degree-of-freedom Morse singularities to the focus-focus case, along the lines of Vũ Ngọc’s focus-focus pseudodifferential theory. ([upcommons.upc.edu](https://upcommons.upc.edu/bitstreams/d858abf8-e232-45e3-a199-3adac6cf7893/download))

Let (P_1, ..., P_n) be a finite-dimensional quantum integrable system in the sense of Section 7.1: self-adjoint semiclassical operators on a quantum Hilbert space corresponding to a symplectic manifold M^{2n}, satisfying [P_i, P_j] = 0 and having principal symbols p_j = sigma(P_j) whose differentials are almost everywhere independent, so that p = (p_1, ..., p_n) defines a classical integrable system. Define a quantum analogue of the classical Chern (Duistermaat-Chern) class of the associated Lagrangian fibration—the classical obstruction, alongside Hamiltonian monodromy, to global action-angle coordinates—and determine how this quantum invariant can be detected from the quantum data, in particular whether it is encoded in the semiclassical joint spectrum or only in phase information of joint eigenfunctions, possibly via shift operators transversal to the Lagrangian fibration.

Let F = (J, H): M -> R^2 be a semitoric integrable system on a symplectic 4-manifold, meaning that all singularities of F are non-degenerate and have only elliptic or focus-focus components, and that J is proper and generates a Hamiltonian S^1-action. Suppose (J-hat_hbar, H-hat_hbar) is a semiclassical quantum integrable system with principal symbols J and H. Is F determined, up to symplectic equivalence, by its semiclassical joint spectrum, namely the set of points (λ, ν) in R^2 such that λ is an eigenvalue of J-hat_hbar and ν is an eigenvalue of H-hat_hbar restricted to the λ-eigenspace of J-hat_hbar, as hbar -> 0? Moreover, can one explicitly construct the associated semitoric system from any such semiclassical joint spectrum?

For a quantum semitoric system F = (J, H)—where semitoric means that all singularities are nondegenerate and of elliptic or focus-focus type, J is proper, and J generates a Hamiltonian S^1-action—fix a focus-focus critical value c0. Consider the formal power series in ħ that appears in the singular Bohr-Sommerfeld quantization rule near c0. Is this formal power series determined by the semiclassical joint spectrum of the quantized pair (Ĵ_ħ, Ĥ_ħ), i.e. by the set of pairs (λ, ν) with λ an eigenvalue of Ĵ_ħ and ν an eigenvalue of Ĥ_ħ on the λ-eigenspace, as ħ → 0? ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/abs/1804.03737))

Let T1,ℏ, ..., Tn,ℏ be a quantum integrable system in the sense of §7.1: pairwise commuting self-adjoint semiclassical operators in a quantization scheme with well-defined principal symbols on a 2n-dimensional symplectic manifold (M, ω), and let fj = σ(Tj,ℏ) ∈ C∞(M; R) have almost everywhere independent differentials. From the semiclassical joint spectrum Spec(T1,ℏ, ..., Tn,ℏ) as ℏ → 0, what information about the classical integrable system (M, ω, f1, ..., fn) is spectrally detectable? In particular, if I(M, ω, f1, ..., fn) is a specified symplectic invariant—for example an integer z or a matrix A—can one compute I explicitly from the semiclassical joint spectrum?

Let T_{1,\hbar},\ldots,T_{n,\hbar} be a quantum integrable system in the sense of §7.1, i.e. commuting self-adjoint semiclassical operators on a quantum Hilbert space whose principal symbols f_1,\ldots,f_n are almost everywhere independent on a symplectic manifold (M,\omega). From the joint spectrum of T_{1,\hbar},\ldots,T_{n,\hbar} in the semiclassical limit \hbar\to 0, can one determine whether a singularity of the associated classical integrable system F=(f_1,\ldots,f_n):M\to\mathbb{R}^n is degenerate rather than nondegenerate?

Let (M,ω) be a compact symplectic manifold equipped with a symplectic S^1-action, motivated in particular by the case in which the fixed points are isolated and the action need not be Hamiltonian. Let μ:M→S^1 denote the associated circle-valued momentum map in the sense of McDuff, and let Q(μ) be a unitary quantisation of μ. Can spectral information about Q(μ) be used to obtain information about the fixed-point set of the S^1-action—at least upper or lower bounds, and ideally the number, of its isolated fixed points? ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6158379/))

Let (M, g) be a Riemannian manifold, let H(x,p) = (1/2) g^{ij}(x)p_i p_j be the geodesic Hamiltonian on T^*M with its canonical symplectic structure, and let H-hat = Delta_g be the corresponding Beltrami-Laplace operator on functions on M. Determine necessary and/or sufficient conditions on g under which every first integral F(x,p) of H that is polynomial in the momenta p_i admits a differential operator F-hat on M such that [H-hat, F-hat] = 0 and the symbol of F-hat is F.

Let N = {1,2,3,...}, and define τ(n,t) = (1/n)[t - (t+n+1)(t/(1+t))^(n+1)] for (n,t) in N × (0,∞). Determine the exact value of the constant α := sup_{(n,t)∈N×(0,∞)} τ(n,t), which is the sharp constant entering the condition s <= 1/(1+α) in the strict complete monotonicity result for f_s(x) = (x+1)^s / [Γ(x+1)]^(1/x) on (-1,∞).

Let G=(V,E) be a finite simple graph, and let M⊆E be a matching. Write G[M] for the subgraph induced by the vertices incident with the edges of M. For a graph property P, call M a P-matching if G[M] has property P. Let β_P(G) denote the maximum cardinality of a P-matching in G, and let β_P^-(G) denote the minimum cardinality of an inclusion-maximal P-matching in G. For each of the P-matching families surveyed in the paper (including ordinary, induced/strong, uniquely restricted, acyclic, disconnected, connected, and isolate-free matchings), determine nontrivial upper bounds for β_P(G) and nontrivial lower bounds for β_P^-(G).

For each P-matching notion actually treated in the survey's P-matching framework—namely, for each specified property P defining a matching M by the condition that the induced subgraph G[M] on the vertices saturated by M has property P—characterize the finite simple graphs G for which every maximal P-matching is a maximum P-matching; equivalently, determine exactly those graphs G satisfying beta_P^-(G) = beta_P(G), where beta_P(G) is the maximum size of a P-matching in G and beta_P^-(G) is the minimum size of a maximal P-matching.

Let P be a graph property, and for a finite simple graph G let beta_P(G) denote the maximum cardinality of a matching M such that the subgraph induced by the vertices incident with the edges of M (the paper’s <M> notation) has property P. Does there exist a graph parameter alpha_P(G) such that beta_P(G) + alpha_P(G) = |V(G)| for every graph G in the class considered in Conjecture 1.1?

Let P be a graph property, and for a finite simple graph G of order n let β_P(G) denote the maximum cardinality of a matching M such that the induced subgraph G[M] on the vertices incident with the edges of M has property P. Determine the sharp Nordhaus-Gaddum bounds for β_P; that is, for each positive integer n, determine the best possible lower and upper bounds, over all graphs G on n vertices, for β_P(G)+β_P(\overline{G}) and for β_P(G)β_P(\overline{G}).

For a graph G and a matching M, let G[M] be the subgraph induced by the vertices saturated by M. The survey considers the seven maximum P-matching parameters β_P(G) obtained when P is, respectively, the properties of being an arbitrary graph, 1-regular (induced), having a unique perfect matching (uniquely restricted), connected, isolatefree, acyclic, or disconnected. Complete the remaining algorithmic picture left open there by determining the computational complexity of the disconnected matching number β_dc(G), and by identifying special graph classes—explicitly including interval graphs—on which the acyclic matching number β_ac(G) can be computed in polynomial time.

For a finite simple graph G, let β_dc(G) denote the maximum cardinality of a matching M such that |M| = 1 or the induced subgraph G[M] on the vertices saturated by M is disconnected. What is the computational complexity of determining β_dc(G) for a given graph G (equivalently, of deciding, given G and k, whether β_dc(G) ≥ k)?

Let F be a finite field of characteristic 2 with even extension degree [F:F_2], let psi:F->C be the canonical additive character of F (equivalently, psi(x)=(-1)^{Tr_{F/F_2}(x)}), and for an invertible exponent d over F (that is, gcd(d,|F^*|)=1) define W_{F,d}(a)=sum_{x in F} psi(x^d-ax) for a in F. Is it true that for every such pair (F,d), there exists a in F^* such that |W_{F,d}(a)-1| >= -1 + 2 sqrt(|F|)?

Let F be a finite field of characteristic p with canonical additive character psi, and let d be a nondegenerate invertible exponent over F, meaning gcd(d,|F|-1)=1 and d is not congruent to a power of p modulo |F|-1. For a in F, define W_{F,d}(a)=sum_{x in F} psi(x^d-ax), and define the valuation of the Weil spectrum by V_{F,d}=min_{a in F^*} v_p(W_{F,d}(a)), where v_p denotes the p-adic valuation extended to Q(zeta_p). If [F:F_p] is not a power of 2 and ℓ is the smallest odd prime divisor of [F:F_p], must one always have V_{F,d} <= ((ℓ+1)/(2ℓ))[F:F_p]?

Let F be a finite field of characteristic p, let psi(x)=exp(2pi i Tr_{F/F_p}(x)/p) be its canonical additive character, and let d be a positive integer with gcd(d, |F*|)=1. For each a in F define W_{F,d}(a)=sum_{x in F} psi(x^d-ax), and consider the Weil spectrum {W_{F,d}(a) : a in F*}, where F*=F\{0}. If this spectrum has exactly three distinct values, must W_{F,d} be symmetric, meaning that its two nonzero values are negatives of each other?

Let F be a finite field of characteristic p, let psi(x)=exp(2 pi i Tr_{F/F_p}(x)/p) be its canonical additive character, and let d be a positive integer with gcd(d,|F|-1)=1. For each a in F define W_{F,d}(a)=sum_{x in F} psi(x^d-ax), and call the associated Weil spectrum {W_{F,d}(a): a in F^*} three-valued if it has exactly three distinct elements. If [F:F_p] is a power of 2, must there be no invertible exponent d over F for which this Weil spectrum is three-valued? ([par.nsf.gov](https://par.nsf.gov/servlets/purl/10090054))

Let F be a finite field of characteristic p with canonical additive character psi, let d be a positive integer with gcd(d, |F^*|) = 1, and define W_{F,d}(a) = sum_{x in F} psi(x^d - ax) for a in F. Write the Weil spectrum as {W_{F,d}(a) : a in F^*}, and say that W_{F,d} is three-valued if this set has cardinality 3. If d and e are invertible exponents over F, say they are equivalent when d ≡ p^k e or d ≡ p^k e^{-1} (mod |F^*|) for some integer k. Is every pair (F, d) for which W_{F,d} is three-valued accounted for, up to this equivalence, by one of the entries in Table 1?

Let F be a finite field of characteristic p, let ψ:F→C be its canonical additive character ψ(x) = exp(2πi Tr_{F/F_p}(x)/p), and for each positive integer d with gcd(d, |F*|) = 1 define W_{F,d}(a) = Σ_{x∈F} ψ(x^d − ax) for a ∈ F. If |F| > 2 and d ≡ 1 (mod p − 1), must there exist some a ∈ F* such that W_{F,d}(a) = 0?

Let f: R^n -> R^m be Lipschitz continuous around x_bar, let y_bar := f(x_bar), and assume that every matrix A in Clarke's generalized Jacobian ∂f(x_bar) is surjective. Does there exist a neighborhood V of y_bar and a continuous map s: V -> R^n such that s(y_bar) = x_bar, f(s(y)) = y for all y in V, and s is calm at y_bar in the sense that for some constant gamma > 0 one has ||s(y) - x_bar|| <= gamma ||y - y_bar|| for all y in V?
