Determine the minimal linkedness k(6) of 6-dimensional convex polytopes, where k(6) := min{k(P) : P is a 6-polytope} and k(P) is the largest integer k such that for every choice of 2k distinct vertices s1, ..., sk, t1, ..., tk in the graph G(P), there exist k pairwise vertex-disjoint paths in G(P) joining si to ti for i = 1, ..., k. Is k(6) = 3?

Let FFS3 denote the combinatorial 3-polytope identified by the graph in Figure 1 of the paper. Is it true that no convex 3-polytope P ⊂ R^3 with combinatorial type FFS3 is decomposable, where decomposable means that P can be written as a Minkowski sum P = A + B of two dissimilar convex bodies, and two polytopes are called similar if one is obtained from the other by a dilation and a translation? ([espace.curtin.edu.au](https://espace.curtin.edu.au/bitstream/handle/20.500.11937/81338/81402.pdf))

Let C_1 and C_2 be nonempty compact convex subsets of a Hilbert space H. Does there always exist a point x ∈ H such that, for each i ∈ {1,2}, if p_i := P_{C_i}(x) denotes the metric projection of x onto C_i, then the continuous linear functional y ↦ ⟨x-p_i, y⟩ strongly exposes p_i in C_i; equivalently, the supporting hyperplane {y ∈ H : ⟨x-p_i, y⟩ = ⟨x-p_i, p_i⟩} strongly exposes the singleton face {p_i} of C_i? In other words, must there exist x ∈ H such that for i=1,2 one has ⟨x-p_i, p_i⟩ = sup_{y∈C_i}⟨x-p_i, y⟩ and every sequence (y_k) in C_i satisfying ⟨x-p_i, y_k⟩ → sup_{y∈C_i}⟨x-p_i, y⟩ converges to p_i? ([espace.curtin.edu.au](https://espace.curtin.edu.au/bitstream/handle/20.500.11937/81338/81402.pdf))

Consider the relaxed Douglas-Rachford iteration for a feasibility problem A∩B≠∅ with proximal sets A and B, where P_A and P_B denote the usual projections and x_{n+1} ∈ T_λ(x_n) with T_λ := λ(2P_B - Id)(2P_A - Id) + (1 - λ)Id for λ ∈ (0,1]. Borwein and Sims analyzed the λ→0+ continuous-time version of this method for the nonconvex circle-line case. In the more general settings considered by Borwein, Lindstrom, Sims, Skerritt, and Schneider—namely a subtransversal ellipse and a line, and a p-sphere and a line, where the discrete Douglas-Rachford method remains locally convergent near feasible points but exhibits much more complicated global behavior—can one analyze the corresponding λ→0+ continuous-time Douglas-Rachford dynamics?

Let a_1, ..., a_m be a finite set of points in a Euclidean space X. Determine whether the solution of min_{x in X} max_{1<=i<=m} ||a_i - x|| can be represented in a neat explicit form, rather than merely computed numerically; equivalently, describe explicitly the unique point x that is the center of the minimal Euclidean sphere containing {a_1, ..., a_m}. More generally, for X a normed linear space or even a metric space (with ||a_i - x|| replaced by d(a_i, x) in the metric case), and with the objective max_{1<=i<=m} d(a_i, x) replaced by an arbitrary norm on R^m applied to the vector of distances (d(a_1, x), ..., d(a_m, x)), determine when such a solution admits an explicit representation. ([espace.curtin.edu.au](https://espace.curtin.edu.au/bitstream/handle/20.500.11937/81338/81402.pdf))

Let Ω_0 be a finite family of convex polytopes in ℝ^n. For each direction g∈S^{n-1} and each P∈Ω, let P_g:=Arg max_{x∈P}⟨x,g⟩ be the support (exposed) face of P in direction g, and define C_Ω(g):=conv(⋃_{P∈Ω}P_g). Set F(Ω):={C_Ω(g): g∈S^{n-1}}, which is again a finite family of convex polytopes, and define iteratively Ω_i:=F(Ω_{i-1}) for i≥1. Characterize those initial finite families Ω_0 for which there exists N∈ℕ such that Ω_{N+2}=Ω_N; that is, characterize exactly which collections eventually fall into a cycle of period dividing 2 under this Demyanov-Ryabova conversion, in a way that extends/generalizes the special cases already known. ([espace.curtin.edu.au](https://espace.curtin.edu.au/bitstream/handle/20.500.11937/81338/81402.pdf))

Does every 3-dimensional convex polytope admit a nonoverlapping net (or unfolding); that is, can one cut the polytope along some of its edges so that the resulting connected surface can be flattened into the plane without overlap?

Fix an integer n >= 1 and a natural 1-parameter family F = {f_t} of rational maps on P^1 defined over Z, for example f_t(x) = x^m + t with m >= 2 or f_b(x) = bx + x^{-1}. Let Phi_{F,n}(x,t) be the nth dynatomic polynomial, let Y_1^dyn(F;n) be the affine curve in A^2_Z defined by Phi_{F,n}(x,t) = 0, so that its geometric points correspond to pairs (f_t, P) with P of formal period n, and let Y_0^dyn(F;n) = Y_1^dyn(F;n)/<sigma>, where sigma(x,t) = (f_t(x), t), so that Y_0^dyn(F;n) classifies formal n-cycles. For these natural integral models, determine exactly which primes p are primes of bad reduction of Y_0^dyn(F;n) and Y_1^dyn(F;n); formulate and justify a natural geometric/dynamical notion of a sporadic bad-reduction prime and explain such primes intrinsically (for the family x^m + t, the paper suggests looking outside the primes dividing 2nm); and characterize the primes p for which the reductions of Y_0^dyn(F;n) and Y_1^dyn(F;n) modulo p are geometrically irreducible over an algebraic closure of F_p.

Determine an explicit ("nice") function C(N,d,D,s) such that for every choice of integers N >= 1, d >= 2, D >= 1, and s >= 0, every number field K with [K:Q] <= D, and every degree-d morphism f: P^N -> P^N defined over K that has bad reduction at at most s finite primes of K, the set PrePer(f, P^N(K)) of K-rational preperiodic points satisfies #PrePer(f, P^N(K)) <= C(N,d,D,s).

For general N\ge 1, is the following Orbit Density Conjecture for affine N-space true: if f:\mathbb{A}^N_{\bar{\mathbb{Q}}}\to\mathbb{A}^N_{\bar{\mathbb{Q}}} is a polynomial self-map, written f=(f_1,\dots,f_N) with f_i\in\bar{\mathbb{Q}}[x_1,\dots,x_N], and there is no nonconstant rational function g\in\bar{\mathbb{Q}}(x_1,\dots,x_N) such that g\circ f=g, must there exist a point P\in\mathbb{A}^N(\bar{\mathbb{Q}}) whose forward orbit O_f(P)=\{f^n(P):n\ge 0\} is Zariski dense in \mathbb{A}^N? ([rlbenedetto.people.amherst.edu](https://rlbenedetto.people.amherst.edu/papers/ADtrends.pdf))

Let K be a number field. If one asks for K-rational points rather than Q̄-rational points in Section 13, are the following K-rational analogues of Theorem 13.1 and Conjecture 13.2 true? (1) For every dominant rational map f: P^N dashrightarrow P^N defined over K, is the set of wandering points in P^N(K)_f, meaning K-points whose full forward orbit avoids the indeterminacy locus and is infinite, Zariski dense in P^N? (2) For every polynomial morphism f = (f_1,...,f_N): A^N -> A^N defined over K, with f_i in K[x_1,...,x_N], and with no nonconstant invariant rational function g in Kbar(x_1,...,x_N) satisfying g∘f = g, does there exist a point P in A^N(K) whose forward orbit O_f(P) is Zariski dense in A^N?

Let f_T = [F_0(T;X_0,...,X_N):...:F_N(T;X_0,...,X_N)] be a family of dominant rational self-maps of P^N over C, where the F_i are homogeneous of the same degree in X_0,...,X_N and their coefficients are rational functions of the parameters T = (T_1,...,T_k). Let f denote the induced dominant rational map over the function field C(T_1,...,T_k), and for any parameter value t in C^k for which the specialization f_t is defined and dominant, let delta(f_t) = lim_{n->infinity} deg(f_t^n)^(1/n), where deg(g) is the common degree of a homogeneous presentation of g after canceling common factors; similarly define delta(f) for the generic map f. Is it true that for every epsilon > 0, the exceptional set E_epsilon = { t in C^k : delta(f_t) <= delta(f) - epsilon } is not Zariski dense in C^k? In particular, when k = 1, must E_epsilon be finite?

Fix an integer N ≥ 1. Does there exist a constant γ_N > 0, depending only on N, such that for every field K and every dominant rational self-map f of P^N defined over K, with dynamical degree δ(f) := lim_{m→∞} (deg(f^m))^{1/m} and with f^0 the identity map, one has δ(f) ≥ γ_N · min_{0≤n<N} (deg(f^{n+1})/deg(f^n))?

Let N >= 1 and let f : P^N dashrightarrow P^N be a dominant rational self-map, written in homogeneous coordinates by polynomials of the same degree with common factors removed. Write deg(f^n) for the degree of the nth iterate defined in the same way, and let delta_f := lim_{n->infty} (deg(f^n))^(1/n) be the dynamical degree of f. Must there exist an integer ell_f with 0 <= ell_f <= N such that deg(f^n) ≍ n^(ell_f) delta_f^n; equivalently, are there constants c1, c2, c3 > 0, depending on f but not on n, for which c1 n^(ell_f) delta_f^n <= deg(f^n) <= c2 n^(ell_f) delta_f^n for all n >= c3?

Let X be a smooth projective variety of dimension N, let f : X ⇢ X be a dominant rational map, and for each 1 ≤ i ≤ N let δ_f^{(i)} denote the ith dynamical degree defined by δ_f^{(i)} := lim_{n→∞} (((f^n)^*L)^i · L^{N−i})^{1/n}, where L is an ample sheaf on X. Is each δ_f^{(i)} an algebraic integer, i.e. a root of a monic polynomial with integer coefficients?

Integrality Conjecture (Bellon-Viallet). Let K be a field, let N >= 1, and let f = [f0,...,fN] : P^N --> P^N be a dominant rational self-map of projective N-space, where after canceling common factors the coordinate functions f0,...,fN belong to Kbar[X0,...,XN] and are homogeneous of the same degree. Define the dynamical degree by delta_f := lim_{n->infty} (deg(f^n))^(1/n), where deg(f^n) denotes the common degree of the homogeneous polynomials defining the nth iterate after common-factor cancellation. Is delta_f always an algebraic integer?

Let f: P^N ⇢ P^N be a dominant rational map defined over Qbar, let I(f) denote its indeterminacy locus, let P^N(Qbar)_f := {P ∈ P^N(Qbar) : f^n(P) ∉ I(f) for all n ≥ 0}, let O_f(P) := {f^n(P) : n ≥ 0}, let h be the logarithmic Weil height on P^N(Qbar), define the arithmetic degree (when it exists) by α_f(P) := lim_{n→∞} h(f^n(P))^(1/n), and define the dynamical degree by δ_f := lim_{n→∞} (deg(f^n))^(1/n). Is it true that for every P ∈ P^N(Qbar)_f: (i) the limit defining α_f(P) exists; (ii) the set {α_f(P) : P ∈ P^N(Qbar)_f} is finite; (iii) each α_f(P) is an algebraic integer; and (iv) if O_f(P) is Zariski dense in P^N, then α_f(P) = δ_f?

Let \(f:\mathbf{P}^N\dashrightarrow \mathbf{P}^N\) be a dominant rational map defined over \(\overline{\mathbf{Q}}\), let \(\delta_f:=\lim_{n\to\infty}(\deg(f^n))^{1/n}\) be its dynamical degree, let \(h\) be the logarithmic Weil height on \(\mathbf{P}^N(\overline{\mathbf{Q}})\), and let \(P\in \mathbf{P}^N(\overline{\mathbf{Q}})_f\), where \(\mathbf{P}^N(\overline{\mathbf{Q}})_f\) denotes the set of points whose entire forward orbit \(O_f(P)=\{f^n(P):n\ge 0\}\) is well-defined. Assume that \(O_f(P)\) is Zariski dense in \(\mathbf{P}^N\). Must there exist integers \(k_f\) and \(\ell_f\), with \(0\le \ell_f\le N\), such that there are constants \(c_1,c_2,c_3>0\), depending on \(f\) and \(P\), for which \(c_1\,\delta_f^n n^{\ell_f}(\log n)^{k_f}\le h(f^n(P))\le c_2\,\delta_f^n n^{\ell_f}(\log n)^{k_f}\) for all \(n\ge c_3\)? Moreover, if \(\delta_f>1\), must one have \(k_f=0\)?

Let X be a smooth projective variety over Qbar, let f: X dashrightarrow X be a dominant rational self-map, and let X(Qbar)_f := {P in X(Qbar) : f^n(P) is defined for every n >= 0}. Fix an embedding i: X -> P^N, let h be the absolute logarithmic Weil height on P^N, and for P in X(Qbar)_f define the arithmetic degree by alpha_f(P) := lim_{n->infty} h(i(f^n(P)))^(1/n) when the limit exists; let delta_f denote the first dynamical degree of f. Is it true that: (i) alpha_f(P) exists for every P in X(Qbar)_f; (ii) the set {alpha_f(P) : P in X(Qbar)_f} is finite; (iii) each alpha_f(P) is an algebraic integer; and (iv) if the forward orbit O_f(P) is Zariski dense in X, then alpha_f(P) = delta_f?

Let B be an algebraic curve over a field K, let K(B) be its function field, let f: P^N -> P^N be a morphism of degree d >= 2 defined over K(B), and let P be a point of P^N(K(B)). If hat h_f denotes the dynamical canonical height over the function field K(B), equivalently hat h_f(P) = lim_{n->infty} d^{-n} h(f^n(P)) with h the usual function-field height on P^N(K(B)), must hat h_f(P) always lie in Q? If not, give necessary and sufficient conditions on the pair (f, P) for hat h_f(P) to be rational.

Let K be a number field, let f:P^N→P^N be a morphism of degree d≥2 defined over K, and for P∈P^N(Q̄) define the dynamical canonical height by ĥ_f(P)=lim_{n→∞} d^{-n}h(f^n(P)). If P=[a_0:…:a_N] and a_i≠0, let K(P)=K(a_0/a_i,…,a_N/a_i), and call P wandering if its forward orbit O_f(P)={f^n(P):n≥0} is infinite. Must there exist a constant C(f)>0, depending only on f, such that every wandering point P∈P^N(Q̄) satisfies ĥ_f(P) ≥ C(f)/[K(P):K]? ([rlbenedetto.people.amherst.edu](https://rlbenedetto.people.amherst.edu/papers/ADtrends.pdf))

Fix integers N ≥ 1 and d ≥ 2. Let End_d^N denote the space of degree-d morphisms f : P^N → P^N, let M_d^N := End_d^N / PGL_{N+1} be the corresponding moduli space up to change of coordinates, and fix a projective embedding iota : M_d^N → P^L. Write h_M(f) := h(iota([f])) for the resulting moduli height, where h is the absolute logarithmic Weil height, and for each degree-d morphism f define the canonical height by hat h_f(P) := lim_{n→∞} d^{-n} h(f^n(P)). Is it true that for every D ≥ 1 there exist positive constants c1(D, N, d) and c2(D, N, d) such that for every number field K/Q with [K:Q] ≤ D, every degree-d morphism f : P^N → P^N defined over K, and every point P ∈ P^N(K) whose forward orbit O_f(P) = {f^n(P) : n ≥ 0} is Zariski dense in P^N, one has hat h_f(P) ≥ c1(D, N, d) h_M(f) + c2(D, N, d)?

Let C_v be an algebraically closed field complete with respect to a nonarchimedean absolute value |·|_v, let P^1_Berk be the Berkovich projective line over C_v, and let f ∈ C_v(z) be a rational function of degree at least 2, viewed as its natural extension f: P^1_Berk → P^1_Berk. If J_f denotes the Berkovich Julia set of f, is it true that the Type I part J_f ∩ P^1(C_v) is exactly the closure in P^1(C_v) of the set of Type I repelling periodic points of f, i.e. periodic points a ∈ P^1(C_v) with |λ_f(a)|_v > 1? citeturn9view0turn13view0turn13view1turn13view2turn13view3

Let C_v be an algebraically closed field complete with respect to a nonarchimedean absolute value, and let f in C_v(z) be a rational function of degree d >= 2 acting on the Berkovich projective line P^1_Berk. Write F_f for the Berkovich Fatou set. If U is a periodic connected component of F_f of exact period n >= 1 such that f^n is 1-to-1 on U (so U is an indifferent periodic Fatou component), and if U is not a disk, can f have infinitely many periodic cycles of such components? If not, is there a bound depending only on d for the number of these cycles? Does the answer, or the value of such a bound, depend on the choice of the field C_v?

Let C_v be an algebraically closed field complete with respect to a nonarchimedean absolute value |.|_v, let K be a locally compact subfield of C_v whose algebraic closure in C_v is dense in C_v, and let f in K(z) be a rational function of degree at least 2, viewed as an induced self-map of the Berkovich projective line P^1_Berk. Must every connected component of the Berkovich Fatou set F_f be preperiodic under iteration; equivalently, does f have no wandering domains?

Let C_v be an algebraically closed field complete with respect to a nonarchimedean absolute value, let P^1_Berk denote the Berkovich projective line over C_v, and let K ⊂ C_v be a discretely valued subfield whose algebraic closure K̄ is dense in C_v. Let p ≥ 0 be the residue characteristic of C_v, and let f ∈ C_v(z) be a rational function of degree at least 2. Assume that f has no wild points on P^1_Berk, i.e. for every ζ ∈ P^1_Berk the local degree of f at ζ is not divisible by p. Is it true that every wandering domain of f — meaning every connected component of the Berkovich Fatou set F_f that is not preperiodic — lies in the attracting basin of a periodic Type II point contained in the Berkovich Julia set J_f? ([rlbenedetto.people.amherst.edu](https://rlbenedetto.people.amherst.edu/papers/ADtrends.pdf))

Let q be a prime power, let N >= 1, let Fbar_q be an algebraic closure of F_q, and let f=[f_0:...:f_N]: P^N dashrightarrow P^N be a dominant rational self-map defined over F_q, where the f_i are homogeneous polynomials of the same degree and I(f) = {f_0 = ... = f_N = 0} is the indeterminacy locus. For any extension field K/F_q, define P^N(K)_f to be the set of points P in P^N(K) whose forward orbit under f is well-defined, equivalently such that f^n(P) notin I(f) for every n >= 0. Is it true that: (a) P^N(Fbar_q)_f is Zariski dense in P^N; and (b) lim_{k->infty} #P^N(F_{q^k})_f / #P^N(F_{q^k}) = 1, where k runs over the positive integers?

Let N >= 1 and d >= 2. Let f: P^N -> P^N be a morphism of degree d defined over Q, and let P ∈ P^N(Q) have Zariski-dense forward orbit O_f(P) = {f^n(P) : n >= 0}. For each prime p, let \tilde{P} ∈ P^N(F_p) be the reduction of P modulo p and let \tilde{f}: P^N(F_p) -> P^N(F_p) be the reduction of f modulo p. Is it true that for every ε > 0, the set of primes p such that #O_{\tilde f}(\tilde P) >= p^((1/2-ε)N) has natural density 1; equivalently, that
lim_{X->∞} #{p <= X : #O_{\tilde f}(\tilde P) >= p^((1/2-ε)N)} / #{p <= X : p prime} = 1?

Let N >= 1 and d >= 2, and let f in End_d^N(Q) be a degree-d morphism f : P^N -> P^N over Q, i.e. a globally defined self-map of P^N given by N+1 homogeneous forms of degree d with no common zero. Let P in P^N(Q) be such that its forward orbit O_f(P) = {f^n(P) : n >= 0} is Zariski dense in P^N. For each prime p of good reduction for f, let P~ in P^N(F_p) and f~ be the reductions modulo p of P and f, so that Proposition 12.5 gives f~^n(P~) = ~(f^n(P)). Under what conditions on f does the following hold: for every epsilon > 0, the set of primes p for which #(O_f~(P~)) <= p^((1/2+epsilon)N) has natural density 1?

Let q be a prime power, let F_q be the finite field with q elements, let f(x) in F_q[x] be an (irreducible) polynomial, and let g(x) in F_q[x]. For each n >= 1, write the composition g(f^n(x)) in F_q[x] as g(f^n(x)) = product_{i=1}^{r_n} p_{i,n}(x)^{e_{i,n}}, where the p_{i,n}(x) are irreducible over F_q. Determine, as n -> infinity, the behavior of factorization statistics such as r_n, sum_{i=1}^{r_n} e_{i,n}, max_{1<=i<=r_n} e_{i,n}, and max_{1<=i<=r_n} deg p_{i,n}(x); determine whether the factorization of g(f^{n+1}(x)) can be described or predicted from a given factorization of g(f^n(x)); and formulate the analogous problem when f(x) in F_q(x) is rational, factoring g(f^n(x)) as a product of irreducibles in F_q[x] with integer exponents, so that sum |e_{i,n}| and max |e_{i,n}| may be the more natural statistics.

Let K be a number field, let f:P^N->P^N be an endomorphism of degree at least 2 defined over K, and let X⊂P^N be an r-dimensional subvariety defined over K and irreducible over K. For each n>=1, write the pull-back of X under f^n as (f^n)^*X = sum_Y m(f^n,X;Y)Y, where the sum runs over K-irreducible subvarieties Y⊂P^N with dim(Y)=r. Say that (f,X) is eventually stable over K if there exists a constant C(f,X) such that sup_{n>=1} sum_Y m(f^n,X;Y) <= C(f,X), and say that (f,X) is geometrically eventually stable if the same condition holds after replacing K by an algebraic closure of K. Assuming that the forward orbit union_{n>=1} f^n(X) is Zariski dense in P^N, must (f,X) be eventually stable over K? If the forward orbit is Zariski dense and r>=1, must (f,X) be geometrically eventually stable? And when r>=1, is eventual stability over K equivalent to geometric eventual stability?

Assuming you intended the first major open problem stated in arXiv:1806.04980: Fix integers N >= 1, d >= 2, and D >= 1. Does there exist a constant C(N,d,D) such that for every number field K with [K:Q] = D and every degree-d morphism f: P^N -> P^N defined over K, the total number of K-rational preperiodic points of f is at most C(N,d,D)?

Let f(x) be a rational function in Q(x) of degree d >= 2, represented on P^1 by a normalized integral model, and for each prime p let tilde f_p in F_p(x) be its reduction modulo p as in Section 12. For every prime p with deg(tilde f_p) >= 2, write tilde f_p^n(x) = F_{n,p}(x)/G_{n,p}(x) in lowest terms. Using the paper's finite-field convention that stability is considered at base point 0, say that (tilde f_p, 0) is stable over F_p if F_{n,p}(x) is irreducible in F_p[x] for every n >= 1, and say that (tilde f_p, 0) is eventually stable over F_p if there exists m >= 0 such that for every beta in tilde f_p^{-m}(0), the pair (tilde f_p, beta) is stable over F_p(beta). Is the set of primes p for which (tilde f_p, 0) is stable over F_p finite? Is the set of primes p for which (tilde f_p, 0) is eventually stable over F_p finite?

Let K be a number field and let d≥2. For a rational function f(x)∈K(x) of degree d, write its nth iterate as f^n(x)=F_n(x)/G_n(x) with relatively prime polynomials F_n,G_n∈K[x]. Let α∈K be a wandering point for f, i.e. O_f(α) is infinite, and assume that f^{-1}(α)∩P^1(K)=∅. Is there a constant κ(d,K) such that, for every such pair (f,α) and every n≥1, the polynomial F_n(x)-αG_n(x) has at most κ(d,K) irreducible factors in K[x], counted with multiplicity? In particular, when d=2 and K=Q, can one take κ(2,Q)=3? More generally, if K is a number field, can the same statement hold with κ depending only on d and [K:Q]? ([rlbenedetto.people.amherst.edu](https://rlbenedetto.people.amherst.edu/papers/ADtrends.pdf))

Let K be a number field, let f: P^N → P^N be an endomorphism of degree at least 2 defined over K, and let P ∈ P^N(K) be a point that is not periodic for f. Viewing P as a 0-dimensional subvariety of P^N, write for each n ≥ 1
(f^n)*P = Σ_{Y/K⊂P^N, dim(Y)=0, Y irreducible over K} m(f^n, P; Y)Y.
Is there a constant C(f, P) such that
sup_{n≥1} Σ_{Y/K⊂P^N, dim(Y)=0, Y irreducible over K} m(f^n, P; Y) ≤ C(f, P)?
Equivalently, is the pair (f, P) eventually stable over K in the sense of Definition 19.8? ([rlbenedetto.people.amherst.edu](https://rlbenedetto.people.amherst.edu/papers/ADtrends.pdf))

Let f(x) ∈ Z[x] be a monic polynomial of degree 2. Assume that f is stable in the sense that every iterate f^n(x) is irreducible over Q, and let c_f be the unique critical point of f (equivalently, the unique root of f'(x)); assume that c_f is wandering, i.e. its forward orbit {f^n(c_f) : n >= 0} is infinite. For an integer α, define A(f, α, 0) := (f^n(α))_{n>=1}, and define Support(A(f, α, 0)) to be the set of primes p such that p divides some nonzero term f^n(α). Is it true that for every α ∈ Z this set of primes has natural density 0, namely that lim_{X->infinity} #{p <= X : p prime and p divides f^n(α) for some n >= 1 with f^n(α) != 0} / #{p <= X : p prime} = 0?

Let K be a number field with ring of integers O_K. For each prime ideal p of O_K, let ord_p: K^* → Z be the normalized valuation, and define ord_p^+(x):=max{ord_p(x),0}. Let f(x) ∈ K(x) be a rational function of degree at least 2, let α ∈ K be a wandering point for f (so O_f(α)={f^n(α): n ≥ 0} is infinite), let β ∈ K, and fix a constant c ∈ R. Is the set of integers n ≥ 0 such that Σ_p ord_p^+(f^n(α)-β) ≤ c finite, where the sum runs over all prime ideals p of O_K?

Let K be a number field with ring of integers O_K. For each prime ideal p of O_K, let ord_p: K^x -> Z be the associated normalized valuation, extend by the standard convention ord_p(0) = +infinity, and define ord_p^+(gamma) = max{ord_p(gamma), 0}. Let f(x) in K(x) be a rational function of degree at least 2, let alpha in K be a wandering point for f (that is, O_f(alpha) = {f^n(alpha) : n >= 0} is infinite), let beta in K, and let c be a fixed constant. Must the set { n >= 0 : sum over all prime ideals p of O_K of ord_p^+(f^n(alpha) - beta) <= c } be finite?

Give a concise characterization, analogous to the quadratic criterion in Conjecture 20.10, of those triples (f, α, β) with f(x) ∈ Q(x) and α, β ∈ Q for which the support of A(f, α, β) := (f^n(α) - β)_{n≥1} has natural density 0; here Support(A(f, α, β)) means the set of primes dividing the numerator of at least one nonzero term f^n(α) - β, and Density(P) means lim_{X→∞} #{p ∈ P : p ≤ X}/#{primes p : p ≤ X}, when this limit exists. ([rlbenedetto.people.amherst.edu](https://rlbenedetto.people.amherst.edu/papers/ADtrends.pdf))

Conjecture 21.4 (Dynamical Lang-Siegel Conjecture for P^N): Let f = [f_0, ..., f_N] : P^N -> P^N be a morphism of degree d >= 2 defined over Q. For each 1 <= n <= N+1, write the iterate f^n = [F_0^(n) : ... : F_N^(n)] by homogeneous polynomials of degree d^n with no common factor, and assume that F_0^(n) is not a constant multiple of X_0^(d^n). If O_f(P) = {f^n(P) : n >= 0} is the forward orbit of P in P^N(Q), must O_f(P) contain only finitely many points that are integral relative to the hyperplane x_0 = 0, i.e. points admitting homogeneous coordinates [1, a_1, ..., a_N] with a_1, ..., a_N in Z? More precisely, if P is wandering and for each n >= 1 one writes f^n(P) = [A_0(n), ..., A_N(n)] in primitive integral coordinates with gcd(A_0(n), ..., A_N(n)) = 1, must lim_{n->infty} log|A_0(n)| / log max{|A_0(n)|, ..., |A_N(n)|} = 1?

Fix N >= 1 and a degree d. For which integers n >= 1 does the following local-global principle hold for every morphism f:P^N -> P^N defined over Q, i.e. every everywhere-defined endomorphism of projective N-space given by homogeneous forms of common degree d with rational coefficients: f has a Q-rational point of exact period n (equivalently, there exists P in P^N(Q) such that f^n(P)=P and f^i(P) != P for all 1 <= i < n) if and only if f has a point of exact period n in P^N(R) and in P^N(Q_p) for every prime p?

Is the following Dynamical Brauer-Manin conjecture true? Let K be a number field, let X/K be a variety, let f : X -> X be a morphism defined over K, let Y subset X be a subvariety defined over K, and let P be a point of X(K). Write O_f(P) = {f^n(P) : n >= 0}. View X(K) diagonally inside X(A_K), where A_K is the adele ring of K, and for any subset S of X(A_K) let C(S) denote its closure in the adelic topology. Must one have C(Y ∩ O_f(P)) = Y(A_K) ∩ C(O_f(P))?

Let K be a number field, viewed via a fixed embedding K ↪ C. Let f,g ∈ K[x] be polynomials of degree at least 2, and let a,b ∈ K. For each nonzero prime ideal 𝔭 of O_K outside a finite set large enough that the reductions f mod 𝔭, g mod 𝔭, a mod 𝔭, and b mod 𝔭 are defined, write O_h(c) = {h^n(c) : n ≥ 0} for a forward orbit, let f̃, g̃, ã, b̃ denote the corresponding reductions modulo 𝔭, and let N𝔭 = #(O_K/𝔭). Is the following local-global statement true? (a) If O_f̃(ã) ∩ O_g̃(b̃) ≠ ∅ for all but finitely many such primes 𝔭, must f and g have the same Julia set in C? If so, does the same conclusion already follow when this nonempty-intersection condition holds for a set of primes 𝔭 of natural density 1? (b) Fix ε > 0. If #(O_f̃(ã) ∩ O_g̃(b̃)) ≥ (N𝔭)^ε for infinitely many such primes 𝔭, must f and g have the same Julia set in C?

Let X/C be a quasi-projective variety, let f : X -> X be a morphism, let P be a point of X, and let Y subseteq X be a subvariety. Writing f^n for the n-th iterate of f, is the set {n >= 0 : f^n(P) in Y} always a finite union of one-sided arithmetic progressions {a k + b : k = 0,1,2,...} with integers a,b >= 0 (allowing a = 0, so singletons are permitted)?

Does the Dynamical Uniform Boundedness Conjecture hold? Namely: for fixed integers N >= 1, d >= 2, and D >= 1, does there exist a constant C(N,d,D) such that for every number field K with [K:Q] = D and every degree-d morphism f : P^N -> P^N defined over K, one has
#PrePer(f, P^N(K)) <= C(N,d,D),
where P^N(K) is the set of K-rational points of projective N-space and
PrePer(f, P^N(K)) := {P in P^N(K) : f^n(P) = f^m(P) for some integers n > m >= 0}? ([rlbenedetto.people.amherst.edu](https://rlbenedetto.people.amherst.edu/papers/ADtrends.pdf))

Let c be a rational number and define f_c(x) = x^2 + c. Is it true that for every integer N >= 4, there is no rational number alpha in Q such that f_c^N(alpha) = alpha and f_c^i(alpha) != alpha for every 1 <= i < N?

Let f_{b,c}: P^1 -> P^1 be the degree-2 rational map defined over Q by f_{b,c}(x)=bx+c/x=(bx^2+c)/x, where b,c ∈ Q^×. Is it true that every Q-rational periodic point P ∈ P^1(Q) of f_{b,c} has exact period 1, 2, or 4, and that the largest possible number of Q-rational preperiodic points in this family is exactly 12; that is, does one have sup_{b,c∈Q^×} #PrePer(f_{b,c}, P^1(Q)) = 12?

Conjecture/open problem (paper-faithful form): Let f in End_2^1(Q), i.e. let f:P^1->P^1 be a degree-2 rational self-map defined over Q. Is it true that every Q-rational periodic point P in P^1(Q) has exact period at most 7, every Q-rational preperiodic point P has forward orbit O_f(P)={f^n(P): n>=0} of cardinality at most 9, and the full set of Q-rational preperiodic points PrePer(f,P^1(Q))={x in P^1(Q): f^n(x)=f^m(x) for some n>m>=0} satisfies #PrePer(f,P^1(Q))<=14?

Conjecture (Poonen, as restated in the paper). Let K be a number field, let K̄ be an algebraic closure of K, let X and S be algebraic varieties defined over K, let π:X→S be a morphism, and let f:X→X be an S-morphism, meaning π∘f=π. For each s∈S(K̄), write X_s:=π^{-1}(s) and let f_s:X_s→X_s be the induced morphism on the fiber. Is it true that for every integer D≥1, one has sup_{L/K, [L:K]=D} sup_{s∈S(L)} #PrePer(f_s, X_s(L)) < ∞, where PrePer(f_s, X_s(L)) denotes the set of L-rational preperiodic points of f_s on the fiber X_s?

Let K be a Hilbertian field of characteristic 0, and let d >= 2. Does there exist a monic polynomial f(X) in K[X] of degree d and a basepoint P in K such that the inverse-image tree T_{f,∞}(P) = {P} ⊔ f^{-1}(P) ⊔ f^{-2}(P) ⊔ ... is complete (equivalently, #f^{-n}(P)=d^n for every n >= 0) and the associated arboreal representation rho^{arb}_{f,P}: Gal(Kbar/K) -> Aut(T_{f,∞}(P)) is surjective?

Let K be a field of characteristic 0, let Kbar be an algebraic closure of K, let f in K(x) be a rational function of degree 2, viewed as a morphism f: P^1 -> P^1 defined over K, and let P in P^1(K). Assume that the full inverse-image tree T_{f,infty}(P) = {P} disjoint union f^{-1}(P) disjoint union f^{-2}(P) disjoint union ... is complete, equivalently #f^{-n}(P) = 2^n for every n >= 0. Let rho^arb_{f,P}: Gal(Kbar/K) -> Aut(T_{f,infty}(P)) be the associated arboreal representation, let G_{f,infty}(P) be its image, and let iota_K(f,P) = [Aut(T_{f,infty}(P)) : G_{f,infty}(P)] be the Odoni index. Is it true that iota_K(f,P) is infinite if and only if one of the following four obstructions occurs: (a) f is postcritically finite, i.e. both critical points of f are preperiodic; (b) if gamma_1 and gamma_2 are the two critical points of f, then f^r(gamma_1) = f^r(gamma_2) for some integer r >= 2; (c) the basepoint P is periodic under f; or (d) there exists a nonidentity Mobius transformation phi in PGL_2(K), written phi(x) = (alpha x + beta)/(gamma x + delta), such that phi o f = f o phi and phi(P) = P?

Dynamical Mordell–Lang Conjecture: Is it true that for every quasi-projective variety X over C, every morphism f:X→X, every point P∈X, and every subvariety Y⊆X, the set {n≥0 : f^n(P)∈Y}, where f^n denotes the n-th iterate of f, is a finite union of one-sided arithmetic progressions in N, i.e. sets of the form {ak+b : k=0,1,2,...} with integers a,b≥0, allowing a=0?

Does the following Ghioca–Tucker–Zhang conjecture hold? Let X/C be a projective variety, let f: X -> X be a polarizable endomorphism (that is, there exist an ample line bundle L on X and an integer d >= 2 such that f^*L is isomorphic to L^{\otimes d}), and let Y be a subvariety of X with no irreducible component contained entirely in Sing(X). If PrePer(f, X) denotes the set of preperiodic points of X and if a subvariety Y is called preperiodic when f^n(Y) is contained in f^m(Y) for some n > m >= 0, is it true that Y is preperiodic under f if and only if Y intersect PrePer(f, X) contains a Zariski-dense subset of points x at which Y is smooth and for each such x the tangent space T_xY, viewed as a point of the Grassmannian bundle Gr_{dim Y}(TX), is preperiodic under the natural map induced by the differential df?

Let F be a holomorphic foliation on the complex projective plane P^2(C), and let Sing(F) denote its finite singular set. If L is any leaf of F in P^2(C) minus Sing(F), must the closure of L in P^2(C) intersect Sing(F)? ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1807.05640))

Fix an integer d >= 2, and let B_d denote the parameter space of holomorphic foliations by Riemann surfaces of geometric degree d on the complex projective plane P^2(C). For a generic foliation F in B_d, is every nonsingular leaf of F, except countably many leaves, biholomorphic to the unit disc?

Fix a geometric degree d and consider the parameter space of singular holomorphic foliations by Riemann surfaces on the complex projective plane P^2(C) of degree d, obtained from nonzero homogeneous holomorphic vector fields on C^3 whose coefficients are homogeneous polynomials of one fixed degree and have no non-trivial common divisor. For a generic foliation in this degree-d space, are all generic leaves—meaning all leaves except countably many—dense in P^2(C)? ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1807.05640))

Let F be a possibly singular foliation by Riemann surfaces on a compact Kähler manifold M with fixed Kähler form ω, and let T be an extremal positive dd^c-closed current of bidimension (1,1) directed by F, assumed to give full mass to the hyperbolic leaves. For T-almost every point a on a hyperbolic leaf L_a, let φ_a: D → L_a be the universal covering map with φ_a(0)=a, and let τ_r^a be the associated Nevanlinna current, defined by τ_r^a := (1/T_a(r))∫_0^r (dt/t)(φ_a)_*[D(t)], where T_a(r):=∫_0^r (dt/t)∫_{D(t)}φ_a^*(ω). Theorem 2.1 proves that if all singularities of F are linearizable, then τ_r^a converges to T as r → 1^- in the sense of currents. Does this same convergence theorem remain valid when the linearizability assumption is dropped, i.e. when singularities of F are allowed to be non-linearizable? ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1807.05640))

In the setting of Theorem 2.1, let F be a possibly singular foliation by Riemann surfaces on a compact Kähler manifold X with Kähler form ω, and let T be an extremal positive dd^c-closed current (dd^c = (i/π)∂∂̄) directed by F, assumed for simplicity to have full mass on the hyperbolic leaves. For a point a on a hyperbolic leaf L_a, let φ^a: D -> L_a be the universal covering with φ^a(0)=a, and let τ_r^a be the associated Nevanlinna current. Assuming that all singularities of F are linearizable so that τ_r^a -> T as r -> 1 for T-almost every a, does there exist such an extremal directed positive dd^c-closed current T for which one can quantitatively estimate the speed of convergence of <τ_r^a, θ> to <T, θ> for smooth test forms θ of bi-degree (1,1) on X?

Let F be a (possibly singular) foliation by Riemann surfaces on a compact Kähler manifold (M,ω), and let T be an extremal positive dd^c-closed current directed by F. Assume, as in Section 2 of the paper, that T gives full mass to the hyperbolic leaves. For a point a on a hyperbolic leaf L_a, let φ_a: D → L_a be the universal covering map with φ_a(0)=a, let D(r)⊂D be the disc of radius r centered at 0, define A(r):=∫_{D(r)} φ_a^*(ω), and define the associated unweighted Ahlfors current by σ_r^a:=(1/A(r))(φ_a)_*[D(r)]. Does σ_r^a converge to T, in the sense of currents on M, as r→1 for T-almost every a?

Let F be a possibly singular holomorphic foliation by Riemann surfaces on a compact Kähler manifold M with Kähler form ω, and let T be an extremal positive dd^c-closed current of bi-dimension (1,1) directed by F. Assume that T gives full mass to the hyperbolic leaves and that all singularities of F are linearizable, so that Theorem 2.1 applies. For a point a on a hyperbolic leaf L_a, let φ_a : D → L_a be the universal covering map with φ_a(0)=a, and define the Nevanlinna characteristic by T_a(r) := ∫_0^r (dt/t) ∫_{D(t)} φ_a^*(ω), for 0<r<1. Since Theorem 2.1 implies that for T-almost every a one has T_a(r) ≥ c(a) log(1/(1-r)) for all r sufficiently close to 1, is this lower bound in fact true for every hyperbolic leaf of F? In particular, does it hold when F admits no diffuse positive dd^c-closed current directed by F?

Let F be a holomorphic foliation by Riemann surfaces of geometric degree d on the complex projective plane P^2(C), having at least one non-hyperbolic singularity, where a singularity is called hyperbolic when the quotient of the eigenvalues of the linearized defining vector field is non-real. Describe all positive dd^c-closed currents of bidimension (1,1) directed by F, in the sense that T wedge alpha = 0 for every local holomorphic 1-form alpha defining F and dd^c = (i/pi) partial bar-partial. Also determine for which such foliations there exist diffuse positive closed directed currents, where diffuse means giving no mass to analytic varieties. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1807.05640))

For each integer d >= 2, let B_d denote the space of holomorphic foliations by Riemann surfaces of geometric degree d on the complex projective plane P^2(C), and let B_d^c ⊂ B_d be the subset of foliations that admit a nonzero directed positive closed current of bidimension (1,1). Is B_d^c a countable union of proper analytic subsets of B_d?

Let A_d be the space of foliations on an affine coordinate chart C^2 ⊂ P^2 defined by a polynomial vector field Z = P(z,w)∂/∂z + Q(z,w)∂/∂w with max(deg P, deg Q) = d, and let B_d be the space of holomorphic foliations of geometric degree d on P^2 (with d ≥ 2 in the paper's notation). Is it true that, for a generic foliation F in A_d (respectively in B_d), all but countably many leaves of F are biholomorphic to the unit disc?

Let \mathcal F be a holomorphic foliation by Riemann surfaces on the complex projective plane \mathbb{P}^2(\mathbb{C}), and let \operatorname{Sing}(\mathcal F) denote its finite singular set. For every leaf L of \mathcal F (so L\subset \mathbb{P}^2\setminus\operatorname{Sing}(\mathcal F)), must its topological closure \overline{L}\subset \mathbb{P}^2 satisfy \overline{L}\cap\operatorname{Sing}(\mathcal F)\neq\varnothing?

Does there exist a smooth or real-analytic Levi-flat real hypersurface M ⊂ ℙ²(ℂ), that is, a real hypersurface locally given by {ρ = 0} for a real-valued C∞ or real-analytic defining function ρ with dρ ≠ 0 on M, such that the Levi form of ρ vanishes on the complex tangent bundle T^{1,0}M?

Let F be a holomorphic foliation by Riemann surfaces of geometric degree d on the complex projective plane P^2(C). Assume that the line at infinity L_infty is F-invariant and that every singularity of F is hyperbolic, meaning that at each singular point the quotient of the eigenvalues of a linearized local vector field defining F is non-real. Must every leaf of F that is not a compact invariant curve admit a Green function?

Let F ∈ B_d with d ≥ 2, where B_d denotes the space of holomorphic foliations on ℙ^2 that, in an affine chart ℂ^2 ⊂ ℙ^2 with coordinates (z,w), are defined by a polynomial vector field P(z,w)∂/∂z + Q(z,w)∂/∂w satisfying max(deg P, deg Q) = d. Assume that F admits a nonzero positive closed current of bidimension (1,1) directed by F. What is the function theory of the leaves of F outside Sing(F), in terms of Green functions; in particular, which leaves are parabolic and which admit Green functions? ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1807.05640))

Construct a holomorphic minimal foliation (respectively, a holomorphic minimal lamination) by Riemann surfaces on a compact complex manifold that carries uncountably many extremal positive dd^c-closed currents of bidimension (1,1), directed by the foliation (respectively, lamination), such that none of these currents is closed; here minimal means that every leaf is dense, and dd^c=(i/π)∂∂̄. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1807.05640))

Let Z be a holomorphic vector field on C^2, and let F_Z be the singular holomorphic foliation by Riemann surfaces induced by Z on C^2 \ Z^{-1}(0). Is it possible that F_Z admits one set of positive measure of leaves whose universal covering surface is biholomorphic to C, and another set of positive measure of leaves whose universal covering surface is biholomorphic to the unit disc Δ?

Let Z be a nonzero holomorphic vector field on C^2, and let F_Z denote the one-dimensional holomorphic foliation by its integral curves on C^2 minus Sing(Z). Suppose there exists a family of leaves of F_Z whose union is a non-pluripolar subset of C^2 and such that each of those leaves is parabolic as a Riemann surface (that is, every bounded subharmonic function on the leaf is constant). Must every leaf of F_Z be parabolic?

Let Z be a global holomorphic vector field on C^2, and let F_Z denote the one-dimensional holomorphic foliation induced by Z on C^2 \ Sing(Z). Find conditions on Z that ensure that, for every leaf L of F_Z, the universal covering surface of L is biholomorphic to the unit disc.

Let Z be a holomorphic vector field on C^k that cannot be written as hY with h holomorphic on C^k and Y a polynomial vector field. For every leaf L of the foliation induced by Z, let φ: Σ -> L be its uniformization (universal covering) map, where Σ is either C or the unit disc D, and regard φ as a map into the projective compactification P^k = C^k ∪ H_infty, where H_infty := P^k minus C^k is the hyperplane at infinity. With ω_FS the Fubini-Study form, D_t := {ζ in Σ : |ζ| < t}, and [D_t] the current of integration on D_t, define T_φ(r) := ∫_0^r (dt/t) ∫_{D_t} φ^*ω_FS and τ_r^φ := (1/T_φ(r)) φ_*(log^+(r/|ζ|)) = (1/T_φ(r)) ∫_0^r (dt/t) (φ_*[D_t]), where log^+(x) := max(log x, 0). Is every cluster point of τ_r^φ, in the sense of currents on P^k, necessarily supported on H_infty as r -> ∞ when Σ = C and as r -> 1^- when Σ = D?

Fix one of the two settings considered in the paper: either H = O(C,C), or H = O(C,P^1), endowed with the topology of uniform convergence on compact sets. Let U be the set of maps h in H such that for every f in H there exists a sequence (a_n) in C with h_{a_n}(z) := h(z+a_n) converging to f in H. Birkhoff’s theorem implies that U is nonempty. Determine the minimal possible asymptotic growth, as r -> infinity, of the Nevanlinna characteristic T_h(r) for h in U, where T_h(r) = ∫_0^r (dt/t) ∫_{D(t)} h^*(omega), D(t) = {z in C : |z| < t}, and omega is the Fubini-Study form on P^1 (with C viewed as the affine chart of P^1 in the C-valued case).

Let E be the space of entire functions f:C->C, endowed with the topology of uniform convergence on compact subsets of C, and let U subset E be the set of universal entire functions, i.e. those f for which, for every g in E, there exists a sequence a_n in C such that f(·+a_n) -> g locally uniformly on C. If mu is a non-trivial ergodic probability measure on E that is invariant under the translation action T_a f(z)=f(z+a) for all a in C, where non-trivial means that mu assigns measure 0 to the set of constant functions, what can be said about the value of mu(U)? ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1807.05640))

Let M be a complex manifold of complex dimension n, homogeneous under a Lie group G acting transitively by holomorphic automorphisms, and let Hol(M,P^n(C)) denote the space of holomorphic maps M -> P^n(C), endowed with the topology of uniform convergence on compact subsets. Consider the induced G-action on Hol(M,P^n(C)) by precomposition, for example (g·f)(x)=f(g^{-1}·x). Under what conditions on the homogeneous pair (M,G) does this action admit a dense orbit; equivalently, when does there exist f in Hol(M,P^n(C)) whose G-orbit is dense in Hol(M,P^n(C))?

Let M be a complex manifold that is homogeneous under the action of a Lie group G, and let O(M,P^n) be the space of holomorphic maps M→P^n endowed with the topology of uniform convergence on compact subsets. Via precomposition with the G-action on M, G acts on O(M,P^n). Can Benjamin Weiss's construction of non-trivial invariant probability measures for the translation action on spaces of entire maps be extended to this setting; that is, can one construct G-invariant Borel probability measures on O(M,P^n) that assign measure zero to the set of constant maps? ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1807.05640))

Equip the spaces Aut(C^n), Aut_vol(C^n) = {F in Aut(C^n) : F^*(dz_1∧...∧dz_n) = dz_1∧...∧dz_n}, and, when n = 2m, Aut_sp(C^{2m}) = {F in Aut(C^{2m}) : F^*omega = omega for a fixed standard holomorphic symplectic form omega}, with the topology of uniform convergence on compact sets. In the sense of Section 9—namely, as analogues of the dense-orbit question and the Weiss-type invariant-probability-measure question previously posed for spaces of holomorphic maps—do these automorphism spaces exhibit the same two phenomena: existence of a dense orbit and existence of invariant probability measures of Weiss type?

Let F be a holomorphic foliation, possibly with singularities, on a compact Kähler manifold X endowed with a fixed Kähler form ω, and assume that the leaves of F have complex dimension greater than 1. In the case of foliations by Riemann surfaces, positive dd^c-closed currents of bidimension (1,1) directed by F are the basic objects used in the ergodic theory. What is the correct higher-dimensional directed notion that should replace these currents when the leaves have dimension greater than 1, in a way that still permits the development of an ergodic theory for F? ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1807.05640))

Can one construct a non-elementary holomorphic foliation, possibly with singularities, in complex projective space \mathbb{P}^k whose leaves have complex dimension strictly larger than 1 and such that no leaf contains a compact complex curve? Here "non-elementary" excludes foliations defined by closed forms and foliations defined by forms that become closed after multiplication by integrating factors; in codimension 1, this in particular excludes the logarithmic first-integral case where the leaves are level sets of multivalued holomorphic functions of the form \prod_i f_i^{\lambda_i} with \lambda_i \in \mathbb{R}.

Let \(\mathcal F\) be a holomorphic foliation on the unit polydisc \(\mathbb D^k\subset \mathbb C^k\) whose leaves have dimension \(d\) with \(1<d<k\). Suppose that \(\mathcal F\) is tangent to holomorphic 1-forms \(\alpha_1,\dots,\alpha_{k-d}\) on \(\mathbb D^k\) that are linearly independent at a generic point of \(\mathbb D^k\) and satisfy the Frobenius integrability condition \(d\alpha_j=\sum_{l=1}^{k-d}\alpha_l\wedge\beta_{j,l}\) for some holomorphic 1-forms \(\beta_{j,l}\) on \(\mathbb D^k\). Is it always possible to approximate \(\mathcal F\) by foliations in \(\mathbb C^k\) or \(\mathbb P^k\)? More precisely, can \(\alpha_1,\dots,\alpha_{k-d}\) be approximated uniformly on compact subsets of \(\mathbb D^k\) by entire holomorphic 1-forms, respectively by polynomial 1-forms, that still satisfy the same Frobenius condition and hence define foliations of the same codimension?

Problem (Oka's Dream). Let pi:X -> C^n be a Riemann domain over C^n in the sense of the paper: X is a possibly singular reduced complex space, pi is holomorphic, and every fiber pi^{-1}({z}) is discrete; do not assume that pi is locally biholomorphic, i.e. consider the ramified case. Assume that for every point a in C^n there exists a neighborhood U of a in C^n such that pi^{-1}(U) is Stein (equivalently, pi is locally Stein over C^n). Find sufficient or necessary conditions under which X is Stein. As noted in the paper, this remains open even when X is non-singular.

Over RCA0, which, if any, of the following principles are equivalent: (A) the Halpern–Läuchli Theorem for every finite number of finitely branching trees; (B) Milliken’s Ramsey theorem for strong trees on one finitely branching infinite tree with no terminal nodes; (C) Sauer’s canonical partition theorem for colorings of copies of a fixed finite graph inside the Rado graph; and (D) the statement that for every finite graph G and every k ≥ 2, every coloring of the copies of G in the Rado graph R into countably many colors, with each color used at most k times, admits an induced subgraph R' isomorphic to R in which no two copies of G have the same color? ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1808.10227.pdf))

Over RCA0, what is the reverse-mathematical strength of the principle that the Rado graph R is rainbow Ramsey for k-bounded colorings of edges—that is, for every k in omega and every k-bounded coloring gamma:[R]^2->omega, does there exist a subgraph R* subseteq R with R* congruent to R such that gamma is one-to-one on [R*]^2—and how does this strength compare with Ramsey’s Theorem and with the rainbow Ramsey theorem for k-bounded colorings of pairs of natural numbers?

For each graph G on exactly three vertices and each integer k >= 2, does RCA0 prove the following implication: if every k-bounded coloring f:[N]^3 -> N admits an infinite set H subseteq N such that f is injective on [H]^3, then every k-bounded coloring c of all copies of G in the countable Rado graph R into N admits a subgraph R' subseteq R with R' isomorphic to R such that c is injective on the copies of G contained in R'?

For each finite d >= 1, in the usual reverse-mathematical setting over RCA0, is the strong-tree version of the Halpern-Läuchli Theorem for d trees strictly weaker than the corresponding strong-tree version for d+1 trees? Here, the d-tree statement is the assertion that for every finite coloring of the level product of d finitely branching infinite trees with no terminal nodes, there exist strong subtrees of those trees with a common level set such that the coloring is constant on the resulting level product.

For each fixed finite d >= 1, over RCA_0, and for d infinite finitely branching trees with no terminal nodes, is the strong-tree form of the Halpern-Lauchli theorem for d trees strictly stronger than the corresponding somewhere-dense-matrix form for d trees, in the reverse-mathematical sense that the strong-tree principle implies the somewhere-dense-matrix principle but the converse is not provable over RCA_0? ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/abs/1808.10227))

Over RCA0, is the statement that the Halpern-Läuchli Theorem holds for every finite number of trees equivalent in reverse-mathematical strength to Milliken’s Ramsey theorem for strong trees on one finitely branching infinite tree with no terminal nodes, i.e. Milliken’s theorem for colorings of finite strong trees?

Over RCA_0, for each fixed n >= 1, what is the reverse-mathematical strength of MTT^n, the restriction of Milliken's tree theorem asserting that for every finite coloring f : S^n(T) -> k of the strong subtrees of height n of an infinite finitely branching tree T with no leaves, there is an infinite strong subtree S of T such that all members of S^n(S) have the same f-color? In particular, does the strength of MTT^n vary with n, especially between the height-2 case and the higher-height cases n >= 3?

Over RCA0, and holding fixed the non-branching parameters of the principle (for the strong-tree Halpern-Läuchli theorem, a finite number d of trees; for Milliken's Ramsey theorem for strong trees on one infinite finitely branching tree with no terminal nodes, the height of the finite strong trees being colored), does the reverse-mathematical strength of either theorem depend on the splitting properties of the ambient trees? More specifically, are the versions restricted to 2-branching trees weaker than the corresponding versions for 3-branching trees, and are these in turn weaker than the corresponding versions for trees that are finitely branching but have no uniform finite bound on branching? ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1808.10227.pdf))

Over RCA_0, what is the reverse-mathematical strength of the assertion that the Rado graph is rainbow Ramsey: namely, that for every countable graph R isomorphic to the Rado graph, every finite graph G, every natural number k >= 1, and every k-bounded coloring γ from the set of induced copies of G in R into ω, there exists an induced subgraph R' of R with R' ≅ R such that γ is injective on the induced copies of G in R'?  How does this principle compare in strength with Ramsey’s theorem and with the rainbow Ramsey theorem for pairs of natural numbers?

For a fixed integer k >= 2, over RCA0, is the following k-bounded rainbow Ramsey principle for the Rado graph equivalent to its (k+1)-bounded version: for every finite graph G, every coloring of all copies of G in the Rado graph R into countably many colors with each color used at most k times admits a subgraph R' subseteq R that is again a Rado graph and in which no two copies of G have the same color?

Over RCA_0, fix a finite graph F and let R be the Rado graph. Compare the reverse-mathematical strength of the following two principles: (1) Sauer’s canonical partition theorem for copies of F in R, namely that for every finite coloring of the copies of F in R there is a subgraph R' isomorphic to R such that on copies of F inside R' the coloring is constant on each canonical (equivalently, strong-similarity) class supplied by Sauer’s theorem; and (2) the rainbow Ramsey principle for R, namely that for every k >= 2 and every k-bounded coloring of the copies of F in R there is a subgraph R' isomorphic to R on which the coloring is injective on copies of F. In particular, is the canonical-partition principle stronger over RCA_0 than the rainbow-Ramsey principle?

Over RCA0, fix an integer k >= 2. For a finite graph G, let RR_R(G,k) be the statement that every coloring of all copies of G in the Rado graph R into countably many colors, with each color used at most k times, admits a subgraph R' subseteq R with R' isomorphic to R such that no two copies of G in R' have the same color. As G ranges over finite graphs, do the principles RR_R(G,k) all have the same reverse-mathematical strength, or can the strength vary with the number of vertices of G?

Fix r >= 1 and let M be a compact two-dimensional manifold. Let X^r(M) be the space of C^r vector fields on M, endowed with the C^r topology, and let Σ^r(M) ⊂ X^r(M) be the subset of structurally stable vector fields. Write X_1^r(M) := X^r(M) \ Σ^r(M) with the induced topology. Characterize the class Σ_1^r(M) of first-order structurally stable systems, namely those vector fields X in X_1^r(M) for which there exists a neighborhood U of X in the relative topology of X_1^r(M) such that every Y in U is topologically equivalent to X (equivalently, has the same phase portrait as X up to a homeomorphism of M). In other words, determine exactly which non-structurally-stable C^r vector fields on a compact surface are nevertheless structurally stable against arbitrarily small perturbations that remain inside X_1^r(M).

Let X = X^r(S^2) be the space of C^r vector fields on the 2-sphere S^2, endowed with the C^r topology, and let S be the subset of C^r-structurally stable vector fields. If gamma:[0,1]→X is a continuous arc, must every neighborhood of gamma in C^0([0,1],X) contain a continuous arc eta:[0,1]→X such that eta(t) lies outside S for only finitely many t in [0,1]? Equivalently: can every continuous arc in X be arbitrarily well approximated by a continuous arc that meets only finitely many bifurcation points, meaning finitely many parameter values at which the arc passes through X minus S?

Do invariant perfect sets—that is, nonempty, compact, invariant sets that are transversally totally discontinuous—exist for differential equations of class C^2 on orientable two-dimensional manifolds?

For a fixed C^r regularity class, characterize the autonomous scalar second-order differential equations x'' = f(x,x') whose phase portraits are preserved up to homeomorphism under sufficiently small perturbations by equations of the same form, and prove that the structurally stable equations form a generic (Peixoto-type open dense) subset of this class.

Fix a differentiability class C^r and a dimension n. Let M be a compact smooth n-dimensional manifold, let X be a C^r vector field on M, and let p in M lie on a non-trivial recurrent trajectory of X. Is it true that X can be arbitrarily approximated in the C^r topology by a C^r vector field Y for which p lies on a periodic trajectory of Y?

Let L>0, let k\in\{1,2,3,4\}, and consider the Korteweg-de Vries initial-boundary value problem on (0,L): u_t+u_x+u_{xxx}+u u_x=0 for x\in(0,L), t>0, with initial condition u(x,0)=\phi(x), and boundary condition B_k u=\vec h(t), where B_k=B_{k,0}+B_{k,1} is one of the four boundary operators introduced in Section 3, with leading part B_{1,0}u=(u(0,t),u(L,t),u_x(L,t)), B_{2,0}u=(u(0,t),u_x(L,t),u_{xx}(L,t)), B_{3,0}u=(u_{xx}(0,t),u(L,t),u_x(L,t)), or B_{4,0}u=(u_{xx}(0,t),u_x(L,t),u_{xx}(L,t)), and with the corresponding lower-order boundary terms B_{k,1}; assuming (\phi,\vec h) satisfy the same regularity and compatibility hypotheses as in the local well-posedness theorem cited earlier in the paper, is this IBVP globally well-posed in H^s(0,L) for some s\ge 0?

For the bounded-interval Korteweg-de Vries initial-boundary value problem singled out in equation (4.18) of the paper, namely
u_t+u_x+u_{xxx}+u u_x=0 on (0,L)\times(0,T),
u(x,0)=\phi(x),
u(0,t)=h_1(t), u(L,t)=h_2(t), and u_x(L,t)=h_3(t),
with L>0 fixed and boundary data taken in the same sharp temporal trace spaces used in the known local theory, does there exist any Sobolev index s\le -1 for which the problem is locally well-posed in H^s(0,L)? More specifically, is the authors’ conjecture correct that this IBVP is ill-posed for every s<-1, leaving at most the endpoint s=-1 as a possible borderline case?

Let L>0 be fixed, let u=u(x,t) be real-valued on (0,L) x (0,∞), and let phi in H^s(0,L). Consider the nonlinear Korteweg-de Vries initial-boundary value problem
u_t + u u_x + u_xxx = 0,  x in (0,L), t>0,
u(x,0)=phi(x),
u(0,t)=0,  u(L,t)=0,  u_x(0,t)=u_x(L,t),  t>0,
where u_x = partial_x u and u_xxx = partial_x^3 u. Does there exist some Sobolev exponent s in R for which this nonlinear IBVP is well-posed in H^s(0,L)?

Let Omega be a smooth bounded domain in R^N with N > 4, let 2^* = 2N/(N-2), and let C1(N) be the constant introduced in Proposition 1.2 of the paper. If a,b > 0 satisfy a^((N-4)/2)b < C1(N), is it true that the conclusion of Theorem 1.1 still holds; namely, that for every sufficiently large lambda > 0 and every convex set C subset of L2(Omega) whose closure in L2(Omega) contains H^1_0(Omega), there exists v* in C such that the critical Kirchhoff problem -(a + b∫_Omega |grad u|^2 dx)Delta u = |u|^(2^*-2)u + lambda(u - v*(x)) in Omega, u = 0 on partial Omega, has at least three weak solutions in H^1_0(Omega), two of which are global minima in H^1_0(Omega) of the energy functional J_{lambda,v*}(u) = (a/2)∫_Omega |grad u|^2 dx + (b/4)(∫_Omega |grad u|^2 dx)^2 - (1/2^*)∫_Omega |u|^{2^*} dx - (lambda/2)∫_Omega |u - v*(x)|^2 dx?

Let X be one of the infinitely many asymptotically conical G2-manifolds constructed in [FHN18], each cohomogeneity-1 under SU(2) x SU(2) x U(1). For the SU(2) x SU(2) x U(1)-invariant G2-instantons whose local existence near the singular orbit of X is guaranteed by the cohomogeneity-1 theory reviewed in [LO18], how many of these local solutions extend to globally defined G2-instantons on all of X? After classifying the global solutions, and assuming a nontrivial family exists, what global features does the resulting moduli space exhibit—especially the kinds of phenomena seen in the Bryant-Salamon case, such as noncompactness/compactification and limiting or bubbling behavior—and in particular what happens for the D7 family of [FHN18], which was not considered in [LO18]? ([discovery.ucl.ac.uk](https://discovery.ucl.ac.uk/10067480/1/1812.11867v1.pdf))

Let M be one of the known nearly Kähler 6-manifolds that occurs as the link of the asymptotic cone of an asymptotically conical G2-manifold, namely M ∈ {S^6, CP^3, S^3 × S^3 (and finite quotients thereof), F2}. For a principal G-bundle over M with compact semisimple structure group G, can one construct pseudo-Hermitian–Yang–Mills connections a on M (equivalently, nearly Kähler instantons, i.e. connections satisfying F_a ∧ ω^2 = 0 and F_a ∧ γ2 = 0 for the nearly Kähler SU(3)-structure (ω, γ2) on M)? For each such a, does there exist a G2-instanton A on an asymptotically conical G2-manifold asymptotic to the cone on M, with pointwise decaying curvature at infinity, whose limit at infinity is a; and, if so, how many such G2-instantons have a as their asymptotic limit?

Let (X^7, phi) be an asymptotically conical G2-manifold, i.e. a complete noncompact torsion-free G2-manifold with one end asymptotic to the cone R^+ x M over a nearly Kähler 6-manifold (M, omega, gamma_2). Fix a principal G-bundle P -> X and a G2-instanton A on P whose curvature decays pointwise at infinity, so that A has an asymptotic limit a on M satisfying F_a wedge omega^2 = 0 and F_a wedge gamma_2 = 0. What is the local deformation theory of A, equivalently the local geometry of the moduli space of G2-instantons on X modulo gauge near [A]? In particular, can one prove uniqueness of the basic G2-instanton on R^7 with gauge group G2, determine whether deformations of symmetric G2-instantons on AC G2-manifolds must preserve the same symmetries (so that at least one cohomogeneity-1 component of the moduli space is still accessible by the symmetric methods used in the survey), and analyze the asymptotic-limit projection from the local moduli space of G2-instantons to the moduli space of nearly Kähler instantons on M, including whether this map is surjective?

Let X = Lambda^2_-(CP^2) be the Bryant–Salamon asymptotically conical G2-manifold, and let Q = SU(3) ×_{U(1)^2} SU(3), where U(1)^2 acts diagonally through a fixed maximal torus. In the notation of §3.1.2, Theorem 3 gives two explicit 1-parameter families of irreducible SU(3)-invariant G2-instantons A_c on Q, written using the decomposition su(3) = u(1)^2 ⊕ C_{α1} ⊕ C_{α2} ⊕ C_{α3}, the invariant forms l and λ_i, the fiber-radius s, and the function u_c(s) = 1 - 2cs^2/(s^2(1 + c) + 2(√(1 + s^2) + 1)), with c ≥ 0. What is the c → +∞ limit of these Theorem 3 instantons, up to gauge transformation, in the natural gauge-theoretic sense? ([discovery.ucl.ac.uk](https://discovery.ucl.ac.uk/10067480/1/1812.11867v1.pdf))

Let A_{y_0} be the 1-parameter family from Proposition 6 of SU(2)^2 x U(1)-invariant, in fact SU(2)^3-invariant, G2-instantons with gauge group SU(2), defined in a neighbourhood of the singular orbit S^3 in the Bryant-Salamon G2-manifold R^4 x S^3 and extending smoothly over S^3 on the bundle P_id = SU(2)^2 x_{(Delta SU(2), id)} SU(2). Theorem 5 shows that the member A_0 extends to a global G2-instanton on all of R^4 x S^3. For each nonzero real parameter y_0, does the corresponding local instanton A_{y_0} extend to a global G2-instanton on R^4 x S^3? If such a global extension exists, must its curvature norm |F_{A_{y_0}}| be unbounded along the noncompact end, i.e. at infinity?

Motivated by Proposition 9, let (1, infinity) x Gamma be the Calabi-Yau cone arising as the asymptotic cone of an ALC G2-manifold, where Gamma carries the Sasaki-Einstein SU(2)-structure of Proposition 8 and hence induces a torsion-free SU(3)-structure (omega, Omega = Omega_1 + i Omega_2) on the cone. On a principal G-bundle, with G compact semisimple, over this Calabi-Yau cone—or more generally over an asymptotically conical Calabi-Yau 3-fold—can one construct and study further Calabi-Yau monopoles, namely pairs (a, Phi) consisting of a connection a and adjoint Higgs field Phi satisfying F_a wedge Omega_2 = -(1/2) d_a Phi wedge omega^2 and F_a wedge omega^2 = 0, which are the natural asymptotic models for U(1)-invariant G2-instantons on ALC G2-manifolds?

Let (X,ϕ) be an asymptotically locally conical holonomy G2-manifold of the kind highlighted in §4.4(b), namely one that is close to a degenerate Calabi–Yau cone limit and typically has only U(1)-symmetry. Writing the ALC end as p:(1,∞)×Σ→X\K, where π:Σ→Γ is a U(1)-bundle and the end determines a Calabi–Yau cone (1,∞)×Γ, can one construct a G2-instanton A on a principal bundle over X such that on the end there exists a U(1)-invariant connection A∞ = a + mΦ⊗η∞ with p^*F_A asymptotic at infinity to F_A∞, so that the limiting pair (a,Φ) is a Calabi–Yau monopole on the cone, i.e. Fa∧Ω2 = -(1/2) d_aΦ∧ω^2 and Fa∧ω^2 = 0? ([discovery.ucl.ac.uk](https://discovery.ucl.ac.uk/10067480/1/1812.11867v1.pdf))

Let (X,φ) be an asymptotically locally conical G2-manifold in the sense of Section 4.1, with end modeled by a U(1)-bundle π:Σ→Γ and diffeomorphism p:(1,∞)×Σ→X\K, where the base cone C=(1,∞)×Γ is Calabi-Yau and η_∞ is Hermitian-Yang-Mills. For a G2-instanton A on a principal G-bundle over X, with G compact semisimple, whose curvature admits a U(1)-invariant asymptotic model A_∞=a+mΦ⊗η_∞ on the end, in the sense that p^*F_A is asymptotic to F_{A_∞}, develop the local deformation theory of A, make precise its relation to the deformation theory of the induced Calabi-Yau monopole (a,Φ) on the end cone C, and, as suggested in the paper, to Calabi-Yau monopoles on AC Calabi-Yau 3-folds; then determine the image of the resulting asymptotic-limit projection A↦(a,Φ) from the moduli space of such G2-instantons on X to the space of Calabi-Yau monopoles on C. ([discovery.ucl.ac.uk](https://discovery.ucl.ac.uk/10067480/1/1812.11867v1.pdf))

Let P_1 := SU(2)^2 x_(Delta SU(2),1) SU(2) be the homogeneous SU(2)-bundle determined by the trivial isotropy homomorphism across the singular orbit {0} x S^3, and let A be a local SU(2)^2 x U(1)-invariant G2-instanton with gauge group SU(2) on the BGGG G2-holonomy metric on R^4 x S^3, defined near {0} x S^3 and smoothly extending on P_1, so that in the invariant ansatz of Proposition 11 and Lemma 3 its coefficients satisfy f^-(t) = f_2^- t^2 + O(t^4), g^-(t) = g_2^- t^2 + O(t^4), f^+(t) = f_1^+ t + O(t^3), and g^+(t) = g_1^+ t + O(t^3) as t -> 0. Determine, for the remaining unresolved initial-data region 0 < f_1^+ - 1/2 < g_1^+ < f_1^+, exactly which such local solutions extend to global irreducible G2-instantons on all of R^4 x S^3 with bounded curvature and which do not, thereby completing the description of the full moduli space M^{BGGG}_{P_1}; and determine, with the suitable modifications indicated by the paper, how the analogous existence/non-existence picture changes for the other metrics in the Bogoyavlenskaya family.

For the 1-parameter (up to overall scale) Bogoyavlenskaya family of complete SU(2)^2 × U(1)-invariant holonomy-G2 metrics on R^4 × S^3, whose ALC end has circle-size parameter m and which includes the BGGG metric and has the Bryant–Salamon metric as a limit, determine how the G2-instantons known on this family behave as m varies: in the large-circle regime m → ∞, do they limit to G2-instantons for the Bryant–Salamon metric on R^4 × S^3, and in the small-circle regime m → 0, is there a limiting relation between these G2-instantons and Calabi–Yau monopoles on the deformed conifold?

On the BGGG G2-manifold R^4 × S^3, let P1 denote the homogeneous SU(2)-bundle over the singular orbit S^3 = {0} × S^3 corresponding to the trivial homomorphism in P_lambda = SU(2)^2 ×_(Delta SU(2), lambda) SU(2). Consider the nonempty unbounded family from Theorem 7 of irreducible SU(2)^2 × U(1)-invariant SU(2) G2-instantons with bounded curvature that extend smoothly over P1, where near t = 0 their local data satisfy f^+(t) = f1^+ t + O(t^3) and g^+(t) = g1^+ t + O(t^3). Can the resulting noncompact end of M_P1^{BGGG} be compactified by analyzing sequences for which f1^+ tends to +infinity and/or g1^+ tends to +infinity? More precisely, after suitable rescaling transverse to the associative S^3, do such sequences exhibit a Bryant–Salamon-type analogue of Theorem 6—namely bubbling of anti-self-dual instantons together with convergence away from S^3 to a limiting G2-instanton—with possible bubbles related to the ASD instantons on Taub–NUT constructed by Etesi–Hausel? ([discovery.ucl.ac.uk](https://discovery.ucl.ac.uk/10067480/1/1812.11867v1.pdf))

Let V be a Jordan pair over a commutative unital ring k, and for each ideal I of V let pi_I: PE(V) -> PE(V/I) be the canonical homomorphism induced by the quotient V -> V/I. Is every normal subgroup N of PE(V) obtained from a unique ideal I of V by the sandwich condition ker(pi_I) <= N <= pi_I^{-1}(Z(PE(V/I)))? Equivalently, are the normal subgroups of PE(V) exactly those lying between the kernel of the natural quotient map to PE(V/I) and the full preimage of the center of PE(V/I), for a unique ideal I of V?

Let V be a Jordan pair over the same commutative unital base ring as in the paper, and let PE(V) denote its projective elementary group. Is it true, as asked in Conjecture 1.1, that the Loos criteria for perfectness and simplicity extend to this full setting: namely, that PE(V) is perfect if and only if V has no simple factor isomorphic to (F2,F2), (F3,F3), or (H2(F2),H2(F2)); and that PE(V) is simple if and only if V is simple and V is not isomorphic to any of these three exceptional Jordan pairs?

Let V=(V+,V−) be a Jordan pair over the base ring used in the paper, let I=(I+,I−)◁V be an ideal, let can:V→V/I be the canonical quotient morphism, and define the relative projective elementary group by PE(V,I):=ker(PE(can):PE(V)→PE(V/I)). Find an explicit, intrinsic presentation of PE(V,I) by generators and defining relations. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/abs/1901.01313))

Let F be a field, let (R,R_1) be the underlying irreducible 3-graded root system of rank 2, 3, or 4, and let V be a Jordan pair with a fully idempotent division root grading (V_alpha)_{alpha in R_1} over F in the sense of the paper. If the associated Steinberg group St(V,R) is not centrally closed, must it follow that dim_F(V_alpha)=1 for every root alpha in R_1 and that F is one of the exceptional small fields listed in Table (3.2.1) for the corresponding type? ([link.springer.com](https://link.springer.com/chapter/10.1007/978-3-030-63849-8_4))

Let J be a quadratic Jordan division algebra, and let St(J) denote the rank-one Steinberg group associated with J in the sense of the paper. Is St(J) centrally closed for every such J, with the only exceptions the cases J ≅ F_q for q ∈ {2,3,4,9}?

Let V be a Jordan pair with the paper's root-grading hypotheses (in particular, a fully idempotent root grading ℜ by a 3-graded root system (R,R_1)), and let pi: St(V,ℜ) -> PE(V) be the canonical homomorphism of Theorem 2.11(a). Assume that R is irreducible of finite rank and that rank(R) >= 5. Is Ker(pi) contained in the center of St(V,ℜ)?

Let k be a commutative associative unital ring, and let V be a Jordan pair over k equipped with the precise root-grading/idempotent-grading hypotheses assumed in Section 1 of the paper. Does the Steinberg group attached to V admit a van-der-Kallen-style "another presentation" formulated intrinsically in terms of the Jordan-pair structure, so that it can be described in a basis-free, type-independent, non-case-by-case way?

Let S be the unit sphere in R^3, let h in L^2(S), and let alpha, beta be fixed real constants such that alpha - beta(k+1) != 0 for every k in N_0. Denote by U_R(r)h the unique exterior Robin solution of Laplace's equation for r > 1 with boundary condition alpha w + beta partial_r w = h on S and decay w(r,phi,theta) -> 0 as r -> infinity; equivalently, in spherical harmonics, U_R(r) has multipliers r^{-(k+1)}/(alpha - beta(k+1)). Except in the limiting Dirichlet case beta = 0 and Neumann case alpha = 0, the family {U_R(e^t)}_{t >= 0} is not a C_0-semigroup on L^2(S). Is there, nevertheless, a Robin-specific analogue of the semigroup interconnection theorem—namely of the resolvent relation lambda R(lambda; B)f = [P + I - lambda^{-1}R(lambda^{-1}; A)]f, which in the invertible case reduces to lambda R(lambda; A^{-1})f = f - lambda^{-1}R(lambda^{-1}; A)f—that links the boundary-approximation behavior of U_R(r) as r -> 1+ to a naturally associated inverse/ergodic problem in the whole space, and thereby yields Robin counterparts of the Dirichlet/Neumann approximation-versus-ergodic equivalences proved in the paper?

Develop algorithmic procedures for the Painlevé equivalence problem: given an ordinary differential equation with the Painlevé property—especially, in the classical setting, a second-order first-degree equation w'' = F(w,w',z) with F rational in w and w' and locally analytic in z—determine whether the equation can, after the appropriate admissible change of variables (classically a Möbius transformation W(ζ) = (a(z)w + b(z))/(c(z)w + d(z)), ζ = φ(z)), be reduced to one of the canonical Painlevé equations PI–PVI, or in Hamiltonian form to one of the associated Painlevé σ-equations SI–SVI; and, if so, identify the canonical target equation and the transformation.

Can one devise an agreed notation for the Painlevé transcendents—that is, for solutions w(z) of the six Painlevé equations PI–PVI with their standard parameters—that distinguishes the qualitatively different solution families each equation possesses, rather than treating the nonlinear equations as if they had only a few representative solutions; in particular, can such a notation separate the kinds of families illustrated in Section 3 for PII (general transcendental, Ablowitz–Segur, Hastings–McLeod, singular and complex variants, quasi-Ablowitz–Segur, quasi-Hastings–McLeod, special-function, rational, tronquée, and tri-tronquée solutions) despite the absence of natural global coordinates on the full solution space?

Can one develop reliable, easy-to-use numerical software for the Painlevé equations PI–PVI that improves on standard generic ODE solvers such as Runge–Kutta by exploiting their integrable structure—specifically the isomonodromic formulation through the associated Riemann–Hilbert problem and the asymptotic information it provides—to compute solutions w(z) numerically at finite values of z?

Can one develop reliable, easy-to-use numerical software for studying solutions w(z) of the Painlevé equations that explicitly exploits their integrable isomonodromic structure—namely, the associated Riemann–Hilbert problem—by combining asymptotic information extracted from that Riemann–Hilbert formulation with efficient numerical schemes so as to compute the Painlevé transcendents accurately at finite values of z, preferably improving on standard Runge–Kutta-type ODE solvers?

When developing numerical software for the continuous Painlevé equations, should one use an "integrable discretization"—that is, a discrete Painlevé equation which is itself integrable and which tends to the corresponding continuous Painlevé equation in an appropriate continuum limit—rather than relying only on generic ODE discretizations such as standard Runge–Kutta-type methods? ([sigma-journal.com](https://sigma-journal.com/2019/006/sigma19-006.pdf))

For the six Painlevé equations PI–PVI defined in equations (1.1)–(1.6), can one develop a complete classification together with a single unifying framework for the special properties currently known for these equations—namely Hamiltonian representations, exact solutions (rational, algebraic, and classical-special-function solutions), Bäcklund transformations, associated isomonodromy problems interpreted as Lax pairs whose compatibility yields the Painlevé equation, and asymptotic approximations in the complex plane together with the corresponding connection formulae—so as to replace the present fragmentary and non-systematic body of results?

Prove or disprove Conjecture 1 in the precise setting of sections 2.1-2.2 of arXiv:1902.10093: for 10d type II supergravity backgrounds with a globally defined 4d de Sitter factor and a compact 6d internal group manifold, 4d-Lorentz-invariant BPS Op/Dp sources of a single size p >= 3, and in the smeared limit A = 0 with constant internal flux components in the flat basis subject to the orientifold projection, does there exist any solution of the full 10d equations of motion and Bianchi identities with one set N = 1 of parallel sources (equivalently, all sources wrap the same internal directions), or must no such classical de Sitter solution exist?

In the paper's well-defined setting of classical 10d type-II de Sitter compactifications given by the smeared ansatz on a compact 6d group manifold with constant flux coefficients and intersecting Op/Dp sources grouped into sets I = 1,...,N of mutually intersecting but individually parallel sources, must every such de Sitter solution be classically perturbatively unstable, in the 4d effective description, in the sense that the scalar potential at the de Sitter critical point necessarily has a negative Hessian eigenvalue, i.e. a tachyonic scalar direction?

Within the paper's standard ansatz for classical de Sitter solutions of 10d type II supergravity with only Op/Dp sources of a single size p in {4,5,6}—namely a 4d de Sitter spacetime times a compact 6d group manifold, with smeared parallel or intersecting sources and constant NSNS/RR fluxes—does there exist any solution for which the average internal length L satisfies L >> l_s, the string coupling satisfies g_s << 1, the effective source number N_s = sum_I (2^(p-5)N^I_Op - N^I_Dp) is bounded above and positive, and the fluxes are quantized with integer quanta N_q as in Eq. (5.1); or must every such classical de Sitter solution fail at least one of these four conditions?

In the standard setup of Andriot's paper, namely 10-dimensional type II supergravity with only BPS Op-planes/Dp-branes of a single size p and vanishing world-volume gauge-field pullback, preserving 4d Lorentz invariance, and further restricted to the smeared ansatz A=0 with e^phi=g_s, a compact 6-dimensional group manifold M as internal space, constant flux components in the orthonormal basis subject to the orientifold projection, and all sources parallel (equivalently N=1), does there exist any classical de Sitter solution solving the remaining 10d Einstein equation, dilaton equation, flux equations of motion, and flux Bianchi identities? Equivalently, is Conjecture 1 true for this ansatz; and, since known constraints already eliminate the other cases, can one exclude such solutions in the only unresolved cases p=4,5,6?

Within the standard ansatz studied in arXiv:1902.10093—namely smeared classical de Sitter solutions of 10-dimensional type II supergravity with Op/Dp sources of a single fixed size p >= 3, on a 6-dimensional compact group manifold, with fluxes having constant coefficients in a flat basis—must every solution with intersecting sources (that is, with N > 1 sets of parallel Op/Dp sources wrapping different internal directions) be classically perturbatively unstable?

Cannot be refined paper-faithfully from arXiv:1902.10093. Please verify the arXiv identifier: the inspected paper is about open problems on classical de Sitter solutions in string theory, not hyperbolically embedded subgroups or membership problems.

In the ring of symmetric functions in superspace over commuting variables x and anticommuting variables theta (with theta_i^2 = 0), let P_Lambda^(alpha) be the Jack superpolynomial indexed by a superpartition Lambda, and let J_Lambda^(alpha) denote its integral-form normalization used in the paper. Writing its monomial-superfunction expansion as J_Lambda^(alpha) = sum_{Omega <= Lambda} v_{Lambda,Omega}(alpha) m_Omega, where Omega ranges over superpartitions and <= is the paper’s dominance order on superpartitions, is it true that for every Lambda and every Omega <= Lambda one has v_{Lambda,Omega}(alpha) in Z[alpha]?
