([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2107.07073))

Can one generalize to the wild setting, over an algebraically closed field of positive characteristic and allowing non-tame (wildly ramified/stacky) phenomena, the Groechenig-Wyss-Ziegler and Loeser-Wyss results on the Hitchin fibration—namely, the Hausel-Thaddeus topological mirror symmetry statement formulated via μ_n-gerbe-twisted stringy Hodge numbers and its motivic refinement?

Let k be an algebraically closed field of characteristic p > 0, and let a finite group G act faithfully and linearly on V = A^d_k without pseudo-reflections, with p dividing |G|; write X = V/G. In the wild McKay framework, the stringy motive of X is given by the motivic integral M_st(X) = integral over Delta_G of L^(-w) d tau, where Delta_G is the moduli space of G-torsors over the punctured formal disk Spec k((t)), w: Delta_G -> Q is the weight function, L is the Lefschetz motive, and d tau is the motivic measure; equivalently, M_st(X) = M_st([V/G]). Can one formulate and prove precise comparison results relating this wild McKay/motivic-integration formalism for [V/G]—and, more generally, motivic integration over wild Deligne-Mumford stacks—to other existing theories on wild ramification in higher dimensions, especially those arising from the restriction-to-curves viewpoint and from phenomena such as non-liftability of arcs along wildly ramified finite covers?

Within the study of wild ramification considered in the paper—more specifically, in connection with the wild McKay correspondence and motivic integration over wild Deligne-Mumford stacks—can one formulate and prove a Grothendieck-Ogg-Shafarevich-type formula using motivic integration and/or a version of stringy invariant?

Let k be an algebraically closed field of characteristic p>0, let G be a finite group with p dividing |G| acting linearly, faithfully, and without pseudo-reflections on an affine space V= A_k^d, and set X=V/G. Assume that X admits a crepant resolution f:Y→X. What object on the “representation-theoretic” side should replace the bounded derived category of G-equivariant coherent sheaves on V so as to yield a wild derived McKay correspondence with D^b(Coh Y), given that the classical equivalence D^b(Coh Y) ≅ D^b(Coh^G V) cannot hold in the wild case because Coh^G(V) has infinite global dimension? ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2107.07073))

For a global field K, especially a number field, can one formulate and develop a global analogue of the local stringy-motive McKay correspondence (2.6) for quotient varieties attached to finite group actions, in which the geometric counting problem of K-rational points of bounded height on the relevant quotient/Fano-type variety is related to the arithmetic counting problem of Galois extensions of K with bounded discriminant, in a way compatible with the Batyrev-Manin and Malle conjectures, including their predicted exponents and leading constants? ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2107.07073))

In the global-field McKay-correspondence setting of Section 13, especially over number fields, can one prove, in a concrete special case, a case of the Batyrev-Manin conjecture for counting rational points of bounded height on a Fano-type variety from a known case of the Malle conjecture for counting Galois extensions with bounded discriminant, or conversely prove such a special case of the Malle conjecture from a known case of the Batyrev-Manin conjecture, where both counting functions are expected to have asymptotic form c B^a (log B)^{b-1} as the bound tends to infinity?

Fix a number field K and the finite-group/representation data needed to define a tuning module. Can one count Galois extensions L/K of bounded value of a tuning-module-derived global weight—namely, a discriminant-like invariant of geometric origin whose non-Archimedean local factors are governed by the local v-function from the wild McKay correspondence—in place of the usual discriminant?

Let k be an algebraically closed field, let G be a finite group, and let Δ_G denote the moduli space of G-torsors over the punctured formal disk Spec k((t)). Since G-torsors have nontrivial automorphisms, can the corresponding moduli functor be represented by a stack, more precisely by an ind-Deligne-Mumford stack over k, i.e. an inductive limit of Deligne-Mumford stacks of finite type over k, in the general finite-group case?

Fix a finite group G. Let K be a local field of characteristic 0, let k be its residue field, and let W(k) be the ring of Witt vectors. Can one construct, over k rather than over K, the mixed-characteristic analogue of Delta_G, namely a geometric moduli object parametrizing G-torsors over the punctured formal disk attached to K (for example, K = Q_p)?

Let k be an algebraically closed field, and let Δ_G denote the geometric moduli object (possibly stack-like, rather than an honest scheme) parametrizing G-torsors over the punctured formal disk over k. For group schemes G more general than the finite-group case, can one construct Δ_G? In particular, for G = α_p, should Δ_G be realized as an ind-pro limit of finite-dimensional spaces?

On the finite interval [0,1] (the normalization adopted in Sect. 2.2), determine the general form of all one-parameter families of operators {I^alpha}_{alpha>=0} and {D^alpha}_{alpha>=0}, for real orders alpha >= 0, acting on suitable nontrivial linear spaces of functions, such that: (1) every I^alpha and D^alpha is linear; (2) I^{alpha1} o I^{alpha2} = I^{alpha1+alpha2} for all alpha1, alpha2 >= 0; (3) D^alpha o I^alpha = Id on the relevant common domain for every alpha >= 0; (4) the limits D^alpha -> D^0 as alpha -> 0 and D^alpha -> D^1 as alpha -> 1 exist in the operative sense of Sect. 2.1 and define linear maps; (5) D^0 = Id; and (6) D^1 coincides with the first-order derivative d/dx, understood on AC([0,1]) in the weak sense of formula (10). Equivalently, characterize the fractional integrals and derivatives for functions on a finite interval in the sense of desiderata (HL1)-(HL6). ([link.springer.com](https://link.springer.com/content/pdf/10.1007/s11071-021-07158-9.pdf))

After normalizing the finite interval to [0,1], let {I^alpha}_{alpha>=0} be the Riemann-Liouville fractional integrals, with (I^alpha f)(x) = (1/Gamma(alpha)) integral_0^x (x-t)^(alpha-1) f(t) dt for alpha>0 and I^0 = Id. Characterize all one-parameter families of linear operators {D^alpha}_{alpha>=0}—in the paper's main finite-interval setting, chiefly 0 < alpha <= 1 on L_1(0,1) and appropriate subspaces—such that each D^alpha is associated with I^alpha through the 1st Fundamental Theorem of Fractional Calculus, i.e. (D^alpha I^alpha phi)(x) = phi(x) for x in [0,1] on an appropriate nontrivial function space. Equivalently, determine all possible left-inverse families of the Riemann-Liouville fractional integrals on a finite interval, in a way that includes the known n-th level families and hence, in particular, the Riemann-Liouville, Caputo, and Hilfer derivatives.

Determine the general form of all one-parameter families of operators {I^alpha}_{alpha>=0} and {D^alpha}_{alpha>=0}, of real order, acting on suitable linear spaces of functions on a finite interval (equivalently, after the paper's normalization, on [0,1]) that qualify as fractional integrals and fractional derivatives in the sense of Section 2.1; namely, I^alpha and D^alpha are linear, I^{alpha_1} composed with I^{alpha_2} equals I^{alpha_1+alpha_2} for all alpha_1, alpha_2>=0, D^alpha composed with I^alpha equals the identity for all alpha>=0 on an appropriate nontrivial function space, the limits of D^alpha as alpha->0 and alpha->1 exist as linear maps, D^0 is the identity operator, and D^1 is the first-order derivative d/dx.

Can one extend to functions defined on the positive real semi-axis (0,+∞) and on ℝ the finite-interval program of Section 2.4(1)-(3), by characterizing the one-parameter linear families {I^α}_{α≥0} of fractional integrals that satisfy the desiderata HL1-HL6 of Section 2.1, characterizing all one-parameter linear families {D^α}_{α≥0} of fractional derivatives linked to the corresponding integral family through the 1st Fundamental Theorem of fractional calculus D^α∘I^α=Id, and determining the general form of such fractional integrals and derivatives on these two domains? ([link.springer.com](https://link.springer.com/content/pdf/10.1007/s11071-021-07158-9.pdf))

Can one formulate and solve the multidimensional analogue of Open Problems 1-4 from Section 2.4 by, on suitable spaces of scalar-valued functions on R^n, characterizing all one-parameter families {I^alpha}_{alpha >= 0} of fractional integrals that satisfy the desiderata (HL1)-(HL6) of Section 2.1, characterizing all families {D^alpha}_{alpha >= 0} of fractional derivatives that are associated with the appropriate multidimensional analogue of the Riemann-Liouville fractional integrals through the 1st Fundamental Theorem of fractional calculus D^alpha I^alpha = Id, and determining the general form of such multidimensional fractional integrals and derivatives, thereby extending the finite-interval / positive-semi-axis / R one-dimensional theory to functions on R^n?

Let C_{α,β}(0,+∞) := {f : f(t) = t^p f1(t) for t > 0, with α < p < β and f1 ∈ C[0,+∞)}, let C_{-1}(0,+∞) := C_{-1,+∞}(0,+∞), and let (f*g)(t) := ∫_0^t f(t-τ)g(τ) dτ denote the Laplace convolution on (0,+∞). Characterize those kernels κ ∈ C_{-1}(0,+∞) for which there exists an associated kernel k ∈ C_{-1,0}(0,+∞) such that (κ*k)(t) = {1} for all t > 0; equivalently, determine when the pair (κ,k) belongs to the class L1 defined by (κ, k ∈ L1) iff (κ, k ∈ C_{-1,0}(0,+∞)) and ((κ*k)(t) = {1}), and derive a representation for the associated kernel k.

For a fixed integer n ∈ ℕ, characterize all kernels κ ∈ C_{-1}(0,+∞)=C_{-1,+∞}(0,+∞) for which there exists a kernel k ∈ C_{-1,0}(0,+∞) such that, with Laplace convolution on (0,+∞), (κ*k)(t)={1}^{<n>}(t)=h_n(t)=t^{n−1}/(n−1)! for every t>0; equivalently, determine when there exists a pair (κ,k) ∈ ℒ_n in the sense of Definition 2, and derive a representation formula for the associated kernel k. ([link.springer.com](https://link.springer.com/content/pdf/10.1007/s11071-021-07158-9.pdf))

In the Section 2.3 framework of general fractional calculus, for a fixed n∈N and a kernel pair (κ,k)∈L_n with κ∈C_{-1}(0,+∞), k∈C_{-1,0}(0,+∞), and (κ∗k)(t)=h_n(t)=t^{n−1}/(n−1)! on R_+=(0,∞), the general fractional integral and the associated Riemann–Liouville- and Caputo-type general fractional derivatives are defined by one-sided convolution formulas on t>0, namely (I_(κ)f)(t)=∫_0^t κ(t−τ)f(τ)dτ, (D_(k)f)(t)=d^n/dt^n ∫_0^t k(t−τ)f(τ)dτ, and (∗D_(k)f)(t)=D_(k)(f−Σ_{j=0}^{n−1}f^(j)(0)h_{j+1})(t). How should these notions be reformulated for functions defined on a finite interval [a,b] and on the whole real line R, with appropriate kernel classes, convolution structure, endpoint/initial-data terms, and function spaces, so that they extend the paper’s GFI/GFD framework and admit analogues of the fundamental-theorem identities proved on R_+?

Let n be a positive integer and let (κ,k) be a pair of kernels in L_n on R_+=(0,∞), so that κ in C_{-1}(0,∞), k in C_{-1,0}(0,∞), and (κ∗k)(t)=h_n(t)=t^(n-1)/(n-1)! for t>0. For the associated arbitrary-order general fractional integral and general fractional derivatives from Section 2.3, namely (I(κ)f)(t)=∫_0^t κ(t−τ)f(τ)dτ, (D(k)f)(t)=d^n/dt^n ∫_0^t k(t−τ)f(τ)dτ, and (*D(k)f)(t)=D(k)(f−Σ_{j=0}^{n-1} f^(j)(0)h_{j+1})(t), can one develop on other conventional function spaces—specifically L_p spaces and Hölder weighted spaces—a theory analogous to the one proved on the C_{-1}-based spaces in Section 2.3, including the appropriate mapping properties and counterparts of the first and second fundamental theorems for these operators?

Let n be a natural number, and let (κ,k) belong to L_n in the sense that κ in C_{-1}(0,∞), k in C_{-1,0}(0,∞), and (κ * k)(t) = h_n(t) = t^(n-1)/(n-1)! for t > 0, where C_{α,β}(0,∞) = {f : f(t) = t^p f_1(t), α < p < β, f_1 in C[0,∞)}. Define the associated general fractional integral and the arbitrary-order general fractional derivatives by I_(κ)f(t) = ∫_0^t κ(t-τ)f(τ)dτ, D_(k)f(t) = d^n/dt^n ∫_0^t k(t-τ)f(τ)dτ, and *_D_(k)f(t) = D_(k)(f - Σ_{j=0}^{n-1} f^(j)(0)h_{j+1})(t), with h_{j+1}(t) = t^j/j!. Within this Sonine-kernel framework, how can one formulate and study time-fractional differential equations on t > 0 with these GFDs of arbitrary order so that they can model, for instance, processes intermediate between diffusion and wave propagation?

For the non-classical O(N)-work, O(1)-memory algorithms of Section 3.1 for Caputo initial value problems ^{C}D_{a+}^α y(t)=f(t,y(t)), y^{(k)}(a)=y_0^{(k)} for k=0,1,...,⌈α⌉−1, that evaluate the operator through the infinite-state representation ^{C}D_{a+}^α y(t)=∫_0^∞ φ(w,t) dw with ∂_t φ(w,t)=h_1(w)φ(w,t)+h_2(w)y^{(⌈α⌉)}(t), φ(w,0)=0, h_1,h_2:(0,∞)→R, can one give a thorough non-heuristic numerical analysis by designing quadrature formulas for (56a) from the analytic properties of the integrand, analyzing the coupled effect of the quadrature nodes and the ODE solver used for (56b), determining how the number and location of nodes, the quadrature weights, the solver choice, and the ODE step size control the total error, and proving error bounds whose constants have explicit dependence on α and in particular remain uniform for α∈(0,1) rather than blowing up as α→0 or α→1?

For spectral or spectral-element Petrov–Galerkin methods for Caputo-type fractional ordinary differential equations on a finite interval, can one construct equation-independent families of trial functions and test functions—rather than families obtained anew from Sturm–Liouville eigenproblems tailored to each given differential equation—that are usable for a broad class of such problems, still guarantee rapid convergence of the approximate solutions to the exact solution, possibly improve the convergence achieved by the currently described construction, and admit convergence/error estimates in the stronger L_∞ norm instead of only in L_2? ([link.springer.com](https://link.springer.com/content/pdf/10.1007/s11071-021-07158-9.pdf))

For the scalar terminal value problem ^C D_{a+}^{alpha} y(t) = f(t,y(t)) on [a, a+T], with 0 < alpha < 1, T > 0, b in (a, a+T], y:[a, a+T] -> R, and y(b) = y* in R, where the genuinely new numerical task is the first-stage recovery of the unknown initial value y(a) from the restriction to [a,b], which algorithm for updating y(a) inside a shooting method gives the best balance of accuracy and computational effort, and how does such a shooting approach compare with direct discretizations of the associated weakly singular Fredholm equation by collocation, Nystrom, or Galerkin methods, including spectral and spectral-element variants whose trial/test bases use generalized polynomials with noninteger exponents chosen to match the t -> a asymptotics and derivative singularities of the exact solution, in terms of convergence behavior and computational cost?

In the paper's applications framework for fractional calculus, can one formulate a general classification of nonlocal phenomena—most explicitly for nonlocality in time, distinguishing memory, distributed lag (time delay), distributed scaling (dilatation/dilation), and related effects, while treating space-nonlocality as a separate direction—and determine, at the level of classes of operator kernels rather than isolated examples, which fractional integrals, derivatives, or differences correspond to each class of phenomenon, with the benchmark examples that Riemann-Liouville/Caputo operators model memory, Hadamard-type/Erdelyi-Kober operators model scaling and dilation, and Laplace-convolution operators with normalized or probability-density-type kernels model distributed lag?

Can one establish, for the exact fractional difference operators of every non-integer order α > 0 arising in lattice fractional calculus/exact discretization, the discrete analogues of the 1st and 2nd Fundamental Theorems of fractional calculus on suitable spaces of lattice functions; that is, the appropriate left- and right-inverse relations between those exact fractional differences and the associated exact fractional summation/integration operators, with any necessary boundary or initial correction terms stated explicitly?

For the fractional operators with distributed lag discussed in Section 4.2—namely Laplace-convolution operators on R_+ = (0,infinity) whose kernels are probability density functions and that are intended to model the simultaneous presence of memory and distributed lag in economics—can one prove general analogues of the first and second fundamental theorems of fractional calculus, in the sense made precise in Section 2.3? More specifically, determine natural hypotheses on the kernel pair (kappa,k) and on the corresponding function spaces on R_+ under which the associated general fractional integral I_(kappa) and the Riemann-Liouville- and/or Caputo-type general fractional derivatives D_(k) and *D_(k) satisfy left-inverse identities D_(k) I_(kappa) f = f and/or *D_(k) I_(kappa) f = f, together with second-fundamental-theorem identities of the form I_(kappa) *D_(k) f = f - sum_{j=0}^{n-1} f^(j)(0) h_(j+1) (and, where appropriate, I_(kappa) D_(k) f = f), for this distributed-lag class; in particular, can this be carried out for the gamma-distribution kernel and related kernels on the positive semi-axis? ([d-nb.info](https://d-nb.info/1258859653/34))

Within the fractional-calculus approach to open quantum systems, and taking the Lindblad equations as the most general explicit Markovian evolution equations for quantum states and observables, construct a consistent non-Markovian generalization for quantum systems with memory (interpreted as nonlocality in time), and extend this theory to include time-dependent parameters, relativistic quantum systems with memory, a path-integral formulation for open quantum systems, uncertainty relations for open quantum systems, and pure stationary states of open quantum systems.

How can one construct a mathematically consistent fractional-calculus formulation of (i) quantum mechanics with nonlocality in space and (ii) quantum field theory with nonlocality in space-time by starting from lattice models with long-range interactions and passing to continuum limits described by fractional differential equations, specifically in the lattice-fractional-calculus / exact-fractional-differences framework where the fundamental theorems of fractional calculus for non-integer-order exact differences are still to be established?

In nonlinear fractional dynamics, identify and characterize the fundamentally new types of self-organization—understood as the formation of ordered spatial or temporal structures without external influences—expected in processes with nonlocality in time and memory, especially in cases where the emergence or change of memory, with all other parameters unchanged, creates a hierarchy of relaxation times and thereby qualitatively changes the behavior of the system, so that self-organization is generated solely by memory.

Let {X_i}_{i\in I} be an arbitrary family of T0 spaces, each equipped with its specialization order \leq_i, and for x\in X_i write \uparrow_i x=\{y\in X_i:x\leq_i y\}. Recall that a T0 space X is called a strong d-space if, for every subset D\subseteq X directed with respect to the specialization order on X, every x\in X, and every open set U\subseteq X, the implication
\[
\bigcap_{d\in D}(\uparrow d\cap \uparrow x)\subseteq U\implies (\exists d\in D)\, (\uparrow d\cap \uparrow x\subseteq U)
\]
holds. If every X_i is a strong d-space, must the product space \prod_{i\in I} X_i, endowed with the product topology, also be a strong d-space?

For every T0 topological space X, does there exist a strong d-space X^sd and a continuous map eta_X:X->X^sd such that for every strong d-space Y and every continuous map f:X->Y, there is a unique continuous map f_bar:X^sd->Y with f=f_bar∘eta_X? Equivalently, is the full subcategory S-Top_d of all strong d-spaces reflective in Top_0, the category of T0 spaces and continuous maps?

Let K be a full subcategory of Top_0, with continuous maps as morphisms, containing Sob and closed under homeomorphisms. For each T_0 space X, let K^d(X) be the family of K-determined subsets of X, let K^d_c(X) be the closed members of K^d(X), and let P_H(K^d_c(X)) denote K^d_c(X) endowed with the lower Vietoris topology. Suppose K is adequate in the sense that P_H(K^d_c(X)) is a K-space for every T_0 space X. Is it true that K is adequate and closed under homeomorphisms if and only if there exists an irreducible subset system H:Top_0->Set such that the K-spaces are exactly the H-sober spaces, i.e. K = H-Sob?

Let H: Top0 → Set be an R-subset system, with no a priori assumption that H has property M, and let {X_i}_{i∈I} be an arbitrary family of T0 spaces such that each X_i is super H-sober, i.e. the Smyth power space P_S(X_i) is H-sober. Must the product space ∏_{i∈I} X_i, equipped with the product topology, also be super H-sober?

Let H: Top0 -> Set be an R-subset system, i.e. H(Z) is a family of irreducible subsets of each T0 space Z. For a T0 space X and a super H-sober space Y (meaning that the Smyth power space PS(Y) is H-sober), let Top0(X,Y) denote the set of all continuous maps f: X -> Y, endowed with the topology of pointwise convergence, equivalently the subspace topology inherited from the product Y^X. Must Top0(X,Y) be super H-sober?

Let H: Top0→Set be an irreducible subset system (equivalently, an R-subset system), and recall that a T0 space Z is called super H-sober when its Smyth power space P_S(Z) is H-sober. If X is a super H-sober space, Y is a T0 space, and f,g:X→Y are continuous maps, must the equalizer E(f,g):={x∈X : f(x)=g(x)}, endowed with the subspace topology from X, also be super H-sober?

Let H: Top0 -> Set be an irreducible subset system (R-subset system), i.e. a covariant functor such that for every T0 space X one has S(X) subseteq H(X) subseteq Irr(X), and for every continuous map f: X -> Y one has H(f)(A) = f(A). For a T0 space X, call X super H-sober if its Smyth power space P_S(X) is H-sober, and let SH-Sob denote the full subcategory of Top0 consisting of all super H-sober spaces. Is SH-Sob reflective in Top0; equivalently, does every T0 space X admit an SH-Sob-reflection, that is, a super H-sobrification of X?

Let 𝓗 be the poset of all irreducible subset systems (R-subset systems) H: Top_0 -> Set, ordered by H_1 <= H_2 iff H_1(X) ⊆ H_2(X) for every T_0 space X. For such an H and a T_0 space X, define H^R(X) to be the family of H-Rudin sets of X, where A ⊆ X is H-Rudin if cl_X(A) belongs to m(K) for some K in H(P_S(X)); here P_S(X) is the Smyth power space, M(K) = {C in Γ(X) : C ∩ K != empty for all K in K}, and m(K) is the set of minimal members of M(K). Assume H has property M, namely that for every T_0 space X, every K in H(P_S(X)), and every A in M(K), the family {upward(K ∩ A) : K in K} lies in H(P_S(X)). Must the operator R: 𝓗 -> 𝓗, defined by R(H)=H^R, be a closure operator; that is, must it be monotone, expansive, and idempotent? ([sciencedirect.com](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0166864120304922?utm_source=openai))

Let X and Y be topological spaces. A nonempty subset F of a topological space is called irreducible if, whenever F is contained in the union of two closed sets C1 and C2, then F is contained in C1 or in C2. A topological space Z is called hyper-sober if for every irreducible subset F of Z there exists a unique point z in F such that F is contained in the closure of {z}. If X and Y are hyper-sober, must the product space X × Y, endowed with the product topology, also be hyper-sober?

In the paper's default setting of countably infinite homogeneous relational structures S, for which such S does every finite structure A that embeds into S (equivalently, A∈Age(S)) have a finite big Ramsey degree T(A), meaning the least positive integer T(A) such that for every finite coloring of the set of copies of A in S, there exists a subcopy S'⊆S with S'≅S in which at most T(A) colors occur on copies of A? ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2110.00655.pdf))

Let K be a countably infinite homogeneous relational structure in a finite relational language, and let Age(K) be its age. For each finite A in Age(K), let T(A) denote the least positive integer such that every finite coloring of the set of copies of A in K has a subcopy K' isomorphic to K in which at most T(A) colors appear on the copies of A. Does K have finite big Ramsey degrees, in the sense that such a T(A) exists for every finite A (equivalently, can one find upper bounds guaranteeing existence of these degrees)? If K does have finite big Ramsey degrees, is there a characterization of the exact values T(A) via canonical partitions of the copies of A in K—where a canonical partition means one whose pieces are forced to be monochromatic on some subcopy K' isomorphic to K under every finite coloring and each piece persists in every such subcopy—and, if so, can the exact degrees be calculated or algorithmically determined from that characterization?

Let K be the Fraïssé limit of an SAP Fraïssé class of finite structures in a finite relational language. For which such classes does K have finite big Ramsey degrees, in the sense that for every finite substructure A of K there is a finite number T(A) such that every finite coloring of the copies of A in K has an isomorphic subcopy K' ≅ K on which at most T(A) colors appear? In particular, if the class has finitely many relation symbols and a finite set of forbidden substructures, must K have finite big Ramsey degrees; and, under those same hypotheses, if every relation symbol has arity at most two, do big Ramsey degrees always exist? Is there a general condition on SAP Fraïssé classes characterizing exactly those whose Fraïssé limits have finite big Ramsey degrees?

Can one replace the existing forcing-based proofs for the big Ramsey results of the countable homogeneous free-amalgamation structures treated in Section 5.2 by proofs that are entirely combinatorial; in particular, can this be done for each Henson graph G_k (the countable homogeneous k-clique-free graph) with k >= 4, and for the other similar Fraisse limits whose ages have the free amalgamation property (FAP) and are currently handled by forcing? (The case G_3 is excluded, since a combinatorial proof is already known.)

Let K be a countably infinite homogeneous relational structure. Assume that K has finite big Ramsey degrees, meaning that for every finite A in Age(K), the big Ramsey degree T(A) exists. Must K carry a big Ramsey structure, namely a finite expansion K* of K such that every finite substructure of K* has big Ramsey degree 1 and the associated unavoidable colorings (canonical partitions) cohere under embeddings A into B in Age(K)? Moreover, is there an exact correspondence, analogous to the Kechris-Pestov-Todorcevic correspondence, between the existence of such big Ramsey structures for K and the topological dynamics of Aut(K)?

Fix a countably infinite homogeneous relational structure K, and represent the family of its copies by a subspace X_K ⊆ [ω]^ω whose elements code copies of K. Can one develop an infinite-dimensional Ramsey theory for X_K extending the Galvin–Prikry theorem and Ellentuck’s theorem—namely, for Borel subsets of X_K, and optimally for all subsets of X_K having the property of Baire in a suitable finer topology, can one pass to a subcopy K' ≅ K so that the induced subspace of codes for copies of K inside K' is either contained in or disjoint from the given set—in a form strong enough to recover the canonical partitions, and hence the exact big Ramsey degrees, of finite substructures A ∈ Age(K)?

For each positive integer n, consider a single-channel slotted multiple-access system with n indistinguishable users who all know n and who independently implement the same decentralized randomized algorithm, receiving after each slot common perfect feedback F[t] in {0,1,...,n} equal to the exact number of transmitters on that slot; a success occurs iff F[t]=1. Let z_n^* denote the infimum expected time to the first success over all such n-user algorithms. Let z_1=1, z_2=2, and for n>=3 let z_n be the value of the paper's recursively defined divide-and-conquer policy: on slot 1 each user transmits independently with probability p in (0,1); if F[1] is 0 or n, restart; if F[1]=1, stop; and if F[1]=i in {2,...,n-1}, partition the users into the transmitting group of size i and the silent group of size n-i, discard the group with larger continuation value, and recurse on the other group, so that z_n = inf over p in (0,1) of (1 + sum from i=2 to n-1 of min{z_i,z_{n-i}} C(n,i) p^i (1-p)^(n-i)) divided by (1 - p^n - (1-p)^n). Is it true that z_n^* = z_n for every positive integer n?

For a fixed positive integer n, consider the infinite-horizon decentralized slotted multiple-access problem with n initially indistinguishable users, common knowledge of n, and no central coordinator, in which each user independently applies the same causal randomized algorithm based only on the common slot-by-slot feedback history, and a success occurs on slot t if and only if exactly one user transmits. Let Z_n denote the time of the first success. The paper studies this problem under full error-free feedback F[t] in {0,1,...,n}, where F[t] is the exact number of transmitters on slot t. If this exact transmitter-count feedback is replaced by a specified weaker common feedback signal (that is, a coarsening of F[t]), which decentralized algorithms minimize E[Z_n]?

Under the paper’s decentralized channel-capture model—slotted time; a known number of unlabeled/indistinguishable users; every user independently running the same randomized algorithm; and common end-of-slot feedback that reports, for each orthogonal channel, the exact number of transmitters—what is the optimal policy in the multi-channel cases treated in the arXiv version (notably the 2-user and 3-user cases) for minimizing the expected time until the first singleton transmission on any channel? In particular, if on each slot a user may transmit on any subset of the m channels, is it optimal to choose channels independently channel-by-channel by applying the single-channel capture rule separately on each channel, or can a user strictly reduce the expected first-success time by correlating its simultaneous channel choices across channels?

Let γ ⊂ R^2 be a closed smooth strictly convex curve bounding a domain Ω, and let d > 0. Form the surface homeomorphic to a sphere by gluing a cylinder of height d and base γ to two copies of Ω. Let s be the arc-length coordinate on γ, let A be the associated billiard phase cylinder with coordinates (s, α), and let T:A → A be the first-return map of the geodesic flow; equivalently, if T1(s, α) = (s1, α1) is the usual billiard map in Ω, then T is given by T(s, α) = (s1 + d cot α1, α1). Are there invariant curves of T? In particular, are there KAM invariant curves near the boundary ∂A of the phase cylinder? ([armj.math.stonybrook.edu](https://armj.math.stonybrook.edu/pdf-Springer-final/022-0198.pdf))

Fix d > 0. Let γ ⊂ R^2 be a closed smooth strictly convex curve bounding a domain Ω, and let A be the phase cylinder with coordinates (s, α), where s is the arc-length coordinate on γ. If T1(s, α) = (s1, α1) is the usual billiard map for Ω, define the symplectic map T : A → A by T(s, α) = (s1 + d cot α1, α1), equivalently T = T2 ∘ T1 with T2(s, α1) = (s + d cot α1, α1). For which curves γ, other than circles, is T an integrable map?

Let gamma be a closed smooth strictly convex plane curve bounding a domain Omega, and let d>0. Form the sphere-like surface obtained by gluing a cylinder of height d with base gamma between two copies of Omega. Let A be the usual billiard phase cylinder with Birkhoff coordinates (s, alpha), and let T1(s, alpha)=(s1, alpha1) be the ordinary billiard map in Omega. Define the associated map T:A->A by T(s, alpha)=(s1 + d cot(alpha1), alpha1), equivalently T=T2 o T1 with T2(s, alpha)=(s + d cot(alpha), alpha). Does there exist a choice of gamma and d for which this billiard-cylinder symplectic map T is ergodic with respect to its natural invariant symplectic measure on A?

Does there exist a smooth closed strictly convex curve γ ⊂ R^2, other than an ellipse, such that the outer billiard map T acting in the vicinity of γ—defined by the rule that for each exterior point A, the segment [A, T(A)] is tangent to γ at its midpoint—is integrable in the usual outer-billiard invariant-curve sense?

Classify the Gutkin billiards on the standard 2-sphere S^2 and on the hyperbolic plane H^2: that is, describe all pairs (gamma, delta), where gamma is a smooth closed strictly convex curve, not a geodesic circle, and delta is in (0, pi/2), such that for the geodesic Birkhoff billiard inside gamma, the set of incoming oriented geodesics meeting gamma at the constant angle delta is an invariant curve of the billiard map.

Let S ⊂ R^d, with d ≥ 3, be a closed smooth strictly convex hypersurface bounding a billiard domain, and let T be the Birkhoff billiard map on its phase space A of oriented lines in R^d that meet S transversally at two points. Does there exist a non-ellipsoidal hypersurface S for which T preserves a smooth hypersurface Σ ⊂ A? If so, what geometric and dynamical properties can such invariant hypersurfaces Σ have?

Let S ⊂ R^d, with d >= 3, be a closed smooth strictly convex hypersurface, and let T be the Birkhoff billiard map on the billiard phase space A of oriented lines in R^d that meet S transversally at two points. In dimension 2, Lazutkin found large families of convex caustics near the boundary, whereas for d >= 3 the paper notes that caustics may exist only for ellipsoids. Does there exist a billiard table S other than an ellipsoid for which T leaves invariant a smooth hypersurface Sigma ⊂ A? If such an S exists, what geometric and dynamical properties do these T-invariant smooth hypersurfaces Sigma have?

Let γ ⊂ R^2 be the boundary of a smooth convex planar billiard table, and assume that γ is symmetric with respect to a line l. For the usual Birkhoff billiard in the domain bounded by γ, let C be a convex caustic, meaning that every billiard trajectory tangent to C remains tangent to C after each reflection. Must C itself be symmetric with respect to l, or does there exist a counterexample, namely a line-symmetric smooth convex planar billiard table admitting a convex caustic that is not l-symmetric? As noted in the paper, any such non-symmetric caustic, if it exists, would have to correspond to an invariant curve of rational rotation number.

Does there exist a projective billiard in the Euclidean plane—namely, a bounded domain Ω ⊂ R^2 with (piecewise) smooth boundary ∂Ω endowed with a smooth transverse line field L, whose reflection law sends an oriented line ℓ hitting ∂Ω at p to the oppositely oriented line ℓ' through p such that ℓ, ℓ', L(p), and T_p∂Ω form a harmonic quadruple—whose associated billiard map has an open set of k-periodic points for some odd integer k ≥ 5?

Let Ω ⊂ R² be a bounded planar domain whose (piecewise) smooth boundary ∂Ω is endowed with a smooth transverse line field L, and let the projective billiard reflection law be defined by the requirement that at each impact point p ∈ ∂Ω the incoming line ℓ, the reflected line ℓ′, the transverse line L(p), and the tangent line T_p∂Ω form a harmonic quadruple. Given an integer k ≥ 4, are there, within a prescribed class of boundary smoothness (for example polygonal, piecewise-algebraic, or analytic), any examples of k-reflective projective billiards other than the known polygonal ones, where “k-reflective” is understood in the paper’s sense that the associated billiard map has an open set of periodic points? ([armj.math.stonybrook.edu](https://armj.math.stonybrook.edu/pdf-Springer-final/022-0198.pdf))

Let Omega ⊂ R^2 be a bounded strictly convex domain with smooth boundary, and consider the Birkhoff billiard in Omega. Assume there exist two nested closed caustics C1 ⊂ int(C2) ⊂ Omega, where a caustic means a closed curve such that every billiard trajectory tangent to it remains tangent after each reflection, and assume moreover that C1 is itself a caustic for the billiard in the domain bounded by C2. Must the boundary of Omega be an ellipse?

Let γ ⊂ R^n be a closed strictly convex hypersurface, and let Π be the phase cylinder for the billiard in the domain bounded by γ, i.e. the open subset of the space of oriented lines in R^n consisting of those lines that intersect γ transversally at two points, equipped with its standard symplectic structure. Fix ε > 0 and k in N. Is every C^∞-smooth Hamiltonian symplectomorphism Φ: Π -> Π a C^∞ limit of finite compositions of reflections from γ and from hypersurfaces that are ε-close to γ in the C^k topology, with no inverses of reflections allowed? ([armj.math.stonybrook.edu](https://armj.math.stonybrook.edu/pdf-Springer-final/022-0198.pdf))

Let n ≥ 1, and let Σ1, ..., Σm be C^∞-smooth germs of hypersurfaces in R^{n+1}. For each Σj, let T_{Σj} denote the corresponding local billiard-reflection map acting on oriented lines transverse to Σj (reflection in the tangent hyperplane at the intersection point, with the usual billiard reorientation), and suppose that the finite nonempty composition T_{Σm} ∘ ... ∘ T_{Σ1} is well-defined on a nonempty open set of oriented lines. Is it true that such a composition can never coincide with the identity map on that open set?

Let C be a plane curve in R^2, and fix the square lattice epsilon Z^2. Consider a one-parameter translation experiment for C with scalar parameter lambda: whenever the translated curve meets a lattice point of epsilon Z^2, a click is recorded, and one retains only the resulting unlabeled distribution of click parameters lambda; by the paper's periodicity remark, this distribution may be viewed modulo epsilon, i.e. on lambda in [0, epsilon]. Does this click distribution determine the shape of C, up to the natural rigid-motion ambiguity, for every epsilon > 0 (perhaps already for sufficiently small epsilon)? If not in general, does the collection of such click distributions for C together with every rotation of C determine the shape of C?

Let C ⊂ R^2 be a curve, let ε > 0, and fix an ε-sized square lattice (say εZ^2). Under a fixed one-parameter translation λ ↦ C_λ of C, record every parameter value λ for which C_λ passes through a lattice point, so that one obtains an indistinguishable point cloud of 'click times' on the λ-line (equivalently on λ ∈ [0, ε], since the cloud is ε-periodic). Is there a "Fourier transform" or analogous procedure that acts on this cloud of clicks and extracts the curvature-induced patterns in its distribution, in the sense suggested by the paper's observation that such patterns encode curvature information, for example near points of very rational slope?

In Mark Levi's lattice-click model, let C ⊂ R^2 be a curve and fix an ε-sized square lattice. As C moves through the given one-parameter family of translates indexed by λ, record the λ-values for which the translated curve contains a lattice point; equivalently, study the resulting cloud of clicks, viewed modulo its natural period ε (so it suffices to consider λ ∈ [0, ε]). Analyze this click set/distribution explicitly in the three special cases where C is a line segment, a polygon, or a circle.

Let g_t : R^2 -> R^2 be a Lebesgue-measure-preserving flow (t in R) or cascade (t in Z), satisfying g_{t+s} = g_t o g_s and g_0 = id. Define the trapped set
T_g = {x in R^2 : {g_t x : t >= 0} is bounded, while {g_t x : t <= 0} is unbounded}.
What is the sharp value of sup_g dim_H(T_g)? More specifically, determine how this supremum depends on the regularity of g: the paper notes that in the merely measurable category there is a cascade with dim_H(T_g) = 2, whereas if g is C^m in x (or in both x and t), one should determine the optimal number d(m) in [1,2] such that sup_g dim_H(T_g) = d(m).

In the planar Newtonian-aerodynamics model, let B be a solid body in R^2, i.e. a compact set with piecewise smooth boundary and uniformly distributed mass, of total mass m > 0. Outside B there is a uniform medium of initially resting point particles, normalized so that the total mass of particles in any exterior domain D equals area(D). When a particle hits a regular boundary point x of B, it is reflected elastically according to the usual billiard law in the inertial frame in which x is instantaneously at rest. If at time t = 0 the body begins a prescribed translational and/or rotational motion, describe the subsequent motion of B for all t >= 0 when B has a simple nontrivial shape such as an ellipse, a triangle, or the rod B = [-1,1] x {0}, excluding the disc. In particular, if the rod, or more generally a centrally symmetric body such as an ellipse or square, starts in pure rotation about its center with no translation, is the total number of turns finite or infinite, does the angular velocity tend to 0 as t -> +infinity, and what is its asymptotic behavior? ([armj.math.stonybrook.edu](https://armj.math.stonybrook.edu/pdf-Springer-final/022-0198.pdf))

In the two-dimensional Newtonian-aerodynamics setup of Plakhov's Problem 2, a body B moves in a uniform medium of point particles initially at rest in R^2 \ B, with the property that the total mass of particles contained in any domain D ⊂ R^2 \ B equals area(D); when a particle hits a regular boundary point of B, it is reflected elastically in the inertial frame in which that boundary point is instantaneously at rest. For the specific shape B = [-1,1] × {0}, assume that at time t = 0 the rod begins a pure rotation about its center, with no translational motion. Is the total number of revolutions of the rod for t ≥ 0 finite or infinite? If it is infinite, does its rotational (angular) velocity ω(t) tend to 0 as t -> +infinity, and what is the asymptotic behavior of ω(t) as t -> +infinity?

In the planar Newtonian-aerodynamics model of Plakhov's Problem 2, let B be a simple non-disc centrally symmetric solid body in R^2 (for example, an ellipse or a square), with piecewise smooth boundary, uniformly distributed mass m > 0, moving in a uniform rarefied medium of point particles initially at rest, normalized so that the total mass of particles in any domain D contained in R^2 \ B equals area(D); assume that particles reflect elastically from the boundary, interpreted in the inertial frame in which the impact point of the boundary is instantaneously at rest. Suppose that at t = 0 the body starts a pure rotation about its center, with zero translation and nonzero angular velocity omega(0). Is the total number of turns made by B for t >= 0 finite or infinite? If it is infinite, does omega(t) tend to 0 as t tends to +infinity? In either case, determine the asymptotic behavior of omega(t) as t tends to +infinity.

In the framework of Newtonian aerodynamics, formulate the coupled evolution equations for a body moving freely in R^n, with n >= 1, through a rarefied medium of infinitesimal particles interacting with the body by elastic reflection, and prove an existence-and-uniqueness theorem for this dynamics. In particular, for n = 1, formulate the evolution of the state (mu_t, X(t), P(t)), where mu_t is a measure on R^2_(x,v) describing the particle distribution at time t, X(t) is the position of a massive point of mass 1, and P(t)=X'(t) is its velocity, and prove existence and uniqueness for that evolution.

Let L be the 2n - 2 dimensional space of oriented lines in R^n, equipped with its natural symplectic structure, and regard a local family of light rays as a local submanifold of L. The paper notes that mirror reflections can trap a parallel beam and, more generally, any local normal family of rays (that is, rays orthogonal to a hypersurface, hence a Lagrangian family in L), while in R^2 Poincare recurrence rules out trapping a 2-parameter family. What is the maximal possible dimension k of a local family of rays in R^n that can be trapped by mirror reflections?

Does there exist, in Euclidean 3-space, a mirror trap for geometric optics that traps every ray in some local 2-parameter family of oriented rays under the usual law of specular reflection, where the family is non-normal—that is, it is not the family of rays orthogonal to a hypersurface?

Let gamma ⊂ R^2 be a planar oval, meaning a smooth closed strictly convex curve. For any choice of two directions d1 and d2, define a map F_{d1,d2}: gamma -> gamma as follows: starting from x ∈ gamma, follow the line through x in direction d1 to its other intersection point with gamma, then from that point follow the line in direction d2 to its other intersection point with gamma; call the final point F_{d1,d2}(x). If for every pair of directions d1,d2 the circle map F_{d1,d2} is topologically conjugate to a rotation of S^1, must gamma be an ellipse?

Let γ be a smooth closed strictly convex curve in the plane. For each point P not on γ, define the involution f_P: γ → γ by letting f_P(x) be the second intersection of γ with the line Px, and for two such points set F_{P,Q} = f_P ∘ f_Q. Assume that for every pair of points P and Q such that either (i) P and Q both lie outside γ and the line PQ intersects γ, or (ii) P and Q both lie inside γ, the map F_{P,Q}: γ → γ is C^∞-conjugate to a Möbius transformation of RP^1. Must γ be an ellipse?

Describe all convex planar polygons P for which the polygonal symplectic billiard map T_P on its phase space of oriented chords of P (excluding the chords for which the map is undefined, such as those with head at a vertex or with endpoints on parallel sides) is fully periodic; that is, every orbit of T_P is periodic.

For a planar polygon P, consider its polygonal symplectic billiard map on oriented chords (the polygonal analogue of the symplectic reflection law in Fig. 7). Must this dynamical system always admit at least one periodic orbit?

For the planar symplectic billiard map on oriented chords of the standard stadium (the convex planar domain bounded by two parallel line segments joined by semicircular arcs), where an oriented chord x y is followed by y z whenever the tangent line to the boundary at y is parallel to x z, does this map exhibit chaotic dynamics? ([armj.math.stonybrook.edu](https://armj.math.stonybrook.edu/pdf-Springer-final/022-0198.pdf))

Let γ be an ellipse in the Euclidean plane, regarded as an ideal mirror, and let p be a point source inside γ in general position. For each integer n >= 1, let C_n be the envelope of the light rays emanating from p after n specular reflections off γ; this envelope is the nth caustic by reflection. Is it true that every generic caustic C_n has exactly four cusps?

Let γ ⊂ R^2 be an oval, i.e. a smooth closed strictly convex plane curve, and let p be a point light source in the interior of γ in general position. For each integer n ≥ 1, let Γ_n be the n-th caustic by reflection, defined as the envelope of the rays issuing from p after n reflections off γ. If every such caustic Γ_n has exactly four cusps, must γ be an ellipse?

Let γ be a planar oval, i.e. a smooth closed strictly convex curve, and let T be the outer billiard map about γ, defined so that for each point A outside γ the segment [A,T(A)] is tangent to γ at its midpoint. Consider the area spectrum of this outer billiard, namely the set of areas of the polygons formed by periodic T-trajectories, equivalently the circumscribed polygons of extremal area. Is this area spectrum related to the spectrum of some differential operator, analogously to the fact that the length spectrum of the ordinary billiard in the domain bounded by γ is related, via the Poisson summation formula, to the spectrum of the Dirichlet Laplacian on that domain?

Let X be a compact subset of R^d, let k : X x X -> R be a positive-definite kernel with respect to a finite Borel measure, let H_k be the associated RKHS, and fix lambda > 0. Suppose f in H_k satisfies ||f||_{H_k} <= B, and an online algorithm chooses x_1, x_2, ... adaptively in the sense that x_i is measurable with respect to the past, then observes y_i = f(x_i) + epsilon_i, where the noise variables are i.i.d. and R-sub-Gaussian: E[exp(eta epsilon_i)] <= exp(eta^2 R^2/2) for all eta in R. For the zero-mean GP surrogate with kernel k and regularization lambda, define y_n = (y_1, ..., y_n)^T, k_n(x) = (k(x,x_1), ..., k(x,x_n))^T, K_n = [k(x_i,x_j)]_{i,j=1}^n, mu_n(x) = k_n(x)^T (lambda^2 I_n + K_n)^(-1) y_n, and sigma_n^2(x) = k(x,x) - k_n(x)^T (lambda^2 I_n + K_n)^(-1) k_n(x). What is the smallest asymptotic growth rate, as n increases, of a factor rho_n(delta) such that for every adaptive online design and every delta in (0,1), one has P(for all x in X, |f(x) - mu_n(x)| <= rho_n(delta) sigma_n(x)) >= 1 - delta? In particular, can one improve the current online bound from Theorem 2, rho_n(delta) = B + (R/lambda) sqrt(2(gamma_{n-1} + 1 + log(1/delta))), by removing an O~(sqrt(gamma_n)) factor, where gamma_n := sup_{x_1,...,x_n in X} log det(lambda^2 I_n + K_n), and perhaps reduce the width to O~(d log n)?

Let X⊂R^d be compact, let k:X×X→R be a positive definite kernel with RKHS H_k, and suppose f∈H_k satisfies ||f||_{H_k}≤B. In the online kernelized bandit setting, observations are y_i=f(x_i)+ε_i, where the ε_i are i.i.d. R-sub-Gaussian and each x_{i+1} is chosen adaptively from the past. Let μ_n and σ_n be the standard regularized GP posterior mean and standard deviation (with regularization λ>0), and let γ_n be the maximal information gain. Since Theorem 2 gives the uniform online confidence bound |f(x)-μ_n(x)|≤ρ_n(δ)σ_n(x) with ρ_n(δ)=B+R√(2(γ_{n-1}+1+log(1/δ))), the standard GP-UCB analysis yields R(N)=O~(γ_N√N). Can one improve this online confidence width by an O~(√γ_n) factor, so that standard GP-UCB on compact domains achieves the paper's predicted regret O~(√(dNγ_N)) rather than O~(γ_N√N), in line with the information-theoretic feasibility suggested by the SupKernelUCB bound up to the compact-domain discretization factor? ([proceedings.mlr.press](https://proceedings.mlr.press/v134/vakili21a/vakili21a.pdf))

Periodic Dilation Completeness Problem (PDCP): characterize all complex-valued 2-periodic functions φ:(0,∞) → ℂ with φ|(0,1) ∈ L^2(0,1) such that the closed complex linear span of the dilation system {x ↦ φ(nx) : n ∈ ℕ} is all of L^2(0,1).
Does every bounded linear operator T:H→H on a separable complex Hilbert space H admit a nontrivial closed invariant subspace; that is, a closed linear subspace M with M ≠ {0}, M ≠ H, and T(M) ⊆ M?

Let H^2 = H^2(D) be the classical Hardy-Hilbert space on the open unit disk D, and let \mathcal{W} = (W_n)_{n in N} be the semigroup of weighted composition operators defined by W_n f(z) = (1 + z + ... + z^{n-1}) f(z^n). For each k >= 2, define h_k(z) = (1/(1 - z)) log((1 + z + ... + z^{k-1})/k), and let \mathcal{N} = span{h_k : k >= 2} subset H^2. Since \mathcal{N} is invariant under every W_n, determine whether there exists an integer n >= 2 such that the H^2-closure of \mathcal{N} is invariant under W_n^*, and whether this property is in fact equivalent to the Riemann Hypothesis.

Let {p_theta(x) = exp(<theta, T(x)> - A(theta)) h(x) : theta in Theta} be a steep, regular exponential family with minimal sufficient statistic T, open convex natural-parameter space Theta, mean-parameter space M, and mean map mu = grad A(theta). Fix a well-specified parameter theta* in Theta, write mu* = grad A(theta*), and let D_n = (X_1, ..., X_n) be iid from p_{theta*}. Define the MLE in mean-parameter form by mu_hat_MLE(D_n) = (1/n) sum_{i=1}^n T(X_i), and for the conjugate prior pi(theta | n0, mu0) proportional to exp(n0 <mu0, theta> - n0 A(theta)) with n0 > 0 and mu0 in M, define the conjugate MAP by mu_hat_MAP(D_n) = (n0 mu0 + sum_{i=1}^n T(X_i)) / (n0 + n); equivalently theta_hat_MLE = grad A*(mu_hat_MLE) and theta_hat_MAP = grad A*(mu_hat_MAP). Can one derive explicit deterministic non-asymptotic upper bounds, valid for finite n and ideally for a broad class of exponential families including few-sample regimes, for the exact frequentist risks E_{D_n}[KL(p_{theta*} || p_{theta_hat_MLE})] = E_{D_n}[B_{A*}(mu*; mu_hat_MLE)] and E_{D_n}[KL(p_{theta*} || p_{theta_hat_MAP})] = E_{D_n}[B_{A*}(mu*; mu_hat_MAP)], with no expectation over D_n left in the final bound, while allowing for the possibility that in some families or sample-size regimes the MLE risk is necessarily infinite?

Let {P_theta : theta in Theta subset R^d} be a steep, regular exponential family with minimal sufficient statistic T and log-partition A, so that mu = grad A(theta), and let theta_star be the true parameter generating iid samples X_1, ..., X_n. For conjugate prior hyperparameters (eta_0, n_0), let theta_hat_n be the MAP estimator, equivalently the last iterate of stochastic mirror descent for the stochastic losses f_x(theta) = A(theta) - <theta, T(x)>, mirror map A, prior-induced initialization, and step sizes gamma_t = 1/(n_0 + t). Since the population objective f(theta) = E[f_X(theta)] is 1-smooth and 1-strongly convex relative to A and satisfies f(theta) - f(theta_star) = KL(P_theta_star || P_theta), prove a non-asymptotic convergence rate for the last iterate of this SMD scheme in expected function suboptimality (equivalently expected KL risk), E[f(theta_hat_n) - f(theta_star)] = E[KL(P_theta_star || P_theta_hat_n)], that applies to conjugate MAP for standard exponential-family models, in particular the centered Gaussian with unknown variance N(0, sigma^2) and other Gaussian barrier objectives, under the natural decreasing schedule gamma_t = 1/(n_0 + t). The rate should recover the O(1/n) behavior suggested by the asymptotic theory and by the explicit centered-Gaussian MAP bound, while avoiding the current relative-smoothness assumptions that either exclude barrier objectives through uniform boundedness requirements or only treat constant-step convergence to a variance ball.

Let G be a simple undirected graph with adjacency matrix A, and let d be the number of distinct eigenvalues of A. For vertices i,j in V(G), define I={beta>0 : [e^{beta A}]_{ii}=[e^{beta A}]_{jj}}. Prove or disprove that if i and j are not cospectral, meaning that there exists an integer r>=0 with [A^r]_{ii} != [A^r]_{jj}, then |I| <= d-1.

Let A be a non-diagonalizable n x n matrix with entries in the nonnegative algebraic numbers, regarded as the adjacency matrix of a weighted directed graph G, and impose no further restriction on the Jordan form of A. Let β be a nonzero algebraic number, and define exp(βA) = sum_{r=0}^infinity (β^r A^r)/r!. If two vertices i and j satisfy [exp(βA)]_ii = [exp(βA)]_jj, must i and j be cospectral, meaning that [A^r]_ii = [A^r]_jj for every integer r ≥ 0? Prove this implication or give a counterexample. ([ricerca.sns.it](https://ricerca.sns.it/bitstream/11384/128462/1/soposc_rev.pdf))

Let G be a simple undirected graph with adjacency matrix A, and for β > 0 define the (exponential) subgraph centrality of vertex i by SC(i,β) = [e^{βA}]_{ii}. For two non-cospectral vertices i and j, call β an interlacing value if SC(i,β) = SC(j,β). Given k ∈ N, characterize the smallest graph(s), by number of vertices, that contain a pair of vertices with at least k interlacing values of subgraph centrality. Conversely, for an n-vertex graph, determine the largest possible number of interlacing values for a pair of vertices, and in particular decide whether there exist classes of graphs for which the general upper bound d-1 is attained, where d is the number of distinct eigenvalues of A.

Prove or disprove the following extension of Theorem 2.9. Let G be a directed graph with positive real edge weights and adjacency matrix A ∈ R^{n×n}, and let d be the number of distinct eigenvalues of A. For vertices i and j, call them non-cospectral if there exists an integer r ≥ 0 such that [A^r]_{ii} ≠ [A^r]_{jj}. Is it always true that the set of positive real parameters β for which the subgraph centralities coincide, [e^{βA}]_{ii} = [e^{βA}]_{jj}, has cardinality at most d - 1? ([ricerca.sns.it](https://ricerca.sns.it/bitstream/11384/128462/1/soposc_rev.pdf))

Let G be a simple undirected graph with adjacency matrix A, and fix two vertices i and j. Define the exponential subgraph centrality and resolvent centrality by SC(v,β) := [e^(βA)]_{vv} for β > 0 and RC(v,α) := [(I − αA)^(-1)]_{vv} for 0 < α < 1/ρ(A), where ρ(A) is the spectral radius of A. Let I_SC(i,j) := {β > 0 : SC(i,β) = SC(j,β)} and I_RC(i,j) := {α in (0,1/ρ(A)) : RC(i,α) = RC(j,α)}. Is it always true that |I_RC(i,j)| ≤ |I_SC(i,j)|? ([ricerca.sns.it](https://ricerca.sns.it/bitstream/11384/128462/1/soposc_rev.pdf))

Let K be an algebraically closed field, let X_1 and X_2 be smooth projective K-varieties, and let alpha_i:D_i -> D^b(X_i) be admissible subcategories for i=1,2, where D^b(X_i) denotes the bounded derived category of coherent sheaves on X_i. If F:D_1 -> D_2 is an exact fully faithful functor, must F be of Fourier-Mukai type; that is, does there exist an object E in D^b(X_1 x X_2) such that alpha_2 o F is isomorphic to the restriction Phi_E|_{D_1}, where Phi_E(-)=p_2*(E tensor p_1^*(-)) and p_i:X_1 x X_2 -> X_i are the natural projections?

Let K be an algebraically closed field, let X_1 and X_2 be smooth projective varieties over K, and let alpha_i: D_i -> D^b(X_i) be admissible subcategories of the bounded derived categories of coherent sheaves. Suppose there is an exact equivalence of triangulated categories F: D_1 -> D_2. Must there exist an exact equivalence G: D_1 -> D_2 of Fourier-Mukai type, i.e. an object E in D^b(X_1 x X_2) such that alpha_2 composed with G is isomorphic to the restriction Phi_E|_{D_1}, where Phi_E(-) = p_{2*}(E tensor p_1^*(-))?

Let K be an algebraically closed field of characteristic 2, and let X1 and X2 be smooth projective surfaces over K. Assume that X1 is an Enriques surface in the characteristic-2 sense used in the paper, i.e. a minimal smooth projective surface with numerically trivial canonical bundle and second Betti number b2(X1)=10. In characteristic 2, such Enriques surfaces fall into three families: classical, with dim H^1(X1,O_X1)=0; singular, with dim H^1(X1,O_X1)=1 and nontrivial Frobenius action; and supersingular, with dim H^1(X1,O_X1)=1 and trivial Frobenius action. For some or all of these three families, is the analogue of Theorem 3.4 true: does every exact equivalence Db(X1) ≅ Db(X2) force X1 ≅ X2?

Let X be an Enriques surface over an algebraically closed field K with char(K) != 2, and let Db(X) = <Ku(X,L), L> be the semiorthogonal decomposition associated to a choice L of exceptional line bundles as in Proposition 3.7 (so Ku(X,L) depends on L). If kappa: Ku(X,L) -> Db(X) denotes the inclusion, Example 2.2 gives only the formal expression S_{Ku(X,L)} ≅ kappa! o ((-) tensor omega_X[2]) o kappa. Does the Serre functor S_{Ku(X,L)} admit a more explicit and computable description?

Let X be an Enriques surface over an algebraically closed field 𝕂 with char(𝕂) ≠ 2. Suppose D^b(X), the bounded derived category of coherent sheaves on X, contains an admissible subcategory 𝓛 = ⟨𝓛_1, …, 𝓛_c⟩ such that the 𝓛_i are orthogonal admissible subcategories, each 𝓛_i = ⟨L^i_1, …, L^i_{n_i}⟩ is an exceptional collection of line bundles, and n_1 + ⋯ + n_c = 10; equivalently, write D^b(X) = ⟨Ku(X, 𝓛), 𝓛⟩ with Ku(X, 𝓛) = 𝓛^⊥. Is the Kuznetsov component Ku(X, 𝓛) indecomposable?

Let K be an algebraically closed field with char(K) ≠ 2. For i = 1, 2, let X_i be Enriques surfaces over K, and let Ku(X_i, L_i) be the Kuznetsov component arising from a semiorthogonal decomposition of D^b(X_i) of the type considered in Proposition 3.7 and Section 4.2, so that Ku(X_i, L_i) depends on the chosen exceptional collection L_i. Does the Enriques-surface specialization of the Fourier-Mukai problem have a positive answer: namely, is every exact fully faithful functor F: Ku(X_1, L_1) → Ku(X_2, L_2) of Fourier-Mukai type (in the sense of Definition 2.6, i.e. induced, after composing with the admissible embeddings, by a kernel on X_1 × X_2), or at least, whenever F is an exact equivalence, does there exist some Fourier-Mukai equivalence Ku(X_1, L_1) ≅ Ku(X_2, L_2)?

For every smooth cubic threefold X ⊂ P^4 over an algebraically closed field K, let Ku(X) be the Kuznetsov component in the canonical semiorthogonal decomposition D^b(X)=⟨Ku(X), O_X, O_X(H_X)⟩, where H_X is the hyperplane class. Is the triangulated category Ku(X) indecomposable, i.e. does it admit no nontrivial semiorthogonal decomposition?

Let X ⊂ P^5_K be a smooth cubic hypersurface over an algebraically closed field K with char(K) ≠ 2, and let Ku(X) be the Kuznetsov component defined by the semiorthogonal decomposition Db(X)=⟨Ku(X), O_X, O_X(H), O_X(2H)⟩, where H is the hyperplane class. Is X K-rational, i.e. birational over K to P^4_K, if and only if there exists an untwisted K3 surface S over K such that Ku(X) is K-linearly equivalent, as an exact triangulated category, to Db(S), the bounded derived category of coherent sheaves on S? ([link.springer.com](https://link.springer.com/content/pdf/10.1007/s12215-022-00796-x.pdf))

Let K be an algebraically closed field, let X ⊂ P^6_K be a smooth complete intersection of type (3,2,2), and let H = O_X(1). Can one prove, for H-slope-semistable torsion-free sheaves on X, a stronger Bogomolov inequality of the same kind as in [96, Theorem 1.1] and [103, Proposition 1.1], strong enough to imply that whenever an object E in D^b(X) is sigma_{s,q}-semistable for some (s,q) in Delta = {(s,q) in R^2 : q > s^2/2}, it satisfies (2q - s^2) Delta_H(E) + 4(H ch_2^s(E))^2 - 6H^2 ch_1^s(E) ch_3^s(E) >= 0, where Delta_H(E) = (H^2 ch_1(E))^2 - 2(H^3 ch_0(E))(H ch_2(E)), ch_1^s(E) = ch_1(E) - sH ch_0(E), ch_2^s(E) = ch_2(E) - sH ch_1(E) + (s^2/2)H^2 ch_0(E), and ch_3^s(E) = ch_3(E) - sH ch_2(E) + (s^2/2)H^2 ch_1(E) - (s^3/6)H^3 ch_0(E)? ([link.springer.com](https://link.springer.com/content/pdf/10.1007/s12215-022-00796-x.pdf))

Let (X,H) be a smooth complex projective polarized variety of dimension n. Is it true that there exist classes B in NS(X) tensor R, Gamma in CH^2_num(X) tensor R with Gamma·H^{n-2} = 0, and gamma_i in CH^i_num(X) tensor R for 3 <= i <= n, defining

gamma := e^{-B}·(1,0,Gamma,gamma_3,...,gamma_n) in CH^bullet_num(X) tensor R,

and an upper semicontinuous function f^gamma: R -> R, such that for every (s,q) in Delta := {(s,q) in R^2 : q > s^2/2} and every object E in D^b(X) that is sigma^gamma_{s,q}-semistable, one has Q_{s,q}(E) >= 0 whenever q > f^gamma(s), where ch^gamma(-) := gamma·ch(-), v_H^gamma(E) := (H^n ch_0^gamma(E), H^{n-1} ch_1^gamma(E), ..., H·ch_{n-1}^gamma(E), ch_n^gamma(E)), and Q_{s,q}(E) is the Bayer–Macrì quadratic form built from the first four components v_0^gamma, v_1^gamma, v_2^gamma, v_3^gamma?

Let X1 and X2 be cubic threefolds over an algebraically closed field K with char(K) != 2,3, and suppose there is an exact equivalence Ku(X1) ≅ Ku(X2). Can one prove X1 ≅ X2, i.e. reprove the categorical Torelli theorem for cubic threefolds (Theorem 6.4), by adapting the Section 4.1 extension method for Fourier-Mukai equivalences—through the semiorthogonal decompositions D^b(X_i) = <Ku(X_i), O_{X_i}, O_{X_i}(H_{X_i})>—so as to extend the equivalence from the Kuznetsov components to the whole derived categories and then apply the derived Torelli theorem for (anti)Fano manifolds?

Over C, let X be a prime Fano threefold, i.e. a smooth projective Fano threefold with Picard rank 1 and index i_X in {1,2}. Write Y_d for the index-2 case, with 1 ≤ d ≤ 5 and Ku(Y_d) = ⟨O_{Y_d}, O_{Y_d}(H)⟩^⊥, and write X_d for the index-1 case, with d = 2g - 2, 2 ≤ g ≤ 12, g ≠ 11, where Ku(X_d) = ⟨E_r, O_{X_d}⟩^⊥ for g ≥ 6 and Ku(X_d) = ⟨O_{X_d}⟩^⊥ for d in {2,4,6,8}. For which of these deformation types does the Kuznetsov component Ku(X) admit a Bridgeland stability condition σ that is Serre-invariant, in the sense that S_{Ku(X)} · σ = σ · g̃ for some g̃ in the universal cover of GL_2^+(R)?

Let \(X\) be a smooth projective variety, let \(\mathscr{D}\subset D^b(X)\) be an admissible subcategory, and let \(\mathscr{N}(\mathscr{D})\) be its numerical Grothendieck group. Assume that \(\mathscr{D}\) admits at least one numerical Bridgeland stability condition \(\sigma\) that is Serre-invariant in the sense that there exists \(\widetilde g\in\widetilde{GL}_2^+(\mathbb{R})\) with \(\mathsf{S}_{\mathscr{D}}\cdot\sigma=\sigma\cdot\widetilde g\), where \(\mathsf{S}_{\mathscr{D}}\) is the Serre functor of \(\mathscr{D}\). If \(\operatorname{rk}\mathscr{N}(\mathscr{D})=2\), must every Serre-invariant numerical stability condition on \(\mathscr{D}\) lie in a single \(\widetilde{GL}_2^+(\mathbb{R})\)-orbit?

Let X ⊂ P^4 be a smooth cubic threefold over C, let H_X denote the hyperplane class, and let Ku(X) := ⟨O_X, O_X(H_X)⟩^⊥ ⊂ D^b(X) be its Kuznetsov component. For admissible real parameters (s,q,mu) with (s,q) in Delta := {(s,q) in R^2 : q > (1/2)s^2}, q < -(1/2)s, and mu_{s,q}(O_X(-H_X)[1]) <= mu < mu_{s,q}(O_X), let sigma(s,q,mu) be the Bridgeland stability condition on Ku(X) constructed in Theorem 6.17 and equation (6.7). Is every Bridgeland stability condition sigma on Ku(X) in the same orbit, under the standard action of the universal cover of GL_2^+(R), as one (equivalently any) such sigma(s,q,mu)?

Over the complex numbers, let Y_1 be the prime Fano threefold of index 2 and degree 1, equivalently the Veronese double cone (a degree-6 hypersurface in the weighted projective space P(1,1,1,2,3)), and let Ku(Y_1) denote its Kuznetsov component, i.e. the residual admissible subcategory in the canonical semiorthogonal decomposition of D^b(Y_1). Is there a unique orbit of Serre-invariant Bridgeland stability conditions on Ku(Y_1) under the natural action of the universal cover of GL_2^+(R), where 'Serre-invariant' means that the Serre functor of Ku(Y_1) sends the stability condition to the same orbit? ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10326895/))

Over C, if Y and Y' are smooth prime Fano threefolds of index 2 and degree 1 (equivalently, smooth Veronese double cones, i.e. smooth degree-6 hypersurfaces in P(1,1,1,2,3)) and their Kuznetsov components Ku(Y) := <O_Y, O_Y(H_Y)>^⊥ and Ku(Y') := <O_Y', O_Y'(H_Y')>^⊥ are equivalent as triangulated categories, must Y and Y' be isomorphic?

Working over C, let X1 and X2 be smooth prime Fano threefolds of Picard rank 1, index 1, and degree 10; equivalently, if Pic(X_i)=Z·H_i, then -K_{X_i}=H_i and H_i^3=10, so X_i is a Gushel-Mukai threefold. Let Ku(X_i) be the Kuznetsov component in the standard semiorthogonal decomposition D^b(X_i)=<Ku(X_i), E_{2,i}, O_{X_i}>. If there exists an exact equivalence Phi: Ku(X1) -> Ku(X2) of Fourier-Mukai type in the sense of Definition 2.6, must X1 and X2 be birational?

Let X ⊂ P^4 be a smooth quartic threefold over C, so that Db(X)=⟨Ku(X), O_X⟩. Consider the Bridgeland stability conditions σ(s,q,μ)=(A(s,q,μ), Z(s,q,μ)) on Ku(X) obtained by the Section 6.3 induction procedure from the weak stability conditions σ_{s,q}, where (s,q) lies in Δ={(s,q) in R^2 : q > (1/2)s^2} and satisfies q < -s/2, and μ is any real number with μ_{s,q}(O_X(-H_X)[1]) ≤ μ < μ_{s,q}(O_X). Does there exist such an admissible choice of parameters for which σ(s,q,μ) is Serre-invariant, i.e. satisfies S_{Ku(X)}·σ = σ·g̃ for some g̃ in the universal cover of GL_2^+(R)? ([link.springer.com](https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s12215-022-00796-x))

Let X_1 and X_2 be smooth quartic hypersurfaces in P^4_C, and let Ku(X_i) := <O_{X_i}>^⊥ ⊂ D^b(X_i) be their Kuznetsov components. Is there a categorical Torelli statement for quartic threefolds—namely, a criterion formulated in terms of an exact equivalence Ku(X_1) ≅ Ku(X_2), possibly with whatever additional compatibility on the equivalence is genuinely required, that is equivalent to X_1 ≅ X_2? Moreover, does an exact equivalence Ku(X_1) ≅ Ku(X_2) imply that X_1 and X_2 are birational?

Let X1 and X2 be smooth cubic hypersurfaces in P^5 over an algebraically closed field K with char(K) != 2, and let Ku(X_i) be the Kuznetsov component defined by the semiorthogonal decomposition Db(X_i)=<Ku(X_i), O_{X_i}, O_{X_i}(H_i), O_{X_i}(2H_i)>. If there exists an exact equivalence Phi: Ku(X1) -> Ku(X2), without assuming that Phi commutes with the degree-shift autoequivalences O_{X_i}, must X1 and X2 be birational?

Let X1 and X2 be smooth complex Gushel–Mukai fourfolds, and let Ku(X_i):=⟨O_{X_i}, U_{X_i}^∨, O_{X_i}(1), U_{X_i}^∨(1)⟩^⊥ ⊂ D^b(X_i) be their Kuznetsov components. Assume there is an exact equivalence Φ: Ku(X1) →~ Ku(X2) together with a natural isomorphism Φ∘𝖮_{X_1} ≅ 𝖮_{X_2}∘Φ, where the degree shift functor is 𝖮_{X_i}:=L_{⟨O_{X_i},U_{X_i}^∨⟩}(-⊗O_{X_i}(1))[-1]. Under what additional assumptions on Φ is one allowed to conclude that X1 and X2 are isomorphic?

Let X1 and X2 be smooth projective Gushel-Mukai varieties over an algebraically closed field K, of the same dimension, and let Ku(X_i) denote the Kuznetsov component of Db(X_i). If there exists an exact K-linear equivalence Ku(X1) ≅ Ku(X2), must X1 and X2 be birational?

Let Ω ⊂ R^d be a bounded domain with periodic boundary conditions, let n ≥ 1, di > 0, γij ∈ R, and define the nonlocal perception term by ujg,R(x,t) = ∫Ω uj(y,t)g(x−y)dy, where g is a detection kernel with perceptual radius R. For suitable nonnegative periodic initial data ui(x,0) = ui,0(x), in what function-space or solution sense do there exist time-dependent solutions to the multispecies system ∂t ui = diΔui − ∇·(ui∇(Σj=1n γij ujg,R)), i = 1, ..., n, on Ω, particularly when g is the top-hat kernel (in 1D, g(z) = 1/(2R) for |z| ≤ R and 0 otherwise), rather than a smoother kernel such as a Gaussian? ([math.ualberta.ca](https://www.math.ualberta.ca/~hwang/WangSalmaniwReview.pdf))

Let Ω ⊂ ℝd be a bounded spatial domain, let n ≥ 1, and consider the multispecies implicit-memory nonlocal advection–diffusion system from equation (2.10): ∂tu_i = d_iΔu_i − ∇·(u_i∇(∑j=1n γiju_j^{g,R})) for i = 1, …, n, where d_i > 0, γ_ij ∈ ℝ, and u_j^{g,R} denotes the perception operator from (2.5), i.e. convolution with a perceptual kernel g of range R satisfying the Section 2.1 hypotheses (with whatever bounded-domain modification near ∂Ω is needed to make the nonlocal term well defined). For the associated stationary problem 0 = d_iΔu_i − ∇·(u_i∇(∑j=1n γiju_j^{g,R})), in what solution framework and under what assumptions can one prove the existence of spatially nonconstant steady states—meaning steady states for which at least one u_i is nonconstant in x—when the system is posed under zero-flux boundary conditions ((d_i∇u_i − u_i∇(∑jγiju_j^{g,R}))·n = 0 on ∂Ω), under homogeneous Neumann boundary conditions (∂nu_i = 0 on ∂Ω), or under periodic boundary conditions? ([math.ualberta.ca](https://www.math.ualberta.ca/~hwang/WangSalmaniwReview.pdf))

For the n-species nonlocal advection-diffusion system (2.10) on a bounded domain Ω, given by ∂_t u_i = d_iΔu_i − ∇·(u_i∇(Σ_{j=1}^n γ_{ij}u_j^{g,R})) for i = 1,…,n, where u_i(x,t) denotes the density of the i-th population, d_i > 0, γ_{ij} ∈ ℝ encodes attraction or repulsion to the perceived density of population j, and u_j^{g,R} denotes the perception of u_j through a detection kernel g with perceptual range R, spatially constant steady states are evident. Assuming spatially non-constant steady states of the associated steady problem exist under zero-flux, homogeneous Neumann, or periodic boundary conditions, what qualitative properties do these inhomogeneous steady states possess?

For the n-species nonlocal advection-diffusion system (2.10) on a bounded domain Ω, given by ∂_t u_i = d_i Δu_i - ∇·(u_i ∇(Σ_{j=1}^n γ_{ij} u_{j,g,R})) for i = 1, …, n, where u_{j,g,R} denotes the perception-function version of u_j associated with a detection kernel g_R satisfying the Sect. 2.1 assumptions and g_R → δ as R → 0+, do the solutions singled out in Open Problems 1–2—namely, time-dependent solutions under periodic boundary conditions and spatially non-constant steady states under zero-flux, homogeneous Neumann, or periodic boundary conditions—remain well defined as R → 0+, and does the nonlocal system converge in a mathematically meaningful sense to its corresponding formal local limit obtained by replacing u_{j,g,R} with u_j? ([math.ualberta.ca](https://www.math.ualberta.ca/~hwang/WangSalmaniwReview.pdf))

For the bounded-domain time-dependent multispecies aggregation/segregation system (2.10), namely for nonnegative densities u_i = u_i(x,t), i = 1,...,n, satisfying partial_t u_i = d_i Delta u_i - div(u_i grad(sum_{j=1}^n gamma_{ij} (u_j)_{g,R})), where (u_j)_{g,R} denotes the nonlocal perception of u_j through a detection kernel g with perceptual radius R, under which non-periodic boundary conditions—especially zero-flux/homogeneous Neumann and homogeneous Dirichlet on a bounded domain—can one prove well-posedness of the time-dependent problem (in an appropriate weak, strong, or classical sense, locally or globally in time), and how should a finite-range detection kernel, particularly the top-hat kernel, be defined near the boundary (for example by truncating and renormalizing the perception window over the part that remains inside the domain, in the style of (4.3)) so that the nonlocal term is mathematically well defined, biologically reasonable, and comparable with the periodic-boundary setting?

Let Ω be a bounded domain with periodic boundary conditions (equivalently, a torus in higher dimensions). For i=1,…,n, let u_i(x,t) denote the density of population i and p_i(x,t) the density of landscape marks foreign to population i, and consider the system ∂_t u_i = d_iΔu_i − γ_i∇·(u_i∇p_i^{g,R}), ∂_t p_i = Σ_{j=1}^n α_{ij}u_j − μp_i, where p_i^{g,R}(x,t)=∫_Ω p_i(y,t)g_R(x−y)dy is the periodic perception convolution and g_R is the top-hat detection kernel (uniform on the ball of radius R and zero outside, normalized to have integral 1). For suitable periodic initial data, in what function-space sense can one establish existence of time-dependent solutions to this explicit landscape-mark model (2.11), and does this solution theory remain well defined as R→0+, in the sense of yielding a meaningful local-limit connection to the system with p_i^{g,R} replaced by p_i? ([math.ualberta.ca](https://www.math.ualberta.ca/~hwang/WangSalmaniwReview.pdf))

For the landscape-mark model (2.11), with unknowns u_i(x,t) (density of population i) and p_i(x,t) (density of marks foreign to population i), i = 1,...,n, given by partial_t u_i = d_i Delta u_i - gamma_i div(u_i grad p_{i,g,R}) and partial_t p_i = sum_{j=1}^n alpha_{ij} u_j - mu p_i on a bounded domain Omega with periodic boundary conditions, where p_{i,g,R}(x) is the periodic spatial convolution of p_i with the top-hat detection kernel g_R from (2.3) (in one dimension, g_R(z) = 1/(2R) for |z| <= R and 0 otherwise), beyond the obvious spatially constant equilibria, in what sense do spatially non-constant periodic steady states (u_i,p_i) exist for the steady-state problem associated to (2.11), and do these steady states remain well defined in the local limit R -> 0+?

Let Omega be a bounded domain with periodic boundary conditions, let g_R be the top-hat detection kernel of perceptual range R, and write f^{g,R}(x) = ∫_Omega f(y) g_R(x-y) dy. For n interacting populations u_i(x,t), consider the explicit landscape-mark model ∂_t u_i = d_i Δu_i - γ_i ∇·(u_i ∇p_i^{g,R}), ∂_t p_i = Σ_{j=1}^n α_{ij} u_j - μ p_i, where p_i is the density of foreign marks left on the landscape. Assuming spatially non-constant steady states of this system exist, what qualitative characteristics can such steady states exhibit, how do they compare with the spatially non-constant steady states of the simpler multispecies nonlocal perception model ∂_t u_i = d_i Δu_i - ∇·(u_i ∇(Σ_{j=1}^n γ_{ij} u_j^{g,R})), and are the dynamics of the explicit landscape-mark model entirely contained in those of the simpler model, or does the explicit mark variable p_i generate genuinely new dynamics? ([math.ualberta.ca](https://www.math.ualberta.ca/~hwang/WangSalmaniwReview.pdf))

Let Omega be a bounded domain in R^d, let i = 1, ..., n, and consider the marks-on-the-landscape system (2.11): partial_t u_i = d_i Delta u_i - gamma_i div(u_i nabla p_i^{g,R}) and partial_t p_i = sum_{j=1}^n alpha_ij u_j - mu p_i, where u_i(x,t) is the density of population i, p_i(x,t) is the density of foreign marks on the landscape, and p_i^{g,R}(x,t) = integral over Omega of p_i(y,t) g(x-y) dy with g the normalized top-hat detection function of perceptual radius R. For prescribed initial data, and with an appropriate boundary-adapted interpretation of the top-hat perception operator near partial Omega, in what sense do solutions to this time-dependent problem exist in a bounded domain when one imposes either the zero-flux condition d_i partial_n u_i - gamma_i u_i partial_n p_i^{g,R} = 0, the homogeneous Neumann condition partial_n u_i = 0, or the homogeneous Dirichlet condition u_i = 0 on partial Omega? ([math.ualberta.ca](https://www.math.ualberta.ca/~hwang/WangSalmaniwReview.pdf))

For the n-population conflict-zone dynamic-memory model (2.13), with d_i > 0, gamma_i >= 0, rho_{ij} >= 0, mu >= 0, beta >= 0, unknowns u_i(x,t) and k_i(x,t) satisfying partial_t u_i = d_i Delta u_i + gamma_i div(u_i grad(k_i^{g,R})) and partial_t k_i = u_i sum_{j=1}^n rho_{ij} u_j - (mu + beta u_i) k_i for i=1,...,n on a bounded periodic domain Omega, where k_i^{g,R}(x,t)=integral_Omega k_i(y,t) g_R(x-y) dy and g_R is the top-hat detection kernel of perceptual radius R>0, in what sense do time-dependent solutions with admissible initial data exist, in what sense do spatially non-constant steady states exist, what qualitative properties do those spatially non-constant steady states possess, and do the solutions remain well defined in the local-perception limit R -> 0+?

For a bounded domain Omega ⊂ R^d and i = 1, ..., n, consider the nonlocal conflict-zone memory system introduced in Sect. 2.2.2, ∂_t u_i = d_i Δu_i + gamma_i ∇·(u_i ∇(k_i)_{g,R}) and ∂_t k_i = (u_i)_{g,R} sum_{j=1}^n rho_ij u_j - (mu + beta u_i) k_i, where (f)_{g,R}(x,t) = ∫_Omega f(y,t) g(x-y) dy, the same perceptual kernel g and radius R are used for every population, and g is the top-hat detection function g(z) = 1/(2R) for |z| ≤ R and 0 otherwise (or its radial higher-dimensional analogue). After specifying a boundary-compatible definition of the nonlocal perception operator near ∂Omega, determine under what assumptions on the parameters and initial data the time-dependent problem admits solutions, and in what precise sense, when u_i satisfies, separately, (a) the zero-flux condition n·(d_i∇u_i + gamma_i u_i∇(k_i)_{g,R}) = 0 on ∂Omega, (b) the homogeneous Neumann condition ∂_n u_i = 0 on ∂Omega, or (c) the homogeneous Dirichlet condition u_i = 0 on ∂Omega. ([math.ualberta.ca](https://www.math.ualberta.ca/~hwang/WangSalmaniwReview.pdf))

Fix a bounded spatial domain Ω⊂R^d, a detection kernel g with perceptual radius R, the same boundary conditions and initial data, and the same parameters di>0, γi≥0, ρ, μ, β≥0. For two interacting populations u1,u2 with conflict-zone cognitive maps k1,k2, where perception is given by fg,R(x,t)=∫Ω f(y,t)g(x−y)dy and the movement law is ∂tui=diΔui+γi∇·(ui∇(ki)g,R) for i=1,2, compare the solutions of the magnitude-based conflict-memory model ∂tki=ρu1u2−(μ+βui)ki with those of the analogous probability-density formulation ∂tki=ρu1u2(1−ki)−(μ+βui)ki.
