For the walking-droplet system consisting of bouncing droplets in a vibrating liquid, can one derive—by averaging over the fast bouncing or forcing scale—an effective hydrodynamic model in terms of real fields rho > 0 and theta on a manifold M, with potential velocity v = grad theta, so that the averaged variables satisfy a barotropic-type compressible Euler or quantum-fluid system of the form (14.1), and hence, under the Madelung transform psi = sqrt(rho) e^{i theta}, the effective dynamics are governed by a nonlinear Schrodinger equation i d_t psi = -Delta psi + V psi - f(|psi|^2) psi as in (14.2), thereby explaining the observed correspondence between bouncing-droplet dynamics and quantum-particle behavior?

In the Section 15.2 countable Hamiltonian model of balls moving in a bounded box D, with families F1, F2, ... such that family Fi contains ni identical balls of radius ri and mass mi, only neighboring families interact through pair potentials U_{i,i+1}(|qj-qk|), and Σ_i ni mi < infinity with mi and ri decreasing sufficiently fast, suppose these parameters can be chosen so that a direct energy cascade transports energy toward larger family index i and lets energy escape to infinity. Can one then give an intrinsic, non-circular mechanism for this energy dissipation that does not use the ad hoc "limit absorption" device of inserting friction on family FN and then sending N to infinity?

For the countable-chamber apparatus of Section 15.3—where each chamber C_i contains n_i identical elastic balls of mass m_i and radius r_i, the lower door has a spring-loaded one-way shutter damped by interactions with the much smaller and more numerous balls in C_{i+1}, and a turbine/ratchet/stirrer mechanism is intended to transfer energy from the ball stream in C_i to the much larger and fewer balls in C_{i-1}—can one choose the sequences (n_i, m_i, r_i) so that the apparatus indeed produces, on average, transfer of energy toward lower-index chambers and concentration of energy in the first few chambers, thereby realizing the intended inverse-cascade mechanism; and does a similar mechanism exist in real hydrodynamics, preferably already for a 2D ideal fluid?

For each integer m>=1, let s_m:=123...(m-1)m=A007908(m), interpreted as a base-10 integer obtained by concatenating the blocks 1,2,...,m. Let A001292 be the increasing sequence formed by taking, for every m>=1, all cyclic permutations of the ordered block list (1,2,...,m), concatenating each such cyclic permutation in base 10, and then sorting all resulting integers increasingly. Disregarding the trivial term A001292(1)=1, determine how many terms of A001292 are perfect powers, i.e. integers of the form a^k with a>=2 and k>=2; Kashihara’s conjecture predicts that this number is 0.

Let A352991 be the sequence of all distinct base-10 integers obtained by concatenating a permutation of 1,2,...,m for some integer m >= 1, with the resulting integers listed in increasing order. For every n >= 2, if A352991(n) is a perfect power of an integer, is it true that there do not exist integers c >= 1 and k >= 3 such that A352991(n) = c^k? In other words, must every nontrivial perfect power occurring in A352991 be a perfect square only?

Let B^(H): L^2(0,1) -> ell^2 be the Hausdorff moment operator defined by [B^(H) z]_j = integral_0^1 t^(j-1) z(t) dt for j = 1,2,.... It is known that B^(H) is injective, bounded, non-compact, and has non-closed range, so the inverse problem B^(H) z = y is ill-posed of type I in the sense of Nashed. Characterize explicitly an infinite-dimensional closed subspace Y_1 of R(B^(H)) contained in ell^2 such that the restricted inverse B^(H)^(-1): Y_1 -> L^2(0,1) is continuous; equivalently, determine a subspace Y_1 and a constant C > 0 for which ||B^(H)^(-1) y||_{L^2(0,1)} <= C ||y||_{ell^2} holds for all y in Y_1.

Let B^(H): L^2(0,1) -> ell^2 be the Hausdorff moment operator defined by [B^(H) z]_j = integral_0^1 t^(j-1) z(t) dt for j = 1,2,..., and let J: L^2(0,1) -> L^2(0,1) be the integration operator [Jx](s) = integral_0^s x(t) dt for 0 <= s <= 1. For the compact, injective composite operator A := B^(H) o J : L^2(0,1) -> ell^2 and the inverse problem Ax = y, determine the actual asymptotic regime of its nonincreasing singular values sigma_i(A): does there exist C > 0 and kappa > 0 such that C i^(-kappa) <= sigma_i(A) for every i in N, so that the problem is moderately ill-posed in the sense of Definition 1, or do there exist C1, C2, theta > 0 such that sigma_i(A) <= C1 exp(-C2 i^theta) for every i in N, so that the problem is exponentially ill-posed?

Motivated by the composite Hausdorff moment operator A = B^(H) o J, let Y be a Hilbert space and let A:L^2(0,1)->Y be a Hilbert-Schmidt operator with non-closed range. Assume that A^*A:L^2(0,1)->L^2(0,1) is an integral operator of the form [A^*Ax](s)=∫_0^1 k(s,t)x(t)dt with k in L^2([0,1] x [0,1]), and that k has limited smoothness in the sense that k is not infinitely many times continuously differentiable on the whole closed square [0,1] x [0,1]. Under what additional conditions can the equation Ax=y still be severely ill-posed, in the sense that polynomial lower bounds C i^{-kappa} <= sigma_i(A) fail for arbitrarily large kappa, and in particular exponentially ill-posed? ([tu-chemnitz.de](https://www.tu-chemnitz.de/mathematik/inverse_probleme/fulltext/GH_2022.pdf))

Let B^(H): L^2(0,1) -> ℓ^2 be the Hausdorff moment operator defined by [B^(H)z]_j = integral from 0 to 1 of t^(j-1) z(t) dt for j in N, and let J: L^2(0,1) -> L^2(0,1) be the integration operator defined by [Jx](s) = integral from 0 to s of x(t) dt for 0 <= s <= 1. For the compact injective operator A := B^(H) ◦ J : L^2(0,1) -> ℓ^2, determine the singular functions u_i(A) in L^2(0,1) and v_i(A) in ℓ^2, i = 1, 2, ..., that is, the complete orthonormal systems in the singular system {sigma_i(A), u_i(A), v_i(A)} satisfying A u_i(A) = sigma_i(A) v_i(A) and sigma_i(A) -> 0.

Let H = (1/(j+k-1))_{j,k=1}^∞ be the infinite Hilbert matrix, and for each n ∈ ℕ let H_n = (1/(j+k-1))_{j,k=1}^n denote its n×n leading principal section. For a fixed i ∈ ℕ (with n ≥ i), let σ_i(H_n) be the i-th singular value of H_n. Is it true that lim_{n→∞} σ_i(H_n) = π for every fixed i? If not, what is the behavior of σ_i(H_n) as n → ∞ for fixed i?

Let H = (1/(i+j-1))_{i,j=1}^∞ be the infinite Hilbert matrix acting on ℓ^2, and for each n ∈ ℕ let H_n = (1/(i+j-1))_{i,j=1}^n denote its n-dimensional segment, viewed as an operator on ℓ^2 by adjoining zero rows and columns outside the first n coordinates. Since each H_n is finite-rank whereas H is non-compact, determine the behavior of the remainder norm ||H-H_n||_{L(ℓ^2,ℓ^2)} as n→∞; in particular, is it in fact equal to π = ||H||_{L(ℓ^2,ℓ^2)}?

Let T_{003}(a,b) denote the number of tilings of the (a,b)-benzel in which neither the right stone nor the left stone is allowed and all three bone orientations are allowed. Section 2 states that a benzel admits such a bone-only tiling only when (a,b) = (k(3k-1)/2, k(3k+1)/2) or its reversal, for some integer k >= 2. Determine an exact formula for T_{003}(k(3k-1)/2, k(3k+1)/2) for k >= 2; failing that, give a method (for example, a recurrence) that computes these numbers more efficiently than brute-force enumeration.

For integers a,b with 2 <= a <= 2b and 2 <= b <= 2a, let T012(a,b) denote the number of tilings of the (a,b)-benzel by translates of the left-pointing stone trihex together with translates of any two of the three bone trihex orientations (vertical, rising, and falling), with right-pointing stones forbidden. Is it true that for every integer n >= 1, T012(3n,3n) = 2^n n!?

Let omega = exp(2pi i/3). For positive integers a,b satisfying 2 <= a <= 2b and 2 <= b <= 2a, the (a,b)-benzel is the union of the unit hexagonal cells lying fully inside the hexagon with vertices a omega + b, -a omega^2 - b, a omega^2 + b omega, -a - b omega, a + b omega^2, and -a omega - b omega^2. For 0 <= i,j <= 1 and 0 <= k <= 3, let T_{ijk}(a,b) denote the number of tilings of the (a,b)-benzel in which the right stone is allowed iff i=1, the left stone is allowed iff j=1, and exactly k of the three bone orientations are allowed. Is it true that, for every integer n >= 1, T_{012}(3n+1,3n+2) = (2n)!! = 2^n n!?

Let ω = e^{2πi/3}. For positive integers a,b with 2 <= a <= 2b and 2 <= b <= 2a, let the (a,b)-benzel be the union of the unit hexagonal cells fully contained in the hexagon with vertices aω+b, -aω^2-b, aω^2+bω, -a-bω, a+bω^2, and -aω-bω^2. Let T013(a,b) be the number of tilings of this benzel by translates of the left stone together with the three bones (vertical, rising, and falling), with right stones forbidden. If I(a,b) denotes the Conway-Lagarias invariant of the (a,b)-benzel, given by I(a,b) = (3a^2-6ab+3b^2-a-b)/2 when a+b ≡ 0 (mod 3), I(a,b) = (-a^2+4ab-b^2-a-b+2)/2 when a+b ≡ 1 (mod 3), and I(a,b) = (3a^2-6ab+3b^2+a+b-2)/2 when a+b ≡ 2 (mod 3), is it true that T013(a,b) > 0 whenever I(a,b) <= 0? ([samuelfhopkins.com](https://www.samuelfhopkins.com/OPAC/files/proceedings/propp.pdf))

For integers a,b with 2≤a≤2b and 2≤b≤2a, let the (a,b)-benzel be Propp’s hexagonal-grid region consisting of the unit hexagonal cells lying fully inside the hexagon with vertices a+b, -aω^2-b, aω^2+bω, -a-bω, a+bω^2, and -aω-bω^2, where ω=e^(2πi/3). Let T_{102}(a,b) denote the number of tilings of this region by the right stone together with any two of the three bone prototiles (vertical, rising, and falling), with the left stone forbidden; by the threefold rotational symmetry discussed in Section 1, this number does not depend on which two bone prototiles are chosen. Is it true that for all integers k≥0 and n≥1, except (k,n)=(0,1), one has T_{102}(n+3k,2n+3k-1)=∏_{i=1}^k ((2i)!(2i+2n-2)!)/((i+n-1)!(i+n+k-1)!)? ([samuelfhopkins.com](https://www.samuelfhopkins.com/OPAC/files/proceedings/propp.pdf))

For integers a,b with 2 <= a <= 2b and 2 <= b <= 2a, let the (a,b)-benzel be the polyhex consisting of unit hexagons whose centers (i,j,k) in Z^3 satisfy i+j+k=1 and -(a-1) <= j-i, k-j, i-k <= b-1. Let T_{103}(a,b) denote the number of tilings of this region by translates of the right stone and the three bone trihexes (vertical, rising, and falling), with the left stone forbidden. Is it true that for every integer n >= 5 one has T_{103}(n, 2n-3) = ((3n+3)(3n-7)!)/((n-5)!(2n-1)!)? As in the paper, the same expression formally gives 0 for n = 3 and n = 4 if 1/(-1)! and 1/(-2)! are interpreted as 0.

For integers a,b with 2 <= a <= 2b and 2 <= b <= 2a, let the (a,b)-benzel be the polyhex consisting of those unit hexagonal cells whose centers (i,j,k) in Z^3 satisfy i + j + k = 1 and -(a-1) <= j-i, k-j, i-k <= b-1. Let T103(a,b) denote the number of tilings of this benzel by translates of the right-pointing stone and the three bone prototiles (vertical, rising, and falling), with left-pointing stones forbidden. Let C(a,b) be the Conway-Lagarias invariant of the benzel, i.e. the tiling-invariant difference total area of right stones minus total area of left stones, given by C(a,b) = (3a^2 - 6ab + 3b^2 - a - b)/2 if a+b ≡ 0 (mod 3), C(a,b) = (-a^2 + 4ab - b^2 - a - b + 2)/2 if a+b ≡ 1 (mod 3), and C(a,b) = (3a^2 - 6ab + 3b^2 + a + b - 2)/2 if a+b ≡ 2 (mod 3). Is it true that T103(a,b) > 0 for every such (a,b) with C(a,b) >= 0?

Let ω = e^{2πi/3}. For integers a,b with 2 <= a <= 2b and 2 <= b <= 2a, let B_{a,b} be the (a,b)-benzel, i.e. the union of unit hexagonal cells lying fully inside the hexagon with vertices aω+b, -aω^2-b, aω^2+bω, -a-bω, a+bω^2, and -aω-bω^2. Let T_{112}(a,b) denote the number of tilings of B_{a,b} by translates of the right stone, the left stone, and exactly two of the three bone prototiles (vertical, rising, and falling); equivalently, this is the paper’s type-112 tiling count, and by 120-degree rotational symmetry it is independent of which bone orientation is forbidden. Define T(n) = T_{112}(3n,3n) for n >= 1. Is it true that for every integer n >= 1, T(n)T(n+2)/T(n+1)^2 = 256(2n+3)^2(4n+1)(4n+3)^2(4n+5) / (27(3n+1)(3n+2)^2(3n+4)^2(3n+5))?

Let T112(a,b) denote the number of tilings of the (a,b)-benzel by translates of the right stone, the left stone, and any fixed two of the three bone prototiles (vertical, rising, and falling), so that only the number of allowed bone orientations matters. For each integer n >= 1, find an explicit formula governing T112(3n+1, 3n+1).

For integers a,b with 2 <= a <= 2b and 2 <= b <= 2a, let the (a,b)-benzel be the union of unit hexagons whose barycentric-center coordinates (i,j,k) in Z^3 satisfy i+j+k=1 and -(a-1) <= j-i, k-j, i-k <= b-1. Let T112(a,b) denote the number of tilings of the (a,b)-benzel by translates of the right stone, the left stone, and any fixed two of the three bone prototiles (vertical, rising, falling); equivalently, this is the paper's type-112 tiling number, and by threefold rotational symmetry it is independent of which bone orientation is excluded. If T(n) := T112(3n+1, 3n+2) for n >= 1, is it true that for every n >= 1 one has T(n)T(n+3)/(T(n+1)T(n+2)) = (65536*(2n+3)*(2n+5)^2*(2n+7)*(4n+3)*(4n+5)^2*(4n+7)^2*(4n+9)^2*(4n+11))/(729*(3n+2)*(3n+4)^3*(3n+5)^2*(3n+7)^2*(3n+8)^3*(3n+10))?

For each integer n >= 1, let B(3n-1,3n) be the (3n-1,3n)-benzel, i.e. the region of hexagonal cells in the triangular grid whose centers (i,j,k) in Z^3 satisfy i+j+k=1 and -(3n-2) <= j-i, k-j, i-k <= 3n-1. Let T_{112}(a,b) denote the number of tilings of the (a,b)-benzel by translates of the right stone, the left stone, and exactly two of the three bone orientations (vertical, rising, falling), where by threefold rotational symmetry the count depends only on the fact that one bone orientation is forbidden, not on which one. Find a formula governing the sequence T_{112}(3n-1,3n) for all n >= 1.

Let ω = e^{2πi/3}. For integers a,b with 2 ≤ a ≤ 2b and 2 ≤ b ≤ 2a, let the (a,b)-benzel be the union of the unit hexagonal cells lying fully inside the hexagon with vertices aω+b, -aω^2-b, aω^2+bω, -a-bω, a+bω^2, and -aω-bω^2. Let T112(a,b) denote the number of unweighted tilings of this region by both stone prototiles (right and left stones) together with any fixed two of the three bone prototiles (vertical, rising, and falling); by the paper’s symmetry discussion, this depends only on the fact that exactly two bone types are allowed. Is it true that for every n ≥ 1, T112(n+2, 2n+1) = S_n, where S_n is the nth large Schröder number, indexed as in OEIS A006318 (so S1=2, S2=6, S3=22, ...)?

For integers a,b with 2 <= a <= 2b and 2 <= b <= 2a, let the (a,b)-benzel be the union of unit hexagonal cells in the triangular grid whose barycentric centers (i,j,k) in Z^3 satisfy i + j + k = 1 and -(a - 1) <= j - i, k - j, i - k <= b - 1. Let T_{112}(a,b) denote the number of tilings of this region by translates of the right stone, the left stone, and any two of the three bone prototiles. Is it true that, for every integer n >= 1, T_{112}(n + 2, 2n) equals the number of royal paths in a lattice of order n (OEIS A006319)? ([samuelfhopkins.com](https://www.samuelfhopkins.com/OPAC/files/proceedings/propp.pdf))

For integers a,b with 2 ≤ a ≤ 2b and 2 ≤ b ≤ 2a, let B_{a,b} denote the (a,b)-benzel, i.e. the polyhex whose cells have centers (i,j,k) ∈ Z^3 satisfying i+j+k=1 and -(a-1) ≤ j-i, k-j, i-k ≤ b-1. Let T_{113}(a,b) be the number of tilings of B_{a,b} by translates of the five prototiles consisting of the right stone, left stone, vertical bone, rising bone, and falling bone. Is it true that T_{113}(a,b)=1 for every admissible pair (a,b) with a+b ≡ 1 (mod 3)?

Let T113(a,b) denote the unweighted number of tilings of the (a,b)-benzel, for integers a,b with 2 <= a <= 2b and 2 <= b <= 2a, when both the right and left stone prototiles are allowed and all three bone orientations are allowed. For integers n >= 5, is the function n -> T113(n,2n-4) 2-adically continuous?

Let B(a,b) be the (a,b)-benzel, i.e. the polyhex whose unit-hexagon centers are the triples (i,j,k) in Z^3 satisfying i+j+k=1 and -(a-1) ≤ j-i, k-j, i-k ≤ b-1. Let T113(a,b) denote the number of tilings of B(a,b) by the right stone, the left stone, and the three bone prototiles (vertical, rising, and falling), so that both stone orientations and all three bone orientations are allowed. For integers n ≥ 4, is the map n ↦ T113(n, 2n−3), viewed as a map from {n in Z : n ≥ 4} to Z with the 2-adic topology, 2-adically continuous? ([samuelfhopkins.com](https://www.samuelfhopkins.com/OPAC/files/proceedings/propp.pdf))

For integers n >= 5, let T113(a,b;3) denote the weighted sum over all type-113 tilings of the (a,b)-benzel, where type 113 means that both stone orientations and all three bone orientations are allowed, and where a tiling containing m stones contributes weight 3^m. If we regard a_n = T113(n,2n-4;3) as a sequence in Z ⊂ Z_2, is the map n -> a_n 2-adically continuous; equivalently, for every r >= 1 does there exist s >= 1 such that whenever n,n' >= 5 and n ≡ n' (mod 2^s), one has T113(n,2n-4;3) ≡ T113(n',2n'-4;3) (mod 2^r)?

Let T_{113}(a,b;3) denote the weighted sum of all tilings of the (a,b)-benzel in which both right and left stones and all three bone orientations are allowed, where a tiling with m stones contributes weight 3^m. For integers n >= 4, define f(n)=T_{113}(n,2n-3;3). Is f 2-adically continuous as a function of n; that is, for every integer r >= 1, does there exist an integer s >= 1 such that whenever n,n' >= 4 and n \equiv n' (mod 2^s), one has T_{113}(n,2n-3;3) \equiv T_{113}(n',2n'-3;3) (mod 2^r)?

Let R be a finite simply-connected region of the hexagonal grid, and consider tilings of R by translates of the five stones-and-bones prototiles: the right stone, the left stone, and the vertical, rising, and falling bones. There are two natural local 2-flips: one replaces two stones of opposite orientation by two bones, and the other replaces a local stone-and-bone pair by a stone of the same orientation together with a bone of a different orientation. Must it be true that any stones-and-bones tiling of R can be mutated into any other stones-and-bones tiling of R by a finite succession of these 2-flips?

Let T_n be the triangle of hexagonal cells with n cells on each side. Conway, Lagarias, and Thurston showed that T_n admits a tiling by stones (equivalently, by T_2 tiles) exactly when n is congruent to 0, 2, 9, or 11 modulo 12. If a_n denotes the number of tilings of T_n by stones for such admissible n, does the sequence a_n converge to 0 in the ring of 2-adic integers Z_2 as n -> infinity through n in N with n ≡ 0, 2, 9, 11 (mod 12)?

Does there exist a poly(n,s,1/epsilon)-time membership-query algorithm that, given epsilon > 0 and query access to an unknown size-s decision tree f:{0,1}^n -> {0,1}, outputs a decision tree h:{0,1}^n -> {0,1} such that Pr_{x ~ U({0,1}^n)}[h(x) != f(x)] <= epsilon? In the strongest intended form, the learner is strictly proper, meaning h is also a size-s decision tree; however, the paper notes that this question remains open even in the weaker properness model where h may be an arbitrary-size decision tree.

Under PAC learning of Boolean functions over {0,1}^n under the uniform distribution with membership queries, let f:{0,1}^n→{0,1} be an unknown size-s decision tree. Consider a top-down proper-learning strategy that, at each recursive step, chooses the next split by searching only among the top-k most influential variables of the current restricted function. Blanc et al. (2021) show that taking the same k = polylog(s) for all log s levels is enough to construct an accurate tree, with resulting runtime s^{O(log log s)}. Is adaptive greediness sufficient to improve this to polynomial time—specifically, can one take k = polylog(s) for the first (log s)/(log log s) levels and then k = O(1) for the remaining log s - (log s)/(log log s) levels, while still outputting a decision-tree hypothesis h with Pr_{x∼{0,1}^n}[h(x) ≠ f(x)] ≤ ε, thereby yielding a poly(n,s,1/ε)-time proper learner?

In the PAC model under the uniform distribution with membership queries, let f:{0,1}^n→{0,1} be an unknown size-s decision tree target, and seek a proper decision tree hypothesis h satisfying Pr_{x∼{0,1}^n}[h(x)≠f(x)]≤ε. Can one strengthen the structural step behind Blanc et al. (2021) so that, for each restricted subproblem f_π arising in the recursive/dynamic-programming view, one can determine the variables queried on the first ℓ = Θ(log log s) levels by examining only polylog(s) candidate multi-level split choices at that stage—possibly via a splitting criterion slightly higher-order than influence—thereby yielding a poly(n,s,1/ε)-time proper learning algorithm for size-s decision trees? ([proceedings.mlr.press](https://proceedings.mlr.press/v178/open-problem-blanc22a/open-problem-blanc22a.pdf))

In the uniform-distribution membership-query setting for properly learning an unknown size-s decision tree f:{0,1}^n→{0,1} to error ε, can the dynamic-programming approach be strengthened so that, for every restricted subproblem f_π, one can pin down the queried variables on the first ℓ=Θ(log log s) levels while exploring only polylog(s) candidate depth-ℓ query patterns at each step—possibly by replacing plain influence with a slightly higher-order splitting criterion when influence alone does not isolate such a small set of near-optimal choices—thereby yielding a poly(n,s,1/ε)-time proper learning algorithm?

Does there exist a poly(n, s, 1/epsilon)-time proper PAC learning algorithm, under the uniform distribution on {0,1}^n, for monotone size-s decision-tree targets f : {0,1}^n -> {0,1}? Here monotone means that x <= x' coordinatewise implies f(x) <= f(x'), and proper means the algorithm outputs a decision-tree hypothesis h with Pr_{x~{0,1}^n}[h(x) != f(x)] <= epsilon. Ideally, can such a learner use only uniformly random labeled examples and no membership queries?

In the PAC-with-membership-queries model under the uniform distribution on {0,1}^n, is there a poly(n,s,1/ε)-time algorithm that, given query access to an unknown size-s decision tree f:{0,1}^n→{0,1}, outputs a hypothesis h from one of the more expressive but still decision-tree-like classes singled out in the paper—namely, a branching program (decision DAG) or a generalized decision tree whose internal nodes test halfspaces rather than singleton variables—such that Pr_{x∼{0,1}^n}[h(x)≠f(x)]≤ε?

Wegner’s Conjecture. For all integers k ≥ 1 and D ≥ 3, let χ_k(D) and ω_k(D) denote, respectively, the maximums over all graphs G with maximum degree Δ(G) ≤ D of χ(G^k) and ω(G^k), where G^k is the graph obtained from G by joining every pair of vertices whose distance in G is at most k. Is it true that χ_k(D) = ω_k(D) for every k and D? citeturn12view0turn15view0

For each integer t, does there exist a constant Delta_t such that every finite simple graph G with maximum degree Delta(G) >= Delta_t satisfies omega(G^2) <= Delta(G)^2 - t, where G^2 is the graph on V(G) in which two vertices are adjacent whenever their distance in G is at most 2? Moreover, can this conclusion be strengthened to any of the following bounds on the square of G: chi(G^2) <= Delta(G)^2 - t, chi_l(G^2) <= Delta(G)^2 - t, chi_p(G^2) <= Delta(G)^2 - t, or even chi_AT(G^2) <= Delta(G)^2 - t?

Is Wegner's Planar Graph Conjecture true? Namely, for every planar graph G, if Delta := Delta(G) and G^2 denotes the graph obtained from G by joining every pair of vertices whose distance in G is at most 2, must the square of G satisfy chi(G^2) <= 7 when Delta = 3, chi(G^2) <= Delta + 5 when 4 <= Delta <= 7, and chi(G^2) <= floor(3 Delta / 2) + 1 when Delta >= 8?

Let 𝒢 be a minor-closed class of finite graphs such that K3,t is not in 𝒢 for some positive integer t. Is it true that there exists an integer Δ0 = Δ0(𝒢) such that every graph H ∈ 𝒢 with maximum degree Δ(H) ≥ Δ0 satisfies χ(H^2) ≤ χ_ℓ(H^2) ≤ ⌊3Δ(H)/2⌋ + 1, where H^2 is the square of H (that is, two vertices are adjacent in H^2 exactly when their distance in H is at most 2) and χ_ℓ denotes list chromatic number?

The paper actually asks the following two-part open problem: Do there exist integers D1 and D2 such that, for every finite simple graph G, (i) if G is 2-degenerate and Delta(G) >= D1, then chi(G^2) <= (5/2)Delta(G); and, more generally, (ii) if mad(G) < 4 and Delta(G) >= D2, then chi(G^2) <= (5/2)Delta(G)? Here G^2 is the square of G, obtained by joining pairs of vertices at distance at most 2 in G, chi(G^2) is its chromatic number, and mad(G) := max_{H subseteq G, |V(H)| >= 1} 2|E(H)|/|V(H)|.

Let G be a graph with maximum degree Delta = Delta(G). Is it true that the strong edge-chromatic number chi_s(G)—that is, the minimum number of colors in an edge-coloring of G such that any two edges receive distinct colors whenever they share an endpoint or whenever they each share an endpoint with the same edge—always satisfies chi_s(G) <= 5 Delta^2 / 4 when Delta is even, and chi_s(G) <= (5 Delta^2 - 2 Delta + 1) / 4 when Delta is odd? ([combinatorics.org](https://www.combinatorics.org/ojs/index.php/eljc/article/download/ds25/pdf/))

Is the following Brualdi–Quinn conjecture true: for every bipartite graph G with parts A and B, if χ_s(G) denotes the minimum number of colors in an edge-coloring of G such that any two edges that share an endpoint, or that each share an endpoint with a common edge, receive distinct colors, and if Δ_A := max{d_G(a) : a ∈ A} and Δ_B := max{d_G(b) : b ∈ B}, then must χ_s(G) satisfy χ_s(G) ≤ Δ_AΔ_B? ([combinatorics.org](https://www.combinatorics.org/ojs/index.php/eljc/article/download/ds25/pdf/))

Is it true that every graph G with no 5-cycle satisfies χ_s(G) ≤ Δ(G)^2, where χ_s(G) denotes the minimum number of colors in a strong edge-coloring of G, that is, an edge-coloring in which any two edges at distance at most 2 receive distinct colors?

Is it true that every bipartite graph G with maximum degree at most 3 and no 4-cycles satisfies χ_s(G) ≤ 7, where χ_s(G) denotes the minimum number of colors in a strong edge-coloring of G (equivalently, an edge-coloring in which every two edges at distance at most 2 receive distinct colors)?

Does every bridgeless graph G with maximum degree at most 3, other than the Wagner graph and the graph formed from the complete bipartite graph K_{3,3} by subdividing one edge, satisfy χ_s(G) ≤ 9, where χ_s(G) denotes the minimum number of colors in a strong edge-coloring of G, i.e. an edge-coloring in which any two edges at distance at most 2 receive distinct colors? ([combinatorics.org](https://www.combinatorics.org/ojs/index.php/eljc/article/download/ds25/pdf/))

Is the following two-part conjecture true? Let G be a subcubic graph, that is, a graph with maximum degree at most 3, and let chi'_s(G) denote the strong chromatic index of G. (i) If G is bridgeless and |V(G)| >= 13, then chi'_s(G) <= 8. (ii) If G has girth at least 5, then chi'_s(G) <= 7.

Does there exist a universal constant C such that every planar graph G with girth g = g(G) >= 5 and maximum degree Δ = Δ(G) satisfies χ_s(G) <= ceil(2g(Δ - 1)/(g - 1)) + C, where χ_s(G) denotes the strong edge-chromatic number of G (the minimum number of colors in an edge-coloring in which any two edges at distance at most 2 receive distinct colors)?

Is the Total Coloring Conjecture true: for every graph G, if χ''(G) denotes the minimum number of colors in a total coloring of G (a coloring of V(G) ∪ E(G) in which adjacent vertices, adjacent edges, and incident vertex-edge pairs receive distinct colors), then must χ''(G) ≤ Δ(G) + 2, where Δ(G) is the maximum degree of G?

Does every graph G with maximum degree Δ(G)=Δ satisfy λ_{2,1}(G) <= Δ^2, where λ_{2,1}(G) is the minimum span of an L(2,1)-labeling of G, that is, an assignment f:V(G) to the positive integers such that |f(u)-f(v)| >= 2 whenever uv is an edge of G and f(u) != f(v) whenever dist_G(u,v)=2?

Fix integers k ≥ 3 and Δ ≥ 3, and let D_{k,Δ} := Σ_{i=1}^k Δ(Δ-1)^(i-1) = Δ((Δ-1)^k-1)/(Δ-2), the largest possible degree of a vertex in the k-th power of a graph of maximum degree Δ. If G^k denotes the graph obtained from a connected graph G by joining every pair of vertices whose distance in G is at most k, then for all but finitely many connected graphs G with Δ(G) = Δ, must one have χℓ(G^k) ≤ D_{k,Δ} + 1 - k, and likewise χp(G^k) ≤ D_{k,Δ} + 1 - k, where χp is the paint number (online list chromatic number)? ([combinatorics.org](https://www.combinatorics.org/ojs/index.php/eljc/article/download/ds25/pdf/))

Let X be a complex projective variety with mild singularities (for example, klt singularities), and let ψ: X ⇢ Y be a maximal rationally connected fibration, i.e. an almost holomorphic rational map to a projective variety Y whose general fibers are rationally connected and such that no horizontal rational curve passes through a very general point of X. Since the base Y is only defined up to birational equivalence and may be replaced by a smooth birational model, when can one choose this birational model so that ψ is represented by a holomorphic morphism X → Y rather than only by an almost holomorphic rational map?

Let X be a compact complex Kähler manifold. Suppose X admits a Kähler metric g such that its holomorphic sectional curvature HSC_g(v)=R_g(v,\bar v,v,\bar v)/|v|_g^4 is strictly positive for every point p in X and every nonzero tangent vector v in T_{X,p}. Must X be a smooth complex projective variety and rationally connected, i.e. must any two points of X be connected by a rational curve?

Let X be a compact complex Kähler manifold, and let g be a Kähler metric on X whose holomorphic sectional curvature is semi-positive, i.e. HSC_g(v) >= 0 for every nonzero v in T_{X,p} and every p in X. For each p in X, let V_flat,p := {v in T_{X,p} : R_g(v, x, y, z-bar) = 0 for all x, y, z in T_{X,p}}, and define ntf(X, g) := dim X - inf_{p in X} dim V_flat,p. If ntf(X, g) = dim X, must H^0(X, Ω_X^q) = 0 for every integer q with 1 <= q <= dim X, and is X necessarily projective?

Let (X, g) be a compact Kähler manifold over C with semi-positive holomorphic sectional curvature. Does the full analogue of Theorem 3.4 hold for (X, g)? Equivalently in expanded form: must there exist a surjective locally trivial holomorphic map phi: X -> Y that serves as a maximal rationally connected (MRC) fibration, with rationally connected fiber F and flat base Y, such that X_univ is biholomorphic to C^m x F for m = dim Y, X is obtained from this product via a representation rho: pi_1(Y) -> Aut(F), and the corresponding fundamental-group and metric-splitting conclusions of Theorem 3.4 also remain valid in the compact Kähler setting? ([numdam.org](https://www.numdam.org/item/10.5802/afst.1712.pdf))

Let (X, g) be a compact Kähler manifold with semi-positive holomorphic sectional curvature. Is the fundamental group π1(X) an extension of a finite group by ℤ^{⊕2m} for some integer m ≥ 0? Moreover, after passing to a finite étale cover X* → X, let α : X* → Alb(X*) be the Albanese map and let F be a fiber of α. Does F admit a Kähler metric g_F such that ntf(F, g_F) = dim F, where ntf(M, h) := dim M − inf_{p∈M} dim V_flat,p and V_flat,p := {v ∈ T_{M,p} : R_h(v, x, y, z-bar) = 0 for all x, y, z ∈ T_{M,p}}? If so, is F projective and rationally connected? ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2211.09153))

Let (X,g) be a compact Kähler manifold over C with semi-positive (or semi-negative) holomorphic sectional curvature, and let V subset T_X denote the distribution of "appropriate" truly flat tangent vectors, where a tangent vector v in T_{X,p} is truly flat if R_g(v,x,y,bar z)=0 for all x,y,z in T_{X,p}. Does V define an integrable holomorphic subbundle of T_X, and can one find a holomorphic subbundle W subset T_X such that T_X isomorphic to W direct-sum V? Moreover, in the semi-positive case, can one obtain a holomorphic maximal rationally connected fibration f: X -> Y with W = T_{X/Y}; and in the semi-negative case, can one obtain the Iitaka fibration f: X -> Z associated with K_X with V = T_{X/Z}?

In the category of smooth complex projective varieties, where semi-positive or positive holomorphic sectional curvature means the existence of a Kähler metric whose holomorphic sectional curvature is everywhere nonnegative or everywhere positive, respectively, do blow-ups of Hirzebruch surfaces admit positive holomorphic sectional curvature? More generally, in fixed dimension—especially dimensions 2 and 3—can one classify all smooth projective varieties admitting semi-positive or positive holomorphic sectional curvature, and can one identify an algebro-geometric notion that serves as the analog of semi-positive or positive holomorphic sectional curvature?

Let X be a smooth complex projective variety such that its tangent bundle T_X is pseudo-effective in the sense of Proposition 4.1; equivalently, there exists an ample line bundle A on X for which A⊗Sym^m(T_X) is generated by global sections at a general point for every integer m>=1. Let φ:X→Y be a holomorphic representative of the maximal rationally connected fibration of X, whose existence with Y smooth projective and φ smooth is provided by Theorem 4.2. Must φ be locally trivial as a holomorphic fibration; that is, after shrinking to sufficiently small analytic open sets U⊂Y, is φ^{-1}(U) isomorphic over U to U×F, where F is the fiber? ([numdam.org](https://www.numdam.org/item/10.5802/afst.1712.pdf))

Let X be a smooth complex projective rationally connected variety whose tangent bundle T_X is pseudo-effective in the sense that there exists an ample line bundle A on X such that A ⊗ Sym^m T_X is generically globally generated for every integer m > 0. Must the anticanonical divisor -K_X be big?

Let X be a compact Kähler manifold over C whose tangent bundle T_X is pseudo-effective in the singular-Hermitian sense used in Section 4. After replacing X by a suitable finite étale cover and again denoting the cover by X, consider its Albanese map alpha: X -> Alb(X), and let F be a fiber of alpha. Must the anti-canonical divisor -K_F be big, or at least must F be projective? Moreover, is alpha the maximal rationally connected fibration of X, i.e. an MRC fibration in the sense of Section 2?

Over \mathbb{C}, let \mathbb{F}_e be a Hirzebruch surface and let X be the blow-up of \mathbb{F}_e at four general points. Does the smooth projective surface X have pseudo-effective tangent bundle T_X? More generally, what can be said about the pseudo-effectivity of T_X when the blow-up centers on \mathbb{F}_e form a special configuration?

Let X and Y be smooth projective varieties over C, let ϕ:X⇢Y be an almost holomorphic rational map (i.e. its general fibers are compact), and let π:Γ→X be a resolution of the indeterminacy of ϕ, with induced morphism φ:Γ→Y. Assume that there exists an effective Q-divisor D on Γ such that (Γ,D) is klt and the Q-divisor -π_*(K_{Γ/Y}+D) on X is nef, where K_{Γ/Y}=K_Γ-φ^*K_Y. Without assuming that ϕ is an RC fibration, does this relative anti-canonical hypothesis imply a structure theorem analogous to the one known when the general fibers are rationally connected? In particular, after replacing Y by a smooth projective birational model Y', does there exist a holomorphic morphism f:X→Y' and a birational map μ:Y'⇢Y such that ϕ=μ∘f as rational maps?

Let X be a smooth projective variety over C with pseudo-effective anti-canonical divisor -K_X. What analogue of the nef anti-canonical structure theorem can be proved for such X? More specifically, does X admit a holomorphic maximal rationally connected fibration phi: X -> Y onto a smooth projective variety Y with numerically trivial canonical divisor K_Y, together with the kind of local triviality (and, in the nef case, universal-cover product structure) appearing in Theorem 5.1?

Let (X, Delta) be a projective klt pair with X smooth and -(K_X + Delta) nef. Does there exist an orbifold morphism in Campana's sense, rho:(X, Delta) -> (R, Delta_R), such that: (i) (R, Delta_R) is a klt pair with R smooth and c1(K_R + Delta_R)=0; (ii) the general orbifold fiber (X_r, Delta_{X_r}) is slope rationally connected; and (iii) for every sufficiently small analytic open set U subset R, there is an isomorphism of pairs over U, (rho^{-1}(U), Delta) ≅ (U, Delta_R|_U) × (X_r, Delta_{X_r}), where X_r is a general fiber of rho?

Let M be a manifold, let P(M) be the space of probability measures on M, and let V: P(M) -> P(TM) be a probability vector field satisfying pi_# V(mu) = mu. For the measure differential equation mu_dot = V[mu], understood weakly by d/dt int_M f dmu(t) = int_TM nabla_x f · v dV[mu(t)](x,v), can one, in the non-variational interpretation where probability vector fields have only an abelian-monoid structure rather than a Lie-algebra structure, explore control properties at the level of the associated flows instead of at the level of individual solutions, by using geometric control techniques?

For controlled versions of the heterogeneous N-agent system dot ξ_i = (1/N) Σ_{j=1}^N G(t, x_i, x_j, ξ_i, ξ_j), where x_i are fixed agent parameters (dot x_i = 0) and ξ_i is the state of agent i, how do the associated optimal control problems behave under the multiscale limiting procedures discussed around Figure 7—namely the passages from the particle description to the Liouville, Vlasov (mean-field), Euler (graph-limit, including the Riemann-sum/graphon viewpoint), and embedding representations? More specifically, in the spirit of Section 4.2, can one formulate the controls so that these passages yield nontrivial limiting controlled dynamics and meaningful convergence of the optimal control problems, rather than a degenerate limit in which the limiting control becomes ineffective? ([degruyterbrill.com](https://www.degruyterbrill.com/document/doi/10.1515/math-2022-0585/html))

For the deterministic finite-horizon multi-agent optimal control problems considered in the Kantorovich framework of reference [112] cited in Section 5.1—where admissible evolutions are represented by probability measures on the space of continuous trajectories, linked to the Eulerian and Lagrangian formulations via the superposition principle, and where equivalence and Γ-convergence results are already available under the corresponding convexity assumptions—can one define and characterize intrinsically sparse, or more generally parsimonious, admissible/optimal controls in that curve-space formulation, and establish necessary and sufficient optimality conditions for such optimal controls within the same framework?

Characterize the finite distributive lattices D for which there exists an SPS lattice L—that is, a finite slim planar semimodular lattice, equivalently a finite planar semimodular lattice with no sublattice isomorphic to M3—such that D is isomorphic to Con L, the congruence lattice of L.

Let B2 be the four-element Boolean lattice, and let D be a finite distributive lattice obtained as the glued sum of a finite distributive lattice D^h and B2, i.e. by identifying the top element of D^h with the bottom element of B2. A finite planar semimodular lattice L is called rectangular if its left and right boundary chains have unique doubly irreducible elements that are complementary, and L is a patch lattice if, in addition, its corners are dual atoms. Since the paper notes that a rectangular lattice is a patch lattice exactly when its congruence lattice has the form E glued-sum B2 for some finite distributive lattice E, what necessary and sufficient properties of D^h characterize exactly when there exists a finite patch lattice L such that Con L isomorphic to D? ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2303.00699))

Let k be finite, let S be the class of k-armed bandit instances μ=(μ1,…,μk) with arm means θ=(θ1,…,θk) and a unique best arm I*(μ)=argmax_{i∈[k]} θ_i, and suppose that at each round t a fixed-budget algorithm adaptively chooses an arm I_t∈[k] from the past history and observes an independent sample Y_{t,I_t}∼μ_{I_t}. After exactly n samples, the algorithm outputs a recommendation I_hat_n, and its error probability is p_{μ,n}=P_μ(I_hat_n≠I*(μ)). Does there exist a desirable natural, possibly stricter-than-consistent, class A of fixed-budget algorithms and a well-defined instance-dependent function Γ*_fb:S→R such that: (i) for every algorithm in A and every μ∈S, liminf_{n→∞} n/log(1/p_{μ,n}) ≥ Γ*_fb(μ); and (ii) there exists a single algorithm in A such that for every μ∈S, limsup_{n→∞} n/log(1/p_{μ,n}) ≤ Γ*_fb(μ)? Equivalently, does fixed-budget best-arm identification admit an exact instance-dependent asymptotic complexity within an appropriate restricted algorithm class? ([proceedings.mlr.press](https://proceedings.mlr.press/v178/open-problem-qin22a/open-problem-qin22a.pdf))

Let S be the class of bandit instances μ=(μ_1,...,μ_k) with finitely many arms and a unique best arm I^*(μ)=argmax_{i∈[k]} θ_i, where θ_i is the mean of μ_i. In the fixed-budget best-arm identification setting, an algorithm uses exactly n samples and then outputs an estimate \hat I_n; for an algorithm A, write p^A_{μ,n}=P_μ(\hat I_n ≠ I^*(μ)). Does there exist a fixed-budget algorithm A, distinct from the uniform-sampling algorithm, such that for every μ∈S, limsup_{n→∞} n/log(1/p^A_{μ,n}) ≤ limsup_{n→∞} n/log(1/p^{unif}_{μ,n})? ([proceedings.mlr.press](https://proceedings.mlr.press/v178/open-problem-qin22a/open-problem-qin22a.pdf))

Let mu=(mu_1,mu_2) be a two-armed Bernoulli bandit instance in S with a unique best arm I*(mu). A fixed-budget algorithm sequentially chooses arms based on past observations and, after exactly n samples, outputs a recommendation hat I_n; write p_{mu,n}=P_mu(hat I_n != I*(mu)). In the nearby non-adaptive large-deviations formulation, the oracle sampling proportion w*(mu) in Sigma_2 achieves Gamma_na^*(mu)=sup_{w in Sigma_2} inf_{nu in Alt(mu)} [w_1 KL(nu_1||mu_1)+w_2 KL(nu_2||mu_2)]^{-1}, but w*(mu) depends on the unknown Bernoulli means and so cannot be fixed a priori. Does there exist an adaptive fixed-budget algorithm that does not know mu_1 or mu_2 in advance and nevertheless, for every such two-armed Bernoulli instance mu, satisfies limsup_{n->infinity} n/log(1/p_{mu,n}) <= Gamma_na^*(mu), i.e. achieves the same asymptotically optimal fixed-budget performance as the oracle rule based on w*(mu)?

Let CTCS(n) be the continuous-time critical beta-splitting random tree on the ordered leaf set [n]={1,...,n}, in its original interval-splitting representation (so the order 1<...<n is the interval order, before the uniform random relabeling introduced later for exchangeability). For 1<=j<=n, let D_{n,j} be the height of leaf j, let D_n denote the height of a typical leaf, and let D_n^*=max_{1<=j<=n} D_{n,j}. Write mu:=1/zeta(2)=6/pi^2 and sigma^2:=2 zeta(3), so that D_n has the CLT and variance asymptotics stated in Theorem 2 and Theorem 3. Prove a quantitative upper-tail decorrelation estimate for leaves separated by order n^0.73 in the interval order; for example, show that for every fixed y_1,y_2 in R, sup_{1<=i<=n-ceil(n^0.73)} |P(D_{n,i}>(mu+mu^3 sigma^2/2)log n+y_1, D_{n,i+ceil(n^0.73)}>(mu+mu^3 sigma^2/2)log n+y_2) - P(D_n>(mu+mu^3 sigma^2/2)log n+y_1) P(D_n>(mu+mu^3 sigma^2/2)log n+y_2)| -> 0 as n->infinity, or establish an equivalent tail-association bound strong enough to justify the heuristic in §6.5 that the maximum height among about n^0.27 suitably separated leaves behaves as if these leaf heights were independent. Deduce from such a bound the dependence input needed for Open Problem 1, namely the conjecture that D_n^* ~ c log n in probability with c=1+mu+mu^3 sigma^2/2.

In the original interval-splitting construction of the critical beta-splitting model on [n]={1,2,...,n}, where a size-m interval splits into subintervals of sizes i and m-i with probability q(m,i)=m/[2 h_{m-1} i(m-i)] and, in continuous time, a size-m interval splits at rate h_{m-1}, do not apply the uniform random permutation of leaf labels used in Section 5.1. Let H_n(j) be the continuous-time height of the deterministically labeled leaf j in CTCS(n), and let h_n(j) be its hop-height in DTCS(n). Determine the label-sensitive tail behavior and, in particular, obtain asymptotic bounds on the association between the tail events {H_n(i)>t} and {H_n(i+⌊n^0.73⌋)>t}, uniformly for admissible i and for the relevant range of t, strong enough to justify the heuristic behind Open Problem 1 that D_n^*~c log n for the maximum height in CTCS(n); formulate the analogous label-sensitive dependence problem for h_n(j) in DTCS(n) in relation to Open Problem 7. ([storage.googleapis.com](https://storage.googleapis.com/arxiv-dataset/arxiv/arxiv/pdf/2303/2303.02529v2.pdf))

In the continuous-time critical beta-splitting random tree CTCS(n), each clade of size m >= 2 waits an Exponential(h_{m-1}) time and then splits into subclades of sizes i and m-i with probability q(m,i)=m/(2 h_{m-1} i (m-i)), where h_{m-1}=sum_{j=1}^{m-1} 1/j. Let D_n^* denote the height of CTCS(n), i.e. the maximum height over its n leaves. Prove the paper’s conjecture that, as n -> infinity, D_n^* ~ c log n in probability, and determine the constant c; namely c = 1 + μ + μ^3σ^2/2 = 1 + 6/pi^2 + 216 zeta(3)/pi^6 ≈ 1.878, where μ = 1/zeta(2) = 6/pi^2 and σ^2 = 2 zeta(3) are the constants from the CLT for the height D_n of a uniform random leaf in CTCS(n).

For the discrete-time critical beta-splitting tree DTCS(n), recursively constructed on the leaf set [n]={1,...,n} by splitting each clade of size m>=2 into subclades of sizes i and m-i with probability q(m,i)=m/[2 h_{m-1} i(m-i)] for 1<=i<=m-1, where h_{m-1}=sum_{j=1}^{m-1} 1/j, let L_n^* denote the tree height, i.e. the maximum number of edges on a path from the root to a leaf. Show that, as n->infinity, there exists a constant c such that L_n^*/(log n)^2 -> c in probability, and identify the constant c (with log denoting the natural logarithm). ([storage.googleapis.com](https://storage.googleapis.com/arxiv-dataset/arxiv/arxiv/pdf/2303/2303.02529v2.pdf))

Fix a finite rooted binary clade chi with i leaves; if chi is interpreted only up to shape, use the Figure 9 convention that left and right branches are not distinguished. In the discrete-time critical splitting tree DTCS(n), defined by recursively splitting each m-leaf clade into j and m-j leaves with probability q(m,j)=m/(2 h_{m-1} j (m-j)) for 1 <= j <= m-1, let N_n(chi) be the number of fringe clades whose induced subtree is isomorphic to chi. Let p(chi) denote the corresponding limit fringe probability, so that n^(-1) E[N_n(chi)] -> p(chi)/i. Prove that there exists a finite constant sigma^2(chi) such that n^(-1) Var(N_n(chi)) -> sigma^2(chi), and prove the corresponding central limit theorem, namely that (N_n(chi)-E[N_n(chi)])/sqrt(n) converges in distribution to Normal(0, sigma^2(chi)).

For n >= 2, consider the continuous-time critical beta-splitting tree CTCS(n) of Section 2: each extant clade of size m >= 2 splits independently at rate h_{m-1}:=sum_{k=1}^{m-1} 1/k, and when it splits it produces subclades of sizes i and m-i with probability q(m,i)=m/(2 h_{m-1} i (m-i)) for 1 <= i <= m-1. Let Lambda_n be the length of CTCS(n), i.e. the sum of all edge lengths, where each edge length is its time duration. Proposition 6 shows that E[Lambda_n]/n -> 6/pi^2. Prove that there exists a constant sigma^2 >= 0 such that Var(Lambda_n)/n -> sigma^2 as n -> infinity, and establish the associated central limit theorem (Lambda_n - E[Lambda_n]) / sqrt(n) => Normal(0, sigma^2). ([storage.googleapis.com](https://storage.googleapis.com/arxiv-dataset/arxiv/arxiv/pdf/2303/2303.02529v2.pdf))

For the discrete-time critical beta-splitting tree DTCS(n), defined recursively by splitting each clade of size m ≥ 2 into subclades of sizes i and m-i with probability q(m,i) = m/(2 h_{m-1} i(m-i)) for 1 ≤ i ≤ m-1, let χ range over finite rooted binary clade shapes, regarded up to left/right reflection, and let N_n(χ) be the number of clades in a realization of DTCS(n) having shape χ. Study the distributions of the following combinatorial clade-shape statistics: K_n := Σ_χ 1{N_n(χ) ≥ 1}, the number of distinct clade shapes present; the maximal leaf-size max{|χ| : N_n(χ) ≥ 2}, i.e. the size of the largest clade shape that appears more than once; and the minimal leaf-size min{|χ| : N_n(χ) = 0}, i.e. the size of the smallest clade shape absent from the realization (with a tie convention added only if one wants a unique extremal shape rather than just the extremal size).

Let X be the continuous-time harmonic descent chain on {1,2,3,...}, started at X_0=n, with absorbing state 1 and transition rates lambda_{m,i}=1/(m-i) for 1<=i<=m-1. For 1<=i<=n define a(n,i):=P_n(X_t=i for some t>=0). By Theorem 5, for each i>=2 the limit a(i):=lim_{n->infinity}a(n,i) exists and is given by a(i)=6 h_{i-1}/(pi^2 (i-1)), where h_{i-1}=sum_{r=1}^{i-1}1/r (and a(1)=1). Obtain explicit quantitative bounds for the error |a(n,i)-a(i)|, for 2<=i<=n, strong enough to measure how accurately the asymptotic fringe distribution approximates the fringe of DTCS(n).

Fix an integer i≥2 and a specific rooted binary clade χ with i leaves, in the critical beta-splitting discrete-time tree DTCS(n), where each m-leaf clade is recursively split into sizes j and m−j with probability q(m,j)=m/[2 h_{m−1} j(m−j)] and h_{m−1}=Σ_{k=1}^{m−1}1/k. Let N_n(χ) be the number of copies of χ that occur as clades in DTCS(n). Let p(χ) denote the asymptotic fringe probability that a uniformly chosen leaf belongs to a clade equal to χ (equivalently, p(χ)=a(i)·P(DTCS(i)=χ), with a(i)=6 h_{i−1}/[π^2(i−1)] from Theorem 5). Since n^{-1}E[N_n(χ)]→p(χ)/i, prove that there exists a finite constant σ^2(χ) such that n^{-1}Var(N_n(χ))→σ^2(χ) as n→∞, and prove the corresponding central limit theorem, namely (N_n(χ)-E[N_n(χ)])/√n ⇒ N(0,σ^2(χ)). ([storage.googleapis.com](https://storage.googleapis.com/arxiv-dataset/arxiv/arxiv/pdf/2303/2303.02529v2.pdf))

For finite observed tree sizes n, carry out a large-scale empirical comparison between real phylogenetic cladograms and numerically simulated DTCS(n) trees by evaluating descriptive tree-shape/balance statistics—at minimum including the balance statistic C(tree), defined as the average over leaves of the number of edges from the root to that leaf (which equals L_n in DTCS(n))—and determine how much, if at all, more elaborate biologically motivated models with fitted parameters improve the fit over this zero-parameter critical beta-splitting model.

For the discrete-time critical beta-splitting model DTCS(n) (beta = -1), in which each clade of size m >= 2 splits into daughter clades of sizes i and m-i with probability q(m,i) = [m/(2 h_{m-1})] * 1/[i(m-i)] and h_{m-1} = Σ_{j=1}^{m-1} 1/j, carry out, by direct simulation at matched leaf counts n, a much larger empirical comparison with rooted phylogenetic cladograms than the paper's initial small-scale studies: specifically, repeat the comparison of (i) split statistics underlying the observation that, among clades of size m, the median size of the smaller daughter clade scales roughly as m^(1/2), and (ii) fringe-distribution statistics given by the proportions of leaves lying in unlabelled clades of each shape (with left/right orientation ignored), as in Figure 9 for clade sizes 2 through 6; then extend the same empirical comparison to additional tree-balance/imbalance indices, in order to test how well this zero-parameter DTCS(n) model matches real phylogenetic tree data.

Fix a finite clade shape χ with i leaves, and let N_n(χ) denote the number of occurrences of χ as a fringe clade in the critical beta-splitting tree DTCS(n). If p(χ) is the asymptotic fringe probability that a distinguished leaf belongs to a clade of shape χ, so that n^{-1}E[N_n(χ)] → p(χ)/i as n → ∞, does there exist a constant σ^2(χ) such that n^{-1}Var(N_n(χ)) → σ^2(χ), and does the central limit theorem hold in the form (N_n(χ)-E[N_n(χ)])/√n ⇒ N(0,σ^2(χ))?

In the continuous-time critical splitting random tree model CTCS(n), viewed in the pruned rooted-tree representation and grown inductively from CTCS(n) to CTCS(n+1) by the following rule—choose a bud uniformly at random, move from the root toward that target bud, let a stop occur along that path at instantaneous rate 1/(current clade size), attach a new side-bud there with random left/right orientation if such a stop occurs before the target bud is reached, and otherwise extend the target bud by an independent Exponential(1) edge to form a bud-pair—does there exist a useful martingale, adapted to the natural filtration of the growth process (CTCS(m))_{m>=2}, that can be exploited to derive asymptotic results from this inductive construction?

For the discrete-time critical beta-splitting tree DTCS(n) on n>=2 leaves, where each m-leaf clade splits into subclades of sizes i and m-i with probability q(m,i)=m/(2 h_{m-1} i(m-i)) for 1<=i<=m-1 and h_{m-1}=sum_{k=1}^{m-1} 1/k, define the draw-height of a clade tree γ by dh(γ)=0 if γ is a leaf and dh(γ)=1+max{dh(γ_1),dh(γ_2)} if γ splits as γ→(γ_1,γ_2). Define the drawn length of its standard cladogram representation recursively by dl(γ_m)=dl(γ_i)+dl(γ_{m-i})+2+|dh(γ_{m-i})-dh(γ_i)| whenever γ_m splits as γ_m→(γ_i,γ_{m-i}), and set DL_n:=E[dl(DTCS(n))]. Is it true that DL_n has order n(log n)^4 as n→∞; equivalently, do there exist constants 0<c<C<∞ such that c n(log n)^4 <= DL_n <= C n(log n)^4 for all sufficiently large n? Here log denotes the natural logarithm.

In the discrete-time critical splitting tree DTCS(n), defined by recursively splitting each m-leaf clade into subclades of sizes i and m-i with probability q(m,i)=m/(2 h_{m-1} i(m-i)) for 1 <= i <= m-1, draw the tree as a standard cladogram with all leaves at level 0 and draw-height defined recursively by dh(leaf)=0 and dh(gamma)=1+max{dh(gamma_1),dh(gamma_2)} for each split gamma -> (gamma_1,gamma_2). For this drawn cladogram, characterize the width-profile process W_n(h), h >= 0, where W_n(h) is the number of vertical line segments crossing the interval (h,h+1). ([storage.googleapis.com](https://storage.googleapis.com/arxiv-dataset/arxiv/arxiv/pdf/2303/2303.02529v2.pdf))

For the discrete-time critical beta-splitting random tree DTCS(n), in which each clade of size m≥2 splits into clades of sizes i and m−i with probability q(m,i)=m/(2h_{m-1}i(m-i)) (1≤i≤m−1, h_{m-1}=∑_{r=1}^{m-1}1/r), let N_n(j) be the number of size-j clades that ever arise and define SS_n^(α):=∑_{j=2}^n N_n(j)j^α. Determine, as n→∞, a detailed asymptotic description of SS_n^(α) as a function of α, by proving and sharpening the regime-dependent behaviors indicated in the paper: for α<1, show that n^{-1}E[SS_n^(α)]→∑_{j≥2}a(j)j^{α-1} with a(j)=6h_{j-1}/(π^2(j−1)); for α=1, recover E[SS_n^(1)]∼n/(2ζ(2))log^2 n; for α=2, prove or refine the heuristic E[SS_n^(2)]≈n^2 log n; and identify precisely how the asymptotics change at the thresholds α=1 and α=2. ([storage.googleapis.com](https://storage.googleapis.com/arxiv-dataset/arxiv/arxiv/pdf/2303/2303.02529v2.pdf))

For the critical beta-splitting tree DTCS(n), in which each clade of size m ≥ 2 splits into subclades of sizes i and m-i with probability q(m,i) = [m/(2 h_{m-1})]/[i(m-i)] and h_{m-1} = sum_{r=1}^{m-1} 1/r, let F denote the asymptotic fringe tree/process, i.e. the local weak limit of DTCS(n) relative to a uniformly random leaf as n -> infinity. Determine an appropriate rescaling of this discrete fringe process and identify its scaling limit, making precise the paper's heuristic that the limiting object should be representable as a point process of branchpoint positions.

Let CTCS(∞) denote the infinite limit object associated with the critical beta-splitting model, where a size-m clade splits with probabilities q(m,i)=m/[2 h_{m-1} i(m-i)] for 1≤i≤m−1 and, in the continuous-time embedding CTCS(n), at rate h_{m-1}; equivalently, CTCS(∞) is the exchangeable partition-valued limit obtained from the consistent family (CTCS(n)) by cutting at each height t≥0. Are there discrete models that are superficially different from this critical beta-splitting model but whose limit object is nevertheless the same CTCS(∞) in distribution? ([storage.googleapis.com](https://storage.googleapis.com/arxiv-dataset/arxiv/arxiv/pdf/2303/2303.02529v2.pdf))

Using the delete-and-prune consistency of the family (CTCS(n))_{n≥1}, formalize the limit object CTCS(∞) as the exchangeable partition process Π(t) of N obtained by cutting at height t; define the asymptotic clade frequencies P_{t,ℓ} = lim_{n→∞} |Π(t)_ℓ ∩ [n]|/n and prove the exact paintbox description of Π(t), the fixed-t self-similar forest decomposition, and the exact tagged-clade law Y_t := -log P_{t,1}, namely that (Y_t)_{t≥0} is the subordinator with Lévy tail ψ∞[a,∞) = -log(1 - e^{-a}) (equivalently E[P_{t,1}^s] = exp(-t(ψ(s+1) - ψ(1))) for all t ≥ 0 and Re(s) > -1)); in particular, make precise that the same subordinator appears for finite n only through the heuristic approximation of the harmonic descent chain, whereas it becomes exact only in the n→∞ limit.

In the canonical inductive construction of the continuous-time critical splitting tree CTCS(n+1) from CTCS(n), suppose that as n -> infinity the probabilities of the three possible placements of the new bud converge to limits p↑, p→, and p↗, corresponding respectively to branch extension, side-bud addition, and the case in which a side-bud grows into a new branch with two terminal buds. Must p↑ = p↗, and if so can this equality be explained by a hidden symmetry of the limiting random tree shape?

Let G=(V,E,ω) be a connected weighted simple graph with ω:E→R_+, and let d_G be the induced geodesic metric on the finite vertex set V. Fix ε>0. An ε-net for G is a subset L⊂V such that: (i) for every v∈V there exists u∈L with d_G(v,u)≤ε, and (ii) for all distinct u,u'∈L one has d_G(u,u')>ε. Determine the optimal upper and lower bounds on |L| over all ε-nets L of (V,d_G).

Given a weighted simple graph G=(V,E,ω), let d_G be the induced geodesic distance on V, and fix ε>0. Devise an algorithm that outputs a subset L⊂V of landmarks forming an ε-net for the metric space (V,d_G)—that is, every vertex v∈V lies within distance ε of some u∈L, and every two distinct landmarks u,u'∈L satisfy d_G(u,u')>ε—such that, for the same graph G and radius ε, the algorithm uses fewer landmarks and has lower execution time than the existing greedy, iterative, and SPTpruning ε-net algorithms.

Fix a field k for persistent homology coefficients. Let G = (V, E, omega) be a connected weighted simple graph with positive edge weights, let d_G be the geodesic metric on V, let W = V, and let L subseteq V be an epsilon-net in (V, d_G), meaning that every v in V satisfies d_G(v, L) <= epsilon and every distinct l, l' in L satisfy d_G(l, l') > epsilon. For the filtered Dowker complex {Dow_alpha(W, L)}_{alpha >= 0}, where a simplex sigma subseteq L lies in Dow_alpha(W, L) iff there exists w in W with d_G(w, l) <= alpha for all l in sigma, determine epsilon > 0 and a rule for choosing the epsilon-net L so that the one-dimensional persistence diagram PD_1({Dow_alpha(W, L)}_{alpha >= 0}) has exactly genus(G) off-diagonal points counted with multiplicity, where genus(G) is the cardinality of a minimal system of cycles of G. Assuming such an epsilon-net L has been chosen, find a bound for the bottleneck distance d_B between PD_1({VR_alpha(G)}_{alpha >= 0}) and PD_1({Dow_alpha(W, L)}_{alpha >= 0}), where VR_alpha(G) is the Vietoris-Rips complex on (V, d_G), in terms of epsilon and the weighted lengths of cycles in G.

Let G=(V,E,omega) be a weighted simple graph whose induced geodesic distance d_G makes V a finite metric space, let W,L subseteq V, and for each alpha>=0 let Dow_alpha^G(W,L) be the Dowker complex on vertex set L consisting of simplices sigma subseteq L for which there exists w in W with d_G(w,l)<=alpha for every l in sigma. Let G'=(V,E,omega') have the same vertex set and edge set as G but a different weight function omega', and let Dow_bullet^G(W,L) and Dow_bullet^{G'}(W,L) denote the corresponding Dowker filtrations. Find a bound, in terms of ||omega-omega'||_infinity := sup_{e in E}|omega(e)-omega'(e)|, for the bottleneck distance between the persistence diagrams associated with these two Dowker filtrations. Furthermore, if L and L' are both epsilon-nets for G (for the same epsilon>=0) and W is fixed, find conditions on the landmark sets ensuring that, for a fixed common scale alpha>=0, the Dowker complexes Dow_alpha^G(W,L) and Dow_alpha^G(W,L') have the same homotopy type. ([archive.intlpress.com](https://archive.intlpress.com/site/pub/files/_fulltext/journals/joc/2023/0014/0004/JOC-2023-0014-0004-a008.pdf))

Let n,t be positive integers and let 1<=k<=n. Let A be the n x m binary matrix whose columns are exactly all nonzero vectors a in {0,1}^n of Hamming weight at most k, listed in any fixed order, so that m = sum_{r=1}^k binom(n,r). For independently uniform x,y in {0,1}^{n x t}, write x=(x_1^T,...,x_t^T) and y=(y_1^T,...,y_t^T) with x_j,y_j in {0,1}^n, and for each column a_i of A define m_i^A(x):=sum_{j=1}^t <a_i,x_j>_2, where <.,.>_2 is the inner product in GF(2)^n and the outer sum is taken in Z. Determine exactly the probability that m_i^A(x)=m_i^A(y) for every column a_i of A. ([archive.intlpress.com](https://archive.intlpress.com/site/pub/files/_fulltext/journals/joc/2023/0014/0004/JOC-2023-0014-0004-a008.pdf))

Let n,t be positive integers, let 1 <= m <= 2^n - 1, and let A = (a_1^T, ..., a_m^T) be an n x m binary matrix whose columns are pairwise distinct and nonzero. For x = (x_1^T, ..., x_t^T), y = (y_1^T, ..., y_t^T) in {0,1}^{n x t}, define m_i^A(x) := sum_{j=1}^t <a_i, x_j>_2, where <.,.>_2 is the inner product in GF(2) and the outer sum is taken in Z. If x and y are sampled uniformly at random from {0,1}^{n x t}, for which choices of A can one compute exactly the probability P[(m_i^A(x) = m_i^A(y)) for all i = 1,...,m], and for which choices of A can this probability be computed efficiently?

Let n,t be positive integers and let 1 <= m <= 2^n - 1. Let A = (a_1^T,...,a_m^T) be an n x m binary matrix whose columns a_i belong to {0,1}^n and are nonzero and pairwise distinct. For x = (x_1^T,...,x_t^T) and y = (y_1^T,...,y_t^T) sampled independently and uniformly from {0,1}^{n x t}, define, for each i = 1,...,m, m_i^A(x) := sum_{j=1}^t <a_i, x_j>_2, where <.,.>_2 is the inner product in GF(2)^n and the outer sum is taken in Z. What is the computational complexity of exactly computing P(m_i^A(x) = m_i^A(y) for all i = 1,...,m) as A varies? Equivalently, in the paper's wording: is this Computational Problem NP-complete for arbitrary A?

Let n and t be positive integers, let 1 <= m <= 2^n - 1, and let A = (a_1^T, ..., a_m^T) be an n x m binary matrix whose columns a_i in {0,1}^n are nonzero and pairwise distinct. For x = (x_1^T, ..., x_t^T) and y = (y_1^T, ..., y_t^T) in {0,1}^{n x t}, define m_i^A(x) = sum_{j=1}^t <a_i, x_j>_2, where < , >_2 denotes the inner product in GF(2)^n and the outer sum is taken in Z. If x and y are sampled independently and uniformly at random from {0,1}^{n x t}, for which choices of A can one approximate the probability that m_i^A(x) = m_i^A(y) for every i = 1, ..., m?

For an arbitrary 4-uniform hypergraph H = (V, E) with distinguished vertices s and t, define for each feasible cut S ⊆ V with s in S and t in V minus S the sets ∂_i(S) = {e ∈ E : min(|e ∩ S|, |e ∩ (V minus S)|) = i}. After the without-loss-of-generality normalization w1 = 1 (for w1 > 0), the cardinality-based hypergraph s-t cut problem is to minimize |∂_1(S)| + w2|∂_2(S)| over all such S. What is the computational complexity of this optimization problem for fixed penalty parameters w2 > 2?

Let H = (V, E) be a finite 4-uniform hypergraph with source vertex s and sink vertex t. For a bipartition {S, V \ S} with s in S and t in V \ S, define ∂i(S) = {e in E : min(|e ∩ S|, |e ∩ (V \ S)|) = i}. What is the computational complexity of solving the optimization problem min{|∂1(S)| : S ⊆ V, s in S, t in V \ S, and ∂2(S) = empty set}? In other words, is the No-Even-Split 4-uniform s-t cut problem polynomial-time solvable, or is it NP-hard?

Given a directed acyclic graph G=(V,E) and a nonnegative integer k, does there exist a complete edge-elimination sequence of total cost at most k, where each step chooses an edge (i,j) in E and either front-eliminates it by adding edges from i to every successor of j, deleting j if (i,j) is its only in-edge, at cost equal to the number of successors of j, or back-eliminates it by adding edges from every predecessor of i to j, deleting i if (i,j) is its only out-edge, at cost equal to the number of predecessors of i, with front-elimination allowed only when j has a nonempty successor set and back-elimination allowed only when i has a nonempty predecessor set, and where complete means that the process ends in the bipartite DAG representing the Jacobian matrix of the underlying numerical program?

In the purely structural vertex-elimination formulation arising from Jacobian accumulation, given a directed acyclic graph G = (V, E) and a nonnegative integer k, does there exist a complete vertex-elimination sequence of total cost at most k, where total cost is the sum of step costs, and where at each step in the current DAG H = (W, F) one may eliminate a vertex j only if it has nonempty predecessor and successor sets P_H(j) = {i ∈ W : (i, j) ∈ F} and S_H(j) = {l ∈ W : (j, l) ∈ F}, replacing H by H - j = (W \ {j}, F ∪ {(i, l) : i ∈ P_H(j), l ∈ S_H(j)}) and paying cost |P_H(j)|·|S_H(j)|?

Let G = (V, E) be the directed acyclic graph induced by evaluating a numerical program y = F(x), where the vertices are topologically ordered and decompose as V = (X, Z, Y) with X = {1, ..., n} the source vertices representing the persistent inputs x in R^n, Z the intermediate vertices, and Y the sinks. Assuming unit cost for each elemental function evaluation Fj, and given integers M >= n and O >= 0, can G be reversed within persistent memory of size less than or equal to M and computational cost less than or equal to O? ([archive.intlpress.com](https://archive.intlpress.com/site/pub/files/_fulltext/journals/joc/2023/0014/0004/JOC-2023-0014-0004-a008.pdf))

Let M ∈ R^(n×n) satisfy ρ(M)=λ<1, and suppose M is partitioned into an ℓ×ℓ block matrix (M_ij)_(i,j=1)^ℓ. Let δ=(δ_ji) ∈ N^(ℓ×ℓ) satisfy δ_ii=0 and 0 ≤ δ_ji ≤ k for all i,j, and set κ := max_{i,j} δ_{ij}. Define asynchronous iterates by x̃_i^(t+1) = Σ_(j=1)^ℓ M_ij x̃_j^(t-δ_ji), and let M(δ):R^((κ+1)n)→R^((κ+1)n) be the corresponding history-update operator sending (x̃^(κ),…,x̃^(0)) to (x̃^(κ+1),…,x̃^(1)). Is it always true that ρ(M(δ)) ≤ λ^(1/(k+1))? If not, does there exist a function f:(0,1)×N→(0,1) such that, for every choice of n, ℓ, M, and δ satisfying these hypotheses, one still has ρ(M(δ)) ≤ f(λ,k)? ([archive.intlpress.com](https://archive.intlpress.com/site/pub/files/_fulltext/journals/joc/2023/0014/0004/JOC-2023-0014-0004-a008.pdf))

Let G = (V, E) be a graph and let k ≥ 1. A zero-forcing move from a blue set S ⊆ V colors a vertex v ∈ V \ S blue if there exists s ∈ S with N(s) \ S = {v}; a set Z ⊆ V is a zero-forcing set if some sequence of zero-forcing moves colors all vertices of G. Following Definition 7.3, call Z an (n − k)-contingent zero-forcing set if for every edge set E' ⊆ E with |E'| ≤ k, Z is a zero-forcing set of G' = (V, E \ E'). For graphs with few cycles, and separately for sparse graphs with large diameter, is there a structural characterization of the (n − k)-contingent zero-forcing sets of minimum cardinality? ([archive.intlpress.com](https://archive.intlpress.com/site/pub/files/_fulltext/journals/joc/2023/0014/0004/JOC-2023-0014-0004-a008.pdf))

Given a graph G = (V,E) from one of the two classes named in the paper—either a graph with few cycles or a sparse graph with large diameter—and a nonnegative integer k, is there an efficient algorithm to determine a minimum-cardinality subset Z ⊆ V such that, for every edge set E' ⊆ E with |E'| ≤ k, starting from Z colored blue and repeatedly applying the zero-forcing rule that a blue vertex with exactly one nonblue neighbor forces that neighbor blue, all vertices of G' = (V, E\E') become blue?

For a given integer k≥1 and a graph G=(V,E), call Z⊆V an (n-k)-contingent zero-forcing set if, for every edge set E'⊆E with |E'|≤k, the set Z is a zero-forcing set of G'=(V,E\E'), where 'zero forcing' means that, starting with Z colored blue, one may repeatedly color any vertex that is the unique uncolored neighbor of a blue vertex until no more such moves are possible. When G ranges over graphs exhibiting structural properties characteristic of power grids, what is the typical size, as a function of |V| and |E|, of a minimum (n-k)-contingent zero-forcing set?

Over C, let V_1,...,V_k be finite-dimensional vector spaces of dimensions n_1,...,n_k, and let d_1,...,d_k be non-negative integers. Let X = V_{d_1,...,d_k} be the image of the Segre-Veronese embedding v_{d_1,...,d_k}: P V_1 × ··· × P V_k → P(S^{d_1}V_1 ⊗ ··· ⊗ S^{d_k}V_k). For each integer r ≥ 1, classify all tuples (n_1,...,n_k; d_1,...,d_k; r) for which the secant variety σ_r(X) is defective, i.e. dim σ_r(X) < min{r dim X + r - 1, dim(S^{d_1}V_1 ⊗ ··· ⊗ S^{d_k}V_k) - 1}, and determine dim σ_r(X) in every defective case.

Let X be a product of projective spaces over the complex numbers, and let L be a line bundle on X. Classify those line bundles L for which there exists an integer r >= 1 and a zero-dimensional scheme Y ⊆ X consisting of r double points supported at general points of X such that Y does not impose independent conditions on L, i.e. dim H^0(I_Y ⊗ L) != max{dim H^0(L) - deg(Y), 0}. More generally, ask the same classification for interesting classes of varieties.

Working over C, let X be a variety, let L be a line bundle on X, and let r >= 1. Determine whether there exists a zero-dimensional subscheme Z ⊆ X that is the union of r pairwise disjoint degree-2 subschemes (equivalently, deg(Z)=2r and deg(Z_red)=r) such that the reduced subscheme Z_red imposes independent conditions on L, namely dim H^0(X, I_{Z_red} ⊗ L)=max{dim H^0(X,L)-r,0}, while Z itself does not impose independent conditions on L, i.e. dim H^0(X, I_Z ⊗ L) > max{dim H^0(X,L)-2r,0}?

Working over C, let V be a finite-dimensional vector space and let d ≥ 1. For a form f ∈ S^dV (identified with a homogeneous polynomial of degree d on V*), let Z ⊂ P(V) be a 0-dimensional scheme apolar to f, meaning that its defining ideal satisfies I_Z ⊂ Ann(f) ⊂ Sym(V*). Assume Z is minimal, in the sense that deg(Z) = cR_{ν_d(P(V))}(f), i.e. Z realizes the cactus rank of f with respect to the degree-d Veronese embedding ν_d(P(V)) ⊂ P(S^dV). Must the Castelnuovo–Mumford regularity of Z satisfy reg(Z) ≤ d?

Working over C, fix a finite-dimensional vector space V and an integer d ≥ 0. For a homogeneous degree-d form f ∈ S^dV, let X ⊆ P(V) be a 0-dimensional scheme apolar to f, meaning I_X ⊆ Ann(f) ⊆ Sym(V*), and assume that X is irredundant (equivalently, non-redundant in the paper’s terminology), i.e. no proper subscheme X' ⊊ X is still apolar to f. What is the maximum possible Castelnuovo-Mumford regularity reg(X) of such an X?

Working over C, let V be a finite-dimensional vector space and let f in S^d V, viewed as a homogeneous polynomial of degree d on V*. If X is the zero-dimensional scheme in P(V) associated, in the technical sense used in BJMR18, to a generalized additive decomposition of minimal length of f, namely to an expression f = sum_{i=1}^s l_i^{d-k_i} g_i with deg(g_i) = k_i, gcd(g_i, l_i) = 1, and l_1, ..., l_s distinct, where the length is deg(X), must the Castelnuovo-Mumford regularity satisfy reg(X) <= d? More generally, for which forms f does there exist a generalized additive decomposition whose associated zero-dimensional scheme has low Castelnuovo-Mumford regularity?

Let X ⊂ PV be a non-degenerate projective variety over C, and for each integer r ≥ 3 let σ_r(X) denote the r-th secant variety, i.e. the Zariski closure of the locus of points of X-rank at most r. Find general lower bounds for the projective degree deg(σ_r(X)) of these higher secant varieties, in a way that extends to r ≥ 3 the second-secant lower-bound perspective recalled immediately before Problem 7, namely the [CR06]-type bound deg(σ_2(X)) ≥ binom(c+2,2) when c = codim σ_2(X).

Working over ℂ, let X ⊂ P(V) be a non-degenerate projective variety and let σ_r(X) denote its r-th secant variety. Classify varieties X of small dimension for which σ_2(X) and/or σ_3(X) has minimal degree; in the case r = 2, this means that if c = codim σ_2(X), then deg(σ_2(X)) attains the lower bound (c+2 choose 2). More generally, for a fixed integer r ≥ 2, construct projective varieties X such that σ_r(X) is a hypersurface, i.e. codim σ_r(X) = 1, of the smallest possible degree.

Work over C. Let V be a complex vector space with dim V = n+1, and fix d. For a homogeneous form f ∈ S^dV, let X_f ⊂ PV be its eigenscheme, defined by the condition ∇f(v) ∧ v = 0; equivalently, in coordinates x_0, ..., x_n on V, X_f is cut out by the 2×2 minors of the matrix whose first row is x_0, ..., x_n and whose second row is ∂_0 f, ..., ∂_n f. Let D_{n,d} be the integer such that, for generic f, X_f is a reduced 0-dimensional scheme of D_{n,d} distinct points, and, more strongly, whenever X_f is finite one has deg(X_f) = D_{n,d}. Define E_{n,d} ⊂ (PV)^(·D_{n,d}) to be the locus of unordered D_{n,d}-point configurations that occur as X_f for some f ∈ S^dV. Determine the equations for E_{n,d}, where 'equations' is understood in the broad sense of Zariski-closed conditions cutting out the locus of eigenconfigurations arising from degree-d symmetric tensors.

Over \mathbb{C}, fix a vector space V with dim V = n+1 and an integer d >= 2. For a symmetric tensor f in S^dV, viewed as a degree-d homogeneous polynomial, let X_f \subseteq \mathbf{P}(V) be its eigenscheme, defined by \nabla f(v) \wedge v = 0 (equivalently, by the 2 x 2 minors of \begin{pmatrix}x_0&\cdots&x_n\\ \partial_0 f&\cdots&\partial_n f\end{pmatrix}). Assume that X_f is finite and non-reduced. Which integers can occur as the scheme-theoretic degrees (lengths) of the irreducible components of X_f, and which 0-dimensional schemes can occur as irreducible components of such eigenschemes?

Fix integers n >= 1 and d >= 2, let V be a complex vector space with dim V = n+1, and use the identification V ≅ V* from the quadratic-form/inner-product setup of Part 2. For a tensor T in V^{⊗ d} and each k = 1, ..., d, let X_T^k be its k-th eigenscheme in PV, namely the 0-dimensional scheme of projective points [v] such that contracting T against v in every tensor factor except the k-th gives a scalar multiple of v. Let D_{n,d} be the degree/length of a finite eigenscheme (D_{n,d} = ((d-1)^{n+1}-1)/(d-2) for d > 2, and D_{n,2} = n+1), and define EC_{n,d} ⊂ (Hilb_{D_{n,d}}(PV))^d to be the locus of d-tuples (X_1, ..., X_d) for which there exists T in V^{⊗ d} with X_i = X_T^i for all i. Determine the dimension and defining equations of EC_{n,d}.

Let V1,...,Vd be real inner-product spaces with dim(Vi)=ni+1, and let S_{n1,...,nd} denote the affine cone over the Segre variety of rank-one tensors in P(V1 ⊗ ··· ⊗ Vd). Write c(n1,...,nd)=EDdeg(S_{n1,...,nd}), equivalently the generic number of singular d-tuples of a tensor of this format, i.e. the coefficient of h1^n1 ··· hd^nd in Prod_{k=1}^d (((Sum_{i != k} hi)^(n_k+1) - h_k^(n_k+1)) / ((Sum_{i != k} hi) - h_k)). Does there exist a tensor T ∈ V1 ⊗ ··· ⊗ Vd such that all c(n1,...,nd) critical points of dist_{S_{n1,...,nd}}(-,T) are defined over R?

Fix real inner-product spaces V_1,...,V_d with dim V_i = n_i + 1, and let S_{n_1,...,n_d} be the affine cone over the Segre variety of rank-one tensors in P(V_1 \otimes ... \otimes V_d). Call T in V_1 \otimes ... \otimes V_d a probability tensor if the sum of its entries is 1. For such a tensor T, consider the affine Euclidean distance problem from T to the variety of rank-one probability tensors S_{n_1,...,n_d} \cap {sum of entries = 1}; for generic T this problem has aEDdeg(S_{n_1,...,n_d}) complex critical points. As T varies over probability tensors, which integers can occur as the number of these critical points whose entries are real?

For each integer d >= 1, let v_d(P^1) ⊂ P(S^d C^2) ≅ P^d be the degree-d Veronese image of P^1, and let sigma_2(v_d(P^1)) be its second secant variety, i.e. the Zariski closure of the points of v_d(P^1)-rank at most 2. Using the Frobenius inner product on S^d C^2 induced from a real form and a positive-definite quadratic form as in §2.4, determine the ordinary Euclidean distance degree of the affine cone over sigma_2(v_d(P^1)); equivalently, determine the number of complex critical points of the squared distance from a generic degree-d binary form to that cone.

Working over C in the homogeneous setting, let (f_n)_{n in N} be a p-family with f_n in S^{d_n} C^{N_n}, where d_n and N_n are polynomially bounded in n. Let VWaring, VChow, and VBP be the classes of such p-families for which, respectively, the Waring rank R_V(f_n) (rank with respect to the Veronese variety), the Chow rank R_Ch(f_n) (rank with respect to the Chow variety Ch_{N,d} of products of d linear forms), and the iterated matrix multiplication complexity imm_C(f_n) are polynomially bounded in n, where imm_C(f) is the least r such that f = M_1 ... M_d with M_1 in C^N tensor Mat_{1xr}, M_j in C^N tensor Mat_{rxr} for 2 <= j <= d-1, and M_d in C^N tensor Mat_{rx1}. Define the corresponding border classes by replacing each measure with its border/semi-continuous analogue, in particular border imm_C(f) = min{r : f = lim_{epsilon -> 0} f_epsilon with imm_C(f_epsilon) <= r}. For each C in {VWaring, VChow, VBP}, is C equal to its corresponding border class?

Over C, in the homogeneous setting, let a p-family be a sequence (f_n)_{n∈N} with f_n ∈ S^{d_n} C^{N_n}, where d_n and N_n are polynomially bounded in n. Let the Waring class consist of those p-families whose Waring rank with respect to the Veronese variety is polynomially bounded, and let the border Chow class consist of those p-families whose border Chow rank with respect to the Chow variety Ch_{N,d} = {ℓ_1⋯ℓ_d : ℓ_i ∈ S^1 C^N} is polynomially bounded. Is the Waring class contained in the border Chow class? More modestly, for every homogeneous polynomial f ∈ S^d C^N, can one prove a non-trivial upper bound for the ordinary Waring rank of f in terms of the border Chow rank of f? ([agates.mimuw.edu.pl](https://agates.mimuw.edu.pl/images/notes_and_reports/Gesmundo_Geometry_of_Tensors_Open_Problems_and_Research_Directions.pdf))

Over C, let V be a finite-dimensional vector space and let d ≥ 1. Identify S^dV with the space of degree-d homogeneous polynomials on V^*. For a homogeneous polynomial f in S^dV, define imm_C(f) to be the least integer r such that f can be written as f = M_1 ... M_d with M_1 in V ⊗ Mat_{1×r}(C), M_j in V ⊗ Mat_{r×r}(C) for 2 ≤ j ≤ d-1, and M_d in V ⊗ Mat_{r×1}(C). Equivalently, imm_C(f) is the minimum width of an algebraic branching program for f. Define IMM_{r,V} := { [f] in P(S^dV) : imm_C(f) ≤ r }. Determine defining equations for the projective variety IMM_{r,V} for small values of r and dim V.

For fixed integers d,r >= 1 and a finite-dimensional complex vector space V over C, let IMM_{r,V} := { [f] in P(S^d V) : imm_C(f) <= r }, where imm_C(f) is the smallest r for which f can be written as f = M_1 ... M_d with M_1 in V tensor Mat_{1 x r}, M_j in V tensor Mat_{r x r} for 2 <= j <= d-1, and M_d in V tensor Mat_{r x 1}.
