Treating IMM_{r,V} as a GL(V)-stable projective variety, implement the geometric complexity theory approach for IMM_{r,V} by determining the irreducible GL(V)-representation content of its ideal I(IMM_{r,V}) subset Sym(S^d V^*) and of its coordinate ring C[IMM_{r,V}], and by seeking multiplicity obstructions that can certify noncontainments involving IMM_{r,V} with other GL(V)-varieties arising from GL(V)-invariant (border) complexity measures.

Over C, let Γ=(v(Γ),e(Γ)) be a graph with v(Γ)={1,…,d}, let m=(m_e)_{e∈e(Γ)} be bond dimensions on the edges, and let T(Γ,m)∈W_1⊗⋯⊗W_d be the associated graph tensor, where W_j=⊗_{e∋j} C^{m_e}. For local dimensions n=(n_1,…,n_d), define TNS^{Γ,∘}_{m,n}={T∈C^{n_1}⊗⋯⊗C^{n_d} : T is a restriction of T(Γ,m)} and TNS^Γ_{m,n}=closure(TNS^{Γ,∘}_{m,n}), with closure taken in the Zariski topology (equivalently, the Euclidean topology). Determine polynomial equations in Sym((C^{n_1}⊗⋯⊗C^{n_d})^*) for the tensor network variety TNS^Γ_{m,n}; if necessary, restrict to particular classes of graphs Γ or to particular assignments of bond and local dimensions.

For integers d,m,n >= 1, with [n]={1,...,n}, let UTNS^{C_d}_{m,n} ⊆ (C^n)^{⊗ d} be the subvariety consisting of tensors of the form sum_{(i_1,...,i_d)∈[n]^d} tr(M_{i_1}⋯M_{i_d}) e_{i_1}⊗⋯⊗e_{i_d}, where M_1,...,M_n ∈ Mat_m(C); equivalently, this is the variety of uniform (translation-invariant) matrix product states of bond dimension m and local dimension n on the cycle graph C_d, with periodic boundary conditions. Study the geometry of UTNS^{C_d}_{m,n}; in particular, use properties of the trace algebra to systematically determine families of polynomial equations vanishing on UTNS^{C_d}_{m,n}.

Over C, let T∈V_1⊗⋯⊗V_d be an arbitrary tensor, let u_d(q)=∑_{i=1}^q e_i⊗⋯⊗e_i denote the rank-q unit tensor on d factors, and define Q(T)=max{q : T restricts to u_d(q)} and \underline{Q}(T)=max{q : T degenerates to u_d(q)}, where restriction and degeneration are taken with respect to the natural action of End(V_1)×⋯×End(V_d), allowing reembedding into a common tensor space when needed. Determine a genuine method for obtaining upper bounds on Q(T) and \underline{Q}(T) directly, without first upper-bounding them through another rank-type invariant such as geometric rank, slice rank, tensor compressibility values, or G-stable rank.

Fix complex vector spaces V_1,…,V_d and a tensor space V_1⊗···⊗V_d. For T∈V_1⊗···⊗V_d, let u_d(q)=Σ_{i=1}^q e_i⊗···⊗e_i∈(C^q)^{⊗ d}, and define the border subrank by Q̄(T)=max{q:T degenerates to u_d(q)}, where degeneration is taken with respect to the End(V_1)×···×End(V_d)-action after re-embedding into a common tensor space. Determine the value of Q̄(T) for a Zariski-generic tensor T in this fixed format, and characterize the tensors in the same format for which Q̄(T) is strictly larger than the generic value Q̄_gen of that format. ([agates.mimuw.edu.pl](https://agates.mimuw.edu.pl/images/notes_and_reports/Gesmundo_Geometry_of_Tensors_Open_Problems_and_Research_Directions.pdf))

For each integer d ≥ 1, let P_d be the d-th Pauli group on (ℂ^2)^{⊗ d}, let C_d be the corresponding d-qubit Clifford quotient acting on projective space, let Stab_d = {U·e_0^{⊗ d} : U ∈ C_d} ⊂ (ℂ^2)^{⊗ d}, and define the exact stabilizer rank of T ∈ (ℂ^2)^{⊗ d} by stabR(T) = min{r : T = α_1T_1 + ··· + α_rT_r with T_i ∈ Stab_d and α_i ∈ ℂ}. Can one exhibit an explicit family of d-qubit states T_d (with the motivating example in the paper being T_d = (e_0 + sqrt(2)e_1)^{⊗ d}) such that stabR(T_d) ≥ f(d) for some function f satisfying f(d)/d → ∞ as d → ∞?

For each integer d >= 1, over the complex vector space (C^2)^⊗d, let C_d denote the d-qubit Clifford group modulo its center and let Stab_d = {U·e_0^⊗d : U in C_d} be the set of stabilizer states. Define the generic stabilizer rank stabR_d to be the smallest integer r such that the symmetric subspace S^d C^2 is contained in the linear span of some r stabilizer states, i.e. S^d C^2 subseteq span(T_1,...,T_r) for some T_1,...,T_r in Stab_d. Determine lower bounds on stabR_d, as a function of d, that improve the trivial dimension bound stabR_d >= d+1.

Let G be a finite simple undirected graph of order n, and let lambda_1, ..., lambda_n be the eigenvalues of its adjacency matrix A(G), counted with multiplicity. Define s^+(G) = sum_{lambda_i > 0} lambda_i^2 and s^-(G) = sum_{lambda_i < 0} lambda_i^2. If G is connected, must both inequalities s^+(G) >= n - 1 and s^-(G) >= n - 1 hold?

Let G be a finite simple undirected graph with n = |V(G)|, clique number ω(G), adjacency matrix A(G), and adjacency eigenvalues λ_1(G), ..., λ_n(G). Define s^+(G) := Σ_{λ_i(G)>0} λ_i(G)^2. Is it true that for every such graph G one has ω(G) ≥ n/(n - sqrt(s^+(G)))?

Is the following Bollobás-Nikiforov conjecture true? For every simple, undirected, unweighted, non-complete graph G with adjacency matrix A(G), adjacency eigenvalues lambda_1(G) >= lambda_2(G) >= ... >= lambda_n(G), edge number m=e(G), and clique number omega(G), must one have lambda_1(G)^2 + lambda_2(G)^2 <= 2(1 - 1/omega(G))m?

Let G be a finite simple non-empty graph with adjacency matrix A(G), m = e(G) edges, clique number omega(G), and adjacency eigenvalues lambda_1(G) >= ... >= lambda_n(G), counted with multiplicity. Let n^+(G) be the number of positive eigenvalues of A(G), and define ell = min{n^+(G), omega(G)}. Is it true for every such graph G that sum_{i=1}^{ell} lambda_i(G)^2 <= 2m(omega(G)-1)/omega(G)?

For every integer n ≥ 9, among all simple planar graphs G with |V(G)| = n, is the join K_2 ∨ P_{n-2}—obtained from K_2 ∪ P_{n-2} by adding all possible edges between the K_2-part and the path P_{n-2}—the unique graph with maximum adjacency spectral radius ρ(G), where ρ(G) denotes the largest eigenvalue of the adjacency matrix A(G)?

Does there exist an integer n_0 such that for every n ≥ n_0, among all planar 3-uniform hypergraphs H on n vertices—where the shadow ∂(H) is the graph with V(∂(H)) = V(H) and uv ∈ E(∂(H)) iff {u,v} ⊆ e for some e ∈ E(H), 'planar' means that ∂(H) has a planar embedding in which every hyperedge of H is the vertex set of a triangular face, and λ(H) = 3! max{∑_{e∈E(H)} ∏_{i∈e} x_i : x ∈ ℝ^n, ∥x∥_3 = 1}—the maximum spectral radius is attained uniquely by the planar 3-uniform hypergraph that is maximal under inclusion and whose shadow is the join K_2 ∨ P_{n-2}?

Let G be a finite simple undirected unweighted graph, and let lambda(G)=lambda_1(G) denote the spectral radius of its adjacency matrix. Suppose there exists a constant c such that every subgraph H \subseteq G satisfies |E(H)| <= c|V(H)|^2. Must it follow that lambda(G) <= 2c|V(G)|? More generally, if every subgraph H \subseteq G satisfies |E(H)| <= c|V(H)|^alpha for some fixed constant alpha<2, what upper bound on lambda(G) in terms of c, alpha, and |V(G)| should replace 2c|V(G)|?

For each fixed integer k >= 3, determine the infimum real number α(k) such that there exists a constant c > 0, independent of k and n, with the following property: every simple undirected graph G on n vertices satisfying n >= c k^{α(k)} and λ(G) > λ(S^+_{n,k}) contains a cycle C_{2k+2}, where λ(H) denotes the adjacency spectral radius of H, S_{n,k} := K_k ∨ (n-k)K_1, and S^+_{n,k} is obtained from S_{n,k} by adding one edge between two vertices of the independent set.

For a fixed positive integer k, does there exist M(k) such that whenever m >= M(k) and G is a simple graph with m edges and no isolated vertices whose adjacency spectral radius rho(G) satisfies rho(G) >= (k - 1 + sqrt(4m - k^2 + 1))/2, the graph G contains a cycle C_t for every integer t with 3 <= t <= 2k + 2, unless G is the complete split graph K_k ∨ I_{(m - k(k-1)/2)/k} (equivalently, S_{m/k + (k+1)/2, k})? ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2305.10290))

What is the maximum real constant C such that, for every epsilon with 0<epsilon<C, there exists n0=n0(epsilon) for which the following holds: whenever G is a finite simple undirected unweighted graph with |V(G)|=n>=n0 and adjacency spectral radius rho(G)>sqrt(floor(n^2/4)), the graph G contains a cycle C_ell for every integer ell satisfying 3<=ell<=(C-epsilon)n?

Let G=(V,E) be a simple connected graph on n vertices, let δ=δ(G) be its minimum degree, and let L(G)=D(G)-A(G) be its Laplacian matrix with eigenvalues ordered as μ_1(G) ≥ μ_2(G) ≥ ... ≥ μ_n(G)=0. Writing c(H) for the number of connected components of a graph H, and defining the toughness of G by t(G)=min{|S|/c(G-S) : S ⊊ V(G), c(G-S)>1} (with the convention t(K_n)=∞), is it true that every such graph satisfies t(G) ≥ μ_{n-1}(G)/(μ_1(G)-δ)?

Does there exist an absolute constant C > 0 such that every simple, undirected, unweighted d-regular graph G on n vertices whose second largest adjacency eigenvalue in absolute value is at most λ′—that is, every (n, d, λ′)-graph—with d/λ′ ≥ C contains a Hamilton cycle? ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2305.10290))

Let F be a color-critical graph with chromatic number χ(F)=k+1≥3, let T_{n,k} denote the k-partite Turán graph on n vertices, and let c(n,F) be the minimum number of copies of F in a graph obtained from T_{n,k} by adding one edge. For simple undirected unweighted n-vertex graphs G, determine an adjacency-spectral analogue of Mubayi's theorem: find the correct condition on the largest adjacency eigenvalue λ(G) that replaces the edge hypothesis e(G)=e(T_{n,k})+q and guarantees, for all sufficiently large n and every integer q with 1≤q<δ_F n (for some δ_F>0 depending only on F), that G contains at least q·c(n,F) copies of F. In the critical case q=1, determine the exact best-possible spectral threshold for particular color-critical graphs F, especially triangles, cliques, books, odd cycles, and even wheels.

For a fixed integer Δ ≥ 3, let 𝒢(n,Δ) be the set of all connected, simple, undirected, nonregular graphs on n vertices with maximum degree exactly Δ that attain the maximum adjacency spectral radius among all such graphs, and let λ(G)=λ1(A(G)) denote the spectral radius of G. If G_n ∈ 𝒢(n,Δ) for each n, does the limit of n^2(Δ-λ(G_n)) exist as n → ∞? More precisely, is it true that
(1) if Δ is odd, then lim_{n→∞} n^2(Δ-λ(G_n))/(Δ-1)=π^2/4; and
(2) if Δ is even, then lim_{n→∞} n^2(Δ-λ(G_n))/(Δ-2)=π^2/2?

Let G(n, Δ) denote the set of connected nonregular simple graphs on n vertices with maximum degree Δ that attain the maximum adjacency spectral radius λ1 among all connected nonregular n-vertex graphs with maximum degree Δ. For each fixed integer Δ ≥ 3, does there exist N(Δ) such that for every n ≥ N(Δ) and every G ∈ G(n, Δ), the degree sequence of G is (Δ, ..., Δ, δ)—that is, exactly n - 1 vertices have degree Δ and one vertex has degree δ—where δ = Δ - 1 if Δ and n are both odd, δ = 1 if Δ is odd and n is even, and δ = Δ - 2 if Δ is even?

Fix integers n and m with H(n,m) nonempty, where H(n,m) denotes the family of connected simple undirected unweighted graphs on n vertices and m edges. If G ∈ H(n,m) minimizes λ(G) − d(G), where λ(G) = λ1(G) is the largest eigenvalue of the adjacency matrix of G and d(G) = 2m/n is the average degree of G, must G satisfy Δ(G) − δ(G) ≤ 1? ([ort.shu.edu.cn](https://www.ort.shu.edu.cn/CN/article/downloadArticleFile.do?attachType=PDF&id=20117&utm_source=openai))

Let H(n,m) denote the family of connected simple graphs on n vertices and m edges, and let λ(G) be the spectral radius of the adjacency matrix of G. Suppose that G in H(n,m) minimizes λ over H(n,m). Let T_{n,r} be the r-partite Turán graph on n vertices, and let r be the unique integer such that e(T_{n,r-1}) < m <= e(T_{n,r}). Does there exist an absolute constant α > 0 such that, for some constants c > 0 and n0, whenever n >= n0 and m >= c n^α, every such minimizer G satisfies χ(G) <= r?

For every connected simple undirected d-regular graph G, does there exist a signature σ:E(G)→{+1,-1} such that the signed adjacency matrix A_σ, defined by A_σ(u,v)=σ(uv) if uv∈E(G) and A_σ(u,v)=0 otherwise, has spectral radius ρ(A_σ)≤2√(d-1)?

Let G be a simple undirected unweighted graph with maximum degree Δ(G)=Δ≥1. Does there exist a signature σ:E(G)→{+1,−1} such that, if Aσ denotes the signed adjacency matrix obtained from A(G) by assigning entry σ(e) to each edge e, then the signed graph (G,σ) satisfies ρ(Aσ)=ρ(G,σ)<2√(Δ−1)?

Let G be a connected simple undirected graph, and let σ:E(G)→{+1,-1} be a signature on its edges. Write Γ=(G,σ) for the resulting signed graph, let A(Γ) be its signed adjacency matrix, let ρ(G,σ):=ρ(A(Γ)) be the spectral radius of A(Γ), and let ρ(G):=ρ(A(G)) be the spectral radius of the ordinary adjacency matrix of G. Must every connected graph G admit a signature σ such that ρ(G,σ)<2√(ρ(G)-1)?

For integers d >= 1 and 1 <= m <= 2^d, let Q_d be the d-dimensional hypercube with vertex set V(Q_d) = {0,1}^d, where two vertices are adjacent iff they differ in exactly one coordinate. For U subseteq V(Q_d), let Q_d[U] denote the induced subgraph on U, and let lambda_1(Q_d[U]) be the largest eigenvalue of its adjacency matrix. Determine
max{lambda_1(Q_d[U]) : U subseteq V(Q_d), |U| = m}.

For integers n and r with n ≥ r ≥ 2, let S_{n,r-1} be the complete split graph on n vertices obtained from a clique of size r-1 and an independent set of size n-r+1 by adding all edges between the two parts. If G is a simple n-vertex K_{r+1}-saturated graph—that is, G contains no copy of K_{r+1}, but G+e contains a K_{r+1} for every nonedge e of G—must the adjacency spectral radius λ(G)=λ1(A(G)) satisfy λ(G) ≥ λ(S_{n,r-1}), with equality if and only if G ≅ S_{n,r-1}?

For a fixed graph F and positive integer n, determine the minimum adjacency spectral radius rho(G) among all simple undirected unweighted graphs G on n vertices that are F-saturated; that is, G contains no copy of F, but G+e contains a copy of F for every non-edge e of G.

Let G be a simple, undirected, unweighted graph on n=|V(G)| vertices, let L(G)=D(G)-A(G) be its combinatorial Laplacian matrix with eigenvalues mu_1(G) >= mu_2(G) >= ... >= mu_n(G), and for each k with 1 <= k <= n define S_k(G)=sum_{i=1}^k mu_i(G). Is it always true that S_k(G) <= e(G) + binom(k+1,2) for every k in {1,2,...,n}?

Let G be a finite simple undirected graph with n = |V(G)| and e(G) = |E(G)|, and let mu_1(G) >= mu_2(G) >= ... >= mu_n(G) = 0 be the Laplacian eigenvalues of G. For 1 <= k <= n-1, write S_k(G) := sum_{i=1}^k mu_i(G). For integers r,s >= 0 with n = k + r + s, let G_{k,r,s} be the graph whose vertex set is partitioned into a clique K of size k and two independent sets R and S of sizes r and s, such that every vertex of R is adjacent to every vertex of K, and every vertex of S has the same neighborhood in K and degree k-1. Is it true that for every graph G and every k in {1,2,...,n-1}, one has S_k(G) <= e(G) + binom(k+1,2), with equality if and only if G is isomorphic to G_{k,r,s} for some choice of r,s with n = k + r + s?

For each integer n >= 2, if G ranges over all connected simple undirected unweighted graphs of order n, with adjacency eigenvalues ordered lambda_1(G) >= lambda_2(G) >= ... >= lambda_n(G), is the minimum possible adjacency spectral gap lambda_1(G) - lambda_2(G) attained by a double kite graph DK(r,s), where DK(r,s) is obtained from a path P_{s+2} and two copies of K_r by identifying the two endpoints of the path with one vertex from each clique (equivalently, for some integers r >= 1 and s >= 0 with 2r + s = n)?

For each integer n≥2, let δ(T):=λ1(A(T))−λ2(A(T)) be the adjacency spectral gap of a tree T on n vertices, where λ1(A(T))≥λ2(A(T)) are the two largest eigenvalues of its adjacency matrix. If C(k,ℓ) denotes the double comet obtained from the path Pℓ by attaching k pendant vertices to each of its two endvertices (so |V(C(k,ℓ))|=ℓ+2k), is it true that among all trees T of order n, the minimum of δ(T) is attained by some double comet C(k,ℓ) with ℓ+2k=n?

Let G be a finite simple undirected unweighted graph with n = |V(G)|, independence number alpha(G), adjacency matrix A(G), and adjacency eigenvalues lambda_1(G) >= ... >= lambda_n(G) in R. Is it always true that sum_{i: lambda_i(G) > 0} lambda_i(G) >= n - alpha(G), where positive eigenvalues are counted with multiplicity?

Is the following Akbari–Hosseinzadeh conjecture true? For every simple undirected unweighted graph G with non-singular adjacency matrix A(G) (that is, det(A(G)) ≠ 0), if E(G) = Σ_i |λ_i(G)| denotes the adjacency energy of G and Δ(G), δ(G) denote the maximum and minimum degrees of G, then E(G) ≥ Δ(G) + δ(G), with equality if and only if G is a complete graph.

Let r ≥ 2 and n ≥ 1 be integers. For a simple undirected unweighted graph G on n vertices, let λ_1(G) ≥ λ_2(G) ≥ ... ≥ λ_n(G) denote the eigenvalues of its adjacency matrix A(G). What is the maximum possible value of λ_1(G) + λ_n(G) over all K_{r+1}-free graphs G of order n?

Let G be a simple undirected unweighted graph with n = |V(G)|, and let λ_1(G) ≥ λ_2(G) ≥ ··· ≥ λ_n(G) be the eigenvalues of its adjacency matrix A(G). Is it true that λ_i(G) ≤ ⌊n/i⌋ for each i ∈ {3,4}?

For a simple, undirected, unweighted graph G on n vertices, let A(G) be its adjacency matrix and let λ1(G) ≥ λ2(G) ≥ ··· ≥ λn(G) be the eigenvalues of A(G). For each index i with 1 ≤ i ≤ n, determine the sharp universal lower bound and the sharp universal upper bound for λi(G) over all such n-vertex graphs.

Let G be a simple planar graph of order n with maximum degree Delta(G) <= 3, and let lambda_1(G) >= ... >= lambda_n(G) be the eigenvalues of its adjacency matrix, counted with multiplicity. If h = floor((n+1)/2) and l = ceil((n+1)/2), define the HL-index of G by R(G) = max{|lambda_h(G)|, |lambda_l(G)|}. Is it true that R(G) <= 1 for every such graph G?

For every connected graph G of order n with chromatic number chi(G)=k>=2, if x=(x_v)_{v in V(G)} is the unit positive eigenvector of the adjacency matrix A(G) corresponding to the spectral radius lambda(G), and S is an independent set in G, must one always have sum_{v in S} x_v^2 <= 1/2 - (k-2)/(2*sqrt((k-2)^2 + 4(k-1)(n-k+1)))? ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2305.10290))

For each integer n≥4, let G range over all connected simple undirected unweighted graphs on n vertices, and let x be the principal eigenvector of the adjacency matrix A(G), meaning the unique positive eigenvector for λ1(G) normalized by ||x||_2=1. Is it true that the kite (lollipop) graph P_{n-3}·K_4, obtained by identifying an end vertex of P_{n-3} with a vertex of K_4, minimizes ||x||_1 among all such graphs?

Do there exist spherical orbifolds S^{d_1}/Γ_1 and S^{d_2}/Γ_2, where each Γ_i is a finite subgroup of O(d_i+1) acting isometrically on the round sphere, such that the two orbifolds are eigenvalue equivalent—that is, their Laplace-Beltrami operators on L^2 have the same set of eigenvalues when multiplicities are ignored—but their Riemannian volumes are different? ([nyjm.albany.edu](https://nyjm.albany.edu/j/2024/30-31v.pdf))

Fix a dimension d. Among all pairs of d-dimensional spherical orbifolds of the form S^d/Γ1 and S^d/Γ2, where Γ1, Γ2 are finite subgroups of O(d+1) and S^d is equipped with its round metric of sectional curvature 1, what is the maximum possible common volume vol(S^d/Γ1) = vol(S^d/Γ2) under the conditions that S^d/Γ1 and S^d/Γ2 are Laplace-isospectral on functions (that is, have the same Laplace-Beltrami spectrum counted with multiplicity) but are not isometric as orbifolds?

For each integer d, determine the maximal common volume, if any, of a pair of d-dimensional spherical space forms M=S^d/Γ and N=S^d/Γ', where S^d is endowed with the round metric of sectional curvature 1 and Γ,Γ' are finite subgroups of Isom(S^d)=O(d+1) acting freely, such that M and N are isospectral for the Laplace-Beltrami operator on functions, counted with multiplicity, but are not isometric.

Does there exist a dimension d, a poset S, and two families of d-dimensional spherical space forms {M_I}_{I in S} and {N_I}_{I in S} such that each family is a tower of covers in the sense that, for every I < J in S, there is a finite-degree Riemannian covering in a fixed direction along the order (descending or ascending), and such that for every I in S the manifolds M_I and N_I have the same Laplace-Beltrami spectrum on functions, counted with multiplicity, but are not isometric?

Let X be a compact simply connected irreducible symmetric space, equipped with its symmetric Riemannian metric. For which such X do there exist finite subgroups Γ1, Γ2 ⊂ Isom(X) acting freely by isometries such that the quotient manifolds X/Γ1 and X/Γ2, with the induced Riemannian metrics, have the same Laplace-Beltrami spectrum on functions (counted with multiplicities) but are not isometric?

For each odd dimension d = 2n-1 >= 5, let M1 = S^d/Gamma1 and M2 = S^d/Gamma2 be spherical space forms with the round metric of sectional curvature 1, and suppose M1 and M2 are isospectral but not isometric for the Laplace-Beltrami operator on functions. If vol(M1) = vol(M2) is maximal among all such pairs in dimension d, must Gamma1 and Gamma2 be cyclic; equivalently, must every maximal-volume isospectral non-isometric pair of d-dimensional spherical space forms be a pair of lens spaces?

For positive integers n and q, do there exist two standard lens spaces L(q; s) = S^{2n-1}/Γ_{q;s} and L(q; s') = S^{2n-1}/Γ_{q;s'}, with gcd(q, si) = gcd(q, s'i) = 1 for all i (so each has fundamental group of order q), that are isospectral for the Laplace-Beltrami operator on functions but not isometric, in the congruence class n ≡ -1 mod (φ(q)/2)?

For each compact simple Lie group K ∈ {SU(3), Sp(2) ≃ Spin(5), Sp(3), G2}, does there exist a pair of finite subgroups Γ1, Γ2 ≤ K such that Γ1 and Γ2 are almost conjugate in K—that is, there exists a bijection φ: Γ1 → Γ2 with γ conjugate to φ(γ) in K for every γ ∈ Γ1—but Γ1 and Γ2 are not conjugate as subgroups of K? ([nyjm.albany.edu](https://nyjm.albany.edu/j/2024/30-31p.pdf))

Determine exactly which compact irreducible symmetric spaces of group type X = (K x K)/diag(K), where K is a compact connected simple Lie group and X is not assumed simply connected, admit two compact manifold quotients M1 and M2 covered by X via finite Riemannian covering maps such that M1 and M2 are isospectral for the Laplace-Beltrami operator on functions, counted with multiplicities, but are not isometric.

Determine which compact simply connected irreducible symmetric spaces X of compact type admit two good orbifold quotients X/Gamma1 and X/Gamma2, where Gamma1 and Gamma2 are finite groups acting effectively and isometrically on X, such that the quotient orbifolds with their induced metrics are isospectral for the Laplacian on functions but are not isometric.

Fix d in N and an admissible volume x > 0. What is the maximal cardinality of a set {M_i} of d-dimensional spherical space forms M_i = S^d/Γ_i, where S^d is endowed with its round metric of constant sectional curvature 1 and each finite subgroup Γ_i < Isom(S^d) acts freely, such that vol(M_i) = x for every i and the manifolds M_i are pairwise isospectral for the Laplace-Beltrami operator on functions and pairwise non-isometric?

Let M = S^d/Gamma be a spherical orbifold, where Gamma is a finite subgroup of O(d+1), and suppose vol(M) = V. What upper bound can be given for the cardinality of a set S of spherical orbifolds containing M such that any two distinct elements of S are non-isometric and have the same Laplace-Beltrami spectrum on functions, counted with multiplicity?

For each n in N, let mathfrak{L}(n,q) denote the set of isometry classes of (2n-1)-dimensional lens spaces L(q;s)=S^{2n-1}/Gamma_{q;s} with the standard spherical metric and fundamental group of order q, and define mathfrak{L}^bullet(n,q)={L in mathfrak{L}(n,q) : Spec(L) != Spec(L') for every non-isometric L' in mathfrak{L}(n,q)}, where Spec(L) is the Laplace-Beltrami spectrum on functions counted with multiplicity. Is it true that for every n in N the asymptotic density U_n(x):=(sum_{q<=x} #mathfrak{L}^bullet(n,q)) / (sum_{q<=x} #mathfrak{L}(n,q)) satisfies lim_{x->infty} U_n(x)=1?

For positive integers n and q, let 𝔏(n, q) denote the set of isometry classes of (2n−1)-dimensional lens spaces with cyclic fundamental group of order q, endowed with the standard constant-curvature-one metric, and let 𝔏•(n, q) = {L in 𝔏(n, q) : Spec(L') ≠ Spec(L) for every L' ≠ L in 𝔏(n, q)}, where Spec denotes the Laplace–Beltrami spectrum counted with multiplicity. Determine conditions on n and q for which 𝔏•(n, q) = 𝔏(n, q).

For a spherical space form M = S^d/Γ, where S^d is equipped with its round metric of sectional curvature 1 and Γ is a finite subgroup of Iso(S^d) acting freely, let Spec(M) denote the Laplace-Beltrami spectrum on L^2(M), counted with multiplicity, and let L(M) denote the length spectrum, i.e. the set of lengths of closed geodesics on M. What is the relationship between Spec(M) and L(M)?

Let M = S^d/Γ1 and N = S^d/Γ2 be d-dimensional spherical space forms, where Γ1, Γ2 ≤ O(d+1) are finite subgroups acting freely on the round sphere S^d, and let M and N carry the induced Riemannian metrics of constant sectional curvature 1. If M and N have the same length spectrum, meaning the same set of lengths of closed geodesics, must M and N be quotient commensurable; that is, must they admit a common finite-degree quotient manifold? ([nyjm.albany.edu](https://nyjm.albany.edu/j/2024/30-31p.pdf))

Do there exist compact hyperbolic manifolds M1 and M2 such that the Laplace-Beltrami operators on L^2(M1) and L^2(M2) have the same spectrum, counted with multiplicity, but M1 and M2 are not strongly isospectral; equivalently in the paper's terminology, there exists some natural vector bundle and some natural strongly elliptic differential operator on square-integrable sections whose spectra on M1 and M2 are different?

Do there exist hyperbolic manifolds M1 and M2 of the same dimension n such that, for every degree p = 0,1,...,n, the Hodge-Laplace operators on p-forms on M1 and M2 are isospectral, but M1 and M2 are not strongly isospectral, meaning that they do not have identical spectra for all natural strongly elliptic differential operators on all natural vector bundles?

Let M be a class of probability measures on a space Z, let E:M→R∪{+∞} be a population variational objective with optimal measure mu_* in argmin_{mu in M} E(mu), and let E_n be a random approximate objective on M—arising, as in the paper, from finite data, modeling limitations, or surrogate/optimization constraints—with optimizer mu_n in argmin_{mu in M} E_n(mu). Can one identify abstract classes of such pairs (E, E_n) for which E(mu_n) converges to E(mu_*) as n→∞, obtain quantitative convergence rates under explicit model assumptions, and show that these classes still cover machine-learning problems of the kind highlighted in the paper (such as generative modeling, uncertainty quantification, out-of-distribution generalization, and weak-information disambiguation)? ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/abs/2306.11928))

Let \Omega be an underlying space and let \mathcal{M} be a class of candidate probability measures on \Omega. Suppose a learning problem is formulated by a population variational objective \mathcal{E}: \mathcal{M} \to \mathbb{R} \cup \{+\infty\}, but in practice one only has access to a random approximation \mathcal{E}_n of \mathcal{E} (for example because only samples, incomplete information, or surrogate optimization objectives are available). Can one define such measure-based objectives and approximations so that an exact or approximate minimizer \mu_n \in \mathcal{M} of \mathcal{E}_n has favorable practical properties, and can one exhibit concrete machine-learning problems—of the kind motivating the paper, such as generative modeling, uncertainty quantification, out-of-distribution generalization, or weak-information disambiguation—in which this measure-based variational viewpoint genuinely advances the state of the art?

Fix k in N. For each dimension d, let D_d be an open subset of R^d with Lebesgue measure 1, and define F_d^k(D_d) to be the class of all integrable functions f : D_d -> R such that ||D^alpha f||_infty <= 1 for every multi-index alpha with |alpha| <= k. Let e(n, F_d^k(D_d)) denote the minimal deterministic worst-case error of approximating the integral of f over D_d by algorithms that use at most n function values. For which families of normalized domains (D_d)_{d in N} does there exist a constant c_k > 0, depending only on k, such that for all d, n in N one has e(n, F_d^k(D_d)) <= c_k d n^(-k/d), and can one explicitly construct cubature algorithms that attain this bound on those domains?

Fix k in N. For d in N, let F_d^k = {f:[0,1]^d -> R : ||D^α f||_∞ <= 1 for every multi-index α in N_0^d with |α| <= k}, and let e_ran(n, F_d^k) denote the minimal randomized worst-case error for approximating S_d(f) = ∫_[0,1]^d f(x) dx by algorithms that use at most n function values. Since e_ran(n, F_d^k) has the optimal rate n^{-k/d-1/2}, and results cited in the paper yield an upper bound of the form e_ran(n, F_d^k) <= C_k d^t n^{-k/d-1/2} with t = (k + 1)/2, what is the smallest exponent t = t(k) for which there exists a constant C_k < ∞, independent of d and n, such that e_ran(n, F_d^k) <= C_k d^{t(k)} n^{-k/d-1/2} for all d,n in N?

Let H_i be reproducing kernel Hilbert spaces of real-valued functions on D_i, and for each i let tilde S_i be a bounded linear functional of unit norm with nonnegative representer h_i. Assume there exist f_i, g_i in H_i and alpha_i in (0,1] such that (h_i, f_i, g_i) is orthonormal in H_i and alpha_i h_i = f_i^2 + g_i^2. For the tensor-product problem S_d = tilde S_1 ⊗ ... ⊗ tilde S_d on the unit ball of F_d = H_1 ⊗ ... ⊗ H_d, Theorem 2 proves the worst-case lower bound e(n,F_d)^2 >= 1 - n prod_{i=1}^d (1 + alpha_i^2)^(-1). Does an analogous Banach-space lower-bound theory exist for this same kind of tensor-product quadrature/integration problem; that is, can one obtain similar worst-case lower bounds for Banach spaces in place of Hilbert spaces? ([scribd.com](https://www.scribd.com/document/936902995/978-3-031-59762-6))

Let S_1(f) = integral from 0 to 1 of f(x) dx, and for k in N let F_1^k = {f : [0,1] -> R | ||f^(j)||_infty <= 1 for all 0 <= j <= k}. In the univariate setting d = 1, study the paper's open problem of comparing in detail the universal randomized schemes discussed in Section 3: (i) for periodic functions on [0,1], choose n randomly from {m, m+1, ..., 2m} and apply a randomly shifted midpoint rule with n equally weighted function values; and (ii) for non-periodic functions on [0,1], with n = 2m, interpolate f at Chebyshev points by a polynomial f_m of degree < m and then use separation of the main part (control variates), i.e. exact integration of f_m plus plain Monte Carlo on f - f_m. For every k, determine as sharply as possible how these schemes compare with respect to deterministic worst-case error e(n, F_1^k) and randomized worst-case error e_ran(n, F_1^k), including asymptotic orders and constants, the logarithmic loss of the second method, and their preasymptotic behavior for small or moderate n and practical ease of implementation.

In the multivariate numerical-integration setting of this paper, where n(ε,d;F) denotes the minimal number of function values needed to approximate the integration operator on a d-dimensional function class F with error at most ε, can one develop a theory of universality at the level of tractability, not only at the level of convergence order? More precisely, for families of smoothness classes for which a single algorithm can be constructed independently of the smoothness parameter and still attain the optimal convergence rate for each class, can one determine whether such universal algorithms also achieve the optimal ε- and d-dependence of the information complexity—e.g. with respect to the curse of dimensionality, polynomial tractability, or strong polynomial tractability—for those classes?

Let D_d ⊂ R^d be a bounded Lipschitz domain with λ_d(D_d) = 1, and let S_D(f) = ∫_{D_d} f(x) dx. Does there exist, for domains D_d other than [0,1]^d, a universal randomized linear cubature algorithm A_n^ω(f) = Σ_{j=1}^n a_j(ω) f(x_j(ω))—ideally unbiased and possibly with x_j iid uniformly distributed on D_d—such that the same algorithm, without being retuned to the smoothness parameter k, achieves on the corresponding Sobolev scales the cube-optimal orders from Theorem 3 simultaneously in the randomized and deterministic worst-case settings; namely, for all k > d/2 on isotropic Sobolev spaces H^k(D_d), e^ran(A_n,H^k(D_d)) ≍ n^(-k/d-1/2) and e(A_n,H^k(D_d)) ≍ n^(-k/d), and for all k ∈ N on mixed-smoothness spaces H^{k,mix}(D_d), e^ran(A_n,H^{k,mix}(D_d)) ≍ n^(-k-1/2) and e(A_n,H^{k,mix}(D_d)) ≍ n^(-k)(log n)^((d-1)/2); or, if exact optimality is impossible, at least these rates up to additional logarithmic factors?

Let D_d subset R^d be an open domain with λ_d(D_d)=1, and define F_d^k(D_d) = {f : D_d -> R | ||D^alpha f||_infinity <= 1 for all multi-indices alpha with |alpha| <= k}. For the integration operator S_d(f) = integral over D_d of f(x) dx, let e(n,F_d^k(D_d)) denote the minimal deterministic worst-case error among all algorithms using n function values. It is known that for every k in N there exists c_k > 0 such that, for all d,n in N and all such D_d, e(n,F_d^k(D_d)) >= min{1/2, c_k d n^{-k/d}}, and that this order is not improvable because cubes satisfy a comparable upper bound. Determine, as sharply as possible, the constants c_k and characterize the extremal volume-one domains D_d, for fixed k,d,n, for which e(n,F_d^k(D_d)) is minimal or especially small. ([scribd.com](https://www.scribd.com/document/936902995/978-3-031-59762-6))

Fix integers d,k >= 1. Let D_d be a Jordan measurable domain in R^d with lambda_d(D_d) = 1, and define F_d^k(D_d) = {f : D_d -> R | ||D^alpha f||_{L_infty(D_d)} <= 1 for every multi-index alpha in N_0^d with |alpha| <= k}. If e(n,F_d^k(D_d)) denotes the minimal worst-case error of numerical integration f -> integral over D_d of f(x) dx based on n function values, then it is known at least for bounded Lipschitz domains that e(n,F_d^k(D_d)) has order n^(-k/d). Is it true that, for fixed d and k, the exact asymptotic constant C_{d,k}(D_d) := lim_{n->infinity} e(n,F_d^k(D_d)) n^{k/d} exists and is independent of the particular domain D_d whenever D_d is Jordan measurable with lambda_d(D_d) = 1, possibly after imposing suitable assumptions on the boundary of D_d?

Let d,n\in \mathbb N, and let D_d\subset \mathbb R^d be an open set with Lebesgue measure \lambda_d(D_d)=1. Define
\widetilde C^2(D_d):=\{f\in C^2(D_d;\mathbb R): \|f\|_\infty\le 1,\ \operatorname{Lip}(f)\le d^{-1/2},\ \operatorname{Lip}(D^\Theta f)\le d^{-1}\ \text{for every }\Theta\in S^{d-1}\},
where D^\Theta f denotes the directional derivative in direction \Theta and \operatorname{Lip}(g):=\sup_{x,y\in D_d,\ x\ne y}|g(x)-g(y)|/\|x-y\|_2. Let e(n,\widetilde C^2(D_d)) be the minimal worst-case error of deterministic algorithms that approximate \int_{D_d} f(x)\,dx using n function values. Is it true that there exists a constant C>0, independent of both d and D_d, such that
 e(n,\widetilde C^2(D_d))\ge C\,n^{-2/d}
for all d,n\in \mathbb N and all such domains D_d?

Let D_d\subset \mathbb{R}^d be the open volume-normalized \ell_p^d-ball (so \lambda_d(D_d)=1) for some p\in[1,2). For the worst-case numerical integration problem over the orthogonally invariant class
\widetilde{C}^2(D_d)=\{f\in C^2(D_d): \|f\|_\infty\le 1,\ \operatorname{Lip}(f)\le d^{-1/2},\ \operatorname{Lip}(D^\theta f)\le d^{-1}\ \text{for every }\theta\in S^{d-1}\},
where \operatorname{Lip}(g)=\sup_{x,y\in D_d,\,x\ne y}|g(x)-g(y)|/\|x-y\|_2 and D^\theta f is the directional derivative in direction \theta, does there exist a constant C>0, independent of n, d, and D_d, such that
 e(n,\widetilde{C}^2(D_d))\ge C\,n^{-2/d}\quad\text{for all }n,d\in\mathbb{N}?
In particular, does numerical integration over \widetilde{C}^2(D_d) suffer from the curse of dimensionality for volume-normalized \ell_p^d-balls with p<2?

For fixed d and k, let H^{k,mix}(T^d) be the Hilbert space of periodic functions of dominating mixed smoothness k on the d-torus, and let P_n = {X_1, ..., X_n} with X_1, ..., X_n iid and uniformly distributed on T^d. For the sampling recovery problem id: H^{k,mix}(T^d) -> L2(T^d), define the Monte Carlo error of an algorithm A based on P_n by sup_{||f||_{H^{k,mix}} <= 1} E ||f - A(f|_{P_n})||_{L2(T^d)} and the uniform error by E sup_{||f||_{H^{k,mix}} <= 1} ||f - A(f|_{P_n})||_{L2(T^d)}. It is known that iid uniform samples are asymptotically optimal for the Monte Carlo error and only optimal up to a logarithmic factor for the uniform error. Can this logarithmic factor be eliminated, i.e. do iid uniformly distributed samples achieve the same asymptotic order for the uniform error as optimally chosen sampling points? In particular, can one thereby remove the corresponding logarithmic loss for numerical integration on H^{k,mix}(T^d) as well? ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2307.06787))

For the approximation and integration problems treated in Section 5—most explicitly, the d-dimensional L_q-approximation problem id_d: W_p^s(Ω_d) → L_q(Ω_d) and the integration problem I_d(f) = ∫_{Ω_d} f on open, bounded domains Ω_d ⊂ R^d satisfying an interior cone condition, with Sobolev parameters in the regime where point evaluation is continuous—define the iid information complexity n_iid(ε,d) by restricting admissible randomized algorithms to operators of the form A_n(f) = φ(X_1, ..., X_n; f(X_1), ..., f(X_n)), where X_1, ..., X_n are iid and uniformly distributed on Ω_d. For each of the Monte Carlo and uniform error criteria used in Section 5, determine whether the resulting family of problems suffers from the curse of dimensionality or is polynomially or strongly polynomially tractable in the sense of Section 2, how these iid tractability properties depend on the problem type, the dimension d, and the domains Ω_d, how they compare with the corresponding tractability properties when the sampling points may be chosen optimally (deterministically or randomly), and whether the relevant asymptotic constants for the minimal iid errors exist and depend only on |Ω_d| rather than on the shape of Ω_d. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2307.06787))

Fix d in N, an open bounded domain D subset R^d satisfying an interior cone condition, an integer s >= 1, and exponents 1 <= p,q <= infinity in the parameter regime of Section 5 for which point evaluations on W_p^s(D) are well defined and the approximation operator APP: W_p^s(D) -> L_q(D) is considered. Let P_n={X_1,...,X_n}, where X_1,...,X_n are iid uniformly distributed on D, and let e_iid(n;W_p^s(D),L_q(D)) denote the minimal approximation error achievable by randomized algorithms that may use only the sampled values f|_{P_n} under one of the two Section 5 error criteria (Monte Carlo error or uniform error). After normalization by the corresponding Section 5 convergence rate for that criterion—in particular by n^{s/d-(1/p-1/q)_+} in the Monte Carlo case, with the additional logarithmic correction in the exceptional endpoint p=q=∞—does the resulting sequence have a limit as n tends to infinity, and, if it does, is that asymptotic constant determined only by vol(D) and not by the shape of D?

Let D_d\subset\mathbb R^d be an open set (with the paper’s standing normalization \(\lambda_d(D_d)=1\)), let \(\rho:D_d\to\mathbb R\) be a weight, and define \(S_d(f)=\int_{D_d} f(x)\rho(x)\,dx\) for integrable real-valued \(f:D_d\to\mathbb R\). Beyond the currently understood case \(\rho\equiv 1\) on \([0,1]^d\), does there exist a single universal family of randomized cubature rules of the linear form \(A_n^\omega(f)=\sum_{j=1}^n a_j(\omega)f(x_j(\omega))\), possibly based on iid points \(x_j\) uniformly distributed on \(D_d\), that extends the universality phenomenon of the randomized Frolov algorithm to this weighted-domain setting and, on the corresponding isotropic Sobolev classes \(H_d^k\) (for \(k>d/2\)) and dominating mixed-smoothness classes \(H_d^{k,\mathrm{mix}}\) (for \(k\in\mathbb N\)), achieves the same benchmark orders as in Theorem 3.1—namely randomized error \(n^{-k/d-1/2}\) and deterministic worst-case error \(n^{-k/d}\) in the isotropic case, and randomized error \(n^{-k-1/2}\) and deterministic worst-case error \(n^{-k}(\log n)^{(d-1)/2}\) in the mixed-smoothness case—or at least these rates up to additional logarithmic factors if exact optimality is computationally impractical?

Over an algebraically closed field k, does there exist a positive integer d such that the Hilbert scheme Hilb_d(A^3_k) has an irreducible component of dimension strictly smaller than 3d? Likewise, does there exist a positive integer d such that the punctual Hilbert scheme Hilb_d(A^3_k,0), namely the scheme of degree-d subschemes of A^3_k supported at the origin, has an irreducible component of dimension strictly smaller than 2(d-1)?

Over an algebraically closed field k, find positive integers d and n and describe a nonempty open subset of an irreducible component of Hilb_d(A_k^n), the Hilbert scheme of degree-d finite subschemes of affine n-space, that is distinct from the smoothable component (the closure of the open locus of smooth degree-d subschemes, equivalently of d distinct k-points). As emphasized in the paper, the ambient dimension n may be large, and it would already be significant to do this even for n=3. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2307.08777))

Fix an integer d at least 2. Let k be an algebraically closed field of characteristic 0, and let S be a normal quasi-projective surface over k with at least one singular point whose complete local ring is not a du Val singularity. Must the Hilbert scheme Hilb_d(S), parametrizing length-d zero-dimensional subschemes of S, be reducible?

Let k be an algebraically closed field of characteristic 0, and let S be a normal quasi-projective surface over k such that for every singular point s in S, the complete local ring \hat{\mathcal{O}}_{S,s} is a du Val singularity. For each integer d \ge 1, is the Hilbert scheme Hilb_d(S) parametrizing zero-dimensional subschemes of S of degree d reduced?

Let k be an algebraically closed field and fix an integer d > 0. Among all length-d zero-dimensional subschemes Z ⊂ A^3_k, what is the maximum possible value of dim_k T_[Z] Hilb^d(A^3_k), where T_[Z] Hilb^d(A^3_k) denotes the Zariski tangent space to the Hilbert scheme of d points on A^3_k at the point [Z]?

Let k be an algebraically closed field, let d > 0, and let [Gamma] in Hilb^d(A^3_k) be the point corresponding to a zero-dimensional subscheme Gamma subset A^3_k of length d. Is it true that the Zariski tangent-space dimension at [Gamma] has the same parity as d; equivalently, that dim_k T_[Gamma]Hilb^d(A^3_k) is congruent to d modulo 2? ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2307.08777))

For every integer d >= 1, let ν_{Hilb_d(A^3_C)} denote the Behrend function of the Hilbert scheme Hilb_d(A^3_C) of length-d subschemes of affine 3-space over C. Is it true that ν_{Hilb_d(A^3_C)}([Z]) = (-1)^d for every point [Z] in Hilb_d(A^3_C)?

Let k be an algebraically closed field. For every integer d >= 1 and every closed point [Γ] in the smoothable component of Hilb^d(A^3_k) (that is, in the closure of the locus of d distinct reduced k-points), assume that dim_k T_[Γ] Hilb^d(A^3_k) = 3d+6. Must the completed local singularity of Hilb^d(A^3_k) at [Γ] be smoothly equivalent, in the sense of §2.6, to the vertex of the affine cone over the Grassmannian Gr(2,6) in its Plücker embedding?

Let k be an algebraically closed field, let d be a positive integer, and let [Gamma] be a closed point of the smoothable component of Hilb_d^Gor(A^4_k). Define the surplus by s([Gamma]) := dim_k T_[Gamma] Hilb_d(A^4_k) - 4d, where 4d is the dimension of the smoothable component. When s([Gamma]) is small, can one classify the complete local singularities at such points, i.e. the complete local rings O-hat_{Hilb_d^Gor(A^4_k),[Gamma]}, up to smooth equivalence (equivalently, up to adding formal power-series variables)?

Let k be an algebraically closed field, let Hilb_d(A^n_k) denote the Hilbert scheme of length-d subschemes of affine n-space A^n_k, and let Hilb_d(A^n_k,0) be the punctual Hilbert scheme, i.e. the fiber over d[0] of the Hilbert-Chow morphism, parametrizing length-d subschemes supported at the origin 0. Let R_d^n subset Hilb_d(A^n_k) be the smoothable component, namely the closure of the locus of smooth length-d subschemes of A^n_k. Call an irreducible component Z of Hilb_d(A^n_k,0) smoothable if Z is contained in R_d^n under the natural inclusion Hilb_d(A^n_k,0) subset Hilb_d(A^n_k). What can be said about these smoothable irreducible components of Hilb_d(A^n_k,0), and for fixed n and d how many such components are there?

Let k be an algebraically closed field. For every n,d >= 1, does every monomial ideal I subset k[x_1,...,x_n] with dim_k(k[x_1,...,x_n]/I) = d and support equal to {0} define a point of the Zariski closure of the curvilinear locus in the punctual Hilbert scheme Hilb_d(A^n_k,0), where the curvilinear locus consists of those length-d subschemes Z supported at 0 that are abstractly isomorphic to Spec k[t]/(t^d)?

Let k be an algebraically closed field, let n,d >= 1, and let Hilb_d(A_k^n,0) := HC^{-1}(d·0) be the punctual Hilbert scheme of length-d subschemes of A_k^n supported at the origin. Let Hilb_d^lci(A_k^n,0) subset Hilb_d(A_k^n,0) denote the open locus parametrizing those subschemes that are locally complete intersections. Determine an upper bound, in terms of d and n, for dim Hilb_d^lci(A_k^n,0).

Exhibit an explicit example of a disconnected Haiman–Sturmfels multigraded Hilbert scheme Hilb_S^H, where S is a polynomial ring over an algebraically closed field equipped with some multigrading and Hilb_S^H parametrizes homogeneous ideals I ⊆ S having multigraded Hilbert function H; moreover, make the example as small/simple as possible, and preferably choose H to be eventually constant (that is, H(a)=c for all sufficiently large multidegrees a).

Over an algebraically closed field k, let Γ ⊂ A^n_k be a finite subscheme. Define its smoothability defect by
δ(Γ) := min{deg(Γ′) - deg(Γ) : Γ ⊂ Γ′ ⊂ A^n_k and Γ′ is a finite smoothable k-scheme}.
What can be said about the function δ on finite subschemes of affine spaces? In particular, does there exist a finite subscheme Γ such that δ(Γ) > deg(Γ)?

Let k be an algebraically closed field, let Γ be a finite k-scheme, and let δ(Γ) denote its smoothability defect, i.e. the minimum of deg Γ′−deg Γ over all finite smoothable k-schemes Γ′ such that Γ ⊆ Γ′. Is it true that for every ε>0, if Γ^{× n}:=Γ×_k⋯×_kΓ denotes the n-fold self-product of Γ, then
lim_{n→∞} δ(Γ^{× n})/(deg Γ)^{n(1+ε)} = 0?
Here deg Γ denotes the degree (length) of Γ. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2307.08777))

Let (M, <.,.>) be a complete d-dimensional Riemannian manifold whose sectional curvatures lie in [-K, K], and let D = Bbar(x_ref, r) be the closed metric ball of radius r about x_ref, assumed to be geodesically convex in the sense that every x, y in D are joined by a unique minimizing geodesic segment contained in D. Let f: D -> R be geodesically convex and L-Lipschitz on D. In the first-order black-box model, a deterministic algorithm may query points x_k in D and receives f(x_k) together with a subgradient g_k in T_{x_k}M satisfying f(y) >= f(x_k) + <g_k, log_{x_k}(y)> for all y in D. Writing f* = min_{x in D} f(x) and zeta_t = t/tanh(t) (with zeta_0 = 1 by continuity), does there exist a deterministic first-order algorithm A such that, for every epsilon in (0,1), A outputs a point x in D with f(x) - f* <= epsilon L r after at most O(poly(zeta_{r sqrt(K)}, d) log(epsilon^{-1})) oracle queries, while each iteration uses only poly(zeta_{r sqrt(K)}, d) arithmetic operations to determine the next query, in addition to the oracle queries?

Let n∈ℤ_+={0,1,2,…} and r∈[0,1). On the unit circle 𝕋 equipped with normalized Lebesgue measure, let K_n f:=F_n*f, where F_n is the n-th Fejér kernel, and let P_r f:=𝒫_r*f, where 𝒫_r is the Poisson kernel. For the classical Hardy spaces H^p(𝕋)={f∈L^p(𝕋): f̂(k)=0 for all k<0} (with the usual H^∞ interpretation when p=∞), determine the exact operator norms ‖I−K_n‖ and ‖I−P_r‖ on L^p(𝕋) for every 1<p<∞, and the exact operator norms ‖I−K_n‖ and ‖I−P_r‖ on H^p(𝕋) for every 1≤p≤∞.

For each real p with 1 ≤ p < ∞, let H^p(T) = {f ∈ L^p(T) : f̂(n) = 0 for all n < 0}, where T is the unit circle with normalized Lebesgue measure and f̂(n) denotes the nth Fourier coefficient. Define the backward shift B:H^p(T)→H^p(T) by (Bf)(e^{iθ}) = e^{-iθ}(f(e^{iθ}) − f̂(0)) (equivalently, if f(e^{iθ}) = Σ_{n≥0} a_n e^{inθ}, then Bf = Σ_{n≥0} a_{n+1} e^{inθ}). Determine the exact value of the operator norm ||B||_{H^p(T)→H^p(T)} as a function of p.

For the classical complex Hardy spaces H^p = H^p(𝕋) on the unit circle 𝕋, determine the exact value of the bounded compact approximation constant M(H^p) for every 1 ≤ p < ∞ and the exact value of the dual compact approximation constant M*(H^p) for every 1 < p < ∞, where M(H^p) is the greatest lower bound of the constants M > 0 such that for every ε > 0 and every finite set F ⊂ H^p there exists a compact operator T ∈ K(H^p) with ||I_{H^p} - T|| ≤ M and ||f - Tf||_{H^p} < ε for all f ∈ F, and M*(H^p) is the greatest lower bound of the constants M > 0 such that for every ε > 0 and every finite set G ⊂ (H^p)* there exists a compact operator T ∈ K(H^p) with ||I_{H^p} - T|| ≤ M and ||φ - T*φ||_(H^p)* < ε for all φ ∈ G.

For the classical Hardy space H^p = H[L^p(𝕋)] on the unit circle 𝕋 with normalized Lebesgue measure, and for each 1 ≤ p < ∞, is its bounded compact approximation constant M(H^p)—that is, the infimum of all M > 0 such that for every ε > 0 and every finite set F ⊂ H^p there exists a compact operator T on H^p with ||I-T|| ≤ M and ||f-Tf|| < ε for all f ∈ F—equal to ||I-K_0||_{B(H^p)}, where K_0 is the zeroth Fejér operator (so K_0f is the constant function given by the zeroth Fourier coefficient of f, and therefore (I-K_0)f is f with its constant term removed)?

Let T be the unit circle endowed with normalized Lebesgue measure. For 1 ≤ q ≤ p < ∞, let L_{p,q}(T) be the Lorentz space of measurable complex-valued functions f on T with norm ||f||_{p,q} = (∫_0^1 [t^{1/p} f*(t)]^q dt/t)^{1/q}, where f* is the non-increasing rearrangement of f, and let H[L_{p,q}] = {f ∈ L_{p,q}(T) : hat f(n) = 0 for all n < 0} be the corresponding Hardy-Lorentz space. Determine a nontrivial lower bound for the optimal bounded compact approximation constant M(H[L_{p,q}]) and improve the known upper bound M(H[L_{p,q}]) ≤ 2. In addition, for 1 < q ≤ p < ∞, determine a nontrivial lower bound for the optimal dual compact approximation constant M*(H[L_{p,q}]) and improve the known upper bound M*(H[L_{p,q}]) ≤ 2.

Does there exist a finitely generated residually finite group G such that, for one (equivalently any) finite generating set S, its residual finiteness growth function F^G_S(n), defined by F^G_S(n) = max{D_G(g) : g is nontrivial and |g|_S <= n}, where D_G(g) is the least index of a finite-index normal subgroup of G that does not contain g, has intermediate growth; that is, is superpolynomial but subexponential?

Fix a prime p. Is it true that for every integer k >= 1 there exists an integer m >= 1 such that, for every integer n >= 1 and every pair of matrices A, B in GL_n(Z_p) satisfying AB ≡ BA mod p^m M_n(Z_p) (equivalently, [A,B] ≡ I_n mod p^m M_n(Z_p)), there exist commuting matrices A', B' in GL_n(Z_p) with A'B' = B'A', A ≡ A' mod p^k M_n(Z_p), and B ≡ B' mod p^k M_n(Z_p)?

Let X be a proper geodesic Gromov hyperbolic space, let Γ < Isom(X) be a discrete cocompact subgroup, and for each subgroup H ≤ Γ let δ(H) denote the exponential orbit-growth rate (critical exponent) of the action H ↷ X. It is known that every infinite normal subgroup N ◁ Γ satisfies the lower cogrowth bound δ(N) > (1/2)δ(Γ). When is this lower bound optimal? More specifically, in the paper’s special geometric case, if Γ is a lattice in real hyperbolic space H^n, does there exist a sequence of infinite normal subgroups N_i ◁ Γ such that δ(N_i) → δ(Γ)/2? ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2310.04207))

Let Γ be a lattice in Isom(H^3), and let δ(H) denote the critical exponent (equivalently, the exponential growth rate in the sense of Section 4) of a discrete subgroup H. Does there exist a sequence of normal subgroups N_i ◁ Γ such that δ(N_i) → δ(Γ)/2 as i → ∞?

Does there exist a sequence (N_i) of discrete subgroups N_i ≤ Isom(H^3) such that each quotient H^3/N_i has finite injectivity radius, and the exponential growth rates delta(N_i) satisfy delta(N_i) -> 1 as i -> infinity?

Let G be a finitely generated hyperbolic group, fix a finite generating set S, and for every faithful action G on a set X define vol_{G,X}(n)=max_{x in X}|B_S(n)·x|, where B_S(n) is the ball of radius n in G. Write f ≼ g if there exists C>0 such that f(n) ≤ C g(Cn) for all n≥1, and say that G has Schreier growth gap f if vol_{G,X} ≽ f for every faithful G-set X. Call the gap nontrivial if f is superlinear. Does there exist a hyperbolic group G that has a nontrivial Schreier growth gap but does not have an exponential Schreier growth gap?

Let G = Mod(Sigma_g) be the mapping class group of a closed orientable surface Sigma_g (in the intended nontrivial case, g >= 2), and fix a finite generating set S of G. For a faithful action G acting on a set X, define vol_{G,X}(n) := max_{x in X} |B_S(n)·x|, i.e. the cardinality of the largest radius-n ball in the possibly disconnected Schreier graph of the action. Does there exist a superlinear function f: N -> N such that every faithful G-set X satisfies vol_{G,X}(n) succcurlyeq f(n), where h preccurlyeq k means that there exists C > 0 with h(n) <= C k(Cn) for all n >= 1?

For every hyperbolic group G, does there exist some finite p and an ℓ^p complex X—meaning a simplicial complex metrized so that each cell is isometric to a simplex of ℓ^p—on which G acts geometrically, such that X admits a convex geodesic bicombing (i.e. a choice of geodesic c_xy joining each pair x,y ∈ X for which t ↦ d(c_xy(t), c_x'y'(t)) is convex for all x,y,x',y' ∈ X)? More strongly, can X be chosen Busemann convex, equivalently uniquely geodesic with its unique bicombing convex? ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2310.04207))

Let G act by isometries on a Gromov-hyperbolic geodesic metric space X, and fix a basepoint x in X. Suppose that for every infinite-order element g in G, the orbit map Z -> X given by n -> g^n x is a quasi-isometric embedding. Beyond the trivial case in which the action is geometric, what additional hypotheses on the action, or on the infinite cyclic subgroups <g>, are sufficient to force G to be a hyperbolic group?

For each fixed k∈{0,1,2}, let Q_n^k denote the set of k-dimensional subcubes of the n-dimensional hypercube Q_n, and let ex_k(n,3) be the maximum size of a family S⊆Q_n^k that is 3-free, meaning that every 3-dimensional subcube of Q_n contains at least one k-subcube that does not belong to S. Define π_k(3):=lim_{n→∞} ex_k(n,3)/|Q_n^k|. Is it true that π_k(3)=3/4 for each k∈{0,1,2}? ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2310.18163))

For each integer m ≥ 7, is the Turán density π_2(3m+2) equal to 1 − 1/(m+1)^3, where for fixed d one defines π_2(d)=lim_{n→∞} ex_2(n,d)/|Q_n^2|, Q_n={0,1}^n, and ex_2(n,d) is the maximum size of a family S⊆Q_n^2 of 2-subcubes that is Q_n^d-free in the sense that every d-dimensional subcube of Q_n contains at least one 2-subcube not belonging to S?

For each integer d >= 3, let Q_d be the d-dimensional hypercube graph on vertex set {0,1}^d, with two vertices adjacent when they differ in exactly one coordinate. A 1-factorization of Q_d is a partition of E(Q_d) into d perfect matchings. Define r(d) to be the least positive integer for which there exists a 1-factorization M of Q_d such that, for every subfamily N ⊆ M with |N| = r(d), the spanning subgraph obtained by taking the union of the matchings in N is connected. Determine the exact value of r(d).

Conjecture. Let b ≥ a ≥ 2 be integers, and let (A_i, B_i)_{i in I} be a collection of pairs of finite sets indexed by a finite set I such that |A_i| = a, |B_i| = b, and |A_i ∩ B_i| = 2 for every i in I. Assume that for every i, j, k in I with i ≠ j, we have A_i ∩ B_j not contained in A_k ∩ B_k. Is it necessarily true that |I| ≤ Σ_{c=2}^{a} 2^{c-2} * ((a+b-2c) choose (a-c))?

For integers t,n with 4≤t≤n, let [n]:={1,2,...,n}, let K_t denote the complete graph on t vertices, and let g_{K_t}(n) be the maximum size of a family F of simple labelled graphs on the common vertex set [n] such that for every G_1,G_2 in F, the intersection graph G_1∩G_2 contains a copy of K_t. Is it true that g_{K_t}(n)=2^{\binom{n}{2}-\binom{t}{2}} for all 4≤t≤n?

For integers n,t with 3 <= t <= n, let F be a family of simple labelled graphs on the vertex set [n] = {1,2,...,n}. Assume that for every G,H in F, the graph G ∩ H on [n] with edge set E(G) ∩ E(H) satisfies χ(G ∩ H) >= t. Must it always be true that |F| <= 2^{binom(n,2)-binom(t,2)}?

Does there exist an absolute constant c>0 such that, for every n in N and every integer t>=3, whenever F is a family of simple labelled graphs on the vertex-set [n]={1,2,...,n} (equivalently F⊂P(binomial([n],2))) with the property that chi(G∩H)>=t for all G,H in F, where G∩H denotes edgewise intersection, one has |F|<=2^{binom(n,2)-ct^2}?

Let P_3 denote the unlabeled path with three edges, and for n in N let g_{P_3}(n) := max{|F| : F is a family of simple graphs on the labelled vertex set [n] = {1,2,...,n} such that for every G_1,G_2 in F, the edge-intersection G_1 ∩ G_2 contains a copy of P_3}. Does there exist an absolute constant c > 0 such that g_{P_3}(n) <= (1-c)2^{binom(n,2)-1} for every n >= 4? ([scribd.com](https://www.scribd.com/document/926651777/A-Collection-of-Open-Problems-in-Celebration-of-Imre-Leader-s-60th-Birthday))

Does there exist an integer t>=1 and an absolute constant c>0 such that, for every n>=1, every K_{t,t}-intersecting family F of labelled graphs on the vertex set [n]={1,2,...,n} satisfies |F| <= (1-c)2^{\binom{n}{2}-1}? Here K_{t,t}-intersecting means that G_1∩G_2 contains a copy of K_{t,t} for every G_1,G_2 in F.

For a fixed unlabelled graph H, let g_H(n) := max{|F| : F is an H-intersecting family of labelled graphs on [n]}, where F is H-intersecting if G1 ∩ G2 contains a copy of H for every G1,G2 in F. Characterize those unlabelled graphs H for which, for every n in N, one has g_H(n) = 2^{binom(n,2)-e(H)}; equivalently, for every n there exists a maximum-sized H-intersecting family of graphs on [n] consisting of all graphs that contain some fixed copy of H. In the paper’s terminology, for which H does H have the Erdős-Ko-Rado property, and is every critical graph H (meaning every proper subgraph of H has smaller chromatic number than H) guaranteed to have this property? ([scribd.com](https://www.scribd.com/document/926651777/A-Collection-of-Open-Problems-in-Celebration-of-Imre-Leader-s-60th-Birthday))

Let S ⊆ N^2, where N = {1,2,3,...}, viewed as a set of points in R^2. Assume that no three distinct points of S are collinear. Writing [n] = {1,2,...,n}, must every such set S satisfy lim inf_{n->infinity} |S ∩ [n]^2| / n = 0?

Let T_n^k be the k-dimensional discrete torus with vertex set Z_n^k, where x is adjacent to x \pm e_i for each i in [k] (mod n), and let c: V(T_n^k) -> {red, blue} be a balanced colouring, i.e. each colour class has size n^k/2. For the simple random walk on T_n^k, define p_R(c) to be the probability that, when the starting vertex is chosen uniformly from the red class and each step then moves to a uniformly random neighbour, the walk remains in the red class for its first two steps; define p_B(c) analogously for blue. For a fixed dimension k >= 3, determine the asymptotic attainable region of pairs (p_R(c), p_B(c)), meaning the set of limit points of such pairs arising from balanced colourings of T_n^k as n -> infinity through admissible values of n. Is this region exactly conv({(0,0)} U {(l/(2k), l^2/(2k)^2) : k <= l <= 2k} U {(l^2/(2k)^2, l/(2k)) : k <= l <= 2k})?

Fix integers k ≥ 2 and t ≥ 3. For each n, let T_{k,n} be the k-dimensional discrete torus with vertex set (Z/nZ)^k, where two vertices are adjacent if they differ by ±1 modulo n in exactly one coordinate and agree in all other coordinates. For a balanced red-blue colouring V(T_{k,n}) = R ⊔ B with |R| = |B|, let p_t^R be the probability that a simple random walk started from a uniformly random vertex of R remains in R for its first t steps, and let p_t^B be the analogous probability for B. Determine, asymptotically as n → ∞, the set of all pairs (x,y) ∈ [0,1]^2 such that for every ε > 0 there exists n and a balanced colouring of T_{k,n} with |p_t^R - x| < ε and |p_t^B - y| < ε.

For every finite colouring c: N -> [r] of the positive integers, does there exist an infinite sequence (y_n)_{n>=1} of positive integers such that the set {a_1 y_1 + a_2 y_2 + ... + a_k y_k : k >= 1, a_i in {1,2} for all 1 <= i <= k, and a_1 = a_k = 1} is monochromatic under c?

Let c: N -> {1,...,r} be a finite colouring of the natural numbers, for some integer r ≥ 1. Must there exist infinite sets A,B ⊆ N such that the set {ab : a ∈ A, b ∈ B} ∪ {a + b : a ∈ A, b ∈ B} is monochromatic under c?

Let [n] = {1,2,...,n}, and let F ⊆ 2^[n]. Suppose that F contains no induced copy of the diamond poset; equivalently, there do not exist four distinct sets A, B, C, D ∈ F such that A ⊂ B ∩ C, B ∪ C ⊂ D, and B ⊄ C and C ⊄ B. Suppose further that F is maximal with respect to this property, in the sense that for every X ∈ 2^[n] \ F, the family F ∪ {X} does contain such an induced diamond. Must there exist constants c > 0 and n0 such that every such family F satisfies |F| ≥ c n for all n ≥ n0?

Does there exist an absolute constant C such that every finite properly edge-coloured graph G = (V,E) admits a family of at most C|V| paths whose union contains E, with each path rainbow (that is, no two edges on the same path have the same colour)?

For every integer n >= 1 and every red-blue edge-colouring c:E(Q_n)->{red,blue} of the n-dimensional hypercube Q_n, must there exist an antipodal pair of vertices x,x' in V(Q_n) such that x and x' are joined by a geodesic (that is, a shortest) path in Q_n—equivalently, a path of length n with no repeated edge direction—whose sequence of edge colours changes from one colour to the other at most once?

Let Q_n be the n-dimensional hypercube with vertex set {0,1}^n and edges joining pairs of vertices that differ in exactly one coordinate. Two vertices are called antipodal if they differ in every coordinate. Is there a function f(n)=o(n) such that, for every n and every red-blue colouring of the edges of Q_n, there exist antipodal vertices x and y joined by an x-y path P for which the number of indices i at which the i-th and (i+1)-st edges of P have different colours is at most f(n)?

For each n, among all red-blue edge-colourings of the n-dimensional hypercube Q_n, determine the maximum possible value of (1/2^n) sum over v in Q_n of m(v), where m(v) denotes the minimum number of colour changes along any path in Q_n from v to its antipode (the vertex differing from v in every coordinate).

For each fixed k in N, is it true that for every n in N, every edge-colouring of the n-dimensional hypercube Q_n with k+1 colours contains a geodesic path between some antipodal pair of vertices x and x̄ (that is, a shortest x-x̄ path in Q_n, equivalently one using each coordinate direction at most once) such that along this path the colours change at most k times?

Does there exist a non-empty compact convex set S subset of R^3 and a non-empty compact convex set K subset of R^3 such that K is S-Kakeya—that is, for every rotation rho in SO(3) there exists w in R^3 with rho(S)+w subset of K—but there are two S-copies rho_0(S)+w_0 and rho_1(S)+w_1 contained in K for which no continuous maps gamma:[0,1]->SO(3) and delta:[0,1]->R^3 satisfy gamma(0)=rho_0, gamma(1)=rho_1, delta(0)=w_0, delta(1)=w_1, and gamma(t)(S)+delta(t) subset of K for every t in [0,1]?

Does there exist an integer d>=3 and a non-empty compact convex set S subseteq R^d, with S neither a segment nor a Euclidean ball, such that for every convex body K subseteq R^d satisfying the S-Kakeya condition
(for every rotation rho in SO(d) there exists x in R^d with rho(S)+x subseteq K),
any two S-copies in K can be rotated into each other within K; that is, whenever rho_0,rho_1 in SO(d) and x_0,x_1 in R^d satisfy rho_i(S)+x_i subseteq K for i=0,1, there exist continuous maps gamma:[0,1]->SO(d) and delta:[0,1]->R^d with gamma(0)=rho_0, gamma(1)=rho_1, delta(0)=x_0, delta(1)=x_1, and gamma(t)(S)+delta(t) subseteq K for all t in [0,1]?

Find further applications of Pinto’s alternative-compressions method in the Boolean-lattice/compression style of extremal set theory: for families F ⊆ Q_n = P([n]), fix a coordinate i and consider the two i-direction operations that either delete every set S in F containing i whose lower shadow S with i removed is absent from F, or add every set S not containing i for which S with i added already lies in F. In Pinto’s prototype application, neither operation by itself is guaranteed to decrease the upwards directed edge boundary of a family, but the two operations cannot both fail simultaneously, so one can choose adaptively at each step and still complete a compression proof. Identify other problems where this same non-simultaneous-badness principle rescues an otherwise failing compression argument.

For every positive integer k, is there a positive integer K = K(k) such that the following holds? For every positive integer r and every choice of coefficients a_1, ..., a_k in Z/2^rZ, let d be the largest integer with 0 <= d <= r for which there exists a nonempty subset I of {1, ..., k} such that sum_{i in I} a_i belongs to 2^d(Z/2^rZ). Does there exist a colouring c: Z/2^rZ -> {1, ..., K} such that every monochromatic solution (x_1, ..., x_k) in (Z/2^rZ)^k to the equation a_1 x_1 + ... + a_k x_k = 0 in Z/2^rZ satisfies x_i in 2^(r-d)(Z/2^rZ) for every i?

Is the following boundedness conjecture for Euclidean Ramsey sets true? For every k,n in N, does there exist d=d(k,n) in N such that, whenever X is a finite Ramsey set with |X|\le n lying in some Euclidean space R^m, every k-colouring of R^d contains a monochromatic subset congruent to X? Here, X is called Ramsey if for every r in N there exists D in N such that every r-colouring of R^D contains a monochromatic congruent copy of X.

For each positive integer n, let g(n) be the minimum number of Cartesian products E(K_{a,b}) × E(K_{c,d}), where K_{a,b} and K_{c,d} are complete bipartite graphs and the parameters a,b,c,d may vary between parts, required to partition E(K_n) × E(K_n). Is it true that, as n → ∞, g(n) = (4/5 + o(1))n^2?

For each positive integer n, let \widetilde g(n) be the minimum integer m for which there exist complete bipartite subgraphs B_1,C_1,\dots,B_m,C_m of K_n such that every pair (e,f) \in E(K_n) × E(K_n) lies in an odd number of the sets E(B_i) × E(C_i). Determine the exact values of \widetilde g(n). ([scribd.com](https://www.scribd.com/document/926651777/A-Collection-of-Open-Problems-in-Celebration-of-Imre-Leader-s-60th-Birthday))

For fixed integers k > 3 and t with k + 1 <= t <= 2(k - 1)!, let f_k(n,t) := min{|P| : P ⊆ S_n and, for every k-subset X ⊆ [n], the restrictions of the permutations in P to X realize at least t distinct orders}. Theorem 14.2 states that f_k(n,t) = t for t in {1,2}, f_k(n,t) = Theta(log log n) for 3 <= t <= k, and f_k(n,t) = Theta(log n) for 2(k - 1)! + 1 <= t <= k!. Does there exist any t in the unresolved interval k + 1 <= t <= 2(k - 1)! for which f_k(n,t) is not in one of these three regimes, as n -> infinity? ([scribd.com](https://www.scribd.com/document/926651777/A-Collection-of-Open-Problems-in-Celebration-of-Imre-Leader-s-60th-Birthday))

For a fixed integer k > 3 and an integer t with k + 1 <= t <= 2(k - 1)!, let f_k(n,t) be the minimum size of a family P ⊆ S_n such that, for every k-subset X ⊆ [n], the restrictions of the permutations in P to X realize at least t distinct orders. Assuming that for every such t the asymptotic growth of f_k(n,t) as n -> infinity falls into one of the three known regimes Theta(1), Theta(log log n), or Theta(log n), determine exactly for which values of t one has f_k(n,t) = Theta(log log n) and for which values of t one has f_k(n,t) = Theta(log n); equivalently, locate the transition from Theta(log log n) to Theta(log n) within the unresolved interval k + 1 <= t <= 2(k - 1)!.

For every integer n ≥ 1, let S = K[x1, ..., xn] be the standard graded polynomial ring over a field K of characteristic 0, and let I ⊂ S be a homogeneous complete intersection ideal such that A = S/I is Artinian (equivalently, I is generated by a homogeneous regular sequence of length n). Must A have the weak Lefschetz property; that is, does there exist a linear form ℓ ∈ A1 such that ×ℓ : Ai → A{i+1} has maximal rank for every i? More strongly, must A have the strong Lefschetz property; that is, does there exist a linear form ℓ ∈ A1 such that ×ℓ^d : Ai → A{i+d} has maximal rank for every i and every d ≥ 1?

Let K be a field of characteristic 0, let R = K[x1, ..., xn], and let I ⊂ R be a homogeneous complete intersection ideal such that A = R/I is a standard graded Artinian complete intersection. If ht(I) = 3, must A have the strong Lefschetz property; that is, does there exist a linear form ℓ ∈ A1 such that for every i, d >= 0 the multiplication map ×ℓ^d : Ai -> A(i+d) has maximal rank? More generally, is the same true for Artinian complete intersections of larger height, already for ht(I) = 4?

Let K be a field of characteristic zero, let S = K[x1, ..., xn] with its standard grading, and let I ⊆ S be a complete intersection ideal generated by homogeneous polynomials all of the same degree d ∈ N. Assume that S/I has the same monomial basis as the monomial complete intersection S/(x1^d, x2^d, ..., xn^d). Must S/I satisfy the strong Lefschetz property; equivalently, does there exist a linear form l ∈ S1 such that for every i ≥ 0 and k ≥ 1 the multiplication map ×l^k : (S/I)i → (S/I)i+k has maximal rank?

For each fixed integer d >= 2, define p_{n,d}(t) in Z[t] by
p_{n,d}(t) = prod_{i=1}^n (1 + t^i + ... + t^{i(d-1)}),
so equivalently p_{n,d}(t) is the generating polynomial for partitions of m <= (d-1)n(n+1)/2 into at most n parts, with each part used at most d-1 times. Is it true that for every fixed d >= 2 there exists an integer N(d) such that, for all n >= N(d), the coefficient sequence of p_{n,d}(t) (in increasing degree) is unimodal?

Over a field K of characteristic zero, let e_i = e_i(x1, ..., xn) ∈ K[x1, ..., xn] be the i-th elementary symmetric polynomial, and for integers n, d ≥ 1 let hat e_i = e_i(x1^d, ..., xn^d). View K[e1, ..., en] with its inherited non-standard grading, so deg(e_i) = i; then hat e_1, ..., hat e_n form a regular sequence and A(n, d) = K[e1, ..., en]/(hat e_1, ..., hat e_n) is a graded Artinian complete intersection. For which pairs (n, d) does A(n, d) have the strong Lefschetz property, i.e. admit some ℓ ∈ A(n, d)_1 such that for all j, m ≥ 0 the multiplication map ×ℓ^m : A(n, d)_j → A(n, d)_{j+m} has maximal rank?

Over a field K of characteristic 0, let A = ⊕_{i≥0} A_i be a graded Artinian Gorenstein K-algebra of codimension (embedding dimension) 3. Must A satisfy the weak Lefschetz property, i.e. for a general linear form ℓ ∈ A_1 the maps ×ℓ: A_i → A_{i+1} have maximal rank for all i, or even the strong Lefschetz property, i.e. ×ℓ^d: A_i → A_{i+d} has maximal rank for all i and all d ≥ 1? If not, can one characterize the codimension-three Artinian Gorenstein algebras that satisfy WLP and/or SLP?

Let K be a field with char(K) = 0 or char(K) > c, and let A = ⊕_{i=0}^c A_i ≅ K[x1, …, xn]/I be a standard graded Artinian Gorenstein K-algebra of socle degree c and embedding dimension n = dim_K(A_1), where I is homogeneous. Assume that I is stable under the natural action of the symmetric group Sn on K[x1, …, xn] by permuting the variables x1, …, xn, so that Sn acts on A by permutation of the variables. Must A have the strong Lefschetz property; that is, does there exist a linear form ℓ ∈ A_1 such that for every d ≥ 1 and every 0 ≤ i ≤ c − d, the multiplication map ×ℓ^d : A_i → A_{i+d} has maximal rank? ([uniwersalizm.uken.krakow.pl](https://uniwersalizm.uken.krakow.pl/wp-content/uploads/sites/122/2024/05/Lefschetz-Preparatory-School-Notes-by-Migliore-and-Favacchio-v2-1.pdf))

Let S=\mathbb{C}[x_0,\dots,x_n], let f\in S be a homogeneous polynomial of degree d, and assume that the projective hypersurface V(f)=\{x\in \mathbb{P}^n\mid f(x)=0\} is smooth. Let J_f=(\partial f/\partial x_0,\dots,\partial f/\partial x_n) and let M(f)=S/J_f be the graded Milnor (Jacobian) algebra. Is it true that for every such f, the algebra M(f) has the weak Lefschetz property, i.e. there exists a linear form L\in M(f)_1 such that \times L\colon M(f)_i\to M(f)_{i+1} has maximal rank for all i? More strongly, must M(f) always have the strong Lefschetz property, i.e. does there exist L\in M(f)_1 such that \times L^m\colon M(f)_i\to M(f)_{i+m} has maximal rank for all i and all m\ge 1?

Let K be a field of characteristic 0, let R = K[x_1, ..., x_n] with its standard grading, and fix positive integers n and t. For the Artinian monomial level quotients A = R/I of type t, determine, or at least bound, the smallest integer d for which there exists such an algebra A failing the weak Lefschetz property and whose last module in the minimal graded free resolution of A over R is R(-d)^t (equivalently, whose last syzygy module is generated in degree d). If for the given pair (n,t) no such algebra exists, determine that as well.

Let K be a field, let R = K[x_1,\dots,x_n] with its standard grading, and let I \subset R be a homogeneous monomial ideal such that A = R/I is Artinian. Assume that over a field of characteristic 0 the algebra A has the weak Lefschetz property, i.e. there exists a linear form l \in A_1 such that for every d the multiplication map \times l : A_d \to A_{d+1} has maximal rank. Fixing the same monomial generators of I and viewing them over fields of varying characteristic, for which positive prime characteristics p does the corresponding Artinian monomial quotient fail to have the weak Lefschetz property?

Over a field K of characteristic 0, let R = K[x1, ..., xm] be the standard graded polynomial ring, where m, d, r are positive integers. Let L1, ..., Lr be general linear forms in R1, and set I = (x1^d, ..., xm^d, L1^d, ..., Lr^d). Determine all triples (m, d, r) for which the standard graded Artinian algebra A = R/I fails the weak Lefschetz property; that is, for which there does not exist a linear form l in A1 such that the multiplication map x l : Aj -> A_{j+1} has maximal rank for every degree j >= 0.

Over a field K of characteristic 0, let S = K[x_0, ..., x_n] with its standard grading, and let I subseteq S be a square-free Gotzmann ideal, i.e. an ideal of the form I = m_1(x_i : i in J_1) + m_1m_2(x_i : i in J_2) + ... + m_1...m_s(x_i : i in J_s), where m_1, ..., m_s are square-free monomials and J_1, ..., J_s are pairwise disjoint subsets of {0, 1, ..., n}. Among those I for which S/I is Artinian, determine which quotients S/I have the weak Lefschetz property, meaning that there exists a linear form ell in (S/I)_1 such that multiplication by ell from (S/I)_d to (S/I)_{d+1} has maximal rank for every d; and, relatedly, determine whether there exist chordal complexes Delta whose Stanley-Reisner ideals I_Delta admit Artinian reductions S/(I_Delta + (ell_1, ..., ell_r)) by a linear system of parameters that have the weak Lefschetz property. ([ibwu-konferencja.uken.krakow.pl](https://ibwu-konferencja.uken.krakow.pl/wp-content/uploads/sites/122/2024/05/Lefschetz-Preparatory-School-Notes-by-Migliore-and-Favacchio-v2.pdf?utm_source=openai))

Let k be a field of characteristic 0, let Z ⊂ P^n_k be a reduced arithmetically Gorenstein finite set of points, and let A = k[x_0,...,x_n]/I_Z be its standard graded homogeneous coordinate ring. If ℓ ∈ A_1 is a general A-regular linear form (so that A/(ℓ) is a general Artinian reduction of A), must A/(ℓ) have the weak Lefschetz property; equivalently, does there exist a linear form L ∈ [A/(ℓ)]_1 such that the multiplication maps ×L : [A/(ℓ)]_i → [A/(ℓ)]_{i+1} have maximal rank for every i?

Let k be a field of characteristic 0, and let X ⊂ P^n_k be a reduced set of points whose homogeneous coordinate ring is Gorenstein (that is, X is arithmetically Gorenstein). Is the h-vector of X always unimodal?

Let K be a field, let C be an irreducible arithmetically Cohen-Macaulay curve in P^4_K, and let R = K[x0,x1,x2,x3,x4]/I_C be its standard graded homogeneous coordinate ring. Does there exist a linear system of parameters theta_1, theta_2 in R_1 such that the Artinian reduction A = R/(theta_1, theta_2) has the strong Lefschetz property; equivalently, does there exist such a reduction A and a linear form ell in A_1 for which every multiplication map times ell^d: A_i -> A_{i+d} has maximal rank for all integers i,d >= 0?

Other than the four known classes of examples—(1) arrangements of 3 or more concurrent distinct lines, (2) the Fermat arrangements, (3) the Klein arrangement of 21 lines, and (4) the Wiman arrangement of 45 lines—does there exist any finite arrangement of distinct lines L_1, ..., L_r in the complex projective plane P^2 such that no point of P^2 lies on exactly two of the lines?

Over an algebraically closed field of characteristic 0, does there exist a finite reduced set Z in P^3 and integers 1 <= a <= b such that, for a general point P in P^3 and the projection pi_P to a fixed plane H isomorphic to P^2, the image X_P = pi_P(Z) is a transverse complete intersection X_P = C_{a,P} intersection C_{b,P} of plane curves of degrees a and b, where Z is non-trivial in the sense that it is neither a degenerate geproci set nor a grid, and where neither C_{a,P} nor C_{b,P} is an unexpected curve for X_P (that is, for d = a and d = b and for a general point Q in P^2, one has h^0(I_{X_P union (d-1)Q}(d)) = max{h^0(I_{X_P}(d)) - binomial(d,2), 0})? If such a set exists, construct one; otherwise prove that no such non-trivial (a,b)-geproci set exists.

Let Z be a finite subset of P^3 such that for a general point P, the projection of Z from P to a plane H isomorphic to P^2 is the transverse complete intersection C_{a,P} intersect C_{b,P} of plane curves of degrees a <= b; equivalently, Z is an (a, b)-geproci set, so |Z| = ab. Assume Z is non-trivial in the sense of the paper, namely that Z is neither one of the degenerate geproci examples already lying in a hyperplane as a complete intersection there nor an (a, b)-grid (the ab intersection points of a skew lines with b skew lines in P^3, each line from one family meeting each line from the other exactly once). Must every such non-trivial (a, b)-geproci set contain a 3-point collinear subset, or does there exist a counterexample with no three collinear points?

Over ℚ, does there exist a finite reduced set of points Z ⊂ ℙ^3 in linear general position (i.e. no four points coplanar), other than a set of four general points, for which there exist integers a ≤ b such that the projection of Z from a general point of ℙ^3 to ℙ^2 is the transverse complete intersection of two plane curves of degrees a and b?
