Let Z and Z' be finite geproci point sets in projective space, where 'geproci' means that the image of the set under projection from a general point to a fixed hyperplane is a complete intersection, and let M(Z) and M(Z') be the matroids determined by the linear dependence relations among the points. If M(Z) is isomorphic to M(Z'), must Z and Z' be projectively equivalent? More generally, if W is a finite point set whose associated matroid is isomorphic to the matroid of some geproci set Z, must W itself be geproci?

Let k be a field of characteristic 0, let S = k[x_1,...,x_n] be standard graded, and let Delta be a balanced simplicial (d-1)-sphere on vertex set [n]. Thus there exists a proper d-coloring kappa:[n] -> [d], and if I_Delta is the Stanley-Reisner ideal of Delta, then the colored linear system of parameters is Theta = (theta_1,...,theta_d) with theta_i = sum_{kappa(v)=i} x_v. For the Artinian reduction A = k[Delta]/Theta k[Delta] ~= S/(I_Delta + (Theta)), must A have the strong Lefschetz property; that is, does there always exist a linear form omega in A_1 such that the maps times omega^(d-2i): A_i -> A_(d-i) are isomorphisms for all 0 <= i <= floor(d/2)? If not, does A at least always have the weak Lefschetz property, meaning that for some linear form omega in A_1 the maps times omega: A_i -> A_(i+1) have maximal rank for every i?

Let K be a field of characteristic 0, let S = K[x_1, ..., x_n] be the standard graded polynomial ring, and let Delta be a centrally symmetric simplicial (d-1)-sphere on vertex set [n] = {1, ..., n}; that is, Delta admits a fixed-point-free involution alpha:[n] -> [n] such that Delta = {alpha(F) : F in Delta}. Extend alpha to S by alpha(x_v) = x_{alpha(v)}, and write S^- = {f in S : alpha(f) = -f}. If Theta = theta_1, ..., theta_d is a generic linear system of parameters for K[Delta] = S/I_Delta with each theta_i in the degree-1 anti-invariant subspace (S^-)_1, and if w = x_1 + ... + x_n, must the Artinian reduction A = S/(I_Delta + (Theta)) have the strong Lefschetz property with respect to w (that is, for every i >= 0 and j >= 1, multiplication by w^j induces a map A_i -> A_{i+j} of maximal rank), or at least the weak Lefschetz property with respect to w (that is, multiplication by w induces a map A_i -> A_{i+1} of maximal rank for every i >= 0)?

Let K be a field of characteristic 0, let S=K[x1,…,xn] be the standard graded polynomial ring, and let Δ be a flag simplicial (d−1)-sphere on [n] with d≥5 and Stanley–Reisner ideal IΔ⊆S. For generic choices of a linear system of parameters Θ=θ1,…,θd for K[Δ]=S/IΔ and additional generic linear forms w,w′∈S_1, is the multiplication map ×w′ : (S/(IΔ+(Θ,w)))_1 → (S/(IΔ+(Θ,w)))_2 injective?

Over a field K of characteristic zero, let Gamma be a CW complex that is Cohen-Macaulay over K, let sd(Gamma) be its barycentric subdivision, let S = K[x_v : v in V(sd(Gamma))], let I_sd(Gamma) be the Stanley-Reisner ideal of sd(Gamma), and let Theta be a linear system of parameters for K[sd(Gamma)] = S/I_sd(Gamma). Does there exist such a Gamma for which, for every linear system of parameters Theta, the Artinian reduction A_Theta = S/(I_sd(Gamma) + (Theta)) fails the weak Lefschetz property; that is, for each Theta there is no linear form w in (A_Theta)_1 such that the multiplication maps A_Theta,i -> A_Theta,i+1 have maximal rank for all i?

Over a field K of characteristic 0, let S = K[x_1, ..., x_n] be standard graded, let Δ be a (d-1)-dimensional simplicial complex with Stanley-Reisner ideal I_Δ, let Θ = θ_1, ..., θ_d be a generic linear system of parameters for K[Δ] = S/I_Δ, and let w in S_1 be a generic linear form. Apart from barycentric subdivisions sd(Γ) of (d-1)-dimensional Cohen-Macaulay CW complexes Γ, are there other classes of simplicial complexes Δ for which the Artinian reduction A = S/(I_Δ + (Θ)) satisfies, for every integer k with 0 ≤ k ≤ floor((d-1)/2), that multiplication by w^(d-2k-1) induces an injective map A_k -> A_{d-1-k} and a surjective map A_{k+1} -> A_{d-k}? ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2311.03081))

Let K be a field of characteristic 0, let F_1,...,F_s be homogeneous forms of common degree d in K[y_1,...,y_n], let x_1,...,x_s be new variables, and for an integer e >= 1 set G_e = sum_{i=1}^s x_i^e F_i in K[x_1,...,x_s,y_1,...,y_n]. Let A_e := K[X_1,...,X_s,Y_1,...,Y_n]/Ann(G_e), where X_i = d/dx_i and Y_j = d/dy_j act by differentiation on G_e, so that A_e is the standard graded Artinian Gorenstein algebra with Macaulay dual generator G_e. Determine for which integers e and which choices of F_1,...,F_s the algebra A_e has the weak Lefschetz property and for which it has the strong Lefschetz property; that is, determine when there exists a linear form ell in (A_e)_1 such that multiplication by ell, respectively by ell^k for every k >= 1, has maximal rank in every degree. In particular, classify the unresolved range e < d, since the paper records that WLP already holds for all F_i when e >= d.

Let k be an infinite field, let A = ⊕_{i≥0} A_i be a graded Artinian k-algebra with maximal ideal m_A = ⊕_{i>0} A_i, and let M be a finite graded A-module. For ℓ in m_A, let P_{ℓ,M} denote the Jordan type of the nilpotent multiplication map ×ℓ: M -> M. Define the generic Jordan type P_M to be P_{ℓ,M} for ℓ in a Zariski-open dense subset of m_A, and, when A_1 ≠ 0, define the generic linear Jordan type P_{1,M} to be P_{ℓ,M} for ℓ in a Zariski-open dense subset of A_1. In the special case M = A, Proposition 2.14 shows that if A is standard graded, H(A) is unimodal with a single maximum and no dips, and P_A = H(A)^∨ (equivalently, A is strong Lefschetz), then P_A = P_{1,A}. Does this equality still hold when H(A) is not unimodal, or when P_A ≠ H(A)^∨? More generally, for which graded modules M over graded Artinian algebras A does one have P_M = P_{1,M}?

Let k be any field, and let H be a non-unimodal Hilbert function that occurs as H(A) for some graded Artinian k-algebra A. For which such H can one find a pair (A, ℓ), where A is a graded Artinian k-algebra with H(A)=H and ℓ∈A1, such that the multiplication map ×ℓ on A has Jordan type Pℓ,A equal to the contiguous Jordan type Pc(H), and similarly, at the finer level, Jordan degree type Pdeg,ℓ,A equal to the contiguous Jordan degree type Pc,deg(H), where Pc(H) and Pc,deg(H) are defined from the bar graph of H? ([uniwersalizm.uken.krakow.pl](https://uniwersalizm.uken.krakow.pl/wp-content/uploads/sites/122/2024/05/Lefschetz-Preparatory-School-Notes-by-Migliore-and-Favacchio-v2-1.pdf))

Let K be an infinite field, let R = K[x_1, ..., x_n], let I be a homogeneous ideal such that A = R/I is a standard graded Artinian algebra, and let in(I) denote the initial ideal of I with respect to a fixed monomial order. If P_deg,ell,A denotes the Jordan degree type of multiplication by a linear form ell in A_1 (recording both the Jordan block lengths and the initial degrees of the ell-strings in a K[ell]-decomposition of A), how does the generic Jordan degree type of A, namely P_deg,ell,A for generic ell in A_1, compare with the generic Jordan degree type of R/in(I)? More specifically, in view of the known inequality dim_K(R/(I, ell^k))_j <= dim_K(R/(in(I), ell^k))_j for generic ell and all j, k, does there exist a pair (A, ell) with ell in A_1 such that the Jordan degree type P_deg,ell,A is not realized by any pair (A', ell'), where A' = R/J is a standard graded Artinian algebra defined by a monomial ideal J and ell' belongs to A'_1?

Over an arbitrary field K, let Z(H) denote the family of non-graded Artinian K-algebras A with Hilbert function H. For which Hilbert function sequences H does Z(H) have several irreducible components Xi_1, Xi_2, ... such that, for a general algebra A on each Xi_i, the Jordan type of multiplication by a general element l of the maximal ideal m_A is the same on all these components, while the components are nevertheless distinguished by one of the refined non-graded Jordan invariants—namely sequential Jordan type, Loewy sequential Jordan type, or double sequential Jordan type?

Let K be any field, let A be an Artinian K-algebra that is a quotient of K[x1, ..., xn] or of the local regular ring K{x1, ..., xn}, and let m = (x1, ..., xn) be its maximal ideal. For a finite A-module X and an element ℓ in m, let P_{ℓ,X} denote the partition of dim_K X given by the Jordan block decomposition of the nilpotent multiplication map ×ℓ : X -> X. Given an exact sequence 0 -> L -> M -> N -> 0 of finite A-modules, how are the generic Jordan types P_L, P_M, and P_N (for a common generic ℓ) related, and under what hypotheses can one obtain an additive relation P_M = P_L + P_N in a suitable partition-theoretic sense? In the graded setting, with A and the modules graded and ℓ a generic linear form in A1, can one formulate and prove the analogous comparison/additivity statements for Jordan degree type; and in the non-graded setting, can one do the same for sequential Jordan type, Loewy sequential Jordan type, and double sequential Jordan type?

Let k be a field and let A = ⊕_{i=0}^d A_i be a standard graded Artinian Gorenstein k-algebra. For a generic linear form ℓ ∈ A_1, let P_{A,ℓ} denote the Jordan partition of the nilpotent multiplication map m_ℓ:A→A, a↦ℓa. For the known families of graded Artinian Gorenstein algebras that fail the weak Lefschetz property, determine the number of parts of P_{A,ℓ}. More generally, if A fails the strong Lefschetz property, determine the full generic linear Jordan type P_{A,ℓ}.

For a fixed finite sequence H that occurs as the Hilbert function H(A) of some graded Artinian Gorenstein K-algebra A, determine the Jordan data compatible with H: namely, which partitions P can occur as the Jordan type of the nilpotent multiplication operator m_ell: A -> A for some pair (A, ℓ) with H(A)=H and ℓ in the maximal ideal of A, and which Jordan degree types can occur for such pairs in the graded setting?

Fix a codimension-two complete-intersection Hilbert function H. In the height-two complete-intersection setting of [10]—that is, for standard graded Artinian algebras A = k[x,y]/I over an algebraically closed field k with char(k) = 0 or char(k) > j, where j is the socle degree, and H(A) = H—determine all pairs of partitions (P,Q) for which there exist linear forms ell_1, ell_2 in A_1 such that P and Q are the Jordan types of the nilpotent multiplication maps m_{ell_1}, m_{ell_2}: A -> A.

For each fixed integer d >= 3, do there exist constants k, lambda > 0 and an infinite family {X_m}_{m>=1} of finite d-dimensional simplicial complexes such that every vertex of every X_m has degree at most k and, for every m and every 0 <= i < d, the i-coboundary Cheeger constant h_B^i(X_m,F2) is at least lambda, where h_B^i(X,F2) is the infimum of ||delta_i alpha|| / d(alpha,B^i(X,F2)) over all F2-valued i-cochains alpha not in B^i(X,F2), with d the normalized distance induced by the paper’s probability distributions on oriented i-cells?

Let G be a simple p-adic Lie group of rank d ≥ 3, let B be the Bruhat–Tits building associated with G, and assume p ≥ p(d) ≫ 0. Is it true that for every lattice Γ ≤ G one has h1(Γ\B, Sym) > 0, where h1(X, Sym) := inf{ ||δα|| / d(α, Z^1(X, Sym)) : α ∈ C^1(X, Sym), ||δα|| ≠ 0 } is the first cocycle Cheeger constant of X with permutation coefficients, and Sym = ⨆_{n≥2} Sym(n) is equipped with the normalized Hamming distance with errors?

Does there exist a finitely presented group Γ ≅ ⟨S|R⟩ that is non-sofic, meaning that there is no sequence of maps f_n: S → Sym(n) such that, with d_h the normalized Hamming distance and f_n(w) denoting evaluation of a word w under f_n, one has d_h(f_n(r), Id) → 0 for every relator r ∈ R, while for every word w not in the normal closure ⟨⟨R⟩⟩ of R in the free group on S one has lim inf_{n→∞} d_h(f_n(w), Id) ≥ 1/2?

Does there exist an infinite family {X_m}_{m=1}^∞ of connected finite polygonal complexes (that is, finite 2-dimensional CW complexes with polygonal 2-cells attached along cyclically reduced loops), each equipped with the probability distributions on oriented cells assumed in Section 2, and a constant k ∈ N such that every vertex of every X_m has degree at most k, together with a constant λ > 0, for which one has h_i^B(X_m, Sym) ≥ λ for every m ∈ N and for i = 0, 1? Here Sym means ⨆_{n≥2} Sym(n) with the normalized Hamming distance with errors d_h, and h_i^B(X, Sym) is the coboundary Cheeger constant h_i^B(X, Sym) = inf { ||δα|| / d(α, B_i(X, Sym)) : α ∈ C^i(X, Sym) \ B_i(X, Sym) }.

Does there exist an infinite family {X_m}_{m∈N} of connected finite polygonal complexes (i.e. finite combinatorial 2-dimensional CW complexes), together with constants k∈N and λ>0, such that every vertex of every X_m has degree at most k and, with permutation coefficients Sym in the sense of the paper (all finite symmetric groups Sym(n), n≥2, equipped with the normalized Hamming distance with errors and the chosen cell measures), one has for every m∈N: h_0(X_m, Sym) ≥ λ, h_1(X_m, Sym) ≥ λ, and CoSyst_1(X_m, Sym) ≥ λ, where CoSyst_1(X_m, Sym) is the infimum of ||α|| over connected non-coboundary 1-cocycles α∈Z_1(X_m, Sym)?

Let X_<S|R> be the presentation complex of a finite presentation <S|R>, equipped with its chosen probability measures on generators and relations, and let h1(X_<S|R>, Sym) denote its dimension-1 cocycle Cheeger constant with permutation coefficients Sym, computed using the normalized Hamming distance with errors. For the standard Steinberg presentation of SL_n(F_p) (more generally, of groups of Lie type), with generators U_ij(a)=Id+e_ij(a) and relations U_ij(a)U_ij(b)=U_ij(a+b) together with the usual Steinberg commutator relations [U_ij(a),U_kell(b)]=1_{j=k}U_iell(ab), is there a constant lambda>0 such that h1(X_Steinberg, Sym) >= lambda uniformly, at least in the regime where n is fixed and p tends to infinity? Conversely, for the Guralnick-Kantor-Kassabov-Lubotzky presentations of these groups, whose size is uniformly bounded and whose relation lengths are O(log n + log p), must h1(X_GKKL, Sym) tend to 0 along any family in which either n tends to infinity or p tends to infinity? ([storage.googleapis.com](https://storage.googleapis.com/arxiv-dataset/arxiv/arxiv/pdf/2311/2311.06706v3.pdf))

Problem 6.9 (§6.4): Does there exist a family of finite groups {G_i} with finite presentations G_i ≅ <S_i|R_i>, considered with the paper’s presentation-complex formalism and generator/relation measures, such that |S_i| and |R_i| are polylogarithmic in |G_i|, every relation r ∈ R_i has word length |r| = polylog(|G_i|), and the presentation <S_i|R_i> is ρ_i-homomorphism stable in permutations—equivalently, its associated presentation complex X_{<S_i|R_i>} is ρ_i-cocycle stable in dimension 1 with permutation coefficients Sym(n) equipped with normalized Hamming distance—with stability rate ρ_i(ε) = polyloglog(|G_i|) · ε^c for some exponent c > 0 independent of i (equivalently, independent of |G_i|)?

Let A be an m x n matrix over F_2, let k = n - rank(A), and let G_A ≅ F_2^k be given by the presentation with generators x_1, ..., x_n and relations x_i^2 = 1 for all i in [n], [x_i, x_j] = 1 for all i, j in [n], and product_{j=1}^n x_j^{A_{ij}} = 1 for all i in [m]. With the associated presentation complex and the presentation-complex notion of permutation-coefficient homomorphism stability from §2 (using the normalized Hamming distance with errors and allowing assignments into arbitrary Sym(N), N >= 2), what is the stability rate ρ of this presentation? Equivalently, beyond the Sym(2) regime that recovers ρ-local testability of Ker(A) under the matrix tester, can one determine this permutation-coefficient stability rate for natural code families such as Reed–Muller codes and the recently constructed good locally testable codes?

Can one find a real Hénon map of some degree on R^2 that admits a wild attractor, namely an invariant Cantor set that attracts a set of positive Lebesgue measure and is strictly contained in a transitive invariant set?

For the real quadratic Hénon family H_{a,c}(x,y)=(ay+x^2+c,ax) (up to the affine-conjugate normal forms allowed in the paper), is there a quick proof that there exist parameter values (a,c) for which H_{a,c} has an attractor supporting an invariant SRB measure, i.e. an invariant measure whose conditional measures along unstable curves are absolutely continuous?

Let f_{c,b}: R^2 → R^2 be a real quadratic Hénon map, f_{c,b}(x,y) = (x^2 + c - by, x), with b,c ∈ R. Is it true that every f_{c,b}-invariant Borel probability measure μ satisfies supp(μ) ⊂ closure(Per(f_{c,b})), where Per(f_{c,b}) denotes the set of periodic points of f_{c,b}? ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2312.03907))

Given the quadratic Hénon family f_{c,b}: R^2 -> R^2 defined by f_{c,b}(x,y)=(x^2+c-by,x), with real parameters (c,b) in R^2, can one construct an algorithm that, for an input pair (c,b), computes a rigorous upper bound for the topological entropy h_top(f_{c,b}|_{R^2})?

Let d ≥ 3 and let f be a polynomial automorphism of C^d. If deg(g) denotes the degree of a polynomial self-map g of C^d and λ(f) := lim_{n→∞} (deg(f^n))^(1/n) is the dynamical degree of f, must λ(f) always be a weak Perron number of algebraic degree at most d−1; that is, an algebraic integer λ ≥ 1 whose Galois conjugates μ all satisfy |μ| ≤ λ and whose degree over Q is ≤ d−1?

Let d >= 3 and let f in Aut(C^d) be a polynomial automorphism. Write deg(f^n) for the polynomial degree of the n-th iterate and define the dynamical degree by lambda(f) := lim_{n->infinity} deg(f^n)^(1/n). Assume lambda(f) = 1. Must there exist an integer k >= 0 and constants c, C > 0 such that c n^k <= deg(f^n) <= C n^k for all sufficiently large n? Moreover, if k >= 1, must f preserve a rational fibration, i.e. is there a nonconstant dominant rational map pi: C^d -> B with 0 < dim(B) < d and a birational self-map g: B -> B such that pi o f = g o pi?

Let f:ℂ^d→ℂ^d be a polynomial automorphism, let deg(f) denote the maximum total degree of its coordinate polynomials, and define its dynamical degree by λ(f):=lim_{n→∞}(deg(f^n))^{1/n}. Assume that λ(f)=1 and that the degree sequence (deg(f^n))_{n≥1} is unbounded. Must there exist a constant C>0 such that deg(f^n)≥Cn for all n≥1?

For every non-Kähler compact complex surface X, i.e. every compact complex manifold of complex dimension 2 over C that is not Kähler, does X admit a birational structure in the following sense: there exists a holomorphic atlas {(U_i, phi_i)} such that each phi_i maps U_i biholomorphically onto an open subset of C^2, and for every nonempty overlap U_i ∩ U_j, the transition map phi_j o phi_i^{-1} is the restriction of a birational self-map of P^2_C? ([math.univ-toulouse.fr](https://www.math.univ-toulouse.fr/~buff/Preprints/Henon/Henon.pdf))

Let f ∈ Aut(C^3) be a polynomial automorphism of complex affine 3-space, and let λ(f) := lim_{n→∞} deg(f^n)^{1/n} denote its dynamical degree. Assume that λ(f)^2 > λ(f^{-1}). Does there exist a projective compactification X of C^3 such that the induced birational map f : X ⇢ X admits a super-attracting fixed point p on the divisor at infinity?

Fix a number field K. Does there exist an infinite family {f_d}_{d≥2} of generalized Hénon maps f_d:A^2_K→A^2_K, where each f_d is a finite composition of Hénon maps H_{a_i,P_i}(x,y)=(a_i y+P_i(x),x) with a_i∈K^* and P_i∈K[x], and where the algebraic degree satisfies deg(f_d)=∏_i deg(P_i)=d, such that f_d admits a K-rational periodic cycle of exact period at least d+3? More ambitiously, can one choose such maps so that the number N_d of K-rational periodic points of f_d satisfies N_d-d→∞, or even N_d/d→∞, as d→∞? ([math.univ-toulouse.fr](https://www.math.univ-toulouse.fr/~buff/Preprints/Henon/Henon.pdf))

Let A:f=0 be a finite reduced arrangement of projective lines in the complex projective plane P^2_C, where f in S=C[x,y,z] is a product of distinct linear forms, and suppose that A is free in the sense that its Jacobian-syzygy module D0(f)=AR(f) is a free S-module of rank 2. If B:g=0 is another line arrangement in P^2_C whose intersection lattice is isomorphic to that of A, must B also be free?

Let A : f = 0 be a line arrangement in the complex projective plane P^2_C, where f = l_1 \cdots l_d belongs to S = C[x,y,z] and is a reduced homogeneous product of d distinct linear forms. Let mdr(f) be the smallest integer r for which there exists a nonzero homogeneous Jacobian syzygy a f_x + b f_y + c f_z = 0 with a,b,c in S_r. Assume that r = mdr(f) < d/2. Is r combinatorially determined by the intersection lattice L(A); equivalently, if B : g = 0 is any line arrangement in P^2_C with L(B) isomorphic to L(A), must one have mdr(g) = mdr(f)?

Let A : f = 0 be a line arrangement of d >= 3 lines in the complex projective plane P^2, where f in S = C[x,y,z] is the reduced homogeneous product of the defining linear forms. Let J_f = (f_x,f_y,f_z), let I_f be the saturation of J_f with respect to the maximal ideal m = (x,y,z), let N(f) = I_f/J_f = H^0_m(S/J_f), and define the freeness defect by ν(A) = max_j dim_C N(f)_j. Is ν(A) determined solely by the intersection lattice L(A) of the arrangement?

Let S=C[x,y,z], let f∈S be a reduced homogeneous polynomial of degree d≥3, and let C:f=0⊂P^2_C be the corresponding reduced plane curve. If J_f=(f_x,f_y,f_z), I_f is the saturation of J_f with respect to m=(x,y,z), N(f)=I_f/J_f, and ν(C)=max_j dim_C N(f)_j, is ν(C) determined by d together with the list of local analytic types of the isolated singularities of C? ([imar.ro](https://imar.ro/journals/Revue_Mathematique/pdfs/2024/2/4.pdf))

Let C:f=0 be a reduced arrangement of d lines in the complex projective plane P^2, where f ∈ S = C[x,y,z] is a reduced homogeneous product of d linear forms. Let D_0(f) = { (a,b,c) ∈ S^3 : a f_x + b f_y + c f_z = 0 }, let E_C = D_0(f)~ = T⟨C⟩(-1), and for a generic line L_0 ⊂ P^2 write E_C|_{L_0} ≅ O_{L_0}(-d_1^{L_0}) ⊕ O_{L_0}(-d_2^{L_0}) with d_1^{L_0} ≤ d_2^{L_0}. Is the generic splitting type (d_1^{L_0}, d_2^{L_0}) determined by the intersection lattice L(C) of the arrangement? Equivalently, if two complex line arrangements in P^2 have isomorphic intersection lattices, must their associated bundles T⟨C⟩(-1) have the same generic splitting type?

Let S = C[x,y,z], and let A:f=0 be a line arrangement in P^2_C, so that f in S_d is the reduced product of d = deg(f) distinct linear forms. Define AR(f) = {(a,b,c) in S^3 : a f_x + b f_y + c f_z = 0} and mdr(f) = min{r : AR(f)_r != 0}. Let J_f = (f_x,f_y,f_z), let I_f be the saturation of J_f with respect to the maximal ideal (x,y,z), and let Sigma_f subset P^2_C be the 0-dimensional singular subscheme defined by I_f. For each integer k, set def_k Sigma_f = tau(A) - dim_C(S_k/(I_f)_k). If mdr(f) < d/2, is the largest integer k such that def_k Sigma_f != 0 determined solely by the intersection lattice L(A) of the arrangement?

Let S = C[x,y,z], and let A:f=0 be a line arrangement in P^2_C, where f in S_d is a homogeneous reduced polynomial that factors as a product of d distinct linear forms. Write J_f = (f_x,f_y,f_z) and M(f) = S/J_f. If f_s in S_d defines a smooth plane curve C_s:f_s=0 of the same degree d, define the coincidence threshold and stability threshold by ct(f) = max{q in Z : dim_C M(f)_k = dim_C M(f_s)_k for every k <= q} and st(f) = min{q in Z : dim_C M(f)_k = tau(A) for every k >= q}, where tau(A) is the total Tjurina number of A. Is the invariant ct(f)+st(f) determined by the intersection lattice L(A) of the arrangement?

Let S = C[x,y,z], let f in S_d be a homogeneous reduced polynomial of degree d >= 3, and let C : f = 0 be the corresponding reduced plane curve in P^2. Write J_f = (f_x,f_y,f_z), M(f) = S/J_f, let I_f be the saturation of J_f with respect to m = (x,y,z), let N(f) = I_f/J_f = H^0_m(M(f)), define the freeness defect by nu(C) = max_j dim_C N(f)_j, and set T = 3(d - 2). With ct(f) = max{q : dim M(f)_k = dim M(f_s)_k for all k <= q}, where f_s is a smooth degree-d homogeneous polynomial, and st(f) = min{q : dim M(f)_k = tau(C) for all k >= q}, what is the general relation between ct(f) + st(f) and nu(C) for reduced plane curves C in P^2? In particular, beyond the plus-one generated case (equivalently, 3-syzygy curves with d1 + d2 = d), for which ct(f) + st(f) = T + nu(C) + 1, can this relation be described in a way consistent with the Section 6 Thom-Sebastiani examples, which show that no universal linear dependence on nu(C) can hold in general, even among 3-syzygy curves?

Let C : f = 0 be a reduced plane curve of degree d in P^2_C, defined by a homogeneous polynomial f in S = C[x,y,z], and assume that C is rational and that all singularities of C are unibranch (so C is a plane rational cuspidal curve). If D0(f) = {(a,b,c) in S^3 : a f_x + b f_y + c f_z = 0} denotes the Jacobian syzygy module of f, must C always be either free, meaning that D0(f) is a free S-module of rank 2, or nearly free, meaning that D0(f) has three minimal homogeneous generators of degrees d1 <= d2 <= d3 with d3 = d2 and d1 + d2 = d?

Let S = C[x,y,z], let f ∈ S be homogeneous of degree d ≥ 3, and let C : f = 0 ⊂ P^2_C be a reduced plane curve. Write AR(f) = {(a,b,c) ∈ S^3 : af_x + bf_y + cf_z = 0} and mdr(f) = min{q : AR(f)_q ≠ 0}. For every integer r with d/2 ≤ r ≤ d−1, does there exist such a curve C with mdr(f)=r and total Tjurina number τ(C) = (d−1)^2 − r(d−r−1) − binom(2r+2−d,2), i.e. a maximal Tjurina curve of type (d,r)? Moreover, for every integer r with d/2 ≤ r ≤ d−2, can one choose C to be a line arrangement of d lines in P^2_C? ([imar.ro](https://imar.ro/journals/Revue_Mathematique/pdfs/2024/2/4.pdf))

Let C : f = 0 ⊂ P^2_C be a non-free arrangement of d >= 4 distinct lines, with f in S = C[x,y,z] homogeneous, and let r = mdr(f) >= 2 be the minimal degree of a nonzero homogeneous Jacobian relation a f_x + b f_y + c f_z = 0. If m(C) denotes the maximal multiplicity of a point of C and n(C) denotes the maximal multiplicity of a point of C \ {p}, where p is a point of multiplicity m(C), then the general lower bound tau(C) >= tau(d,r)_min := (d-1)(d-r-1) is known not to be optimal for line arrangements, while Theorem 6.2 and Corollary 6.3 give the stronger bounds tau(C) >= tau(d,r)_min + binom(r,2) + binom(n(C),2) + 1 and, when r != d - m(C), tau(C) >= tau(d,r)_min + binom(r,2) + binom(m(C),2) + 1, hence in particular tau(C) >= tau(d,r)_min + binom(r,2) + 4 when r >= 3 and n(C) >= 3. What is the optimal universal lower bound for tau(C) for such non-free line arrangements?

For every integer m ≥ 2, does there exist a maximizing curve C_{2m+1}, meaning a reduced projective plane curve C = V(f) ⊂ ℙ^2 over ℂ defined by a reduced homogeneous polynomial f ∈ ℂ[x, y, z] of degree d = 2m + 1, whose singularities are all simple of type A, D, E and whose total Tjurina number is τ(C) = 3m^2 + 1? ([imar.ro](https://imar.ro/journals/Revue_Mathematique/pdfs/2024/2/4.pdf))

Let C = V(f) subset P^2_C be a reduced plane curve, where f is a reduced homogeneous polynomial in S = C[x,y,z]. Suppose there exists a point p in C such that the central projection pi_p: P^2_C \ {p} -> P^1_C restricts to a locally trivial fibration on the complement M(C) = P^2_C \ C; equivalently, suppose C is supersolvable in the sense of Definition 8.1. Must C be a free plane curve, i.e. must its Jacobian syzygy module D0(f) = {(a,b,c) in S^3 : a f_x + b f_y + c f_z = 0} be a free S-module of rank 2?

For a fixed real parameter s, let L_TW,s be the self-adjoint differential operator on L^2([s,+infinity)) introduced by Tracy and Widom, acting on sufficiently smooth f by (L_TW,s f)(x) = d/dx((x-s) f'(x)) - x(x-s) f(x). Since L_TW,s is the differential operator that commutes with the Airy kernel operator in the soft-edge GUE Tracy-Widom setting, study the L^2([s,+infinity))-eigenvectors of L_TW,s.

Fix n in N and s in R. Let K_n be the GUE kernel operator on L^2([s,+infinity)) obtained by restricting the orthogonal projection in L^2(R) onto the span of the first n probabilistic Hermite functions {phi_0,...,phi_{n-1}}, so that K_n has kernel K_n(x,y)=sum_{k=0}^{n-1} phi_k(x)phi_k(y). Does there exist a differential operator D_{n,s} acting on L^2([s,+infinity)) such that D_{n,s}K_n=K_nD_{n,s}? If so, describe its eigenvectors. The sought operator is not required to be of second order, but under the standard soft-edge rescaling that sends K_n to the Airy kernel operator it should converge, in an appropriate sense, to the Tracy-Widom differential operator for the Airy kernel from Question 1. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/html/2312.07754v1))

Fix an integer n >= 2 and real numbers f_0,...,f_n. Define
P_n(z) = sum_{k=0}^n f_k f_{n-k} binom(n,k) [(z)_k (z)_{n-k} - (z+1)_k (z-1)_{n-k}],
where (z)_0 = 1 and (z)_m = z(z+1)...(z+m-1) for m >= 1. Assume that the generating polynomial F(x) = sum_{k=0}^n f_k x^k has only real strictly negative zeros. Must every zero of P_n(z) also be real and strictly negative?

Let n be a nonnegative integer and let {f_k}_{k=0}^n be a finite real sequence. Define f(x;z)=sum_{k=0}^n f_k (x)_k z^k/k!, where (x)_0=1 and (x)_k=x(x+1)...(x+k-1). For each integer r>=2, form the r x r Toeplitz determinant F_r(x,z)=det[f(x+j-i;z)]_{i,j=1}^r and expand it as F_r(x,z)=sum_{m>=0} P_m^r(x) z^m/m!; equivalently, P_n^r(x)=sum_{k_1+...+k_r=n} (n!/(k_1!...k_r!)) f_{k_1}...f_{k_r} det[(x+j-i)_{k_j}]_{i,j=1}^r. If the ordinary generating polynomial sum_{k=0}^n f_k t^k has only real negative zeros, must the coefficient polynomial P_n^r(x) also have only real negative zeros for every integer r>=2?

Let r >= 2 and define f(x;z) = sum_{k>=0} f_k (x)_k z^k/k!, where (x)_k is the rising factorial. Form the Toeplitz determinant
F_r(x,z) = det[f(x+j-i;z)]_{i,j=1}^r = sum_{m>=0} z^m P_m^r(x).
Suppose the finite sequence {f_0,f_1,...,f_n} is a Pólya frequency sequence of order r, i.e. after extending by f_k = 0 outside {0,1,...,n}, all minors of order at most r of the Toeplitz matrix [f_{j-i}] are nonnegative. Must the coefficient polynomial P_n^r(x) be Hurwitz stable, meaning that every zero of P_n^r lies in the open left half-plane Re x < 0 (and hence, in particular, P_n^r has positive coefficients)?

Let d be a positive integer, let a_1,...,a_d,b be real parameters, let m_1,...,m_d be positive integers, and set m = m_1 + ... + m_d. Define A(x) in R[x] by the identity of Taylor series at x = 0, _{d+1}F_d(a_1+m_1,...,a_d+m_d,b ; a_1,...,a_d ; x) = A(x)/(1-x)^(m+b), where _pF_q denotes the generalized hypergeometric series and (u)_n is the Pochhammer symbol. (By the Miller-Paris transformation, A(x) is indeed a polynomial.) Find sufficient conditions on the parameters a_1,...,a_d,b,m_1,...,m_d that guarantee that A(x) has only real zeros.

Let P be a monic polynomial of degree n with zeros z_1,...,z_n counted with multiplicity, and define its normalized zero counting measure by ν(P)=n^{-1}∑_{j=1}^n δ_{z_j}. Let V: C → R ∪ {+∞} be a continuous external field, not identically +∞, such that lim_{|z|→∞}(V(z)-log(1+|z|))=+∞. For each n∈N, let P_n be the unique monic polynomial of degree n satisfying the planar orthogonality conditions ∫_C P_n(z) z^k e^{-nV(z)} dA(z)=0 for k=0,1,...,n-1, where dA denotes area measure on C. Determine which external fields V—especially beyond the trivial radial case V(z)=V(|z|), for which P_n(z)=z^n and ν(P_n)=δ_0—have the property that the sequence {ν(P_n)} converges weakly, as n→∞, to a probability measure μ_V on C, and characterize the limiting measure μ_V. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/html/2312.07754v1))

For each n ≥ 1, let P_n be the space of real algebraic polynomials of degree at most n, and let μ:[-1,1]→[0,∞) be a majorant for which the n-th snake polynomial ω_{n,μ} exists, meaning that ω_{n,μ}∈P_n is unique up to overall sign, satisfies |ω_{n,μ}(x)|≤μ(x) for all x∈[-1,1], and has an alternation set τ_0<⋯<τ_n in [-1,1] with ω_{n,μ}(τ_i)=(-1)^i μ(τ_i) after choosing an orientation. Characterize the majorants μ for which, for every such n, one can choose the orientation of ω_{n,μ} so that its expansion in the Chebyshev polynomials of the first kind, ω_{n,μ}(x)=∑_{i=0}^n a_i T_i(x), is either coefficientwise non-negative (a_i≥0 for all i) or sign-alternating in the Chebyshev basis (equivalently, up to overall sign, (-1)^i a_i≥0 for all i). In particular, is this property guaranteed when μ is continuous, even, and convex on [-1,1], and in that case does one always get the non-negative alternative?

For each n for which it is defined, let P_n denote the real polynomials of degree at most n, and let ω_{μ,n}∈P_n be the n-th snake polynomial associated with a majorant μ:[-1,1]→[0,∞), meaning the unique (up to orientation) degree-n polynomial satisfying |ω_{μ,n}(x)|≤μ(x) on [-1,1] and possessing n+1 alternation points -1≤τ_0<⋯<τ_n≤1 with ω_{μ,n}(τ_i)=(-1)^i μ(τ_i). If μ is continuous, even, and convex on [-1,1], must every such ω_{μ,n} admit a Chebyshev expansion of the first kind ω_{μ,n}(x)=∑_{j=0}^n a_j T_j(x) with a_j≥0 for all j? ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/html/2312.07754v1))

Let d >= 2 and let s satisfy d-2 < s < d. For fixed radii 0 < r < R, define the closed annulus B_{r,R} := {x in R^d : r <= |x| <= R}. Determine the Riesz s-equilibrium measure of B_{r,R}; that is, determine a Borel probability measure mu on R^d with supp(mu) subseteq B_{r,R} such that mu minimizes the Riesz s-energy
I_s(mu) := ∬ |x-y|^{-s} dmu(x) dmu(y)
among all Borel probability measures supported on B_{r,R}.

Let P(z)∈C[z] be a univariate polynomial of degree d≥2. For integers n≥1 and 0≤m≤nd, define Q_{n,m}(z):=d^m/dz^m(P(z)^n), and let Υ_P⊂C be the closure of the union of the zero sets of all Q_{n,m}. If the roots of P are in convex position, but do not form a regular polygon, is it true that: (i) Υ_P is a closed domain contained in the convex hull of the roots of P; (ii) every critical point of P lies on ∂Υ_P; (iii) ∂Υ_P has no inflection points; and (iv) ∂Υ_P is contained in the union, over α∈[0,d], of the critical values with respect to z of the rational function F_α(z)=z-αP(z)/P'(z)? ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/html/2312.07754v1))

Let x_1, ..., x_N be distinct fixed points in R^3 carrying nonzero real point charges q_1, ..., q_N, and let V(x) = sum_{i=1}^N q_i / |x - x_i| for x in R^3 \ {x_1, ..., x_N}. Suppose the electrostatic field ∇V has only finitely many zeros in R^3 \ {x_1, ..., x_N} (equivalently, V has only finitely many critical points). Is the total number of such equilibrium points always at most (N - 1)^2?

For every finite configuration of fixed positive point charges q_1,\dots,q_N at points a_1,\dots,a_N in Euclidean space, does the associated electrostatic field have only finitely many equilibrium points; equivalently, are there only finitely many points x \notin \{a_1,\dots,a_N\} at which the total electrostatic force generated by the charges vanishes?

Does every weakly compactly generated Banach space X admit a norming Markushevich basis; that is, does there exist an indexed biorthogonal family {(x_i, x_i^*)}_{i in I} subseteq X x X^* such that overline{span}{x_i : i in I} = X and span{x_i^* : i in I} is a norming subspace of X^* (equivalently, for some lambda >= 1, sup{|f(x)| : f in B_{span{x_i^*}}} >= lambda^(-1) ||x|| for all x in X)?
Let X be an Asplund Banach space with a norming Markushevich basis. Must X be weakly compactly generated (WCG)?

Fix a function ϱ:{(α,β)∈ω1×ω1:α<β}→ω satisfying the properties used in Proposition 4.8 of the paper: ϱ(α,β)>0 for all α<β<ω1, ϱ(α,γ)≤max{ϱ(α,β),ϱ(β,γ)} and ϱ(α,β)≤max{ϱ(α,γ),ϱ(β,γ)} for all α<β<γ<ω1, and ϱ(α,γ)≠ϱ(β,γ) for all α<β<γ<ω1; extend it by ϱ(α,α)=0. For n<ω and α<ω1 let F_n(α)={ξ≤α:ϱ(ξ,α)≤n}, let F_ϱ={F_n(α):n<ω, α<ω1}, and let K_ϱ=cl(F_ϱ)⊆P(ω1)={0,1}^{ω1}, where the closure is taken in the pointwise/product topology. Must the Banach space C(K_ϱ) of continuous real-valued functions on K_ϱ, with the supremum norm, admit a norming Markushevich basis (equivalently, a fundamental total biorthogonal system whose dual functionals span a norming subspace of C(K_ϱ)^*)?

Let K be a scattered compact Hausdorff space, and let C(K) be the Banach space of continuous scalar-valued functions on K endowed with the supremum norm. If C(K) admits a norming Markushevich basis, must K be an Eberlein compact space?

Let K be a scattered compact space, and let C(K) denote the Banach space of scalar-valued continuous functions on K with the supremum norm. Suppose that C(K) admits a Markushevich basis such that either (i) the subspace of C(K)^* generated by its biorthogonal functionals is lambda-norming for C(K) for some lambda >= 1, or (ii) the subspace of functionals that are countably supported with respect to that basis is lambda-norming for C(K) for some lambda >= 1. Must K be a Valdivia compact space?

Let K be a scattered Valdivia compact Hausdorff space, and suppose that K contains a subspace A homeomorphic to the ordinal interval [0,ω1] with its order topology. Writing C(L) for the Banach space of continuous scalar-valued functions on L with the supremum norm, must there exist a bounded linear extension operator E:C(A)→C(K) such that E(f)|A=f for every f∈C(A)? More generally, must C(A)≅C([0,ω1]) admit a Banach-space isomorphic embedding into C(K)?

Is the class of Banach spaces admitting a norming Markushevich basis hereditary with respect to closed linear subspaces? Equivalently, if X is a Banach space that admits a norming Markushevich basis—i.e. a fundamental total biorthogonal system whose biorthogonal functionals span a norming subspace of X^*—and Z is a closed linear subspace of X, must Z, with the inherited norm, also admit a norming Markushevich basis? ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2402.18442))

For every uncountable set Γ and every closed linear subspace Y of ℓ1(Γ), does Y admit a norming Markushevich basis; that is, does there exist a biorthogonal system {(yα,yα*)}_{α∈A} ⊂ Y×Y* such that span{yα : α∈A} is dense in Y, span{yα* : α∈A} is weak*-dense in Y*, and for some λ ≥ 1 one has ||y|| ≤ λ sup{|f(y)| : f ∈ span{yα* : α∈A}, ||f|| ≤ 1} for every y ∈ Y?

Let X be a Banach space admitting a Markushevich basis (x_i,x_i^*)_{i\in I} such that the subspace M={f\in X^*: {i\in I : f(x_i)\neq 0} is countable} is norming for X, i.e. there exists \lambda\ge 1 such that \|x\|\le \lambda\sup\{|f(x)|: f\in M, \|f\|\le 1\} for all x\in X; equivalently, let X be a Plichko Banach space. If Z\subseteq X is a closed linear subspace, must Z also be Plichko?
Let X be a Banach space. If its bidual X** is Plichko, i.e. if X** admits a countably norming Markushevich basis, must X itself be Plichko?

Let X be a Plichko Banach space, i.e. a Banach space admitting a countably norming Markushevich basis, and let Z be a complemented closed linear subspace of X (equivalently, there exists a bounded linear projection P:X->Z). Must Z also be a Plichko Banach space?

For every ordinal η, where [0, η] is endowed with the order topology and C([0, η]) denotes the Banach space of scalar-valued continuous functions on [0, η] with the supremum norm, must C([0, η]) be Plichko—that is, admit a countably λ-norming Markushevich basis for some λ ≥ 1—only when η < ω2?

Does the Banach space C([0,ω₂]), consisting of scalar-valued continuous functions on the compact ordinal interval [0,ω₂] with the order topology and the supremum norm, admit a bounded linear isomorphic embedding into a Plichko Banach space?

Let X be a Banach space and let Z⊆X be a complemented subspace, i.e. Z=P(X) for some bounded linear projection P:X→X. Assume that X admits a norming Markushevich basis: a biorthogonal system {e_α, φ_α}_{α∈Γ}⊆X×X* whose vectors span a dense subspace of X, whose functionals are w*-total in X*, and such that span{φ_α: α∈Γ} is norming for X (equivalently, λ||x|| ≤ sup{|φ(x)| : φ∈span{φ_α}, ||φ||≤1} for some 0<λ≤1 and all x∈X). Must Z also admit a norming Markushevich basis?

Characterize the Banach spaces X for which the weak* compact closed dual unit ball (B_{X*}, w*) is semi-Eberlein; equivalently, determine for which X there exist a set Γ and a homeomorphic embedding h:(B_{X*}, w*) → [-1,1]^Γ such that h(B_{X*}) ∩ c0(Γ) is dense in h(B_{X*}), where c0(Γ) denotes the scalar functions on Γ that vanish at infinity.

Let X be a Banach space, and write (BX*, w*) for its dual unit ball with the weak* topology. Recall that a compact space K is called semi-Eberlein if it is homeomorphic to a compact subset L ⊆ [-1,1]^Γ for some set Γ such that L ∩ c0(Γ) is dense in L. Suppose X admits a norming Markushevich basis {eα; φα}α∈Γ, meaning that {eα; φα}α∈Γ is a biorthogonal system with span{eα} dense in X, span{φα} weak*-dense in X*, and span{φα} norming in X*. Must (BX*, w*) be semi-Eberlein? More generally, if for every equivalent norm ||·||' on the underlying linear space X the renormed weak* dual ball (B(X,||·||')*, w*) is semi-Eberlein, must X be a subspace of a weakly compactly generated Banach space? Finally, let ϱ:[ω1]^2→ω satisfy conditions (ϱ1)–(ϱ4) of Proposition 4.8, define Fn(α) = {ξ ≤ α : ϱ(ξ, α) ≤ n} for n < ω and α < ω1, let Fϱ = {Fn(α) : n < ω, α < ω1}, and let Kϱ be the closure of Fϱ in the pointwise topology of P(ω1) = {0,1}^ω1. Are the dual balls of C([0, ω1]) or C(Kϱ) semi-Eberlein? ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2402.18442))

Can a scattered semi-Eberlein compactum contain a homeomorphic copy of the ordinal interval [0, ω2] with its order topology, where "semi-Eberlein" means homeomorphic to a compact K ⊆ [-1,1]^Γ such that K ∩ c0(Γ) is dense in K?

Open Problem 2.1 (paper-faithful reformulation). Let G be a finite connected graph with m edges and diameter D, let A=A(G) be its adjacency matrix, and let U(t)=exp(itA) be the transition matrix of the continuous-time quantum walk on G. Suppose G admits perfect state transfer in the adjacency-matrix model; that is, there exist vertices u,v ∈ V(G), a time t ∈ R, and a phase γ ∈ C with |γ|=1 such that U(t)e_u=γe_v. Can one improve the known cubic bound D^3 ≤ 80m by proving that there exist absolute constants c>0 and a fixed exponent k>3 such that every such graph satisfies m ≥ cD^k for all sufficiently large D?

Find an infinite family {G_n} of finite graphs with unbounded diameter and a fixed polynomial p such that, for every n, there exist vertices u_n,v_n in V(G_n), a time t_n in R, and a phase γ_n in C with |γ_n|=1 for which exp(i t_n A(G_n))e_{u_n}=γ_n e_{v_n}, and such that the edge count satisfies |E(G_n)| ≤ p(diam(G_n)). ([pure.uva.nl](https://pure.uva.nl/ws/files/234177391/Selected_open_problems_in_continuous-time_quantum_walks.pdf))

Given a finite graph G with adjacency matrix A(G) and two distinct vertices u,v in V(G), find a polynomial-time algorithm that decides whether pretty good state transfer occurs between u and v, in the sense that there exists a sequence of pairwise distinct real times (t_j)_{j >= 0} such that |(exp(i t_j A(G)))_{uv}| converges to 1 as j -> infinity; and, whenever the answer is yes, find an algorithm that computes such a witnessing sequence of times (equivalently, a subsequence of times representing pretty good state transfer, in the paper's wording).

Let G be a graph on n vertices with adjacency matrix A, and let U(t)=exp(itA) be the transition matrix of the continuous-time quantum walk on G. Define the mixing matrix by M(t)=U(t)∘U(-t). Say that G admits instantaneous uniform mixing at time τ if all entries of M(τ) are equal (equivalently, all entries of U(τ) have the same absolute value). Show that if G admits uniform mixing at time τ, then every eigenvalue of U(τ) is a root of unity, or else give a counterexample.

Let C9 be the cycle graph on 9 vertices, with adjacency matrix A(C9). For the adjacency-based continuous-time quantum walk U(t)=exp(itA(C9)), define the mixing matrix by M(t)=U(t)∘U(-t). Does there exist a real time tau such that C9 admits instantaneous uniform mixing, i.e. M(tau)=J/9?

Let G be a finite graph on n vertices with adjacency matrix A and spectral decomposition A=∑_{r=0}^d θ_r E_r. For the continuous-time quantum walk U(t)=e^{itA}, determine necessary and sufficient conditions, expressed solely in terms of the spectral data {(θ_r,E_r)}_{r=0}^d, for the existence of a real time τ such that G admits instantaneous uniform mixing; that is, such that all entries of U(τ) have the same absolute value. The characterization should depend only on the eigenvalues and eigenspaces, rather than on a time-dependent criterion tailored to a particular τ. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2404.02236))

Let G be a primitive distance-regular graph on n=|V(G)| vertices, with adjacency matrix A=A(G). Define the continuous-time quantum walk transition matrix by U(t)=exp(itA), the mixing matrix by M(t)=U(t)∘U(-t), where ∘ denotes the Schur (Hadamard) product, the finite-interval average by Mc[0,T]=(1/T) integral_0^T M(t) dt, and the average mixing matrix by Mc = lim_{T->infinity} Mc[0,T]. Is it true that rank(Mc)=n; equivalently, does every primitive distance-regular graph have a full-rank average mixing matrix?

Let G be a finite graph on n=|V(G)| vertices with adjacency matrix A(G)=\sum_{r=0}^d \theta_r E_r. Define U(t)=e^{itA(G)}, M(t)=U(t)\circ U(-t), and the average mixing matrix \widehat M=\lim_{T\to\infty}\frac{1}{T}\int_0^T M(t)\,dt=\sum_{r=0}^d E_r\circ E_r, where \circ denotes the Schur product. Characterize those graphs G for which the non-negative rank of \widehat M, defined by \operatorname{rank}_+(\widehat M)=\min\{k: \widehat M=\sum_{s=1}^k N_s,\ N_s\in \mathbb{R}_{\ge 0}^{n\times n},\ \operatorname{rank}(N_s)=1\}, is equal to n. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2404.02236))

Let G be a graph on n vertices with adjacency matrix A(G), transition matrix U(t)=exp(itA(G)), mixing matrix M(t)=U(t) ◦ U(-t), and average mixing matrix M_c := lim_{T→∞} (1/T) ∫_0^T M(t) dt, equivalently M_c = sum_{r=0}^m E_r ◦ E_r when A(G)=sum_{r=0}^m θ_rE_r is the spectral decomposition of A(G). Determine the completely positive semidefinite rank of M_c; that is, find the smallest integer k for which there exist k×k positive semidefinite matrices P_1,...,P_n such that (M_c)_{ij}=Tr(P_iP_j) for all i,j.

For a graph G on n vertices with adjacency spectral decomposition A(G)=sum_{r=0}^d theta_r E_r and average mixing matrix Mhat(G)=sum_{r=0}^d E_r ∘ E_r, where ∘ denotes the entrywise product, determine when the non-negative rank of Mhat(G) is equal to n, how small the non-negative rank of Mhat(G) can be, and what combinatorial consequences for G follow in these extremal cases. Here the non-negative rank of a non-negative n×n matrix M is the least k such that M can be written as a sum of k rank-1 matrices with non-negative entries.

Let G be a graph on n vertices with adjacency matrix A(G), continuous-time quantum walk U(t)=exp(itA(G)), mixing matrix M(t)=U(t)∘U(-t), and average mixing matrix widehat{M}=lim_{T→∞}(1/T)∫_0^T M(t)dt=∑_r E_r∘E_r, where A(G)=∑_r theta_r E_r is the spectral decomposition. Assume widehat{M} is completely positive (in particular, by Lemma 4.1 this holds whenever G has simple eigenvalues). For which graphs G is the completely positive rank of widehat{M}—that is, the least d such that widehat{M} is a Gram matrix of non-negative vectors in R^d—equal to n=|V(G)|?

For a finite graph G with adjacency matrix A(G), let U(t)=exp(itA(G)) be the transition matrix of the continuous-time quantum walk on G, and let M(t)=U(t)∘U(-t) be its mixing matrix. If R is a real-valued random variable with probability density function f_R, define the R-average mixing matrix by \widehat{M}^R := E[M(R)] = integral from minus infinity to infinity of M(t) f_R(t) dt. Develop a spectral graph theory for \widehat{M}^R; in particular, determine how the spectral data of G govern basic linear-algebraic invariants of \widehat{M}^R, especially its rank, diagonal entries, trace, and eigenvalues, in analogy with the known theory of the standard average mixing matrix \widehat{M}.

Let X be a complex projective smooth minimal surface with κ(X)=1, let π:X→C be its elliptic fibration with fiber class f, let H be a v-suitable ample line bundle, and, in the paper’s main κ(X)=1 case, take v=(2,0,c2) and write M(c2):=M_H(v) for the coarse moduli scheme of rank-two H-stable sheaves on X. How is the birational structure of M(c2), for example what is its Kodaira dimension κ(M(c2))?

Let X be a complex projective smooth minimal surface with κ(X)=1, let v=(2,0,c2) for a fixed integer c2, and let H be a v-suitable ample line bundle on X. Write M(c2)=M_H(v) for the coarse moduli scheme of rank-two H-stable sheaves E on X with c1(E)=0 and c2(E)=c2. Is every singular point E in M(c2) a canonical singularity of the moduli scheme M(c2)?

Let X be a complex projective smooth surface, let H be an ample line bundle on X, and let M be the coarse moduli scheme of rank-two H-stable sheaves on X with fixed Chern classes (in the paper's Section 2 context, kappa(X)=1 and c_1=0). For a singular point E in M, write the completed local ring of M at E in deformation-theoretic form as C[[t_1,...,t_{D+b}]]/(F_1,...,F_b), where each F_i has no linear term. If the quadratic parts of the F_i do not suffice to determine whether the germ (M,E) is a canonical singularity, is there a method to compute or control the cubic and higher-degree terms of these local defining equations, and can such higher-order information be used to decide whether (M,E) is canonical?

Let X be a complex projective smooth minimal surface with κ(X)=1, let v=(2,0,c2), and let H be a v-suitable ample line bundle on X. If M=M_H(v) denotes the coarse moduli scheme of rank-two H-stable sheaves on X with Chern classes v, can one determine the Kodaira dimension κ(M) by a method that avoids directly confronting the singularities of M, in particular without first having to decide whether those singularities are canonical?

Let X be a smooth complex projective minimal surface with κ(X)>0, fix Chern data v=(2,c1,c2) with c2 sufficiently large, and let M_H(v) be the coarse moduli scheme of rank-two H-stable sheaves of type v. By Theorem 3.2, moving an ample polarization H toward K_X across finitely many v-walls produces a moduli-theoretic sequence of flips and reaches an ample polarization tilde H for which no v-wall separates tilde H from K_X and K_{bar M_{tilde H}(v)} is nef. How is M_H(v) improved along this flip sequence? In particular, in the desirable case where the relevant moduli spaces admit only log-terminal singularities, do these wall-crossing birational maps realize a genuine minimal model program for M_H(v); and what can be learned by instead starting from an ample polarization near K_X, preferably one for which M_H(v) is easy to understand, and then moving the polarization away from K_X while tracking the resulting wall-crossing flips?

Let F(x_1,...,x_n) be a nonconstant polynomial in Z[x_1,...,x_n], and let V_F(Z) = {(x_1,...,x_n) in Z^n : F(x_1,...,x_n)=0}. Determine whether V_F(Z) can be written as a finite union of polynomial families, where a polynomial family means a subset S of Z^n for which there exist an integer m >= 1 and polynomials f_1,...,f_n in Z[u_1,...,u_m] such that, for every x=(x_1,...,x_n) in Z^n, x belongs to S if and only if there exist integers u_1,...,u_m with x_i = f_i(u_1,...,u_m) for all i=1,...,n. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/html/2404.08518v5))

For each of the Diophantine equations y^2+z^2=x^3+1 and y^2+z^2=x^3-1, determine the complete set of integer triples (x,y,z)∈Z^3 satisfying the equation, giving for each equation a fully explicit and mathematically usable description of all solutions. A paper-faithful answer may be a finite parametrization, a description by recurrence relations, or finitely many initial solutions together with solution-preserving transformations; no positivity, primitiveness, or coprimality restriction is imposed. These are precisely the size-H=17 equations highlighted in the paper as the smallest open cases for the problem of describing all integer solutions.

Treating the equations separately, determine the complete set of rational solutions (x,y,z) in Q^3 to each of the following affine equations:
1) y^2 + z^2 = x^3 + 1,
2) y^2 + z^2 = x^3 - 1,
3) y^2 - x^2 y + z^2 + 1 = 0.
An acceptable resolution should give a complete explicit description of every rational point on each surface; it need not consist of a single parametrization, but it must account for all rational solutions.
Determine all integer triples (x,y,z) in Z^3 satisfying x^2 y + y^2 z + z^2 x = 1, or prove that there are infinitely many such triples.

Do there exist any nonconstant polynomial triples x(t), y(t), z(t) in Q[t] satisfying the identity x(t)^3 + y(t)^3 + z(t)^3 = 2 that are not obtained, up to permutation of the three coordinates, from the standard family (1 + 6u(t)^3, 1 - 6u(t)^3, -6u(t)^2) for some polynomial u(t) in Q[t]?

For each of the Diophantine equations x^3 y + y z^2 + z = 0 and x + x^3 y + y z^2 = 0, determine the full set of integer solutions (x,y,z) in Z^3. In particular, prove or disprove that the only integer solutions are the obvious ones: for x^3 y + y z^2 + z = 0, the families (t,0,0) and (0,t,0) with t in Z together with the isolated solutions (0,1,-1) and (0,-1,1); and for x + x^3 y + y z^2 = 0, the families (0,t,0) and (0,0,t) with t in Z.

Given a homogeneous polynomial P(x1,...,xn) in Z[x1,...,xn], determine whether the Diophantine equation P(x1,...,xn)=0 has a non-trivial integer solution; that is, whether there exists (x1,...,xn) in Z^n with (x1,...,xn) ≠ (0,...,0) such that P(x1,...,xn)=0.

Solve the finiteness problem for the nine polynomial Diophantine equations in integers x, y, z listed in Table 1 of arXiv:2404.08518, namely: z^2 + y^2 z + x^3 - 2 = 0; z^2 + y^2 z + x^3 - x - 1 = 0; z^2 + y^2 z + x^3 + x - 1 = 0; z^2 + y^2 z + x^3 + x + 1 = 0; z^2 + y^2 z + x^3 - 3 = 0; z^2 + y^2 z + x^3 + 3 = 0; z^2 + y^2 z + x^3 - x - 2 = 0; z^2 + y^2 z + x^3 - x + 2 = 0; z^2 + y^2 z - z + x^3 + 2 = 0. That is, for each equation determine whether its integer solution set is finite or infinite, and, in the precise sharpened form proposed in the paper, prove that each of these nine equations has infinitely many integer solutions. citeturn28view0turn28view1
Prove that the Diophantine equation z^2 + y^2 z + x^3 - 3 = 0 has infinitely many integer solutions (x,y,z) in Z^3.

Within Grechuk’s systematic ordering of Diophantine equations by size H(P), where for a homogeneous polynomial P in Z[x1,...,xn] the size is obtained by replacing each coefficient by its absolute value and evaluating the resulting polynomial at (2,...,2), determine the smallest homogeneous equations P(x1,...,xn)=0 for which it remains open whether there exists a non-trivial integer solution (x1,...,xn) in Z^n with (x1,...,xn) ≠ (0,...,0).

Given a single polynomial Diophantine equation P(x1,...,xd)=0, where P belongs to Z[x1,...,xd] and has at least one nonconstant monomial (so d>=1), decide whether there exists an integer tuple (x1,...,xd) in Z^d such that P(x1,...,xd)=0. No restriction on degree, homogeneity, symmetry, cyclicity, or number of monomials is assumed. ([ar5iv.labs.arxiv.org](https://ar5iv.labs.arxiv.org/html/2404.08518v5))

Determine whether each of the following polynomial Diophantine equations has an integer solution: y^3 + xy + x^4 + 4 = 0, y^3 + xy + x^4 + x + 2 = 0, y^3 + y = x^4 + x + 4, and y^3 - y = x^4 - 2x - 2, where x,y are required to lie in Z.
Decide whether there exist integers x, y, z ∈ ℤ such that 7x^3 + 2y^3 = 3z^2 + 1.

Rokhlin’s multiple-mixing problem for a single automorphism: does there exist a measure-preserving automorphism T of a probability space (X, B, μ) that is mixing (that is, 1-fold mixing) but is not k-fold mixing for some integer k ≥ 2? Here T is k-fold mixing if for every measurable sets A_0, ..., A_k in B and every sequences of integers m_1(n), ..., m_k(n) with m_i(n) → +∞ for each i, one has μ(A_0 ∩ T^{m_1(n)}A_1 ∩ T^{m_1(n)+m_2(n)}A_2 ∩ ... ∩ T^{m_1(n)+...+m_k(n)}A_k) → ∏_{j=0}^k μ(A_j). In the paper’s notation: is there a mixing automorphism that fails to belong to Mix(k) for some higher k?

Does there exist an ergodic probability-preserving automorphism T of a standard nonatomic probability space (X,μ) such that the Koopman operator U_T, restricted to L^2_0(X,μ)=L^2(X,μ) orthogonal to the constants, has Lebesgue maximal spectral type and spectral multiplicity equal to 1 almost everywhere; equivalently, does there exist an automorphism with simple Lebesgue spectrum?

For an ergodic measure-preserving automorphism T of a probability space (X,μ), viewed through its Koopman operator U_T on L^2_0(X,μ), what spectra can occur? More specifically, can U_T have maximal spectral type that is absolutely continuous with respect to Lebesgue measure on the unit circle but not equivalent to Lebesgue measure, and which sets can occur as the spectral multiplicity set of U_T?

Does there exist an ergodic measure-preserving automorphism T of a probability space (X, B, mu) such that the Koopman operator U_T on L^2(X, mu) orthogonal to the constants has a nonzero absolutely continuous spectral part with finite spectral multiplicity (with absolute continuity understood with respect to Lebesgue measure on the unit circle)?

Let T be a mixing measure-preserving automorphism of a standard probability space (X, B, mu), meaning that for all measurable sets D, E in B one has mu(D ∩ T^n E) -> mu(D)mu(E) as n -> +infinity. Must T be lightly 2-mixing; that is, for every pair of integer sequences m_i, n_i -> +infinity and every measurable sets A, B, C in B with mu(A), mu(B), mu(C) > 0, does one necessarily have limsup_{i->infinity} mu(A ∩ T^{m_i}B ∩ T^{m_i+n_i}C) > 0?

Let T be a mixing measure-preserving automorphism of a probability space (X, B, μ). For A in B and a in (0,1), define D(T,A,N,a) to be the set of integer pairs (m,n) with aN<m,n<N such that μ(A∩T^mA∩T^{m+n}A)>2μ(A)^3. Does there exist such a mixing automorphism T for which the paper’s extremal deviation property holds, namely: there exist a measurable set A with μ(A)>0 and a constant a>0 such that limsup_{N->infinity} |D(T,A,N,a)|/N > 0?

Fix an integer k>1, and let S be a measure-preserving automorphism of a probability space that has the k-fold mixing property Mix(k), meaning that for all measurable sets A0, A1, ..., Ak one has μ(A0 ∩ S^{n1}A1 ∩ ... ∩ S^{nk}Ak) → ∏_{i=0}^k μ(Ai) whenever the time shifts separate pairwise. In the space Ext(S) of skew-product extensions of S, endowed with the Halmos metric, is the set of extensions R that also belong to Mix(k) generic (equivalently: is a typical extension of S again k-fold mixing)?

Let T be a measure-preserving action on a probability space (X,μ). For integers n>m>1, say that T has property S(m,n) if every n-fold self-joining λ of T—that is, every T^{×n}-invariant probability measure on X^n with one-coordinate marginals μ—whose projection to every m-dimensional coordinate face of X^n equals μ^m is trivial, i.e. λ=μ^n; write S_n:=S(n-1,n). It is known that the even properties S_{2k} are all mutually equivalent and imply every odd property S_{2ℓ-1}. What implication or equivalence relations hold among the odd properties S_3,S_5,S_7,… themselves? ([ar5iv.labs.arxiv.org](https://ar5iv.labs.arxiv.org/html/2405.03641v1))

Let T be a weakly mixing measure-preserving automorphism of a standard Lebesgue probability space (X, mu) with Kolmogorov-Sinai entropy h(T)=0. Is it true that T satisfies property S_n: namely, for every n-fold self-joining lambda of T on X^n, if for each i=1,...,n the projection of lambda onto the complementary (n-1)-coordinate face is mu^{n-1}, then necessarily lambda = mu^n?

Let T be a measure-preserving automorphism of a probability space (X, B, μ), and assume that the product automorphism T⊗T on (X×X, B⊗B, μ⊗μ) is ergodic. Suppose there exists a T⊗T-invariant factor F ⊆ B⊗B that is independent of each of the two coordinate factors B⊗{∅,X} and {∅,X}⊗B. Must the Kolmogorov–Sinai entropy h(T) be positive?

Let (X, B, μ, T) be an ergodic Gaussian automorphism of a probability space with zero Kolmogorov–Sinai entropy. For each n>2, say that T has property S_n if every n-fold self-joining λ of T whose projection to every (n-1)-dimensional coordinate face is μ^{⊗(n-1)} is necessarily λ = μ^{⊗ n}. Must every zero-entropy ergodic Gaussian automorphism satisfy S_n for every n>2? ([ar5iv.labs.arxiv.org](https://ar5iv.labs.arxiv.org/html/2405.03641v1))

Let T be an ergodic invertible measure-preserving transformation of a standard Lebesgue probability space (X, B, μ). For n≥2, say that T belongs to MSJ(n) if every ergodic self-joining λ of order n, i.e. every ergodic T×...×T-invariant probability measure on X^n with all one-coordinate marginals equal to μ, is either the product measure μ^{⊗ n} or else has at least one two-coordinate marginal equal to an off-diagonal joining Δ_{T^m}=(Id×T^m)_*Δ for some m∈Z, where Δ=(Id,Id)_*μ. Is it true that MSJ(2)=MSJ(3) for ergodic measure-preserving Z-actions (equivalently, ergodic automorphisms T)?

Do there exist two measure-preserving automorphisms of probability spaces that are not metrically isomorphic mod 0 but whose Koopman operators have one and the same continuous spectrum, and in particular one and the same Lebesgue spectrum?

Let T be a mixing measure-preserving automorphism of a standard Lebesgue probability space (X,B,mu), and assume T has positive local rank: there exist beta>0 and Rokhlin tower unions U_j=\bigsqcup_{i=0}^{h_j-1} T^i B_j with mu(U_j)->beta such that for every measurable set A in B there are index sets S_j(A)\subset\{0,1,\dots,h_j-1\} satisfying mu(((A\cap U_j)\,\Delta\,\bigsqcup_{i\in S_j(A)} T^i B_j))->0. Must T be mixing of all orders, i.e. k-fold mixing for every k\ge 2? Equivalently in the sense emphasized by Ryzhikov’s discussion of consequences, does there fail to exist a counterexample of positive local rank, whose existence would in particular produce a mixing factor whose Koopman spectrum on L^2_0(X,mu) is absolutely continuous of finite multiplicity?

For the Li-Cao stochastic scheduling model on an unreliable machine with general hazard-rate functions lambda, mu, eta : [0, infinity) -> [0, infinity), let p0(x,t) and p1(x,t) be defined on [0, infinity) x [0, infinity) by
(1) d/dt p0(x,t) + d/dx p0(x,t) = -(lambda(x)+mu(x)) p0(x,t),
(2) d/dt p1(x,t) + d/dx p1(x,t) = -eta(x) p1(x,t),
with boundary conditions
p0(0,t) = delta(t) + integral from 0 to infinity of p1(x,t) eta(x) dx,
p1(0,t) = integral from 0 to infinity of p0(x,t) lambda(x) dx,
and initial data
p0(x,0) = delta(x), p1(x,0) = 0.
Here p0(x,t) dx is the probability that at time t the machine is processing the job and its elapsed processing time lies in [x, x+dx), while p1(x,t) dx is the probability that at time t the machine is under repair and its elapsed repair time lies in [x, x+dx). The paper solves the constant-rate case explicitly and, in the general nonconstant case, derives only Laplace-domain formulas for the time-dependent solution. The sharp open question is: determine the inverse Laplace transforms of the paper's general-case formulas for p0-hat(x,s) and p1-hat(x,s), and hence write down an explicit time-domain formula for the full solution (p0(x,t), p1(x,t)) in the general nonconstant case.

For the stochastic scheduling model on an unreliable machine with general up-times and general set-up times, described by a system of partial differential equations with Dirac-delta terms in the boundary and initial conditions, and in the general case where the job-dependent processing rate, up-time rate, and repair rate are nonconstant functions, can one establish well-posedness of the resulting nonautonomous abstract Cauchy problem in the evolution-family framework, recover the actual time-dependent solution (rather than only its Laplace transform), and determine its long-time asymptotic behavior?

For the 1993 two-unit parallel reliability model described by a coupled system of first-order partial differential equations with state densities p0,i(x,t), p1,i(x,t), p2(x,u,t), p3(x,t), and p4(x,u,t), with x,u,t >= 0, rate data a1 > 0, a2(x), b1(x), b2(x), and boundary/initial conditions containing Dirac-delta terms (including relations of the form p0,1(0,t) = integral from 0 to infinity of p1,1(x,t)b2(x)dx + delta(t)), determine in the general-coefficient case whether the model is well posed in the paper's abstract-Cauchy-problem/evolution-family formulation, and determine the long-time asymptotic behavior as t -> infinity of its time-dependent solution.

Consider Su’s 1997 supplementary-variable model for a two dissimilar unit system with three modes and random check, with state variables p_{0,0,k}(x,t) (k>=0), p_{1,0,0}(x,t), p_{0,1,0}(x,t), p_{0,1,1}(x,t), p_{1,0,1}(x,t), p_{0,2,0}(x,t), p_{2,0,0}(x,t), p_{1,1,0}(x,t), p_{1,1,1}(x,t), p_{1,2,0}(x,t), and p_{2,1,0}(x,t), governed for x,t>=0 by partial_t p_{0,0,k}+partial_x p_{0,0,k}=-(lambda_{0,1}+lambda_{1,0}+alpha(x))p_{0,0,k} (k>=0); partial_t p_{0,1,0}+partial_x p_{0,1,0}=-(lambda_{1,0}+lambda_{0,2}+alpha(x))p_{0,1,0}+sum_{k>=0} lambda_{0,1} p_{0,0,k}; partial_t p_{1,0,0}+partial_x p_{1,0,0}=-(lambda_{0,1}+lambda_{2,0}+alpha(x))p_{1,0,0}+sum_{k>=0} lambda_{1,0} p_{0,0,k}; partial_t p_{0,1,1}+partial_x p_{0,1,1}=-mu_{0,1}(x)p_{0,1,1}; partial_t p_{1,0,1}+partial_x p_{1,0,1}=-mu_{1,0}(x)p_{1,0,1}; partial_t p_{0,2,0}+partial_x p_{0,2,0}=-mu_{0,2}(x)p_{0,2,0}; partial_t p_{2,0,0}+partial_x p_{2,0,0}=-mu_{2,0}(x)p_{2,0,0}; partial_t p_{1,1,0}+partial_x p_{1,1,0}=-(lambda_{0,2}+lambda_{2,0}+alpha(x))p_{1,1,0}+lambda_{1,0}p_{0,1,0}+lambda_{0,1}p_{1,0,0}; partial_t p_{1,1,1}+partial_x p_{1,1,1}=-mu_{1,1}(x)p_{1,1,1}; partial_t p_{1,2,0}+partial_x p_{1,2,0}=-mu_{1,2}(x)p_{1,2,0}; partial_t p_{2,1,0}+partial_x p_{2,1,0}=-mu_{2,1}(x)p_{2,1,0}. Impose the boundary conditions p_{0,0,0}(0,t)=delta(t)+int_0^infinity [mu_{0,1}(x)p_{0,1,1}(x,t)+mu_{1,0}(x)p_{1,0,1}(x,t)+mu_{0,2}(x)p_{0,2,0}(x,t)+mu_{2,0}(x)p_{2,0,0}(x,t)+mu_{1,2}(x)p_{1,2,0}(x,t)+mu_{2,1}(x)p_{2,1,0}(x,t)+mu_{1,1}(x)p_{1,1,1}(x,t)] dx, p_{0,0,k}(0,t)=int_0^infinity alpha(x)p_{0,0,k-1}(x,t) dx for k>=1, p_{0,1,0}(0,t)=p_{1,0,0}(0,t)=p_{1,1,0}(0,t)=0, p_{0,1,1}(0,t)=int_0^infinity alpha(x)p_{0,1,0}(x,t) dx, p_{1,0,1}(0,t)=int_0^infinity alpha(x)p_{1,0,0}(x,t) dx, p_{0,2,0}(0,t)=int_0^infinity lambda_{0,2}p_{0,1,0}(x,t) dx, p_{2,0,0}(0,t)=int_0^infinity lambda_{2,0}p_{1,0,0}(x,t) dx, p_{1,1,1}(0,t)=int_0^infinity alpha(x)p_{1,1,0}(x,t) dx, p_{1,2,0}(0,t)=int_0^infinity lambda_{0,2}p_{1,1,0}(x,t) dx, and p_{2,1,0}(0,t)=int_0^infinity lambda_{2,0}p_{1,1,0}(x,t) dx, together with initial data p_{0,0,0}(x,0)=delta(x), p_{0,0,k}(x,0)=0 for k>=1, and all other components initially zero. Assume lambda_{1,0}, lambda_{2,0}, lambda_{0,1}, lambda_{0,2} > 0, alpha(x) >= 0 with int_0^infinity alpha(x) dx = infinity, mu_{i,0}(x) >= 0 and int_0^infinity mu_{i,0}(x) dx = infinity for i=1,2, mu_{0,i}(x) >= 0 and int_0^infinity mu_{0,i}(x) dx = infinity for i=1,2, and mu_{i,j}(x) >= 0 with int_0^infinity mu_{i,j}(x) dx = infinity for i,j in {1,2}. In a natural Banach lattice/state space compatible with the Dirac boundary and initial data, does this full infinite coupled PDE system admit a unique positive time-dependent solution depending continuously on the data, and what is the asymptotic behavior of that solution as t -> infinity, in particular whether it converges to a steady-state solution?

Consider the Li–Cao stochastic scheduling model on an unreliable machine with elapsed-time variable x>=0 and time t>=0, governed by
partial_t p0(x,t)+partial_x p0(x,t)=-(lambda(x)+mu(x))p0(x,t),
partial_t p1(x,t)+partial_x p1(x,t)=-eta(x)p1(x,t),
with boundary conditions
p0(0,t)=delta(t)+integral_0^infty eta(x)p1(x,t)dx,
p1(0,t)=integral_0^infty lambda(x)p0(x,t)dx,
and initial data
p0(x,0)=delta(x), p1(x,0)=0,
where p0(x,t)dx is the probability that at time t the machine is processing job i with elapsed processing time in [x,x+dx), p1(x,t)dx is the probability that at time t the machine is under repair with elapsed repair time in [x,x+dx), and lambda(x), mu(x), eta(x) are the hazard-rate functions of the random up-time of job i, the random processing time of job i, and the random repair time, respectively. Determine the time-dependent solution and its asymptotic behavior in the special constant-rate case lambda(x)≡lambda, mu(x)≡mu, eta(x)≡eta, and, in the general nonconstant-rate case, determine the Laplace transform of the time-dependent solution and reformulate the system as an abstract Cauchy problem governed by an evolution family.

Assuming the Riemann Hypothesis for the Riemann zeta function, give an explicit version of Harper's upper bound for the 2k-th moment of zeta: for each fixed real k>0, with I_k(T) := ∫_0^T |ζ(1/2+it)|^(2k) dt, determine an explicit computable constant C_k = C_k(k) > 0 and a threshold T_0(k) such that I_k(T) <= C_k T (log T)^(k^2) for every real T >= T_0(k).

Fix real constants 0<c1<c2. For each sufficiently large T, let ω=ωT be a smooth compactly supported function on R with supp(ω)⊂[c1T,c2T]. Show that, for every ε>0, one has
∫_{-∞}^{∞} ω(t)|ζ(1/2+it)|^4 dt = O_{ω,ε}(T^(1/2+θ+ε)),
where θ is an admissible upper bound toward the Ramanujan conjecture.

Let I_2(T)=∫_0^T |ζ(1/2+it)|^4 dt, where ζ(s) is the Riemann zeta function. Zavorotnyi proved in 1989 that, as T→∞, I_2(T)=T P_4(log T)+O(T^(2/3+ε)) for every ε>0, where P_4 is the specific degree-4 polynomial occurring in this fourth-moment asymptotic. Prove a stronger error term by showing that there exists θ<2/3 such that I_2(T)=T P_4(log T)+O(T^(θ+ε)) for every ε>0. ([personal.math.ubc.ca](https://personal.math.ubc.ca/~gerg/papers/downloads/MLPL.pdf))

For each fixed positive integer k, let I_k(T)=∫_0^T |ζ(1/2+it)|^{2k} dt, and let P_{k^2} be the degree-k^2 polynomial predicted by Conrey et al. in the conjectural asymptotic I_k(T)=T P_{k^2}(log T)+E_k(T). Given that the cases θ_1=1/4 and θ_2=1/2 are widely believed to be best possible (with omega-results in both cases), formulate the optimal conjectural constants θ_k for which E_k(T) <<_ε T^{θ_k+ε} should hold for every ε>0. In particular, should one have θ_3=3/4 and θ_4=1 as suggested by N. Ng, and more generally θ_k=(k-1)/2 for k>=5 as suggested by Ivić and Motohashi? Can the Multiple Dirichlet Series method be used to derive this conjectural error-term scale?

Assuming the Riemann Hypothesis, let m ≥ 1 be fixed, let k = (k_1, …, k_m) with k_i > 0, and let α = (α_1, …, α_m) where each α_i = α_i(T) is a real-valued function satisfying α_i = o(T), such that each limit lim_{T→∞} α_i log T and each limit lim_{T→∞}(α_i − α_j) log T exists in ℝ ∪ {±∞}, and for i ≠ j one has α_i ≠ α_j and α_i − α_j = O(1). Define
M_k(T, α) = ∫_0^T ∏_{i=1}^m |ζ(1/2 + i(t + α_i))|^(2k_i) dt.
Use Harper’s method to prove that, for all sufficiently large T,
M_k(T, α) ≪_k T (log T)^(k_1^2 + ··· + k_m^2) ∏_{1≤i<j≤m} (min{1/|α_i − α_j|, log T})^(2k_i k_j),
thereby removing the ε from Chandee’s quoted bound while keeping the same hypotheses on the shifts. ([personal.math.ubc.ca](https://personal.math.ubc.ca/~gerg/papers/downloads/MLPL.pdf))

Let Ik(T) := ∫0^T |ζ(1/2 + it)|^(2k) dt for k ≥ 0, and let ak := ∏p ((1 - p^(-1))^(k^2) Σm=0^∞ (Γ(m+k)/(m!Γ(k)))^2 p^(-m)). Soundararajan proved that, as T → ∞, I3(T) ≥ (20.26 a3 / 9!)(1 + o(1)) T (log T)^9. Can one improve the numerical constant 20.26 in this sixth-moment lower bound, ideally up to the paper’s stated best possible value 42, and likewise improve the leading numerical constants in analogous lower bounds for Ik(T) for fixed k > 3? ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2405.17800))

Assume the ternary additive divisor conjecture in the sense intended for the sixth-moment problem. For the unsmoothed sixth moment of the Riemann zeta function, I_3(T):=∫_0^T |ζ(1/2+it)|^6 dt, prove an omega theorem by showing that, as T→∞, there exists a fixed constant Θ>0 such that I_3(T)=T P_9(log T)+Ω(T^Θ), where P_9(x) is the specific degree-9 polynomial giving the conjectural main term for I_3(T), and Ω(T^Θ) is understood in the usual Landau sense.

Let I_4(T):=∫_0^T |ζ(1/2+it)|^8 dt, the eighth moment of the Riemann zeta function. Assume the Riemann Hypothesis and the smoothed quaternary additive divisor conjecture. Starting from the conditional asymptotic I_4(T)∼C_4 T(log T)^16 for some positive constant C_4, prove as T→∞ a full asymptotic formula of the shape I_4(T)=T P_16(log T)+o(T) (or with a power-saving error term), where P_16 is the degree-16 polynomial giving the complete main term; obtain a corresponding shifted analogue; and, under the same hypotheses, asymptotically evaluate ∫_{-∞}^{∞} ω(t)∏_{j=1}^4 ζ(1/2+a_j+it)ζ(1/2+b_j-it) dt for complex shifts a_j,b_j (j=1,...,4) satisfying |a_j|,|b_j|<<1/log T, where ω is a smooth compactly supported function with support contained in [c_1 T,c_2 T] for positive constants 0<c_1<c_2.

Can one rigorously implement, in the special case k = 2, the approximate-functional-equation 'recipe' of Conrey, Farmer, Keating, Rubinstein, and Snaith for moments of the Riemann zeta function, and thereby give a new recipe-based proof that, as T → ∞, I_2(T) := ∫_0^T |ζ(1/2 + it)|^4 dt = T P_4(log T) + O(T^(1-δ)) for some δ > 0, where P_4 is the specific degree-4 polynomial giving the full main term in the fourth-moment asymptotic?

For a natural number k, let I_k(T) = ∫_0^T |ζ(1/2 + it)|^{2k} dt. In the CFKRS/Diaconu-Goldfeld-Hoffstein conjectural framework, the main term for I_k(T) is expected to be T P_{k^2}(log T), where P_{k^2} is a degree-k^2 polynomial. Can one recover the conjectural lower-order coefficients of this polynomial main term by refining the splitting conjecture in the Gonek-Hughes-Keating hybrid Euler-Hadamard product model for the Riemann zeta function?

As T -> infinity, let f run over holomorphic Hecke cusp eigenforms of weight k_f <= T (in the full-level weight-aspect family intended by the paper), with one Hecke-normalized representative for each eigenspace. Prove that for every epsilon > 0 there exist polynomials P_3 and P_6 of degrees 3 and 6 such that sum_{k_f <= T} L(1/2,f)^3 / L(1, ad f) = T^2 P_3(log T) + O_epsilon(T^(1+epsilon)) and sum_{k_f <= T} L(1/2,f)^4 / L(1, ad f) = T^2 P_6(log T) + O_epsilon(T^(4/3+epsilon)). Here k_f denotes the weight of f and L(1, ad f) is the adjoint L-value.

Let f be a fixed Hecke–Maass cusp form. As Dirichlet characters χ vary with conductor tending to infinity, prove a Weyl-strength upper bound for the sixth moment of the central twists L(1/2, f ⊗ χ), in direct analogy with Heath-Brown’s bound ∫_0^T |ζ(1/2+it)|^12 dt ≪_ε T^(2+ε), Jutila’s t-aspect sixth-moment bound for L(1/2+it,f), and the recent level-aspect twelfth-moment bounds for Dirichlet L-functions.

Fix T0>0. Let B_q(T0) be an orthonormal Hecke basis of Hecke–Maass cusp forms f of level q for Γ0(q) with trivial nebentypus, Laplace eigenvalue 1/4+t_f^2, and 0≤t_f≤T0, and let L(s,ad f) denote the adjoint L-function of f. Prove a level-aspect analogue of Jutila’s level-1 bound Σ_{t_f≤T} L(1/2,f)^12/L(1,ad f) ≪_ε T^{4+ε}, namely obtain the corresponding Weyl-strength twelfth-moment upper bound for Σ_{f∈B_q(T0)} L(1/2,f)^12/L(1,ad f) as q→∞ (naturally, one expects ≪_{T0,ε} q^{2+ε}).

Let f be a fixed Hecke–Maass cusp form of level 1 with Laplace eigenvalue 1/4 + t_f^2, and let L(s,f) denote its Hecke L-function. Good showed that, as T -> infinity, one has
∫_0^T |L(1/2 + it, f)|^2 dt = T P_{1,f}(log T) + O_{t_f,epsilon}(T^(2/3 + epsilon)),
where P_{1,f}(x) is a polynomial of degree 1. Make the dependence of the implied constant on the spectral parameter t_f explicit. In particular, for each fixed delta > 0, determine whether one can choose the error term uniformly in t_f throughout the range T ≥ t_f^(3/2 + delta). Obtain the corresponding analogue for holomorphic Hecke eigenforms of weight k_f.

Let H_k^*(1) denote the set of primitive holomorphic Hecke eigenforms of level 1 and weight k, and fix a constant C > 0. Using the methods of Humphries-Khan [42], determine an explicit upper bound, as K -> infinity, for the dyadic weight-aspect sixth moment M_6(K) := sum_{substack{k, ell in 2N, K < k + ell <= 2K, |k-ell| <= C}} sum_{f in H_k^*(1)} sum_{g in H_ell^*(1)} |L(1/2, f ⊗ g)|^6, where L(s, f ⊗ g) is the Rankin-Selberg convolution of f and g.

As X -> infinity, let S(X) := sum over all integers d with 0 < d < X, d odd, and d squarefree, of L(1/2, chi_{8d}), where chi_{8d} is the quadratic Dirichlet character associated to the fundamental discriminant 8d. Young proved that S(X) = X P(log X) + O(X^(1/2+epsilon)). Improve this first-moment asymptotic by lowering the error-term exponent 1/2. Ideally, prove the sharper asymptotic suggested by Florea, namely S(X) = X P(log X) + c X^(1/4) + O(X^theta) for some constant c in R and some theta with 0 < theta < 1/4. ([personal.math.ubc.ca](https://personal.math.ubc.ca/~gerg/papers/downloads/MLPL.pdf))

As X -> infinity, determine a polynomial P(x) of degree 10 such that sum_{0<d<X, d odd square-free} L(1/2, chi_{8d})^4 = X P(log X) + o(X), where chi_{8d} denotes the quadratic Dirichlet character associated to the fundamental discriminant 8d. Can the error term o(X) be sharpened to a power-saving error term O(X^{1-delta}) for some delta > 0? Can the Multiple Dirichlet series method be used to obtain the first coefficients of P?

Fix a prime p>2 and a power q of p. Let L(u,f,ψ) be the Artin-Schreier L-function attached to a rational function f∈F_q(x) and an additive character ψ. For the three families
AS_d^0={f∈F_q[x]: deg f=d, (d,p)=1},
AS_d^{0,odd}={f∈F_q[x]: deg f=d, f(x)=-f(-x), (d,2p)=1},
and
AS_d^{ord}={f=h/g: h,g∈F_q[x], (g,h)=1, g squarefree, deg f=max(deg h,deg g)=d, deg g∈{d,d-1}},
let M_k(F_d):=(1/|F_d|)∑_{f∈F_d} L_c(f,ψ)^k denote the k-th family moment at the central value L_c(f,ψ). In the regime where q is fixed and d→∞, determine the limiting 1-level density of zeros with respect to a Schwartz test function φ for the support ranges requested in Problem (20)—namely: for AS_d^{ord}, either supp φ̂⊂(-1-δ,1+δ) for some δ>0 or supp φ̂⊂(-2-δ,2+δ) for some δ>0; for AS_d^0, supp φ̂⊂(-(2-2/p)-δ, 2-2/p+δ); and for AS_d^{0,odd}, supp φ̂⊂(-(1-1/p)-δ, 1-1/p+δ)—and compute the corresponding low moments M_1,...,M_6 for AS_d^{ord}, M_1,...,M_4 for AS_d^0, and M_1,M_2 for AS_d^{0,odd}.

For fixed 1/2<σ<1 and large T, investigate how Ingham-type zero-density bounds for the number of zeros ρ=β+iγ of the Riemann zeta function with β≥σ and 0≤γ≤T depend on the critical-line moment estimates available for ζ(s). In particular, can Ingham’s zero-density argument, which uses the dyadic fourth moment ∫_T^{2T}|ζ(1/2+it)|^4 dt, be adapted to use other proved nontrivial moment bounds—such as Heath-Brown’s twelfth-moment estimate ∫_0^T|ζ(1/2+it)|^12 dt ≪ε T^(2+ε)—to obtain corresponding zero-density estimates for ζ(s); and can the same moment-based method be generalized to other L-functions?

Assuming the Riemann Hypothesis, does there exist a constant C < (log 2)/2 such that, for all sufficiently large real t, one has |ζ(1/2 + it)| ≪ exp(((C + o(1)) log t)/(log log t)), where the o(1) term tends to 0 as t → ∞? In other words, improve the Chandee–Soundararajan RH bound by lowering the admissible leading constant from (log 2)/2.

Assume the Riemann Hypothesis. Let S(t) = (1/pi) arg zeta(1/2 + it), with arg zeta defined in the standard way. Carneiro, Chandee, and Milinovich proved that |S(t)| <= (1/4 + o(1)) log t / log log t as t -> infinity. Can one lower the leading constant 1/4? Equivalently, prove that there exists a constant c < 1/4 such that, under RH, |S(t)| <= (c + o(1)) log t / log log t for all sufficiently large real t.

Can one prove the following Weyl-strength subconvex estimate posed in the paper? Let f be a Hecke-Maass cusp form of level 1 with spectral parameter t_f (so the Laplace eigenvalue is 1/4+t_f^2).
