If S is embeddable in a group, in the sense that S admits an injective semigroup homomorphism into some group, must ∼p be transitive on S; that is, must every group-embeddable semigroup satisfy: for all a, b, c ∈ S, if a ∼p b and b ∼p c, then a ∼p c?

Let S be a semigroup, and define primary conjugacy on S by a ~_p b if there exist u,v in S^1 such that a=uv and b=vu, where S^1 denotes S with an identity adjoined if necessary. For each c in S, let S_c=(S,◦_c) be the variant of S at c, defined by x ◦_c y = xcy for all x,y in S. If the relation ~_p is transitive on every variant S_c, must ~_p already be transitive on S?

Let S be a semigroup, and let S^1 denote S with an identity adjoined. Define Otto conjugacy on S by declaring a ~_o b if and only if there exist g,h in S^1 such that a g = g b and b h = h a. Does there exist a semigroup S for which ~_o is a semigroup congruence and the quotient semigroup S/~_o is not cancellative?

Does there exist a finite semigroup S such that the Otto conjugacy relation ∼o on S, defined by a∼ob if and only if there exist u,v∈S with au=ub and va=bv, is a semigroup congruence (that is, x∼ox' and y∼oy' imply xy∼ox'y' for all x,x',y,y'∈S), and such that the quotient semigroup S/∼o is not cancellative (equivalently, it fails left or right cancellation)?

Does there exist an infinite set of pairwise distinct first-order definable semigroup conjugacies—that is, equivalence relations on semigroups, each definable by a first-order formula in the language of semigroups and coinciding with ordinary group conjugacy whenever the semigroup is a group—such that these conjugacies form a chain under the global inclusion order, meaning that for any two of them one is included in the other and inclusion is interpreted across all semigroups? ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2411.16284))

Does there exist an infinite set of first-order definable semigroup conjugacies {rho_i : i in I} such that, for every group G, each rho_i coincides with ordinary group conjugacy on G, and for any distinct i,j in I neither rho_i is contained in rho_j nor rho_j is contained in rho_i, where containment of conjugacies means: for every semigroup S and all a,b in S, if a is rho_i-conjugate to b in S, then a is rho_j-conjugate to b in S?

Does there exist a semigroup conjugacy relation ~—that is, an equivalence relation on semigroups which coincides with ordinary group conjugacy whenever the semigroup is a group—that is not partition-covering, in the sense that there exist a set X and a partition P of X for which no semigroup S with underlying set X has its ~-conjugacy classes exactly equal to the blocks of P? ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2411.16284))

For an arbitrary semigroup S, let ∼_G be the reflexive relation such that, for a≠b, one has a∼_G b iff there exists a subgroup H≤S containing a and b and an element g∈H with g^{-1}ag=b. Let U(S) be the group of units of S, and define unit conjugacy by a∼_u b iff there exists u∈U(S) such that u^{-1}au=b and ubu^{-1}=a. Call a relation on semigroups a semigroup conjugacy relation if it is an equivalence relation and coincides with ∼_G whenever the semigroup is a group; order such conjugacies by inclusion, meaning ∼_1⊆∼_2 if a∼_1b implies a∼_2b for every semigroup and every a,b. Is ∼_u the least semigroup conjugacy relation distinct from ∼_G under this order? ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2411.16284))

Let S be an epigroup. Define Green’s H-relation on S by a H b iff aS^1 = bS^1 and S^1a = S^1b. Define primary conjugacy by a∼p b iff a=uv and b=vu for some u,v∈S, and let ∼p∗ be the transitive closure of ∼p. Define epigroup conjugacy by a∼tr b iff there exist g,h∈S^1 such that ghg=g, hgh=h, hg=a^ω, gh=b^ω, and ga^{ω+1}h=b^{ω+1}. Is it always true that a H b and a∼tr b imply a∼p∗ b; equivalently, does ∼tr ∩ H ⊆ ∼p∗ hold for every epigroup S? ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2411.16284))

For every finite semigroup S with |S| < 13, is the relation (∼u ∩ H) equal to subgroup conjugacy ∼g on S? Here, for a,b ∈ S, a ∼g b means that either a = b or there exists a subgroup G ≤ S containing a and b together with an element g ∈ G such that g^{-1}ag = b; a ∼u b means that there exists g ∈ U(S) such that g^{-1}ag = b and gbg^{-1} = a; and H is Green’s H-relation, i.e. a H b iff a L b and a R b.

Let S be a finite semigroup. Define a ~_n b to mean that there exist g,h in S^1 such that ag=gb, bh=ha, hag=b, and gbh=a. Let ~_g denote subgroup conjugacy, i.e. the reflexive relation such that for distinct a,b in S, one has a ~_g b iff a and b belong to a common subgroup of S and are conjugate within that subgroup. Let H be Green's H-relation. Is it true that (~_n ∩ H) = ~_g for every semigroup S with |S|<13?

Let S be an epigroup, and let H = L ∩ R be Green’s H-relation on S. Define primary conjugacy by a ~p b iff a = uv and b = vu for some u,v in S^1, and let ~p* be the transitive closure of ~p. Let ~tr denote trace conjugacy on S, i.e. a ~tr b iff there exist g,h in S^1 such that ghg = g, hgh = h, g a^(omega+1) h = b^(omega+1), hg = a^omega, and gh = b^omega, where a^omega is the idempotent power of a. Does there exist an epigroup S and elements a,b in S such that a H b and a ~tr b, but a is not ~p*-conjugate to b?

On the class of all semigroups, does there exist a first-order definable semigroup conjugacy ρ, with ρ ≠ ∼g, such that ρ is strictly contained in ∼u ∩ H in the inclusion order on conjugacies? Here ∼g is the relation that two elements are conjugate inside a common subgroup of the semigroup, ∼u is unit conjugacy, H is Green’s H-relation, and 'ρ is strictly contained in ∼u ∩ H' means that ρ is contained in ∼u ∩ H for every semigroup and that the containment is strict for at least one semigroup.

For every continuous graph Γ=(V,E) in the sense of the paper—where V is finite, each edge in E is a unit-length continuous interval, and Γ is endowed with its shortest-path metric d—and for every real r>0, does there exist a finite predetermined set D=D(Γ,r) of points of Γ (for example, all endpoints together with finitely many additional subdivision points on the edges) such that α_r(Γ)=max{|I|: I⊆D and d(p,q)≥2r for all distinct p,q∈I}, equivalently, some maximum r-independent set of Γ can be chosen entirely from D? ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2501.14554))

Fix a positive rational number r. Let Γ be a general continuous graph in the sense of Definitions 1–4: Γ has a finite endpoint set, each edge is a unit-length rectifiable continuous interval, and distances are measured by the induced shortest-path metric d. If I⊆Γ is r-independent when d(p,q)>2r for every distinct p,q∈I, and α_r(Γ) is the maximum size of such a set, does the maximum r-independent set problem on arbitrary continuous graphs admit a certificate of size polynomial in the input description of Γ that encodes and permits verification of an optimal r-independent set of size α_r(Γ)? ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2501.14554))

Let Gamma be a continuous graph in the sense of the paper: Gamma has finitely many endpoints, every edge is a unit-length rectifiable interval, and distances are measured by shortest-path length. For r > 0, let alpha_r(Gamma) denote the maximum size of a set S subseteq Gamma such that d(x,y) >= r for every two distinct points x,y in S. Does there exist a predetermined finite discretization of the edge set of Gamma that preserves alpha_r(Gamma); and, if such a discretization exists, for which values of r is computing alpha_r(Gamma) on general continuous graphs polynomial-time solvable and for which values is it computationally intractable, beyond the trivial sufficiently-large-r regime where the diameter bound forces at most one selected point per connected component?

Let G be a finite combinatorial graph with n = |V(G)| ≥ 1, and let Γ(G) be the continuous graph obtained by replacing each edge uv of G by a unit-length continuous edge e_{u,v} and equipping the resulting point set with the shortest-path metric. Let α(G) denote the maximum size of an independent vertex set of G, and let α1(Γ(G)) denote the maximum cardinality of a set I of points of Γ(G) such that d(p,q) ≥ 2 for all distinct p,q ∈ I. Is it true that α1(Γ(G))/α(G) ≤ n/2 for every G, and if so is this bound tight? More specifically, how do structural properties of G affect this ratio on special classes of graphs? ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2501.14554))

Fix a rational number r>0. Let Γ=(V,E) be a finite continuous graph in the sense of the paper: V is a finite set of endpoints, each edge in E is a unit-length rectifiable interval, and Γ is equipped with the induced shortest-path metric d. If α_r(Γ) denotes the maximum cardinality of a set S⊆Γ such that d(x,y)>2r for all distinct x,y∈S, does there exist a polynomial-time algorithm that, for every such Γ, computes an r-independent set of size at least α_r(Γ)/c_r for some constant c_r depending only on r (equivalently, a constant-factor approximation for the maximum r-independent set problem on general continuous graphs)?

Let Γ=(V,E) be a continuous graph in the sense of the paper: each edge is a unit-length rectifiable interval, distances are measured by the induced shortest-path metric, and n=|V| is the number of endpoints. For a real number r>0, let α_r(Γ) be the maximum cardinality of a set I⊆E such that d(p,q)≥2r for all distinct p,q∈I, and let β_r(Γ) be the minimum cardinality of an r-cover of Γ by balls B(p,r) whose centers p may lie anywhere in E. Since for r=1 one has α_1(Γ)+β_1(Γ)=n, determine the sharp bound, as a function of n and r alone, on α_r(Γ)+β_r(Γ) for arbitrary continuous graphs Γ with n endpoints, and decide whether that bound is tight.

Let G be a finite combinatorial graph, and let Γ(G) be its continuous counterpart obtained by replacing each edge of G with a unit-length interval and equipping the resulting space with the induced shortest-path metric. Let β(G) denote the minimum size of a vertex cover of G, and let β1(Γ(G)) denote the minimum cardinality of a 1-cover of Γ(G), i.e. a family of metric balls {B(pi,1)} whose centers pi may be arbitrary points of Γ(G) and whose union covers all points of Γ(G). What is the supremum of β(G)/β1(Γ(G)) over all finite graphs G? In particular, is it always true that β(G) <= 2β1(Γ(G)), and if so is the constant 2 best possible?

Let G be a continuous graph in the sense of the paper: a metric graph obtained from a finite endpoint set with each edge realized as a unit-length continuous interval, and with distance given by the shortest-path metric on all points of G. For a rational radius r > 0, let tau_r(G) denote the minimum number of radius-r balls, with centers allowed anywhere in G, whose union covers all points of G. Hartmann et al. are cited as showing that this minimum r-cover problem is polynomial-time solvable when r is a unit fraction and NP-hard when r is a non-unit fraction. For the hard regime—namely, rational radii r that are non-unit fractions (not of the form 1/q with q in N)—what lower bounds can be proved on the polynomial-time approximability of tau_r(G), i.e. which approximation ratios can be ruled out for the minimum r-cover problem on general continuous graphs unless P = NP?

For every natural number n, let Γ(K_n) be the continuous graph obtained from the complete graph K_n by replacing each edge with a unit-length interval and equipping the resulting space with the shortest-path metric. Is it true that χ_{1/2}(Γ(K_n)) = ⌈n/2⌉, where χ_{1/2}(Γ) is the minimum number of colours needed for a family of radius-1/2 balls with arbitrary centers in Γ that covers all of Γ and assigns different colours to every two balls with non-empty intersection?

Let G be a loopless planar combinatorial graph, and let Γ(G) denote its continuous counterpart in the sense of Definition 4, where each edge of G is replaced by a unit-length interval. Must Γ(G) be (1/2,3)-colourable; that is, does there always exist a family of balls B={B(p,1/2): p∈E(Γ(G))} whose union covers every point of Γ(G), together with a colouring f:B→{1,2,3}, such that whenever B,B'∈B have nonempty intersection, one has f(B)≠f(B')? ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2501.14554))

Let Γ=(V,E) be a finite continuous graph in the sense of the paper, with each edge realized as a unit-length interval and distance given by the shortest-path metric, and let n=|V|. Define χ_{1/2}(Γ) to be the minimum number c such that Γ admits a 1/2-cover by metric balls of radius 1/2, centered at arbitrary points of E, together with a colouring of those balls by c colours so that any two intersecting balls receive different colours. Is the classical hardness threshold for graph colouring preserved in this continuous setting—namely, for every ε>0, is it NP-hard to approximate χ_{1/2}(Γ) within a factor n^(1-ε)—or does allowing centers on continuous edges lead to strictly better polynomial-time approximation guarantees than in the combinatorial chromatic-number problem?

Let Γ=(V,E) be a finite continuous graph in the sense of Definitions 1–4, with unit-length continuous edges and shortest-path metric, let G(Γ) be its corresponding combinatorial graph on the same endpoint set V, and let n:=|V|. Define χ_{1/2}(Γ) to be the least integer c for which there exists a 1/2-cover B={B(p,1/2): p∈E} of Γ together with a colour map f:B→{1,…,c} such that f(B)≠f(B') whenever B∩B'≠∅. What general lower and upper bounds can be established for χ_{1/2}(Γ) as functions of χ(G(Γ)) and n, and, if stronger, as functions of other polynomial-time computable parameters of Γ or G(Γ)?

Given a finite combinatorial graph G, let Γ(G) be the continuous graph obtained by replacing each edge of G with a unit-length continuous interval and equipping the resulting space with the shortest-path metric. A 1-bramble of Γ(G) is a set of subtrees of Γ(G) such that for every two subtrees T1 and T2 in the set, there exist points p in T1 and q in T2 with d(p,q) <= 1. The order of a 1-bramble is the minimum cardinality of a set X subseteq Γ(G) that intersects every subtree in the bramble, and the 1-bramble number of Γ(G) is the maximum order over all 1-brambles of Γ(G). For a given small integer k > 0, is there a polynomial-time algorithm that decides whether the 1-bramble number of Γ(G) is at most k?

Fix a positive algebraic real number r. Let G be a continuous graph with unit-length edges, endowed with its shortest-path metric, and let an r-cover of G mean a family of radius-r balls, centered at arbitrary points of G, whose union contains every point of G. What is the computational complexity of the decision problem "given G and k, does G admit an r-cover of size at most k?" In particular, is this problem NP-hard for every fixed algebraic real r that is not a unit fraction, i.e. not of the form 1/q for any positive integer q?

Does there exist a packing array PA(21,14,9), that is, a 21x14 array with entries in {0,1,...,8} such that for every pair of distinct columns, each ordered pair of symbols from {0,1,...,8}^2 appears at most once in the corresponding 21x2 subarray?
Does there exist a skew weighing matrix W(18,9), that is, an 18×18 matrix W with entries in {0,1,-1} such that WW^T = 9I_18 and W^T = -W?

Does there exist a balanced ternary design BTD(17,17;8,2,12;12,8), equivalently a collection of 17 multiset blocks on 17 points encoded by a matrix M = (m_{vb}) in {0,1,2}^{17x17}, such that each column has total multiplicity 12, each row has exactly eight entries equal to 1 and exactly two entries equal to 2 (hence row sum 12), and for every distinct points v,w in {1,...,17} one has sum_{b=1}^{17} m_{vb} m_{wb} = 8?

Determine whether there exists a balanced ternary design BTD(12,26;3,5,13;6,5) in the sense of the paper: a collection of 26 multiset blocks, each of total cardinality 6, on a 12-point set, equivalently represented by a 12 x 26 incidence matrix M = (m_{vb}) with entries in {0,1,2}, such that each row sums to 13 and has exactly three entries equal to 1 and five entries equal to 2, each column sums to 6, and for every pair of distinct points v != w one has sum_{b=1}^{26} m_{vb} m_{wb} = 5; if no such design exists, prove nonexistence.
Construct a symmetric weighing matrix W(21,9); that is, find a matrix W in {0,1,-1}^{21x21} such that W^T = W and WW^T = 9I_21.

Does there exist—and if so, construct—an equidistant permutation array EPA(12,8,21), that is, a 21 x 12 array whose rows are permutations of {0,1,...,11} and such that every pair of distinct rows has Hamming distance exactly 8?

Fix n≥3, p∈[1,∞), an open set Ω⊂R^n, and a homeomorphism f:Ω→f(Ω)⊂R^n with f∈W^{1,p}(Ω,R^n). Prove or disprove that f can be approximated in the W^{1,p}(Ω,R^n)-norm by a sequence of smooth diffeomorphisms f_j:Ω→f_j(Ω)⊂R^n. Separately, ask the analogous question with smooth diffeomorphisms replaced by piecewise affine homeomorphisms. In particular, is this true in the physically relevant case n=3?

Let n >= 3, let Omega, Delta be open subsets of R^n, and let f: Omega -> Delta be a locally finitely piecewise affine homeomorphism such that f in W^{1,p}(Omega, R^n) and f^{-1} in W^{1,q}(Delta, R^n) for some 1 <= p, q < infinity. Is it true that for every epsilon > 0 there exists a diffeomorphism g: Omega -> Delta such that ||f-g||_{W^{1,p}(Omega, R^n)} + ||f^{-1}-g^{-1}||_{W^{1,q}(Delta, R^n)} < epsilon?

Does there exist a higher-dimensional counterexample to the Ball-Evans approximation problem at or above the threshold p = ⌊n/2⌋? More precisely, do there exist n ≥ 3, an open set Ω ⊂ R^n, an exponent p ≥ ⌊n/2⌋, and a homeomorphism f: Ω → f(Ω) ⊂ R^n with f ∈ W^{1,p}(Ω, R^n) such that f is not the strong W^{1,p}-limit of a sequence of diffeomorphisms, or alternatively of a sequence of piecewise affine homeomorphisms?

Let Omega be a bounded domain in R^2, and let f:Omega->f(Omega) be an orientation-preserving homeomorphism. Assume either (i) f belongs to W^{1,p}(Omega;R^2) for some p>=1 and E1(f)=\int_Omega (|Df(x)|^p+J_f(x)^{-a}) dx<infinity for some a>0, or (ii) f belongs to W^{1,2}(Omega;R^2) and E2(f)=\int_Omega (|Df(x)|^2+|Df(x)|^2/J_f(x)) dx<infinity. Is it true that one can find a sequence of smooth diffeomorphisms f_m:Omega->f(Omega), preserving the prescribed boundary data when such data are part of the admissible class, such that f_m->f strongly in W^{1,p}(Omega;R^2) in case (i) (respectively strongly in W^{1,2}(Omega;R^2) in case (ii)) and, simultaneously, E1(f_m)->E1(f) in case (i) (respectively E2(f_m)->E2(f) in case (ii))?

Let Omega subset R^n be a domain, let 1 <= p < infinity, and let f: Omega -> f(Omega) be a homeomorphism in W^{1,p}(Omega,R^n) such that det Df = 1 almost everywhere in Omega. Must there exist a sequence of volume-preserving diffeomorphisms f_j: Omega -> f(Omega), with det Df_j = 1, such that f_j -> f strongly in W^{1,p}(Omega,R^n)? If the paper formulates the piecewise affine version in parallel, can one equivalently ask for strong W^{1,p}-approximation by volume-preserving piecewise affine homeomorphisms?

Let Omega be a planar domain in R^2, and let f: Omega -> R^2 be a homeomorphism with f in W^{2,1}(Omega, R^2). Must there exist a sequence of diffeomorphisms f_j: Omega -> f(Omega) such that ||f_j - f||_{W^{2,1}(Omega, R^2)} -> 0?

Fix n ≥ 3 and 1 ≤ p < ∞. Let Ω, Ω' ⊂ R^n be bounded domains for which homeomorphisms Ω → Ω' exist. Is it true that every map f ∈ W^{1,p}(Ω, R^n) that arises as a weak W^{1,p}-limit of a sequence of W^{1,p} homeomorphisms f_k : Ω → Ω' also arises as a strong W^{1,p}-limit of a sequence of homeomorphisms Ω → Ω'? Equivalently: in dimensions n ≥ 3, do the weak and strong W^{1,p} sequential closure classes of homeomorphisms Ω → Ω' coincide?

Let n>2, let 1 <= p < infinity, and let Omega, Omega' be bounded open subsets of R^n. If D(Omega,Omega') denotes the class of diffeomorphisms f: Omega -> Omega', is the sequential weak W^{1,p}(Omega;R^n)-closure of D(Omega,Omega') equal to its strong W^{1,p}(Omega;R^n)-closure?

Conjecture 1.1. Let Omega be a domain in R^n with n >= 4. Is it true that there does not exist a homeomorphism f: Omega -> f(Omega) with f in W^{1,floor(n/2)}_loc(Omega, R^n) such that its weak Jacobian J_f = det Df is positive on a set of positive Lebesgue measure and negative on a set of positive Lebesgue measure?

Let n >= 4 and 1 <= p < floor(n/2). Does there exist a sense-preserving homeomorphism f : (-1,1)^n -> (-1,1)^n such that f belongs to W^{1,p}((-1,1)^n, (-1,1)^n), satisfies f(x) = x for every x in the boundary ∂(-1,1)^n, and has Jacobian determinant J_f(x) < 0 for almost every x in (-1,1)^n?

Let n\ge 3, and assume either \lfloor n/2\rfloor < p \le n-1, or, in the special case n=3, 1\le p\le 2. If \Omega\subset\mathbb{R}^n is a connected open set and f\in W^{1,p}_{loc}(\Omega,\mathbb{R}^n) is a nonconstant continuous, open, and discrete mapping, must its Jacobian determinant J_f=\det Df have a constant sign almost everywhere in \Omega? Equivalently, is it impossible that both sets \{x\in\Omega:J_f(x)>0\} and \{x\in\Omega:J_f(x)<0\} have positive Lebesgue measure?

For every integer n >= 6 and every q with 1 <= q <= floor(n/2)/2, does there exist a homeomorphism f of the n-cube onto itself, with f in W^{2,q}((-1,1)^n, R^n), such that the Jacobian determinant J_f = det Df is positive on a set of positive n-dimensional Lebesgue measure and negative on a set of positive n-dimensional Lebesgue measure?

For every n >= 3 and every 1 <= q < n/2, does there exist a self-homeomorphism f of a standard bounded domain in R^n (in the paper's normalized form, a cube with identity boundary values) such that f belongs to W^{2,q}, its Jacobian satisfies J_f(x) = det Df(x) = 0 for almost every x, and, analogously, does there exist such a self-homeomorphism in the class of maps with Df in BV?

Does every closed connected simply-connected PL 4-manifold M admit a trisection M=H0∪H1∪H2 in the sense that each Hi is a 4-dimensional 1-handlebody, each pairwise intersection Hij=Hi∩Hj is a 3-dimensional handlebody, the triple intersection H0∩H1∩H2 is a closed connected surface, and one of the sectors Hi is PL-homeomorphic to the 4-ball D^4 (equivalently, one trisection parameter ki is 0)?

Can the Section 3.1 Kirby-diagram-to-gem construction be extended to generalized Kirby diagrams in the sense of de Sa that also encode non-orientable 1-handles, so as to algorithmically produce a gem of the compact PL 4-manifold encoded by such a diagram; and, if so, do the resulting gems admit gem-induced trisections in the form needed to apply the non-orientable Laudenbach-Poenaru-type closure argument, thereby extending the existing orientable gem-theoretic upper-bound method to the trisection genus of the associated closed PL 4-manifolds, and hence to all closed PL 4-manifolds, orientable or non-orientable?

Let M be a compact orientable PL 4-manifold with ∂M ≅ #_r(S^1 × S^2), r > 0, and let Γ ∈ G_s^(4) be a gem of M. Proposition 9 shows that if the singular 4-residue Γ_hat4 contains r ρ_3-pairs of some fixed color i ∈ Δ_3 whose switchings yield a gem of S^3, then one can pass from Γ to the closed manifold stage: if those pairs are ρ_3-pairs in Γ, their switchings produce a gem of bar M = M ∪ Y_r, while if r' ≤ r of them are ρ_4-pairs in Γ, switching all of them yields a gem of N with bar M ≅ #_{r'}(S^1 × S^3) # N. When a given gem Γ of M does not satisfy these Proposition 9 hypotheses, is there an algorithmic gem-theoretic procedure—possibly by recognizing a suitable sequence of standard combinatorial moves that creates the required ρ_3-pairs—to construct directly from Γ a gem of the associated closed 4-manifold bar M?

Let M be a compact orientable PL 4-manifold, let (L,d) be a connected Kirby diagram of M whose dotted components, if any, are in good position, and form a Kirby diagram of the double D(M) by adding a 0-framed meridian to each framed component of (L,d). If Γ is the 5-colored graph obtained from this doubled diagram by the Kirby-diagram-to-gem construction of Theorem 5, is there a standard algorithmic modification of Γ that brings the resulting compact 0/1/2-handlebody into the setting of Proposition 9(i), namely by producing, for some color i in Δ3, ρ3-pairs in Γ_hat4 whose switchings yield a gem of S3 and whose corresponding switchings in Γ then yield directly a gem of the closed double D(M)?

Characterize topologically the closed simply-connected PL 4-manifolds M that admit a 5-colored graph (gem) Gamma and a cyclic permutation epsilon of Delta_4 satisfying the minimality hypotheses isolated in Proposition 26, with T(Gamma, epsilon) a gem-induced trisection, so that the trisection arising from Gamma realizes the trisection genus of M; equivalently, determine which such manifolds admit gem-based trisections with g_T(M)=beta_2(M) (and, in the weak-simple crystallization case singled out there, also g_T(M)=G(M)/2), or at least identify natural classes of manifolds with this property.

Give a topological characterization of the compact PL 4-manifolds M with empty or connected boundary that admit a weak semi-simple crystallization Γ with respect to some cyclic permutation ε of Δ_4 and such that T(Γ,ε) is a gem-induced trisection. In particular, which closed simply-connected PL 4-manifolds admit such a Γ and ε (equivalently, in this closed simply-connected case, a crystallization with g_{ε_i,ε_{i+2},ε_{i+4}}=1 for every i mod 5), so that Proposition 26 applies and yields g_GT(M)=g_T(M)=β₂(M)?

Let M be a compact PL 4-manifold with connected boundary, homeomorphic to \#_m(S^2\times S^1) if M is orientable or to \#_m(S^2\widetilde\times S^1) if M is non-orientable, with m>0, and assume that M admits gem-induced trisections. Let \bar M\cong M\cup Y_m^4 in the orientable case or \bar M\cong M\cup \widetilde{Y}_m^4 in the non-orientable case be the closed 4-manifold obtained by gluing the unique genus-m 4-dimensional handlebody along \partial M, and let g_{GT}(M) denote the minimum genus among all gem-induced trisections of M. Under what conditions is the upper bound of Theorem 13 sharp, that is, when does one have g_T(\bar M)=g_{GT}(M)?

Does there exist a transcendental entire function f:C->C with infinitely many zeros such that either (f'(z))^2 + (f''(z))^2 = (f(z))^2 for all z in C, or f(z+c1)^2 + f(z+c2)^2 = f(z)^2 for all z in C, where c1,c2 are distinct nonzero complex constants?

Let c1,c2 be fixed complex constants with c1,c2 \in C\setminus\{0\} and c1 \neq c2. Classify all finite-order transcendental meromorphic functions f on C such that, for every z \in C, one has f(z+c1)^2+f(z+c2)^2=f(z)^2; equivalently, determine the exact Riccati-type representation of all such solutions that the paper obtains in its Proposition 1.2/Theorem 1.3 formulation.

Let F_{μ,L}^{(1)} := {f: ℝ → ℝ : f is μ-strongly convex and L-smooth}, and consider the constant-parameter Polyak heavy-ball iteration x_{t+1} = x_t - γ f'(x_t) + β(x_t - x_{t-1}). For each pair 0 < μ ≤ L (equivalently κ = L/μ), does there exist a tuning (γ, β), depending only on μ and L, such that heavy-ball attains an accelerated worst-case convergence rate on the full scalar class F_{μ,L}^{(1)}—namely a dependence of order O(sqrt(κ) log(1/ε)), as opposed to the non-accelerated O(κ log(1/ε)) scaling—or is exact acceleration impossible even in dimension one?

Let HB_{γ,β} denote Polyak’s heavy-ball method x_{t+1} = x_t - γ∇f(x_t) + β(x_t - x_{t-1}) applied to functions f in F_{μ,L}, where F_{μ,L} is the class of differentiable functions f : R^d -> R, for arbitrary d, that are L-smooth and μ-strongly convex. Do there exist tunings (γ,β) for which one can prove both that HB_{γ,β} admits no Lyapunov sequence of the specific type searched in the paper—namely V_t = l(f(x_t)-f_*, f(x_{t-1})-f_*) + q(x_{t-1}-x_*, ∇f(x_{t-1}), x_t-x_*, ∇f(x_t)), with l linear and q homogeneous quadratic, decreasing along every HB trajectory on every f in F_{μ,L}—and that HB_{γ,β} admits no cycle counterexample on F_{μ,L}, i.e. there is no K-periodic HB orbit arising from any initialization on any f in F_{μ,L}? If such tunings exist, what is the actual behavior of HB in those blank regions of the (γ,β)-plane: convergence without such a Lyapunov certificate, divergence without periodic cycling, or some third type of dynamics?

Fix 0<μ<L, and consider the scalar Heavy-Ball method x_{t+1}=x_t-γ f'(x_t)+β(x_t-x_{t-1}) on functions f:ℝ→ℝ in F_{μ,L}, the class of L-smooth, μ-strongly convex functions. Let P_{purple}(μ,L) denote the purple cycle region from the paper, i.e. the set of tunings already known in dimension 2 to admit a heavy-ball cycle on some function in F_{μ,L}. Is it true that every tuning (γ,β)∈P_{purple}(μ,L) is also realized in dimension 1, in the sense that there exist an integer K≥2, a scalar function f∈F_{μ,L}, and an initialization of the Heavy-Ball method whose trajectory is exactly K-periodic? If so, this would establish that Heavy-Ball does not accelerate over scalar functions in F_{μ,L} either.

For the heavy-ball method x_{t+1} = x_t - gamma f'(x_t) + beta (x_t - x_{t-1}) applied to scalar objectives f in F_{mu,L} (the class of L-smooth, mu-strongly convex functions f : R -> R), can one prove that every tuning (gamma,beta) in the full purple cycle region already admits a one-dimensional cycle, and moreover prove this by restricting to cycles x_0,...,x_{K-1} whose sorted points x_(0) <= ... <= x_(K-1) are visited in the single Figure 4 order (x_0,...,x_{K-1}) = (x_(0), x_(1), x_(3), x_(5), ..., x_(4), x_(2)) for some cycle length K, thereby recovering the whole dimension-1 cycle region and hence ruling out acceleration of heavy-ball on F_{mu,L} in dimension 1?

Fix 0 < mu <= L and consider Polyak's Heavy-Ball method HB_{gamma,beta}, x_{t+1} = x_t - gamma nabla f(x_t) + beta (x_t - x_{t-1}), on the class F_{mu,L} of L-smooth, mu-strongly-convex functions f : R^d -> R. In Figure 2, the green region consists of tunings (gamma, beta) for which the authors numerically found a Lyapunov sequence of the form V_t = l(f(x_t)-f^*, f(x_{t-1})-f^*) + q(x_{t-1}-x^*, nabla f(x_{t-1}), x_t-x^*, nabla f(x_t)), with l linear and q homogeneously quadratic, satisfying f(x_{t+1})-f^* <= V_{t+1} <= rho V_t, while the purple region consists of tunings for which there exists a genuine integer-length cycle, i.e. some K >= 3, some K-tuple (x_0, ..., x_{K-1}), and some f in F_{mu,L} whose HB_{gamma,beta} trajectory is exactly (x_{t mod K})_{t >= 0}. Using the closed-form formula for the border of each integer-K cycle region recalled from [Goujaud et al., 2023b, Theorem 3.5], Figure 8 formally substitutes fractional values of K and produces intermediate regions whose continuum appears to fill the unfilled part of the (gamma, beta)-plane without entering the green region. What, if anything, is the precise mathematical object or dynamical behavior encoded by this fractional-K continuation, and what does it imply about the unfilled tunings in Figure 2 where the authors found neither the above Lyapunov sequence nor a genuine cycle?

In the topos SymSet = PSh(F) of symmetric simplicial sets, where F is the category of non-empty finite sets and all maps, the levels are indexed by the total order -infinity < 0 < 1 < 2 < ... < infinity, with level l induced by the inclusion of the full subcategory F_l on sets of cardinality at most l+1. For each level l, let a_l be the least level m such that every l-skeletal symmetric set is m-coskeletal. Here l-skeletal means that the counit sk_l X -> X is an isomorphism (equivalently, every structure in X has mass at most l+1), and m-coskeletal means that the unit X -> cosk_m X is an isomorphism (equivalently, every k-cycle with k > m has a unique filler). Determine the exact Aufhebung function l |-> a_l for PSh(F), and hence the precise way-above relation between levels in combinatorial terms.

Fix an integer n > 2. Let G = (V,E) be a finite simple undirected graph with |V| = n, and define a map Phi_G: P(V) -> P(V) by Phi_G(S) = S union {v in V : there exist distinct s0, s1 in S with {s0,v} in E and {s1,v} in E}. Call G propagative if for every subset S subseteq V with |S| = 2, there exists k >= 1 such that Phi_G^k(S) = V. Determine the sharp minimum-degree threshold for propagativity: what is the smallest integer m = m(n) such that every n-vertex graph G with minimum degree delta(G) >= m is necessarily propagative?

Question 2.1 (Virtual Euler class one conjecture). Let M be a closed oriented hyperbolic 3-manifold with b1(M) >= 1, and let a in H^2(M; R) be an even integral class of dual Thurston norm 1 (that is, a comes from H^2(M; Z) and is divisible by 2 there). Does there exist a finite-sheeted cover p: M̃ -> M and a transversely oriented taut foliation F on M̃ such that the Euler class e(F) of the oriented tangent plane field TF is equal to p^*(a), where p^*(a) is understood via the Poincaré duality identifications H1(M) ≅ H^2(M) and H1(M̃) ≅ H^2(M̃)?

Let M be a closed oriented 3-manifold with a transitive pseudo-Anosov flow phi, and let gamma_1, ..., gamma_k be closed orbits of phi. After fixing slope coordinates on the k boundary tori of the orbit complement M \setminus \bigsqcup_i nu(gamma_i), let Z \subseteq R^k be the closure of the set of multislopes r = (r_1, ..., r_k) such that simultaneous Dehn surgery on gamma_1, ..., gamma_k with slopes r_1, ..., r_k yields a closed 3-manifold carrying a pseudo-Anosov flow transverse to a codimension-1 foliation. Describe the structure of Z; more specifically, is Z a stepwise 'ziggurat' generated by its corners under the coordinatewise interval property, with rational corners whose accumulation points are exactly the S^1 x S^2-surgery points?

Let M be a closed, connected, oriented, smooth 3-manifold, and let (xi^-, xi^+) be a pair of cooriented contact structures on M with opposite signs. Assume there exists a vector field Z on M transverse to both xi^- and xi^+, and assume that both xi^- and xi^+ are tight. Must M admit a cooriented Reebless C^0 codimension-one foliation?

Let M be a closed, connected, oriented, smooth, irreducible rational homology 3-sphere, and let (ξ_-, ξ_+) be a pair of (co)oriented contact structures of opposite signs on M that are homotopic as plane fields. Assume that both ξ_- and ξ_+ are tight. Must M admit a cooriented Reebless C^0-foliation?

Let M be a closed, oriented, smooth, irreducible rational homology 3-sphere, and let (ξ−, ξ+) be a pair of (co)oriented contact structures on M with opposite signs. Assume that their Heegaard Floer contact invariants satisfy ⟨c(ξ−), c(ξ+)⟩ = 1 under the natural duality pairing. Does M admit a Reebless foliation?

Let M be a closed hyperbolic 3-manifold with first Betti number b_1(M)≥1. For every class a ∈ H^2(M; R) that is integral and even (that is, a lies in the image of H^2(M; Z)→H^2(M; R) and is twice another integral class) and whose norm with respect to the norm on H^2(M; R) dual to Thurston's norm on H_2(M; R) is 1, does there exist a tight contact structure ξ on M with Euler class e(ξ)=a? ([conferences.cirm-math.fr](https://conferences.cirm-math.fr/wp-content/uploads/2025/03/Problem_list_3082.pdf))

Does there exist a smooth closed 4-manifold M, together with an Engel structure D ⊂ TM—namely, a rank-2 distribution whose Lie brackets generate a rank-3 hyperplane field E = [D,D] and for which E is even-contact, i.e. E + [E,E] = TM—such that the Engel automorphism group Aut(M,D) = {f ∈ Diff(M) : df(D) = D} is trivial, equivalently Aut(M,D) = {id_M}?

Let (M,D) be an Engel manifold, meaning that M is a smooth 4-manifold and D ⊂ TM is a rank-2 distribution such that E := [D,D] is a hyperplane field and [E,E] = TM. Writing Aut(M,D) := {φ ∈ Diff(M) : φ_*D = D}, is Aut(M,D) trivial for a generic Engel manifold (M,D)?

Let M be a smooth 4-manifold and let {D_t}_{t∈[0,1]} be a homotopy through Engel structures on M. For each t, write E_t := [D_t,D_t] and let W_t ⊂ D_t denote the unique kernel/characteristic line field characterized by [W_t,E_t] = E_t. Are there any dynamical properties of W_t that persist under such homotopies of the Engel structure? ([conferences.cirm-math.fr](https://conferences.cirm-math.fr/wp-content/uploads/2025/03/Problem_list_3082.pdf))

Can one give a general construction scheme, serving as input to Mitsumatsu’s prequantum prolongation, for triples ((M, ξ), L, ω) where M is a smooth 3-manifold with contact plane field ξ, L ⊂ ξ is a smooth line field, and ω is a nowhere-vanishing closed 2-form on M whose de Rham class [ω] is integral and such that ι_Xω = 0 for every local nonzero section X of L? ([conferences.cirm-math.fr](https://conferences.cirm-math.fr/wp-content/uploads/2025/03/Problem_list_3082.pdf))

Let M be a smooth 4-manifold equipped with a foliation ℱ by surfaces, so that Tℱ ⊂ TM is an integrable rank-2 distribution. Assuming the necessary splitting condition noted in the paper—namely that Tℱ and a complementary rank-2 subbundle of TM both split as direct sums of line bundles—can the tangent plane field Tℱ be perturbed, among smooth rank-2 plane fields on M, to an Engel distribution D ⊂ TM (that is, a rank-2 distribution for which E := [D,D] is a rank-3 even-contact hyperplane field and [E,E] = TM)? ([conferences.cirm-math.fr](https://conferences.cirm-math.fr/wp-content/uploads/2025/03/Problem_list_3082.pdf))

Let M be a 4-manifold endowed with a codimension-1 foliation F. Suppose there is a rank-2 plane field ξ ⊂ TF such that, for every leaf L of F, the restriction ξ|L is a contact structure on the 3-manifold L, and suppose moreover that ξ splits globally as a direct sum of two line fields, ξ = λ ⊕ μ. Can this foliated contact data be perturbed to an Engel structure D on M, i.e. to a rank-2 distribution D ⊂ TM whose Lie bracket generates a rank-3 hyperplane field E = [D,D] and such that E is even-contact?

Let ω be a volume form on S^3, and let Diff_0(S^3, vol) denote the identity component of the group of smooth ω-preserving diffeomorphisms of S^3. Is Diff_0(S^3, vol) uniformly perfect, i.e. does there exist an integer N such that every element of Diff_0(S^3, vol) can be expressed as a product of at most N commutators?

Let Diff0(D2, ∗) denote the group of smooth orientation-preserving diffeomorphisms of the 2-disk D2 that fix a marked point ∗ (for example, the origin). Is the real vector space of homogeneous quasimorphisms φ: Diff0(D2, ∗) → R one-dimensional? Here, “homogeneous quasimorphism” means a map φ with bounded defect sup_{g,h}|φ(gh)-φ(g)-φ(h)|<∞ and satisfying φ(g^n)=nφ(g) for every g∈Diff0(D2, ∗) and every n∈Z.

Let Σ_g be a closed oriented surface of genus g, and let κ_i ∈ H^{2i}(Diff(Σ_g); R) denote the i-th Miller-Morita-Mumford class for flat Σ_g-bundles, where Diff(Σ_g) is viewed as a discrete group for group cohomology. Morita showed, using the Bott vanishing theorem, that κ_i = 0 in H^{2i}(Diff(Σ_g); R) for every i > 2. Does the same vanishing hold in bounded group cohomology; that is, is κ_i = 0 in H_b^{2i}(Diff(Σ_g); R) for every i > 2?

For each integer n ≥ 2, does there exist a simple orderable group G that admits a classifying space K(G,1) with finite n-skeleton, but does not admit any classifying space K(G,1) with finite (n+1)-skeleton? ([conferences.cirm-math.fr](https://conferences.cirm-math.fr/wp-content/uploads/2025/03/Problem_list_3082.pdf))

Does there exist a simple orderable group G that is boundedly acyclic, in the standard sense that H_b^n(G; R) = 0 for all n ≥ 1, and that is either finitely presented or, even more strongly, of type F∞ (equivalently, of type Fn for every n, or admits a K(G,1) with finite n-skeleton for each n)?
Are the simple Burger–Mozes groups constructed in [BM00, Lattices in product of trees] orderable; that is, does each such group admit a left-invariant total order?

Fix an oriented circle bundle p:E→Σ over a closed oriented surface, and write n := |⟨E(p), [Σ]⟩| for its absolute Euler number. For ε > 0, let g_{E(p)}(ε) denote the smallest genus g for which there exist a closed oriented surface Σ_g, an oriented circle bundle p_g:E_g→Σ_g with |⟨E(p_g), [Σ_g]⟩| = n, a symmetric generating set S ⊂ π1(Σ_g), and a topologically flat connection with holonomy representation ρ:π1(Σ_g)→PSL(2,R) such that every element of ρ(S) lies in the sup-norm ε-neighborhood of the rotation subgroup U(1) ⊂ PSL(2,R). Is it true that, for all sufficiently small ε > 0, one has g_{E(p)}(ε) ≥ c n / (ε^2 + O(ε^3)) for some universal constant c > 0, perhaps c = 2π, where O(ε^3) denotes a term bounded by Cε^3 as ε → 0?

Let Σ_g be a closed oriented surface of genus g > 0, and let ρ: π1(Σ_g) → Diff_0(S^1) be a representation. Assume there exists a generating set S of π1(Σ_g) such that every ρ(s), for s in S, is within ε of the Möbius subgroup PSL(2,R) ⊂ Diff_0(S^1), with "within ε" understood in the same sense as the preceding Freedman discussion in Section 3.4 (namely sup-norm distance on circle maps). For sufficiently small ε > 0, is there a bound B(g, ε) such that the pulled-back Godbillon-Vey class ρ^*(GV) ∈ H^2(π1(Σ_g); R) ≅ H^2(Σ_g; R) satisfies |⟨ρ^*(GV), [Σ_g]⟩| ≤ B(g, ε)?

Question 3.12 (Freedman). Suppose S^3 -> S^7 -> S^4 is a "generalized" Hopf fibration. Does there exist a closed oriented homology 4-sphere H and a degree-one map f: H -> S^4 such that the pullback of this S^3-bundle along f is a flat S^3-bundle over H (in the topological/C^0 sense used in the surrounding discussion)?

Let p:E→M be an S^3-bundle over a 4-manifold M whose Euler class e(p) and first Pontryagin class p1(p) are both nontrivial. Mather–Thurston theory for C^0-foliations implies that p is bordant to a C^0-flat S^3-bundle p':E'→M'. Can one choose such a bordism so that the simplicial volume ||M'|| of the base M' is bounded above by a constant independent of the original bundle map p?

For n > 1, let e_{2n} denote the universal Euler class of oriented flat S^{2n-1}-bundles, viewed as a class in H^{2n}(BHomeo_0(S^{2n-1}); Z), where Homeo_0(S^{2n-1}) is the identity component of the homeomorphism group of S^{2n-1}. Hirsch-Thurston implies that the restriction of e_{2n} to every amenable subgroup of Homeo_0(S^{2n-1}) vanishes, while bounded-cohomology methods show that e_{2n} is unbounded. How can this dichotomy be explained? More precisely, is e_{2n} hyperbolic in Gromov's sense, and, after passing to real coefficients and restricting to the identity component Homeo_0^{vol}(S^{2n-1}) of the homeomorphism group preserving a fixed volume form on S^{2n-1}, does the Euler class lie nontrivially in the image of the comparison map H_b^{2n}(BHomeo_0^{vol}(S^{2n-1}); R) -> H^{2n}(BHomeo_0^{vol}(S^{2n-1}); R)?

For every n >= 1, let G be an amenable discrete group and let rho: G -> Diff^1_+(R^{2n}) be an action by C^1 (or smoother) orientation-preserving diffeomorphisms. If e(rho) in H^{2n}(G; Z) denotes the Euler class of the associated flat oriented R^{2n}-bundle over BG, must e(rho) vanish?

Let Σ be a closed oriented surface, and let ρ: π1(Σ) → Diff^ω_+(R^2) be an orientation-preserving real-analytic action. If e ∈ H^2(Homeo_0(R^2); Z) denotes the Euler class for planar actions, must the Euler number of ρ, namely ⟨ρ^*e,[Σ]⟩, always satisfy the classical Milnor–Wood bound |⟨ρ^*e,[Σ]⟩| ≤ |χ(Σ)|?

For every closed oriented surface Sigma_g of genus g>1 and every representation rho: pi_1(Sigma_g) -> Homeo_0(R^2) whose image preserves the standard Lebesgue area on R^2, if e in H^2(Homeo_0(R^2); Z) denotes the universal Euler class for planar actions and e(rho)=rho^*e in H^2(pi_1(Sigma_g); Z), must the Euler number satisfy |<e(rho), [Sigma_g]>| <= 2g-2?

Determine the higher-codimension C^0 analogue of Thurston-type stability asked in the paper: if F is a C^0 transversally oriented foliation of codimension q > 1 and L is a compact leaf, what condition on the holonomy of L guarantees that L is stable? In particular, if q = 2, F is a C^0 codimension-2 foliation, the normal microbundle of L has trivial Euler class, pi_1(L) is amenable, and H^1(L; R) = 0, must L be stable? ([conferences.cirm-math.fr](https://conferences.cirm-math.fr/wp-content/uploads/2025/03/Problem_list_3082.pdf))

Let Σ be a Riemann surface with finitely many cusps, let Γ = π1(Σ), and let ρ: Γ -> Homeo_+(S^1) be a geometric action in the sense of Theorem 3.21 (i.e. faithful, with discrete image contained in a finite-dimensional Lie subgroup of Homeo_+(S^1)). Can one formulate and prove a cusped analogue of Mann’s theorem asserting that any appropriately defined deformation ρ' of ρ is semi-conjugate to ρ, with the formulation modified to account for the cusped setting—where the classical suspension-bundle Euler number is trivial and Burger–Iozzi–Wienhard’s bounded-cohomological Euler number is the relevant substitute, and where the closed-case connected-component condition from Theorem 3.21 cannot be used verbatim because Γ is free and Hom(Γ, Homeo_+(S^1)) is connected?

Let π:M→B be a fibration over a closed manifold B with closed fiber L satisfying π1(L) ≅ Z^k, and let F be the foliation of M whose leaves are the fibers of π. What hypotheses on this fibration, in particular on its monodromy, guarantee the following persistence property: every foliation G sufficiently close to F has a compact leaf contained in a neighborhood of some fiber of π?

Let π: M → S be a torus T^2-bundle over a closed surface S, with bundle monodromy ρ, and let F be the foliation of M by the torus fibers of π. Under what hypotheses on ρ does there exist a foliation G that is C^1-close to F and has no compact leaves close to a fiber of π? ([conferences.cirm-math.fr](https://conferences.cirm-math.fr/wp-content/uploads/2025/03/Problem_list_3082.pdf))

Let Homeo_0(R^2) denote the identity component of the homeomorphism group of R^2, endowed with its usual C^0 topology, and let Hom(Z^2, Homeo_0(R^2)) be the corresponding representation space of homomorphisms rho: Z^2 -> Homeo_0(R^2) (equivalently, commuting pairs of homeomorphisms of R^2 isotopic to the identity), with the induced subspace topology from Homeo_0(R^2)^2. For each integer k, let Hom_k(Z^2, Homeo_0(R^2)) be the subspace of representations whose Euler number e(rho) = <rho^*e,[T^2]> is k, where e is the Euler class for planar actions. Is Hom_k(Z^2, Homeo_0(R^2)) connected for every integer k?

Beyond the known cases in which <f, g> is infinite cyclic or f and g belong to a common flow on S^1, under what hypotheses on a commuting pair f, g ∈ Diff(S^1) does the standard 2-cycle (f, g) - (g, f) bound a 3-chain in BDiff(S^1)_δ, the classifying space of Diff(S^1) with the discrete topology?

Let Φ: G → Homeo_+(R^2) be a topological group action on the plane preserving two transverse foliations F^+ and F^- (possibly with prong singularities), and let φ: G → Homeo_+(S^1) be the induced action on the circle at infinity associated to the pair (F^+, F^-). Can one determine from φ alone whether Φ is smoothable, in the sense that the same induced circle action arises from some smooth action on R^2 preserving two transverse foliations? ([conferences.cirm-math.fr](https://conferences.cirm-math.fr/wp-content/uploads/2025/03/Problem_list_3082.pdf))

Does there exist a group G and an orientation-preserving action φ:G→Homeo_+(S^1) such that φ is the action on the circle at infinity associated to a pair of transverse foliations (F^+,F^-) of R^2, possibly with prong singularities, induced by some orientation-preserving topological action Φ:G→Homeo_+(R^2) preserving F^+ and F^-, but φ is not the action on the corresponding circle at infinity induced by any smooth orientation-preserving action Ψ:G→Diff_+(R^2) preserving two transverse foliations? ([conferences.cirm-math.fr](https://conferences.cirm-math.fr/wp-content/uploads/2025/03/Problem_list_3082.pdf))

Let G be a finitely generated amenable orderable group, and let phi: G -> Homeo_+(R) be an action without global fixed points. Must it be the case that either (i) phi is semi-conjugate to an action of G by orientation-preserving affine transformations of R, meaning that there exists a non-decreasing map h: R -> R intertwining the two actions, or else (ii) phi is laminar, in the sense that there exists an interval I subset R such that for every g, h in G, the intervals g(I) and h(I) are either nested or disjoint, and union over g in G of g(I) equals R?

Characterize the pairs (Λ+, Λ-) of prelaminations on S^1 with the following property: for every group action ρ: G → Homeo(S^1) that preserves both Λ+ and Λ-, the induced action of G on the bifoliated plane associated to (Λ+, Λ-) is Anosov-like.

Is every orientation-preserving C^\infty diffeomorphism of the circle a single commutator in Diff^\infty_+(S^1)? Equivalently: for every f \in Diff^\infty_+(S^1), do there exist g,h \in Diff^\infty_+(S^1) such that f = [g,h] = ghg^{-1}h^{-1}? ([conferences.cirm-math.fr](https://conferences.cirm-math.fr/wp-content/uploads/2025/03/Problem_list_3082.pdf))

Let Σ_g be a surface of genus g ≥ 1. Does there exist an element f in the identity component Diff_0^∞(Σ_g) of the C^∞ diffeomorphism group such that its stable commutator length scl(f), defined by scl(f) = lim_{n→∞} cl(f^n)/n where cl is commutator length, is zero, but f is not a single commutator [a,b] = aba^{-1}b^{-1}? Likewise, does such an example exist in Homeo_0(Σ_g)?

Let Σ be an oriented surface of genus at least 1, let Homeo0(Σ) denote the identity component of its homeomorphism group, let π: Σ̃ → Σ be the universal cover, choose a fundamental domain D ⊂ Σ̃ for the deck action and a deck-invariant lift of a compatible metric on Σ, and for f ∈ Homeo0(Σ) let tilde f be the lift of f associated to an isotopy from the identity (equivalently, the lift commuting with deck transformations). If lim_{n→∞} diameter(tilde f^n(D))/n = 0, must f be a distorted element of Homeo0(Σ), i.e. must there exist a finitely generated subgroup H ≤ Homeo0(Σ) containing f such that the word length of f^n in H is o(n)?

Let f ∈ Homeo_0(T^2), where T^2 = ℝ^2/ℤ^2, and let f̃: ℝ^2 → ℝ^2 be a lift. Fix a fundamental domain D ⊂ ℝ^2 for the covering ℝ^2 → T^2 and a deck-invariant lift to ℝ^2 of a compatible metric on T^2. Assume that f is non-spreading in the sense that lim_{n→∞} diam(f̃^n(D))/n = 0. Must there exist a torus rotation R_α(x) = x + α mod ℤ^2 such that R_α belongs to the C^0-closure of the conjugacy class of f in Homeo_0(T^2), equivalently, such that for every ε > 0 there is h ∈ Homeo_0(T^2) with d_{C^0}(hfh^{-1}, R_α) < ε?

For each regularity r >= 1 (and also for r = omega, meaning the real-analytic case), let G^r be the group of germs at 0 of C^r diffeomorphisms of R fixing 0. Which elements g in G^r are distorted; that is, which germs g belong to some finitely generated subgroup H <= G^r such that, for a finite generating set S of H, the word lengths satisfy lim_{n->infinity} l_S(g^n)/n = 0?

In the setting of a real-analytic (C^ω) codimension-1 foliation with an exceptional minimal set—so that an extremal leaf, i.e. a leaf through an endpoint of an interval component of the complement in a transversal section, has infinitely many ends—can one generalize the theory developed for finitely generated analytic groups of circle diffeomorphisms with Cantor minimal sets (and its extensions to analytic actions of groups with infinitely many ends) to this foliated setting? In particular, can such a generalization be used to establish the Dippolito conjecture for codimension-1 real-analytic foliations?

Let χ_Q ∈ H^2(BDiff_+^ω(S^1)_δ; ℚ) denote the universal Euler class of flat real-analytic S^1-bundles with rational coefficients, where Diff_+^ω(S^1)_δ is the orientation-preserving real-analytic diffeomorphism group of S^1 endowed with the discrete topology. Is the k-fold cup power χ_Q^k nonzero in H^{2k}(BDiff_+^ω(S^1)_δ; ℚ) for every integer k ≥ 2?

Let G_1:=PSL(2,ℝ)=SL(2,ℝ)/{±I}. For each integer n≥1, let p_n:G_n→G_1 be the n-fold cyclic covering, let R_1⊂G_1 be the subgroup of rotations, and set R_n:=p_n^{-1}(R_1). After fixing identifications R_n≅R:=ℝ/ℤ for all n, define G(n):=G_1 *_R G_2 *_R ··· *_R G_n, the free product of G_i (1≤i≤n) with the subgroups R_i amalgamated through these identifications, and let G:=colim_n G(n) under the natural inclusions G(n)↪G(n+1). Via the standard lifted real-analytic actions of the groups G_n on S^1, regard G as a subgroup of Diff^ω(S^1)_0, the identity component of the real-analytic diffeomorphism group of the circle. Is G dense in Diff^ω(S^1)_0 with respect to the usual C^ω topology?

For positive integers k and l, let G_1 = PSL(2,R) = SL(2,R)/Z_2, let p_n: G_n -> G_1 be the n-fold cyclic covering, let R_1 < G_1 be the rotation subgroup, and let R_n = p_n^{-1}(R_1), with the fixed identifications R_n ~= SO(2) ~= R/Z from Section 8.4. Writing PSL(2)^(n) for the corresponding subgroup G_n < Diff^ω(S^1), is the subgroup <PSL(2)^(k), PSL(2)^(l)> inside Diff^ω(S^1) isomorphic to the amalgamated free product PSL(2)^(k) *_{SO(2)} PSL(2)^(l)?

For each integer q \ge 0, in the smooth C^\infty Haefliger setting, let B\Gamma_q be Haefliger’s classifying space of codimension-q \Gamma_q-structures, and let B\overline{\Gamma}_q denote the fibre of the normal-bundle map B\Gamma_q \to BO(q) (equivalently, the classifying space of codimension-q Haefliger structures with trivial normal bundle). Is B\overline{\Gamma}_q 2q-connected; that is, does \pi_i(B\overline{\Gamma}_q)=0 for every 0 \le i \le 2q?

For a fixed integer q\ge 1, in the smooth (C^\infty) category, let \gamma be the codimension-q Haefliger \overline{\Gamma}_q-structure on SO(q) with trivial normal bundle SO(q)\times\mathbb{R}^q whose microfoliation is the suspension of the standard linear action of SO(q) on \mathbb{R}^q. Is the associated classifying map SO(q)\to B\overline{\Gamma}_q null-homotopic? ([conferences.cirm-math.fr](https://conferences.cirm-math.fr/wp-content/uploads/2025/03/Problem_list_3082.pdf))

For each integer q ≥ 1, let Γ_q^+ be the groupoid of germs of orientation-preserving local C^∞ diffeomorphisms of R^q, and let Γ_q^0 ⊂ Γ_q^+ be the isotropy subgroup fixing 0. Is the inclusion-induced classifying map BΓ_q^0 → BΓ_q^+ null-homotopic; equivalently, is BΓ_q^0 homotopically trivial inside BΓ_q^+?

Let M be a piecewise linear manifold. Is PL_0(M), the group of piecewise linear homeomorphisms of M that are isotopic to the identity, simple as an abstract group? ([conferences.cirm-math.fr](https://conferences.cirm-math.fr/wp-content/uploads/2025/03/Problem_list_3082.pdf))

Let BΓ_n^{PL} denote the classifying space of codimension-n piecewise-linear Haefliger structures. Is BΓ_n^{PL} (n+1)-connected? ([conferences.cirm-math.fr](https://conferences.cirm-math.fr/wp-content/uploads/2025/03/Problem_list_3082.pdf))

Fix a PL manifold M and a prime p. Let PL(M)^δ denote the group of PL homeomorphisms of M equipped with the discrete topology, and let BPL(M)^δ -> BPL(M) be the map induced by the identity homomorphism PL(M)^δ -> PL(M). Is the induced map on homology H_*(BPL(M)^δ; F_p) -> H_*(BPL(M); F_p) an isomorphism in every degree * >= 0? ([conferences.cirm-math.fr](https://conferences.cirm-math.fr/wp-content/uploads/2025/03/Problem_list_3082.pdf))

Let \(B\bar\Gamma_1^\infty\) and \(B\bar\Gamma_1^\omega\) denote the smooth and real-analytic codimension-one Haefliger classifying spaces, and let \(\Gamma_H\) be the discrete Haefliger group with \(B\bar\Gamma_1^\omega\simeq K(\Gamma_H,1)\). The preceding discussion records two split Godbillon-Vey surjections, one on \(\pi_1(B\bar\Gamma_1^\infty)\) and one on \(H_3(B\Gamma_H;\mathbb Z)\), yielding decompositions \(\pi_1(B\bar\Gamma_1^\infty)\cong \mathbb R\oplus \ker(GV)\) and \(H_3(B\Gamma_H;\mathbb Z)\cong \mathbb R\oplus \ker(GV)\). Are the two kernels \(\ker(GV:\pi_1(B\bar\Gamma_1^\infty)\to\mathbb R)\) and \(\ker(GV:H_3(B\Gamma_H;\mathbb Z)\to\mathbb R)\) trivial? ([conferences.cirm-math.fr](https://conferences.cirm-math.fr/wp-content/uploads/2025/03/Problem_list_3082.pdf))
Let Γ_H := π₁(BΓ_1^ω), the Haefliger group, where Haefliger proved that BΓ_1^ω is a K(π,1). Is Γ_H simple as a discrete group?

For the weighted Riesz energy I_{s,V}(μ)=∬(K_s(x−y)+V(x)+V(y)) dμ(x)dμ(y) on probability measures μ∈P(R^d), where −2 < s < d, K_s(x)=∥x∥^(−s)/s for s≠0 and K_0(x)=−log(∥x∥), and the external field is radial of the form V(x)=v(∥x∥^2) with v:[0,∞)→(−∞,+∞] lower semicontinuous, bounded from below, and finite on some interval, what can be said about the equilibrium measure μ_eq, when it exists, in the regime d−3 < s < d? In particular, how should one characterize the support of μ_eq in this s-range—e.g. whether it is a sphere, a ball, or more generally lower-dimensional versus full-dimensional—and what is the corresponding minimizing measure in each case?

Consider the full-space Riesz equilibrium problem on R^d, d >= 2, with kernel K_s(x) = 1/(s ||x||^s) for s != 0 and K_0(x) = -log ||x||, and with power-law radial external field V(x) = (gamma/alpha) ||x||^alpha, where gamma > 0, -2 < s < d, and alpha > max{-s,0}. Let mu_eq be the equilibrium measure minimizing I_{s,V}(mu) = ∬(K_s(x-y) + V(x) + V(y)) dmu(x) dmu(y) over probability measures on R^d. After the sharp classification of the spherical-support regime given in Theorem 1.1 of this section (equivalently, [1, Theorem 1.3]), determine for which parameter choices (d,s,alpha) the support supp(mu_eq) has a full-dimensional component in R^d, and for which parameter choices supp(mu_eq) is supported on a set of dimension strictly smaller than d. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2504.04845))

Fix d >= 2 and -2 < s < d - 3. Let K_s(x) = 1/(s ||x||^s) for s != 0 and K_0(x) = -log ||x||, and consider the weighted Riesz energy I_{s,V}(mu) = ∬ (K_s(x-y) + V(x) + V(y)) dmu(x) dmu(y) over probability measures mu on R^d, with power-law external field V(x) = (gamma/alpha) ||x||^alpha for gamma > 0 and alpha > max{-s,0}. Define c_{s,d} = 2F1(s/2, (2+s-d)/2; d/2; 1), and when s = 0 define b_d = -log 2 + (1/4) 3F2(1,1,(d+1)/2; 2,d; 1). Let alpha_{s,d} = max{ s c_{s,d}/(2 - 2 c_{s,d}), 2 - (s+2)(d-s-4)/(2(d-s-3)) } for s != 0, and alpha_{0,d} = max{ -1/(2 b_d), 2 - (d-4)/(d-3) }. Since Theorem 1.3 shows that if alpha >= alpha_{s,d} then the equilibrium measure is the uniform measure sigma_{R_*} on a sphere, while if max{-s,0} < alpha < alpha_{s,d} no spherical-shell measure sigma_R minimizes I_{s,V}, characterize the equilibrium measure mu_eq in this subthreshold regime.

Establish or refute the following conjecture for the discrete minimal Riesz 2-energy on the unit sphere S^2 ⊂ R^3 with respect to the Euclidean distance: if
E_2(S^2; N) := min_{x_1,...,x_N ∈ S^2} Σ_{i≠j} 1/||x_i - x_j||^2,
then, as N → ∞,
E_2(S^2; N) = (1/4) N^2 log N + C_{2,2} N^2 + o(N^2),
where
C_{2,2} = (1/4)(γ - log(2√(3π))) + (√3/(4π))(γ_1(2/3) - γ_1(1/3)),
and γ_1(a) denotes the generalized Stieltjes constant appearing in the Laurent expansion of the Hurwitz zeta function ζ(s,a) at s = 1.

On the unit sphere S^2 with Euclidean distance, let E_log(S^2;N)=min_{x_1,...,x_N∈S^2} Σ_{i≠j} log(1/|x_i-x_j|) and E_2(S^2;N)=min_{x_1,...,x_N∈S^2} Σ_{i≠j} |x_i-x_j|^{-2}. Given the Brauchart-Hardin-Saff logarithmic-side constant C_BHS and the conjectured Riesz-2 asymptotic E_2(S^2;N)=(1/4)N^2 log N + C_{2,2}N^2 + o(N^2) as N→∞, for which Theorem 2.1 proves C_BHS - 2C_{2,2} = log 2 - γ, can one establish any further explicit relations between coefficients appearing in the large-N asymptotic expansions of minimal discrete energies for different kernels on the sphere?

For the discrete minimal energies E_log(S^2; N) := min_{x_1,...,x_N∈S^2} ∑_{i≠j} log(1/||x_i-x_j||) and E_2(S^2; N) := min_{x_1,...,x_N∈S^2} ∑_{i≠j} ||x_i-x_j||^(-2) on the unit sphere S^2 ⊂ R^3 with Euclidean distance, is there a resummation method more efficient than the current approach based on expanding log(1/||x-y||) as a power series in the inner product ⟨x,y⟩, one that yields sharper lower bounds for E_log(S^2; N) and/or sharper asymptotic information compatible with the conjectured expansion E_2(S^2; N) = (1/4)N^2 log N + C_{2,2}N^2 + o(N^2) as N → ∞?

For the discrete minimal logarithmic energy E_log(S^d;N) = min_{x_1,...,x_N ∈ S^d} Σ_{i ≠ j} log(1/||x_i-x_j||) and the discrete minimal Riesz energy E_s(S^d;N) = min_{x_1,...,x_N ∈ S^d} Σ_{i ≠ j} ||x_i-x_j||^(−s), with s > 0, on the unit sphere S^d ⊂ R^(d+1) and in the asymptotic regime N → ∞, is there a method that can replace the current expansion of the kernel in powers of the inner product ⟨x,y⟩ and still be effective for studying lower bounds or asymptotic expansions of these energies? ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2504.04845))

Let Q^d ⊂ R^d be the d-dimensional hypercube, let K_s be the Riesz s-kernel, and let μ_eq be a Borel probability measure on Q^d minimizing the unweighted Riesz s-energy I_s(μ)=∫∫_{Q^d×Q^d} K_s(x,y) dμ(x) dμ(y). In the hypercube case, it is known that for an integer q with -2 < s ≤ q - 2, the support supp(μ_eq) is contained in the union of the (q - 1)-dimensional faces of Q^d, and hence one has the bound s ≤ dim(supp(μ_eq)) ≤ q - 1. Can one improve the lower bound s in this dimension estimate? ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2504.04845))

Let Q^d be a hypercube in R^d, let s < d, and let mu_eq be a probability measure on Q^d minimizing the Riesz s-energy I_s(mu) = double integral over Q^d x Q^d of K_s(x,y) dmu(x) dmu(y), where K_s(x,y) = |x-y|^{-s}/s for s != 0 and K_0(x,y) = -log|x-y|. In the regime -2 < s <= q - 2 for some q in {1, ..., d}, where existing results imply that supp(mu_eq) is contained in the union of the (q-1)-dimensional faces of Q^d and hence satisfies s <= dim(supp(mu_eq)) <= q - 1, determine more precise structural information about supp(mu_eq) than its dimension alone.

Let C be a compact convex body in R^d, let s < d, and let mu_eq minimize the Riesz s-energy I_s(mu) = ∬_{C×C} |x-y|^{-s} dmu(x) dmu(y) over probability measures mu on C. In Section 3, the paper notes that for the hypercube Q^d the support of mu_eq can collapse onto lower-dimensional faces (in particular, onto the vertices when -2 < s ≤ -1), and that the same type of face-support formulation can be made for convex polytopes. Can analogous support-concentration results be proved for a larger class of convex bodies with lower-dimensional faces beyond polytopes, for example for the Reuleaux triangle?

For every positive integer d and every real p>2 with p∉2N, let P(S^{d-1}) be the Borel probability measures on the real unit sphere S^{d-1}⊂R^d, and define F(t)=|t|^p and I_F(μ)=∫_{S^{d-1}}∫_{S^{d-1}}|⟨x,y⟩|^p dμ(x)dμ(y). If μ∈P(S^{d-1}) is a global minimizer of I_F over P(S^{d-1}), must μ be a discrete measure? ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2504.04845))

Let d >= 2, let kappa:[-1,1] -> R have Gegenbauer expansion kappa(t) = sum_{ell>=0} c_ell C_ell^{((d-2)/2)}(t), and consider the energy I_kappa(mu) = ∬_{S^{d-1} x S^{d-1}} kappa(<x,y>) dmu(x) dmu(y) over Borel probability measures mu on S^{d-1}. Assume that kappa has a negative Gegenbauer coefficient in some sufficiently high degree, namely c_ell < 0 for some large ell > N. If I_kappa admits a discrete minimizing measure mu, what bounds or structural restrictions can one prove for the cardinality of supp(mu)?

For alpha > 0, let T^2 = R^2/Z^2 be the flat torus equipped with the quotient Euclidean metric rho(x,y) = min_{k in Z^2} ||x - y + k||, and for each Borel probability measure mu on T^2 define I_alpha(mu) = \iint_{T^2 x T^2} rho(x,y)^alpha dmu(x)dmu(y). Knowing that the Haar probability measure sigma maximizes I_alpha at alpha = 1, and that at alpha = 2 every maximizer is of the form (1/2)(delta_p + delta_{p*}) with p* = p + (1/2,1/2) mod Z^2, determine all phase transition values of alpha (in particular, all alpha in (1,2)) at which the maximizing regime for I_alpha on T^2 changes.

Fix a sphere or projective space Ω of dimension d, endowed with a fixed distance ρ equivalent to the geodesic distance, and let σ be the uniform probability measure on Ω. For 0 < s < d, define the Riesz s-energy of a probability measure μ on Ω by I_s(μ)=∫_Ω∫_Ω ρ(x,y)^(-s) dμ(x)dμ(y). If σ minimizes I_{s*} for some s* in (0,d), must σ also minimize I_s for every s with s* < s < d?

Fix r and n, let P_n^r denote the space of spherical polynomials on S^r of degree at most n, and set N = dim P_n^r. If X_N = {x_1,\ldots,x_N} \subset S^r is a random fundamental system of N points on the sphere—for example, N uniform i.i.d. points or N points drawn from a determinantal point process—and if {\ell_i}_{i=1}^N \subset P_n^r is the associated Lagrange basis satisfying \ell_i(x_j)=\delta_{ij}, with interpolation weights w_i = \int_{S^r} \ell_i(x)\,d\sigma(x), can one quantify the quality of the random configuration in terms of whether the weights w_i are positive, or in terms of how close they are to the uniform value 1/N?

Let P_n denote the real algebraic polynomials of degree at most n. For a nonnegative majorant μ:[-1,1]→[0,∞) and an integer n≥1, assume there exists a nonzero polynomial p∈P_n such that |p(x)|≤μ(x) on [-1,1], and let ω_{μ,n}∈P_n be the corresponding n-th snake polynomial, unique up to sign, characterized by |ω_{μ,n}(x)|≤μ(x) on [-1,1] and by the existence of alternation points τ_0^*>⋯>τ_n^* in [-1,1] with ω_{μ,n}(τ_i^*)=(-1)^i μ(τ_i^*). Determine classes of such majorants μ for which, for every n for which ω_{μ,n} exists, one can choose the orientation of ω_{μ,n} so that its Chebyshev expansion of the first kind, ω_{μ,n}(x)=Σ_{j=0}^n a_j T_j(x), has either a_j≥0 for all j or (-1)^j a_j≥0 for all j.

For every n in N, let P_n be the real algebraic polynomials of degree at most n, and let mu in C[-1,1] satisfy mu(x) >= 0, mu(-x) = mu(x), and convexity on [-1,1]. Assume there exists a nonzero polynomial P in P_n such that -mu(x) <= P(x) <= mu(x) for all x in [-1,1], and let omega_{mu,n} in P_n denote the n-th snake polynomial associated with mu, normalized by the alternation condition omega_{mu,n}(tau_i^*) = (-1)^i mu(tau_i^*) at some points 1 >= tau_0^* > tau_1^* > ... > tau_n^* >= -1 and by |omega_{mu,n}(x)| <= mu(x) on [-1,1]. Must omega_{mu,n} always admit a first-kind Chebyshev expansion omega_{mu,n}(x) = sum_{j=0}^n a_j T_j(x) with all coefficients a_j >= 0?

For a fixed radius R > \sqrt{5}/2, let \chi(S^{d-1}(R)) denote the chromatic number of the Euclidean sphere S^{d-1}(R) \subset \mathbb{R}^d with forbidden Euclidean distance 1. In Prosanov's three-step construction underlying Theorem 8.1, Step 1 fixes an angle 0 < \varphi(R) < \pi/4, chooses a maximal set X \subset S^{d-1}(R) such that the spherical caps C(x,\varphi) are pairwise disjoint, and uses the Voronoi tiling \Psi induced by X; Steps 2 and 3 then shrink the cells of \Psi by a factor \lambda(R) and cover S^{d-1}(R) by copies of the resulting set. Is there another choice of initial configuration in Step 1 that would yield, for d \to \infty, a strictly better upper bound than Prosanov's current asymptotic upper bound for \chi(S^{d-1}(R))?

For every integer n >= 1, can one find many nice/simple explicit constructions of real n x n matrices A_n in {-1,1}^{n x n} such that there exist absolute constants 0 < c <= C < infinity, independent of n, with c sqrt(n) ||x||_2 <= ||A_n x||_2 <= C sqrt(n) ||x||_2 for all x in R^n, and with a provably small absolute upper bound on the ratio C/c?

Conjecture (Matrix Spencer). Does there exist a positive universal constant C such that, for every positive integer n and every choice of n self-adjoint real n×n matrices A1,...,An satisfying ||Ai|| <= 1 for all i in [n], where ||·|| denotes the spectral norm, one has min_{epsilon in {±1}^n} ||sum_{i=1}^n epsilon_i Ai|| <= C sqrt(n)? ([anmaillard.github.io](https://anmaillard.github.io/assets/pdf/publications/bandeira2025randomstrasse.pdf))

Does there exist a positive universal constant C such that for every finite group G of order n, if A_1, ..., A_n are the n x n matrices corresponding to the regular representation of G (one for each group element), then one can choose signs epsilon_1, ..., epsilon_n in {+1,-1} so that ||sum_{i=1}^n epsilon_i A_i|| <= C sqrt(n), where ||.|| denotes the spectral norm?

For each even n, let G_n be a uniformly random 3-regular graph on n vertices, let A be its adjacency matrix, and define the Kuramoto energy on phase vectors theta in [0, 2pi)^n by E(theta) = (1/2) sum_{i,j=1}^n A_ij (1 - cos(theta_i - theta_j)). Say that G_n is globally synchronizing if the only local minima of E are the global minima corresponding to constant phases, i.e. theta_i = c for all i. Is it true that P(G_n is globally synchronizing) -> 1 as n -> infinity?

For every fixed \(\varepsilon>0\), let \((\delta_n)_{n\ge1}\) satisfy \(\delta_n \ge (1+\varepsilon)\sqrt{\frac{\log n}{2n}}\). For each n, let \(A^{(n)}\) be the random symmetric matrix in \(\mathbb{R}^{n\times n}\) with \(A^{(n)}_{ii}=0\) and, independently for \(1\le i<j\le n\), \(A^{(n)}_{ij}=A^{(n)}_{ji}=+1\) with probability \(\frac12+\delta_n\) and \(-1\) with probability \(\frac12-\delta_n\). Is it true that, with probability tending to 1 as \(n\to\infty\), every local minimum \(\theta\in[0,2\pi)^n\) of
\[E_n(\theta)=\frac12\sum_{i,j=1}^n A^{(n)}_{ij}\bigl(1-\cos(\theta_i-\theta_j)\bigr)\]
is a constant-phase configuration, i.e. \(\theta_1=\cdots=\theta_n\) modulo \(2\pi\)?

Is the following density-threshold conjecture for Kuramoto global synchrony true? For every ε > 0, does there exist a positive integer n and an n-vertex graph G with adjacency matrix A and minimum degree δ(G) ≥ (3/4 - ε)n such that the Kuramoto energy E(θ) = (1/2) ∑_{i,j=1}^n A_{ij}(1 - cos(θ_i - θ_j)) on phase configurations θ ∈ [0, 2π)^n has a local minimum that is not a global constant-phase minimum θ1 = ··· = θn = c?

Let d → ∞ and let n = n(d) be a sequence of integers with n,d ≥ 1. Let x_1, …, x_n be i.i.d. random vectors in ℝ^d with law N(0, I_d/d). Say that (x_i)_{i=1}^n admits an origin-centered ellipsoid fit if there exists an ellipsoid E ⊂ ℝ^d centered at the origin whose boundary contains every x_i. Is it true that, for every ε > 0, one has

(1) if limsup_{d→∞} n(d)/d^2 ≤ (1−ε)/4, then lim_{d→∞} P[there exists an origin-centered ellipsoid fit to (x_i)_{i=1}^n] = 1;

and

(2) if liminf_{d→∞} n(d)/d^2 ≥ (1+ε)/4, then lim_{d→∞} P[there exists an origin-centered ellipsoid fit to (x_i)_{i=1}^n] = 0?

In other words, does exact centered ellipsoid fitting for i.i.d. N(0, I_d/d) points undergo a sharp satisfiability threshold at n/d^2 = 1/4?

Consider the dense multi-frequency synchronization model with all pairwise measurements and additive Gaussian noise. In the SO(2) ≅ U(1) case, let x = (x_1,...,x_n) be sampled uniformly from U(1)^n and observe L channels Y_ℓ = (λ/n)x^(ℓ)(x^(ℓ))* + (1/√n)W^(ℓ), for ℓ = 1,...,L, where x^(ℓ) = (x_1^ℓ,...,x_n^ℓ) and W^(1),...,W^(L) are independent noise matrices; more generally, consider the analogous multi-frequency synchronization model over a finite group, with channels indexed by irreducible representations and the signal sampled uniformly over group elements. Find a scaling L = L_n of the number of frequencies for which there exists a polynomial-time algorithm that reliably detects the signal for every λ > λ_comp,L, for some computational threshold λ_comp,L < 1, as n → ∞. ([anmaillard.github.io](https://anmaillard.github.io/assets/pdf/publications/bandeira2025randomstrasse.pdf))

Fix either G = SO(2) (equivalently U(1)) or a fixed finite group G. Consider the dense multi-frequency synchronization model from Entry 4, where measurements are available for every pair (j, k) and, for a fixed collection Ψ of L frequency/representation channels with L independent of n, the planted observation is Y_kj^ρ = (λ/n)ρ(g_k)ρ(g_j^(-1)) + n^(-1/2)W_kj^(ρ) for ρ in Ψ (in the SO(2) case, equivalently, Y_ell = (λ/n)x^(ell)(x^(ell))* + n^(-1/2)W^(ell) for ell = 1,...,L), with g = (g_1,...,g_n) sampled uniformly from G^n and Gaussian noise W. For every fixed signal-to-noise ratio λ in the computationally hard regime λ ∈ (λ_stat, 1), where λ_stat is the statistical detection threshold and 1 is the spectral threshold, does there exist a possibly λ-dependent algorithm running in time exp(n^δ) for some δ < 1 that distinguishes the planted model from the corresponding null all-noise model with error probability o(1) as n → ∞?

Let r and ℓ be fixed positive integers with r even and ℓ ≥ r/2, and for each n ≫ ℓ let M^{(n)}(λ) be the real symmetric matrix of size (n choose ℓ) × (n choose ℓ), indexed by ℓ-subsets I, J ⊂ [n], defined by M^{(n)}(λ)_{I,J} = λ + Z_{IΔJ} if |IΔJ| = r and M^{(n)}(λ)_{I,J} = 0 otherwise, where for each r-subset S ⊂ [n] the variables Z_S are independent N(0,1) random variables and IΔJ = (I ∪ J) \ (I ∩ J). Let λ^natural_{r,ℓ} denote the asymptotic eigenvalue pop-out threshold of this family, in the sense that for every λ > λ^natural_{r,ℓ} there exists ε > 0 such that E[λ_max(M^{(n)}(λ))] > (1 + ε + o_n(1)) E[λ_max(M^{(n)}(0))] as n → ∞. Is it true that, for each fixed even r, one has n^{r/4} λ^natural_{r,ℓ} → 0 as ℓ → ∞, with the ℓ-limit understood only after the large-n asymptotic in the definition of λ^natural_{r,ℓ}?

For each positive integer n and each real square matrix A ∈ ℝ^{n×n}, define its discrepancy by disc(A) := inf_{x∈{±1}^n} ||Ax||_∞. Suppose every column of A has Euclidean norm 1. Does there exist a universal constant K > 0, independent of n and A, such that disc(A) ≤ K for every such square matrix A?

For each positive integer n and each sign matrix A ∈ {±1}^{n×n}, define its discrepancy by disc(A) := min_{x∈{±1}^n} ||Ax||_∞, where ||·||_∞ is the usual ℓ∞-norm on R^n. What is the exact value of the extremal normalized discrepancy
sup_{n∈N} sup_{A∈{±1}^{n×n}} disc(A)/√n ?

For each positive integer n and each real sign matrix A ∈ {±1}^{n×n}, define its discrepancy by disc(A) := inf_{x∈{±1}^n} ||Ax||∞, where ||·||∞ is the usual ℓ∞-norm on ℝ^n. Is it true that limsup_{n→∞} sup_{A∈{±1}^{n×n}} n^{-1/2} disc(A) > 1?

For each k ≥ 0, let H_0 = (1) and define the Sylvester Hadamard matrices recursively by H_k = [[H_{k-1}, H_{k-1}], [H_{k-1}, -H_{k-1}]], so that H_k is a 2^k × 2^k real ±1 matrix. For an n × n real matrix A, define its discrepancy by disc(A) := inf_{x ∈ {±1}^n} ||Ax||_∞. Is it true that for every odd positive integer k, disc(H_k) = √2·√(2^k) = 2^{(k+1)/2}?

Hadamard Conjecture: For every positive integer n with 4|n, does there exist an n x n matrix H with entries in {+1,-1} whose columns are pairwise orthogonal under the standard real inner product (equivalently, (1/sqrt(n))H is an orthogonal matrix)? ([anmaillard.github.io](https://anmaillard.github.io/assets/pdf/publications/bandeira2025randomstrasse.pdf))

For the Sherrington-Kirkpatrick Ising model on {+1,-1}^n with Gibbs measure mu_{J,h}(x) proportional to exp((1/2) x^T J x + h^T x), where h in R^n is arbitrary and J = beta W with W ~ GOE(n), consider the discrete-time single-site Glauber dynamics that at each step chooses i uniformly from [n] and resamples x_i from the conditional law mu_{J,h}( . | x_{-i}). Is it true that, with probability tending to 1 over the disorder W as n -> infinity, the total-variation mixing time T_epsilon of this chain is bounded by n^{O(1)} for every fixed epsilon in (0,1) and every inverse temperature beta up to the replica-symmetry-breaking threshold beta* = 1?

Let Ψ: Σ → R^3 be a compact embedded surface of constant mean curvature whose boundary is exactly one round circle S^1 (that is, Ψ|∂Σ: ∂Σ → S^1 is a diffeomorphism). Must Ψ(Σ) be either the planar disk bounded by S^1 or a spherical cap bounded by S^1?

Let C be a planar closed curve contained in a plane P ⊂ R^3, and let Σ ⊂ R^3 be a compact embedded surface of constant mean curvature with boundary ∂Σ = C. Under what conditions on the boundary curve C must Σ be contained in one of the two closed half-spaces determined by P? In particular, what can be said when C is convex?

Let Σ ⊂ R^3 be a compact surface with constant mean curvature H and boundary ∂Σ = S^1, where S^1 is a round circle. Assume that Σ is star-shaped with respect to some point q ∈ R^3, in the sense that every ray emanating from q meets Σ at most once. Must Σ be either the planar disk bounded by S^1 or a spherical cap bounded by S^1?

Let C⊂P⊂R^3 be a simple closed convex curve in a plane P, and let Σ⊂R^3 be a compact embedded surface of constant mean curvature with boundary ∂Σ=C. Assume that Σ\C is contained in one of the two open half-spaces determined by P. Must Σ be homeomorphic to the closed disk?

Let C be a simple closed convex curve contained in a plane P subset R^3, let D subset P be the planar domain bounded by C, and let Sigma subset R^3 be a compact embedded constant-mean-curvature surface with ∂Sigma = C that lies entirely on one side of P. Assume moreover that, in a neighborhood of C, Sigma is a graph over the exterior planar region P \ D. Is Sigma necessarily a bigraph in the following sense: does there exist a planar domain Omega subset P with D subset Omega such that Sigma = Sigma_1 union Sigma_2, where Sigma_1 is a graph over D and Sigma_2 is a topological annulus that is a graph over Omega \ D?

Let C_1,C_2 subset R^3 be two closed convex Jordan curves lying in distinct parallel planes. If Sigma subset R^3 is a compact connected embedded surface of constant mean curvature H, for some constant H in R, with boundary partial Sigma = C_1 union C_2, must Sigma be homeomorphic to an annulus?

Let C1, C2 ⊂ R^3 be two coaxial circles lying in parallel planes, and let Σ ⊂ R^3 be a compact embedded surface of constant mean curvature with boundary ∂Σ = C1 ∪ C2. Must Σ be a surface of revolution about the common axis of C1 and C2?

Let Sigma be a compact immersed constant-mean-curvature surface in Euclidean three-space R^3, topologically a disk, whose boundary is mapped diffeomorphically onto a round circle S^1(r). Must Sigma necessarily be either the planar disk bounded by S^1(r) or a spherical cap spanning S^1(r)?

Let Ψ: Σ → R^3 be an isometric immersion of a compact surface with non-empty boundary such that Ψ(Σ) has constant mean curvature and Ψ|∂Σ: ∂Σ → S^1 is a diffeomorphism onto a round circle S^1 ⊂ R^3. If Ψ(Σ) is stable, meaning that the second variation of area is non-negative for every volume-preserving variation that fixes the boundary, must Ψ(Σ) be either the planar disk bounded by S^1 or a spherical cap bounded by S^1?

Can one produce numerical pictures of the specific compact constant-mean-curvature surfaces in Euclidean three-space R^3 constructed by Kapouleas that span a round circle S^1 as boundary, namely the self-intersecting high-genus (g>2) examples lying in one of the half-spaces determined by the boundary plane?

Let Sigma be a compact embedded surface in R^3 with constant mean curvature H and boundary equal to a single round circle S^1(r). Assume Sigma is stable for the area functional under volume-preserving variations that fix the boundary; equivalently, for every u in C^2(Sigma) with u|_{partial Sigma} = 0 and integral_Sigma u dSigma = 0, one has integral_Sigma u (Delta u + |sigma|^2 u) dSigma <= 0. Must Sigma necessarily be one of the umbilical examples spanning S^1(r), namely the planar disk (if H = 0) or a spherical cap (if H != 0)?

Let Σ ⊂ R^3 be a compact embedded surface of constant mean curvature, homeomorphic to the closed 2-disk, such that its boundary ∂Σ is a round circle. Must Σ be either the planar disk bounded by ∂Σ or a spherical cap with boundary ∂Σ? ([digibug.ugr.es](https://digibug.ugr.es/bitstream/handle/10481/110069/conm16439-offprints.pdf?isAllowed=y&sequence=1))

Let C ⊂ P ⊂ R^3 be a simple closed planar curve of length L, and let D ⊂ P be the bounded domain enclosed by C. Is it true that for every H ∈ [0, L/(2|D|)] there exists a compact connected immersed surface Σ ⊂ R^3 of constant mean curvature H whose boundary is C (equivalently, the boundary map is a diffeomorphism from ∂Σ onto C)?
