Let C be a simple closed curve contained in a plane P \subset R^3, let L be the length of C, and let D \subset P be the bounded planar domain enclosed by C. Without imposing any a priori embeddedness or disk-topology assumption, does there exist a compact immersed constant-mean-curvature surface Sigma \subset R^3 whose boundary maps diffeomorphically onto C and whose mean curvature is the extremal value H = L/(2|D|)? If such a surface exists, what geometric rigidity can be deduced for Sigma at this equality case?

In Euclidean 3-space R^3, let S_w be a slab, meaning the region between two parallel planes at distance w > 0. For every nonzero real number H and every closed curve C ⊂ S_w with |H| < 2/w, does there exist a compact immersed surface Σ ⊂ S_w of constant mean curvature H, homeomorphic to a closed disk, such that Σ has boundary C in the paper’s sense, namely that the boundary map ∂Σ → C is a diffeomorphism?

In R^3, let S_w be a slab of width w > 0, and let Σ be a compact immersed surface of constant mean curvature H ≠ 0 whose boundary maps diffeomorphically onto a round circle S^1(r). If Σ is contained in S_w and |H| < 2/w, must Σ be a spherical cap? More sharply, if one strengthens the bound to |H| < 1/w, must Σ be the small spherical cap bounded by S^1(r), i.e. the smaller of the two spherical caps cut from the sphere of radius 1/|H| by the plane of the boundary circle?

Let H ∈ ℝ with H ≠ 0. If Σ ⊂ ℝ^3 is a closed surface (that is, compact and without boundary) of constant mean curvature H, and Σ is contained in the closure of a slab bounded by two parallel planes at distance 2/|H|, must Σ be the sphere of radius 1/H?

Let Psi: Sigma -> R^3 be an isometric immersion of a compact surface with nonempty boundary and constant mean curvature, and assume that Psi|_{∂Sigma}: ∂Sigma -> C is a diffeomorphism onto a simple closed convex curve C contained in a plane P. Let D subset P be the bounded domain enclosed by C. After a rigid motion sending P to a horizontal plane, assume that Psi(Sigma) is contained in the vertical cylinder D x R over D. Without any further hypotheses such as embeddedness or disk-type, must Psi(Sigma) be a single-valued graph over D with respect to orthogonal projection onto P?

Let C⊂R^3 be a smooth closed convex planar curve that is not a round circle, and let P be the plane containing C. Does there exist a constant V_C>0, depending only on C, such that every compact embedded constant-mean-curvature topological disk Σ⊂R^3 with boundary C and prescribed volume V>0 satisfies the following trichotomy: (i) if V≤V_C, then Σ is contained in one of the two closed half-spaces determined by P; (ii) if V=V_C, then Σ is tangent to P at the points of C where the curvature of C is minimal; and (iii) if V>V_C, then Σ meets both open half-spaces determined by P? ([digibug.ugr.es](https://digibug.ugr.es/bitstream/handle/10481/110069/conm16439-offprints.pdf?isAllowed=y&sequence=1))

Let C_1, C_2 ⊂ R^2 ⊂ R^3 be two simple closed convex planar curves whose bounded planar interiors are disjoint. Does there exist a constant V_0 = V_0(C_1, C_2) > 0 such that, whenever Σ ⊂ R^3 is a compact constant-mean-curvature surface having boundary C_1 ∪ C_2 and volume V < V_0, the surface Σ is not connected?

Let Ω⊂R² be a bounded convex domain, let H∈R be constant, let |Ω| denote the Euclidean area of Ω, L the Euclidean length of ∂Ω, and diam(Ω) its Euclidean diameter. Consider the classical Dirichlet problem div(Du/√(1+|Du|²)) = 2H in Ω, u = 0 on ∂Ω, for a classical solution u that is C² on Ω and continuous on Ω̄. Determine, separately for each of the three hypotheses (i) |Ω|H² < π, (ii) L|H| < 2π, and (iii) diam(Ω) < 2/|H|, whether the problem is solvable; uniqueness is already known whenever a solution exists.

Let Omega be a bounded convex domain in R^2, let H be a real constant, and let u solve the zero-boundary constant-mean-curvature Dirichlet problem div(Du/sqrt(1+|Du|^2)) = 2H in Omega, u = 0 on partial Omega. Give a control, in terms of H, of how the convex members of the level-set family {u = t} are distributed. Moreover, can one extend Wang's counterexample—namely, a constant-mean-curvature graph over a convex domain whose level curves are not all convex—to the case of a nonbounded convex domain Omega (necessarily in the solvable regime, e.g. Omega contained in a strip of width 1/|H|)?

Let Ω ⊂ R^2 be a bounded convex domain, let H ∈ R, and let u ∈ C^2(Ω) ∩ C^0(closed Ω) solve the constant-mean-curvature Dirichlet problem div(Du/sqrt(1+|Du|^2)) = 2H in Ω with u = 0 on ∂Ω. For the graph Σ = {(x,y,u(x,y)) : (x,y) ∈ Ω} ⊂ R^3, find sufficient conditions under which Σ is convex in the sense of the paper, namely that its Gauss curvature K is positive at every point of Σ.

Let m,n be positive integers, let G = F_m x Z^n, and let G act geometrically on X = T_{2m} x R^n by the standard product action, where T_{2m} is the 2m-regular Cayley tree of F_m and Z^n acts on R^n by translations. If H <= G is quasiconvex with respect to this action, must H act cocompactly on the convex hull in X of an H-orbit Hx_0 (equivalently, is H convex with respect to this action)?

Let G act geometrically on a CAT(0) space X, and let H ≤ G be a subgroup that is quasiconvex with respect to this action (equivalently, some H-orbit in X is a quasiconvex subset of X). Must H itself be a CAT(0) group?

Conjecture. For every virtually polycyclic group P and every subgroup H ≤ P, does H have the bounded packing property in P? Equivalently: for every proper left-invariant metric d on P and every r > 0, does there exist N = N(P,H,r) such that any collection of N distinct left H-cosets in P contains two cosets gH and g'H with d(gH,g'H) ≥ r, where d(gH,g'H) := inf{d(x,y) : x ∈ gH, y ∈ g'H}?

Let P_{n,φ} = ℤ^n ⋊_φ ℤ, where φ ∈ Aut(ℤ^n) is diagonalizable and all eigenvalues of φ are real. Does every subgroup H ≤ P_{n,φ} have bounded packing in P_{n,φ}; that is, for every r > 0, is there an N = N(P_{n,φ}, H, r) such that any collection of N distinct left cosets of H contains two cosets whose distance is at least r (equivalently, not all pairwise distances are < r), with respect to any proper left-invariant metric on P_{n,φ}?

In the phase-retrieval model I = A(f) = |Af|^2, with Section 3 focused on standard coherent diffraction imaging (A = F) and ptychography (A given by a subsampled short-time Fourier transform matrix), can one estimate the intrinsic difficulty of recovering an unknown complex-valued object f from the measured intensities alone, prior to reconstruction? More concretely, in the standard CDI formulation I = |Ff|^2 with autocorrelation gamma = F^{-1} I on a rectangular D-dimensional grid G, can one identify or justify measurement-only complexity statistics that predict phase-retrieval difficulty, such as the overdetermination ratio Omega = (1/2)|S_f - S_f|/|S_f| with S_f = {r in G : f(r) != 0}, a weighted generalization of Omega that accounts for |f(r)|, or the normalized second-order moment B = (int ||r||^2 |gamma(r)|^2 dr)/(int |gamma(r)|^2 dr) (equivalently B = (int ||grad I(q)||^2 dq)/(int |I(q)|^2 dq))?

In the phase retrieval setting I = A(f) = |Af|^2 for complex-valued objects f (either f:R^d→C or f∈C^n), with primary focus on coherent diffraction imaging (A = F) and ptychography (A given by a subsampled STFT operator), and under the requirement that any useful complexity statistic should be inferable from the measurements I alone because the object structure is unknown a priori, which structural features of f are already rigorously connected to intrinsic reconstruction difficulty—through autocorrelation-based quantities γ = F^{-1}I, the overdetermination ratio Ω = (1/2)|Sγ|/|Sf|, the radius-of-gyration statistic B, local stability bounds up to global phase, support-connectivity/Cheeger effects, and transversality—and what mathematical results are still needed to turn these into justified predictors of reconstruction difficulty, especially of the convergence behavior of gradient-based phase retrieval (for example via explicit dependence on smoothness class or on Hessian conditioning)?

In the phase-retrieval model I = A(f) = |Af|^2, considered in both the continuous and finite-dimensional settings and motivated mainly by coherent diffraction imaging (A = F) and ptychography (A given by a subsampled short-time Fourier transform matrix), can one make the dependence of reconstruction speed on the complexity of the ground-truth object f explicit? More precisely, in the finite-dimensional setting with f in C^n, A in C^(m x n), and measured data y = (y_j)_(j=1)^m, for the gradient-descent iteration f^(t+1) = f^t - mu grad L(f^t) applied to the square-root objective L(f) = sum_{j=1}^m ( |(Af)_j|^(1/2) - y_j^(1/2) )^2, whose current global guarantee for arbitrary initialization f^0 is grad L(f^t) -> 0 and max_{1 <= t <= T} ||grad L(f^t)|| <= ((L(f^0) - inf_f L(f))^(1/2)) / (||A|| sqrt(T)), can one identify object-complexity descriptors - for example a smoothness class of f, or statistics derived from the Hessian grad^2 L and its conditioning - that explain how complexity manifests during reconstruction and yield an explicit quantitative dependence of the convergence rate on that complexity, rather than leaving it implicit in the term L(f^0) - inf_f L(f)?

For the phase-retrieval problem of recovering an unknown object f from intensity-only measurements I = 𝒜(f) = |Af|² in the continuous setting or I = 𝒜(f) = |A f|² in the discrete setting—especially in coherent diffraction imaging (A = F) and ptychography, where A is a (subsampled) short-time Fourier transform matrix—can one justify an obtained reconstruction of f by constructing valid confidence intervals for the reconstructed image or its parts, possibly pixel-wise, with the usual confidence-interval interpretation relative to the true object, in a way that remains computationally feasible beyond the current Fisher-information/Hessian-based maximum-likelihood approach? ([ir.cwi.nl](https://ir.cwi.nl/pub/35739/35739.pdf))

In the physics-informed object-parameterization model of Section 4.1, where an object is written as f = a_0 λ + Σ_{j=1}^N a_j S_{t_j} μ_j(σ), with λ the Lebesgue-measure background, each μ_j a normalized localized complex measure representing a feature, μ_j drawn from an application-specific admissible feature set E satisfying |E| ≪ N, and S_{t_j} the translation placing μ_j at position t_j, what efficient strategy can establish the set E when it is not known a priori, ideally in a way that avoids the reliability and interpretability difficulties of patch-based learned dictionaries? ([ir.cwi.nl](https://ir.cwi.nl/pub/35739/35739.pdf))

In the physics-informed object-parameterization model for phaseless reconstruction, f = a0 λ + Σ_{j=1}^N a_j S_{t_j} μ_j(σ), where λ is the Lebesgue-measure background, each μ_j is a normalized localized complex measure chosen from an admissible feature set E, S_{t_j} translates μ_j to position t_j, a_j gives its strength, and σ captures experimental conditions, how should one determine the number of features N and the specific feature measures μ_j appearing in the parametrized representation from the phase-retrieval problem data?

Let f be modeled by the physics-informed parametrization f = a0 λ + Σ_{j=1}^N a_j S_{t_j} μ_j(σ), where λ is the Lebesgue-measure background, each μ_j belongs to an admissible set E of normalized, localized complex features, and the unknown parameter tuple is ((a_j, μ_j, t_j)) for 1 ≤ j ≤ N. Can one establish uniqueness and stability guarantees for recovering these parameters from phaseless measurements of f, and identify reasonable sufficient conditions under which such recovery holds? ([ir.cwi.nl](https://ir.cwi.nl/pub/35739/35739.pdf))

Let f be the simplified sparse crystallographic object on R^2 given by f = lambda + sum_{j=1}^N a_j delta_{t_j}, where lambda is the Lebesgue measure, N < infinity, t_j in R^2, and a_j = e^{i omega_j} - 1 in C. Let w in S(R^2) be a known probe, let S_r w(x) = w(x-r), and let F[g](xi) = integral over R^2 of g(x)e^{-i<x,xi>} dx. Given the phaseless ptychographic measurements A(f)(r,xi) = |F(f · S_r w)(xi)|^2 for all probe shifts r in a prescribed set R and frequencies xi in a prescribed set Omega, can one recover the atom positions t_j and weights a_j for j = 1,...,N?

In the finite-dimensional discretization of the sparse-crystallography model from Section 4.2, let f = 1 + Σ_{j=1}^N a_j e_{t_j} ∈ ℂ^n, where N is fixed, 1 is the constant background, e_{t_j} denotes the coordinate vector at location t_j ∈ {0,...,n-1}, and a_j ∈ ℂ are unknown weights. For a fixed probe w ∈ ℂ^n, unitary DFT matrix F, and cyclic shift operator S_r, the phaseless measurements are A(f)(r,k) = |(Fw)_k + Σ_{j=1}^N (a_j/√n)(S_r w)_{t_j} exp(-2π i k(t_j-r)/n)|^2 for all Fourier indices k ∈ {0,...,n-1} and probe shifts r ∈ R. How large must the probe-shift set R be to ensure unique reconstruction of the full parameter tuple {(a_j,t_j)}_{j=1}^N from these measurements?

In the finite-dimensional sparse crystallography model, let [n] = {0,1,...,n-1}, let F in C^{n x n} be the unitary discrete Fourier transform with entries F_{k,j} = exp(-2π i k j/n)/sqrt(n), let (S_r x)_j = x_{j-r} be the shift operator, let w in C^n be a probe, and let R be a set of probe shifts. Suppose the unknown signal has the form f = 1 + sum_{j=1}^N a_j e_{t_j} in C^n, where 1 is the all-ones background vector, e_t is the t-th standard basis vector, the coefficients a_j in C and locations t_j in [n] are unknown, and the measurements are A(f)(r,k) = |(F w)_k + sum_{j=1}^N (a_j/sqrt(n))(S_r w)_{t_j} exp(-2π i k(t_j-r)/n)|^2 for all r in R and k in [n]. Which reconstruction methods can provably recover the unknown weights and atom positions {(a_j,t_j)}_{j=1}^N efficiently and stably from these phaseless data, and what sufficient assumptions on the probe w and the shift set R are required for those guarantees?

Let y = A(f_0) + epsilon be noisy measurements of an unknown signal f_0 in C^n under an injective measurement map A:C^n -> C^m, and let G:C^k -> C^n, with k < n, be a generative prior used through the latent reconstruction problem z-tilde in argmin_{z in C^k} ||A(G(z)) - y||_2^2. In the out-of-distribution defect model f_0 = G(z_0) + eta, where G(z_0) represents the 'perfect' signal and eta models imperfections or manufacturing defects, can one, from the measurements y and the computed latent minimizer z-tilde, detect or quantitatively estimate the bias ||G(z-tilde) - f_0||_2?

Let y = A(f_0) + epsilon be noisy measurements of an unknown signal f_0 in C^n, where A : C^n -> C^m is the measurement map and G : C^k -> C^n, k < n, is a generative model. For the unified estimator defined by equation (13), min over z in C^k and f in C^n of ||A(f)-y||_2^2 + lambda^2 ||G(z)-f||_2^2, which interpolates between the conventional reconstruction problem (11) when lambda = 0 and the pure generative-prior problem (12) as lambda -> infinity, can one obtain sharper reconstruction-error bounds for the resulting estimate f~ than those currently given by Lemmas 5.3 and 5.5, under appropriate assumptions on A, G, and f_0, in particular in regimes where A is not globally bi-Lipschitz and for specific learned or model-based classes of generative models G, with the bias quantified through z_0 = arg min_z ||G(z)-f_0||_2?

In the Section 5 framework of the paper, where y=A(f0)+ε with f0∈C^n and bounded additive ε∈C^m, A:C^n→C^m and G:C^k→C^n are assumed injective and bi-Lipschitz, A∘G is better conditioned than A, and phase retrieval is the special case A(f)=|Af|^2, can one design an efficient algorithm with provable convergence guarantees for the generic nonlinear optimization problem min_{x∈C^d} ||A∘B(x)-y||_2^2 + λ^2 ||w⊙x||_2^2 — in particular for the unified instance d=k+n, B(x1,x2)=G(x1)+x2, w(t)=0 on the first k coordinates and w(t)=1 on the remaining n coordinates — and prove robustness under assumptions on the additive noise ε and the generative-approximation bias G(z0)-f0, where z0:=argmin_z ||G(z)-f0||_2, including a principled rule for updating λ during the iterations when the signal-to-noise ratio is not known in advance? ([link.springer.com](https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s43670-025-00117-0))

In the high-dimensional noiseless complex phase-retrieval model y = |Af0|^2 with A ∈ C^{m×n} a random sensing matrix, f0 ~ Unif(S^{n-1}) ⊂ C^n, and m,n → ∞ with fixed oversampling ratio α = m/n, determine, as a function of the statistical law of A, the weak-recovery and full-recovery thresholds α_WR and α_FR defined by MMSE(α) = lim_{n→∞} E||f-tilde - f0||_2^2, where f-tilde is the Bayes-optimal estimator of f0 for the given α, α_WR = inf{α > 0 : MMSE(α) < E||f0||_2^2}, and α_FR = inf{α > 0 : MMSE(α) = MMSE_0} with MMSE_0 = inf_{α>0} MMSE(α).

In the probabilistic noiseless phase-retrieval model of Section 6, where the ground-truth object f_0 in C^n is uniformly distributed on the complex unit sphere S^{n-1}, the data are y = |A f_0|^2, and m,n -> infinity with fixed oversampling ratio alpha = m/n, let f~ be the Bayes-optimal estimator, define MMSE(alpha) = lim_{n->infinity} E||f~ - f_0||_2^2 and MMSE_0 = inf_{alpha>0} MMSE(alpha), and set alpha_WR = inf{alpha > 0 : MMSE(alpha) < E||f_0||_2^2} and alpha_FR = inf{alpha > 0 : MMSE(alpha) = MMSE_0}. For the physically implementable structured random Fourier-diffuser sensing ensembles considered in Section 6.2—denoted in the paper by A = FDF and A = F D_1 F D_2 ... F D_ell with ell >= 2, F the unitary discrete Fourier transform, D = diag(w), D_k = diag(w_k), and w_k(j) = exp(i u_{k,j}) with u_{k,j} i.i.d. Unif.[0,2pi]—can one derive information-theoretic and algorithmic bounds on the threshold values alpha_WR and alpha_FR?

In the probabilistic noiseless phase-retrieval framework of Section 6, let f0 ∈ C^n be recovered from measurements y = |Af0|^2 with random sensing matrix A ∈ C^{m×n}, and let m, n → ∞ with fixed oversampling ratio α = m/n. If f_Bayes denotes the Bayes-optimal estimator of f0, define MMSE(α) = lim_{n→∞} E||f_Bayes − f0||_2^2, MMSE_0 = inf_{α>0} MMSE(α), α_WR = inf{α > 0 : MMSE(α) < E||f0||_2^2}, and α_FR = inf{α > 0 : MMSE(α) = MMSE_0}. When the baseline prior f0 ~ Unif(S^{n−1}) is replaced by object priors such as positivity constraints, support constraints, or a low-dimensional generative prior f0 = G(z0) with z0 ∈ C^d and d < n, how do the thresholds α_WR and α_FR depend on these object priors?

Let f in C^n be an unknown object and let the phaseless measurement map be A(f)=|Af|^2, where in the ptychographic 4D-STEM setting the measurement matrix has the form A = [F D_1; ...; F D_l] with D_k = diag(S_k w), probe w in C^n, and F the discrete Fourier transform. Suppose the data are acquired in the event-driven low-dose regime, so that the detector counts satisfy y_j ~ Poisson(A(f)(j)) independently, but in practice only first-arrival/one-bit data min{y_j,1} are available, with m >> n and low overall dose so that most detector pixels record 0 and only a few record 1. Can one design an efficient reconstruction method that recovers f up to global phase from this structured acquisition model, and prove rigorous reconstruction and stability guarantees for this event-driven 4D-STEM measurement setup?

In the finite-dimensional discrete Wigner Distribution Deconvolution setting for ptychography, let f,w ∈ C^n, let [n] = {0,1,...,n-1}, and define the measurements by I_{xi,x} = |F[f ∘ S_x w]_{xi}|^2 for all scan positions x ∈ [n] and frequencies xi ∈ [n], where F is the unitary discrete Fourier transform, S_x is the cyclic shift, and ∘ is the coordinatewise product. Assume the window is known and localized, supp(w) = [delta] with delta < n/2, so that the discrete WDD identity (F^{-1}IF)_{xi,x} = F[f ∘ S_xi conj(f)]_x · conj(F[conj(w) ∘ S_xi w]_x) applies. If some of the window ambiguity coefficients F[conj(w) ∘ S_xi w]_x are allowed to vanish, how many such zero coefficients can be tolerated while still guaranteeing unique recovery of f from the discrete ptychographic measurements I (up to the unavoidable global phase)?

In the finite-dimensional discrete Wigner Distribution Deconvolution setting, with object f in C^n, known localized window w in C^n with supp(w) = [delta] = {0, ..., delta - 1} for some delta < n/2, all scan positions X = [n] = {0, ..., n - 1}, unitary DFT F, circular shifts S_r, and measurements I_{xi,x} = |F[f ◦ S_x w]_{xi}|^2 satisfying (F^{-1} I F)_{xi,x} = F[f ◦ S_xi f]_x F[w ◦ S_xi w]_x, can one design a version of Subspace Completion that extends the current case where one diagonal f ◦ S_{xi0} f is fully recovered and every other diagonal is missing at most one Fourier coefficient, to the case of an arbitrary number of missing coefficients F[f ◦ S_xi f]_x (for instance because F[w ◦ S_xi w]_x vanishes or is truncated when small), while keeping the operational cost reasonable?

In the discrete ptychographic Wigner Distribution Deconvolution setting, let f,w be in C^n, let I_{xi,x} = |F(f ◦ S_x w)_{xi}|^2 for x in [n] and xi in [n], assume full scan positions X = [n], and let the known window be localized with supp(w) = [delta] for some delta < n/2. When zeros in the window factor F(conjugate(w) ◦ S_xi w) cause missing Fourier coefficients in the diagonals f ◦ S_xi conjugate(f), and specifically in the Subspace Completion regime where one diagonal f ◦ S_xi0 conjugate(f) is completely recovered for some xi0 in [delta] while each remaining diagonal f ◦ S_xi conjugate(f), xi in [delta], is missing at most one Fourier coefficient, can one rigorously justify SC by proving explicit conditions under which the linear-system completion step recovers the missing coefficients and thereby yields unique recovery of the object from the discrete WDD data?

In the discrete Wigner Distribution Deconvolution setting, let n ∈ N, f,w ∈ C^n, let F be the unitary discrete Fourier transform, S_x the cyclic shift, and ◦ the Hadamard product, and suppose the phaseless measurements are I_{ξ,x} = |F[f \circ S_x w]_ξ|^2 for all x,ξ ∈ [n], with w localized so that supp(w) = [δ] for some δ < n/2. When the usual nonvanishing condition on the window-side WDD factors F[\overline{w} \circ S_ξ w]_x fails, in particular for symmetric windows, what band limit on f is sufficient to guarantee unique recovery via WDD, and more generally what quantitative relation between the vanishing of |F[\overline{w} \circ S_ξ w]_x| and the band-limitedness of f ensures uniqueness?

In the discrete ptychographic setting of Section 8, let f,w be in C^n and let the measurements be I_{xi,x}=|F(f ⊙ S_x w)_{xi}|^2 for frequencies xi in [n] and scan positions x in a scan set X⊂[n]. Can one derive a Wigner Distribution Deconvolution formula analogous to the full-scan identity (26) for arbitrary reasonable scan patterns X—rather than only for the full scan X=[n] or the grid scan X={sk : k in [n/s]}—and, in that generalized setting, determine which structural assumptions on the object f are required for recovery via WDD (in the spirit of the currently known bandlimited or piecewise-constant cases for grid scans)?

Fix B>0. Characterize those window functions w in L^2(R) for which there exists a lattice Omega subset R^2 such that the sampled spectrogram map f -> (|V_w f(x,xi)|^2)_{(x,xi) in Omega} is injective on {f in L^2(R) : supp(f) subset [-B,B]}/~, where f ~ g iff f = e^(i alpha) g for some alpha in R.

Fix B > 0 and a sufficiently "nice" window function w in L2(R). In the one-dimensional sampled short-time Fourier transform phase retrieval problem for compactly supported complex-valued signals f in L2(R) with support(f) ⊂ [-B,B], where V_w f(x, ξ) = ∫_R f(t) w(t - x)e^(-itξ) dt, for which spiral-like—and, more generally, for which sampling sets Ω ⊂ R^2—do the sampled magnitude measurements {|V_w f(x, ξ)|^2 : (x, ξ) ∈ Ω} determine f uniquely up to a global phase, i.e. modulo the relation f ~ g iff there exists α ∈ R with f = e^(iα)g?

In the one-dimensional Gaussian Gabor setting, let w(t)=2^{1/4}e^{-π t^2}, let G:=V_w be the corresponding short-time Fourier transform, and let Ω=aZ×bZ⊂R^2. Since recovery is understood only up to the global-phase relation f∼g iff f=e^{iα}g for some α∈R, is there a dense subset D⊂L^2(R), consisting of functions other than the Gaussian w, such that every f∈D is uniquely determined up to ∼ by its sampled Gabor magnitude data |Gf|^2_Ω? If such a dense recoverable set exists, is D of the first or of the second category in L^2(R)?

For a fixed dimension d >= 1, can one construct a window w in L^2(R^d), finite sampling sets Omega_k = {(x_j, xi_j) : 1 <= j <= k} subset R^d x R^d, and a family of practical phase-retrieval algorithms A_k : [0, infinity)^k -> L^2(R^d) such that, if V_w f(x, xi) = integral_{R^d} f(t) w(t - x)e^{-i <t, xi>} dt and y_k(f) = (|V_w f(x_j, xi_j)|^2)_{j=1}^k, then, for example, inf_{alpha in S^1} ||alpha f - A_k(y_k(f))||_{L^2(R^d)} -> 0 as k -> infinity for every f in some dense subset of L^2(R^d), especially in the higher-dimensional case d > 1?

For integers n≥1 and 0≤m≤n, let T be a rooted labelled tree of size n on [n], and let f:[n]→[n] be an n-mapping. Write S(T,m) and S(f,m) for the numbers of sequences s∈[n]^m for which, under the tree/mapping parking procedure, all m drivers park successfully. Since these counts are invariant under relabelling, can one in general give a simple characterization of the numbers S(T,m) and S(f,m), beyond the general bounds, extremal cases, and explicit formulas known for only some simple classes of trees or mappings?

For each n >= 1, determine the counting sequence and corresponding generating functions for tree parking functions on rooted labelled ordered trees, rooted labelled unordered trees, and rooted labelled binary trees of size n with n successful drivers, and derive exact as well as asymptotic enumeration formulas; more generally, characterize the corresponding generating functions when the tree has size n and there are m < n drivers (equivalently load factor alpha = m/n in (0,1)).

For the tree-parking model on labelled rooted trees—where each driver chooses a preferred vertex and, if that vertex is occupied, moves along the unique path toward the root until finding the first vacant vertex—can one determine the total number of successful preference sequences for increasing or decreasing tree families, in particular for recursive trees regarded as unordered increasing trees? If the corresponding differential-equation method does not lead to tractable explicit solutions, can one at least obtain analogous sum-enumerator statistics for these families, in the spirit of the classical sums of parking functions?

For integers n≥1 and 0≤m≤n, let T be a rooted labelled tree on [n] with edges directed toward the root, or let f:[n]→[n] be an n-mapping, and let s=(s_1,…,s_m)∈[n]^m be a parking function for T or f with output-function π:[m]→[n]. For each driver i, define its displacement d_i to be the length of the parking path from its preferred parking space s_i to its eventual parking space π(i), and define the total displacement D:=∑_{i=1}^m d_i. Determine, over all (n,m)-tree parking functions and all (n,m)-mapping parking functions, the displacement enumerators/distributions for these statistics—specifically, the total displacement D and, for fixed 1≤k≤m, the individual displacement d_k.

For integers n>=1, m>=0, and 0<=k<=m, let T range over rooted labelled trees on [n] with edges oriented toward the root, and let f range over n-mappings f:[n]->[n] viewed as functional digraphs. For a preference sequence s=(s_1,...,s_m) in [n]^m, drivers arrive in order; driver i first tries vertex s_i and, if it is occupied, repeatedly follows the unique outgoing edge (toward the root in T, or along f in the mapping digraph) until reaching a free vertex, and fails if all reachable vertices are already occupied. Determine, exactly or asymptotically, the number of pairs (T,s) and the number of pairs (f,s) for which exactly k drivers fail to park; equivalently, develop the defective analogues of the total counts F_{n,m} and M_{n,m} from the successful case.

For rooted labelled trees T on [n] (with edges oriented toward the root) and n-mappings f:[n]->[n] viewed through their functional digraphs, a sequence s in [n]^m is a parking function if each driver, starting at its preferred vertex and then following the directed edges until the first vacant vertex, eventually parks. Beyond the unrestricted total counts F_{n,m} and M_{n,m} of all successful pairs (T,s) and (f,s), can one obtain analogous exact or asymptotic enumeration results for a specified nontrivial restricted subclass of tree or mapping parking functions?

For each n >= 1, choose uniformly at random a rooted labelled unordered tree T with n vertices, and let X_n be the number of length-n preference sequences that are tree parking functions for T, i.e. for which all n drivers successfully park on T under the tree parking rule. If F_n denotes the total number of such tree parking functions over all rooted labelled unordered trees of size n and T_n denotes the total number of rooted labelled unordered trees of size n, so that E[X_n] = F_n/T_n exactly, can one determine higher moments of X_n, or at least obtain further nontrivial information about the distribution of X_n?

Consider the critical parking process on a rooted random tree with n vertices, where cars arrive according to the parking rule used in the paper and one is in the heavy-tailed infinite-third-moment regime: either the offspring law of the underlying conditioned random tree or the law governing car arrivals at vertices has power-law decay with exponent gamma in (3,4). Is the largest critical parked component in this regime—using the precise connected-component notion fixed in Section 1—of order n^{(gamma-2)/(gamma-1)} as n tends to infinity?

At criticality, for parking on random trees in a regime where either the offspring distribution or the car-arrival distribution has infinite third moment and tail c·k^{-γ} with c > 0 and γ in (3,4), and especially when this heavy-tailed regime is combined with the frozen modification of the Erdős–Rényi process, can one prove that the strong or weak parked components—conjecturally of size order n^{(γ−2)/(γ−1)}—admit nontrivial scaling limits as rooted measured metric spaces in Gromov-weak or Gromov-Hausdorff-Prokhorov-type topologies, and can one identify the limiting objects in terms of additive/multiplicative coalescent behavior or inhomogeneous continuum random trees?

Starting from the usual parking process on a random rooted tree—where cars arrive sequentially at vertices, each car moves toward the root until it finds the first vacant vertex and parks there, or exits through the root if none is vacant—can this model be extended to formulations based on different metric topologies, in a way that still admits meaningful analogues of the phase-transition and scaling-limit results surveyed for parking on random trees?

Let T = {T_k}_{k=1}^K with K ≥ 2 be a finite iterated-function system of affine contractions T_k:[0,1]→[0,1], and let Γ = ⋂_{n=0}^∞ T^{∘n}([0,1]) = ⋃_{k=1}^K T_k(Γ) be its attractor. Assuming Γ is a deterministic Cantor set on the real line and the maps T_k do not preserve bilateral symmetry, develop explicit or recursive set-theoretic formulas for Γ.

Within the paper’s set-theoretic framework for deterministic Cantor sets on the real line, can one find set-theoretic descriptive formulas for Cantor sets Γ ⊂ [0,1] whose stage-wise retained closed intervals have irrational end-points, while allowing Γ to arise as the attractor Γ = ⋂_{n=0}^∞ T^{∘n}([0,1]) of a finite affine iterated-function system T = {T_k}_{k=1}^K with K ≥ 2?

Let (alpha_n)_{n>=1} be a fixed sequence in (0,1) such that 1 - sum_{n=1}^infinity 2^{n-1} alpha_n >= 0. Starting from C_0 = [0,1], define recursively for each n>=1 the set C_n by removing from each of the 2^{n-1} closed interval components of C_{n-1} its symmetric open middle subinterval of length alpha_n, and let C = intersection_{n>=0} C_n. Find a recursive set-theoretic (nested) descriptive formula for the resulting deterministic Cantor set C subset of [0,1].

Let I_0 = [0,1], and let (α_n)_{n>=1} be a sequence with 0 < α_n < 1 and 1 - sum_{n=1}^∞ 2^{n-1} α_n >= 0. In the symmetric variable-gap construction, at stage n remove from each surviving interval its open middle subinterval of length α_n, thereby obtaining a deterministic Cantor subset of [0,1]. Provide recursive descriptive formulae for this Cantor set, and determine how those formulae vary when bilateral symmetry is enforced versus when that symmetry assumption is relaxed.

For deterministic Cantor sets C subseteq [0,1], determine conditions under which the intersection of the four Cantor-set families singled out in Section 4(i)-(iv) is nonempty, namely: the family of sets admitting an explicit or recursive set-theoretic description via a finite affine iterated-function system {T_k}_{k=1}^K with K >= 2 whose maps do not preserve bilateral symmetry; the family whose retained intervals have irrational end-points, again allowing IFS components; the family obtained by variable-gap middle deletions in which, at stage n, the open middle interval of length alpha_n is removed for a sequence (alpha_n)_{n>=1} satisfying 0 < alpha_n < 1 and 1 - sum_{n=1}^infinity 2^{n-1} alpha_n >= 0; and the symmetry-enforced or symmetry-relaxed versions of that variable-gap construction?

For each subset A ⊆ R, let I(A) = {f : H^f(A) > 0}, where f ranges over gauge functions in the standard Hausdorff-measure sense and H^f denotes the associated Hausdorff f-measure. As A ranges over all subsets of R, is the range {I(A) : A ⊆ R} of the map A ↦ I(A) equinumerous with the power set P(R), i.e. does it have cardinality 2^{|R|}?

Fix a standard effective coding of gauge functions and of arithmetic formulas. For A⊆ℝ, let I(A) = {f : f is a gauge function and H^f(A) > 0}, where H^f is the Hausdorff measure associated with f. It is known that for every closed set C⊆ℝ, the set I(C) is arithmetic, in fact Σ^0_2. What is the lightface descriptive complexity of the set S of Gödel codes of Σ^0_2 arithmetic formulas φ such that φ defines, under the chosen coding, exactly I(C) for some closed set C⊆ℝ? The paper notes that S is already Π^1_1-hard; in particular, is S Σ^1_2-complete?

For each set A ⊆ ℝ, let I(A)= {f : f is a gauge function and H^f(A) > 0}, where H^f denotes the Hausdorff measure associated with f. Is it independent of ZFC whether the Borel hierarchy is proper on the family {I(A) : A ⊆ ℝ}, equivalently in the paper’s wording, whether the Borel hierarchy is proper with respect to the range of the map A↦I(A)? ([tianyuan.amss.ac.cn](https://tianyuan.amss.ac.cn/upload/fab78d36-bd52-42eb-84d3-ff99c953bb08/20250708/67111751937959724.pdf?utm_source=openai))

Is it relatively consistent with ZFC that for every Hausdorff gauge function f:[0,∞)→[0,∞) and every set A ⊆ ℝ, if the associated Hausdorff f-measure H^f(A) is positive, then there exists a subset A_0 ⊆ A such that 0 < H^f(A_0) < ∞?

For each fixed integer k >= 4, consider the Even Number Game G_k played on the natural numbers as follows: on each round, Player 1 chooses a k-element set A of natural numbers such that none of the elements of A has been played earlier by Player 1; then Player 2 chooses an even natural number e with min(A) <= e <= max(A) such that e has not been played earlier by Player 2. Does Player 1 have a winning strategy in G_k, i.e. can she force Player 2 eventually to have no legal move?

Let Tr denote the standard Polish space of trees T ⊆ ω^{<ω}, coded as reals, and define WF = {T ∈ Tr : T has no infinite branch} and UB = {T ∈ Tr : T has exactly one infinite branch}. Saint Raymond proved that (WF, UB) is a complete pair of coanalytic sets: for every disjoint coanalytic A, B ⊆ ω^ω, there is a continuous function f : ω^ω → Tr such that A = f^{-1}[WF] and B = f^{-1}[UB]. Goh later proved, by recursion-theoretic methods, that every coanalytic separator C of WF and UB (that is, every coanalytic C ⊆ Tr with WF ⊆ C and C ∩ UB = ∅) is coanalytic-complete. Can this separator-completeness theorem be proved by purely descriptive-set-theoretic methods?

Fix a universal prefix-free oracle machine U. For each oracle x in 2^omega and each finite binary string sigma in 2^{<omega}, define K^x(sigma) = min{|tau| : U^x(tau) = sigma}, and define Omega^x = sum_{sigma in 2^{<omega}} 2^{-K^x(sigma)}. Does there exist an oracle x such that Omega^x computes the second Turing jump of the empty set, i.e. Omega^x >=_T 0''?

Let A ⊆ ω^ω be an analytic (Σ^1_1) set of reals such that sup{ω_1^{CK(x)} : x ∈ A} = ω_1, where ω_1^{CK(x)} is the Church–Kleene ordinal relative to x. Is there a purely recursion-theoretic proof of the Velickovic–Woodin theorem that for every real γ there exist x_0,x_1,x_2,x_3 ∈ A such that γ is hyperarithmetically reducible to the Turing join x_0 ⊕ x_1 ⊕ x_2 ⊕ x_3, i.e. γ ≤_h x_0 ⊕ x_1 ⊕ x_2 ⊕ x_3?

For every real y and every Σ^1_1(y) set A of reals, if A contains some real x with relative Church–Kleene ordinal ω_1^{CK(x)} > ω_1^{CK(y)}, must it follow that for every real γ there exist reals x_0, x_1, x_2, x_3 ∈ A such that γ ≤_h x_0 ⊕ x_1 ⊕ x_2 ⊕ x_3, where ≤_h denotes hyperarithmetic reducibility and ⊕ denotes join? ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2507.03972))

Over the base system RCA_0, let T ⊆ 2^{<ω} be a binary tree, let [T] ⊆ 2^ω denote its set of infinite paths, and call T positive if μ([T]) > 0 for the usual product measure μ on 2^ω. Define P to be the statement that every positive tree T has a perfect subtree S ⊆ T, where 'perfect' means that every node of S has two incompatible extensions in S. Define P^- to be the statement that every positive tree T has a sequence (X_n)_{n∈ω} of pairwise distinct paths in [T]. Does RCA_0 prove P^- -> P?

Over RCA_0, let T ⊆ 2^{<ω} be a binary tree and [T] ⊆ 2^ω its path set. If one redefines 'positive' to mean that [T] has positive Hausdorff dimension (in the usual Cantor-space metric), and correspondingly defines P^+_dim, P_dim, and P^-_dim by replacing 'positive measure' with 'positive dimension' in the Section 5 principles—namely, P^+_dim: every positive-dimension tree has a perfect subtree of positive dimension; P_dim: every positive-dimension tree has a perfect subtree; and P^-_dim: every positive-dimension tree has an infinite countable family of paths—which of the Section 5 measure-based implications and nonimplications continue to hold for these dimension analogues, and in particular does the analogue of Problem 10, RCA_0 ⊢ P^-_dim → P_dim, hold? ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2507.03972))

Fix a positive integer n. In the language of first-order arithmetic, does IΣ_n prove WPHP(Σ_{n+1}) → FRT^2_2(Σ_{n+1})? Here WPHP(Σ_{n+1}) asserts that for every x > 0 there is no injective Σ_{n+1}-definable map F: 2x → x, and FRT^2_2(Σ_{n+1}) asserts that for every x there exists y such that every Σ_{n+1}-definable 2-coloring C: [y]^2 → 2 has a homogeneous set H ⊆ y with |H| = x.

For each fixed n >= 0, working over the ambient fragment IΣ_n used in the surrounding discussion of Section 5, does FRT^2_2(Σ_{n+1}) imply FRT^3_2(Σ_{n+1})? Here FRT^e_k(Σ_{n+1}) is the scheme asserting that for every natural number x there exists y such that every Σ_{n+1}-definable coloring C:[{0,...,y-1}]^e -> k has a homogeneous set H subseteq {0,...,y-1} with |H| >= x, i.e. C is constant on [H]^e.

Does there exist a finitely generated group L ≅ F_k/N such that N, equivalently the word problem of L with respect to a finite generating set, is a Π^0_1 set but not decidable, and such that L is effectively residually finite in the sense that there is an algorithm which, given any w ∈ F_k with w ∉ N, computes a finite group Q and a homomorphism r:F_k→Q satisfying r(N)={e} and r(w)≠e?

Does there exist a finitely generated group S = F_k/N such that: (i) its word problem N ⊆ F_k is Π^0_1 (equivalently, S is a Π-group in the sense of the paper); (ii) S is residually finite, i.e. every nonidentity element of S survives in some finite quotient; but (iii) S is not effectively residually finite, meaning that there is no algorithm which, given w ∈ F_k with w ∉ N, outputs a finite group Q and a homomorphism r : F_k → Q such that r(N) = {e} and r(w) ≠ e? ([tianyuan.amss.ac.cn](https://tianyuan.amss.ac.cn/upload/fab78d36-bd52-42eb-84d3-ff99c953bb08/20250708/67111751937959724.pdf?utm_source=openai))

Does there exist a finitely generated residually finite group L = F_k/N whose word problem is Π^0_1 and which is not isomorphic to any subgroup of S_rec, the group of computable permutations of ℕ—that is, can Morozov’s 2000 example of a Π-group not isomorphic to a subgroup of S_rec be made residually finite? The paper notes that any such example would necessarily not be effectively residually finite, meaning that there is no algorithm which, given w ∈ F_k with w ∉ N, computes a finite group Q and a homomorphism r:F_k→Q such that r(N)={e} and r(w)≠e.

Does there exist a Borel class C of profinite groups such that, under Borel reducibility, the topological isomorphism relation on C is properly between smooth and S∞-complete? In particular, can one take C to be the class of profinite Abelian groups?

Let Olig(S∞) be the standard Borel space of closed oligomorphic subgroups G ≤ S∞ = Sym(ω), where oligomorphic means that for each n ∈ ω, the action of G on ω^n has only finitely many orbits. Consider the equivalence relation of topological group isomorphism on Olig(S∞). Given the known upper bound that this relation is Borel reducible to E∞, is it in fact smooth; equivalently, is it Borel reducible to equality on a standard Borel space such as 2^ω?

Let G be an oligomorphic closed subgroup of Sym(ω). Let Aut(G) denote the group of continuous automorphisms of G, equipped with the natural Polish topology from Theorem 20, and let Out(G)=Aut(G)/Inn(G) be given the quotient topology. Must Out(G) always be a profinite topological group?

Does there exist a class C of closed subgroups of S∞ = Sym(ω) such that C is Borel and invariant under topological isomorphism, and the topological isomorphism relation on C is not Borel reducible to graph isomorphism? ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2507.03972))

Let S∞ = Sym(ℕ), and let C be a Borel subset of the space of closed subgroups of S∞ that is invariant under isomorphism. Does there exist such a class C for which the isomorphism relation on C is not Borel reducible to the isomorphism relation on countable graphs? More specifically, can the isomorphism relation on such a class C be complete analytic?

Let Subg(S∞) denote the standard Borel space of closed subgroups of the full symmetric group S∞ on N, each equipped with its inherited Polish topology, and let ≅top denote topological group isomorphism. Does there exist a Borel ≅top-invariant class C ⊆ Subg(S∞) such that ≅top restricted to C is not Borel reducible to isomorphism of countable graphs, or even is analytic-complete among analytic equivalence relations under Borel reducibility? In particular, can one take C to be the class of pro-countable groups?

Let L ⊆ ω be an oracle. Say that L is index guessable if there is a Turing functional Γ such that for every e, whenever Φ_e^L is a computable function, Γ^{∅′}(e) halts and outputs an index for Φ_e^L. Theorem 3.4 shows that every Δ^0_2 1-generic set is index guessable. Is the converse true? In other words, if L is index guessable, must L be both Δ^0_2 and 1-generic?

Let T be the mass problem of codes G for sequences <G_n>_{n in omega} of computable subsets of omega such that G_0 = omega, G_{n+1} subseteq* G_n for every n (where A subseteq* B means A \ B is finite), G_n \ G_{n+1} is infinite for every n, and for every infinite computable set R subseteq omega there exists n with R \ G_n infinite. Fix an effective list <Phi_e>_{e in omega} of Turing functionals, and write phi_i for the i-th partial computable function. Call an oracle L subseteq omega index guessable if there is a Turing functional Gamma such that for every e, whenever Phi_e^L is a computable function, Gamma^{emptyset'}(e) is defined and phi_{Gamma^{emptyset'}(e)} = Phi_e^L. Is it true that for every oracle L, if no member of T is Turing reducible to L, then L is index guessable?

Define Diag = { d : d is a Turing degree and, for every computably enumerable equivalence relation E on ω with more than one equivalence class, there exists a total d-computable function g: ω -> ω such that for every x in ω, g(x) is not E-equivalent to x }. Describe the class Diag.

What is the reverse-mathematical strength of the following principle: for every Σ^0_1-definable equivalence relation E on ω, if E is not the one-class equivalence relation Id1, then there exists a total function g: ω → ω such that for every x ∈ ω, g(x) is not E-equivalent to x?

What is the Weihrauch degree of the multivalued problem that, given as input a code for a Sigma^0_1-definable equivalence relation E on omega with E != Id_1, outputs a diagonal function for E, that is, a total function g: omega -> omega such that for every x in omega, not (g(x) E x)?

Let X be a Polish space that admits an effectively compact left-c.e. presentation, i.e. a presentation by a countable dense metric space whose distances are uniformly left-c.e. Must the homeomorphism type of X admit a computable Polish presentation? If not, must it at least admit a right-c.e. Polish presentation?

Does there exist an infinite computable Polish space X such that X is topologically computably categorical, in the sense that for every pair of computable metric spaces M and N whose metric completions are both homeomorphic to X, there is a computable homeomorphism between the completions of M and N?

Let X = ω^ω be the Baire space with its usual product topology, viewed as a computable Polish space. Does there exist a least Turing degree α such that for every pair of computable metric spaces M and N whose metric completions are homeomorphic to X, there is an α-computable homeomorphism between those completions? Equivalently stated in the paper’s terminology: does the Baire space have a degree of (topological) categoricity?

Does every computably enumerable Turing degree a—and, if not, does at least one computably enumerable Turing degree—occur as the degree of topological categoricity of some computable Polish space X; that is, as the least Turing degree d such that whenever M and N are computable metric spaces homeomorphic to X, there is a d-computable homeomorphism from M onto N?

Fix n. Let M be a model of RCA_0 + BΣ_n + ¬IΣ_n, let X ⊆ M be a Π_n-definable subset of M, and let ⟨A_s : s ∈ M⟩ be an internal sequence of pairwise disjoint M-finite sets such that A_s ∩ X ≠ ∅ for every s ∈ M. Must there exist a function f : M → M definable in M such that for every s ∈ M, f(s) ∈ A_s ∩ X?

Let M be a model of RCA_0 + BΣ_2 + ¬IΣ_2, and let T be a tree coded in M that is Π^0_1(∅′) over M. Suppose there exists a path g ∈ [T] such that the extension M[g] obtained by adjoining g satisfies BΣ_2. Must there exist a path h ∈ [T] that is definable in M and such that M[h] also satisfies BΣ_2? ([tianyuan.amss.ac.cn](https://tianyuan.amss.ac.cn/upload/fab78d36-bd52-42eb-84d3-ff99c953bb08/20250708/67111751937959724.pdf?utm_source=openai))
In the Polish space 2^{ω×ω}, is the set { G ∈ 2^{ω×ω} : G is an irreflexive symmetric relation on ω and G ≅ G^c }, where G^c = { (m,n) ∈ ω×ω : m ≠ n and (m,n) ∉ G }, a Borel subset?

Let X be a standard Borel space, and let E be a countable Borel equivalence relation on X. Suppose that E = ⋃_{n∈ω} F_n as a subset of X × X, where each F_n is a hyperfinite Borel subequivalence relation of E and F_n ⊆ F_{n+1} for all n. Must E itself be hyperfinite (equivalently, an increasing union of finite Borel subequivalence relations)?

Let E be a countable Borel equivalence relation on a standard Borel space X. Say that E is hyperfinite-over-hyperfinite (hf/hf) if there exists a Borel partial order ≤ on X such that (i) x ≤ y implies x E y, and (ii) for every x in X, the restriction ≤|[x]_E has order type a suborder of Z^2. Must every hf/hf equivalence relation be hyperfinite, that is, an increasing union of finite Borel equivalence relations?

Assume there exists a countable Borel equivalence relation E on a standard Borel space X that is hyperfinite-over-hyperfinite (hf/hf), meaning that E admits a Borel partial order ≤ on X such that (i) x ≤ y implies x E y, and (ii) for each x in X, the ordered class ([x]_E, ≤↾[x]_E) has order type embeddable into the lexicographically ordered Z×Z; and assume moreover that E is not hyperfinite. Does it follow that, in the usual coding of countable Borel equivalence relations, the class of hyperfinite countable Borel equivalence relations is Σ^1_2-complete?

For every countable amenable group G and every Borel action G ↷ X on a standard Borel space X, is the induced orbit equivalence relation E_G^X on X, defined by x E_G^X y iff there exists g in G such that g·x = y, hyperfinite; that is, can E_G^X be written as an increasing union of finite Borel equivalence relations?

Let G be a locally finite Borel graph on a standard Borel space X, and let E_G be its connectedness equivalence relation. Assume that G has uniform subexponential growth in the specific sense indicated in Problem 41: there exist constants C>0 and c in (0,1) such that for every x in X and every r in N, the ball B_G(x,r) has size at most C exp(r^c). Must E_G be hyperfinite; equivalently, is E_G an increasing union of finite Borel equivalence relations?

Let Aut([0,1], λ) be the space of automorphisms of Lebesgue measure on [0,1], equipped with the weak topology, and let Act(F∞,([0,1], λ)) ⊆ Aut([0,1], λ)^{F∞} be the closed subspace consisting of actions of F∞ on [0,1] by such automorphisms. For x ∈ Act(F∞,([0,1], λ)), let Sch(x) denote the Schreier graph of the action on [0,1]. Is the set {x ∈ Act(F∞,([0,1], λ)) : Sch(x) has a measurable perfect matching} Σ^1_1-complete?

Let λ be Lebesgue measure on [0,1], and let Aut([0,1], λ) be the space of Lebesgue-measure-preserving automorphisms of [0,1] equipped with the weak topology. What is the descriptive-set-theoretic complexity of the set R = {T ∈ Aut([0,1], λ) : there exists S ∈ Aut([0,1], λ) such that T = S^2 = S ◦ S}? In particular, is R Σ^1_1-complete?

Let X be a standard Borel space, and let G⃗ be a Borel locally finite directed graph on X. Assume that there is a uniform bound M < infinity such that every vertex has in-degree at most M, and that the forward balls have polynomial growth, in the sense that there exist constants C, d < infinity such that for every x in X and every n in N, the set B_n^+(x) of vertices reachable from x by a directed path of length at most n has cardinality at most C n^d. If E_G⃗ is the equivalence relation on X of belonging to the same connected component of the symmetrization of G⃗, must E_G⃗ be hyperfinite? ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2507.03972))

Let alpha be a free, probability-measure-preserving, ergodic action of F_2 on a probability space (X, mu), and fix x in F_2 with x != e. Let E_alpha be the orbit equivalence relation induced by alpha on X, i.e. u E_alpha v iff v = alpha(g)(u) for some g in F_2. Does there exist another free, probability-measure-preserving action beta of F_2 on the same space (X, mu) such that E_beta = E_alpha and the single transformation beta(x) is ergodic? ([tianyuan.amss.ac.cn](https://tianyuan.amss.ac.cn/upload/fab78d36-bd52-42eb-84d3-ff99c953bb08/20250708/67111751937959724.pdf?utm_source=openai))

Let α: F_2 ↷ (X, μ) be a free, probability-measure-preserving, ergodic action, and let E_α denote its orbit equivalence relation. Does there exist a free, probability-measure-preserving action β: F_2 ↷ (X, μ) such that E_β = E_α and, for every nonidentity element x ∈ F_2, the transformation β(x) is ergodic on (X, μ)?

Consider ordinary single-response unlinked linear regression over ℝ: Y ≍ β0^T X + ε, where ε is independent of X and the zero set of its characteristic function contains no open nonempty interval, so that identifiability is governed by B0 := {β ∈ ℝ^d : β^T X ≍ β0^T X}. Assume X = (X1,…,Xd) has independent components with Var(Xj) = 1 for every j, at most one component Xj is Gaussian, and the representation β0^T X is minimal in the sense that there is no strict subset I ⊊ {1,…,d} and no a ∈ ℝ^|I| such that β0^T X ≍ a^T X_I. Must every β ∈ B0 be of the form β = DPβ0 for some permutation matrix P and some diagonal matrix D with diagonal entries in {−1,1}? ([ar5iv.labs.arxiv.org](https://ar5iv.labs.arxiv.org/html/2507.14986v1))

Let X = (X1, X2) with independent components X1 ~ Laplace(0, 1/√2) and X2 ~ t5(0, √(3/5)), so that E[X1] = E[X2] = 0 and Var(X1) = Var(X2) = 1. For a fixed coefficient pair (α, β) in R^2 with α^2 + β^2 = 1, define B_{α,β} := {(a,b) in R^2 : aX1 + bX2 =d αX1 + βX2}. Is it true that for every such (α,β), one has B_{α,β} ⊆ {(σα, τβ) : σ,τ in {-1,1}}? Equivalently, does Example 3 after Theorem 6 hold conjecturally in full, namely that this Laplace/t5 design is identifiable up to coordinatewise sign flips, even though the fourth-moment sufficient condition from Theorem 6—namely min{w1,w2} < 1 with m_i = E[X_i^4], c = E[(αX1 + βX2)^4], and w_i = (m_i - 3)/(c - 3)—fails numerically at least on the region |α| ≥ 0.1835?

For integers n and g with 3 <= g <= n, determine
max { EUS(G) : G is a finite simple connected graph with |V(G)| = n and girth(G) = g },
where
EUS(G) = sum over uv in E(G) of sqrt(d_G(u)^2 + d_G(v)^2 + d_G(u)d_G(v)),
and characterize all graphs G for which this maximum is attained.

For integers n and p with 0 <= p <= n - 1, let C_{n,p} be the class of all finite simple connected graphs G with |V(G)| = n and exactly p pendant (degree-one) vertices. Determine the minimum value of EUS(G) over G in C_{n,p}, where EUS(G) = sum over uv in E(G) of sqrt(d_G(u)^2 + d_G(v)^2 + d_G(u)d_G(v)), and characterize all graphs in C_{n,p} for which this minimum is attained.

Let σ:N→N be a λ-permutation, meaning that (i) for every convergent real series ∑_{n=0}^∞ b_n, the rearranged series ∑_{n=0}^∞ b_{σ(n)} also converges, and (ii) there exists at least one divergent real series ∑_{n=0}^∞ c_n such that ∑_{n=0}^∞ c_{σ(n)} converges. If ∑_{n=0}^∞ a_n is a conditionally divergent series of real numbers and
S = {L ∈ R : ∑_{n=0}^∞ a_{σ(n)} converges to L for some λ-permutation σ},
must one always have S = ∅ or S = R?

For every ε > 0, if m tends to infinity through even integers and A is a subset of (Z/mZ)^× with |A| > (1/2 + ε)φ(m), must the binary sumset A + A := {a + a' mod m : a, a' in A} contain almost all even residue classes modulo m; equivalently, if E_m denotes the set of even residue classes in Z/mZ, is it true that |E_m \ (A + A)| = o(m) as m -> infinity through even m?

For every real epsilon > 0, does there exist M(epsilon) such that, for every even integer m >= M(epsilon), every subset A ⊆ (Z/mZ)^* with |A| > (1/2 + epsilon)phi(m) satisfies
3A := {a1 + a2 + a3 mod m : a1,a2,a3 ∈ A} ⊇ {x ∈ Z/mZ : x ≡ 1 mod 2}?

Let Q \subseteq \mathbb{P} be a set of prime numbers such that
\[\liminf_{x\to\infty}\frac{|Q\cap[1,x]|}{\pi(x)} > \frac12,\]
where \pi(x) denotes the number of primes \le x (equivalently, by Proposition 1.2, \(\liminf_{x\to\infty} (\log x/x)\,|Q\cap[1,x]| > 1/2\)). Must there exist a constant N_0 = N_0(Q) such that every odd integer N \ge N_0 can be written as
\[N=q_1+q_2+q_3\]
with q_1,q_2,q_3 \in Q (not necessarily distinct)?

Let N = {N(μ,σ^2) | μ ∈ ℝ, σ > 0} be the statistical Lie group of univariate normal distributions, equipped with its standard Lie-group structure and the Fisher metric g_F. Determine the moduli space of left invariant affine connections ∇ on N that are compatible with g_F in the information-geometric sense relevant here, namely those for which (N, g_F, ∇) is a left invariant statistical structure.

Let N = {N(μ,σ^2) : μ ∈ ℝ, σ > 0} be the statistical manifold of univariate normal distributions on ℝ, equipped with its Fisher metric. Can one formulate variational principles—namely, natural functionals whose critical-point or Euler-Lagrange conditions single out, respectively, the exponential connection and the mixture connection on N?

Fix n >= 2, and let \mathcal{N}_n = \mathbb{R}^n 	imes \mathrm{Sym}^+(n,\mathbb{R}) be the manifold of n-variate normal distributions, endowed with the solvable Lie group structure coming from the simply transitive action of \mathrm{Aff}^s(n,\mathbb{R}) given by (A,b) \cdot (\Sigma,\mu) = (A\Sigma A^	op, A\mu + b), where A is upper triangular with positive diagonal entries. If 
abla^e = 
abla^{A(1)} denotes the exponential (Amari-Chentsov) connection on this statistical Lie group, does there exist any left-invariant semi-Riemannian metric h on \mathcal{N}_n whose Levi-Civita connection is exactly 
abla^e?

Let (M, ∇, g) be a 1-dimensional Hessian manifold, meaning a 1-manifold M endowed with a flat torsion-free affine connection ∇ and a metric g that is locally expressible as the Hessian of a potential in ∇-affine coordinates. Investigate 1-dimensional Hessian manifolds, especially those realized as statistical manifolds of families of probability distributions, taking the statistical manifold of binomial distributions as the standard motivating example.

Let (M,g,∇) be a statistical manifold, let ∇^g denote the Levi-Civita connection of g, and set K:=∇−∇^g. Since the tension field of the identity map satisfies τ(id_M)=tr_g K, investigate the statistical manifolds for which the vector field τ(id_M) is parallel. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/html/2509.06989))

Let (M,g,∇) be a statistical manifold, and let ∇* be the affine connection conjugate to ∇ with respect to g. Determine the statistical manifolds for which the identity map id_M:(M,g,∇)→(M,g,∇*) is a critical point, for every relatively compact region Ω⊂M, of the bienergy E_2(id_M;Ω)=(1/2)∫_Ω |τ(id_M)|^2 dν_g under variations supported in Ω, where τ(id_M) is the tension field of id_M computed with domain connection ∇ and target connection ∇*. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2509.06989))

In Jan Maas's optimal-transport framework for Markov jump processes, where the logarithmic mean is introduced between two probabilities or two flows and appears natural for the gradient-flow/heat-equation structure, can one explain the distinguished role of the logarithmic mean among generalized means (for example those arising in Benamou-Brenier-type generalizations, for which a Legendre duality can still be defined) in genuinely information-geometric terms? More precisely, is there an information-geometric interpretation of the dual structures associated with generalized means that explains why the logarithmic mean is special, in a way analogous to the special roles of Chentsov's characterization of the Fisher metric, the Kullback-Leibler divergence, or the Amari-Chentsov connections, and that yields a unified understanding of variants of optimal transport theory for Markov jump processes?
In quantum information theory, generalized means give rise to a variety of quantum Fisher metrics. Is there an information-geometric framework for treating this variety of quantum Fisher metrics?

Let M be a base manifold already equipped with the conventional dually flat structure of static information geometry. Motivated by diffusion processes, optimal transport, Markov jump processes, and chemical reaction networks, how can one construct, purely within information geometry and with full mathematical rigor, an additional dynamic joint-structure—namely, another metric or dually flat structure on the dual pair (T_xM, T_x^*M) encoding the velocity and force that drive dynamics on M? ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2509.06989))

For the non-commutative matrix-scaling problem of operator scaling, does there exist a divergence on the space of density matrices—ideally a quantum analogue of the Kullback-Leibler divergence, but more generally any divergence at all—such that Gurvits’s operator Sinkhorn algorithm is exactly realized as an alternating minimization procedure, in the same sense that the classical Sinkhorn algorithm for matrix scaling is alternating minimization of the Kullback-Leibler divergence?

Let (M,g) be a smooth n-dimensional Riemannian manifold. Determine necessary and sufficient conditions for the following local property: for every point p in M, there exists a neighborhood U of p and two smooth local coordinate systems x=(x^1,...,x^n) and y=(y_1,...,y_n) on U such that g(∂/∂x^i, ∂/∂y_j)=δ_i^j on U for all i,j=1,...,n; that is, characterize exactly when a Riemannian manifold admits bi-orthogonal local coordinates in this sense, without assuming any affine connection a priori.

Let (M,g) be a smooth real Riemannian n-manifold, and let U=(U;x^1,...,x^n) and V=(V;y^1,...,y^n) be local coordinate systems such that g(∂/∂x^i, ∂/∂y^j)=δ_ij for all i,j=1,...,n on U∩V (so U and V are bi-orthogonal). In dually flat information geometry, such charts can be chosen as dual affine coordinates. Without assuming any pair of mutually dual affine connections, can one formulate a local analogue of the standard generalized Pythagorean theorem using only the Riemannian metric g and this bi-orthogonal coordinate structure? ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2509.06989))

Let M be a smooth manifold, and let ∇ and ∇* be affine connections on M. What is a sufficient condition for the existence of a Riemannian metric g on M such that, for all vector fields X, Y, Z on M, X[g(Y,Z)] = g(∇_X Y, Z) + g(Y, ∇*_X Z), i.e. such that ∇* is the dual (conjugate) connection of ∇ with respect to g?

What is a good definition of a "divergence" function in information geometry, broad enough to encompass standard examples such as the Kullback-Leibler and Bregman divergences, but not requiring either positivity of the divergence when one studies the geometry of dual connections or the requirement that the Riemannian metric be induced by second derivatives of the divergence in singular statistical models? In that sense, what should count as the appropriate notion of divergence in information geometry, and how should it relate to the existing notion of canonical divergence?

Let M be a statistical model, g its Fisher metric, and ∇^(α) its Amari α-connection. Following the paper, call (M, g, ∇^(α)) an invariant statistical manifold, and call it an invariant dually flat space when ∇^(α) is flat. Besides the classical exponential/mixture cases with α = ±1, find useful examples—preferably with genuine statistical or physical meaning—of invariant dually flat spaces (M, g, ∇^(α)) for some α ≠ ±1, in the spirit of the paper's motivating q-Gaussian (equivalently Student's t) location-scale family.

In the finite-sample-space setting, Sanov's theorem and its relation (equivalence in some sense) to Cramér's theorem via the Legendre transformation are understood as reflecting the underlying dually flat structure of information geometry. For the extensions of Sanov's theorem and Cramér's theorem to arbitrary Polish sample spaces, where the relative entropy D(nu||mu) is obtained through a rigorous functional-analytic Legendre-transform argument, is there a corresponding infinite-dimensional differential-geometric structure to which these results can be related?

Within the infinite-dimensional extension of information geometry, let M be a suitable infinite-dimensional manifold of probability distributions on an infinite sample space, and let S be a finite-dimensional statistical model on that same sample space. Can S be usefully treated as a submanifold of M in such a way that traditional statistical discussions about S are clarified or simplified—especially by reformulating the complicated regularity conditions that arise in the asymptotic theory of parameter estimation as geometric conditions on the submanifold S?

Let M be a finite-dimensional statistical model on an infinite sample space, viewed as a finite-dimensional submanifold of an infinite-dimensional manifold of probability distributions satisfying the standing conditions needed to make that ambient geometry rigorous. In the traditional asymptotic theory of parameter estimation for M, can the several complicated regularity conditions usually imposed on the model be reformulated as geometric conditions on the submanifold M, in a way that clarifies or simplifies the statistical theory, specifically on the parameter-estimation side rather than the large-deviation or hypothesis-testing side?

Fix a finite-dimensional Hilbert space H, let S be the totality of strictly positive density operators on H, let g be a monotone Riemannian metric on S, let ∇^(m) be the flat connection on S induced by the natural affine embedding S → A into the real vector space A of Hermitian operators on H, and let ∇^(e) be the connection dual to ∇^(m) with respect to g. Determine the ∇^(e)-autoparallel submanifolds of S; equivalently, characterize all pairs (rho, V) with rho ∈ S and V a linear subspace of T_rho S for which there exists an ∇^(e)-autoparallel submanifold M ⊂ S such that rho ∈ M and T_rho M = V.

Given a Riemannian manifold (M,g) and an affine connection ∇ on M, let ∇* be the g-dual connection, defined by X[g(Y,Z)] = g(∇_X Y, Z) + g(Y, ∇*_X Z) for all vector fields X, Y, Z on M. Assuming that ∇* is flat, determine the ∇-autoparallel submanifolds of M; that is, determine all submanifolds N ⊂ M such that ∇_X Y is tangent to N whenever X and Y are tangent vector fields on N. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2509.06989))

Let {P_θ}_{θ∈Θ} be an exponential family with natural parameter domain Θ ⊂ R^d, potential function ψ, and expectation parameter space η(Θ) := ∇ψ(Θ). Since Section 7 notes, via the cited Theorem 9.2 of Barndorff-Nielsen, that steepness forces η(Θ) to be the interior of the convex closure of the support, can one develop a systematic theory for the non-steep case that characterizes the possible shapes of non-convex expectation parameter spaces η(Θ), including the bounded non-convex examples exhibited there?

Let ν be a measure on ℝ^d, let ψ(θ) = log ∫ e^{⟨θ,x⟩} ν(dx), let Θ = {θ ∈ ℝ^d : ψ(θ) < ∞}, and let M := ∇ψ(Θ) be the expectation-parameter space of the associated exponential family. Since the paper notes that if ψ is steep then M is the interior of conv(supp ν), so any non-convex M can occur only in the non-steep case and necessarily requires unbounded supp(ν), while Figure 1 shows that M can still be bounded and non-convex, characterize the subsets M ⊂ ℝ^d that can arise as non-convex expectation-parameter spaces of such exponential families. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2509.06989))

In the specific setting where the q-exponential family is reparameterized as a λ-exponential family and each fixed deformation parameter yields a well-behaved leaf M_λ that, under suitable regularity conditions, carries a natural dualistic geometry of constant sectional curvature, can one systematically treat the deformation parameter itself as an additional parameter by viewing the resulting collection of models as a foliated statistical manifold M and endowing the total space M with a natural geometric structure useful for statistical inference? ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2509.06989))

In the setting of Section 8.1, where the q-exponential family is reparameterized as a lambda-exponential family and one allows the deformation parameter lambda itself to vary, so that the total model M = union over admissible lambda of M_lambda becomes a foliated statistical manifold whose fixed-lambda leaves M_lambda are individually well behaved, is there a systematic way to treat lambda as an additional parameter and endow M itself with a natural information-geometric structure, extending the geometry available on each leaf, that is useful for statistical inference?

Let P_0 and P_1 be two non-degenerate elliptical probability distributions on R^d with finite second moments, parameterized by means μ_0, μ_1 ∈ R^d, covariance matrices Σ_0, Σ_1, and radial distributions ν_0, ν_1 on [0,∞) under the paper’s elliptical parametrization. Can one prove, within this elliptical class, a Gelbrich-type lower bound for the squared 2-Wasserstein distance W_2^2(P_0,P_1) that strictly sharpens the classical moment-based Gelbrich bound by depending explicitly on the radial laws ν_0 and ν_1 in addition to μ_0, μ_1, Σ_0, and Σ_1?

Let mu = Ell_d(m, Sigma, R) and nu = Ell_d(n, Xi, S) be non-degenerate elliptical distributions on R^d with finite second moments, where an elliptical law is parameterized by a mean vector, a positive-definite covariance matrix, and a radial law on [0, infinity), normalized so that the covariance is Sigma or Xi respectively. Can one sharpen Gelbrich’s lower bound for the quadratic Wasserstein distance, namely W_2^2(mu, nu) >= ||m-n||^2 + Tr(Sigma + Xi - 2(Sigma^{1/2} Xi Sigma^{1/2})^{1/2}), by adding dependence on the radial laws R and S (especially when R and S differ), and thereby develop the W_2-geometry of the semiparametric manifold of elliptical distributions in the spirit of the known Wasserstein geometry of Gaussian measures?

For the three-dimensional Brezis-Nirenberg Dirichlet problem on the unit ball B_1:=B(0,1)⊂R^3,
-Δu=λu+|u|^4u in B_1,
 u∈H_0^1(B_1),
can one give a substantially more direct proof—preferably a purely variational proof—that for every λ>0 there exist infinitely many solutions u that are sign-changing (u^+≢0 and u^-≢0) and non-radial with respect to the center of B_1, thereby in particular recovering the recent full resolution of Brezis's first open problem in this setting?

For each fixed λ > 0, and for a general smoothly bounded domain Ω ⊂ R^3 (possibly under the additional assumption that Ω is convex if needed), does the Brezis-Nirenberg problem -Δu = λu + |u|^4u in Ω, u = 0 on ∂Ω, admit infinitely many sign-changing solutions u_k ∈ H_0^1(Ω) (equivalently, u_k^+ ≠ 0 and u_k^- ≠ 0) such that their energies satisfy J_λ(u_k) → +∞, where J_λ(u) = (1/2)∫_Ω(|∇u|^2 - λu^2) dx - (1/6)∫_Ω|u|^6 dx?

Let \(\Omega\subset \mathbb{R}^4\) be a smoothly bounded domain, and let \(\sigma(-\Delta)\) denote the Dirichlet spectrum of \(-\Delta\) on \(H_0^1(\Omega)\). For every spectral value \(\lambda\in\sigma(-\Delta)\), does the Brezis-Nirenberg problem
\[-\Delta u=\lambda u+|u|^2u\quad\text{in }\Omega,\qquad u=0\quad\text{on }\partial\Omega\]
admit a nontrivial sign-changing weak solution \(u\in H_0^1(\Omega)\)?

For each fixed λ>0, for every smoothly bounded domain Ω⊂ℝ^N with 3≤N≤6, does the Brezis-Nirenberg problem −Δu=λu+|u|^{2^*-2}u in Ω, u=0 on ∂Ω, where 2^*=2N/(N−2), admit infinitely many distinct sign-changing weak solutions u∈H_0^1(Ω)?

Let Ω ⊂ ℝ^3 be a smoothly bounded domain, and consider the Brezis-Nirenberg problem
−Δu = λu + |u|^4u in Ω,
u = 0 on ∂Ω.
For a fixed parameter value λ̄ > 0, call a family {u_λ} ⊂ H_0^1(Ω) of solutions a blow-up family with finite energy at λ̄ if ||u_λ||_{L^∞(Ω)} → +∞ and
E_λ(u_λ) = (1/2)||∇u_λ||_{L^2(Ω)}^2 − (λ/2)||u_λ||_{L^2(Ω)}^2 − (1/6)||u_λ||_{L^6(Ω)}^6
remains uniformly bounded as λ → λ̄. Is it possible, in a general smoothly bounded domain Ω (and, if necessary, under the additional assumption that Ω is convex), to construct such finite-energy blow-up solutions at a fixed concentration value λ̄ different from the value λ* predicted by Druet for the three-dimensional Brezis-Nirenberg problem?

Let Ω ⊂ ℝ^N be a smoothly bounded domain, with N >= 7, and assume convexity of Ω only if needed. For the Brezis-Nirenberg problem
-Δu = λu + |u|^{2^*-2}u in Ω,  u = 0 on ∂Ω,
where 2^* = 2N/(N-2), can one construct a family of real-valued solutions u_n ∈ H_0^1(Ω) with parameters λ_n -> λ_* such that the corresponding energies J_{λ_n}(u_n) = (1/2)∫_Ω(|∇u_n|^2 - λ_n u_n^2)dx - (1/2^*)∫_Ω|u_n|^{2^*}dx remain uniformly bounded, while ||u_n||_{L^∞(Ω)} -> ∞, for some fixed concentration value λ_* that is different from the concentration value predicted by Druet in the higher-dimensional regime?

Let Ω ⊂ R^N, N ≥ 3, be a smooth bounded domain, let 2^* = 2N/(N-2), and fix λ > 0. Suppose {u_n} is a family of solutions of
-Δu_n = λu_n + |u_n|^{2^*-2}u_n in Ω,  u_n = 0 on ∂Ω,
such that sup_n ∫_Ω |∇u_n|^2 dx < ∞ and ||u_n||_{L^∞(Ω)} → ∞. After passing to a subsequence, what asymptotic behavior can such fixed-parameter finite-energy blow-up families exhibit in a general bounded domain Ω? In particular, does additional geometry of Ω—such as convexity, or even strict star-shapedness—force a sharper classification or exclude some (or all) blow-up scenarios?

Let Ω ⊂ ℝ^N be a smooth bounded domain with nontrivial topology, let N ≥ 6, let λ ≥ 0 be fixed, and consider the Brezis-Nirenberg problem
-Δu = λu + |u|^{2^*-2}u in Ω,  u = 0 on ∂Ω,
where 2^* = 2N/(N-2). Can one construct sign-changing solutions exhibiting boundary concentration at this fixed parameter value, with asymptotic profile of nodal-cluster type
u \approx u_0 - \sum_j W_{μ_j,ξ_j},
where u_0 is the background solution and W_{μ_j,ξ_j} are the projected Aubin-Talenti bubbles concentrating near ∂Ω?

Let Omega be a smooth bounded domain in R^N with nontrivial topology, let 3 <= N <= 5, and let 2^* = 2N/(N-2). For each fixed lambda >= 0, does the Brezis-Nirenberg Dirichlet problem -Delta u = lambda u + |u|^(2^*-2)u in Omega, u = 0 on partial Omega, admit a family of sign-changing finite-energy solutions that blows up and concentrates at point(s) of the boundary partial Omega while lambda remains fixed?

Let Ω ⊂ ℝ^N be a smoothly bounded domain, with N ≥ 3, and consider the Brezis-Nirenberg Dirichlet problem −Δu = λu + |u|^{2^*−2}u in Ω, u = 0 on ∂Ω, where λ > 0 and 2^* = 2N/(N−2). Is it true that if there exists a family u_λ of bubble-tower solutions as λ → 0^+—that is, solutions whose blow-up profile contains at least two bubbles concentrating at the same point on different scales—then necessarily N ≥ 7? ([aimsciences.org](https://www.aimsciences.org/article/doi/10.3934/dcds.2026046))

Let Ω ⊂ ℝ^N be a smooth bounded domain, let 2* = 2N/(N-2), and consider the Brezis-Nirenberg problem
-Δu = λu + |u|^{2*-2}u in Ω,
u = 0 on ∂Ω,
for real-valued u, where the boundary condition is u = 0 on ∂Ω. Beyond the known bubble-tower regime associated with λ -> 0, does there exist, for a prescribed fixed parameter λ > 0 when N >= 4, and analogously for a prescribed fixed parameter λ > λ*(Ω) when N = 3, a sign-changing bubble-tower solution in a general smooth bounded domain Ω; that is, a nodal solution whose positive and negative bubbles concentrate at the same point with different scales?

Let Ω ⊂ R^4 be a smoothly bounded domain, let σ(-Δ) denote the Dirichlet spectrum of -Δ on H_0^1(Ω), and for λ > 0 consider the Brezis-Nirenberg problem
-Δu = λu + |u|^2u in Ω,  u = 0 on ∂Ω.
Does there exist, for every λ ∈ σ(-Δ), a sign-changing weak solution u ∈ H_0^1(Ω) that has least energy among all sign-changing solutions of this problem?

Let Omega be a smoothly bounded domain in R^3, and for lambda > 0 consider the Brezis-Nirenberg problem -Delta u = lambda u + |u|^4 u in Omega, u = 0 on partial Omega. Define E_lambda(u) = (1/2)||grad u||_{L^2(Omega)}^2 - (lambda/2)||u||_{L^2(Omega)}^2 - (1/6)||u||_{L^6(Omega)}^6 and N_sg = {u in H_0^1(Omega) minus {0} : u^+ != 0, u^- != 0, E'_lambda(u^+)u^+ = 0, E'_lambda(u^-)u^- = 0}. Does there exist, for every lambda > 0 and for a general bounded domain Omega (in particular, possibly convex or even strictly star-shaped), a sign-changing critical point u_hat in N_sg such that E'_lambda(u_hat) = 0 in H^{-1} and E_lambda(u_hat) = inf_{v in N_sg} E_lambda(v)?

Let Ω ⊂ ℝ^N be a smoothly bounded domain and λ > 0. Can the very recent results obtained for the classical Brezis-Nirenberg problem -Δu = λu + |u|^{2^*-2}u in Ω be generalized to the three Brezis-Nirenberg-type models explicitly listed in the paper, namely: the fractional critical problem (-Δ)^s u = λu + |u|^{2_s^*-2}u with 0 < s < 1 and 2_s^* = 2N/(N-2s), the higher-order critical problem (-Δ)^m u = λu + |u|^{2_m^*-2}u with m ≥ 2 and 2_m^* = 2N/(N-2m), and the critical p-Laplacian analogue with 1 < p < N and p^* = Np/(N-p), all posed on smooth bounded domains with the corresponding zero-boundary conditions?

For each positive integer r, classify up to poset isomorphism all r-differential posets; that is, determine all locally finite graded posets P with a unique minimum element such that (i) for any two distinct elements x,y in P, the number of elements covered by both x and y equals the number of elements that cover both x and y, and (ii) every element of P that covers exactly d elements is itself covered by exactly d + r elements.

Let SSYT be the rooted tree whose vertices are all shifted standard Young tableaux (including the empty tableau), where T is adjacent to U when T is contained in U and |U| = |T| + 1; equivalently, U is obtained from T by adding one new largest entry. For a vertex T and each d >= 0, let r_d(T) denote the number of vertices in the subtree rooted at T that lie at distance d from T. Determine whether every automorphism of the abstract underlying unlabeled tree SSYT is the identity, and whether the map T -> (r_0(T), r_1(T), r_2(T), ...) is injective; that is, whether each shifted standard Young tableau is uniquely determined by the census of rank sizes of its rooted subtree.

Let SYT be the rooted tree whose vertices are all unshifted standard Young tableaux, with tree structure generated by containment (equivalently, U is a child of T when U is obtained from T by adding one box containing the next largest entry). Regard SYT only as its underlying unlabeled tree. For each tableau T whose Young shape is symmetric, i.e. self-conjugate, the paper notes that there is an automorphism tau_T of this unlabeled tree that sends every vertex U in the subtree rooted at T to its transpose tableau U^t and fixes every vertex outside that subtree. Is every automorphism of the unlabeled tree SYT a composition of these transpose automorphisms tau_T? Moreover, if c_T(d) denotes the cardinality of rank d in the subtree rooted at T (equivalently, the number of descendants of T at distance d), does the sequence (c_T(d)) for d>=0 determine T up to transpose; that is, whenever c_T(d)=c_T'(d) for all d>=0, must T'=T or T'=T^t?

Fix a positive integer r. For the differential lattice of Young diagrams with at most r rows, Fomin’s general theory yields an RSK algorithm from the associated r-colored permutations to weighted pairs of corresponding tableaux. In close analogy with the classical theories for ordinary and shifted Young diagrams, can one extend this r-row theory by defining (i) a jeu de taquin for these tableaux and (ii) a Greene-type invariant for those r-colored permutations whose equivalence classes are exactly the sets of permutations having the same insertion tableau P?

Let λ range over strict partitions of n (equivalently, shifted Young diagrams of size n), let ℓ(λ) be the number of parts of λ, let g_λ denote the number of shifted Young tableaux of shape λ without coloring, and let c_λ = 2^{|λ| - ℓ(λ)}. For each weight w(λ) in {1, g_λ, g_λ^2, c_λ, g_λ c_λ, g_λ^2 c_λ}, define a probability measure on strict partitions of n by P_n^{(w)}(λ) proportional to w(λ). After rescaling the shifted diagram of λ by the factor 1/sqrt(n) in both coordinate directions, determine whether the random diagram has a deterministic limit shape as n tends to infinity, in the sense used for ordinary Young diagrams: the average rescaled diagrams converge, and for each fixed point, the probability of lying in the random rescaled diagram tends to 1 inside the limiting region and to 0 outside it. Determine the resulting limit shape(s) for these six shifted-diagram measures.

Fix a positive integer r.
