Using the RSK algorithm coming from the degree-r differential lattice of Young diagrams with at most r rows, which maps r-colored permutations to pairs of tableaux of common bounded-row shape with suitable weighting, determine the asymptotic behavior, as the size tends to infinity, of the resulting Young-diagram shapes, and from that asymptotic identify a scaling under which these bounded-row Young diagrams admit a well-defined limit-shape theory parallel to the classical theory for ordinary Young diagrams. ([theworld.com](https://theworld.com/~worley/Math/problem-notebook.pdf))

Let YF_r be the r-differential Young–Fibonacci lattice, and let YF_r^(k) denote its rank-k words (diagrams). Develop, in the sense of the ordinary Young-diagram limit-shape theory recalled in Problem 5, a limit-shape theory for YF_r by first defining a scaling between ranks—e.g. a doubling embedding D: YF_r^(k) -> YF_r^(2k) that is nearly isometric for the Hasse-diagram metric, meaning that it sends nearby words to nearby words, reflects nearness back to preimages, and has image coarsely dense in YF_r. In the resulting limit space, as n -> infinity, do the Young–Fibonacci diagrams associated with random r-colored permutations of size n admit a deterministic limit shape, under the three natural diagram distributions available because YF_r has unique weighting 1 as a dual graded graph? If so, determine that limit shape.

For a fixed integer k >= 1, let k-SYT be the infinite tree whose vertices are the ordinary standard Young tableaux T whose shapes have at most k rows, with an edge between T and U whenever U is obtained from T by adding one cell containing the new largest entry |T|+1 (equivalently, T is obtained from U by deleting its largest entry, or T is the restriction of U to the entries 1, ..., |T|). When this containment tree is regarded only as its underlying abstract unlabeled tree, determine its full automorphism group Aut(k-SYT).

Let SYFT be the tree whose vertices are standard Young–Fibonacci tableaux and whose edges are given by the containment relation; equivalently, SYFT is the tree of upward paths in the Young–Fibonacci lattice. Determine the full automorphism group Aut(SYFT) when SYFT is regarded purely as an unlabeled tree.

For a permutation w = a_1 ... a_n in S_n, let S_w in Z[x_1, x_2, ...] be the Schubert polynomial of w, and define nu_w := S_w(1,1,...) (equivalently, the sum of the coefficients of S_w). Is it true that nu_w = 2 if and only if there is exactly one triple 1 <= i < j < k <= n such that a_i < a_k < a_j; that is, w contains exactly one 132-pattern?

For each integer n >= 1, let S_n be the symmetric group on n letters. For each permutation w in S_n, let S_w denote the Schubert polynomial of w, and define nu_w := S_w(1, ..., 1), equivalently the sum of the coefficients of S_w. Let u(n) := max_{w in S_n} nu_w. Determine sharper asymptotic bounds for u(n): in particular, determine the exponential growth rate of u(n) on the scale 2^(c n^2), and decide whether there exists a constant alpha with 1/4 <= alpha <= 1/2 such that u(n) ~ 2^(alpha n^2) as n -> infty. The paper records the baseline bounds 1/4 <= liminf_{n->infty} log_2 u(n)/n^2 <= limsup_{n->infty} log_2 u(n)/n^2 <= 1/2, together with cited improvements of the lower bound to about 0.2932362762 and the upper bound to 0.37. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2509.25446))

For each integer n >= 1, let S_n be the symmetric group and, for w in S_n, let Sch_w denote the type-A Schubert polynomial of w. Define nu_w := Sch_w(1,1,...) (equivalently, the sum of the coefficients of Sch_w), and set u(n) := max_{w in S_n} nu_w. Determine the full maximizing set M_n := {w in S_n : nu_w = u(n)}. In particular, decide whether every maximizer is a Richardson/layered permutation of the form (i_1, i_1-1, ..., 2, 1, i_2, i_2-1, ..., i_1+1, i_3, ..., i_2+1, ...) for some i_1 < i_2 < ... < i_k = n. As n -> infinity, do the maximizers in M_n admit a limiting description or limit shape under the standard rescaling of their permutation plots (equivalently, permutation matrices) to [0,1]^2, and if so, what is it?

For each positive integer n, let u(n) := max_{w in S_n} ν_w, where S_n is the symmetric group on {1, ..., n}, S_w is the Schubert polynomial of w, and ν_w := S_w(1, 1, ...) is the sum of the coefficients of S_w. Is it true that every permutation w in S_n with ν_w = u(n) is a Richardson (equivalently, layered) permutation; that is, do there exist integers 1 <= i_1 < i_2 < ... < i_k = n such that w = (i_1, i_1 - 1, ..., 2, 1, i_2, i_2 - 1, ..., i_1 + 1, i_3, i_3 - 1, ..., i_2 + 1, ..., i_k, i_k - 1, ..., i_{k-1} + 1)?

Let S_w denote the Schubert polynomial of a permutation w, and define Upsilon_w := S_w(1,1,...) (equivalently, the sum of the coefficients of S_w). For permutations w in S_m and v in S_n, let w ⊗ v in S_mn be the permutation whose permutation matrix is the Kronecker product of the permutation matrices of w and v, and let 1_k denote the identity permutation in S_k. Is it true that for every permutation w and every integer k >= 2, one has Upsilon_{w ⊗ 1_k} >= (Upsilon_w)^(k^2)?

Fix a positive integer r, and let P be an r-differential poset; that is, P is a locally finite poset with minimum element hat{0} such that (i) if an element x covers k elements, then x is covered by exactly k+r elements, and (ii) if distinct elements x and y cover exactly t common elements, then exactly t elements cover both x and y. Is it true that P is a lattice, meaning that every pair of elements of P has both a meet and a join, if and only if P does not contain, as an induced subposet, a 9-element configuration consisting of a 3-crown {x,y,z} covering {a,b,c} (with x covering a,b; y covering b,c; z covering c,a) together with a second 3-crown {u,v,w} covering {x,y,z} (with u covering x,y; v covering y,z; w covering z,x), and with no other comparabilities among those nine elements?

For fixed integers r >= 1 and n >= 0, let P range over all r-differential posets in Stanley's standard sense, i.e. locally finite posets with a unique minimum 0-hat such that: (i) if an element covers k elements, then it is covered by k + r elements; and (ii) if two distinct elements both cover exactly t elements, then exactly t elements cover both of them. What is the minimum possible cardinality |P_n| of the nth rank P_n? Is this minimum attained by Y^{×r}, where Y denotes Young's lattice of integer partitions and Y^{×r} its r-fold Cartesian product? ([theworld.com](https://theworld.com/~worley/Math/problem-notebook.pdf))

For each integer n >= 1, let f(n) be the maximum possible number of meet-irreducible elements of a finite lattice L with exactly n join-irreducible elements; equivalently,

f(n)=max\{|M(L)| : L \text{ is a finite lattice and } |J(L)|=n\},

where J(L) and M(L) denote the sets of join-irreducible and meet-irreducible elements of L, respectively (so in a finite lattice, join-irreducible means covering exactly one element and meet-irreducible means being covered by exactly one element). Determine f(n).

For each integer n ≥ 0, let Λ_n be the finite poset of all integer partitions of n, ordered by refinement; that is, λ ≤ ρ if ρ can be obtained from λ by repeatedly merging parts, equivalently if the parts of λ can be grouped so that their group-sums are exactly the parts of ρ. Determine the poset Möbius function μ_{Λ_n}(λ,ρ) for every comparable pair λ ≤ ρ in Λ_n.

Classify, up to lattice isomorphism, all finite modular lattices L such that every closed interval [x,y] of L is self-dual, i.e. [x,y] is order-isomorphic to its dual interval [x,y]^*. Likewise, classify, up to lattice isomorphism, all finitary modular lattices L with finite covers—where finitary means that every principal ideal of L is finite, and finite covers means that each element has only finitely many upper covers and finitely many lower covers—such that every closed interval [x,y] of L is self-dual.

For each integer n >= 1, let S_n denote the set of permutations of [n], partially ordered by the strong Bruhat order. Determine exactly which intervals [u,v] = { w in S_n : u <= w <= v } are isomorphic to a finite Boolean lattice 2^[r] ordered by inclusion for some r >= 0, and, for each n, compute the total number of such intervals in S_n.

For each positive integer n, let SW_n denote the poset of all permutations of [n] ordered by the weak Bruhat order, and for u <= v in SW_n let [u,v] = {w in SW_n : u <= w <= v} be the corresponding interval with the induced order. Characterize exactly which intervals [u,v] are distributive lattices, and determine, as a function of n, the total number of intervals [u,v] in SW_n that are distributive lattices; the paper records the initial values 1, 2, 16, 124, 1262, 15898, 238572, 4152172 for 1 <= n <= 8.

Let P = disjoint union over i >= 0 of P_i be a graded, locally finite poset with a unique element of rank 0, and let r be a positive integer. Assume that P is an r-differential poset in the standard sense: if an element x covers m elements, then x is covered by exactly m + r elements; and if two distinct elements cover exactly k common elements, then they are covered by exactly k common elements. For each i >= 0, let p_i := |P_i| be the cardinality of rank i. Prove that p_i < p_{i+1} for every i >= 0, except in the unique case (r,i) = (1,0).

For each integer n >= 1, let A = C[x_1, ..., x_n, y_1, ..., y_n]. Let S_n act on A by w·f(x_1, ..., x_n, y_1, ..., y_n) = f(x_{w(1)}, ..., x_{w(n)}, y_{w(1)}, ..., y_{w(n)}) for every w in S_n. Let I = < f in A : w·f = f for all w in S_n and f(0) = 0 >, i.e. the ideal generated by the S_n-invariant polynomials of positive degree. Prove that the Catalan number C_n = (1/(n+1)) * binom(2n,n) satisfies C_n = dim { [f] in A/I : w·[f] = (sgn w)[f] for all w in S_n }.

For each integer n >= 1 and each partition lambda, let s_lambda(x1, ..., xn) denote the Schur polynomial in Z[x1, ..., xn] (with the usual convention that s_lambda(x1, ..., xn)=0 if ell(lambda) > n). What can be said in general about the size of its monomial support, namely the cardinality of {alpha in N^n : [x1^alpha1 ... xn^alphan] s_lambda(x1, ..., xn) != 0}, i.e. the number of distinct monomials that occur with nonzero coefficient in s_lambda(x1, ..., xn)?

Let Λ = Sym_Q be the ring of symmetric functions in variables x_1, x_2, ... equipped with the Hall inner product ⟨·,·⟩. Fix an integer n ≥ 1 and an integer k with 0 ≤ k ≤ binom(n,2). Let λ and μ be partitions of length at most n with μ ⊆ λ, and regard them as elements of Z^n by appending trailing zeros. Set δ := (n−1, n−2, ..., 1, 0). For w ∈ S_n, let ℓ(w) be its inversion number and ε_w := sgn(w). For α = (α_1, ..., α_n) ∈ Z^n, define h_α := ∏_{i=1}^n h_{α_i}, with the standard conventions h_0 = 1 and h_r = 0 for r < 0. Define

t_{λ/μ,k} := (−1)^k ∑_{w∈S_n, ℓ(w)≥k} ε_w h_{λ+δ−w(μ+δ)}.

This is the truncation of the Jacobi–Trudi expansion of the skew Schur function s_{λ/μ} obtained by keeping only those terms indexed by permutations w with ℓ(w) ≥ k. Since t_{λ/μ,k} is homogeneous of degree |λ|−|μ|, ask for each partition ν of |λ|−|μ|: is there a nice combinatorial interpretation of the Hall inner product ⟨t_{λ/μ,k}, s_ν⟩?

For a fixed integer n ≥ 1 and each partition λ ⊢ n, let ρ^λ : S_n → GL(f^λ, ℂ) be the irreducible representation of S_n with character χ^λ. Determine the number of partitions λ of n for which the image ρ^λ(S_n) is contained in SL(f^λ, ℂ).

For every finite group G of order g, define f:G→Z by f(w)=the number of pairs (u,v)∈G×G such that w=uvu^{-1}v^{-1}. Let Irr(G) denote the irreducible ordinary complex characters of G. Since f is a class function and, in fact, f=Σ_{χ∈Irr(G)} (g/χ(1))χ, find an explicit finite-dimensional complex G-module M whose character is exactly f. Such a construction should directly exhibit f as an actual ordinary character of G (the paper phrases this as showing that f is a "real character") and, by the linear independence of Irr(G), recover the divisibility χ(1) | |G| for every χ∈Irr(G).

For each integer n ≥ 1 and each partition λ ⊢ n, let ψ_{S_n} be the character of the action of the symmetric group S_n on itself by conjugation, i.e. of the permutation representation ρ: S_n → S_{S_n} defined by ρ(x)(y) = xyx^{-1}. Let χ^λ denote the irreducible character of S_n indexed by λ, and define κ_n^λ := ⟨ψ_{S_n}, χ^λ⟩, where ⟨·,·⟩ is the standard inner product of class functions on S_n. Since κ_n^λ > 0 except in the single case (n, λ) = (2, (1,1)), can one give a nice combinatorial interpretation of the numbers κ_n^λ?

For every Coxeter system (W,S) with S finite, let T=⋃_{w∈W} wSw^{-1} be the set of reflections and let ℓ:W→N be the Coxeter length function with respect to S. Is the Poincaré series of reflections
T(q):=∑_{t∈T} q^{ℓ(t)} ∈ Z[[q]]
rational, i.e. does T(q) belong to Q(q) (equivalently, can it be expressed as a ratio of two polynomials in q)?

Combinatorial Invariance Conjecture: Let (W1,S1) and (W2,S2) be Coxeter systems, let u,v be elements of W1 and w,z be elements of W2 with u ≤ v and w ≤ z in Bruhat order, and suppose the Bruhat intervals [u,v] = {x in W1 : u ≤ x ≤ v} and [w,z] = {y in W2 : w ≤ y ≤ z} are isomorphic as posets. If P_{u,v}(q), P_{w,z}(q) in Z[q] denote the ordinary Kazhdan-Lusztig polynomials, must one have P_{u,v}(q) = P_{w,z}(q)?

Let (W, S) be a Coxeter system, let ≤ denote the Bruhat order on W, and let P_{x,y}(q) \in Z[q] denote the ordinary Kazhdan–Lusztig polynomial of W. For every pair u, v \in W with u ≤ v, does there exist a Coxeter system (W', S') and an element w \in W' such that P_{u,v}(q) = P_{e,w}(q), where e is the identity element of W'?

Given a Coxeter system (W,S) and elements u,v∈W with u≤v in the Bruhat order, construct, in an explicit combinatorial way, a set M(u,v) and a statistic s:M(u,v)→N such that the ordinary Kazhdan–Lusztig polynomial P_{u,v}(q)=P^{∅,-1}_{u,v}(q)=P^{∅,q}_{u,v}(q)∈Z[q] satisfies P_{u,v}(q)=Σ_{a∈M(u,v)} q^{s(a)} for every such pair u≤v. ([mat.uniroma2.it](https://www.mat.uniroma2.it/~brenti/65.pdf))

Let L be a lattice. Call L linear if there exists a set X and a lattice embedding e: L -> Eq(X) into the lattice of equivalence relations on X such that for every a, b in L, the equivalence relations e(a) and e(b) permute. Is the class of all linear lattices self-dual; equivalently, whenever L is linear, must the dual lattice L^op also be linear?
Is the class of all linear lattices—that is, all lattices isomorphic to lattices of commuting equivalence relations on some set—an equational class of lattices (equivalently, a variety)?

Does there exist a lattice L that satisfies every higher-dimensional Arguesian law (i.e. all orders of the Arguesian law) but is not linear, meaning that L is not isomorphic to any lattice of pairwise commuting equivalence relations on a set? If such a lattice exists, can one be chosen finite?

Let C be the class of lattices L for which there exists a group G such that L is isomorphic to a sublattice of the lattice N(G) of normal subgroups of G, ordered by inclusion. Is C self-dual; that is, whenever L belongs to C, must the dual lattice L^op also belong to C?

Let K be the class of all lattices L such that there exists a group G for which L is lattice-isomorphic to a sublattice of N(G), the lattice of normal subgroups of G ordered by inclusion. Is K a variety of lattices; that is, is there a set of lattice identities whose models are exactly the lattices in K?

Let L be an abstract lattice. Suppose there exists an Abelian group A such that L is isomorphic to a sublattice of the subgroup lattice Sub(A), ordered by inclusion. Must the dual lattice L^op also be isomorphic to a sublattice of Sub(B) for some Abelian group B?

Let K be the class of all lattices L for which there exists an Abelian group G such that L is lattice-isomorphic to a sublattice of the subgroup lattice Sub(G). Is K a variety of lattices, that is, is K definable by a set of lattice identities in the language {meet, join}?

Please provide the correct arXiv identifier: arXiv:2509.25446 is a tableaux-combinatorics problem notebook and does not contain the lattice-representation question in your draft, so a paper-faithful stand-alone refinement cannot be produced from this source.

Let r=(r_0,r_1,r_2,...) be an infinite sequence of integers, and let L(r), if it exists, denote the unique up to isomorphism distributive lattice that is r-differential in Stanley's sense: L(r) is a locally finite graded poset with a least element such that (i) for any distinct elements x and y, the number of elements covered by both x and y equals the number of elements covering both x and y, and (ii) every element x of rank i that covers exactly k elements is itself covered by exactly k+r_i elements. Stanley notes that L(r) exists whenever the sequence r_0,r_1,r_2,... increases "sufficiently fast." Can one describe precisely the necessary rate of growth of the sequence r_i for the existence of L(r)?

Fix r in Z_{>0}. In the r-differential Young–Fibonacci lattice YF_r, does there exist an infinite chain p_0 < p_1 < p_2 < \cdots such that, for every k >= 0, the closed intervals [p_n, p_{n+k}] are pairwise isomorphic as posets for all n >= 0? If such a chain exists, can it be used, in the same role that the translated partitions lambda+n play in Young’s lattice, to prove a Young–Fibonacci analogue of Liang–Sagan’s Theorem 3.1—namely, that the interval-cardinality sequence a_k := #[p_0, p_k] is log-concave—and would such a result suggest some semidistributive-type property of YF_r?

Let P be a distributive lattice that is also a sequentially differential poset in the sense referenced in [Stan1990, sec. 2], and suppose its associated r-vector (r_0, ..., r_{N-1}) is an arithmetic progression r_i = r_0 + iΔ with Δ < 0, so that P is necessarily finite in the setting of Problem 44. Besides the Cartesian powers of the 2-element chain and of the 3-element chain, do any such finite distributive differential lattices exist, and can all cases with negative common difference Δ be classified completely?

Let K be a field, let V = ⊕_{n>=0} V_n be an N-graded K-vector space, and let D:V→V be a K-linear map of degree -1, meaning that D(V_0)=0 and D(V_n)⊆V_{n-1} for every n>=1. Must there exist an associative K-bilinear product V×V→V and a unit 1 in V_0 such that V becomes a unital graded K-algebra with V_i V_j⊆V_{i+j} for all i,j>=0, and such that D is a derivation of this algebra, i.e. D(ab)=D(a)b+aD(b) for all a,b in V?

Open problem. Let G : {e} = G_0 ⊂ G_1 ⊂ G_2 ⊂ ··· be a tower of finite groups. Let R(G) = ⊕_{n≥0} R(G_n), where R(G_n) is the complex representation ring of G_n, and let Ind, Res : R(G) → R(G) be the operators induced by induction and restriction along G_n ⊂ G_{n+1}. Let P(G) be the Bratteli (splitting) diagram of the tower: its vertices are the irreducible complex representations of the groups G_n, and the multiplicity of an edge records the corresponding branching multiplicity. Fix r ∈ Z_{>0}. Assume G is an r-dual tower of groups, meaning that Res Ind - Ind Res = rI on R(G); if, in addition, every branching multiplicity is 0 or 1, call G an r-differential tower of groups. Is it true that: (a) if G is r-differential, then P(G) is isomorphic, as a graded graph, to the r-fold Cartesian product Y^r of Young's lattice, and there exists a fixed abelian group A of order r such that G_n ≅ A wr S_n for every n > 0; and (b) if G is r-dual, then P(G) is isomorphic to (d_1Y) × ··· × (d_kY), where dY denotes the graded graph with underlying simple graph Y and all edge multiplicities multiplied by d, and there exists a fixed finite group H of order r such that G_n ≅ H wr S_n for every n > 0? ([combinatorics.org](https://www.combinatorics.org/ojs/index.php/eljc/article/download/v26i1p25/pdf/))

Let Ω be a simply connected open subset of R^n that is two-convex, meaning that for every 3-simplex Δ in R^n, if three faces of Δ lie in Ω, then Δ is contained in Ω. Is it true that for every affine 2-plane L in R^n, every connected component of Ω ∩ L is simply connected?

For each integer n>=2, let H_n=\bigcup_{1\le i<j\le n}\{(z_1,\dots,z_n)\in\mathbb{C}^n:z_i=z_j\}, let W_n=\mathbb{C}^n\setminus H_n with the path metric induced by the standard Euclidean metric on \mathbb{C}^n, and let B_n be the metric completion of the universal metric covering of W_n. Is B_n a CAT(0) space for every n?

Let M be a compact simply connected Riemannian manifold. Suppose that M is isometric, with the quotient metric, to H/Γ for some Hilbert space H and some group Γ of isometries of H; more generally, suppose only that there exists a Riemannian submersion H → M from a Hilbert space H. Must M be isometric to a quotient of a compact Lie group endowed with a bi-invariant metric by a group of isometries?

Characterize the Riemannian metrics g on S^n for which there exist an integer k ≥ 0, a Euclidean space R^N, and a chain of subsets Σ_0 ⊂ Σ_1 ⊂ ... ⊂ Σ_k ⊂ R^N such that, for each i < k, Σ_i is a complete smooth convex hypersurface in Σ_{i+1}, Σ_k is a complete smooth convex hypersurface in R^N, each Σ_i carries the metric induced from its ambient space, and the Riemannian manifold (S^n, g) is isometric to Σ_0.

Let n ≥ 1, let E^n be n-dimensional Euclidean space, and let Γ act effectively, isometrically, and totally discontinuously on E^n. Is it true that Γ has at most 2^n conjugacy classes of finite subgroups that are maximal with respect to inclusion among finite subgroups of Γ?

Let K be a compact connected subset of R^n, and let p,q in K. Is it true that for every epsilon>0 there exists a continuous curve gamma:[0,1]->R^n with gamma(0)=p and gamma(1)=q such that the portion of gamma lying in R^n\K has total Euclidean length less than epsilon?

Let (S^3,g) be a Riemannian manifold diffeomorphic to the 3-sphere such that sec_g >= 1 everywhere. Suppose there exists an isometric involution iota:(S^3,g) -> (S^3,g) with iota^2 = id whose fixed-point set is a closed geodesic gamma, i.e. Fix(iota) = gamma. Must one have length_g(gamma) <= 2*pi?

Let d be the distance function of the Fubini–Study metric on the complex projective plane CP^2. Does there exist a sequence {d_n}_{n>=1} of polyhedral length metrics on the fixed manifold CP^2 such that, for each n, every simplex in some triangulation of CP^2 is isometric to a Euclidean simplex, the total angle around every codimension-two simplex is at most 2π (equivalently, d_n has Alexandrov curvature >= 0), and d_n(x,y) -> d(x,y) for all x,y in CP^2? ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2510.11908))

Let O_3 be the 1-skeleton of the octahedron, with opposite pairs (x,x'), (y,y'), and (z,z'). Say that a geodesic metric space X satisfies O_3-comparison if for every six-point configuration x, x', y, y', z, z' in X there exists a corresponding six-point configuration in a real Hilbert space H such that the distances between corresponding edge-pairs of O_3 do not increase, while the distances between the three opposite pairs xx', yy', and zz' do not decrease. Must every geodesic metric space satisfy O_3-comparison?

Does there exist an integer N such that, for every n >= N, the n-dimensional Lobachevsky (real hyperbolic) space admits a discrete cocompact subgroup Γ of its isometry group Isom(H^n) such that Γ is generated by elements of finite order? ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2510.11908))

Does there exist an integer N such that, for every n >= N, the n-dimensional Lobachevsky (real hyperbolic) space H^n admits a cocompact action by a discrete subgroup Γ <= Isom(H^n) such that Γ is generated by central symmetries, i.e. point-reflection involutions?

For each fixed integer k>=2, does there exist N(k) such that for every n>=N(k), the real hyperbolic space H^n admits a discrete cocompact subgroup Gamma<=Isom(H^n) generated by isometries whose fixed-point sets are totally geodesic subspaces of codimension k?

Let Ω ⊂ S² be a round geodesic disc of radius α, where 0 < α < π/2, on the unit sphere S² with its standard spherical metric, and let Ω′ ⊂ S² be a geodesically convex domain whose spherical area equals that of Ω. Show that there exists a map f: Ω′ → ℝ² such that for all x,y ∈ Ω′, one has d_{S²}(x,y) ≤ |f(x) - f(y)| ≤ (α/sin(α)) d_{S²}(x,y), where d_{S²} denotes the spherical geodesic distance and |·| the Euclidean distance. In other words, Ω′ admits a (1, α/sin(α))-bi-Lipschitz map to the Euclidean plane.

Let X be a complete CAT(0) length space, and let K be a compact subset of X. A subset C of X is called convex if every geodesic joining two points of C is contained in C. Is the closed convex hull of K—that is, the intersection of all closed convex subsets of X that contain K—necessarily compact, even without assuming that X is locally compact? ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2510.11908))

Let T^2 be the 2-dimensional torus. Call a homeomorphism h ∈ Homeo(T^2) simple if there exists an embedded open disc D ⊂ T^2 such that h|_{T^2 \setminus D} = id. Define the disc norm of h to be the least integer n such that h can be written as h = h1 ∘ ··· ∘ hn with each hi simple. Is it true that for every N ∈ N there exists a homeomorphism h : T^2 → T^2 whose disc norm is at least N?

Let D^n denote the closed n-dimensional ball. Does there exist an embedding e:D^4 -> S^2 × R^2 such that the restricted first-factor projection pr_1 ∘ e:D^4 -> S^2 is an open map; that is, for every open subset U of D^4 (in the subspace topology), (pr_1 ∘ e)(U) is open in S^2?

Let M be a closed connected orientable surface of genus 2 equipped with a Riemannian metric whose Gaussian curvature K satisfies K ≤ 0 everywhere. If one chooses an initial unit tangent vector v in the unit tangent bundle SM according to normalized Liouville measure and lets γv : R → M be the corresponding complete geodesic, is it true that for Liouville-almost every v the geodesic γv intersects the set {x in M : K(x) < 0}?

Let (M,g) be a simply connected complete Riemannian manifold and let p∈M. Define the symmetric 2-tensor h=exp_p^*g on T_pM by h_v(ξ,η)=g_{exp_p(v)}((d exp_p)_v ξ,(d exp_p)_v η); in general h may be degenerate at points v where d exp_p is singular. If (M',g',p') is another simply connected complete Riemannian manifold and there exists a linear isomorphism L:T_pM→T_{p'}M' such that L^*(exp_{p'}^*g')=exp_p^*g, must there exist an isometry F:(M,g)→(M',g') with F(p)=p'? Equivalently, does the possibly degenerate tensor h determine the pointed manifold (M,g,p) up to pointed isometry?

Let V be a bounded body in R^3 whose boundary consists of two plane figures F1 and F2 (the ends) and a smooth surface Sigma (the tube). Assume that V is an optical fiber in the sense of Section 17: a light ray entering V through one end and reflecting perfectly from the interior wall exits through the other end with probability 1, and any light ray starting in the interior of V exits through one of the two ends with probability 1. Must every such optical fiber admit a slicing into plane figures that meet the walls at right angles?

Does there exist a body Ω ⊂ R^3 bounded by two plane figures E0 and E1 and a smooth lateral surface Σ such that, under perfect specular reflection from Σ, a light ray entering Ω through one end exits through the other end with probability 1, and a light ray originating in the interior of Ω exits through one of the two ends with probability 1, but the end figures E0 and E1 are not congruent?

For a fixed integer n ≥ 1, does there exist a constant ε_n > 0 such that every open set U ⊂ R^n with n-dimensional Lebesgue measure vol_n(U) ≤ ε_n admits an embedding f: U → B^n(1), where B^n(1) is the Euclidean unit n-ball, that is length-increasing with respect to the ambient Euclidean length structures; that is, Length(f∘γ) ≥ Length(γ) for every rectifiable curve γ in U? ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2510.11908))

Let (eta_t)_{t>=0} be the one-dimensional Fredrickson-Andersen one-spin facilitated process (FA-1) on Z, with state space {0,1}^Z, in which a site x may refresh only if at least one of its nearest neighbors x-1 or x+1 is infected, and upon a legal refresh the site becomes infected with probability q and healthy with probability 1-q, independently of the past. Let pi be the Bernoulli product equilibrium measure with infected density q, where q in (0,1). Is it true that, for every initial probability measure nu on {0,1}^Z satisfying nu(there exists at least one infected vertex)=1, and for every local function f:{0,1}^Z->R depending on finitely many coordinates, one has lim_{t->infinity} |E_nu[f(eta_t)] - pi(f)| = 0?

For the one-dimensional Fredrickson-Andersen one-spin facilitated model (FA-1f) on Z, with state space {0,1}^Z, infected sites given by η_x=0, healthy sites by η_x=1, constraint c_x(η)=1_{η_{x-1}=0 or η_{x+1}=0}, and reversible Bernoulli product measure π=Ber(q)^{\otimes Z} with q in (0,1), suppose the initial law ν satisfies ν([-L,L] is healthy)=O(e^{-κL}) for some κ>0 and all sufficiently large L. Is it true that, for every local function f depending on finitely many vertices, the convergence in equation (1.1), namely E_ν[f(η(t))] -> π(f) as t -> infinity, actually occurs at an exponential rate; equivalently, do there exist constants C_f,c_f>0 such that |E_ν[f(η(t))]-π(f)| <= C_f e^{-c_f t} for all t>=0?

Let (η_t) be a kinetically constrained model on Ω = {0,1}^{Z^d} whose update constraint c_x is local of finite range and does not depend on η_x, and let π be its Bernoulli product reversible measure (with infected density q ∈ (0,1), equivalently healthy density p = 1 - q). Let BP denote the associated bootstrap-percolation map obtained by iteratively emptying every site whose KCM constraint is satisfied, and let E := {β ∈ Ω : BP(β) = β} be the set of BP-stable configurations. For each β ∈ E, write π_β := π(· | BP(η) = β). If μ is a stationary measure of the KCM, must there exist a probability measure μ_* on E such that μ = ∫_E π_β dμ_*(β)?

For each positive integer n, let r_nn(n) be the least integer m such that every red-blue coloring of the edges of the ordered complete graph on [m] = {1,2,...,m} contains a monochromatic matching M_n whose edges are pairwise non-nested; that is, no two edges ab and cd of the matching satisfy a < c < d < b or c < a < b < d. Determine r_nn(n); in particular, is r_nn(n) = 3n - 1?

Let G_n be the random 4-regular graph considered in Section 2 of the paper, obtained by taking the union of two independent uniformly random Hamiltonian cycles on the same labeled n-vertex set (so formally this may be a multigraph if the cycles share edges). For the graph polynomial P_{G_n} = ∏_{uv∈E(G_n)} (u-v), where the variables are the vertices of G_n, is it true that as n → ∞ the coefficient of the monomial ∏_{v∈V(G_n)} v^2 is asymptotically almost surely non-zero?

For each n, let G_n be the random 4-regular graph model used in Section 2 of the paper: the union of two independent uniformly random Hamilton cycles on the labeled vertex set [n] (so, formally, a multigraph; if a double edge occurs, count it with multiplicity in the product below). In the commutative polynomial ring Z[x_1, ..., x_n], define the graph polynomial P_{G_n} = prod_{uv in E(G_n)} (x_u - x_v), where x_i is the variable corresponding to vertex i. Since G_n is 4-regular, P_{G_n} is homogeneous of total degree |E(G_n)| = 2n, so in the Alon-Tarsi criterion for k = 3 the only degree-compatible monomial is x_1^2 x_2^2 ... x_n^2. Is it true that Pr(the coefficient of x_1^2 x_2^2 ... x_n^2 in P_{G_n} is nonzero) tends to 1 as n -> infinity?

For every integer m >= 1, every simple 2-regular graph C on 4m vertices, and every spanning graph K on V(C) whose connected components are m vertex-disjoint copies of K_4, must the graph C ∪ K satisfy χ(C ∪ K) <= 4?

Does every diamond-free claw-free cubic graph H admit a strong edge-coloring with 6 colors, where a strong edge-coloring is an edge-coloring in which any two edges that are adjacent or adjacent to a common edge receive distinct colors?

Let G be a cubic graph (that is, a 3-regular graph). A proper vertex coloring c of G is called 2-homogeneous if for every vertex v in V(G), exactly two distinct colors appear on the open neighborhood N(v), i.e. |{c(u) : u in N(v)}| = 2. If G admits a 2-homogeneous coloring, must G admit a 2-homogeneous coloring with at most 4 colors? ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2511.02892))

Let G be a finite connected bridgeless cubic graph. Are there only finitely many such graphs for which no proper vertex-coloring c: V(G) -> C satisfies |c(N(v))| = 2 for every vertex v in V(G), where N(v) denotes the open neighborhood of v?

Fix an orientation of the edges of a snark S. For A in {Z_2^2, Z_4}, call S almost-A-connected if for every nonzero map b: V(S) -> A with sum_{v in V(S)} b(v) = 0, there exists a map f: E(S) -> A \ {0} such that ∂f = b, where ∂f(v) is the sum of f(e) over edges leaving v minus the sum of f(e) over edges entering v. A snark is a cubic non-3-edge-colourable cyclically 4-edge-connected graph of girth at least 5, and it is bicritical if deleting any two distinct vertices yields a 3-edge-colourable graph. Is every bicritical snark almost-Z_2^2-connected and almost-Z_4-connected?

Does there exist a dimension d and a Poisson bivector P on the real affine space R^d such that Kontsevich's tetrahedral cocycle γ3 induces a genuinely nontrivial infinitesimal deformation Ṗ = Q_{γ3}(P^{⊗4}), in the sense that there is no vector field X on R^d with Q_{γ3}(P^{⊗4}) = [[P, X]]; equivalently, the first-order family P_t = P + t Q_{γ3}(P^{⊗4}) + O(t^2) is not obtained from P by a coordinate change and therefore yields inequivalent Poisson structures? ([bjp-bg.com](https://www.bjp-bg.com/papers/bjp2025_s1_090-095.pdf))

Let P = P[ρ,a_1,...,a_{d-2}] be the Poisson bivector on the affine space R^d corresponding to the Nambu-determinant bracket {f,g}_d(x) = ρ(x) det(∂(f,g,a_1,...,a_{d-2})/∂(x^1,...,x^d)), where f, g, a_i ∈ C^1(R^d) and the a_i are Casimirs. Assuming, as in the paper’s higher-dimensional setting, that Kontsevich’s tetrahedral cocycle γ3 restricts to this Nambu subset for d > 3, does the induced infinitesimal deformation Ṗ = Q_{γ3}(P^{⊗4}) become genuinely nontrivial in the unresolved higher-dimensional cases, or is it always infinitesimally trivial, i.e. generated by a coordinate change along some dimension-dependent vector field X_d^{γ3}(P^{⊗3}) on R^d satisfying Q_{γ3}(P^{⊗4}) = [[P, X_d^{γ3}(P^{⊗3})]]?

Let d > 3 be fixed, and let P be a Nambu–Poisson bivector on affine R^d determined by the Jacobian-determinant bracket {f,g}_d(x) = rho(x) det(∂(f,g,a_1,...,a_{d-2})/∂(x_1,...,x_d)), where a_1,...,a_{d-2} are Casimirs. For Kontsevich’s tetrahedral graph cocycle gamma_3, does the induced tetrahedral flow Pdot = Q_{gamma_3}^d(P⊗4) define a genuinely nontrivial infinitesimal deformation of P on this Nambu–Poisson class, or does there exist a differential-polynomial vector field X_{gamma_3}^d(P⊗3) on R^d such that Q_{gamma_3}^d(P⊗4) = [[P, X_{gamma_3}^d(P⊗3)]], where [[.,.]] is the Schouten bracket, so that the deformation is only an infinitesimal coordinate change? ([bjp-bg.com](https://www.bjp-bg.com/papers/bjp2025_s1_090-095.pdf))

For each fixed d >= 2, let P be the Nambu-determinant Poisson bivector on the affine space R^{d+1}, defined by {f,g}_{d+1}(x) = ϱ(x) det(∂(f,g,a_1,...,a_{d-1})/∂(x^1,...,x^{d+1})). Assume that the tetrahedral Kontsevich γ3-flow on this Nambu class is Poisson-trivial in dimension d+1, i.e. there exists a cubic 1-vector X_{γ3}^{d+1}(P^{⊗3}) such that Q_{γ3}^{d+1}(P^{⊗4}) = [[P, X_{γ3}^{d+1}(P^{⊗3})]]. Must one then be able to choose X_{γ3}^{d+1} as an R-linear combination of the (iterated) (d+1)-dimensional Nambu micro-graph descendants of the two-dimensional sunflower graph X_{γ3}^{d=2} = (0,1;1,3;1,2) + 2·(0,2;1,3;1,2), where “descendants” are understood in the sense of Section 2 via adjoining the new Casimir and expanding the relevant arrows by Leibniz rule? ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2511.06121))

Let P be a Nambu-determinant Poisson bivector on the affine space R^{d+1}, given by {f,g}_{d+1}(x) = rho(x) det(partial(f,g,a_1,...,a_{d-1}) / partial(x^1,...,x^{d+1})). Assume that the restricted tetrahedral flow in dimension d+1 is trivial on this Nambu class, so that Q_{gamma_3}^{d+1}(P^{tensor 4}) = [[P, X_{gamma_3}^{d+1}(P^{tensor 3})]], and assume further that X_{gamma_3}^{d+1} is sought as a linear combination of (d+1)-dimensional descendants of the 2D sunflower graph X^{gamma_3} = (0,1;1,3;1,2) + 2·(0,2;1,3;1,2). Is it then sufficient to search for X_{gamma_3}^{d+1} only in the union of (i) the (d+1)-descendants of the underlying d-dimensional solution X_{gamma_3}^d and (ii) the (d+1)-descendants of vanishing 1-vector Nambu micro-graphs over R^d, where 'descendant' is understood in the paper’s d to d+1 sense of adjoining the new Casimir and expanding by the Leibniz rule?

For the Nambu–Poisson brackets {f,g}_k(x)=ρ(x)·det(∂(f,g,a1,…,a_{k−2})/∂(x1,…,xk))(x) on affine real space R^k, consider the dimensional step d→d+1 with d≥3 and the tetrahedral cocycle trivialization problem Q^{γ3}_{d+1}(P)=[[P, X^{γ3}_{d+1}(P)]]. Working with 1-vector Nambu micro-graphs built from m=1 sink and n=3 copies of the Nambu bracket, and defining descendants by adjoining to each Levi-Civita vertex a new Casimir a_{d−1} and expanding every incoming edge that previously hit a Casimir via the Leibniz rule, suppose one seeks X^{γ3}_{d+1} over the union of the (d+1)-descendants of the underlying d-dimensional solution X^{γ3}_d and some indispensable vanishing d-dimensional micro-graphs Γ with φ(Γ)=0. Must every such indispensable vanishing d-dimensional micro-graph arise as a d-descendant of a vanishing (d−1)-dimensional Nambu micro-graph, or can indispensable vanishing micro-graphs first appear in dimension d by a genuinely new vanishing mechanism?

In the setting of Kontsevich’s tetrahedral graph-cocycle flow on the Nambu-determinant Poisson brackets {f,g}_d(x)=rho(x) det(partial(f,g,a_1,...,a_{d-2})/partial(x_1,...,x_d)) on R^d for d >= 3, determine a conceptual criterion, expressed in terms of the automorphism group and the topology of the underlying directed Nambu micro-graph, that explains exactly when a Nambu micro-graph Gamma built from whole copies of bracket (1), or an R-linear combination of such micro-graphs, has identically vanishing encoded formula phi(Gamma)=0; in particular, account both for vanishing caused by an automorphism with Gamma congruent to -Gamma and for the symmetry-free pairwise cancellations observed for nonzero graphs with Aut(Gamma) = {1}. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2511.06121))
Determine whether there exist positive integers A > B such that A, B, A + B, and A - B are all perfect squares; if so, exhibit such a pair.

Determine whether there exist positive integers a, b, c, d such that a, b, and c are perfect squares, a + b + c = d^2, and a^2 + b^2 = c^2, b^2 + c^2 = a^2, and c^2 + a^2 = b^2. If such nonzero square numbers exist, find them; otherwise prove that no such triple exists.

Does there exist a nondegenerate right triangle whose three side lengths are all perfect squares; equivalently, do there exist positive integers x, y, z such that the side lengths are x^2, y^2, z^2 and (x^2)^2 + (y^2)^2 = (z^2)^2?

Given a prescribed rational number N, determine all rational solutions (x,y) with x+y=10 and xy≠0 such that x((x/y)+(y/x))^2=N, where x is the part chosen for the final multiplication. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/html/2511.08400v1))

In the arithmetic setting of Ibn al-Khawwām’s problem, determine whether there exist two positive rational numbers x and y such that x+y=10 and x*sqrt(x)+y*sqrt(y)=26; if such numbers exist, find them exactly.
Find positive integers a, b, c, d such that a^2, b^2, c^2 are in continued geometric proportion (that is, a^2:b^2 = b^2:c^2) and a^2 + b^2 + c^2 = d^2.
Determine whether there exist positive integers a and b, each a perfect square, such that a(a + b) = b^2.

Determine whether there exists an ordered quadruple of square numbers with the following multiplicative self-reproduction property: starting from the first square, multiply successively by the first, then by the second, then by the third, and finally by the fourth, in such a way that the successive results reproduce the original four square numbers.
Determine whether there exist nonnegative rational numbers u, v, r, s such that u^2 + v^2 = 10, u^2 + u = r^2, and v^2 + v = s^2.

Determine whether there exist positive integers x and y such that y^3 = x^3 + 1; in other words, does there exist a positive perfect cube which becomes another positive perfect cube after adding one unit (one dirham)?

Determine whether there exist positive rational numbers a, b, c such that a and b are cubes and a/b + b/a = c^2; equivalently, do there exist positive rational numbers x, y, z satisfying x^3/y^3 + y^3/x^3 = z^2?

Find positive integers x, y, and a, with x,y nonzero, such that x^2((x^2)/(y^2) + (y^2)/(x^2)) = a^2; in other words, find two nonzero square numbers for which the sum of their reciprocal quotients, when multiplied by one of the two squares, is itself a perfect square.

Given a prescribed number N, determine all positive rational numbers x and y with 0 < x < y and x+y=10 such that, after dividing the smaller part by the larger part, adding that quotient to the larger part, and multiplying the result by the smaller part, one obtains N; equivalently, determine all positive rational solutions of x(y + x/y) = N under x+y=10 and x<y.

Determine whether there exists a positive integer N that is a perfect square such that N - 10√N - 10 is also a perfect square; if so, exhibit such an N. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/html/2511.08400v1))
Determine all pairs (x,y) of nonnegative rational numbers, interpreted as inheritance amounts in dirhams, such that x = 10 - √y and y = 5 - √x, where √ denotes the principal nonnegative square root.
Determine whether there exists a rational number x such that x, x+10, and x-10 are all squares of rational numbers.

Determine whether there exist rational numbers x, y, z such that x^2 + x + 2 = y^2 and x^2 - x - 2 = z^2; equivalently, find a square quantity for which adding its root and 2 dirhams yields a square, and subtracting its root and 2 dirhams also yields a square.
Determine a positive rational square a such that, if x = sqrt(a), then a + 10x + 20 is also a positive rational square.

Find a positive square number N such that, if one subtracts its positive square root sqrt(N) from N and then multiplies the remainder by sqrt(N), the product is again N; in modern notation, find N with N a square and (N - sqrt(N))·sqrt(N) = N.
Determine all positive real numbers x>y such that x-y = 10 sqrt(y) and x/y + y/x = sqrt(y), where y is the smaller of the two numbers.
Determine whether there exist positive integers n and m such that n is a perfect cube and n^2-n=m^2; if so, exhibit such an n.

Given positive rational numbers N and M, determine whether there exist positive rational numbers x>y such that x+y=N and N/x + N/y + N/(x-y)=M; if so, find such a decomposition of N into the two parts x and y.

Given a prescribed positive rational number a, find positive rational numbers x and y such that a = x^3 + y^2; equivalently, decompose a into two positive parts, one a rational perfect cube and the other a rational perfect square, if such a decomposition exists.
Given a number n, can one decompose it into two cubic numbers; equivalently, do there exist x and y such that x^3 + y^3 = n?
Does there exist a positive square S, written S = x^2 with x > 0, such that the remainder S - S/3 - x is itself a square, say y^2, and its positive root y satisfies 10y = S/3 + x? If so, determine S.

Given positive integers a and b, find all positive rational numbers x and positive integers y such that x is the price of one robe (in dirhams), y is the number of robes, the total value is xy = a, and the price of one robe plus the square root of the number of robes satisfies x + sqrt(y) = b. Equivalently: decide whether such robes exist for the given a and b, and if they do, determine both the number of robes y and the unit price x.

Given a prescribed positive rational number N, determine whether there exist positive rational numbers A, B, and C, each of which is a perfect cube, such that ABC = N; if such cubes exist, construct them. This is the closest modern stand-alone rendering of Section 5.6, Problem 30. ([ar5iv.labs.arxiv.org](https://ar5iv.labs.arxiv.org/html/2511.08400v1))

Given a known amount a > 0 of dirhams, determine the unknown positive monthly salary x of an employee, measured in dirhams, under the assumptions that the month has 30 days, the employee worked √x days, and the pay received is proportional to the number of days worked.
Find nonzero rational numbers x and y such that x+y=10 and x/y + y/x = x.
For a given positive integer d, determine all positive rational numbers x and y with x > y and x + y = 10 such that x^2/y - y^2/x = d.

Let r>0 and let M=\partial B_R(O)\subset \mathbb{R}^2 be a circumference of radius R centered at O, with r<R<4.98r. Classify all connected compact sets \Sigma\subset \mathbb{R}^2 that minimize \mathcal{H}^1(\Sigma) among all connected compact sets satisfying \max_{y\in M}\operatorname{dist}(y,\Sigma)\le r (equivalently, M\subset \overline{B_r(\Sigma)}). In other words, determine the maximal distance minimizers for a circumference in the open range r<R<4.98r.

In the planar maximal-distance-minimizer problem, fix r>0 and let M⊂R^2 be an R-stadium, meaning the boundary of the closed R-neighborhood of a line segment. Determine the set of all r-minimizers Σ for M in the open regime r<R<5r. More sharply, determine the sharp constant C_*:=sup{C>0: for some Cr-stadium there exists an r-minimizer that is not a horseshoe} and the sharp constant c_*:=inf{c>0: for every closed convex curve M with minimal radius of curvature at least c r, every r-minimizer for M is a horseshoe}, where a horseshoe is the union of an arc of the inner parallel curve of M at distance r and two tangent segments at the endpoints of that arc. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/html/2511.18217v1))

For every integer d ≥ 3, every compact set M ⊂ R^d, and every r > 0, if Σ ⊂ R^d is a maximal distance minimizer for M at scale r—that is, Σ is a connected compact set minimizing H^1(Γ) among all connected compact sets Γ ⊂ R^d such that M ⊂ B_r(Γ), where B_r(Γ) denotes the closed r-neighborhood of Γ—must Σ be expressible as a union of finitely many injective curves?

Let d\ge 1, let r>0, and let M\subset\mathbb{R}^d be compact. Suppose \Sigma\subset\mathbb{R}^d is a connected compact set with minimal one-dimensional Hausdorff measure \mathcal H^1 among all connected compact sets \Gamma satisfying M\subset\overline{B_r(\Gamma)}. Must \Sigma be the unique connected compact set of minimal \mathcal H^1 among all connected compact sets \Gamma satisfying \overline{B_r(\Sigma)}\subset\overline{B_r(\Gamma)}? In other words, if \Sigma is an r-minimizer for some compact set M, is \Sigma the unique r-minimizer for its own closed r-neighborhood \overline{B_r(\Sigma)}?

Let \(M\subset\mathbb{R}^2\) be compact and let \(r>0\). Let \(\Sigma\subset\mathbb{R}^2\) be an \(r\)-minimizer for \(M\), i.e. a connected compact set of minimal \(\mathcal H^1\)-length among all connected compact sets with \(F_M(\Sigma):=\max_{y\in M}\operatorname{dist}(y,\Sigma)\le r\) (equivalently, \(M\subset \overline{B_r(\Sigma)}\)). Define a point \(x\in\Sigma\) to be energetic if \(F_M(\Sigma\setminus B_\rho(x))>F_M(\Sigma)\) for every \(\rho>0\), and let \(G_\Sigma\) be the set of all energetic points of \(\Sigma\). Is the whole minimizer \(\Sigma\) uniquely determined by the set \(G_\Sigma\)?

Let M be a finite subset of Euclidean space and let r > 0. For maximal distance minimizers Σ, that is, connected compact sets of minimal H^1-length subject to M ⊂ B_r(Σ), obtain a full algebraic characterization of the minimizer(s) for finite M: describe Σ by explicit defining equations and determine the algebraic degrees involved; moreover, determine to what extent a minimizer is characterized or can be reconstructed from its set G_Σ of energetic points.

Let \(A \subset \mathbb{R}^d\) be a finite set of terminals, where \(d \ge 3\). A Steiner tree for \(A\) is a closed connected set \(T \subset \mathbb{R}^d\) of minimal one-dimensional Hausdorff measure \(\mathcal{H}^1(T)\) among all closed sets \(S\) such that \(S \cup A\) is connected. Does there exist such a terminal set \(A\) for which there are two distinct Steiner trees \(T_1\) and \(T_2\) connecting \(A\), but the directions of all straight segments incident to the terminals are the same in \(T_1\) and \(T_2\); equivalently, \(T_1\) and \(T_2\) coincide in a neighborhood of every terminal?

In the Steiner-set problem in Euclidean space, existence is known for compact input sets: if A \subset \mathbb{R}^d is compact, one seeks a closed set S of minimal one-dimensional Hausdorff measure \mathcal{H}^1(S) such that S \cup A is connected. Does there exist some Euclidean dimension d and some bounded set A \subset \mathbb{R}^d for which the variational problem inf\{\mathcal{H}^1(S): S \subset \mathbb{R}^d,\ S \cup A \text{ is connected}\} is not attained by any admissible set S?

For each integer d ≥ 2, determine the Steiner ratio of Euclidean space R^d, namely
ρ(R^d) = inf { L(SMT(A)) / L(MST(A)) : A ⊂ R^d is finite, |A| ≥ 2 },
where MST(A) is a minimum spanning tree on A and SMT(A) is a Steiner minimal tree for A, i.e. a shortest Euclidean network connecting A in R^d and allowing additional Steiner points.

Let St ⊂ ℝ^d be a Steiner tree with terminal set A. Fix x ∈ ℝ^d and r > 0 such that A ∩ B_r(x) = ∅, and assume the local length is finite in the sense that H^1(St ∩ B_r(x)) < ∞. What is the maximal possible cardinality of St ∩ ∂B_{r/2}(x)? More generally, for a fixed t ∈ (0,1), what is the maximal possible cardinality of St ∩ ∂B_{tr}(x)?

Let St ⊂ R^d be a Steiner tree for a terminal set A, let x ∈ R^d and r > 0 be such that A ∩ B_r(x) = ∅, and assume H^1(St ∩ B_r(x)) < ∞. Is it true that St has at most one branching point in B_{r/2}(x)? Here a branching point means a non-terminal point of St with tripod local structure (equivalently, under the local finite-length assumption, a degree-3 non-terminal point).

Let St be a Steiner tree for a compact terminal set A ⊂ R^d with d > 2. Fix x ∈ R^d and r > 0 such that B_r(x) ∩ A = ∅, and assume H^1(St ∩ B_r(x)) < ∞. If, in addition, the local configuration St ∩ B_r(x) is full in the Steiner-tree sense (every terminal has degree 1), then for a given t ∈ (0,1), what is the largest possible value of H^1(St ∩ B_{tr}(x)) / r?

Let A=(A_1,...,A_n) be a finite labeled set of points in R^d, and let St be a Steiner tree for A, i.e. a connected compact set of minimal H^1-length among connected compact sets containing A. For r>0 and compact M subset R^d, call Sigma an r-minimizer for M if Sigma is connected and compact, M is contained in the closed r-neighborhood of Sigma, and H^1(Sigma) is minimal among all such connected compact competitors. Is it true that St is an r-minimizer for some n-tuple M=(M_1,...,M_n) of points and some sufficiently small r>0 if and only if St is the unique Steiner tree for its terminal set A?

Let d≥2, let Ω⊂R^d be a bounded Borel set with 0<|Ω|<∞, and let X_1,...,X_N be i.i.d. random points uniformly distributed in Ω. If St({X_1,...,X_N}) denotes a Steiner tree of minimum one-dimensional Hausdorff measure connecting the terminal set {X_1,...,X_N}, is there a deterministic constant β_ST(d) such that the minimal Steiner-tree length satisfies H^1(St({X_1,...,X_N}))/(|Ω|^(1/d)N^((d-1)/d))→β_ST(d) as N→∞ (for example almost surely, or at least in expectation)?

Let X_N={x_1,…,x_N} be N i.i.d. points sampled uniformly from a bounded domain Ω⊂R^d of positive volume, and let ST(X_N) denote a Euclidean Steiner minimal tree spanning X_N. Is there a sharp asymptotic law, or at least constants 0<β_1(Ω,d)≤β_2(Ω,d)<∞ valid for all sufficiently large N, such that β_1 N^((d-1)/d) ≤ E[H^1(ST(X_N))] ≤ β_2 N^((d-1)/d)? More precisely, can one determine the asymptotic constant for E[H^1(ST(X_N))]/N^((d-1)/d) and compare it with the corresponding constants for the Euclidean minimum spanning tree, the rectilinear Steiner minimal tree, and the Euclidean traveling salesperson problem? In the same random model, what are the correct asymptotic upper and lower bounds for the associated Steiner ratio?
For every integer n≥2, is it true that any set P⊂R^2 of n points contained in a rectangle of side lengths √3 and n−1 can be connected by a connected set Σ⊂R^2 with P⊂Σ and H^1(Σ)≤√3(n−1)?

For a fixed Euclidean dimension d and an integer n, what is the maximum number of distinct full Steiner topologies that can simultaneously occur as Steiner minimal trees for one and the same finite terminal set A⊂R^d with |A|=n, where a topology means the abstract graph of a labeled Steiner tree (terminals labeled by A and Steiner points unlabeled) and full means that every terminal has degree 1?

Fix an integer n >= 3. Let Q \subset \mathbb{R}^3 be the vertex set of a regular n-gon contained in the plane \{x=1\} and centered at (1,0,0). For 0 < \lambda < \lambda_0(n), let f(x)=\lambda x be the homothety of \mathbb{R}^3 centered at the origin, and define the self-similar terminal set A_{n,\lambda}:=\bigcup_{k\ge 0} f^k(Q). In the Euclidean Steiner problem for A_{n,\lambda}—that is, minimizing \mathcal{H}^1(S) over closed connected sets S \subset \mathbb{R}^3 such that S \cup A_{n,\lambda} is connected—describe the minimizers (Steiner trees) for sufficiently small \lambda, and in particular determine whether there exists an indecomposable minimizer.

Can one construct a compact set A ⊂ R^d for some d >= 3 such that the Steiner problem for A—namely, minimizing H^1(Sigma) over closed sets Sigma with A ∪ Sigma connected—has a unique solution Sigma, where Sigma is full (every terminal point has degree 1), Sigma has infinitely many branching points (equivalently, infinitely many nonterminal degree-3 Steiner points), and Sigma is genuinely non-planar, i.e. not contained in any affine 2-plane?

For nonprincipal ultrafilters U and V on N, determine when the tracial matrix ultraproducts prod_U(M_n(C), tr_n) and prod_V(M_n(C), tr_n) are elementarily equivalent in the first-order theory of tracial von Neumann algebras; equivalently, classify the elementary-equivalence classes realized by the family {prod_U(M_n(C), tr_n) : U a nonprincipal ultrafilter on N}. Likewise, classify the elementary-equivalence classes realized by the operator-norm matrix ultraproducts prod_U^||·|| M_n(C) as U ranges over nonprincipal ultrafilters on N.

Fix a nonprincipal ultrafilter 𝒰 on ℕ, and let 𝓜_𝒰 denote the corresponding tracial matrix ultraproduct. Is it true that for every Connes-embeddable non-Gamma type II_1 factor N there exists a unital trace-preserving *-embedding π: N → 𝓜_𝒰 such that π(N)' ∩ 𝓜_𝒰 = ℂ? ([ar5iv.labs.arxiv.org](https://ar5iv.labs.arxiv.org/html/2511.20377v2))

Let U be a nonprincipal ultrafilter on N, and let ∏_U M_n(C) denote the tracial matrix ultraproduct of the complex matrix algebras M_n(C). Following the paper, call a II_1 factor M without Property Gamma pseudocompact if, in the language of tracial von Neumann algebras, M is elementarily equivalent to ∏_U M_n(C) for some such U. If F_n is the free group on n generators and L(F_n) its group von Neumann algebra, is L(F_n) pseudocompact for every integer n >= 2?

Does there exist a group G such that its group von Neumann algebra L(G) is a pseudocompact non-Gamma II_1 factor, in the sense that there exists a nonprincipal ultrafilter U on N for which L(G) is elementarily equivalent, as a tracial von Neumann algebra, to the tracial matrix ultraproduct ∏_U M_n(C)? Moreover, does there exist an icc, non-inner-amenable group G such that L(G) is not pseudocompact in this sense? ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2511.20377))

Fix a nonprincipal ultrafilter U on N, and let M_U = ∏_{n→U}(M_n(C), tr_n) be the tracial matrix ultraproduct of the full matrix algebras with their normalized traces. If N ⊂ M_U is a II_1 subfactor with finite Jones index [M_U : N] < ∞, must N be isomorphic, as a tracial von Neumann algebra, to a tracial matrix ultraproduct M_V for some nonprincipal ultrafilter V on N?

Fix a nonprincipal ultrafilter U on N. Let S_U be the metric ultraproduct of the symmetric groups S_n equipped with the normalized Hamming distance, and let M_U = prod_{n->U}(M_n(C), tr_n) be the tracial matrix ultraproduct. Via the permutation-matrix embeddings S_n ⊂ M_n(C), view S_U as a trace-preserving subgroup of M_U, and let W*(S_U) ⊂ M_U be the von Neumann algebra generated by S_U. Does W*(S_U) contain a von Neumann subalgebra isomorphic to a tracial matrix ultraproduct?

Does there exist a separable II_1 factor N and an existential embedding i: L(F_2) -> N, in the sense that for some nonprincipal ultrafilter U on N there is an embedding j: N -> L(F_2)^U such that j o i is the diagonal embedding of L(F_2), with the property that N is not isomorphic, as a tracial von Neumann algebra, to any nontrivial tracial free product P * Q (that is, with both P and Q non-scalar)?

Do there exist II1 factors N and M and a unital trace-preserving *-embedding i:N→M such that: (1) N is strongly solid, meaning that for every diffuse amenable von Neumann subalgebra A⊂N, the von Neumann algebra generated by the normalizer of A in N is amenable; (2) i is existential, in the sense that for some nonprincipal ultrafilter U on ℕ there exists a unital trace-preserving *-embedding j:M→N^U with j∘i equal to the diagonal embedding N→N^U; and (3) M admits a Cartan subalgebra, i.e. a maximal abelian self-adjoint subalgebra whose normalizer generates M? ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/html/2511.20377v1))

Does there exist a discrete group Γ containing the rank-two free group F_2 as an existential subgroup such that the group von Neumann algebra L(Γ) is not isomorphic to L(F_n) for some n in N? More specifically, can Γ be taken to be a non-elementary surface group? Here F_n denotes the free group of rank n and L(·) denotes the group von Neumann algebra.

Fix a nonprincipal ultrafilter U on N, and let N^U denote the tracial ultrapower of N. Let N be a nonamenable biexact II_1 factor, and let M be a separable II_1 factor. Suppose there is a normal unital trace-preserving *-embedding i:N->M such that i is existential, in the sense that there exists a normal unital trace-preserving *-embedding j:M->N^U with j∘i equal to the diagonal embedding Δ_N:N->N^U. Must M be prime, i.e. must M fail to admit a nontrivial tensor-product decomposition M ≅ P \bar\otimes Q with P and Q II_1 factors?

Let N ⊂ M be II_1 factors. Assume that N has the Haagerup property and that the inclusion N -> M is existential, meaning that for some nonprincipal ultrafilter U there exists a unital trace-preserving embedding M -> N^U whose restriction to N is the diagonal embedding N -> N^U. Is it possible for M to have Kazhdan's property (T)?

Let 𝒰 be a nonprincipal ultrafilter on ℕ, and let N be a Connes-embeddable II_1 factor with the Haagerup property. If B ⊂ N^𝒰 is a von Neumann subalgebra with Property (T), must there exist finite-dimensional von Neumann subalgebras N_n ⊂ N such that B ⊂ ∏_𝒰 N_n ⊂ N^𝒰? ([ar5iv.labs.arxiv.org](https://ar5iv.labs.arxiv.org/html/2511.20377v2))

Fix a nonprincipal ultrafilter U on N, let M^U := ∏_{n→U} M_n(C) be the tracial matrix ultraproduct, and let L(F_2) denote the group von Neumann algebra of the free group on two generators. Does there exist an embedding ι:L(F_2)→M^U that is existential, in the sense that there exists an embedding θ:M^U→L(F_2)^U such that θ∘ι is the diagonal embedding of L(F_2) into L(F_2)^U? Moreover, for the Haar-sampled random embedding of L(F_2) into M^U alluded to in the paper, is that embedding existential?

Does there exist a countable discrete group G such that its group von Neumann algebra L(G) is an existentially closed II_1 factor, in the sense that for every embedding of L(G) into a II_1 factor M, that embedding is existential—equivalently, for a nonprincipal ultrafilter U, there exists an embedding M into the tracial ultrapower L(G)^U whose restriction to L(G) is the diagonal embedding?
Fix a nonprincipal ultrafilter U on N. Does there exist a sequence (N_i)_{i in N} of separable non-Gamma II_1 factors such that the tracial ultraproduct ∏_{i→U} N_i has property Gamma?

Do there exist non-Gamma II_1 factors M and N that are Connes embeddable and not elementarily equivalent, in the sense that there do not exist nonprincipal ultrafilters U,V on the natural numbers for which M^U is isomorphic to N^V? More generally, does there exist a family {M_i : i in I} of non-Gamma II_1 factors with |I| = 2^{aleph_0} such that M_i and M_j are not elementarily equivalent whenever i ≠ j?

Does there exist a discrete group G that is icc (that is, every nontrivial conjugacy class is infinite) and not inner amenable such that its group von Neumann algebra L(G) is not elementarily equivalent to the free group factor L(F_2), where F_2 is the free group on two generators and where two II_1 factors M and N are called elementarily equivalent if there exist ultrafilters U and V for which the tracial ultrapowers M^U and N^V are isomorphic?

Let U be a nonprincipal ultrafilter on ℕ, and for a II_1 factor M let M^U denote its tracial ultrapower. Recall that M is called super McDuff if M' ∩ M^U is itself a II_1 factor, and that II_1 factors M and N are elementarily equivalent in the paper's sense if M^U ≅ N^V for some nonprincipal ultrafilters U and V on ℕ. Do there exist two Connes embeddable super McDuff II_1 factors that are not elementarily equivalent? More strongly, do there exist continuum many pairwise non-elementarily-equivalent Connes embeddable super McDuff II_1 factors?

Do there exist two II_1 factors M and N such that both M and N have property Gamma, neither M nor N is McDuff, and M and N are not elementarily equivalent in the paper's sense (that is, there do not exist ultrafilters U and V such that M^U is isomorphic to N^V)? More generally, do there exist continuum many II_1 factors with property Gamma that are not McDuff and are pairwise not elementarily equivalent?

Let F be Thompson's group F, let L(F) be its group von Neumann algebra, and let 𝒰 be a nonprincipal ultrafilter on N, as fixed throughout the paper. Is L(F) super McDuff; that is, is the relative commutant L(F)' ∩ L(F)^𝒰 a II_1 factor?

Let M, N_1, and N_2 be II_1 factors, and suppose that M \cong N_1 \bar\otimes N_2, where \bar\otimes denotes the spatial von Neumann tensor product. If M is McDuff (equivalently, M \cong M \bar\otimes R for the hyperfinite II_1 factor R), must at least one of the tensor factors N_1 or N_2 be McDuff? ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2511.20377))

Fix an integer n >= 3. Does there exist a complex type II1 factor M with faithful normal tracial state tau such that M does not have property Gamma, the sequential commutation equivalence relation ~_M on the set H(M) := {u in U(M) : tau(u^m) = 0 for all m >= 1} of Haar unitaries has exactly one orbit, and the associated commutation diameter is exactly n? Here, for a fixed nonprincipal ultrafilter U, one defines u ~_M v if there exist Haar unitaries w_1, ..., w_k in M^U with [u,w_1] = 0, [w_i,w_{i+1}] = 0 for 1 <= i < k, and [w_k,v] = 0; if p_M(u,v) is the least such k, then the commutation diameter is sup_{u,v in H(M)} p_M(u,v).

Fix a nonprincipal ultrafilter U on the natural numbers, and write M^U for the tracial ultrapower of a II1 factor M. Does there exist a II1 factor M with Property (T) such that for every pair of Haar unitaries u,v in M there are Haar unitaries w_1,...,w_n in M^U, for some finite n, satisfying [u,w_1]=[w_1,w_2]=...=[w_{n-1},w_n]=[w_n,v]=0?

Fix a nonprincipal ultrafilter U on N. Does there exist a II_1 factor N with faithful normal trace tau such that N has no diffuse von Neumann subalgebra A⊂N for which the inclusion A⊂N has Popa’s relative property (T), and such that the sequential commutation equivalence relation on the Haar unitaries of N has a single orbit; equivalently, for every pair of Haar unitaries u,v in N (that is, tau(u^m)=tau(v^m)=0 for all m>=1), there exist Haar unitaries w_1,...,w_n in N^U with [u,w_1]=0, [w_k,w_{k+1}]=0 for 1<=k<n, and [w_n,v]=0? Can one moreover choose N to have the Haagerup property?

Let N be a II_1 factor, let h(N) denote its 1-bounded entropy, let H(N) be the set of Haar unitaries in N, and let ~_N be the sequential commutation equivalence relation on H(N), defined by u~_N v if there exist a free ultrafilter U and Haar unitaries w_1,...,w_n in N^U such that [u,w_1]=[w_k,w_{k+1}]=[w_n,v]=0 for all 1<=k<n. Writing O_N(u)={v in H(N): v~_N u}, does there exist a II_1 factor N with h(N)=0 such that ~_N has continuum many equivalence classes on H(N)? And does there exist a II_1 factor N with h(N)=0 such that W*(O_N(u)) is a proper subalgebra of N for every u in H(N)?

Fix a nonprincipal ultrafilter U. Let (M, tau) = (N1, E1) *_B (N2, E2) be a tracial amalgamated free product over a common tracial von Neumann subalgebra B, and let ui in U(Ni) for i = 1,2 be Haar unitaries satisfying E_B(ui^k) = 0 for every k >= 1. Suppose vi in U(M^U) are Haar unitaries such that, after identifying ui with its diagonal copy in M^U, one has ui ~M vi for i = 1,2 (equivalently: ui and vi are connected by a finite chain of Haar unitaries in M^U with consecutive terms commuting), and E_{B^U}(vi^k) = 0 for every k >= 1. Must v1 and v2 be freely independent in M^U with respect to the ultrapower trace?

Let N be a non-prime II_1 factor, i.e. N admits a nontrivial tensor product decomposition N \cong P \bar\otimes Q into II_1 factors. Fix the paper’s nonprincipal ultrafilter \mathcal U on \mathbb N, and let \sim_N denote the sequential commutation relation on Haar unitaries of N: for Haar unitaries u,v \in N, write u \sim_N v if there exist Haar unitaries w_1,\dots,w_n \in N^\mathcal U such that [u,w_1]=0, [w_k,w_{k+1}]=0 for 1 \le k < n, and [w_n,v]=0. Must \sim_N have exactly one orbit on the Haar unitaries of N?

Let N be a separable II_1 factor and let t>0. If N^t denotes the standard t-amplification of N, is it true that N and N^t have the same number of sequential commutation orbits on Haar unitaries; equivalently, does |H(N)/~_N|=|H(N^t)/~_{N^t}|, where H(M) denotes the Haar unitaries of M and u~_M v means that u and v can be joined in an ultrapower M^U by a finite chain of Haar unitaries whose consecutive terms commute?

Let N be a tracial von Neumann algebra and \mathcal U a nonprincipal ultrafilter on \mathbb N. Suppose one is given independent unitaries in U(N^\mathcal U), where "independent" means ∞-independent in the sense that every alternating centered word in them has trace 0. Can one choose representing sequences of unitaries in N for these ultrapower elements so that, for every index m, the chosen representatives are pairwise independent unitaries in N? ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/html/2511.20377v1))

Fix an integer k >= 1. Let U be a nonprincipal ultrafilter on N, let N be a tracial von Neumann algebra, and write N^U for its tracial ultrapower. If u,v are unitaries in U(N^U) that are k-independent in the paper's sense (equivalently, the abelian von Neumann algebras W*(u) and W*(v) are k-independent, i.e. the trace vanishes on the relevant alternating centered words up to order k), must there exist lifts u = (u_n)_U and v = (v_n)_U with each u_n,v_n in U(N) such that for every n, the pair u_n,v_n is k-independent in N?

Fix a nonprincipal ultrafilter U on ℕ, and let N^U denote the tracial ultrapower of the ambient II_1 factor N. Let M be a separable subfactor, and let pi_1, pi_2 : M -> N^U be embeddings. Suppose there exists a sequence of unital completely positive maps phi_n : N -> N such that the induced ultrapower map Phi = (phi_n)^U : N^U -> N^U satisfies Phi o pi_1 = pi_2. Must there exist a unitary u in N^U such that u pi_1(x) u^* = pi_2(x) for every x in M?

Fix a nonprincipal ultrafilter U on N, and for a tracial von Neumann algebra N let N^U denote its tracial ultrapower. Does there exist a nonamenable separable II1 factor N such that for every pair of unital *-embeddings pi1, pi2: N -> N^U, there is a unitary u in N^U satisfying pi2(x) = u pi1(x) u* for all x in N?

Let U be a nonprincipal ultrafilter on the natural numbers, let R denote the hyperfinite II1 factor, and let R^U be its tracial ultrapower. If N is a Connes embeddable separable II1 factor such that for every pair of embeddings pi, rho : N -> R^U there exists an automorphism alpha in Aut(R^U) with rho = alpha composed with pi, must N be isomorphic to R?

For distinct integers n,m ≥ 2, where F_n denotes the free group on n generators, are the free group factors L(F_n) and L(F_m) elementarily equivalent as tracial II_1 factors; that is, do there exist nonprincipal ultrafilters U and V on N such that L(F_n)^U ≅ L(F_m)^V? ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2511.20377))

Fix a nonprincipal ultrafilter U on N, let R denote the hyperfinite II_1 factor, and write R^U for its tracial ultrapower. For every separable Connes embeddable II_1 factor N, does there exist a unital trace-preserving embedding pi: N -> R^U such that the relative commutant pi(N)' ∩ R^U is a factor? ([ar5iv.labs.arxiv.org](https://ar5iv.labs.arxiv.org/html/2511.20377v2))

Let N be a II_1 factor and let 𝒰 be a nonprincipal ultrafilter on ℕ. If N_0 ⊆ N^𝒰 is a Jones-index-2 subfactor of the tracial ultrapower N^𝒰, must there exist Jones-index-2 subfactors N_i ⊆ N, for i ∈ ℕ, such that N_0 = ∏_{i→𝒰} N_i as a subfactor of N^𝒰?

Do there exist a II1 factor N, a nonprincipal ultrafilter U on ℕ, and a discrete group G such that the tracial ultrapower N^U is isomorphic, as a von Neumann algebra, to the group von Neumann algebra L(G)?

Fix a nonprincipal ultrafilter \mathcal U on \mathbb N, and let N^{\mathcal U} denote the tracial ultrapower of a II_1 factor N. Does there exist a II_1 factor N such that its 1-bounded entropy satisfies h(N) = 0 while h(N^{\mathcal U}) = \infty? ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2511.20377))

Let U be a nonprincipal ultrafilter on N, let N^U denote the tracial ultrapower of a II1 factor N, and regard N as diagonally embedded in N^U. If the relative commutant bicommutant condition (N' ∩ N^U)' ∩ N^U = N holds inside N^U, must N be isomorphic to the hyperfinite II1 factor R?

Fix a nonprincipal ultrafilter \mathcal U on \mathbb N, and let M^\mathcal U denote the tracial ultrapower of a II_1 factor M. For an arbitrary II_1 factor M, must the spatial tensor product M_2(\mathbb C)\bar\otimes M admit a unital embedding into M^\mathcal U? (As noted in the paper, this is immediate if M is Connes embeddable.) ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2511.20377))

Fix a non-principal ultrafilter 𝒰 on ℕ. For a II_1 factor M, let M^𝒰 denote its tracial ultrapower. Say that M is solid if every von Neumann subalgebra A ⊂ M with diffuse relative commutant A' ∩ M is amenable, and say that M is 𝒰-solid if every von Neumann subalgebra A ⊂ M with diffuse relative commutant A' ∩ M^𝒰 is amenable. Are solidity and 𝒰-solidity equivalent for II_1 factors?

Do there exist II_1 factors M and N such that, in the paper's standing sense of elementary equivalence for II_1 factors, there are nonprincipal ultrafilters U and V with M^U ≅ N^V, but such that the underlying unital C*-algebras of M and N are not elementarily equivalent in the first-order language of C*-algebras?

Fix the non-principal ultrafilter 𝒰 on ℕ used throughout the paper. Does there exist a II_1 factor N such that its tracial ultrapower N^𝒰 has non-full fundamental group; equivalently, such that F(N^𝒰) = { t > 0 : (N^𝒰)^t ≅ N^𝒰 } is a proper subgroup of the positive real multiplicative group?

Fix a nonprincipal ultrafilter U on ℕ, and for a tracial von Neumann algebra N write N^U for its tracial ultrapower. Let N_1, N_2, M_1, M_2 be separable II_1 factors. If the von Neumann tensor products N_1^U ⊗ N_2^U and M_1^U ⊗ M_2^U are isomorphic as tracial von Neumann algebras, must there exist a permutation σ of {1,2} such that, for each i = 1,2, the factors N_i and M_{σ(i)} are elementarily equivalent (that is, some ultrapowers of N_i and M_{σ(i)} are isomorphic)?

Let I and J be finite sets, and let (N_i)_{i∈I} and (M_j)_{j∈J} be separable II1 factors. Suppose that their tracial free products are isomorphic as II1 factors: ∗_{i∈I} N_i ≅ ∗_{j∈J} M_j. Must there exist a bijection σ:I→J such that N_i ≡ M_{σ(i)} for every i∈I, where ≡ denotes elementary equivalence of II1 factors in the sense fixed at the start of the paper (equivalently, existence of ultrafilters U and V with N_i^U ≅ M_{σ(i)}^V)? ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2511.20377))

Let x = (x_n) be an absolutely summable real sequence, and define its achievement set by E(x) := { sum_{n in A} x_n : A subset N }. By the Guthrie-Nymann Classification Theorem, E(x) belongs to exactly one of four broad classes: a finite set, a multi-interval set (a finite union of bounded closed intervals), a Cantor set, or a Cantorval. Find necessary and sufficient conditions stated directly in terms of the generating sequence x that determine which of these four classes E(x) has. The paper notes that the finite case is trivial and the multi-interval case is already known, so the substantive unresolved part is to characterize from x when E(x) is a Cantor set and when it is a Cantorval.

Let x_n = 2^{-n}+(-1)^n 3^{-n} for n >= 1, and let E(x_n) = {sum_{n=1}^infty epsilon_n x_n : epsilon_n in {0,1}} be the achievement set of the convergent positive series sum_{n=1}^infty x_n. What is the topological type of E(x_n) in the Guthrie–Nymann classification: is E(x_n) a finite union of closed intervals, a Cantor set, or a Cantorval?

Let (x_n)_{n≥1} be the real sequence defined by x_{2n-1} = 2^{-(2n-1)} and x_{2n} = 2^{-(2n+1)} for every n ∈ N. Define its achievement set by E(x_n) = {∑_{n∈A} x_n : A ⊆ N} ⊆ R. Which Guthrie–Nymann topological type does E(x_n) have? In other words, is E(x_n) a finite set, a finite union of closed intervals, a Cantor set, or a Cantorval?

Does there exist a real sequence (x_n) such that the limit lim_{n→∞}|x_{n+1}/x_n| exists and the achievement set AS(x_n) := {\sum_{n=1}^{\infty} \varepsilon_n x_n : \varepsilon_n \in \{0,1\},\ \sum_{n=1}^{\infty} \varepsilon_n x_n\ \text{converges}} contains an interval but is not a finite union of closed intervals?

For every real number $q\in(1/2,1)$, does the geometric sequence $(q^n)_{n\in\mathbb{N}}$ contain a subsequence $(q^{n_k})_{k\in\mathbb{N}}$, with $n_1<n_2<\cdots$, such that its achievement set
$E\big((q^{n_k})_{k\in\mathbb{N}}\big):=\left\{\sum_{k\in A} q^{n_k}: A\subseteq\mathbb{N}\right\}\subseteq\mathbb{R}$
is a Cantorval?

Let n >= 2 and let k_1,...,k_m be positive integers such that none of k_1,...,k_m is divisible by n. Define
Sigma := {sum_{i=1}^m epsilon_i k_i : epsilon_i in {0,1}},
and assume that |Sigma| = n. Write Sigma = {sigma_0 < sigma_1 < ... < sigma_{n-1}}, and for each i let t_i in {0,1,...,n-1} be the residue determined by sigma_i ≡ t_i (mod n). If the achievement set of the multigeometric sequence (k_1,...,k_m;1/n), namely E(k_1,...,k_m;1/n), has positive Lebesgue measure in R, must Sigma be a complete residue system modulo n; equivalently, must {t_0,...,t_{n-1}} = {0,1,...,n-1}?

Let C⊂R be an achievable Cantor set, i.e. the achievement set of some absolutely convergent real series and homeomorphic to the classical ternary Cantor set. Must there exist achievable Cantor sets C',C''⊂R such that the algebraic sum C+C'={x+y:x∈C, y∈C'} is a Cantor set, while C+C'' is a Cantorval?

Let C ⊂ R be an achievable Cantor set, i.e. C = E(x_n) = {∑_{n∈A} x_n : A ⊂ N} for some absolutely convergent real series ∑ x_n, and assume that C is homeomorphic to the classical ternary Cantor set. Must there exist achievable Cantorvals D', D'' ⊂ R such that, for the algebraic sum A+B := {a+b : a∈A, b∈B}, the set C + D' is a Cantorval and the set C + D'' is an interval?

Let D ⊂ R be an achievable Cantorval, i.e. D = E((x_n)) is the achievement set of some absolutely convergent real series and D is a Cantorval. Must there exist achievable Cantorvals D′, D′′ ⊂ R such that, for the algebraic sum A + B := {a + b : a ∈ A, b ∈ B}, the set D + D′ is a Cantorval while D + D′′ is a single interval?

Let a=(a_n)_{n\ge 1} be a sequence of dissection ratios for a central Cantor set, and let C(a)\subset[0,1] be the corresponding central Cantor set obtained by starting from [0,1] and, at stage n, removing from each basic interval its centered open subinterval so that the two remaining closed subintervals each have length a_n times the length of their parent interval. If the algebraic difference set C(a)-C(a):=\{x-y:x,y\in C(a)\} has nonempty interior in \mathbb{R}, must 0 belong to \operatorname{int}(C(a)-C(a))?

In the natural parameter space/topology for central Cantor sets C1, C2 subset of R (with the paper’s default normalization to fundamental interval [0,1]), is it true that for a generic pair (C1, C2) the arithmetic sum C1 + C2—equivalently, since central Cantor sets are symmetric, the difference C1 - C2—satisfies the Palis dichotomy, namely: it has Lebesgue measure zero or contains a nonempty interval?

Let E subseteq R be an infinite achievable set, meaning that E is the set of subsums of some absolutely convergent real series, E = {sum_{n=1}^infty ε_n x_n : ε_n in {0,1}}. Must there exist achievable sets A,B subseteq R such that dim_H(A)=dim_H(B)=0 and E=A+B:= {a+b : a in A, b in B}?

Let (x_n) be a summable sequence of positive real numbers, and let E(x_n) = {\sum_{n=1}^\infty \varepsilon_n x_n : \varepsilon_n \in {0,1}} \subset \mathbb{R} be its achievement set. Assume that the Minkowski self-sum E(x_n)+E(x_n) = {u+v : u,v \in E(x_n)} is a Cantor set. Must one then have

\dim_H(E(x_n)) \ge \frac{\log 2}{\log 3}\, \dim_H(E(x_n)+E(x_n))?

Let x=(x_n)_{n>=1} be a summable sequence of positive real numbers, and let E(x)={sum_{n=1}^infty eps_n x_n : eps_n in {0,1}} be its achievement set. Assume that E(x) is a Cantorval, i.e. a bounded regularly closed subset of the real line whose boundary is a Cantor set. Must the topological boundary partial E(x) itself be an achievement set? In other words, does there always exist a summable sequence of positive real numbers y=(y_n)_{n>=1} such that E(y)=partial E(x)?

Let E(x_n) = {∑_{n∈A} x_n : A ⊂ ℕ} and E(y_n) = {∑_{n∈A} y_n : A ⊂ ℕ} be achievable Cantorvals in ℝ, i.e. Cantorvals arising as achievement sets of absolutely convergent real series. Do there exist such E(x_n) and E(y_n) for which E(x_n) ∪ E(y_n) is a closed interval? Under the standard normalization x_n > 0 and y_n > 0, this can occur only if the two Cantorvals have the same fundamental interval, equivalently ∑ x_n = ∑ y_n.

Does there exist a Cantorval C ⊂ ℝ that is achievable—i.e. C = E(x) := {∑_{n=1}^∞ ε_n x_n : ε_n ∈ {0,1}} for some absolutely summable real sequence x = (x_n)—such that its topological boundary ∂C has positive one-dimensional Lebesgue measure?

Let E = E(a_n) = {sum_{n=1}^infty epsilon_n a_n : epsilon_n in {0,1}} subset R be an achievable Cantorval, meaning that (a_n) is a convergent sequence of positive reals and E(a_n) is a Cantorval. Must the boundary Fr E have strictly intermediate Hausdorff dimension, i.e. is it always true that 0 < dim_H(Fr E) < 1? Equivalently, can there exist an achievable Cantorval whose boundary has Hausdorff dimension exactly 0 or exactly 1?
