Let (x_n) be a summable sequence of positive real numbers, and let E(x_n)=\{\sum_{n=1}^\infty \varepsilon_n x_n:\varepsilon_n\in\{0,1\}\}. Assume that E(x_n) is a Cantorval. If a and b are the left endpoints of two distinct nondegenerate interval components of E(x_n), must there exist ε>0 such that (E(x_n)∩[a-ε,a])+(b-a)=E(x_n)∩[b-ε,b]?

Characterize, up to homeomorphism, the subsets of R^2 that arise as planar achievement sets of absolutely convergent series; that is, determine exactly which homeomorphism classes are realized by sets of the form E((x_n,y_n)) := { sum_{n=1}^infty epsilon_n (x_n,y_n) : epsilon_n in {0,1} for every n }, where sum_{n=1}^infty (x_n,y_n) is an absolutely convergent series in R^2.

Let x=(x_n)_{n>=1} be a sequence of positive real numbers with X:=sum_{n=1}^infty x_n<infty, and let y=(y_n)_{n>=1} be a conditionally convergent real series. Define a planar series u=(u_n)_{n>=1} in R^2 by u_{2n-1}=(x_n,y_n) and u_{2n}=(x_n,0), and let E(u):={sum_{n=1}^infty eps_n u_n : (eps_n) in {0,1}^N}. Find sharp, checkable sufficient conditions on x ensuring that E(u) has nonempty interior; in particular, is the hypothesis int(E(x))!=emptyset sufficient for this paired planar achievement set to have nonempty interior?

For p,q in (0,1), define the planar achievement set E(p^n,q^n) := { sum_{n=1}^infty eps_n (p^n,q^n) : eps_n in {0,1} } subset of R^2. Characterize the topological type of E(p^n,q^n) for all pairs p,q in (0,1), in particular determine what happens in the remaining regime p > q > 1/2.

Let x = (x_n) be a nonincreasing sequence of positive real numbers with x in l_1 \ c_00, let E(x) = {sum_{n=1}^infty epsilon_n x_n : (epsilon_n) in {0,1}^N}, and define the cardinal function f_x : E(x) -> {1,2,3,...,omega,c} by f_x(t) = |{A subseteq N : sum_{n in A} x_n = t}|. Which subsets C of {1,2,3,...,omega,c} occur as the exact range rng(f_x) for some such sequence x?

Does there exist an absolutely convergent real sequence x=(x_n) such that, if f_x:{0,1}^N→R is defined by f_x((ε_n))=Σ_{n=1}^∞ ε_n x_n and F_x(t)=card(f_x^{-1}(t)), then the range of F_x contains an unbounded sequence of natural numbers but contains neither ω nor c? ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2512.17285))

Let x=(x_n) be a summable sequence of positive real numbers, let A(x)={Σ_{n=1}^∞ ε_n x_n : (ε_n)∈{0,1}^N} be its achievement set, and define the cardinal function F_x:A(x)→N∪{ω,𝔠} by F_x(t)=|{A⊆N : Σ_{n∈A} x_n=t}|. If F_x^{-1}(𝔠) is nonempty, must F_x^{-1}(𝔠) contain a Cantor set? ([link.springer.com](https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s00025-020-01260-x))

Let (x_n)_{n≥1} be a nonincreasing positive absolutely summable sequence, let E(x_n) = {Σ_{n=1}^∞ ε_n x_n : ε_n ∈ {0,1}} be its achievement set, and write r_n = Σ_{k>n} x_k. Assume that E(x_n) is a Cantorval, i.e. an achievable Cantorval. Recall that (x_n) is called a minimal representation of E(x_n) if, after deleting any infinite subsequence of (x_n), the achievement set of the remaining terms is no longer a Cantorval. It is known that for achievable multi-interval sets this minimality is equivalent to x_n < r_{n+1} for only finitely many n. Does the same equivalence hold for achievable Cantorvals?

Let C(X) denote the center of distances of a set X⊂R in the usual metric, that is, C(X)={α≥0: for every x∈X there exists y∈X with |x-y|=α}. Is it true that for every Borel set A⊂[0, infinity) with 0∈A, there exists a Borel set B⊂R such that C(B)=A?

Let C be a compact subset of [0, infinity) with 0 in C. Does there exist a compact set K subset of R such that S(K) = C, where S(K) := {t in [0, infinity) : for every x in K there exists y in K with |x-y| = t} is the center of distances of K (with respect to the usual metric on R)?

For each q in (0,1/2), let C_q:=E((q^n)_{n>=1})={sum_{n=1}^infinity eps_n q^n : eps_n in {0,1}} subset R, let G_n be the union of the open intervals removed at the n-th step in the standard construction of the central Cantor set C_q from [0,q/(1-q)], and define its adjoint Cantorval by A_q:=C_q union (union over k>=1 of G_{2k-1}) (so the case q=1/3 gives the model Cantorval up to the chosen normalization). Determine exactly the center of distances S(A_q):={alpha>=0 : for every x in A_q there exists y in A_q with |x-y|=alpha}.

Does there exist a positive fast convergent sequence x=(x_n) in l_1 with sum_{n=1}^infty x_n=1 and x_n>r_n:=sum_{k>n}x_k for every n, such that, if C=E(x)={sum_{n=1}^infty epsilon_n x_n : (epsilon_n) in {0,1}^N} is the associated central Cantor set in [0,1] and U_n denotes the union of all open intervals removed at stage n in the central construction of C, then its adjoint Cantorval A(C):=[0,1]\setminus \bigcup_{n\ge 1}U_{2n}=C\cup\bigcup_{n\ge 1}U_{2n-1} is achievable, i.e. A(C)=E(y) for some absolutely summable real sequence y?

Let λ(G) denote the spectral radius of the adjacency matrix of a simple undirected graph G, and, as usual in the fixed-size edge-spectral Turán problem, ignore isolated vertices. For a positive even integer m, determine the extremal graph among all non-bipartite triangle-free graphs G with |E(G)|=m that maximizes λ(G).

For all sufficiently large even integers m, determine the unique simple non-bipartite graph G with m edges and no subgraph isomorphic to C_3 or C_5 — equivalently, with odd girth at least 7 — that maximizes the adjacency spectral radius λ(G), identifying the extremal graph in each relevant congruence class of m modulo 3 exactly as in the paper.

Fix an integer k>=2 and an even integer m>=30k+45. Among all finite simple undirected graphs G with m edges and no isolated vertices that are non-bipartite and contain no odd cycle C_{2i+1} for 1<=i<=k, determine the maximum possible adjacency spectral radius lambda(G) and characterize the unique extremal graph. More precisely, is the unique maximizer given by one of the following three constructions according to the residue of m-(2k-1) modulo 3: (i) if m-(2k-1)≡0 (mod 3), the graph S_{2k-1}(K_{3,(m-2k+1)/3}); (ii) if m-(2k-1)≡1 (mod 3), the graph obtained from S_{2k-1}(K_{2,(m-2k)/2}) by attaching a pendant edge to a vertex of maximum degree; and (iii) if m-(2k-1)≡2 (mod 3), the graph obtained from C_{2k+3} by blowing up one vertex to an independent set of size (m-2k-1)/3 and then adjoining one new vertex adjacent to every vertex of that blown-up set? Here S_{2k-1}(K_{s,t}) denotes the graph obtained from K_{s,t} by replacing one edge with a path on 2k+1 vertices.

For each fixed integer k >= 1, does there exist an integer N(k) such that, for every even integer m >= N(k), every non-bipartite graph G in 𝒢(m,{C_3,C_5,...,C_{2k+1}}) (that is, every finite simple graph with exactly m edges, no isolated vertices, and containing none of C_3,C_5,...,C_{2k+1} as a subgraph) satisfies the following exact adjacency-spectral extremal classification: if λ(G) denotes the spectral radius of the adjacency matrix of G, then
(1) if m-(2k-1) ≡ 0 (mod 3), one has λ(G) <= λ(S_{2k-1}(K_{3,(m-2k+1)/3})), with equality if and only if G ≅ S_{2k-1}(K_{3,(m-2k+1)/3});
(2) if m-(2k-1) ≡ 1 (mod 3), one has λ(G) <= λ(S_{2k-1}^+(K_{2,(m-2k)/2})), with equality if and only if G ≅ S_{2k-1}^+(K_{2,(m-2k)/2}); and
(3) if m-(2k-1) ≡ 2 (mod 3), one has λ(G) <= λ(S_{2k-1}^-(K_{3,(m-2k+2)/3})), with equality if and only if G ≅ S_{2k-1}^-(K_{3,(m-2k+2)/3})?
Here S_{2k-1}(K_{s,t}) is the graph obtained from K_{s,t} by replacing one edge by a path on 2k+1 vertices (equivalently, subdividing that edge 2k-1 times); S_{2k-1}^+(K_{2,t}) is obtained from S_{2k-1}(K_{2,t}) by attaching a pendant edge to a vertex of maximum degree; and S_{2k-1}^-(K_{3,t}) is obtained from K_{3,t} by deleting one edge and then replacing an edge incident to the resulting degree-2 vertex by a path on 2k+1 vertices.

Fix an integer k >= 1. Is there an integer m_0(k) such that every simple graph G with m >= m_0(k) edges and no copy of the generalized book B_{2,k} = K_2 join I_k (equivalently, no set of k triangles sharing a common edge) satisfies lambda(G)^2 <= m? Equivalently, does every such G satisfy lambda(G) <= sqrt(m), and if equality holds, must G be a complete bipartite graph?

For each fixed integer r ≥ 1, does there exist m_0(r) such that, for every m ≥ m_0(r), every finite simple non-bipartite B_{2,r+1}-free graph G with m edges satisfies λ(G) ≤ ρ(m,r), where B_{2,r+1} = K_2 ∨ (r+1)K_1, ρ(m,r) is the largest root of x^3 - x^2 - (m-1)x + m - 2r - 1 = 0, and equality holds if and only if m ≡ 1 (mod r) and G is isomorphic to K^+_{r,(m-1)/r}, with K^+_{a,b} obtained from K_{a,b} by adding an edge inside the part of size b? ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2512.19395))

For each integer r ≥ 1, does there exist an integer M(r) such that whenever m ≥ M(r) and G is a finite simple non-bipartite graph with |E(G)| = m that contains no copy of the book graph B_{2,r+1} = K_2 ∨ (r+1)K_1, the spectral radius λ(G) of its adjacency matrix satisfies λ(G) ≤ ρ(m,r), where ρ(m,r) is the largest real root of x^3 − x^2 − (m−1)x + m − 2r − 1 = 0? Moreover, does equality hold if and only if m ≡ 1 (mod r) and G ≅ K^+_{r,(m−1)/r}, where K^+_{a,b} is obtained from the complete bipartite graph K_{a,b} by adding an edge inside the part of size b? ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2512.19395))

Fix a positive integer k >= 2. Does there exist an integer m_0 = m_0(k) such that, for every finite simple graph G with m >= m_0 edges and no isolated vertices, if G is either C_{2k+1}-free or C_{2k+2}-free, then its adjacency spectral radius satisfies lambda(G) <= (k - 1 + sqrt(4m - k^2 + 1))/2, with equality if and only if G is isomorphic to K_k vee tK_1, where t = m/k - (k - 1)/2 and vee denotes graph join?

For each fixed integer k ≥ 2, does there exist m_0 = m_0(k) such that for every integer m ≥ m_0 and every finite simple graph G with exactly m edges and no isolated vertices, if G is either θ_{1,2,2k-1}-free or θ_{1,2,2k}-free, where θ_{1,p,q} denotes the graph consisting of three internally disjoint paths of lengths 1, p, and q between the same two vertices, then the adjacency spectral radius λ(G) satisfies λ(G) ≤ (k - 1 + √(4m - k^2 + 1))/2, with equality if and only if m/k - (k - 1)/2 is an integer and G ≅ K_k ∨ ((m/k - (k - 1)/2)K_1)? citeturn10view0turn1view1turn9view1turn6view1

For each fixed integer k ≥ 3 and each integer l with 1 ≤ l ≤ k − 1, if m is an integer satisfying m + k(k+1)/2 ≡ l (mod k), determine all finite simple undirected graphs G with exactly m edges and no isolated vertices that maximize the adjacency spectral radius λ(G) over the class 𝒢(m, θ_{1,2,2k−1}) ∪ 𝒢(m, θ_{1,2,2k}), where 𝒢(m, F) denotes the set of F-free graphs with m edges and no isolated vertices, and θ_{1,2,q} is the graph obtained by joining two distinct vertices by three internally disjoint paths of lengths 1, 2, and q.

Let θ_{1,p,q} denote the theta graph formed by three internally disjoint paths of lengths 1, p, and q joining the same two endpoints, and let 𝒢(m,θ_{1,p,q}) be the family of simple θ_{1,p,q}-free graphs with exactly m edges and no isolated vertices. For integers q ≥ p ≥ 3, determine the maximum adjacency spectral radius λ(G) over all G ∈ 𝒢(m,θ_{1,p,q}) and characterize the extremal graphs attaining it; in the paper’s actual resolution, this must be stated with the paper’s two-case split, namely the special case (p,q)=(3,3) with m ≥ 43, and the general case in which k ≥ 3, p+q ∈ {2k+1, 2k+2}, and m ≥ (9/4)k^6 + 6k^5 + 46k^4 + 56k^3 + 196k^2.

For each fixed integer k ≥ 2, does there exist an integer m0 = m0(k) such that every simple finite undirected graph G with exactly m ≥ m0 edges that is F_{k,3}-free, where F_{k,3} = K_1 ∨ kK_2 is the friendship graph consisting of k triangles sharing a common vertex, satisfies λ(G) ≤ (k - 1 + √(4m - k^2 + 1))/2, where λ(G) is the adjacency spectral radius of G; and, moreover, is equality possible only when G is isomorphic to the join K_k ∨ sK_1 with s = (m - C(k,2))/k = (m/k) - (k - 1)/2 (so in particular s is a nonnegative integer)?

Fix an integer k ≥ 2. Is it true that there exists m0 = m0(k) such that, for every m ≥ m0 and every finite simple graph G with m edges that is either F_{2k+1}-free or F_{2k+2}-free, where F_s = K_1 ∨ P_{s-1}, one has λ(G) ≤ (k − 1 + √(4m − k^2 + 1)) / 2, with equality if and only if G ≅ K_k ∨ ((m / k) − (k − 1) / 2)K_1?

Let F_t := K_1 ∨ P_{t-1} be the fan graph on t vertices, and let λ(G) denote the spectral radius of the adjacency matrix of a simple graph G with m edges (equivalently, G is taken from the survey’s edge-spectral setting 𝒢(m,F), so isolated vertices are ignored). Fix k ≥ 2. For all sufficiently large m in the residue class for which (m/k) - (k - 1)/2 is an integer, if G is F_{2k+1}-free or F_{2k+2}-free, must one have λ(G) ≤ (k - 1 + sqrt(4m - k^2 + 1))/2, with equality if and only if G ≅ K_k ∨ ((m/k) - (k - 1)/2)K_1? ([themoonlight.io](https://www.themoonlight.io/en/review/a-survey-of-edge-spectral-turn-type-problems-in-spectral-graph-theory-results-conjectures-and-open-problems))

Let theta_{r,p,q} be the graph obtained by joining two distinct vertices with three internally disjoint paths of lengths r, p, and q, where q >= p >= r >= 2. Let G(m, theta_{r,p,q}) denote the family of theta_{r,p,q}-free graphs with exactly m edges and no isolated vertices, and let lambda(G) be the spectral radius of the adjacency matrix of G. For all sufficiently large integers m, determine the unique graph G in G(m, theta_{r,p,q}) that maximizes lambda(G).

Fix k ≥ 3, and let p,q,r,s be integers with q ≥ p ≥ 3, s ≥ r ≥ 3, p+q = 2k+1, and r+s = 2k+2. Let θ_{1,a,b} denote the theta graph consisting of three internally disjoint paths of lengths 1, a, b with the same two endpoints, and let 𝒢(m,F) be the class of finite simple F-free graphs with m edges and no isolated vertices. For m ≥ 9/4 k^6 + 6k^5 + 46k^4 + 56k^3 + 196k^2, determine the maximum possible adjacency spectral radius λ(G) among graphs G in 𝒢(m,θ_{1,p,q}) ∪ 𝒢(m,θ_{1,r,s}); equivalently, is it true that every such G satisfies λ(G) ≤ (k−1+√(4m−k^2+1))/2, with equality if and only if G ≅ K_k ∨ ((m/k)−(k−1)/2)K_1?

Fix an integer k>=2. Let F_{k,3}:=K_1∨kK_2 be the friendship graph, let λ(G) denote the adjacency spectral radius of a finite simple graph G, and for integers n,k,l with 1<=l<k define S^{1,l}_{n,k}:=K_l∨((K_{k-l}∨(n-k-1)K_1)∪K_1). Does there exist m_0=m_0(k) such that for every integer m>=m_0, every integer l with 1<=l<=k-1 and m + k(k+1)/2 ≡ l (mod k), and every graph G in 𝒢(m,F_{k,3}) (that is, every F_{k,3}-free graph with m edges and no isolated vertices), one has λ(G)<=λ(S^{1,l}_{(m-l)/k + (k+3)/2, k}), with equality if and only if G ≅ S^{1,l}_{(m-l)/k + (k+3)/2, k}?

Fix an integer k >= 2, let F_{2k+2} = K_1 ∨ P_{2k+1}, and write lambda(G) for the largest eigenvalue of the adjacency matrix of a simple graph G. In the notation of the paper, is it true that there exists m_0 = m_0(k) such that, for every integer m >= m_0, every l in {1, ..., k-1} with m + k(k+1)/2 ≡ l (mod k), and every F_{2k+2}-free graph G with m edges and no isolated vertices, one has lambda(G) <= lambda(S^{1,l}_{(m-l)/k + (k+3)/2, k}), with equality if and only if G is isomorphic to S^{1,l}_{(m-l)/k + (k+3)/2, k}?

For a fixed integer k >= 2, does there exist m_0 = m_0(k) such that, for every integer m >= m_0 and every graph G in 𝒢(m, W_{2k+1}) (that is, every W_{2k+1}-free graph with m edges and no isolated vertices), where W_{2k+1} := K_1 ∨ C_{2k}, the adjacency spectral radius λ(G) satisfies λ(G) <= λ(H_{k,m}) with equality if and only if G is isomorphic to H_{k,m}, where H_{k,m} is determined solely by the residue of m + k(k+1)/2 modulo k, namely H_{k,m} = K_k ∨ ((m/k) - (k - 1)/2)K_1 when m + k(k+1)/2 ≡ 0 (mod k), and H_{k,m} = S^{1,l}_{(m-l)/k + (k+3)/2, k} in the paper’s notation when l in {1,...,k-1} is the residue defined by m + k(k+1)/2 ≡ l (mod k)?

For each fixed integer k>=2, does there exist m_0(k) such that, for each j in {2k+1,2k+2}, every finite simple F_j-free graph G with m>=m_0(k) edges satisfies lambda(G)<= (k-1+sqrt(4m-k^2+1))/2, where lambda(G) is the adjacency spectral radius and F_j:=K_1∨P_{j-1} is the fan graph on j vertices; and, moreover, does equality hold if and only if G is isomorphic to K_k∨sK_1 with s=(m-k(k-1)/2)/k?

For every integer r >= 3, does every finite simple undirected K_{r+1}-free graph G on at least r + 1 vertices with m = |E(G)| edges satisfy
lambda_1(G)^2 + lambda_2(G)^2 <= (1 - 1/r) * 2m,
where lambda_1(G) >= lambda_2(G) are the two largest eigenvalues of the adjacency matrix A(G)?

For each fixed integer r >= 3 and all sufficiently large integers m, determine the graph(s) G with exactly m edges and no isolated vertices that are K_{r+1}-free but not r-partite, and that maximize the adjacency spectral radius lambda(G).

For fixed integers r >= 3 and k >= 1, does there exist m0 = m0(r,k) such that every finite simple B_{r,k+1}-free graph G with m >= m0 edges, where B_{r,k+1} := K_r \vee (k+1)K_1 and lambda(G) denotes the adjacency spectral radius of G, satisfies lambda(G)^2 <= (1 - 1/r)2m, with equality if and only if G is a regular complete r-partite graph?

For each fixed integer k ≥ 2, does there exist m_0 = m_0(k) such that every finite simple undirected W_{2k+2}-free graph G with m ≥ m_0 edges and no isolated vertices satisfies λ(G) ≤ √(4m/3), where λ(G) denotes the spectral radius of the adjacency matrix of G and W_{2k+2} = K_1 ∨ C_{2k+1}? Moreover, does equality hold if and only if G is a regular complete 3-partite graph (equivalently, a balanced complete tripartite graph)?

For a fixed color-critical graph F with χ(F)=r+1≥4, and a positive integer m, which finite simple F-free graphs G with exactly m edges and no isolated vertices maximize the adjacency spectral radius λ(G)?

Let F be a finite simple color-critical graph, meaning that some edge e∈E(F) satisfies χ(F-e)<χ(F), and suppose χ(F)=r+1≥4. Write \mathcal{G}(m,F) for the family of F-free graphs with exactly m edges and no isolated vertices. Determine, for every integer m≥m_0(F) for some sufficiently large threshold m_0(F), all graphs G∈\mathcal{G}(m,F) that are not r-partite and maximize the adjacency spectral radius λ(G).

Let f be either a rational map of degree at least 2 on the Riemann sphere or a transcendental meromorphic function on C, and let U be a periodic Fatou component of f with f^p(U)=U for some p>=1. If U is doubly connected, must U necessarily be a Herman ring; that is, must f^p|_U be conformally conjugate to an irrational rotation of an annulus?

Let f be a meromorphic map in the sense of this survey—either a rational map of degree at least 2 on the Riemann sphere or a transcendental meromorphic function. Does there exist a distinguished dynamical point for f, analogous to a Siegel point (the periodic point giving rise to a Siegel disk), whose existence guarantees that f possesses a Herman ring, that is, a periodic doubly connected Fatou component on which some iterate of f is conformally conjugate to an irrational rotation of an annulus?

For rational maps f \in \mathrm{Rat}_d on \hat{\mathbb{C}}, determine in the lowest degrees where Herman rings can occur exactly which low-degree configurations are realizable: in particular, classify the cubic maps admitting a fixed Herman ring and clarify which period-two Herman-ring configurations require degree 4, formulating realizability in terms of the associated critical-orbit constraints and Shishikura-style configuration/tree data, and describe the corresponding low-degree parameter loci by quasiconformal surgery and the resulting modulus-and-twist (Teichmüller-type) coordinates whenever such a parameterization is available.

In a natural parameterized family {f_lambda} of rational maps or transcendental meromorphic maps, how can a Herman ring—that is, a periodic doubly connected Fatou component on which some iterate of f_lambda is conformally conjugate to an irrational rotation of an annulus—be created or destroyed as the parameter lambda varies, and what are the structure and size of the parameter locus {lambda : f_lambda has a Herman ring}?

Let f be either a rational map of degree at least 2 on the Riemann sphere or a transcendental meromorphic function on the complex plane, and let H be a Herman ring of f (so H is a doubly connected periodic Fatou component with two connected boundary components). Determine the possible geometry of the connected components of ∂H: under what conditions are they Jordan curves or quasicircles, when can they instead have fractal structure, what can be said about the Hausdorff dimension and Lebesgue measure of ∂H, and can ∂H have positive area?

For a transcendental meromorphic function f with a Herman ring, can one develop an obstruction theory and identify structural conditions under which the Julia dynamics of f admit a topological mating with the action of a Fuchsian group on the upper half-plane, determine when such a topological mating can be promoted to a conformal mating, and characterize what dynamical feature distinguishes the resulting correspondence map in the presence of a Herman ring, including possible obstructions coming from incompatibility of laminations, singular value distributions, or boundary correspondences?
Let f be a rational map of degree at least 2 on the Riemann sphere whose Julia set J(f) is disconnected. If f has a Herman ring, must J(f) contain a buried Julia component?

Does there exist an iterative root-finding method for complex polynomials—i.e. a scheme that assigns to each complex polynomial p a rational map T_p whose roots are attracting fixed points—such that for at least one polynomial p, the Fatou set F(T_p) contains a Herman ring, that is, a periodic doubly connected Fatou component on which an iterate of T_p is conformally conjugate to an irrational rotation of an annulus?

Let f be a transcendental meromorphic function on C with at least one omitted value, and let H be a p-periodic Herman ring of f. If h denotes the number of H-relevant poles of H, meaning the number of poles that are surrounded by some Herman ring in the cycle containing H, does there exist a general upper bound p <= Phi(h) depending only on h? In particular, can such an upper bound be proved in the finitely-many-poles omitted-value setting singled out in the paper, thereby complementing the lower bounds of Theorem 5.9?

Let f be a transcendental meromorphic function on C with a stable Baker omitted value a; that is, a is an omitted value for which there exists a disk D centered at a such that every component of the boundary of f^{-1}(D) is bounded, and every iterate f^n is analytic in a neighborhood of a. Must f have no Herman ring?

Let f belong to M_o, the class of transcendental meromorphic functions with at least one omitted value, where M denotes the class of general meromorphic functions (those with at least two poles, or with exactly one pole that is not an omitted value). For a fixed period n (necessarily n >= 3 in this setting), is the number of possible configurations of an n-periodic cycle of Herman rings of f bounded above by a finite quantity depending only on n? Here, as in the paper, a configuration means the arrangement of the rings in the plane together with the locations of the H-relevant poles enclosed by the cycle and the mapping pattern of the rings under f.

Let f be a transcendental meromorphic function in M_o, where M is the class of transcendental meromorphic functions with at least two poles or with one pole that is not an omitted value, and M_o = {f in M : O_f is nonempty}. Suppose f has a quasi-nested wandering domain U; that is, U is a wandering Fatou component, U_n denotes the Fatou component containing f^n(U), and there exists a subsequence n_k -> infinity such that each U_{n_k} is bounded, each U_{n_k} surrounds 0, and U_{n_k} -> infinity. Must it follow that f has no Herman ring of any period?

Let f: ℂ → ℂ̂ be a transcendental meromorphic function in the paper’s class of general meromorphic maps, i.e. f has at least two poles, or exactly one pole whose location is not an omitted value of f. Assume that f has a finite omitted value a ∈ ℂ, meaning f(z) ≠ a for every z ∈ ℂ. Must it follow that f has no Herman ring of any period? ([ar5iv.labs.arxiv.org](https://ar5iv.labs.arxiv.org/pdf/2512.24118))

For fixed numerical invariants (n, N, V), can the characteristic-0 K-moduli theorem for log Fano pairs be extended to fields of positive characteristic, or even to an arithmetic setting over Spec Z; that is, can one construct in those settings an Artin stack of K-semistable log Fano pairs with those invariants, together with a separated proper good moduli space parameterizing K-polystable pairs and carrying an ample CM line bundle?
Let X \subset \mathbb{P}^{n+1}_{\mathbb{C}} be a smooth hypersurface of degree d, where 3 \le d \le n+1. Is X K-stable as a Fano variety?

For integers n and d with 3\le d\le n+1, let \mathfrak{H}_{n,d}^K denote the K-moduli good moduli space attached to the K-semistable degree-d hypersurfaces X_d\subset \mathbb{P}^{n+1}, whose general points correspond to general smooth n-dimensional degree-d hypersurfaces. Give an explicit description of \mathfrak{H}_{n,d}^K. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/html/2601.15576v1))

For every pair of integers n,k >= 1 and every choice of positive integers d_1,...,d_k satisfying k+2 <= d_1+...+d_k <= n+k, let X = H_1 ∩ ... ∩ H_k ⊂ P^{n+k} be a general n-dimensional complete intersection with deg(H_i)=d_i (over an algebraically closed field of characteristic 0). Must X be K-stable?

Fix integers g, r, d with gcd(r,d)=1, and let C be a smooth projective curve of genus g. Let M_{d,r}(C) denote the moduli space of rank-r polystable vector bundles on C with fixed determinant of degree d; as recalled in the paper, M_{d,r}(C) is then a smooth Fano variety. Is M_{d,r}(C) K-stable for every such curve C? Moreover, as [C] varies in M_g, the points [M_{d,r}(C)] lie in a K-moduli space that admits a birational map to M_g and is conjecturally isomorphic over M_g if the first question has an affirmative answer. Can one give a modular interpretation of the limiting points of this K-moduli space?
Is every smooth Fano threefold X with Picard number ρ(X)=1 K-semistable? ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2601.15576))
Is every smooth Gushel-Mukai Fano variety X, necessarily of dimension 3 <= dim X <= 6, K-stable?

Let X be a K-semistable Q-Fano variety (equivalently, a normal projective klt Fano variety). Can one give a purely algebraic proof that the reflexive tangent sheaf T_X is slope semistable with respect to the anticanonical polarization -K_X? More generally, assuming that T_X is slope polystable with respect to -K_X, can one give a purely algebraic proof that there exists a finite quasi-etale cover f:Y→X and a product decomposition Y ≅ X_1 × ... × X_r into Q-Fano varieties such that T_Y ≅ f^{[*]}T_X ≅ ⊕_{i=1}^r pr_i^*T_{X_i}, with each T_{X_i} slope stable with respect to -K_{X_i} (= c_1(X_i))?

Let X be a Fano variety, let Omega_X^[1] denote its reflexive cotangent sheaf, and let E be the canonical extension defined by the image of c_1(X) in H^1(X, Omega_X^[1]), namely
0 -> Omega_X^[1] -> E -> O_X -> 0.
Give an algebraic proof that E is slope-semistable with respect to the polarization -K_X whenever X is K-semistable, and slope-polystable with respect to -K_X whenever X is K-polystable.

Let x in X be a 2n-dimensional complex symplectic singularity, and let v_* in Val_{X,x} be the unique minimizer up to positive scaling of the normalized volume \hat{vol}_{x,X}(v)=A_X(v)^{2n} vol(v). Must v_* be divisorial, namely v_*=ord_E for a Kollár component E over x; equivalently, does there exist a projective birational morphism pi:(Y,E)->X extracting a prime divisor E with center x such that (Y,E) is purely log terminal and -E is pi-ample? If so, must its log discrepancy satisfy A_X(E)=rn for some r in {1,2}, and must the adjoint log Fano pair (E,Delta_E), defined by K_E+Delta_E=(K_Y+E)|_E, underlie an orbifold contact structure and be K-polystable?

Let x in X be an n-dimensional singular klt germ, with no boundary (so widehat{vol}(x,X) means the normalized volume widehat{vol}(x,X) := inf_{v in Val_{X,x}} A_X(v)^n vol(v)). Must one have widehat{vol}(x,X) <= 2(n-1)^n, with equality if and only if x in X is the n-dimensional A_1 singularity (ordinary double point)?

Let (X,\Delta) be a projective klt pair of log general type over an algebraically closed field of characteristic 0. Does there exist a constant \varepsilon=\varepsilon(X,\Delta)>0 such that for every (K_X+\Delta)-nonnegative birational map \phi\colon X\dashrightarrow X' to a normal projective variety, with \Delta' the strict transform of \Delta on X', and for every closed point x\in X', one has
\widehat{\mathrm{vol}}(x,X',\Delta')\ge \varepsilon?
Here '(K_X+\Delta)-nonnegative' means that on a common resolution p\colon W\to X and q\colon W\to X' one has p^*(K_X+\Delta)\le q^*(K_{X'}+\Delta').

Let x ∈ (X = Spec(R), Δ) be a germ of a klt singularity, let a• be a graded sequence of m_x-primary ideals, and set c := lct(X, Δ; a•) < +∞. Define
LCP(X, Δ + c·a•) := { v ∈ Val_{X,x} | c = A_{X,Δ}(v) / v(a•) }.
Is every valuation in LCP(X, Δ + c·a•) quasi-monomial? More strongly, does there exist a log smooth model (Y, E) → X such that LCP(X, Δ + c·a•) ⊆ QM(Y, E) and this subset is a cone over a connected convex set?

Can one develop software that generates benchmark families of parameterized linear systems, coming from parameterized discretizations of model partial differential equation problems rather than isolated one-off matrices, such that the resulting instances are broadly accepted as practically relevant and also suitable for rigorous theoretical analysis of linear-system solvers?

Fix a benchmark family of linear systems arising from a practically relevant, theoretically analyzable parameterized discretization of a model PDE—of the kind discussed in Section 2.1, such as diffusion, convection-diffusion, or Helmholtz problems, with parameters like coefficient field, convection field, wavenumber, and discretization choices. For each such benchmark family, can one develop algorithms for solving the resulting linear systems that are both provably fast and fast in practice across the family’s parameter range?

Problem 2.3 (Algebraic Multigrid Analysis for Theoretical Computer Scientists). Let M \in \mathbb{R}^{n\times n} belong to a c-polynomially bounded family of symmetric weakly-chained diagonally dominant M-matrices (SWCDDM), meaning that M is symmetric diagonally dominant, has nonpositive off-diagonal entries, and every weakly diagonally dominant row i (i.e. M_{ii}=\sum_{j\neq i}|M_{ij}|) lies on a chain of indices leading to a strictly diagonally dominant row; assume moreover that the family is c-polynomially bounded in the sense that \max_{i,j}|M_{ij}|\le n^c for some constant c independent of n. Show that, on input M, Algebraic Multigrid runs in \tilde{O}(\mathrm{nnz}(M)) time to compute an implicit symmetric operator Z that can be applied to a vector in O(\mathrm{nnz}(M)) time and satisfies \alpha M^{-1} \preceq Z \preceq \beta M^{-1} for absolute constants \alpha,\beta>0 independent of n, where \mathrm{nnz}(M) is the number of nonzero entries of M and \preceq denotes the Loewner order.

Fix ε>0 and p>0. For each n≥1, let A_n∈C^{n×n} be a random positive definite matrix of the form A_n=U_nΛ_nU_n^*, where U_n is Haar unitary and Λ_n=diag(1^{-p},2^{-p},...,n^{-p}); let z_n∈C^n be uniformly distributed on the unit sphere and set b_n=A_n z_n. For a strictly positive definite system Ax=b with exact solution x*=A^{-1}b and A-weighted norm ||v||_A=<Av,v>^{1/2}, define T_CG(A,b,ε)=min{t≥0: ||x_t^{CG}-x*||_A^2≤ε||x_0-x*||_A^2} and T_RCD(A,b,ε)=min{t≥0: ||x_t^{RCD}-x*||_A^2≤ε||x_0-x*||_A^2}, where RCD is the method from Definition 2.3: at each step choose i_t∈{1,...,n} with probability A(i_t,i_t)/tr(A) and update the i_t-th coordinate so that the i_t-th equation is satisfied exactly. What is the asymptotic behavior, as n→∞, of T_CG(A_n,b_n,ε) relative to T_RCD(A_n,b_n,ε)?

In the direct access model, where one may compute with A directly rather than only through oracle queries v -> {Av, A^⊤v}, does there exist an algorithm that, for every n×n matrix A with singular values σ1≥⋯≥σn>0 satisfying σ_{k+1}/σ_n ≤ κ (equivalently, A is an (n,k,0,κ) matrix in the sense of Definition 2.4) and every right-hand side b, solves Ax=b to high accuracy using ~O(k^ω + nnz(A)κ) arithmetic operations? ([znakschoola.ru](https://www.znakschoola.ru/?_=%2Fpdf%2F2602.05394%23UE7DkG0PaBHZOakR54g1Wl8%3D&utm_source=openai))

What is the smallest real number p>0 such that, for every invertible n×n matrix A with singular values \sigma_1\geq\cdots\geq\sigma_n>0 and every right-hand side b, the linear system Ax=b can be solved to high accuracy using \widetilde{O}(T_A\,\bar\kappa_p) arithmetic operations, where \bar\kappa_p:=\left(\frac{1}{n}\sum_{i=1}^n(\sigma_i/\sigma_n)^p\right)^{1/p} for p<\infty, \bar\kappa_\infty:=\sigma_1/\sigma_n, and T_A is either n^2 or nnz(A) (the number of nonzero entries of A)?

Let A be an n×n matrix with singular values σ1 ≥ ··· ≥ σn > 0, let l ∈ {0,…,n−1}, and suppose that A is an (n,0,l,κ) matrix in the sense of Definition 2.4, i.e. σ1/σn−l ≤ κ. For a given n-dimensional vector b, what is the complexity of solving the linear system Ax=b, and how does that complexity depend on whether A is given in the direct-access model or only through matrix-vector products?

Let A be an n × n random matrix with i.i.d. Gaussian, Rademacher, or Bernoulli entries, and let b be an arbitrary real n-dimensional vector. Is it possible, conditioned on a high-probability event over the draw of A, to solve the linear system Ax = b to high accuracy faster than O(n^ω), where ω denotes the matrix-multiplication exponent? ([znakschoola.ru](https://www.znakschoola.ru/?_=%2Fpdf%2F2602.05394%23UE7DkG0PaBHZOakR54g1Wl8%3D&utm_source=openai))

Let $A\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times n}$ (or $\mathbb{C}^{n\times n}$) have singular values $\sigma_1\ge\sigma_2\ge\cdots\ge\sigma_n>0$, and let $k,l\in\{0,\dots,n\}$ satisfy $k+l<n$. Following Definition 2.4, call $A$ an $(n,k,l,\kappa)$ matrix if $\sigma_{k+1}/\sigma_{n-l}\le\kappa$. What is the bit complexity, in the Word-RAM / finite-precision model, of solving linear systems $Ax=b$ when $A$ is an $(n,k,l,\kappa)$ matrix? In particular, when $l=0$, can the exact-arithmetic direct-access bound \u007etilde-O$(k^\omega+n^2\kappa)$ (where $\omega$ is the matrix multiplication exponent) for solving $(n,k,0,\kappa)$ systems be extended to the Word-RAM model?

What is the bit complexity, in the Word-RAM model, of solving a sparse n × n linear system Ax = b when nnz(A) denotes the number of nonzero entries of A? In particular, does the real-RAM \~O(n · nnz(A)) running time extend to the Word-RAM model?

Can the eigenvalue-localization approach of [GNS22, NS24]—which, for certain elliptic PDE model problems such as −∇·(k(x)∇u)=f and the associated discretized linear systems, yields exact localization of the eigenvalues of the discretized operator and of the left-preconditioned matrix under Laplacian preconditioning—be extended to other classes of PDEs or to other preconditioners? ([znakschoola.ru](https://www.znakschoola.ru/?_=%2Fpdf%2F2602.05394%23UE7DkG0PaBHZOakR54g1Wl8%3D&utm_source=openai))

For a square nonsingular nonnormal matrix A over R or C and a linear system Ax = b, can one derive a GMRES convergence bound for the relative residual history ||r_k||_2 / ||r_0||_2, where r_k = b - A x_k, that is genuinely descriptive of the observed iteration-by-iteration convergence and, in particular, captures the early transient (pre-asymptotic) phase rather than only asymptotic behavior?

Identify a concrete, interesting non-selfadjoint model problem (or, at the matrix level, a nonsymmetric linear system Ax=b) together with a preconditioner M such that the proven eigenvalue distribution of the left-preconditioned matrix M^{-1}A genuinely matches the actual convergence behavior of GMRES—for example, if M^{-1}A has m eigenvalue clusters, then GMRES reaches an acceptable approximate solution in O(m) iterations—and determine which specific properties of the model problem and preconditioner make this eigenvalue-distribution/convergence correspondence valid.

Let A be a highly nonnormal nonsymmetric matrix arising from a streamline-upwind/Petrov-Galerkin (SUPG) discretization of a convection-diffusion model problem, and suppose GMRES is applied to Ax=b. In examples of this type, the GMRES residual often exhibits an initial transient phase of slow decay followed by a noticeably faster decay. Which properties of the underlying PDE, the SUPG discretization, or the matrix A govern this post-transient acceleration, and can the speed of this later GMRES convergence be explained in terms of spectral data of A—specifically the locations of its eigenvalues together with the conditioning of its eigenvectors—or is such eigeninformation insufficient?

Let A be the coefficient matrix of a symmetric positive definite linear system Ax = b, and let CG or steepest descent be implemented in floating-point arithmetic from an initial guess x_0 via the standard short recurrences x_k = x_{k-1} + a_{k-1} p_{k-1} and r_k = r_{k-1} - a_{k-1} A p_{k-1}, where a_{k-1} and p_{k-1} are the computed step length and search direction. Since these recursively updated vectors r_k need not equal the true residuals b - A x_k in finite precision arithmetic, determine conditions on A that guarantee that the norms ||r_k|| eventually drop below machine precision, or else construct examples of matrices A for which these recursively updated residual vectors do not drop below machine precision.

Let A ∈ R^{n×n} be symmetric positive definite, let b ∈ R^n, and fix an initial guess x0 (so the common starting residual is r0 = b − Ax0). Although CG and Lanczos are equivalent in exact arithmetic, determine whether standard good floating-point implementations of CG and of Lanczos, when both are used to solve Ax = b from the same starting data, must exhibit similar finite-precision behavior, or whether they can behave genuinely differently.

For the standard unpreconditioned conjugate-gradient method executed in finite-precision floating-point arithmetic with b-bit significand precision, what is the smallest worst-case precision b = b(n, ε) that guarantees the following: for every real symmetric positive definite matrix A ∈ R^{n×n}, every right-hand side b_vec ∈ R^n, and every tolerance ε > 0, the computed CG iterates contain some x_hat_k with k ≤ n whose normwise backward error is at most ε, in the standard normwise sense for linear systems?

For the standard non-block symmetric Lanczos algorithm applied to a symmetric matrix A, possibly with a preconditioner M, suppose that matrix-vector products and/or preconditioner applications are available only through a general inexact model—for example, computed products satisfy fl(Ax)=(A+ΔA)x and computed preconditioned vectors z for residuals r satisfy (M+ΔM)z=r, without requiring an explicit formula for ΔA or ΔM. Develop a Paige-style analysis of the resulting computed Lanczos process under such general inexact-operator models, obtaining bounds or structural descriptions that either genuinely extend Paige’s finite-precision analysis or provide a simpler, more interpretable account of the algorithm’s behavior. ([znakschoola.ru](https://www.znakschoola.ru/?_=%2Fpdf%2F2602.05394%23UE7DkG0PaBHZOakR54g1Wl8%3D&utm_source=openai))

In the finite-precision setting for symmetric Krylov methods, extend Paige's finite-precision analysis of the standard Lanczos algorithm to the block Lanczos algorithm for a real symmetric matrix A and an initial block V1: after either (i) specifying quantitative accuracy assumptions for the within-block orthogonalization, or (ii) fixing a specific standard numerically "good" orthogonalization procedure, develop a Paige-style description of the computed block Lanczos process that explicitly handles block rank deficiency and deflation and that yields theoretical justification and insight for the practical behavior of block Krylov methods in finite precision arithmetic.

Problem 3.1 (Deterministic Pseudospectral Shattering). Given an arbitrary matrix A ∈ ℂ^{n×n} and a parameter δ>0, design a provably correct deterministic algorithm that outputs a perturbation E with ∥E∥≤δ such that κ_eig(A+E)≤C(n/δ)^c for universal constants C,c>0, where κ_eig(B):=κ_V(B)/gap(B), gap(B):=min_{i≠j}|λ_i−λ_j|, and κ_V(B) denotes the condition number of a matrix of normalized eigenvectors of B. The algorithm should run in O(n^3 log^c(n/δ)) arithmetic operations; more ambitiously, achieve the same guarantee in finite precision using only O(log^c(n/δ)) bits of precision.

Given an n x n Hermitian tridiagonal matrix A and a perturbation size δ>0, design a deterministic algorithm that outputs a diagonal Hermitian perturbation E such that the minimum gap between consecutive eigenvalues of A+δE satisfies gap(A+δE) >= C(δ/n)^c for some constants C,c>0 independent of A, n, and δ. The algorithm should be efficient in the paper's sense: asymptotically faster than the parent eigenvalue algorithm in which the perturbation is used, with O(n^3 log^k(n/δ)) arithmetic operations as the benchmark scale for full diagonalization.

Given n, an arbitrary matrix A in C^{n x n}, and a backward-error tolerance δ > 0, give a provable randomized algorithm that computes either (i) a backward-error diagonalization of A, meaning an invertible matrix V and a diagonal matrix D with ||A - VDV^{-1}|| <= δ after the standard normalization ||A|| <= 1 (equivalently, after rescaling the input), or (ii) a backward-error Schur form of A, meaning a unitary matrix Q and an upper-triangular matrix T with ||A - QTQ*|| <= δ; and do so in O(n^3 log^c(n/δ)) arithmetic operations for some universal constant c while using only O(log(n/δ)) bits of precision throughout. ([ar5iv.labs.arxiv.org](https://ar5iv.labs.arxiv.org/html/2602.05394v1))

Let A ∈ ℂ^{n×n}. Let V̂ ⊂ ℂ^n be a d-dimensional approximate invariant subspace of A in the sense that there exists a d-dimensional A-invariant subspace V with ∠(V, V̂) small. Let W ⊂ ℂ^n be any subspace of dimension r < n - d, and let Q ∈ ℂ^{n×(d+r)} have orthonormal columns spanning the (generically) d + r dimensional space 𝒬 = V̂ + W. What conditions guarantee that d eigenvalues of the Ritz matrix Q*AQ approximate the d eigenvalues of A associated with the invariant subspace V? You may impose additional assumptions on those eigenvalues of A, such as spectral separation, if needed.

Let A ∈ C^{n×n}, let b be a random starting vector, and let Q be an orthonormal basis of a Krylov subspace K_k(A,b)=span{b,Ab,...,A^{k-1}b} generated by A and b. Is the eigenvector condition number κ_V(Q*AQ) polynomially bounded in n with high probability, where κ_V(M):=inf_{M=VDV^{-1}} ||V||·||V^{-1}|| (with κ_V(M)=∞ if M is not diagonalizable)? Alternatively, does one have an upper bound E[area(Λ_ε(Q*AQ))] ≤ poly(n)·ε^β for some exponent β close to 2, where Λ_ε(M)={z∈C:σ_min(zI−M)≤ε} and area denotes planar Lebesgue measure on C? This problem remains open even when A is a circulant shift matrix.

Let A ∈ C^{n×n} be non-Hermitian, and let Q ∈ C^{n×k}, with 1<k<n, have orthonormal columns. Writing Λ(Q^*AQ) for the Ritz values of A with respect to Q and W(A)={v^*Av : ||v||_2=1} for the numerical range of A, what deterministic or probabilistic statements can be made about how the Ritz values Λ(Q^*AQ) are distributed within W(A)? In particular, what can be proved when Q is (i) an orthonormal basis of the Krylov subspace K_k(A,b)=span{b,Ab,...,A^{k-1}b}, or (ii) an orthonormal basis of a k-dimensional random subspace of C^n?

Give a rigorous theoretical-computer-science-style analysis of a floating-point implementation of the Multiple Relatively Robust Representations (MRRR, or MR3) algorithm for the real symmetric tridiagonal eigenproblem: namely, identify sufficient conditions on an input matrix T in R^{n x n} that are easy to verify from the input and prove that, whenever those conditions hold, MR3 converges/terminates and correctly computes the desired eigenvalues and eigenvectors of T.

Let B ∈ C^{n×n} be an n×n (upper) bidiagonal matrix, let 1 ≤ k ≤ n, and let ε denote machine precision. Does there exist an algorithm that uses O(kn) operations and outputs k approximate singular triplets (σ_i, v_i, u_i) for B, with σ_i ≥ 0 and unit vectors v_i, u_i ∈ C^n, such that for every i = 1, ..., k one has ||B v_i - σ_i u_i||_2 = O(ε n ||B||_2), and for every i ≠ j one has |v_i^H v_j| = O(ε n) and |u_i^H u_j| = O(ε n)?

Let A∈C^{n×n} be a diagonalizable, not necessarily normal matrix with diagonalization A=VΛV^{-1}. Let λ1:=max_i |λ_i(A)| be the largest eigenvalue modulus, and assume the eigenvector condition number κ_V:=∥V∥∥V^{-1}∥ is finite. Given only oracle access to matrix-vector products v↦Av and an accuracy parameter ε∈(0,1), does there exist an algorithm that uses poly(log(nκ_V),1/ε) such matrix-vector products and returns a scalar λ∈C for which there exists an eigenvalue λ′ of A satisfying |λ′|≥(1−ε)λ1 and |λ−λ′|≤ελ1? ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2602.05394))

For the discrete Lehmann representation kernel K(t,ω)=e^{-tω}/(1+e^{-ω}), arising in G(t)=∫_{-Λ}^{Λ} K(t,ω)ρ(ω)dω and restricted to (t,ω)∈[0,1]×[-Λ,Λ], prove improved error-versus-rank bounds for the rank-k cross approximation ĤK_k produced by Gaussian elimination with complete pivoting. More precisely, by exploiting the specific structure of this kernel, obtain a GECP guarantee in the paper’s infinity norm that is substantially sharper than the existing analytic-kernel bound k=O(Λ+log(1/ε)) ⇒ ||K-ĤK_k||∞≤ε, ideally clarifying why GECP empirically behaves much closer to the benchmark existence rate k=O(log(Λ)log(1/ε)) ⇒ ||K-K_k||∞≤ε.

Let Q ∈ R^{n×k} with k < n and Q^TQ = I_k. Apply the standard QR factorization with column pivoting (QRCP) to Q^T, and let I ⊂ {1,…,n}, |I| = k, be the indices corresponding to the first k pivot columns of Q^T (equivalently, the k selected rows of Q). It is known that there exists an index set I for which ||(Q(I,:))^{-1}||_2 ≤ √(k(n-k+1)). Does the QRCP algorithm used in practice itself always return an index set I satisfying this bound, or at least a comparably strong non-exponential bound on ||(Q(I,:))^{-1}||_2, for every such Q?

Let A \in \mathbb{C}^{n\times m} with n \gg m be a (generally non-symmetric) kernel matrix with entries A_{ij}=f(x_i,\omega_j). Assume that A admits an accurate k-column approximation, i.e. there is a set J of k column indices such that A \approx A(:,J)T, equivalently \Pi_J A is a good column-subset approximation, where \Pi_J denotes the projection onto \operatorname{col}(A(:,J)). If I \subseteq \{1,\dots,n\} is a uniformly random set of r=O(k) row indices and one chooses a set \u007eJ of column indices from the sampled matrix A(I,:) so that A(I,:) \approx A(I,\u007eJ)\u007eT, what direct, efficiently verifiable sufficient conditions on r and on the kernel f guarantee, with high probability over I, that \|\Pi_{\u007eJ}A-A\|_F \le c(n,m,k)\,\|\Pi_JA-A\|_F, where c(n,m,k) grows at most logarithmically in n, m, and k? In other words, when does column selection on a uniformly row-subsampled kernel matrix perform comparably to column selection on the full matrix?

Fix integers n >= 1 and 1 <= k < n, and let λ=(λ_1,...,λ_n) in (0,∞)^n. For each orthogonal matrix V in O(n), set K=V^\top diag(λ)V, and for each subset I \subseteq [n]:={1,...,n} with |I|=k define the column-subset-selection/Nyström trace residual by R(K,I):=Tr(K-K_{:,I}K_{I,I}^{-1}K_{I,:}). Define x_k(λ):=max_{V in O(n)} min_{I \subseteq [n], |I|=k} R(K,I), where K=V^\top diag(λ)V. Also define y_k(λ):=(E_{I ~ k-DPP(K)} R(K,I))|_{K=diag(λ)}=(k+1)e_{k+1}(λ)/e_k(λ), where e_j(λ)=sum_{J \subseteq [n], |J|=j} prod_{i in J} λ_i. Prove sharp comparison bounds between x_k(λ) and y_k(λ), uniformly over λ; equivalently, determine how tight the spectrum-only k-DPP/volume-sampling objective y_k(λ) is as a proxy for the worst-case optimal column-subset-selection trace error x_k(λ).

Let A in R^{n x d} have full column rank, let B in R^{n x p}, and let Omega in R^{n x k} be a random matrix that is an oblivious subspace injection for d-dimensional subspaces with injectivity 1-epsilon, in the sense that E||Omega^T x||_2^2 = ||x||_2^2 for every x in R^n, and for every fixed d-dimensional subspace V subseteq R^n one has (1-epsilon)||x||_2^2 <= ||Omega^T x||_2^2 for all x in V with probability at least 1-delta, where delta is some fixed small constant (suppressed in the paper when unspecified). Define the sketch-and-solve estimator X~ := (Omega^T A)^+ (Omega^T B) in R^{d x p}, and let X := A^+ B, equivalently the unique minimizer of min_{Y in R^{d x p}} ||AY-B||_F. Prove or disprove: does the OSI assumption alone force the relative-error bound ||AX~ - B||_F <= (1 + O(epsilon)) min_{Y in R^{d x p}} ||AY - B||_F (with the corresponding success probability over Omega)?

Let \(A\in\mathbb R^{n\times d}\), let \(r\in\mathbb N\), and let \(\Omega\in\mathbb R^{n\times k}\) be an oblivious subspace injection of dimension \(r\) and injectivity \(1-\varepsilon\) in the sense of Definition 5.1: for every \(x\in\mathbb R^n\), \(\mathbb E\|\Omega^\top x\|_2^2=\|x\|_2^2\), and for every fixed \(r\)-dimensional subspace \(V\subseteq\mathbb R^n\), with the OSI failure probability (which, if left unspecified as in the paper, may be taken to be a fixed small absolute constant), one has \(\|\Omega^\top x\|_2^2\ge (1-\varepsilon)\|x\|_2^2\) for all \(x\in V\). Define the randomized SVD approximation by \(\widetilde A:=(A\Omega)(A\Omega)^+A\), where \((\cdot)^+\) denotes the Moore–Penrose pseudoinverse, and let \(A_r\) be a best rank-\(r\) approximation to \(A\) in Frobenius norm. Prove or disprove that OSI alone guarantees a relative-error bound of the form \(\|A-\widetilde A\|_F\le (1+C\varepsilon)\|A-A_r\|_F\) for some absolute constant \(C\), uniformly over all such \(A\) and \(\Omega\).

In Definition 5.1, an oblivious subspace injection (OSI) is an ℓ_2-based condition on a random sketching matrix Ω ∈ R^{n×k}. For the ℓ_p linear regression problem min_{x∈R^d} ||Ax-b||_{ℓ_p}, where A ∈ R^{n×d} and b ∈ R^n, and for the sketch-and-solve estimator ṽx ∈ argmin_{x∈R^d} ||Ω^T(Ax-b)||_{ℓ_p}, formulate an ℓ_p analogue of the OSI property—that is, a condition on the distribution of Ω playing the role of OSI in the ℓ_p setting—which is sufficient to guarantee constant-factor accuracy of sketch-and-solve: ||Aṽx-b||_{ℓ_p} ≤ C · min_{x∈R^d} ||Ax-b||_{ℓ_p} for some absolute constant C. ([znakschoola.ru](https://www.znakschoola.ru/?_=%2Fpdf%2F2602.05394%23UE7DkG0PaBHZOakR54g1Wl8%3D&utm_source=openai))

Let n,r ∈ N with r ≤ n and let ε ∈ (0,1). For integers ζ,b ≥ 1, set k := bζ, and let Ω ∈ R^{n×k} be a SparseStack random matrix in the sense of Definition 5.2: the i-th row of Ω is (1/√ζ)[ρ_{i1}e^*_{s_{i1}}, …, ρ_{iζ}e^*_{s_{iζ}}], where the ρ_{ij} are iid Rademacher random variables and the s_{ij} are iid uniform on {1,…,b} (equivalently, Ω^T ∈ R^{k×n} has exactly ζ nonzeros in each column, one in each of ζ blocks of size b). Prove or disprove that there exist absolute constants C1,C2 and an absolute failure probability δ < 1 such that, whenever ζ ≤ C1(log r)/ε and k ≤ C2 r/ε^2, then for every fixed r-dimensional subspace V ⊆ R^n, with probability at least 1−δ over Ω, one has (1−ε)||x||_2^2 ≤ ||Ω^T x||_2^2 ≤ (1+ε)||x||_2^2 for all x ∈ V.

Let ζ, b ∈ N with k = bζ, and let Ω ∈ R^{n×k} be a SparseStack random matrix in the sense of Definition 5.2: for each i ∈ {1, ..., n} and j ∈ {1, ..., ζ}, choose iid Rademacher signs ϱ_{ij} and iid locations s_{ij} uniformly from {1, ..., b}, and set Ω to be (1/√ζ) times the horizontal concatenation of the corresponding one-sparse row blocks. Assume the subspace dimension and ambient dimension satisfy r ≤ C n/\log n for some absolute constant C, and let V ⊆ R^n be any fixed r-dimensional subspace. Prove or disprove that there exist absolute constants ζ_0, c, α > 0 such that whenever Ω is drawn with row sparsity ζ ≤ ζ_0 and embedding dimension k ≤ c r, then with at least 0.99 probability it is an oblivious subspace injection for V; that is, E||Ω^T x||_2^2 = ||x||_2^2 for every x ∈ R^n and α||x||_2^2 ≤ ||Ω^T x||_2^2 for every x ∈ V. In particular, does the fixed choice ζ = 4 and k = 2r (equivalently b = r/2, so literally when r is even) satisfy this OSI property for all sufficiently large r? ([znakschoola.ru](https://www.znakschoola.ru/?_=%2Fpdf%2F2602.05394%23UE7DkG0PaBHZOakR54g1Wl8%3D&utm_source=openai))

Let Omega in R^{n x k} be the rerandomized subsampled randomized Hadamard transform defined by Omega = sqrt(n/k) D1 F D2 F S, where F is the n x n Walsh-Hadamard matrix, D1 and D2 are independent diagonal matrices with iid Rademacher (+/-1) entries, and S is the random coordinate-selection matrix that keeps k uniformly random positions. Assume n = Omega(log r). Prove or disprove that, for k = O(r/epsilon^2), Omega is an oblivious subspace embedding for r-dimensional subspaces of R^n with distortion parameters alpha = 1 - epsilon and beta = 1 + epsilon; that is, for every fixed r-dimensional subspace V subseteq R^n, with some fixed small failure probability over the randomness in Omega, one has (1 - epsilon)||x||_2^2 <= ||Omega^T x||_2^2 <= (1 + epsilon)||x||_2^2 for all x in V.

Fix an m-node tree tensor network T (for example, tensor train or Tucker) together with prescribed dimensions on its internal edges, and let S be the set of tensors in R^{d_1 x ... x d_n} representable by that fixed network. Does there exist a polynomial-time algorithm that, given any tensor A in R^{d_1 x ... x d_n}, outputs X in S satisfying ||X-A||_F^2 < (m-1) min_{Y in S} ||Y-A||_F^2? If not, can one show, under standard complexity-theoretic assumptions, that the factor (m-1) achieved by the known recursive SVD-based algorithms is optimal?

For each integer m >= 0 and each gap parameter delta in (0,1), let I_delta = [-1,-delta] union [delta,1], and let Pi_{2m}^* be the set of real univariate polynomials p whose corresponding matrix functions p(A) can be computed using at most m matrix-matrix multiplications together with arbitrarily many matrix additions and scalar multiplications. Define epsilon_m^*(delta) := min_{p in Pi_{2m}^*} max_{x in I_delta} |p(x) - sign(x)|, where sign(x) = -1 for x < 0 and sign(x) = 1 for x > 0. Determine the asymptotic dependence of epsilon_m^*(delta) on m and delta.

For the standard magnetic billiard in a strong constant magnetic field, where the particle moves between reflections along Larmor circles, does total integrability in the paper's sense - namely, that the relevant phase-space region is foliated by invariant graphs - imply that the billiard table is a circle?

Let N be a possibly non-symmetric Minkowski norm on R^2, let B_N={x∈R^2:N(x)≤1} be its unit ball, and let γ=∂B_N be parameterized by N-arclength, so that N(γ̇(s))=1. Consider the Minkowski billiard in B_N, viewed as the twist map generated by L(s_0,s_1)=N(γ(s_1)-γ(s_0)). If this billiard is totally integrable on its whole phase space, in the sense that the phase space is foliated by invariant graph tori, must N be a Euclidean norm? ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/html/2602.12896v1))

For the time-periodic Newton equation \ddot u=-\partial_u V(u,t), with V periodic in both u and t (equivalently V:\mathbb T^2\to\mathbb R), let H(u,p,t)=\tfrac12 p^2+V(u,t) be the associated Hamiltonian system on the extended phase space. Here "totally integrable at infinity" means that there exists C>0 such that the region \{|p|>C\} is foliated by invariant graph tori of the flow. Besides the known family V(u,t)=W(nu+mt) with m,n\in\mathbb Z, for which there is an additional first integral quadratic in p and hence total integrability in a neighborhood of infinity, are there any other periodic potentials V for which the system is totally integrable at infinity?

Let V: R^n x R -> R be a potential that is 1-periodic in all n+1 variables, and consider the Euler-Lagrange equation Delta u(x) = -partial_u V(x,u(x)) for functions u: R^n -> R, associated with the functional integral of (1/2)|grad u|^2 + V(x,u). Assume that for every rotation vector alpha in R^n, the torus T^(n+1) = R^(n+1)/Z^(n+1) admits a foliation by the projected graphs of minimal solutions of this equation having slope alpha. Must it follow that V is independent of u?

Let N be a closed orientable surface of genus at least 2 equipped with a hyperbolic metric g, let D_g^*N := {(q,p) in T^*N : |p|_g <= 1} be its unit cotangent disk bundle, and let λ denote the canonical Liouville 1-form on T^*N. Is the Hofer-Zehnder capacity c_HZ(D_g^*N, dλ) finite?

Fix an orientable closed hyperbolic surface N. Does there exist a sequence (Ω_i)_{i≥1} of embedded billiard tables Ω_i⊂N, each open and simply connected (hence lifting to an open subset of the hyperbolic plane with compact closure), such that Ω_i-sys→∞ as i→∞, where Ω_i-sys denotes the billiard-systolic length of Ω_i, i.e. the length of the shortest billiard trajectory in the sense used in the paper?

Let (M,ω) be a closed (compact, without boundary) symplectic manifold, and let φ∈Ham(M,ω) be a Hamiltonian diffeomorphism, i.e. the time-one map of a Hamiltonian isotopy. For T>0, let P(T) denote the number of primitive periodic orbits of φ whose least period n∈ℕ satisfies n≤T, where each periodic orbit is counted once at its least period (so iterates are not counted separately). Must the following dichotomy hold: either φ has only finitely many periodic orbits, or liminf_{T→∞} (log P(T))/(log T) ≥ 2?

Let varphi be a Hamiltonian diffeomorphism of a standard symplectic torus (T^{2n}, omega_std), and for T>0 let P(T) denote the number of primitive periodic orbits of varphi whose least period is at most T (so multiply covered orbits are not counted). Must one have lim inf_{T -> +infinity} log P(T) / log T >= 2? More generally, does the same quadratic-growth lower bound hold for every Hamiltonian diffeomorphism of an arbitrary aspherical closed symplectic manifold? ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2602.12896))

Let phi be a Hamiltonian diffeomorphism of complex projective space CP^n, equipped with its standard symplectic structure, and for each T > 0 let P(T) denote the number of primitive periodic orbits of phi of period at most T (so iterates are not counted separately). If phi has infinitely many periodic orbits, must one have lim inf_{T -> +infinity} log P(T) / log T >= 2? ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/html/2602.12896v1))

Can one construct nontrivial physically meaningful infinite-dimensional billiard systems whose free-flight dynamics come from geodesic equations on infinite-dimensional spaces arising in mathematical physics—especially Euler-Arnold equations such as incompressible Euler on the group of volume-preserving diffeomorphisms with its right-invariant L^2 metric, and analogously KdV, magnetohydrodynamics, or the Heisenberg chain—and, in particular, can one formulate a billiard-type reflection theory for a continuum of particles hitting a boundary by using the generalized-flow/diffeomorphism-groupoid framework for two-phase or multi-phase fluids, via suitable boundary conditions that encode billiard reflection? ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/html/2602.12896v1))

Does there exist a planar pensive billiard on a smooth domain D⊂R^2 with smooth closed boundary γ=∂D and delay function \tilde{\ell}(\theta) (equivalently ℓ(p), p=\cos\theta), where the pensive billiard map is the classical billiard map followed by translation along γ by arc-length \tilde{\ell}(\theta) depending only on the incidence angle, such that \tilde{\ell}\not\equiv0 and the resulting dynamics is integrable, and can one exhibit explicit genuinely nontrivial examples beyond the easy cases of the circle with arbitrary delay and the ellipse with its special delay?

Construct a continuous version of the one-dimensional elastic-collision theory of point particles with positive and negative masses that is motivated by the three-bead-on-a-ring model: for masses m1, m2, m3 on a frictionless ring, after reduction by rotational symmetry the dynamics is equivalent to billiards in a triangle with tan(alpha1) = sqrt(m1(m1 + m2 + m3)/(m2 m3)) and cyclic permutations, and allowing negative masses subject to (m1 + m2 + m3)m1m2m3 > 0 yields the obtuse-triangle regime. In the corresponding fixed-triangle viewpoint, where negative masses lead to a pseudo-Euclidean metric, formulate the associated Euler-like equations for a "fluid of negative density" and investigate whether they exhibit interesting phenomena.

Let L be the symplectic manifold of oriented affine lines in R^(n+1), canonically symplectomorphic to T^*S^n. For a convex billiard table T subset R^(n+1), let W_T subset L be its induced billiard domain, namely the set of oriented lines that intersect T; under the identification L ≅ T^*S^n, W_T becomes a fiber-wise convex domain. Characterize exactly which fiber-wise convex domains W subset T^*S^n arise in this way, i.e. for which W there exists a convex billiard table T subset R^(n+1) such that W = W_T.

Let L(R^{n+1}) denote the symplectic manifold of oriented lines in R^{n+1}, identified symplectomorphically with T^*S^n. For a convex billiard table K in R^{n+1}, let W_K be the induced billiard domain consisting of oriented lines that intersect K; under the identification L(R^{n+1}) ≅ T^*S^n, W_K is a fiber-wise convex domain. Its billiard reflection map beta_K: W_K -> W_K preserves the symplectic form, is smooth and Hamiltonian on int(W_K), and is only continuous along ∂W_K (in the paper's terminology, it is C^0-Hamiltonian). Characterize those C^0-Hamiltonian self-maps f: W -> W of a fiber-wise convex domain W ⊂ T^*S^n for which there exists a convex billiard table K ⊂ R^{n+1} and a symplectic identification W ≅ W_K carrying f to the billiard map beta_K.

Conjecture. Let M be a closed manifold that is not a K(pi,1), and equip T^*M with its standard symplectic form. If Sigma subset T^*M is a closed connected hypersurface and H:T^*M -> R is a smooth autonomous Hamiltonian with Sigma = H^{-1}(c) a regular energy level for some c in R, must there exist epsilon > 0 such that for Lebesgue-almost every e in (c - epsilon, c + epsilon), the energy level H^{-1}(e) carries a contractible periodic orbit of the Hamiltonian flow of H?

For a tiling billiard on a periodic plane polygonal tiling—where a trajectory moves straight inside each tile and crosses an edge into the adjacent tile by the tiling-billiard refraction rule—is there a finite list of generic archetypal behaviors for typical trajectories? More specifically, does the general dichotomy suggested by the known examples hold for all such periodic tiling billiards: namely, that typical trajectories are either dense in open sets of the plane, or else the dynamics is integrable in the sense that typical trajectories are periodic or linearly escaping?

For the tiling billiard on the periodic tiling of R^2 by copies of a single parallelogram, where a particle moves linearly inside each tile and, upon crossing an edge, is refracted according to Snell's law with refraction coefficient -1, and where the tile has sides parallel to a_vec=(a,0) and b_vec=(b sin alpha, b cos alpha) with a,b>0, alpha in (0,pi), and shape parameter m=a/b, describe the dynamics of the trajectories, at least for generic initial conditions, as a function of the parameters (alpha,m). ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2602.12896))

Exhibit a concrete real-world dissipative system—arising naturally in physics, mechanics, biology, economics, or a comparable applied domain—whose evolution is genuinely modeled by a locally conformal symplectic structure rather than merely by the globally conformally symplectic constant-factor case: namely, find a smooth phase space carrying a locally conformal symplectic structure (M, η, ω), with η a closed 1-form and ω a nondegenerate 2-form satisfying d_ηω = 0 for d_η = d - η∧, together with a continuous-time dynamics generated by a vector field X for which there exists a smooth function a such that L_Xω = aω and L_Xη = da (and, if one wishes to work in discrete time, an analogous map preserving the l.c.s. structure up to local conformal rescaling). In particular, identify examples that realize the paper’s intended regime of non-uniform or spatially dependent dissipation and are not just globally conformally symplectic models in disguise. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/html/2602.12896v1))

Let M be a finite-dimensional compact connected smooth Riemannian manifold, let λ be the Liouville 1-form on T^*M, let η be a closed 1-form on T^*M, and endow T^*M with the exact locally conformal symplectic form ω := -d_η λ = -dλ + η ∧ λ. Suppose X = (ẋ, ṗ) is a conformally symplectic vector field with Hamiltonian H in the sense that i_Xω = d_ηH. Writing locally η = η̄_x(x,p) · dx + η̄_p(x,p) · dp and setting f := η(X), so that the motion satisfies ẋ = ∂_pH + (p · ẋ - H)η̄_p and ṗ = -∂_xH + fp - (p · ẋ - H)η̄_x, does there exist a genuine physical or mechanical system whose dynamics is modeled by these equations, and what physical interpretation should be assigned to the locally conformal correction terms—especially, in the special case η = π^*η̄ and H Tonelli, to the term (p · ẋ - H)η̄_x = L(x, ẋ)η̄_x?

In the exact locally conformal symplectic cotangent-bundle model of Section 2.2, let M be a finite-dimensional compact connected smooth Riemannian manifold, let lambda be the Liouville 1-form on T^*M, let bar_eta = pi^*eta for a closed 1-form eta on M, and let H: T^*M -> R be a Tonelli Hamiltonian with Legendre transform L(x,v) = <p,v> - H(x,p), where v = partial_p H(x,p). For the Hamiltonian conformally symplectic flow associated to H in this setting, the equations reduce to xdot = partial_p H and pdot = -partial_x H + f p - L(x,xdot) bar_eta_x, with f = i_X bar_eta = eta_x(xdot). Beyond the expected momentum-related dissipation/repulsion term f p, does the additional term -L(x,xdot) bar_eta_x admit a natural physical or mechanical interpretation, and does it arise in any genuine real-world system modeled by these locally conformal symplectic equations?

Given a projective billiard table, namely a convex domain with smooth boundary equipped with a transverse field of directions, with reflection law defined so that the tangential component of the incoming velocity is preserved and the transverse component is reversed, characterize precisely when the induced billiard dynamics on the same phase space as the conventional billiard preserves a symplectic form, and characterize when it admits a variational description.

For a fixed integer n ≥ 2 and a closed immersed submanifold i: M → R^N, estimate from below, in terms of the topology of M and the immersion i, the number of generalized n-periodic billiard trajectories on M, where such a trajectory means an n-gon inscribed in M (all vertices on M) whose perimeter is extremal among inscribed n-gons. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2602.12896))

Let P be a planar convex polygon, with its sides labeled by a finite alphabet, and consider all symplectic billiard trajectories in P for which the polygonal symplectic billiard map is defined. For each such trajectory, record the bi-infinite symbolic word of the labels of the sides visited by the trajectory, and let p_P(n) be the number of distinct length-n subwords occurring among all these bi-infinite codes. Determine the asymptotic growth of the complexity function p_P(n) for polygonal symplectic billiards, allowing in particular for the fully periodic examples noted in the paper, where the complexity may have zero growth rate. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/html/2602.12896v1))
Does there exist a convex planar domain Ω ⊂ R^2 with C^1-smooth boundary such that the associated planar symplectic billiard map for Ω exhibits chaotic dynamics?

Let M be a germ of a smooth hypersurface in the standard symplectic vector space (R^{2n}, ω_0), and let its characteristic curves be the integral curves of the characteristic line field ker(ω_0|_{TM}). Assume that every characteristic curve of M is planar, i.e. each such curve is contained in an affine 2-plane of R^{2n}. How restrictive is this condition on M?

Let Ω ⊂ R^n be a domain with smooth boundary, and let P ∈ Ω be a generic interior point. For each t ≥ 0, let F_t ⊂ Ω be the time-t wave front, namely the set of endpoints at time t of all unit-speed rays starting at P in every initial direction and reflecting from ∂Ω according to the usual optical/specular billiard law. Is it true that F_t becomes dense in Ω as t → ∞, in the sense that every nonempty open subset of Ω intersects F_t for all sufficiently large t?

Let Σ be a strictly convex closed hypersurface, and consider the associated multidimensional outer symplectic billiard. Prove the period-3 case of Ivrii’s conjecture: the set of phase-space points whose outer symplectic billiard trajectories are 3-periodic has zero measure with respect to the invariant symplectic measure on the phase space. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2602.12896))

Let gamma be a smooth convex closed plane curve (an oval), and let Omega be the compact convex domain in R^2 bounded by gamma. For each integer n >= 3, define E_gamma(n) = inf { Area(Omega symmetric_difference P) : P is a plane n-gon }. Is the function n -> E_gamma(n) naturally related to some billiard-like dynamical system, analogously to the way the four classical optimal polygon-approximation functionals are realized as minimal actions of conventional (Birkhoff), outer, symplectic, and outer-length billiards?

In Euclidean n-space, let L be the space of oriented lines, equipped with the symplectic structure induced from the canonical symplectic structure on the cotangent bundle of the ambient space by symplectic reduction. A smooth mirror, i.e. a smooth hypersurface locally given as the graph of a function of n-1 variables, defines a local optical reflection map on L; hence any finite collection of smooth mirrors defines, locally, a composition of such symplectic reflection maps. How can one characterize, within the full set of local symplectic transformations of L, the subclass consisting exactly of those local symplectic transformations realizable by reflection in finitely many smooth mirrors? ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/html/2602.12896v1))

Let X be a compact Riemann surface of genus g >= 2, let SU_X(r) be the moduli space of semistable rank-r vector bundles on X with trivial determinant, and for any N in J^{g-1}(X) define Theta_N = {E in SU_X(r) | h^0(X,E⊗N) >= 1}; write L := O(Theta_N), which is independent of N. Then the base locus of the complete linear system |L| is B = {E in SU_X(r) | h^0(X,E⊗N) != 0 for every N in J^{g-1}(X)}. Raynaud's results show that |L| is base-point free for r=2, and for r=3 when g=2 or when g >= 3 and X is generic, while |L| has base points for r = ng whenever an integer n >= 2 divides g. Apart from these known cases, for which other ranks r can B be nonempty, can B have positive dimension, and is there a reasonable upper bound for dim B?

Let X be a compact Riemann surface of genus g >= 2, and let SU_X(r) be the moduli space of semistable rank-r vector bundles on X with trivial determinant. For any line bundle M on X of degree g - 1, define Θ_M = {E in SU_X(r) | h^0(X, E ⊗ M) >= 1}, and let L := O(Θ_M), the determinant line bundle on SU_X(r), which is independent of M. Is the complete linear system |L^2|, where L^2 denotes the tensor square of L, base-point free on SU_X(r) for every X and every r?

Let X be a compact Riemann surface of genus g(X)≥2, and let E be a semistable holomorphic vector bundle of rank r on X with det E ≅ O_X (so E determines a point of SU_X(r)). Does there exist an étale covering π:Y→X such that, if g(Y) denotes the genus of Y, the theta locus θ(π^*E):={M∈J^{g(Y)-1}(Y) | h^0(Y,π^*E⊗M)≥1} is not equal to the whole degree-(g(Y)-1) Picard variety J^{g(Y)-1}(Y)?

Let X be a compact Riemann surface of genus g ≥ 3 that is not hyperelliptic. Let SU_X(2) be the moduli space of S-equivalence classes of semistable rank-2 vector bundles with trivial determinant, let J^{g-1}(X)=Pic^{g-1}(X), and let Θ ⊂ J^{g-1}(X) be the canonical theta divisor. For a moduli point [E] ∈ SU_X(2), define Θ_E := { M ∈ J^{g-1}(X) | h^0(X,E⊗M) ≥ 1 }. In rank 2 this gives an everywhere-defined theta morphism θ: SU_X(2) → |2Θ|. Is θ an embedding for every non-hyperelliptic X? ([studylibfr.com](https://studylibfr.com/doc/9890806/http---arxiv.org-pdf-alg-geom-9404001v1.pdf))

Let X be a compact Riemann surface of genus g ≥ 2, let SU_X(r) be the moduli space of semistable rank-r vector bundles on X with trivial determinant, and let 𝓛 be its determinant line bundle. For arbitrary rank r and every integer k ≥ 1, can one give a direct proof of Beauville’s Theorem 5, namely dim H^0(SU_X(r), 𝓛^k) = (r/(r+k))^g Σ_{S ⊔ T = {1,…,r+k}, |S|=r} ∏_{s∈S, t∈T} |2 sin(π(s−t)/(r+k))|^(g−1), preferably by computing χ(𝓛^k) directly from the Riemann–Roch formula and the Chern numbers of SU_X(r), rather than by the indirect degeneration or conformal-block methods surveyed earlier in the paper? ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/alg-geom/9404001v1.pdf))

Let X be a compact Riemann surface of genus g ≥ 2, and let r, k ≥ 1. Let SU_X(r) denote the moduli space of semistable rank-r vector bundles on X with trivial determinant, and let L = O(Θ_A) be its determinant line bundle, where for any A ∈ J^{g−1}(X) one sets Θ_A = {E ∈ SU_X(r) | h^0(X, E ⊗ A) ≥ 1}. Let U_X^*(k) be the moduli space of semistable vector bundles on X of rank k and degree k(g−1), with canonical theta divisor Θ_k = {F ∈ U_X^*(k) | h^0(X, F) ≠ 0} and M = O(Θ_k). For the tensor-product morphism τ_{k,r}: SU_X(r) × U_X^*(k) → U_X^*(kr), (E, F) ↦ E ⊗ F, the divisor τ_{k,r}^*Θ_{kr} defines, up to scalar, a linear map ϑ_{k,r}: H^0(U_X^*(k), M^r)^* → H^0(SU_X(r), L^k). Is ϑ_{k,r} an isomorphism for every X, r, and k?

Let X be a smooth complex projective curve (compact Riemann surface) of genus g >= 2, let SU_X(r) be the moduli space of semistable rank-r vector bundles on X with trivial determinant, and let L_X be its determinant line bundle. For each integer k >= 1, Theorem 7 states that, as X varies in the moduli stack M_g of smooth genus-g curves, the linear systems |L_X^k| form a flat projective bundle. Hence one obtains a projective monodromy representation
ρ_{r,k}: Γ_g = π_1(M_g, X) -> PGL(H^0(SU_X(r), L_X^k)).
What is this projective representation ρ_{r,k}?

Let X be a smooth compact Riemann surface of genus g >= 2, let SU_X(r) be the moduli space of semistable rank-r vector bundles on X with trivial determinant, and let L be its determinant line bundle. For fixed integers r, k >= 1, Theorem 7 gives, as X varies over the moduli stack of smooth genus-g curves (informally M_g in the paper), a flat projective bundle with fibre P(H^0(SU_X(r), L^k)); equivalently, for a base curve X, a projective monodromy representation rho_{r,k} : Gamma_g = pi_1(M_g, X) -> PGL(H^0(SU_X(r), L^k)). Does there exist a flat Hermitian metric H_X on H^0(SU_X(r), L^k) making this projective connection projectively unitary, i.e. such that rho_{r,k}(Gamma_g) is contained in PU(H_X)? ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/alg-geom/9404001))

Let X be a compact Riemann surface of genus g ≥ 2, let SU_X(r) be the moduli space of semistable rank-r vector bundles on X with trivial determinant, and let L be its determinant line bundle. For a given integer k ≥ 1 (in the genuinely non-Abelian case r ≥ 2), is there a sufficiently simple and flexible way to express the generalized theta functions H^0(SU_X(r), L^k) as holomorphic functions on some natural explicit auxiliary complex space attached to SU_X(r), analogous to the classical realization of H^0(J_X, O(kΘ)) by theta functions on a Jacobian? ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/alg-geom/9404001v1.pdf))

Let f: A^n_C -> V be a finite surjective morphism of complex algebraic varieties, where V is a normal affine variety over C. Must the underlying complex analytic space V(C) be contractible in the classical topology?

Over C, let p:C^2 -> C be a primitive rational polynomial, where 'primitive' means that the generic fibers are connected and 'rational' means that the generic compact fiber is P^1 (equivalently, the generic affine fiber is a punctured Riemann sphere). Assume that the zero fiber Gamma_0 = p^{-1}(0) is isomorphic to C^* and is degenerate. Determine all such p up to polynomial change of coordinates on C^2 by proving that there exists a coordinate system (x,y) in which p(x,y) has one of the two forms p(x,y) = a(psi(x,y)^(nm+1) + (psi(x,y)^n + x)^m)/x^m or p(x,y) = a(psi(x,y)^(nm-1) + (psi(x,y)^n + x)^m)/x^m, where a is in C^*, m,n are natural numbers with m >= 2 and n >= 1, with the extra restriction n >= 2 in the second family when m = 2, and where psi(x,y) = x^m y + a_(m-1)x^(m-1) + ... + a_1 x - 1, the coefficients a_(m-1),...,a_1 being uniquely determined by the requirement that the displayed expression be a polynomial.

No paper-faithful refinement is possible from arXiv:alg-geom/9506006. Please provide the correct arXiv identifier for the paper about Artin local rings and Kähler differentials, and I can then extract and sharpen the exact conjecture or open problem.

The supplied arXiv identifier appears to be mismatched. If the intended paper is the one whose opening conjecture concerns derivations of Artin local k-algebras, then the sharp stand-alone version of your draft is: Let (A,m) be an Artin local k-algebra with residue field A/m \cong k, where k is an algebraically closed field of characteristic 0, and let M be a finitely generated A-module. Writing D(M)=Der_k(A,M), s(M)=Soc_A(M)=0:_M m, and \ell_A(-) for A-module length, is it true that \ell_A(D(M)) \ge \ell_A(M)-\ell_A(s(M)) for every finitely generated A-module M; and, if equality holds, is this precisely the case that A \cong k[x]/(x^n) for some n \ge 1 and M is a finite free A-module? Please provide the correct arXiv ID if you want this checked and aligned to the paper verbatim.

Let K be a field of characteristic 0, let R be a finitely generated noetherian K-algebra domain with quotient field L=Q(R), and let δ:R→R be a K-derivation. Call a nonzero element h∈L δ-integral if there exists b∈R such that δ(h)=bh; such a b is called a δ-integral factor of h. Let X_δ^f={b∈R : there exists a nonzero h∈L with δ(h)=bh}, viewed as a subgroup of the additive group (R,+). Must X_δ^f be a finitely generated abelian group? ([cmjpapers.math.cas.cz](https://cmjpapers.math.cas.cz/full/63/2/cmj63_2_17.pdf))

Let K be as in the paper, let R = K[x,y], let Q(R) be its fraction field, and let δ be a nonzero K-derivation of R. Set A_0 = {f in R : δ(f)=0} and L_0 = {ξ in Q(R) : δ(ξ)=0}, and assume that δ is of general type, i.e. A_0 = L_0 = K. For a nonzero f in R, call f δ-integral if δ(f) is divisible by f in R (equivalently, δ(f)=bf for some b in R), and let A be the K-subalgebra of R generated by all δ-integral elements. Is it true that, for every derivation δ of general type on K[x,y], the δ-integral ring A is generated by a single polynomial (equivalently, apart from the trivial case A=K, one has A=K[p] for some single nonconstant δ-integral polynomial p)?

Let k be a field of characteristic p > 0, let K be the perfect closure of k, and let A be a finitely generated integral k-algebra such that A⊗_k K ≅ K[X_1,...,X_n]. If A is k-rational, i.e. Frac(A) ≅ k(T_1,...,T_n), must A already be k-isomorphic to the polynomial ring k[X_1,...,X_n]?
