Let (A,M) be a Noetherian regular local domain with fraction field K, let a in M\M^2 and b in M^2 satisfy (a,b)=A, and set B=A[a/b] as a subring of K. Assume that B is regular. Under these hypotheses, for which choices of A, a, and b is the extended ideal MB a complete-intersection ideal of B, i.e. generated by ht(MB) elements forming a B-regular sequence?

Let p ∈ C[x,y] be a nonconstant polynomial such that the affine plane curve V(p) ⊂ A^2_C is smooth, irreducible, and rational. Must p divide some field generator of C[x,y]; that is, must there exist h ∈ C[x,y] and G ∈ C(x,y) such that C(ph,G)=C(x,y)?
Over C, classify, up to projective equivalence, all irreducible reduced cuspidal plane curves C contained in P^2 whose geometric genus is 0 or 1.

In the complex projective plane P^2, determine the maximum number of cusps that can occur on an irreducible rational cuspidal plane curve, where "rational" means that the normalization is isomorphic to P^1 and "cuspidal" means that every singular point is a cusp; the maximum is taken over curves of all degrees.

Let A := C[Y, XY, X^2Y, X^3Y - X] be the subring of C[X,Y]. Is it true that there do not exist polynomials f,g in A such that J(f,g) := det(∂(f,g)/∂(X,Y)) is a nonzero constant in C and the polynomial map F=(f,g): C^2 -> C^2 is not a polynomial automorphism?

Let X be a smooth complex contractible affine algebraic surface with logarithmic Kodaira dimension kappa(X)=2. Does X contain an algebraic curve Gamma that is a smooth once-punctured curve, i.e. a smooth affine curve whose smooth projective completion has exactly one point at infinity? More generally, is the set of such curves in X finite?

Let X be a smooth contractible affine algebraic surface over C with logarithmic Kodaira dimension κ(X)=2. Are there only finitely many irreducible algebraic curves C⊂X having one place at infinity; equivalently, such that for the smooth projective completion \bar C of C one has #(\bar C\setminus C)=1?

Let X be a smooth affine contractible algebraic surface over C with X not isomorphic to A^2_C. Fix a proper algebraic embedding X into C^N, let rho = ||.||^2|_X, and for all sufficiently large R let X_R = {x in X : rho(x) < R^2}; then X_R is a contractible strictly pseudoconvex domain in X with smooth real-algebraic boundary. Must it be true that, for every sufficiently large R, X_R is not biholomorphic to any domain in C^2?

Let D ⊂ C^2 be a bounded strictly pseudoconvex domain with smooth boundary S = ∂D. Assume that S is a homology 3-sphere, i.e. H_*(S; Z) ≅ H_*(S^3; Z). Must S be diffeomorphic to the standard 3-sphere S^3?

Conjecture (Flenner–Zaidenberg). Let X be a smooth complex affine algebraic surface with the rational homology of a point, i.e. H_0(X; Q) ≅ Q and H_i(X; Q)=0 for all i>0. If X is of log-general type, equivalently if its logarithmic Kodaira dimension satisfies kappa(X)=2, must X be rigid (in the deformation-theoretic sense, i.e. admit no nontrivial deformations)?

Let X be a smooth complex Q-acyclic affine surface of log-general type, and let (V,D) be a minimal smooth projective completion with D a simple normal crossings divisor and X = V \ D. Is X rigid and are the infinitesimal deformations of the pair (V,D) unobstructed? In particular, must one have chi(Theta_V⟨D⟩) = K_V·(K_V + D) = 0; equivalently, 3c_2(X) - c_1^2(X) = 5, where c_1^2(X) = (K_V + D)^2?

Over C, let X be a smooth Q-acyclic affine algebraic surface of log-general type, meaning that b_i(X)=0 for all i>0 and the logarithmic Kodaira dimension of X is 2. If (V,D) is a minimal smooth SNC-completion of X — i.e. V is a smooth complete surface, D is the reduced simple normal crossings boundary at infinity, and D contains no rational (-1)-component D_i with D_i·(D−D_i)≤2 — is the set of combinatorial types of Eisenbud–Neumann diagrams associated with D finite? ([math.univ-toulouse.fr](https://www.math.univ-toulouse.fr/~orevkov/tono.pdf))

Let X be a smooth complex affine algebraic surface with H_i(X;Z)=0 for all i>0 (i.e. an acyclic surface, equivalently a complex homology plane). Assume that for every non-constant regular function p in C[X] there exists a regular function q in C[X] such that the algebraic morphism F=(p,q):X->C^2 is proper. Must X be algebraically isomorphic to the affine plane C^2? ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/alg-geom/9506006))

For every integer n\ge 4, does there exist a smooth affine hypersurface X\subset \mathbb{A}^n_{\mathbb{C}}=\mathbb{C}^n such that X is contractible in the Euclidean topology and is of log-general type, i.e. its logarithmic Kodaira dimension is maximal: \bar\kappa(X)=\dim X=n-1? ([numdam.org](https://www.numdam.org/item/AST_1993__217__251_0.pdf))

Let p in C[x_1, ..., x_n], and let X = {p = 0} be the reduced irreducible hypersurface in C^n defined by p. If X is topologically contractible, must the polynomial map p: C^n -> C be isotrivial; that is, is there a Zariski-open dense subset U of C such that the fibres p^(-1)(c) for c in U are pairwise isomorphic?

Describe the complex plane polynomials f in C[x,y] such that there exists a nonempty Zariski-open subset U of C with the property that, for every t in U, the affine curve f^{-1}(t) has a smooth projective model independent of t up to isomorphism; equivalently, for general t1,t2 in C, the smooth projective models of f^{-1}(t1) and f^{-1}(t2) are isomorphic.

Let X = {p = 0} be a reduced irreducible hypersurface in C^n, where p belongs to C[x_1,\ldots,x_n], and assume that X is topologically contractible and that Sing(X) consists of a single point. Must there exist a polynomial automorphism Phi of C^n such that p \circ Phi is a quasihomogeneous polynomial, i.e. weighted homogeneous for some positive weights on the variables?

Let k be an algebraically closed field of characteristic p>0. Classify, up to composition with automorphisms of A^1_k and A^2_k, all polynomial embeddings φ:A^1_k↪A^2_k; equivalently, determine the positive-characteristic analogue of the Abhyankar-Moh-Suzuki theorem for embedded affine lines in the affine plane. ([numdam.org](https://www.numdam.org/item/SB_1994-1995__37__295_0.pdf))

Does there exist an integer n >= 1 and smooth affine complex algebraic varieties X and Y such that each of X and Y is diffeomorphic, as a real smooth manifold, to the complex affine space C^n but is not algebraically isomorphic to C^n (that is, each is an exotic C^n), while X and Y are biholomorphic as complex manifolds but not algebraically isomorphic to one another?

For some n >= 3, do there exist two smooth complex affine algebraic varieties X and Y, each giving an exotic algebraic structure on C^n (that is, each is diffeomorphic to R^{2n} but not algebraically isomorphic to A^n_C), such that X and Y are biholomorphic as complex analytic manifolds but not isomorphic as algebraic varieties?

For n >= 3, let X be a smooth affine algebraic variety over C such that X is diffeomorphic, as a real C^\infty manifold, to R^{2n}. If the analytification X^{an} is biholomorphic to C^n, must X already be algebraically isomorphic to the affine n-space A^n_C?

Let X be a smooth affine algebraic variety over C which is diffeomorphic to R^{2n} but not algebraically isomorphic to C^n (that is, an exotic algebraic structure on C^n). Must X fail to be biholomorphic to C^n as a complex analytic manifold?

Does there exist, for some integer n >= 3, a smooth affine algebraic variety X over C such that X is diffeomorphic to R^{2n}, X is not isomorphic (as an algebraic variety) to the affine n-space A^n_C = C^n, and X is non-rational?

Let X be a smooth affine complex algebraic variety such that X is diffeomorphic, as a real manifold, to R^{2n} but is not isomorphic as an algebraic variety to the affine space A^n_C; in other words, let X be an exotic C^n. Must the natural action of the full algebraic automorphism group Aut(X) on X be non-transitive?

Let X be a smooth affine algebraic variety over C such that X is diffeomorphic, as a real manifold, to R^{2n}, but X is not isomorphic, as an algebraic variety, to the affine space A^n_C = C^n; in the terminology of the paper, X is an exotic algebraic structure on C^n. Must the natural action of the group Aut_an(X) of biholomorphic self-automorphisms of X on X be non-transitive?

Let X be a complete Kähler manifold that is elliptically connected in the following sense: for every pair of points x,y in X, there exists a finite chain of holomorphic images of non-hyperbolic irreducible smooth quasiprojective curves and of complex tori joining x to y. Must the fundamental group pi_1(X) be almost abelian; or at least, in the weaker form stated in the paper, must pi_1(X) be almost nilpotent, i.e. contain an abelian, respectively nilpotent, subgroup of finite index?

For every integer Δ >= 3, if G = (V,E) is a countably infinite graph of maximum degree at most Δ and the hard-core lattice gas on G has nonnegative site fugacities {w_x}_{x in V} satisfying 0 <= w_x <= (Δ-1)^(Δ-1)/(Δ-2)^Δ for every x in V, must the corresponding infinite-volume Gibbs measure be unique?

Let T = (V,E) be a countably infinite non-regular tree of maximum degree Δ >= 3. Consider the nearest-neighbor hard-core lattice gas on T with uniform fugacity λ >= 0, so that finite-volume configurations are independent sets I weighted proportionally to λ^{|I|}. Can one prove that the associated infinite-volume Dobrushin-Lanford-Ruelle Gibbs measure is unique for every λ < ((Δ-1)^(Δ-1))/((Δ-2)^Δ), thereby establishing the non-regular-tree, equal-fugacity special case explicitly singled out after Conjecture 2.1? (As in Sokal's parenthetical comment in Conjecture 2.1, one may also ask whether uniqueness could persist at the endpoint λ = ((Δ-1)^(Δ-1))/((Δ-2)^Δ).)

Let X be a finite single-particle state space, let w={w_x}_{x in X} be complex fugacities, and let W:X x X -> C be a symmetric two-particle Boltzmann factor. For the grand partition function Z(w,W)=sum_{N=0}^infty (1/N!) sum_{x_1,...,x_N in X} (prod_{i=1}^N w_{x_i})(prod_{1<=i<j<=N} W(x_i,x_j)), assume W is physical and repulsive, i.e. 0<=W(x,y)<=1 for all x,y in X, but do not assume hard-core self-repulsion W(x,x)=0. Can one obtain, by a Dobrushin-style elementary induction analogous to Theorem 3.1, a direct zero-free criterion for Z(w,W) (or for the restricted partition functions Z_Lambda) in a specified polydisc D_R={w in C^X: |w_x|<R_x for all x}, so that analyticity of log Z and convergence there of the Mayer expansion (3.22) follow afterwards, without relying first on the usual explicit combinatorial bounds for the Mayer coefficients?

For each integer Δ≥3, let Z_G(w)=sum_{I independent in G} w^{|I|} be the hard-core lattice-gas partition function (independence polynomial) of a finite graph G with maximum degree at most Δ. Does there exist a complex domain D_Δ⊂C containing the real interval [0, ((Δ-1)^(Δ-1))/((Δ-2)^Δ)) such that Z_G(w)≠0 for every such graph G and every w∈D_Δ?

For every finite simple claw-free graph G, define its univariate hard-core partition function (independence polynomial) by Z_G(w) = sum over all independent sets I of G of w^{|I|}. Is every complex zero of the polynomial Z_G(w) a negative real number?

For the hard-core lattice gas on an infinite locally finite graph G, with finite-volume weights proportional to w^{|I|} on independent sets I and fugacity w > 0, determine the equilibrium phase diagram as a function of w: for which w is the infinite-volume Gibbs measure unique, for which w is it nonunique, what are the extremal Gibbs measures that occur for sufficiently large w, and when a transition occurs, is the resulting order-disorder transition first-order or second-order?

For the nearest-neighbor q-coloring model on the infinite hexagonal lattice with q=3, and on the infinite square lattice with q=4,5,6, prove that zero temperature is in the disordered regime: namely, for every exhaustion by finite subgraphs and every proper boundary condition, the corresponding finite-volume Gibbs measures on proper q-colorings converge to a single infinite-volume Gibbs measure independent of the boundary condition, and the resulting correlations (equivalently, boundary-condition influence on local observables) decay exponentially with graph distance.

Let G be an infinite graph of maximum degree Δ, and consider the q-coloring model on G (equivalently, the zero-temperature antiferromagnetic q-state Potts model with uniform activities), where a Gibbs measure means an infinite-volume DLR measure whose finite-volume conditional distributions are uniform on proper q-colorings compatible with the boundary condition. Is it true that for every integer Δ≥2 and every integer q>Δ there is a unique Gibbs measure on every such G? In other words, is the sharp general uniqueness threshold q_c(Δ)=Δ+1, matching the regular-tree threshold (nonuniqueness possible for q≤Δ and uniqueness on the infinite Δ-regular tree for q≥Δ+1), rather than the older sufficient bound q>2Δ coming from the Dobrushin method? ([sciencedirect.com](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/abs/pii/S0167715202000548?utm_source=openai))

For each integer Δ≥2, let C_opt(Δ):=sup{|q| : P_G(q)=0 for some finite loopless graph G with maximum degree Δ(G)≤Δ}, where P_G(q) is the chromatic polynomial of G. What is the sharp value of C_opt(Δ)? In particular, is it true that for every Δ≥4 the complete bipartite graph K_{Δ,Δ} has the chromatic root of largest modulus among all finite loopless graphs of maximum degree Δ, so that C_opt(Δ) is attained by K_{Δ,Δ} (and hence has asymptotic slope |α|, with α=-2/W(-2/e))? Moreover, beyond such radial bounds, can one prove a universal noncircular zero-free region for all graphs with Δ(G)≤Δ—most notably the conjectured region Re q>Δ(G), or at least positivity on the real interval q>Δ(G)?

For the single-site Glauber dynamics of the hard-core lattice gas on a finite graph G, at fixed fugacity λ and with state space Ω equal to the independent sets of G, what is the precise correspondence between rapid-mixing proofs obtained from a Markovian/probabilistic coupling and Dobrushin-type analytic proofs? More specifically, can one formulate the coupling argument as the statement that the one-step transition operator P on observables f:Ω→R is a strict contraction, with operator norm < 1, in some explicitly identified norm or seminorm that vanishes exactly on constants (equivalently, a norm on functions modulo constants), thereby giving an analytic reformulation of the coupling-based rapid-mixing proof in the hard-core setting treated in the paper?

For each integer Delta >= 2, does there exist an open domain D_Delta subset C containing the real interval [0, 1/(Delta-1)) such that, for every finite graph G of maximum degree at most Delta, if I(G) is the set of independent sets of G and P_{G,w} is the single-site heat-bath Glauber operator for the hard-core lattice gas at fugacity w in C acting on C^{I(G)}, then for every w in D_Delta the induced operator on C^{I(G)} / <1> (where <1> is the one-dimensional space of constant functions) has spectral radius strictly less than 1?

For each integer Δ ≥ 3, does there exist an open set N_Δ ⊂ ℂ containing the real interval [0, λ_c(Δ)), where λ_c(Δ)=((Δ-1)^(Δ-1))/((Δ-2)^Δ) is the critical activity of the hard-core model on the infinite Δ-regular tree, such that for every finite graph G of maximum degree at most Δ, the hard-core partition function Z_G(λ)=∑_{I\subseteq V(G)\,\text{independent}} λ^{|I|} is nonzero for every λ ∈ N_Δ? ([tifr.res.in](https://www.tifr.res.in/~piyush.srivastava/docs/LSS20.pdf))

In the sense of Sokal’s 2000 open problem, classify the finite fully periodic triangular-lattice tori (equivalently, via the zero-temperature 4-state triangular/3-state kagomé correspondence, the corresponding fully periodic kagomé lattices) for which the zero-temperature Wang–Swendsen–Kotecký dynamics is ergodic; that is, determine for which torus sizes the proper 4-colorings of the triangular lattice, equivalently the proper 3-colorings of the kagomé lattice, form a single Kempe-equivalence class.

For the zero-temperature 3-state Potts antiferromagnet on the periodic square lattice, i.e. the uniform measure on proper 3-colorings of the n x n square-lattice torus, in the bipartite case n even where the zero-temperature Wang-Swendsen-Kotecký chain is the Kempe-chain dynamics, can one prove that this Markov chain mixes rapidly as n grows—ideally with a mixing time bounded uniformly in n (equivalently, no critical slowing down), and at minimum polynomially in n—thereby placing the numerically observed bounded autocorrelation times in the square-lattice q=3 case on a rigorous footing?

For the infinite antiferromagnetic spin-1/2 Heisenberg XXX chain with Hamiltonian H_XXX = sum_{j=-∞}^{∞}(σ_j^xσ_{j+1}^x + σ_j^yσ_{j+1}^y + σ_j^zσ_{j+1}^z), let |GS> be its unique ground state in the thermodynamic limit, and for any n consecutive sites define a local correlation function by C_{a_1,...,a_n} = <GS|prod_{k=1}^n σ_k^{a_k}|GS>, where each σ_k^{a_k} belongs to {σ_k^0, σ_k^x, σ_k^y, σ_k^z}; in particular, P(n) = <GS|prod_{j=1}^n ((σ_j^z+1)/2)|GS> is the emptiness formation probability. Since these correlators are known to be expressible as polynomials over Q in the alternating zeta values ζ_a(1), ζ_a(3), ζ_a(5), ... , can one give an efficient and tractable description of the rational coefficients appearing in those polynomial expressions for arbitrary n and arbitrary choices of the local operators?

For the infinite spin-1/2 XXZ chain with Hamiltonian H_XXZ = -Σ_{j=-∞}^{∞}(σ_j^xσ_{j+1}^x + σ_j^yσ_{j+1}^y + Δσ_j^zσ_{j+1}^z), let |GS⟩ denote the ground state, let A be a contiguous block of n neighboring spins and B its complement, define ρ(n) = Tr_B(|GS⟩⟨GS|), and set S(ρ(n)) = -Tr(ρ(n) ln ρ(n)). In the gapped antiferromagnetic regime Δ < -1, compute analytically the saturation constant S(∞) := lim_{n→∞} S(ρ(n)). ([pos.sissa.it](https://pos.sissa.it/038/006/pdf))

Consider the infinite spin-1/2 XXZ chain with Hamiltonian H_XXZ = -∑_{j∈ℤ}(σ_j^xσ_{j+1}^x + σ_j^yσ_{j+1}^y + Δσ_j^zσ_{j+1}^z + hσ_j^z). In the critical region −1 ≤ Δ < 1 and at finite temperature T, derive an explicit analytic formula for the leading exponential term in the large-space/large-time asymptotics of time-dependent thermal correlation functions of the XXZ chain, with any dependence of the decay rate on the space-time direction made explicit; in particular, the formula should apply to correlation functions of the same type as the prototype g(n,t)=Tr(e^{-H/T}σ^+_{n2}(t2)σ^-_{n1}(t1))/Tr(e^{-H/T}), where n=n2−n1 and t=t2−t1. ([pos.sissa.it](https://pos.sissa.it/038/006/pdf))

For the six-vertex model on a finite N×N square lattice with domain wall boundary conditions—arrows on the upper and lower boundaries pointing into the lattice and arrows on the left and right boundaries pointing out—obtain explicit formulas for the correlation functions both in the bulk and at the boundary, extending beyond the presently known determinant formulas for the 1-point and 2-point boundary correlators in this non-translation-invariant setting. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/cond-mat/0701491))

For models beyond the six-vertex model, can one construct genuine generalizations of domain wall boundary conditions such that the corresponding partition function, in direct analogy with the six-vertex DWBC formula highlighted in Section V, admits a determinantal representation whose matrix dimension is proportional to the system size? ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/cond-mat/0701491))

Let AP_H := { a in R | a is a regular value of H and the regular energy level H^{-1}(a) carries no periodic orbit of the Hamiltonian flow X_H }. The paper's sharpened form of the Hamiltonian Seifert size problem asks: if 2n >= 6, H_0(z) = sum_{j=1}^n lambda_j |z_j|^2 on R^{2n} with lambda_1,...,lambda_n > 0 rationally independent, and K subset (0,infinity) is a compact set of Lebesgue measure zero, does there exist a C^infty Hamiltonian H: R^{2n} -> R, C^0-close and compactly supported isotopic to H_0, such that AP_H = K?

For each n > 1, let T^{2n} = R^{2n}/Z^{2n} be equipped with the standard translation-invariant symplectic form ω_std = Σ_{j=1}^n dx_j∧dy_j. Is the Hofer-Zehnder capacity of this compact symplectic torus finite; equivalently, is c_HZ(T^{2n}, ω_std) < ∞?

Let R^{2n} ≅ C^n carry its standard symplectic structure, with 2n ≥ 6, and let H0(z) = Σ_{j=1}^n λj|zj|^2, where λ1,...,λn > 0 are rationally independent, so that {H0 = 1} is an irrational ellipsoid. If K ⊂ (0,∞) is a compact set of measure zero, does there exist a C^∞ Hamiltonian H : R^{2n} → R, C^0-close and isotopic to H0 through an isotopy with compact support, such that for every a ∈ K the level set {H = a} carries no closed Hamiltonian trajectory? ([math.uni-bielefeld.de](https://www.math.uni-bielefeld.de/~rehmann/ECM/cdrom/3ecm/pdfs/pant3/ginzbu.pdf))

Let X be the C^1-smooth divergence-free vector field on S^3 constructed by G. Kuperberg. Does there exist a C^2 embedding i:S^3→R^4 (or even a C^1 embedding), with R^4 equipped with its standard symplectic form omega_st, such that the characteristic line field ker(i^*omega_st) on S^3 coincides with the line field spanned by X? A positive answer would realize i(S^3) as a compact regular hypersurface in symplectic dimension four with no closed characteristics, and hence would give a C^2-smooth counterexample to the Hamiltonian Seifert conjecture in dimension four.

For every compact Riemannian manifold M and every symplectic 2-form σ on M, let π:T*M→M be the bundle projection, let ω0 be the canonical symplectic form on T*M, and equip T*M with the twisted symplectic form ω = ω0 + π*σ. If H:T*M→R is the standard metric Hamiltonian (kinetic energy), so that its Hamiltonian flow is the twisted geodesic flow, is it true that there exists a neighborhood U of the zero section M ⊂ T*M with finite Hofer-Zehnder capacity c_HZ(U), that for Lebesgue-almost every positive energy value a the level {H = a} carries a periodic orbit, and that every sufficiently small positive energy level {H = a} carries a contractible periodic orbit?

Let M be a compact surface of genus g ≥ 2 endowed with a metric of constant curvature K = -1, let σ be the area form on M, let π : T^*M → M be the cotangent projection, let ω = ω0 + π^*σ be the twisted symplectic form on T^*M, and let H : T^*M → R be the standard metric Hamiltonian (the kinetic energy). In the horocycle-flow setting of Example 4.1, where the Hamiltonian flow of H on the regular energy level {H = 1} is smoothly equivalent to the horocycle flow and hence has no periodic orbits, is it true that for every a > 1 the open sublevel domain {H < a} ⊂ (T^*M, ω) has finite Hofer-Zehnder capacity, i.e. c_HZ({H < a}, ω) < ∞?

Does there exist a compact Riemannian manifold M equipped with a closed nondegenerate 2-form σ such that, for the standard metric Hamiltonian H (the kinetic energy) on the twisted cotangent bundle (T^*M, ω0 + π^*σ), the resulting twisted geodesic flow has at least two distinct regular compact energy levels {H = a1} and {H = a2}, with a1 != a2, each carrying no periodic orbits?

For a fixed real number d>0 and a fixed plane figure F in the Euclidean plane (or, more generally, a fixed body B in Euclidean 3-space), determine: (a) the largest possible cardinality of a subset S of F (respectively of B) such that |x-y|>=d for every pair of distinct points x,y in S; and (b) the smallest possible cardinality of a subset C={A1,A2,...} of F (respectively of B) such that every point A of F\C (respectively of B\C) satisfies |A-A_i|<d for some A_i in C.

In base 10, (a) for a fixed integer n with 1 < n < 9 and distinct digits a1, ..., an ∈ {0,1,2,...,9}, determine how many distinct prime numbers are obtained by permuting these digits so that each is used exactly once, excluding permutations with leading digit 0; more generally, for n ∈ N* and distinct positive integers a1, ..., an, determine how many distinct primes are obtained by concatenating the decimal expansions of a1, ..., an in all possible orders; and (b) for a fixed digit a ∈ {0,1,2,...,9}, determine the number of occurrences of a in the decimal expansion of the n-th prime p_n, of n!, and of n^n, and more generally ask the analogous question for the decimal block corresponding to a fixed nonnegative integer a. ([fs.unm.edu](https://fs.unm.edu/36UnsolvedProblems.pdf))
In mathematical logic, is it true that every question has at least one answer? Conversely, is every assertion the result of at least one question?

Can one explicitly construct a function f:D→R, for some explicitly specified domain D, whose image is exactly R\Q, the set of irrational real numbers; and likewise can one explicitly construct a function g:E→R, for some explicitly specified domain E, whose image is exactly the set of transcendental real numbers?

For each integer t >= 1, let ES_3(t) denote the smallest integer N such that every set of N points in Euclidean 3-space R^3 in general position (that is, with no four points coplanar) contains a t-point subset in convex position, equivalently, t points that are the vertices of a convex polyhedron. Is it true that ES_3(t) = 2^{Theta(sqrt(t))} as t -> infinity?

For a given radius parameter n>0, determine the maximum number M(n) of circles of radius 1 that can be wholly contained in a circle of radius n, under the condition that the small circles are pairwise interior-disjoint and may meet only by tangency (the paper's phrase is "at most tangential by twos"). In the generalized form stated in the paper, determine the analogous maximum when the small circles have radius i(n), where i(n) is a prescribed function of n; then study the same type of packing question for unit circles contained in a given triangle (in connection with Malfatti's problem), and similarly for spheres, cones, cylinders, regular pyramids, and, more generally, for planar figures contained in a given planar figure and for corresponding spatial packings. ([fs.unm.edu](https://fs.unm.edu/36UnsolvedProblems.pdf))

For each integer m>5, determine the minimum integer n=n(m) such that every set of n points in three-dimensional space with no four points coplanar contains an m-point subset lying on the surface of a common sphere. In the same sense, ask the analogous extremal question for an arbitrary prescribed spatial figure (for example, a cone or a cube); and ask the planar analogue for m>4, where one has n points in the plane with no three collinear and seeks m points lying on a common circle, and more generally on a prescribed planar figure. ([fs.unm.edu](https://fs.unm.edu/36UnsolvedProblems.pdf))

Fix an integer base b >= 2 and a finite block of base-b digits a1,a2,...,am with each ai in {0,1,...,b-1}. Does the ordered contiguous block a1a2...am occur in the standard base-b expansion of at least one prime number? Likewise, does it occur in the standard base-b expansion of n! for some n >= 1, and in the standard base-b expansion of n^n for some n >= 1?

For each fixed positive integer k > 2, are there infinitely many tuples of prime numbers (x1, x2, ..., xk, y) such that y = 2 x1 x2 ... xk + 1, with no further assumptions such as distinctness or ordering of the primes? ([fs.unm.edu](https://fs.unm.edu/36UnsolvedProblems.pdf))

Let p_n be the n-th prime (with p_1 = 2), and for n = 1, 2, ... define d_n = (p_{n+1} - p_n)/2. Does the set of values of the sequence (d_n) contain infinitely many prime integers? Does it contain a value of the form m! for some positive integer m? Does it contain a value of the form m^m for some positive integer m? More generally, for each i in N* = {1,2,3,...}, define d_n^(i) = (p_{n+i} - p_n)/2 for n = 1, 2, ..., and also consider the related sequence written in the paper as d_{n,i}^{(i-1)} = (d_{n+1} - d_n)/2. For each of these sequences, ask the same three questions. ([fs.unm.edu](https://fs.unm.edu/36UnsolvedProblems.pdf))

Let n be a positive integer. Is it true that for every coloring of the entire Euclidean plane R^2 with n colors, there exists a color c such that for every real d>0 there are points A,B in R^2 of color c with |AB|=d and with every point of the Euclidean line through A and B also colored c? (The paper adds parenthetically that the analogous statement should hold in space as well.) ([fs.unm.edu](https://fs.unm.edu/36UnsolvedProblems.pdf))

Let k,n belong to N* with k < n. Define a decreasing sequence of integers by n_0 = n, and for each i >= 0 such that the set {p prime : p <= n_i - k} is nonempty, define n_{i+1} = max{p prime : p <= n_i - k}. Determine, for the given pair (k,n), the exact length of this sequence, i.e. the total number of defined terms n_0,n_1,n_2,... before the construction stops.

Determine the largest integer R > 3, if any, such that for every partition of the positive integers N* = {1,2,3,...} into infinitely many pairwise disjoint classes whose union is N*, at least one class contains a finite arithmetic progression of length R; equivalently, there exist a,d in N* and a class C in the partition such that a, a+d, ..., a+(R-1)d all belong to C.

Let p_n denote the n-th prime. For fixed integers a,b with gcd(a,b)=1, how many terms of the sequence (a p_n + b)_{n \ge 1} are prime, how many are equal to m! for some positive integer m, and how many are equal to m^m for some positive integer m? Ask the analogous three questions for the exponential sequence (a^n + b)_{n \ge 1} with fixed integers a,b and a not in {-1,0,1}, and also for each of the two sequences (k^k + 1)_{k \ge 1} and (k^k - 1)_{k \ge 1}.
Fix a nonzero integer k. Are there only finitely many quadruples (p, q, x, y) of integers with p, q, x, y > 1 such that x^p - y^q = k?

Let k be a fixed decimal digit, and let (x_n)_{n\ge 1} be a sequence of integers. Define the position sequence (U_n^(k)) by setting U_n^(k) = i if k is the i-th digit of the decimal expansion of x_n, and U_n^(k) = 0 if the digit k does not occur in x_n; in particular, the paper's example gives U_2^(7) = 2 for x_2 = 17 and U_3^(7) = 1 for x_3 = 715. For x_n = p_n, where p_n is the n-th prime, and likewise for x_n = n! and x_n = n^n, determine whether the sequence (U_n^(k)) converges, whether it is monotone, and whether it contains infinitely many prime terms; then ask the same questions, with the same digit-position convention, when (x_n) is a sequence of rational numbers. ([scribd.com](https://www.scribd.com/document/333540693/Florentin-Smarandache-Thirty-Six-Problems-in-Number-Theory-pdf?utm_source=openai))

For fixed integers n and m with n > m > 2, let N = {1,2,...,n}. Determine the maximum cardinality of a subset A ⊆ N such that no m distinct elements of A form an arithmetic progression. Ask the analogous extremal question when "arithmetic progression" is replaced by "geometric progression." More generally, given an ambient set X (the paper literally says "a field N") together with an m-ary relation R, determine the largest possible cardinality of a subset A ⊆ X such that no m distinct elements of A satisfy R; in particular, what is the corresponding extremal problem when X has continuum size, for example when X is an interval of R?

Let ω be a complex n-th root of unity satisfying ω^{n-1}+ω^{n-2}+⋯+1=0, and let Z[ω]={a+bω : a,b∈Z} be assumed to enjoy unique factorization, with units ±1, ±ω, ±ω^2, …, ±ω^{n-1}. Viewing Z[ω] as a subset of C, is the configuration of its prime elements (the ω-primes) invariant under the symmetries of a regular 2n-gon? ([fs.unm.edu](https://fs.unm.edu/36UnsolvedProblems.pdf))
Up to permutation of the variables, how many integer triples (x,y,z) in Z^3 satisfy x^3 + y^3 + z^3 = 1 and (x+y)(y+z)(z+x) != 0, beyond the two listed nontrivial examples (9,10,-12) and (-6,-8,9)?

Let A be the family of all infinite strictly increasing sequences of integers 1 < a_1 < a_2 < ... such that no three terms of the sequence form an arithmetic progression, and define S((a_n)) = sum_{n>1} 1/a_n. Is it true that S((a_n)) < 2 for every (a_n) in A, and, if so, does every real value in (0,2) arise from exactly one such sequence? More generally, for a fixed integer m >= 1 and a fixed function f:(0,∞)^m -> (0,∞), among all strictly increasing positive sequences 0 < a_1 < a_2 < ... for which there is no tuple of terms (a_{i_1},...,a_{i_m},a_{i_{m+1}}) satisfying f(a_{i_1},...,a_{i_m}) = a_{i_{m+1}}, determine the maximum possible value of sum_{n>1} 1/a_n. ([fs.unm.edu](https://fs.unm.edu/36UnsolvedProblems.pdf))

For n, m in the positive integers and real x > 2, let sigma(n) = sum_{d|n} d, J(x) = #{primes p <= x}, omega(n) = #{distinct prime divisors of n}, d(n) = #{positive divisors of n}, and p(n) = the largest prime factor of n; for any function f, let f^(k) denote its k-fold iterate. Determine, for each fixed admissible input, the least positive integer k such that (a) sigma^(k)(n) > m, (b) J^(k)(x) = 1, (c) omega^(k)(n) = 1, (d) d^(k)(n) > m, and (e) T^(k)(n) = 1 for T(n) = p(n) - 1; and formulate the analogous least-iteration questions for the variants sigma_r(n), J(x; a, b), and Omega(n).
Fix a positive integer n. Do there exist n geometric progressions of positive integers, say G_j = {a_j q_j^m : m >= 0} with a_j, q_j in N* for 1 <= j <= n, whose union is all of N*?

For a fixed positive integer n, find necessary and sufficient conditions on a class C of sequences of positive integers such that there exist n distinct sequences in C whose union is the set of all positive integers. As the concrete example singled out in the paper, let i be a positive integer, let f map i-tuples of positive integers to positive integers, and let A_f be the class of all sequences (a_n)_{n>=1} with arbitrary positive initial values a_1, ..., a_i and recurrence a_n = f(a_{n-1}, ..., a_{n-i}) for every n >= i + 1. Under the hypothesis that f omits some positive integer value, i.e. there exists y > 0 such that f(x_1, ..., x_i) != y for every positive-integer tuple (x_1, ..., x_i), does the class A_f cover all positive integers? The paper further notes that if this hypothesis is replaced by surjectivity of f on the positive integers, then in general the answer is no.

Given a fixed parallelogram P in the Euclidean plane with adjacent side lengths R1, R2 > 0 and one interior angle pi/3, what is the maximal cardinality of a finite set S contained in the interior of P such that the Euclidean distance between any two distinct points of S is at least 1? Analogously, given a fixed prism in Euclidean 3-space with side lengths R1, R2, R3 > 0, all of whose faces are parallelograms with an angle pi/3, what is the maximal cardinality of a finite interior set S whose distinct points are pairwise at Euclidean distance at least 1?

Let F ⊂ R^2 be a given plane figure and, in the spatial version, let K ⊂ R^3 be a given space body. For a fixed real number d > 0, determine (i) the maximum cardinality of a subset S ⊂ F (respectively S ⊂ K) such that the Euclidean distance between any two distinct points of S is at least d, and (ii) the minimum cardinality of a subset C = {A1, A2, ...} ⊂ F (respectively ⊂ K) such that every point A of F (respectively K) lies within distance d of some Ai. Study exactly the additional variants listed in the paper: the versions using only interior points, using interior together with frontier points, using frontier points only, and the strict-inequality versions obtained by replacing the separation condition by |PQ| > d and, on the covering side, by the corresponding strict covering inequality. ([fs.unm.edu](https://fs.unm.edu/36UnsolvedProblems.pdf))

In the setting of Unsolved Problem 36, after the EPR-inspired discussion of entangled particles and the hypothesis that there is no speed barrier in the universe, does the infinitude of space imply that the maximum possible speed is itself infinite?
For a fixed positive integer k, does the exponential Diophantine equation x^p - y^q = k have only finitely many solutions in integers x, y, p, q with x, y, p, q >= 2?

Is Grimm’s conjecture true? Namely, for every positive integer k and every integer n such that the k consecutive integers n+1,n+2,...,n+k are all composite positive integers, do there exist pairwise distinct primes p_1,p_2,...,p_k with p_j dividing n+j for each j=1,2,...,k? ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/math/0312440))

For every integer k >= 2, if n_1 < n_2 < ... < n_k are positive integers that are multiplicatively dependent—that is, if there exist integers a_1, ..., a_k, not all zero, such that n_1^{a_1} n_2^{a_2} ... n_k^{a_k} = 1—must there exist a prime number p satisfying n_1 <= p <= n_k?

Let R(n) = ∏_{p|n} p denote the radical (square-free part) of a positive integer n. Is it true that for every epsilon > 0 there exists a positive constant kappa(epsilon) such that for all positive integers a, b, c with gcd(a,b,c) = 1 and a + b = c, one has c < kappa(epsilon) R(abc)^(1+epsilon)?

Let R(t) = ∏_{p|t} p denote the radical (square-free part) of a positive integer t. Does there exist a positive integer k such that, for all positive integers m and n, the conditions R(m+i) = R(n+i) for every i = 0, 1, ..., k-1 imply m = n?
Let R(n)=∏_{p\mid n} p denote the radical (squarefree part) of a positive integer n. If a and b are positive integers with a<b and R(a)=R(b), must there exist a prime number p such that a<p<b?
Hall's conjecture: Does there exist an absolute constant C > 0 such that for every pair of positive integers x and y with y^2 != x^3, one has |y^2 - x^3| >= C max{y^2, x^3}^{1/6}?

Do Z-numbers exist; that is, does there exist a nonzero real number α such that, for every integer n ≥ 1, if {x}=x-⌊x⌋ denotes the fractional part of x, then {α(3/2)^n} ∈ [0,1/2)? ([webusers.imj-prg.fr](https://webusers.imj-prg.fr/~michel.waldschmidt/articles/pdf/ODP-MoscowMathJ.pdf))
Is it true that the sequence of fractional parts {e^n} = e^n - floor(e^n), for n = 1, 2, 3, ..., does not converge to 0 as n tends to infinity?

For every integer n >= 1 and every choice of positive integers k_1, ..., k_n, does there exist a real number x such that ||k_i x|| >= 1/(n+1) for all i = 1, ..., n, where ||t|| denotes the distance from t to the nearest integer?

Determine whether each of the following real constants is irrational (that is, does not belong to Q): Euler’s constant γ:=lim_{n→∞}(∑_{m=1}^n 1/m-log n), Catalan’s constant G:=∑_{n≥0}(-1)^n/(2n+1)^2, Γ(1/5):=∫_0^∞ e^{-t}t^{-4/5}dt, the numbers e+π, e^γ, ζ(5), ζ(3)/π^3, and, for k=1,2, the sums ∑_{n≥1}σ_k(n)/n!, where ζ(s)=∑_{n≥1}n^{-s} for s>1 and σ_k(n)=∑_{d|n} d^k.

Schanuel’s Conjecture: For every positive integer n and every n-tuple x_1,...,x_n of Q-linearly independent complex numbers, must the field Q(x_1,...,x_n,e^{x_1},...,e^{x_n}) have transcendence degree at least n over Q, where e^z=exp(z)? ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/math/0312440))

Conjecture 3.3 (§3.1): Let n ≥ 1 and let λ1, ..., λn ∈ C be Q-linearly independent. If e^{λ1}, ..., e^{λn} are algebraic numbers, must λ1, ..., λn be algebraically independent over Q? ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/math/0312440))

Four Exponentials Conjecture. Let x_1,x_2 be Q-linearly independent complex numbers, and let y_1,y_2 be Q-linearly independent complex numbers. Must at least one of the four numbers exp(x_i y_j), for 1 <= i,j <= 2, be transcendental over Q?
Let zeta(s) be the Riemann zeta function. Is the set of real numbers {pi} union {zeta(2n+1) : n >= 1} algebraically independent over Q?

Fix an integer g >= 1, and let A_g(C) denote the moduli space of principally polarized abelian varieties of dimension g over C. If Z is a closed irreducible algebraic subvariety of A_g(C) whose complex points contain a Zariski-dense set of CM points (that is, points corresponding to principally polarized abelian varieties of CM type), must Z be a subvariety of Hodge type? ([annals.math.princeton.edu](https://annals.math.princeton.edu/wp-content/uploads/annals-v157-n2-p07.pdf))

Let L be the set of Liouville numbers, i.e. the real numbers xi such that for every n >= 1 there exist integers p and q >= 2 with 0 < |xi - p/q| < q^(-n). Does there exist a transcendental entire function f: C -> C such that f(L) is contained in L?

Does there exist an absolute constant c > 0 such that every nonzero algebraic number α of degree d = [Q(α):Q] that is not a root of unity satisfies h(α) ≥ c/d, where h(α) = (1/d) log M(α) is the absolute logarithmic height and M(α) is the Mahler measure of the minimal polynomial of α in Z[X]? ([webusers.imj-prg.fr](https://webusers.imj-prg.fr/~michel.waldschmidt/articles/pdf/odp.pdf))

For θ ∈ (0, π), let V_theta = { z ∈ C : z ≠ 0 and |Arg z| > θ }, where Arg z ∈ (-π, π). For an open set V ⊂ C, define its Lehmer–Langevin constant by L(V) = inf{ M(α)^(1/[Q(α):Q]) : α ∈ Qbar, α ≠ 0, α is not a root of unity, and every conjugate of α over Q lies outside V }, where, if f(X)=a0∏_{i=1}^d (X-α_i) ∈ Z[X] is the minimal polynomial of α, then M(α)=|a0|∏_{i=1}^d max(1,|α_i|). Determine L(V_theta) as a function of θ. ([imj-prg.fr](https://www.imj-prg.fr/preprints/282.pdf))

Let K be a number field equipped with a real embedding, let V be a smooth variety over K, and let Z be the closure of V(K) in V(R) for the real topology. Assume that K = Q and that V(Q) is Zariski dense in V. Is Z necessarily a union of connected components of V(R)?

For an integer n >= 2, let A_n be the set of real numbers xi such that there exist constants c_1(xi), c_2(xi) > 0 with the following properties: for every algebraic number alpha with [Q(alpha):Q] <= n, one has |xi - alpha| >= c_2(xi) H(alpha)^(-(n+1)); and there exist infinitely many algebraic numbers alpha with [Q(alpha):Q] <= n such that |xi - alpha| <= c_1(xi) H(alpha)^(-(n+1)), where H(alpha) denotes the usual height of the minimal polynomial of alpha over Z. Does A_n strictly contain the set of real algebraic numbers of degree n+1?

Let (n_i)_{i>=0} be a strictly increasing sequence of positive integers. Suppose there exists a prime number p such that the formal power series f(z) = ∑_{i>=0} z^{n_i} in F_p[[z]] is algebraic over F_p(z) and irrational in the sense that f(z) does not belong to F_p(z). Must the real number α = ∑_{i>=0} 10^{-n_i} be transcendental?

Given that the Kishino virtual knot is already known to be nontrivial by the 3-strand Jones polynomial, the Ξ-polynomial, the quaternionic biquandle, the surface bracket polynomial, and Kadokami’s genus-two shadow-curve method, can one find further illuminating recognitions/proofs of its nontriviality and, more fundamentally, classify exactly when a nontrivial compact virtual knot can occur as a connected sum of two trivial virtual knots, taking into account that connected sum for closed virtual knots is not well defined, whereas for long virtual knots it is an ordered well-defined operation; closely relatedly, can one classify the long virtual knots whose closures are equivalent to the unknot?

For flat virtual knots and links (also called virtual strings), defined as diagrams with virtual crossings and undecorated flat crossings modulo generalized flat Reidemeister moves, can one construct new combinatorial invariants of flat virtuals and clarify the structure of the flat biquandle algebra, which the paper notes is isomorphic to the Weyl algebra and has no non-trivial finite-dimensional representations, in particular with the aim of obtaining invariants that detect flat linking phenomena beyond the mod 2 linking number?

For each ordinal α, classify the equivalence classes of flat virtual knot and link diagrams in which every flat crossing is labeled by an element of α, where equivalence is generated by the generalized flat Reidemeister moves for flat virtual diagrams (including the usual detour move for virtual crossings) except that a flat third Reidemeister move is allowed only when the strand incident with two crossings both labeled a is slid across a crossing labeled b with a>b. ([ymsc.tsinghua.edu.cn](https://ymsc.tsinghua.edu.cn/__local/9/84/D5/2B246EB7EE7966BCCB35D74B76D_AAB7F286_40CAA.pdf))

What is the precise relationship between the theory of flat virtual knots and links—namely, equivalence classes of diagrams with flat crossings and virtual crossings modulo the generalized flat Reidemeister moves, with detour moves allowed for virtual crossings across flat crossings but not conversely—and the theory of doodle links, in which there is only one crossing type and that crossing is not allowed to slide over itself?

In the Kauffman-Dye theory of virtual 3-manifolds, where a virtual 3-manifold is a Kirby equivalence class of framed virtual links, do the two equivalence relations on ordinary 3-manifolds coming from this viewpoint coincide: namely, if framed classical links K and L present ordinary 3-manifolds by surgery and K and L are equivalent under the virtual Kirby calculus, must they already be equivalent under the classical Kirby calculus? In the same setting, what geometric-topology object is represented by these virtual Kirby-equivalence classes, and does the alternative theory obtained by performing surgery on links in thickened surfaces S_g x R, taken up to stabilization, coincide with the Kauffman-Dye theory? ([impan.pl](https://www.impan.pl/shop/en/publication/transaction/download/product/89015))

Let a welded knot be the equivalence class of a virtual knot diagram under the generalized Reidemeister moves together with only one forbidden move (for example, the upper forbidden move). Since the fundamental group and quandle are invariant under this upper forbidden move and every welded knot is the closure of a welded braid, can one construct good invariants of welded knots and, if possible, classify welded knots; and, for welded knots or links, is Satoh's map from these equivalence classes to ambient isotopy classes of ribbon torus embeddings in four-space faithful, even though it is already known to induce an isomorphism from the welded knot's combinatorial fundamental group, indeed quandle, to the fundamental group of the complement of the corresponding torus embedding? ([impan.pl](https://www.impan.pl/shop/en/publication/transaction/download/product/89015))

In the setting of long knots viewed as 1-1 tangles, can one enlarge Manturov’s long-knot invariant structure by combining it with the biquandle construction to obtain more powerful invariants of long knots, determine whether these long-knot methods yield genuinely new classical knot invariants via the classical compact-to-long correspondence, and, for a long flat virtual knot diagram F, exploit Turaev’s descending diagram D(F)—obtained by resolving every flat (non-virtual) crossing so that one always goes over before going under, with the long virtual knot type of D(F) depending only on F—so that every virtual-knot invariant I produces a long-flat invariant I[D(F)], with the aim of carrying out effective sample calculations toward the full classification of long flat knots? ([ymsc.tsinghua.edu.cn](https://ymsc.tsinghua.edu.cn/__local/9/84/D5/2B246EB7EE7966BCCB35D74B76D_AAB7F286_40CAA.pdf))

Can one explicitly construct, for oriented virtual knot and link diagrams, a generators-and-relations presentation of a virtual biquandle by assigning one generator to each edge, imposing at each classical crossing the relations of a linear biquandle over a non-commutative coefficient ring (in the sense of the non-commutative linear/quaternionic example discussed nearby), and imposing at each virtual crossing additional virtual-quandle-type operations, so that the resulting presented algebra is invariant under the generalized Reidemeister moves?

Does there exist a birack whose associated action on virtual braids is faithful, and is Manturov’s invariant of virtual braids from [87]—also cited in [74], [3], and [51]—faithful, i.e. injective on virtual braids? ([ymsc.tsinghua.edu.cn](https://ymsc.tsinghua.edu.cn/__local/9/84/D5/2B246EB7EE7966BCCB35D74B76D_AAB7F286_40CAA.pdf))

For oriented virtual links considered up to generalized Reidemeister equivalence, is the fundamental biquandle BQ(K) a complete invariant up to mirror images, with the explicit caveat that the authors already know BQ takes the same value on the orientation-reversed mirror image obtained by reflecting in a plane perpendicular to the diagram plane; can one exhibit good examples of biquandles that satisfy the Section 3.2 axioms but are not strong, in the sense that the elements x, y, z, t required in axiom (3) exist but are not uniquely determined; and, in the linear case coming from the Alexander biquandle, what more can be understood about the algebra with generators A and B and relation [B,(A - 1)(A, B)] = 0 cited in [5]? ([ymsc.tsinghua.edu.cn](https://ymsc.tsinghua.edu.cn/__local/9/84/D5/2B246EB7EE7966BCCB35D74B76D_AAB7F286_40CAA.pdf))

Problem 11 (Virtualization and Unit Jones Polynomial): let crossing virtualization mean replacing a classical crossing by that crossing flanked by two virtual crossings. Determine whether the following assertions hold: (i) if K is a nontrivial classical knot and \tilde K is a nontrivial virtual knot obtained from K by virtualizing some subset of its crossings, with Jones polynomial V_{\tilde K}(t)=1, then \tilde K is not classical, i.e. it is not virtually equivalent to any classical knot; (ii) every virtual knot diagram K with unit Jones polynomial V_K(t)=1 is equivalent to a classical diagram by virtual equivalence together with crossing virtualization; and (iii) whenever classical knots K and K' are related by crossing virtualizations and virtual Reidemeister moves, they are already classically equivalent. ([ymsc.tsinghua.edu.cn](https://ymsc.tsinghua.edu.cn/__local/9/84/D5/2B246EB7EE7966BCCB35D74B76D_AAB7F286_40CAA.pdf))

Construct and study a homology theory for virtual quandles arising in virtual knot theory—where the usual quandle formalism is used at classical crossings and extra structure is added at virtual crossings—in direct analogy with the quandle homology theories cited in [10, 33].

Can one construct, over the ring of integers, a generalization of the Khovanov complex for virtual knots that works for arbitrary virtual diagrams and extends the existing integral theory for the large class of virtual link diagrams with orientable atom; and, in the formulation of virtual Khovanov homology used in [91] and [78], classify K-full and Kho-full virtual knots, where K-full means that some diagram has its leading term, lowest term, or both coming from the B-state, Kho-full is the analogous notion for the Khovanov invariant, and such diagrams are called optimal; determine whether optimal diagrams are always minimal with respect to the number of classical crossings, classify the diagram moves that preserve optimality, decide whether a classical knot with minimal classical diagram of n crossings can admit any virtual diagram with fewer than n classical crossings, and determine whether any virtual knot can have torsion in the B-state of its Khovanov homology, i.e. in the genuine leading term of some diagram? ([impan.pl](https://www.impan.pl/shop/en/publication/transaction/download/product/89015))

Let B_n denote the Brauer algebra obtained by adjoining virtual crossings to the Temperley-Lieb algebra on n boundary points, so that B_n is the diagram algebra of all connection patterns from n points to n points (the paper's "Virtual Temperley Lieb Algebra"). What is the structure of the Jones-Wenzl projectors when placed in B_n, and can these projectors be used to formulate a virtual analogue of the classical Temperley-Lieb recoupling theory in this Brauer-algebra setting? ([ymsc.tsinghua.edu.cn](https://ymsc.tsinghua.edu.cn/__local/9/84/D5/2B246EB7EE7966BCCB35D74B76D_AAB7F286_40CAA.pdf))

Using the interpretation of virtual knots as stable equivalence classes of embeddings in thickened surfaces, determine an appropriate definition of an alternating virtual knot, classify alternating virtual knots in that sense, formulate and prove the correct virtual analogue of the Tait flyping conjecture, and, prior to passing to stable equivalence, classify alternating weaves on fixed surfaces (that is, without allowing stabilization or destabilization by adding or removing empty handles).

For each virtual link L, let C(L), V(L), and T(L) denote, respectively, the minima over all virtual-diagram representatives of L of the numbers of classical crossings, virtual crossings, and total crossings. For a virtual knot K, let u_cl(K) be the minimum number of crossing switches needed to unknot K, taken over all diagrams of K, and let u_v(K) be the minimum number of direct flattenings (changing a classical crossing into a virtual crossing) needed to unknot K, taken over all virtual diagrams of K. Determine the basic relations and effective estimates for these invariants: in particular, develop the theory of the virtual unknotting number u_v(K); relate V(K) to the least genus among stable surface realizations of K; decide whether T(L)=C(L)+V(L) (the paper prints "T=V+L"); find algorithms for computing V(L) in some classes of virtual knots/links; and obtain nontrivial upper and lower bounds for C(L), V(L), and T(L) from virtual-knot polynomials.

Within the paper’s topological model of virtual knot theory—where virtual links are represented by stable equivalence classes of embeddings of links in thickened surfaces S_g × R, with stable equivalence generated by isotopy in the thickened surface, homeomorphisms of the surface, and addition or subtraction of empty handles—can one define a category of wild virtual knots, state explicit axioms for that category, and prove a criterion specifying when a wild equivalence between two tame virtual links implies that those links are tamely equivalent as virtual links? ([ymsc.tsinghua.edu.cn](https://ymsc.tsinghua.edu.cn/__local/9/84/D5/2B246EB7EE7966BCCB35D74B76D_AAB7F286_40CAA.pdf))

Within the Goussarov-Polyak-Viro framework recalled in Section 5—where virtual knots are studied via Gauss diagrams, semi-virtual dotted chords, the Polyak algebra P, and its truncations P_n—what is the connection between virtual knot polynomials and Vassiliev knot invariants of virtual knots in Kauffman’s sense, and, in particular, does every finite-type Vassiliev invariant of classical knots admit an extension to a finite-type invariant of long virtual knots in the sense of [32], whose restriction to classical long knots (equivalently, classical knots) is the original invariant, rather than only to an invariant of the alternate finite-type kind mentioned in [59]?

Let K be a non-trivial virtual knot, interpreted via the thickened-surface model as a stable equivalence class of knot embeddings in surfaces times an interval. Does there exist a realization of K as a knot in N = S_g × I, where S_g is a compact oriented surface of minimal possible genus among all such realizations of K, together with an unknotted embedding e: N ↪ R^3, such that the image e(K) is a non-trivial classical knot in R^3? ([ymsc.tsinghua.edu.cn](https://ymsc.tsinghua.edu.cn/__local/9/84/D5/2B246EB7EE7966BCCB35D74B76D_AAB7F286_40CAA.pdf))

Let K and K' be long virtual knots, with # denoting the ordered connected sum in the long-knot category. If K#K' is isotopic to K'#K as long knots, must there exist a long virtual knot L, classical long knots Q and Q', and integers m,n ≥ 0 such that K = L^m#Q and K' = L^n#Q', where L^m denotes the connected sum of m copies of L? ([ymsc.tsinghua.edu.cn](https://ymsc.tsinghua.edu.cn/__local/9/84/D5/2B246EB7EE7966BCCB35D74B76D_AAB7F286_40CAA.pdf))

For the rack space of the dihedral rack, whose low-dimensional integral homology is interpreted by virtual link diagrams consistently colored by the rack in dimension 2 and by such diagrams together with region colorings in dimension 3, is it true that, for each prime p, the third homology contains a cyclic summand Z_p, as suggested by computer calculations?

Let X be a smooth projective genus-1 curve over an algebraically closed field of characteristic 2 whose moduli point is generic among genus-1 curves. Show that there exists a tame morphism f : X -> P^1 of degree 5 such that the monodromy group of f, in its natural degree-5 transitive action, is A_5 and such that f has ramification type (3,3,3,3,3), i.e. exactly five branch points, each with local cycle type 3-1-1.

Let σ = (σ_1, ..., σ_r) be a tuple of permutations in S_n whose product is 1 and which generate a transitive subgroup G ⊂ S_n, and let g be the genus determined by σ through the Riemann–Hurwitz formula. Let H_σ denote the Hurwitz space parametrizing degree-n covers f: X → P^1 with branch-cycle description σ, and let φ_σ: H_σ → M_g be the forgetful morphism sending such a cover to the isomorphism class of its source curve X. For a prime p for which this ramification data are tame in characteristic p, determine whether the geometric fiber H_σ ⊗ F_p is nonempty; and, when it is nonempty, determine the dimension of the image of φ_σ ⊗ F_p in M_g ⊗ F_p.

Let G ⊂ S_n be a transitive permutation group and let σ = (σ_1,...,σ_r) be a Hurwitz datum as in the paper, with σ_1···σ_r = 1 and the σ_i generating G, and let φ_σ: H(σ) → M_g be the Hurwitz-space morphism sending a tame cover f: X → P^1 to its source curve X, where g is determined by σ via Riemann-Hurwitz. Fix a prime p for which the characteristic-p fiber H(σ) ⊗ F_p is nonempty, and let f be the generic point of an irreducible component of H(σ) ⊗ F_p. Is the Zariski tangent map dφ_σ at f of the expected generic rank—equivalently, does φ_σ in characteristic p have the same generic rank as in characteristic 0?

Let k be a perfect field of characteristic p>0, let G be a profinite group, and let V be a finite-dimensional k-vector space with the discrete topology, equipped with a continuous k-linear action of G such that End_{kG}(V)=k. If R(G,V) denotes the universal deformation ring of V over W(k), the ring of infinite Witt vectors over k, does there exist such a triple (G,k,V) for which R(G,V) is Noetherian but not a local complete intersection?

Let k be a field of characteristic p > 0, let X/k be a smooth projective curve, and let rho: G -> Aut_k(X) be an action of a finite group G on X. Let W(k) be the ring of Witt vectors of k, let C be the category of local Artinian W(k)-algebras with residue field k, and let D(X, rho) be the deformation functor sending A in C to the set of isomorphism classes of liftings of (X, rho) to A, where a lifting means a smooth finite-type A-scheme X' with special fiber X together with a G-action G -> Aut_A(X') lifting rho. Let R(X, rho) be the Schlessinger prorepresentable hull of D(X, rho), and define nu(X, rho) := char(R(X, rho)). Give an example of a group action (X, rho) such that nu(X, rho) = p^n for some finite integer n > 1.

Let k = \bar{\mathbf{F}}_q be an algebraic closure of a finite field, and let X and Y be connected smooth projective curves over k. For each integer r >= 1, let pi_1^(r)(X) (resp. pi_1^(r)(Y)) denote the rank-r Tannakian quotient attached to the neutral Tannakian category of stratified vector bundles on X (resp. Y). If pi_1^(r)(X) is isomorphic to pi_1^(r)(Y) for every r >= 1, must X and Y be isomorphic up to Frobenius twist; equivalently, does there exist an integer n such that Y is k-isomorphic to X^(n)?

Fix a positive integer r. Let k be the algebraic closure of a finite field, let X be a connected smooth projective curve over k, and let π_1^{(r)}(X) denote the Tannaka group of the Tannakian subcategory SS(X)_r whose objects are sequences {E_n, σ_n} with E_n a vector bundle on X, σ_n : F^*(E_n) ≅ E_{n-1}, and Card({(E_n, σ_n)}) ≤ r. Can one characterize π_1^{(r)}(X) geometrically, without mentioning stratified vector bundles; that is, can one characterize the finite étale Galois coverings Y → X whose associated quotient map π_1(X) → Gal(Y/X) factors through π_1^{(r)}(X)? ([numdam.org](https://www.numdam.org/item/RSMUP_2005__113__129_0.pdf))

Let k=\overline{\mathbf F}_p, let X/k be a connected smooth projective curve, and for each integer r\ge 1 let \pi_1^{(r)}(X) denote the rank-r quotient of the algebraic fundamental group considered in the paper, i.e. the quotient governing stratified bundles (equivalently, coherent \mathcal D_X-modules) on X of rank at most r. Is \pi_1^{(r)}(X) always an extension of a finite group by a p-group?

Let X be a smooth projective curve over an algebraically closed field k of characteristic p > 0, and fix an integer r >= 1. For the paper's rank-r group pi_1^(r)(X) attached to flat/stratified bundles on X, how is the finiteness of pi_1^(r)(X) related to whether the Jacobian Jac(X) is ordinary or not ordinary?

Let X be a smooth connected projective variety over an algebraically closed field k of characteristic p>0, and fix a base point x. Let π_1^str(X,x) be the Tannaka group of stratified vector bundles on X, and for each integer r≥1 let π_1^(r)(X,x) denote the quotient of π_1^str(X,x) determined by stratified bundles of rank at most r. If the étale fundamental group π_1^ét(X,x) is trivial, must π_1^(r)(X,x) be trivial for every r≥1?

Let k be an algebraically closed field of characteristic p, let M_g be the moduli space of smooth curves of genus g, let H_g ⊂ M_g be the locus of smooth hyperelliptic curves of genus g, and for 0 <= f <= g let V_{g,f} ⊂ M_g be the locus of curves X with p-rank at most f, i.e. dim_{F_p} Hom(mu_p, Jac(X)) <= f. For each g and f, is the natural scheme-theoretic intersection H_g ∩ V_{g,f} reduced?

Let k be an algebraically closed field of characteristic p > 2, and let C -> P^1_k be a smooth hyperelliptic cover of genus g. Is every such C deformable, through hyperelliptic covers of P^1_k of the same genus, to an ordinary hyperelliptic curve by varying only one of its branch points while keeping all the other branch points fixed?

Let k be an algebraically closed field of characteristic p > 2. Let M denote the unique isomorphism class of the p-torsion group scheme of a supersingular elliptic curve over k, and let N denote the p-torsion group scheme of a supersingular abelian surface that is not superspecial. Suppose λ1, λ2, λ3 are distinct supersingular values in k, meaning that for each i the elliptic curve branched at {0,1,∞,λ_i} is supersingular. If X is the smooth genus-2 hyperelliptic curve X → P^1_k branched exactly at {0,1,∞,λ1,λ2,λ3}, then, as the triple (λ1, λ2, λ3) varies over all such distinct supersingular triples, which of the four group schemes (Z/p ⊕ μ_p)^2, M ⊕ (Z/p ⊕ μ_p), N, and M^2 can occur, up to isomorphism, as the Jacobian p-torsion group scheme Jac(X)[p]?

Let k be an algebraically closed field of characteristic p > 2, and let Q denote the p-torsion finite commutative group scheme of an abelian variety of dimension 3 over k with p-rank 0 and a-number 1. Does there exist a smooth hyperelliptic k-curve X of genus 4, respectively of genus 5, such that Jac(X)[p] is isomorphic, as a finite commutative group scheme over k, to Q ⊕ (Z/p ⊕ μ_p), respectively to Q ⊕ (Z/p ⊕ μ_p)^2?

Let k be an algebraically closed field of characteristic p > 0, and let C_f be the Artin-Schreier curve C_f : W^p - W = f(X) with f(X) in k[X]. It is known that a p-Sylow subgroup G of Aut(C_f) is an extension 1 -> Z/pZ -> G -> (Z/pZ)^n -> 1 for some n >= 0, where the kernel Z/pZ is the Artin-Schreier covering group of C_f, and conversely every such extension occurs for some C_f. Given such an extension G, can one choose f(X) in F_p[X] so that C_f realizes G as a p-Sylow subgroup of Aut(C_f), with the kernel Z/pZ equal to the Artin-Schreier covering group of C_f?

Let k be an algebraically closed field of characteristic p>0, let C/k be a connected nonsingular projective curve of positive genus, and let G be a finite p-subgroup of Aut_k(C). Assume that (C,G) satisfies condition (N), namely g(C)>0 and |G|/g(C) > 2p/(p-1). By Proposition 1.2 this forces C/G ≅ P^1_k, the cover C -> C/G to have a unique ramification point, and C to have p-rank 0. Classify all such pairs (C,G).

Let k be an algebraically closed field of characteristic p>0, let C/k be a connected nonsingular projective curve of genus g>=2, and let G be a p-subgroup of Aut_k(C) such that (C,G) satisfies condition (N), namely |G|/g > 2p/(p-1). If infinity is the unique ramification point of the cover C -> C/G, so that G=G_1 is the wild inertia group at infinity, must the second lower ramification group G_2 at infinity be abelian?

Let k be an algebraically closed field of characteristic p > 0, let C be a non-singular projective curve over k of genus g_C >= 2, and let G be a p-subgroup of Aut_k(C) such that (C, G) satisfies condition (N), i.e. g_C > 0 and |G|/g_C > 2p/(p-1). By Proposition 6.3, there is a unique point infinity in C such that G is the wild inertia subgroup at infinity for the cover C -> C/G ~= P^1_k; let G_i denote the ramification groups in lower numbering at infinity. Is it possible for the second lower ramification group G_2 to be nonabelian?

Let k be an algebraically closed field of characteristic p > 0, let C/k be a nonsingular projective curve of genus g_C >= 2, and let G be a p-subgroup of Aut_k(C) such that (C, G) satisfies Nakajima’s condition (N), i.e. g_C > 0 and |G|/g_C > 2p/(p - 1). Let infinity be the unique ramification point of the cover C -> C/G given by Proposition 6.3, and let G_2 be the second ramification group of G at infinity in lower numbering. Assuming G_2 is abelian, can G_2 have exponent strictly greater than p?

Let k be an algebraically closed field of characteristic p>0, let C be a non-singular projective k-curve of genus g_C>=2, and let G be a p-subgroup of Aut_k(C) such that (C,G) satisfies Nakajima's condition (N), namely g_C>0 and |G|/g_C > 2p/(p-1). By Proposition 6.3, the quotient map pi:C->C/G has a unique ramification point infinity, the quotient C/G is isomorphic to P^1_k, and G=G_0=G_1 ⊋ G_2 ⊇ G_3 ⊇ ... denotes the lower ramification filtration at infinity. Classify all such actions (C,G) for which the second lower ramification group G_2 is elementary abelian, i.e. G_2 is isomorphic to (Z/pZ)^n for some n.

Let k be an algebraically closed field of characteristic p>0, let C be a nonsingular projective curve over k of genus g_C=g>=2, and let G be a finite p-subgroup of Aut_k(C) such that (C,G) satisfies Nakajima’s condition (N), namely g_C>0 and |G|/g_C>2p/(p-1). Describe the set of values attained by the quotient |G|/g_C^2 for such pairs (C,G), and for each attained value give an upper bound for the dimension of the subvariety of M_g consisting of curves C that admit such a big p-group action.

Let n > 1 be an integer, and let C/Q_2 be the hyperelliptic curve defined by y^2 = 1 - x^(2n). In the finite-monodromy setup of Definition 6.14, let L/Q_2 be the finite monodromy extension, i.e. the minimal finite Galois extension over which C acquires stable reduction; when g(C) = n - 1 >= 2, let C_st denote the stable model of C_L over the valuation ring of L, with special fiber C_k. Determine the stable reduction C_k of C, determine the wild monodromy group Gal(L/Q_2)_w (the 2-Sylow subgroup of Gal(L/Q_2)), and describe its induced faithful action on the special fiber C_k of the stable model.

Let K be a strict henselization of Q_2 with residue field k, and let X/K be the smooth projective curve birationally defined by Y^4 = (1+X)^2 + X^3 =: F(X). Equivalently, X -> P^1_K is a 2^2-cyclic cover ramified at the three finite branch points x_i satisfying F(x_i)=0 and at infinity; in particular, it satisfies Raynaud’s condition. Let L/K be the finite monodromy extension in the sense of Definition 6.14, i.e. the minimal Galois extension over which X_L has semistable reduction, and let X^st be the stable model of X_L. Determine the special fiber X^st_k (the stable reduction), the wild monodromy group Gal(L/K)_w (the 2-Sylow subgroup of Gal(L/K)), and the induced faithful action Gal(L/K)_w -> Aut_k(X^st_k) on the special fiber.

Let K be in the mixed-characteristic local setting of Section 6.2.1 (equivalently, in the authors' reformulation, take K=Q_p^tame), and let X_K -> P^1_K be a p-cyclic cover of genus g=((p-1)(m-1))/2. Let L/K be the minimal finite Galois extension over which X_K has stable reduction, let X be the stable model of X_L, let X_k be its special fiber, and let Gal(L/K)_w be the p-Sylow subgroup of the finite monodromy group Gal(L/K). For a prescribed type of degeneration of the stable reduction of X_K, for which previous work gives an upper bound on the size of the wild automorphism group (equivalently, the p-part of Aut_k(X_k)) of the special fiber, does there exist such a p-cyclic cover with that degeneration type for which Gal(L/K)_w is maximal, i.e. attains that upper bound?

Let X be the generic smooth projective curve of genus 1 over an algebraically closed field of characteristic 2. Does there exist a tame rational function f : X -> P^1 of degree 5 whose monodromy group is A5 and whose ramification type is (3,3,3,3,3), i.e. a cover branched at five points with local monodromy a 3-cycle at each branch point?

Let K = Q_p^tame with valuation ring R, let q = p^s, and let C/K be the p-cyclic cover of P^1_K birationally given by Z^p = 1 + cX^q + X^{q+1}. In the specific case of Proposition 6.19(b), where C has potentially good reduction and the wild monodromy group Gal(L/K)_w of the finite monodromy extension L/K is known to be extraspecial of order p q^2 and exponent p when p > 2 (and, for p = 2, the corresponding central product built from Q8 and D8), determine the ramification filtration of Gal(L/K)_w.

Let R be a strictly henselian discrete valuation ring of mixed characteristic (0,p), with fraction field K and residue field k, let X_K/K be a smooth projective geometrically connected curve of genus g(X_K) >= 2, let L/K be the minimal finite Galois extension over which X_K acquires a stable model 𝓧/R_L, and let X_k be the special fiber of 𝓧. Via the Deligne–Mumford faithful action, view Gal(L/K) as a subgroup of Aut_k(X_k). In what precise sense is the higher ramification filtration on the wild monodromy subgroup Gal(L/K)_w reflected by, or recoverable from, the action of its image on X_k; equivalently, can one read the wild monodromy filtration directly from the corresponding automorphism data on the stable special fiber?

In the p-cyclic case G = Z/pZ considered in Section 6.2.1-6.2.2, with X_K/G congruent to P^1_K and L/K the finite monodromy extension of a smooth proper curve X_K (that is, the minimal Galois extension over which X_K acquires semistable reduction), a fixed degeneration type determines an analytic open subset of the genus-g moduli space M_g. For that analytic open, which finite Galois extensions of the tame base field K^tame (in the paper's notation, with the nearby model family taken over Q_p^tame) can occur as the finite monodromy extensions?

Let p be a prime, let k be an algebraically closed field of characteristic p>0, and let G be a nonabelian group of order p^3. Does G have the weak local lifting property in the sense of Definition 7.2; that is, does there exist a discrete valuation ring R finite over the Witt ring W(k), a faithful homomorphism i: G -> Aut_k(k[[z]]), and a homomorphism \tilde{i}: G -> Aut_R(R[[Z]]) whose reduction modulo the maximal ideal of R is i?

Let p be a prime, k an algebraically closed field of characteristic p > 0, and let n,m be positive integers with gcd(m,p)=1. Does there exist an n-dimensional F_p-vector space L_{m+1,n} of meromorphic differential forms on P^1_k such that every nonzero ω in L_{m+1,n} is logarithmic (i.e. ω = df/f for some f in k(P^1)^×) and has a unique zero at infinity of order m-1? If so, is Pagot's conjectural criterion true, namely that such a space exists if and only if p^(n-1)(p-1) divides m+1? ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/abs/math/0203259))

Let k be a countable algebraically closed field, for example the algebraic closure of Q, and let g >= 4. Does there exist an abelian variety A over k of dimension g such that A is not isogenous, as an unpolarized abelian variety, to the Jacobian J(C) of any curve C of compact type over k?

Fix a prime number p. Let k be an algebraically closed field of characteristic p, and for each integer g >= 2 let mu(g,p) denote the maximum of #Aut(C) as C ranges over all complete, irreducible, nonsingular algebraic curves of genus g defined over k (equivalently, smooth projective genus-g curves over k). Does there exist a polynomial M_p(T) in Q[T] such that mu(g,p) >= M_p(g) for every integer g >= 2, and such that mu(g,p) = M_p(g) for infinitely many values of g?

For a prime number p, let m(g; p) denote the maximum of #Aut(C) as C ranges over complete, irreducible, nonsingular algebraic curves of genus g >= 2 over an algebraically closed field of characteristic p. Assume there exists a polynomial M_p(T) in Q[T] such that m(g; p) >= M_p(g) for every g >= 2 and m(g; p) = M_p(g) for infinitely many values of g. Must this polynomial be the same for all prime numbers p, and in fact equal to the polynomial 8(T+1)?

Let k be an algebraically closed field of characteristic 0, let k[n] := k[x_1,...,x_n] with n > 1, and let Aut_k^* k[n] := {sigma in Aut_k k[n] | det((partial sigma(x_j)/partial x_i)_(1<=i,j<=n)) = 1}. Let T := {diag(t_1,...,t_n) in Aut_k^* k[n] | sigma(x_i) = t_i x_i, t_i in k, and product_{i=1}^n t_i = 1}. A nonzero locally nilpotent k-derivation D of k[n] (that is, for every f in k[n] there exists m = m(f) >= 1 with D^m(f) = 0) is called a root vector of Aut_k^* k[n] with respect to T if there exists a nontrivial character chi: T -> G_m such that sigma o D o sigma^{-1} = chi(sigma)D for every sigma in T; chi is then called the corresponding root. Find all roots and all root vectors of Aut_k^* k[n] with respect to T.

Let k be an algebraically closed field of characteristic 0, let k^[n] = k[x1,...,xn] with n > 1, and let G = Aut*_k(k^[n]) = {σ ∈ Aut_k(k^[n]) : Jac(σ) = 1}. Let T = {diag(t1,...,tn) ∈ G : ti ∈ k^× and t1⋯tn = 1}, acting by xi ↦ ti xi. Describe the centralizer C_G(T) and the normalizer N_G(T).

Let k be an algebraically closed field of characteristic 0, let k[n]:=k[x_1,...,x_n], and let Aut*_k k[n]:={σ in Aut_k k[n] | det((∂σ(x_j)/∂x_i)_{1<=i,j<=n})=1}. A k-derivation D of k[n] is called locally nilpotent if for every h in k[n] there exists m=m(h) such that D^m(h)=0. A subgroup G of Aut*_k k[n] is called ∂-generated if there exists a set 𝒢 of locally nilpotent derivations of k[n] such that G is generated by the automorphisms exp(D) with D in 𝒢; it is called finitely ∂-generated if there exists a finite set 𝒢 of locally nilpotent derivations such that G is generated by all exp(fD) with D in 𝒢 and f in Ker(D). For each integer n>=1, is the full volume-preserving affine Cremona group Aut*_k k[n] ∂-generated? If so, is it finitely ∂-generated?

Let k be an algebraically closed field of characteristic 0, let A = k[x_1, ..., x_n], and let G = Aut_k^*(A) be the special affine Cremona group, i.e. the subgroup of k-automorphisms of A with Jacobian determinant 1. For locally nilpotent k-derivations P, Q of A, consider the one-dimensional unipotent subgroups U_P = {exp(tP) | t in k} and U_Q = {exp(tQ) | t in k} of G. When is the minimal closed subgroup of G containing U_P and U_Q a finite-dimensional algebraic subgroup?

Assume k is an algebraically closed field of characteristic 0. For every connected semisimple algebraic group G over k and every finite-order k-automorphism σ ∈ Aut_k(G), with fixed-point subgroup G^σ := { g ∈ G | σ(g) = g }, is the homogeneous algebraic variety G/G^σ rational over k? ([citeseerx.ist.psu.edu](https://citeseerx.ist.psu.edu/document?doi=5c2c8c4b99931b1cc791ac09768c3eed7420f9a3&repid=rep1&type=pdf&utm_source=openai))

Let B = {B(s,t)}_{s,t >= 0} be a two-parameter d-dimensional Brownian sheet in R^d, so that Cov(B_i(s,t), B_j(u,v)) = min(s,u) min(t,v) delta_{ij}. Assume d is 2 or 3. For each s>0, define the zero set of the slice along s by T_d(s) := {t>0 : B(s,t)=0}. Theorem 1.2 shows that there exists an event of probability 1 on which dim_H T_d(s) = 0 for every s>0. Is it true that there exists an event of probability 1 on which T_d(s) is finite for every s>0?

Let B={B(s,t)}_{s,t>=0} be a two-parameter d-dimensional Brownian sheet in R^d, where d is either 4 or 5, and write R_+=[0,infinity). For each s>0, define the nontrivial slice double-point set by Y_d(s):={(t_1,t_2) in R_+^2 : 0<t_1<t_2 and B(s,t_1)=B(s,t_2)}. Also define the global slice double-point sets Dhat_d:={(s,t_1,t_2) in R_+^3 : 0<t_1<t_2 and B(s,t_1)=B(s,t_2)} and Dbar_d:={(s,t_1) in R_+^2 : there exists t_2>t_1>0 with B(s,t_1)=B(s,t_2)}; Section 5 and the codimension argument in Section 8.2 imply that dim_H(Dhat_d)=(3-d/2)_+ and dim_H(Dbar_d)=2 ∧ (3-d/2)_+. Must it nevertheless be true that there exists an event Omega_0 with P(Omega_0)=1 such that, for every omega in Omega_0 and every s>0, dim_H(Y_d(s)(omega))=0?

Let B={B(s,t)}_{s,t>=0} be a two-parameter Brownian sheet with values in R^d, where d is either 4 or 5; that is, B is a centered Gaussian field with Cov(B_i(s,t),B_j(u,v))=min(s,u)min(t,v)δ_{ij}. For each s>0, define the set of nontrivial double-point time pairs in the slice along s by Y_d(s):={(t_1,t_2) in (0,infinity)^2 : t_1<t_2 and B(s,t_1)=B(s,t_2)}. Is it true that there exists an event Omega_0 of probability one such that, for every omega in Omega_0 and every s>0, the set Y_d(s;omega) is finite?

Let B = {B(s,t)}_{s,t >= 0} be a two-parameter Brownian sheet in R^d, with d in {2,3}, and let Z := {(s,t) in (0,∞)^2 : B(s,t)=0}. Theorem 1.1 shows that the fixed projection Z_d = {s >= 0 : B(s,t)=0 for some t > 0} of Z onto the x-axis has Hausdorff dimension 2 - d/2 almost surely, which the introduction notes is also the Hausdorff dimension of Z itself. Does there exist a random orthogonal projection Pi of the parameter plane R^2 onto a line, possibly chosen as a measurable function of B, such that dim_H Pi(Z) differs from 2 - d/2 on an event of positive probability?

Let Bdot_1,...,Bdot_d be independent two-parameter white noises, and let u=(u^1,...,u^d) solve, under reasonable boundary conditions, the nonlinear hyperbolic system partial^2 u^i/(partial t partial x)=b^i(u)+sigma^i(u)·Bdot, 1<=i<=d, where sigma is bounded, C^infinity, and strongly elliptic. In the additive case partial^2 u^i/(partial t partial x)=Bdot_i+b^i(u), the paper notes that the law of u is mutually absolutely continuous with that of the d-dimensional Brownian sheet, so the Brownian-sheet results proved earlier in the paper transfer to u. Does the same remain true for the multiplicative-noise system; that is, do all of the preceding Brownian-sheet conclusions of the paper—specifically the zero-set and double-point capacity/hitting criteria, the associated Hausdorff-dimension statements, the Section 5 double-point analogues, and the slice escape-rate results—also hold for u?

For the d-vector solution u=(u_1,...,u_d) of the additive linear one-dimensional parabolic SPDE system ∂_t u_i(t,x)=∂_x^2 u_i(t,x)+ξ_i(t,x), i=1,...,d, where ξ_1,...,ξ_d are independent space-time white noises and the boundary conditions are left “reasonable” in the sense of the paper, can one develop a theory of the time-slices x↦u(t,x), as t varies, that is directly analogous to the Brownian-sheet slice theory established earlier in the paper—specifically, analogues of the paper’s results on slice zeros, slice double points, and exceptional slice behavior? ([math.utah.edu](https://www.math.utah.edu/~davar/PPT/SLICES/SlicesFinal.pdf))

Prosoluble analogue of Grothendieck's problem: let Gamma and Delta be residually soluble groups, and let psi: Gamma -> Delta be a homomorphism such that the induced map on true prosoluble completions PS(psi): PS(Gamma) -> PS(Delta) is an isomorphism, where PS(G)=lim_{N normal in G, G/N soluble} G/N.
