Suppose A is a stable GKK τ-matrix; that is, A is a P-matrix, it is weakly sign-symmetric in the sense that A[α,β] A[β,α] >= 0 for every minor of dispersal 1, it is a τ-matrix with l(A) := min(σ(A) ∩ R) (and min ∅ := ∞) satisfying l(A(α,α)) <= l(A(β,β)) < ∞ whenever ∅ != β ⊆ α and l(A) >= 0, and it is positive stable, meaning σ(A) lies in the open right half-plane. Must A satisfy Newton’s inequalities c_j(A)^2 >= c_{j-1}(A) c_{j+1}(A) for every j = 1,...,n-1? ([people.math.wisc.edu](https://people.math.wisc.edu/hans/paper_archive/other_papers/hs144.pdf))

Let X ⊆ ℝ be a set of reals. Let Γ be the family of countable nontrivial open γ-covers of X and Ω the family of countable nontrivial open ω-covers of X, where a γ-cover is an infinite open cover U of X such that every x ∈ X belongs to all but finitely many members of U, and an ω-cover is an open cover U of X such that every finite F ⊆ X is contained in some U ∈ U. Is the property U_fin(Γ,Ω)—for every sequence ⟨U_n : n ∈ ℕ⟩ of members of Γ with no U_n containing a finite subcover, there exist finite (possibly empty) F_n ⊆ U_n such that {⋃F_n : n ∈ ℕ} ∈ Ω—equivalent to S_fin(Γ,Ω)—for every sequence ⟨U_n : n ∈ ℕ⟩ of members of Γ, there exist finite (possibly empty) F_n ⊆ U_n such that ⋃_{n∈ℕ} F_n ∈ Ω? If these two properties are not equivalent, does the Hurewicz property U_fin(Γ,Γ) nevertheless imply S_fin(Γ,Ω) for sets of reals? ([u.cs.biu.ac.il](https://u.cs.biu.ac.il/~tsaban/Pdf/PublishedBackUp/FuturespmBU.pdf))

In ZFC, does there exist a set of reals X such that X satisfies Ufin(O,O) but fails Ufin(O,Γ), where O is the family of nontrivial open covers of X, Γ is the family of open γ-covers of X, and Ufin(U,V) means that for every sequence (U_n) of members of U having no finite subcover, there exist finite sets F_n ⊆ U_n such that the family {⋃F_n : n ∈ N} belongs to V?

Let S1(U,V), Sfin(U,V), and Ufin(U,V) be the usual selection principles for classes of covers of a space X. Here a cover means a nontrivial cover U of X, i.e. X = ⋃U and X ∉ U; O, Λ, Ω, and Γ denote the families of open covers, open large covers, open ω-covers, and open γ-covers of X, respectively, and B, BΛ, BΩ, and BΓ denote the corresponding countable Borel-cover classes. Find, in ZFC alone and without any additional set-theoretic assumptions, arbitrary topological spaces, and separately Lindelöf topological spaces, that witness non-implications among the distinct classical selection properties appearing in Figure 2 of the paper; that is, for a failed implication P ⇒ Q among those classical properties, construct a space X with X satisfying P but not Q.

In ZFC, let N ∪ {∞} be the one-point compactification of N, and let Z ⊆ (N ∪ {∞})^N be the subspace of all functions f such that f(n) ≤ f(n+1) for every n and, whenever f(n) < ∞, one has f(n) < f(n+1). For each increasing finite sequence s ∈ N^{<ω}, define q_s ∈ Z by q_s(k) = s(k) for k < |s| and q_s(k) = ∞ for k ≥ |s|, and let Q = {q_s : s is an increasing finite sequence}. If B = {f_α : α < 𝔟} ⊆ N^N is a 𝔟-scale of strictly increasing functions (that is, B is <=*-unbounded and α < β implies f_α <=* f_β), viewed as a subset of Z, and H = B ∪ Q, must H satisfy S1(Γ, Γ)? Equivalently: for every sequence (𝒰_n) of open γ-covers of H in the subspace topology from Z, where a γ-cover means an infinite nontrivial open cover in which each x ∈ H belongs to all but finitely many members, can one choose U_n ∈ 𝒰_n for each n so that {U_n : n ∈ N} is again a γ-cover of H?

Is there, provably in ZFC and without additional set-theoretic hypotheses, an uncountable set of reals X ⊆ R such that X satisfies S_1(B_Γ, B); that is, for every sequence (U_n)_{n in N} of members of B_Γ(X), where each U_n is a countable nontrivial Borel γ-cover of X, one can choose U_n in U_n for each n so that {U_n : n in N} is a countable nontrivial Borel cover of X?

Let X ⊆ R be an uncountable set of reals, and let B, BΩ, and BΓ denote the families of countable Borel covers, countable Borel ω-covers, and countable Borel γ-covers of X, respectively. In the reduced Borel diagram of Figure 2 (using the Borel equivalences S1(BΓ,V) = Sfin(BΓ,V) = Ufin(BΓ,V) for V ∈ {B, BΩ, BΓ}), can one, under Martin’s Axiom or under hypotheses weaker than Martin’s Axiom, construct for each configuration consistent with that diagram but different from the four already realized in Figure 3(a)–(d), an uncountable set of reals X that realizes exactly that pattern of satisfaction/failure among the front-plane properties S1(BΓ,BΓ), S1(BΓ,BΩ), S1(BΓ,B), Sfin(BΩ,BΩ), S1(BΩ,BΓ), S1(BΩ,BΩ), and S1(B,B)?

For a space X in the paper’s default setting (typically a set of reals), let B_Ω(X) be the family of countable Borel ω-covers of X, where a cover 𝒰 is nontrivial (X = ⋃𝒰 and X ∉ 𝒰) and every finite subset of X is contained in some U ∈ 𝒰. Is at least one of the two selection properties S_1(B_Ω, B_Ω) or S_fin(B_Ω, B_Ω) hereditary; that is, if X satisfies one of these properties, must every subset Y ⊆ X, with the induced topology and its own family B_Ω(Y) of countable Borel ω-covers, satisfy the same property?

For a set of reals X, let B_Ω(X) and B_Γ(X) denote the families of countable Borel ω-covers and countable Borel γ-covers of X, respectively, and let S_1(U,V) and S_fin(U,V) be the usual Scheepers selection principles. Which, if any, of the three Borel selection properties S_1(B_Ω, B_Γ), S_1(B_Ω, B_Ω), and S_fin(B_Ω, B_Ω) are closed under taking finite powers; that is, if X satisfies one of these properties, must X^n satisfy the same property for every positive integer n? ([u.cs.biu.ac.il](https://u.cs.biu.ac.il/~tsaban/Pdf/PublishedBackUp/FuturespmBU.pdf))

Let X be a set of reals. Let B, B_Ω, and B_Γ denote, respectively, the families of countable Borel covers, countable Borel ω-covers, and countable Borel γ-covers of X, where a cover U is nontrivial (X = ⋃U and X ∉ U), an ω-cover means that every finite F ⊆ X is contained in some U ∈ U, and a γ-cover means that U is infinite and each x ∈ X belongs to all but finitely many members of U. For collections U and V of covers, write S_1(U, V) if for every sequence (U_n)n∈N with each U_n ∈ U there exist U_n ∈ U_n such that {U_n : n ∈ N} ∈ V, and write S_fin(U, V) if for every such sequence there exist finite F_n ⊆ U_n such that ⋃n∈N F_n ∈ V. Must the following hold: (a) if X satisfies S_1(B_Ω, B_Ω), then X^n satisfies S_1(B, B) for every n ≥ 1; and (b) if X satisfies S_fin(B_Ω, B_Ω), then X^n satisfies S_1(B_Γ, B) for every n ≥ 1?

Let X be a set of reals. A cover U of X is nontrivial if X = ⋃U and X is not an element of U. Let Ω(X) be the family of countable open ω-covers of X, meaning that every finite subset of X is contained in some member of U, and let Γ(X) be the family of countable open γ-covers of X, meaning that U is infinite and every x in X belongs to all but finitely many members of U. For classes A and B of covers, S1(A, B) means that for every sequence ⟨Un : n ∈ N⟩ from A one can choose Un ∈ Un for each n so that {Un : n ∈ N} belongs to B, and Sfin(A, B) means that for every sequence ⟨Un : n ∈ N⟩ from A one can choose finite Fn ⊆ Un for each n so that ⋃n Fn belongs to B. Is it consistent with ZFC that, for at least one of the three classes of sets of reals satisfying Sfin(Ω, Ω), S1(Γ, Ω), or Sfin(Γ, Ω), that class is closed under finite unions?

Is it consistent with ZFC that the class of sets of reals X satisfying Sfin(BΩ, BΩ) is closed under finite unions? Explicitly: if X1, ..., Xm are sets of reals, each of which has the property that for every sequence ⟨Un : n ∈ ℕ⟩ of countable Borel ω-covers of Xi there exist finite subsets Fn ⊆ Un with ⋃n Fn again a countable Borel ω-cover of Xi, must ⋃j=1m Xj also satisfy this property in some model of ZFC? Here a cover is understood to be nontrivial, and an ω-cover is one in which every finite subset of the space is contained in some member of the cover.

For the class of sets of reals X, let O be the family of nontrivial open covers of X and Γ the family of open γ-covers of X, where a γ-cover is an infinite open cover such that each x ∈ X belongs to all but finitely many members. Let Ufin(Γ, O) denote the property that for every sequence ⟨Un : n ∈ ℕ⟩ of members of Γ with no finite subcover, there exist finite subfamilies Fn ⊆ Un such that {⋃Fn : n ∈ ℕ} is an open cover of X. If add(Ufin(Γ, O)) is the least cardinal κ such that there exist sets of reals {Xα : α < κ}, each satisfying Ufin(Γ, O), whose union fails Ufin(Γ, O), is add(Ufin(Γ, O)) equal to b, the least cardinality of an unbounded family in (ℕ^ℕ, ≤*)?

For the class of sets of reals X satisfying S1(Γ, Γ), where Γ(X) is the family of nontrivial open γ-covers of X (that is, infinite open covers U of X such that every x in X belongs to all but finitely many members of U), and S1(Γ, Γ) means that for every sequence ⟨U_n : n in ω⟩ from Γ(X) there exist choices U_n in U_n such that {U_n : n in ω} is again a γ-cover of X, is the additivity number add(S1(Γ, Γ))—the least cardinal κ for which there is a family {X_α : α < κ} of sets of reals each satisfying S1(Γ, Γ) but with ⋃_{α<κ} X_α failing S1(Γ, Γ)—equal to the bounding number b, the least cardinality of an ≤*-unbounded subset of ω^ω?

Is it consistent with ZFC that add(N) < add(S_1(O,O)), where N is the ideal of Lebesgue null subsets of R, a set of reals X satisfies S_1(O,O) (the Rothberger property) if for every sequence of open covers (U_n : n in N) of X there exist U_n in U_n such that {U_n : n in N} is still an open cover of X, and add(S_1(O,O)) is the least cardinal κ for which there exists a family of κ sets of reals, each with property S_1(O,O), whose union does not satisfy S_1(O,O)?

For each n∈N, let p_{2n} be the degree-2n polynomial in Kaliaguine's multiple-orthogonality system defined by ∫_{-1}^{0} p_{2n}(x)x^k w(x)dx = ∫_{0}^{1} p_{2n}(x)x^k w(x)dx = 0 for k=0,1,...,n-1, where w(x)=x^γ(1-x)^α(1+x)^β and α,β,γ>-1. Since p_{2n} has exactly n zeros in each of the intervals (-1,0) and (0,1), is it true that each of these two n-point zero sets is an equilibrium position of n positive unit charges on its own subinterval, under mutual logarithmic repulsion and the external field generated by fixed charges α/2, β/2, γ/2 at 1,-1,0, respectively, together with n fixed charges of weight 1/2 located at the zeros on the opposite subinterval? ([e-archivo.uc3m.es](https://e-archivo.uc3m.es/bitstreams/8b68af7f-af5a-4e36-b863-db1686a0058e/download))

For each fixed n in N, let P_n^(lambda) be the degree-n Freud-type orthogonal polynomial for the perturbed measure dmu_lambda(x) = exp(-x^4) dx + lambda delta_0 on R, and let X_n^*(lambda) be its zero set. In the electrostatic model attached to P_n^(lambda), with total energy E(X) = -sum_{i<j} log|x_i - x_j| + sum_i phi_n(x_i), where the external field has long-range part x^4/2 and Freud-type short-range part (1/2) log|Q_4(x,n)/x^2|, is there, for each n, a critical value lambda_0(n) > 0 such that X_n^*(lambda) is the global minimizer of E for 0 <= lambda < lambda_0(n), whereas for lambda > lambda_0(n) the zeros still form a critical configuration but no longer a stable equilibrium (that is, they cease to minimize E)?

Let X* be the zero set of the degree-n Freud-type orthogonal polynomial for the semiclassical measure obtained by perturbing the Freud weight e^{-x^4} dx by adding a point mass λ > 0 at x = 0. In the electrostatic model described in Section 4, whose external field is Φ(x) = x^4/2 + (1/2) ln|Q4(x,n)/x^2|, the zeros X* are known to satisfy the critical-point equations (2.6) for the total logarithmic energy E(X). Must X* in fact be a stable equilibrium, i.e. satisfy E(X*) = min E(X)? More generally, beyond mere criticality, which of the stronger equilibrium notions from Section 2 remain valid for X*—in particular, is X* at least a local minimum of E, or a Nash-type equilibrium in which each coordinate minimizes its own energy when the other zeros are fixed? The paper’s nearby conjectural scenario is that, for each n, there may exist a threshold λ0(n) such that stability holds for 0 ≤ λ < λ0(n) but fails for λ > λ0(n).

For a fixed n in N and real parameters α,β, let E(X) be the Jacobi electrostatic energy of an n-point configuration X = {x_1,...,x_n} in C, with logarithmic pair interaction, external field generated by fixed charges (β+1)/2 at -1 and (α+1)/2 at +1, and E(X)=+infinity if two points coincide. In the classical case α,β > -1, Theorem 1 considers the family F of compact continua K subset C containing -1 and +1, defines m(K)=inf{E(X): X subset K, #X=n}, and proves that E*=sup_{K in F} m(K) is attained uniquely at the zero set of P_n^(α,β). Does this max-min characterization remain valid, after replacing F by the appropriate admissible family of continua, for every real-parameter orthogonality regime of the Jacobi polynomial P_n^(α,β)? In particular, when 2n + α + β < -1, should the admissible family consist of continua extending to infinity and separating -1 from +1, with the additional requirements that +1 belong to the continuum when α + n > 0, -1 belong to it when β + n > 0, and infinity belong to it when n + α + β + 1 < 0, so that the unique extremal configuration is again the zero set of P_n^(α,β)?

For the examples of orthogonal matrix polynomials {P_n}_{n>=0} considered by Duran and Grünbaum, which satisfy a second-order linear matrix differential equation of the form P_n''(x)A_2(x) + P_n'(x)A_1(x) + P_n(x)A_0(x) = Γ_n P_n(x), where A_j are matrix polynomials independent of n with degrees <= 2, 1, and 0 respectively and Γ_n are Hermitian matrices, can one construct and analyze an electrostatic interpretation of the zeros of these orthogonal matrix polynomials analogous to the scalar hypergeometric/classical case?

In the generalized Lame or Heine-Stieltjes setting, let E_n be a degree-n polynomial solution of E_n''(x) + (sum_{i=0}^p gamma_i/(x-a_i)) E_n'(x) - C_n(x) E_n(x)/A(x) = 0, where A(x) = product_{i=0}^p (x-a_i) and deg C_n <= p-1, and suppose that the zeros X_n of E_n form a critical configuration of the discrete logarithmic energy E(X) rather than a global minimizer. If mu_n = nu_{E_n}/n denotes the normalized zero-counting measure of E_n, does mu_n converge in the weak-* sense as n -> infinity to a continuous critical measure mu for the same electrostatic problem, and conversely, does every such continuous critical measure arise as the weak-* limit of a sequence of these discrete critical measures? In the real-line case, 'continuous critical measure' means that the logarithmic potential of mu, plus the external field when present, is constant on each connected component of supp(mu), although the constants may differ from one component to another.

In the semiclassical limit n -> infinity, for Heine-Stieltjes polynomials whose zeros form critical configurations of the discrete logarithmic energy E(X) rather than its global minimum, can one obtain a feasible description of the multi-parameter family of continuous critical probability measures mu on the real line that arise in this Heine-Stieltjes class, where U^mu (together with the external field, when present) is constant on each connected component of supp(mu), with the constants allowed to differ from component to component?

Over an algebraically closed field k of characteristic 0, does there exist a connected semisimple algebraic group G and a finite-dimensional algebraic G-module V, whose stabilizer in G of a point in general position is trivial, such that V and the dual G-module V* are not birationally G-isomorphic; equivalently, such that there is no G-equivariant birational map V dashed arrow V*?

Let k be an algebraically closed field of characteristic 0. Does there exist a connected semisimple algebraic k-group G, a finite-dimensional algebraic G-module V whose stabilizers of points in general position are trivial, and an automorphism σ of G, such that, if σV denotes the same underlying variety V endowed with the twisted G-action g·v := σ(g)·v, then there is no G-equivariant birational map from V to σV; equivalently, V and σV are not birationally G-isomorphic as G-varieties?

Let k be an algebraically closed field of characteristic 0, let d ≥ 1 be an integer, let G := SL_d/μ_d, and let V := Sym^d(k^d) with its natural G-action. Let σ be the automorphism of G induced by the automorphism g ↦ (g^T)^(-1) of SL_d, and let σV denote the corresponding twist of V, i.e. the same underlying variety with G-action g · v := σ(g) acting through the original action on V. Are the G-varieties V and σV G-equivariantly birationally isomorphic? ([publications.mfo.de](https://publications.mfo.de/bitstream/handle/mfo/2987/OWR_2007_01.pdf?isAllowed=y&sequence=1))

Let k be an algebraically closed field of characteristic 0, and let G be a connected simple algebraic k-group with Lie algebra Lie(G). Endow G with the conjugation action of G and Lie(G) with the adjoint action. Define the Cayley degree Cay(G) to be the least positive integer d for which there exists a dominant rational G-equivariant map G --> Lie(G) of degree d. Determine Cay(G) for every connected simple algebraic group G.

Over an algebraically closed field k of characteristic 0, let SL_5 act on itself by conjugation and on sl_5 = Lie(SL_5) by the adjoint action. Determine the exact value of the Cayley degree Cay(SL_5), defined as the minimum of [k(SL_5) : φ^*k(sl_5)] over all dominant SL_5-equivariant rational maps φ: SL_5 ⇢ sl_5.

Over an algebraically closed field k of characteristic 0, let G be a connected linear algebraic group with Lie algebra Lie(G), and define Cay(G) to be the minimum of deg(φ) over all generalized Cayley maps φ: G ⇢ Lie(G), i.e. dominant rational G-equivariant maps for the conjugation action on G and the adjoint action on Lie(G). Does there exist such a group G with Cay(G) > 2? More specifically, does there exist a connected simple algebraic group G with Cay(G) > 2?

Working over an algebraically closed field k of characteristic zero, let G be a connected reductive algebraic k-group, with G acting on itself by conjugation and on Lie(G) by the adjoint action. Define the Cayley degree Cay(G) to be the minimum of deg(φ), where φ ranges over dominant G-equivariant rational maps φ: G ↛ Lie(G) (equivalently, deg(φ) = [k(G):φ^*k(Lie(G))]). Given a positive integer d, does there exist such a group G with Cay(G) > d? Moreover, does there exist a connected simple algebraic k-group G with Cay(G) > d?

Let G be a connected complex reductive algebraic group acting algebraically on C^n, and let π: C^n -> C^n//G be the affine (categorical) quotient. Assume that dim(C^n//G) = 2. Must the quotient surface C^n//G be isomorphic, as an affine algebraic surface over C, to C^2/Γ for some finite cyclic subgroup Γ of GL_2(C)?

Let G be a connected complex reductive algebraic group acting algebraically on C^n. Assume that the categorical quotient C^n//G has dimension 2, so that, by the theorem recalled in the paper, there exists a finite group Γ acting algebraically on C^2 with C^n//G ≅ C^2/Γ. Must Γ be cyclic?

For the quadratic polynomial f_λ: ℂ → ℂ given by f_λ(z)=λ z+z^2, where λ=exp(2πiθ) and θ is irrational, assume that f_λ is a Cremer polynomial, i.e. the irrationally indifferent fixed point 0 is not analytically conjugate to a rotation near 0. Does the Julia set J(f_λ) contain a topological arc with endpoints 0 and -λ, where -λ is the nonzero preimage of 0 under f_λ?

Let f_lambda(z)=lambda z+z^2 be a quadratic polynomial on ℂ, where lambda=e^{2πiθ} with θ∈ℝ\ℚ. Assume that f_lambda is not analytically conjugate in any neighborhood of the fixed point 0 to the rotation z↦lambda z; equivalently, in the terminology of the paper, assume that f_lambda is a Cremer polynomial. Give a plausible topological model for the Julia set J(f_lambda).

Can one make a good computer picture of the Julia set J(f_λ) for some Cremer quadratic polynomial f_λ(z)=λz+z^2 on ℂ, where λ=e^{2π i θ} with θ irrational and f_λ is not analytically conjugate near the fixed point 0 to the rotation z↦λz? ([web.pdx.edu](https://web.pdx.edu/~veerman/bielefeld.pdf))

Let f_λ(z)=λz+z^2 with λ=e^{2π iθ}, where θ is irrational, and suppose that f_λ is a Cremer polynomial, meaning that f_λ is not analytically conjugate near the fixed point 0 to the rotation z↦λz. Does there exist an external ray of the Julia set J(f_λ) that lands at the fixed point 0?

For which parameters λ=e^{2πiθ} with θ irrational, such that the quadratic polynomial f_λ(z)=λz+z^2 is a Cremer polynomial (that is, f_λ is not analytically conjugate near its fixed point 0 to the rotation z↦λz), is the unique critical point z_c=-λ/2 accessible from the complement of the Julia set J(f_λ); equivalently, for which such λ does there exist an arc γ:[0,1]→ℂ with γ([0,1))⊂ℂ∖J(f_λ) and γ(1)=z_c?

Let f_λ(z) = λz + z^2 be a quadratic polynomial on C, where λ = exp(2πiθ). Assume that θ is irrational and that f_λ is a Cremer polynomial, i.e. f_λ is not analytically conjugate near its fixed point 0 to the rigid rotation z ↦ λz. For the Julia set J(f_λ), how many connected components does the punctured set J(f_λ) - {0} have? In particular, is J(f_λ) - {0} composed of countably infinitely many connected components?

Let f_lambda(z) = lambda z + z^2 be a quadratic polynomial on C, where lambda = exp(2 pi i theta) with theta irrational, and assume that f_lambda is analytically conjugate near the fixed point 0 to the rigid rotation z |-> lambda z; equivalently, f_lambda is a Siegel polynomial and has a Siegel disk centered at 0. Does there exist such an f_lambda whose Siegel disk has boundary that is not a Jordan curve (that is, not a simple closed curve)?
Let P_c(z)=z^2+c with complex parameter c ∈ ℂ, and assume that the Julia set J(P_c) is connected. For exactly which parameters c is the Julia set J(P_c) locally connected?
For the quadratic polynomial P_c:C→C defined by P_c(z)=z^2+c, with c real and with connected Julia set J(P_c), is J(P_c) locally connected?

Let P_c: C → C be the quadratic polynomial P_c(z)=z^2+c, and let c=c_Feig denote the real Feigenbaum parameter of the quadratic family (the accumulation point of the period-doubling cascade, so that J(P_c) is connected). Is the Julia set J(P_{c_Feig}) locally connected as a subset of C? ([math.stonybrook.edu](https://www.math.stonybrook.edu/preprints/ims90-1.pdf))

Let P_c(z)=z^2+c with c∈C, and let M={c∈C : J(P_c) is connected}. For a fixed c∈M, write QC(c)⊂Top(c)⊂Com(c)⊂C for the quasiconformal, topological, and combinatorial classes of P_c. Assume that every quadratic polynomial in Com(c) (respectively, in Top(c)) satisfies the secondary limbs condition and has a priori bounds. Must it follow that Com(c)={c} (respectively Top(c)={c})? In particular, since combinatorial rigidity Com(c)={c} is equivalent to local connectivity of the Mandelbrot set M at c, does this yield local connectivity of M at c?

For the quadratic family P_c(z) = z^2 + c, let M be the quadratic connectedness locus (the Mandelbrot set), and for a reduced rational interior angle tau = p/q let M_tau denote the limb of M with interior angle p/q. Does there exist a universal constant K > 0, independent of tau, such that diam(M_tau) < K/q^2 for every tau? If not, does there at least exist a universal constant K > 0 such that diam(M_tau) < K log(q)/q^2 for every tau?

Let P_c(z)=z^2+c, with connected Julia set J(P_c). If the unique critical point 0 is nonrecurrent under iteration of P_c, must there exist a conformal metric of the form ρ(z)|dz|, allowing integrable singularities, with respect to which P_c is expanding on J(P_c)?

Let P,Q∈C[z] be monic polynomials of the same degree d≥2, and suppose the following mating construction is defined: compactify each dynamical plane by a circle at infinity on which the map acts by θ↦dθ, identify the two boundary circles by θ∼−θ, and then collapse every external ray of P and Q to a point, obtaining a branched self-map of the topological sphere. For which pairs (P,Q) is this mating conjugate to a rational function of degree d on the Riemann sphere?

Given two complex monic polynomials P1,P2 in C[z] of the same degree d, form their topological mating as in §2 by viewing each polynomial as a map of a closed disk obtained by adjoining the circle at infinity, extending the boundary dynamics by theta -> d theta, gluing the two circles at infinity, and collapsing each external ray to a point; the resulting branched self-map of the sphere is expected to be conjugate to a rational map of degree d. Can this mating be realized by quasiconformal surgery, i.e. by finding a conformal structure preserved by the branched map so that the Ahlfors-Bers theorem produces the corresponding rational map?

Fix a common degree d and consider the topological mating of two monic complex polynomials P and Q of degree d, formed by gluing their dynamical disks along the circle at infinity and collapsing external rays, whenever this quotient is realized by a degree-d rational map. Is the resulting rational map, viewed up to Möbius conjugacy, continuous as a function of the pair (P,Q) in the coefficient topology?

Let P1 and P2 be complex polynomials with connected Julia sets. Assume that P1 has a periodic critical point omega of period k, and that no other critical point of P1 lies in the full basin of the corresponding superattracting cycle. Let d be the local degree of P1 at omega, and assume that P2 has exactly one critical point, also of degree d. In the first topological description of tuning from Section 2, assume moreover that the closure bar(B) of the immediate basin B of omega is homeomorphic to the closed unit disk bar(D) and that J(P2) is locally connected, so that after choosing a conjugacy between P1^k|bar(B) and z -> z^d on bar(D), one forms a branched self-map P3 by replacing B with a copy of the dynamical plane of P2, identifying the circle at infinity of that copy with partial B so that external angles for P2 correspond to internal angles in bar(B), collapsing each external ray of P2 to a point, and making the analogous modification at each preimage of B (with the map on the modified B given by P2 and on the other inverse images by the identity). Must the resulting topological map P3 be conjugate to a polynomial of the same degree as P1? ([math.stonybrook.edu](https://www.math.stonybrook.edu/preprints/ims90-1.pdf))

Let P1 be a complex polynomial with a periodic critical point ω of period k, such that no other critical points lie in the full basin of the corresponding superattracting cycle, and let P2 be a complex polynomial with exactly one critical point whose local degree equals the local degree of ω; assume that J(P1) and J(P2) are connected. In the topological tuning construction described in §2—where one replaces the immediate basin of ω and its preimages in the dynamical plane of P1 by copies of the dynamical plane of P2, matching external angles of P2 to internal angles of the basin (in the first description assuming additionally that the basin closure is a closed disk and J(P2) is locally connected)—can this tuning be realized by quasiconformal surgery? ([math.stonybrook.edu](https://www.math.stonybrook.edu/preprints/ims90-1.pdf))

Fix a complex polynomial P1 with a periodic critical point ω of period k, assume that no other critical points lie in the full basin of the associated superattracting cycle, and let d be the local degree of ω. Let P2 be a complex polynomial with one critical point of degree d, and assume that J(P1) and J(P2) are connected; in the explicit tuning setup described in §2, also assume that the closure of the immediate basin of ω is homeomorphic to the closed unit disk and that J(P2) is locally connected, with one of the possible conjugacies to z -> z^d chosen when d > 2. Whenever the tuning construction produces a polynomial P3 of degree deg(P1), called P1 tuned with P2 at ω, does the resulting tuned polynomial P3, regarded up to conjugacy, vary continuously as P2 varies?

Fix a complex polynomial P2 whose Julia set is connected and locally connected and which has exactly one critical point of local degree d. Let P1 vary among complex polynomials of degree greater than 2 with connected Julia set, having a periodic critical point ω of fixed period k and local degree d, such that no other critical points lie in the full basin of the corresponding superattracting cycle and the closure of the immediate basin of ω is homeomorphic to the closed unit disk; when d > 2, fix one of the possible conjugacies between P1^k on that closed basin and z ↦ z^d on the closed unit disk. For the tuning obtained by tuning P1 with P2 at ω, does the resulting tuning vary continuously as P1 varies within this family? ([math.stonybrook.edu](https://www.math.stonybrook.edu/preprints/ims92-7/S1-Ben.pdf))

In the tuning setup of §2, let {P_{1,k}} be a sequence of admissible source polynomials converging in polynomial parameter space, where each P_{1,k} has a periodic critical point ω_k whose basin contains no other critical points, and let P_2 be an admissible polynomial with exactly one critical point of the same local degree as ω_k, with the connectedness and local-connectivity assumptions required for the tuning construction; after fixing the necessary conjugating choice when the common critical degree is greater than 2, do the tuned polynomials obtained by tuning P_{1,k} with P_2 converge, and is the limiting polynomial independent of the choice of P_2?

Fix a reduced rational p/q in Q/Z and an odd integer m=2k+1 with 1 <= m <= 2q-1. Let M_{p/q} be the small copy of the Mandelbrot set growing from the hyperbolic component H_{p/q}, with root root_{p/q}, and let C_{p/q,m} be the locus of marked cubic polynomials P_{A,D} whose fixed point is the landing point of 2q distinct external rays of combinatorial rotation number p/q, with exactly m of those rays encountered when moving counterclockwise from the critical point -1 to the critical point +1. For every pair c,c' in M_{p/q} \ {root_{p/q}}, does the Epstein-Yampolsky intertwining surgery on quadratic-like maps hybrid equivalent to k_c(z)=z^2+c and k_{c'}(z)=z^2+c' straighten to a unique cubic polynomial P_{A,D} in C_{p/q,m}, and do these polynomials vary so as to define a homeomorphic embedding h_{p/q,m}:(M_{p/q} \ {root_{p/q}}) x (M_{p/q} \ {root_{p/q}}) -> C_{p/q,m} that sends H_{p/q} x H_{p/q} onto a disjoint-type component H_{p/q,m} of type D_{q,q}?

Let P1 be a monic complex polynomial with connected Julia set, and suppose that P1 has a repelling fixed point x0 at which a ray lands with rotation number p/q. Let P2 be a monic complex polynomial with a ray of the same rotation number landing at a repelling periodic point whose period divides q. Form the topological intertwining by cutting the dynamical plane of P1 along the q forward images of the first ray to obtain q wedges, slitting the dynamical plane of P2 along the corresponding rays, inserting those wedges, and modifying the map near inverse images of the cut rays so as to make it continuous. Can this intertwining be constructed by quasiconformal surgery, so that the resulting map is conjugate to a polynomial? ([citeseerx.ist.psu.edu](https://citeseerx.ist.psu.edu/document?doi=d0fa5df0854b718da3750160d8ff2cd99feb850c&repid=rep1&type=pdf&utm_source=openai))

Fix a monic polynomial P1 with connected Julia set and a repelling fixed point x0 such that an external ray of combinatorial rotation number p/q lands at x0. Cut the dynamical plane of P1 along the q forward images of that ray to obtain q wedges, and perform the intertwining surgery with a monic polynomial P2 that has a ray of the same combinatorial rotation number landing on a repelling periodic point whose period divides q, by slitting the P2 plane along the corresponding rays, inserting those wedges, and adjusting the map near inverse images of the cut rays to make it continuous. In the cases where this intertwining construction yields a map conjugate to a polynomial, does the resulting polynomial depend continuously on P2?

Fix an integer n >= 2, and let X_n be the space of monic complex polynomials P(z) = z^n + a_{n-1}z^{n-1} + ... + a_1 z with |a_1| >= 1, endowed with the usual coefficient topology. For every P in X_n, the origin is a nonattracting fixed point, and the Julia set of P is not assumed to be connected. On the subset of X_n for which at least one external (dynamic) ray lands at 0, let rho(P) in R/Z denote the well-defined rotation number of the external rays landing at 0 under the angle map theta -> n theta mod 1. Does rho extend uniquely to a continuous map X_n -> R/Z, normalized by the condition that whenever a_1 = e^{2 pi i theta}, the extended map has value theta mod 1?

Let P=P(n,μ) be the space of piecewise monotone maps f:[0,1]→[0,1] with n laps and prescribed boundary map μ on {0,1}. Starting from f_0∈P, define inductively for each k≥0 the unique degree-n polynomial p_k∈P whose critical points all lie in [0,1] and whose critical values occur in the same order as those of f_k; let h_k:[0,1]→[0,1] be the unique homeomorphism sending the critical points of f_k to those of p_k and satisfying p_k∘h_k=f_k; and set f_{k+1}=h_k∘p_k=h_k∘f_k∘h_k^{-1}. Assume first that f_0 is post-critically finite and has no Thurston obstruction, so that Thurston's argument yields p_k→p_∞ with the same kneading sequence as f_0. Under what explicit hypotheses on f_0 (and in what natural topology on P, e.g. uniform convergence on [0,1]) can one prove that the conjugated maps f_k also converge to the same limit p_∞? In particular, can one formulate and prove such a convergence theorem for some class of non-post-critically-finite maps as well?

In the setting of §3, let P = P(n, μ) be the space of piecewise monotone maps f : I = [0,1] → I with prescribed boundary map μ, and run Thurston’s interval-map algorithm starting from f0 ∈ P by replacing the polynomial lift at each step with a lift pk chosen from the family p(x) = -|x|^α + c, where α > 1. If f0 has a preperiodic or periodic kneading sequence, does this modified Thurston algorithm converge?

In the setting of §3, let P = P(n, mu) be the space of piecewise monotone maps f:I=[0,1]->I with n laps and prescribed boundary action mu on {0,1}. Starting from f_0 in P, modify Thurston's interval algorithm by replacing the polynomial lift with a lift chosen from a fixed family F subset P: at each stage choose p_k in F having the same critical values as f_k, encountered in the same order, let h_k:[0,1]->[0,1] be the homeomorphism carrying the critical points of f_k to those of p_k and satisfying p_k o h_k = f_k, and define f_{k+1} = h_k o f_k o h_k^{-1}. What general structural property of the lifting family F guarantees convergence of this modified Thurston algorithm whenever the initial map f_0 has a periodic or preperiodic kneading sequence?

In the setting of §3, fix P=P(n,μ), the space of piecewise monotone maps f:I=[0,1]→I with n laps and prescribed boundary map μ:{0,1}→{0,1}. Starting from any f0∈P, run the interval Thurston algorithm but, instead of taking polynomial lifts, choose at each step a lift p_k from a fixed family F⊂P having the same critical values as f_k, encountered in the same order, and let h_k:[0,1]→[0,1] be the unique homeomorphism sending the critical points of f_k to those of p_k with p_k∘h_k=f_k, so that f_{k+1}=h_k∘f_k∘h_k^{-1}. What general property of the lifting family F is sufficient to guarantee convergence of this Thurston iteration for arbitrary kneading sequences, without restricting to the preperiodic or periodic case?

Let f be a polynomial diffeomorphism of C^2 with Jacobian determinant δ, and suppose that K^+(f):={z∈C^2 : {f^n(z)}_{n≥0} is bounded} has non-empty interior. Let U be a connected component of int(K^+(f)). By Montel, the family of iterates {f^n|_U} has a locally uniformly convergent subsequence f^{n_j}|_U→g:U→C^2. If |δ|<1, the rank r of g is 0 or 1, while if |δ|=1, r=2. Can U be a wandering component? If so, necessarily |δ|<1; in that case, can the limit map g occur with rank 0 or with rank 1, and can such a wandering U be bounded, unbounded of finite volume, or unbounded of infinite volume? ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/math/9201271))

Let f be a polynomial diffeomorphism of C^2 with Jacobian determinant δ, and suppose that K^+(f) := {z in C^2 : the forward orbit {f^n(z)} is bounded} has nonempty interior. Let U be a connected component of int K^+(f) that is not wandering; after replacing f by a finite iterate, assume f(U)=U. Let g: U -> C^2 be the limit of a convergent subsequence of the iterates f^n|_U. In the rank-one case (so rank(g)=1, hence |δ|<1 in the paper's setup), Milnor notes that if g has a fixed point in U, then g is a retraction of U onto a Siegel disk. Can such a rank-one limit map g instead be a retraction of U onto a Herman ring, or onto a punctured Siegel disk?

Let f be a polynomial diffeomorphism of C^2 with Jacobian determinant δ, assume that K^+(f):={z∈C^2 : the forward orbit of z is bounded} has non-empty interior, let U be a connected component of Int(K^+(f)), and let g:U→C^2 be a holomorphic limit of a convergent subsequence of iterates of f|_U. In the nonwandering case, after replacing f by a finite iterate so that f(U)=U, suppose rank(g)=2 (hence |δ|=1). If g has a fixed point, then U is a Siegel bi-disk. Besides this case, can such a rank-two stable region U be biholomorphic to the product of two Herman rings, or to the product of a Herman ring with a Siegel disk?

For a fixed degree d, let Rat_d be the space of degree-d rational self-maps of the Riemann sphere and Poly_d the space of degree-d complex polynomials, each equipped with the topology of uniform convergence. If, for a map f, C(f) denotes its set of critical points, P(f) = ∪_{n≥1} f^n(C(f)) its post-critical set, and J(f) its Julia set, and if f is called expanding when P(f) ∩ J(f) = ∅ (equivalently, when some iterate f^n uniformly expands the spherical metric on J(f)), is the set of expanding maps dense in Rat_d and in Poly_d?

Let f: P^1(C) -> P^1(C) be a rational map of degree at least 2, let C be its set of critical points, let P = union_{n>=1} f^n(C) be its post-critical set, and let J = J(f) be its Julia set. Assume f is geometrically finite in the sense that P intersect J is finite (equivalently, every critical point of f that lies in J is preperiodic). Must one have the following dichotomy: either J = P^1(C) and the action of f on J is ergodic, or else delta := dim_H(J) < 2? In the latter case, what can be said about the delta-dimensional Hausdorff measure of J and about the dynamics of f with respect to that measure class?

Let f be a rational map of the Riemann sphere, let C be its set of critical points, let P = union_{n>=1} f^n(C) be its post-critical set, and let J = J(f) be its Julia set. Assume that f is geometrically finite in the sense that P ∩ J is finite (equivalently, every critical point of f that lies in J is preperiodic; rationally indifferent cycles are allowed). Must every connected component of J be locally connected?

Let f be a rational map of the Riemann sphere, with critical set C, post-critical set P(f)=⋃_{n≥1} f^n(C), and Julia set J(f). Assume f is geometrically finite, meaning that P(f)∩J(f) is finite. Develop for f an analogue of the Haken decomposition for 3-manifolds. In particular, if J(f) is disconnected, can f be constructed by surgery from rational maps whose Julia sets are connected?

Let f be a rational self-map of the Riemann sphere, with critical set C(f), postcritical set P(f) = union over n >= 1 of f^n(C(f)), and Julia set J(f). Assume that f is geometrically finite in the sense that P(f) intersect J(f) is finite (equivalently, every critical point in J(f) is preperiodic; in particular, rationally indifferent cycles are allowed). Extend Thurston's combinatorial theory for critically finite rational maps, that is, for maps with finite postcritical set |P(f)| < infinity, to this geometrically finite setting: find a finite amount of topological/combinatorial data that determines f up to combinatorial equivalence relative to P(f) in the Thurston sense, and characterize exactly which such combinatorial types are realized by rational maps.

For each integer n >= 1, does there exist a constant R_n < infinity, depending only on n, such that whenever N = H^3/Γ is a complete hyperbolic 3-manifold whose fundamental group π1(N) can be generated by n elements, every embedded hyperbolic ball contained entirely in the convex core C(N) — where C(N) is the quotient by Γ of the convex hull of the limit set of Γ — has radius at most R_n?

For complex projective space P^n(C) with n > 1, are there nontrivial rational self-maps f : P^n -> P^n that are critically finite in the sense that there exist possibly reducible hypersurfaces V ⊂ W ⊂ P^n such that f : (P^n - W) -> (P^n - V) is a covering map, and for which P^n - V is Kobayashi hyperbolic? If so, how do such maps behave dynamically?

Let f be a polynomial diffeomorphism of C^2 with constant Jacobian determinant δ, and let K^+(f) be the set of points with bounded forward orbit. Suppose U is a connected component of int K^+(f) that is not wandering; after replacing f by a suitable positive iterate, assume f(U) = U. Let g: U -> C^2 be a subsequential limit of the iterates f^n|U, and assume that g has rank 0, so g(U) = {x0}. If x0 lies in ∂U, must the eigenvalues of Df at x0 be {1, ν} with 0 < |ν| < 1?

Let M ⊂ C^n be a smooth real hypersurface, let p0 ∈ M, and let r be a smooth real-valued defining function on a neighborhood U of p0 such that M ∩ U = {z ∈ U : r(z) = 0} and dr ≠ 0 on M ∩ U. Determine the local conditions on the germ of M at p0 under which every C-R function on M ∩ U admits a holomorphic extension to the one-sided neighborhood U ∩ {z ∈ U : r(z) > 0}.

Let D \subset \mathbb{C}^n, with n \ge 2, be a bounded domain with C^\infty-smooth boundary, and let \pi: \widetilde D \to \mathbb{C}^n denote the envelope of holomorphy of D, regarded as a Riemann domain over \mathbb{C}^n. Must \widetilde D be finitely sheeted over \mathbb{C}^n? If this is not known, does \widetilde D at least have finite total Euclidean volume (equivalently, finite Lebesgue volume counted with multiplicity via \pi)?

Let D be a bounded strictly pseudoconvex domain in C^2 with smooth boundary, diffeomorphic to the 4-ball, and let A be an embedded analytic disc in C^2\setminus D, smooth up to the boundary, such that bA is a smooth embedded curve contained in bD. Assume, as in Proposition 1.2, that there exists an embedded smooth closed disc M\subset \overline{D} with bM=bA, int(M)\subset D, and M totally real except at exactly one elliptic complex tangent point. Is it true that the envelope of holomorphy of a sufficiently small neighborhood of M contains the whole analytic disc A?

Let X be a Stein complex space, and let U \subset X be an open subset that is locally Stein in the sense that for every point x \in \partial U there exists an open neighborhood V of x in X such that V \cap U is a Stein space. Must U itself be a Stein space?

Find geometric conditions on a compact complex manifold M such that every proper open subset U ⊊ M which is locally Stein—in the sense that for every boundary point p ∈ ∂U there exists an open neighborhood V ⊂ M with V ∩ U Stein—is itself a Stein manifold.

Let B ⊂ C^n be the unit ball, let X ⊂ B be a complex subvariety with an isolated singularity at 0, and let {Ω_t}_{0≤t≤1} be a continuously increasing family of Stein open subsets of X such that 0 ∈ ∂Ω_{1/2} and 0 ∈ Ω_t for every t > 1/2. Is it true that Ω_s is Runge in Ω_t for every 0 ≤ s < t ≤ 1? ([citeseerx.ist.psu.edu](https://citeseerx.ist.psu.edu/document?doi=ddcbe25077121277bed380761981c39a92aad464&repid=rep1&type=pdf&utm_source=openai))

Let X ⊂ ℂ^n be a complex analytic set with an isolated normal singularity at 0. Let K ⊂ X \ {0} be compact, and assume that 0 belongs to the polynomial hull widehat{K} of K in ℂ^n. If L ⊂ X is a compact set that contains a neighborhood of K in the relative topology of X, must the polynomial hull widehat{L} contain a neighborhood of 0 in X?
Let X be a Stein complex space, and let U_1 ⊂ U_2 ⊂ ... be an increasing sequence of open subsets of X such that every U_n is Stein. Must the union U := \bigcup_{n\ge 1} U_n also be a Stein space?

Let M be a complex manifold of complex dimension 2. Assume that for every compact subset K ⊂ M there exists an open set U with K ⊂ U ⊂ M such that U is biholomorphic to the open unit ball B = {z ∈ C^2 : ||z|| < 1}. Must M be biholomorphic to one of the following three complex manifolds: B, Delta x C, or C^2, where Delta = {z ∈ C : |z| < 1}? (The analogous statement is false in complex dimension 3.)

Let X be a complex manifold of complex dimension 2 such that X admits an exhaustion X = ∪j=1^∞ Xj by a countable increasing sequence of proper open subsets X1 ⊂ X2 ⊂ ⋯, with each Xj biholomorphic to ℂ^2. Must X itself be biholomorphic to ℂ^2?

Let \(\Omega \Subset \mathbb{C}^n\) be a pseudoconvex domain with \(C^\infty\)-smooth boundary. For each integer \(k\ge 1\), let \(A^k(\overline{\Omega}) := H(\Omega)\cap C^k(\overline{\Omega})\), endowed with the \(C^k\)-topology, and let \(A^\infty(\overline{\Omega}) := H(\Omega)\cap C^\infty(\overline{\Omega})\). Is \(A^\infty(\overline{\Omega})\) dense in \(A^k(\overline{\Omega})\) for every \(1\le k\le \infty\)?

Let Ω ⊂ ℂ^n be a bounded pseudoconvex domain with C^∞ boundary, and assume that the closure Ω̄ has a Stein neighborhood basis; that is, for every open neighborhood V of Ω̄ there exists a pseudoconvex open set U such that Ω̄ ⊂ U ⊂⊂ V. Is it true that every function f ∈ A^∞(Ω) := O(Ω) ∩ C^∞(Ω̄) can be uniformly approximated on Ω̄ by functions holomorphic on open neighborhoods of Ω̄? Equivalently, for every ε > 0, does there exist an open neighborhood U of Ω̄ and a function g ∈ O(U) such that sup_{z ∈ Ω̄} |f(z) - g(z)| < ε?

Let n ≥ 2 and let Ω be either the unit ball B^n ⊂ C^n or the unit polydisc D^n ⊂ C^n. If f_1, ..., f_k ∈ H^∞(Ω) satisfy the corona condition ∑_{j=1}^k |f_j(z)| ≥ c > 0 for every z ∈ Ω, must there exist g_1, ..., g_k ∈ H^∞(Ω) such that ∑_{j=1}^k f_j(z)g_j(z) = 1 for all z ∈ Ω?

Let H be the skew field of real quaternions, let Ω ⊂ C^2 ≅ R^4 be a domain, and let Φ = {Φ0, Φ1, Φ2, Φ3} ⊂ H be a structural set satisfying Φp Φ̄q + Φq Φ̄p = 2δp,q. On C^1(Ω; H) define DΦ = Σ_{k=0}^3 Φk ∂/∂xk and MΦ(Ω; H) = ker DΦ. For the standard structural set Φ̂ = {1, i, j, -k}, identify H with C^2 by q = z1 + z2 j, so that the ordinary holomorphic maps Hol(Ω; C^2) are viewed as a subclass of MΦ̂(Ω; H). Describe the genuinely quaternionic part MΦ̂(Ω; H) \ Hol(Ω; C^2), and determine precisely how the holomorphic class Hol(Ω; C^2) and its non-holomorphic complement sit inside MΦ̂(Ω; H), including how this picture depends on the choice of the domain Ω.

Let D be a smooth bounded pseudoconvex domain in C^n, and suppose that D is of finite type at every boundary point in the sense of D'Angelo (equivalently: for each p in boundary D, there is a finite upper bound on the order of contact of nontrivial complex analytic varieties with boundary D at p). Must every p in boundary D be a peak point for A(D)=O(D) intersect C(closure D); that is, for each p does there exist f in A(D) such that f(p)=1 and |f(z)|<1 for all z in closure D minus {p}?

Let Ω ⊂ C^n be a weakly pseudoconvex domain of finite type. Characterize the boundary sets E ⊂ ∂Ω that are peak sets for the natural domain algebra of functions holomorphic on Ω and continuous on Ω-bar; that is, determine exactly which closed boundary sets E admit a function f, holomorphic on Ω and continuous on Ω-bar, such that f = 1 on E and |f| < 1 on Ω-bar \ E. ([ar5iv.labs.arxiv.org](https://ar5iv.labs.arxiv.org/pdf/math/9509202))

Let B_n = {z \in \u2102^n : \|z\| < 1} with n \ge 2, let S = \u2202B_n, and let A(B_n) = P(S) denote the ball algebra, i.e. the uniform closure on S of the holomorphic polynomials. Characterize all Borel probability measures \mu on S that represent evaluation at the origin, in the sense that f(0) = \int_S f\,d\mu for every f \in A(B_n).

Let n >= 1, and let X be a compact, totally disconnected subset of C^n with finite one-dimensional Hausdorff measure H^1(X) < ∞. Must X be polynomially convex; equivalently, is it true that \hat X = X, where \hat X := {z in C^n : |p(z)| <= sup_{x in X} |p(x)| for every complex polynomial p}?

Open problem. Let \(n\ge 1\), let \(\Omega\subset\mathbb{C}^n\) be a bounded smoothly bounded pseudoconvex domain, and let \(V\subset \Omega\) be a divisor (i.e. an analytic hypersurface, with multiplicities allowed). Assume that \(V\) is bounded away from the Šilov boundary \(S(\Omega)\) of \(\Omega\), for instance in the sense that \(\operatorname{dist}(\overline V,S(\Omega))>0\). Must there exist a nonzero bounded holomorphic function \(f\in H^\infty(\Omega)\) such that \(f|_V\equiv 0\)? The corresponding statement is known for the polydisc by a result of Rudin.

Let Ω ⊂ ℂ^n be a bounded smoothly bounded strictly (strongly) pseudoconvex domain, and fix p > 0. Give necessary and sufficient geometric conditions on an effective divisor M in Ω, with multiplicities counted and including any indispensable topological obstruction such as the vanishing of its canonical class in H^2(Ω; ℤ), for there to exist a holomorphic function F ∈ H^p(Ω) whose zero divisor is exactly M.

Let Ω⊂ℂ^n be a smoothly bounded pseudoconvex domain. Can one formulate the ∂̄-Neumann problem in the W^1 Sobolev topology—meaning that ∂̄^* is taken as the Hilbert-space adjoint with respect to the W^1 inner product—identify the induced Sobolev boundary condition for dom ∂̄^*, and develop the corresponding ∂̄-Neumann/Hodge theory for □=∂̄∂̄^*+∂̄^*∂̄: existence and uniqueness modulo a finite-dimensional harmonic space, Sobolev regularity (including the basic/subelliptic estimate needed for the canonical solution of ∂̄u=f), and the resulting orthogonal Hodge decomposition?

Can one formulate and solve the standard \bar\partial-Neumann problem in the Hilbert space L^2(\Omega,d\mu), with d\mu a measure—i.e. obtain a measure-based L^2 theory for \bar\partial, its L^2(d\mu)-adjoint, and the associated complex Laplacian/Neumann operator—already in the basic case \Omega=\mathbb{D}\subset\mathbb{C} (the unit disc)?

Let \Omega\subset\mathbb C be a smooth bounded planar domain, let T:L^2(\Omega)\to L^2(\Omega) be the canonical L^2-minimal solution operator for \bar\partial on functions (so that for each f\in L^2(\Omega), u=Tf is the unique solution of \bar\partial u=f orthogonal to the Bergman space A^2(\Omega)), and for h\in L^\infty(\Omega) define the compact operator S_h:L^2(\Omega)\to L^2(\Omega) by S_hf=\overline{h}\,Tf. Under what conditions does S_h have a nonzero eigenvalue? In particular, when h\in H^\infty(\Omega) is holomorphic, it is easy to see that if h admits a single-valued holomorphic primitive H\in O(\Omega) on \Omega, then S_h has no nonzero eigenvalues. Is the converse true: if the holomorphic 1-form h(z)\,dz has a nontrivial period on \Omega (equivalently, h has no single-valued holomorphic primitive), must S_h possess a nonzero eigenvalue? For annuli, the answer is yes.

Let D ⊂ C^n be a bounded pseudoconvex domain with real-analytic boundary. Is the standard ∂̄-Neumann problem on D globally real-analytic hypoelliptic up to the boundary; that is, do real-analytic data give rise to solutions that are real analytic on D̄?

Does every bounded pseudoconvex domain \Omega \subset \mathbb{C}^n with real analytic boundary admit a global solution theory for the \bar\partial-equation with Hölder estimates; equivalently, for every such \Omega, can one solve \bar\partial u=f for \bar\partial-closed data f in the relevant bidegrees by a solution operator that is bounded in Hölder spaces up to the boundary?

Let Ω⊂⊂ℂ^n be a bounded pseudoconvex domain, with no smoothness assumption on ∂Ω, and let 1<p<2. Is it true that for every ∂̄-closed (0,1)-form f with coefficients in L^p(Ω), there exists u∈L^p(Ω) such that ∂̄u=f on Ω, ideally with an estimate of the form ||u||_{L^p(Ω)}≤C_{p,Ω}||f||_{L^p(Ω)}?

Let Ω ⊂⊂ C^n be a smooth bounded pseudoconvex domain. Is it true that for every bounded ∂̄-closed (0,1)-form f on Ω there exists a function u on Ω such that ∂̄u = f and ||u||_{L^∞(Ω)} ≤ C_Ω ||f||_{L^∞(Ω)} for some constant C_Ω depending only on Ω?

Let \Omega\subset\mathbb{C}^2 be a smoothly bounded convex domain. Is it true that there exists a constant C_\Omega>0 such that for every bounded \bar\partial-closed (0,1)-form f on \Omega, one can find a bounded function u on \Omega with \bar\partial u=f and \|u\|_{L^\infty(\Omega)}\le C_\Omega\,\|f\|_{L^\infty(\Omega)}?

Let \Omega \subset\subset \mathbb{C}^n be a bounded pseudoconvex domain, and consider uniform a priori estimates for solving \bar\partial u=f (for \bar\partial-closed (p,q)-forms f, 1\le q\le n). Exactly which geometric invariants of \Omega determine the constants in such estimates? In particular, beyond the basic L2 estimate controlled by a coarse size parameter such as the diameter of \Omega, which features of the domain's geometry (for example dimension, boundary regularity, pseudoconvexity/finite type, or Levi-geometric data) enter the sharp uniform bounds?

Let \(\Omega\Subset\mathbb{C}^n\) be a pseudoconvex domain with smooth boundary, and let \(0<\alpha<\beta\). If \(\Lambda_\gamma(\overline\Omega)\) denotes the Hölder/Lipschitz space of order \(\gamma\) on \(\overline\Omega\), and \(\Lambda_\alpha^{(0,1)}(\overline\Omega)\) denotes the space of \((0,1)\)-forms on \(\overline\Omega\) whose coefficients lie in \(\Lambda_\alpha(\overline\Omega)\), does the operator \(\bar\partial: \Lambda_\beta(\overline\Omega)\to \Lambda_\alpha^{(0,1)}(\overline\Omega)\) have closed range?

Let \Omega \subset \mathbb{C}^n be a bounded domain that is biholomorphic to the unit ball B^n \subset \mathbb{C}^n. Must the \bar\partial-equation on \Omega satisfy uniform estimates? The question is especially intended for the case in which the boundary \partial\Omega is very rough.
Does there exist a Stein domain Ω ⊂ C^2 that is homotopically equivalent to the 2-sphere S^2?
Let D ⊂ ℂ^n be a bounded pseudoconvex domain with Lipschitz boundary. Must D be complete with respect to its Bergman metric ds_D^2?

Characterize the bounded domains Ω ⊂ ℂ^n whose Bergman kernel K_Ω(z,w) is zero-free on Ω × Ω; that is, determine for which domains one has K_Ω(z,w) ≠ 0 for all z,w ∈ Ω (equivalently, which bounded domains are Lu Qi-Keng domains).
Does there exist a bounded smooth pseudoconvex domain G \subset \mathbb{C}^n that is not c_G-finitely compact, or even more strongly, that is not k_G-complete?

Does there exist, for some n, a smoothly bounded pseudoconvex domain D ⊂ C^n such that the infinitesimal Kobayashi metric k_D and infinitesimal Caratheodory metric c_D are not uniformly comparable on D; that is, there do not exist constants A,B > 0 such that A c_D(z;v) ≤ k_D(z;v) ≤ B c_D(z;v) for every z ∈ D and every nonzero tangent vector v ∈ C^n?

Let \Omega \subset \mathbb{C}^n be a C^\infty-smooth pseudoconvex domain, let p \in b\Omega, and let L be a germ of a smooth tangential (1,0)-vector field on b\Omega with L(p) \neq 0. If t(L,p) denotes the commutator type of L at p (the smallest length of an iterated commutator of L and \overline{L} whose normal component at p is nonzero) and c(L,p) denotes the Levi type of L at p (the smallest order at which a derivative in the directions L and \overline{L} of the Levi form in the direction L is nonzero at p), must one always have t(L,p)=c(L,p)?

Let D⊂ℂ² be a domain with real-analytic pseudoconvex boundary, and let p∈∂D be a boundary point of finite type 4. Must D be locally convexifiable near p; that is, do there exist local holomorphic coordinates in a neighborhood of p in which ∂D is convex?
Let D \subset \mathbb{C}^n be a bounded smooth pseudoconvex domain of finite D'Angelo type. Is D complete with respect to its Kobayashi metric (equivalently, the associated Kobayashi distance)?

Let D \subset C^n be a pseudoconvex domain whose boundary is of finite type. What is the boundary asymptotic behavior of its Kobayashi metric k_D; more precisely, for each boundary point p \in \partial D, how does k_D(z;X) behave as z \in D approaches p, in terms of the local finite-type geometry of \partial D and the direction X \in T_zD?

Let n ∈ N, and let D ⊂ C^n be a bounded pseudoconvex complete-circular domain, written as D = {z ∈ C^n : h(z) < 1}, where h is the Minkowski function of D. Determine necessary and sufficient conditions on h that characterize when D is complete with respect to the Carathéodory metric, the Bergman metric, and the Kobayashi metric. In doing so, preserve the paper's stated partial information: if h is continuous, then D is Bergman complete; however, when n ≥ 3, continuity of h does not by itself imply Kobayashi completeness.

Let X subset P^n(C) be a reduced projective hypersurface of degree d >= n+2 whose singularities are only normal crossings, and set U := P^n(C) \ X. Is it true that the infinitesimal Kobayashi–Royden pseudometric kappa_U is nondegenerate outside a proper complex hypersurface of U; equivalently, does there exist a proper complex hypersurface Y subset U such that kappa_U(p;v) > 0 for every point p in U \ Y and every nonzero tangent vector v in T_pU?

Does there exist a complete hyperbolic complex manifold M (that is, M is Kobayashi hyperbolic and complete for its Kobayashi distance k_M) such that k_M(p,q)=c_M(p,q) for every p,q in M, yet M is not biholomorphic to any convex domain in some C^N? If such an M exists, construct one; otherwise prove that no such manifold exists. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/math/9509202))

Let Ω ⊂ ℂ^n be a bounded C^∞-smooth pseudoconvex domain, and let ξ0 ∈ ∂Ω be an h-extendible finite-type boundary point with Catlin multitype (1,m2,…,mn). In local holomorphic coordinates z = (z1,z′) centered at ξ0, assume a defining function has the form ρ(z) = Re z1 + P(z′) + R(z), where P is a Λ-homogeneous plurisubharmonic polynomial, Λ = (1/m2,…,1/mn), and P has no pluriharmonic terms. If ηj → ξ0 nontangentially, εj := |ρ(ηj)| ≈ dist(ηj,∂Ω), and π_{1/εj}(η′j) → α under the anisotropic dilation πt(z′) = (t^{1/m2}z2,…,t^{1/mn}zn), must one have, for every integer k ≥ 1 and every X ∈ ℂ^n, the weighted limit lim_{j→∞} F^k_Ω(ηj,(π_{εj})_*X) = F^k_{M_{P,α}}((-1,0′),X), equivalently F^k_{MP}((-1 − P(α),α),X), so that in particular for k = 1 the weighted nontangential boundary behavior of the ordinary Kobayashi metric is exactly governed by the Levi invariants encoded by P?

Let \Omega\subset\subset\mathbb{C}^n be a bounded pseudoconvex domain with smooth boundary, and for each compact set K\subset\overline\Omega define its boundary plurisubharmonic hull by \widehat K:=\{z\in\overline\Omega:\varphi(z)\le \sup_K\varphi\text{ for every }\varphi\in C(\overline\Omega)\text{ that is plurisubharmonic on }\Omega\}. Is it true that if \widehat K\cap\partial\Omega=K\cap\partial\Omega for every compact K\subset\overline\Omega, then \overline\Omega admits a Stein neighborhood basis; equivalently, does every open neighborhood U of \overline\Omega contain a pseudoconvex (hence Stein) open set V with \overline\Omega\subset V\subset U?

Let Omega be a domain in C^n, and let u_m,u belong to PSH(Omega) in a class where the Bedford-Taylor Monge-Ampere measures are defined (for example, u_m,u in L^infty_loc(Omega)). Assume that u_m -> u in L^1_loc(Omega) (equivalently, weakly as plurisubharmonic functions). Find sufficient additional hypotheses on the sequence (u_m) under which the Monge-Ampere measures (dd^c u_m)^n converge weakly to (dd^c u)^n in Omega.

Let V_a be the germ of a complex analytic variety at a real point a ∈ R^d, and let X_a := V_a ∩ R^d. Define the germwise extremal function by ω_{a,V}(z) := limsup_{ζ→z} sup{u(ζ) : u is plurisubharmonic on V_a, u ≤ 1 on V_a, and u ≤ 0 on X_a}. Classify those germs V_a for which ω_{a,V} is dominated near a by the imaginary distance, i.e. for which there exists C > 0 such that ω_{a,V}(z) ≤ C|Im z| for z near a on V_a; equivalently, determine which real analytic germs X_a are of type PL via their complexification. ([www2.math.uni-wuppertal.de](https://www2.math.uni-wuppertal.de/~vogt/preprints/Eigene/106.pdf))
Classify the domains Ω ⊂ C^n with smooth boundary for which the biholomorphic automorphism group Aut(Ω), equipped with its usual compact-open topology, is noncompact.

For every n ≥ 1, if P(z) ∈ C[z_1, ..., z_n] is a homogeneous polynomial of degree 4 whose Hessian matrix Hes(P) = (∂^2P/∂z_i∂z_j) is nilpotent, must Δ_n^m(P(z)^{m+1}) = 0 for all sufficiently large integers m, where Δ_n = Σ_{i=1}^n ∂^2/∂z_i^2?

Let n≥1 and let P(z)∈C[z_1,...,z_n] be a homogeneous polynomial of degree 4 whose Hessian matrix Hes(P)=(∂^2P/∂z_i∂z_j) is nilpotent. If Δ:=Σ_{i=1}^n ∂^2/∂z_i^2 denotes the Laplace operator, must Δ^m(P(z)^{m+1}) vanish for all sufficiently large integers m (that is, does there exist M such that Δ^m(P^{m+1})=0 for every m≥M)?

Classify all proper holomorphic correspondences from the unit disc D = {z in C : |z| < 1} to itself; that is, describe all pure one-dimensional complex-analytic subsets Gamma subset D x D such that the first coordinate projection pi_1|_Gamma : Gamma -> D is surjective and proper (equivalently, Gamma intersect (D x partial D) = empty set), allowing multivalued and branched correspondences and not restricting to single-valued proper self-maps of D.

Let U,V be bounded domains in C^n, with n > 1, whose boundaries are real analytic, and assume no pseudoconvexity hypothesis on either domain. If f: U -> V is biholomorphic, must f extend biholomorphically across the boundary; equivalently, does f extend to a biholomorphic map between neighborhoods of \overline{U} and \overline{V}?

Let \Omega_1, \Omega_2 \subset \mathbb{C}^n be bounded pseudoconvex domains with C^\infty boundaries, and let f:\Omega_1 \to \Omega_2 be biholomorphic. Must f extend to a C^\infty diffeomorphism \overline{\Omega_1} \to \overline{\Omega_2}?

Let M be a Stein manifold of complex dimension n whose complex tangent bundle TM is holomorphically trivial (that is, M is holomorphically parallelizable). Must there exist a holomorphic map f:M→C^n such that df_x:T_xM→C^n is injective for every x∈M?
For each integer n >= 2, does the complex special linear group SL(n,C) admit a holomorphic immersion into C^(n^2-1)?

Let C be a smooth cubic curve in the complex projective plane P^2(C). Does the complement P^2(C) \ C admit a holomorphic immersion into C^2, necessarily by a nonalgebraic map since algebraic immersions into C^2 are known not to exist?

Let F \in C[w_0,\dots,w_n] be a polynomial such that the level hypersurface X = {w \in C^{n+1} : F(w)=1} is smooth, equivalently dF(w) \neq 0 for every w \in X. Then X is a smooth affine algebraic hypersurface of complex dimension n, and its holomorphic tangent bundle is trivial. Must every such X admit a holomorphic immersion f:X \to C^n (that is, a holomorphic map whose differential is injective at every point)?

Does there exist a proper domain Ω ⊊ ℂ^2 and a biholomorphism F: ℂ^2 → Ω such that Ω is not Runge in ℂ^2, i.e. such that not every holomorphic function on Ω can be approximated uniformly on compact subsets of Ω by entire functions on ℂ^2?

Does there exist a dissipative complex polynomial Hénon map f:C^2→C^2 of the form f(x,y)=(y,p(y)-δx), where p∈C[y] has degree at least 2 and 0<|δ|<1, that has a wandering Fatou component; that is, a Fatou component Ω whose forward images f^n(Ω) are pairwise distinct for all n≥0?

Let f: C^2 -> C^2 be a polynomial automorphism that is not conjugate to an elementary map, and let Omega be a periodic connected component of the set of points near which the forward iterates {f^n}_{n>=1} are locally bounded. Choose m >= 1 such that f^m(Omega) = Omega, and set F = f^m, so that Omega is F-invariant. If Omega is recurrent, then the paper notes that Omega is known to be either the basin of an attracting fixed point of F, the basin of a Siegel disk, or the basin of a Herman ring; can the Herman-ring case actually occur? If Omega is non-recurrent, must Omega be a semi-parabolic basin in the following precise sense: does there exist a point P in partial Omega such that F(P) = P, F^k(Q) -> P for every Q in Omega, and one eigenvalue of DF(P) is a root of unity e^(2 pi i p/q)?

For the quadratic symplectic Hénon automorphism F_c:C^2->C^2 given by F_c(z,w)=(z^2+c-w,z), with c in C, does there exist a parameter c and a periodic orbit O of F_c such that some point of O lies on the boundary of a periodic Siegel domain of F_c (that is, a periodic Fatou component on which some iterate of F_c is holomorphically conjugate to an irrational rotation)?

Let f: P^2(C) -> P^2(C) be a holomorphic endomorphism of algebraic degree d >= 2. Must there exist a fixed point p in P^2(C) with f(p)=p such that every eigenvalue of the complex linear map Df_p has modulus greater than 1?

Let F:P^k(C)->P^k(C) be a holomorphic endomorphism of algebraic degree d>=2. Must F admit a repelling periodic point; that is, does there exist p in P^k(C) and n>=1 such that F^n(p)=p and every eigenvalue of D(F^n)_p has modulus greater than 1? More generally, if F is a meromorphic self-map of P^k(C), must F admit at least one periodic orbit on which all iterates are defined?

Does there exist an integer k >= 2 and a nonlinear holomorphic endomorphism F : P^k(C) -> P^k(C) of algebraic degree d >= 2 with a wandering Fatou component U; that is, a connected component U of the Fatou set Fat(F) such that F^n(U) cap F^m(U) = emptyset for all integers n,m >= 0 with n != m?

Let k>=1, let p be a fixed point of a holomorphic map f, either globally as a holomorphic self-map f:P^k(C)->P^k(C) or locally as a holomorphic map (equivalently, a germ) defined on a neighborhood of p with f(p)=p. Classify the local dynamical behavior of the iterates {f^n} near p; in particular, determine the possible local dynamical types that can occur near p and how they are governed by the linear part Df_p together with the nonlinear terms.

Let f: P^2(C) -> P^2(C) be a holomorphic endomorphism of algebraic degree d >= 2, let C=C(f) denote its critical set, and let K ⊂ P^2(C) be a compact totally invariant set (i.e. f^{-1}(K)=K). Assume that ⋂_{n=1}^∞ f^n(C)=∅. Must f be hyperbolic on K?

Does there exist an integer d > 0, a holomorphic self-map G of complex projective space P^2 of algebraic degree d, an open neighborhood N subset H_d of G (where H_d denotes the space of holomorphic self-maps of P^2 of degree d, endowed with the supremum metric induced by the natural distance on P^2), and a compact set Ebar subset P^2 such that the set of maps H in N having infinitely many attracting periodic points (sinks) contained in Ebar is a dense G_delta subset of N?

Let f: P^2(C) -> P^2(C) be a holomorphic endomorphism of algebraic degree d >= 2. Let T be the Green current of f, and let μ := T ∧ T be its equilibrium measure (equivalently, the invariant measure of maximal entropy). If λ1 <= λ2 are the two Lyapunov exponents of f with respect to μ, must one have λ1 > 0?

Let z=(z_1, ..., z_n) and let Delta = sum_{i=1}^n d^2/dz_i^2 act on C[z]. If P(z) in C[z] is a homogeneous polynomial of degree 4 whose Hessian matrix Hes P(z) = (d^2P/dz_i dz_j) is nilpotent, must one have Delta^m(P(z)^(m+1)) = 0 for all sufficiently large integers m (equivalently, for every m > (3/2)(3^(n-2)-1))?
Does every compact reduced complex analytic space X admit a biholomorphism onto a complex-analytic subvariety of some complex manifold M? If yes, can the ambient complex manifold M be chosen compact?

Let C ⊂ P^2(C) be a smooth plane cubic curve, and set X = P^2(C) \ C. It is known that X is algebraically parallelizable and that X admits no algebraic immersion into C^2. Does X nevertheless admit a holomorphic immersion X -> C^2?

Let π:C^2→C be the projection π(λ,w)=λ, let Δ={λ∈C:|λ|<1}, and let Y⊂C^2 be a compact set with π(Y)⊂∂Δ. Assume we are in the nontrivial hull situation relevant to the paper, namely that the polynomial hull \widehat{Y} reaches the disk (equivalently, in the intended setting, π(\widehat{Y}) contains \overline{Δ}). Is it true that for every open neighborhood U of \widehat{Y} in C^2 there exists a connected one-dimensional complex submanifold S⊂U such that the restriction π|S:S→Δ is a proper finite branched covering? Equivalently: can every such polynomial hull be approximated arbitrarily closely by a finitely sheeted Riemann surface lying over the unit disk?

Let M be a complete simply connected Kähler manifold whose sectional curvature K satisfies -a^2 <= K <= -b^2 < 0 for some constants a >= b > 0. Must there exist a nonconstant bounded holomorphic function f:M -> C?

Let M be a smooth abstract CR manifold of type (2,1) (equivalently, a CR hypersurface of real dimension 5), and let p ∈ M. If M is strictly pseudoconvex at p, must M be locally CR embeddable at p into C^3; equivalently, is there a neighborhood U of p and three smooth complex-valued CR functions on U whose differentials are linearly independent? ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/0711.0227))

Let M \subset \mathbf{CP}^n be a compact embedded smooth CR manifold of odd real dimension 2p-1. What necessary and sufficient conditions on M ensure that there exists a pure p-dimensional complex analytic variety V \subset \mathbf{CP}^n \setminus M, allowed to have interior singularities, such that M is the boundary of V?

Let M_1 and M_2 be smooth strongly pseudoconvex CR 3-manifolds, each equipped with the Carnot-Carathéodory metric determined by its contact distribution and Levi form. If f:M_1->M_2 is a homeomorphism that is conformal in the metric sense, namely it sends infinitesimal Carnot-Carathéodory spheres to infinitesimal Carnot-Carathéodory spheres, must f be a CR map (equivalently, after imposing the natural orientation-preserving condition, a CR diffeomorphism)?

Let f:(M,H_M,J_M)->(N,H_N,J_N) be a smooth quasiconformal diffeomorphism between smooth strongly pseudoconvex CR manifolds of real dimension 2n+1 with n>1, and suppose f_*(H_M)=H_N. For Hermitian metrics h_M on H_M and h_N on H_N, define the pointwise distortion by K_{h_M,h_N}(f)(q)=max{|f_*X|_{h_N}: X in H_qM, |X|_{h_M}=1}/min{|f_*X|_{h_N}: X in H_qM, |X|_{h_M}=1}, and the corresponding maximal dilatation by K_{h_M,h_N}(f)=ess sup_{q in M} K_{h_M,h_N}(f)(q). Since, unlike the 3-dimensional case, this distortion depends on the chosen Hermitian metrics when n>1, does there exist a choice of Hermitian metrics h_M and h_N on the contact bundles that minimizes K_{h_M,h_N}(f) among all such choices?

Let Ω ⊂ ℂ^n be a bounded strongly pseudoconvex domain, let k_Ω denote its Kobayashi distance, and let ρ_Δ denote the Poincaré distance on the unit disc Δ. Does there exist an integer K = K(Ω) such that for every pair of points p, q ∈ Ω there are holomorphic maps f_1, ..., f_N : Δ → Ω with N ≤ K and points a_j, b_j ∈ Δ satisfying f_1(a_1) = p, f_j(b_j) = f_{j+1}(a_{j+1}) for 1 ≤ j < N, f_N(b_N) = q, and k_Ω(p, q) = Σ_{j=1}^N ρ_Δ(a_j, b_j)? Equivalently, is the minimal length of a Kobayashi chain realizing the distance between p and q uniformly bounded over all p, q ∈ Ω?

Let Ω ⊂ C^n be a pseudoconvex domain with C^∞ boundary, and let p ∈ bΩ. Assume that p has finite D'Angelo 1-type, i.e. Δ1(bΩ,p) < ∞. Must p be of finite ideal-type in Kohn's sense; equivalently, in the ring C^∞_p of germs of smooth functions at p, does Kohn's algorithm of subelliptic multiplier ideals terminate at 1, so that 1 ∈ Ik for some integer k?

For the site-disordered asymmetric zero-range process considered in the paper, with bounded nondecreasing jump-rate function r and disorder-induced critical density rho* defined from the equilibrium family, does the Euler-scale hydrodynamic limit extend from the subcritical regime to initial macroscopic density profiles that may exceed rho*, so that the empirical density still converges to the entropy solution of the corresponding conservation law and the macroscopic flux is constant on the supercritical region rho>=rho*?

For the one-dimensional totally asymmetric disordered zero-range process considered in Theorem 2, with jump rate r(k) = 1_{k >= 1}, i.i.d. site disorder alpha = (alpha_x) taking values in [c,1], and phase-transition regime p* = c integral_{[c,1]} (a - c)^(-1) Q(da) < infinity, Theorem 2 shows that under the hyperbolic scaling pi^n(nt) the empirical density converges to the entropy solution of partial_t u + partial_x f(u) = 0, where f(p) = c for p >= p*; hence if the initial macroscopic profile satisfies u_0(x) >= p* everywhere, the hydrodynamic profile does not move. Can one rigorously prove, on spatial scales finer than this hydrodynamic n-scale, that in the high-density regime p > p* the system develops spatial inhomogeneities, specifically that particles concentrate on exceptionally slow sites (alpha_x near c), and thereby describe the subhydrodynamic behavior hidden by the trivial macroscopic limit?

For the disordered asymmetric zero-range process of Section 2 on Z^d, with fixed quenched site rates alpha=(alpha_x), generator L^alpha f(eta)=sum_{x,y in Z^d} p(y-x) alpha_x r(eta(x))[f(eta^{x,y})-f(eta)], finite-range translation-invariant jump kernel p, and bounded nondecreasing jump-rate function r with r(0)=0 and r(infinity)<infinity, let eta(0) have a spatially ergodic distribution of density p. Do the distributions of eta(t) on S=Z_+^{Z^d} converge weakly, as t tends to infinity, to one of the equilibrium product measures v^alpha_phi? In the phase-transition case p*<infinity, if the initial density satisfies p>p*, does eta(t) converge weakly to the equilibrium with density p*?

Let f_K denote the hydrodynamic flux of the one-dimensional nearest-neighbor totally asymmetric simple K-exclusion process in the quenched random environment considered in the paper. Is there a critical density rho_c with 0 <= rho_c < K/2 such that f_K is constant on the entire interval [rho_c, K-rho_c] (equivalently, does the macroscopic current-density relation develop a nontrivial flat segment centered at density K/2)? In the paper’s language, this is the precise phase-transition/platoon-formation question for the disordered K-exclusion model, with the disordered TASEP as the case K=1.

Let ω be a fixed free ultrafilter on the natural numbers, let R denote the hyperfinite type II₁ factor with faithful normal trace τ, and define its Ocneanu ultrapower R^ω = l^∞(R)/I_ω where I_ω = {(x_n)_n ⊂ R : lim_{n→ω} τ(x_n^* x_n)^{1/2} = 0}. Does every type II₁ factor acting on a separable Hilbert space admit a unital, trace-preserving *-homomorphic embedding into R^ω?

Let A be an n×n complex matrix and let W(A)={x*Ax: x∈C^n, ||x||=1} denote its field of values. Let f be a function analytic on an open set containing W(A) and continuous on its closure, and let ||·|| denote the spectral operator 2-norm on C^n. Does the inequality ||f(A)|| ≤ 2 sup_{z∈W(A)}|f(z)| hold for every such A and f?

Let A and B be n×n normal matrices over the complex numbers, and let λ_1(A),…,λ_n(A) and λ_1(B),…,λ_n(B) denote their eigenvalues. For each permutation σ in the symmetric group S_n, define the complex number z_σ=∏_{i=1}^n(λ_i(A)+λ_{σ(i)}(B)). Is it true that det(A+B) lies in the convex hull of the set {z_σ: σ∈S_n} in the complex plane?

Let G be a discrete group and R a unital ring. 1) Let VCYC(G) denote the family of virtually cyclic subgroups of G and let E_{VCYC}(G) be a G–CW–complex characterized by having isotropy in VCYC(G) and contractible fixed points for each H∈VCYC(G).  Let KR_*^G(–) and LR_*^G(–) be equivariant homology theories with KR_n^G(*)≅K_n(R[G]) and LR_n^G(*)≅L_n(R[G]).  Does the projection p:E_{VCYC}(G)→* induce isomorphisms KR_*^G(E_{VCYC}(G))→K_*(R[G]) and LR_*^G(E_{VCYC}(G))→L_*(R[G]) in all degrees?  2) (Bost conjecture)  Let FIN(G) be the family of finite subgroups of G and E_{FIN}(G) its classifying space.  Let K_{l^1}^{top} be the equivariant homology theory associated to the Banach algebra l^1(G), so that H_*^G(*;K_{l^1}^{top})=K_*(l^1(G)).  Does the assembly map H_*^G(E_{FIN}(G);K_{l^1}^{top})→K_*(l^1(G)) induce an isomorphism in all degrees?

Let F be an arbitrary field and let n≥1 be an integer. For each k=1,…,n, let B_k(F) denote Goncharov’s k-th Bloch group over F, let F_ℚ^×=F^×⊗_ℤℚ, and let Λ^pF_ℚ^× be its p-th exterior power. Define the complex Γ_F(n) concentrated in cohomological degrees 1 through n by

Γ_F(n):
  B_n(F)
    → B_{n-1}(F)⊗F_ℚ^×
    → ⋯ → Λ^nF_ℚ^×

with differentials as in Goncharov (1995). Is it true that for each i=1,…,n the i-th cohomology group H^i(Γ_F(n)) is canonically isomorphic to the motivic cohomology group H^i_mot(F,ℚ(n))?

Let K be a number field and let E be an n-dimensional vector bundle over the projective line P^1_K equipped with an integrable algebraic connection ∇ defined by the linear differential system dv/dz = A(z)v with A(z) a matrix in M_n(K(z)). For a nonzero prime ideal p of the ring of integers O_K at which (E, ∇) has good reduction, let ψ_p denote the p-curvature endomorphism of the reduced connection over the finite field O_K/p. The Grothendieck–Katz p-curvature conjecture asks: If ψ_p = 0 for almost all prime ideals p of O_K, does it follow that (E, ∇) admits a full set of algebraic solutions over the algebraic closure of K(z) (equivalently, that its monodromy representation has finite image)?
For each positive integer n, let D(n) denote the maximum value of det(A) over all n×n matrices A whose entries are each either +1 or −1. Determine D(n) for every positive integer n.

Establish rigorously, and with an exact determination of their limits of validity, the numerical invariants (geometrical numbers) computed by Schubert’s enumerative calculus—namely, those obtained via the principle of special position—by carrying out explicitly the necessary elimination processes for equations of special form so as to foresee both the degrees of the final equations and the multiplicities of their solutions.

In the real projective plane RP², for each positive integer n, let C be a non-singular real algebraic curve of degree n whose real locus has the maximal number (n² − 3n + 4)/2 of connected components (Harnack’s bound). Determine, up to homeomorphism (or isotopy) of RP², all possible arrangements of these connected components (ovals), specifying their mutual positions and nesting structure.

Let A, R, and S be Noetherian commutative rings over a common base, with R local having maximal ideal m_R, and let M and N be finitely generated R-modules. Decide whether each of the following statements holds in full generality: 1. (Zero Divisor Theorem) If M≠0 has finite projective dimension over R and r∈R acts injectively on M, then r is not a zero divisor in R. 2. (Bass’s Question) If M≠0 admits a finite injective resolution, then R is Cohen–Macaulay. 3. (Intersection Theorem) If M⊗_R N≠0 has finite length, then dim N≤proj dim_R M. 4. (New Intersection Theorem) For any finite complex of free R-modules 0→G_n→…→G_0→0 whose homology ⊕H_i(G_•) has finite nonzero length, one has dim R≤n. 5. (Improved New Intersection Conjecture) If in such a complex H_i(G_•) has finite length for i>0 and H_0(G_•) admits a generator annihilated by a power of m_R, then dim R≤n. 6. (Direct Summand Conjecture) For every module-finite extension R⊆S with R regular, R is an R-module direct summand of S. 7. (Canonical Element Conjecture) For any system of parameters x_1,…,x_d of R, any lifting of the identity map K_•(x_1,…,x_d)→F_• from the Koszul complex to any free resolution F_• of the residue field R/m_R has nonzero last component. 8.
